# Code Index

## `(root)` — The repository root of tianluo (formerly SE3), a Python "Software Engineering 3.0" flow engine whose deterministic `luo` CLI, state machine, agent runners, daemon/server, and web console supervise AI coding agents — packaged via `pyproject.toml`/Hatchling with PyPI publishing on tag, and surrounded by bilingual READMEs and `docs/`, example and self-hosting `tianluo.yaml` configs, a full `tests/` suite, operational `scripts/`, and the read-only `.claude/` framework spec. <!--#ef400f4fa6888d69|84260a3073518118-->

### `.gitignore` (text) — Repository-root gitignore that inverts the usual model — it ignores everything at the root by default and then explicitly whitelists tracked top-level entries (docs/, src/, tests/, scripts/, tianluo/, config and metadata files) — plus global ignore patterns for build/cache/runtime artifacts, with carefully documented guards that keep the e2e subsystem, packaged preset prompts, and committed tianluo/ assets (charter, issues, code-index, e2e content, version-intents) trackable. <!--#00987a25504964fc|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `LICENSE` (text) — The Apache License 2.0 full legal text under which the project is licensed, defining terms, conditions, and grants for use, reproduction, and distribution of the work. <!--#2f8292753ff1e47a|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `NOTICE` (text) — Legal attribution notice stating the project tianluo (formerly SE3) is copyright 2026 Zhendong Zhang (CRE) and includes software developed by him. <!--#895577a555ca8f30|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `README.md` (markdown) — The project's main English README, introducing tianluo (CLI `luo`) as a cross-session, program-as-supervisor flow engine and covering its design rationale, the code-index/charter/why-comments knowledge system, installation and migration, quick start, the flow state machine and task types, PLAN decomposition, the three operating modes plus the web console and its auth, and a full command reference. <!--#621b2adbc1fa7cc1|ff0079e95212d38c-->
- `tianluo (田螺) — the Software Engineering 3.0 flow engine` (heading) — Top-of-README introduction presenting tianluo (formerly se3, CLI command `luo`) with version/Python/license badges and a language switcher, framing it as a project-level, cross-session flow engine — CLI + persistent state machine + code-first knowledge system — that supervises an AI coding agent unattended until the work is done. <!--#afe91e0747e4978d-->
  - `Why tianluo` (heading) — Lays out the project's five load-bearing bets — attention over tokens, a deterministic program as supervisor, code as the single source of truth, code-enforced (not LLM-promised) invariants, and runner-agnosticism — each paired with one line of concrete evidence. <!--#5a851fd534f18403-->
  - `Design Philosophy` (heading) — Parent heading grouping the rationale behind SE3's program-as-supervisor paradigm. <!--#77e6f8f8921f18d9-->
    - `1. A different paradigm: program-as-supervisor, human out-of-the-loop` (heading) — Contrasts tianluo with skills/subagents/dynamic workflows, arguing its unit of work is a whole project task supervised by a deterministic Python state machine rather than a single human-in-the-loop turn. <!--#506edb2cf4261393-->
    - `2. The real pain: attention is all you need` (heading) — Argues that human attention, not LLM capacity, is the bottleneck, and sketches the ideal five-stage session (prompt → discover → optional plan gate → fire-and-forget → pick up the deliverable) where only the first two steps require a person. <!--#70dd457357052f15-->
    - `3. The four moats that make this paradigm work` (heading) — Describes the four capabilities in-session tools lack — cross-session state machine, the code-first knowledge system, built-in failure recovery, and a portable `AgentRunner` substrate with three shipped adapters. <!--#aac3c7847ccefb3b-->
    - `luo vs Claude Code Dynamic Workflows (complementary, not competing)` (heading) — Positions tianluo (cross-session project governance) and Dynamic Workflows (in-session parallelism) as complementary and composable rather than competing. <!--#362bd7c3101f36ee-->
  - `The knowledge system: code-index + charter + why-comments` (heading) — Introduces the knowledge system that replaced the old drift-prone `tianluo/specs/**` spec mirror and its `sync_*` governance machinery with three code-colocated artifacts. <!--#d9d12e65a23e9046-->
    - `The three pieces` (heading) — Describes the three artifacts of tianluo's code-first knowledge system — code-index (a deterministically enumerated, fingerprinted structure map committed as `tianluo/code-index.md`), charter (`tianluo/charter.md`, the altitude-gated project-wide spec injected into every step), and why-comments (colocated intent comments, with the `WHY:`/`INVARIANT:` subset hard-guarded by `invariant_check`). <!--#e7e1950cae0d2ff7-->
    - `What actually got better (an honest accounting)` (heading) — An honest accounting of what replacing the spec mirror actually bought — truth back in the code, staleness eliminated by the enumerator, a collapsed governance surface, explicit granularity knobs, and a higher failure floor — while conceding summaries can still be semantically wrong. <!--#c27bcc7ece337d26-->
    - `A concrete before/after — and why spec-index could never win this` (heading) — Uses the retired `spec_index.py` as a worked example to argue code-index's coverage-over-depth bet beats a spec-index, whose upside is fundamentally capped by sitting one layer above the code. <!--#0360f6ac476f1229-->
  - `Installation` (heading) — Installation section giving the `pip install tianluo` variants (core, `[server]`, `[browser]`), a table of the installed console scripts (`luo`, `tianluo`, the transitional `se3`/`se3-server` aliases removed in 13.0.0, and `tianluo-server`), and notes that the core CLI never imports the web stack. <!--#66f43065d110ee6b-->
    - `Migrating an existing project` (heading) — Maps a project's vintage to the migrators it must run (`spec-to-new-system`, then `rename-to-tianluo`) and notes that the legacy `se3` compatibility layer works through 12.x but is removed in 13.0.0. <!--#047470af148695db-->
  - `Quick Start` (heading) — A copy-pasteable sequence covering `luo init`, discovery runs, running and resuming a task, and browsing the codebase via `luo code-index`. <!--#ca1868253e815b1d-->
    - `The flow state machine` (heading) — Presents the full step sequence as a mermaid state diagram and calls out its three subtleties: `investigate` is conditional, the post-`plan` `confirm` gate is opt-in, and `test` / `self_check` / `invariant_check` all share one fix loop back into `implement`. <!--#d0a8df4539270863-->
    - `Task types` (heading) — Documents the five accepted `luo run --type` values and their default step sequences, plus the fact that `discovery` is a `--discover` run mode rather than a type and that `confirm` steps only appear via `confirmation.steps`. <!--#0bffa1adebd61718-->
      - `PLAN decomposition: how the PLAN → IMPLEMENT phase runs` (heading) — Explains the single ANALYZE → PLAN → IMPLEMENT path, how the group count PLAN emits determines execution shape (one autonomous call vs. a parallel/dependent DAG in worktrees), and how `workflow.plan_decomposition` (`capability` vs `granular`), `plan_granularity` (`auto`/`single`/`conservative`), the optional `plan` confirmation gate, and SELF_CHECK/TEST/review scoping interact. <!--#393ba97dc7a85fc2-->
    - `Three operating modes` (heading) — Compares the three ways to run tianluo — isolated `luo run --worktree` runs with mutex-serialized merge-back, the resident `luo daemon`, and the multi-machine `tianluo-server`. <!--#dcf3447e3f36f865-->
    - `The web console` (heading) — Describes the bundled web console as the second full control surface: cross-machine fleet overview, browser task launch, discovery answering, intervention gates, history, issues, file uploads, and a mobile layout. <!--#590fe44bf51536ce-->
      - `Web console authentication` (heading) — Documents the central server's multi-tenant auth first-run flow: mint a break-glass admin token, log in, create users, and self-mint daemon keys to bind workers. <!--#b8bafac1065dcadf-->
  - `Command Reference` (heading) — Opens the command reference, noting every documented command is registered in `src/tianluo/cli.py` or one of its sub-typers. <!--#1ec4a2cc1de19b91-->
    - `Top-level commands` (heading) — Reference table of the primary `luo` CLI commands (`run`, `init`, `merge`, `merge-respond`, `merge-unlock`, `salvage`, `end-session`) with their purpose and flags. <!--#3f72177a3fd0b262-->
      - ``luo run` flags worth knowing` (heading) — Describes the notable `luo run` options — `--preset` for the two-layer prompt library, `--from-issue`, `--plan-decomposition`, `--plan-granularity`, and the deprecated `--implementation-strategy` mapping. <!--#fca613133280d2f2-->
    - ``luo code-index` — the structure map` (heading) — Documents the `luo code-index` command family, whose subcommands render the adaptive/literal structure map, show one file's symbol detail, grep the map, rebuild it incrementally or with `--force`, and report index stats. <!--#a95ad4efb93ea9e7-->
    - ``luo history` — flow history` (heading) — Documents the `luo history` subcommands for listing, showing, restoring, and filtering archived flows, and describes the per-call/step/flow usage-cost, plan-mode, and self-check regions that `show` (and the web console) present. <!--#56eb5d9a91690f0b-->
    - ``luo issue` — project issues` (heading) — Documents the `luo issue` subcommands for listing, showing, creating, editing, closing, and resetting project issues. <!--#35b8ee4dd336915c-->
    - ``luo migrate` — layout / format migrations` (heading) — Documents the `luo migrate` subcommands that list the registered migrators (`spec-to-new-system`, `rename-to-tianluo`) and run one as a single revertable change. <!--#ea25c3274b0dc8ca-->
    - ``luo worktree` — isolation worktrees` (heading) — Documents `luo worktree gc`, which archives and removes leaked terminal-state `--worktree` runs past an age threshold while deleting branches only when provably merged. <!--#45436b21ae760f77-->
    - ``luo daemon` — resident control plane` (heading) — Documents the `luo daemon` start/stop/status subcommands for running the resident control-plane process and reporting its server registration and tracked flows. <!--#9979cb3c403770d3-->
  - `Directory Layout` (heading) — Annotated tree of a tianluo project showing the config files and the `tianluo/` runtime root, marking which sub-paths are git-tracked (code-index, charter, issues, scripts, prompts, version-intents) versus runtime-only. <!--#1b33e71583219a31-->
  - `Navigating the codebase` (heading) — Shows how to use the code-index itself as the entry point into this repository, drilling from the root map down to a file's symbol tree before opening source. <!--#3e3ae001383cd229-->
  - `Further documentation` (heading) — Points to the configuration reference and the daemon-and-server guide (each with a Chinese translation), and notes `tianluo.example.yaml` is a starter config rather than the reference. <!--#c4486452398836da-->
  - `Version & License` (heading) — States that the version lives only in `pyproject.toml` and is written by the engine, the Apache-2.0 license, and where to find the changelog. <!--#3e197462975cb3d9-->

  - `为什么选 tianluo` (heading) — Pitch section laying out five load-bearing bets behind tianluo — saving human attention rather than tokens, a deterministic Python state machine (not the LLM or a human) driving step routing, code as the single source of truth after the `tianluo/specs/**` mirror was retired, guarantees enforced by code rather than LLM goodwill (invariant_check, critical_tests, net-zero investigate diffs, mandatory fix loops), and agent-agnostic runners — each backed by a one-line evidence claim. <!--#0e47842df297f9d3-->
  - `设计哲学` (heading) — Top-level 'Design Philosophy' heading introducing the rationale subsections that follow. <!--#ce29128b166f3fe9-->

    - `2. 真正的痛点：attention is all you need` (heading) — Argues that human attention, not LLM capacity, is the real bottleneck, and sketches the ideal fire-and-forget session (prompt → discover → optional `confirmation.steps.plan` gate → unattended implement/test/check/commit → collect deliverables) where only the first steps demand a person. <!--#6faccb45d272b1ac-->
    - `3. 撑起这种范式的四件套护城河` (heading) — Describes the four capabilities that make program-as-supervisor viable — a cross-session state machine, the code-first knowledge system, built-in failure recovery (`luo salvage`, test baselines, issue discovery), and a portable `AgentRunner` layer with three shipped adapters. <!--#0b199f560830528c-->
    - `luo vs Claude Code Dynamic Workflows（互补，而非竞争）` (heading) — Positions Dynamic Workflows (in-session parallel orchestration) and tianluo (cross-session project governance) as complementary layers that can compose, deliberately avoiding pinning DW's evolving API names. <!--#6f37b5db1f196b66-->

    - `三件套` (heading) — Introduces the three artifacts at the core of the system — the deterministically extracted, LLM-summarized, version-controlled structure map `tianluo/code-index.md`; the fully injected `tianluo/charter.md` holding only project-wide invariants an altitude gate admits; and colocated why-comments carrying intent that code cannot express. <!--#073c93b6268017a8-->
    - `真正变好了什么（诚实的账）` (heading) — Gives an honest accounting of what replacing the spec mirror actually bought — source of truth back in the code, staleness eliminated by the enumerator, far less governance surface, explicit granularity knobs, charter size decoupled from project size, and a higher failure floor — while conceding it does not improve summary accuracy. <!--#40c16634ebb17ce4-->

### `VERSIONS.md` (markdown) — Chronological changelog of the tianluo (formerly SE3) framework, listing user-facing changes per released version (newest first, e.g. 12.15.0 WebUI history windowing, 12.14.1 history delivery fixes, 12.14.0 lazy detail bundles, 12.13.0 draft caching and message history). <!--#9065a434bf401a4e|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `progress.md` (markdown) — A reverse-chronological session log for the SE 3.0 project, recording per-session Done/Changes/Open Issues/Next Steps entries that track feature work such as loop branch and collab modes, requirement-capture intake, CLI toolization (se3 lint/sync/verify/status), spec cleanup, and versioned protocol updates. <!--#e1332e31ececfbc4|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `pyproject.toml` (text) — Hatchling-based packaging manifest for the `tianluo` package (v12.15.0), declaring its Python >=3.9 floor and core runtime dependencies, the optional `server` / `browser` / `e2e` extras, the `luo` / `tianluo` / `tianluo-server` console scripts plus transitional `se3` aliases, and explicit sdist/wheel include lists that keep runtime directories out of the build. <!--#6b5b76ece7dafb31|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tianluo.example.yaml` (yaml) — Shipped, non-authoritative reference configuration for the tianluo (SE 3.0) framework — copied to `tianluo.yaml`/`tianluo.local.yaml` to configure a project — annotating a getting-started subset of blocks: `human_call`, `session`, the `agents` registry and its `llm_caller`/`confirmation` consumers, `version` bumping, `language`, optional container-based `e2e`, `test` critical tests, `workflow` fix/adjudicate/plan-decomposition tuning, `investigation` bounds, the `tianluo[server]` history cache, and `presets`. <!--#fb605cfdb29d7e72|1d26da507520bbd1-->
- `human_call` (yaml-key) — Configures the human-in-the-loop escalation channel, pointing to the `tianluo/calls` directory where requests for human input are written and setting a 7-day timeout. <!--#588fce804dae8836-->
- `session` (yaml-key) — Controls per-session progress tracking, capping the rolling log at 20 entries in `progress.md`. <!--#c067eb90db8bd1a7-->
- `agents` (yaml-key) — Declares the pool of callable coding agents (`primary`, `backup`, `low`), each with a shell command, `claude-code` type, and dispatch priority. <!--#2f9b309d4148ee7b-->
- `llm_caller` (yaml-key) — Maps workflow steps to which agents handle them, defaulting to `primary` and routing `implement`/`summarize` to `primary`. <!--#5e4a39a06783b3ed-->
- `confirmation` (yaml-key) — Sets per-step human confirmation limits, allowing up to 3 iterations on the `plan` step. <!--#664dfa6489595c1d-->
- `version` (yaml-key) — Enables automatic version bumping and its inclusion in commit messages, with no explicit version file path configured. <!--#8864db448db15952-->
- `language` (yaml-key) — Sets the runtime/output language to `zh-CN` while keeping spec authoring in `en-US`. <!--#fae409e34c1f163b-->
- `e2e` (yaml-key) — Configuration block for the end-to-end (e2e) testing feature — disabled by default (`enabled: false`) — covering container runtime selection (`runtime: "auto"`, `oci_runtime`), build/scenario timeouts, `keep_environment` retention, and lists of `scenarios` and `critical_scenarios` to run. <!--#6a9fd59170c516c0-->
- `test` (yaml-key) — Designates critical tests that must pass, here the headless-browser daemon render e2e test. <!--#95f606ea092ea271-->
- `workflow` (yaml-key) — Tunes the fix/adjudication loop, adjudicating every 10 periods and allowing up to 100 fix iterations. <!--#40aef48cce75ad25-->
- `investigation` (yaml-key) — Configuration block for the bugfix investigation step, exposing `max_iterations` (default 3) to cap how many investigate/verify loops the engine performs. <!--#b5186041df87d1eb-->
- `server` (yaml-key) — Example `server` config block whose sole subsection `history_cache` caps the web server's in-RAM per-flow conversation mirror (`budget_mb`, LRU-by-viewed eviction) and tunes its occupancy diagnostic logging (`report_interval_seconds`, `report_threshold_percent`). <!--#76363ba2b6bfe336-->
- `presets` (yaml-key) — Defines reusable workflow presets, here a `doc-sync` feature preset backed by the `tianluo/prompts/doc-sync.md` prompt file. <!--#f1274982fede24da-->

### `tianluo.yaml` (yaml) — The self-hosting tianluo project config for this repository, carrying only a `documentation:` block (a shields.io dynamic version badge template deliberately written with no placeholder so DocumentationUpdater's README rewrite is a no-op) and a `test:` block (`parallel: auto`, handing pytest to pytest-xdist with one worker per CPU), with extensive comments on the whole-file select-one config precedence and the `--dist loadgroup`/`repo_serial` requirement. <!--#f2324a1ba655d069|7159a59ef087f216-->
- `documentation` (yaml-key) — Documentation settings block whose sole key `readme_badge_template` holds the shields.io dynamic-badge markdown that renders the project version by querying `$.project.version` from `pyproject.toml` on the master branch of the GitHub repo. <!--#7358120b7ef90352-->
- `test` (yaml-key) — Configuration block for the test step, setting `parallel: "auto"` so the test runner auto-selects parallel execution (worker count) instead of running serially. <!--#384d924251b3040f-->

## `.claude/` — The read-only framework-spec directory for the SE3 self-bootstrapping project, holding the published SE3 specs and root CLAUDE.md instructions (project purpose, the `luo run` entry point, the `tianluo/` runtime layout, and optional per-step confirmation/review config) plus a session-state file tracking whether a Claude session is active. <!--#9622d82f73f44a00|ee9fa220890c234d-->

### `.claude/.session.json` (json) — A session-state file recording whether a Claude session is currently active, when it started (ISO 8601 timestamp), and the OS process ID used to detect if the session is still alive. <!--#75a1e2b905ccc3f1|97f010ab8e013eb0-->
- `status` (json-key) — Marks whether the session is currently active. <!--#5768e3a2fd58cd66-->
- `started_at` (json-key) — ISO 8601 timestamp recording when the session began. <!--#6cd43ee6b2d1a12c-->
- `pid` (json-key) — Operating-system process ID of the running session, used to detect whether it is still alive. <!--#6184dd5c70a9c3ce-->

### `.claude/CLAUDE.md` (markdown) — Project-root instructions for the SE3 bootstrapping project, explaining that it generates new SE3 specs while developing against the read-only published specs in `.claude/`, and documenting the `luo run` entry point, the `tianluo/` runtime directory layout, and the optional per-step confirmation/review configuration in `tianluo.yaml`. <!--#6aef8fe0dc5e296b|24c7dda92181f60f-->
- `SE3 自举项目` (heading) — Document title heading naming the SE3 bootstrapping project. <!--#18e5a852b854462e-->
  - `项目性质` (heading) — Explains the project's nature: it produces new SE3 specs while simultaneously being developed using the existing published SE3 specs. <!--#a108c216d1b6d9f7-->
  - `重要约束` (heading) — States the key constraint that generating new specs must not modify the published, read-only spec files under `.claude/`. <!--#4663a50343327fd5-->
  - `SE3 命令入口` (heading) — Lists SE3's command entry points, notably `luo run` to start the flow engine. <!--#479eb24aec6d90d6-->
  - `目录结构` (heading) — Describes the runtime directory layout under `tianluo/` (specs, state, cache, logs, calls, collab) plus `tianluo.yaml` config and the read-only `.claude/` framework specs. <!--#d3e9ce41d48eaa8c-->
  - `确认步骤配置（可选）` (heading) — Documents the optional per-step confirmation/review model in `tianluo.yaml`, covering agent registration, llm_caller defaults, and per-step reviewer/max_iterations fields with fail-fast on unregistered agents. <!--#7721b2cce827a2b8-->

## `.github/` — The GitHub Actions configuration directory, holding a `workflows/publish.yml` pipeline that, on any `v*` tag push, builds the sdist+wheel, verifies the tag matches the `pyproject.toml` version, and publishes to PyPI via OIDC Trusted Publishing (no stored secrets, `skip-existing` to tolerate re-pushed tags). <!--#3bcb68f07afed1a6|e2f7749de44db035-->

## `.github/workflows/` — The GitHub Actions workflows directory, containing a single `publish.yml` workflow that builds and uploads the package to PyPI via OIDC Trusted Publishing whenever a `v*` version tag is pushed. <!--#7876820abbe2b8c0|b6b7c1fe3a352e75-->

### `.github/workflows/publish.yml` (yaml) — A GitHub Actions workflow named "publish" that, on pushes of `v*` version tags, runs a single `publish` job to check out the repo, build the sdist and wheel, verify the pushed tag matches the `pyproject.toml` version, and upload to PyPI via OIDC Trusted Publishing with `skip-existing` to no-op on already-released tags. <!--#46c055019d101f8f|4f45287e504ec09f-->
- `name` (yaml-key) — Names the GitHub Actions workflow "publish", the PyPI release pipeline. <!--#7243aff4233df20d-->
- `True` (yaml-key) — The `on` trigger (parsed as the YAML key `True`) firing the workflow on pushes of `v*` version tags. <!--#b46ab94325f860c4-->
- `jobs` (yaml-key) — Defines the single `publish` job that checks out the repo, builds the sdist and wheel, sanity-checks the pushed tag against the `pyproject.toml` version, and publishes to PyPI via OIDC Trusted Publishing with `skip-existing` to no-op on already-uploaded tags. <!--#4bf36f7d07c7a97c-->

## `docs/` — The project's end-user documentation set for tianluo, holding the bilingual (en/zh) authoritative configuration reference and the bilingual daemon/server control-plane guide, plus a `docs/assets/` folder of icon and WebUI screenshot images referenced by those pages. <!--#214d111dee91cfd5|400d673aafd912f1-->

### `docs/configuration.md` (markdown) — The authoritative configuration reference for tianluo, documenting the four-tier config-file lookup and global-layer merge rules, then giving a per-key breakdown of every block the engine reads (`agents`, `llm_caller`, `confirmation`, `language`, `workflow`, `test`, `e2e`, `merge`, `server`, `presets`, …) together with PLAN decomposition/granularity doctrine, self-check review scoping, legacy `se3.*` and retired-key compatibility notes, and troubleshooting guidance. <!--#85e6d54aa2c36248|be0aca094bd6c1cf-->
- `tianluo Configuration Reference` (heading) — Document preamble declaring this file the authoritative, code-mirroring reference for every configuration block tianluo reads, and noting it outranks the getting-started `tianluo.example.yaml` sample when the two disagree. <!--#9ec82638951fff7f-->
  - `Table of Contents` (heading) — A linked table of contents laying out the document's structure: configuration file resolution rules and pitfalls, a per-block reference for every `tianluo.yaml` section (`agents`, `llm_caller`, `workflow`, `test`, `e2e`, `merge`, `server`, `presets`, …), legacy blocks, and a troubleshooting section. <!--#98b6e2518122970e-->
  - `Configuration files and resolution rules` (heading) — Section header introducing which config file is selected, how the global layer merges into it, and how to read the per-key tables that follow. <!--#deaabbc77cbc343c-->
    - `Which file is read: the four-tier lookup` (heading) — Explains that `get_project_config_path()` selects exactly one project config from a four-candidate probe (worktree/main × `tianluo.local.yaml`/`tianluo.yaml`), and that symlinks are followed while relative paths resolve against the running process's project root. <!--#731ef1b4f866411b-->
    - `Pitfall 1 — `tianluo.local.yaml` replaces the whole file` (heading) — Warns that `tianluo.local.yaml` is a whole-file replacement rather than a per-key patch, so keys defined only in `tianluo.yaml` silently fall back to defaults or to the global layer's agent chain. <!--#fbe1e0f16f959866-->
    - `The global layer (`~/.se3/config.yaml`)` (heading) — Documents the per-user global config at `~/.se3/config.yaml` (path unchanged by the se3 → tianluo rename) and tabulates which blocks merge with the project file and at what granularity — entry-level for `agents`/`confirmation.steps`, whole-list for `llm_caller.defaults`, per-step for `llm_caller.steps`, field-level for `language`, whole-block for `server`, and project-only for everything else. <!--#481a78da6294e960-->
    - `Legacy `se3.yaml` / `se3.local.yaml`` (heading) — States that pre-rename `se3.*` filenames remain honoured at every lookup tier (always losing to the `tianluo.*` name at the same tier) through 12.x and are removed in 13.0.0. <!--#0fb03dcddd44ade5-->
    - `How to read this document` (heading) — Reading conventions for the per-key tables: defaults quote real code constants, types are YAML types, loading is clamp-and-warn unless a fail-fast exception is flagged, and *inert* marks parsed-but-unconsumed keys. <!--#bcc449bc39113941-->
  - `Blocks` (heading) — Section header opening the per-block reference for every configuration block the engine actively reads. <!--#954c09420da81b31-->
    - ``agents`` (heading) — Reference for the top-level agent identity registry that every `llm_caller` and reviewer name resolves against — `AgentDef` keys (`type`, `cmd`, `provider`, `model`, deprecated `priority`), the three valid runner types, shorthand form, fail-fast on unknown names, entry-level global merge, PATH auto-probe when omitted, and handling of the removed list form and legacy `claude_commands`. <!--#52498f506fe4bf24-->
    - ``llm_caller`` (heading) — Documents `defaults` and per-step `steps` agent chains, where written order is rotation order and rotation happens only on infrastructure errors strictly within the selected list. <!--#197e3011942db5f7-->
      - `Pitfall 2 — `llm_caller.steps.<step>` is a hard override with no fallback` (heading) — Warns that a per-step chain wholly replaces `defaults` (and the global declaration for that step) with no implicit append, and lists the degenerate forms that warn and revert to `defaults`. <!--#e228fdab53148280-->
      - ``self_check`: nested per-pass chains` (heading) — Describes the list-of-lists form of `llm_caller.steps.self_check` that assigns a distinct agent chain per pass, its flat/nested/mixed semantics, and how it implies the pass count when `workflow.self_check_passes_required` is unset. <!--#479f373f5678cff5-->
    - ``confirmation`` (heading) — Documents the `confirmation` config block, where a step is gated only if listed under `confirmation.steps` (with `reviewer` and `max_iterations`), noting that plan-confirm is now opt-in, how the review differs under the `capability` vs `granular` doctrines, that `adjudicate` is ungated by default, and which legacy keys are deprecated. <!--#54640885a6578e17-->
    - ``language`` (heading) — Documents the field-level-merged `language` (human/UI language) and `spec_language` (knowledge-asset language) settings, the CLI UI-text resolution chain, and their non-retroactive scope. <!--#46270cd164321294-->
    - ``workflow`` (heading) — Reference table for the `workflow` config block backing `WorkflowConfig` — fix-loop and self_check knobs (`max_fix_iterations`, `self_check_passes_required`, `baseline_fix_max_attempts`, `self_check_defer_fix_threshold`, `adjudicate_period`) plus the PLAN keys `plan_decomposition` / `plan_granularity` — with each key's type, default, validation behaviour, and the retired `self_check_convergence_enabled` compatibility note. <!--#e82f7aa125547abc-->
      - `PLAN decomposition doctrine and granularity` (heading) — Explains the single ANALYZE → PLAN → IMPLEMENT path and how `plan_decomposition` (`capability` default vs legacy `granular`) and `plan_granularity` (`auto` / `single` / `conservative`) shape only what PLAN emits — task-sized groups split solely at the capability edge, with the group count driving single-call vs parallel-worktree DAG execution, decided once at flow creation and persisted. <!--#f752bdde8e586920-->
      - `Retired: `workflow.implementation_strategy`` (heading) — Notes that the `implementation_strategy` routing axis is retired but accepted for one more version, and gives the mapping table from `direct`/`planned`/`auto` onto the new `plan_granularity`/`plan_decomposition` keys, with new keys always winning over the legacy fallback. <!--#58fb7903984c5706-->
      - `Self-check review scope (full-incremental-closure)` (heading) — Documents how SELF_CHECK rounds are scoped: judged against the effective task description plus charter/`WHY:`/`INVARIANT:` constraints, with `full` and `incremental` naming which persisted baseline (implementation vs. earliest unreviewed fix) the round's diff is taken from, the full → incremental → closure round cycle, the forced-full fallback on description changes or an undecidable baseline, the rule that TEST always runs the full configured test commands, the persisted scope audit fields, the derived non-config `self_check_passes_required_explicit` field, and the project-wide `0`/`null` = unlimited iteration-cap sentinel convention. <!--#97e5ccec83d0e183-->
    - ``pricing`` (heading) — Reference for the `PricingConfig` block that overrides per-million-token model prices on top of the built-in versioned catalog, covering the supported price categories, model-alias normalization, per-entry drop-on-invalid-value behaviour, and the rule that provider-reported cost wins while unknown prices render as "unknown cost" rather than `$0`. <!--#920b192747e42fdb-->
      - `Usage and cost visibility in history and the web console` (heading) — Describes the unified per-call usage record as the single accounting unit rendered identically by session summaries, `luo history show` and the web console, with de-duplicated provider actual cost kept separate from estimated cost and missing data shown as unknown/partial rather than `$0`. <!--#4fb745306a591afe-->
    - ``investigation`` (heading) — Documents the `investigate` step's own `max_iterations` exploration budget, deliberately separate from the fix loop, whose exhaustion degrades to a low-confidence hypothesis rather than failing the flow. <!--#8591395a0e33883f-->
    - ``test`` (heading) — Reference section for the `test` config block loaded into `TestConfig` — documenting all eight keys (`command`, `timeout`, `phases`, `timeout_multiplier`, `min_dynamic_timeout`, `max_dynamic_timeout`, `critical_tests`, `parallel`), the `phases[]` entry schema, the all-defaults fallback gotcha when `timeout` fails to parse, the `critical_tests` skip-is-not-a-pass gate, and the opt-in pytest-xdist `parallel` switch with its `--dist loadgroup` behaviour. <!--#feabbf3f477ada03-->
    - ``e2e`` (heading) — Reference for the `e2e` runtime block (`enabled`, `runtime`, `oci_runtime`, build/scenario timeouts, scenario selection and `critical_scenarios`, `keep_environment`), explaining that e2e is off by default, follows the clamp-and-warn policy, and deliberately keeps runtime knobs separate from the flow-authored `tianluo/e2e/` content. <!--#396a06ec41232340-->
      - `Prerequisite: a container runtime you can run without sudo` (heading) — States the host prerequisite for e2e — a Docker or Podman the current user can run without sudo (docker group, rootless Docker, or Podman) — plus the `luo e2e doctor` check and the optional `pip install 'tianluo[e2e]'` extra needed only for tier-2 screenshot diffs. <!--#14c748affae56f08-->
      - `Runtime selection` (heading) — Explains how `runtime: auto` picks a container runtime by actually executing `docker info` then `podman info` (not a `PATH` lookup), why Docker wins ties, why naming a runtime explicitly disables silent fallback, and that the probe result is fixed for the session with failures reported as environment problems. <!--#801fd649bb648f14-->
      - `The other half: `tianluo/e2e/` content configuration` (heading) — Describes the git-tracked `tianluo/e2e/` directory (`environment.yaml`, `scenarios/`, `baselines/`) that the flow generates and incrementally evolves, with worked examples of service topology, readiness-probe placement (in-container vs host-dialled), action ordering and the `browser` batching rule, `base_kind` templates, driver/capability validation, and the schema-enforced assertion ladder. <!--#6fd0ce8d3a3fd72b-->
      - `Where the E2E step sits, and how failures route` (heading) — Explains that the `E2E` step is inserted immediately after `test` (and never into `review`/`survey` sequences), and that a failing scenario is treated as a code defect entering the normal fix loop while an environment problem fails the step with remediation without consuming a fix iteration. <!--#c1e50140a8bc93da-->
    - ``implement`` (heading) — Documents the `implement` config block's `group_loc_threshold` (a `granular`-only LOC threshold for merging groups and the sequential-vs-DAG decision, fail-fast on unparseable values) and `use_worktree` (with its `SE3_IMPLEMENT_USE_WORKTREE` env override), explaining why capability plans dispatch on group count and topology instead of LOC. <!--#b82f8ddb47c71317-->
    - ``steps`` (heading) — Documents the append-only `steps.append` sequence extension, its YAML-key/dataclass-field name mismatch with `append_steps`, and the silent ignoring of unknown or duplicate step names. <!--#c7f969e47cc97cd3-->
    - ``version`` (heading) — Documents the commit step's version-bump settings, flagging the `version_file`-not-`file_path` naming trap, the many inert legacy fields, deprecated `bump_rules`/`smart_version_analysis`, and the worktree/merge split of the release point. <!--#ce1194085b462975-->
    - ``documentation`` (heading) — Documents the templates `DocumentationUpdater` uses for README badge and VERSIONS.md entries, the `{{double-brace}}` placeholder context, the badge match-or-insert order, and the placeholder-free idempotent-no-op dynamic badge this repo relies on. <!--#37ed6fc7f9ab621b-->
    - ``code_index`` (heading) — Documents all eight knobs for building and rendering `tianluo/code-index.md` — degrade triggers, chunk sizes, exclusions, root-view byte budget, `primary_roots`, and summarisation concurrency — all clamp-and-warn. <!--#460a8490d84ba18c-->
    - ``merge`` (heading) — Documents the `luo merge` orchestrator's `fast`/`safe`/`strict` conflict tiers, branch-deletion default, runtime-sync strictness, resolution-round cap, and the fail-fast rejection of the removed `default`/`robust` names. <!--#0c7eee9cf87bba9d-->
    - ``conflict_resolver`` (heading) — Documents the single `strategy` key (`human` or `llm`, fail-safe coerced to `human`) governing loop-branch merge conflicts, distinct from the `merge` block's orchestrator strategy. <!--#25533042f9224150-->
    - ``claude_subprocess`` (heading) — Documents the `claude_subprocess.setting_sources` key (default `["user"]`, passed as `--setting-sources`) that isolates spawned Claude CLI workers from the target project's `.claude/settings.json`, notes its fail-fast validation, and warns that duplicate `--settings` flags are last-wins. <!--#91d971596d09505d-->
    - ``server`` (heading) — Documents the optional `server:` top-level config block for the central control plane (`tianluo-server`), noting that a project-level block wholly replaces the global one and tabulating `db_path`, `auth`, and `history_cache` with their defaults. <!--#02baebb445efeec9-->
      - ``server.history_cache`` (heading) — Documents the memory ceiling for the server's in-RAM per-flow history mirror — explaining LRU-by-view eviction and its one-round-trip rebuild cost — and tabulates `budget_mb`, `report_interval_seconds`, and `report_threshold_percent`. <!--#26ca1ff001520004-->
      - ``server.auth`` (heading) — Documents the ordered `providers` chain (`local`/`oidc`/`proxy_header`) with dedup, dropping of invalid entries, and a `["local"]` fallback so the chain is never empty. <!--#e44b5d6016db0c6a-->
      - ``server.auth.session`` (heading) — Documents the UI session cookie attributes (name, `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite`, lifetime) whose defaults are fail-safe for public deployment behind a TLS-terminating proxy. <!--#c67e04a866a123cc-->
      - ``server.auth.local`` (heading) — Documents the built-in password provider's two independent brute-force guards — consecutive-failure lockout and a sliding rate limit — each clamp-and-warn so a typo cannot disable them. <!--#752955b2484eb99f-->
      - ``server.auth.oidc`` (heading) — Documents the disabled-by-default OIDC config seam (issuer, client credentials, redirect, scopes) reserved for a future social-login provider not implemented in v1. <!--#148dfd8954fe737e-->
      - ``server.auth.proxy_header`` (heading) — Documents the disabled-by-default seam for trusting a reverse-proxy-injected identity header, with the security precondition that the proxy must strip client-supplied copies or the identity is forgeable. <!--#76e2fe545bf8c687-->
    - ``presets`` (heading) — Documents named prompt templates for `luo run --preset`, read by `preset_loader`, and the two-layer resolution where project `tianluo/prompts/*.md` scans plus this block override the package's built-in presets. <!--#a4a3e42ce2d601dc-->
  - `Legacy / historical configuration` (heading) — Notes that the retired spec-mirror era blocks (`spec_governance`, `spec_loading`, `spec_write_protection`, `merge.guardrail_repair`) have no loader at all and are silently ignored, the code itself now being the single source of truth. <!--#3fb5814ae35c0f33-->
    - `Blocks the engine no longer reads` (heading) — Documents the vestigial `human_call` and `session` blocks that still ship in `tianluo.example.yaml` but have no reader in `src/`, plus a note that the old no-op `e2e` block's name has been reclaimed by the real e2e subsystem and its four legacy keys are ignored. <!--#502c46c361631578-->
  - `Troubleshooting: "I changed the config and nothing happened"` (heading) — A debugging playbook for config edits that appear to have no effect — check the active file via `get_project_config_path`, print resolved values with the plain loader functions, then work a checklist of causes (local-file shadowing, YAML syntax errors, non-falling-back per-step chains, wrong key names, inert/legacy blocks, clamped values, env-var overrides, editing the example file). <!--#cf3ae93a8a85246a-->

### `docs/configuration.zh.md` (markdown) — Chinese-language authoritative configuration reference for tianluo, written against `src/tianluo/config.py`: it documents the four-level config file lookup and project/global (`~/.se3/config.yaml`) merge semantics plus legacy `se3.*` filenames, then gives per-block reference tables for `agents`, `llm_caller` (including per-pass `self_check` chains), `confirmation`, `language`, `workflow` (fix loop, PLAN decomposition/granularity, self-check full-incremental-closure scoping, retired `implementation_strategy`), `pricing` and the remaining blocks, calling out pitfalls such as whole-file `tianluo.local.yaml` replacement and no-fallback per-step agent chains. <!--#8b61813af4471051|7ad713c790c65ccb-->
- `tianluo 配置参考` (heading) — Chinese-language authoritative reference for every configuration block tianluo reads, written against `src/tianluo/config.py` and taking precedence over the illustrative `tianluo.example.yaml`. <!--#253a50e63d21914c-->
  - `目录` (heading) — Table of contents for the Chinese configuration reference, linking every config block section (`agents`, `llm_caller`, `workflow`, `test`, `e2e`, `merge`, `server`, `presets`, …) plus the file-resolution rules, legacy blocks, and the troubleshooting chapter. <!--#27d9ba76c0db3d1a-->
  - `配置文件与解析规则` (heading) — Section covering how tianluo locates and merges its configuration files before any block is interpreted. <!--#e5116835a13d9d7a-->
    - `读取哪个文件:四级查找` (heading) — Explains the four-candidate probe order `get_project_config_path()` uses (worktree/main × `tianluo.local.yaml`/`tianluo.yaml`), why levels 2 and 4 exist for git worktrees, symlink-following via `is_file()`, and that relative paths resolve against the running project root. <!--#60fe4f7bfbdf7734-->
    - `坑 1 —— `tianluo.local.yaml` 替换整个文件` (heading) — Pitfall 1: `tianluo.local.yaml` is a whole-file replacement rather than a per-key merge, so anything only in `tianluo.yaml` silently falls back to defaults (or to the global layer), and an unparsable local file shadows just the same. <!--#3e023d076189f908-->
    - `全局层(`~/.se3/config.yaml`)` (heading) — Documents the per-user global config layer at `~/.se3/config.yaml` (path unchanged by the se3 → tianluo rename) and tabulates which blocks merge with the project file and at what granularity — `agents` and `confirmation.steps` per-entry, `llm_caller.defaults`/`steps.<step>` by whole-value replacement, `language` per-field, `server` whole-block, everything else project-only. <!--#5414101e5971b128-->
    - `遗留的 `se3.yaml` / `se3.local.yaml`` (heading) — States that legacy `se3.*` filenames are still honored at every lookup level (always losing to the canonical `tianluo.*` name at the same level) through 12.x and removed in 13.0.0. <!--#b24068acd950893b-->
    - `如何阅读本文档` (heading) — Reading conventions for the tables: defaults are literal code values, types are YAML types, loading is clamp-and-warn unless a fail-fast exception is marked, and *inert* keys are parsed but consumed by nothing. <!--#edc4718a55b01fc8-->
  - `配置块` (heading) — Section heading introducing the reference tables for all actively-read configuration blocks. <!--#4009d6705fa9170e-->
    - ``agents`` (heading) — Documents the top-level `agents` registry that every `llm_caller` entry and reviewer resolves by name — per-entry keys (`type`, `cmd`, `provider`, `model`, deprecated `priority`), the shorthand form, the valid runner types (`claude-code`, `codex`, opt-in `claude-interactive`), fail-fast on unknown agent names, project/global per-entry merging, PATH auto-detection when omitted, and handling of the removed list form and legacy `claude_commands`. <!--#74f6cc2984e0a3ef-->
    - ``llm_caller`` (heading) — Documents `defaults` and per-step `steps` agent chains, where written order is rotation order and rotation on infrastructure errors stays strictly within the selected list. <!--#e4ad29c019c4d167-->
      - `坑 2 —— `llm_caller.steps.<step>` 是无 fallback 的硬覆盖` (heading) — Pitfall 2: a per-step chain fully replaces `defaults` with no implicit append or fallback (including across config sources), and degenerate values warn back to `defaults` while unknown agent names stay fatal. <!--#64fba24c1541b3bb-->
      - ``self_check`:按 pass 的嵌套链路` (heading) — Explains that `llm_caller.steps.self_check` also accepts a list-of-lists giving one chain per pass, reusing the last chain beyond the declared count, rejecting mixed forms, and implying the pass count when `workflow.self_check_passes_required` is unset. <!--#fcedb88a37592576-->
    - ``confirmation`` (heading) — Documents the `confirmation` config block, whose `steps` mapping is the sole opt-in for review gates (with per-step `reviewer` and `max_iterations`), explains that plan-confirm and `adjudicate` are now off by default and what each doctrine reviews, and lists the deprecated keys that warn and are ignored. <!--#8ddc3735661cd6b9-->
    - ``language`` (heading) — Documents the two independent, field-wise-merged settings — `language` for human/UI text and `spec_language` for knowledge assets — plus the CLI text resolution chain (`SE3_LANG` > config > locale > `en-US`) and that changes are not retroactive. <!--#05c8486bf23b79c9-->
    - ``workflow`` (heading) — Reference table for the `WorkflowConfig` keys governing the fix loop and self_check — `max_fix_iterations`, `self_check_passes_required`, `baseline_fix_max_attempts`, `self_check_defer_fix_threshold`, `adjudicate_period`, `plan_decomposition`, `plan_granularity` — spelling out defaults, sentinel values, and which keys fail fast versus warn-and-fall-back. <!--#ebc73259dbffa3b1-->
      - `PLAN 的分解学说与粒度` (heading) — Explains the single ANALYZE → PLAN → IMPLEMENT path and the two keys that shape it — `plan_decomposition` (`capability` default, task-based coarse grouping with a hard ban on artifact/layer-typed groups, vs. legacy `granular` per-task lists) and `plan_granularity` (`auto` / `single` / `conservative`) — plus the precedence order and the fact that the decision is made once at flow creation and persisted. <!--#fb465200c00441dc-->
      - `已退役:`workflow.implementation_strategy`` (heading) — Records the retirement of the `implementation_strategy` routing axis, giving the one-version compatibility mapping of `direct`/`planned`/`auto` onto the new `plan_granularity`/`plan_decomposition` keys, where that mapping happens, and that explicit new keys always win. <!--#b42a0d0a6c1faec9-->
      - `Self-check 审查范围(full-incremental-closure)` (heading) — Documents how SELF_CHECK scopes each review round as a diff against a recoverable baseline — `full` from the implementation baseline, `incremental` from the earliest unreviewed fix baseline, followed by a mandatory full closure round before INVARIANT_CHECK — plus the forced-full triggers, the always-full TEST rule, persisted `scope_mode` audit fields, the derived `self_check_passes_required_explicit` non-config field, and the `0`/`null` = unlimited sentinel convention for iteration caps. <!--#60341ef5a1a480a2-->
    - ``pricing`` (heading) — Documents the `pricing` block that overrides per-model, per-category prices (USD per million tokens) on top of the built-in versioned price table, covering model-alias normalization, per-entry discard of invalid values, precedence of provider-reported actual cost, and the rule that unknown model/price always renders as unknown cost rather than `$0`. <!--#bd964d6850c545ad-->
      - `history 与 Web 控制台的用量与成本可见性` (heading) — Describes the unified per-call usage record as the accounting unit and the single backend aggregation shared by flow summaries, `luo history show`, the daemon payload and the Web console — keeping provider actual cost and estimated cost in separate columns, showing unknown/partial instead of misleading `$0`, and never rewriting pre-unified-record flows. <!--#49289ab758aba905-->
    - ``investigation`` (heading) — Documents the `investigate` step's own bounded loop via `max_iterations`, why exhausting the budget proceeds to `plan` with a low-confidence hypothesis, and why this budget is kept separate from the fix loop. <!--#413f7fa8ffa2abc8-->
    - ``test`` (heading) — Reference section for the `test` config block loaded into `TestConfig`, documenting all eight keys (`command`, `timeout`, `phases`, `timeout_multiplier`, `min_dynamic_timeout`, `max_dynamic_timeout`, `critical_tests`, `parallel`), the `phases[]` entry schema, the pitfall that a malformed `timeout` silently drops the whole block to defaults, the `critical_tests` guard against skipped/missing tests counting as verified, and the opt-in pytest-xdist `parallel` switch with its `--dist loadgroup` and plugin-missing behavior. <!--#65a16296a61a60dd-->
    - ``e2e`` (heading) — Documents the `e2e` runtime config block (`enabled`, `runtime`, `oci_runtime`, `build_timeout`, `scenario_timeout`, `estimated_e2e_duration`, `scenarios`, `critical_scenarios`, `keep_environment`) loaded into `E2EConfig`, explaining that it is off by default, follows clamp-and-warn validation, and deliberately holds only runtime knobs while e2e content lives in `tianluo/e2e/`. <!--#6e83a2f9ec2993f6-->
      - `前置条件:一个你无需 sudo 就能跑的容器 runtime` (heading) — States the e2e prerequisite that the current user can run `docker` or `podman` without sudo (docker group, rootless Docker, or Podman), points at `luo e2e doctor` for host checks, and explains the `tianluo[e2e]` optional extra needed for tier-2 image diffing. <!--#d0a38e7212d2186f-->
      - `Runtime 选择` (heading) — Explains how `auto` picks a container runtime by actually running `docker info` then `podman info` (rather than probing PATH), why Docker wins ties, why an explicit `runtime` disables fallback, and that the choice is fixed for a session with probe failures reported as environment problems. <!--#24f38f94f507c840-->
      - `另一半:`tianluo/e2e/` 内容配置` (heading) — Describes the git-tracked `tianluo/e2e/` content directory (`environment.yaml`, `scenarios/`, `baselines/`), the `luo e2e bootstrap|list|run` commands and exit codes, and the schema rules for services, readiness probes, action ordering, `base_kind`/driver capability matching, and the enforced three-tier assertion escalation ladder including baseline generation via `--write-baselines`. <!--#33ccc105da5f4b6e-->
      - `E2E step 在流程中的位置,以及失败如何路由` (heading) — Explains that the `E2E` step is inserted immediately after `test` (before `self_check`) when enabled, and that scenario failures route to the normal fix loop as code defects while environment problems fail the step with remediation guidance without consuming fix iterations. <!--#7ba9910e245d684a-->
    - ``implement`` (heading) — Documents the `implement` block's two keys — `group_loc_threshold` (granular-only, fail-fast on unparseable values, bypassed under `capability` where dispatch goes by group count and topology) and `use_worktree` (overridable by `SE3_IMPLEMENT_USE_WORKTREE`). <!--#f413473b5436a046-->
    - ``steps`` (heading) — Documents the append-only `steps.append` list (note the YAML key/dataclass `append_steps` name mismatch), validated against `StepType` with unknown names silently ignored and no remove/replace support. <!--#24c3f5358a742b8a-->
    - ``version`` (heading) — Documents the commit step's version-bump config, warns that the real key is `version_file` (not the alias `file_path`), marks the many inert/legacy fields, and notes deprecated keys plus the worktree/merge split where `version_reconcile` writes the version file. <!--#dd93a0865d8406dd-->
    - ``documentation`` (heading) — Documents the templates `DocumentationUpdater` actually uses for README badge / VERSIONS entry / README header, the `{{...}}` placeholder set, badge match-or-insert ordering, and the idempotent no-op badge trick this repo relies on. <!--#6fe2991dd47d471c-->
    - ``code_index`` (heading) — Documents all eight knobs for building and rendering `tianluo/code-index.md` — degrade triggers, chunk sizes, `exclude`, root-view byte budget, `primary_roots`, `max_concurrency` — all clamp-and-warn so a bad block never fails a rebuild. <!--#2776147291b4d0a3-->
    - ``merge`` (heading) — Documents the `luo merge` orchestrator's `strategy` tiers (`fast`/`safe`/`strict`), branch deletion default, strict runtime sync, and iteration cap, plus the `ConfigError` raised for the removed `default`/`robust` strategy names. <!--#8653505886efe2c9-->
    - ``conflict_resolver`` (heading) — Documents the single `strategy` key (`human`/`llm`, unknown values silently coerced to `human`) governing loop-branch merges, as distinct from the `merge` block that governs `luo merge`. <!--#b9b07db2a73bc9ed-->
    - ``claude_subprocess`` (heading) — Documents the `claude_subprocess.setting_sources` key that controls which Claude settings files the spawned worker CLI loads (default `["user"]`, to isolate tianluo workers from the target project's `permissions.deny`), noting it fails fast on invalid values and warning that duplicate `--settings` args are last-wins so the engine never appends its own. <!--#08d8dba01f149f9c-->
    - ``server`` (heading) — Documents the optional `server:` top-level config section (server-only extra, whole-section replacement rather than deep merge) and its `db_path`, `auth`, and `history_cache` keys. <!--#1804eed673f9a698-->
      - ``server.history_cache`` (heading) — Documents the `budget_mb`, `report_interval_seconds`, and `report_threshold_percent` keys that cap and report on the server's in-memory history bundle mirror so long-running memory-constrained deployments aren't oom-killed. <!--#97cb87796027b654-->
      - ``server.auth`` (heading) — Documents `providers`, the ordered auth provider chain (`local`/`oidc`/`proxy_header`) that drops invalid entries, dedupes, and falls back to `["local"]` so the chain is never empty. <!--#d9eb1868a9dd03db-->
      - ``server.auth.session`` (heading) — Documents the UI session cookie attributes (name, `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite`, max age) whose defaults are fail-safe for a public server behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy. <!--#fbbbef11cb7b5fb6-->
      - ``server.auth.local`` (heading) — Documents the built-in username/password provider's two independent brute-force defenses — consecutive-failure lockout and sliding-window rate limiting — all clamp-and-warn. <!--#4200af814f039e1b-->
      - ``server.auth.oidc`` (heading) — Documents the disabled-by-default OIDC seam (issuer, client credentials, redirect URL, scopes), unimplemented in v1 and inert while `enabled` is false. <!--#9b629e68a9b4d568-->
      - ``server.auth.proxy_header`` (heading) — Documents the disabled-by-default reverse-proxy identity-header seam and the security preconditions (proxy must strip the client header, server must not be reachable directly) required before enabling it. <!--#182fd8bb8d076426-->
    - ``presets`` (heading) — Documents named prompt templates run via `luo run --preset <name>`, read by `preset_loader` rather than `config.py`, and the two-layer resolution where packaged built-ins are overridden by a `tianluo/prompts/*.md` scan plus this block's metadata overlay. <!--#68eca1849e02513f-->
  - `Legacy / 历史遗留配置` (heading) — Notes that blocks from the retired spec-mirror era (`spec_governance`, `spec_loading`, `spec_write_protection`, `merge.guardrail_repair`) no longer have loaders and are silently ignored — harmless to leave in the file, but meaningless. <!--#4d0d3f69033620b7-->
    - `引擎已不再读取的配置块` (heading) — Lists the `human_call` and `session` blocks still present in `tianluo.example.yaml` that the engine verifiably never reads, and notes that the old dead `e2e` block's name has been reclaimed by the real e2e subsystem with an entirely different schema. <!--#35033bed759fc4f8-->
  - `排错:改了配置却没有任何变化` (heading) — Troubleshooting guide for config edits that appear to have no effect, starting with a `tianluo.local.yaml` shadowing check via `get_project_config_path`, then showing how to print each loader's resolved value, and listing further suspects (YAML syntax errors, no-fallback `llm_caller.steps.<step>`, misspelled keys such as `steps.append`/`version.version_file`, dead legacy blocks, clamped values, `SE3_*` env overrides, and editing `tianluo.example.yaml`). <!--#b3eade43c5dd7924-->

### `docs/daemon-and-server.md` (markdown) — The complete user and architecture guide to tianluo's optional always-on control plane, covering the per-machine `luo daemon` and the standalone `tianluo-server` across five parts: quick start (installation, command reference, a worked session), deployment and operations (outbound connection model, foreground vs. detached mode, runtime files under `~/.se3/`, flow discovery/supervision, systemd memory guardrails), internal architecture (daemon task structure, FastAPI server structure, the end-to-end task-publish and file-upload/read-back paths), the mandatory multi-tenant authentication and sqlite identity store, and the bundled web frontend. <!--#4bca3a638eb7c7b2|de3097fa4d9c1dca-->
- `tianluo Daemon & Central Server` (heading) — Top-level overview of the doc, introducing the optional always-on control plane — the per-machine `luo daemon` and the standalone `tianluo-server` — layered on top of tianluo's one-shot CLI core. <!--#9303dc8216796c10-->
  - `Table of Contents` (heading) — A five-part navigation index for the document, linking to Quick Start, Deployment & Operations, Architecture & How It Works, Authentication & Multi-Tenant Access, and The Web Frontend along with their subsections. <!--#618e9a50ebb1ef2f-->
  - `Quick Start` (heading) — Section heading grouping installation and the basic commands to get the daemon and server running. <!--#629a4900e292c455-->
    - `Installation` (heading) — Explains that `luo daemon` ships with the core `tianluo` package while the central server's heavier web deps live in the optional `tianluo[server]` extra, which the daemon's outbound client also requires. <!--#8ba81d6bd59e78c6-->
    - `The `luo daemon` command` (heading) — Reference for the `luo daemon` subcommand group (start/stop/status), documenting its options like `--server-url`, `--daemon-key`, and `--foreground` and their behaviors. <!--#2fa1071b80aa48ea-->
    - `The `tianluo-server` command` (heading) — Reference for the standalone `tianluo-server` entry point and its options (`--host`, `--port`, `--db-path`, `--log-level`, `bootstrap-token`), noting it blocks in the foreground and mandates authentication. <!--#abbe4c732366d961-->
    - `A typical session` (heading) — A worked end-to-end example: install and start the server, mint a bootstrap token, start a daemon with a daemon key on a worker, and monitor/publish from the browser. <!--#74a721a0d6287d21-->
  - `Deployment & Operations` (heading) — Section heading grouping the operational topics: connection model, run modes, runtime files, and flow supervision. <!--#7a1eddb2450f7c7a-->
    - `The outbound connection model` (heading) — Describes the single-direction daemon→server WebSocket dial, its NAT-friendliness and exponential-backoff resilience, and the scheme-aware default-port handling for `--server-url`. <!--#b925cd6111f91281-->
    - `Foreground vs. background (detached) mode` (heading) — Contrasts the default detached double-fork background daemon with `--foreground` mode, and notes only one daemon may run per pid directory. <!--#cbc8ceb66211213f-->
    - `Runtime files: pidfile and status file` (heading) — Documents the daemon's `~/.se3/` runtime files (`daemon.pid`, `daemon_status.json`, `daemon.log`), their purposes, the `SE3_DAEMON_DIR` override, and their atomic writes. <!--#079f28712c78c0d3-->
      - `Connection state in `status`` (heading) — Explains how `daemon_status.json` records the daemon's real outbound-connection result and how `luo daemon status` surfaces it on a `Connection:` line (local-only / connected / not connected with a verbatim reason). <!--#0a7f089dd2698d67-->
    - `Flow discovery and supervision` (heading) — Describes how the daemon tracks spawned vs. discovered `luo run` flows, resolves each `flow_id` from `engine.json`, polls liveness, and gracefully terminates only flows it spawned. <!--#45543e810da4387c-->
    - `systemd memory guardrails` (heading) — Explains that `server.history_cache.budget_mb` is the real bound on server memory growth while a sample systemd unit (`Restart=on-failure`, `MemoryHigh`/`MemoryMax`, `[Unit]` crash-loop rate limits) acts as a backstop, and points to the `history-cache` journal lines for post-incident attribution. <!--#4c9191eb571125d5-->
  - `Architecture & How It Works` (heading) — Section heading grouping the internal-design subsections for the daemon, the server, and the end-to-end task-publish path. <!--#37fc459f8df19bd0-->
    - `Inside the daemon` (heading) — Architecture of the daemon as a single asyncio process of four pieces — Supervisor, Spawner, Aggregator, and the optional outbound WebSocket Client — running as concurrent tasks sharing one graceful-stop signal. <!--#dad409d41e4f9969-->
    - `Inside the central server` (heading) — Architecture of `tianluo-server` as a FastAPI app: `/ws` daemon connections, an in-memory `ServerState` aggregate, a sqlite identity store, the `/api/*` owner-filtered REST routes, and the bundled frontend on `/ws/ui`. <!--#8cc1366a41f8e732-->
    - `End-to-end: publishing a task from a remote machine` (heading) — Traces the full round trip of publishing a task from the web UI or `POST /api/flows` — server sends `SPAWN_FLOW` down the daemon's existing outbound WebSocket, the daemon spawns a real `luo run` child, and aggregated `MachineStatus` snapshots flow back to all frontends — plus the mirror-image `RESPOND_CALL` path for answering a flow's pending interjection. <!--#5630aa2e3479380b-->
    - `The file-upload channel` (heading) — Explains how web-UI file attachments are relayed via `POST /api/uploads` and an `UPLOAD_COMMAND` frame down the daemon's outbound socket to land on disk under `<project_root>/tianluo/uploads/`, with the prompt carrying only the project-relative path, plus the operational properties that govern it (20 MiB limit enforced at all three layers, sha256-prefixed dedup naming, registered-project requirement, protocol revision gating, gitignoring, and the absence of any automatic cleanup). <!--#7169c85a38109a9c-->
      - `Reading an attachment back` (heading) — Describes the protocol revision 6 read-back leg — `GET /api/uploads/file?path=...` translated into a `FETCH_COMMAND`/`FETCH_RESULT` round trip so the web UI can render attached images inline — together with the safeguards that make it exposable (resolved-path containment against `..`/absolute/symlink escapes, the same 20 MiB cap decided from `stat()`, pre-dispatch version gating, `private` immutable caching justified by content-hash naming, a raster-image `Content-Type` whitelist with `nosniff`, and silent degradation to a hidden thumbnail on any failure). <!--#3a367cdd3db59693-->
  - `Authentication & Multi-Tenant Access` (heading) — Introduces the server's multi-tenant model since 8.0.0 where every request resolves to an owner, and outlines the end-to-end setup motion from bootstrap token to per-owner machine isolation. <!--#edc872485ba62860-->
    - `Why authentication is mandatory` (heading) — Explains the server fails closed: providers are configured via `server.auth.providers` (default `local`), and it raises `AuthNotConfigured` or returns HTTP 401 rather than reverting to anonymous access. <!--#b97a4ff02285d6f5-->
    - `The persistence layer (`~/.se3/server.db`)` (heading) — Describes the embedded stdlib-sqlite store that persists only identity facts a daemon reconnect cannot rebuild (owner records, identity bindings, password hashes, daemon-key hashes, break-glass token hashes), not live machine/flow state. <!--#1ebe2d9195b32bd8-->
    - `Bootstrapping the first admin (`bootstrap-token`)` (heading) — Explains the re-runnable `tianluo-server bootstrap-token` command that mints a one-time break-glass admin token (plaintext shown once, only its SHA-256 hash stored) and how it is consumed via the login screen or `POST /api/auth/breakglass`. <!--#099fe940bad528db-->
    - `Logging in and creating users` (heading) — Documents the human login ceremony (login/logout/me endpoints) and admin-only user creation, noting no public self-registration in v1. <!--#49803a3994826103-->
    - `Issuing daemon keys and binding machines` (heading) — Documents the owner-scoped daemon-key REST endpoints and how a daemon carries a key in its HELLO handshake so the server binds the machine to an owner, with WELCOME accept/reject semantics and TLS-backed reverse trust. <!--#8935a77698c91a48-->
    - `Deploying behind a TLS reverse proxy (wss)` (heading) — Explains that `tianluo-server` speaks only plaintext and needs a reverse proxy to terminate TLS, and how a single `location /` can serve both static HTTP and the `/ws`/`/ws/ui` WebSocket upgrades. <!--#a851c2bc60b1968e-->
      - `nginx` (heading) — Provides the idiomatic nginx reverse-proxy config (an http-level `map` for `Connection`, `proxy_http_version 1.1`, lengthened read timeouts) with notes on common pitfalls like panel-injected `map` placement. <!--#2e1ab8d8d510ecd3-->
      - `Caddy` (heading) — Provides the minimal Caddy reverse-proxy config that terminates TLS and proxies WebSockets transparently, with an optional variant for a longer idle read timeout. <!--#3237bb0419f03d38-->
      - `Verifying the proxy: a `curl --http1.1` handshake probe` (heading) — Shows how to confirm the proxy upgrades a WebSocket end-to-end with a raw `curl --http1.1` handshake expecting `HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols`, plus guidance on interpreting 404s, HTTP/2, and default ports. <!--#4ae597e9336f2799-->
    - `Owner isolation` (heading) — Describes how both the UI/REST channel and the daemon `/ws` channel are owner-scoped, with cross-owner targets reading as 404 and additive provider linking. <!--#b7529003bf01a4e6-->
  - `The Web Frontend` (heading) — Describes the bundled pure-static web frontend mounted at the server root: mandatory owner-scoped login, the real-time `/ws/ui` snapshot/status_update stream, and its watch/publish/respond capabilities routed through the REST API. <!--#293db9cf7095afb2-->

### `docs/daemon-and-server.zh.md` (markdown) — The Chinese-language guide to tianluo's resident control plane, covering `luo daemon` and `tianluo-server` end to end: quickstart and CLI reference, deployment/operations (outbound WebSocket model, foreground vs detached mode, `~/.se3/` runtime files, systemd memory guardrails), internal architecture and the remote task-publishing, file-upload and read-back paths, plus the mandatory multi-tenant auth model (bootstrap-token, sqlite identity store, daemon keys) and the web frontend. <!--#6e1bb7b9fb2c607e|9653e18a6b7fac18-->
- `tianluo Daemon 与中心服务器` (heading) — Top-level intro to the doc, framing the optional `luo daemon` (per-machine supervisor) and `tianluo-server` (central aggregating server) as a resident control plane layered atop the one-shot `luo run` CLI core. <!--#74aca4558d74ef92-->
  - `目录` (heading) — Table of contents for the Chinese daemon-and-server guide, linking its five top-level parts (quick start, deployment/operations, architecture, authentication and multi-tenant access, and the web frontend) with their subsections. <!--#32fc8834bb24e098-->
  - `快速上手` (heading) — Quickstart section header grouping installation, the two commands, and a typical session walkthrough. <!--#d6e457a6857ef50f-->
    - `安装` (heading) — Explains that `luo daemon` ships with the core `pip install tianluo`, while the central server and daemon's WebSocket client require the heavier optional `tianluo[server]` extra (FastAPI/uvicorn/websockets). <!--#3170a7a0c45bad2d-->
    - ``luo daemon` 命令` (heading) — Reference for the `luo daemon` subcommand group (start/stop/status) with its options like `--server-url`, `--daemon-key`, `--foreground`, and `--json`. <!--#de2896a8e022d056-->
    - ``tianluo-server` 命令` (heading) — Reference for the `tianluo-server` entry point and its options (`--host`, `--port`, `--db-path`, `--log-level`, `bootstrap-token`), noting that auth is mandatory since 8.0.0. <!--#efc222964267abaf-->
    - `一次典型会话` (heading) — A worked end-to-end example session: start the server, mint a bootstrap-token, issue a daemon key, start a daemon dialing in on a worker machine, then observe/publish tasks in the browser. <!--#e6b43fb7d1daba26-->
  - `部署与运维` (heading) — Deployment and operations section header covering the connection model, foreground/background modes, runtime files, and process supervision. <!--#60d1e2a31c5eb564-->
    - `出站连接模型` (heading) — Describes the one-directional daemon→server outbound WebSocket model, its NAT-friendliness and exponential-backoff resilience, and the scheme-based default port completion (`ws`→8080, `wss`→443). <!--#413e952f88ea832c-->
    - `前台模式 vs 后台(detached)模式` (heading) — Contrasts the daemon's default detached (double-fork) background mode against `--foreground` mode, noting only one daemon may run per pid directory. <!--#29219d84d6b95a68-->
    - `运行时文件:pidfile 与状态文件` (heading) — Documents the daemon's runtime files under `~/.se3/` (`daemon.pid`, `daemon_status.json`, `daemon.log`), overridable via `SE3_DAEMON_DIR`, and their atomic write guarantee. <!--#bddaa0111283d945-->
      - ``status` 中的连接状态` (heading) — Details how `daemon_status.json` records the real outbound connection outcome surfaced by `luo daemon status` on a `Connection:` line (local-only / connected / not connected with human-readable reason). <!--#181db3fd1582eab3-->
    - `流程的发现与监管` (heading) — Explains the daemon's tracking of two flow classes — spawned (daemon-owned) and discovered (via psutil) — polling liveness and terminating only its own spawned flows on shutdown. <!--#f5ec7b78ca632816-->
    - `systemd 内存护栏` (heading) — Explains that `server.history_cache.budget_mb` is the primary in-code cap on the server's per-flow conversation memory, and gives a sample `tianluo-server.service` systemd unit whose `Restart=on-failure`, `StartLimitIntervalSec`/`StartLimitBurst`, and `MemoryHigh`/`MemoryMax` settings act as a backstop, plus how to inspect `history-cache` occupancy reports via `journalctl`. <!--#0ba2abfabcfc2ef5-->
  - `架构与工作原理` (heading) — Architecture section header covering daemon internals, server internals, and the end-to-end task-publishing flow. <!--#f9184f4e8ec18234-->
    - `daemon 内部` (heading) — Describes the daemon's internal architecture as a single asyncio process with four concurrent parts: Supervisor, Spawner, Aggregator (disk reader), and optional outbound Client. <!--#9cf3485fb178a88f-->
    - `中心服务器内部` (heading) — Describes `tianluo-server` as a FastAPI app: accepts daemon WebSockets at `/ws`, holds an in-memory `ServerState` aggregate, persists only identity facts to sqlite, and exposes REST APIs plus the web frontend. <!--#ba03c81e85d1209b-->
    - `端到端:从远端机器发布任务` (heading) — Walks through the end-to-end path for launching a flow on a remote machine — browser/`POST /api/flows` → server → `SPAWN_FLOW` pushed down the existing outbound WebSocket → daemon spawns `luo run` → aggregator polls state → `MachineStatus` snapshot broadcast back — plus the mirrored `RESPOND_CALL` path via `tianluo/calls/`. <!--#bbc1060f6d76ae61-->
    - `文件上传通道` (heading) — Documents the WebUI file-upload channel — how `POST /api/uploads` dispatches an `UPLOAD_COMMAND` frame over a machine's existing outbound daemon socket so files land in `<project_root>/tianluo/uploads/` and prompts carry only project-relative paths — plus its 20 MiB limit, content-hash naming and dedup, project-registration and protocol-version ≥ 5 gating, `.gitignore` coverage, and deliberate absence of any cleanup policy. <!--#00ee9613b7dd30cf-->
      - `把附件读回来` (heading) — Documents the mirror read-back path added in protocol revision 6 — `GET /api/uploads/file?path=...` relaying a `FETCH_COMMAND`/`FETCH_RESULT` round-trip over the daemon socket so the WebUI can inline uploaded images — along with its resolved-path containment rule, size cap, pre-dispatch version gate, `private, immutable` caching, raster-only `Content-Type` allowlist, and intentionally silent failure degradation. <!--#51c0a2ac6c87a10f-->
  - `鉴权与多租户访问` (heading) — Introduces the mandatory multi-tenant auth model (every request/connection resolves to an owner since 8.0.0) and diagrams the end-to-end setup flow from bootstrap-token to per-owner isolation. <!--#d0e22fe7c52dc458-->
    - `为什么鉴权是强制的` (heading) — Explains the server's fail-closed behavior: auth providers come from `server.auth.providers` (default `["local"]`), and with no usable provider the server raises `AuthNotConfigured` rather than allowing anonymous access. <!--#fd53fd47c9b98d75-->
    - `持久化层(`~/.se3/server.db`)` (heading) — Describes the embedded single-file sqlite store (`~/.se3/server.db`) that persists only non-rebuildable identity facts: owner records, identity bindings, password/daemon-key/break-glass hashes. <!--#16ce60960310c361-->
    - `引导首个管理员(`bootstrap-token`)` (heading) — Explains `tianluo-server bootstrap-token`, the IdP-independent entry that mints a one-time break-glass admin token (plaintext printed once, only its SHA-256 hash stored), consumable via `POST /api/auth/breakglass`. <!--#902dea3c5fac80c1-->
    - `登录并创建用户` (heading) — Describes the human/UI login flow through the provider chain (login/logout/me endpoints) and admin-only user creation, with no v1 public self-registration. <!--#0acb5b9085ab94d8-->
    - `签发 daemon key 并绑定机器` (heading) — Describes owner self-service daemon-key management (`/api/daemon-keys` endpoints), how a daemon presents the key in its HELLO to bind its machine to an owner, and the `WELCOME(accepted=...)` handshake result. <!--#ab1a42998816edb0-->
    - `在 TLS 反向代理后部署(wss)` (heading) — Explains that `tianluo-server` speaks only plaintext and needs a reverse proxy to terminate TLS for `wss://`, forwarding both static HTTP and `/ws`/`/ws/ui` upgrades to one backend via a single `location /`. <!--#67f6ef4d9c491699-->
      - `nginx` (heading) — Provides a worked nginx reverse-proxy config for TLS/WebSocket termination (using an http-context `map` for `$connection_upgrade`), with pitfalls around `map` placement, `proxy_http_version 1.1`, and `proxy_read_timeout`. <!--#687a8bf961363f7b-->
      - `Caddy` (heading) — Provides the minimal Caddy reverse-proxy config that auto-terminates TLS and transparently proxies WebSocket, plus a variant with a relaxed `read_timeout`. <!--#9da11ef67e43262c-->
      - `验证代理:`curl --http1.1` 握手探测` (heading) — Shows how to verify a proxy passes WebSocket upgrades through with a `curl --http1.1` handshake probe expecting `HTTP/1.1 101`, with gotchas around 404 on `/ws`, HTTP/2, and scheme-default ports. <!--#24c15b2359e16613-->
    - `owner 隔离` (heading) — Explains how both channels are owner-scoped — frontend/`/api/*` filtered by owner (cross-owner reads as 404) and daemon `/ws` bound via HELLO key — and how adding a second auth provider is purely additive. <!--#6afda22934aebcb0-->
  - `网页前端` (heading) — Describes the server's bundled static web frontend (mounted at root, login-gated and owner-scoped) that connects via `/ws/ui` for live updates and lets users view flow progress, publish tasks, and respond to calls. <!--#e8ad3ebad1aa0f63-->

## `scripts/` — A collection of standalone, one-off maintenance and diagnostic utilities that sit outside the package: history/registry cleanup scripts (`cleanup_history_leak.py`, `cleanup_project_roots.py`, `compact_history_jsonl.py`), a backlog-to-Issue-YAML migration script (`migrate_backlog.py`), performance measurement harnesses for server/WebSocket history relay stalls (`measure_history_relay_backpressure.py`, `measure_server_loop_stalls.py`), and a userspace shell helper that stages headless Chromium's shared libraries for browser tests (`install_browser_test_libs.sh`). <!--#061b8b2450be686e|125e8d3a6faeb9c4-->

### `scripts/cleanup_history_leak.py` (python) — A one-time maintenance script that scans tianluo/history/ and deletes (or dry-run lists) test-leak residue — empty dirs, single bare-`.jsonl` leak dirs, and known test-fixture residue names — while hard-protecting real flow, recovery-snapshot, and uuid-style history directories, exposing a `--dry-run`/`--history-dir` CLI. <!--#fd7b4169d57fa292|42358c5eed1e937d-->
- `_project_root` (function) — Returns the project root directory (two levels up from this script's file path). <!--#515f3ee622c6e172-->
- `_is_leak_jsonl_file` (function) — Reports whether a path is a file literally named `.jsonl` — the name-only signature of an empty-step_id test leak, regardless of content. <!--#8e81921bac079a9b-->
- `_is_protected_name` (function) — Reports whether a directory name denotes a real flow (valid flow-id) or a `recovered_` snapshot that must never be deleted. <!--#6a5379f5e6be4cc6-->
- `_is_residue_name` (function) — Predicate that returns True for known test-fixture history directory names ("se3", "tianluo", or names starting with "test-flow"/"prompt_history") that never belong to a real flow. <!--#8d9b1f9b39e9717c-->
- `classify_dir` (function) — Classifies a history subdirectory into a leak category (empty / single-`.jsonl` / residue-name) or None to keep it, letting content signals override name protection but never deleting real uuid-style flow dirs by name. <!--#45c870fb4386af61-->
- `cleanup` (function) — Scans the history directory, deletes (or in dry-run lists) leak dirs and stray root files by category while preserving real flows and uuid dirs, then prints a summary report and returns an exit code. <!--#e58a7cd10e6fe0a1-->
- `main` (function) — CLI entry point that parses --dry-run and --history-dir args, resolves the history directory (preferring tianluo/history, falling back to se3/history under the project root), and delegates to cleanup() to remove leaked directories. <!--#0ff658775d6095e3-->

### `scripts/cleanup_project_roots.py` (python) — A one-time maintenance CLI script that scrubs the daemon's project_roots.json registry of pytest-tempdir residue (and optionally vanished paths) leaked into it by test-spawned `luo run` stubs, atomically rewriting the file (unless --dry-run) while preserving real project roots. <!--#b46534e2efc7aecb|c64ce9ab7db4dcff-->
- `_default_registry` (function) — Resolves the path to the daemon's project_roots.json registry, honoring the SE3_DAEMON_DIR override and falling back to ~/.se3. <!--#f4bd2951eb4fb929-->
- `_is_pytest_residue` (function) — Predicate that returns whether a project-root path matches the pytest-residue regex (i.e., a leaked temp path from test runs). <!--#3ed4f14b96ddca01-->
- `cleanup` (function) — Loads the registry, drops pytest-residue (and optionally missing) project-root entries, atomically rewrites the file unless dry-run, and prints a cleanup report. <!--#063b65147aadad9d-->
- `main` (function) — CLI entry point parsing --dry-run/--registry/--prune-missing flags and invoking cleanup on the resolved registry path. <!--#1b63029c7edf6cf8-->

### `scripts/compact_history_jsonl.py` (python) — Standalone maintenance CLI that scans existing daemon history `*.jsonl` step streams and backfills the online record-budget compaction, rewriting only oversized lines under `--apply` via an atomic, line-count-verified temp-file replace (dry-run by default) and reporting per-file byte savings. <!--#1e75db0582447841|c01f7a3c199347f3-->
- `_project_root` (function) — Returns the repository root directory, derived from this script's own location two levels up. <!--#515f3ee622c6e172-->
