- `_load_record_budget` (function) — Loads the pure `record_budget` module directly from the checkout's source file (falling back to a normal import) so the script runs without installing or importing the heavyweight `tianluo.daemon` package. <!--#e9dbdcfd05f96c9e-->
- `_dumps` (function) — Serialises a compacted record with exactly the same JSON encoder settings the daemon→server link uses, so backfilled and online-compacted records measure identically against the byte budget. <!--#19e588682f0c1954-->
- `LineOutcome` (class) — Small dataclass recording what happened to a single physical line — whether it was oversized, compacted or failed, plus its before/after byte sizes. <!--#fca69b44752b3b11-->
- `FileReport` (class) — Per-file accumulator holding line/byte counts, whether the file was rewritten, and any error, with a derived `saved_bytes` figure. <!--#e73ab8833a5f023e-->
  - `FileReport.saved_bytes` (method) — Returns the (non-negative) byte savings for the file as oversized bytes minus compacted bytes. <!--#d4948676ccbfe2ee-->
- `RunReport` (class) — Aggregate result of one pass: the list of per-file reports, the scanned-file count, and a `failed` flag. <!--#e2664b961ed6489c-->
  - `RunReport.failed` (method) — Reports whether any file in the run recorded an error. <!--#0200c4944d1ed9c6-->
- `compact_line` (function) — Compacts one physical line if it exceeds the record budget, returning the original bytes verbatim on any parse, compaction, validity or no-shrink failure so the write stays 1:1 with the read. <!--#7d70d3e3a31ccd53-->
- `count_physical_lines` (function) — Counts a file's physical lines by chunked byte scan, matching how the reader assigns ordinals (an unterminated tail still occupies a slot). <!--#c5468554ec3d6743-->
- `_has_oversized_line` (function) — Cheap pre-scan returning the line count and whether any line exceeds the budget, judged from line lengths alone so untouched files are never parsed or copied. <!--#c7bf49d178eed214-->
- `_stream` (function) — Streams a file line by line through `compact_line`, optionally writing the result to a writer, while tallying counts into the file's report. <!--#c03595d27c49309d-->
- `_tmp_path` (function) — Builds a deterministic, injective sibling scratch path whose percent-escaped name contains no `.jsonl` substring, so no history-stream discovery (reader or this script) ever mistakes the temp file for a real step stream. <!--#2a7ecaafbd81ade4-->
- `process_file` (function) — Scans one history jsonl file and, under `--apply`, rewrites it via an fsynced temp file plus atomic replace — abandoning the rewrite unless the physical line counts match exactly and at least one line actually shrank. <!--#586a4dd13f330e21-->
- `_unlink` (function) — Best-effort file deletion that swallows OS errors. <!--#d78a9f126cc725fd-->
- `_step_files` (function) — Lists a flow directory's physical history streams — both `*.jsonl` and `*.jsonl.from-*` sidecars, name-sorted — to match exactly what the daemon reader delivers. <!--#d2e92971afaec839-->
- `iter_targets` (function) — Collects the history step files to process, either for one flow id or across every flow directory plus the history root, in a stable order. <!--#c602259b48d7a969-->
- `_fmt_bytes` (function) — Formats a byte count as a human-readable B/KB/MB/GB string. <!--#a590b78c7eba6db6-->
- `compact_history` (function) — Drives a whole pass over the target files, printing per-file lines for files that would change plus a summary report, and returning an exit code (0 ok, 1 missing dir, 2 some file failed) with the run report. <!--#adf564a360271f7a-->
- `main` (function) — CLI entry point that parses arguments, resolves the history directory (with a legacy `se3/history` fallback), enforces dry-run as the default and as the winner over `--apply`, and runs the pass. <!--#93ab8ea0a2950728-->

### `scripts/install_browser_test_libs.sh` (text) — A userspace bash fallback script that downloads and extracts (via `apt-get download`/`dpkg -x`, no root needed) the system shared libraries headless Chromium requires into a gitignored `.browser-libs/lib`, so the Playwright-based headless-browser acceptance test can run on hosts where `playwright install --with-deps` isn't possible. <!--#fe72f339a1f471d9|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `scripts/measure_history_relay_backpressure.py` (python) — A standalone measurement harness that replays real or synthetic `DaemonHistoryReader` drain frames through the real `_serve_loop`/`UiHub` stack into a deliberately slow `/ws/ui` client, reporting bundle completeness, daemon receive-path park times, event-loop lateness and relayed byte volume to quantify history-relay backpressure. <!--#7400f27f78e01829|641df20fbffdc8c7-->
- `_SlowUiClient` (class) — Test double for a `/ws/ui` browser client whose `send_text` awaits a fixed delay per frame, modelling a slow link/main thread while tallying relayed frames, bytes and payload types. <!--#ebc03fa34816a91d-->
  - `_SlowUiClient.__init__` (method) — Stores the per-frame delay and zeroes the frame, byte and per-type counters. <!--#9a638e077b47aabd-->
  - `_SlowUiClient.send_text` (method) — Sleeps for the configured delay, then records the frame's count, UTF-8 byte size and decoded `type` field. <!--#68614df1233b6595-->
- `_real_frames` (function) — Replays `DaemonHistoryReader` over a real on-disk flow, looping on the cursor until untruncated, to collect the actual sequence of wire frames a drain would emit. <!--#39aabc98ee175cf2-->
- `_synthetic_frames` (function) — Fabricates a drain-shaped frame sequence (one `full` head then `append` chunks) with each non-final frame padded to `MAX_BYTES_PER_REPORT` and correct `cursor`/`cursor_base` values so the server classifies it as one continuing pull reply. <!--#a285a73e2f419df9-->
- `_ReplayingDaemonSocket` (class) — Stand-in daemon-leg socket that hands `_serve_loop` pre-encoded frames one at a time while timing the gap between each hand-off and the next read — the 'park' during which the daemon's inbound queue (and keepalive Pongs) go undrained. <!--#ff11dc7ce61e462c-->
  - `_ReplayingDaemonSocket.__init__` (method) — Captures the frame list and initialises the replay index, hand-off timestamp and park-duration log. <!--#011e97db42c12a36-->
  - `_ReplayingDaemonSocket.receive_text` (method) — Records the elapsed park since the previous frame was handed out, then returns the next frame or raises once the replay is exhausted. <!--#b6d12484459ac9ad-->
  - `_ReplayingDaemonSocket.send_text` (method) — No-op sink for outbound heartbeat PING frames. <!--#c76ca4e63c9f9452-->
  - `_ReplayingDaemonSocket.close` (method) — No-op close so the socket satisfies the interface `_serve_loop` expects. <!--#afbdab25a562492c-->
- `_drive` (function) — Wires up a real `ServerState`/`UiHub`/`ConnectionManager` with a parked REST waiter and armed replay marker, runs the real `_serve_loop` over the replayed frames against a slow UI client, and prints bundle completeness plus daemon receive-path park, event-loop lateness and relayed-byte statistics. <!--#6ad1e02c2c1b2fed-->
- `main` (function) — CLI entry point that parses options to choose real-flow or synthetic frames (with size/delay/tick knobs) and runs `_drive` under `asyncio.run`. <!--#578006fa5d449930-->

### `scripts/measure_server_loop_stalls.py` (python) — A standalone benchmark CLI that builds synthetic daemon history bundles and reports both the per-operation cost (REST render, gzip, frame decode, `/ws/ui` fan-out, `ServerState._lock` helpers) and the resulting asyncio event-loop lateness for inline vs `to_thread` vs chunked execution, to pinpoint what stalls the server loop. <!--#938624f8aff5bc6d|8cf260e5074da437-->
- `_record` (function) — Builds one synthetic history record shaped like the daemon's (envelope + assistant message of `chars` filler + a usage_records entry) for use as benchmark input. <!--#e56d2825abd466db-->
- `_bench` (function) — Times a callable over `runs` repetitions and appends a (label, best-ms, median-ms) row to the shared results list. <!--#5a6ae1ae011a4294-->
- `measure` (function) — Builds a synthetic bundle of a given record count/size and prints a sorted cost table for the REST render, gzip, frame decode, `/ws/ui` fan-out render, and the unmemoized O(bundle) helpers that run under `ServerState._lock`. <!--#c2ea67898e6d089f-->
- `_worst_timer_lateness` (function) — Runs a 5 ms ticker on an otherwise-idle loop and returns the worst delay that ticker suffers while the given work runs inline or via `asyncio.to_thread` — the operational measure of loop blocking. <!--#3c8d3803c06ab778-->
- `measure_lateness` (function) — Prints the event-loop lateness table comparing inline vs `to_thread` vs batched (`dump_json_chunked`) execution of the JSON render, gzip pass, and frame decode, showing which offloads actually release the GIL. <!--#e700d5bf00c08856-->
- `main` (function) — CLI entry point that parses `--runs` and runs both the cost and loop-lateness measurements for each bundle shape in `SHAPES`. <!--#7fa67412e3c54f2a-->

### `scripts/migrate_backlog.py` (python) — A one-time migration script that converts tianluo/specs/_backlog/*.md files into Issue YAML records by parsing each file's title, phase/status, and description, creating a tagged issue via IssueManager (with type inferred from phase), deleting the source markdown, and printing a migration report. <!--#4485da5ad9cd4d32|760a7a4bef36feb3-->
- `_extract_title` (function) — Returns the first markdown '# ' heading as the issue title, or 'Untitled' if none is found. <!--#5831f459c0a33fa4-->
- `_extract_phase` (function) — Finds and returns the markdown line containing both 'status' and 'backlog' to capture the phase/status info. <!--#5713b308209b36b0-->
- `_infer_type` (function) — Maps a phase/status line to an issue type (phase 1→task, phase 2/3→feature, phase 4/future→idea, default feature). <!--#c7e5b6978408cc9f-->
- `_extract_description` (function) — Collects body text under the Idea/Goal/Motivation section as the issue description, falling back to a default string. <!--#a6e466f1c2d9273a-->
- `migrate` (function) — Main entry point that iterates backlog markdown files, creates a tagged issue for each, deletes the source file, and prints a migration report. <!--#ce12a1e953eb33a1-->

## `src/` — The project's source root, containing the active `tianluo/` package (the `luo` CLI, flow engine, agent runners, daemon/server, and supporting subsystems) alongside the thin deprecated `se3/` compatibility shim that meta-path-aliases legacy `se3.*` imports onto `tianluo.*`. <!--#1a58538b287d46c7|d0a5eeef6b374640-->

## `src/se3/` — The deprecated se3 compatibility package (removed in 13.0.0), consisting solely of an __init__.py shim that aliases the renamed se3 namespace onto tianluo via an _AliasFinder meta-path finder so every se3.* import resolves to the same tianluo.* module object, while emitting a DeprecationWarning. <!--#46eda211108bb985|c7dabd73a08e338c-->

### `src/se3/__init__.py` (python) — A deprecated compatibility shim (removed in 13.0.0) that aliases the renamed se3 package onto tianluo, installing an _AliasFinder meta-path finder so every se3.* import resolves to the same module object as its tianluo.* counterpart, and emits a DeprecationWarning. <!--#1228657d3026d8ee|c24feb23df88e562-->
- `_AliasLoader` (class) — An importlib Loader that resolves an aliased se3.* module name to the already-imported real tianluo.* module, returning that module from create_module and doing nothing in exec_module since it is already executed. <!--#d22a040836da02e9-->
  - `_AliasLoader.__init__` (method) — Stores the canonical tianluo.* module name (_real_name) that this loader should resolve the alias to. <!--#b2c8a8e5531837e5-->
  - `_AliasLoader.create_module` (method) — Returns the real tianluo.* module by importing _real_name, so the aliased se3.* import reuses the already-executed module object. <!--#f42c27d20906d1e3-->
  - `_AliasLoader.exec_module` (method) — A no-op because the aliased target module has already been executed, leaving its canonical __name__/__spec__ intact. <!--#bde76bd6c3267568-->
- `_AliasFinder` (class) — A meta-path finder that intercepts se3.* imports and redirects them to the corresponding tianluo.* modules via _AliasLoader, while declining se3.__main__ so `python -m se3` executes tianluo/__main__.py normally. <!--#3f41d42aba42c070-->
  - `_AliasFinder.find_spec` (method) — Maps an se3.* fullname to its tianluo.* counterpart, returning a spec backed by _AliasLoader when that real module exists, and returning None for non-se3 names, se3.__main__, or unresolvable targets. <!--#e44d3d747f556eab-->

## `src/tianluo/` — The main `tianluo` (SE 3.0) Python package: a CLI-driven AI software-engineering framework whose `engine/` state machine runs LLM flow steps against pluggable agent backends (`agent_runner.py`, `claude_runner.py`, `claude_interactive_runner.py`, `codex_runner.py`), exposed through the Typer `commands/` layer and localized via `i18n/`, with `templates/` for project scaffolding, `e2e/` for containerized end-to-end scenario testing, `core/` for shared primitives, and an optional `daemon/`+`server/` control plane that streams run status to a multi-tenant FastAPI server and WebUI. <!--#81da81afefbaaa36|9b4aa294181e0164-->

### `src/tianluo/__init__.py` (python) — Package init for the SE 3.0 framework CLI that resolves and exposes the package version (via `__version__` / `SE3_FRAMEWORK_VERSION`) from installed metadata with a pyproject.toml fallback. <!--#cb87e5d43de335eb|52ccc8955ede7d6c-->
- `_get_version` (function) — Resolves the package version by first querying installed package metadata for "tianluo", falling back to reading the version field from pyproject.toml (via tomllib/tomli) in a source checkout, and finally to the literal "unknown" so that importing tianluo never fails. <!--#56551bf09b5ce270-->

### `src/tianluo/__main__.py` (python) — Package entry point enabling `python -m tianluo` to invoke the CLI (via `.cli.app`), used as the daemon spawner's fallback when no `luo`/`tianluo`/`se3` console script is on `PATH`. <!--#de15268a7a4e72dc|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/agent_runner.py` (python) — Defines the vendor-neutral agent backend contract for LLMCaller — the abstract AgentRunner base class (synchronous run, monitored run with wall/inactivity timeouts, intent-to-CLI argument construction, infrastructure-error detection, startup provider/model reporting) along with its supporting types InfraErrorType, AgentInvocationIntent, RunResult, and RunnerStartupMetadata. <!--#c83118e3d4506f57|dc30fbf4dade56ec-->
- `InfraErrorType` (class) — Enum classifying infrastructure-level failures (usage limit, timeout, hang, startup failure) that warrant rotating to a different agent. <!--#b4559b2f7002857f-->
- `AgentInvocationIntent` (class) — A string enum (DEFAULT, DIRECT_IMPLEMENTATION) declaring the vendor-neutral semantic purpose of a runner invocation, currently informational-only and kept as the seam for future runners to map an intent onto a native CLI feature. <!--#664d78a8b4cac602-->
- `RunResult` (class) — Dataclass bundling a runner execution's exit code, stdout, stderr, and detected infrastructure-error type. <!--#d425154633ceb3f4-->
- `RunnerStartupMetadata` (class) — A small data holder for provider identity a runner can verify at launch time — provider, model, and provider_session_id — before any stream metadata arrives. <!--#2d0ed2496c88312e-->
- `AgentRunner` (class) — Abstract base class defining the contract every agent runner must implement — synchronous `run`, monitored `run_with_monitor`, intent-to-CLI translation via `build_call_args`, and `detect_infra_error` — plus startup provider/model metadata used by LLMCaller to drive any agent backend uniformly. <!--#bf8e067733a8ea8f-->
  - `AgentRunner.get_startup_metadata` (method) — Returns the runner's declared provider and model as RunnerStartupMetadata, so callers get verified launch identity instead of guessing from command names. <!--#5af87687c4204d87-->
  - `AgentRunner.run` (method) — Abstract method to run the agent synchronously with optional timeout/cwd/env and a retry callback, returning a CompletedProcess. <!--#36ae2f398d60a19e-->
  - `AgentRunner.run_with_monitor` (method) — Abstract method to run the agent under wall/inactivity timeouts with output and activity callbacks, returning a monitored result. <!--#b42f4e02affb6ec5-->
  - `AgentRunner.build_call_args` (method) — Abstract hook where each runner subclass translates caller intent (effective prompt, read-only flag, context files, invocation intent) into that agent's concrete CLI argument list. <!--#a010fc1c9480fc06-->
  - `AgentRunner.detect_infra_error` (method) — Abstract method that inspects a run's exit code and output to classify whether an infrastructure error occurred. <!--#9da392a3d03fdbc7-->

### `src/tianluo/claude_interactive_runner.py` (python) — A third concrete `AgentRunner` adapter (alongside `ClaudeCodeRunner` and `CodexRunner`) that drives the interactive `claude` TUI inside a PTY — lazily importing `pexpect`, feeding the effective prompt as bracketed-paste input once the input box is ready, supervising the process group with wall/inactivity timeouts and force-kill, and tailing the on-disk session transcript JSONL to emit Claude stream-json NDJSON with accumulated `usage` totals, a synthesized `type:"result"` line, turn-completion detection, and infra-error classification (usage limit / startup failure). <!--#a4718f316fd7c3b7|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/claude_runner.py` (python) — Defines the `ClaudeCodeRunner` `AgentRunner` adapter (plus its `MonitoredResult`/`_SingleRunResult` records and stdin/stderr/confirmation-prompt helper functions) that builds Claude Code CLI argv from intent-level parameters and executes it as a monitored subprocess, handling `--setting-sources` isolation, oversized-prompt rerouting to stdin, activity/timeout monitoring, interactive confirmation answering, and infra-error detection for retry logic. <!--#0668b720e6f5c925|8abf5e983b2a7a07-->
- `_spawn_stdin_writer` (function) — Module helper that writes a large prompt payload to the child's stdin from a daemon thread (then closes it) to avoid pipe-buffer deadlock on the large-prompt path. <!--#19dde2ba6f7be9f0-->
- `_spawn_stderr_reader` (function) — Module-level helper that starts a daemon thread to continuously drain a child process's stderr pipe, optionally tee-ing lines to a log file, a bounded buffer, and the parent's stderr, so the pipe never fills and blocks the child. <!--#2212811151becfaf-->
- `detect_confirmation_prompt` (function) — Module function that conservatively detects an interactive CLI confirmation prompt in a line of child output, returning the prompt text and any inline numeric option labels (or None). <!--#5c28f457ef473dae-->
- `_write_stdin_response` (function) — Module helper that writes a confirmation answer (newline-terminated) back to the child's stdin, swallowing failures so undeliverable answers degrade to a no-op. <!--#a2717e89116de7e9-->
- `ClaudeCodeRunner` (class) — An `AgentRunner` adapter that wraps a single Claude Code CLI command (e.g. `claude`/`kclaude`), handling setting-source isolation via `--setting-sources`, rerouting oversized `-p` prompts to stdin, and executing the subprocess — while leaving multi-command fallback to `LLMCaller`. <!--#e700cfe2f4baf424-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner.__init__` (method) — Initializes the runner from a single command (with legacy `commands` support) and resolves the Claude CLI setting-sources list from explicit args or project config. <!--#b59445d42c87ca93-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner._resolve_args` (method) — Static method that rewrites oversized `-p`/`--prompt` argv values to stdin (preserving `@file` references) to avoid execve E2BIG limits. <!--#181b40b864d27e84-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner.run` (method) — Runs Claude synchronously via subprocess.run for a single command, assembling the full argv, feeding any stdin prompt, and returning a CompletedProcess (124 on timeout). <!--#4f8bee1df17dbf47-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner.get_command` (method) — Returns the command string at the given index in the backward-compatibility commands list (clamping to the last entry). <!--#55afbbe111e290a0-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner.get_next_command` (method) — Returns the command following a given one in the commands list, or None if it is last or not found. <!--#0f38633a0bb6a7c2-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner.build_call_args` (method) — Builds the Claude CLI argv for a step from intent-level inputs (prompt, read-only flag, context files), emitting stream-json output flags, exactly one merged `--disallowedTools` flag, and `--file` entries, deliberately omitting `--settings`. <!--#aa4f7499a4534f71-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner.detect_usage_limit` (method) — Static method that inspects the tail of failed-command output for known usage/rate-limit keywords to detect quota exhaustion. <!--#f864b51cf98d6564-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner.detect_timeout` (method) — Static method that reports whether a return code (124) indicates a timeout failure. <!--#3e76609d6d367ce6-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner.detect_infra_error` (method) — Combines usage-limit and timeout detection into a single InfraErrorType verdict for LLMCaller's retry logic. <!--#b63bfc06170b32ad-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner.run_with_monitor` (method) — Public entry point that runs the configured Claude command under activity-based monitoring (wall and inactivity timeouts, output/activity/confirmation callbacks, optional log file) and wraps the outcome in a MonitoredResult. <!--#7efb86362b70b278-->
  - `ClaudeCodeRunner._run_single_with_monitor` (method) — Internal workhorse that spawns one Claude subprocess and drives its lifecycle — stdin routing for oversized prompts, background stderr draining, select()-based stdout polling with hang and timeout detection, and interactive confirmation-prompt answering. <!--#a44318440c17f798-->
- `MonitoredResult` (class) — A dataclass carrying the outcome of `run_with_monitor` — return code, captured output, which command/index ran, retry and interrupt flags, a bounded `stderr_tail` for diagnostics, plus a `success` convenience property. <!--#9dc9e302680592a3-->
  - `MonitoredResult.success` (method) — Property returning True when the monitored run's return code is zero. <!--#787b46b245897e2b-->
- `_SingleRunResult` (class) — Internal per-invocation result record adding success and should_retry decision flags alongside the exit code, output, interrupt state, and stderr tail. <!--#f07c6bcf691bb414-->

### `src/tianluo/cli.py` (python) — The Typer-based command-line entry point for tianluo (`luo`, plus the deprecated `se3` alias), defining the root callback and every top-level command — `run`, `init`, `daemon start/stop/status`, `merge`, `merge-respond`, `merge-unlock`, `salvage`, and `end-session` — as thin option-validating adapters that dispatch into the flow engine, daemon, merge, and session-recovery libraries. <!--#8556ebbcdd8b846f|d679163560e3f783-->
- `legacy_app` (function) — Entry point for the deprecated `se3` console script that prints a stderr migration notice pointing at `luo`/`tianluo` before delegating to the normal `app()`, slated for removal in 13.0.0. <!--#a4b4a52e21d13aa7-->
- `_version_callback` (function) — Typer eager callback for `--version` that echoes the localized version string and exits immediately. <!--#1daa43ccf5bfdbde-->
- `main` (function) — Root Typer callback that initializes the display console, wires the `--version` option, and prints help when no subcommand is given. <!--#b4f9f0eb2adc72b2-->
- `_init_display` (function) — Initializes the global Rich console for consistent CLI output. <!--#bc1892294d2bdfda-->
- `_read_multiline_input` (function) — Reads multiline user input from stdin, using prompt_toolkit (with Ctrl+D-to-accept bindings and history) when interactive and a plain read when piped, returning None on cancel. <!--#9941ab8d25f9a95a-->
- `_param_from_commandline` (function) — Helper that uses click/typer's ParameterSource to tell whether a given option (notably `--type`) was actually typed on the command line rather than defaulted, since an explicit type is persisted and overrides analyze's classification. <!--#fcacf3ae08eda849-->
- `run_cmd` (function) — The `luo run` Typer command — the unified CLI entry point into the flow engine, which validates and normalizes user-supplied options (`--output-format`, `--type`, `--plan-decomposition`, `--plan-granularity`, the deprecated `--implementation-strategy`) before dispatching to `run_flow`, `run_worktree_mode`, or `resume_run` for normal, worktree-isolated, resumed, discovery, or issue-sourced runs. <!--#ab72a6a7439e89c1-->
- `init_cmd` (function) — The `luo init` command that binds the project root and scaffolds a new SE3 project's standard directory structure (tianluo.yaml, specs/base/spec.md). <!--#f658a6c04f8e551c-->
- `_precheck_websockets` (function) — Warns on the CLI when the `websockets` package is missing so the user knows a `--server-url` daemon would silently fall back to local-only mode. <!--#ce7c7d98cc33fa03-->
- `_report_connection_result` (function) — Polls the daemon status file after a detached start and reports the real server-connection outcome, trusting only status written by the fresh daemon and treating early errors as transient. <!--#784e4427a440b106-->
- `daemon_start_cmd` (function) — The `luo daemon start` command that launches the daemon detached (or in the foreground), resolves the daemon key from flag or environment, and reports the resulting connection state. <!--#cd92a1f90509fdd6-->
- `daemon_stop_cmd` (function) — The `luo daemon stop` command that stops the running daemon and reports stopped / not-running / stop-timeout outcomes with matching exit codes. <!--#4579fb698e0918f4-->
- `daemon_status_cmd` (function) — The `luo daemon status` command that prints (or emits as JSON) the daemon's PID, machine, configured server, real connection state, and tracked flows. <!--#fe248f8d79b8de72-->
- `merge_cmd` (function) — The `luo merge` command, a thin adapter over the merge library that validates branch names/strategy, resolves config, and runs `integrate()`+`reconcile()` to merge branches sequentially into the current branch with no confirmation gate. <!--#46ff72a84234338d-->
- `merge_respond_cmd` (function) — The `luo merge-respond` command that processes an edited MCP call-response file to execute merge-conflict decisions and exits with its result code. <!--#db2f74f8b8b23182-->
- `merge_unlock_cmd` (function) — Typer command `luo merge-unlock` that inspects the project's merge lock — reporting lock-file path, holder PID/machine, and alive/stale/corrupt/remote state — auto-cleans stale locks, refuses live holders unless `--force`, and exits with the release outcome's code. <!--#6b113b51c47122d3-->
- `salvage_cmd` (function) — The `luo salvage` command that performs best-effort recovery of an abnormally terminated session (reads state, commits changes, files issues for unfinished work, archives the session). <!--#d766a6f00af9e210-->
- `end_session_cmd` (function) — The `luo end-session` command that terminates a live run process and archives a session — cleaning up worktrees without merging uncommitted work into the main branch. <!--#2a7e0ebe6a99e153-->

### `src/tianluo/codex_runner.py` (python) — AgentRunner adapter for the `codex` CLI: it builds the codex invocation, streams the process's `--json` JSONL output through a stateful `CodexEventConverter` that translates codex thread/turn/item events into Claude stream-json NDJSON (agent messages, tool_use/tool_result chips, touched files, usage/cost and terminal result metadata), and wraps execution with stdin/stderr pump threads, monitored/retry runs, and infra-error detection such as shell-snapshot failures. <!--#72b74d82da920166|a5cb31cd55108708-->
- `_detect_shell_snapshot_failure` (function) — Module-level helper that returns True if the given stderr text contains any known shell-snapshot validation failure pattern. <!--#285b07575c27a81d-->
- `CodexEventConverter` (class) — Stateful converter that turns codex `--json` JSONL events into Claude stream-json NDJSON lines, tracking agent messages, tool chips, touched files, and terminal turn metadata while never raising. <!--#bfcbbaf161834cff-->
  - `CodexEventConverter.__init__` (method) — Initializes the per-invocation conversion state — id-keyed agent messages, tool counter, touched files, tool_use/tool_result dedup sets, in-flight tool names, and provider/model metadata. <!--#b081ad7600c73285-->
  - `CodexEventConverter.touched_files` (method) — Property exposing the set of file paths collected from `file_change` items for dependency tracking. <!--#21dde3ceae6fa2d8-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._next_tool_id` (method) — Generates a unique synthetic tool-use id (`codex_tool_N`) when an event lacks its own call id. <!--#abc4b1e4bae8e685-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._resolve_item_id` (method) — Returns a stable id for a codex item, preferring `call_id` then `id` and otherwise memoizing a synthesized id on the item so one item never splits into two chips. <!--#e17e1236f02ba9b9-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._is_terminal_item` (method) — Reports whether an item has reached its final state, accepting either an `item.completed` event type or a terminal `status` value. <!--#9e57e36c343179e7-->
  - `CodexEventConverter.convert_line` (method) — Parses one codex JSONL line and dispatches it to the matching metadata/item/turn handler, returning zero or more NDJSON strings and swallowing malformed or unknown input. <!--#236966a1bc424727-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._merged_event` (method) — Flattens an event by shallow-merging its nested `data` object into a copy of the top level so handlers can read fields from either shape uniformly. <!--#ef86479a49fb5184-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._metadata_value` (method) — Looks up the first non-empty string value for any of the given keys, searching the event top level and its `thread`/`turn`/`session`/`message`/`response` sub-objects. <!--#92adc2ef8138a7d6-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._update_metadata` (method) — Extracts provider, model, and provider session id from an event, caches them on the converter, and returns only the fields that were explicitly present in this event. <!--#2bab883344d12e4e-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._handle_metadata_event` (method) — Handles `thread.started`/`turn.started` by refreshing cached metadata and emitting a `type: init` NDJSON line, or nothing when the event carries no metadata. <!--#b3b3cddb6c3bff0e-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._usage_payload` (method) — Pulls a token-usage dict from the event (or its `message`/`turn`/`response` sub-objects) and normalizes it via per-field alias mapping, deliberately preserving each provider shape's cache-token marker field so the downstream normalizer does not double-count cached input. <!--#de1a05fe6f179ceb-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._cost_payload` (method) — Searches the event and its `turn`/`message`/`response` sub-objects for any cost field (`actual_cost_usd`, `total_cost_usd`, `cost_usd`) and returns a (found, value) pair so a legitimate zero cost is distinguishable from absence. <!--#b7530e2035ed6dc8-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._apply_terminal_metadata` (method) — Stamps a terminal `result` event with provider, model, provider session id, a derived `usage_event_id`, and any passthrough usage/cost semantics, falling back to the converter's cached metadata when the event omits them. <!--#063f7cc14f948e7c-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._tool_use_line` (method) — Builds the JSON-serialized Claude `assistant` event carrying a single `tool_use` block for the given id, name, and input. <!--#13fd55759b5176de-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._tool_result_line` (method) — Builds the JSON-serialized Claude `user` event carrying a single `tool_result` block for the given tool_use id, content, and error flag. <!--#ec38c7d125a6fe78-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._emit_tool_events` (method) — Emits the tool_use/tool_result pair for one item deduped by id — tool_use on first sight, tool_result only once the item is terminal. <!--#2895e9a372fbceba-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._status_text` (method) — Returns an item's `status` lowercased and stripped, or an empty string when absent or non-string. <!--#4f32fa045aee4482-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._stringify` (method) — Renders an arbitrary item payload value as chip-displayable text, using `json.dumps` for structured values instead of Python `repr`. <!--#5c8cfa0a5f65896a-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._join_argv` (method) — Flattens a codex argv or `parsed_cmd` list, including nested command dicts, into a single space-joined command string. <!--#89274713075249c2-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._command_text` (method) — Extracts the command string of a `command_execution` item via a `command` → `parsed_cmd` fallback chain rather than a codex-version check. <!--#90e4548988926bba-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._command_output` (method) — Extracts a `command_execution` item's captured output, preferring the real `aggregated_output` field with `output` and the stdout/stderr pair as fallbacks. <!--#f70fd54f7d3acdbc-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._command_is_error` (method) — Reports whether a `command_execution` item failed, counting only a `failed` status or an explicit non-zero integer `exit_code`. <!--#ab0d139019c12d06-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._change_path` (method) — Returns a file-change entry's path from either the `path` or `file_path` key, or an empty string when neither is usable. <!--#08795631fb2f7945-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._map_change_kind` (method) — Maps a codex file-change `kind` to the closest Claude tool name — `Write` for adds, `Delete` for removals, `Edit` otherwise. <!--#7f152485506db32c-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._handle_file_changes` (method) — Emits one suffix-keyed tool_use/tool_result pair per entry of a `file_change` item's `changes` list and records each path as touched. <!--#32a7652b524fe6b2-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._handle_item_event` (method) — Dispatches `item.started`/`item.updated`/`item.completed` payloads by item type — agent_message, command_execution, file_change, and the remaining codex item kinds — into deduped Claude events. <!--#e34e99c1434ada5f-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._map_tool_name` (method) — Maps codex's generic tool/function names (shell, apply_patch, etc.) to the closest Claude tool names for display. <!--#24273fa0354b0a63-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._close_inflight_tools` (method) — Synthesizes an interrupted tool_result for every still-open tool_use so no chip renders as running forever after the turn ends. <!--#4705854dc0bb9ad5-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._reset_turn_state` (method) — Clears per-turn lifecycle state — accumulated agent messages, emission dedup sets, and in-flight tools — so a following turn starts clean. <!--#e0418c9614ae5d1e-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._result_text` (method) — Joins the accumulated agent messages with newlines in arrival order to form the terminal result text. <!--#c4595fc3896bec94-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._handle_turn_completed` (method) — Handles `turn.completed` by closing dangling chips and emitting a `type: result` event with joined agent text plus usage, cost, and terminal metadata. <!--#961e0e3e2bde9c09-->
  - `CodexEventConverter._handle_turn_failed` (method) — Handles `turn.failed`/`error` by closing dangling chips and emitting an error `type: result` event carrying the extracted error message plus usage, cost, and metadata. <!--#3496a4a60ee77cc8-->
  - `CodexEventConverter.finalize` (method) — Emits trailing events after the codex process exits, closing in-flight tools and synthesizing a `type: result` (or an error result when nothing was accumulated) if no turn terminal was seen. <!--#8db2eb519456be36-->
- `_spawn_stdin_writer` (function) — Launches a daemon thread that writes a prompt payload to the subprocess stdin and closes it, avoiding pipe-buffer deadlock. <!--#136c5b7ec66b9827-->
- `_spawn_stderr_reader` (function) — Launches a daemon thread that drains the subprocess stderr, optionally logging to a sidecar file and capturing the tail into a bounded buffer. <!--#af4e0e85a2eb715f-->
- `CodexRunner` (class) — An `AgentRunner` adapter for the OpenAI Codex CLI that builds and executes a single `codex exec --json` command (synchronously or with streaming monitoring), translating its JSONL events into Claude-compatible stream-json NDJSON via `CodexEventConverter` so upper layers work unchanged. <!--#e96a4bc6ff5667ff-->
  - `CodexRunner.__init__` (method) — Initializes the runner with a single command dict, defaulting to `{cmd: codex, priority: 0}`. <!--#c5b52427c53670a9-->
  - `CodexRunner.build_call_args` (method) — Translates intent-level parameters (prompt, read-only flag, context files) into the `codex exec --json` argv, choosing the sandbox mode, inlining context-file contents into the prompt, and switching to stdin (`-`) when the prompt exceeds `_MAX_ARG_BYTES`. <!--#a23dad7009490f79-->
  - `CodexRunner.run` (method) — Runs codex synchronously with captured output (stripping `CLAUDECODE` from the env, piping any deferred stdin prompt), converts every stdout line to Claude NDJSON, and returns a `CompletedProcess` — or returncode 124 on timeout. <!--#e6b3bb509a092943-->
  - `CodexRunner.run_with_monitor` (method) — Runs codex with activity-based monitoring, streaming converted NDJSON to buffer/log/callbacks and returning a MonitoredResult. <!--#a4ed41c0d1b0f6de-->
  - `CodexRunner._run_single_with_monitor` (method) — Streams one codex invocation under `Popen` with `select`-based line reading, converting events to NDJSON live for the log file and `on_output`/`on_activity` callbacks, while draining stderr into a bounded tail buffer and enforcing missing-command, wall-timeout, and psutil-backed inactivity/hang detection, returning a `_SingleRunResult`. <!--#4e6e3473328f849c-->
  - `CodexRunner.detect_infra_error` (method) — Classifies a codex run's exit code and output tail into an InfraErrorType (timeout, usage/auth limit, shell-snapshot startup failure, or none). <!--#d00ad55f4e702f64-->
- `MonitoredResult` (class) — Dataclass holding the outcome of `run_with_monitor` (return code, output, command, retry/interrupt flags, stderr tail) with a `success` property. <!--#6ac9ba61952cbdea-->
  - `MonitoredResult.success` (method) — Property returning True when the return code is zero. <!--#787b46b245897e2b-->
- `_SingleRunResult` (class) — Internal dataclass capturing the result of a single monitored command run (return code, output, success, retry/interrupt flags, stderr tail). <!--#25c02f14463c799c-->

### `src/tianluo/config.py` (python) — Central configuration layer for Tianluo: resolves the project config path across worktree/main-repo and canonical (`tianluo.yaml`) vs legacy (`se3.yaml`) tiers, loads and merges the project YAML, and exposes typed dataclass sections (version, docs, language, workflow, test/E2E, agents & LLM-caller chains, confirmation steps, pricing, investigation, code-index, etc.) with `load_*` helpers and step-list assembly utilities used throughout the codebase. <!--#90acb1e2e2931551|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/preset_loader.py` (python) — Loads and resolves SE3 'preset prompts' from a dual-layer registry — built-in markdown templates plus project-local overrides from tianluo/prompts and tianluo.yaml — exposing listing and name-to-(task_type, prompt, layer) resolution with explicit errors for unknown presets or missing prompt files. <!--#edc3213ae0afbeb7|d2564ec60747f605-->
- `PresetError` (class) — Base exception for any preset resolution failure (e.g. a declared prompt file that does not exist). <!--#6030b307aeecbc5f-->
- `PresetNotFoundError` (class) — Exception raised when a requested preset name is absent from the registry. <!--#58c5c0d2faa5b1d9-->
- `PresetEntry` (class) — Dataclass representing one resolved preset registry entry (name, task type, on-disk prompt file path, and source layer). <!--#02e2f636bc038da6-->
- `_scan_builtin_presets` (function) — Enumerates built-in presets by globbing the packaged templates/prompts directory and attaching declared metadata. <!--#8fc5ae2abd3383b6-->
- `_load_project_presets` (function) — Enumerates a project's local presets by scanning `<project_root>/tianluo/prompts/*.md` for zero-config presets (file stem as name) and then overlaying metadata (type, prompt_file redirects) from the `presets:` section of `tianluo.yaml`, returning the merged list of `PresetEntry` objects at the project layer. <!--#be010ccce5b8a46e-->
- `load_registry` (function) — Builds the merged name→PresetEntry registry, loading built-ins first then letting project presets override same-named entries. <!--#6fface6d1a6916f9-->
- `list_presets` (function) — Returns all available presets (built-in plus project) sorted by name. <!--#1039d20edae71e6c-->
- `resolve` (function) — Resolves a preset name to its (task_type, prompt_text, layer) tuple, raising explicitly on unknown names or missing prompt files. <!--#e9990726bc48d1f3-->

### `src/tianluo/pricing.py` (python) — Versioned model pricing catalog for LLM token cost estimation: defines the six mutually exclusive `TokenCategory` classes, `ModelPrice` entries with provenance, built-in Anthropic/OpenAI rate tables, model-name canonicalization (alias and dated-snapshot resolution), validated project `pricing.models` overrides, and `estimate_cost`, which returns an explicit unknown-cost `CostEstimate` rather than a misleading partial sum when any nonzero category lacks a price. <!--#2d087f9f2510aaab|0affa7f55e732859-->
- `TokenCategory` (class) — String enum naming the six mutually exclusive token classes (uncached input, output, cache read, and the three cache-creation variants) that a price entry can cover, deliberately mirroring `UsageRecord` fields so no token is billed twice. <!--#8fac63ccf642807f-->
- `ModelPrice` (class) — Dataclass holding one model's USD-per-million rate for each of the six token categories plus provenance (`catalog_version`, `source`, `effective_date`), with per-category lookup and dict round-tripping. <!--#83ca47c9da1b60e9-->
  - `ModelPrice.price_for` (method) — Returns the USD-per-million rate for a given `TokenCategory`, or `None` when that category has no known price. <!--#cd55c656bbeee527-->
  - `ModelPrice.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the price entry — all six category rates plus catalog version, source, and effective date — into a plain dict. <!--#dbb3beb336b01af1-->
  - `ModelPrice.from_dict` (method) — Classmethod rebuilding a `ModelPrice` from a mapping, defaulting missing metadata to the current catalog version and empty strings. <!--#9196c197932e4bad-->
- `CostEstimate` (class) — Result of a cost estimation: the USD total (`None` when not fully computable), which nonzero categories lacked prices, the per-category priced breakdown, and a human-readable reason. <!--#f011dd6218b696c5-->
  - `CostEstimate.is_estimated` (method) — Property reporting whether a usable cost figure was produced (i.e. `estimated_cost_usd` is not `None`). <!--#1df16f5a0301c525-->
- `estimate_cost` (function) — Computes USD cost from six-category token counts against a `ModelPrice`, returning an explicit "unknown" estimate rather than a misleading partial sum whenever any nonzero category lacks a price. <!--#effd1aa08c82e6bd-->
- `canonicalize_pricing_model` (function) — Normalizes a reported model name to its canonical price-table key, resolving aliases and stripping dated snapshot suffixes, and returning `None` for empty or unexpanded-variable names. <!--#e81e6cd29724e9e3-->
- `_anthropic` (function) — Helper building an Anthropic `ModelPrice` from base input/output rates, deriving cache read/write rates as the published fixed multiples (0.10x, 1.25x, 2.0x). <!--#efa53b0d194d1877-->
- `_openai` (function) — Helper building an OpenAI `ModelPrice` where cached input is a published subset rate and all cache-creation categories stay `None` because OpenAI does not report them. <!--#f03489dc85d49736-->
- `_builtin_entries` (function) — Constructs the versioned built-in price table of Anthropic and OpenAI models with per-entry source and effective date, deliberately omitting subscription-billed Codex models. <!--#f9f6b7649b73ef52-->
- `_validate_price_value` (function) — Validates a config-supplied price, returning `(number, None)` for non-negative finite numerics and an error string otherwise, explicitly rejecting booleans. <!--#fdff5b218cbed8f0-->
- `PricingOverrideError` (class) — `ValueError` subclass raised when a project's `pricing.models` override is structurally invalid. <!--#345b61c0da7127f0-->
- `PricingCatalog` (class) — Versioned model price table that resolves aliased model names to entries, merges validated project overrides, and serializes to/from dicts. <!--#784609b179245e6f-->
  - `PricingCatalog.builtin` (method) — Classmethod returning the built-in versioned price table with no project overrides applied. <!--#a44d62ce02314ee7-->
  - `PricingCatalog.get` (method) — Looks up a possibly-aliased model name's price entry, returning `None` for unknown or unexpandable names so callers report unknown cost instead of guessing. <!--#d5e3e4e975688607-->
  - `PricingCatalog.with_overrides` (method) — Validates `pricing.models` overrides and returns a new catalog with them merged in, raising `PricingOverrideError` on bad values and routing unknown model/category keys to a `warn` callback. <!--#c9b180da848f4fd2-->
  - `PricingCatalog.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the catalog to a dict of its version plus all entries sorted by model name. <!--#5ebbeffc530cf25b-->
  - `PricingCatalog.from_dict` (method) — Classmethod rebuilding a `PricingCatalog` from a mapping, skipping non-mapping entries and defaulting the version to the current catalog version. <!--#1592bedad5bcb3ee-->

### `src/tianluo/runtime_paths.py` (python) — Central helper module for resolving a project's runtime directory across the 12.x rename transition, providing layout-aware absolute (`runtime_dir`), relative (`runtime_relpath`), uploads (`uploads_dir`), and dual-name glob (`dual_runtime_glob`) path resolution that prefers the canonical `tianluo/` directory while still honouring a legacy `se3/` one. <!--#21a3ccacc860b558|dfecbb5b5f4d2ca7-->
- `runtime_dir_name` (function) — Resolves the runtime directory *name* under a project root, preferring canonical `tianluo/` but falling back to legacy `se3/` (with a one-time deprecation log per root) when only the latter exists. <!--#f02cd78b4c7375f7-->
- `runtime_dir` (function) — Returns the absolute runtime directory *path* under a project root by joining the root with the name chosen by `runtime_dir_name`. <!--#0e04119937caed64-->
- `uploads_dir` (function) — Returns the web-UI attachments directory for a project by appending `UPLOADS_DIR_NAME` to the layout-aware `runtime_dir(project_root)`, so projects still on the legacy `se3/` layout don't get a stray untracked top-level directory. <!--#c7cc3208ef0da8d9-->
- `runtime_relpath` (function) — Builds a *relative* runtime path (e.g. `tianluo/...` or `se3/...`) with the correct leading directory name for git-relative call sites that compare against `git status` output. <!--#27ff10db0fe29d54-->
- `dual_runtime_glob` (function) — Globs a `<prefix><runtime>/<tail>` pattern against both the canonical `tianluo/` and legacy `se3/` directory names (canonical first) so scans see runtime state regardless of layout during the 12.x transition. <!--#1e85c8605456fa75-->

### `src/tianluo/strategy_view.py` (python) — Read-only projection helpers that turn a flow's persisted State into JSON-safe display views — resolving hot/cold context and PLAN step bodies (with content-hash memoization) to report plan group counts, the plan-decomposition mode (including legacy/inferred strategy fallbacks for pre-model flows), and the `self_check_review` round-controller scope — so CLI, daemon, and WebUI describe strategies consistently. <!--#679670aaf2143ae2|cd496bb91583017f-->
- `has_choice_surface` (function) — Predicate telling whether a task type's step sequence ever offers a PLAN -> IMPLEMENT segment, mirroring the engine's unknown-type fallback so legacy flows are described consistently across CLI/daemon and engine projections. <!--#30216162a4851bf4-->
- `_optional_str` (function) — Small helper that normalizes a value to a stripped non-empty string or `None`. <!--#4d916768359f28c1-->
- `_optional_int` (function) — Coerces a value to an int or None, deliberately rejecting bool so a True never masquerades as a group count of 1. <!--#5cf05a4bb95b6a76-->
- `resolve_flow_context` (function) — Returns a flow's State.context, following a context_ref into the hot/cold layer's live or archived _context.json when the header only carries a reference, degrading to the inline value on unreadable files. <!--#5cd9fe5efd33babd-->
- `plan_group_count_from_state` (function) — Reports how many task groups the flow's PLAN step produced, reading the inline step outputs or following the externalized cold_ref, and returning None for "unknown" rather than guessing. <!--#b350c6464b90a483-->
- `_group_count_from_outputs` (function) — Counts groups in a PLAN step's outputs mapping, preferring the actual task_groups list over the recorded counter so plan revisions never show a stale count. <!--#8ddeb2386c9d2b15-->
- `_group_count_from_cold_ref` (function) — Loads a PLAN step's externalized body from the live or archived cold path to count its groups, memoizing results by content hash while refusing to cache transient read failures. <!--#03bd59756567eebd-->
- `plan_mode_view` (function) — Builds the JSON-safe display projection of a flow's PLAN decomposition mode, answering not_applicable for no-surface task types, echoing persisted decomposition/granularity when recorded, and otherwise describing pre-model flows via their legacy strategy (persisted or inferred from steps) with None for the new fields. <!--#ffc8794186ebfdad-->
- `_legacy_projection` (function) — Helper that assembles the uniform projection dict used for flows predating the plan-decomposition model, with null decomposition/granularity and inferred set to True. <!--#a3a1a6bc375ca513-->
- `scope_view` (function) — Projects the persisted `self_check_review` round-controller state (active/last round, last clean full round, completed full-round count) for display, returning `None` when no audit data is present. <!--#9c5ea3382fa76092-->

### `src/tianluo/usage.py` (python) — A stdlib-only, provider-neutral usage layer shared by the engine, runner adapters, history readers, and daemon: it defines the `UsageRecord`/`SessionCostSnapshot` data model plus `UsageStatus`/`UsageSemantics`/`CostSemantics` enums, resolves model identity from provider/config/runner sources, parses and deduplicates terminal NDJSON usage events via `UsageEventAggregator`, and aggregates token counts and actual-versus-estimated costs into a `UsageSummary` with completeness diagnostics. <!--#37e3a64eb81bad60|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/utils.py` (python) — Shared helper utilities for the SE3/tianluo CLI, covering exit-code mapping from validation results, file discovery/copying/mtime lookups, framework version and documentation-consistency checks, git staged-change detection for framework paths, verification-marker search by scenario ID, and status.md parsing. <!--#6f13fbe74f4281dc|6c3c2e79502b9117-->
- `get_exit_code` (function) — Maps a list of validation results to a CLI exit code (0 success, 1 errors, 2 runtime error). <!--#61082e083fb6cc05-->
- `discover_outputs` (function) — Lists all regular files directly inside a given directory. <!--#ec09c48061154c4d-->
- `get_file_mtime` (function) — Returns a file's modification timestamp, or None if it doesn't exist. <!--#730f41c0d4c2440a-->
- `copy_file` (function) — Copies a file to a destination, creating parent directories as needed. <!--#78cd0cb36fae02a0-->
- `get_source_mappings` (function) — Returns the (now-empty) mapping of source files to synced output files, since under the SE3 module system `output/` only holds `luo init` templates and runtime files are no longer synced. <!--#fc4ec9e2c7ab66ec-->
- `find_verification_markers` (function) — Searches Python files for pytest markers or comments verifying a given scenario ID. <!--#7dbaf5c1ee6b6e20-->
- `get_framework_version` (function) — Extracts the SE3 framework version string from pyproject.toml. <!--#1d5ec79da290223b-->
- `check_documentation_consistency` (function) — Validates that README.md and VERSIONS.md exist, cross-reference each other, and reflect the current framework version. <!--#5401b568afd9afa1-->
- `has_framework_file_changes` (function) — Checks git's staged files for changes to known framework source paths. <!--#dbfdb9481646fa39-->
- `parse_status_md` (function) — Parses status.md into structured fields (active change, current task, status, blockers). <!--#2c4ec321050f973f-->

## `src/tianluo/commands/` — The Typer CLI command layer for tianluo (`luo`), housing one module per user-facing subcommand — project scaffolding and format migration (`init_cmd.py`, `migrate_cmd.py`), the flow lifecycle drivers `run.py`, `end_session_cmd.py`, `salvage_cmd.py` and `worktree_cmd.py`, branch integration via `merge_cmd.py`/`merge_respond.py` atop the shared `merge/` infrastructure package, and the inspection/authoring surfaces `issue_cmd.py`, `history_cmd.py`, `code_index_cmd.py`, `review_scope_cmd.py` and `e2e_cmd.py` — each resolving the project root, delegating to the engine, and rendering localized Rich output with meaningful exit codes. <!--#af38e6ff8fa8d3ad|a9242d60f5b9a87c-->

### `src/tianluo/commands/__init__.py` (python) — Package initializer for the SE 3.0 CLI commands module, containing only a docstring and marking the directory as the namespace that holds the individual command implementations. <!--#7bf1513a2bce3e63|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/commands/code_index_cmd.py` (python) — Defines the Typer `luo code-index` command family that lets humans and the LLM navigate the project's structure map — the adaptive budgeted root view plus literal drill-in (`index`), single-file detail (`show`), regex/literal grep of item lines (`search`), incremental/full (re)build (`rebuild`), and on-disk health stats (`inspect`) — all reading render-only from the authoritative `tianluo/code-index.md` except `rebuild`, which writes it. <!--#282bce7c575f9863|2fda5866aca58b78-->
- `get_project_root` (function) — Walks up from the cwd to find the project root (a `.git` dir or SE3 config), rebinding the i18n language to that root before returning it. <!--#6bb957ad4b0017c5-->
- `_render_adaptive_map` (function) — Helper that renders the bare `luo code-index` adaptive root view — a byte-budgeted zoomable directory tree using primary roots and view budget from the `code_index` config — erroring out if the index isn't built. <!--#1ded18b12336ae4c-->
- `code_index_main` (function) — The `code-index` command group entry point that renders the adaptive root view when invoked with no subcommand, otherwise dispatching to subcommands (index/show/search/rebuild/inspect). <!--#7232f00ebe3b9a58-->
- `index_cmd` (function) — The `index [<path>]` subcommand that renders exactly one literal level at a path (a directory's immediate children or a file's full symbol tree) without auto-expansion. <!--#2ad072533dd75854-->
- `show_cmd` (function) — The `show <path>` subcommand that prints one file's full function/method/class detail (or a directory prefix's file one-liners) from the authoritative `tianluo/code-index.md`. <!--#83ea87fbcb84d5d2-->
- `search_cmd` (function) — The `search <pattern>` subcommand, a grep-compatible matcher over the rendered code-index item lines that supports `-i`/`-F`/`-m`/`-n` flags and follows grep's exit-code contract (0 on match, 1 on none). <!--#26e1a9bf0ec7bff4-->
- `_build_matcher` (function) — Compiles a search pattern into a per-line predicate — literal substring under `-F`, otherwise a regex — exiting 2 on an invalid regex. <!--#4894c9fafcd9565d-->
- `rebuild_cmd` (function) — The `rebuild` subcommand that (re)builds the code-index and writes `tianluo/code-index.md`, incrementally by default or re-summarising everything with `--force`, then reports file/symbol counts. <!--#c3f586e58a3bc963-->
- `inspect_cmd` (function) — The `inspect` subcommand that reads `tianluo/code-index.md` and prints summary health stats — file, symbol, and degraded counts plus a per-kind file breakdown. <!--#bc1c1d785b3abcc4-->

### `src/tianluo/commands/e2e_cmd.py` (python) — CLI command layer for the `luo e2e` subcommands — `run`, `list`, `doctor` and `bootstrap` — resolving the project root, loading the e2e content configuration, delegating to the e2e engine, and rendering localized console output with distinct exit codes for scenario, environment and config failures. <!--#226002bd882fa1a6|a08d0c340d15e231-->
- `_resolve_root` (function) — Resolves the effective project root for an e2e command — absolutizing an explicit `--project-root` (so it is valid as a container bind-mount host path) and binding the UI language to it, or delegating to `get_project_root()` when not given. <!--#dda9bc8cc5f8b87a-->
- `_note_if_disabled` (function) — Prints an informational notice when `e2e.enabled` is off, making the flow-side switch visible without blocking a manually invoked `luo e2e` command. <!--#24d92eb251e9bcec-->
- `_print_environment_error` (function) — Small helper that writes a container-runtime unavailability message plus its remediation hint to stderr. <!--#6af54f439c30fb72-->
- `run_command` (function) — The `luo e2e run` command: preflights the container runtime, loads the e2e content configuration, executes the selected scenarios via `run_e2e`, then prints notices, the pass/fail summary and artifacts path, exiting 0/1/3/4 for success, scenario failure, environment and config errors. <!--#d0c48a6705190f5b-->
- `_scenario_line` (function) — Renders one scenario's pass/fail outcome as a localized console line (deliberately not the fixed-English `summary_line()` used for logs and reports). <!--#fe6c1109f7ec9099-->
- `_print_artifacts` (function) — Prints the artifacts directory line when the run summary reports that artifacts were produced. <!--#8defeff69e5be74b-->
- `list_command` (function) — The `luo e2e list` command: loads and validates the content configuration and prints the declared services and scenarios, without touching any container runtime. <!--#64bb85dc9077a78f-->
- `doctor_command` (function) — The `luo e2e doctor` command: runs the same runtime probe as the E2E step's preflight against the configured (or, under `auto`, every supported) runtime and reports each one's state plus remediation, exiting 3 when none is usable. <!--#8c8bbfec7302eb13-->
- `bootstrap_command` (function) — The `luo e2e bootstrap` command: generates the project's `tianluo/e2e/` content configuration when absent, or incrementally evolves it from `--hint` values, reporting what changed and never rewriting `tianluo.yaml`. <!--#f66a2616dd72210f-->

### `src/tianluo/commands/end_session_cmd.py` (python) — Implements the `luo end-session` command: it resolves the main project root and target flow, discovers any worktree session, safely terminates the live `luo run` process tree (guarding on `run.pid` ownership/foreign-machine markers), then claims that marker and archives or cleans up the worktree/main-branch session state, history, and review baselines, re-verifying ownership before every irreversible step. <!--#6ba21632eeb7381a|13ef1fe9885cd8a0-->
- `end_session` (function) — Top-level `luo end-session` pipeline that resolves the main project root and flow id, finds any worktree session, terminates the live `luo run` process, claims the flow's ownership marker, and then archives/cleans up the session, reporting each step's OK/SKIP/FAIL outcome as the exit code. <!--#0734bd019ec08639-->
- `_find_project_root` (function) — Walks up from the current directory to locate the project root via a `.git` dir or an SE3 config file. <!--#3c8eb6032ea041a2-->
- `_resolve_main_root` (function) — Resolves the project root for end-session archival, auto-detecting it when unset, absolutizing relative `-p` inputs into the same canonical form `luo run` derives, and normalizing a `tianluo/worktrees/<name>` isolation path back to its owning main project so writes don't land in a worktree about to be deleted. <!--#826dc89c2514ccf0-->
- `_read_main_flow_id` (function) — Best-effort reads the `flow_id` field from a project's `tianluo/state/engine.json`, returning None on any read/parse failure. <!--#ada51fed283ece07-->
- `_find_worktree_session` (function) — Scans `<main>/tianluo/worktrees/*/tianluo/state/engine.json` for the worktree session matching a given `flow_id` (regardless of status) and returns its path/branch metadata, or None for a main-branch/already-cleaned session. <!--#2ced2336c94a8f8b-->
- `_proc_alive` (function) — Returns whether a pid names a live, non-zombie process (using psutil when available, else `os.kill(pid, 0)`). <!--#afc851908ba03f0c-->
- `_collect_descendants` (function) — Returns the given pids plus all their live recursive descendants (via psutil) so the whole process tree can be signalled before the parent is killed and its children orphaned. <!--#c26ba24e9c5c8587-->
- `_any_alive` (function) — Returns whether any pid in the given collection is currently alive. <!--#325a42539d7156fa-->
- `_terminate_one` (function) — Terminates a single pid and its entire descendant tree with SIGTERM → grace period → SIGKILL, returning ok=True only when every process is confirmed dead so the caller can gate the destructive archive path. <!--#b8e9069548a52eea-->
- `_read_run_pidfile` (function) — Reads the pid recorded in `<state_root>/tianluo/state/run.pid` (supporting both the machine-stamped and legacy bare-pid formats), returning `None` when the marker is missing or was written by another machine so a foreign pid is never mistaken for a local process. <!--#085f1146f02209cb-->
- `_run_marker_roots` (function) — Returns the candidate roots whose `run.pid` marker could belong to the session being ended — the worktree path (for `--worktree` runs) followed by the main project root — mirroring the pid discovery order. <!--#7bc8edfe748b364e-->
- `_clear_stale_local_run_pidfile` (function) — Best-effort removal of an abandoned `run.pid` marker, unlinking it only when the record belongs to this machine (or is legacy/unstamped) and its pid is no longer a live `luo run`, which is the operator recovery path that unblocks cross-machine resume. <!--#71ebfe5db150ef35-->
- `_claim_run_marker` (function) — Takes exclusive ownership of the flow's `run.pid` marker via the same `acquire_run_marker` (O_CREAT|O_EXCL) protocol a starting run uses, returning the marker path or `None` when another owner got there first. <!--#8499df6f72d81f66-->
- `_release_run_marker` (function) — Releases an ownership claim taken by `_claim_run_marker`, only unlinking the marker when it still names this process so a concurrent run's marker is never destroyed. <!--#db1e50b710fd97cf-->
- `_claim_still_held` (function) — Re-reads the `run.pid` marker to check that this command's ownership claim has not been overwritten, used as the liveness gate immediately before each irreversible step. <!--#2d0459c84e314ee2-->
- `_abandon_if_claim_lost` (function) — Guard helper that records a step as FAIL/ownership-lost and tells the caller to skip it when `_claim_still_held` reports the claim is gone. <!--#f19c8d04d39432f5-->
- `_claim_session_ownership` (function) — Chooses the single state dir the target flow actually writes (the worktree's for a `--worktree` session, otherwise the main root) and claims its run marker for the destructive phase, returning the marker and whether cleanup may proceed. <!--#c419f97c1e0bdc96-->
- `_pid_is_live_se3_run` (function) — Decides whether a pid recorded in `run.pid` is a genuinely live `luo run` (vs dead or recycled), biasing every inconclusive cmdline read toward "live" so a running flow is never signalled or destroyed. <!--#6cb17ffe1d2729c4-->
- `_proc_has_descendant_in_dir` (function) — Determines whether a process's tree is anchored inside a target worktree directory — by a descendant's cwd or any open file under it — to positively identify a `--worktree` flow's parent that never chdirs out of the main root. <!--#49b0e48a8a7426f6-->
- `_discover_pids_for_flow` (function) — Discovers the live `luo run` pids belonging to a `flow_id`, preferring the authoritative on-disk `run.pid` marker and falling back to a psutil scan matching by `--flow-id`, cwd + engine.json confirmation, or a worktree-anchored descendant. <!--#644cf7a9687c6e3a-->
- `_blocking_run_marker` (function) — Scans the worktree and main state dirs for a `run.pid` this host cannot judge dead — foreign-machine, unstamped, or undecodable — and returns it so termination is reported inconclusive rather than successful. <!--#3bae93ac05fe249d-->
- `_terminate_session_process` (function) — Terminates the session's live `luo run` process(es) — by supplied pid or by flow-id discovery, SIGTERM then SIGKILL — after first refusing outright on any blocking foreign/unreadable run marker, returning `(ok, summary)`. <!--#0c0e4882ab54f8e5-->
- `_archive_worktree_session` (function) — Archives a worktree session by reusing the merge-cleanup machinery — copying the worktree (excluding review baselines and this command's own claim), promoting its terminal engine state, syncing history, then reclaiming baselines and deleting the worktree/branch — with each sub-step fault-tolerant and re-checking ownership before every irreversible action. <!--#8b0ce499e30a6e0d-->
- `_archive_main_session` (function) — Archives a main-branch session by clearing engine state only when the live `engine.json` is positively confirmed to belong to the requested flow, then retiring its resumable snapshot and review baselines, re-reading the ownership claim before each destructive step. <!--#3784547dbdc99937-->
- `_infer_worktree_branch` (function) — Infers the branch checked out at a worktree path by parsing `git worktree list --porcelain`, used when engine.json did not record a worktree_branch. <!--#c0d9e792ab67fa0a-->
- `_sync_worktree_history` (function) — Copies the worktree's per-flow history files into the main project's history directory append-only — writing `<name>.from-<branch>[-N]` sidecars on collision and skipping byte-identical targets — returning the number of files copied. <!--#7bcf8c326ae8d04a-->
- `_same_file` (function) — Fault-tolerantly returns whether two files have byte-identical content via filecmp. <!--#43129f0a76c9cfd1-->
- `_resolve_history_target` (function) — Resolves where to copy a history file without overwriting, returning the primary path, a uniquified `.from-<branch>` sidecar, or None if an identical copy already exists. <!--#cd2db7cff1fe7516-->
- `_clear_resumable` (function) — Retires a flow's resumable snapshot under the given root and, only if that clear is confirmed, the terminal disposition landed, and the ownership claim still holds, also discards its review baselines. <!--#877b956721e1328b-->
- `_display_results` (function) — Renders the collected (step, status, detail) rows as a styled Rich table with localized headings and OK/SKIP/FAIL status styling. <!--#3d2b950c6b36e0a5-->

### `src/tianluo/commands/history_cmd.py` (python) — Implements the `luo history` CLI command group — listing, showing, restoring and inspecting archived flows — by resolving flow records across the three data sources (active engine.json, on-disk archives, history-only chat sessions) and rendering them as Rich tables or JSON with localized plan-mode, review-scope and token-usage/cost projections that mirror the WebUI and daemon surfaces. <!--#a0ae60bd1f6e68e4|3a5b0213feec891b-->
- `get_project_root` (function) — Walks up from the cwd to find the enclosing project root (a `.git` dir or SE3 config) and rebinds the i18n language to that root before returning it. <!--#7f65c0c23bdaba9f-->
- `format_datetime` (function) — Converts an ISO datetime string into a human-readable `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM` format, falling back to the raw string on error. <!--#0f5d25170fb3009a-->
- `format_duration` (function) — Computes and formats the elapsed duration between two ISO timestamps as minutes/hours/days. <!--#212868504b98e854-->
- `list_all_flows` (function) — Returns all flows from every data source via the PersistenceManager. <!--#6ed7050a4e181cb1-->
- `list_archived_flows_from_disk` (function) — Scans the runtime state/archive directory for engine_*.json snapshots and returns a listing of archived flows, parsing each archive's timestamp from its filename (tolerating collision suffixes, falling back to mtime) and reading only the identity header of giant legacy snapshots. <!--#fd99a9ce5a152d64-->
- `_plan_decomposition_label` (function) — Maps a raw decomposition doctrine value (`capability`/`granular`) to its localized `history.plan.decomposition.*` label, falling back to the raw text or an "unknown" label. <!--#e33649a844ce5208-->
- `_plan_granularity_label` (function) — Maps a raw granularity tier (`auto`/`single`/`conservative`) to its localized `history.plan.granularity.*` label, mirroring the WebUI wording. <!--#e948ced133180e1f-->
- `_legacy_strategy_label` (function) — Localizes a retired implementation-strategy value (`direct`/`planned`/`not_applicable`) recorded by flows created before the decomposition model. <!--#a8e2cfc713672081-->
- `_scope_mode_label` (function) — Localizes a persisted SELF_CHECK `scope_mode` value (`full` / `incremental`) into a WebUI-parity display label via `history.scope.mode.*`, falling back to the raw text or `-`. <!--#7cee3b2ca7dc48ed-->
- `_plan_group_count` (function) — Scans a flow's step details for the PLAN step and returns how many task groups it emitted, preferring the live `task_groups` list over the recorded counter and returning `None` when PLAN never ran. <!--#a441f27452248168-->
- `_plan_mode_display_value` (function) — Renders the plan-mode table row — doctrine/granularity (plus group count) for current flows, or the recorded legacy strategy with provenance notes for pre-migration flows — returning "" when nothing is recoverable. <!--#aa67ef98885d1b67-->
- `_plan_mode_reason_text` (function) — Produces the plan-mode reason row, translating projection-authored `reason_key` values through the CLI catalog while showing a persisted flow-recorded reason verbatim. <!--#181509ac60756654-->
- `_pricing_catalog` (function) — Loads the project's effective pricing catalog for cost estimation, degrading to the built-in price table when `tianluo.yaml` is missing or invalid instead of blocking history display. <!--#90d2a1b561b6ef6b-->
- `_state_usage_payload` (function) — Builds the token-usage/cost payload for a state-backed (active or archived) flow from authoritative session and per-step `UsageRecord`s, falling back to an adapted legacy five-field tally only when `legacy_usage_ledger` marks it as the flow's sole usage fact. <!--#93c988b6c030f0c6-->
- `_detail_from_flow` (function) — Builds the full detail dict for a live `FlowInstance`, flattening step history, progress and chat-session counts, and attaching the shared plan-mode / review-scope / usage projections so CLI output matches the daemon and server surfaces. <!--#8115addac5131cc2-->
- `_load_archived_flow` (function) — Loads a FlowInstance from archive files matching a flow_id by delegating to PersistenceManager's split-aware, size-guarded archive loader, returning None when a legacy archive can only be read in degraded form. <!--#9ca69887edfc101e-->
- `_detail_from_history` (function) — Builds a reduced detail dict for a flow that survives only as archived history, reconstructing timestamps, task summary, self_check pass numbering and usage totals from the chat sessions on disk (plan mode and review scope are unavailable). <!--#256d68bd4f46de4a-->
- `get_flow_detail` (function) — Returns detailed information for a given flow_id by searching three data sources in order — active engine.json, archived snapshots, then history-only records. <!--#4619d2c2ffc7a79a-->
- `_status_color` (function) — Maps a flow status string to a Rich display color. <!--#d24adeb7ceeee4ff-->
- `_step_status_color` (function) — Maps a step status string to a Rich display color. <!--#8bb2cea2c4630c05-->
- `_render_flows_table` (function) — Prints a list of flow dicts as a colour-coded Rich table (id, status, truncated description, progress, updated time, source) plus a hint line. <!--#a4ac2cfcb1d583d9-->
- `default_cmd` (function) — The `luo history` callback that, when no subcommand is given, lists all flows with optional `--active-only`/`--archived-only` filtering and JSON or table output. <!--#83b1fb3853154c77-->
- `list_cmd` (function) — The explicit `history list` subcommand: same as the default callback, listing all/active/archived flows as JSON or a Rich table. <!--#8e030e18e2d18738-->
- `show_cmd` (function) — Typer command that resolves a flow id (including unique prefix matches) and prints its detail as JSON or as Rich tables covering status, task, progress, timestamps, PLAN decomposition mode, SELF_CHECK scope audit, and per-step status/retries/errors. <!--#d3f0e4886e659bd0-->
- `_show_plan_artifacts` (function) — Renders a compact, non-authoritative table of legacy PLAN/adjudication artifacts (PLAN `task_groups`, `adjudicated_plan`, `plan_task`-sourced findings) found in step outputs so they stay inspectable in their historical section. <!--#20ec2c536e538d8b-->
- `_show_detailed_sessions` (function) — Loads a flow's chat history, interleaves the sessions for display, and prints each one's rendered LLM call detail under a rule header. <!--#1e705327054f02e8-->
- `_show_detailed_json` (function) — Outputs a flow's detail plus full chat history as JSON. <!--#3757b11347d645fd-->
- `restore_cmd` (function) — The `luo history restore` CLI command that validates a flow_id across all sources (with prefix-match resolution) and resumes it by delegating to `luo run --resume --flow-id`, supporting a `--dry-run` preview. <!--#2cd2ffafb03b017a-->
- `archived_cmd` (function) — The `history archived` subcommand that lists only on-disk archived flows as JSON or a Rich table with status colouring and archive timestamps. <!--#7f63e5d869ada8f7-->

### `src/tianluo/commands/init_cmd.py` (python) — Implements the `luo init` command — scaffolding a new project's runtime directory, `tianluo.yaml`, `tianluo/charter.md`, and `VERSIONS.md` from templates, initializing git when needed, and idempotently ensuring the required `.gitignore` rules (with glob-aware coverage checks and negation detection) — split into a testable `run_init` core and a Typer entry point that reports i18n-translated status. <!--#0201b03a08d291e4|7fe7d35ce0ac71a9-->
- `_render_template` (function) — Loads a named template file from TEMPLATES_DIR and substitutes `{key}` placeholders via literal string replacement (not str.format) to avoid choking on incidental braces. <!--#760a3c5ebb7fdbb8-->
- `is_git_repository` (function) — Returns True if the given path lies inside an existing git repository by walking up parents looking for a .git directory. <!--#0d770de078464a79-->
- `init_repository` (function) — Runs `git init` in the given directory and returns a (success, message) tuple, handling git-not-installed and command-failure cases. <!--#6268849a7cbf7dd5-->
- `_EnsuredPattern` (class) — A NamedTuple describing one gitignore rule `luo init` guarantees, pairing the pattern with the target path to probe, a sibling `broad_probe` path used to distinguish narrow from wide negations, and the explanatory comment written above it. <!--#db8bcd5e902c155b-->
- `_ensured_patterns` (function) — Returns the tuple of `_EnsuredPattern` rules an existing `.gitignore` must carry — the local config override file and the uploads directory, spelled with the project's actual runtime directory name so legacy `se3/` projects are covered correctly. <!--#e788b654a5c1987d-->
- `GitignoreResult` (class) — A NamedTuple carrying the outcome of `create_gitignore` as `(status, message, patterns)`, where `patterns` names only the rules the status is actually about so the CLI can report precisely what happened. <!--#7639238ee848a799-->
- `_normalize_gitignore_pattern` (function) — Strips gitignore's anchor (`/`), recursive-glob (`**/`), and directory (`/` suffix) markers from a pattern line so it can be matched against a filename with `fnmatch`. <!--#619f00ba9b238d8e-->
- `_gitignore_covers` (function) — Returns True when the given `.gitignore` content already ignores a target path, matching literal lines, globs, and slash-free patterns at any depth (skipping negations) so init does not append redundant rules. <!--#5255b26807ad7ca0-->
- `_gitignore_narrowly_negates` (function) — Returns True when `.gitignore` contains a `!` negation that specifically un-ignores the target path but not the broader sibling probe, distinguishing a deliberate user opt-out from an incidentally-matching wide rule. <!--#a8c0ee778e506bfd-->
- `create_gitignore` (function) — Ensures `.gitignore` carries every ensured rule, returning one of five statuses — `created`, `appended`, `negated`, `unchanged`, or `error` — and refusing to write anything when an explicit negation would fight the append. <!--#5e47cdc0ff4855f5-->
- `_get_charter_template` (function) — Builds the initial `tianluo/charter.md` content for `luo init` by delegating to `charter.render_charter_template` with Chinese fill-in placeholder prompts plus the seeded parallel-safe-tests and workflow conventions, so a fresh project starts with a committable charter. <!--#3c24c9db7923b0b3-->
- `_get_versions_md_template` (function) — Renders the initial `VERSIONS.md` from the `versions_md.md` template, filling in the project name and current date to seed the changelog with a `0.1.0` entry. <!--#c4446f4e85d0ca2e-->
- `run_init` (function) — The testable core of `luo init`: creates the runtime directory, `tianluo.yaml`, `tianluo/charter.md`, and `VERSIONS.md`, initializes git if needed, ensures `.gitignore`, and returns a dict of created/skipped paths plus git, gitignore, and local-override status flags. <!--#7db04a1fd340e5d6-->
- `init_cmd` (function) — The Typer CLI entry point for `luo init` that resolves the project root and name, calls `run_init`, and echoes i18n-translated status lines for created files, git, `.gitignore` outcome, local-override shadowing, and next steps. <!--#76ed5af04836c52f-->

### `src/tianluo/commands/issue_cmd.py` (python) — Defines the Typer CLI command group for issue management (list, show, create, edit, close, reset), backed by IssueManager, with helpers for project-root resolution, Rich color/datetime formatting, external-editor YAML round-tripping, and description resolution from args/stdin/prompt. <!--#c51826181a267914|491264dd703bea1f-->
- `get_project_root` (function) — Walks up from the cwd to find the project root (a `.git` dir or SE3 config) and rebinds the i18n language to that root before returning it. <!--#7f65c0c23bdaba9f-->
- `_status_color` (function) — Maps an IssueStatus enum value to a Rich color string for table/detail rendering. <!--#440d3dc2ee8afeb2-->
- `_priority_color` (function) — Maps a priority string (critical/high/medium/low) to a Rich color for display. <!--#decc56c974d7023c-->
- `_type_color` (function) — Maps an issue type string (bug/feature/etc.) to a Rich color for display. <!--#bd6f4aa758834f96-->
- `_format_datetime` (function) — Formats a datetime as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`, falling back to its string form on error. <!--#622e5ed38538305d-->
