- `_get_editor` (function) — Resolves the editor command from $EDITOR, defaulting to `vi` when unset or malformed. <!--#6da17e089dc60c09-->
- `EditorError` (class) — Exception raised when the external editor binary cannot be found or launched. <!--#5e3c13fe86988091-->
- `_open_editor_with_content` (function) — Writes the given text to a temp YAML file, opens it in the user's `$EDITOR`, and returns the edited content (None if the editor exits non-zero, raising `EditorError` if it can't be launched). <!--#98c16e9f3627f5b0-->
- `_issue_to_editor_yaml` (function) — Renders an existing Issue as a human-editable YAML template containing only editable fields plus a read-only id. <!--#b0abf28b8150969b-->
- `_new_issue_editor_yaml` (function) — Generates a blank YAML template for creating a new issue via the external editor. <!--#f32e849fd690fa51-->
- `_parse_edited_issue_yaml` (function) — Parses editor-returned YAML into a dict, raising `ValueError` if it is malformed, empty, or missing a non-blank description. <!--#b0bc2963e0175f06-->
- `default_cmd` (function) — Default callback that lists open issues when no subcommand is invoked. <!--#78df7f33146891ba-->
- `list_cmd` (function) — The `issue list` command: validates the `--source` filter, queries `IssueManager`, and renders matching issues as a colour-coded Rich table. <!--#069c51df462c5f38-->
- `show_cmd` (function) — The `issue show` command: loads one issue by id and prints its full details in a colour-coded block, exiting 1 if not found. <!--#fa4bc9120a3d8a64-->
- `create_cmd` (function) — Typer command implementing `luo issue create`, which builds a new issue via IssueManager from one of four input modes (positional arg, piped stdin, interactive prompt, or an $EDITOR YAML template) and echoes the created issue's id and title. <!--#c59f3554e49b8664-->
- `_resolve_description` (function) — Resolves an issue description from (in priority order) the positional argument, piped stdin, or an interactive multiline prompt, returning None on cancellation and raising `ValueError` when empty. <!--#b14899d61ce9b0e5-->
- `edit_cmd` (function) — The `issue edit` command: round-trips an existing issue through `$EDITOR` as YAML and applies every editable field back via `update_fields`, treating removed keys as cleared. <!--#84fcb082db8fcf51-->
- `close_cmd` (function) — The `issue close` command: closes an issue by id with an optional `--reason`, exiting 1 on error. <!--#4befdf6b1706c9ed-->
- `reset_cmd` (function) — The `issue reset` command: moves an in-progress issue back to open status, exiting 1 on error. <!--#d55b458abfe4d14a-->

### `src/tianluo/commands/merge_cmd.py` (python) — CLI entry point for `luo merge`: validates branch names and working-tree/branch preconditions, then drives the locked integrate() -> reconcile() sequence with git helpers, stash-based fast-strategy recovery, source-issue backfill, deferred branch cleanup, and localized summary/failure reporting. <!--#904a8c12caa3fb09|60d104de6e62cda6-->
- `_run_git` (function) — Thin wrapper that runs a git subcommand in a given project root via subprocess, capturing output with configurable check/timeout. <!--#8bdb8c6f53ca2c0b-->
- `_resolve_git_dir` (function) — Resolves the real git directory (handling linked worktrees where .git is a pointer file) via `git rev-parse --git-dir`, returning None if unavailable. <!--#39d970125e3b9d76-->
- `_is_working_tree_clean` (function) — Returns whether the working tree has no uncommitted tracked changes and no in-progress git operation, ignoring untracked files. <!--#0b796ef88d8b0242-->
- `_git_operation_in_progress` (function) — Detects whether git is mid-merge/cherry-pick/revert/rebase by checking for the corresponding marker files in the git directory. <!--#bfe6f2d49513bda6-->
- `_branch_exists` (function) — Checks whether a local branch exists via `git show-ref`, failing closed (False) on any infrastructure error so indeterminate refs are refused. <!--#e9891f12d3b59534-->
- `validate_branch_names` (function) — Validates user-supplied branch names before any git command runs, rejecting empty/leading-dash/shell-metachar/git-ref-invalid names and raising a ValueError that lists each rejected name and the rule it broke. <!--#f281be8158f162ea-->
- `_append_runtime_sync_lines` (function) — Renders all runtime-sync signals (skipped branches/files, idempotent bypasses, discarded tier-B, tier-A collisions) plus committed issue renumbers and ambiguous issue references into the merge summary lines, on both success and failure paths. <!--#d17adf52b3eb8264-->
- `_append_human_call_lines` (function) — Renders the operator-facing recovery text for a failed merge branch, printing the real tianluo/calls/ file path in normal mode or the recorded escalation payload plus rerun instructions in suppress/library mode. <!--#99415f90c88db2ab-->
- `_split_merged_buckets` (function) — Splits a merge report's branches into `(newly_merged, already_ancestor)` buckets for CLI rendering, folding `merged_with_warnings` into the newly-merged side and falling back to `git merge-base --is-ancestor` classification when the report only carries the legacy `merged_branches` aggregate. <!--#4489181052066917-->
- `_append_split_branch_lines` (function) — Appends the per-bucket listings of newly-merged versus already-ancestor branches to the summary lines. <!--#b2b30c538c4b00fc-->
- `_has_user_uncommitted_changes` (function) — Returns whether the user's working tree has genuine tracked/untracked WIP (ignoring SE3/tianluo runtime state and cache paths) so the fast strategy can decide if a pre-merge stash is needed. <!--#aa8d90a39c039725-->
- `_fast_stash_dirty` (function) — Stashes a dirty working tree under a labeled se3-pre-fast-merge stash before a fast-strategy merge, returning the stash label or None (best-effort; failures only warn). <!--#57aa3f6ed62d0ec4-->
- `_fast_stash_pop` (function) — Pops the fast strategy's labeled pre-merge stash through the shared no-data-loss resolver, archiving conflicts and filing an audit issue, returning True when recovery did not finalize so the caller must not report clean success. <!--#4dccabf6f5f5f83e-->
- `_map_branches_to_source_issues` (function) — Captures a {branch: source_issue_id} mapping (via a lazy run.py worktree scanner) before the merge runs, so the link survives after --delete-merged removes each worktree's engine.json; best-effort, never raises. <!--#e2e3917a9c4cece0-->
- `_backfill_resolved_source_issues` (function) — The single idempotent choke point that transitions IN_PROGRESS source issues of successfully-merged (or already-ancestor) branches to RESOLVED, swallowing all IssueManager errors so it never affects the merge exit code. <!--#323a8404fc815909-->
- `_acquire_merge_lock_with_callbacks` (function) — Acquires the merge lock (legacy blocking acquire when no callbacks), and when on_lock_wait is given, probes non-blocking first to fire wait/acquired callbacks only when queuing behind a live holder. <!--#c333700a77818d2a-->
- `_run_deferred_branch_cleanup` (function) — Deletes the merged source branches only after reconcile has settled (keeping whole-command rerun recoverable), mirroring the orchestrator's partial-failure handling by recording aborting exceptions in the report instead of raising. <!--#b506996b6c4740ca-->
- `_lock_busy_message` (function) — Formats the user-facing "merge lock is busy" error for a MergeLockBusy exception, choosing a remote-machine variant that names the holding machine when the lock holder is not on this machine so the operator can act (e.g. `luo merge-unlock --force`). <!--#5a4461fbd939b230-->
- `run_merge` (function) — Entry point for the `luo merge` command that validates branch names and working-tree/git state, then drives the `integrate() -> reconcile()` sequence under the main-worktree merge lock (with optional lock-wait callbacks and `suppress_human_call` library mode) and returns a process exit code. <!--#7c6df814273d0663-->
- `_failure_title_and_summary` (function) — Maps a merge `failure_reason` code (including prefixed compound reasons like `fast_abort: <stderr>`) to a localized `(title, first_line)` pair for the failure report, degrading to a generic message for unrecognised reasons. <!--#59e8056fcdd79fcb-->

### `src/tianluo/commands/merge_respond.py` (python) — Implements the `luo merge-respond` command, which processes a human's response file for a merge-conflict MCP call under a project-wide MergeLock and dispatches accept (write/stage resolved files, commit, then verify the merge completed and the version was bumped), abort, or manual outcomes. <!--#dc048f6b7ba1289e|99a070f86ef36d6c-->
- `_first_parent_sha` (function) — Returns the first-parent SHA of HEAD via `git rev-list --parents`, treating octopus merges like 2-parent merges and raising RuntimeError on git failure or a parentless root commit. <!--#b8325d34356dfe2f-->
- `_extract_version_from_string` (function) — Parses a version string out of TOML (`pyproject.toml`) or JSON (`package.json`) content, returning None (and warning on TOML parse failure) when no version can be extracted. <!--#0322f245c4574684-->
- `_check_version_unchanged` (function) — Compares the version in pyproject.toml / package.json between a pre-merge SHA and HEAD, returning a localized error message when the version did not advance or became unparseable after the merge, and None otherwise. <!--#b4cb6f21eae334d9-->
- `process_merge_response` (function) — Entry point for `luo merge-respond`: validates the merge call file, resolves the project-wide merge lock root, and runs the response handling under a blocking MergeLock so it cannot race other merge-completing paths. <!--#e5d43f62e28c9c69-->
- `_process_merge_response_locked` (function) — Under the merge lock, parses the call/.response JSON pair and dispatches the user's choice — accept (reject strict-mode placeholders, write/stage/remove resolved files, commit, then assert merge and version-bump postconditions), abort (`git merge --abort`, or a no-op acknowledgement for already-rolled-back call types), or manual (acknowledge only). <!--#c8acb5b0e303bad3-->

### `src/tianluo/commands/migrate_cmd.py` (python) — Implements the `luo migrate` command as a registry-based (`MIGRATORS`) channel for one-shot, fault-tolerant, git-revertable format migrations, whose shipped migrators salvage why/intent from the retired `tianluo/specs/` corpus into the code-index + charter + WHY-comment triad (`spec-to-new-system`) and perform the se3/-to-tianluo/ layout rename, with helpers for registration, gitignore rewriting, report accumulation, and Rich CLI display. <!--#8895f9c9299ddcc0|e19c4ce9c86889c7-->
- `ColocatedWhy` (class) — Dataclass pairing a project-relative source file path with a prose why/intent fragment to be inserted into that file as a comment. <!--#cfd51d5498faf0ca-->
- `SalvageInput` (class) — Dataclass bundling everything the salvager needs (project root, base spec text, non-base spec corpus, admission standard, charter template, project name) so the salvager does no discovery of its own. <!--#a03d93eb1581a162-->
- `SalvageResult` (class) — Dataclass holding the migration salvage product: the full assembled charter.md body, a list of code-bound why/intent colocations to insert as comments, and advisory notes for the human reviewer. <!--#aff27a6b97970151-->
- `Migrator` (class) — A dataclass describing one registered migration: its id, an i18n key for its human-readable description, and the callable that runs it and returns a MigrationReport. <!--#0de3df9b26a5406a-->
- `register_migrator` (function) — Registers a migrator under its unique id in the MIGRATORS registry, raising on duplicate ids. <!--#29ecb08e2108fe0e-->
- `get_migrator` (function) — Looks up and returns a registered migrator by id, or None if not found. <!--#f654e0789ae24328-->
- `list_migrators` (function) — Returns all registered migrators sorted by id. <!--#f112e419974b0265-->
- `StepOutcome` (class) — Dataclass recording one pipeline step's name, status (OK/SKIP/FAIL), and detail string. <!--#b595caa244d380a1-->
- `MigrationReport` (class) — Dataclass accumulating per-step outcomes and notes, exposing overall success (`ok`) and a process `exit_code`. <!--#624b9b55c9e82f75-->
  - `MigrationReport.add` (method) — Appends a StepOutcome with the given name, status, and detail to the report. <!--#5b0f45dfab323d34-->
  - `MigrationReport.ok` (method) — Property that is True only when no recorded step has FAIL status. <!--#c434422828d4983f-->
  - `MigrationReport.exit_code` (method) — Property returning process exit code 0 on success, 1 on any failure. <!--#4299b082776eeaeb-->
- `_load_spec_corpus` (function) — Tolerantly loads the spec corpus from a specs directory, returning the base spec text and a {name: text} map of non-base specs while skipping unreadable, hidden, and underscore-prefixed entries. <!--#1727d96aa1f76583-->
- `_project_name_from_base` (function) — Best-effort extraction of the project name from the base spec's title line, with a fallback. <!--#4208a2781e9fec9b-->
- `_make_llm_salvager` (function) — Builds the default LLM-backed `SpecSalvager` closure that runs two defensive passes over the old spec corpus — assembling the full `tianluo/charter.md` body from the base spec plus a digest of the other specs, then extracting per-file code-bound why/intent as `ColocatedWhy` entries — degrading to fallbacks rather than aborting when any LLM call fails. <!--#87a439f29c13651c-->
- `_strip_code_fence` (function) — Strips a single wrapping triple-backtick code fence from a text body if present. <!--#620f4e9b5e0d1c5d-->
- `_fallback_charter` (function) — Produces the degraded, lossless charter used when LLM assembly fails: the rendered charter template (still carrying the parallel-safe tests convention) followed by a loud review banner and the pre-migration base spec verbatim. <!--#6173b19feca9420d-->
- `_comment_prefix` (function) — Returns the line-comment prefix for a file based on its extension, defaulting to `#`. <!--#edaf021548cf685e-->
- `_render_why_comment` (function) — Renders a why/intent fragment into a list of commented lines prefixed by the WHY marker. <!--#4017fdd2f97275ce-->
- `_insert_why_comment` (function) — Inserts a rendered why-comment block at a safe top-of-file location, preserving any leading shebang. <!--#0385c973b5aaea6c-->
- `_apply_colocations` (function) — Writes each salvaged why-comment into its target source file, returning how many were applied plus reasons for any skipped (missing or unreadable) targets instead of aborting. <!--#35856e640a3e605f-->
- `_write_charter_once` (function) — Writes the fully-assembled charter body to tianluo/charter.md in a single atomic write with no overwrite window. <!--#5542c0bfe1b1099e-->
- `_gitignore_whitelists` (function) — Returns the list of .gitignore whitelist patterns (code-index.md, charter.md, version-intents/) that must stay tracked under the runtime directory after migration. <!--#44ddcf1da08a7789-->
- `_gitignore_remove` (function) — Returns the retired specs-directory whitelist pattern that the .gitignore rewrite should remove. <!--#8cac610ef8a32d8f-->
- `_tracked_toplevel_whitelists` (function) — Helper that runs `git ls-files` to enumerate all tracked top-level paths and returns `!/<name>` whitelist lines (dirs with trailing slash, .gitignore first), or None if git is unavailable so callers won't add a root default-deny without existence protection. <!--#a1fd1234efe43966-->
- `_rewrite_gitignore` (function) — Idempotently rewrites .gitignore to add the code-index/charter whitelists, drop the specs whitelist, and introduce a root default-deny (/*) form with existence-protected top-level whitelists, returning a human-readable list of the changes made. <!--#f6e9baeae86ab8aa-->
- `run_spec_to_new_system` (function) — Orchestrates the one-shot, uncommitted spec-to-new-system migration as an ordered tolerant pipeline (assemble+write charter, colocate why-comments, build code-index, delete specs only after salvage is confirmed, rewrite .gitignore), returning a MigrationReport. <!--#3ec85e9fd19b5be3-->
- `_rename_git` (function) — Thin helper that runs a git subcommand in the project root via subprocess and returns the CompletedProcess. <!--#45a4354ae8230388-->
- `_rewrite_gitignore_names` (function) — Performs a pure textual line-mapping rewrite of se3-name rules in .gitignore to their tianluo equivalents, returning whether the file changed. <!--#b47fda2dda707fdd-->
- `run_rename_to_tianluo` (function) — Executes the one-shot se3/-to-tianluo/ layout rename for an existing project (git mv of the runtime dir and config files, .gitignore rule rewrite) landing it as one reviewable/revertable commit, with every step tolerant, re-runnable, and skipping the commit when the index already held foreign staged changes. <!--#bf437efb76a3dc85-->
- `_display_report` (function) — Renders a MigrationReport as a Rich table of step/status/detail rows plus any accumulated notes. <!--#1d18b5d52d53ae61-->
- `list_command` (function) — CLI subcommand that prints a table of the registered migrations (id and description), or a message when none exist. <!--#7d771de463846e0a-->
- `run_command` (function) — CLI subcommand that resolves the project root (binding the UI language), looks up the named migrator, runs it with the --no-delete-specs flag, displays the report, and exits with the report's status code. <!--#8d1c2bf9d7e0fd75-->

### `src/tianluo/commands/review_scope_cmd.py` (python) — Implements the `review-scope diff` CLI command, resolving a flow and its baseline (with distinct exit codes for not-found, cleaned, missing, and undecidable states) and printing the baseline-to-workspace diff either filtered by `--path` or as a `--stat` summary. <!--#9842af00878ffd1c|fcdc58647713aa53-->
- `get_project_root` (function) — Walks up from the cwd to find the project root (a `.git` directory or SE3 config marker) and re-binds the i18n language to that root before returning it. <!--#6bb957ad4b0017c5-->
- `_fail` (function) — Prints a message to stderr and aborts the CLI with the given exit code via `typer.Exit`. <!--#68f14b0567a96659-->
- `_resolve_flow` (function) — Resolves a flow selector (explicit id or the active flow) into its id, its own project root, and its persisted context, looking in both live and archived records and returning `None` context when the flow record is gone. <!--#f8ced5e05301bca7-->
- `_render_stat` (function) — Prints the `--stat` view of a review scope: a header, one padded `+added -removed` line per file using the same C-quoted path tokens as the diff headers, and a totals summary. <!--#f160218608d39d7d-->
- `diff_cmd` (function) — The `review-scope diff` CLI command: validates the `--baseline` selector, resolves the flow, looks up and diagnoses the baseline (distinct exit codes for flow-not-found, cleaned, missing, and undecidable), reconstructs the baseline-to-workspace diff, and prints it filtered by `--path` or summarised by `--stat`. <!--#5c8977f4bc6ab815-->

### `src/tianluo/commands/run.py` (python) — Implements the `luo run` CLI command — the unified entry point that creates, drives, pauses/resumes, and finalizes SE3 state-machine flows, covering project-root discovery, run pidfile/lock claims, DISCOVERY and CONFIRM pause gates answered from either the terminal or the web console, step-failure retry decisions, interjection draining, usage reporting, and worktree-mode runs with their branch/issue cleanup. <!--#6fecf3bef5f07dac|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/commands/salvage_cmd.py` (python) — The SE3 `salvage` command that rescues work from abnormally terminated sessions by running a fault-tolerant pipeline — tolerantly loading session state, assessing the git diff, committing uncommitted changes, creating tracking issues for unfinished work, and archiving the session — then reports per-step outcomes in a Rich table. <!--#9516afc77f561789|c03e0c8fc18c4581-->
- `salvage` (function) — Entry point for the `salvage` command: locates the project root, re-binds the i18n language to it, then runs five independently error-guarded recovery steps (read session state, assess git diff, commit changes, create salvage issues, archive the session), prints a summary table, and returns 1 if any step failed. <!--#41f5d396f4efd5dd-->
- `_find_project_root` (function) — Walks up from the current directory to locate the project root by finding a .git directory or an SE3 config file. <!--#3c8eb6032ea041a2-->
- `_load_session` (function) — Tolerantly loads the persisted flow/session state via PersistenceManager, returning the FlowInstance (or None) plus any warnings. <!--#8c64b4dd4cc982ab-->
- `_assess_git_diff` (function) — Runs git status/diff to collect a dict of uncommitted-change info (status lines, changed file count/list, diff stat, truncated diff summary). <!--#c6bf085dac297a44-->
- `_commit_changes` (function) — Stages and commits all uncommitted changes with a generated `[salvage]` message, returning the new commit hash (or None if nothing to commit). <!--#2047b9ff2adde17e-->
- `_create_salvage_issues` (function) — Creates tracking issues for unfinished work, summarizing flow step history, interruption point, and changed files (or just changed files when no session state exists). <!--#782c49e6c54a7315-->
- `_archive_session` (function) — Archives the current session by clearing the persisted engine state and, for a salvaged (dispositioned, non-resumable) flow, retiring its resumable snapshot and — only once that clear is confirmed — discarding its review baselines, returning True if there was any state to archive. <!--#98513e6404972612-->
- `_display_results` (function) — Renders the collected (step, status, detail) tuples from the salvage pipeline as a localized Rich table with colour-styled OK/SKIP/FAIL statuses. <!--#4c27b4a953753f03-->

### `src/tianluo/commands/worktree_cmd.py` (python) — The `luo worktree gc` CLI command group — a thin render/exit-code shell over the engine's worktree garbage collector that reclaims leaked terminal `luo run --worktree` runs and prints a three-part Rich report (archived/reclaimed, retained-unmerged branches, skips/errors), with a byte-formatting helper. <!--#857a85cc96729016|0f35a4dcafa2f080-->
- `_format_bytes` (function) — Helper that formats a raw byte count into a compact human-readable size string using binary (1024-based) units from B up to TB. <!--#9cafc2a1079fcdba-->
- `gc_command` (function) — Typer CLI handler for `luo worktree gc` that delegates to the engine's `gc_worktree_runs` to reclaim terminal, idle leaked `--worktree` runs (archiving them and deleting only provably-merged branches), then renders a three-part Rich report — archived/reclaimed space, retained unmerged branches, and skipped/errored runs — and exits non-zero if any run errored. <!--#89af8e5938f14a57-->

## `src/tianluo/commands/merge/` — The foundational infrastructure package for the tianluo merge command, bundling the lightweight, import-cheap building blocks shared by the merge orchestrator, CLI, and engine — typed result/report models (result_model.py), a subsystem-grouped FailureReason enum with legacy-string interop (failure_reason.py), a flock-based main-worktree mutex (merge_lock.py), an append-only JSONL per-LLM-call tracer (llm_trace.py), pre-write secret redaction (secret_redact.py), and post-merge success assertions (postcondition.py), all re-exported from __init__.py. <!--#5431ca37532ff80e|5c21613b45dcb89a-->

### `src/tianluo/commands/merge/__init__.py` (python) — Package init for the SE3 merge subsystem's foundation infrastructure, re-exporting the lightweight (no heavy git/LLM import cost) building blocks—typed Result models, failure-reason enums, concurrency locking, per-LLM-call tracing, secret redaction, and post-condition assertions—consumed by the merge orchestrator, CLI entry points, and engine internals. <!--#cf78c40f0e1bc931|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/commands/merge/failure_reason.py` (python) — Defines the FailureReason IntEnum (a typed, subsystem-grouped catalog of every merge-orchestration failure/pause mode) plus bidirectional converters (from_legacy_string/to_legacy_string and a legacy_string property) that translate between the enum and the orchestrator's older compound 'prefix: detail' string surface, backed by a legacy-string map and a longest-first-ordered compound-prefix table guarded by a defensive ordering assertion. <!--#e3d6ff3038195e7d|216dcac12bc54b0b-->
- `FailureReason` (class) — An `IntEnum` cataloguing every reason a merge orchestration can fail or pause — grouped into gap-numbered families (git merge, conflict resolution, fast-strategy abort, rollback, human-call, runtime sync, post-condition, version anomaly, repo state, lock contention, plus `NONE` and `UNEXPECTED`) — whose member *names* (exposed lower-cased via the `legacy_string` property) are the stable identifier for persisted reports rather than the integer values. <!--#544e08907356a662-->
  - `FailureReason.legacy_string` (method) — Property returning the canonical legacy-string spelling of a reason as its lower-cased enum name, without any compound diagnostic detail. <!--#c0b7d910ff47c044-->
- `_assert_compound_prefix_order_longest_first` (function) — Test-importable defensive assertion that verifies the _COMPOUND_PREFIXES list is ordered longest-first so no shorter prefix can silently shadow a longer one during matching. <!--#a215f7b873024d92-->
- `from_legacy_string` (function) — Translates a legacy failure_reason string (None, empty, bare reason, or compound 'prefix: detail' form) into a (FailureReason, detail) tuple, falling back to UNEXPECTED with the raw text preserved as detail. <!--#14977706905a8d7c-->
- `to_legacy_string` (function) — Renders a FailureReason back into its legacy string form, mapping None to None and FailureReason.NONE to an empty string to preserve round-trip semantics. <!--#6e4cedb31364c905-->

### `src/tianluo/commands/merge/llm_trace.py` (python) — Defines an append-only JSONL LLM-call tracer for the merge command, pairing an `LLMCallRecord` dataclass (per-call metadata plus dict serialization) with a thread-safe `LLMTrace` writer that opens, size-rotates, batch-fsyncs, and closes trace files while recording each call as a line, usable directly or as a context manager. <!--#5d5f767a3b8fd304|cd3eec9a59d5ee7c-->
- `LLMCallRecord` (class) — Dataclass capturing a single LLM call's metadata (sequence, timestamp, agent, token estimate, prompt/response previews, duration, outcome, error, and arbitrary meta). <!--#6f024f9b4e32d840-->
  - `LLMCallRecord.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the call record into a plain dict ready for JSON encoding into a trace line. <!--#66bd42648a913924-->
- `LLMTrace` (class) — A thread-safe, append-only JSONL trace writer that records LLM calls made during `luo merge`, handling file rotation by size, batched-or-timed fsync throttling, preview truncation, and start/stop lifecycle management. <!--#9bdfb3766675d68c-->
  - `LLMTrace.__init__` (method) — Constructor that resolves the trace directory (defaulting to `runtime_dir/logs/llm`), stores rotation/fsync tuning parameters, and initializes the sequence counters, RLock, and file-handle state used by the writer. <!--#27f91f0afcbb56dc-->
  - `LLMTrace._ensure_dir` (method) — Creates the trace output directory (and parents) if it does not yet exist. <!--#bcc55e51d2a7b05f-->
  - `LLMTrace._new_file_path` (method) — Generates a unique rotation-counter-suffixed, UTC-timestamped JSONL file path for a new trace file. <!--#dc1884017308886f-->
  - `LLMTrace._rotate_if_needed` (method) — Closes and reopens a fresh trace file once the current one exceeds the configured size limit. <!--#41851d34db6d1884-->
  - `LLMTrace._open_file` (method) — Ensures the directory exists and opens a new trace file for writing at a freshly generated path. <!--#3f16d51fc8ed6b8e-->
  - `LLMTrace._fsync_now` (method) — Forces a flush plus os.fsync of the current file and resets the fsync throttle counters. <!--#585ae5672b2847f9-->
  - `LLMTrace._close_file` (method) — Flushes the tail to disk via fsync and closes the current trace file so no buffered record is lost. <!--#9b59062c89518c78-->
  - `LLMTrace.start` (method) — Idempotently opens the initial trace file and marks the writer as started. <!--#6d6bb5dfdab16afe-->
  - `LLMTrace.stop` (method) — Closes the trace file (forcing a final fsync) and marks the writer as stopped. <!--#e7137789ab5bc682-->
  - `LLMTrace.record` (method) — Appends one LLM call as a JSONL line (truncating previews, rotating if needed, flushing, and conditionally fsyncing) and returns its sequence number. <!--#ca81df8dded5e875-->
  - `LLMTrace.__enter__` (method) — Context-manager entry that starts the trace and returns the instance. <!--#d1285a98c0961099-->
  - `LLMTrace.__exit__` (method) — Context-manager exit that stops the trace, ensuring the file is closed and synced. <!--#53eaf3af0d2e4827-->

### `src/tianluo/commands/merge/merge_lock.py` (python) — Implements the cross-machine-aware exclusive merge lock for `luo merge` — an `fcntl.flock`-based `MergeLock` context manager that stamps a fixed-width PID+machine-id holder record, plus `MergeLockBusy`/`MergeLockStale` errors, blocking/fail-fast acquisition with bounded jittered stale-lock breaking, and read-only `inspect_lock`/`release_merge_lock`/`break_lock_file` helpers backing the CLI status and manual-unlock paths. <!--#342838b2dfb3e0e1|2dcff088a25115c7-->
- `_resolve_lock_path` (function) — Helper that resolves a merge-lock path against the project root, mapping the default sentinel to `<runtime>/state/merge.lock` and joining any other relative path onto the root. <!--#4e21226101e556f1-->
- `is_lock_held_in_process` (function) — Advisory, syscall-free check that returns True when the current process already holds the merge lock, based on the in-memory `_HELD_LOCK_PATHS` registry, used to short-circuit redundant acquisitions. <!--#dc4202ed3517cf80-->
- `_stale_break_jitter` (function) — Returns a random fraction in [0,1) for stale-break backoff jitter, wrapped as a function so tests can monkeypatch it deterministically. <!--#8652290c3ab2f41a-->
- `_encode_holder_record` (function) — Serialises `(pid, machine_id)` into the fixed-width `_HOLDER_RECORD_LEN` holder record (zero-padded PID line + truncated machine-id line + space padding) so every write fully overwrites the previous one. <!--#8b6a0c19fc00d31c-->
- `_decode_holder_record` (function) — Parses a holder record back into `(pid, machine_id, corrupt)`, tolerating legacy pure-PID records (machine id `None` = local) and flagging an unparseable PID line as corrupt. <!--#a013e2c3007b3e34-->
- `MergeLockBusy` (class) — Error raised when another live `luo merge` process holds the lock, carrying the holder's PID and machine id (and naming the machine only when the holder is foreign). <!--#6bfbd0354815af0e-->
  - `MergeLockBusy.__init__` (method) — Stores the lock path, holder PID and holder machine, and builds the message, appending the machine only for non-local holders. <!--#87043014dc8eeaae-->
- `MergeLockStale` (class) — Error signalling the lock file looks reclaimable (dead holder PID, no PID, or a corrupt record), with distinct operator-facing messages per case so callers can decide to break it. <!--#a225922ec73d2ace-->
  - `MergeLockStale.__init__` (method) — Records the holder PID/machine and `corrupt` flag and composes the corresponding stale message — dead PID, no PID recorded, or corrupt record needing manual cleanup. <!--#06dcee4fe748eb07-->
- `MergeLock` (class) — `fcntl.flock`-based exclusive merge lock (context manager or explicit acquire/release) that stamps a fixed-width PID+machine holder record and supports blocking queueing, staleness detection, and bounded stale-lock breaking. <!--#8b294a21f639786d-->
  - `MergeLock.__post_init__` (method) — Resolves the configured lock_path against the project root (unless already absolute) into the instance's _resolved_path. <!--#0949665977013300-->
  - `MergeLock.held` (method) — Property reporting whether this specific instance currently owns an open, acquired lock file descriptor. <!--#69f47245bd20560f-->
  - `MergeLock._read_holder_pid` (method) — Reads at most one holder record from the lock file (with `O_NOFOLLOW`), returning the PID and setting the sticky `_last_read_corrupt` / `_last_read_machine_id` state for callers. <!--#508c92f5ccdc8ee8-->
  - `MergeLock._write_pid` (method) — Stamps this process's PID and `stable_machine_id()` into the lock file through the held fd via a fixed-width `pwrite`-then-truncate-then-fsync sequence, so concurrent readers never observe a partial or empty record. <!--#f3b2908f822a52e2-->
  - `MergeLock._is_pid_alive` (method) — Method that probes a PID with signal 0 to decide liveness for stale-lock detection, treating ESRCH as dead and EPERM as conservatively alive, with documented caveats about cross-PID-namespace containers. <!--#71aaa1dbf36ec688-->
  - `MergeLock._try_break_stale_and_acquire` (method) — Unlinks a stale lock file and retries `flock` up to `_MAX_BREAK_STALE_ATTEMPTS` times with jittered exponential backoff, re-proving local staleness each round and raising `MergeLockBusy` rather than evicting a live or foreign winner. <!--#67a4abaacd9eec90-->
  - `MergeLock.acquire` (method) — Opens and flocks the lock file — blocking (queueing) or fail-fast — and on contention classifies the holder as foreign/busy, live/busy, or stale, optionally breaking a stale local lock when `break_stale=True`. <!--#d718dcbdc6c7d877-->
  - `MergeLock.release` (method) — Releases the flock, closes the file descriptor, and removes the path from the in-process held-locks registry, idempotently. <!--#60e5949e76255cfe-->
  - `MergeLock.__enter__` (method) — Context-manager entry that acquires the lock using the instance's configured blocking default and returns self. <!--#4b90db2205610f11-->
  - `MergeLock.__exit__` (method) — Context-manager exit that releases the lock. <!--#8f781b847877252c-->
- `LockStatus` (class) — Immutable snapshot of the lock file's state (existence, holder PID/machine, liveness, staleness, corruption) shared by the release logic and the CLI status display. <!--#b1134eb07e0f7b48-->
- `ReleaseOutcome` (class) — Result dataclass of a manual release decision, holding an exit code, the observed LockStatus, and a categorical action label. <!--#ecd40e485c6e7e55-->
- `inspect_lock` (function) — Read-only probe that builds a `LockStatus` using the same holder-record and liveness semantics as acquisition, reporting a missing file as stale and a foreign-machine holder as alive/not-stale. <!--#62534a9bea234ff1-->
- `break_lock_file` (function) — Unlinks the lock file (the only way an external process can clear an flock-held lock), returning whether a file was actually removed. <!--#fcf13b779b14aba0-->
- `release_merge_lock` (function) — Pure decision logic for a manual lock release that inspects state and removes the file for stale or force cases while refusing to evict a live holder without force. <!--#8b93ee87f470279b-->
- `_lock_file_removed` (function) — Removes the lock file and re-probes the path to confirm it is actually gone, distinguishing real removal from a swallowed permission error. <!--#81738d415b225947-->
- `acquire_merge_lock` (function) — function acquire_merge_lock <!--#345e208a00ddaf0b-->

### `src/tianluo/commands/merge/postcondition.py` (python) — Post-condition assertions verifying every merge the orchestrator deems successful: that the branch is an ancestor of HEAD, that HEAD is a merge commit (allowing no-ops and optional fix-up commits), and that the version file was bumped to the expected value, each violation raising a typed PostConditionViolated with hardening (bounded version-file reads, git timeouts, parent-count safety caps) so failures route to the correct diagnostic bucket. <!--#17921fb74be743f5|53dfd51b51cc4b95-->
- `_bounded_read_version_file` (function) — Reads a version file with size, duration, and regular-file-only guards so a pathological or streaming version file cannot hang or OOM the post-merge check. <!--#b4ca393bdf6263b1-->
- `PostConditionViolated` (class) — RuntimeError raised when a post-condition fails, carrying a typed FailureReason plus the offending branch and diagnostic detail so callers can route the failure. <!--#0da431b628261e1a-->
  - `PostConditionViolated.__init__` (method) — Constructs the exception from a FailureReason, optional branch, and detail string, assembling them into a human-readable message. <!--#f70bb7761adb86d6-->
- `CorruptCommitGraphError` (class) — RuntimeError signalling that a commit's parent count hit the safety cap, indicating a malformed commit graph rather than a non-merge commit. <!--#1294b6b69466ee14-->
  - `CorruptCommitGraphError.__init__` (method) — Builds the corrupt-graph error from the offending ref and the parent-count cap that was exceeded. <!--#fb3fa4e6616ab5a0-->
- `_run_git` (function) — Helper that runs a git subcommand in the project root with captured output, a timeout, and disabled stdin, returning the CompletedProcess. <!--#aec14a50bb4519da-->
- `assert_branch_merged` (function) — Post-condition that a branch is an ancestor of HEAD via git merge-base --is-ancestor, distinguishing a definitive not-merged verdict from unresolvable git errors. <!--#4596f5a4b25b218b-->
- `_resolve_parent_count_cap` (function) — Returns the parent-count safety cap, defaulting to 64 but honoring the SE3_MERGE_PARENT_COUNT_CAP environment override with validation. <!--#a59ca6631aa99934-->
- `_count_parents` (function) — Counts a ref's parents via repeated rev-parse --verify ref^N, reporting whether the ref itself resolves and raising CorruptCommitGraphError past the safety cap. <!--#c41f49fe5bd6b316-->
- `assert_head_is_merge_commit` (function) — Asserts that HEAD is a merge commit (at least `min_parents` parents), optionally tolerating one or more linear fix-up/version-bump commits stacked on top via `allow_fixup_parent`/`max_fixup_depth`, raising `PostConditionViolated` with `FailureReason.POSTCOND_HEAD_NOT_MERGE_COMMIT` otherwise. <!--#4dcb625b8e4095e4-->
- `assert_version_bumped` (function) — Post-condition that the version file contains the expected version, parsing TOML/JSON to avoid substring false-positives and optionally cross-checking the committed HEAD tree. <!--#2da0110c10472f23-->
- `_assert_committed_version_matches` (function) — Verifies HEAD's committed version file matches the expected version, distinguishing transient git-plumbing failures from positive commit-hook tampering signals. <!--#5a603880f7db03aa-->
- `check_all` (function) — Convenience entry-point that orchestrator success paths call to run all applicable merge post-condition checks — branch ancestry, HEAD merge-commit shape (skipped when `already_ancestor`), and optional version-bump verification. <!--#ffb656dee6c9d15a-->

### `src/tianluo/commands/merge/result_model.py` (python) — Defines the typed result model for a merge run — the frozen per-branch `MergeOutcome` and the aggregating `MergeReport` (semantic branch buckets, typed `FailureReason`, escalation/version/cleanup/rollback state, plus `to_legacy_dict` for backward compatibility with the legacy `orchestrator.MergeReport` shape). <!--#fdb488bafd156570|d4f16e542a16f0e8-->
- `MergeOutcome` (class) — Frozen per-branch dataclass recording the terminal fate of one branch merge attempt — success, typed `FailureReason`/detail, no-op (`already_ancestor`), merge commit SHA, and the `git_merge_succeeded` flag that distinguishes a clean git merge from a later sub-step failure. <!--#d5ee4680dbff763e-->
- `MergeReport` (class) — Typed successor to the legacy `orchestrator.MergeReport` holding a whole merge run's result: semantically split branch buckets (`newly_merged_branches`/`already_ancestor_branches`/`merged_with_warnings` plus the compatible `merged_branches` aggregate), typed-or-string failure reason, per-branch `outcomes`, human-escalation, version-aggregation, runtime-sync, issue-renumber, cleanup and rollback state, with legacy-dict conversion for backward compatibility. <!--#305d69811057e05e-->
  - `MergeReport.failure_reason_enum` (method) — Property returning the typed FailureReason for the report, parsing a legacy string (or passing through an existing enum) and mapping unknown strings to UNEXPECTED. <!--#ee363d13b2f99528-->
  - `MergeReport.add_outcome` (method) — Appends a branch outcome and routes it into the appropriate summary bucket (already-ancestor, newly-merged, with-warnings) while recording the first failed branch. <!--#938bedc6b8a3486a-->
  - `MergeReport.newly_merged` (method) — Backward-compatibility alias property returning newly_merged_branches. <!--#2ddc24cb4dd75dff-->
  - `MergeReport.already_merged` (method) — Backward-compatibility alias property returning already_ancestor_branches. <!--#7aa051f1613716f0-->
  - `MergeReport.all_merged_branches` (method) — Returns the combined backward-compatible view of all branches that were newly merged, already ancestors, or merged with warnings. <!--#cd3e3997fa557f3e-->
  - `MergeReport.call_file_str` (method) — Returns the human-call file path as a string or actual None, avoiding the legacy 'Call file: None' rendering bug. <!--#9ece35c501a4547a-->
  - `MergeReport.to_legacy_dict` (method) — Serializes the typed MergeReport into a plain dict matching the legacy orchestrator.MergeReport shape (normalizing FailureReason enums to legacy strings and flattening records) for JSON persistence, test fixtures, and un-migrated log consumers. <!--#9e8556acf438cce8-->

### `src/tianluo/commands/merge/secret_redact.py` (python) — A secret-redaction utility that detects and masks common secret patterns (API keys, bearer/GitHub/PyPI tokens, password fields) in text and git diffs before they are written to merge logs and traces, via a configurable thread-safe SecretRedactor class, an allowlist for intentional fake secrets, and module-level convenience functions backed by a cached default redactor. <!--#b643e520097c799f|d4452133f4d3d1d7-->
- `RedactConfig` (class) — Dataclass holding redaction configuration — an allowlist of exempt strings, extra regex/replacement patterns, and a preview length. <!--#59b0056d5d87e29e-->
- `SecretRedactor` (class) — Stateful, thread-safe redactor that applies the built-in plus configured patterns to mask secrets in text and diffs, restoring allowlisted fakes. <!--#c18072db25b8f560-->
  - `SecretRedactor.__init__` (method) — Initializes the redactor with a config and combines the default patterns with any configured extra patterns. <!--#85ccebb496ffc9a9-->
  - `SecretRedactor.redact` (method) — Applies all redaction patterns to a string, then restores any allowlisted values that were accidentally masked. <!--#fa9c0623cedad71a-->
  - `SecretRedactor._mask_fake` (method) — Static helper that runs the default patterns over a single known-fake value to compute its masked form for allowlist restoration. <!--#4fdd627f585d7c01-->
  - `SecretRedactor.redact_diff` (method) — Redacts secrets in a git diff line-by-line so diff markers and structure are preserved. <!--#eadedc33a38bbaa8-->
- `_get_default` (function) — Lazily constructs and caches a module-level default SecretRedactor singleton. <!--#a18335149677cff0-->
- `redact_text` (function) — Module-level convenience function that redacts secrets from text using the default redactor. <!--#ae56d65c5e441865-->
- `redact_diff` (function) — Module-level convenience function that redacts secrets from a git diff using the default redactor. <!--#c2475d3670220c02-->

## `src/tianluo/core/` — Shared low-level utility package for tianluo, holding cross-cutting primitives with no domain dependencies: process-stable machine identity and local-host checks (`machine_id.py`), the `run.pid` marker record and foreign-holder detection for a run's state dir (`run_pidfile.py`), and small text helpers such as `truncate_preview` (`utils.py`). <!--#c53ae46452078bed|aec26401b62aa923-->

### `src/tianluo/core/__init__.py` (python) — Package initializer marking `src/tianluo/core` as the home for SE3's shared core utilities, containing only a module docstring and no runtime code. <!--#48e466c636635268|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/core/machine_id.py` (python) — Small utility module providing a process-stable `<hostname>-<nodehex>` machine identifier and a `is_local_machine` check (treating an empty id as local for backward compatibility), so lock and pid records can distinguish hosts sharing a filesystem. <!--#322f4bb141d760ca|f723cbb8b4031d1d-->
- `stable_machine_id` (function) — Returns a process-stable, human-readable machine identifier of the form `<hostname>-<nodehex>` (cached after first call) so hosts sharing a filesystem can be told apart in holder messages. <!--#dd07e26bc6430f66-->
- `is_local_machine` (function) — Reports whether a given machine id refers to the current host, deliberately treating a missing/empty id as local so pre-upgrade lock and pid records stay reclaimable. <!--#d81b0c365b7b79b0-->

### `src/tianluo/core/run_pidfile.py` (python) — Defines the `run.pid` state-dir ownership marker protocol — encoding/decoding a `RunHolder` (pid, machine_id, flow_id), probing a marker's presence versus undecodability, and the atomic `O_CREAT | O_EXCL` acquire/hold/release lifecycle — so exactly one engine claims a state dir and destructive callers fail closed when ownership cannot be proven. <!--#66f5791c02253ea7|989bfdd63ffaf8c9-->
- `RunHolder` (class) — A `NamedTuple` describing the owner recorded in a `run.pid` marker — `pid` plus the optional `machine_id` / `flow_id` lines that older or not-yet-stamped records may lack — with a helper for deciding whether the marker belongs to a given flow. <!--#a4054bf6200acf18-->
  - `RunHolder.owns_flow` (method) — Decides whether this marker can be attributed to `flow_id`, matching on the recorded flow id when present and otherwise claiming an unstamped marker only when `flow_scoped=True` (a state dir that can host just that one flow). <!--#1b0dbbc90b7612a7-->
- `encode_run_pidfile` (function) — Serialises a `run.pid` record as a pid line, machine-id line, and optional flow-id line, omitting the flow line when the flow id is not yet known. <!--#6a99bb776a581c21-->
- `MarkerProbe` (class) — A NamedTuple reporting the on-disk state of `<state_dir>/run.pid` as two separate facts — whether a marker is present and who its decoded owner is — so callers can tell "no marker" apart from "marker exists but unreadable". <!--#517dce6fcd0d2837-->
  - `MarkerProbe.undecidable` (method) — Property that is true when a marker file exists but its owner could not be decoded, the case destructive callers must treat as "someone holds this state dir" rather than as absent. <!--#7af5c0877dde76cb-->
- `_decode_run_holder` (function) — Parses a `run.pid` record body into a `RunHolder` (pid, machine_id, flow_id), returning `None` for empty, non-integer or non-positive-pid records. <!--#0c16db0130b51805-->
- `probe_run_marker` (function) — Reads `<state_dir>/run.pid` and returns a `MarkerProbe`, counting only "no such file" as absent so permission/I-O failures surface as present-but-undecidable. <!--#f5fa3d5662a90c8c-->
- `read_run_holder` (function) — Convenience reader returning just the decoded `RunHolder` for a state dir (or `None` for absent/unreadable/malformed markers), for callers whose next move is not destructive. <!--#5b5ea58fde94398e-->
- `read_run_pidfile` (function) — Narrow `(pid, machine_id)` view over `read_run_holder` for callers that only need to decide whether the recorded pid is theirs to signal. <!--#fba29fc56a6ad713-->
- `foreign_run_holder` (function) — Returns the marker's holder only when it is recorded on another machine, the signal to refuse starting a second engine against a state dir a remote host is running. <!--#c64d0deba039100e-->
- `MarkerClaim` (class) — A NamedTuple describing the result of trying to take `run.pid`, separating "acquired" from "blocked" so a caller knows whether it must stand down or merely failed to refresh a marker it already owns. <!--#aeb871864f577d70-->
- `_rewrite_owned_marker` (function) — Rewrites a marker this process already owns via tmp-file-plus-rename (used to fill in a flow id once minted), reporting whether the rewrite landed. <!--#ed1e38263eee4976-->
- `_unestablished_claim` (function) — Builds the fail-closed `MarkerClaim` for a claim attempt that died on I/O error — reported as blocked, since such a failure cannot prove no other owner exists. <!--#bf81cc7fcaf3beaf-->
- `acquire_run_marker` (function) — Atomically claims `<state_dir>/run.pid` for the current process via `O_CREAT | O_EXCL` — the single sanctioned way to publish a run marker — returning a fail-closed `MarkerClaim` on any environmental error, re-taking a marker this process already owns, optionally reclaiming a locally-owned stale marker through the `is_stale` callback, and rejecting a non-absolute `state_dir` with `ValueError`. <!--#65772274a18efbbb-->
- `holds_run_marker` (function) — Re-checks that `run.pid` still names this process on this machine, used at the destructive boundaries of `luo end-session` to catch a marker overwritten by a non-conforming writer. <!--#52e448a0c01fa785-->
- `release_run_marker` (function) — Removes `run.pid` only if it still names this process (optionally also dropping an undecodable record for the owning `luo run`, so a corrupted marker cannot wedge the flow forever), never raising. <!--#69be1a2f31883b31-->

### `src/tianluo/core/utils.py` (python) — A shared SE3 core utilities module providing truncate_preview, which shortens overlong text to a maximum length with an appended ellipsis for consistent console preview formatting. <!--#e3c9d16af367d231|63fffa8987576585-->
- `truncate_preview` (function) — Truncates a string to a maximum length and appends an ellipsis indicator, returning the text unchanged when it already fits, for consistent text previews in console output. <!--#ae15e4e349281ce9-->

## `src/tianluo/daemon/` — The resident daemon control-plane package: a long-lived per-machine process that supervises and spawns local `luo run` flows, aggregates on-disk project state (engine.json, calls, issues, history, usage) into status snapshots, and relays them to the central server over an outbound NAT-friendly WebSocket link using a versioned JSON protocol — with supporting layers for flow spawning/reaping, incremental history reads, attachment uploads, disk-JSON caching, record size budgeting, and wire-traffic metrics. <!--#ae2c4985883475d7|5fde03be41d7cc4d-->

### `src/tianluo/daemon/__init__.py` (python) — Package entry point for the resident SE3 daemon control-plane process, documenting its role as the long-lived bridge between one-shot `luo run` flows and the central server, and re-exporting the public API of its sub-modules (`aggregator`, `daemon`, `client`, `spawner`, `supervisor`, `uploads`, `protocol`). <!--#e8a10dbc28b422f8|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/daemon/aggregator.py` (python) — Defines the daemon's status-aggregation layer — the `PendingCall`/`FlowSnapshot`/`IssueSnapshot`/`MachineStatus` wire dataclasses plus `DaemonAggregator`, which polls registered and historical project roots' on-disk artifacts (engine.json, calls/, issues, worktree runs) into a single `MachineStatus` snapshot for STATUS_UPDATE broadcasts, while maintaining the durable project-root registry and the stat-signature/TTL caches that keep idle polling cheap. <!--#908cc7c299571e1c|945f614f99f2c0a6-->
- `PendingCall` (class) — A dataclass modeling one queued human-in-the-loop interaction backed by a file under a project's tianluo/calls/ directory, carrying the call's kind, prompt, context, options, and step_id for the WebUI to render. <!--#c25a00365f542080-->
  - `PendingCall.to_dict` (method) — Serializes a PendingCall to a plain dict, optionally clipping the (potentially large) prompt body to the history _DESC_CLIP length so full prompts never inline into periodic STATUS_UPDATE snapshots. <!--#0b608df35b38505c-->
- `FlowSnapshot` (class) — Dataclass capturing one flow's aggregated state read from its `engine.json` — identity, task/status, step progress, counts, pending calls, the `waiting_for_lock` and `resumable` sub-states, and the plan_mode/review_scope/usage_summary control-plane projections — plus a wire-serialization helper. <!--#5733f88b77567a98-->
  - `FlowSnapshot.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the snapshot to a wire dict, clipping pending-call prompts to the preview form and omitting the plan_mode/review_scope/usage_summary keys entirely when they are unrecoverable so absence reads as "unknown" rather than a fabricated empty answer. <!--#21f8838dda1ddd19-->
- `IssueSnapshot` (class) — A dataclass holding one issue's webui-relevant summary fields (id, title, clipped description, status, priority, type, tags, source, timestamps) for inclusion in a MachineStatus snapshot. <!--#7770d28711f04186-->
  - `IssueSnapshot.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the IssueSnapshot to a dict, omitting optional fields (title/priority/type) when unset. <!--#ac44a97529a64719-->
- `MachineStatus` (class) — Dataclass holding one machine's full status snapshot — flows, pending calls, project roots, issues, and the registered-projects view — with a `to_dict` serializer for the STATUS_UPDATE wire payload. <!--#bc09a7d7983f9901-->
  - `MachineStatus.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the snapshot to a JSON-ready dict, clipping pending-call prompts (full bodies are fetched on demand) and emitting only the three per-project keys the WebUI dialog renders. <!--#f30a34501e30e15c-->
- `ProjectRegistryError` (class) — `RuntimeError` subclass signalling that the durable project registry could not be rewritten, kept distinct from "nothing was registered" so a failed delete stays actionable up to the WebUI. <!--#76f08108571788a0-->
- `DaemonAggregator` (class) — The daemon's polling engine that scans on-disk flow artifacts (active and resumable `engine.json`, calls, logs, issues) across all known project roots into a `MachineStatus` snapshot, backed by a persistent project-root registry, a live-process gate for resume eligibility, and TTL/stat-signature caches that keep idle polling cheap. <!--#0ff4b8e4d7f36c45-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.__init__` (method) — Constructs the aggregator, wiring optional registry load/persist/remove and live-roots callbacks and initializing the mtime, historical-roots, issue, and pending-calls signature caches. <!--#e1633eba0c9e4026-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.add_project_root` (method) — The single write-through seam that registers a project root (normalizing worktree sandboxes back to their main root) into the in-memory active set and the persistent registry, busting the historical-roots cache only for genuinely new roots. <!--#ebb67d422abe9c95-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.remove_project_root` (method) — Drops a root from the in-memory polled set only (the registry file is untouched), leaving durable deregistration to `unregister_project_root`. <!--#10a11d6fa61b1a7b-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.registered_projects` (method) — Builds the WebUI project-dialog view — one sorted `{path, exists, active}` entry per root in the raw registry ∪ active set — so stale entries whose directory is gone remain visible and removable. <!--#b30067c320993d14-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.unregister_project_root` (method) — Durably deregisters a root (worktree→main normalized): deletes it from the registry file first, then from the active and persisted-roots sets, returning whether anything was removed and raising `ProjectRegistryError` on write failure. <!--#b604d646b49ad58b-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.set_project_roots` (method) — Replaces the entire polled project-root set and invalidates the historical-roots cache. <!--#b0860aaf9c1796da-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._invalidate_hist_roots_cache` (method) — Drops the cached historical-root enumeration so the next `all_project_roots` re-runs the on-disk history walk. <!--#9f1c834431d818f3-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.project_roots` (method) — Returns a sorted snapshot list of the currently registered active project roots. <!--#424a9b11cd59d976-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.has_changes` (method) — Returns whether any tracked engine.json mtime changed since the last call, updating the internal mtime cache so consecutive change-free calls report False. <!--#a9a3a7ad3f9e2084-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.get_snapshot` (method) — Builds the full MachineStatus snapshot by producing per-flow FlowSnapshots (including supplemental resumable snapshots), aggregating all pending calls and issues across observable roots, and attaching project-root and registered-project lists. <!--#88960f9173ae1d4d-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._live_roots` (method) — Resolves the normalized set of roots with a live `luo run` process via the injected provider, used to gate the resumable flag. <!--#42348cabae23a503-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.all_project_roots` (method) — Returns the deduplicated, sorted union of active, persistent-registry, and disk-history project roots — the source of truth for the New Task dropdown and history index — with the expensive historical enumeration throttled behind a TTL/fingerprint cache. <!--#2588463043255e5c-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.all_observable_roots` (method) — Returns all_project_roots plus active --worktree run subdirectories, the root view used for building flow snapshots so an isolation run is observable in the WebUI throughout its flow body rather than only after its trailing merge. <!--#72f12db158cc888b-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._active_worktree_run_roots` (method) — Scans each tracked main root's tianluo/worktrees/*/ for children whose cached engine.json header describes an is_worktree_mode flow and returns those child paths so live worktree runs are observable. <!--#ecba2d8a1ba205dc-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._historical_roots` (method) — Returns the on-disk historical roots for a given base set, reusing the cached enumeration while within HISTORICAL_ROOTS_TTL and the base fingerprint is unchanged, atomically reading cache fields to stay thread-safe against concurrent invalidation. <!--#42d18b5b19eafdd3-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.pending_calls_signature` (method) — Returns a cheap kind-agnostic stat fingerprint (name, mtime, size) of every tianluo/calls/ file across active and worktree roots, honoring the history reader's dirty-sentinel gate, so the daemon can poll frequently and run the heavy snapshot only when the signature moves. <!--#4dc51e44c0b10ece-->
  - `DaemonAggregator.set_calls_gate_source` (method) — Injects the history reader's idle-root gate callback so pending_calls_signature can skip and reuse fingerprints for sentinel-gated idle roots. <!--#146ae9e41fffe267-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._merge_project_roots` (method) — Produces the snapshot's `project_roots` field by delegating to `all_project_roots`. <!--#f97c43f045028b11-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._projection_fields` (method) — Static helper that derives the (plan_mode, review_scope, usage_summary) projections for an engine dict by delegating to the shared `strategy_view.py` and usage backends, returning all-`None` for a degraded header read with no `state`. <!--#70848cd851ef6304-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._snapshot_for_root` (method) — Builds the `FlowSnapshot` for one project root's active `engine.json` — computing step progress, filtered/deduped pending calls, log & issue counts, projections and the live-process-gated `resumable` flag — returning `None` when there is no active flow rather than fabricating an untitled card. <!--#764364c96205a771-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._enumerate_resumable_snapshots` (method) — Enumerates a root's tianluo/state/resumable/*.json per-flow snapshots and emits a resumable FlowSnapshot for each whose flow_id is not already active, filename-matched, and still has a resumable status, so paused/failed flows superseded in the single-slot engine.json remain visible for resume. <!--#4e85d6954de21532-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._snapshot_from_resumable` (method) — Builds a `FlowSnapshot` from a superseded per-flow resumable snapshot dict, deriving progress the same way as the active path but leaving live-flow-owned fields (pending calls, counts, summary) empty and deriving `resumable` through the same status/live-process gate. <!--#6f98aa613d37aaaa-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._enumerate_calls` (method) — Lists genuinely pending human-call files under tianluo/calls/, excluding response files and any call that already has a sibling .response/.response.json answer, returning the rest as parsed PendingCall objects. <!--#63629c7ffbba93e6-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._filter_calls_for_flow` (method) — Filters a call list to those whose context.flow_id matches the given flow, dropping unattributed calls to prevent cross-flow leakage, and returns the list unfiltered when no flow_id is supplied. <!--#86844e1e6eff07b0-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._filter_stale_calls` (method) — Drops calls whose owning step the flow has already moved past (no longer current or in a processed status), with a retry_decision exemption that keeps the FAILED-step decision chip visible, and keeps step-unresolvable calls untouched. <!--#8c377888214d1286-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._dedup_calls_by_step` (method) — Keeps only the newest unanswered call per (flow_id, step_id) so superseded clarification-round leftovers don't pile up as stale chips. <!--#252191d67ed75681-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._parse_call_file` (method) — Builds a PendingCall from one tianluo/calls/ file by reading its JSON body for display metadata (kind/prompt/context/options/step_id), with legacy fallbacks for message/question prompts and top-level flow_id, degrading gracefully to a bare CALL_KIND_CALL on non-JSON. <!--#927cd5c14baa6f0c-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._read_summary` (method) — Returns the most recent `summary-*.json` summary text for a flow, if any. <!--#a4e35352515c5261-->
  - `DaemonAggregator._collect_issues` (method) — Reads open/ and closed/ issue YAML files under tianluo/issues/ into clipped IssueSnapshots behind a per-root directory stat-signature cache, skipping worktree-copy roots to avoid double-counting and using the fast libyaml loader when available. <!--#7da50685cb267bc5-->
- `_is_resumable_status` (function) — Returns whether a status string names a resumable flow — everything except `completed` qualifies. <!--#e302c0e8083cfeec-->
- `_safe_realpath` (function) — Helper returning `os.path.realpath` of a path, falling back to the literal string on `OSError`, used to make roots comparable keys without worktree folding. <!--#5c6df0ca9d6fb13d-->
- `_normalize_root` (function) — Normalizes a project root to the canonical live-process-gate key by folding a worktree-copy sandbox back to its owning main root and resolving symlinks with realpath, so aggregator and supervisor root sets compare on identical keys. <!--#6dd98e7ede7268c3-->
- `_resumable_with_live_gate` (function) — Computes a flow's resumable flag from its status via _is_resumable_status, tightening it to non-resumable only for a RUNNING flow whose normalized root is in the live-process set (leaving all other cases and the no-provider case unchanged). <!--#f892af501a86f85a-->
- `_safe_mtime` (function) — Returns a path's mtime, or None if it does not exist or is unreadable. <!--#11651aaac368a47d-->
- `_safe_stat` (function) — Returns a path's (mtime, size) tuple, or (0.0, 0) when unreadable, pairing mtime with size so a signature changes even for two writes within the filesystem's mtime resolution. <!--#c115e80c50b26a4d-->
- `_read_json` (function) — Reads and parses a JSON file, returning None on any OS or parse error. <!--#5d8c043c7c84672b-->
- `_call_step_id` (function) — Resolves the step a PendingCall belongs to, preferring its `step_id` field then `context.step_id`, else None. <!--#6fb85d6e474a8859-->
- `_call_sort_key` (function) — Returns a recency sort key (created_at mtime, then call_id tie-breaker) for a PendingCall. <!--#7c1a397b9866544b-->
- `_current_step` (function) — Resolves a human-readable current-step label from a flow `state` dict. <!--#b7b602ad33735782-->
- `_count_dir` (function) — Counts regular files anywhere under a path (0 if it does not exist). <!--#745c695aa4dafe04-->
- `_count_issues` (function) — Counts open issue YAML records under a tianluo/issues/ directory (preferring the open/ subtree), returning 0 when the directory is absent. <!--#c40fe373e6925fce-->

### `src/tianluo/daemon/client.py` (python) — Defines `DaemonClient`, the daemon's NAT-friendly outbound WebSocket client to the central server, which announces itself with HELLO, pushes periodic STATUS_UPDATE snapshots (with an idle gear when no browsers are watching), answers PING heartbeats, routes server commands (SPAWN_FLOW, RESPOND_CALL, END_SESSION, PROJECT_COMMAND, UPLOAD_COMMAND, FETCH_COMMAND, history-window reads) to daemon handlers, and reconnects with capped exponential backoff, lazily importing the optional `websockets` dependency so a daemon without it degrades to local-only operation. <!--#06fdec59351609a8|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/daemon/daemon.py` (python) — Defines the resident `Daemon` control-plane process — its `DaemonConfig` runtime paths/cadences, logging and pid-dir helpers, the typed `ProjectCommandError` codes, and worktree-state lookup — which supervises local `luo run` flows, maintains the machine-local project-root registry, aggregates status/history snapshots, and serves spawn/resume/end-session/project/upload/fetch requests arriving over the outbound WebSocket connection to the central server. <!--#d482b29112602220|69318eda00299dff-->
- `_configure_daemon_logging` (function) — Installs a single idempotent, timestamped log handler for the daemon process so its log lines are attributable across detached and foreground modes. <!--#9280268fece7609c-->
- `_default_pid_dir` (function) — Returns the directory for daemon runtime files (pidfile/status/log), defaulting to ~/.se3 but overridable via the SE3_DAEMON_DIR env var for test isolation. <!--#64e9a9b21d5ed8cd-->
- `DaemonConfig` (class) — A dataclass holding a Daemon instance's configuration (server URL, in-memory daemon key, pid/status/log/registry file paths derived from pid_dir, poll and history-poll cadences, worktree-GC interval and age threshold, and shutdown grace). <!--#ef51b6bdee38b9fa-->
  - `DaemonConfig.__post_init__` (method) — Coerces the configured pid_dir into a Path after dataclass construction. <!--#c8319b96022c643e-->
  - `DaemonConfig.pid_file` (method) — Property giving the pidfile path under pid_dir. <!--#db80f9021d5529bf-->
  - `DaemonConfig.status_file` (method) — Property giving the status-file path under pid_dir. <!--#1d551dccb5cefe59-->
  - `DaemonConfig.log_file` (method) — Property giving the daemon log-file path under pid_dir. <!--#1ad7ba864a0ad3ee-->
  - `DaemonConfig.project_roots_file` (method) — Property giving the persistent project-roots registry file path under pid_dir. <!--#bd196da4c4c0757e-->
- `ProjectCommandError` (class) — Exception raised when a project-registry add/remove request is rejected, carrying a stable machine-readable `code` (e.g. `invalid_path`, `not_found`, `live_flow`, `not_registered`, `registry_error`) so the WebUI can render a localized message instead of the raw English text. <!--#29c75e82e7c05d70-->
  - `ProjectCommandError.__init__` (method) — Stores the rejection `code` and falls back to using it as the exception message when no human-readable message is supplied. <!--#b76c830fb6bfb3e3-->
- `_worktree_state_dir_for_flow` (function) — Module-level helper that scans a project root's `tianluo/worktrees/*/state/engine.json` (both `tianluo/` and legacy `se3/` layouts, via size-guarded header reads) and returns the state directory of the isolation worktree currently carrying the given `flow_id`, or `None` when no worktree hosts it. <!--#f587e525cef2eda0-->
- `Daemon` (class) — The resident control-plane process that wires together the flow supervisor, spawner, project-root registry-backed aggregator and history reader, exposes the remote control surface (spawn/resume), and serves the outbound WebSocket connection to the central server while running the periodic poll loop and worktree-GC sweeps. <!--#aea3054d50db55dc-->
  - `Daemon.__init__` (method) — Constructs the Daemon by building its supervisor/spawner and its aggregator with project-roots registry callbacks, sanitizing stale registry entries, constructing the worktree-inclusive history reader, sharing the reader's dirty-sentinel gate, and initializing lazy client/stop-event/GC-timestamp state. <!--#b097e65644d933e8-->
  - `Daemon.request_spawn` (method) — Public entry point for remote spawn requests: starts a new `luo run` flow via the spawner (with discover / worktree / from-issue / plan-decomposition options) and registers its project root with the aggregator so the next poll picks up its state. <!--#3c0e1ae379e253c4-->
  - `Daemon.request_resume` (method) — Remote-request entry point that resumes a flow by id — locating it in the active `engine.json` or the per-flow `state/resumable/<flow_id>.json` snapshot, rejecting only COMPLETED flows, and refusing double-writers when a live local process or a foreign-machine `run.pid` marker (read from the flow's own worktree state dir when it runs `--worktree`) still owns it — before delegating the actual relaunch. <!--#312a6ab2baf9c5ef-->
  - `Daemon.request_end_session` (method) — Remote entry point that finds a flow (or accepts a caller-supplied root), normalizes the root to its owning main project, and dispatches an `luo end-session` subprocess to terminate and archive the flow off the event loop. <!--#a2987d86fd2fea54-->
  - `Daemon.request_add_project` (method) — Remote entry point that validates a project root (absolute, existing directory, not the filesystem root) and registers it through the aggregator's single registration seam, returning the normalized path. <!--#7c351b526e52b60c-->
  - `Daemon.request_remove_project` (method) — Remote entry point that deregisters a project root (registration only, no data deleted), refusing roots with a live flow and surfacing typed ProjectCommandError codes. <!--#c8e4b73a7c73482a-->
  - `Daemon._live_project_roots` (method) — Returns the set of project roots with a live `luo run` process (worktree→main folded), computed from the same supervisor + is_alive view as the resume double-spawn guard, degrading to an empty set on any error. <!--#20af847bb16e2d60-->
  - `Daemon.snapshot` (method) — Returns a fresh MachineStatus aggregation snapshot from the aggregator. <!--#18881f0b4dc950ac-->
  - `Daemon.stop` (method) — Signals the running event loop to shut down gracefully by setting the stop event. <!--#8c421937c52e8b71-->
  - `Daemon.run_forever` (method) — Foreground entry point that configures daemon logging and runs the async serve loop until interrupted. <!--#28c8017c1d0d57e6-->
  - `Daemon.serve` (method) — The async main that writes the pidfile, installs signal handlers, and runs the poll loop plus optional outbound server client concurrently on one event loop before shutting down. <!--#c99097a39e82fbf1-->
  - `Daemon._start_server_client` (method) — Lazily constructs the outbound `DaemonClient` (with all snapshot/history providers and request handlers bound to this daemon) and launches it as an asyncio task, returning `None` when no `server_url` is configured so local-only daemons pay no WebSocket cost. <!--#df5e9c72b4c888c4-->
  - `Daemon._handle_spawn_request` (method) — Thin adapter that converts an inbound server `SPAWN_FLOW` message's fields into a `request_spawn` call, applying defaults for empty project root and task type. <!--#6ac3499323b06ec3-->
  - `Daemon._handle_resume_request` (method) — Adapts an inbound server SPAWN_FLOW-with-resume_flow_id message into a request_resume call. <!--#a1397f1fc3be07ee-->
  - `Daemon._handle_end_session_request` (method) — Adapts an inbound server END_SESSION message into a request_end_session call. <!--#785f8ebae74029dc-->
  - `Daemon._handle_project_request` (method) — Adapts a server `PROJECT_COMMAND` into the corresponding add/remove registry request and returns the normalized path, rejecting unknown operations with a `ProjectCommandError`. <!--#afb70d6eb59e298b-->
  - `Daemon._handle_upload_request` (method) — Adapter that turns a server UPLOAD_COMMAND into an attachment write via `store_upload`, keeping all server-initiated side effects routed through the Daemon object. <!--#fd6b023a6cc7c71e-->
  - `Daemon._handle_fetch_request` (method) — Handler seam that adapts a server `FETCH_COMMAND` into an attachment read by delegating to `uploads.read_upload`, which owns the containment/existence/size policy. <!--#40ca62f7a9df2ddd-->
  - `Daemon._handle_ensure_request` (method) — Pre-spawn hook that runs `luo init` in the target directory if needed (auto-initializing a fresh path from the New Task form) and registers it with the aggregator, returning the EnsureResult. <!--#198a13c02b3e31b8-->
  - `Daemon._handle_respond_request` (method) — Adapts a server RESPOND_CALL by writing the call response file to disk and then re-spawning the paused flow with `--resume` so a daemon-spawned flow advances past a human call. <!--#eaeff977d0fcd282-->
  - `Daemon._resume_paused_flow` (method) — Best-effort helper that re-spawns a project's flow with `--resume` only when its engine.json header shows a PAUSED flow and no live process already owns the root. <!--#849dfeacd61e0e86-->
  - `Daemon._poll_loop` (method) — The async aggregation loop that runs _poll_once and gated _maybe_run_gc each tick, then waits on a gear-aware interval (dropping to _IDLE_POLL_INTERVAL when there are zero viewers) until the stop event fires. <!--#4370802cfba59839-->
  - `Daemon._client_viewer_count` (method) — Returns the outbound client's effective viewer count, or None (meaning 'assume someone is watching') for any degraded state such as no client, a dropped connection, or a malformed/missing count. <!--#2e98efab73821e2e-->
  - `Daemon._presence_idle` (method) — Returns True when the poll loop may run in the low-power idle gear, i.e. when the client viewer count is exactly zero. <!--#f91015a95ff98825-->
  - `Daemon._poll_once` (method) — A single aggregation tick that offloads flow discovery, root registration, and snapshot building to worker threads (keeping disk JSON parsing off the event loop), then persists the status file. <!--#b64a94b40ba2bd51-->
  - `Daemon._register_discovered_roots` (method) — Worker-thread helper that registers each discovered flow's project root with the aggregator, folding any worktree copy back to its main root. <!--#1db87ee1b36c35e6-->
  - `Daemon._maybe_run_gc` (method) — Gates the worktree-GC sweep to fire at most once per gc_interval (or never if disabled), stamping the timestamp before offloading the actual sweep to a worker thread. <!--#daba86981c6025aa-->
  - `Daemon._gc_once` (method) — Worker-thread routine that sweeps each tracked project root for leaked worktree runs via gc_worktree_runs, isolating per-root failures and logging each sweep's report. <!--#222ba97fc36b37e3-->
  - `Daemon._log_gc_report` (method) — Emits a GC sweep's outcome to the daemon log, raising retained-unmerged branches to WARNING as operator-actionable signals while logging reclamations and errors. <!--#1934263e345da6b8-->
  - `Daemon._install_signal_handlers` (method) — Wires SIGTERM/SIGINT to a graceful stop on the event loop, falling back to signal.signal on platforms without loop signal handlers. <!--#49b2ae2f6678bb85-->
  - `Daemon._shutdown` (method) — Terminates any spawned flows within the grace period and removes the status/pid runtime files on shutdown. <!--#943e2b7baa719500-->
  - `Daemon._write_pidfile` (method) — Writes the daemon pidfile (pid/start time/server/machine id), refusing to start if another live daemon already holds it. <!--#4e6caf9c4c17a9d6-->
  - `Daemon._write_status` (method) — Persists the latest snapshot plus live outbound-client connection state, wire-byte metrics, presence/poll-gear info, and tracked flows to the status file via an atomic JSON write. <!--#11cbb656b4a05038-->
- `DaemonAlreadyRunning` (class) — RuntimeError subclass raised when a daemon is started while another instance is alive, carrying the conflicting pid. <!--#da58834df4e58342-->
  - `DaemonAlreadyRunning.__init__` (method) — Initializes the error with a message and stores the conflicting pid. <!--#75516beb68cdd4c3-->
- `_se3_version` (function) — Best-effort helper returning the installed SE3/tianluo `__version__` string, or `"unknown"` on failure. <!--#8f24a37dc6b92297-->
- `_read_pidfile` (function) — Reads and JSON-parses a daemon pid/status file, returning None if absent or corrupt. <!--#5aa376cf77d5cd0f-->
- `_pid_alive` (function) — Returns whether an int-like pid names a live process via os.kill(pid, 0), treating permission errors as alive. <!--#166d012dcd6de729-->
- `_atomic_write_json` (function) — Atomically writes a payload as JSON to a path using a temp-file-plus-rename. <!--#dcff051d0bc329f1-->
- `_read_project_roots_raw` (function) — Reads the persisted project-roots JSON registry verbatim (no existence filtering, empty on missing/corrupt), providing the raw on-disk view that the sanitize/self-heal logic compares against. <!--#d0dc15ff0a431b5b-->
- `_read_project_roots` (function) — Returns the live project roots by reading the raw registry and dropping any root whose directory no longer exists on disk, so consumers never see a since-deleted project. <!--#9273ec53a134058c-->
- `_append_project_root` (function) — Registry writer that folds worktree copies to their main root, realpath-deduplicates, skips nonexistent roots, and atomically rewrites the sorted registry (also pruning stale entries) only when a genuinely new root appears. <!--#f0825eab4c20483a-->
- `_remove_project_root` (function) — Registry writer (inverse of append) that removes a root from the raw registry using the same worktree→main and realpath normalization, rewriting the file only on an actual match and returning whether an entry was removed. <!--#9dbd12fb21669a23-->
- `_sanitize_project_roots` (function) — One-time startup cleanup that drops worktree-copy and no-longer-existent entries from the raw registry and atomically rewrites it only when something was removed, fully fault-tolerant so it never blocks startup. <!--#dccc6de39a9fb208-->
- `start_daemon` (function) — Public entry point that starts the daemon foreground (blocking) or fully detached via double-fork/subprocess, raising DaemonAlreadyRunning if one is already live. <!--#856f4e1148be83db-->
- `_start_detached_fork` (function) — Detaches the daemon via a classic double-fork (reparenting the real daemon onto init) and polls the pidfile before returning to the launcher. <!--#e621687e3abf6b96-->
- `_detach_streams` (function) — Redirects the detached daemon's stdin/stdout/stderr to /dev/null and the log file. <!--#02d4194e10a76e4a-->
- `_start_detached_subprocess` (function) — Windows/no-`os.fork` fallback that launches a detached foreground daemon subprocess (passing the daemon key via env, wiring PYTHONPATH) and polls the pidfile to report started/starting status. <!--#9ac7651a05e02eb6-->
- `stop_daemon` (function) — Signals a running daemon to shut down via SIGTERM and waits for it to exit, reporting stopped/not_running/stop_timeout. <!--#def767d191f88bfb-->
- `daemon_status` (function) — Reports whether the daemon is running plus its tracked flows, snapshot, and real outbound-connection state read from the pid/status files. <!--#472f7d019b97062f-->
