### `src/tianluo/daemon/disk_json_cache.py` (python) — A unified, thread-safe disk-JSON parse cache for the daemon control plane that parses each on-disk artifact (engine.json, archived snapshots, resumable and _meta.json files) at most once per real content change — keying immutable snapshots by (path, mtime, size), re-validating the live engine.json with a whole-content hash to catch same-(mtime,size) middle-of-file rewrites, and offering a bounded degraded head+tail header scan for oversized legacy files — to eliminate the per-tick json.loads freeze and archive re-parse saturation behind the WebUI stalls (#243/#260). <!--#aca724f3f2e30b91|ff1c47e561fe96e9-->
- `clear_cache` (function) — Test-only helper that drops every cached parse, degraded-header entry, and once-warned marker to restore cache isolation between tests. <!--#4e0b69e9d138db14-->
- `_store` (function) — Lock-held helper that inserts/refreshes a cache entry as most-recently-used and evicts the oldest entries once the LRU cap is exceeded. <!--#1f90857dea1c197c-->
- `_drop_entry` (function) — Removes a path's main-cache and degraded-header entries when its backing file no longer stats, so a deleted worktree/archive file's parse isn't pinned for the daemon's lifetime. <!--#432a10b983836a79-->
- `cached_content_digest` (function) — Accessor that returns the cached whole-content digest from a path's last active engine.json read (or None if unavailable), letting the change-detection signature fold in content changes to catch same-(mtime,size) in-place rewrites without a second read or hash. <!--#f1c3197761855712-->
- `peek_cached_header` (function) — Cheap stat-only probe returning a path's already-cached parse on a (mtime_ns, size) hit (refreshing its LRU recency) and None otherwise, letting the 1s fast tick skip the verify_content read for terminal flows. <!--#4e0b235cf2492887-->
- `_warn_once_degraded` (function) — Emits a once-per-path warning that degraded header extraction failed for an oversized file, deduplicated so a persistently broken file doesn't flood the log. <!--#bf9238330491dc5d-->
- `_safe_stat` (function) — Helper that stats a path and returns an integer-based (st_mtime_ns, st_size) cache key, or None if the file is inaccessible. <!--#2b2346a3ef96b23f-->
- `_read_active_content` (function) — Reads a live engine.json's whole (size-guarded) content for the verify_content freshness hash, catching middle-only rewrites that leave (mtime, size) and head/tail windows unchanged, returning None on I/O error. <!--#0794ad20fbc378c3-->
- `_json_loads` (function) — Thin, separately-patchable json.loads wrapper serving as the innermost GIL-bound decode seam for parse-counting tests. <!--#2998e22c3d77cbf7-->
- `_parse_json` (function) — Parses whole-file JSON text into a top-level dict (or None), routing the decode through the patchable _json_loads seam. <!--#dd3d34f8d9787ed3-->
- `_parse_json_file` (function) — Reads a file's text and parses it into a dict (or None), the outer parse seam that regression tests patch to count full-file parses. <!--#4f108527de729a80-->
- `read_json_cached` (function) — The daemon's unified thread-safe entry point for every disk-JSON read: it parses a file at most once per content change by keying immutable snapshots on (path, mtime, size) and re-hashing the live engine.json's whole content (verify_content) to catch same-stat middle-of-file rewrites, skips oversized files (returning None), caches parse failures, and supports force_fresh to bypass the cache for a true-value disk re-confirmation. <!--#41b2e00a595c37a1-->
- `read_engine_header` (function) — Returns an engine.json/snapshot's small top-level header cheaply — via the unified read_json_cached cache at/under MAX_PARSE_BYTES (with active/force_fresh for the live flow) or a bounded, degraded-cached head+tail scan for oversized legacy files that must stay WebUI-visible without freezing the loop. <!--#7a73d96564901f84-->
- `_join_head_tail` (function) — Joins bounded head and tail windows into scannable text, dropping the tail's truncated first line so only genuine top-level keys can be matched. <!--#7b1bfd11987d6e6d-->
- `_degraded_header` (function) — Extracts top-level header keys from an oversized indent=2 JSON file via a bounded head+tail regex scan (never a full parse), warning once and returning None if flow_id can't be found. <!--#6c3a84424823ceb6-->

### `src/tianluo/daemon/history.py` (python) — Defines `DaemonHistoryReader`, the daemon's read-only historical-session layer that enumerates each tracked project root's `engine.json`, `state/archive/engine_*.json` and `tianluo/history/<flow_id>/` artifacts into a `SessionMeta` session index for the web UI, and serves incremental per-flow `jsonl` conversation reads as `full` snapshots or `append` deltas driven by a per-step line/offset cursor with full-prefix-hash rewrite detection and record-count (`MAX_RECORDS_PER_REPORT`) plus byte-volume (`MAX_BYTES_PER_REPORT`) truncation caps that keep each wire frame small enough to complete over a flaky daemon↔server link. <!--#cc8bbd76fe2ad0e6|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/daemon/protocol.py` (python) — The single source of truth for the daemon↔server WebSocket wire protocol: it pins PROTOCOL_VERSION and size limits, enumerates every MSG_* frame type (hello/welcome, status and call notifications, spawn/respond/interject/end-session commands, issue/project/upload/fetch command-result pairs, ping/pong/viewers presence, and the history index/window/detail request-response family), defines the Message dataclass plus encode/decode and ProtocolError for validated JSON framing, provides a make_* builder per frame that normalizes and validates its payload, and exposes supports_* version-gate predicates so each side only sends frames the peer's advertised version understands. <!--#b0b5407de8cc8f5c|9b7b08ebd47fe771-->
- `supports_traffic_reduction` (function) — Predicate that decides, per peer, whether its advertised protocol version is recent enough (>= the revision-3 threshold) to safely receive the lean traffic-reduction messages, degrading to False for missing/non-numeric versions. <!--#4bafdcc6c4ebfe54-->
- `supports_presence` (function) — Predicate that returns whether a peer's version string meets MIN_VERSION_PRESENCE, i.e. whether it emits revision-4 presence signals (MSG_VIEWERS / PING viewers), degrading to False (assume watched) on missing or non-numeric versions. <!--#bf886deadad47f8f-->
- `supports_uploads` (function) — Capability check returning whether a peer daemon's reported protocol version is new enough (>= MIN_UPLOAD_PROTOCOL_VERSION) to accept upload frames, degrading to False on a missing or non-numeric version. <!--#b0be6417e0db8e94-->
- `supports_fetch` (function) — Predicate returning whether a peer daemon's reported protocol version meets `MIN_FETCH_PROTOCOL_VERSION` (revision-6 fetch channel), degrading to `False` on missing or non-numeric versions so the server never dispatches a frame the peer would drop. <!--#fe4b4d5185b3acf1-->
- `supports_spawn_strategy` (function) — Capability check that returns whether a peer's advertised protocol version is at least MIN_SPAWN_STRATEGY_PROTOCOL_VERSION (revision 7), i.e. whether it understands the spawn `implementation_strategy` field, returning False for unparseable versions. <!--#1e4c99521efd8fe7-->
- `supports_spawn_plan_mode` (function) — Predicate that parses a peer's advertised protocol version as an int and reports whether it is at least `MIN_SPAWN_PLAN_MODE_PROTOCOL_VERSION`, i.e. whether the peer understands the revision-8 plan-mode fields (returning False on unparseable input). <!--#a5d51853aa98454d-->
- `supports_history_window` (function) — Capability probe returning whether a peer's reported protocol version is new enough to understand the step-window history read. <!--#5b4b71952414fe8c-->
- `ProtocolError` (class) — A ValueError subclass raised when a wire frame cannot be parsed as a valid protocol message. <!--#8844b8e7e818cf89-->
- `Message` (class) — A dataclass representing one protocol frame (type, payload, seq, timestamp) with serialization/parsing helpers to and from JSON dicts and strings. <!--#6d471563b76576f9-->
  - `Message.to_dict` (method) — Returns the JSON-friendly dict form of the message with its four canonical top-level keys. <!--#759de46712e4b25b-->
  - `Message.to_json` (method) — Serializes the message to a compact JSON string. <!--#4ea1594e9d498330-->
  - `Message.from_dict` (method) — Classmethod that validates and builds a Message from a decoded JSON object, raising ProtocolError on a malformed or unknown-type frame. <!--#fc4a7b6821d1c6ea-->
  - `Message.from_json` (method) — Classmethod that parses a JSON string into a validated Message, raising ProtocolError on bad JSON or an invalid frame. <!--#e82ebe85cf35c624-->
- `encode` (function) — Builds a Message of the given type/payload/seq and returns it JSON-encoded in one call. <!--#3f319ca1e3054bfe-->
- `decode` (function) — Parses a raw JSON wire string into a validated Message. <!--#c008cfff05ac0ddc-->
- `make_hello` (function) — Constructs the daemon→server HELLO message announcing a daemon's machine identity, version, and optional secret owner key. <!--#e11c4df49538cc4c-->
- `make_welcome` (function) — Constructs the server→daemon WELCOME message acknowledging a HELLO with server version and acceptance status. <!--#a9085ee42f4fc840-->
- `make_status_update` (function) — Constructs the daemon→server STATUS_UPDATE message carrying an aggregated machine-status snapshot. <!--#7525f2e92673100b-->
- `make_call_notification` (function) — Constructs the daemon→server CALL_NOTIFICATION message reporting a freshly-detected pending human call. <!--#677dd0e2384a7f58-->
- `make_spawn_flow` (function) — Builder for the server → daemon `MSG_SPAWN_FLOW` message that assembles the spawn payload (task, project root, task type, discover/worktree flags, resume/from-issue targets and validated `implementation_strategy` / `plan_decomposition` / `plan_granularity` plan-mode fields), omitting unset optional keys so plain fresh-spawn frames stay byte-for-byte backward compatible. <!--#b1fbf38f219b6833-->
- `make_spawn_failed` (function) — Builds a daemon→server MSG_SPAWN_FAILED Message reporting that a dispatched spawn/resume/project-init failed after the server already returned 202, carrying project_root and error plus optional echoes of the originating request so the UI can correlate the failure. <!--#95a1fb5ffbae33df-->
- `make_respond_call` (function) — Constructs the server→daemon RESPOND_CALL message delivering a human response for a pending call. <!--#8aaa1c0ac739b1bf-->
- `make_interject_flow` (function) — Builds a server→daemon MSG_INTERJECT_FLOW Message delivering a mid-flow user interjection (flow_id, text, project_root) that the daemon writes as an interjection call file for the running flow to fold in at its next step boundary. <!--#d9516f41d4992adf-->
- `make_end_session` (function) — Builds a server→daemon MSG_END_SESSION Message telling the daemon to terminate and archive a supervised flow (via an `luo end-session` subprocess), with optional project_root and free-form reason omitted from the wire when empty for backward compatibility. <!--#e4c5f6e4bf6887f6-->
- `make_issue_command` (function) — Constructs the server→daemon ISSUE_COMMAND message requesting an issue write operation (create/edit/close/reopen) with operation-specific fields. <!--#ea7e983f451ab580-->
- `make_issue_result` (function) — Constructs the daemon→server ISSUE_RESULT message acknowledging an issue write command, correlated by request_id. <!--#81cd9f6eebb1d8f3-->
- `make_project_command` (function) — Builds the server → daemon MSG_PROJECT_COMMAND message that asks the daemon to add or remove a project root, validating the operation against PROJECT_OPERATIONS and attaching an optional request_id for reply correlation. <!--#064b96ca560b707f-->
- `make_project_result` (function) — Builds the daemon → server MSG_PROJECT_RESULT acknowledgement for a project-registry command, echoing the request_id and carrying either the normalized project_root on success or a stable error_code plus fallback error prose on failure. <!--#44d9205499855119-->
- `make_upload_command` (function) — Builds the server → daemon MSG_UPLOAD_COMMAND message carrying an absolute project_root, the original filename, base64 file content and declared size, raising ProtocolError for an empty filename, a relative project_root, or a size beyond MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES. <!--#9820b01a7727735a-->
- `make_upload_result` (function) — Builds the daemon → server MSG_UPLOAD_RESULT acknowledgement, carrying the project-relative stored path plus size and deduplicated flag on success, or a validated UPLOAD_ERROR_CODES error_code with fallback prose on failure. <!--#505c63824c7fa167-->
- `make_fetch_command` (function) — Builds the server → daemon `MSG_FETCH_COMMAND` message asking for one file to be read back out of a project's uploads dir, raising `ProtocolError` on a non-absolute `project_root` or an empty/absolute/`..`-containing relative `path` as a cheap early reject ahead of the daemon's authoritative containment check. <!--#f0ed279b73fe928e-->
- `make_fetch_result` (function) — Builds the daemon → server `MSG_FETCH_RESULT` reply carrying either the base64-encoded file bytes with `size`/`name` or an error with a stable `FETCH_ERROR_CODES` code, validating the size against `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` and rejecting unknown error codes. <!--#c6a58c15f4bcf30a-->
- `make_ping` (function) — Constructs a server→daemon PING heartbeat Message, optionally piggybacking the current browser-presence viewers count as a per-heartbeat level that repairs any lost 0↔non-0 edge while staying byte-compatible with revision-3 when viewers is None. <!--#8f6caa9cbd450ef4-->
- `make_pong` (function) — Constructs the daemon→server PONG heartbeat-reply message. <!--#2b41c9ace39e5f99-->
- `make_viewers` (function) — Constructs a server→daemon MSG_VIEWERS edge Message carrying the browser-presence count, broadcast only on the 0↔non-0 boundary crossing to drive the daemon between full-speed and low-power idle gears (revision 4). <!--#63b66b83ffdd2db3-->
- `make_history_index` (function) — Builds a daemon→server MSG_HISTORY_INDEX Message carrying the list of known history session-meta dicts (one per `luo history` entry), sent on connect and whenever the index changes. <!--#a59ca47dba8d865c-->
- `make_history_index_request` (function) — Constructs the payload-less server→daemon HISTORY_INDEX_REQUEST message forcing a fresh rebuild and re-push of the history index. <!--#946e3b425098a9e1-->
- `make_history_request` (function) — Constructs the server→daemon HISTORY_REQUEST message pulling a flow's history records, optionally with a per-step cursor for incremental fetch. <!--#b51051e6cfa89ccd-->
- `make_history_data` (function) — Builds the daemon → server `MSG_HISTORY_DATA` message carrying a flow's history records in `full` or `append` mode, along with the resume `cursor`/`cursor_base` window and optional additive fields (`usage`, `usage_catalog`, `final`) that are omitted from the wire when unset so version-skewed peers degrade safely; raises `ProtocolError` on an unrecognized *mode*. <!--#818b825f27a8a299-->
- `make_keepalive` (function) — Builds the minimal daemon→server heartbeat Message sent in place of a full STATUS_UPDATE when the status snapshot's content signature is unchanged, keeping the server's liveness timer alive without re-sending the snapshot. <!--#2bd0ff4e380f4c1b-->
- `make_history_index_delta` (function) — Builds a daemon→server incremental history-index Message carrying only upserted SessionMeta dicts and removed flow_ids, so index traffic scales with changed flows instead of the total flow count. <!--#39b955ee1b6fb00e-->
- `make_history_window_request` (function) — Builds the server → daemon MSG_HISTORY_WINDOW_REQUEST frame asking for one step-block window of a flow's history — tail blocks, blocks before a named one, or exactly-named blocks — with an optional if_signature conditional-read probe, raising ProtocolError on a missing flow_id/request_id or non-positive count. <!--#a5876c2f044d5288-->
- `make_history_window_data` (function) — Builds the daemon → server MSG_HISTORY_WINDOW_DATA reply chunk carrying the window's records plus the whole-window descriptors (full step index, covered block ids, per-file line counts, signature) repeated on every chunk, with final marking the closing frame and not_modified signalling an unchanged flow. <!--#9e78fad5f0059411-->
- `make_detail_request` (function) — Builds a server→daemon Message requesting the full untruncated text of one issue or pending call (by kind and target_id, optionally scoped by project_root and correlated by request_id), raising ProtocolError on an unrecognised detail kind. <!--#3f067d241441dfd1-->
- `make_detail_data` (function) — Builds the daemon→server reply Message delivering the requested full-text detail (or an error when ok is False), echoing request_id and kind and raising ProtocolError on an unrecognised detail kind. <!--#056bc8a670d10b31-->

### `src/tianluo/daemon/record_budget.py` (python) — Size-budget enforcement for daemon→server record frames: measures wire-serialised byte sizes, folds runs of zero-render telemetry events into markers, and water-fills a fair truncation watermark to shrink oversized string leaves — all while preserving every event, respecting an immune-event list, and reporting what it did via CompactionStats. <!--#500a7a100673c0e2|ad5fdf690e6f17fe-->
- `CompactionStats` (class) — Dataclass-style record of what compact_record did to a single record (original/compacted/raw_json byte counts, folded and shrunk event counts, dropped bytes, chosen watermark, and the compacted/overflow flags). <!--#a5fee767b42aa43b-->
  - `CompactionStats.to_dict` (method) — Serialises the stats fields into a plain dict for logging or telemetry. <!--#6bac481f12508d35-->
- `_dumps` (function) — JSON-serialises an object with exactly the encoder settings the daemon→server wire uses (ensure_ascii=False, default separators), so measured sizes match the real frame. <!--#01929718d429934c-->
- `_byte_len` (function) — Returns the UTF-8 byte length of a string. <!--#f13ed7bf50ffc330-->
- `event_size` (function) — Measures the serialised byte size of one raw_json event. <!--#11c3803db126eafe-->
- `record_size` (function) — Measures the serialised byte size of an entire record. <!--#9548488f2db271a9-->
- `needs_compaction` (function) — Fast-path gate deciding whether a record of the given raw byte length is large enough to be analysed for compaction. <!--#b2574ecda9f05725-->
- `_event_kind` (function) — Extracts an event's (type, subtype) pair as strings, tolerating non-dict or malformed events. <!--#80714fb1e45c2fa1-->
- `is_foldable_event` (function) — Tests whether an event is one of the whitelisted zero-render telemetry kinds eligible for folding. <!--#907b91d7a10d130e-->
- `is_immune_event` (function) — Tests whether an event's type is on the immune list and must be passed through byte-for-byte. <!--#8ec69defaf5007bc-->
- `_fold_marker` (function) — Builds the synthetic system/folded marker event summarising a folded run's member count and distinct kind labels. <!--#b1473b607b8dc837-->
- `_fold_runs` (function) — Walks the event list collapsing consecutive foldable telemetry runs into markers — but only when the marker is strictly cheaper than the run — reusing pre-measured sizes and returning the new events, their sizes, and the folded count. <!--#51be1d3f36d4b252-->
- `fold_telemetry_events` (function) — Public wrapper that measures every event then folds consecutive telemetry runs in place, returning the new event list and how many original events were folded away. <!--#05081ee23fbb8dab-->
- `solve_watermark` (function) — Computes the water-filling level — the largest cap-bounded L where sum(min(size, L)) fits the budget — giving a position-independent, fair truncation threshold. <!--#3b158125147f7c10-->
- `_collect_string_leaves` (function) — Recursively gathers (container, key, text) triples for every string leaf large enough and not immune, so they can be truncated. <!--#2aece38eb5d44e62-->
- `_split_marker` (function) — Peels an existing truncation marker off a previously-shrunk string, returning the body and the byte count already dropped so repeated passes don't nest markers. <!--#7007fb9c777c23ea-->
- `_truncate_leaf` (function) — Cuts one string leaf down to a byte budget on a valid UTF-8 boundary and appends a truncation marker carrying the cumulative dropped-byte count. <!--#fde16d455d7b75df-->
- `shrink_event` (function) — Shrinks a single event to at most a byte limit by water-filling its largest string leaves over several passes, returning the original object untouched when it already fits or nothing could be given up. <!--#da5bc316eaddbc8d-->
- `compact_record` (function) — Top-level entry point that brings one record within the wire budget — fast-path gate, optional telemetry folding, watermark solve over non-immune events, per-event shrinking — while preserving every event and refusing to emit a result larger than the original. <!--#db1d2d69a8f1234f-->

### `src/tianluo/daemon/spawner.py` (python) — Daemon-side process launcher module that resolves the `tianluo` CLI argv and full login-shell PATH, auto-initializes projects via `luo init`, and spawns/tracks/terminates detached `luo run`, `--resume`, and `end-session` child processes with per-flow NDJSON log redirection and supervisor/callback registration. <!--#909c6d5c80f284ae|d923908190a13f3b-->
- `resolve_login_shell_path` (function) — Module-level helper that probes `$SHELL -lc 'echo $PATH'` once (falling back to `/bin/bash`, with a short timeout) to recover the full login-shell PATH, returning it as a string or `None` on any failure, so daemon-spawned children inherit a complete PATH even under sparse init environments. <!--#c003b2fa1fe2fdb2-->
- `merge_path_env` (function) — Combines a login-shell PATH ahead of the current PATH, deduplicating entries while preserving order, so spawned children inherit the richer PATH idempotently. <!--#97a7fecfa2117609-->
- `SpawnedProcess` (class) — Dataclass wrapping a daemon-launched `luo run` child — its `Popen` handle, cwd/task metadata, argv, start time, and log-file paths — exposing `pid`/`returncode`/`is_running` properties and a `to_dict()` JSON view. <!--#594e431476f10930-->
  - `SpawnedProcess.pid` (method) — Property returning the child process's PID. <!--#723aab9ae510a1e7-->
  - `SpawnedProcess.returncode` (method) — Property returning the child's exit code, or `None` while it is still running. <!--#2ae567e522946e10-->
  - `SpawnedProcess.is_running` (method) — Property giving a non-blocking boolean probe of whether the child is still executing. <!--#46892e7692d315b1-->
  - `SpawnedProcess.to_dict` (method) — Returns a JSON-serializable dict of the process's PID, root, task, status, start time, and log paths. <!--#2405a3194bc0f30a-->
- `_resolve_se3_command` (function) — Module-level helper that resolves the argv prefix invoking the `tianluo` CLI, preferring a console script (`luo`/`tianluo`/`se3`) next to `sys.executable`, then `[sys.executable, '-m', 'tianluo']`, then `shutil.which`, so spawned children always run the same wheel/version as the daemon. <!--#c5a90e16aa9bfacb-->
- `EnsureResult` (class) — Dataclass reporting the outcome of `DaemonSpawner.ensure_se3_project` — whether `luo init` ran (`initialized`), any `error` string (non-empty means callers must short-circuit), and captured `stdout`/`stderr`. <!--#4c42814f47940bba-->
- `_is_se3_project` (function) — Module-level predicate that returns whether a directory is already SE3-initialized by checking for the `<root>/tianluo/charter.md` marker file created by `luo init`. <!--#1cdc56fef06ef332-->
- `_plan_mode_args` (function) — Helper that builds the `--plan-decomposition` / `--plan-granularity` CLI options for a spawn, deliberately omitting empty values so the project's own `workflow.plan_decomposition` / `plan_granularity` configuration stays in charge. <!--#9500f8794fdc5e92-->
- `DaemonSpawner` (class) — Daemon-side launcher that starts and tracks `luo run` child processes — auto-initializing a project via `luo init` when needed, merging the cached login-shell PATH into the child environment, redirecting child output to per-flow log files, and registering/de-registering each process with an optional supervisor plus `on_spawn` / `on_exit` callbacks. <!--#de8c6768d5d6ded0-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.__init__` (method) — Constructor that stores the optional supervisor and spawn/exit callbacks, initializes the process registry and spawn counter, and resolves-and-caches the login-shell PATH once (unless overridden via the `login_shell_path` sentinel argument). <!--#5da5df19d87f6018-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.ensure_se3_project` (method) — Method that ensures a project root is SE3-initialized — a no-op when the `tianluo/charter.md` marker exists, otherwise creating the directory and running `luo init -p <root>` as a subprocess (with merged PATH) and returning an `EnsureResult` capturing success, skip, or error. <!--#ad85b9fdf7c8a173-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.spawn` (method) — Builds the argv for a new flow — either `luo run <task> --type <type>` or the `--from-issue <id>` variant, plus optional `--discover`, `--worktree`, plan-mode and extra args — and hands it to `_launch` with the resolved project root as cwd, returning the resulting `SpawnedProcess`. <!--#6a00a47fda548f5c-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.resume` (method) — Method that relaunches a paused flow via `luo run --resume --flow-id <id> --output-format json` through `_launch`, so a flow that exited on a human pause continues from its persisted state after the web UI responds. <!--#263a93823582df3e-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.end_session` (method) — Method that spawns `luo end-session <flow_id> -p <cwd>` (optionally `--pid`) as a child, delegating graceful termination and worktree archival to the CLI so the daemon's event loop is never blocked. <!--#7c49556c4c9e08d0-->
  - `DaemonSpawner._launch` (method) — Shared internal method that starts a given argv as a detached child with merged-PATH environment and per-flow log-file redirection, closes parent-side handles, records the `SpawnedProcess`, and fires supervisor registration and the `on_spawn` callback. <!--#fc412d9690605665-->
  - `DaemonSpawner._allocate_log_paths` (method) — Helper method that creates `<project_root>/tianluo/logs/daemon/` and returns timestamped, counter-suffixed stdout (`.ndjson`) and stderr (`.stderr.log`) paths, or `(None, None)` when the directory cannot be created (caller falls back to `/dev/null`). <!--#e717787c23c3a6ee-->
  - `DaemonSpawner._open_log_targets` (method) — Opens the stdout/stderr log files for Popen redirection (falling back to DEVNULL on failure) and returns the targets plus handles for the caller to close. <!--#f4e9be468f03f95c-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.get` (method) — Returns the tracked `SpawnedProcess` for a given PID, or `None`. <!--#afe4d346453eb0a2-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.processes` (method) — Returns a snapshot list of all currently tracked spawned processes. <!--#98f0b6899e671ee8-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.poll` (method) — Non-blocking exit-code probe for a tracked PID, returning `None` while it runs or is untracked. <!--#9ddea01204faba20-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.wait` (method) — Blocks up to a timeout for a tracked PID to exit and returns its code, raising `TimeoutExpired` if still running. <!--#1e54bd90cc51f142-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.iter_events` (method) — Tails a child's stdout log file, yielding each line parsed as an NDJSON event dict and stopping once the child has exited and the log is drained. <!--#b4e8468ca8557bde-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.terminate` (method) — Gracefully stops a tracked PID via SIGTERM, waits the grace period, then escalates to SIGKILL, returning the exit code. <!--#a3530ad10bca19d0-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.terminate_all` (method) — Gracefully terminates every still-running tracked process. <!--#2c13b58e7138e052-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.orphans` (method) — Returns the tracked processes still running that would be orphaned if the daemon exited. <!--#b330fd95d71db3f9-->
  - `DaemonSpawner.reap` (method) — Drops tracking for finished children, firing supervisor de-registration and the on-exit callback, and returns the reaped processes. <!--#e777ee62d549b294-->

### `src/tianluo/daemon/supervisor.py` (python) — Thread-safe SE3-daemon module that discovers, registers, tracks liveness of, and reaps local `luo run` flow processes—via a PID→FlowRecord map fed by daemon-spawned flows and best-effort psutil-based external scans—firing exit callbacks when tracked processes die. <!--#20732aa1355f465d|364622291f8163f9-->
- `_proc_opted_out_of_scan` (function) — Best-effort helper that returns whether a psutil process carries the EXTERNAL_SCAN_IGNORE_ENV opt-out marker, treating any failure to read its environment as 'not opted out' so real flows are never hidden from discovery. <!--#5531503ebadaa6b7-->
- `FlowRecord` (class) — Dataclass modelling one supervised `luo run` process (pid, project_root, flow_id, task_description, spawned/discovered origin, start time) with a `to_dict` JSON-serialization helper. <!--#20b35b6032adc848-->
  - `FlowRecord.to_dict` (method) — Returns a JSON-serializable dict of the record's fields. <!--#db07055256e060a1-->
- `_is_alive` (function) — Returns whether a pid names a live process using `os.kill(pid, 0)`, treating permission errors as alive. <!--#cefb5946976f093c-->
- `resolve_worktree_main_root` (function) — Returns the main project root for a `<main>/tianluo/worktrees/<name>` worktree-isolation sandbox path (stripping one level, validated by an existing runtime dir), or None for an ordinary run. <!--#3f034f3407f0f12a-->
- `is_worktree_copy_root` (function) — Predicate that returns True exactly when a path is a worktree isolation copy directory, i.e. when `resolve_worktree_main_root` can attribute it back to a main project root. <!--#2cfb933585d929dc-->
- `_read_flow_id` (function) — Best-effort reads only the `flow_id` key from a project's live engine.json via the size-guarded, same-stat-verified header reader so registration never fully parses a giant file or misattributes a just-swapped flow. <!--#532460e3a58967aa-->
- `DaemonSupervisor` (class) — Thread-safe supervisor that registers, reaps, and discovers local `luo run` processes, tracking each as a FlowRecord and firing exit callbacks when tracked processes die. <!--#af17784a134c42a2-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.__init__` (method) — Initializes the supervisor's pid→FlowRecord map, reentrant lock, exit-callback list, and the include_scan_ignored flag that controls whether opt-out-marked processes are surfaced during external discovery. <!--#a913c2ebb3712f97-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.register` (method) — Tracks a pid as a supervised flow (updating metadata in place if already known) and returns its FlowRecord. <!--#553d17a1289ca485-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.unregister` (method) — Stops tracking a pid, returning its record if it was tracked. <!--#974100ca92149eb8-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.on_exit` (method) — Registers a callback invoked once per process found dead during reaping. <!--#bf51ed3636e3c140-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.is_alive` (method) — Static wrapper exposing `_is_alive` to report whether a pid is a live process. <!--#92412c191d795dea-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.reap` (method) — Prunes records for exited processes, firing exit callbacks (errors swallowed) and returning the reaped records. <!--#e3b14bf6bd4807b3-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.discover_flows` (method) — Reaps dead processes, optionally scans for externally-started flows via psutil, and returns all currently-tracked FlowRecords sorted by start time. <!--#b098088860299a65-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor._scan_external` (method) — Best-effort psutil scan that finds externally-started `luo run` processes, skipping the daemon itself and scan-opt-out marked processes, and registers each (attributing worktree copies back to their main root) as a discovered flow. <!--#7ed588de8a1834e0-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.get` (method) — Returns the FlowRecord for a pid, or None if untracked. <!--#8e9bd7dae72840c9-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.flows` (method) — Property returning a snapshot list of all tracked records. <!--#e98310c8ea90711a-->
  - `DaemonSupervisor.count` (method) — Property returning the number of currently-tracked records. <!--#7a98b600786cd252-->
- `_cmdline_is_se3_run` (function) — Structurally decides whether an observed argv is a genuine `tianluo run` invocation by requiring `run` to be the immediate token after the `se3` program/module, matching console-script and `-m` module forms while excluding interpreter `-c` inline-code stubs. <!--#13f1b7a6cdcfb825-->

### `src/tianluo/daemon/uploads.py` (python) — Server-side attachment storage layer for the daemon: sanitizes untrusted browser filenames, writes uploads as content-hash-prefixed files under a project's uploads directory (atomically, with dedup and a size cap), reads them back for download, and maps every refusal to a stable protocol error code plus a project-relative path the agent can use. <!--#395bbe49dee0b89b|2d4f3856f6748b7b-->
- `_truncate_utf8` (function) — Helper that trims a string to the longest prefix fitting a UTF-8 byte limit, cutting on a codepoint boundary so no half-written multibyte sequence is left behind. <!--#0456ce3ad209a680-->
- `UploadError` (class) — Exception for a refused upload that carries a stable `protocol.UPLOAD_ERROR_CODES` code (the actual contract with the server and web UI) alongside a diagnostic-only message. <!--#a84da3811c999b92-->
  - `UploadError.__init__` (method) — Constructor that stores the stable error `code` and falls back to using the code itself as the message when none is supplied. <!--#f3af1afd1259247e-->
- `UploadStored` (class) — Result record for a successful `store_upload`, holding the project-relative posix `path` the prompt/agent will use, the byte `size`, and whether the write was `deduplicated`. <!--#dff2dc225bdb2c12-->
- `UploadContent` (class) — A small dataclass-style record returned by `read_upload`, carrying an attachment's bytes, size, and the on-disk basename that the server uses for the download filename and Content-Type. <!--#1d7f6262f15497c3-->
- `sanitize_upload_filename` (function) — Reduces a fully untrusted browser-supplied filename to one safe path component — stripping directories, folding unsafe/control/whitespace/surrogate characters, dropping leading dots and dashes, and capping at `MAX_NAME_BYTES` encoded bytes while preserving the extension. <!--#cc07c9c0593c84c7-->
- `store_upload` (function) — Stores upload bytes as a content-hash-prefixed file in the project's uploads directory — enforcing the size limit before any I/O, verifying the resolved target really is a direct child of that directory, short-circuiting on an existing identical file, and publishing via an O_EXCL temp file plus `os.replace` so readers never see a partial write. <!--#b96ddf68c87bd017-->
- `read_upload` (function) — Reads a previously stored attachment back out of a project's uploads directory, failing closed with stable `FETCH_ERROR_CODES` (`invalid_path`, `not_found`, `too_large`, `read_failed`) for absolute or escaping paths, non-regular files, and oversized reads checked both before and after loading the bytes. <!--#a4b8bd15966583a2-->
- `_relative_path` (function) — Builds the project-relative posix path reported back to the browser and agent from the runtime directory *name*, so the daemon's absolute layout never leaks and symlinked roots still resolve for the agent. <!--#7fc02a99caad3802-->

### `src/tianluo/daemon/usage_backend.py` (python) — Shared usage/cost read helper for the daemon's polling surfaces that delegates all pricing and aggregation to the project's configured `PricingCatalog` and `tianluo.usage`, adding an mtime-keyed per-root catalog cache and a CLI-parity fallback chain (session ledger → per-step records recovered from inline or cold-file `outputs.usage_records` → legacy session tally) so daemon/WebUI usage summaries match the CLI's. <!--#ce7d14348b041fec|bcacb7519a2f647e-->
- `project_pricing_catalog` (function) — Returns the effective pricing catalog for a project root, memoised in a lock-guarded cache keyed by `tianluo.yaml` mtime and degrading to the built-in price table whenever the root or config is unusable. <!--#2f1bfd768e718bd6-->
- `_builtin` (function) — Tiny helper that lazily imports `PricingCatalog` and returns its built-in default price table. <!--#29bd5de1c8b80a1e-->
- `_resolve_steps_roots` (function) — Computes the candidate cold-file partition directories (live `state/steps/<leaf>` plus the archived `state/archive/steps/<leaf>`) that a step header's `cold_ref` may resolve against, returning an empty list when the project root is unusable. <!--#012dd4c9a18c5281-->
- `_per_step_usage_records` (function) — Best-effort recovery of `UsageRecord` objects from every step's `outputs.usage_records`, reading inline legacy outputs or loading the externalized cold-file body via `cold_ref`, and silently skipping unreadable or malformed entries. <!--#de68ffe126c94909-->
- `flow_usage_summary` (function) — Builds the compact wire-format usage summary for one raw engine `state` dict, following the CLI's fallback chain (session ledger → per-step records → legacy session tally) and returning `None` when the flow records no usage at all. <!--#6564abb3dedb7d75-->

### `src/tianluo/daemon/wire_metrics.py` (python) — A dependency-free, stdlib-only module providing WireMetrics, a thread-safe per-message-type sent-byte/frame accumulator held at each end of the daemon↔server↔WebUI link to make wire-traffic-by-message-type verifiable at runtime and guard against traffic-reduction regressions. <!--#bf121e28da25d4d4|81efb6cfe5411c03-->
- `WireMetrics` (class) — A thread-safe, in-process accumulator that tallies sent bytes and frame counts per WebSocket message type, with one instance held at each end (daemon client and server relay) to report which link/message type dominates wire traffic. <!--#087dde7db7931df8-->
  - `WireMetrics.__init__` (method) — Initializes the accumulator with a threading lock and empty per-message-type byte and count dictionaries. <!--#ee5f8f65e32594fa-->
  - `WireMetrics.record` (method) — Adds a frame's byte length (and one to the frame count) to the running total for a message type under the lock, defensively coercing bad/negative sizes to zero so accounting can never crash the real send path. <!--#71fe02f3289d22e7-->
  - `WireMetrics.snapshot` (method) — Returns a fresh point-in-time copy of per-type {bytes, count} counters plus a synthetic '__total__' roll-up, so callers can report both the breakdown and grand total without mutating internal state. <!--#0220956e757e3bf0-->
  - `WireMetrics.reset` (method) — Clears all byte and count counters under the lock, mainly for tests and per-window sampling. <!--#67395f01807f54d0-->

## `src/tianluo/e2e/` — The end-to-end testing subsystem: a bottom-up layered package (errors → backend contract → runtime_probe → config_schema/content_config validation and loading of the `tianluo/e2e/` YAML bundle → templates/readiness → container_backend → assertions → executor → session orchestration) that LLM-bootstraps environment and scenario content, provisions isolated docker/podman environments, runs scenario action sequences with tiered assertions, and classifies results into verdicts with blame-routed fix context. <!--#2eab17c7cff2445f|a1392bd4632cc702-->

### `src/tianluo/e2e/__init__.py` (python) — Package declaration for the end-to-end testing subsystem that deliberately re-exports nothing at import time — it only lists the submodule names in `__all__` and documents the bottom-up layering (errors → backend → runtime_probe → config_schema → content_config → templates → readiness → container_backend → assertions → executor → session), so that a core-only `pip install tianluo` can `import tianluo.e2e` without pulling in the optional `tianluo[e2e]` third-party dependencies. <!--#6e6cf0bd66d01352|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/e2e/assertions.py` (python) — Implements the e2e assertion layer: an `AssertionContext` carrying everything a run observed (execs, HTTP exchanges, DOM/browser bridge, screenshots, budget) plus `AssertionResult` records and the per-kind assertion functions spanning tier-1 deterministic checks (exit code, streams, HTTP status/body, files, DOM) and tier-2 screenshot-baseline diffing. <!--#abcd584f1e00c958|6174e0b39fa1504b-->
- `AssertionResult` (class) — Immutable record of one assertion's outcome — pass/fail, tier, expected/actual strings, evidence, artifacts and machine-readable details — consumed by reports, the WebUI and fix instructions. <!--#968f0815e525a06b-->
  - `AssertionResult.describe` (method) — Renders the result as a single `[PASS]/[FAIL] kind — message — expected/actual` line for reports and fix text. <!--#7d74727c27089679-->
- `ExecRecord` (class) — Record of one command run inside the environment, with an `internal` flag marking tianluo's own helper commands so they never become the `last_exec` that exit_code/stdout/stderr assertions describe. <!--#8ec9a4ffe1f1b1da-->
- `HttpRecord` (class) — Record of one HTTP exchange during a scenario — URL, status, body, transport error and originating service. <!--#c7e6e299a916b4c4-->
- `AssertionContext` (class) — Plain mutable record of everything an assertion may read about the run (backend, handle, driver, budget/clock, browser bridge, execs, HTTP, screenshots, artifacts, notes and fatal failures), making every assertion a pure function of declaration plus context. <!--#a22c43f33a1a8efb-->
  - `AssertionContext.last_exec` (method) — Property returning the most recent command the scenario itself declared, skipping internal helper execs. <!--#97b55b8bc4c3a48a-->
  - `AssertionContext.remaining` (method) — Returns the seconds left in the scenario's time budget, or None when unbounded. <!--#1be343f82c77dc93-->
  - `AssertionContext.timeout_for` (method) — Clamps a default per-call timeout to the remaining scenario budget, with a 1-second floor so a call-level timeout never masks scenario exhaustion. <!--#0af643fa5c15329a-->
  - `AssertionContext.record_exec` (method) — Appends an ExecRecord for a command run against a service and returns it. <!--#1386523959c0990c-->
  - `AssertionContext.add_artifact` (method) — Registers a host-side artifact path on the context, de-duplicating repeats. <!--#134e0a445b790aca-->
- `_clip` (function) — Truncates any value's string form to a display limit, appending an ellipsis. <!--#a482ef589beab703-->
- `_as_argv` (function) — Normalises a command declaration into an argv list, wrapping a bare string as `sh -lc` so shell pipelines survive intact. <!--#96af23c6cac36e3d-->
- `_match_text` (function) — Applies a `matches`/`contains`/`equals` expectation to observed text, returning the pass flag plus a human-readable description of what was expected. <!--#861c3246098ed7b1-->
- `_numeric` (function) — Coerces a YAML value to float with a fallback default, rejecting booleans rather than silently reading them as 1.0/0.0. <!--#9d8bc59657299a64-->
- `budget_seconds` (function) — Coerces a declared time budget (timeout/interval) to positive finite seconds, tolerating numeric strings and raising a located E2EConfigError naming the field and scenario otherwise. <!--#c803b0837fc698f1-->
- `_tier_of` (function) — Maps an assertion kind string to its tier number (1 deterministic, 2 baseline diff, 3 LLM). <!--#a2033cd4c889f9ef-->
- `_parse_marked_json` (function) — Extracts the last marker-prefixed JSON payload from captured stdout, returning None when absent or unparseable. <!--#8c7f8e851665711b-->
- `fetch_http` (function) — Performs one GET — from the host by default, or routed through a named container when `from:` is declared — using only the stdlib, and reports status/body/error as an HttpRecord. <!--#bb1c1cd56b19aecb-->
- `BrowserBridge` (class) — Accumulates selector-based browser ops and DOM queries into a single JS program, runs it once via `node -e` inside the driver container, and exposes the parsed op/query results. <!--#caa571d032f0bfcf-->
  - `BrowserBridge.__init__` (method) — Binds the bridge to a backend/handle/service and initialises the empty op, query and result buffers. <!--#0bfec1e1dcbafc9e-->
  - `BrowserBridge.add_op` (method) — Queues one browser operation and returns its index in the program. <!--#25b757824756eca3-->
  - `BrowserBridge.add_query` (method) — Queues one DOM query (selector, url, wait_until, attribute) and returns its index. <!--#7e388d8e053be971-->
  - `BrowserBridge.pending` (method) — Property reporting whether any ops or queries are queued for execution. <!--#f85f88990f7057c0-->
  - `BrowserBridge.render_program` (method) — Renders the queued ops and queries into the JS source string handed to `node -e`. <!--#e43dfb4d45ffa95e-->
  - `BrowserBridge.run` (method) — Executes the accumulated browser program once inside the driver container and parses its marked JSON payload into op/query results or an error. <!--#cfab3674927a1ef4-->
  - `BrowserBridge.observation` (method) — Returns the DOM query result registered at a given index, or None if the program did not produce one. <!--#787f6ece1c898a14-->
  - `BrowserBridge.failed_ops` (method) — Returns the browser operations that reported failure. <!--#a6140fc31c114b99-->
- `_assert_exit_code` (function) — Tier-1 assertion comparing the last scenario command's exit code against `equals`, failing on a timed-out or missing exec. <!--#66ef16d130dcb68f-->
- `_assert_stream` (function) — Tier-1 assertion matching the last scenario command's stdout or stderr against the declared expectation, failing outright when the command timed out. <!--#9adf9af602d2fc83-->
- `_http_record_for` (function) — Performs the HTTP fetch a declaration asks for and stores it as the context's `last_http`. <!--#ec2c130cb96e4c71-->
- `_assert_http_status` (function) — Tier-1 assertion checking that a GET returns the expected status code, reporting unreachability distinctly from a wrong status. <!--#cb6fbef9ac642a3c-->
- `_assert_http_body` (function) — Tier-1 assertion matching a GET's body — or a value extracted via `json_path` — against the declared expectation. <!--#53494c7fc0f02b31-->
- `_read_json_path` (function) — Resolves a deliberately minimal dotted/`[n]`-indexed path inside a JSON body, returning presence plus the value as text. <!--#f9babdf7a5656d7d-->
- `_assert_file` (function) — Tier-1 assertion probing a path inside a service for existence/absence, or reading it and matching its contents, treating a probe that could not run as a failure rather than as absence. <!--#c118f5f340512381-->
- `_assert_dom` (function) — Tier-1 web assertion querying the driver's live DOM by selector — count, absence, attribute or text — reusing the executor's observation or lazily running a one-query browser program. <!--#1878d5457b42942f-->
- `_resolve_screenshot` (function) — Resolves the host image a visual assertion compares by reusing an already-captured shot, copying one out of the container, or capturing a fresh screenshot through the backend. <!--#c1729bac54f5993f-->
- `_safe_stem` (function) — Sanitises arbitrary text into a filesystem-safe filename stem. <!--#70371f349c9717b6-->
- `_assert_screenshot_diff` (function) — Tier-2 assertion comparing a screenshot against a git-tracked baseline within a pixel-difference threshold, gated on the `visual_regression` opt-in and a contained baseline name, and never passing on first baseline capture. <!--#6bfec3882f5d9326-->
- `compare_images` (function) — Compares two images per colour channel with a pixel tolerance and reports the differing/total pixel counts, ratio and any size mismatch. <!--#3c89a985878f8a18-->
- `_load_pillow` (function) — Imports Pillow lazily so core-only installs stay importable, raising E2EDependencyMissingError with install guidance when the `tianluo[e2e]` extra is absent. <!--#be1ac20203989c4b-->
- `_assert_visual_semantic` (function) — Tier-3 assertion asking an LLM a question about a screenshot, gated on the `semantic_visual` opt-in and failing unless the verdict comes with reviewable evidence and within the scenario budget. <!--#dfa4bf63ee5c82df-->
- `_semantic_timeout_result` (function) — Builds the tier-3 failure result used when the scenario budget ran out around the LLM call. <!--#403da5e569d6f866-->
- `_call_bounded` (function) — Runs a callable on a daemon thread and abandons it after the budget expires, so an unbounded LLM call cannot hold the E2E step open. <!--#0891768abf3df4a4-->
- `_call_semantic_llm` (function) — Builds the tier-3 prompt and asks the configured (or injected) LLM about an image under the remaining budget, returning the parsed answer, None on failure, or the timeout sentinel. <!--#b43bb1d0b1fe2569-->
- `evaluate` (function) — Public dispatcher routing one assertion declaration to its tier-appropriate handler, optionally reusing a DOM observation the executor already collected, and rejecting unknown kinds. <!--#d0db3a4c9164fe05-->
- `tier_of` (function) — Public helper returning the tier (1/2/3) of an assertion declaration. <!--#ec15f7a9b0970f4e-->

### `src/tianluo/e2e/backend.py` (python) — Defines the e2e isolation-backend seam: the declarative dataclasses for environments (BindMount, ReadinessProbe, ServiceSpec, EnvironmentSpec), the live-resource and result records (EnvironmentHandle, ExecResult, Snapshot), and the abstract five-verb IsolationBackend contract (create/start/exec/snapshot/destroy) that keeps container-specific details out of the scenario layer. <!--#8d5ef25c0bd85b29|8a4b6a2b433c88b9-->
- `BindMount` (class) — Dataclass describing a host path bind-mounted into a service container (source, target, read_only), used so source edits take effect without rebuilding the image. <!--#3753b40609e23200-->
- `ReadinessProbe` (class) — Dataclass declaring how to detect that a service has finished starting — kind of `command`/`http`/`tcp`/`log` plus its target, expected status, timeout and poll interval. <!--#06dbdbe3f6427919-->
- `ServiceSpec` (class) — Dataclass describing one container in the environment — base image, optional Dockerfile template and build steps, readiness probe, ports, env, mounts, command and workdir — whose name is both the container and DNS name. <!--#bbfb6c807b5207b0-->
- `EnvironmentSpec` (class) — Dataclass for a complete e2e environment (project root, network name, services, labels) with a lookup helper for a service by name. <!--#282d9cfadd55fd44-->
  - `EnvironmentSpec.service` (method) — Returns the `ServiceSpec` declared under the given name, or `None` if the environment has no such service. <!--#a2a7be2f670c0a34-->
- `EnvironmentHandle` (class) — Mutable record of the live resources realized from an `EnvironmentSpec` (runtime, network id, per-service container ids and images, started flag), filled in progressively so teardown works after a partial create. <!--#aa37d0c367e709a7-->
- `ExecResult` (class) — Dataclass capturing the outcome of a command run inside a container — exit code, stdout/stderr, duration and timeout flag. <!--#813ad6bab7c280d4-->
  - `ExecResult.ok` (method) — Property that is true only when the command exited 0 and did not time out. <!--#3c628121a8534c69-->
- `Snapshot` (class) — Dataclass describing an artifact extracted from a running environment (screenshot, file or log), with its host path — `None` for in-memory diagnostic log reads — and metadata. <!--#ec23109c16db5ad9-->
- `IsolationBackend` (class) — Abstract base class defining the deliberately minimal five-verb execution-backend contract (`create`/`start`/`exec`/`snapshot`/`destroy`) for one e2e environment, keeping container-specific concerns below this seam and exposing `last_handle` so partially created environments can still be torn down. <!--#533598147317d8a9-->
  - `IsolationBackend.create` (method) — Abstract hook that materializes the network, images and (stopped) containers for a spec and returns the handle, leaving `last_handle` populated even when it raises. <!--#9d463744db42ee24-->
  - `IsolationBackend.start` (method) — Abstract hook that starts the created containers and blocks until every readiness probe passes or the readiness budget runs out. <!--#a93fb26d1a9727ac-->
  - `IsolationBackend.exec` (method) — Abstract hook that runs an argv inside a named service — the single execution seam for all scenario steps — and returns an `ExecResult`. <!--#4dc74ae944ac6769-->
  - `IsolationBackend.snapshot` (method) — Abstract hook that extracts a file, screen or log from a service onto the host and returns a `Snapshot` describing where it landed. <!--#8edcf52f2a0f982d-->
  - `IsolationBackend.destroy` (method) — Abstract hook that idempotently tears down every resource in a handle, tolerating resources that are already gone. <!--#88639acac72d1d40-->

### `src/tianluo/e2e/bootstrap.py` (python) — LLM-driven bootstrap/evolution layer for e2e content that generates, validates in memory against the schema-derived vocabulary and `validate_content`, and then writes `tianluo/e2e/` environment and scenario YAML documents through a single path-containment chokepoint, exposing `ensure_content`, `evolve_content`, and `suggest_enable` and reporting each pass via `BootstrapResult` without ever deleting existing content. <!--#68d1528853c753f7|951e04f5e96e5444-->
- `BootstrapResult` (class) — Dataclass reporting the outcome of one bootstrap/evolution pass — whether content was created or evolved, which files were written or skipped, any errors, and a human-readable note. <!--#fae70e8a4c6efb4e-->
  - `BootstrapResult.changed` (method) — Property that is true when the pass actually wrote at least one file. <!--#4a123399b2e44105-->
  - `BootstrapResult.ok` (method) — Property that is true when the pass recorded no errors. <!--#38b7f83ab7308f10-->
- `ensure_content` (function) — Public entry point that guarantees `tianluo/e2e/` holds a runnable environment plus scenarios, generating only the missing parts via the LLM and raising `E2EConfigError` (writing nothing) when admissible content cannot be produced or existing content is unreadable. <!--#fef723fb56bc18a2-->
- `evolve_content` (function) — Public entry point that incrementally evolves existing e2e content through key-scoped `set`/`append` operations, falling back to `ensure_content` when nothing exists and degrading gracefully (errors in the result, disk untouched) when a proposal fails validation. <!--#49c6a2f6406a5839-->
- `suggest_enable` (function) — Returns a text-only suggestion to turn e2e on for a project that looks like a good fit, writing nothing so the `e2e.enabled` switch stays the user's decision. <!--#d2fe3e894cf6a8cd-->
- `_generate` (function) — Drives first-time generation of a validated `{environment, scenarios}` pair, folding the model's answer over any content already on disk and handing back only the newly produced scenarios for writing. <!--#016f811a53789a5d-->
- `_call_model` (function) — Shared retry loop that prompts the model, applies its answer, and validates the candidate in memory with the loader's own `validate_content` (baseline-existence relaxed) for up to `MAX_GENERATION_ATTEMPTS`, feeding validation errors back as the next prompt's feedback. <!--#b6518264e6d1e0e2-->
- `_ask` (function) — Performs one LLM round trip in JSON mode and returns the parsed object, collapsing every transport, parse, or shape failure to `None` so the retry policy lives in one place. <!--#d604b0bad6cfc781-->
- `_build_caller` (function) — Lazily constructs the engine `LLMCaller` for a bootstrap round with `force_read_only=True`, so the model can only propose documents while this module decides what lands on disk. <!--#929eedeabcef9f17-->
- `_apply_evolution` (function) — Folds the model's per-scenario evolution operations (`add` for new files, `update` for existing ones) into copies of the live documents, recording refused or unusable entries as skipped and never deleting anything. <!--#b12fec35adc059f6-->
- `_apply_ops` (function) — Applies `set` (replace top-level keys) and `append` (extend list keys, de-duplicated so replays don't accumulate) operations to a deep copy of a document. <!--#6f804656ecfc316d-->
- `_resolve_target` (function) — Resolves one LLM-supplied write path against the content directory and refuses anything escaping it — the single containment chokepoint every write in this module passes through. <!--#69bf8b9acba19a61-->
- `_write_documents` (function) — Serializes accepted environment and scenario documents to YAML, resolving all targets up front so a containment violation leaves no partial write, and returns the repo-relative paths written. <!--#55c9c092a4bf386e-->
- `_dump` (function) — Renders a document to YAML text prefixed with the generated-file header. <!--#35256b0fcc542e48-->
- `_seed_baselines_dir` (function) — Creates the `baselines/` directory with a `.gitkeep` so `--write-baselines` has a git-tracked place to land screenshots. <!--#baaa119016853b9b-->
- `_existing_scenarios` (function) — Parses the scenario YAML files already present on disk into a mapping keyed by file name. <!--#5cfb96d5065436cd-->
- `_read_document` (function) — Parses one on-disk content document, raising a located `E2EConfigError` for unreadable, empty, or non-mapping YAML instead of silently degrading to an empty document. <!--#a588b4c6187673c3-->
- `_as_mapping` (function) — Coerces a value to a plain dict, returning an empty one when it is not a mapping. <!--#e33d6233ba2185c8-->
- `_iter_mappings` (function) — Extracts the mapping entries from a value expected to be a list, tolerating anything else by returning an empty list. <!--#465d42cbdb2c9317-->
- `_scenario_filename` (function) — Normalizes a model-supplied scenario file name (adding a `.yaml` suffix, enforcing the single-component pattern) or returns `None` when it is unusable. <!--#379026231567387f-->
- `_scenario_entries` (function) — Extracts `{filename: document}` pairs from a generation response, accepting both wrapped and bare document shapes and stripping bookkeeping keys. <!--#27cfecc5069d1ccf-->
- `_bundle` (function) — Assembles a candidate environment and scenarios into the raw bundle shape `validate_content` expects, using the same repo-relative labels the loader uses so error messages point at real paths. <!--#30194c508e6e2c82-->
- `_vocabulary` (function) — Derives the admissible base kinds, readiness kinds, actions, and assertion tiers directly from the schema module so the prompt cannot drift from the validator. <!--#849ec3d157d035d4-->
- `_generate_prompt` (function) — Builds the first-time-generation prompt from project context, shipped example documents, the derived vocabulary, ladder rules, any existing content, and prior validator feedback. <!--#947599d883cffc0b-->
- `_evolve_prompt` (function) — Builds the evolution prompt showing the current environment and scenarios, task hints, vocabulary and ladder rules, and instructs the model to answer with key-scoped `add`/`update` operations only. <!--#dfb32cfcf5d17d3b-->
- `_project_context` (function) — Assembles the tech-stack context block for prompts — project name, current task, top-level entries, truncated dependency manifests, and a charter excerpt. <!--#184fa6399214aefa-->
- `_runtime_charter_relpath` (function) — Resolves the runtime-relative path to `charter.md` via `tianluo.runtime_paths`. <!--#ec1a1f373f8e32be-->
- `_top_level_entries` (function) — Lists up to `limit` non-hidden top-level entries of the project root, marking directories with a trailing slash. <!--#6011af6f3a6fd54b-->
- `_read_text` (function) — Reads a file as text with a size limit, returning `""` on OS errors and appending a truncation marker when over the limit. <!--#5bd877023efebb28-->
- `_read_asset` (function) — Loads a shipped example YAML from the package's `templates` directory via `importlib.resources`, falling back to a filesystem path so wheels and source checkouts behave alike. <!--#2fd46324dc67e0e9-->

### `src/tianluo/e2e/config_schema.py` (python) — Pure, IO-light validation layer for the `tianluo/e2e/` content bundle: `validate_content` checks the `environment.yaml` document (services, images, base_kind, build steps, readiness probes and host reachability) and every `scenarios/*.yaml` (driver capability, actions ordering, assertion tiers, ladder opt-in flags and baseline containment), collecting localised, path-prefixed errors before any conversion or execution happens. <!--#8158729441447a2b|d4f5153f632b8688-->
- `_type_name` (function) — Returns the Python type name of a value, used to render "actual: <type>" details in schema error messages. <!--#ffed989a8b51e167-->
- `_err` (function) — Appends one localised validation problem to the error list, prefixed with its source file and YAML path so the offending block is unambiguous. <!--#8b9ffd7ab7ebb636-->
- `_require_mapping` (function) — Asserts a value is a mapping, returning it or recording a `not_mapping` error and returning None. <!--#6ad9187cbdc9d508-->
- `_require_string` (function) — Asserts a value is a present, non-blank string (optionally tolerating absence), returning it or recording the matching missing/not_string/empty error. <!--#41e3f0195f27a765-->
- `_require_positive` (function) — Asserts a numeric field is a finite positive number, rejecting bools, `.inf` and `.nan` before they reach the conversion layer. <!--#6ba11426e86d5b94-->
- `_check_choice` (function) — Asserts a value is one of an allowed enum of choices, reporting `invalid_choice` and returning False otherwise. <!--#8d25b92e8295e500-->
- `_check_required_fields` (function) — Enforces a per-kind field spec of always-required plus at-least-one-of fields for an entry, naming the context in each error. <!--#9999c9500f122858-->
- `validate_environment` (function) — Validates an `environment.yaml` document — network name, service list, unique/valid names, image, base_kind, build steps, readiness probes and field shapes — returning the errors plus the declared service names for scenario validation. <!--#83c83732e457d28a-->
- `service_base_kinds` (function) — Reads the raw environment document into a `{service name: base_kind}` map so scenario validation can check driver capability, including for not-yet-written bundles. <!--#4bd6f60f5062682f-->
- `_validate_build_steps` (function) — Validates that a service's optional `build` value is a list of non-empty command strings. <!--#25949ae4c0de80e2-->
- `_validate_readiness` (function) — Validates a service readiness probe: kind, required fields, field shapes, positive timeout/interval, HTTP status, and host-reachability for `http`/`tcp` probes. <!--#3c83b4c0a953c41c-->
- `_check_readiness_shapes` (function) — Type-checks each present readiness field against its declared shape (string, port, or argv) before the conversion layer coerces it. <!--#dc2a3c44cd86389c-->
- `_require_port` (function) — Asserts a value is an integer TCP port in 1–65535 (bools excluded). <!--#bbc12122b25a5fe6-->
- `_require_argv` (function) — Asserts a command field is either a non-empty shell string or a non-empty list of non-empty argv strings. <!--#82d97536335c83ab-->
- `_require_http_status` (function) — Asserts an expected HTTP status is an integer in 100–599 (bools excluded). <!--#2ac3f6d988d92bde-->
- `_published_host_ports` (function) — Parses a service's `ports` mapping into the set of fixed host ports it publishes, returning None when the shape is a range, ephemeral, or otherwise unreadable. <!--#6e9735f0bec7909d-->
- `_probe_address` (function) — Derives the (host, port) an `http`/`tcp` readiness probe will actually dial, mirroring how the readiness layer interprets `url`/`port` and its loopback default. <!--#2a8b4b1656534025-->
- `_check_probe_reachability` (function) — Rejects readiness probes the host process cannot reach — those addressing a peer by in-network service name, or dialling a loopback port the service never published. <!--#7025ac4dba9ae049-->
- `validate_scenario` (function) — Validates one `scenarios/*.yaml` document — name, driver existence and capability, timeout, declaration flags, actions and assertions — against the environment's declared services. <!--#3e8e95b8f01fbaed-->
- `_check_driver_capability` (function) — Rejects, at validation time, a scenario whose driver's `base_kind` lacks a browser while the scenario declares browser-only actions or DOM/visual assertions. <!--#32df39c850bcf792-->
- `_validate_actions` (function) — Validates the scenario `actions` list — kind, required fields, the no-action-after-browser ordering invariant, and the visual-driving ladder rules for `visual_click`. <!--#9d956d733e2dc52f-->
- `_validate_assertions` (function) — Validates that `assertions` is a present, non-empty list of mappings and delegates each entry to per-assertion validation. <!--#775785ac213cf899-->
- `_validate_one_assertion` (function) — Validates a single assertion against its tier — required fields, correct ladder opt-in flags, no stray tier flags, threshold range, downgrade-available detection, and baseline containment/existence. <!--#5e0553a004702ec8-->
- `_declared_flag` (function) — Reads a ladder opt-in flag, requiring a genuine boolean so truthy non-bools are reported and treated as undeclared. <!--#715235948fe6a4d9-->
- `_check_downgrade` (function) — Reports an escalated assertion whose own configuration fields prove a lower assertion tier would suffice. <!--#e39c6b72ba79b027-->
- `baseline_is_contained` (function) — Returns whether a baseline name stays inside the baselines directory, rejecting POSIX/Windows-anchored paths and `..` traversal; shared with the runtime assertions module. <!--#2e7ef99db945a15f-->
- `_check_baseline` (function) — Validates a tier-2 `baseline` value as a contained non-empty string and, unless first capture is expected, checks the image file exists on disk — the module's only IO. <!--#873025e832565938-->
- `validate_content` (function) — Top-level entry point that validates a whole `tianluo/e2e/` content bundle: the environment document, every scenario against its services and base kinds, and uniqueness of scenario names. <!--#71437407fcb3d8fe-->

### `src/tianluo/e2e/container_backend.py` (python) — Implements the docker/podman container isolation backend for e2e environments — deriving collision-safe network/container names and fingerprint-keyed image tags, creating the shared network and per-service images (pull or build), starting and readiness-probing containers, executing commands inside them, capturing file/screenshot/log snapshots, and idempotently tearing everything down. <!--#6be5ac55cf779262|07fbc0a1c30df497-->
- `_sanitize` (function) — Replaces unsafe characters in a name fragment with hyphens and guarantees a non-empty result, so config-derived strings are safe in container/image identifiers. <!--#dc05b9cfcbf1e566-->
- `container_name` (function) — Builds the host-unique `<network>-<service>` container name, prefixing with the network so concurrent projects/worktrees never collide on generic service names. <!--#7f44990bb7abbc16-->
- `build_fingerprint` (function) — Returns a short SHA-256 digest of a rendered Dockerfile, used as the cache-stable identity of a build recipe. <!--#06a7574c549dfd9f-->
- `image_tag` (function) — Mints the local `tianluo-e2e/<service>:<fingerprint>` image tag keyed on the build recipe, so unchanged environments reuse the existing image instead of accumulating per-flow images. <!--#ea89880c6b17c23a-->
- `ContainerBackend` (class) — The docker/podman isolation backend that creates a shared network and service images, runs and probes containers, executes commands, captures snapshots, and tears everything down idempotently. <!--#56e0b2049fa4d24b-->
  - `ContainerBackend.__init__` (method) — Pins the probed runtime binary and stores the injectable subprocess runner plus OCI-runtime, SELinux, timeout, and env-override settings for the session. <!--#f8e29a3143c9ae81-->
  - `ContainerBackend.is_podman` (method) — Tells whether the pinned runtime is podman, gating the podman-specific flags and env handling. <!--#f0da06e0927765cf-->
  - `ContainerBackend._environ` (method) — Builds the environment for runtime CLI calls, enabling BuildKit for docker and applying caller-supplied overrides. <!--#86b75150f9599079-->
  - `ContainerBackend._cli` (method) — Runs a single runtime CLI invocation and returns its captured `ExecResult`, never raising on non-zero exit but converting a missing/unusable binary into an `E2EEnvironmentError` and a timeout into exit 124. <!--#99c2cc59be9aaefb-->
  - `ContainerBackend.parse_json` (method) — Parses `{{json .}}` CLI output tolerantly, returning `None` for empty or unparseable text and salvaging the first valid line of multi-document output. <!--#fd389777aedde6c4-->
  - `ContainerBackend.inspect` (method) — Inspects a container, image, or network via the runtime CLI, returning the parsed JSON or `None` when absent or unreadable. <!--#3c70d58893a422b5-->
  - `ContainerBackend.create` (method) — Creates the reusable half of the environment — the shared network and one image per service — publishing the handle first so a partial failure is still cleanable. <!--#f0ab3f03fdf44b8d-->
  - `ContainerBackend._create_network` (method) — Creates the environment's shared network, reusing an existing one of the same name and raising an environment error on any other failure. <!--#282a56bd43d9e333-->
  - `ContainerBackend._materialize_image` (method) — Decides per service whether to pull its published base image or build a project-specific one, returning the image reference to run. <!--#0bf6571d0acaa264-->
  - `ContainerBackend._pull` (method) — Pulls a base image, tolerating pull failure when the image is already present locally so offline hosts still work. <!--#eb21af7365137f00-->
  - `ContainerBackend._image_present` (method) — Checks whether an image already exists in the local image store. <!--#a3f585c65df40f62-->
  - `ContainerBackend._build` (method) — Renders the service's Dockerfile, builds it in a throwaway context directory holding only that Dockerfile (never the project root), and returns the fingerprint-keyed tag. <!--#9b1fea2e19cb327b-->
  - `ContainerBackend.start` (method) — Starts every service container and then blocks on each service's readiness probe before marking the handle started. <!--#1b41e7ba8444913c-->
  - `ContainerBackend._run_service` (method) — Runs one service container, transparently removing and retrying past a leftover container squatting on this environment's own deterministic name, and records the resulting container reference. <!--#8d066662a53840df-->
  - `ContainerBackend._remove_stale_container` (method) — Force-removes only the container holding this service's deterministic `<network>-<service>` name, logging rather than raising when removal fails. <!--#770f293660ecb128-->
  - `ContainerBackend.build_run_args` (method) — Assembles the full `run -d` argv for a service — name, network alias, OCI runtime, podman `--userns=keep-id`, labels, env, ports, mounts, workdir, image and command — split out so it is inspectable without executing anything. <!--#90ebb07203900d2e-->
  - `ContainerBackend._shared_mount_sources` (method) — Computes which host paths this environment mounts into more than one service, which decides each mount's SELinux relabel mode. <!--#80bd37eb7c5ff770-->
  - `ContainerBackend.format_mount` (method) — Renders one bind mount as a `-v` argument, adding `ro` and choosing the shared `:z` versus private `:Z` SELinux label so multi-container mounts are never relabelled out from under a peer. <!--#516f642e04addbe2-->
  - `ContainerBackend.exec` (method) — Executes a command inside a service's container with optional workdir, environment, and timeout, returning the captured result. <!--#ee55af57dff32ea6-->
  - `ContainerBackend._require_container` (method) — Resolves a service name to its running container reference, raising a config error for an unknown service and an environment error for one that was never started. <!--#7b802e6b5275362c-->
  - `ContainerBackend.snapshot` (method) — Pulls an artifact out of a service onto the host, dispatching on `kind` to file copy, display screenshot, or container log capture. <!--#cad64322b5d9d229-->
  - `ContainerBackend._destination` (method) — Resolves a snapshot's host path, creating parent directories for an explicit destination or minting a temp file otherwise. <!--#69c57752430c4ab1-->
  - `ContainerBackend._snapshot_file` (method) — Copies a path out of the container with `cp`, cleaning up the temp placeholder and raising an environment error when the extraction fails. <!--#0adef9af11b37969-->
  - `ContainerBackend._snapshot_screenshot` (method) — Captures the container's virtual display with `scrot -o` and copies the resulting image to the host as a screenshot snapshot. <!--#951bd7c0da3244f8-->
  - `ContainerBackend._snapshot_log` (method) — Captures the container's log stream into snapshot metadata, writing a host file only when a destination is named so per-poll readiness probes leak nothing. <!--#c3f593a95f527f8f-->
  - `ContainerBackend.destroy` (method) — Idempotently removes every declared and recorded container plus the shared network — never raising, and deliberately leaving reusable images behind. <!--#b1340770c4d95133-->
  - `ContainerBackend._removal_targets` (method) — Lists, in stable order and without duplicates, every container reference teardown must attempt: recorded ids, deterministic names, and entries for services the spec no longer declares. <!--#d50769ed31590181-->
- `_mount_key` (function) — Normalises a bind mount's host-side source path into the key used for shared-mount detection. <!--#6bf78e6212194ee7-->
- `_name_taken` (function) — Detects the narrow case where `run` failed purely because the container name is occupied, deliberately excluding genuine port conflicts. <!--#7efe34877dedf32d-->
- `_already_gone` (function) — Detects whether a removal failed only because the resource no longer exists, which is what makes teardown idempotent. <!--#9d8c39c6755ff178-->
- `_detail` (function) — Collapses a captured stdout/stderr stream into a short single-paragraph, length-capped detail string for error messages. <!--#892fff3c5f7167c2-->

### `src/tianluo/e2e/content_config.py` (python) — Loads the project's `tianluo/e2e/` content directory (environment topology plus scenario documents) into schema-validated, typed declarations — `ServiceDecl`, `ActionDecl`, `AssertionDecl`, `ScenarioDecl` bundled as `E2EContent` — and converts them into the backend-facing `EnvironmentSpec`/`ServiceSpec` objects, treating any read, parse, or validation failure as a fatal `E2EConfigError` rather than falling back to defaults. <!--#b0608abcb5b2a41d|f08ce8ada1e44c93-->
- `content_dir` (function) — Returns the absolute path of the project's e2e content directory, resolved through `runtime_dir` so legacy `se3/` checkouts still map to their own runtime directory. <!--#08325ab82e6024fc-->
- `content_relpath` (function) — Builds a repo-relative path inside the e2e content directory, suitable for error messages and git references. <!--#66425667f6b2dd9b-->
- `baselines_dir` (function) — Returns the directory under the e2e content root that holds git-tracked baseline screenshots. <!--#1a2570af4b96954c-->
- `ServiceDecl` (class) — Typed declaration of one container in the environment topology (image, `base_kind` template family, build steps, readiness, ports, env, source mount) that can convert itself into a backend `ServiceSpec`. <!--#ba4388949e1c55c3-->
  - `ServiceDecl.pulls_image_as_is` (method) — Property reporting whether the service runs its base image unmodified (generic `base` kind with no build steps), so environment creation can skip building a local image. <!--#e092b529873c0a2f-->
  - `ServiceDecl.to_spec` (method) — Converts the declaration into a backend-facing `ServiceSpec`, attaching the project source bind mount, the readiness probe, and a default workdir when not declared. <!--#1e119ab5339415ae-->
- `ActionDecl` (class) — Typed declaration of one scenario action, holding the driving `kind` plus the remaining mapping verbatim in `params` for the executor to interpret. <!--#7b49f4cfac204a11-->
  - `ActionDecl.get` (method) — Looks up one action parameter by key with an optional default. <!--#caf9f2aca74c9354-->
- `AssertionDecl` (class) — Typed declaration of one assertion, carrying its parameters plus the explicit tier opt-in flags (`visual_regression`, `semantic_visual`, `require_evidence`) that the schema enforces. <!--#8d75d9c827756888-->
  - `AssertionDecl.get` (method) — Looks up one assertion parameter by key with an optional default. <!--#caf9f2aca74c9354-->
- `ScenarioDecl` (class) — Typed declaration of one test scenario — its driver, source file, actions, assertions, timeout, tags, and the opt-in `fail_fast` / `visual_driving` switches. <!--#a19a5b6520b6064d-->
- `E2EContent` (class) — The whole parsed `tianluo/e2e/` directory as typed declarations (network, services, scenarios, baselines), with lookup helpers and conversion to a backend `EnvironmentSpec`. <!--#b40a8fb5fca734e3-->
  - `E2EContent.service` (method) — Finds a declared service by name, returning `None` when it is not present. <!--#e1aaaeb0433c8339-->
  - `E2EContent.scenario` (method) — Finds a declared scenario by name, returning `None` when it is not present. <!--#0579712802889a3c-->
  - `E2EContent.to_environment_spec` (method) — Converts the parsed content into a backend-facing `EnvironmentSpec`, allowing the network and labels to be overridden per run. <!--#c5cea4ae527c2c91-->
- `_readiness_to_probe` (function) — Builds a `ReadinessProbe` from a validated readiness mapping, normalising a bare string command into a `sh -lc` invocation and coercing numeric fields. <!--#b2eef98e4dfe3928-->
- `_read_yaml` (function) — Parses a single e2e YAML document, turning any read or parse failure into a fatal `E2EConfigError` rather than degrading to defaults. <!--#31f9fade4c1b56e0-->
- `read_raw_content` (function) — Reads the content directory into the raw bundle the schema validates, returning `None` when unbootstrapped and raising `E2EContentIncompleteError` when only half the structure is present. <!--#a3861eae195d2f24-->
- `load_content_config` (function) — Top-level entry point that reads, schema-validates, and builds the typed `E2EContent`, returning `None` when not yet bootstrapped and relaxing baseline-existence checks only for first-capture runs. <!--#fb721a8f72778eed-->
- `_as_tuple` (function) — Normalises a scalar-or-list YAML value into a tuple of strings. <!--#bc1ca56ee8e0b3f1-->
- `_build_service` (function) — Constructs a `ServiceDecl` from one validated service mapping in `environment.yaml`. <!--#dd7eb7184400b427-->
- `_build_scenario` (function) — Constructs a `ScenarioDecl` from one validated scenario document, splitting actions and assertions into their typed declarations and normalising the timeout. <!--#053649ac870ba91b-->
- `_flag` (function) — Reads a declaration flag by identity against `True`, matching the schema's boolean-only rule so parsed scenarios never disagree with the validated document. <!--#4a1a003c36b237bd-->
- `_ceil_seconds` (function) — Rounds a declared timeout up to whole seconds, rejecting non-numeric and non-finite values with a locatable `E2EConfigError`. <!--#cb667515a8e5cf12-->
