### `src/tianluo/e2e/errors.py` (python) — Defines the e2e exception taxonomy rooted at `E2EError`, splitting failures by blame — config/content problems (`E2EConfigError`, `E2EContentIncompleteError`), host-environment problems that route to `FAILED` with remediation hints (`E2EEnvironmentError`, `E2EDependencyMissingError`), and code-defect scenario assertion failures that route to `REVISION_NEEDED` with structured results (`E2EScenarioFailure`). <!--#60e2e1800479874a|4f8db021cfe4b8c7-->
- `E2EError` (class) — Base exception for the entire e2e subsystem, letting callers either catch everything or route on the blame-specific subclasses. <!--#6b8ecfa130f5703d-->
- `E2EConfigError` (class) — Raised when e2e configuration is malformed or violates the schema (bad `tianluo.yaml` `e2e:` block, bad `tianluo/e2e/` content file, or an assertion-ladder violation), with messages naming the offending file and YAML path. <!--#185dc96cbe740c90-->
- `E2EContentIncompleteError` (class) — Config-error subclass marking a half-populated `tianluo/e2e/` directory (environment without scenarios or vice versa) — the one content problem `evolve_content` may repair rather than surface, kept a distinct class so the distinction never depends on message-text matching. <!--#ea04164feed4817c-->
- `E2EEnvironmentError` (class) — Signals that the host environment — not the project's code — cannot run e2e, carrying localized `remediation` guidance and acting as the fix-loop firewall by mapping to `FAILED` instead of `REVISION_NEEDED`. <!--#763b19a13dacbdfc-->
  - `E2EEnvironmentError.__init__` (method) — Stores the message and an optional (defaulted-to-empty) `remediation` hint alongside the base exception initialization. <!--#ca5e370c2e4aaa83-->
  - `E2EEnvironmentError.__str__` (method) — Renders the message with the remediation hint appended on its own line when one is present. <!--#a83f335597cc443a-->
- `E2EDependencyMissingError` (class) — Environment-error subclass raised when a lazily imported third-party package from the `tianluo[e2e]` extra is absent, replacing a bare `ModuleNotFoundError` with an actionable install hint while inheriting the same `FAILED` routing. <!--#d300315321ed02e9-->
  - `E2EDependencyMissingError.__init__` (method) — Records the missing dependency and optional feature, builds a localized message via `t()` when none is supplied, and attaches the `pip install` extra remediation. <!--#8842aea2cb5faf6a-->
- `E2EScenarioFailure` (class) — Raised when e2e scenarios fail their assertions — the code-defect half of the taxonomy that maps to `REVISION_NEEDED` and enters the bounded fix loop — carrying structured per-scenario `results` for building fix instructions. <!--#dfe4fada1eee3477-->
  - `E2EScenarioFailure.__init__` (method) — Stores the message plus the optional scenario name and a copied list of structured scenario results. <!--#083243c417c08da0-->
  - `E2EScenarioFailure.__str__` (method) — Returns the plain failure message without decoration. <!--#4eaca0f0f0ca5812-->

### `src/tianluo/e2e/executor.py` (python) — The E2E scenario execution engine: resolves each scenario's driver container, runs its action sequence (exec, http, browser, wait, screenshot, visual click) under a time budget, then evaluates all assertions into rich ScenarioResult objects that carry pass/fail, timings, evidence and artifacts for reports, step outputs and the WebUI. <!--#1df9fbaff1ac8a7c|acfe0e9edf58e699-->
- `DriverTarget` (class) — Frozen-style dataclass naming the service container a scenario is driven in, plus whether it is a Playwright browser service (batched browser program) or an ordinary exec target. <!--#82b033c7334093b5-->
- `ScenarioResult` (class) — Dataclass holding one scenario's full outcome — pass/fail, every assertion (passed included), timing, timeout/error state, action failures, notes, evidence, artifacts and logs — with helpers to render and serialize it. <!--#efcacc08d5204b07-->
  - `ScenarioResult.failed_assertions` (method) — Property returning only the assertion results that did not pass. <!--#c0c171f701d4c1c9-->
  - `ScenarioResult.summary_line` (method) — Formats the result as a single PASS/FAIL line with assertion counts and duration for reports and the CLI. <!--#fc91b3df42b6e618-->
  - `ScenarioResult.to_dict` (method) — Converts the result, including each assertion's kind/tier/expected/actual/evidence, into the JSON-serializable form written to step outputs and the WebUI. <!--#856b462a68a31b5c-->
- `Executor` (class) — Core runner that executes a content bundle's scenarios against a live environment — resolving drivers, applying timeout budgets, performing actions, then evaluating assertions into ScenarioResult objects. <!--#231e8843709d8276-->
  - `Executor.__init__` (method) — Stores the isolation backend, content bundle, config and live handle along with injectable clock/sleeper and options for artifacts dir, LLM factory, baseline writing and fail-fast. <!--#31018d84312e7f90-->
  - `Executor.resolve_driver` (method) — Maps a scenario's declared driver name to a DriverTarget, raising E2EConfigError rather than silently running elsewhere when the service is undeclared. <!--#eeb76ef0c44b17d0-->
  - `Executor.scenario_budget` (method) — Returns the scenario's time budget, preferring its own timeout, then the config's scenario_timeout, then a built-in default. <!--#cd04867762e18c2c-->
  - `Executor.run_scenario` (method) — Drives one scenario end to end — building the AssertionContext (and BrowserBridge for browser drivers), running actions then assertions, and assembling the ScenarioResult whose pass requires no timeout, no action failures and all assertions green. <!--#df66eabcfc28b8f2-->
  - `Executor._run_actions` (method) — Runs the whole action sequence without aborting on failure (so one round exposes everything) and reports whether the time budget was exhausted. <!--#47795bf147422fc2-->
  - `Executor._run_action` (method) — Dispatches a single action to its handler by kind, rejecting unknown kinds and any action declared after a batched browser action. <!--#f9bbaeb5a6e2e403-->
  - `Executor._action_exec` (method) — Executes a declared command in a service via the backend, records it as the scenario's last exec, and notes (rather than fails on) a non-zero exit since exit_code/stdout/stderr assertions adjudicate it. <!--#0d1cc328654a0dc5-->
  - `Executor._action_http` (method) — Performs a driving HTTP request (optionally from inside a service), stores it as the last HTTP record, and marks an unreachable request as an action failure. <!--#e6e01bdd1f4f1481-->
  - `Executor._action_browser` (method) — Validates the op against BROWSER_OPS and queues it on the BrowserBridge, remembering in-container paths for named screenshots so later assertions reuse the same capture. <!--#e7070123af129c17-->
  - `Executor._action_wait` (method) — Handles a wait action — either sleeping a bounded number of seconds or delegating to the until-command poller. <!--#cd174586d3ce8b1f-->
  - `Executor._wait_until` (method) — Polls a project-supplied check command in the driver at an interval until it succeeds or the budget runs out, recording the polls internally so they never masquerade as the scenario's own exec. <!--#db87dea150f314d7-->
  - `Executor._action_screenshot` (method) — Captures a screenshot of a service through the backend, saving it under the artifacts dir and registering it by name for later assertions. <!--#4e781b522a48784a-->
  - `Executor._action_visual_click` (method) — Injects a coordinate click via xdotool for GUIs with no programmatic entry point, requiring the scenario to declare visual_driving and failing the scenario if the click did not land. <!--#c1b7d54b3e481697-->
  - `Executor._run_assertions` (method) — Runs the batched browser program (collecting its op failures) then evaluates every assertion in order — all of them by default so a fix loop sees the whole failure surface — honouring fail_fast and reporting budget exhaustion. <!--#5ae08261e7664e3d-->
  - `Executor._register_dom_queries` (method) — Registers each dom assertion's query on the browser program before it runs and returns the assertion-position to query-index mapping, so all queries share the one driven browser session. <!--#d5be2b2863432730-->
  - `Executor._exhausted` (method) — Returns whether the context's remaining time budget has run out. <!--#b02082c7abbc7ac7-->
- `_argv_of` (function) — Normalises a declared command into argv, wrapping a bare string in `sh -lc` so authored pipelines and redirections keep working. <!--#a3b04a6521c045f7-->
- `_slug` (function) — Sanitises arbitrary text into a filesystem-safe slug for artifact and screenshot filenames. <!--#4a245306aedbed15-->
- `run_scenarios` (function) — Module-level helper that runs a sequence of scenarios through one Executor in declaration order and collects all results. <!--#b0df12b9b74fa1dc-->

### `src/tianluo/e2e/readiness.py` (python) — Implements E2E service readiness polling: dispatches the four probe kinds (`command`, `http`, `tcp`, `log`) against a backend-managed service and exposes `wait_ready`, which retries on the probe's interval until a deadline and then raises `E2EEnvironmentError` with a log tail (or `E2EConfigError` for malformed/unknown probes). <!--#7db26c53ba04782e|268bc6018f8c8c6a-->
- `read_log_tail` (function) — Best-effort helper that fetches the last N lines of a service's log via the backend's generic `snapshot(kind="log")` verb (metadata text first, file path as fallback), swallowing all errors so a diagnostic failure never masks the failure being reported. <!--#f29ca43971088fd8-->
- `_check_command` (function) — Runs a `command` probe by exec'ing the declared command in the service through the backend, raising `E2EConfigError` when `command` is missing and returning whether the result reported ok. <!--#efd81a03da40aca8-->
- `_NoRedirectHandler` (class) — A `urllib` redirect handler that refuses to follow 3xx responses so a probe declaring a redirect status can actually observe it (as an `HTTPError`) instead of the terminal status. <!--#c276873b1fa0bc1c-->
  - `_NoRedirectHandler.redirect_request` (method) — Returns `None` to suppress redirect following, letting the 3xx surface to the caller. <!--#ac126f23d21a5d39-->
- `_open_http` (function) — Opens the probe URL with the default opener, switching to a private non-redirecting opener only when the probe declares a 3xx `status`, so a redirect-as-healthy service can match its own expectation. <!--#26465cbde90b2653-->
- `_check_http` (function) — Runs an `http` probe from the host against the service's published port, comparing the observed status (including `HTTPError` codes) against the declared `status` or a default OK set, and treating connection errors as not-ready. <!--#f8ac36f7467a9c5a-->
- `_check_tcp` (function) — Runs a `tcp` probe by attempting a socket connection to the probe's host and port within the attempt timeout, requiring `port` and reporting connection failure as not-ready. <!--#fe3b138d320ecb6d-->
- `_tcp_host` (function) — Resolves the host a `tcp` probe should dial, parsing it out of the probe's `url` when given and defaulting to `127.0.0.1` (the host-published port). <!--#83186a091d0aac11-->
- `_check_log` (function) — Runs a `log` probe by compiling the declared `pattern` (config error on a bad regex or missing pattern) and searching it against a large tail of the service's log. <!--#ad55a7f43c502fc9-->
- `wait_ready` (function) — The module's entry point: polls the service's readiness probe on its declared interval within a budget-bounded deadline (with injectable clock/sleeper for tests), returning `True` on success, raising `E2EConfigError` for an unknown probe kind, and raising `E2EEnvironmentError` with a log tail on timeout so the E2E step reports an environment failure rather than triggering the fix loop. <!--#3cf093f06235f8e0-->

### `src/tianluo/e2e/runtime_probe.py` (python) — Preflight probe for the e2e container runtime: normalizes the `e2e.runtime` preference, runs `<name> info` against docker/podman to test usability and rootless mode, and returns the single pinned `RuntimeProbeResult` or raises a localized `E2EEnvironmentError` with remediation guidance when no runtime works. <!--#40d13dc85fb14d44|066d3bd0b7772ff5-->
- `RuntimeProbeResult` (class) — Frozen dataclass holding the outcome of probing one container runtime — its name/binary, whether it is usable, whether it runs rootless, and localized error/remediation text (plus their i18n keys) when it is not. <!--#0c479719d9b6efa2-->
  - `RuntimeProbeResult.__bool__` (method) — Makes a probe result truthy exactly when the runtime is usable, so callers can write `if result:` instead of checking `.ok`. <!--#81ad16b987ed9e70-->
- `_remediation_text` (function) — Returns the localized fix-menu text listing the ways to get an unprivileged container runtime working. <!--#ec1d002c55803ae0-->
- `_detail` (function) — Collapses captured stdout/stderr into a single whitespace-normalized paragraph truncated to a display limit. <!--#be59a4c36340dd51-->
- `_parse_rootless` (function) — Best-effort parse of a runtime's JSON `info` output to tell whether it runs rootless, degrading to `False` on any parse failure since the flag is only informational. <!--#bed6178f6e7fc924-->
- `probe_one` (function) — Probes a single runtime by running `<name> info` as the current user and returns a `RuntimeProbeResult`, never raising — unusable runtimes come back as `ok=False` with localized error and remediation. <!--#f1c34c6ad6c4cbb2-->
- `_failure` (function) — Helper that builds a failed `RuntimeProbeResult` from an i18n error key and format fields, attaching the standard remediation menu and both i18n keys. <!--#ff4faf7d30c5465a-->
- `normalize_preference` (function) — Normalizes a raw `e2e.runtime` preference to a lowercase supported runtime or `auto`, raising `E2EConfigError` for unrecognized or non-string values. <!--#9af6aafa45de6d78-->
- `probe_runtime` (function) — Resolves a runtime preference into the one runtime the session will pin — `auto` tries docker then podman and takes the first usable one, while an explicit choice is probed alone and never silently falls back — raising `E2EEnvironmentError` when nothing usable is found. <!--#5e64deb49ed8f15e-->
- `preflight` (function) — Public entry point for the e2e environment preflight: accepts an `E2EConfig`-like object, a bare preference string, or `None`, and returns the pinned `RuntimeProbeResult` (letting `E2EEnvironmentError` surface as an environment failure). <!--#1b74b066a14e9a5c-->

### `src/tianluo/e2e/session.py` (python) — Session-level orchestrator for one end-to-end run: it selects scenarios (always forcing the critical set), provisions and awaits the isolated container environment, executes each scenario while collecting per-service logs, and classifies everything into an `E2EVerdict` carrying summary, fix instructions and fix context for the E2E step handler. <!--#5f1d8747f9e46c97|062c9edf67020bdd-->
- `E2EVerdict` (class) — Dataclass holding the classified outcome of one e2e run — pass/fail, environment error plus remediation, per-scenario results, fix instructions/context, summary dict and user-facing notices — shaped to mirror `TestVerdict` so the E2E step handler stays a thin mapping. <!--#b84646319d4a3dde-->
  - `E2EVerdict.should_fix` (method) — Property returning whether the verdict should enter the fix loop — true only for scenario failures, deliberately false for environment failures no code change could repair. <!--#005bd88acc2fc82e-->
  - `E2EVerdict.failed_scenarios` (method) — Property returning the subset of scenario results that did not pass. <!--#922b9c704ec7dab7-->
  - `E2EVerdict.as_failure` (method) — Converts a fixable verdict into an `E2EScenarioFailure` exception naming the failed scenarios, for callers (the CLI) that prefer raising over returning. <!--#0678c63529fdb9e6-->
- `run_e2e` (function) — The module's entry point: preflights the container runtime, loads e2e content, selects scenarios (force-including critical ones), creates/starts the isolated environment, awaits readiness, runs each scenario through `Executor` while collecting container logs for failures, and returns an `E2EVerdict` — turning any environment error into a verdict rather than an exception, and always cleaning up (or keeping and reporting) the environment. <!--#d846ee2b1b08cf5d-->
- `_default_backend_factory` (function) — Lazily imports and constructs the `ContainerBackend`, so callers injecting their own backend never pay the container implementation's import cost. <!--#8dffcb59d385ed2f-->
- `_critical_names` (function) — Resolves the configured `critical_scenarios` into declaration-ordered, de-duplicated names, raising a locating `E2EConfigError` for any name no declared scenario answers to. <!--#c1739b106919a74f-->
- `_select_scenarios` (function) — Decides which scenarios this run executes — explicit `--scenario` request over configured selection over all declared — erroring on unknown names and always appending the critical set so it cannot be quietly excluded. <!--#54145ae3739d5545-->
- `_environment_spec` (function) — Builds the backend `EnvironmentSpec` from the e2e content, sanitising and appending a run suffix to the network name so concurrent runs of the same project stay isolated. <!--#b6936f67425b02be-->
- `_await_services` (function) — Re-checks every declared readiness probe at the session level before scenarios start, so readiness is a session guarantee rather than a per-backend one. <!--#3186d3097377d735-->
- `_collect_logs` (function) — Gathers labelled log tails from every service in the environment (not just the driver) while containers are still alive, so the fix loop sees the server-side cause alongside the client-side symptom. <!--#a1f76495fc6b9eb7-->
- `_verdict_for` (function) — Assembles the final `E2EVerdict` from scenario results, treating both outright failures and unverified critical scenarios as failing and attaching fix instructions, fix context and the summary. <!--#e5571f09ecbd307d-->
- `_unverified_critical` (function) — Returns the critical scenario names that produced no passing result in this run. <!--#1f3fb6763091aa67-->
- `_build_summary` (function) — Builds the structured record written to `step.outputs["e2e_results"]` — runtime, declared/selected/critical scenario lists, pass-fail counts, durations (scenario and environment), artifacts and per-scenario detail. <!--#96c975dba938259c-->
- `_fix_instructions` (function) — Renders the deliberately unlocalized, LLM-facing narrative of what broke — unverified critical scenarios, per-scenario errors, timeouts, action notes, verbatim expected/actual assertion values and container log tails. <!--#a20389d5b39719a1-->
- `_fix_context` (function) — Builds the structured fix context consumed by the implement step, flattening action failures, failed assertions, assertion-less scenario failures and unverified critical scenarios into a uniform issue list tagged with `FIX_REASON`. <!--#6a56a211b1d0218e-->

### `src/tianluo/e2e/templates.py` (python) — Loads the shipped e2e Dockerfile templates as package data and renders them per service kind, merging per-kind defaults with caller context and expanding declared `build_steps` into Dockerfile layers, raising `E2EConfigError` on unknown kinds or missing placeholders. <!--#2a0fc8a00d0f8839|56446589a59f2172-->
- `available_kinds` (function) — Returns the list of template kinds `render_dockerfile` accepts. <!--#531d8250a1730cdb-->
- `_read_resource` (function) — Loads the text of a bundled e2e template file (`templates/<name>`) as package data via `importlib.resources.files`, falling back to `pkgutil.get_data` so the read works for zipped or non-file package loaders, and returns `None` when the template cannot be read. <!--#a1e62397d6684ea3-->
- `load_template` (function) — Returns the raw template text for a kind, raising `E2EConfigError` for an unknown kind or a missing shipped resource. <!--#b7b6eb12e7ef9cb7-->
- `expand_build_steps` (function) — Expands declared build steps (scalar or sequence) into Dockerfile layer text in verbatim declared order. <!--#37dc1d1bc8cc5ac3-->
- `_logical_lines` (function) — Splits one declared step into Dockerfile logical lines, honouring backslash continuations. <!--#f7028f08ca4e2b99-->
- `_as_instruction` (function) — Prefixes `RUN` to a logical line unless it is a comment or already begins with a Dockerfile instruction. <!--#62788147ecf59fed-->
- `_build_context` (function) — Merges per-kind defaults with the caller's context, expanding `build_steps` and selecting the GUI debug-tools layer. <!--#97fb2868c0ae23a2-->
- `render_dockerfile` (function) — Renders the named template with the merged context into Dockerfile text, raising `E2EConfigError` on unknown kind or missing placeholder. <!--#e4b653c4f3448bd2-->
- `render_for_service` (function) — Convenience wrapper mapping a `ServiceSpec`'s fields onto `render_dockerfile`. <!--#9dce46949fa13c3a-->

## `src/tianluo/e2e/templates/` — The e2e template assets directory: `string.Template` Dockerfile scaffolds (base, playwright browser-driver, gui-xvfb headless desktop) rendered into e2e service images at bootstrap time, plus annotated `environment.example.yaml` and `scenario.example.yaml` reference samples injected into the bootstrap generation prompt to teach the environment and scenario vocabularies. <!--#1255ad2f0c2707c4|e10b6e2d64d12b13-->

### `src/tianluo/e2e/templates/base.Dockerfile.tmpl` (text) — A `string.Template` Dockerfile skeleton for the generic e2e service image (rendered via `render_dockerfile("base", ...)`) that substitutes `$base_image`, `$workdir`, and `$build_steps`, deliberately baking only the environment into the image while the project source is bind-mounted at runtime to keep the BuildKit layer cache warm across fix-loop iterations. <!--#163e949790d18907|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/e2e/templates/environment.example.yaml` (yaml) — A heavily annotated reference sample of `tianluo/e2e/environment.yaml` — shipped inside tianluo and injected into the bootstrap generation prompt — that teaches the environment vocabulary through one `tianluo-e2e` network plus four services: an `app` under test (`base_kind: base`, build layers, published `18000:8000` port, host-side `http` readiness probe), a stock `postgres:16` `db` with `mount_source: false` and a `command` probe, a `playwright` `browser` driver, and a commented-out `gui-xvfb` desktop service. <!--#433cbf503e929068|b2895fa915584a85-->
- `network` (yaml-key) — Names the shared container network (`tianluo-e2e`) that every service in this environment joins, so service names resolve as hostnames between peers. <!--#4c605e4a467cb7a0-->
- `services` (yaml-key) — Illustrates the service list vocabulary with three annotated examples — an `app` under test built on a `base` image with published ports and an `http` readiness probe, a stock `postgres:16` dependency with `mount_source: false` and a `command` probe, and a `playwright` browser driver — plus a commented-out `gui-xvfb` desktop service. <!--#a1fe0ee8930784e7-->

### `src/tianluo/e2e/templates/gui-xvfb.Dockerfile.tmpl` (text) — A Docker image template for headless desktop-GUI e2e targets that installs the Xvfb/openbox/scrot/xdotool X stack onto a Debian-family base and generates an entrypoint script bringing up the virtual display and window manager before running the container command, with $base_image/$display/$screen/$workdir/$debug_tools_layer/$build_steps placeholders filled in at render time. <!--#7f20d05685676a2e|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/e2e/templates/playwright.Dockerfile.tmpl` (text) — A `string.Template` Dockerfile scaffold for the e2e browser-driver image, deriving from a pinned official Playwright `$base_image` (so fonts/browsers stay matched for visual-baseline diffing), setting `$workdir` as the bind-mount point for project source, and appending declarative `$build_steps`. <!--#6a27d66aa23d921a|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/e2e/templates/scenario.example.yaml` (yaml) — Annotated reference scenario file shipped with tianluo and injected into the e2e bootstrap generation prompt, showing a schema-valid `api-smoke` CLI/HTTP scenario (driver, description, timeout, tags, exec/wait actions, tier-1 assertions) plus commented-out browser, screenshot_diff, and visual_semantic variants that document the enforced tier-1/2/3 assertion ladder. <!--#30c653cc328fa570|ac7fda26cee187a1-->
- `name` (yaml-key) — Scenario identifier `api-smoke`, the human/machine-readable name this example scenario is referenced by. <!--#6f0511261474b7e9-->
- `driver` (yaml-key) — Names the environment service (`app`) that acts as the driver container in which the scenario's actions are executed. <!--#951123c743b71b96-->
- `description` (yaml-key) — Prose explanation that this scenario seeds fixture data via the CLI and then verifies the HTTP API returns it, all as non-visual tier-1 checks. <!--#f163dadd7c72671a-->
- `timeout` (yaml-key) — Per-scenario execution time limit in seconds (120) before the run is aborted. <!--#e48dcd2c464af54f-->
- `tags` (yaml-key) — Selection labels (`smoke`, `api`) used to filter which scenarios a given e2e run includes. <!--#5fc2f678585b301a-->
- `actions` (yaml-key) — Ordered list of steps to perform — an `exec` of the seed CLI command followed by a one-second `wait` — illustrating the supported action forms. <!--#747472db9ab81fcc-->
- `assertions` (yaml-key) — Post-action checks demonstrating each assertion kind: `exit_code`, `stdout` substring, `http_status`, `http_body` regex, and `file_exists`. <!--#ff42cab54e0c397c-->

## `src/tianluo/engine/` — The core flow-engine package of tianluo/SE3: it defines the workflow state machine, flow/step models, persistence and event streaming, drives each StepType handler (discovery → analyze/plan → implement → test → self_check/adjudicate → confirm → commit/version/merge) through an LLM caller with prompt-context assembly, chat/prompt history and retry context, and supplies the supporting subsystems — project charter, code index, issue discovery/management, DAG scheduling and worktrees, version bumping and git tags, merge conflict resolution, and Rich-based display/formatting. <!--#e12dd913a6a2d43a|577bee0eb15ffcd8-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/__init__.py` (python) — Public API surface of the SE3/tianluo flow engine package, re-exporting the state machine, flow/step models, plan decomposition, review scope, persistence, LLM caller, schema, logging, event stream (aliasing `EventEmitter` as `EventStream`) and sinks under a single `__all__`. <!--#3419f2b0e32e8b41|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/adjudication.py` (python) — A pure, dependency-free module implementing the adjudication trigger layer: it normalizes issue quotes into stable position keys and fingerprints, maintains an append-only ledger of SELF_CHECK observations and fix resolutions in engine state, and evaluates three structural signals (oscillation, contradiction/'打脸', repeated reproduction) plus a periodic backstop to decide whether the ADJUDICATE step must run and convergence be suppressed. <!--#da16fe23f918c07d|f2e8cf58d5c204a4-->
- `_normalize_for_quote_match` (function) — Symmetric string normalizer (literal-newline unescape → NFKC → smart-quote replacement → whitespace collapse), deliberately duplicated from the self_check step to keep this pure module import-cycle-free while guaranteeing ledger keys and source-pool checks normalize identically. <!--#9810f5963a6c10cd-->
- `relaxed_quote_candidates` (function) — Single source of truth generating relaxed substring variants of a normalized quote (trimmed trailing ellipsis, stripped bullet/id prefix) so that source-pool validation and dead-clause abolition accept the same set of re-quotes. <!--#f77b5de029d4e1c1-->
- `_pk_quote` (function) — Extracts the normalized-quote component from a position_key string, returning empty when the key carries no quote. <!--#c6dee106c5a3e6d1-->
- `_issue_file` (function) — Derives an issue's fingerprint file-path component, preferring the first evidence line (with its trailing :N line number stripped) and falling back to the first missing_in path. <!--#195a3bda23d126ce-->
- `_issue_quote` (function) — Returns an issue's normalized verbatim expectation-source quote, or empty if absent. <!--#18dc6bcac691d7e8-->
- `_issue_expected` (function) — Returns an issue's normalized expected_behavior text. <!--#122306771b268131-->
- `position_key` (function) — Builds a location identity key from file path plus normalized quote (deliberately excluding expected content so disagreements at a shared position surface as oscillation/contradiction signals). <!--#a0ab61724e4d692b-->
- `fingerprint` (function) — Builds the full finding identity (file + normalized quote + normalized expected) used for reproduction counting, where a shared position but differing expected yields distinct fingerprints but the same position key. <!--#794ee82d97c609d1-->
- `_ensure_ledger` (function) — Returns (initializing if absent) the ctx ledger sub-tree with its append-only observation/resolution lists and counters, tolerating legacy ledger-less engine state and remaining idempotent on re-invocation. <!--#9aa4dae7f004f60c-->
- `_observation_from_issue` (function) — Constructs a single ledger observation record (round, file, quote, expected, position key, fingerprint, abolished flag) from an issue dict. <!--#181c6347e4b04084-->
- `record_self_check_round` (function) — Appends one SELF_CHECK round's issues as observations to the ledger, collapsing intra-round duplicate fingerprints, returning the assigned round index, and skipping replays that reuse a prior round_id token. <!--#6e9e5625d69d4c0d-->
- `record_fix_resolutions` (function) — Appends a fix round's previous_issue_resolution verdicts to the ledger, normalizing each into a fingerprint/position record and anchoring 'fixed' verdicts to the latest prior observation round so trigger (b)/(c) counting stays correct. <!--#57e0817ee5910623-->
- `mark_abolished` (function) — Flags (but retains) all ledger observations and resolutions whose fingerprint is in the given set so they stop driving triggers after an adjudication overrides their grounding clause, returning the count flagged. <!--#5e5be73c64f95acd-->
- `record_rejected_candidates` (function) — Records position keys the ADJUDICATE LLM ruled non-contradictions so they are permanently excluded from trigger (a) and never re-fire the adjudicator. <!--#eaf6ef6e95143091-->
- `AdjudicationDecision` (class) — Dataclass holding the trigger layer's structural verdict — whether ADJUDICATE should run, which triggers fired, the triggering positions/fingerprints, and whether convergence must be suppressed. <!--#bb634298bda7e1d8-->
  - `AdjudicationDecision.suppress_convergence` (method) — Property that is True whenever any signal trigger (a/b/c) fired, indicating convergence must yield to adjudication (the periodic backstop alone does not suppress). <!--#d82f9ae3758eefa2-->
- `_active_observations` (function) — Returns the ledger observations that are not abolished and therefore still count toward triggers. <!--#41c1adef493d761c-->
- `_current_round_index` (function) — Returns the index of the most recently recorded round (round_count − 1), the 'current' round given recording precedes trigger evaluation. <!--#0265ccca0b075e96-->
- `_detect_oscillation` (function) — Trigger (a): flags quote-anchored, non-rejected positions that were flagged in a prior round demanding a materially different expected than this round's, using set-difference so genuine A/B flips survive even self-contradicting earlier rounds. <!--#6e4cc932716bd02c-->
- `_detect_contradiction` (function) — Trigger (b) '打脸': flags any current quote-anchored, non-rejected position that carries a live 'fixed' resolution yet still shows a current fingerprint, firing immediately since a re-flagged or opposite finding conflicts with the resolved claim. <!--#1139e32d33fab517-->
- `_detect_reproduction` (function) — Trigger (c): flags full fingerprints that reappear at least the reproduction threshold (3) times strictly after their earliest declared-fixed round, skipping rejected and quoteless fingerprints to avoid livelocks. <!--#790d5a04b352c9b9-->
- `evaluate_triggers` (function) — Aggregates the three structural detectors plus the periodic backstop over the current round's issues into an AdjudicationDecision, doing purely structural judgement and leaving truth-determination to the ADJUDICATE LLM. <!--#ee8ae6aa71554754-->
- `note_adjudication_ran` (function) — Resets the ledger's periodic-backstop baseline to the current fix iteration so the next periodic sweep is measured from the last adjudication rather than flow start. <!--#440ca23de70e6f61-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/baseline_fix_memory.py` (python) — A cross-flow persistent store (schema-versioned JSON at tianluo/state/baseline_fix_attempts.json, written atomically and LRU-bounded, read corruption-tolerantly) that records which inherited/baseline test failures a fix loop has given up on so subsequent flows skip re-attempting the same un-fixable failures. <!--#e196c52c6ddbbabd|4b4720d265c83075-->
- `memory_path` (function) — Returns the filesystem path to the baseline-fix memory file (the gitignored `baseline_fix_attempts.json` under the project's runtime dir) for a given `project_root`. <!--#b66168e7d93c264f-->
- `_read_entries` (function) — Corruption-tolerant reader that loads the memory's entries map, returning an empty dict on any missing/corrupt/schema-mismatched file rather than raising. <!--#d3d6de9e35eb54ba-->
- `load_given_up` (function) — Returns the set of test ids already given up on, reading an empty set when the store is missing or corrupt. <!--#27086faf5a83f3a9-->
- `load_given_up_details` (function) — Returns the full per-test_id metadata map (attempts/reason) so callers can surface why a baseline failure was abandoned. <!--#62d3a0c6091dc142-->
- `record_given_up` (function) — Atomically marks test ids as given-up, accumulating attempt counts and latest reason while LRU-trimming the store to MAX_ENTRIES. <!--#e31f6cbd4ec5c077-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/charter.py` (python) — Side-effect-free, stdlib-only module for the project charter (tianluo/charter.md, the shrunk successor to the base spec that is injected in full into every run step): it locates, loads, and template-renders the charter and implements the 'altitude gate' admission check plus the LLM prompt builder for the charter_freshness auto-update loop, where a non-blocking byte-size 'monitoring light' and a normative admission standard guard against low-level content leaking into the high-level charter. <!--#1e3eaa49b59834af|b7b14d4357355953-->
- `AdmissionResult` (class) — Dataclass capturing the outcome of the charter altitude gate: byte size, threshold, advisory over-threshold flag, the normative admission-standard text, and an optional monitoring-light warning. <!--#254a712e6734b8f1-->
- `charter_path` (function) — Returns the absolute path to a project's charter file (`tianluo/charter.md`) by joining its runtime directory. <!--#30cf6b0bd6e4c023-->
- `load_charter` (function) — The single entry point that reads the full `tianluo/charter.md` text for unconditional whole-text injection into every step, returning "" (never raising) when the file is missing or unreadable. <!--#f93372b11d60dd2d-->
- `load_charter_template` (function) — Returns the raw packaged charter.md template text without any placeholder substitution. <!--#14e46cbcc4abd4d3-->
- `render_charter_template` (function) — Renders the packaged charter template by literal-replacing {key} placeholders, leaving incidental braces untouched, for use by init/migrate. <!--#30f6fa7d05c57c78-->
- `_changed_paths_touch_charter` (function) — Helper predicate returning True when the charter file (current `tianluo/` or legacy `se3/` path) appears among a list of changed files, matching on the path tail and tolerating absolute/Windows-style entries. <!--#4d123752b2245bb6-->
- `admission_check_for_changes` (function) — The flow trigger that runs the charter altitude gate (`check_admission`) only when the charter was among the changed files, returning None otherwise and a non-blocking monitoring `AdmissionResult` when it fires. <!--#3bac2c8af713db7d-->
- `build_admission_gate_prompt` (function) — Pure string builder that assembles the binding LLM admission-gate prompt for the `charter_freshness` auto-update loop, injecting the admission standard, candidate charter, removed passages, diff summary, and removal-weakening question, and eliciting a JSON verdict. <!--#8ca4a369c1b63871-->
- `check_admission` (function) — Runs the charter altitude gate against given text, computing a non-blocking monitoring-light warning when the UTF-8 byte size exceeds the threshold and attaching the normative admission standard. <!--#d2630d46b30139ac-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/chat_history.py` (python) — The chat-history subsystem: defines the ChatMessage/ChatSession records persisted as one JSONL file per flow step under tianluo/history/{flow_id}/{step_id}.jsonl, and provides the append-side recorders (LLM prompts/responses, user interjections, step lifecycle and status events, stream/group/index progress), the read-side queries (per-step and per-flow history, flow listing, lifecycle-event lookups), and the parsing/rendering helpers that extract conversation turns, token usage, model and agent names from raw NDJSON to build retry-context prompts and human- or web-readable transcripts. <!--#9ac9a78ad330d1d0|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/code_index.py` (python) — The core module that builds the deterministic code-index structure map: it enumerates the project tree, extracts within-file symbols per language (Python AST, markdown/YAML/JSON keys, or degraded chunks) into Fingerprint/Symbol/FileEntry/CodeIndex dataclasses, computes recursive and mechanical 'list' fingerprints so only changed nodes are re-summarised while human corrections are preserved, and atomically renders/reparses the authoritative fingerprint-embedded `tianluo/code-index.md` under an advisory build lock. <!--#6c123c68222b3278|0d15b6b6f30c1992-->
- `Fingerprint` (class) — A dataclass holding one file's content fingerprint — cheap mtime/size signals plus the authoritative sha256 prefix used as the change signal. <!--#9451c48c84db3103-->
- `Symbol` (class) — Dataclass for one within-file node (class/function/method, structural unit, or degraded chunk) carrying its id, kind, location, hash, summary, and optional verbatim content. <!--#a009f18727b02756-->
- `FileEntry` (class) — Dataclass holding one enumerated file's path, kind, fingerprints (whole-file plus a direct-symbol-roster 'list' fingerprint that gates reuse without cascading on body edits), summary, and extracted child symbols. <!--#c08141b42a516794-->
  - `FileEntry.symbol_id` (method) — Returns a symbol's full id by joining the file's relpath and the symbol's local id with '::'. <!--#c3974e13d18e0fdf-->
- `CodeIndex` (class) — The dataclass holding the in-memory structure map — a relpath→FileEntry table plus per-directory summaries and two kinds of content fingerprints — with a from_md classmethod that reconstructs a render-sufficient index (structure and summaries, fingerprints zeroed) by parsing the authoritative markdown. <!--#2906eccb841b1663-->
  - `CodeIndex.from_md` (method) — Classmethod that rebuilds a render-sufficient CodeIndex by parsing directory headings, file headings, and symbol bullets out of the authoritative md, capturing only structure and summaries (fingerprints left zeroed). <!--#1ad25495637898a3-->
- `_split_fp` (function) — Helper that strips an md line's embedded fingerprint comment, returning the bare line plus its parsed content-fp and (optional) list-fp before any heading/bullet regex runs. <!--#fca7095dc35bd53e-->
- `_fp_comment` (function) — Helper that renders the trailing fingerprint HTML comment for an md line, emitting the legacy single-fp shape or the dual content|list shape when a list-fp is supplied. <!--#af268880669ba2d9-->
- `SummaryTarget` (class) — A dataclass describing one node (symbol, file, or directory) that needs an LLM summary, carrying its id, owning path, kind, name, and content to summarise. <!--#784c7c0812cd97aa-->
- `_sha256_prefix` (function) — Returns a hex sha256 of the given bytes truncated to a configurable prefix length. <!--#4a3d0b21f35268a9-->
- `_sha256_text` (function) — Hashes a string by UTF-8 encoding it and delegating to _sha256_prefix. <!--#4f7607d84cf5f60a-->
- `_fp` (function) — Helper that truncates a node's sha256 to the first `_FP_LEN` hex chars for embedding in the md. <!--#7dc034e8bbda50ba-->
- `_slice_lines` (function) — Returns the 1-based inclusive line range of a list of lines joined by newlines, clamping out-of-range bounds. <!--#b6d736c0ae3a5c02-->
- `_extract_python` (function) — Extracts top-level classes/functions and class methods from Python source via AST, stopping at the function/method level. <!--#8977c5a354cfcd6a-->
- `_extract_markdown` (function) — Extracts markdown headings (ignoring fenced code blocks) as structural units, each spanning to the next heading. <!--#e78a2c67046c83eb-->
- `_line_of_top_key` (function) — Best-effort lookup of the 1-based line number where a top-level YAML/key declaration appears. <!--#cf55f29734a6211c-->
- `_extract_yaml` (function) — Extracts top-level YAML mapping keys as symbols, carrying each key's serialized value as content. <!--#03759e3e86c28e59-->
- `_extract_json` (function) — Extracts top-level JSON object keys as symbols, carrying each key's serialized value as content. <!--#915a274e73e1db64-->
- `_extract_structure` (function) — Dispatches structural extraction to the right per-extension extractor, returning [] when none applies or none is found. <!--#25e24dfeb6fb8a76-->
- `_file_kind` (function) — Classifies a file as python/markdown/yaml/json/text by its extension. <!--#8090ae4dd5164009-->
- `is_degrade_eligible` (function) — Returns whether a file qualifies for last-resort chunk degradation by requiring all three conditions: text, no structure, and over a size threshold. <!--#08b26f76b777e5f6-->
- `_chunk_degraded` (function) — Splits a structure-less oversized file into line/byte-bounded chunks, each emitted as one degraded symbol. <!--#93818e7aaf52f59e-->
- `_index_file` (function) — Builds a structural FileEntry for one path (no summaries) — handling binary/unreadable files, structural symbol extraction, oversized-file collapsing, and structure-less degradation to chunks. <!--#d4b21d66db7f2546-->
- `md_path` (function) — Returns the filesystem path of the authoritative code-index markdown file within the project's runtime directory. <!--#d22c39aa04144a09-->
- `lock_path` (function) — Returns the path of the advisory lock file (under the gitignored cache directory) used to serialize concurrent index (re)builds. <!--#fcbc75b522533e62-->
- `_build_lock` (function) — Context manager holding an exclusive advisory flock across a build's load→enumerate→write critical section to serialize concurrent rebuilds, falling back to unlocked when fcntl is unavailable. <!--#bfdd14e1fa8107ed-->
- `_atomic_write_text` (function) — Writes text to a path atomically via a unique per-write temp file plus os.replace, so concurrent writers never clobber each other. <!--#b1565ce44f841b76-->
- `_dir_of` (function) — Returns the directory key of a file's immediate parent directory. <!--#29c094ab2953dd41-->
- `_parent_dir` (function) — Returns the parent directory key of a directory key (None for the root). <!--#a3be6ae8fa72d759-->
- `_depth` (function) — Computes the nesting depth of a directory key (root = 0, incrementing per path separator). <!--#3f3467e3bc5c8678-->
- `_all_dir_keys` (function) — Computes the set of every directory key in the tree — every ancestor of every file plus the root. <!--#a754c18a54352d82-->
- `_child_files` (function) — Returns the sorted relpaths of files whose immediate parent directory is the given directory key. <!--#a60e7ddda26ff7ca-->
- `_child_dirs` (function) — Returns the sorted directory keys whose immediate parent is the given directory key. <!--#336d66009c59273a-->
- `_compute_dir_fps` (function) — Computes a recursive per-directory content fingerprint bottom-up so any change in a subtree propagates up and re-summarises every ancestor while untouched siblings reuse cached summaries. <!--#eb5bf3ca6ead4260-->
- `_compute_file_list_fp` (function) — Computes a file's mechanical 'list' fingerprint by hashing only its direct symbols' sorted (kind, name) roster — ignoring bodies, summaries, position, and order — so body-only edits don't change it. <!--#06db726193d7e3a4-->
- `_compute_dir_list_fps` (function) — Computes each directory's non-recursive 'list' fingerprint by hashing only its direct child names (immediate files and subdirs), so a deep edit never bubbles up and each level reuses independently. <!--#51135b8b8c0187f7-->
- `render_full` (function) — Renders the complete authoritative md map — every directory level, file, and symbol — embedding each node's content (and list) fingerprint only when it already has a real summary so partial flushes stay safe resume points. <!--#4b2fc507f56d93d1-->
- `_write_md` (function) — Atomically writes the rendered authoritative md for an index to its md path. <!--#e0d9f93ae34e6f6a-->
- `_parse_md` (function) — Parses the authoritative md into three node-id-keyed maps (reusable summaries, content fingerprints, and migrated file/dir list fingerprints), reading everything from the committed md with no out-of-band cache. <!--#75f859777f45cf86-->
- `_parse_md_summaries` (function) — Convenience wrapper returning just the `{id: summary}` map from the parsed md. <!--#7b2c20ea52847695-->
- `_flatten_summary` (function) — Collapses an LLM summary's whitespace (including newlines) to a single physical line so the one-node-per-line md format isn't corrupted. <!--#ab4fda75898c4eba-->
- `_heuristic_summary` (function) — Produces a deterministic placeholder summary used when no LLM is available or a call fails, keeping builds from crashing. <!--#5e95c0cfd0580e7b-->
- `_make_llm_summarizer` (function) — Factory that builds the default LLM-backed summariser for the code index, batching targets into one LLM call per owning path, running those per-path groups concurrently (each with its own LLMCaller instance for thread safety), firing an optional per-group progress callback, and falling back to heuristic summaries whenever a call fails. <!--#be8e06fa18f9393c-->
- `_make_target` (function) — Builds the summary target for a symbol (using its own content or a line slice) or, as a fallback, a file node from its own source. <!--#3bcb90fc368a7d51-->
- `_make_file_target` (function) — Builds a file's summary target bottom-up — from a digest of its symbols' one-line summaries, or its own source when it has no symbols. <!--#303ef86543b2fdf0-->
- `_make_dir_target` (function) — Builds a directory's summary target bottom-up from its immediate child subdirectory and file summaries. <!--#0490470f87f95416-->
- `_summarize_wave` (function) — Summarises one dependency wave by invoking the summariser and assigning each result onto its dir/symbol/file node, skipping empty waves and firing on_node per assigned target (the progress path used for injected, opaque summarisers). <!--#53c05db5ae43802d-->
- `build_index` (function) — The single (re)build entry point that enumerates the project, extracts structure, summarises changed nodes bottom-up and writes the authoritative md, running the whole critical section under a best-effort exclusive advisory lock. <!--#1e7a8ba29d5f15e1-->
- `_build_index_locked` (function) — The lock-held body of build_index that parses any prior md, enumerates files and directories, computes content and direct-member list fingerprints, and uses per-level list-fp reuse gates to seed unchanged summaries with no LLM before re-summarising only the changed nodes. <!--#bf34cf54fa4f39a5-->
- `load_or_build` (function) — Thin lazy-incremental entry point that delegates to build_index, forwarding force and an optional progress emitter to refresh only changed nodes (or everything under force). <!--#1d7726c26d3419c1-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/code_index_render.py` (python) — Renders two display views over the authoritative `tianluo/code-index.md` — a byte-budgeted zoomable adaptive root map and a literal one-level drill-in — plus a flat grep-able line dump, all reconstructed read-only from the md. <!--#9d0ac02addb3c9dd|631c387dbec56708-->
- `load_for_display` (function) — Reconstructs a render-only CodeIndex by reading the authoritative tianluo/code-index.md from disk, returning None if the file is absent or unreadable. <!--#39f4182ded7606b8-->
- `_top_of` (function) — Returns the top-level ancestor directory key of a given directory key (or the key itself if already top-level). <!--#42c3cefff4559ca3-->
- `_auto_primary_roots` (function) — Auto-detects the code-bearing top-level directories to treat as primary expansion roots, falling back to all top-level dirs when none contain code. <!--#6ea444b4ecf816de-->
- `_subtree_file_counts` (function) — Computes, in one pass, the number of files contained in the subtree of every directory by incrementing each file's ancestor directories. <!--#7afffc3c5eead1ed-->
- `_render_view` (function) — Renders the directory tree as a bulleted markdown map, descending only into the expanded directories and showing files under expanded parents. <!--#ef2c6ecc16fafe5c-->
- `_expansion_costs` (function) — Precomputes the byte cost of expanding each directory (its immediate children block) so the render budget can be checked incrementally in O(1) per candidate. <!--#af7dd118de471c22-->
- `render_adaptive` (function) — Produces the byte-budgeted zoomable root view, expanding frontier directories shallowest-and-densest-first within primary roots until the budget is exhausted. <!--#d164459ab4fc6ed8-->
- `_render_file_detail` (function) — Helper that formats a single file's heading plus its indented function/method symbol tree, marking degraded symbols. <!--#68467cdf328f6577-->
- `_render_one_level` (function) — Renders exactly the immediate children (subdirs and files) of a single directory key as a markdown section. <!--#0ecd37d78e015b3a-->
- `iter_search_lines` (function) — Renders every directory, file, and in-file symbol of a CodeIndex as individual grep-able bullet lines built from the structured index, giving each symbol its full file-qualified path without the md's fingerprint comments. <!--#24f1804e40e40064-->
- `render_path` (function) — Renders the one-level drill-in view for a given path — root level, a file's full symbol tree, a directory's immediate children, or a not-found note. <!--#e9351a5830007db3-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/conftest.py` (python) — Pytest fixture module scoped to engine tests that sandboxes the live repo — redirecting chat-history writes into tmp dirs, stubbing out real LLM code-index refreshes, and pinning the UI language to en-US for deterministic assertions. <!--#12acdd7652aa4dad|1ec988100dc42efb-->
- `_real_history_roots` (function) — Helper that returns the set of filesystem paths considered the live repo root (the package's top-level parent and the current working directory), used to detect when test writes would leak into the real repository. <!--#6f2232fb1afc6fc6-->
- `_no_chat_history_leak_to_real_repo` (function) — An autouse-style engine-test fixture that reroutes chat_history._history_dir (and state_machine's import-time copy) into a per-test tmp dir whenever a writer resolves to a real repo root, preventing test runs from leaking fake history jsonl files into the committed tianluo/history/. <!--#77e9c5d7f2010e3c-->
- `_no_real_code_index_refresh` (function) — An engine-test fixture that monkeypatches context_builder.ensure_code_index_fresh to a no-op, stopping analyze/commit step handlers from triggering a real, slow, flock-taking LLM code-index rebuild against the live repo during unit tests. <!--#dcd80e40330e4244-->
- `_force_en_us_ui_language` (function) — An engine-test fixture that pins the i18n UI language to en-US (via SE3_LANG plus singleton/cache resets) so t()-rendered display strings stay in English despite the repo's zh-CN tianluo.yaml, keeping English assertions stable. <!--#38d0d1fb01dca641-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/context.py` (python) — Defines the read-only Context wrapper around workflow State plus the pure effective_task_type resolver, centralizing the logic that surfaces a real task type (feature/bugfix) rather than a run mode like 'discovery' for commit-message, version, and UI display consumers. <!--#452bcd230af5840e|90feb89a44d2ba97-->
- `effective_task_type` (function) — Pure resolver that returns the real task type (feature/bugfix/etc.) for commit-message and version consumers, preferring an explicit --type, then analyze's persisted type, then a sanitized flow fallback, never returning a run mode like 'discovery'. <!--#bcfd3dadd820ea37-->
- `Context` (class) — Read-only wrapper around workflow State that exposes the task description and display-friendly task-type properties, encapsulating the logic that distinguishes resolved task types from run modes and pending state. <!--#81e0e2bc8cdbd3e4-->
  - `Context.__init__` (method) — Constructor storing the original task description and the workflow State reference. <!--#8242df2429226234-->
  - `Context.task_description` (method) — Property returning the original task description string. <!--#9ad8135cc0823e21-->
  - `Context.task_type` (method) — Property that resolves the current task type from state (resolved_type, explicit_type, flow type, or analyzed_type), skipping run modes and returning the 'pending' sentinel when no real type is available yet. <!--#3bb2d6106a2e5b27-->
  - `Context.display_type` (method) — Property returning the display-friendly task type from resolved_type (mapping a run mode to its real analyzed type), or None while the type is still pending. <!--#ad0cf2c8ef999b33-->
  - `Context.is_type_pending` (method) — Returns whether the task type is still unresolved, delegating to State's method when available. <!--#a8174bd77d016406-->
  - `Context.__repr__` (method) — Debug string representation showing the task type and pending status. <!--#ac43d00ede6802c8-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/context_builder.py` (python) — Central assembler of per-step prompt context for the run engine: it produces the conditional injection blocks (language instructions, runtime environment, issue discovery, project charter, code-index root map, read-only constraints, worktree runtime state) and builds the specialized review/confirm prompts and display payloads used by LLM review, plan, CONFIRM, and adjudicate gates. <!--#b33707e55ef13a9e|a864fd6172f0d5fb-->
- `get_step_language_instruction` (function) — Returns the language instruction to append to a run-engine step's prompt, routing spec steps to spec_language, human-facing/confirmed steps to the general language, and everything else to no injection. <!--#69f7354a76473892-->
- `get_spec_language_instruction` (function) — Returns the spec-flavored language instruction (driven by language.spec_language) for the sync_* knowledge-asset writers that can't route through the step-language path, or "" when spec_language is unset. <!--#9c65bbedbf450eb3-->
- `_load_runtime_environment_markdown` (function) — Reads and process-caches runtime_environment.md, returning empty string with a one-time warning on read failure. <!--#c69d2cc539e7ddc0-->
- `_reset_runtime_environment_cache` (function) — Test-only helper that clears the runtime_environment.md cache so reload paths can be exercised. <!--#8fcfcfa91ac8350c-->
- `get_runtime_environment_injection` (function) — Returns the runtime_environment.md prompt injection for whitelisted (config- or default-listed, minus forbidden) steps, rewriting canonical paths for legacy se3-layout projects, else "". <!--#4a99626cb080eb4e-->
- `get_issue_discovery_injection` (function) — Returns the ISSUE_DISCOVERY_PROMPT injection for steps in the config/default whitelist and not forbidden, else an empty string. <!--#cc3230133c0ea208-->
- `get_charter_injection` (function) — Loads `tianluo/charter.md` and wraps it in a labelled "Project Charter" section for unconditional injection into every step's prompt, returning "" when the charter is missing or empty. <!--#fe1492a96119eb52-->
- `get_self_check_constraint_sources` (function) — Collects the project-constraint context for a SELF_CHECK review — the project charter plus marked WHY:/INVARIANT: comments harvested from changed files (including their baseline revision) — returning them as a source-name → text mapping suitable for prompt rendering and verbatim-quote validation, silently omitting any unavailable source. <!--#ce4e1f9d2fe37257-->
- `get_code_index_injection` (function) — Returns the code-index root-map injection — the drill-down protocol header plus the adaptive byte-budgeted root view rendered from tianluo/code-index.md (or a build note when the map is absent), never triggering a rebuild. <!--#c006c6de19f45285-->
- `ensure_code_index_fresh` (function) — Best-effort lazy-incremental rebuild of an already-built code-index before a consuming step, wiring per-node progress to the web console when a flow/step context is supplied and swallowing any failure. <!--#8a4e6b4e41c6f013-->
- `is_step_read_only` (function) — Single source of truth deciding whether a step type runs read-only, by looking up `read_only` in STEP_POOL and falling back to the internal pure-data sub-agent step set. <!--#edf31cc5e135ebfe-->
- `get_read_only_injection` (function) — Returns the READ-ONLY STEP CONSTRAINT prompt block (forbidden/allowed tool lists) for read-only steps, with a `force` flag for call-level overrides, else an empty string. <!--#a3e76b4d6eeecd9b-->
- `get_runtime_context_injection` (function) — Detects worktree isolation and injects context (open issues, flow state, history counts) from the main repo's gitignored runtime dirs absent in the worktree, else "". <!--#bd69dae70f320b6b-->
- `_detect_main_repo_root` (function) — Uses `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` to detect the main repository root from a possible worktree path, returning it or None on failure. <!--#814766e030db1137-->
- `build_llm_review_prompt` (function) — Builds the structured prompt for LLM-based review of a step's output, formatting the output, optional revision feedback, evaluation criteria, and required JSON response format. <!--#bf66f623e57bd0bb-->
- `_build_capability_grouping_review_prompt` (function) — Renders the capability-doctrine plan review prompt that grades only the task grouping on three dimensions (group count, forbidden artifact/layer splits, `depends_on` validity), with count wording selected by the flow's granularity. <!--#982c7470475f8448-->
- `build_plan_confirm_prompt` (function) — Builds the plan step's specialized `{approved, feedback}` review prompt, dispatching to the capability grouping review or the legacy granular requirement-coverage review based on the flow's persisted decomposition mode. <!--#fe86c2e872d6b475-->
- `build_confirm_prompt` (function) — Returns the one-line human-readable question shown at a CONFIRM approval gate, with a special wording for adjudicate reviews and a generic "review the <step type> output" fallback. <!--#625a3476caf9d1a5-->
- `_display_covered_surfaces` (function) — Defensively sanitizes a ruling's raw `covered_surfaces` value into a list of well-formed {surface, justification} dicts, silently dropping malformed entries so the human-approval display degrades instead of crashing. <!--#7aa129def41bb195-->
- `build_adjudicate_review_context` (function) — Builds the display payload a CONFIRM gate needs to review an ADJUDICATE ruling — rationale, adjudicated description, the pre-ruling baseline description (resolved excluding the reviewed step), and the sanitized covered-surfaces sweep — returning an empty dict for non-adjudicate steps. <!--#fc9df5ee52290489-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/dag_scheduler.py` (python) — Event-driven parallel scheduler that builds a validated DAG from task-group dependencies and runs groups via a ThreadPoolExecutor, using relay planning (classify_chains/RelayPlan/RelayContext) to reuse, fork, or converge worktree branches while emitting per-group lifecycle status and returning GroupResults. <!--#9f4a305db6d4857c|8e398420b3a80b98-->
- `ConvergenceInfo` (class) — Dataclass capturing, for a node with multiple predecessors, which predecessor's worktree is inherited (primary) and which predecessors' branches are merged in (secondary). <!--#1b7a60866faacf8e-->
- `RelayContext` (class) — Runtime context handed to the executor telling a group how to obtain its worktree — reuse a predecessor's, fork a new branch, or create fresh — plus any convergence branches to merge. <!--#05abe19424a373e2-->
- `RelayPlan` (class) — Dataclass holding the full relay execution strategy (relay map, fork sources, leaf/root nodes, convergence points) produced by classify_chains and consumed by the scheduler. <!--#06c133c34947e5d3-->
- `classify_chains` (function) — Analyzes DAG topology to produce a RelayPlan, deciding per group whether to create a new worktree, relay from a primary predecessor, fork, or merge at a convergence point. <!--#a14041499502d9b6-->
- `_relay_plan_is_linear` (function) — Helper returning True when a RelayPlan describes a single-root, fork-free linear chain, letting callers skip DAG-parallel execution that would yield no parallelism. <!--#195dd89fd4eb9574-->
- `GroupResult` (class) — Dataclass representing the outcome of executing one task group (status, files/tests changed, branch, worktree, completion details) with skipped/failed constructor helpers. <!--#c16bb24282ecaca3-->
  - `GroupResult.skipped` (method) — Classmethod constructing a GroupResult marked as skipped because an upstream dependency failed. <!--#41b078e164946dde-->
  - `GroupResult.failed` (method) — Classmethod constructing a GroupResult marked as failed with the given error message. <!--#fb9f926def640ccf-->
- `DAGScheduler` (class) — Core class that builds a validated DAG from group dependencies and drives parallel execution via ThreadPoolExecutor + Condition, emitting per-group lifecycle status and building relay contexts. <!--#2a8c65cc167d157f-->
  - `DAGScheduler.__init__` (method) — Initializes the scheduler's config and DAG bookkeeping structures and builds the DAG from the supplied groups. <!--#7fbf3b1d94a456b5-->
  - `DAGScheduler._emit_status` (method) — Safely invokes the optional on_group_status callback, swallowing and logging any exception so a faulty status sink cannot disrupt scheduling. <!--#6944feb1a073cafa-->
  - `DAGScheduler._build_dag` (method) — Builds the group map, forward/reverse adjacency, and in-degrees from depends_on edges and validates the graph is acyclic. <!--#1d7fc2a08282d9bd-->
  - `DAGScheduler._kahn_topo_sort` (method) — Computes a topological ordering of groups via Kahn's algorithm, with a short result signaling a cycle. <!--#e8ecf8fb870b4c2b-->
  - `DAGScheduler._build_relay_context` (method) — Constructs a RelayContext for a group from the relay plan and completed predecessor results, resolving worktree reuse, fork source, and convergence merge branches. <!--#50778ecfac8bbe73-->
  - `DAGScheduler.run` (method) — Executes all groups in dependency order, submitting ready groups to a thread pool, propagating failures to downstream groups, and returning their GroupResults. <!--#a61ec96384e2fe46-->
  - `DAGScheduler.get_fallback_leaves` (method) — Returns completed groups whose downstream all failed or were skipped (excluding normal leaves), so their valid work can be merged back as fallback. <!--#516fb66a7a14bfae-->
  - `DAGScheduler.topological_merge_order` (method) — Returns groups in topological order to guide the sequence of branch merges back to the main branch. <!--#277ba115a8b5b1be-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/display.py` (python) — Rich-based terminal rendering layer for the engine: owns the global Console singleton and provides reverse-color block chrome plus formatters for token/cost usage blocks and summaries, proposals, designs, specs, plain text, code, diffs, and markdown. <!--#33ef818780300588|cf8b5f734feebf33-->
- `get_console` (function) — Lazily creates and returns the module-global Rich Console singleton. <!--#34af9b63623b3216-->
- `set_console` (function) — Overrides the module-global Console instance, mainly for testing. <!--#3c900a44fe46127f-->
- `_reverse_title` (function) — Builds a reverse-color ` ## Title ` heading as a Rich Text object on a colored background. <!--#548f67b20e68a7ec-->
- `_reverse_footer` (function) — Builds a fixed-width reverse-color whitespace block used as a block's bottom boundary marker. <!--#b3b374c4e5cfae09-->
- `render_block_header` (function) — Public wrapper that prints a reverse-color block title followed by a blank line. <!--#6bc1573d1ddb863c-->
- `render_block_footer` (function) — Public wrapper that prints the fixed-width reverse-color block footer followed by a blank line. <!--#b02ffd2b25f0e7e4-->
- `render_usage_block` (function) — Renders a UsageTotals (object, dict, or None) as the standard reverse-color token/cost block, silently rendering nothing for empty or absent usage. <!--#0a0e660eca6adbb0-->
- `_render_usage_rows` (function) — Shared helper that prints a label/value pair list as the fixed two-column, column-aligned usage table with reverse-color title and footer chrome. <!--#51a0ff7dbb91017b-->
- `_format_optional_cost` (function) — Formats a possibly-unknown cost value, showing the i18n "Unknown" label instead of misleadingly rendering $0. <!--#ba25af96daa5c9d3-->
- `render_usage_summary_block` (function) — Prints a session-level UsageSummary block with separate actual vs. estimated cost columns and unknown-measurement counts, skipping output when nothing was measured. <!--#4dd722be12bdf04a-->
- `_summary_has_measurements` (function) — Predicate deciding whether a records-free (wire-shaped) UsageSummary still has totals or costs worth displaying. <!--#22fdb427de340d7e-->
- `_usage_status_label` (function) — Translates a UsageStatus member or raw wire string into its i18n label, falling back to the verbatim value when unrecognized. <!--#5bd6f39ca2413d39-->
- `_usage_summary_renderable` (function) — Builds (without printing) the Rich renderable list for a usage summary block so both the printing path and history display share one visual shape. <!--#d357b888e84bce28-->
- `build_history_usage_renderables` (function) — Turns a build_usage_payload dict into Rich renderables — per-call table, per-step table, and flow-total summary block — for `luo history show` to print with its own console. <!--#c81a88c9b557c359-->
- `render_full` (function) — Prints arbitrary content in full without truncation, optionally wrapped in a blue title/footer block. <!--#cc2bafbda92f1b83-->
- `render_proposal` (function) — Formats a proposal dict — summary, files to modify/create with reasons, rationale, plus any extra fields — into styled markup and prints it via render_full. <!--#6d0f1e9bb416f3b6-->
- `render_design` (function) — Formats a design-document dict — overview, components, interfaces, key decisions, and any additional sections — into section-headed styled text rendered via render_full. <!--#d062764c0cce5794-->
- `render_spec_content` (function) — Formats a spec dict — title/version/type metadata header, description, requirements, and extra sections — into styled text rendered via render_full. <!--#bc18d620c9aa9fbd-->
- `render_text` (function) — Renders plain text left-aligned with an optional title block and optional Rich style. <!--#02638b45c952b7be-->
- `render_code` (function) — Renders code with syntax highlighting and line numbers under an optional green title block. <!--#5b51ac6cd6788d16-->
- `render_diff` (function) — Prints a unified diff for a file with red/green/cyan coloring, gutter line numbers derived from hunk headers, and truncation past a max-line limit. <!--#034a49466dfa98af-->
- `render_markdown` (function) — Renders markdown content via Rich's Markdown under an optional magenta title block. <!--#57673343920809b3-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/docs_updater.py` (python) — Module providing the DocumentationUpdater class (plus a small {{key}}-substituting Template helper and template-path resolvers) that updates a project's README.md version badge/header and inserts or idempotently merges VERSIONS.md changelog entries using configurable, template-driven placeholders. <!--#b4e48d19f90536e8|95d19a05a7460871-->
- `_versions_md_template_path` (function) — Module-level helper returning the path to the packaged versions_md.md template (resolved relative to this module so tests can monkeypatch it). <!--#76ac7c1506576aea-->
- `_versions_entry_template_from_file` (function) — Reads the first ## section of the packaged versions_md.md template and returns it as a fallback entry template only if it contains the required {{version}} and {{changes}} placeholders, else None. <!--#fcd606d5ab77c4ed-->
- `Template` (class) — Simple template holder that substitutes {{key}} placeholders with merged default and context values. <!--#aa02c2559079b161-->
  - `Template.__init__` (method) — Stores the template content string and an optional dict of default placeholder values. <!--#4aeb58f2bd29890e-->
  - `Template.render` (method) — Returns the content with each {{key}} replaced by its value from the merged placeholder/context dictionary. <!--#3ea1ee9e956e5b1b-->
- `DocumentationUpdater` (class) — The core class that updates a project's README.md version badge/header and inserts or merges VERSIONS.md changelog entries using configurable placeholder templates. <!--#bb255f0881fe7061-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater.__init__` (method) — Stores the project root and config, then loads the template set via _load_templates. <!--#bdedeb61dfc386a6-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._load_templates` (method) — Builds the readme_badge, optional readme_header, and versions_entry templates from config with file/default fallbacks. <!--#92a84c251a5f850e-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater.update_readme` (method) — Reads README.md, replaces its version badge (and header if configured), and writes back only if the content changed; raises if README.md is missing. <!--#04e75a628f5ca34d-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._build_context` (method) — Constructs the base render context (version, current date, year) merged with any additional context. <!--#df355d4c1e939574-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._replace_version_badge` (method) — Replaces an existing version badge by regex, or inserts a freshly rendered badge after the title heading (skipping YAML front-matter and leading HTML comments). <!--#b5f47aef81a18505-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._replace_version_header` (method) — Replaces the first matching version-header line in README content using the configured readme_header template, leaving content unchanged if none exists. <!--#5eba858b38211444-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater.update_versions_md` (method) — Renders a new changelog entry and inserts it into an existing VERSIONS.md (or creates the file with a header if absent). <!--#9d948f317e8bb930-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._format_changes` (method) — Formats a list of change descriptions into a markdown bullet block, falling back to the 'No changes recorded' placeholder when the list is empty. <!--#6aaf04eb5c1d653b-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._insert_version_entry` (method) — Inserts a new rendered version entry into VERSIONS.md, or merges its bullets into an existing same-version block, after normalizing head blank lines to avoid duplicate-version data loss. <!--#4a3f9b50baa3328a-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._versions_entry_header_line` (method) — Returns the version-bearing header line of the effective versions_entry template (the line carrying `{{version}}`) so header detection works for any heading level or non-heading template. <!--#d3dfd87db700bf82-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._version_header_pattern` (method) — Builds a regex that matches an existing VERSIONS.md block header for a given version, derived from the template's literal prefix/suffix so bracketed, suffixless, and varied header shapes are all recognized for merging. <!--#b67ee467f635bc25-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._version_header_marker` (method) — Returns the literal `#`-prefix (or non-heading literal) that begins every version block header, used to bound block scans at the correct heading level. <!--#edfbb8461630f2d1-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._inline_changes_from_header` (method) — Recovers changelog text rendered on the same line as the version (single-line entry templates like `ENTRY {{version}} | {{changes}}`) so those inline bullets participate in dedupe/merge. <!--#36200207e8bbba0e-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._merge_change_lines` (method) — Merges an entry's new changelog bullets into an existing version block idempotently, deduping against existing bullets, dropping the no-changes placeholder once real bullets exist, and inserting before the block's trailing blanks. <!--#6263d26215adb9b9-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._normalize_head_blanks` (method) — Idempotently collapses the blank-line run immediately after the VERSIONS.md title heading to a single blank line, leaving title-less or non-title-first files untouched. <!--#6faaa3b0d08c4748-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater._create_new_versions_md` (method) — Returns brand-new VERSIONS.md content with a 'Version History' header followed by the first entry. <!--#1f2a677e05d7bc42-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater.render_template` (method) — Renders a named template with the given context, raising KeyError if the template is not registered. <!--#ed1913f03093bd06-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater.add_template` (method) — Registers a custom named template with optional default placeholders. <!--#a2e403c04c0432e5-->
  - `DocumentationUpdater.update_both` (method) — Convenience method that updates both README.md and VERSIONS.md, returning a dict of per-file success flags and tolerating missing files. <!--#e95fc6040805098f-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/event_stream.py` (python) — Defines SE3's unified in-memory flow event stream: the EventType lifecycle enum, the serializable Event dataclass with its new_event factory, and an EventEmitter pub/sub hub that fans events out to pluggable sinks (CLI/JSON) with per-sink fault isolation and scoped subscriptions. <!--#943bb8a1b5189590|a0e685a12504c7b1-->
- `EventType` (class) — A str-backed Enum enumerating every flow-lifecycle event type (flow started/paused/completed/failed, step started/output/completed/failed, interjection/call needed) with JSON-serializable string values. <!--#5042d02dff7f81ca-->
- `Event` (class) — Dataclass representing one structured stream event (type, timestamp, flow/step ids, step type, arbitrary data payload) with dict serialization round-trip helpers. <!--#8025abee4638212c-->
  - `Event.to_dict` (method) — Serializes an Event to a plain JSON-friendly dict, reducing the type enum to its string value and passing data through verbatim. <!--#c81b31aedb4967c2-->
  - `Event.from_dict` (method) — Classmethod that reconstructs an Event from a to_dict payload, supplying defaults for missing optional fields. <!--#e7515b91e274fa52-->
- `new_event` (function) — Convenience factory used by run_flow that builds an Event, collecting keyword payload arguments into its data dict. <!--#3da965c97a496c47-->
- `EventEmitter` (class) — In-memory pub/sub hub holding an ordered list of subscribed sinks and fanning each emitted Event out to them, with isolation against failing sinks and a scoped-subscription context manager. <!--#13f76d85d2b8b4ac-->
  - `EventEmitter.__init__` (method) — Initializes the emitter with an empty subscriber-sink list. <!--#777bfe63b8aa5014-->
  - `EventEmitter.sinks` (method) — Property returning a copy of the currently subscribed sinks in subscription order. <!--#6eaaeda2e99bfed6-->
  - `EventEmitter.subscribe` (method) — Registers a sink to receive future events, ignoring duplicate subscriptions of the same instance. <!--#91dda552eaf06e71-->
  - `EventEmitter.unsubscribe` (method) — Removes a sink from the subscriber list, silently ignoring sinks that aren't subscribed. <!--#7e72619f09833308-->
  - `EventEmitter.emit` (method) — Delivers an event to every subscribed sink in order, swallowing any sink exception so one rendering fault can't break delivery or the flow. <!--#8494582ed4c615e6-->
  - `EventEmitter.scope` (method) — Context manager that snapshots the subscriber list on entry and restores it on exit, so subscriptions made inside the block are automatically undone. <!--#c65503c1b0064a8d-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/file_enum.py` (python) — Gitignore-respecting file enumeration for the code-index: wraps `git ls-files` (tracked ∪ untracked-non-ignored) as the primary inclusion filter, backstopped by an explicit exclude-pattern guard and per-file binary/size classification, exposing `enumerate_index_files` as the deterministic entry point for the set of files the index should cover. <!--#d9b0e2f49d2c2125|7524aebd7fe113ac-->
- `_is_se3_path` (function) — Predicate that returns True when a project-relative path lies inside the runtime directory, matching either the current `tianluo/` name or the legacy `se3/` name. <!--#6ce5ea8c58580c00-->
- `_git_ls_files_paths` (function) — Runs `git ls-files` to return the index view of every tracked file's relative path, returning empty on git failure. <!--#d5658f06054df9fb-->
- `_git_ls_files_other` (function) — Runs `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` to return untracked-but-not-ignored files so new files are picked up without registration. <!--#056a2ea4677d010d-->
- `matches_exclude` (function) — Secondary glob-based guard testing whether a relative path matches any explicit `code_index.exclude` pattern, with basename and directory-subtree conveniences. <!--#65ebacc0b391b57e-->
- `is_binary` (function) — Sniffs a file's leading bytes to classify it as binary (NUL byte or largely-undecodable UTF-8) so the indexer keeps it at a single file-level line. <!--#25bf9ae9141d17de-->
- `FileSize` (class) — Dataclass holding a text file's cheap size measurement as line count and byte count. <!--#47930e403c8c718f-->
  - `FileSize.from_bytes` (method) — Classmethod constructing a FileSize from already-read content without re-reading the file. <!--#4179f5c88553b475-->
- `measure_file` (function) — Reads a file and returns its FileSize, or None if it cannot be read. <!--#cfe51f3a660821c6-->
- `enumerate_index_files` (function) — Enumerates the deterministic, gitignore-respecting set of files the code-index should cover — the union of tracked and untracked-non-ignored git files, minus the runtime directory, `code_index.exclude` matches, and deleted/non-file ghosts — returned as sorted absolute Paths. <!--#4d426d2902e43680-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/git_tags.py` (python) — Git version-tagging helper module: derives canonical `v`-prefixed tag names, applies the SemVer major/minor policy to decide when a version bump warrants a tag, and creates annotated tags on a commit (using its subject as the message) via git subprocesses that surface failures as `VersionTagError`. <!--#0b7b9e8407c2045e|b81d26127b16a400-->
- `VersionTagError` (class) — A RuntimeError subclass raised when a version tag cannot be created, carrying the tag name, target commit, git stderr, and exit code. <!--#6d7e7d08e14c4ae5-->
  - `VersionTagError.__init__` (method) — Stores the tag/commit/stderr/returncode context and builds a message naming both the tag and its commit so the failure can be recovered manually. <!--#bb1bb3fd1fecbabe-->
