- `tag_name_for_version` (function) — Normalizes a version string into the canonical `v`-prefixed git tag name. <!--#33784bcdc0144716-->
- `should_tag_semver_bump` (function) — Returns whether a textual bump type (`major`/`minor`) warrants a tag under the default SemVer policy. <!--#35d0d2832a1ae3e2-->
- `semver_tag_decision` (function) — Decides tag/no-tag by comparing the major.minor components of the current and new versions, returning None when either version is not SemVer-comparable. <!--#2c580f3b4adb98dd-->
- `semver_advance_requires_tag` (function) — Boolean convenience wrapper over `semver_tag_decision` that treats an undecidable comparison as no tag. <!--#93fd3781902bed28-->
- `_semver_major_minor` (function) — Parses a version string into an integer `(major, minor)` tuple, stripping `v`, build, and pre-release parts, or None if unparseable. <!--#bb5b85c2f4596587-->
- `commit_subject` (function) — Reads a commit's raw message body via git and returns only its first physical line, for use as the tag message. <!--#6bea55ccd663659f-->
- `create_annotated_version_tag` (function) — Creates an annotated version tag on the given commit, using that commit's subject as the tag message, and returns the tag name. <!--#3b89535357ca8b9e-->
- `_run_git` (function) — Runs a git subprocess in the project root, converting timeouts, OS errors, and non-zero exits into `VersionTagError`. <!--#1bcd63c9e89f6246-->
- `_tag_name_from_args` (function) — Recovers the tag name from a `git tag -a <name> …` argument tuple for error reporting, falling back to `<unknown>`. <!--#5435883bc6dfd449-->
- `_decode_output` (function) — Coerces possibly-bytes or None subprocess output into a string, replacing undecodable characters. <!--#c3e2b02481034ff7-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/interaction_calls.py` (python) — The single producer/consumer helper for SE3's unified `tianluo/calls/` file channel, reading and writing kind-tagged JSON call files (MCP calls, mid-flow interjections, retry/failure decisions, and CLI confirmations) plus their sibling `.response` answer files, with backward-compatible defaulting of legacy untagged artifacts to a plain `call` kind. <!--#c92812fb20cceed4|0634ff752c4ef491-->
- `calls_dir_for` (function) — Returns the `tianluo/calls/` directory Path under a given project_root's runtime dir, where interaction call files live. <!--#9a1327a53a38f063-->
- `classify_kind` (function) — Resolves a parsed call dict's interaction kind, defaulting legacy or unrecognized files to `CALL_KIND_CALL` so old artifacts work without migration. <!--#880f7c9758d2615c-->
- `write_call` (function) — Atomically writes a call file of a given kind with prompt/context/options payload, returning its path. <!--#5eb93b7be0ca617f-->
- `read_call` (function) — Parses a call file into a dict (always carrying a `kind` key), returning `None` on any read/parse error. <!--#a51ef169b9c2eacf-->
- `response_path` (function) — Returns the canonical sibling `.response` path for a given call file. <!--#6943622212596f29-->
- `read_response` (function) — Returns the parsed sibling answer file, recognizing both `.response` and `.response.json` variants, or `None` if none exists. <!--#f16ade7359cac25c-->
- `write_response` (function) — Atomically writes a sibling `.response` answer file (wrapping non-dict values) and returns its path. <!--#8d02ff1e8ce9e6d0-->
- `write_interjection_request` (function) — Daemon-side producer that queues a mid-flow user interjection as a `CALL_KIND_INTERJECTION` call file (carrying the text and flow_id) for the running `luo run` process to consume. <!--#9c0d9a8e37705a45-->
- `drain_interjection_requests` (function) — `luo run` consumer that scans `tianluo/calls/` for unanswered interjection call files, returns one dict per drained item (oldest first) with text/call_id/step_id/step_type/created_at, and seals each via an idempotent write-response-then-unlink protocol. <!--#4cf8f02d9983cb9f-->
- `write_retry_decision_call` (function) — Writes a `CALL_KIND_RETRY_DECISION` call file for a failed step on the no-TTY path so an external responder (e.g. the web console) can choose retry/skip/abort, keying the call_id off step_id so resumes reuse the same file. <!--#d1a45880672ca06a-->
- `write_interaction_call` (function) — Project-root-addressed convenience wrapper around `write_call` that writes an arbitrary-kind interaction call file under `<project_root>/tianluo/calls/`, folding extra keyword args into the payload. <!--#2f02c7961adb915d-->
- `read_interaction_response` (function) — Returns the bare answer value for a call (unwrapping `{response: ...}` envelopes from either `.response.json` or plain `.response`), or `None` when no answer exists yet. <!--#318712f1706b9339-->
- `make_cli_confirm_handler` (function) — Builds an `on_confirm` callback for the agent runner that writes a `cli_confirm` call file, polls for the sibling response while the subprocess lives, and marks orphaned calls consumed if the child exits unanswered. <!--#1f5d19c172a19a06-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/issue_discovery.py` (python) — Flow-engine module for automatic issue discovery, providing A-class system triggers (fix-loop exhaustion, pre-existing failures), B-class whitelist-based prompt injection and output collection with title-based deduplication via the IssueDiscovery class, plus a scoped executor that applies LLM-emitted create/update/delete issue operations under tracking-set constraints. <!--#21191a002ee07633|fbd916824bfc4e68-->
- `_normalize_issue_id` (function) — Helper that strips leading zeros from an issue ID so zero-padded variants like '5' and '005' compare equal in membership checks. <!--#3d9056ee5983eaff-->
- `apply_discovery_issue_operations` (function) — Engine-side executor that runs LLM-emitted create/update/delete issue intents for a discovery step, enforcing the tracking-set scope guarantee and isolating each operation so one failure doesn't abort the batch. <!--#ffeb9af8ec081bdb-->
- `_apply_create` (function) — Creates a new issue with source='human' and adds its ID to the discovery step's tracking set. <!--#3c972612bf74020d-->
- `_apply_update` (function) — Updates a tracked issue's editable fields (title/description/priority/type/tags only), rejecting out-of-scope IDs and dropping malformed non-list tags. <!--#8108bd67f54f0192-->
- `_apply_delete` (function) — Deletes a tracked issue and removes its ID from the tracking set, rejecting out-of-scope IDs. <!--#cebe0d8a0b5000ed-->
- `IssueDiscovery` (class) — A per-flow helper class that manages automatic issue discovery for the SE3 flow engine, creating deduplicated auto-discovered Issues (with tags/priority) from A-class system triggers like fix-loop exhaustion and pre-existing test failures. <!--#dd0cf60508918dcb-->
  - `IssueDiscovery.__init__` (method) — Initializes the discovery instance with an IssueManager, flow ID, and an empty list of created titles for deduplication. <!--#1292078f24c6befe-->
  - `IssueDiscovery.create_from_fix_loop_exhaustion` (method) — An A-class trigger method that, when the fix loop hits its max iterations, builds a rich high-priority bug Issue (task/refined description, flow ID, trigger step, fix iteration count, last test output, fix history, and fix instructions) and creates it via IssueManager unless deduplicated. <!--#a881e85ce86db3ff-->
  - `IssueDiscovery.create_from_pre_existing_failures` (method) — A-class trigger that creates a medium-priority issue documenting inherited baseline test failures not introduced by the current change. <!--#bf9800b8f2e5bb00-->
  - `IssueDiscovery.get_injection_prompt` (method) — Returns the issue-discovery prompt fragment for whitelisted step types (B-class injection), or None otherwise. <!--#2979579ce1738652-->
  - `IssueDiscovery.collect_issues_from_output` (method) — B-class collector that parses a whitelisted step's discovered_issues output and creates deduplicated source=system issues from each valid entry. <!--#2b8bce29a5aede95-->
  - `IssueDiscovery._is_duplicate` (method) — Checks whether a title matches any already-created title in this flow using normalized similarity comparison. <!--#1a096e2f501e6ea8-->
  - `IssueDiscovery._normalize_title` (method) — Normalizes a title for comparison by lowercasing, stripping punctuation, and collapsing whitespace. <!--#28516bc357948272-->
  - `IssueDiscovery._titles_similar` (method) — Determines if two normalized titles are near-duplicates via exact match or >70% token-overlap ratio. <!--#16f9009715e698f8-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/issue_manager.py` (python) — Module implementing SE3's YAML-based issue tracker — the Issue dataclass/IssueStatus enum plus the IssueManager class that creates, adopts, loads, lists, updates, moves, and deletes issue files across tianluo/issues/open and closed/, with collision-free ID allocation serialized through a shared fcntl-locked .next_id counter and #NNN reference rewriting on renumber. <!--#649ec3086ca88eda|41f028bbfbcc2c98-->
- `IssueStatus` (class) — Enum of the five issue lifecycle states (open, in-progress, resolved, won't-fix, closed). <!--#decbedd5a7c9f2d6-->
- `Issue` (class) — Dataclass representing a single issue record with serialization helpers and a derived display title. <!--#ff53e1ff54ead2d9-->
  - `Issue.display_title` (method) — Property that returns a human-readable title, falling back from explicit title to the first non-empty description line to "untitled". <!--#1a19b1f1da95d214-->
  - `Issue.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the issue to a YAML-ready dict, including optional fields only when set. <!--#5baf46152d4ccfe9-->
  - `Issue.from_dict` (method) — Classmethod that deserializes an issue from a dict, tolerating missing/legacy fields and parsing timestamps defensively. <!--#1fb4f2a14503faab-->
- `_numeric_id_or_none` (function) — Helper that parses an issue ID into an int (or None if non-numeric), used to decide whether an adopt actually renumbered the issue before invoking the #NNN reference-rewrite/trace primitives. <!--#9b63cfc2f30db776-->
- `_make_slug` (function) — Helper that converts a title into a lowercase, hyphenated URL/filesystem-friendly slug. <!--#0de7a9734d3c82a6-->
- `_derive_slug_for_issue` (function) — Helper that derives a filename slug for an issue using the same title-priority logic as display_title. <!--#f32424f3c00139e5-->
- `IssueManager` (class) — Class managing the full issue lifecycle (create, adopt, load, list, status updates, and file movement between open/ and closed/ directories) backed by per-issue YAML files under the project's runtime issues dir. <!--#c183b404f985473c-->
  - `IssueManager.__init__` (method) — Constructor that records the project root and derives the issues directory paths (issues/, open/, closed/) from the project's runtime dir. <!--#6123584715091f25-->
  - `IssueManager._ensure_dirs` (method) — Creates the open/ and closed/ issue directories if they don't already exist. <!--#8e38a3b44bcd372f-->
  - `IssueManager._next_id` (method) — Allocates the next zero-padded 3-digit issue ID by delegating to the shared fcntl-locked reserve_next_id primitive, which reconciles the .next_id counter against the on-disk store so IDs are never reused across concurrent allocators. <!--#e788fbbc79efdb21-->
  - `IssueManager._find_issue_file` (method) — Locates an issue's YAML file by ID across open/ and closed/, tolerating zero-padding differences. <!--#395484abb8bf782f-->
  - `IssueManager.create` (method) — Creates a new open issue from a required description (plus optional metadata), writing its YAML to open/. <!--#fe8f1910d7c1a7a6-->
  - `IssueManager.adopt_issue` (method) — Folds an externally-originated issue into this project under a freshly-allocated non-colliding ID (preserving all other fields), writing it to open/ or closed/ by status and, unless deferred, rewriting #<old> references, appending a renumber trace, and advancing .next_id — used by luo merge runtime-sync. <!--#e875ca419b314b40-->
  - `IssueManager.append_renumber_trace` (method) — Appends the 'old → new' audit line to an already-written issue file, completing a deferred adopt after the batch bulk reference rewrite so the trace's embedded #<old> is not repointed, returning None if the issue has no file. <!--#fefa502e3904bbaf-->
  - `IssueManager.load` (method) — Loads and returns an issue by ID from open/ or closed/, or None if not found. <!--#020eb18913a1d3ab-->
  - `IssueManager.list_issues` (method) — Lists issues (open by default, optionally closed) with optional type and source filters, sorted by ID. <!--#83ee845dc598e516-->
  - `IssueManager.update_status` (method) — Validates and applies a status transition, updating the YAML and moving the file between open/ and closed/ as needed. <!--#d96cdeb912e9e247-->
  - `IssueManager.reset_to_open` (method) — Resets an in-progress issue back to open, erroring if it is in any other state. <!--#a22f7bfa163b4e22-->
  - `IssueManager.find_open_by_title` (method) — Finds an open issue whose display title case-insensitively matches the given title. <!--#83a2c1627c6282c0-->
  - `IssueManager.close_issue` (method) — Closes an open issue (falling back to resolved when needed) and moves its file to closed/. <!--#77684cefd8dabbd4-->
  - `IssueManager.delete_issue` (method) — Permanently deletes an issue's YAML file by ID with no status transition or file move. <!--#25390c6a0d56a160-->
  - `IssueManager.list_by_tags` (method) — Lists issues that contain all of the specified tags, optionally including closed ones. <!--#a4ef3ff5e8af3ded-->
  - `IssueManager.update_fields` (method) — Updates editable issue fields and renames the YAML file when the derived slug changes. <!--#712c1fc23aaca8f1-->
  - `IssueManager.reopen_issue` (method) — Reopens a closed/resolved/won't-fix issue back to open, moving its file to open/. <!--#53e5b2dd713901f3-->
  - `IssueManager._read_issue` (method) — Reads and parses an issue YAML file into an Issue, returning None on parse failure. <!--#33a506ffef4077af-->
  - `IssueManager._write_issue` (method) — Serializes an issue and writes it as YAML to the given filepath. <!--#26627c78c08ec256-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/json_extractor.py` (python) — Two-phase JSON extractor that reliably recovers a schema-complete JSON dict from raw LLM output, using a direct-parse fast path first and, on failure, stripping stream-json to assistant text and invoking a lightweight second LLM pass to restructure it. <!--#aaed016a6e055540|1d927ac6d6a985f9-->
- `JSONExtractor` (class) — Class that extracts a JSON dict from raw LLM output, trying a direct parse first and a lightweight second LLM pass as fallback. <!--#16dfa7c498bda86b-->
  - `JSONExtractor.__init__` (method) — Constructor storing the project root (for the LLM caller) and the extraction call timeout. <!--#5c1837782c47b8c5-->
  - `JSONExtractor.extract` (method) — Public entry point that returns parsed JSON via the direct-parse fast path, or delegates to LLM extraction when that fails. <!--#08106d958854572b-->
  - `JSONExtractor._try_direct_parse` (method) — Helper that attempts to parse the raw output directly using the shared json_parser utility without invoking an LLM. <!--#c74809bed98aaa51-->
  - `JSONExtractor._extract_text_from_stream_json` (method) — Helper that parses stream-json (NDJSON) output and concatenates the text content of assistant messages, dropping tool calls and results. <!--#1c3d95c718342e3c-->
  - `JSONExtractor._extract_with_llm` (method) — Fallback that strips stream-json to assistant text, prompts a non-JSON LLMCaller to restructure it into schema-complete JSON, and parses the result. <!--#903e5a4227f7fd73-->
- `extract_json_two_phase` (function) — Module-level convenience function that constructs a JSONExtractor and runs two-phase extraction in one call. <!--#f6b6bb2c3227af8b-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/json_modes.py` (python) — Defines the JsonMode enum (STRICT, EXTRACT, TWO_PHASE, OFF) of strategies for obtaining structured JSON from LLM calls, plus a get_json_mode helper that resolves the active mode from explicit and legacy parameters via a fixed backward-compatible priority order. <!--#ce8dd0cd45ed60bb|92767f0284f446eb-->
- `JsonMode` (class) — Enum enumerating the available JSON extraction strategies (STRICT, EXTRACT, TWO_PHASE, OFF) used to control how an LLM call produces structured output. <!--#3c44b448f5440910-->
- `get_json_mode` (function) — Resolves a JsonMode from a mix of explicit and legacy parameters (json_mode, two_phase_json, require_json), applying a fixed priority order for backward compatibility. <!--#45eacf3bde2932c4-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/llm_caller.py` (python) — The engine's LLM invocation layer: `LLMCaller` builds prompts (extra-prompt injection, retry history with dedup and a `_post_dedup_safety_cap` head-truncation guard), drives `AgentRunner`/`ClaudeRunner` subprocesses in strict, extract, and two-phase JSON modes, retries with agent rotation on infrastructure errors, and streams NDJSON output through `StreamJSONTracker` to surface progress, touched files, and token-usage totals. <!--#ec95cdb4fdb9eb02|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/logging_config.py` (python) — Defines the flow engine's structured logging subsystem — log-level and event-type enums, a serializable StructuredLogEntry value object, and a singleton StructuredLogger that writes JSON-lines daily log files with an in-memory buffer, console output, per-flow/step/LLM timing helpers, and log retrieval/export. <!--#5b6a21ef813d6dc6|7c79a7fcdeb5af16-->
- `LogLevel` (class) — String enum defining the five severity levels (debug through critical) used for log entries and filtering. <!--#0afc90c8e31e38f7-->
- `LogEventType` (class) — String enum enumerating the categories of flow-engine log events across flow, step, LLM, persistence, and tool operations. <!--#e6e9c091fe6eacd7-->
- `StructuredLogEntry` (class) — Value object representing a single structured log event with metadata and serialization to dict/JSON. <!--#b3501160ecd27907-->
  - `StructuredLogEntry.__init__` (method) — Constructs a log entry, stamping the current UTC timestamp and storing event type, level, and optional flow/step/LLM context. <!--#059a51e6b392ac75-->
  - `StructuredLogEntry.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the entry to a dictionary, omitting unset optional fields and rounding the duration. <!--#234f02f7ff69c0bf-->
  - `StructuredLogEntry.to_json` (method) — Serializes the entry to a JSON string via its dict representation. <!--#6f39524c89de5837-->
- `StructuredLogger` (class) — A structured JSON-lines logger that writes engine events (flows, steps, LLM calls) to daily-rotated log files under the runtime logs dir, keeps an in-memory buffer of recent entries for status queries, optionally mirrors human-readable colored output to stderr, and exposes level filtering plus convenience methods for common event types. <!--#c9b4c1e3d593e170-->
  - `StructuredLogger.__init__` (method) — Initializes the logger by resolving the log directory (default: runtime logs dir), creating it, selecting today's rotated log file, and setting up the console/min-level config, the bounded recent-logs buffer, and step/LLM timing trackers. <!--#93f30507ea2e9013-->
  - `StructuredLogger._get_log_file` (method) — Returns the date-stamped JSON-lines log file path for the current day. <!--#4f29bb52bebeaebd-->
  - `StructuredLogger._should_log` (method) — Determines whether a given level meets the configured minimum threshold. <!--#60722b42c6fbf2cb-->
  - `StructuredLogger._write_log` (method) — Appends an entry to the current log file, updates the bounded in-memory buffer, and emits console output if enabled. <!--#845a6fa3db9a39bb-->
  - `StructuredLogger._console_output` (method) — Prints a human-readable, color-coded one-line summary of an entry to stderr. <!--#3428059cb34f263a-->
  - `StructuredLogger.log` (method) — Core logging method that builds a StructuredLogEntry and writes it if the level passes the threshold. <!--#b5c689d8f1d507d8-->
  - `StructuredLogger.flow_started` (method) — Convenience method logging a flow-started event with the task and task type. <!--#010d617a47430eb6-->
  - `StructuredLogger.flow_completed` (method) — Convenience method logging a successful flow-completion event with its duration. <!--#6334121e6557f6d8-->
  - `StructuredLogger.flow_failed` (method) — Convenience method logging a flow-failure event with the error and optional duration. <!--#19591ad845bb411a-->
  - `StructuredLogger.step_started` (method) — Starts a per-step timer and logs a step-started event. <!--#c898e0b04a6e3713-->
  - `StructuredLogger.step_completed` (method) — Logs a step-completion event with computed duration and optional outputs. <!--#16ba47376084468d-->
  - `StructuredLogger.step_failed` (method) — Logs a step-failure event with duration, error, and retry indication, downgrading severity when a retry will follow. <!--#b8368ebbb9097a76-->
  - `StructuredLogger.llm_call_started` (method) — Starts an LLM-call timer and logs the call-started event with model and prompt size. <!--#0b2900cc5c77e4b3-->
  - `StructuredLogger.llm_call_completed` (method) — Logs an LLM-call-completed event with duration and input/output token counts. <!--#634b0aa95a7ac233-->
  - `StructuredLogger.llm_call_failed` (method) — Logs an LLM-call-failure event with duration, model, and error. <!--#1a7b3576bbc26ef7-->
  - `StructuredLogger.state_saved` (method) — Convenience method logging a state-saved event referencing the persisted state file. <!--#593c9924dc51089d-->
  - `StructuredLogger.get_recent_logs` (method) — Returns recent buffered log entries, optionally filtered by event type and flow ID and capped by a limit. <!--#8c123a66b7b211f9-->
  - `StructuredLogger.export_logs` (method) — Reads all daily log files and exports matching entries (filtered by time and event type) to a JSON file, returning the count. <!--#cbed0084601dd847-->
- `get_logger` (function) — Module-level accessor that lazily creates and returns the singleton StructuredLogger instance. <!--#45e4799fe4cca297-->
- `reset_logger` (function) — Resets the global logger singleton, primarily for testing. <!--#1cb3faeb6146c533-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/models.py` (python) — Defines the flow engine's core data model — the StepType/StepStatus/FlowStatus enums plus the Step, Transition, State, and FlowInstance dataclasses — together with their full-inline and header-only (hot/cold split) serialization helpers that round-trip a run through `engine.json` while deferring heavy step bodies, `context`, and `fix_history` to external cold payloads. <!--#d1342694cc1ccce9|eb1bb24dcec9b77d-->
- `StepType` (class) — Enum enumerating every workflow step kind in the step pool — from discovery/analyze/plan through implement/test/self_check and the various check and spec steps, to commit/summarize plus the two merge-side steps (MERGE_INTEGRATE, VERSION_RECONCILE) that only a worktree flow appends — with inline comments marking which values are deprecated. <!--#517c09dd8cb0f1a6-->
- `StepStatus` (class) — Enum of a step's execution lifecycle states (pending, running, completed, partial, failed, retrying, paused, revision_needed). <!--#38d6ab911468a93f-->
- `Step` (class) — A dataclass modeling one workflow step — its type, status, timing/retry and LLM-model config, optional cwd override, inputs/outputs/artifacts, error fields, and hot/cold lazy-load bookkeeping — with methods to serialize (full, header-only, cold payload) and materialize its externalized body. <!--#e2d7e5aa1edcf793-->
  - `Step.to_dict` (method) — Serializes a step to a full inline dictionary including all metadata plus the heavy inputs/outputs/artifacts bodies. <!--#257609c083c1358d-->
  - `Step.to_header_dict` (method) — Serializes only the KB-scale status-table fields, omitting the heavy inputs/outputs/artifacts body for the hot/cold-split header. <!--#a632cd902601e663-->
  - `Step.cold_payload` (method) — Returns just the heavy per-step body (inputs/outputs/artifacts) that gets externalized to a cold file. <!--#067d19099d525307-->
  - `Step.apply_cold` (method) — Lazily materializes a header-only step's externalized body, with a data-loss guard that leaves the step unloaded on a failed cold read so an intact file is never overwritten with empty data. <!--#cb38dad39673e591-->
  - `Step.from_dict` (method) — Reconstructs a Step from its dictionary (full inline form), restoring hot/cold provenance markers so a transiently-unreadable cold file is re-emitted rather than overwritten with empty data. <!--#937a996c0e28916b-->
  - `Step.from_header_dict` (method) — Deserializes a header-only step, leaving its body empty and cold_loaded False while retaining the cold_ref for on-demand hydration or unchanged re-emit. <!--#4070520bb875d5c6-->
- `Transition` (class) — Dataclass describing a state-machine transition rule from one step type to another with an optional condition. <!--#7a2689d2166206ee-->
  - `Transition.to_dict` (method) — Serializes a Transition to a dictionary. <!--#4540da1b0410523c-->
  - `Transition.from_dict` (method) — Reconstructs a Transition from its serialized dictionary form. <!--#cdfa73691c44022b-->
- `State` (class) — Central dataclass holding all mutable flow-engine state — current/selected/completed steps, shared `context`, review and fix-loop counters, the pre-implement `baseline_failures` snapshot, session-wide token/cost usage, and hot/cold persistence bookkeeping — plus the serialization helpers that round-trip it through `engine.json`. <!--#dc61aad493726edf-->
  - `State.add_session_usage_record` (method) — Appends one per-call `UsageRecord` to the session ledger, skipping exact `(call_id, attempt)` duplicates, and recomputes `session_token_usage` as a projection of that ledger. <!--#89167cf3200471a9-->
  - `State.get_current_step` (method) — Returns the currently active Step, or None if none is set. <!--#918e318297b74364-->
  - `State.add_step` (method) — Registers a Step in the state, auto-generating a sortable human-readable step_id and appending it to history. <!--#8764118b5d041b38-->
  - `State.get_step_to_review` (method) — Finds the step preceding a given confirm step (the one being reviewed) from history. <!--#7a52d05a0edb06c5-->
  - `State.increment_review_iteration` (method) — Increments and returns the review-cycle iteration count for a given step. <!--#7dcf9130950ebe0b-->
  - `State.get_review_iteration` (method) — Returns the current review iteration count for a step (0 if never reviewed). <!--#19414144af977a06-->
  - `State.increment_fix_iteration` (method) — Increments the test-verify-fix loop counter, appends a capped history entry, and mirrors the count into context. <!--#3550ebf4a7e40719-->
  - `State.get_fix_iteration` (method) — Returns the current fix-loop iteration count. <!--#6b71e3bdd412a0bc-->
  - `State.update_task_type` (method) — Stores the analyze-step-resolved task type in the shared context. <!--#a1d6daf59f1e228d-->
  - `State.is_type_pending` (method) — Reports whether the task type has not yet been resolved. <!--#4e7aadf82393a590-->
  - `State.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the full state (inline steps, context, fix history, baseline, usage ledger plus its five-field tally) to a plain dict for persistence. <!--#acd9ab7d8e22e4db-->
  - `State.to_header_dict` (method) — Serializes the KB-scale state header — per-step status table with bodies replaced and the unbounded context/fix_history dropped for external cold storage. <!--#243b70e8f3069785-->
  - `State.cold_context` (method) — Returns the shared cold payload (context and fix_history) externalized out of the state header. <!--#613d3836030a3441-->
  - `State._restore_session_usage` (method) — Helper that rebuilds the `(usage_records, totals)` pair from serialized data, falling back to the legacy five-field tally and its embedded records for older `engine.json` files. <!--#f6c264d07b689c15-->
  - `State.from_header_dict` (method) — Deserializes a header-only state whose step bodies and shared `context`/`fix_history` stay deferred to external cold payloads, marking the context as not-yet-loaded so a failed cold read cannot overwrite it. <!--#e87ce86e69d39426-->
  - `State.from_dict` (method) — Deserializes a fully inline state dict, clamping oversized `fix_history` to the sliding-window cap, preserving the tri-state `baseline_failures`, restoring usage records, and picking up hot/cold context provenance markers when present. <!--#1e54337bf440bb89-->
- `FlowStatus` (class) — Enum of a flow instance's overall lifecycle status (init, running, paused, completed, failed, recovering). <!--#2e96c050c86ed8d4-->
- `FlowInstance` (class) — The top-level dataclass representing a single flow-engine run, bundling identity/status, the task description, the embedded State machine, timestamps, change/issue tracking, worktree-isolation fields, and a waiting_for_lock sub-state, with to_dict/from_dict plus header-only (to_header_dict/from_header_dict) serialization for the hot/cold engine.json persistence format and a get_progress helper. <!--#1604ab361e742ce6-->
  - `FlowInstance.to_dict` (method) — Serializes a flow instance to a full dictionary, emitting the waiting_for_lock key only when actually waiting to stay backward-compatible with old engine.json readers. <!--#39bfc2e2a3eb1289-->
  - `FlowInstance.to_header_dict` (method) — Serializes the KB-scale flow header, identical to to_dict except the heavy state block is replaced by State.to_header_dict. <!--#aa1b15eb1063dcd8-->
  - `FlowInstance.from_header_dict` (method) — Deserializes a header-only flow, reusing from_dict for identity/metadata with an empty state then installing the header-only State via State.from_header_dict. <!--#350e037e5afda9f8-->
  - `FlowInstance.from_dict` (method) — Reconstructs a FlowInstance from its dictionary, reading each metadata/worktree field and defaulting missing legacy keys (like waiting_for_lock) to safe values. <!--#78e16df247ad23b5-->
  - `FlowInstance.get_progress` (method) — Returns flow completion as a (completed_count, total_count) tuple. <!--#382fd14e9da0d282-->
- `get_step_info` (function) — Looks up a step type's metadata entry from the STEP_POOL. <!--#9d66a58a6cd35598-->
- `get_default_step_sequence` (function) — Returns the initial (analyze-modifiable) list of StepType values for a given task type from a static table covering feature, bugfix, review, small, survey and discovery, falling back to the feature sequence for unknown or retired types so old flows still resume; StepType.E2E is deliberately absent and inserted conditionally elsewhere. <!--#e40d076ae1ee4085-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/output.py` (python) — A utility module providing helpers to format arbitrary data into strings, log messages at named levels, and format and render errors and success messages (with optional context/details) through the display module. <!--#089611ad36a74f8d|c0b1b9557353d0db-->
- `format_output` (function) — Converts any data type (string, dict/list as pretty JSON, else str) to a string representation without truncation, ignoring the deprecated truncate flag. <!--#1fb8dc97c460cf5b-->
- `log_output` (function) — Logs a message at a named level via the module logger, used for internal logging output that bypasses the display module. <!--#bcd99a66853b242d-->
- `format_error` (function) — Builds a Rich-markup error string from an exception or message, with an optional context key/value block, using i18n-translated labels. <!--#0eb718e4817745ef-->
- `display_error` (function) — Renders a formatted error message into a full-width error panel via `render_full`. <!--#0a0dbeaf6ce8adfd-->
- `display_success` (function) — Renders a green success message plus optional key/value details into a full-width success panel. <!--#2d9bad1ac7706454-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/output_formatter.py` (python) — Module providing a name-keyed registry and factory for SE3 output formatters, exposing a lazily-created global FormatterRegistry singleton (seeded with the default 'tasks' TaskFormatter) plus module-level convenience functions to register, retrieve, and list formatters. <!--#4dcdfd93fddf90e8|eca8291d052da2a1-->
- `FormatterRegistry` (class) — Class that maintains a name-to-formatter-class mapping and acts as a factory for instantiating formatters, seeded with default formatters on construction. <!--#059002186071d632-->
  - `FormatterRegistry.__init__` (method) — Initializes the empty formatter mapping and registers the default formatters. <!--#d42322823229516e-->
  - `FormatterRegistry._register_default_formatters` (method) — Registers the built-in default formatters (currently the 'tasks' TaskFormatter). <!--#e0ff2860430fe51d-->
  - `FormatterRegistry.register_formatter` (method) — Stores a formatter class under a given name, warning if it overwrites an existing registration. <!--#8566348c910c841e-->
  - `FormatterRegistry.get_formatter` (method) — Looks up and instantiates a formatter by name with optional constructor kwargs, returning None (and logging) on missing name or instantiation failure. <!--#56a1016d3a6b9cd2-->
  - `FormatterRegistry.list_formatters` (method) — Returns a dict mapping each registered formatter name to its class name. <!--#ad7a2621dacf661f-->
  - `FormatterRegistry.unregister_formatter` (method) — Removes a formatter by name, returning whether it was present. <!--#ec59bc018e1528a2-->
- `get_registry` (function) — Lazily creates and returns the module-level singleton FormatterRegistry. <!--#0450178df4985dc7-->
- `register_formatter` (function) — Module-level convenience that registers a formatter class on the global registry. <!--#defcad979b65f3de-->
- `get_formatter` (function) — Module-level convenience that retrieves a formatter instance from the global registry by name. <!--#f3cc7acf1ada4e92-->
- `list_formatters` (function) — Module-level convenience that lists all formatters registered in the global registry. <!--#cb28e95009c9c96e-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/persistence.py` (python) — Defines `PersistenceManager` and its helpers, the flow engine's state-persistence layer: it atomically writes and loads `engine.json`, resumable snapshots, archives, context exports and progress Markdown, using a hot/cold split format (`hotcold/1`) that stores each step's heavy inputs/outputs in content-hashed cold files, hydrates them lazily via `_LazyStepDict`, and falls back to tolerant/repairing reads for legacy or corrupted fully-inline state files. <!--#b20ec4e7e3bf1dad|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/plan_decomposition.py` (python) — Defines the PLAN decomposition model — the `PlanDecomposition`/`PlanGranularity` enums, the immutable `PlanModeView` projection, and the write-once `PlanModeResolver` (explicit request > project config > default) — plus the shared `effective_mode`/`is_forced_single_group`/`holistic_execution_mode` helpers that give PLAN, plan CONFIRM, IMPLEMENT, and the state machine a single consistent answer about a flow's grouping shape, including a non-mutating projection for legacy `direct` flows predating the model. <!--#413af527a47fb05b|874eca35828e1d0c-->
- `PlanDecomposition` (class) — A string enum naming the doctrine PLAN uses to break work down — `CAPABILITY` for coarse task-level groups split only at the capability edge, or the legacy `GRANULAR` per-task listing. <!--#448e9a22b61de97e-->
- `PlanGranularity` (class) — String enum for the group-count pressure applied under the capability doctrine — `AUTO`, `SINGLE`, or `CONSERVATIVE`. <!--#0813fa1624d1328a-->
- `PlanModeError` (class) — `ValueError` subclass raised when a requested decomposition or granularity value is not one of the legal enum members. <!--#d614e85bdc493007-->
- `PlanModeView` (class) — Immutable read-only projection of a flow's plan mode (decomposition, granularity, human-readable reason) plus the `legacy_strategy`/`inferred` annotations used when the values were derived from a pre-model flow. <!--#c21fb425b035673e-->
  - `PlanModeView.to_dict` (method) — Renders the view as the primitive context write payload keyed by `PLAN_DECOMPOSITION_KEY`, `PLAN_GRANULARITY_KEY`, and `PLAN_MODE_REASON_KEY`. <!--#56eae07d8cce8b6b-->
  - `PlanModeView.to_projection` (method) — Returns the presentation-shaped dict — the write payload plus the `legacy_strategy` annotation for display surfaces. <!--#4875df126c5f6107-->
- `PlanModeResolver` (class) — Classmethod-only resolver that decides the PLAN decomposition/granularity (explicit request > project configuration > default), persists it write-once into a new flow's context, and projects persisted or legacy state back out as a `PlanModeView`. <!--#bf30382f40a895a6-->
  - `PlanModeResolver.resolve_requested` (method) — Resolves a decomposition/granularity pair from an explicit request, workflow configuration, or defaults without touching any flow context. <!--#529de945e0185747-->
  - `PlanModeResolver.initialize_context` (method) — Writes the resolved decomposition, granularity, and reason into a new flow's context exactly once, returning the already-persisted view unchanged on re-entry so mid-flow config edits cannot re-interpret an existing plan. <!--#5bdfaac264e3a714-->
  - `PlanModeResolver.view` (method) — Returns the persisted plan mode, or — for a flow predating the model — a non-mutating view projected from the retired `effective_implementation_strategy` (or current defaults), never upgrading the stored state. <!--#af5bbb01248b9985-->
  - `PlanModeResolver._resolve_with_sources` (method) — Internal helper resolving both axes and reporting, per axis, whether the value came from an explicit request, configuration, or the default. <!--#4404fc83c370be5d-->
  - `PlanModeResolver._from_configuration` (method) — Reads one axis off a `WorkflowConfig`-shaped object or mapping, using the companion `*_explicit` flag to distinguish a deliberate project choice from a dataclass default. <!--#d97de93264362230-->
  - `PlanModeResolver._build_reason` (method) — Formats the human-readable reason string stating each axis's chosen value and whether it was explicit, configured, or defaulted. <!--#217c5e85436f26d2-->
  - `PlanModeResolver._persisted_view` (method) — Builds a `PlanModeView` from persisted context keys, returning `None` when the decomposition key is absent or unreadable so callers fall back to the legacy projection rather than failing a resume. <!--#e3bfe5944362c850-->
- `plan_group_count` (function) — Returns how many task groups PLAN handed downstream — `task_groups` length preferred, `plan_group_count` as fallback, `None` meaning PLAN has not been read yet (never to be treated as one). <!--#7446f355f877d865-->
- `_legacy_direct_projection` (function) — Internal predicate that is true only when the flow recorded no new-model decomposition and its retired strategy projects onto the capability/forced-single shape (i.e. the old `direct` path). <!--#f6b08dd255fbb304-->
- `effective_mode` (function) — The single shared projection of the doctrine/granularity a flow is actually executing under, overlaying step inputs on flow context so PLAN, plan CONFIRM, and IMPLEMENT can never disagree about the decomposition. <!--#77b9256fee2d4d8f-->
- `is_forced_single_group` (function) — Reports whether the flow is mechanically pinned to the one-call shape, reading the raw `plan_granularity` key (or the legacy `direct` projection) so the guarantee never depends on PLAN obeying a prompt directive. <!--#9f7e317fce7dbac4-->
- `is_capability_decomposition` (function) — Returns whether the flow runs the capability doctrine, delegating to `effective_mode` so planning and implementation share one answer. <!--#316297371cc7a352-->
- `is_legacy_direct_flow` (function) — Returns True only for flows created under the retired `direct` execution axis that still carry no `task_groups`, so such a flow keeps its whole-task single-call shape on resume instead of being handed an empty group list — once ANALYZE re-adds PLAN and groups appear, the check yields False and the shape is read from the plan via `holistic_execution_mode`. <!--#875d64ca34a665ca-->
- `holistic_execution_mode` (function) — The one decision point — shared by the IMPLEMENT handler and the state machine — returning the whole-task execution shape (`small`, legacy-direct, or single-group) or `None` for genuinely grouped work. <!--#aa76c87159b600f4-->
- `_coerce` (function) — Coerces a raw value into the given enum, raising `PlanModeError` naming the source and the legal value set on failure. <!--#c4bab224fb428745-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/project_context.py` (python) — Defines `ProjectContextCollector`, which gathers project-wide context for a project root — git status, flow-engine history (both via `commands/status.py` helpers), and backlog items parsed from `tianluo/specs/_backlog/*.md` — into a single dict under the `git`, `flow_engine`, and `backlog` keys, degrading each source to a safe default on failure. <!--#4f98b604536d8860|dd5f9df27f60d102-->
- `ProjectContextCollector` (class) — Aggregates project-wide context for a given project root — git status, flow-engine history (both delegated to `commands/status.py` helpers), and backlog items parsed from `tianluo/specs/_backlog/*.md` — returning it as one structured dict with per-source failures degrading to safe defaults. <!--#bcc445339a658bc5-->
  - `ProjectContextCollector.__init__` (method) — Constructor storing the project root path as a Path. <!--#9812ec98f69838a9-->
  - `ProjectContextCollector.collect` (method) — Entry point that runs the three private collectors and returns their results under the `git`, `flow_engine`, and `backlog` keys. <!--#40fd20a9676b74c0-->
  - `ProjectContextCollector._collect_git` (method) — Returns git status via the commands/status helper, falling back to an unknown-branch default on error. <!--#acb96af4ae25b142-->
  - `ProjectContextCollector._collect_flow_engine` (method) — Returns flow engine history via the commands/status helper, or None on failure. <!--#056dd30cb3a17c33-->
  - `ProjectContextCollector._collect_backlog` (method) — Scans the runtime `tianluo/specs/_backlog/*.md` directory and parses each markdown file into a backlog item (slug, title, status, phase), skipping unreadable files. <!--#3a755b1cc8df097a-->
  - `ProjectContextCollector._parse_backlog_item` (method) — Parses a backlog markdown file's first lines to extract title, status, and phase. <!--#512c11b5f66af35a-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/prompt_dedup.py` (python) — A standalone utility module whose `deduplicate_prompt_lines` function collapses repeated contiguous line-blocks in an LLM prompt string, keeping the first occurrence and replacing later copies with content-hash `[DUPLICATED CONTENT:...]` markers via O(n) fingerprint matching. <!--#14e7b640b0b10a2c|72b2d7612e58296b-->
- `deduplicate_prompt_lines` (function) — Scans a prompt for repeated contiguous line blocks of at least `min_block_lines`, keeping the first occurrence and replacing duplicates with content-hash-based `[DUPLICATED CONTENT:...]` markers via fingerprint-based O(n) matching. <!--#371239b146ce980e-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/prompt_history.py` (python) — Module that provides prompt_toolkit FileHistory instances for SE3's interactive input, storing prompts at tianluo/history/prompt_history and truncating the file to the most recent MAX_ENTRIES (500) before use. <!--#47885db9a8cd6ea2|04bd12b146c2d87e-->
- `_truncate_history` (function) — Helper that parses a prompt_toolkit history file and rewrites it to retain only the most recent MAX_ENTRIES entries, failing silently on I/O errors. <!--#2200a06d776996fb-->
- `get_prompt_history` (function) — Returns a prompt_toolkit FileHistory instance backed by the tianluo/history/prompt_history file under project_root, creating the directory and truncating the file to MAX_ENTRIES beforehand so interactive prompts support up/down navigation. <!--#f1f10322a54b9ed3-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/prompt_markers.py` (python) — Defines the HTML-comment sentinel markers and pure helper functions that delimit the template-prefix / user-content / framework-suffix segments of a step prompt so the web console can render the user's literal input as its own bubble, providing both the preferred three-segment wrapper (wrap_user_section) and its extractor (extract_user_content), a bounded jsonl scanner for the first user-content record (first_user_content), and legacy two-segment compatibility helpers (inject_boundary, wrap_user_content). <!--#8890d27426b1d937|2ad3dabcf08b54e5-->
- `_strip_edge_newlines` (function) — Helper that strips only leading/trailing CR/LF (preserving other whitespace) from a marker-bounded segment, mirroring the JS console's newline-stripping. <!--#c325d55079417749-->
- `extract_user_content` (function) — A pure function that parses a step-prompt body and returns only the user's literal input segment—the text between the canonical TEMPLATE_PREFIX_END, USER_CONTENT_BEGIN, and USER_CONTENT_END markers—or None when the markers are missing/out-of-order, in the legacy BEGIN-without-END layout, or the segment is empty, mirroring the web console's splitUserPromptByMarker so the two stay in sync. <!--#c2fa7465361d7ce9-->
- `first_user_content` (function) — Scans a bounded number of jsonl lines forward, skipping event/non-user/empty records, and returns the content of the first genuine user-content record (or None). <!--#2906efc562d20f94-->
- `_marker_pair_present` (function) — Predicate returning True only when text already contains all three markers in canonical order, used to make wrapping idempotent and distinguish the legacy two-marker form. <!--#7264f000ac385a29-->
- `wrap_user_section` (function) — Wraps user_content as an explicitly marked middle segment between prefix and suffix (the preferred three-segment layout), idempotently skipping re-wrapping if markers already exist. <!--#32884d24dfcf9446-->
- `inject_boundary` (function) — Legacy two-segment helper that splices the marker pair into a template just before a given anchor substring, idempotent and defensive when the anchor or markers are absent. <!--#85d4d148f339ac22-->
- `wrap_user_content` (function) — Legacy two-segment helper joining a template prefix and user content with the marker pair (no suffix), with empty-side and idempotency fallbacks. <!--#f94f37a3057dc0f6-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/retry_context.py` (python) — Neutral shared-constants module defining the retry-history block's marker and separator sentinels plus the env-configurable post-dedup safety limit, exposing this API to both the retry-context producer (chat_history) and consumer (llm_caller) without cross-importing private names. <!--#a5a0cbe752a64910|d1925360b2c56d65-->
- `_load_safety_limit` (function) — Resolves the post-dedup safety limit from the SE3_POST_DEDUP_SAFETY_LIMIT env var, falling back to the built-in default when the value is missing, non-integer, or non-positive. <!--#273086c8defce832-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/review_scope.py` (python) — Implements diff-scoped SELF_CHECK review baselines — capturing and reconstructing a pre-IMPLEMENT/pre-FIX workspace snapshot (git blobs for clean files, a content-addressed store under runtime state for dirty/untracked ones) via ReviewBaseline/ReviewScope/ReviewScopeManager, plus the round controller and the diff utilities (git-style path quoting, section splitting, path matching, line-range algebra, and stat/snapshot helpers) that turn that baseline into the scoped diff SELF_CHECK reviews. <!--#fbd231a3f15793cc|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/runtime_environment.md` (markdown) — A prompt-injected guidance document that tells an agent working inside a tianluo-managed project which `luo` runtime commands are safe to call proactively (read-only history, issue, and code-index lookups) versus which state-mutating commands (`history restore`, `issue create/reset`, `salvage`, `merge`, `sync`, `init`) must only be run at the user's explicit request. <!--#630a3cb8bce546dd|f760f90470b1ad83-->
  - `tianluo Runtime Environment` (heading) — A prompt-injected guidance document telling an agent running inside a tianluo-managed project which `luo` runtime commands are safe to call proactively versus which require explicit user request. <!--#bf2ceaccc37e13dd-->
    - `Safe to call proactively (read-only)` (heading) — Lists the read-only `luo` commands and triggers for proactively consulting past session history (`luo history`), related issue context (`luo issue list/show`), and code location via the code-index (`luo code-index index/show/search`), each with a recommended overview-then-search workflow. <!--#44a4422984081ed7-->
    - `Do NOT call proactively` (heading) — Lists the state-mutating `luo` commands (`luo history restore`, `luo issue create`/`reset`, `luo salvage`, `luo merge`/`merge respond`, `luo init`) that the agent must never invoke on its own initiative unless the user explicitly asks in the current session. <!--#f6282d0468ec97c7-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/schema.py` (python) — Defines the TypedDict/Enum schema contracts for the engine's persisted JSON files — `engine.json` (FlowInstanceSchema/StateSchema/StepSchema plus status, step-type and plan-mode value enums, supporting both the hot/cold-split cold_ref format and the legacy inline format) and the AI-oriented `context.json` (ContextSchema) — together with `build_context_from_flow` and its helpers for distilling a full flow into that context payload. <!--#81b3df16f3a50a89|05d8afda99c3913d-->
- `StepStatusValue` (class) — A str-backed Enum enumerating every valid step status (pending, running, completed, partial, failed, retrying, paused, revision_needed) that engine.json is allowed to contain, mirroring the model layer's StepStatus so schema validation accepts all statuses the models can emit. <!--#84756dc8b13a8844-->
- `StepTypeValue` (class) — A `str`-based `Enum` enumerating every valid workflow step type string (discovery, plan, implement, test, e2e, commit, etc., including deprecated aliases), mirroring `tianluo.engine.models.StepType` so JSON-schema validation of `engine.json` accepts all serializable step types. <!--#75b6d957d099355b-->
- `FlowStatusValue` (class) — String enum of valid overall flow statuses (init, running, paused, completed, failed, recovering). <!--#39df2b604e1da00c-->
- `PlanDecompositionValue` (class) — Enum of the valid PLAN decomposition doctrines (`capability`, `granular`) as stored in flow context. <!--#053f9d7f027713d0-->
- `PlanGranularityValue` (class) — Enum of the valid group-count pressure settings (`auto`, `single`, `conservative`) as stored in flow context. <!--#f258e26fa8071e3d-->
- `ColdRefSchema` (class) — A TypedDict describing a header→cold-file reference (a `file` name plus content `hash`) used by the new hot/cold-split engine.json to point each step's externalized heavy inputs/outputs stored under tianluo/state/steps/, enabling incremental rewrites of only changed cold files. <!--#a33a1eb729227841-->
- `StepSchema` (class) — A TypedDict describing one step entry in engine.json, accepting both the new hot/cold format (externalized payloads via cold_ref) and the legacy inline format (inputs/outputs/artifacts). <!--#679c1899dc00745f-->
- `ContextRefSchema` (class) — A TypedDict describing the header→cold-file reference (`file` + `hash`) for the externalized shared context (and fix_history) kept in tianluo/state/steps/<flow_id>/_context.json under the hot/cold split. <!--#619d2b581a927d3f-->
- `StateSchema` (class) — A `TypedDict` describing the `state` object of `engine.json` — current/step history, per-step records, selected steps, inline counters and token-usage ledgers — supporting both the new hot/cold format (`context_ref`) and the legacy inline `context`/`fix_history`. <!--#a804aae3c971003d-->
- `FlowInstanceSchema` (class) — A TypedDict defining the root schema of engine.json — the top-level container for one flow execution, holding identity/status/task metadata, timestamps, worktree fields, nested StateSchema, and the hot/cold-split markers (engine_format, waiting_for_lock). <!--#084d519555d67437-->
- `ContextStepInfo` (class) — TypedDict holding a condensed per-step summary (type, status, timestamps, key outputs) used inside context.json. <!--#44e8c429cad17650-->
- `ContextSchema` (class) — TypedDict defining the root shape of `context.json` — the AI-optimized, distilled export of a flow's state (task, progress, steps, key outputs, plan-mode fields) used for handoff and resumption rather than full state reconstruction. <!--#3f92c70df1c031ff-->
- `build_context_from_flow` (function) — Transforms a full `FlowInstance` dict into the `ContextSchema` context payload, summarizing step history, computing progress, and projecting the flow's plan decomposition mode and group count read-only. <!--#c5b33ec71a92bd5e-->
- `_extract_plan_group_count` (function) — Derives how many task groups PLAN emitted from its outputs, preferring the actual `task_groups` length over the recorded `plan_group_count` and returning `None` when PLAN has not run. <!--#a3ded22f610db8d3-->
- `_summarize_outputs` (function) — Helper that selects and truncates the key output fields per step type for inclusion in a context step summary. <!--#8d53669a401b3363-->
- `_extract_key_outputs` (function) — Filters a step's outputs down to the few fields that matter per step type, using a per-`step_type` key allowlist. <!--#2c37b45b36a2591a-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/sink.py` (python) — Defines pluggable event-stream sinks that consume unified Event objects and render them as concrete output, with concrete CliSink (Rich CLI rendering), JsonSink (NDJSON for daemon mode), and HistorySink (per-step chat-history persistence for the web console). <!--#892181218b663a0b|c74fbe7a84cd7382-->
- `Sink` (class) — Abstract base class defining the event-stream consumer interface — a single abstract consume(event) method that concrete sinks implement to turn emitted Events into a concrete side effect. <!--#087874209123a94d-->
  - `Sink.consume` (method) — Abstract method each concrete sink overrides to perform its side effect on a single event. <!--#bb2390a15e6f138f-->
- `CliSink` (class) — Rich-rendering sink for CLI mode that delegates step-output/usage rendering to step_renderers (keeping luo run output byte-for-byte identical) while treating flow-level lifecycle and interactive CONFIRM/DISCOVERY/PLAN reports as no-ops owned by the orchestrator, surfacing only per-type token usage where the orchestrator does not. <!--#04671949c8e8c591-->
  - `CliSink.__init__` (method) — Constructor that optionally installs a supplied Rich Console as the global display console for all delegated renderers. <!--#7670536357cf51e0-->
  - `CliSink.consume` (method) — Dispatches terminal step events to `_render_step` and STEP_OUTPUT events to `_render_step_usage`, ignoring all other event types. <!--#4fb42242ff9754f9-->
  - `CliSink._render_step` (method) — Routes a terminal step event to the step-output renderer, skipping full reports for confirm/discovery/plan but still surfacing their token usage via per-type renderers. <!--#c17bf533ba7cf189-->
  - `CliSink._render_step_usage` (method) — Renders per-step token usage for a non-terminal STEP_OUTPUT event, applying the same per-type (discovery/confirm/default) rules as the terminal path. <!--#02ac269cfbbc8c1d-->
  - `CliSink._render_confirm_usage_footer` (method) — Renders confirm's token usage as a compact dim single-line footer (round equals cumulative since confirm calls the LLM at most once), rendering nothing when usage is empty. <!--#d0d721be80846166-->
  - `CliSink._render_discovery_cumulative_usage` (method) — Renders the discovery step's whole-run cumulative token usage (read from `step.outputs['token_usage']`) as a single dim i18n line via `format_usage_line`, printing nothing when the usage is absent or empty. <!--#ddf32cf5f5ac2d47-->
- `JsonSink` (class) — Structured NDJSON sink for daemon mode that serializes each event via Event.to_dict() and writes it as one JSON line (compact or pretty), using default=str for non-serializable payloads and flushing after each write. <!--#8daee639d5e7fd3d-->
  - `JsonSink.__init__` (method) — Constructor selecting the destination text stream (default stdout) and compact-vs-pretty serialization mode. <!--#f494e6176cbf27cf-->
  - `JsonSink.consume` (method) — Serializes an event via `to_dict` and writes it as a newline-terminated JSON line, flushing while swallowing closed/unflushable-stream errors. <!--#620cbdd2cd131156-->
- `HistorySink` (class) — Sink that persists step-lifecycle events (STEP_STARTED anchors plus STEP_COMPLETED/STEP_FAILED/STEP_OUTPUT records) into tianluo/history/<flow_id>/<step_id>.jsonl for the web console, keeping writes idempotent/state-aware and swallowing filesystem errors so a flaky disk cannot break the running flow. <!--#d319ea21198368c9-->
  - `HistorySink.__init__` (method) — Constructor that records the project root used to locate the per-step history files. <!--#72ade7501cf2da27-->
  - `HistorySink.consume` (method) — Records STEP_STARTED via `_record_started` and persists terminal/output events' full step dict through `record_step_event`, ignoring other event types. <!--#85f85df1bccb1bbe-->
  - `HistorySink._record_started` (method) — Persists a STEP_STARTED event as a state-aware `running` anchor, skipping when a terminal record exists or the last anchor is already running, and re-arming '进行中' when a paused step resumes. <!--#091c894d34c9cc7a-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/stash_utils.py` (python) — Shared no-data-loss recovery helpers for `git stash pop` conflicts—used by both the DAG implement step and the `luo merge` robust strategy—that label-resolve stashes, archive all recoverable content (tracked and untracked, both sides) to a gitignored archive dir before touching it, classify and resolve conflicts, drop the labeled stash only after recovery is proven, and render an operator-facing audit manifest. <!--#796858f501756ea9|9022da602294d82a-->
- `ArchivedEntry` (class) — A dataclass representing one stashed file persisted to the archive directory, tracking its relative path, archive location, blob SHA, conflict class (case 'a' tracked vs 'b' untracked), and which side ('stashed'/theirs or 'head'/ours) it holds for recovery. <!--#37c71d5a84923444-->
- `_resolve_stash_ref` (function) — Resolves the live `stash@{N}` ref whose message exactly matches a given label, by parsing `git stash list`, so concurrent stashes can't be confused for SE3's own (returns None if none match). <!--#d30a07a7548e9662-->
- `pop_stash_by_label` (function) — Performs `git stash pop` on the specific stash entry resolved by label (never a bare pop), returning a synthetic non-zero result if the label doesn't resolve so the no-data-loss recovery path takes over instead of popping an unrelated stash. <!--#eb99645738aef351-->
- `_git_show_bytes` (function) — Returns the raw bytes of `git show <spec>` so binary blobs round-trip intact and hash back to the original git object, or None if the object can't be read. <!--#fbe303964dff7cba-->
- `_sanitize_label` (function) — Replaces filesystem-unsafe characters in a label so an embedded branch-name slash can't spill the archive across directories, making it a single safe path segment. <!--#6067e278401649bd-->
- `_archive_run_rel` (function) — Returns the project-root-relative base directory name (under worktrees/.archive, keyed by timestamp and sanitized stash label) where a single recovery run's archived payload—both stashed-side and case-a HEAD-side—should be collected together. <!--#c27f41601f94d386-->
- `_prepare_unique_archive_run` (function) — Atomically claims a never-reused archive run directory for one recovery by mkdir'ing the base name with exist_ok=False and falling back to -2, -3, … suffixes on collision, so same-second recoveries of the same label can't overwrite each other's archived bytes. <!--#9401e8c6320152a9-->
- `_archive_blob` (function) — Persists a single git object into the run directory, recording its blob SHA and returning an ArchivedEntry, raising RuntimeError on any read/resolve/write failure so a caller relying on it as recovery proof refuses to drop. <!--#b8140b47f14d554a-->
- `archive_stash_payload` (function) — Persists a live stash's entire recoverable content (untracked files via `^3` and non-deleted tracked changes) to the archive directory and returns the recovery manifest, raising rather than silently skipping so the caller never drops without proven-complete persistence. <!--#beca1d2bea64fe6d-->
- `parse_stashpop_already_exists` (function) — Parses `git stash pop` output to extract file paths reported as 'already exists, no checkout', which git doesn't mark as unmerged. <!--#740f82b591b8253f-->
- `take_ours_for_stashpop` (function) — Resolves stash-pop conflicts by keeping the merged HEAD (ours) version via `checkout --ours`, the default no-resolver fallback for case-a conflicts, safe only because the discarded stashed side was already archived first. <!--#9381e724e451d872-->
- `_archive_case_a_head_side` (function) — Archives the merged HEAD (ours, `:2:<path>`) version of each case-a conflict path into a side-namespaced location before resolution, so both sides of a tracked 3-way conflict are recoverable regardless of which the resolver discards. <!--#8396eab3d118aef2-->
- `StashPopOutcome` (class) — A dataclass holding the result of `resolve_stashpop_safely` — the recovery manifest, whether the stash was dropped, the case-a/case-b file split, an archive-failure flag, and the still-unmerged files that must block reporting a clean merge. <!--#f488a7c7eb37e6be-->
- `resolve_stashpop_safely` (function) — The single shared entry point that recovers a non-clean git stash pop without data loss by archiving all recoverable content first, classifying case-a (tracked 3-way) vs case-b (untracked-collision) conflicts, resolving case-a via an injected resolver or take-ours fallback, and dropping only the labeled stash once recovery is proven and conflicts are resolved. <!--#aa433bd5d6940e11-->
- `format_archived_manifest` (function) — Renders a list of ArchivedEntry records into identical audit-issue body text (archive path, blob sha, and conflict class per file) shared across both merge paths so operators get a byte-for-byte consistent recovery pointer. <!--#225564b3913453d3-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/stashpop_llm_resolver.py` (python) — The LLM-integration layer that builds a case-a stash-pop `conflict_resolver`, sending marker-bearing files to the LLM-as-editor, staging only the paths whose unmerged index entry is provably cleared, and falling back to the deterministic `take_ours_for_stashpop` for everything else so the working tree is left marker-free without data loss. <!--#8ff950f0230cae6b|e70e458b5fa15562-->
- `_path_is_unmerged` (function) — Returns whether a path still has an unmerged index entry via `git ls-files --unmerged`, treating any git error as still-unmerged so the caller never optimistically drops the stash over an unresolved conflict. <!--#1b9b4d31a66b2af4-->
- `llm_resolve_stashpop_conflicts` (function) — Reconciles case-a `git stash pop` conflicts by feeding each conflict-markered file to the LLM (via LLMCaller) and staging the result WITHOUT committing, returning only the paths whose unmerged index entry is provably cleared while leaving untrustworthy cases (LLM unavailable, exceptions, remaining markers, modify/delete shape, or unstaged) to the caller's deterministic fallback. <!--#95cf16ed694e69ae-->
- `make_llm_stashpop_resolver` (function) — Builds the `resolve_stashpop_safely` conflict-resolver callable that tries the LLM resolver first and falls back to the deterministic `take_ours_for_stashpop` for any unresolved files, leaving the working tree marker-free. <!--#60bd80d7d596bc9a-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/state_machine.py` (python) — The flow engine's central `StateMachine`: it builds a flow's step sequence (worktree merge steps, e2e/confirmation insertion), executes each step via registered handlers with the right working directory and locking, assembles per-step inputs, and drives all transition logic — fix/revision loops, adjudication and its confirmation gate, investigation and self-check repeat rounds, review-scope/baseline capture, usage accounting and progress reporting. <!--#0de7da70bda51e7f|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/step_renderers.py` (python) — CLI presentation layer for completed engine steps: it holds a `StepType` → renderer registry (`register_renderer` / `render_step_output`) plus a generic key/value fallback, per-step Rich/i18n panel renderers for every step type (analyze, plan, implement, test, e2e, spec_gate, investigate, self_check, confirm, verify_spec, update_spec, merge_integrate, version_analyze/reconcile, summarize, …), and shared helpers for step titles, value formatting, test-result summaries and token-usage blocks. <!--#71435c172341f67b|061b76de27fcf445-->
- `step_display_title` (function) — Returns the localized display title for a given StepType via the shared STEP_TITLE_KEYS map (falling back to the raw enum value), exposed publicly so the `luo run` console and renderer Panels resolve step titles consistently in one language. <!--#48722b54e0220eaf-->
- `register_renderer` (function) — Decorator factory that registers a function as the custom renderer for a given StepType in the STEP_RENDERERS registry. <!--#d32f2f04d911965a-->
- `render_step_output` (function) — Main entry point that renders a completed step by dispatching to its registered custom renderer (or the generic fallback) and then appending the step's token-usage block. <!--#0cc6d9917694653b-->
- `render_step_usage` (function) — Prints a step's token-usage block to the CLI, preferring the richer `usage_summary` projection (which distinguishes actual/estimated/unknown cost) and falling back to the legacy `token_usage` dict, rendering nothing when neither is present. <!--#6d02f0f5296f082b-->
- `_format_value` (function) — Helper that formats an arbitrary output value into a display string, JSON-encoding dicts/lists and stringifying everything else. <!--#de91dc9da5c3e62f-->
- `_default_render` (function) — Fallback CLI renderer that dumps a step's outputs as bold key/value lines (truncating long strings to a preview with a character count), prefixed by a non-terminal status line and suffixed by any error message. <!--#e80a39df1016b618-->
- `_render_remaining` (function) — Helper that renders the leftover `step.outputs` keys a specialised renderer did not consume, using the same generic key/value formatting under a "remaining" titled panel. <!--#6ea552fa6fadf30a-->
- `_render_version_analyze` (function) — Renders the version_analyze step as a current→suggested version headline plus bump type, confidence, reasoning and any error. <!--#4460e5c62eda9db3-->
- `_render_merge_integrate` (function) — Renders the merge_integrate step, listing which branches landed on master, flagging escalation to a human, and showing any error. <!--#cf26edeb58f59974-->
- `_render_version_reconcile` (function) — Renders the version_reconcile step as the base→final version derived at merge, plus release channel, reconcile commit, and the clean already-reconciled no-op case. <!--#8e1bbb1b4148f135-->
- `_render_summarize` (function) — Renders the summarize step's `summary` output as markdown. <!--#2d06117faf4f22a8-->
- `_build_test_summary_lines` (function) — Shared helper that turns a `test_results` dict into summary-only lines (overall pass/fail, per-phase results, command) with no raw pytest output. <!--#2db7e1ac1b1d1f59-->
- `_render_test` (function) — Renders the test step's CLI panel as a summary of its `test_results` outputs (plus any `e2e_suggestion` hint), falling back to the generic renderer when structured results are missing. <!--#b96bf2f91042df40-->
- `_e2e_clip` (function) — Helper that flattens an expected/actual assertion value to a single trimmed line capped at `E2E_MAX_VALUE_CHARS`, returning `-` for empties. <!--#9b4939abec1d03cc-->
- `_render_e2e` (function) — Renders the e2e step as a scenario-level summary panel — skip/environment/config-error branches, pass-fail status with unverified-critical scenarios, counts, runtime and durations, then a truncated list of failed scenarios and their failed assertions — falling back to the generic renderer when `e2e_results` is absent or malformed. <!--#f257289398ceff08-->
- `_render_spec_gate` (function) — Renders the spec_gate step as a gate conclusion (passed/failed/skipped plus fallback route), fix instructions, and a reused summary-only test-results block. <!--#a0a7d43e41767694-->
- `_render_propose` (function) — Renders the propose step via the shared proposal renderer when a proposal dict is present, then any uncovered outputs; otherwise falls back to the generic renderer. <!--#0f0edcb30f6edf74-->
- `_render_design` (function) — Renders the design step via the shared design renderer when a design dict is present, then any uncovered outputs; otherwise falls back to the generic renderer. <!--#b3afb38e46c172e0-->
- `_render_plan` (function) — Renders a completed PLAN step to the CLI by displaying its proposal, design, and task-group summary sections (with an i18n line variant for task-less capability groups), falling back to the default step rendering when none of those sections are present and otherwise appending any uncovered output keys. <!--#ad48e6dfbaa73c7c-->
- `_group_files_by_directory` (function) — Helper that groups a list of file paths by their top-level directory into a sorted OrderedDict for display. <!--#f9bc34f5641dd2ca-->
- `_render_implement` (function) — Builds and prints the Rich-formatted CLI panel for an implement step, laying out a status bar (complete/partial/failed with group/file/test counts), per-group summaries, files changed grouped by directory, tests added, incomplete tasks or neutral notes, restricted-edit results, and any error message. <!--#5c9d886b42e17fce-->
- `_render_analyze` (function) — Renders the analyze step as a task-type/complexity/scope status bar plus reasoning and the selected relevant spec items. <!--#dac29330f5fad146-->
- `_render_investigate` (function) — Renders a completed investigate step to the CLI as a single panel, laying out the conclusive/inconclusive verdict with confidence and iteration round, then the root cause, evidence list, files involved, suggested fix direction, any net-zero-diff workspace_delta violation, and the error message, all via i18n keys and Rich markup. <!--#f1e061c9c7d34b1d-->
- `_render_self_check` (function) — Renders the self_check step's pass/fail/actionable-count status, summary, and issues grouped and colored by severity (with schema compatibility for legacy verify_spec issues). <!--#bf9dee1a5dd7c798-->
- `_render_invariant_check` (function) — Renders the invariant-check step as a compact report card — pass/fail verdict, summary, and issues grouped and colour-coded by severity — deliberately omitting the bulky audit payloads the generic renderer would have dumped. <!--#c24c187ada5dac26-->
- `_render_confirm` (function) — Renders a CONFIRM step's review verdict as a report card (approved / revision requested, reviewer, reviewed step, feedback, and revision feedback only when it differs), kept in field parity with the WebUI's `renderConfirmReport`. <!--#95bd8c3374b0a79c-->
- `_render_verify_spec` (function) — Renders the verify_spec step's verified status, summary, issues grouped by in/out-of-scope and colored by priority with suggestions, and recommendations. <!--#4cfa969f07fd1e3c-->
- `_render_update_spec` (function) — Renders the update_spec step's list of updated specs and new capabilities, or a "nothing updated" panel when both are empty. <!--#af36182188d46fa3-->
- `_render_commit` (function) — Renders the commit step as short hash plus optional bumped version and the commit message, showing the "no changes" shortcut only when there is also no error to report. <!--#94a60b13b0bfcd7d-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/task_description.py` (python) — Owns the canonical rendering of persisted user interjections into an '## Additional Instructions (added during run)' section appended to a step's base task description, shared by all call sites so immediate re-runs and downstream step propagation produce byte-identical output. <!--#5bfbec42e2f34e85|86c2c9cd1e02d20d-->
- `compose_task_description_with_interjections` (function) — Renders a list of interjection dicts into a '## Additional Instructions' section appended to the base task description, skipping empty entries and returning the base unchanged when none are usable. <!--#0330964a0329ae3c-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/test_adjudicate_step.py` (python) — In-package pytest suite for the ADJUDICATE engine step, covering oscillation-candidate detection, effective task description/plan resolution, ruling override placement and validation (description-only, plan-only rejection, null coercion), ledger effect staging vs. landing (abolish/reject), revision-feedback prompting, multi-generation auditability, and graceful failure on unparseable LLM output. <!--#45bb66b4e8d7023c|d14c9d587fde9e70-->
- `_issue` (function) — Test factory that builds a canonical self-check issue dict (severity, expected/actual behavior, verbatim-quote expectation source, evidence lines) with overridable file/line/quote/expected fields. <!--#d96d19b9391b4932-->
- `_flow_with_ledger` (function) — Test factory that builds a FlowInstance whose adjudication ledger holds one position, optionally seeded with two opposing self-check rounds to make it an oscillation candidate. <!--#3c9817e99a3650e3-->
- `_adj_step` (function) — Test helper that creates an ADJUDICATE Step with the given inputs and appends it to the flow's state. <!--#1db08f9da8fe61a7-->
- `_mock_call` (function) — Test helper returning a fake LLMCaller class whose call() always returns the given payload serialized as JSON. <!--#ac2021013da00311-->
- `test_candidate_positions_picks_oscillating` (function) — Asserts _candidate_positions surfaces an oscillating position and its timeline captures both opposing expectations. <!--#0a034c6dd028cc55-->
- `test_candidate_positions_ignores_single_expectation` (function) — Asserts _candidate_positions returns nothing for a position that carried only a single (non-oscillating) expectation. <!--#ce03340f3db35ec0-->
- `test_candidate_positions_honors_explicit_trigger` (function) — Asserts a single-expectation position is surfaced as a candidate when explicitly passed via the trigger's explicit position list. <!--#c2f68d55612f8d52-->
- `test_candidate_positions_skips_quoteless` (function) — Asserts quoteless (evidence-only) findings that collapse to a per-file position_key are not presented as a bogus A/B oscillation candidate. <!--#d1805d93b5896836-->
- `test_handler_reads_flat_trigger_inputs` (function) — Asserts the handler consumes the flat trigger keys the state machine writes, rendering the real trigger reason and surfacing an explicitly-unioned single-expectation candidate. <!--#e6bcc8b565e14798-->
- `test_effective_task_description_ignores_interjection_composed_input` (function) — Asserts _effective_task_description adjudicates over the pre-interjection base, stripping the interjection-composed '## Additional Instructions' section. <!--#7e84625d83761d5f-->
- `test_effective_task_description_honors_clean_base_input` (function) — Asserts a clean task_description_base input is used verbatim by _effective_task_description. <!--#6eaf3f927012790a-->
- `test_handler_writes_override_to_own_outputs` (function) — Asserts a successful adjudication ruling lands its override (adjudicated_description, rationale, timestamp, contradiction_type) on the ADJUDICATE step's own outputs and emits no self_check-style `issues` key. <!--#d9234c0df9878297-->
- `test_handler_supersedes_fix_instructions` (function) — Asserts the handler stashes and flags any pending fix_instructions as superseded by the new ruling. <!--#b8c217f516672aef-->
- `test_contradiction_verdict_abolishes_position` (function) — Asserts a contradiction verdict only stages position abolition until the ruling lands, after which apply_landed_ledger_effects abolishes the observations and the position stops suppressing convergence. <!--#17aa0ba1d1287545-->
- `test_benign_verdict_records_rejected_candidate` (function) — Asserts a benign verdict stages a rejected candidate that is recorded on the ledger's rejected_positions only after landing, excluding it from future oscillation triggers. <!--#e6d4c8cb7cb7030a-->
- `test_plan_only_override_is_rejected_for_modern_ruling` (function) — Asserts a ruling that supplies only an `adjudicated_plan` with no `adjudicated_description` FAILS with an explanatory error and writes no plan override. <!--#16596e534cfc633e-->
- `test_null_string_override_coerced_to_none` (function) — Verifies that when the LLM emits literal 'null'/'none' strings for a review_divergence ruling, the transparent no-op path never writes the (coerced) description/plan overrides. <!--#b7712e88a9d29ee5-->
- `test_override_without_verdicts_still_abolishes_candidates` (function) — Asserts a description patch with no explicit verdicts still abolishes the flagged candidates whose quoted clause left the adjudicated text. <!--#6bd6eceb9ff213ea-->
- `test_handler_does_not_touch_prior_step_outputs` (function) — Asserts adjudication never mutates completed DISCOVERY/PLAN step outputs in place — overrides are layered onto the adjudication step alone. <!--#b00a7b9bfaa2c49d-->
- `test_effective_task_groups_prefers_prior_adjudication` (function) — Asserts _effective_task_groups reads the latest prior adjudicated_plan rather than the raw plan step's task_groups. <!--#afaacfa00e1341c8-->
- `test_handler_threads_revision_feedback_into_prompt` (function) — Asserts a confirmation-gate revision re-run surfaces the reviewer's rejection feedback in the ruling prompt. <!--#135388ae1d329f2f-->
- `test_handler_ignores_revision_feedback_when_not_revision` (function) — Asserts revision_feedback is omitted from the prompt when the step is not flagged as a revision. <!--#3fc782c269419024-->
- `test_handler_fails_gracefully_on_unparseable_llm` (function) — Asserts an unparseable LLM response makes the handler return FAILED with an error message set. <!--#61d82941cc407e1c-->
- `test_multi_generation_rulings_are_each_auditable` (function) — Asserts each ADJUDICATE generation retains its own rationale/timestamp while _latest_adjudicated resolves the effective text to the newest ruling. <!--#3a7b9fd906a92857-->
- `test_ruling_description_drops_dead_clause_issue_via_source_pool` (function) — Test verifying that after `adjudicate_handler` rewrites the task description, the adjudicated text becomes the verbatim-quote source pool so that a later self_check issue re-quoting the now-abolished clause is dropped by `_validate_and_filter_issues` (raising `quote_not_in_source_count`) while the live-clause issue survives. <!--#238829ad18e19498-->
- `test_handler_stages_but_does_not_apply_ledger_effects` (function) — Asserts the handler only stages abolish/reject effects, leaving the persisted ledger clean and abolished_count unwritten until landing. <!--#314120db143bb6af-->
- `test_rejected_ruling_leaves_ledger_untouched` (function) — Asserts a confirmation-rejected ruling and its revision re-run leave no abolish/reject side effects on the ledger since nothing was ever applied. <!--#5e91eb9cbeda40cf-->
- `test_plan_only_override_cannot_land` (function) — Asserts a derived plan cannot serve as a requirement patch: a plan-only ruling over a real oscillating contradiction fails and abolishes no ledger observations. <!--#816ac97a3326b6e9-->
- `test_description_rewrite_abolishes_only_the_removed_clause` (function) — Asserts a description rewrite abolishes only the position whose clause was removed while a preserved hard-constraint clause keeps its history. <!--#c099276c48037401-->
