- `test_charter_grounded_position_survives_a_description_only_rewrite` (function) — Asserts a self_check position grounded in a charter clause is not abolished when the ruling rewrites only the task description, since the quoted charter sentence stays live. <!--#a6a1add963975b66-->
- `test_why_comment_grounded_position_survives_a_description_only_rewrite` (function) — Same survival guarantee as the charter case, but for a position grounded in a marked WHY:/INVARIANT: source comment in a changed file. <!--#764bc8f2d0789e30-->
- `test_unreadable_constraint_channel_abolishes_nothing` (function) — Asserts that when constraint source texts cannot be read, the ruling stages zero abolished fingerprints rather than clearing live oscillation history. <!--#e305c9948f65aef4-->
- `test_description_ruling_ignores_plan_restatement` (function) — Asserts a plan restating a clause the description rewrite dropped cannot keep it alive — the fingerprints are abolished and self_check's filter then discards the plan_task-sourced issue. <!--#d5853b3b175b81ba-->
- `test_noop_contradiction_ruling_fails_after_retries` (function) — Asserts a contradiction verdict carrying no covering patch is rejected as FAILED after retries, writing nothing to outputs or the ledger, instead of reflowing to SELF_CHECK against an unchanged spec. <!--#4d0c272e08fae66c-->
- `test_noop_contradiction_ruling_retries_then_succeeds` (function) — Asserts the retry branch of the no-op guard: the second prompt carries a strict 'was rejected' re-ask demanding a covering patch, and the corrected ruling lands as COMPLETED. <!--#7f7237dcdb352bb0-->
- `test_review_divergence_needs_no_patch` (function) — Asserts that a review_divergence verdict legitimately completes with no override patch, flagging adjudication_noop and leaving description/plan unset. <!--#a358bda30dd8a1bb-->
- `test_review_divergence_blank_rationale_is_rejected` (function) — Asserts a whitespace-only adjudication_rationale is non-actionable, so even a review_divergence ruling retries and FAILS without writing a blank audit or rejected candidates. <!--#09d88aaf99b8c675-->
- `test_review_divergence_without_verdicts_rejects_all_candidates` (function) — Asserts a no-patch review_divergence ruling omitting candidate_verdicts still stages every flagged position as rejected so the oscillation cannot re-trigger. <!--#cf07644616324582-->
- `test_review_divergence_stray_contradiction_verdict_is_rejected` (function) — Asserts a no-patch review_divergence ruling with a stray per-candidate contradiction verdict still rejects the position since there is no patch to abolish against. <!--#04c770bb9254894f-->
- `test_review_divergence_with_patch_discards_override` (function) — Regression test ensuring a review_divergence ruling that also carries an override patch discards the override (no spec rewrite, nothing abolished) and instead stages the candidate as rejected. <!--#ef9c9a3d26a77bce-->
- `test_review_divergence_is_transparent_noop` (function) — Verifies a no-real-contradiction ruling is a transparent no-op: it flags adjudication_noop and records an audit-only verdict plus rejected_positions bookkeeping, but writes none of the supersede/override fields so IMPLEMENT keeps the original fix_instructions. <!--#1c2d3e59f62a712c-->
- `test_real_contradiction_is_not_a_noop` (function) — Confirms a real internal_contradiction takes the patch path — superseding pending fix_instructions and writing the override — and never sets adjudication_noop. <!--#16f9ad04dd1445f3-->
- `test_noop_reruling_clears_rejected_patch_ruling` (function) — Regression test asserting that when a rejected patch ruling re-runs the same ADJUDICATE step in place and the LLM then rules a benign review_divergence (no-op), the handler fully wipes the earlier ruling's adjudicated_description/adjudicated_plan/superseded_fix_instructions/fix_instructions_superseded keys so the never-approved rewrite can't linger as the effective task description. <!--#1dd078998aaa36cd-->
- `test_contradiction_reruling_clears_stale_noop_flag` (function) — Regression test that a re-run following a prior no-op ruling forces adjudication_noop back to False when it now rules a real contradiction, so routing takes the patch/supersede path. <!--#f240956d4d300f1c-->
- `_sequenced_caller` (function) — Test helper that builds a fake LLMCaller class returning a scripted sequence of JSON payloads while appending each prompt it receives to a shared list, so tests can assert on prompt content across retries. <!--#53663eb20cf7c926-->
- `test_prompt_demands_homomorphic_sweep_and_conservatism` (function) — Asserts the adjudication prompt includes the HOMOMORPHIC SURFACES sweep instruction, the WHEN IN DOUBT LEAVE IT OUT / AUTO-PASS conservatism rules, and the covered_surfaces/justification schema. <!--#51eb9cfb7158e023-->
- `test_prompt_does_not_inject_plan_as_requirement_authority` (function) — Asserts the effective plan's task groups are never injected into the ruling prompt, so a derived plan is not treated as requirement authority. <!--#47ec8dcf7fd48090-->
- `test_covered_surfaces_persisted_on_patch_path` (function) — Verifies that for a real-contradiction ruling the handler sanitizes (strips whitespace from) the LLM's covered_surfaces entries and persists them into the step's outputs. <!--#ece18460b35de397-->
- `test_covered_surfaces_absent_or_empty_still_actionable` (function) — Checks that an omitted, null, or empty covered_surfaces field is a legitimate outcome — the ruling still completes and outputs an empty list rather than forcing the LLM to invent surfaces. <!--#c041f884594c6117-->
- `test_normalized_covered_surfaces_shapes` (function) — Unit-tests the private `_normalized_covered_surfaces` helper directly, covering the well-formed/absent/empty cases (valid, list returned) and a battery of malformed shapes (invalid flag). <!--#892de7bc12fed5c1-->
- `test_incomplete_covered_surfaces_entry_triggers_semantic_retry` (function) — Confirms that a covered_surfaces entry missing its justification makes the handler re-ask the LLM with the malformed-field reason in the retry prompt, and that the corrected second ruling lands. <!--#2200cf1b8716816b-->
- `test_covered_surfaces_never_valid_fails_with_reason` (function) — Confirms two consecutive malformed covered_surfaces rulings fail the step with an error message naming the gate, leaving nothing written to the outputs. <!--#eaea15e00ad318f0-->
- `test_review_divergence_ignores_malformed_covered_surfaces` (function) — Confirms a no-op (review_divergence) ruling ignores malformed covered_surfaces rather than blocking, and omits the key entirely from its outputs since no boundary clause is written. <!--#e8deeca2120bb88e-->
- `test_noop_rerun_pops_stale_covered_surfaces` (function) — Confirms that when a rejected patch ruling re-runs in place as a no-op review_divergence, the stale covered_surfaces governance claim from the earlier ruling is removed from the step's outputs. <!--#8fbc0d67a039cc35-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/test_adjudication.py` (python) — Unit tests for the adjudication ledger: issue fingerprint/position_key stability and quote normalization, idempotent per-round observation recording, and the firing conditions for the oscillation, contradiction, reproduction, and periodic-backstop triggers including abolished/rejected exclusions and JSON round-trip safety. <!--#dddc739140e3680b|510698fa0134f458-->
- `_issue` (function) — Test helper that builds a minimal self_check issue dict with configurable file, line, verbatim quote, and expected behavior. <!--#91b0474f9f5473c0-->
- `test_fingerprint_stable_under_line_drift` (function) — Asserts an issue's fingerprint and position_key stay constant when only its line number shifts after a fix iteration. <!--#ec3c45b08e6f0ef6-->
- `test_fingerprint_differs_on_expected` (function) — Asserts that identical positions with opposing expected behaviors yield different fingerprints but the same position_key. <!--#c2442c47438993a3-->
- `test_normalization_matches_source_pool_semantics` (function) — Verifies quote normalization (NFKC, smart quotes, whitespace, literal \n) collapses semantically-equal quotes to the same position_key. <!--#e1da97afa131e12b-->
- `test_missing_in_fallback_for_unimplemented` (function) — Checks that a wholly-missing task with empty evidence_lines grounds its position via the missing_in file instead. <!--#e14283244ccfa2b0-->
- `test_empty_ledger_on_legacy_context` (function) — Verifies a legacy context lacking the ledger key tolerates evaluation as empty and lazily initializes the ledger. <!--#d6bc73a31814b5c5-->
- `test_record_accumulates_across_rounds_only_grows` (function) — Confirms recording self_check rounds monotonically grows the ledger's round_count and observations, never clearing them. <!--#4808167f9c8eccc2-->
- `test_record_dedupes_within_round` (function) — Asserts identical issues within a single recorded round collapse to one observation. <!--#f7a4bf9831a0fd31-->
- `test_record_idempotent_on_round_id_replay` (function) — Verifies replaying the same round_id (e.g. on --resume) does not double-count rounds or observations. <!--#adecf2322021bc3f-->
- `test_trigger_a_oscillation_fires_on_flipped_expected` (function) — Asserts trigger (a) fires the oscillation reason when the same position flips its expected behavior across rounds. <!--#8ad29b6cfe0648bf-->
- `test_trigger_a_no_fire_when_expected_stable` (function) — Confirms the oscillation trigger stays silent when a position's expectation is stable across rounds. <!--#0c5ec22f9280bb7c-->
- `test_trigger_a_no_fire_first_time_seen` (function) — Confirms the oscillation trigger does not fire on an issue's first appearance. <!--#f8a738b4ca1e5f56-->
- `test_trigger_a_only_structural_not_truth` (function) — Asserts oscillation is a purely structural signal that sets suppress_convergence. <!--#0557ce3d6ba56700-->
- `test_trigger_b_contradiction_reads_previous_resolutions` (function) — Asserts trigger (b) fires contradiction (and suppresses convergence) when a fixed position re-opens with the opposite expectation. <!--#c15c096f431eac3e-->
- `test_trigger_b_fires_when_same_fixed_fingerprint_reopens` (function) — Asserts contradiction fires immediately when a self_check re-flags the exact fingerprint just declared fixed, rather than waiting for reproduction threshold (c). <!--#299f5af7f697bb54-->
- `test_trigger_b_ignores_still_present_resolutions` (function) — Confirms contradiction does not fire when the prior resolution was 'still_present' rather than 'fixed'. <!--#a73cd8deee12ee54-->
- `test_trigger_b_accepts_inlined_resolution_fields` (function) — Verifies contradiction detection works when resolution carries issue fields inline instead of in a nested issue. <!--#3d476a3f2fd7f65f-->
- `test_trigger_c_reproduction_third_appearance_after_fix` (function) — Asserts trigger (c) reproduction fires only on the third genuine post-fix recurrence of a fingerprint, not the second. <!--#5ec3c10e82b621be-->
- `test_trigger_c_no_fire_before_third_or_without_fix` (function) — Confirms reproduction does not fire for a recurring issue that was never declared fixed. <!--#d229b6da597b97f7-->
- `test_trigger_c_pre_fix_flags_do_not_inflate_count` (function) — Verifies pre-fix and at-fix flags are excluded so reproduction is scored strictly from post-fixed recurrences. <!--#abceed5933c6a7c9-->
- `test_trigger_c_quoteless_fingerprint_never_fires` (function) — Asserts a quoteless (regression-type) fingerprint, whose position collapses to per-file identity, is excluded from firing reproduction. <!--#32cbf6e6004385a9-->
- `test_period_backstop_fires_every_n_iterations` (function) — Asserts the periodic backstop fires the period reason at the configured iteration interval without suppressing convergence. <!--#5e09c2f2501dd1ea-->
- `test_period_backstop_measures_from_baseline` (function) — Verifies the periodic backstop counts iterations from the last adjudication baseline rather than absolute iteration zero. <!--#c83633b3f8ebe7c2-->
- `test_abolished_entries_excluded_from_triggers` (function) — Confirms abolished fingerprints are excluded so a would-be oscillation no longer triggers. <!--#3d5fed2e7f519413-->
- `test_abolished_excludes_reproduction` (function) — Confirms marking a fingerprint abolished vetoes an otherwise-firing reproduction trigger. <!--#8296842e146bb5ef-->
- `test_rejected_candidate_position_not_retriggered` (function) — Asserts a previously rejected candidate position no longer re-triggers oscillation. <!--#f172f40ae9b302c2-->
- `test_ledger_survives_dict_round_trip` (function) — Verifies the ledger is plain JSON-serializable so triggers evaluate identically before and after a dict round-trip. <!--#a050b343c8f5d136-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/test_adjudication_effective.py` (python) — Unit tests covering how adjudication rulings take effect downstream — that `_latest_adjudicated_output` picks the newest COMPLETED ruling per key, that `_effective_task_description_base` layers adjudicated over refined over original text, that `_build_step_inputs`/fix-loop transitions feed the adjudicated description (but not a legacy `adjudicated_plan`) into IMPLEMENT and self_check, and that `_build_source_pool` drops superseded original text so self_check issues quoting abolished clauses are filtered out while live-clause issues survive. <!--#8fd405e9e8013337|1a83c02bcd15b843-->
- `_completed` (function) — Test helper that builds a Step of a given type marked COMPLETED and seeded with the supplied outputs dict. <!--#ec2cc074b6aae5fd-->
- `_flow` (function) — Test helper that constructs a fresh FlowInstance with the given task description. <!--#97841846d17670b6-->
- `_add` (function) — Test helper that appends a Step to a flow's state and returns it. <!--#12a1809111f84c8c-->
- `_issue` (function) — Test helper that produces a well-formed self_check issue dict whose grounding is valid except for the verbatim_quote substring check. <!--#3fa09ca9b801427e-->
- `test_latest_adjudicated_output_none_without_ruling` (function) — Asserts _latest_adjudicated_output returns None when no adjudicate step has produced the requested key. <!--#aaefb95207f06ff2-->
- `test_latest_adjudicated_output_latest_wins` (function) — Asserts _latest_adjudicated_output returns the value from the most recent adjudication generation. <!--#834eedbec3dba46b-->
- `test_latest_adjudicated_output_skips_empty_newer_generation` (function) — Asserts a newer adjudication that omits the key does not veto an earlier generation's value for that key. <!--#e38fad32fbd15828-->
- `test_latest_adjudicated_output_ignores_non_completed` (function) — Asserts _latest_adjudicated_output ignores outputs from adjudicate steps that are not COMPLETED. <!--#611aec2c12668a1f-->
- `test_base_original_without_any_override` (function) — Asserts _effective_task_description_base returns the original task text when nothing overrides it. <!--#d035d0e068937e95-->
- `test_base_refined_overrides_original` (function) — Asserts a discovery step's refined_description overrides the original task text in the effective base. <!--#8e7e230a151d5517-->
- `test_base_adjudicated_overrides_refined_and_original` (function) — Asserts an adjudicated_description takes precedence over both refined and original text in the effective base. <!--#445b1569b0badcfd-->
- `test_base_multi_generation_takes_latest_adjudication` (function) — Asserts the effective base uses the latest adjudication generation's description across multiple rulings. <!--#e8d0b9c5089ec22e-->
- `test_base_plan_only_ruling_falls_through_to_refined` (function) — Asserts a ruling that changed only the plan leaves the effective base description at the refined value. <!--#ebe202195a85c064-->
- `_sm` (function) — Test helper that instantiates a StateMachine rooted at a fresh temp directory. <!--#310be166a0b8631d-->
- `test_build_step_inputs_uses_adjudicated_description` (function) — Asserts _build_step_inputs feeds the adjudicated description as task_description into the implement step. <!--#3706b795bca36d67-->
- `test_build_step_inputs_no_adjudication_unchanged` (function) — Asserts _build_step_inputs passes through the original description and plan task_groups when no adjudication exists. <!--#2f5dcc16a6cddff3-->
- `test_build_step_inputs_legacy_plan_override_is_history_only` (function) — Asserts that an ADJUDICATE step's `adjudicated_plan` is recorded for history only and does not override the PLAN step's `task_groups` in the inputs `_build_step_inputs` hands to IMPLEMENT. <!--#33673f9f10462ff9-->
- `test_build_step_inputs_self_check_signals_adjudication` (function) — Asserts self_check inputs expose the adjudicated text as both task_description_base and adjudicated_description. <!--#ad5eb229103bef00-->
- `test_transition_to_fix_uses_adjudicated_description` (function) — Asserts re-entering implement on the fix loop composes the adjudicated description into the implement step's inputs. <!--#7da8ff8b193017b1-->
- `test_source_pool_unchanged_without_adjudication` (function) — Asserts that with no `adjudicated_description` present, `_build_source_pool` grounds self_check issues on `task_description_base` alone and excludes `original_task_description` from the pool. <!--#a2a783f602668869-->
- `test_source_pool_drops_original_when_adjudicated` (function) — Asserts _build_source_pool drops the superseded original text from the pool once an adjudicated description is in effect. <!--#72003edca75d4ab1-->
- `test_dead_clause_issue_dropped_after_adjudication` (function) — Asserts a self_check issue quoting a clause abolished by adjudication is filtered out with a quote-not-in-source stat. <!--#57aed40e3c1bdd4b-->
- `test_live_clause_issue_kept_after_adjudication` (function) — Asserts a self_check issue quoting a still-live clause survives filtering after adjudication. <!--#b0738d13f9fbe2f8-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/test_baseline.py` (python) — Captures the set of tests already failing at flow start — via a background test-suite subprocess (BaselineCapture) plus a git-HEAD/dirty-hash keyed on-disk cache — so later test/verify_spec steps can tell inherited failures apart from regressions this flow introduced. <!--#ba7b621d5dbf3fdd|3a16cb9889dc135e-->
- `compute_baseline_key` (function) — Builds a deterministic cache key from the git HEAD sha plus a working-tree dirty hash, so any commit or content change invalidates a stale baseline. <!--#8dd9a8fe1224c6b5-->
- `_git_head_sha` (function) — Returns the current git HEAD sha, degrading to the literal "no-head" when the directory isn't a git repo or git is unavailable. <!--#6d07afeb323ea303-->
- `_file_content_hash` (function) — Returns the SHA-256 hex digest of a file's bytes, or None if it can't be read. <!--#857a05eb3f930681-->
- `_working_tree_dirty_hash` (function) — Hashes the working tree's dirty state — the raw `git diff HEAD` plus the names and content hashes of untracked non-ignored files — into a content-sensitive digest. <!--#695425e98c6d4c13-->
- `_git_untracked_files` (function) — Returns the sorted relative paths of untracked, non-ignored files via `git ls-files --others`, or an empty list on failure. <!--#64b04d87e8a279d9-->
- `cache_path` (function) — Helper that returns the filesystem Path to the baseline cache file for a given project_root, resolved under that project's runtime_dir. <!--#00434cecbd6ce337-->
- `_read_cache_entries` (function) — Best-effort reader of the cache's `entries` map that returns an empty dict on any problem (missing/corrupt/wrong-shape/schema-mismatch) so a damaged cache reads as a clean miss. <!--#e5a6072715306eca-->
- `load_cached` (function) — Looks up the cached failing-test-id set for a key, returning a (possibly empty) set on a hit or None on any miss. <!--#e3cd6b779c7a8b44-->
- `save_cache` (function) — Atomically persists a failing-set under a key (preserving other keys, LRU-bounded to MAX_CACHE_ENTRIES) via tempfile + os.replace. <!--#5c020aadea086148-->
- `resolve_baseline_timeout` (function) — Resolves the wall-clock bound for a baseline run by reusing `test.timeout` from tianluo.yaml, falling back to DEFAULT_BASELINE_TIMEOUT on any config error. <!--#cf0c6e1d36901294-->
- `BaselineCapture` (class) — Runs the project's test suite as a background subprocess before the implement step and resolves it into a baseline set of already-failing test ids — supporting launch/is_ready/wait/wait_or_kill lifecycle with a timed_out flag, and returning the None sentinel when the capture itself failed so callers fall back to a synchronous re-measurement instead of mistaking an unmeasured baseline for 'no failures'. <!--#a38324a137712019-->
  - `BaselineCapture.__init__` (method) — Initializes the capture's project root, optional command override, and the process/result/timeout bookkeeping state. <!--#496945c492d18e32-->
  - `BaselineCapture.launch` (method) — Starts the background test subprocess (with SE3_TEST_RUNNING=1 to prevent recursion), idempotently and without raising, recording any launch failure for later. <!--#e3d786d17860ee0e-->
  - `BaselineCapture.is_ready` (method) — Returns True when `wait` would resolve without blocking — i.e. the subprocess finished, launch failed, or nothing was ever launched. <!--#cf4e7fa49e0f2d9f-->
  - `BaselineCapture.wait` (method) — Blocks until the capture finishes and returns the cached failing-id set, or None on capture failure, raising TimeoutExpired (resumable) if a timeout is given and hit. <!--#e1642a76f1abaa60-->
  - `BaselineCapture.timed_out` (method) — Reports whether the capture was killed for exceeding its time bound, letting the caller skip a synchronous retry that would just hang again. <!--#f66c64ed5690fb8f-->
  - `BaselineCapture.wait_or_kill` (method) — Bounded wait that kills the subprocess on timeout and resolves to the None sentinel (setting timed_out), instead of leaving the capture resumable like `wait`. <!--#58778a3528d13e61-->
  - `BaselineCapture.kill` (method) — Best-effort, idempotent teardown that terminates and reaps the subprocess, cleans up the temp output file, and marks the capture as a failed (None) measurement. <!--#5d1609d8c4dcd876-->
  - `BaselineCapture._resolve_command` (method) — Builds the baseline test command exactly the way steps/test.py would — using the configured test.command or _detect_test_command, forcing a verbose pytest flag so per-test PASSED/FAILED ids are parseable, and applying the same test.parallel mode so baseline and test-step results are comparable. <!--#5624178397a2a155-->
  - `BaselineCapture._parse_result` (method) — Parses the captured output into a failing-id set, returning None when a non-zero exit produced no parseable per-test results (a collection/infra error) to signal fallback. <!--#0b6275a2089ff0ef-->
  - `BaselineCapture._close_stdout_file` (method) — Closes the open stdout temp-file handle, swallowing any OSError. <!--#b5e92b79a12c5410-->
  - `BaselineCapture._cleanup_stdout_file` (method) — Closes and deletes the temp stdout file once it has been read, ignoring errors. <!--#59ca266f4db1a002-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/test_code_index_concurrency.py` (python) — Co-located pytest suite verifying the code-index's concurrent LLM summariser: config validation of max_concurrency, bounded fan-out that reaches but never exceeds the concurrency cap with one caller per group, serial/concurrent output parity, per-group failure isolation, byte-identical and resumable batched Pass-2 rebuilds, concurrent handling of scattered incremental edits, and correct progress-callback firing. <!--#ac60520b08bfd48c|bbfcb101094aeadd-->
- `_ids_in_prompt` (function) — Helper that extracts the list of node ids embedded in a summariser prompt via a module-level regex. <!--#9a8e067c62be815e-->
- `_EchoCaller` (class) — Deterministic stub LLMCaller that echoes each requested id back as `sum:<id>` and records every constructed instance so tests can prove one caller is built per concurrent group. <!--#7d9075dc679adb6e-->
  - `_EchoCaller.__init__` (method) — Registers each new instance on the class's shared instance list under a lock. <!--#5f2e552e2b28f659-->
  - `_EchoCaller.call` (method) — Returns a JSON map of each prompt id to `sum:<id>`. <!--#2b9cdb94e0fbd974-->
  - `_EchoCaller.reset` (method) — Clears the recorded instance list between tests. <!--#5fc86487a4adf402-->
- `_Recorder` (class) — Builds a stub-caller class that uses a shared counter and a Barrier(workers) to deterministically record peak concurrent in-flight calls and each caller instance. <!--#7f7d1605fd927297-->
  - `_Recorder.__init__` (method) — Initialises the lock, in-flight/peak counters, instance list, and a barrier sized to the expected worker count. <!--#119d80ee5b16bebd-->
  - `_Recorder.caller_cls` (method) — Returns a closure-bound `_BarrierCaller` class whose calls bump the peak counter, rendezvous on the barrier, then return empty JSON. <!--#37e41f5f9bac7c87-->
- `_file_targets` (function) — Factory producing `n` distinct file-level SummaryTargets so each becomes an independent by-file summary group. <!--#a98d7d1f8b796af4-->
- `TestMaxConcurrencyConfig` (class) — Tests that CodeIndexConfig's max_concurrency defaults to four, reads valid values, and falls back with a warning on illegal ones. <!--#ce5a7f60f4834d2b-->
  - `TestMaxConcurrencyConfig.test_default_is_four` (method) — Asserts the default max_concurrency (and its constant) is four across constructor and from_dict. <!--#9b6bdbcccd2f808b-->
  - `TestMaxConcurrencyConfig.test_valid_value_read` (method) — Asserts a valid max_concurrency value is read through from_dict unchanged. <!--#e4c6dc2d40c20677-->
  - `TestMaxConcurrencyConfig.test_illegal_value_falls_back_with_warning` (method) — Parametrised test asserting illegal max_concurrency values revert to four and log a warning. <!--#f3f2f842688847f3-->
- `TestConcurrentSummarizer` (class) — Test suite verifying the LLM code-index summarizer's concurrency behavior: peak worker count matches max_concurrency, each group builds its own distinct LLMCaller, serial and concurrent runs yield identical results, and a single failing group degrades to the heuristic summary. <!--#194cfb218dd3366e-->
  - `TestConcurrentSummarizer.test_reaches_exactly_max_concurrency` (method) — Asserts that with 2*max_conc groups the summarizer's peak concurrency exactly equals max_concurrency and spawns one distinct caller instance per group. <!--#7317e974df9fd099-->
  - `TestConcurrentSummarizer.test_serial_when_max_concurrency_one` (method) — Asserts that max_concurrency=1 runs the summarizer fully serial (peak == 1) while still building one caller instance per group. <!--#2f09b39161ff2d35-->
  - `TestConcurrentSummarizer.test_each_group_builds_its_own_caller` (method) — Asserts that six summary groups produce six distinct, non-shared LLMCaller instances. <!--#4777c5184ea8912d-->
  - `TestConcurrentSummarizer.test_results_identical_serial_vs_concurrent` (method) — Asserts that running the summarizer serially (max_concurrency=1) and concurrently (=8) over the same targets yields identical, expected result maps. <!--#a31fe40a1fcb0f00-->
  - `TestConcurrentSummarizer.test_single_group_failure_degrades_to_heuristic` (method) — Asserts that when one group's LLM call raises, that group falls back to the "<kind> <name>" heuristic while healthy groups summarise normally and all ids are still returned. <!--#5073164f9081e2ce-->
- `_git` (function) — Helper running a git subcommand in a repo root with output captured and errors raised. <!--#881bf8d1b379498d-->
- `_DeterministicSummarizer` (class) — Injected summariser bypassing the LLM path that returns `S:<name>` per target so md differences are attributable to Pass-2 batching alone. <!--#b18c2289df6ead18-->
  - `_DeterministicSummarizer.__call__` (method) — Returns a map of each target id to `S:<name>`. <!--#1d61334eb28ddb92-->
- `project` (function) — Pytest fixture that creates a committed git project with a pkg/ directory of seven module files and a README, used to exercise multi-batch code-index builds. <!--#c03ac0dcee072b4a-->
- `TestBatchedPass2` (class) — Tests that batched Pass-2 summarisation yields byte-identical md across concurrency levels and that a partial flush is a valid incremental resume point. <!--#c434e352e4f839a8-->
  - `TestBatchedPass2.test_md_byte_identical_across_concurrency` (method) — Asserts the generated code-index.md is byte-identical whether built with concurrency 1 or 8. <!--#fecf85e9f821daa9-->
  - `TestBatchedPass2.test_partial_flush_is_a_superset_resume_point` (method) — Asserts an unchanged incremental rebuild reuses every already-summarised node and hands the summariser no targets. <!--#61460bd575d9cc6d-->
- `_ScatterRecorder` (class) — Peak-concurrency recorder that gates only the summary calls for a known set of edited files on a barrier, proving scattered incremental edits batch together and run concurrently rather than being serialised. <!--#02a4420e0f199d92-->
  - `_ScatterRecorder.__init__` (method) — Initialises the edited-path set, counters, and a barrier sized to the edited count. <!--#3e05bea13f08f97d-->
  - `_ScatterRecorder.caller_cls` (method) — Returns a caller class that gates prompts matching an edited path on the barrier (tracking peak) and always echoes id summaries. <!--#3067b2d46df01891-->
- `TestIncrementalConcurrency` (class) — Test suite (single regression test) ensuring the commit-time incremental index path reaches max_concurrency even when edited files are scattered across the sorted file list. <!--#f89866ef9dbc1382-->
  - `TestIncrementalConcurrency.test_scattered_incremental_edits_run_concurrently` (method) — Regression test that edits three widely-separated files and asserts they re-summarise concurrently (peak == 3), proving stale-file batching rather than positional slicing. <!--#ca1ee6824df3429f-->
- `TestProgressCallback` (class) — Tests the build's progress callback fires once per stale file/dir node, reports body-only edits at file granularity, is a no-op when omitted, and stays silent on fully-reused builds. <!--#12160670cc6faa76-->
  - `TestProgressCallback.test_fires_once_per_file_and_dir_node` (method) — Asserts a forced build fires exactly one monotonic callback per file/dir node with constant total and file phase preceding dir phase. <!--#f632cf62339de46c-->
  - `TestProgressCallback.test_body_only_edit_still_reports_its_file` (method) — Regression test asserting a body-only edit still reports its file at file granularity exactly once even though the file node is reused. <!--#acc26694ab906219-->
  - `TestProgressCallback.test_progress_none_is_noop` (method) — Asserts omitting the progress callback still produces the md file without error. <!--#7827272b623aefb0-->
  - `TestProgressCallback.test_no_callback_for_fully_reused_build` (method) — Asserts a no-change incremental rebuild fires zero progress callbacks. <!--#fe40f1c086abc140-->
- `TestRecordIndexProgress` (class) — Test suite for chat_history.record_index_progress: index_progress records are written to the raw jsonl but skipped by step-history/retry views, missing ids are a soft no-op, and OSErrors are swallowed. <!--#a3c4162fcab58159-->
  - `TestRecordIndexProgress.test_write_and_history_retry_skip` (method) — Asserts index_progress records land as well-formed jsonl lines yet are excluded from get_step_history and retry-context views. <!--#777aea871069d8e1-->
  - `TestRecordIndexProgress.test_missing_ids_soft_noop` (method) — Asserts that calling record_index_progress with empty flow/step ids writes nothing (no history directory created). <!--#f2d2ac0ff5af988b-->
  - `TestRecordIndexProgress.test_oserror_is_swallowed` (method) — Asserts that a mkdir OSError during record_index_progress is warned-and-swallowed rather than propagated. <!--#9804afe8155599e0-->
- `TestEnsureCodeIndexFreshProgress` (class) — Test suite for ensure_code_index_fresh: it silently refreshes with no flow context, and writes monotonic file/dir index_progress history (without bleeding system-role turns into the session) when given a commit context. <!--#d6b54d3ce56cfdf3-->
  - `TestEnsureCodeIndexFreshProgress._build_with_echo` (method) — Helper that builds a forced code index over the fixture project using the _EchoCaller stub at max_concurrency=3. <!--#242955f60586ffcb-->
  - `TestEnsureCodeIndexFreshProgress.test_no_flow_context_is_noop` (method) — Asserts that ensure_code_index_fresh with no flow/step context refreshes silently, writing no history and never raising. <!--#e738f23aad9b5a40-->
  - `TestEnsureCodeIndexFreshProgress.test_commit_context_writes_progress` (method) — Asserts that adding a file and running ensure_code_index_fresh with a commit context writes monotonic file/dir index_progress records that are kept out of the reconstructed session history. <!--#260997aff0e2c7a3-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/test_code_index_degrade.py` (python) — Co-located unit tests pinning the code-index degrade mode: the three-condition (text + structure-less + over-threshold) eligibility gate, line/byte-based chunking into degraded 'chunk' units, and the DEGRADED_MARKER render annotation. <!--#608d167de07e70b7|71775928e2399a22-->
- `_small_cfg` (function) — Test helper returning a CodeIndexConfig with tiny line/chunk thresholds so tests can trip degrade with only a few lines. <!--#53bc45df86825aa9-->
- `TestDegradeGate` (class) — Test class covering when a file becomes degrade-eligible — the three-condition gate and independent byte-threshold triggering. <!--#d0d6098b67194f0e-->
  - `TestDegradeGate.test_all_three_conditions_required` (method) — Asserts degrade eligibility requires structure-less AND over-threshold, voided by either having structure or being under threshold. <!--#2199039eeb4e2357-->
  - `TestDegradeGate.test_byte_threshold_trips_independently` (method) — Verifies the byte-size threshold can trip degrade on its own, even for a single-line file under the line threshold. <!--#46459083602a0c70-->
- `TestChunking` (class) — Test class verifying the code_index degradation path: that oversized/structureless files are split into line-limited `chunk` symbols marked `degraded`, that tiny structureless files stay as a single file-level entry, and that the `DEGRADED_MARKER` surfaces in rendered output. <!--#7aab2480c1ef63b1-->
  - `TestChunking.test_chunks_respect_line_limit_and_mark_degraded` (method) — Checks _chunk_degraded splits text into degraded 'chunk' units that each stay within the configured chunk_lines limit. <!--#e1f3a47db522d4b6-->
  - `TestChunking.test_small_structureless_file_stops_at_file_level` (method) — Verifies a small structure-less file stays a single file-level text entry with no chunk symbols. <!--#6740dfa1b46eb647-->
  - `TestChunking.test_large_structureless_file_degrades_to_chunks` (method) — Verifies a large structure-less file is indexed into degraded chunk symbols. <!--#95e53b825cb305cd-->
  - `TestChunking.test_degraded_marker_in_render` (method) — Test that a large structureless file indexed via `code_index._index_file` and rendered through `code_index_render.render_path` includes the `DEGRADED_MARKER` in its output. <!--#ab35d3b6cd011cb1-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/test_engine.py` (python) — Unit-test suite for the flow engine's core: data models and default step sequences per task type, PersistenceManager save/load/atomic-write behaviour, StateMachine flow creation, resume, step dispatch and on_running callbacks, plus crash/mid-step recovery and end-to-end state-transition, failure and retry scenarios. <!--#12719eeef329a162|9a7a24fd5dfc257a-->
- `TestModels` (class) — Unit-test class covering the engine's core data models — `Step`/`FlowInstance` creation, serialization round-trips, and progress calculation — plus the `get_default_step_sequence` table for every task type (exact ordering, survey's code-free sequence, absence of retired spec steps, `INVARIANT_CHECK`/`CHARTER_FRESHNESS` placement, and the trailing `SUMMARIZE`). <!--#46b7e5b7c52d070c-->
  - `TestModels.test_step_creation` (method) — Asserts a freshly created Step has the given type, PENDING status, and a string step_id. <!--#03395a96573ee1e6-->
  - `TestModels.test_step_serialization` (method) — Verifies a Step survives a to_dict/from_dict round-trip with type, status, inputs, and outputs intact. <!--#847efa99565cc90a-->
  - `TestModels.test_flow_instance_creation` (method) — Checks a new FlowInstance gets a well-formed dated flow_id, INIT status, and the supplied task description. <!--#bbbccfb954c27a8e-->
  - `TestModels.test_flow_progress` (method) — Confirms get_progress reports completed-over-total counts as steps are added and completed. <!--#5a57696221608554-->
  - `TestModels.test_flow_serialization` (method) — Verifies a FlowInstance with a step survives a to_dict/from_dict round-trip preserving its fields and steps. <!--#b4bbc96f9e25d2e2-->
  - `TestModels.test_default_step_sequences` (method) — Sanity-checks that feature/bugfix/small default sequences contain (or omit) the expected step types and relative lengths. <!--#6f246bdfcbcd5390-->
  - `TestModels.test_charter_refactor_sequences_exact` (method) — Asserts `get_default_step_sequence` returns the exact charter-refactor step list for each of the six task types, guards that the hand-written expectation table still covers the full type set, and checks the retired `directive` type now falls back to the feature sequence. <!--#dfd7cae5a2dc5921-->
  - `TestModels.test_survey_sequence_has_no_self_check` (method) — Asserts the `survey` sequence is exactly ANALYZE → INVESTIGATE → SUMMARIZE and contains none of the change-guarding steps (`SELF_CHECK`, `INVARIANT_CHECK`, `IMPLEMENT`, `TEST`, `VERSION_ANALYZE`, `COMMIT`). <!--#567ffd6381da8ed1-->
  - `TestModels.test_retired_spec_steps_absent_from_all_sequences` (method) — Asserts the retired spec-governance steps (`VERIFY_SPEC`, `UPDATE_SPEC`, `SPEC_GATE`) appear in no default task-type sequence. <!--#4c3c34d49e780e92-->
  - `TestModels.test_invariant_check_placement` (method) — Asserts positional invariants of the default sequences — `INVARIANT_CHECK` directly follows `SELF_CHECK` (or `ANALYZE` for review) and `CHARTER_FRESHNESS` directly precedes `VERSION_ANALYZE`, while `small` gets only the non-blocking freshness check. <!--#718847938a7b379f-->
  - `TestModels.test_default_sequences_end_with_summarize` (method) — Asserts `SUMMARIZE` terminates every default sequence exactly once, sits immediately after `COMMIT` in the non-review sequences, and is still present via the unknown-task-type fallback. <!--#45c4fbace14262dc-->

  - `TestSessionUsageRecordsModel.test_add_drops_exact_duplicate_call_attempt` (method) — Asserts `add_session_usage_record` ignores a record repeating the same call id and attempt, so the ledger and projection are not double-counted. <!--#8395a425317a597e-->

  - `TestSessionUsageRecordsModel.test_old_projection_with_embedded_records_is_imported` (method) — Asserts an old engine.json shape, where usage records live only inside the `session_token_usage` projection, is migrated into `session_usage_records` on load. <!--#086172a0a5966f4b-->
  - `TestSessionUsageRecordsModel.test_legacy_ledger_flag_survives_a_modern_re_save` (method) — Asserts a pre-ledger flow with a non-zero tally keeps `legacy_usage_ledger` true across a modern re-save (which always emits an empty `session_usage_records`), for both `from_dict` and `from_header_dict`, so accumulated billing data is not dropped. <!--#baa8a03272efec1f-->
  - `TestSessionUsageRecordsModel.test_modern_empty_ledger_is_not_legacy` (method) — Asserts a freshly serialized state with zero calls is not flagged as a legacy ledger, so an all-zero tally is never adapted into a fabricated unknown call. <!--#f64c59e4fcae8dd5-->
  - `TestSessionUsageRecordsModel.test_ledger_with_records_is_never_legacy` (method) — Asserts a state containing real usage records round-trips with `legacy_usage_ledger` false. <!--#d60a9aa6481e9167-->
  - `TestSessionUsageRecordsModel.test_records_serialize_once_not_twice` (method) — Asserts serialization stores records only under `session_usage_records`, with no duplicate `usage_records` list embedded in the `session_token_usage` projection. <!--#a913d8922d4c83ae-->
- `TestRunStepTokenAggregation` (class) — Test class verifying that `StateMachine.run_step` opens a usage scope that merges multiple LLM calls into `step.outputs["token_usage"]`, publishes per-call `usage_records`/`usage_summary`, omits usage fields for call-free steps, accumulates across steps into the session total, and carries usage across re-executed and paused (multi-round) step runs. <!--#64fc5e407171408f-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation._make_usage` (method) — Helper constructing a UsageTotals from keyword fields. <!--#61d9bd91f9c0d33a-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_single_step_merges_multiple_calls` (method) — Verifies two calls within one step merge into the step's token_usage and the session total. <!--#c39903bd03e6bf4d-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_no_call_step_writes_no_usage_field` (method) — Confirms a step making no LLM call writes no token_usage field and leaves the session total empty. <!--#f7afd427ad3b2dbf-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_multi_step_session_accumulation` (method) — Verifies the session total equals the sum of usage across multiple separately-run steps. <!--#d0f0e4c88a4e0921-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_step_publishes_usage_records_and_summary_from_shared_backend` (method) — Asserts a completed step publishes the authoritative per-call `usage_records` plus a self-sufficient `usage_summary` (totals, status, completeness) that reproduces the same numbers when re-summarized, and that the session ledger holds the same record. <!--#e09eca11ba8c5ef2-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_reused_step_accumulates_usage_records_across_executions` (method) — Asserts a step re-executed in a fix loop keeps both runs' records on its per-step ledger, so the per-step summary totals match the session ledger. <!--#8874523452adab42-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_exception_step_still_aggregates_and_resets_scope` (method) — Confirms a raising handler still records usage gathered before the raise and resets the step scope (no contextvar leak). <!--#498168edce99d8ce-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_paused_run_usage_carried_into_next_emitted_record` (method) — Asserts that non-terminal (PAUSED) rounds publish both `token_usage` for display and `carried_token_usage` for cross-round accumulation, and that the final terminal round reports the all-round sum while clearing the carry, matching the session total. <!--#88d0868cd095318d-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_aggregated_usage_survives_persistence` (method) — Confirms both step-level and session token usage round-trip through engine.json persistence. <!--#e87aadc8e5ee2ef4-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_revision_needed_step_publishes_visible_token_usage` (method) — Verifies a REVISION_NEEDED step publishes visible token_usage (the G2 fix) alongside carried_token_usage. <!--#23c0cc57791d6903-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_non_terminal_then_terminal_usage_equals_sum_of_rounds` (method) — Confirms after a revision then a completion round the terminal token_usage and session total equal the sum of both rounds' increments. <!--#a6bfda3a51da181c-->
  - `TestRunStepTokenAggregation.test_session_usage_not_duplicated_by_combined_totals` (method) — Verifies the session total sums each round's per-round increment rather than combined carry totals, avoiding double-counting across re-entries. <!--#5fd1b8051bd165b1-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/test_steps.py` (python) — Unit-test suite for the engine's step handlers — analyze, test, commit, version_analyze, summarize/discovery, and step sequencing — covering worktree de-versioning (VersionIntent files instead of authoritative bumps), the in-lock commit version race guard, retired spec-selection surfaces, issue-discovery injection, step input building, and round token-usage footer rendering. <!--#e3ec5b1bfd6774d2|d781b3ff219a4954-->
- `TestAnalyzeStep` (class) — Test class covering the analyze step handler: successful classification output, the conservative `root_cause_clear` default that routes unclear bugfixes to INVESTIGATE, and failure handling for invalid JSON or `LLMCallError` from the LLM. <!--#39cd7f8e5d97b2d0-->
  - `TestAnalyzeStep.test_analyze_success` (method) — Asserts a successful `analyze_handler` run emits the classification fields plus a programmatic `project_summary`, while the retired spec-selection surface degrades to empty `relevant_specs`/`selected_items` and never emits `spec_content` or `selected_specs`. <!--#1bc5565f5db69237-->
  - `TestAnalyzeStep.test_analyze_missing_root_cause_clear_defaults_to_false` (method) — Asserts that when the LLM omits `root_cause_clear`, the step defaults it to false with a warning log and schedules an `INVESTIGATE` step for the bugfix flow. <!--#ad5491b9609fedaa-->
  - `TestAnalyzeStep.test_analyze_invalid_json` (method) — Asserts analyze fails (with an error message) when the LLM returns unparseable JSON. <!--#da519831bd138dbe-->
  - `TestAnalyzeStep.test_analyze_llm_error` (method) — Asserts analyze fails when the LLM call itself raises an LLMCallError. <!--#9b9696993d33a034-->
- `TestTestStep` (class) — Unit tests for the test step's run_test_step handler, verifying COMPLETED on passing tests and REVISION_NEEDED (blocking) on unparseable failures against an empty baseline, with a fixture that pre-warms the git-root cache and clears SE3_TEST_RUNNING. <!--#3a96836f8702b808-->
  - `TestTestStep._warm_main_repo_root_cache` (method) — Autouse fixture that warms the git main-repo-root lru_cache before subprocess.Popen is patched and clears the SE3_TEST_RUNNING recursion-guard env var, so the test step's real path runs regardless of isolation or outer-suite invocation. <!--#314791e96460f238-->
  - `TestTestStep.test_test_success` (method) — Asserts a zero-exit pytest run completes the test step and records test_results. <!--#9549f65cd5ea7dcc-->
  - `TestTestStep.test_test_failure` (method) — Asserts an unparseable non-zero pytest failure is treated as introduced (blocking) and returns REVISION_NEEDED. <!--#b51593f06f5def18-->
- `TestCommitStep` (class) — Unit tests for the commit step's handler dispatching mocked git subcommands, asserting COMPLETED for a successful pure-git commit (version bumping disabled) and for a no-changes commit. <!--#bafb9c3048f1a722-->
  - `TestCommitStep.test_commit_success` (method) — Verifies commit_handler returns COMPLETED by mocking git calls dispatched by subcommand with version bumping disabled. <!--#5acc02711e1bcd11-->
  - `TestCommitStep.test_commit_no_changes` (method) — Asserts the commit handler completes successfully even when git reports no changes. <!--#441ea7bef6ef446b-->
- `TestVersionAnalyzeDeVersioning` (class) — Unit tests asserting version_analyze emits a provisional VersionIntent file (no authoritative suggested_version) for worktree flows while synchronous flows keep the authoritative version and write no intent, with intent body completeness independent of bump_type. <!--#a517f6bc8c960826-->
  - `TestVersionAnalyzeDeVersioning._run` (method) — Helper that runs version_analyze_handler with a mocked LLMCaller over a feature flow in either worktree or synchronous mode, returning the flow, step, and result. <!--#892e86b63b9af23c-->
  - `TestVersionAnalyzeDeVersioning.test_worktree_flow_emits_intent_and_no_authoritative_version` (method) — Asserts a worktree flow persists a VersionIntent (provisional version, bump hint, baseline, changelog, non-empty change_summary) and exposes no authoritative suggested_version. <!--#02e984308b107795-->
  - `TestVersionAnalyzeDeVersioning.test_worktree_intent_body_complete_without_usable_bump_type` (method) — Test that a worktree flow with a date-based version and no bump_type in the LLM response still persists a complete VersionIntent (change_summary + versions_changes) via read_intent. <!--#b3a18e2295301dfd-->
  - `TestVersionAnalyzeDeVersioning.test_synchronous_flow_keeps_authoritative_version` (method) — Asserts a non-worktree flow still exposes the authoritative suggested_version and writes no VersionIntent file. <!--#54d6f86f33083468-->
- `TestCommitDeVersioning` (class) — Unit tests asserting worktree commits never touch the version file/docs and stamp only a bump-intent decoration (no Version: line), that synchronous commits keep the Version: line, and that discovery flows use the real analyzed task_type as the commit subject prefix. <!--#1605031ab4cca1d6-->
  - `TestCommitDeVersioning._fake_git` (method) — Helper returning a fake subprocess.run side-effect that stubs git status/commit/rev-parse and captures the commit message. <!--#41664d63231a0f0d-->
  - `TestCommitDeVersioning.test_worktree_commit_skips_version_and_docs` (method) — Asserts that with version bumping enabled but in worktree mode, the commit never touches the version file and stamps no Version: line, only the bump decoration. <!--#7d18d60756c6bec6-->
  - `TestCommitDeVersioning.test_worktree_commit_message_has_no_version_line` (method) — Unit-tests _generate_commit_message with new_version=None (worktree path) to confirm the bump decoration appears but no Version: line. <!--#7182fc4b4c03de94-->
  - `TestCommitDeVersioning.test_synchronous_commit_message_keeps_version_line` (method) — Contrast unit test confirming _generate_commit_message with a written version still includes the Version: line for synchronous flows. <!--#8d22481f45e51b90-->
  - `TestCommitDeVersioning.test_discovery_flow_commit_prefix_uses_real_analyzed_type` (method) — Asserts that a discovery flow with an `analyzed_type` of "feature" in state context produces a commit message prefixed "feature:" via effective_task_type, never "discovery:". <!--#f4a777db8a1128be-->
  - `TestCommitDeVersioning.test_discovery_flow_without_analyzed_type_falls_back_to_feature` (method) — Asserts that a discovery flow lacking any `analyzed_type` still avoids a "discovery:" prefix and degrades gracefully to a "feature:" commit-subject prefix. <!--#e37d3fde0bc9dc38-->
- `TestCommitVersionRaceGuard` (class) — Unit tests for the commit step's in-lock version race guard, verifying that on-disk drift versus version_analyze's observed current_version triggers a re-analyze against the drifted baseline to avoid a double-bump collision, while no drift writes the resolved target unchanged. <!--#c537fb3a0c9b0161-->
  - `TestCommitVersionRaceGuard._fake_git` (method) — Helper returning a fake subprocess.run side-effect stubbing git status/commit/rev-parse and capturing the commit message. <!--#ff5591844863b501-->
  - `TestCommitVersionRaceGuard._make_flow_with_version_analyze` (method) — Helper building a non-worktree flow carrying a completed version_analyze step with configurable observed current_version and baseline. <!--#6d93bf332c9e07ce-->
  - `TestCommitVersionRaceGuard._make_commit_step` (method) — Helper building a COMMIT step preloaded with a suggested version, pre-session baseline, and patch bump_type. <!--#0f81df148bbf4e20-->
  - `TestCommitVersionRaceGuard.test_drift_triggers_reanalyze_and_avoids_collision` (method) — Asserts that when disk drifted past the baseline (concurrent bump), the stale suggested_version is discarded and version_analyze re-runs against the drifted baseline to write a non-colliding version. <!--#153cb98227a7ff38-->
  - `TestCommitVersionRaceGuard.test_no_drift_writes_target_unchanged` (method) — Asserts that when the disk version still equals the baseline (no concurrent bump), version_analyze is not re-run and the resolved target is written verbatim. <!--#23c58e9348e1dba0-->
  - `TestCommitVersionRaceGuard.test_own_session_advance_is_not_drift` (method) — Asserts that a version file advanced by this flow's own session commits (disk == observed current_version but > baseline) is not treated as drift, discriminating the guard's operand from pre_session_version. <!--#1500673daabe5691-->
  - `TestCommitVersionRaceGuard.test_drift_reanalyze_failure_halts_commit` (method) — Asserts the commit halts with FAILED (never writing the stale colliding target) when the drift re-analysis fails to produce a version. <!--#b5007fbf516e519c-->
  - `TestCommitVersionRaceGuard.test_crash_resume_uncommitted_own_write_kept` (method) — Asserts that a crash-resume drift (disk written but HEAD blob still pre-crash, i.e. head != disk) is recognized as the flow's own uncommitted residue and the target is kept/re-written rather than re-analysed. <!--#21fe007a74b62463-->
  - `TestCommitVersionRaceGuard.test_concurrent_drift_committed_head_triggers_reanalyze` (method) — Asserts the inverse of crash-resume: a committed drift (HEAD blob == disk) is a concurrent bump, so self-heal must not fire and version_analyze is re-run against the drifted baseline. <!--#752cb45cd645f0e4-->
  - `TestCommitVersionRaceGuard.test_drift_reanalyze_regression_halts_commit` (method) — Asserts the commit halts with FAILED when drift re-analysis hallucinates a version lower than the drifted disk version, blocking a monotonicity-violating regression. <!--#e63ac36b62538d39-->
- `TestStepHandlers` (class) — Test suite verifying the STEP_HANDLERS registry covers all non-retired step types with callable handlers. <!--#8076771bd49382b1-->
  - `TestStepHandlers.test_all_step_types_have_handlers` (method) — Asserts every step type except the retired spec steps has a registered handler. <!--#3250f8784dac9d41-->
  - `TestStepHandlers.test_handler_consistency` (method) — Asserts every registered handler is callable. <!--#e32c966dbfac38c3-->
- `TestLLMCallerIntegration` (class) — Unit tests for LLMCaller retry logic with agent rotation pinned off, asserting retries on the same mocked runner eventually succeed and that exhausting max_retries raises LLMCallError. <!--#44599e4b85ab68c6-->
  - `TestLLMCallerIntegration.test_llm_retry_success` (method) — Asserts LLMCaller.call retries a failing runner and returns the output once a later attempt succeeds, after exactly the expected number of invocations. <!--#b39dce2720d96457-->
  - `TestLLMCallerIntegration.test_llm_retry_exhausted` (method) — Asserts LLMCaller.call raises LLMCallError once max_retries attempts have all failed, without exceeding the retry budget. <!--#81190593d694e9fe-->
- `TestContextBuilderSpecSurfaceRemoved` (class) — Regression guard asserting the spec-loading surface of `context_builder` (the `ContextBuilder` class and spec-name injection) is gone along with the spec mirror, while charter injection survives. <!--#c23a38b0d0174c53-->

- `TestIssueDiscoveryInjection` (class) — Unit tests for get_issue_discovery_injection, verifying the now-empty default whitelist injects nothing, that custom tianluo.yaml whitelists are honored, and that forbidden steps (implement/test) always return empty even when configured. <!--#a1eb1f37e87c7d7d-->

  - `TestIssueDiscoveryInjection.test_forbidden_step_test_returns_empty` (method) — Asserts the forbidden test step returns an empty injection. <!--#75393d92b5816f7a-->
  - `TestIssueDiscoveryInjection.test_custom_whitelist_from_config` (method) — Test that a custom tianluo.yaml issue_discovery whitelist injects into a listed step (design) while an unlisted step (verify_spec) receives no injection. <!--#f9ffdd10f9288ae3-->
  - `TestIssueDiscoveryInjection.test_forbidden_step_overrides_config` (method) — Test that a forbidden step (implement) returns an empty injection even when explicitly whitelisted in tianluo.yaml. <!--#5b5a6d9bb45430d3-->
  - `TestIssueDiscoveryInjection.test_missing_config_uses_empty_default` (method) — Test that with no tianluo.yaml the empty default whitelist yields no injection for summarize. <!--#cab21d15ce74aa19-->
  - `TestIssueDiscoveryInjection.test_default_whitelist_is_empty` (method) — Asserts ISSUE_DISCOVERY_DEFAULT_STEPS is an empty list. <!--#160ecf07f623b2ae-->

- `TestStepSequences` (class) — Tests over `get_default_step_sequence` verifying no task type still includes the deprecated `PROJECT_SUMMARY`/`READ_SPEC` steps and that the small, feature, review, and discovery sequences match their post-charter-refactor shapes. <!--#fefcdce481625b76-->
  - `TestStepSequences.test_all_task_types_exclude_project_summary` (method) — Asserts that the default step sequence for every task type (feature, bugfix, review, small, discovery) is free of the deprecated `PROJECT_SUMMARY` step. <!--#09a6a0efac4e92f2-->

- `TestFormatRoundUsageFooter` (class) — Unit tests for `token_usage.format_round_usage_footer`, asserting the compact "This round … · Total …" string uses comma thousands separators, shows only input/output tokens (no cache or cost), renders zeros, and degrades `None` inputs to zeros instead of raising. <!--#4a5e4a0f4db5f27b-->
  - `TestFormatRoundUsageFooter.test_normal_values_render_round_and_cumulative` (method) — Asserts the footer for typical round and cumulative usage renders as the exact en-US string with comma-separated in/out counts. <!--#9d86858d2639c8f9-->

- `TestDiscoveryRoundUsageFooter` (class) — Tests that the discovery step's message block appends the per-round usage footer only when the round actually called the LLM, and that `discovery_handler` passes round usage plus carried-forward cumulative usage into the display (with the programmatic-confirm fast path rendering nothing). <!--#f4f93c77438052c6-->

  - `TestDiscoveryRoundUsageFooter.test_no_footer_when_round_usage_none` (method) — Asserts no footer text is emitted when the discovery message is displayed without any round usage (e.g. redraw or `--resume`). <!--#5dab080d327e7dac-->

- `TestCliSinkUsageRendering` (class) — Unit tests for CliSink per-step token-usage routing, asserting confirm/discovery render compact dim footer/cumulative lines (or nothing when no LLM call), plan keeps the big usage block, and other step types go through the full report renderer. <!--#fdde81b3814807c7-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/test_version_intent.py` (python) — Pytest suite for the version_intent module, verifying VersionIntent serialization round-trips (including bump_type-less custom-rules and is_tag cases), on-disk write/read and corruption tolerance, cross-branch collect_intents gathering, consumed-marker idempotency, and the .gitignore self-heal guard that keeps version-intent JSON files trackable. <!--#986869f49a3de6af|bbc64db1166fe54d-->

  - `TestSerialization.test_round_trip_preserves_all_fields` (method) — Asserts a VersionIntent survives a to_dict/from_dict round-trip unchanged. <!--#470de33d03265dac-->

  - `TestSerialization.test_custom_rules_intent_without_bump_type` (method) — Asserts an intent with no bump_type still round-trips through disk with its versions_changes and change_summary intact. <!--#3ac688e6c33306cb-->
  - `TestSerialization.test_from_dict_requires_flow_id` (method) — Asserts from_dict raises ValueError when the flow_id key is missing. <!--#542d3977fc8c6a2e-->
  - `TestSerialization.test_from_dict_ignores_unknown_keys` (method) — Asserts from_dict silently ignores unrecognized keys for forward compatibility. <!--#222fb045399e2c4d-->

  - `TestSerialization.test_is_tag_round_trip` (method) — Asserts that a False is_tag flag survives a to_dict/from_dict round-trip rather than being lost or coerced. <!--#08873247576bff02-->
  - `TestSerialization.test_from_dict_missing_is_tag_defaults_none` (method) — Asserts that VersionIntent.from_dict leaves is_tag as None when the key is absent from the input dict. <!--#0abb31032f899504-->

  - `TestSerialization.test_read_corrupt_returns_none` (method) — Asserts read_intent returns None rather than raising when the on-disk JSON is malformed. <!--#7ba505b6cc83b488-->

  - `TestWriteIntentGitignoreGuard.test_ignored_error_is_oserror_subclass` (method) — Asserts VersionIntentIgnoredError subclasses OSError so it rides version_analyze's OSError-to-fail channel. <!--#a8510774fd9d94af-->
  - `TestWriteIntentGitignoreGuard.test_whitelisted_path_writes_normally` (method) — Asserts that an already-whitelisted .gitignore (`/tianluo/*` plus `!/version-intents/`) lets write_intent succeed and is left byte-for-byte untouched with no self-heal churn. <!--#f6fc2b141ca2c6eb-->
  - `TestWriteIntentGitignoreGuard.test_non_repo_does_not_block_write` (method) — Asserts write_intent falls back to writing the file when there is no git repo to probe check-ignore against. <!--#05dfe28b4d02ac27-->
  - `TestWriteIntentGitignoreGuard.test_heals_gitignore_with_se3_contents_anchor` (method) — Verifies shape (a) healing: when `/tianluo/*` exists without a version-intents whitelist, the heal inserts `!/tianluo/version-intents/` immediately after the anchor so the intent writes un-ignored. <!--#0dbee33e396a36fe-->
  - `TestWriteIntentGitignoreGuard.test_heals_gitignore_with_whole_se3_dir_ignored` (method) — Verifies shape (b) healing: a fully-ignored `/tianluo/` tree gets the re-include/re-exclude/whitelist trio appended so the intent writes and read_intent round-trips it. <!--#ac314bc0e537d23c-->
  - `TestWriteIntentGitignoreGuard.test_self_heal_is_idempotent` (method) — Confirms two consecutive intent writes into the same stale repo produce no second .gitignore change and no duplicate whitelist/re-include/re-exclude lines. <!--#cc7e211b19f90b83-->
  - `TestWriteIntentGitignoreGuard.test_heals_whole_dir_with_preexisting_void_whitelist` (method) — Checks the OLD-error-text state (whole-dir ignore plus a void bare whitelist) is healed by repositioning the whitelist after the `/tianluo/*` re-exclude so the negation wins and the path is no longer ignored. <!--#49da130dc36a884d-->
  - `TestWriteIntentGitignoreGuard.test_unrepairable_gitignore_raises_with_worktree_guidance` (method) — Asserts a read-only .gitignore makes the heal fail loud with VersionIntentIgnoredError carrying truthful worktree guidance (no `se3 init` hint) and writes no intent file. <!--#ffde382bf962ac3c-->
  - `TestWriteIntentGitignoreGuard.test_non_utf8_gitignore_raises_not_crashes` (method) — Ensures a non-UTF-8 .gitignore that also ignores tianluo/ degrades the heal's UnicodeDecodeError into a fail-loud VersionIntentIgnoredError, leaving the undecodable file byte-for-byte intact. <!--#ba8387ed99797e89-->
  - `TestWriteIntentGitignoreGuard.test_unrelated_ignore_rule_rolls_back_mutation` (method) — Verifies that when an unrelated `*.json` rule re-matches the intent, the heal fails loud and rolls back its appended lines, leaving no stray `/tianluo/*` re-exclude behind. <!--#4f8945c9a9e9892f-->
  - `TestWriteIntentGitignoreGuard.test_heals_gitignore_with_whole_dir_and_anchor_coexisting` (method) — Checks a legacy .gitignore holding both `/tianluo/` and `/tianluo/*` is healed by adding the `!/tianluo/` re-include before the anchor plus the whitelist, and stays idempotent across a second write. <!--#7f6a759e6510e579-->
  - `TestWriteIntentGitignoreGuard.test_unreadable_gitignore_is_not_deleted_on_fail_loud` (method) — Asserts that when the ignore verdict comes from .git/info/exclude and the pre-existing .gitignore is unreadable, the guard fails loud without unlinking or altering the user's file. <!--#e056b3a7f25a2a01-->
- `TestReconcileCommitDetection` (class) — Test suite for git-durable reconcile detection via commit trailers: matching by flow_id, consumed-via-commit even when the file flag is unset, and non-git-dir safety. <!--#f9cecb8c90d35738-->
  - `TestReconcileCommitDetection.test_detects_reconcile_commit_by_trailer` (method) — Asserts reconcile_commit_exists finds a commit carrying the reconcile trailer for the matching flow_id and rejects other flow_ids. <!--#ccf900047b5505e4-->
  - `TestReconcileCommitDetection.test_is_consumed_via_reconcile_commit` (method) — Asserts is_consumed reports True from a committed reconcile trailer alone, even when the on-disk consumed flag was never set. <!--#f862da3a5c85a809-->
  - `TestReconcileCommitDetection.test_reconcile_commit_exists_non_git_dir` (method) — Asserts reconcile_commit_exists returns False rather than raising when run outside a git repository. <!--#88172b190e07bcb5-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/token_usage.py` (python) — Defines the engine's LLM token-accounting layer: the `UsageTotals` dataclass (authoritative `UsageRecord` list plus a legacy five-field token/cost projection, with additive folding, dedup/partial-provenance tracking, and dict round-tripping), ContextVar-based step-scoped accumulators (`accumulate_step_usage`/`current_step_usage`/`use_step_usage`/`add_call_usage`) that collect per-call usage across threads, and i18n-aware formatters that render costs, round footers, and compact usage lines for display. <!--#967a6bb671892833|d9b87a7fb70eb37d-->
- `_coerce_int` (function) — Best-effort coerces any value to an int, returning 0 for None/missing/unparseable input so malformed usage payloads never raise. <!--#c97b0fddc8bb6dee-->
- `_coerce_float` (function) — Best-effort coerces any value to a float, returning 0.0 for None/missing/bad input. <!--#9a7b6843df4c055e-->
- `UsageTotals` (class) — Dataclass tally of input/output/cache token counts plus USD cost for one step or a whole session, holding the authoritative `UsageRecord` list alongside the legacy five-field projection and supporting additive folding, dedup/partial-provenance tracking, and dict (de)serialization. <!--#c91f063877a24af5-->
  - `UsageTotals.from_usage_records` (method) — Classmethod that aggregates a list of authoritative `UsageRecord`s into the legacy five-field `UsageTotals` projection, carrying over partial status and diagnostics. <!--#3653663cae0c935d-->
  - `UsageTotals.from_usage_record` (method) — Convenience classmethod building a `UsageTotals` from a single `UsageRecord`. <!--#fa4311713c431c22-->
  - `UsageTotals.add` (method) — Folds another (possibly `None`) tally into this one — re-aggregating from usage records when either side has them, otherwise summing fields with source-identity dedup that skips duplicate record-less folds and marks the result partial. <!--#d8e52bb87394109d-->
  - `UsageTotals._source_identity` (method) — Returns (lazily minting) a per-instance random token used to attribute and dedup record-less folds. <!--#6173f703f4d9e1b0-->
  - `UsageTotals._legacy_call_id` (method) — Builds a stable per-tally call id (`legacy:<kind>:<token>`) for records synthesized when adapting a legacy tally. <!--#1e885fb9f247c8d4-->
  - `UsageTotals.total_tokens` (method) — Returns input plus output tokens, treating the cache fields as classifications of input rather than extra tokens. <!--#29305a01201e3ffe-->
  - `UsageTotals.has_usage_records` (method) — Predicate reporting whether this tally carries authoritative usage records. <!--#c1a9b11c21254b00-->
  - `UsageTotals.is_empty` (method) — Predicate that is true when all token fields and the cost are zero, letting the display layer suppress an empty usage block. <!--#7a378dcf1c5dc055-->
  - `UsageTotals.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the tally to a stable JSON-primitive dict of the five legacy fields, appending serialized `usage_records` when present. <!--#2659fce21e68eb4c-->
  - `UsageTotals.from_dict` (method) — Classmethod reconstructing a tally from a possibly partial or `None` mapping, detecting single-record and record-list payloads and otherwise coercing the legacy five fields with zero defaults. <!--#2946a32723051c16-->
  - `UsageTotals.to_usage_records` (method) — Exposes the tally as `UsageRecord`s, synthesizing a legacy-adapted record (or a missing-usage marker) when none were recorded. <!--#85ef2588bc6d8388-->
- `accumulate_step_usage` (function) — Context manager that opens a fresh step-scoped accumulator (via ContextVar) for its body and yields it so the caller can read the merged step total afterward. <!--#cc56e3c1d6f5a823-->
- `current_step_usage` (function) — Returns the currently in-scope step accumulator, or None when no step scope is active. <!--#7fd09ce3743acedc-->
- `use_step_usage` (function) — Context manager that re-binds a given existing accumulator into the current context, used to carry a parent step's scope across ThreadPoolExecutor thread boundaries (no-op for None). <!--#3dbb8ce677b8dd31-->
- `add_call_usage` (function) — Module-level best-effort helper that normalizes one LLM call's usage (record, tally, or raw mapping) and folds it under a lock into the current step's contextvar accumulator, no-oping outside a step scope and swallowing all errors. <!--#c3ae6cc72c593f2e-->
- `format_cost` (function) — Renders a USD cost as a 4-decimal-place string (e.g. $0.0123), tolerant of None/non-numeric input. <!--#1d2dadbbbc3b7703-->
- `_format_tokens` (function) — Renders a token count with thousands separators (e.g. 12,345). <!--#6ac1c2bfe7972253-->
- `format_round_usage_footer` (function) — Renders a compact, i18n-localized single-line footer showing a CLI interactive round's incremental token in/out counts alongside the running cumulative totals, defaulting None inputs to zeros. <!--#a5732918e48f8bd9-->
- `format_usage_line` (function) — Renders a compact, i18n-localized single-line usage summary (input/output tokens, cache read/write, and cost) from a UsageTotals, safely rendering zeros for None or empty input. <!--#3af7a75c9953bf97-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/tool_formatters.py` (python) — Presentation-layer helpers that turn raw agent tool_use/tool_result payloads into short human-readable previews, merged success/failure chip headers, and structured detail payloads (input dumps, unified edit/write diffs) for the CLI and web UI, with per-tool formatters for Edit/Write/Read/Bash/Grep/Glob plus generic fallbacks and path/text truncation utilities. <!--#c078532ec103a604|dd9e0452a503b6d3-->
- `set_project_root` (function) — Sets the module-level project root used for relative-path truncation. <!--#dfcc75f6b64065c1-->
- `get_project_root` (function) — Returns the currently configured module-level project root. <!--#7154a7b54664f7dd-->
- `truncate_path` (function) — Shortens a file path by converting to project-relative and abbreviating middle segments while always preserving the filename. <!--#af68e886ed526bb5-->
- `truncate_preview` (function) — Collapses text to a single line and truncates it to a max length with an ellipsis. <!--#430e41a2779956b6-->
- `_generic_tool_use_preview` (function) — Fallback one-line preview for tools with no registered formatter, rendering the tool name plus up to three truncated `key=value` input pairs (with path-aware shortening for `file_path`). <!--#94b715dad63d0fc1-->
- `_generic_tool_result_preview` (function) — Fallback formatter producing a short preview of an arbitrary tool result, handling errors, dicts, lists, and strings. <!--#48f2fbefea36c20f-->
- `_format_edit_use` (function) — Builds the short `Edit: <path> (N lines → M lines)` preview for an Edit tool_use, omitting the line counts when the upstream reported no `old_string`/`new_string` at all. <!--#5dc98190a24e228a-->
- `_format_edit_result` (function) — Formats an Edit tool_result preview with a success/failure check mark. <!--#85c9245a8efa4b63-->
- `_format_write_use` (function) — Builds the short `Write: <path> (N lines)` preview for a Write tool_use, showing path only when the `content` key is absent and `(empty)` when it is present but empty. <!--#7da06cb24a788ae2-->
- `_format_write_result` (function) — Formats a Write tool_result preview with a success check mark. <!--#bb864e49ebf169af-->
- `_format_read_use` (function) — Formats a Read tool_use preview showing the path and optional offset/limit line range. <!--#033bed8e51562302-->
- `_format_read_result` (function) — Formats a Read tool_result preview reporting the number of lines read. <!--#64139de5213892f1-->
- `_format_bash_use` (function) — Formats a Bash tool_use preview showing a truncated command string. <!--#1d81716ea4607e32-->
- `_format_bash_result` (function) — Formats a Bash tool_result preview reporting the output line count. <!--#cadb1cac2322ffa6-->
- `_format_grep_use` (function) — Formats a Grep tool_use preview showing the pattern and search path. <!--#f358d0cddd652f2f-->
- `_format_grep_result` (function) — Formats a Grep tool_result preview reporting the number of matches. <!--#db18d2ecd441d75f-->
- `_format_glob_use` (function) — Formats a Glob tool_use preview showing the pattern and search path. <!--#a5fb2a263b26c807-->
- `_format_glob_result` (function) — Formats a Glob tool_result preview reporting the number of matched files. <!--#15d57808a43d6f30-->
- `_extract_text` (function) — Normalizes a tool result of varied shapes (string, dict, content-block list) into plain text. <!--#9ccecf462228bddd-->
- `format_tool_use_preview` (function) — Public entry point that routes a tool_use to its registered formatter or the generic fallback. <!--#384bca508e74b524-->
- `format_tool_result_preview` (function) — Public entry point that routes a tool_result to its registered formatter or the generic fallback. <!--#be3e1b30f642fff2-->
- `generate_edit_diff` (function) — Produces unified-diff lines from an Edit tool's old and new strings. <!--#12314b9f4beec6e1-->
- `_generic_use_body` (function) — Strips the `Tool: <name> | Input: ` (or `<name>: `) framing off the generic tool-use preview so only the `k=v, ...` body remains for chip headers. <!--#bc6cccbad460b52d-->
- `format_tool_chip_in_flight_header` (function) — Builds the in-flight tool chip's header text, delegating to the registered `_format_*_use` formatter or falling back to `<tool_name>: <k=v summary>` so unregistered tools still lead with their real name. <!--#77a9bee28a233f2d-->
- `_error_preview` (function) — Extracts a short error description from a failed tool_result payload. <!--#355770af1dbe4956-->
- `_success_combined_edit` (function) — Renders the combined use+result success line for Edit as the truncated path plus old→new line counts, dropping the counts when the input carried no text. <!--#4f7eea65fd40148e-->
- `_success_combined_write` (function) — Renders the combined use+result success line for Write as the truncated path plus written line count, dropping the count when the input carried no `content`. <!--#216cd359b1378c0f-->
- `_success_combined_read` (function) — Builds the merged success-chip body for a Read call (path, range, and lines read). <!--#8301d4b64ec2f5f6-->
- `_success_combined_bash` (function) — Builds the merged success-chip body for a Bash call (command plus output line count). <!--#7244951a7d393507-->
- `_success_combined_grep` (function) — Builds the merged success-chip body for a Grep call (pattern, path, and match count). <!--#2cf5893c148f574d-->
- `_success_combined_glob` (function) — Builds the merged success-chip body for a Glob call (pattern, path, and file count). <!--#a0ffe282c52331a7-->
- `_failure_use_body` (function) — Returns the use-side summary body for a chip with the tool-name prefix stripped off. <!--#42b4af467d9e996a-->
- `format_tool_chip_header` (function) — Builds the merged success (✓) or failure (✗) chip header combining input and result/error summaries for a settled tool call. <!--#0289b350323d1bb4-->
- `_parse_first_hunk_start` (function) — Parses the first hunk's old/new starting line numbers from unified-diff lines. <!--#9423216a302e5b77-->
- `_maybe_truncate_text` (function) — Tail-truncates text to a max character count, returning the text and a truncation flag. <!--#ec5a2a60e03451e2-->
- `_maybe_truncate_lines` (function) — Truncates a list of lines to a max item count, returning the list and a truncation flag. <!--#2fbed4dc3f10a384-->
- `_json_safe_value` (function) — Coerces a single tool-input value into something `json.dumps` can encode, falling back to `str(value)` so one bad value can't poison the whole detail record. <!--#ed15ba8193cc6fe6-->
- `_build_input_payload` (function) — Converts a tool's raw input dict into a JSON-safe payload with full (per-value tail-truncated) values, returning it alongside a flag saying whether anything was cut. <!--#eb6259cf3852760c-->
- `build_tool_in_flight_detail_payload` (function) — Produces the `kind="tool_input"` detail payload for a result-pending tool call so the web chip's panel can show the call's full arguments while it runs. <!--#ac42e33c8afdf72a-->
- `_build_file_path_only_detail` (function) — Constructs the `kind="file_path_only"` detail payload used when an upstream reports that a file changed but carries no file text, so the renderer can say so instead of fabricating a diff. <!--#8ea0ec821884b575-->
- `_build_edit_detail` (function) — Builds the structured `edit_diff` detail payload (unified diff, first-hunk start lines, truncation flag) for an Edit, falling back to a file-path-only payload when no text was reported. <!--#e7734e08adda7910-->
- `_build_write_detail` (function) — Builds the structured Write detail payload — `write_full` for a new file, `write_diff` against prior content, or file-path-only when `content` is absent. <!--#1af2895f502222be-->
- `_build_read_detail` (function) — Builds the read_text detail payload (file text and start line) for a Read call. <!--#0cd9954a4b3a9156-->
- `_build_bash_detail` (function) — Builds the bash_output detail payload (command, stdout, stderr) for a Bash call. <!--#92b7bb8c3d4fd9bf-->
- `_build_grep_detail` (function) — Builds the grep_matches detail payload (pattern, path, match lines) for a Grep call. <!--#f8f884afae6d79fa-->
- `_build_glob_detail` (function) — Builds the glob_matches detail payload (pattern, path, file list) for a Glob call. <!--#f5ce9cb5e0ed9cdc-->
- `_build_generic_text_detail` (function) — Fallback settled-detail builder for tools with no registered detail builder, emitting `kind="text"` with both the extracted result text and the call's own input. <!--#295ebeba859782ec-->
- `build_tool_detail_payload` (function) — Public entry point that dispatches to the per-tool detail builder (diff/write/read/bash/grep/glob shapes) to build the settled chip panel payload, falling back to the generic text detail on missing builder or builder error. <!--#ca2460de5949252b-->
- `format_tool_diff` (function) — Renders Edit/Write diffs (or a "Created" summary for new files) to the console, and is a no-op for other tools or when the upstream reported no file text. <!--#45d79228b44176d9-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/transitive_reduction.py` (python) — Performs transitive reduction on a task-group dependency DAG, returning a deep copy in which each redundant direct `depends_on` edge (one also reachable via a longer intermediate path, detected by a BFS helper) is removed while the input is left unmutated. <!--#e9031a4a3db90475|0f08cb4ec581ddce-->
- `transitive_reduce` (function) — Public function returning a deep copy of the input groups with each redundant direct dependency (one reachable via a longer path) removed from its `depends_on` list, leaving the originals untouched. <!--#41aca8aef443ed63-->
- `_has_long_path` (function) — Internal BFS helper that reports whether the adjacency graph has an indirect path of length ≥ 2 from source to target, ignoring the direct source→target edge. <!--#d3ec927b055eff6d-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/truncation.py` (python) — Central module of shared truncation-limit constants (phase stdout/stderr tails, test-history and archive-slimming limits, fix-instruction and failures-section caps, self_check task-groups/scope-diff budgets, and the web tool-detail payload cap) so all LLM-consumed content limits across step handlers stay consistent and tunable in one place. <!--#b105179070bdbff0|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/version_bumper.py` (python) — Version-management module providing a SemVer 2.0.0 `Version` value object (parse, compare, bump) plus pluggable format-specific version-file handlers (JSON/TOML/Python/setup.py) and a `VersionDetector` that identifies a project's type and locates, reads, and updates its version file. <!--#f10ee1578849d135|febbe367307b6b96-->
