- `ProjectType` (class) — Enum of supported project types (Python, Node.js, Unknown) used to drive version-file detection. <!--#2c6662747efb04b7-->
- `BumpType` (class) — Enum naming the three semantic-versioning bump kinds: major, minor, and patch. <!--#da8d688705155657-->
- `Version` (class) — Immutable SemVer 2.0.0 value object that parses, validates, stringifies, compares, and bumps version components. <!--#6343759176871ea6-->
  - `Version.parse` (method) — Classmethod that parses a SemVer string into a Version, raising ValueError on empty or malformed input. <!--#96dad270505dc81c-->
  - `Version.validate` (method) — Classmethod returning True if a string is a valid SemVer version (parse succeeds), else False. <!--#a520043f7f23f28d-->
  - `Version.__str__` (method) — Renders the Version back to its canonical MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-prerelease][+build] string form. <!--#ba5738e57d5afb3e-->
  - `Version.bump_major` (method) — Returns a new Version with major incremented and minor/patch reset to zero. <!--#f3339b07dd8dfb40-->
  - `Version.bump_minor` (method) — Returns a new Version with minor incremented and patch reset to zero. <!--#3d59389e3f5867ab-->
  - `Version.bump_patch` (method) — Returns a new Version with patch incremented. <!--#ddc46dd1a9d0bc33-->
  - `Version.with_prerelease` (method) — Returns a copy of the Version with the prerelease identifier replaced. <!--#6da00fb8dfe0907e-->
  - `Version.with_build` (method) — Returns a copy of the Version with the build metadata replaced. <!--#c78c75cdc85a37d8-->
  - `Version.bump` (method) — Dispatches to bump_major/minor/patch based on the given BumpType. <!--#1621340211520461-->
  - `Version.__eq__` (method) — Equality comparison against another Version (ignoring build metadata) or a 3-tuple of numbers. <!--#60b50cf04371f68a-->
  - `Version.__hash__` (method) — Hashes the Version on its numeric components and prerelease, excluding build metadata. <!--#0d62c0a2d0e94ec0-->
  - `Version.__lt__` (method) — Implements SemVer precedence ordering, including prerelease identifier comparison rules. <!--#08963aa698cc60d5-->
  - `Version.__le__` (method) — Less-than-or-equal comparison derived from __eq__ and __lt__. <!--#abc20a7cc2141ee0-->
  - `Version.__gt__` (method) — Greater-than comparison derived from __le__. <!--#00451315f65f92a1-->
  - `Version.__ge__` (method) — Greater-than-or-equal comparison derived from __lt__. <!--#24ebfdfd27ae87fc-->
- `VersionInfo` (class) — Dataclass bundling detected project type, version-file path, raw version string, and parsed Version. <!--#802e8ec3419df566-->
- `VersionFileHandler` (class) — Abstract base class defining the read/write/ensure/create interface for format-specific version file handlers. <!--#a07b8f65236b1ffc-->
  - `VersionFileHandler.can_handle` (method) — Abstract predicate indicating whether the handler supports a given file path/format. <!--#db58566b8a10520b-->
  - `VersionFileHandler.read_version` (method) — Abstract method to read and return the version string from a file. <!--#5035056e002230d5-->
  - `VersionFileHandler.write_version` (method) — Abstract method to write a new version string into the file. <!--#a475c00f546c0bb6-->
  - `VersionFileHandler.ensure_version` (method) — Optional hook (default unsupported) that idempotently inserts a version field if one is missing. <!--#c9a4431ce5153943-->
  - `VersionFileHandler.create_version_file` (method) — Optional hook (default unsupported) that creates a new version file with an initial version. <!--#6a4f7c21938ff82f-->
- `JsonVersionHandler` (class) — Version file handler for JSON files like package.json, reading/writing the top-level version field. <!--#ce928dc45bec4d5f-->
  - `JsonVersionHandler.can_handle` (method) — Returns True for .json files or files named package.json. <!--#2bf682d38aefb50b-->
  - `JsonVersionHandler.read_version` (method) — Loads the JSON and returns its version field, raising if absent. <!--#83346fccd78f5315-->
  - `JsonVersionHandler.write_version` (method) — Updates the JSON version field and rewrites the file with 2-space indentation. <!--#de1b95612151f94f-->
  - `JsonVersionHandler.create_version_file` (method) — Creates a minimal package.json with name/version/description fields, erroring if one already exists. <!--#a274cb9243bcc633-->
- `TomlVersionHandler` (class) — Version file handler for TOML files like pyproject.toml, supporting PEP 621 and Poetry version fields. <!--#6fe3d2c4bfecb0f0-->
  - `TomlVersionHandler.can_handle` (method) — Returns True for .toml files or files named pyproject.toml. <!--#cf5108c660cb6332-->
  - `TomlVersionHandler.read_version` (method) — Parses the TOML and returns project.version or tool.poetry.version, raising if neither is present. <!--#09f2a22b558ba011-->
  - `TomlVersionHandler.write_version` (method) — Regex-replaces the version string in the [project] or [tool.poetry] section while preserving formatting. <!--#1992edca58aa8de2-->
  - `TomlVersionHandler.ensure_version` (method) — Adds a version field under [project] (creating the section if needed) when none exists. <!--#ae9fafd9dd9ff935-->
  - `TomlVersionHandler.create_version_file` (method) — Creates a minimal PEP 621 pyproject.toml with build-system and project sections. <!--#5ecc875d7ab5fac3-->
- `PythonVersionHandler` (class) — Version file handler for .py files exposing __version__, version, or VERSION assignments. <!--#16a991b3b7e0ddb0-->
  - `PythonVersionHandler.can_handle` (method) — Returns True for any .py file. <!--#b096d66b4d0a6776-->
  - `PythonVersionHandler.read_version` (method) — Regex-extracts the version from __version__, version, or VERSION assignments. <!--#20c1d195b1aab75d-->
  - `PythonVersionHandler.write_version` (method) — Regex-replaces the version in __version__, version, or VERSION assignments. <!--#d549e76c5f9c361d-->
  - `PythonVersionHandler.ensure_version` (method) — Prepends a __version__ assignment to the file if no version is found. <!--#6dfb4e1ab685ea1d-->
  - `PythonVersionHandler.create_version_file` (method) — Creates a version.py with __version__ inside the detected package or src/ directory. <!--#ad58a4cb4acc90dd-->
- `SetupPyHandler` (class) — Version file handler for setup.py that reads/writes the version keyword of the setup() call via AST. <!--#b8ea17a61702ecba-->
  - `SetupPyHandler.can_handle` (method) — Returns True only for files named setup.py. <!--#faafe99ad3e31b2c-->
  - `SetupPyHandler.read_version` (method) — Walks the AST to locate the setup() call's version keyword and returns its constant value. <!--#a7cd71c89280a9c8-->
  - `SetupPyHandler._get_func_name` (method) — Helper extracting a callable's name from an AST Name or Attribute node. <!--#bec71767409a06e2-->
  - `SetupPyHandler.write_version` (method) — Locates the version argument via AST positions and replaces its string, falling back to regex for multi-line cases. <!--#a009ee54b96ba372-->
  - `SetupPyHandler.create_version_file` (method) — Creates a minimal setup.py invoking setuptools.setup() with name and version. <!--#f241b6ce5dd61c41-->
- `VersionDetector` (class) — Detects a project's type and locates/reads its version file by checking known markers and file locations in priority order. <!--#4fea9be4e65f2ddf-->
  - `VersionDetector.__init__` (method) — Initializes the detector with its ordered list of TOML/JSON/Python/setup.py handlers. <!--#48f8b1a48b142f73-->
  - `VersionDetector.detect_project_type` (method) — Classifies the project as Python, Node.js, or Unknown by checking characteristic marker files. <!--#d0ebb06157a824d2-->
  - `VersionDetector.detect_project_type_without_version_file` (method) — Classifies project type from language/framework markers and source structure when no version file exists yet. <!--#54ca047bc8b24a52-->
  - `VersionDetector.get_version_file_path` (method) — Returns the first known version-file location that both matches a handler and yields a readable version. <!--#3714d693e64ea4a4-->
  - `VersionDetector.read_version` (method) — Reads a version string from a path by delegating to the first capable handler. <!--#d4769f408e454856-->
  - `VersionDetector.detect` (method) — Main entry point that detects project type, finds the version file, and returns a populated VersionInfo. <!--#4a30496f59d5ac93-->
- `VersionConfig` (class) — Configuration dataclass controlling whether bumping is enabled, an explicit version-file path, and commit-message inclusion. <!--#014d4efef42053a3-->
  - `VersionConfig.validate` (method) — Returns a list of validation errors, e.g. when the configured version file path does not exist. <!--#9d8ace4382297af9-->
- `VersionBumper` (class) — High-level orchestrator that detects, reads, bumps, sets, and rolls back versions via file handlers or an optional version script. <!--#511ac50dd45ecfd1-->
  - `VersionBumper.__init__` (method) — Initializes the bumper with config, handler list, detector, backup state, and script-mode flags. <!--#987a05dfe1c3fdb4-->
  - `VersionBumper.register_handler` (method) — Appends a custom version file handler to the bumper's handler list. <!--#32122fd9d619e3d1-->
  - `VersionBumper.detect_version_file` (method) — Locates the version file, preferring a version script, then an explicit config path, then auto-detection. <!--#16c556251b1d2a5c-->
  - `VersionBumper._find_and_init_script` (method) — Searches for a version script and, if found, switches the bumper into script mode with a VersionScriptRunner. <!--#adc59518a3995bb0-->
  - `VersionBumper.initialize_version_system` (method) — Bootstraps versioning for a project by generating a version script or creating/updating an appropriate version file. <!--#f85719e10f4d362b-->
  - `VersionBumper._get_handler_for_new_file` (method) — Returns a handler capable of creating a new file with the given suffix. <!--#2ab4976ca4b6c6d7-->
  - `VersionBumper.detect_project_type` (method) — Delegates to the detector to classify the project's type. <!--#aec769c16a3c72d1-->
  - `VersionBumper._get_handler` (method) — Returns the first registered handler that can process the given file path, raising if none apply. <!--#c46fafc4e8a5aaa4-->
  - `VersionBumper.read_version` (method) — Reads the current version via the script runner in script mode, otherwise via the detected file's handler. <!--#fe3a2746035c133f-->
  - `VersionBumper.parse_version` (method) — Static convenience wrapper delegating to Version.parse. <!--#55545ad66a6934ff-->
  - `VersionBumper.validate_semver` (method) — Static convenience wrapper delegating to Version.validate. <!--#b4dfccabd4c8fb35-->
  - `VersionBumper.bump_version_string` (method) — Static helper that parses a version string, applies a bump, and returns the new string. <!--#5a9b2633882efb56-->
  - `VersionBumper.bump_version` (method) — Bumps the version in the file or script, capturing a backup for rollback and returning the new version. <!--#53f37d782d5be3e5-->
  - `VersionBumper.set_version` (method) — Validates and writes an explicit version directly (no bump computation), capturing a rollback backup. <!--#b2acecbc992d2fa9-->
  - `VersionBumper.save_original_version` (method) — Records the current version and its path as a backup for potential rollback. <!--#58bfbb0699c085d9-->
  - `VersionBumper.rollback` (method) — Restores the backed-up version via handler or script, then clears the backup state. <!--#059becaee9ad1190-->
  - `VersionBumper.clear_backup` (method) — Discards the saved backup so the last bump becomes permanent, typically after a successful commit. <!--#a854889561986177-->
  - `VersionBumper.atomic_bump` (method) — Context manager that applies a bump and yields the new version, auto-rolling back on exception and clearing the backup on success. <!--#8520e55a31d36db5-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/version_intent.py` (python) — Defines the VersionIntent dataclass and its git-committed read/write/idempotency helpers that let a worktree session emit a version-bump *intent* on its flow branch for the merge-side version_reconcile step to collect and consume once, including gitignore self-heal, atomic writes, and git-ref/merge-base introspection so branch-introduced intents are computed and never double-bumped. <!--#a872644ccc5eda44|9eaf1c7d59ff9ca3-->
- `intent_dir_relpath` (function) — Returns the runtime-directory-relative path string of the version-intents directory for a given project root. <!--#6b868670cd2f65f6-->
- `IntentReadError` (class) — A RuntimeError signalling that a git ref's version intents could not be read (infrastructure fault), kept distinct from a genuine 'no intents' so the merge CLI never treats a git failure as an empty version-bump scope. <!--#41470ddc83654816-->
- `VersionIntentIgnoredError` (class) — An OSError raised at intent write time when the intent path is gitignored, surfacing the .gitignore root cause early instead of as a misleading merge-side failure. <!--#aaee15b22aecb21c-->
- `VersionIntent` (class) — A serializable dataclass capturing a worktree session's version-bump intent (change summary, changelog bullets, optional SemVer hint and tag flag, baseline/provisional version, and consumption markers) that travels with the flow branch as committed JSON for the merge-side reconcile step. <!--#7aa5924d53c58943-->
  - `VersionIntent.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the VersionIntent into a plain JSON-safe dict via dataclasses.asdict. <!--#ce32cc6f66e77914-->
  - `VersionIntent.from_dict` (method) — Classmethod that rebuilds a VersionIntent from a dict, validating that a non-empty flow_id is present while tolerantly ignoring unknown keys and defaulting missing ones for forward/backward compatibility. <!--#5f4f1945e7766aae-->
- `_normalize_optional_str` (function) — Helper that coerces a value to a stripped string, mapping None and empty strings to None so absent and blank hints read identically. <!--#da1f215e25acc584-->
- `intent_path` (function) — Returns the committed `<runtime>/version-intents/<flow_id>.json` path for a flow, keying files by flow_id so merged branches' intents coexist. <!--#55e104fb2ef8ae21-->
- `write_intent` (function) — Atomically persists a VersionIntent to its committed path (creating the dir), first asserting the path is not gitignored, and returns the path. <!--#46fc134e96f110e9-->
- `_gitignore_heal_rules` (function) — Computes the root-aware .gitignore rule strings (whitelist line, contents anchor, whole-dir re-include, whole-dir rule set) used by the self-heal logic. <!--#db9cc46404bdb4e6-->
- `_probe_ignored` (function) — Best-effort helper that returns True only when `git check-ignore` definitively reports a relative path as ignored (exit 0), treating a missing git, non-repo, timeout, or probe fault as not-ignored so it never blocks the write. <!--#1e959cc286e98fa7-->
- `_probe_not_ignored_definitive` (function) — Stricter post-heal re-verification helper that returns True only on `git check-ignore` exit 1 (a positive not-ignored verdict), treating any fault, timeout, or exit 128 as unproven (False) so only a proven-clear path may release the write. <!--#3bf1680ed51deafb-->
- `_heal_gitignore_for_intents` (function) — Idempotently rewrites the project's `.gitignore` so the version-intents whitelist genuinely takes effect across legacy anchor/whole-dir-ignore shapes, returning whether it changed the file. <!--#d09e81c28e12e19e-->
- `_restore_gitignore` (function) — Best-effort rollback that reverts `.gitignore` to its pre-heal bytes (or deletes a heal-created file), swallowing OSError. <!--#213e0b8edfca369d-->
- `_assert_intent_path_not_ignored` (function) — Probes whether the intent path is gitignored and, if so, self-heals `.gitignore`, re-probes, and either allows the write or rolls back and raises VersionIntentIgnoredError. <!--#32a272df7459af7f-->
- `read_intent` (function) — Reads a flow's intent from the working tree by path, returning None if absent. <!--#a4ea9ca56ca36de0-->
- `read_intent_file` (function) — Parses a single intent file, returning None (with a warning) on missing, corrupt, or invalid content so one damaged intent doesn't abort collecting the rest. <!--#6238dde42b5c20bc-->
- `collect_intents` (function) — Scans the working-tree version-intents directory and returns all VersionIntent objects (optionally including consumed ones), sorted deterministically by flow_id. <!--#6d772c3b6804ed6c-->
- `intent_flow_ids_at_ref` (function) — Reads the committed tree at a git ref (canonical and legacy relpaths) via `git ls-tree` to return the set of intent flow_ids present there, raising IntentReadError on git infrastructure faults rather than degrading to empty. <!--#8ff22ed30b924b34-->
- `_merge_base` (function) — Returns the merge-base sha of two refs, None when there is no common ancestor, and raises IntentReadError on a git infrastructure fault. <!--#314c8d98b3a586fc-->
- `_is_ancestor` (function) — Returns whether ref_a is an ancestor of ref_b via `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, raising IntentReadError on any non-0/1 exit or subprocess fault. <!--#739718bf0dd269ac-->
- `intent_flow_ids_introduced` (function) — Computes the intent flow_ids a branch actually contributes to a merge (its own intents minus those inherited at the fork point), with a rerun-recovery carve-out that reconstructs the pre-integration baseline from the --no-ff merge commit. <!--#c13307aeb46f1e8a-->
- `_integration_baseline_ids` (function) — Rerun-recovery helper that reconstructs the intents a branch inherited by locating its --no-ff integration merge, finding the fork point against the merge's other parent(s), and returning those baseline flow_ids (or None if no merge is found). <!--#e87894c73356e464-->
- `mark_consumed` (function) — Idempotently rewrites a flow's on-disk intent with consumed=True (and the reconcile commit sha), returning whether a marking write actually occurred. <!--#7acec8900631ac4f-->
- `is_consumed` (function) — Reports whether a flow's intent has been reconciled, defaulting to the git-durable reconcile-commit signal (with a test-only flag-based opt-out) rather than the bare on-disk consumed flag. <!--#10a211365c643f51-->
- `reconcile_commit_exists` (function) — Authoritative idempotency check that searches commits under a ref for the exact `Version-Reconcile-Session: <flow_id>` trailer line, retrying once and raising IntentReadError on persistent probe faults so it never falsely reports absent. <!--#915e68152c18da13-->
- `_atomic_write_text` (function) — Writes text to a path atomically via a temp file plus os.replace, refusing to overwrite a destination symlink to prevent redirect-onto-tracked-file attacks. <!--#fa39f8a5ed909e57-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/version_script_interface.py` (python) — Module providing a subprocess-based version-script interface for SE3, exposing a VersionScriptRunner that delegates get/bump/set version operations to a project's version script, plus helpers to locate, validate, and LLM-generate that script from the project structure. <!--#d913e3d061d7b8a6|c410e6e037c8df3a-->
- `VersionScriptRunner` (class) — Class that runs a version script's get/bump/set subcommands via subprocess and returns parsed Version objects. <!--#98b4f61a5c96e0ff-->
  - `VersionScriptRunner.__init__` (method) — Initializes the runner with a script path and project root (used as cwd), raising FileNotFoundError if the script is missing. <!--#0928b5697a4b7343-->
  - `VersionScriptRunner._run_script` (method) — Invokes the version script (via python/bash/direct) with given args and a timeout, returning stripped stdout or raising RuntimeError on failure. <!--#dea2c93f7c197c77-->
  - `VersionScriptRunner.get_version` (method) — Calls the script's 'get' command and returns the parsed current Version. <!--#f9aaac75f0d15371-->
  - `VersionScriptRunner.bump_version` (method) — Calls the script's 'bump' command with the given bump type and returns the new Version. <!--#f094221c393e8096-->
  - `VersionScriptRunner.set_version` (method) — Calls the script's 'set' command to explicitly set a version string and returns the resulting Version. <!--#2e00806c0b7fe690-->
- `find_version_script` (function) — Locates the project's version script by checking a configured script_path first (resolving relative paths against project_root) and otherwise falling back to the DEFAULT_SCRIPT_PATHS, returning the found Path or None. <!--#cccc6318fc282506-->
- `validate_script` (function) — Validates a version script by running its 'get' command, returning a (is_valid, error_message) tuple. <!--#98058fd72961d58c-->
- `generate_version_script` (function) — Generates a version script by scanning the project structure, prompting an LLMCaller to write the file directly to disk (default tianluo/scripts/version.py), then validating, marking it executable, and running validate_script, raising RuntimeError on failure. <!--#e2814e43a210d186-->
- `_validate_generated_script` (function) — Checks that the LLM-written script exists, is non-empty, has valid Python syntax, and contains a read_version() function. <!--#16d30943aaff6188-->
- `_scan_project_for_generation` (function) — Scans the project to detect its type, candidate version files, and current version to inform script generation. <!--#de357e474966dba1-->
- `_load_template` (function) — Loads the bundled version script template from the templates directory, or a placeholder if absent. <!--#4965c6c93641fa49-->
- `_build_generation_prompt` (function) — Constructs the LLM prompt instructing it to write a version script to the target path based on project info and the template. <!--#3a98ca7c38f412ef-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/workspace_snapshot.py` (python) — Utility module that captures point-in-time, git-based snapshots of a project's uncommitted working-tree state (WorkspaceSnapshot) and diffs two of them into a WorkspaceDelta describing exactly which tracked/untracked paths changed and how to undo them, degrading gracefully to an 'undecidable' verdict whenever git is unavailable or its output cannot be parsed. <!--#0a887585e849d22d|6ff31753fb7b54f0-->
- `WorkspaceSnapshot` (class) — Serializable dataclass capturing a point-in-time view of a working tree's uncommitted state (aggregate and per-path tracked diff hashes, untracked file hashes, HEAD commit) plus availability flags so an unreadable git repo degrades to 'undecidable' instead of a false verdict. <!--#62b9a2cd746aa0a0-->
  - `WorkspaceSnapshot.to_dict` (method) — Serializes the snapshot to a plain dict so a pre-step baseline can be persisted in a step's inputs and survive retries. <!--#8e5a7f60be861b5b-->
  - `WorkspaceSnapshot.from_dict` (method) — Classmethod that rebuilds a snapshot from its serialized form, returning None on malformed data so callers fall back to a fresh capture rather than crashing. <!--#c8be8d68721aee94-->
- `WorkspaceDelta` (class) — Dataclass describing what changed between two snapshots — tracked/untracked added, removed and modified paths, HEAD movement, and an undecidable flag — with helpers to list affected paths, test cleanliness, and render an LLM-facing revert instruction. <!--#d364d38b3cd6c60b-->
  - `WorkspaceDelta.tracked_paths` (method) — Property returning the deduplicated, sorted union of all tracked paths the delta can name. <!--#fba7a09ee67e7c20-->
  - `WorkspaceDelta.changed_paths` (method) — Property returning every path the delta can name, tracked and untracked, deduplicated and sorted. <!--#b28e632fed2b28fe-->
  - `WorkspaceDelta.is_clean` (method) — Property reporting whether the two snapshots are indistinguishable, deliberately also returning True when the comparison was undecidable. <!--#736044c37f66fd2c-->
  - `WorkspaceDelta.describe` (method) — Renders the delta as human/LLM-readable text explaining what changed and what must be undone, without prescribing any (potentially destructive) git command. <!--#abf82c872ee382c2-->
- `_run_git` (function) — Helper that runs a read-only git subcommand in the project root and returns stdout bytes, or None when git is missing or the command fails, centralizing the degradation path. <!--#2dbdc47b8a57f44a-->
- `_runtime_pathspec` (function) — Builds the git pathspec that scopes every query to the project while excluding the (per-project resolved) runtime directory, keeping the mandatory positive '.' so exclusions don't match nothing. <!--#4831640407674a6f-->
- `_split_diff_per_file` (function) — Splits raw `git diff` output into one normalized chunk per `diff --git` header so each file's changes can be hashed independently. <!--#d61c8b186468dcaa-->
- `_tracked_diff_hashes` (function) — Aligns diff chunks with `--name-only -z` paths to map each dirty tracked path to a hash of its own chunk, returning None when alignment fails so only the aggregate hash is trusted. <!--#263d6c10b98d98fa-->
- `_file_content_hash` (function) — Returns the SHA-256 of a file's bytes, or the sentinel 'unreadable' when the file cannot be read. <!--#587a50b7120e7de5-->
- `snapshot_workspace` (function) — Captures a WorkspaceSnapshot for a project root by running read-only git queries (rev-parse HEAD, diff HEAD, ls-files --others) under a common pathspec, never raising and marking the snapshot unavailable when git cannot be consulted. <!--#37d0b685a4abba2a-->
- `compare_snapshots` (function) — Diffs a before/after snapshot pair into a WorkspaceDelta, reporting only changes introduced between the two captures (pre-existing dirt cancels out), comparing HEAD separately, and degrading to undecidable if either snapshot was unavailable. <!--#1cf6a2643d25d0a9-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/worktree.py` (python) — Git worktree lifecycle utilities for the engine — creating, forking, and resiliently force-removing per-branch worktrees under `<runtime>/worktrees/` (including seeding web-UI uploads into them), plus branch/commit inspection helpers and merge-conflict detection, stale-unmerged recovery, and LLM-assisted conflict resolution, exposed both as functions and a `WorktreeContext` context manager. <!--#0dd62050886e5cc2|1fc6b478d4af82f4-->
- `_run_git` (function) — Internal helper that runs a git subcommand in a given project root via subprocess, with configurable error-checking and timeout. <!--#fde166d981df8704-->
- `has_commits` (function) — Returns whether the repository has at least one commit by checking if HEAD resolves. <!--#eedc238ff332a101-->
- `get_current_branch` (function) — Resolves the current branch name, working on both populated and empty repos via symbolic-ref with a rev-parse fallback. <!--#2e6f604688447f87-->
- `_branch_safe_name` (function) — Converts a branch name into a filesystem-safe directory name by replacing slashes with hyphens. <!--#cc8e98cb43f0ac71-->
- `seed_uploads` (function) — Materializes a project's web-UI upload attachments into a newly created worktree by hard-linking (falling back to copy) each stored file into the transplanted `<runtime>/uploads/` path, returning the count seeded and logging rather than raising on failure. <!--#4b09a7f8683abe48-->
- `create_worktree` (function) — Creates a git worktree for the given branch under `<runtime>/worktrees/<safe-name>`, pruning stale entries and retrying with doubled timeouts on `TimeoutExpired`, then seeds uploads into it and returns its path. <!--#9a1cf0ac2829da9c-->
- `fork_worktree` (function) — Creates a new branch from a source branch and sets up a worktree for it (used by the relay strategy). <!--#f48d9ef83b40d95d-->
- `remove_worktree` (function) — Removes a git worktree resiliently, handling already-deleted directories, locked worktrees (double-force), and stale metadata via pruning. <!--#1829e020bd67d3d9-->
- `_force_remove_if_still_registered` (function) — Force-removes a worktree entry when git still tracks it after pruning, by inspecting porcelain worktree-list output. <!--#89eb514629084d02-->
- `_cleanup_git_worktree_metadata` (function) — Last-resort helper that directly deletes the internal .git/worktrees/<safe_name> metadata directory. <!--#5b0e5d350a7da2a3-->
- `force_cleanup_worktree` (function) — Forcefully and fault-tolerantly tears down a branch's worktree through independent steps (unlock, force-remove, rmtree, prune, .git metadata cleanup, and verification), used for resume scenarios where the worktree may be locked or inconsistent. <!--#fed3390d2a4524d4-->
- `delete_branch` (function) — Deletes a local branch, first force-cleaning any worktree still registered for it. <!--#eef8cbd9d7138774-->
- `has_new_commits` (function) — Returns whether a branch has any commits ahead of a given base branch. <!--#f4edc123aabe5a25-->
- `exists_for_branch` (function) — Returns whether a worktree is already registered for a given branch by parsing porcelain worktree-list output. <!--#74103a50bb9fc065-->
- `get_conflicting_files` (function) — Returns the list of files with merge conflicts via a worktree-vs-index unmerged diff. <!--#3f1832ae28ca0082-->
- `detect_unmerged_paths` (function) — Returns deduped paths in unmerged-index state by reading the index directly (catching modify/delete cases that get_conflicting_files misses). <!--#e556cc1055c95525-->
- `merge_in_progress` (function) — Returns whether a real git merge/cherry-pick/rebase/revert is mid-flight by checking for marker files in the resolved git directory. <!--#9ced3782cc2dca53-->
- `recover_stale_unmerged_paths` (function) — Auto-resolves stale unmerged-index entries left by a prior failure when safe (working tree matches HEAD), returning resolved and human-needing-attention path lists. <!--#50f627f74a09fbdd-->
- `get_diff_stat` (function) — Returns the `git diff --stat` summary string between a branch and a base branch. <!--#d14c134710526000-->
- `resolve_merge_conflicts_with_context` (function) — Resolves git merge conflicts by sending each conflicted file's marker-laden content to an LLM along with the task description and per-group summaries, retrying up to max_retries and writing/staging/committing only marker-free results (never falling back to --theirs). <!--#b42b904141ae15a9-->
- `WorktreeContext` (class) — Context manager providing exception-safe worktree lifecycle—creating one on enter and removing it (but preserving the branch) on exit. <!--#bd0659262faa940f-->
  - `WorktreeContext.__init__` (method) — Initializes the context manager with project root, branch, and an empty worktree-path slot. <!--#bc42ff0de12cc5de-->
  - `WorktreeContext.__enter__` (method) — Validates no existing worktree for the branch, creates one, and returns its path. <!--#a4162b03623770c5-->
  - `WorktreeContext.__exit__` (method) — Removes the created worktree on exit (including on exceptions), logging the cleanup. <!--#0c7666626a47f293-->

## `src/tianluo/engine/formatters/` — Engine subpackage providing output formatters for flow-engine data structures, currently centered on task formatting — it re-exports the public API (TaskFormatter, TaskDataValidator, TaskValidationError, format_task_groups) from task_formatter, which validates/normalizes plan_tasks output (dependency and cycle checks) and renders task groups into Rich tree, table, detail, summary, dependency-map, and implementation-plan views with topological execution waves, DAG topology, complexity, and LOC statistics. <!--#764b50fd86880c3e|213bb63c349ab8d7-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/formatters/__init__.py` (python) — Package init for SE3 engine output formatters that re-exports the task formatting public API (TaskFormatter, TaskDataValidator, TaskValidationError, and format_task_groups) from the task_formatter module. <!--#22f9c3569771702b|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/formatters/task_formatter.py` (python) — Rich-based presentation layer for task plans: validates and normalizes task/task-group data (required fields, unique IDs, resolvable dependencies, cycle-free graphs) via TaskDataValidator, then renders tree, table, detail, summary, dependency-map, and implement-step plan views — including strategy banner, DAG topology waves, and LOC statistics — with graceful fallbacks for coarse capability groups that carry no per-task breakdown. <!--#7eb2f803b5299afd|1909b404b5fb0339-->
- `_md_heading` (function) — Helper that builds a reverse-color block heading Text via _reverse_title. <!--#f1f52807a66af571-->
- `_heading_group` (function) — Helper that wraps body renderables with a reverse-color heading and matching footer into a Rich Group. <!--#9d666073ce164827-->
- `TaskValidationError` (class) — Exception type raised when task-data validation fails. <!--#868e99ba0adf3b5e-->
- `_group_has_tasks` (function) — Predicate returning True only when a task group carries a non-empty per-task list, so callers can treat a coarse capability group's absent `tasks` as a legitimate shape rather than missing data. <!--#f80b529f4e41e601-->
- `_any_group_has_tasks` (function) — Predicate returning True when at least one group in a task-group list carries a per-task breakdown, used to switch presentation between fine-grained and capability-group plans. <!--#a905298202fd1b3b-->
- `TaskDataValidator` (class) — Validator class that checks and normalizes task and task-group structures before formatting, enforcing required fields, unique IDs, valid dependency references, and cycle-free dependency graphs while tolerating task-less capability groups. <!--#ce99d840a31a2a44-->
  - `TaskDataValidator.validate_groups` (method) — Validates and normalizes a task-group list under either decomposition doctrine, requiring `group_id` and uniqueness, allowing an absent/empty `tasks` array, and delegating inter-group dependency and cycle checks. <!--#f7e91a8ef0df7921-->
  - `TaskDataValidator._validate_group_dependencies` (method) — Verifies that every inter-group `depends_on` reference resolves to a known group and raises on circular dependencies via a three-color DFS that reports the offending cycle path. <!--#d8557ef69ad30661-->
  - `TaskDataValidator.validate` (method) — Validates a full task list, normalizing each task, rejecting duplicate IDs, and checking dependencies. <!--#2f2a9aad43fa2dc0-->
  - `TaskDataValidator._validate_task` (method) — Validates one task dict, enforcing required fields and filling optional fields with defaults. <!--#e9a09cff2880eb69-->
  - `TaskDataValidator._validate_dependencies` (method) — Checks that dependency/depends_on fields are lists of known task IDs and triggers cycle detection. <!--#ab8aa6e10809309e-->
  - `TaskDataValidator._check_circular_dependencies` (method) — Detects circular dependencies among tasks via a three-color DFS over the dependency graph. <!--#849b5c958fd28e7d-->
- `TaskFormatter` (class) — Renders task-plan data into Rich output — tree, table, summary, dependency map, and implement-step plan views — with complexity color/icon styling and dedicated fallbacks for coarse capability groups. <!--#e4f4c41ff153d746-->
  - `TaskFormatter.__init__` (method) — Initializes the formatter with a Rich console and a TaskDataValidator instance. <!--#d4734cdcc8d08064-->
  - `TaskFormatter.format_tasks` (method) — Dispatches task-group formatting to tree or table view based on the requested mode. <!--#f39588af93915899-->
  - `TaskFormatter._format_tree_view` (method) — Renders task groups as a hierarchical Rich `Tree` with group dependencies, per-task complexity badges, files, and criteria counts, plus a trailing totals summary that degrades to a group count when no tasks exist. <!--#efc39e44f2c78905-->
  - `TaskFormatter._format_table_view` (method) — Renders task groups as a flat Rich `Table` of tasks, emitting one group-level row per task-less capability group so a valid plan never produces an empty table. <!--#25bed8184241c336-->
  - `TaskFormatter.format_task_detail` (method) — Renders a detailed single-task view as a key/value table under a per-task heading with complexity icon. <!--#18fe44ea3fef9117-->
  - `TaskFormatter.format_summary` (method) — Builds a Rich statistics table of group/task counts, complexity mix, dependency and criteria totals, and an effort estimate, falling back to a group-level breakdown when no group carries tasks. <!--#468cd044202cfada-->
  - `TaskFormatter._calculate_avg_complexity` (method) — Computes the weighted average complexity score across tasks (small=1, medium=2, large=3). <!--#2ac50f195b62aa79-->
  - `TaskFormatter._estimate_effort` (method) — Derives a human-readable effort estimate (hours/days/weeks) from task count and average complexity. <!--#732f9190234d3afd-->
  - `TaskFormatter.format_implement_plan` (method) — Assembles the implement-step `## Implementation Plan` renderable: strategy summary line, task tree, optional DAG topology diagram for parallel relay plans, and LOC statistics when per-task estimates exist. <!--#45efa82033ea2d56-->
  - `TaskFormatter._format_strategy_line` (method) — Builds the one-line execution-strategy banner with a per-strategy icon and description, appending the sequential fallback reason and suppressing LOC-threshold wording when the plan carries no per-task estimates. <!--#10d3900809674c90-->
  - `TaskFormatter._build_implement_tree` (method) — Builds the implement-plan Rich `Tree` of task groups with dependency lines and per-task complexity, LOC estimate, and file annotations, showing a group's description instead of a task count for capability groups. <!--#b4fda5ce2206b293-->
  - `TaskFormatter._compute_topo_waves` (method) — Computes topological execution waves of parallelizable groups via Kahn's algorithm, ordered by group_order. <!--#60000bbf915c98d5-->
  - `TaskFormatter._build_dag_topology` (method) — Builds a layered DAG topology diagram showing waves, LLM call numbering, and relay/fork/merge annotations from a RelayPlan. <!--#85583c02477a7016-->
  - `TaskFormatter._format_loc_summary` (method) — Builds the total and per-group LOC statistics line for the implement plan. <!--#90bd438f64d33add-->
  - `TaskFormatter.format_dependencies` (method) — Renders the task-level dependency map as a Rich table of each task's dependencies and dependents, delegating to the group-level view when the plan contains only coarse capability groups. <!--#c845dffb6a465120-->
  - `TaskFormatter._format_group_dependencies` (method) — Renders the inter-group dependency map for coarse capability groups as a Rich table of each group's `depends_on` edges and reverse dependents. <!--#214cb0eb81869b3c-->
- `format_task_groups` (function) — Module-level convenience function combining task, summary, and dependency sections into a single renderable view. <!--#1a59b24466bca805-->

## `src/tianluo/engine/merge/` — The SE3 merge engine package implementing `luo merge`: it sequentially merges branches via an orchestrator that builds three-way conflict context, resolves conflicts deterministically or through an LLM resolver gated by a safe/strict/fast strategy decider (escalating to human-review call files when needed), then syncs git-ignored runtime state and renumbers colliding issue IDs, reconciles/aggregates SemVer version bumps, and finally cleans up merged branches and garbage-collects leaked isolation worktrees. <!--#aa944df6141d9b6f|e6de009d9d6cfe27-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/merge/__init__.py` (python) — Public API surface of the SE3 merge engine, re-exporting the sequential branch-merge machinery — conflict context building and LLM-based resolution, merge orchestration, strategy decisions, issue renumbering, runtime/issue sync, version reconciliation and aggregation, human-call escalation, and worktree cleanup/GC. <!--#199ab3da1a202546|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/merge/cleanup.py` (python) — Post-merge branch/worktree cleanup module: it resolves protected branches, parses `git worktree list --porcelain`, archives a worktree's WIP and promotes its terminal engine.json (plus hot/cold partitions) into the main archive, and only then deletes merged branches and their worktrees, failing closed on any uncertainty and recording every action or skip in a `CleanupReport`. <!--#f1fe5c990544240d|e92ca2ef915b4c3c-->
- `_read_init_default_branch` (function) — Reads git's `init.defaultBranch` config value (or None) so a repo's custom integration branch can be auto-added to the protected set. <!--#c6d785bb210037c8-->
- `_load_protected_branches` (function) — Computes the effective set of branches that must never be deleted, unioning the hardcoded main/master baseline with git's init.defaultBranch and any merge.protected_branches from tianluo.yaml, falling back to the baseline on any config-load error. <!--#e6b34f36460d189f-->
- `_build_locale_env` (function) — Returns a copy of the environment with `LC_ALL`/`LANG` pinned to C (and `LANGUAGE` cleared) so git stderr stays English for reliable keyword matching (J2). <!--#695fbdcf800c9c55-->
- `_run_git_locale` (function) — Wrapper that runs a git command against a project root in the locale-pinned C environment with captured output and DEVNULL stdin (J2). <!--#fa3542eba6c79592-->
- `CleanupReport` (class) — Dataclass tallying the outcome of a branch-cleanup run, listing branches that were deleted, archived, or had their completed state promoted, plus the various skip categories (dirty, protected, not-merged, unknown-state, worktree-remove-failed, archive-failed). <!--#bc95073b61324e79-->
- `_WorktreeRecord` (class) — Dataclass holding one parsed `git worktree list --porcelain` entry (path, head, branch, detached/bare flags, and a non-local-ref flag for J7). <!--#28d19ef401ec29c8-->
- `_parse_worktree_porcelain` (function) — Parses `git worktree list --porcelain` output block-by-block into validated `_WorktreeRecord`s, logging and dropping malformed blocks instead of silently skipping them (J1, J7). <!--#9922630aafe049fa-->
- `_get_worktree_path_for_branch` (function) — Returns the filesystem path of the local-branch worktree bound to a given branch (or None), skipping non-local-ref records (J7). <!--#2906c7bf2f8b62fe-->
- `_archive_ignore` (function) — Builds the path-aware `copytree` ignore callable that always drops `.git` plus any caller-supplied worktree-relative paths (rejecting absolute/escaping entries), so an exclusion targets one exact location rather than every same-named directory. <!--#c826399556d027b1-->
- `_archive_worktree` (function) — Copies a worktree (including untracked/gitignored operator WIP, minus `.git` and excluded paths) into a timestamped `tianluo/worktrees/.archive/<slug>-<ts>/` directory and writes a `.se3-archive-meta.json` recovery pointer, so failure to archive can block the destructive branch/worktree deletion step. <!--#6439d7ab787db7b8-->
- `_promote_completed_engine_state` (function) — Copies a worktree flow's terminal engine.json (COMPLETED-only by default, any status when force=True) into the main project's state/archive/ before the worktree is deleted, so the daemon/webui still shows the flow's completed lifecycle rather than dropping it straight into history. <!--#8946f6d152d8ffd4-->
- `_is_hotcold_header` (function) — Predicate returning True when engine.json data is a new-format hot/cold-split header, detected by its format key beginning with 'hotcold/'. <!--#a0c233c1502caf71-->
- `_promote_cold_partition` (function) — Copies a new-format (hot/cold split) flow's per-step cold data partition from the worktree into the main archive's steps/ dir (with collision-suffixing that also restamps the header), returning False on failure so the caller fails closed and never publishes a header whose cold_ref entries point at missing files. <!--#05e00defd38784e9-->
- `_is_worktree_clean` (function) — Returns whether a worktree has no uncommitted or untracked changes (treating a missing dir as clean and an unreadable one as dirty) so `git worktree remove` can run without `--force`. <!--#13fcb50dbcbbb210-->
- `_is_branch_ancestor_of_head` (function) — Returns True/False/None for whether a branch is an ancestor of HEAD via `merge-base --is-ancestor`, with None meaning undecidable and treated by callers as do-not-delete (J4). <!--#b716a8e760161657-->
- `CleanupManager` (class) — Manager class that safely deletes merged branches and their bound worktrees after a successful merge, failing closed when the current branch can't be determined and skipping protected/current/unmerged branches before any destructive operation. <!--#f2fe1e0c341600cd-->
  - `CleanupManager.__init__` (method) — Stores the project root and initializes the `_current_report` field that exposes in-progress cleanup state to callers' exception handlers. <!--#80bf35838fa3650d-->
  - `CleanupManager.delete_merged_branches` (method) — Per-branch cleanup loop that skips protected/current branches, verifies each branch is an ancestor of HEAD, checks any bound worktree is clean, then archives+removes the worktree and runs git branch -d, recording each result in a CleanupReport also exposed via self._current_report for partial-failure recovery. <!--#72780861a516ba60-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/merge/conflict_context.py` (python) — Read-only builder that assembles a complete three-way merge conflict picture for the LLM resolver — resolving branch SHAs, merge base, commit messages and oneline logs, and for each conflicting path collecting its base/ours/theirs/working versions with binary detection (.gitattributes patterns plus magic-byte sniffing), BOM-aware lossy decoding, and parsed `<<<<<<<`...`>>>>>>>` hunk ranges into ConflictContext/ConflictFile dataclasses. <!--#1a5f1aa6f5495729|936f8562ee91ad2d-->
- `ShaResolutionError` (class) — Exception raised when a git ref cannot be resolved to a commit SHA, so the merge halts visibly instead of silently continuing with an empty SHA. <!--#14181aca2a4ac79d-->
- `ConflictHunk` (class) — Dataclass holding the 1-based start/end line range of a single `<<<<<<<`...`>>>>>>>` conflict block. <!--#bd6d9147dc8b0d55-->
- `ConflictFile` (class) — Dataclass holding everything known about one conflicting file in a merge — its path, the base/ours/theirs/working versions and their existence flags, parsed conflict hunks, plus binary and lossy-decoding markers. <!--#7561239d5046c1d7-->
- `ConflictContext` (class) — Dataclass capturing the full three-way merge picture handed to the LLM resolver: repo root, both branch names, merge base and head SHAs/messages, each side's oneline log, and the list of ConflictFile entries. <!--#89410bf35ad02be7-->
- `_git_show_bytes` (function) — Runs `git show <ref>` (including `:N:<path>` index stages) and returns the raw bytes plus an existence flag, handling timeouts and errors gracefully. <!--#46008387dee37aaf-->
- `_decode_text` (function) — Decodes bytes to text by detecting UTF-32/16/8 BOMs and falling back to lossy UTF-8 replacement, returning the text, encoding name, and a lossy flag. <!--#bc0a2e7c3743390d-->
- `_decode_lossy` (function) — Backwards-compatible wrapper around `_decode_text` that returns only the decoded text for external callers. <!--#b45b47dcee7b2866-->
- `_looks_binary` (function) — Heuristic that classifies bytes as binary by matching known magic-byte signatures (at offset 0 and within the first 512 bytes) or detecting NUL bytes. <!--#a9ab25300ea6b325-->
- `_read_gitattributes_binary_paths` (function) — Parses the project's `.gitattributes` to return glob patterns explicitly marked binary (`binary`/`-text`/`-diff`). <!--#ee82061393628243-->
- `_path_matches_binary_pattern` (function) — Returns whether a relative path matches any of the given binary glob patterns, testing both the full path and the bare basename. <!--#ae169f13c2436b9c-->
- `_parse_hunks` (function) — Scans conflict-marker text to find `<<<<<<<`...`>>>>>>>` blocks and return their line ranges, tolerating diff3 markers and unmatched starts. <!--#b2f42f8ef9ca0ce8-->
- `_read_working_tree` (function) — Reads the working-tree version of a file as bytes, returning an existence flag and handling missing/unreadable files. <!--#a833da06d43a858d-->
- `_resolve_sha` (function) — Resolves a ref to a full commit SHA via `git rev-parse`, raising `ShaResolutionError` on any failure or empty result. <!--#ca2413026b4efe5f-->
- `_commit_message` (function) — Returns the full commit message (subject + body) for a ref, or an empty string on failure. <!--#e964eb7f6f75ff78-->
- `_merge_base` (function) — Returns the merge-base commit SHA between two refs, raising `ValueError` on empty input arguments. <!--#14f71f9b25b208c8-->
- `_oneline_log` (function) — Returns the `git log <base>..<head> --oneline` commits (up to a limit) as a list of strings. <!--#19cd724550e13c5d-->
- `_build_conflict_file` (function) — Internal helper that gathers one conflicting path's stage-1/2/3 blobs and working-tree bytes, classifies it as binary (via .gitattributes patterns or byte sniffing), otherwise decodes each version while recording the encoding and any lossiness, and parses conflict hunks into a ConflictFile. <!--#4c1c62aec5e54d1e-->
- `build` (function) — Public entry point that, while git is mid-merge, read-only assembles a ConflictContext by resolving both sides' SHAs and merge base, collecting commit messages and oneline logs, and building a ConflictFile for every conflicting path. <!--#9065fe20ebe5ec2b-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/merge/conflict_resolver.py` (python) — Defines the ConflictResolver and its supporting dataclasses/enums (MergeStrategy, HunkResolution, FileResolution, LLMResolution, BatchResolveOutcome) plus conflict-marker detection helpers, resolving merge conflicts by iteratively prompting an LLM to edit working-tree files in place and rescanning for residual markers until resolved or a max-iterations cap forces escalation. <!--#1ddd571ac82fba95|2b9ebe4a720c4c46-->
- `_normalize_unicode_whitespace_for_marker_detection` (function) — Helper that maps a set of Unicode whitespace prefix characters (NBSP, zero-width, BOM, etc.) to ASCII spaces for marker detection only, so disguised conflict markers can't evade the regexes. <!--#b53f346f2ca1d839-->
- `_has_conflict_markers` (function) — Returns whether a text blob still contains git conflict markers, tolerating up to 7 leading spaces/tabs and normalized Unicode whitespace, and also catching a stray ======= divider. <!--#917d39cfa8592ae6-->
- `_has_any_conflict_marker` (function) — Reads the file at a path and reports whether it still has conflict markers, treating a missing file as resolved and a read error as unresolved. <!--#ff273679e9eaf157-->
- `_scan_unresolved` (function) — Filters a list of paths down to those whose files still contain conflict markers, preserving input order. <!--#4914e931eee5f132-->
- `_load_max_conflict_resolve_iterations` (function) — Reads the configured max conflict-resolution iteration count from project config, falling back to 10 on any error. <!--#71204d72e0685063-->
- `_preview` (function) — Trims a string to a short truncated preview (with a remaining-char suffix) for storing on outcome records. <!--#a08e37d395298bcd-->
- `HunkValidationError` (class) — Exception raised when a HunkResolution payload (e.g. line numbers) is malformed. <!--#fdd34bd771c38197-->
- `ResolvedContentTooLargeError` (class) — Exception raised when an LLM resolution's content exceeds the configured size cap. <!--#d03720d1f58c1128-->
- `Confidence` (class) — String enum of resolution confidence levels (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW). <!--#dc02a14650d6e871-->
- `MergeStrategy` (class) — A string enum defining the three merge conflict-resolution tiers — `fast` (LLM-only, aborts on failure), `safe` (LLM with human-MCP fallback), and `strict` (always human) — plus a strict parser that rejects the removed legacy names. <!--#7d7496e6923c746d-->
  - `MergeStrategy.from_str` (method) — Classmethod that parses a case-insensitive strategy name into a `MergeStrategy`, raising migration-friendly errors for the retired `default`/`robust` names and a list of allowed values for anything else unrecognized. <!--#75614be5e330bb36-->
- `HunkResolution` (class) — Dataclass holding the resolution result for a single conflict hunk (validated 1-based line range, confidence, reasoning). <!--#b764faf99e100832-->
  - `HunkResolution.__post_init__` (method) — Validates the hunk's start/end line numbers and enforces end_line >= start_line, raising HunkValidationError on bad values. <!--#1014dae11a150b03-->
  - `HunkResolution._validate_line` (method) — Classmethod that coerces/validates a line-number field to a positive bounded int, rejecting None, bools, non-ASCII numerals, and out-of-range values. <!--#472cc527f6b2bbe5-->
- `FileResolution` (class) — Dataclass holding one file's merge-conflict resolution — its path, resolved content, per-hunk results, overall confidence, and boolean flags such as requires_human_review. <!--#38225eb8c901c8e1-->
- `LLMResolution` (class) — Dataclass aggregating the complete LLM resolution result across all conflict files, with overall confidence, flags, and raw response/parse-error fields. <!--#43b3a064635d1b4c-->
- `BatchContext` (class) — Dataclass carrying merge-level metadata (project root, ours/theirs branches and heads, merge base, commit logs, strategy) for a resolve_batch call, deliberately decoupled from the per-file conflict list so it can be reused across iterations. <!--#2031260e39f5801f-->
- `IterationFailure` (class) — Dataclass recording one iteration's failure mode and affected files, fed back into the next iteration's prompt instead of triggering take-theirs. <!--#0bfe4e4812133b90-->
- `BatchResolveOutcome` (class) — Dataclass summarizing a resolve_batch run: resolved/unresolved paths, iterations used, escalation reason, failure history, timing, and prompt/response previews. <!--#29444bc8647cbf34-->
  - `BatchResolveOutcome.success` (method) — Property returning True when no escalation occurred and no files remain unresolved. <!--#0d36d6f331e2183b-->
- `ConflictResolver` (class) — Resolves git merge conflicts by driving an LLM-as-editor loop that edits working-tree files directly, judging success by whether conflict markers remain and synthesising an LLMResolution for the downstream strategy/apply pipeline. <!--#e76ba76780dc368d-->
  - `ConflictResolver.__init__` (method) — Constructs the resolver with a project root, an optional shared LLMCaller and LLMTrace, and a validated positive cap on per-file resolved-content size. <!--#0d4c02aa169fc5e4-->
  - `ConflictResolver.resolve` (method) — Public entry point that converts a ConflictContext into a BatchContext, runs the resolve_batch editor loop (iteration cap from config when unspecified), and returns the synthesised LLMResolution. <!--#b6e6879274ab308c-->
  - `ConflictResolver._synthesize_resolution_from_outcome` (method) — Translates a BatchResolveOutcome into an LLMResolution by reading back each cleared file from disk, flagging unresolved or unreadable files for human review (never synthesising an accidental deletion), and attaching the outcome for callers. <!--#bff3c0596551c0b4-->
  - `ConflictResolver.resolve_batch` (method) — Core iteration loop that repeatedly builds an editor prompt, calls the LLM, and rescans files for markers until resolved or max_iterations is hit, returning a BatchResolveOutcome with the appropriate escalation reason. <!--#009706a6d1f4d769-->
  - `ConflictResolver._build_editor_prompt` (method) — Builds the per-iteration LLM-as-editor prompt: goal and iteration count, merge metadata and commit logs, prior-iteration failure history, per-file path/hunk blocks (contents referenced rather than inlined to bound prompt size), and resolution rules. <!--#a4204b6db59e714d-->
  - `ConflictResolver._call_llm` (method) — Issues one LLM call via the injected or lazily-built LLMCaller, timing it and recording a redacted success/error entry to the optional LLMTrace. <!--#5894bc7d397bd7c0-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/merge/deterministic_resolvers.py` (python) — Defines the mechanical merge-conflict resolvers (code-index md entry-wise merge, `.next_id` max-counter) behind a `DeterministicResolver` protocol, plus the `resolve_deterministic` entry point that applies and stages what it can and hands the rest back to the LLM fallback. <!--#b9a0f860574b5ca4|91a18b49771c6d4e-->
- `DeterministicResolver` (class) — Protocol defining a mechanical merge rule: a named resolver that claims some conflicting paths via `matches` and produces their merged content via `resolve`. <!--#479c430dab88c580-->
  - `DeterministicResolver.matches` (method) — Predicate stating whether this resolver owns the given repo-relative path. <!--#0710e1696ccd2fa0-->
  - `DeterministicResolver.resolve` (method) — Returns the merged content for a path (empty string means delete; raising means defer to the LLM). <!--#af369647c5627c88-->
- `DeterministicOutcome` (class) — Dataclass partitioning a conflict list into mechanically `resolved` paths, `remaining` ones left for the LLM, and per-path `failures`. <!--#d94121d2a12528a9-->
- `_git_show_stage` (function) — Reads a conflicted path's blob at a given merge stage as UTF-8 text, returning None when that stage is legitimately absent while letting git invocation errors propagate. <!--#f83f3331fee76e19-->
- `_git_add` (function) — Stages a path with `git add`, raising on failure. <!--#8bec845a81c24051-->
- `_git_rm` (function) — Removes and stages the deletion of a path with `git rm -f`, raising on failure. <!--#a0954d5a4eba66e4-->
- `FileBlock` (class) — Dataclass holding one code-index md entry — a file heading plus its symbol bullets and fingerprints — treated as the atomic, never-split unit of the index merge. <!--#d1b274542a59855a-->
- `_parse_md_blocks` (function) — Parses a rendered code-index md into its directory headings and per-file blocks, keeping lines verbatim so a parse→render round trip is byte-identical. <!--#47c54eb8fe12e873-->
- `_render` (function) — Rebuilds a full code-index md from directory headings and file blocks in `render_full`'s deterministic sorted order. <!--#15a81765fe17e8e0-->
- `_actual_content_fp` (function) — Recomputes the content fingerprint of a post-merge working-tree file (None if unreadable), used to adjudicate which side's index entry is current. <!--#3e68b3682946bf0d-->
- `CodeIndexResolver` (class) — A deterministic merge resolver that unions the two regenerated `tianluo/code-index.md` sides entry-by-entry, breaking per-entry disagreements by hashing the actual post-merge file and deterministically defaulting to theirs when fingerprints cannot decide. <!--#5e180444bc6682c4-->
  - `CodeIndexResolver.matches` (method) — Predicate that returns whether a given relpath is one of the tracked code-index paths this resolver handles. <!--#fad861dfcea8962e-->
  - `CodeIndexResolver.resolve` (method) — Parses both index sides, drops entries for files the merge deleted, adjudicates each surviving entry, and re-renders the merged index. <!--#2b0b6dfc8172a6ef-->
  - `CodeIndexResolver._pick` (method) — Chooses the winning FileBlock for one entry (and a reason string), preferring whichever side's fingerprint matches the working tree and otherwise falling back to theirs. <!--#8a47f64a5df8f74c-->
- `_parse_counter` (function) — Parses one side of the `.next_id` counter into an int, returning None when the side is absent or malformed. <!--#fac5586bf30c119c-->
- `NextIdResolver` (class) — A deterministic merge resolver that reconciles the `tianluo/issues/.next_id` counter by taking the larger of the two sides so no already-allocated issue ID can be reissued. <!--#5624a8690188e756-->
  - `NextIdResolver.matches` (method) — Predicate that returns whether a given relpath is one of the tracked `.next_id` counter paths this resolver handles. <!--#cf2ffb0aedc3bb9d-->
  - `NextIdResolver.resolve` (method) — Returns the maximum of the two readable counter sides, raising when neither side yields a usable value. <!--#5b04a1df110529a0-->
- `_find_resolver` (function) — Returns the first registered resolver claiming the path, or None. <!--#d0b1a44823e3efa8-->
- `resolve_deterministic` (function) — Public entry point that runs each conflict path through its registered resolver, staging what it can and returning the resolved/remaining/failures partition for the LLM fallback. <!--#224789a18bf1b44e-->
- `_apply` (function) — Writes and stages a resolver's output atomically — deleting on empty output, rejecting conflict markers, and restoring the original working-tree state if staging fails. <!--#0055c2fa4d5fd43a-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/merge/human_call.py` (python) — Serialises merge-conflict escalations into human-review MCP call files under the project's runtime `calls/` directory — `HumanCallWriter` writes either a full three-way conflict call (with orphan-resolution rejection and evidence scanning) or a degraded fallback call, plus localised response instructions, backed by module helpers for fork-safe collision-resistant filenames and atomic, fsync'd, symlink-guarded JSON writes. <!--#c1cb8e2149a5838c|e3f654ff8dda3637-->
- `_reset_call_seq_after_fork_in_child` (function) — os.register_at_fork child handler that reinitializes the process-level call-sequence counter and its lock so a forked child cannot reuse the parent's seq values. <!--#93f0ed501bc55d98-->
- `_generate_call_filename` (function) — Builds a collision-resistant call filename from prefix, UTC microsecond timestamp, pid, an atomic sequence number, an 8-char SHA, and a sanitized branch label. <!--#c8159a35d9364bee-->
- `_atomic_write_json` (function) — Module-level helper that atomically writes call-file JSON to disk via a same-directory temp file plus os.replace, with fsync (file and parent dir), symlink-refusal TOCTOU guards, and permission-bit preservation/widening. <!--#032d535465da6ec8-->
- `_scan_orphan_content_for_evidence` (function) — Module-level helper that inspects a rejected orphan file's resolved content and returns a structured evidence dict (size, 500-char preview, plus `has_conflict_markers` / `oversize` / `critical_oversize` flags) so a human reviewer can judge what the LLM smuggled in. <!--#305475a2ac85ffca-->
- `HumanCallWriter` (class) — Writer that serialises merge-conflict escalations for human review — producing full or degraded MCP call files under the project's runtime `calls/` directory and printing the matching response instructions. <!--#13bde06a934221f7-->
  - `HumanCallWriter.__init__` (method) — Stores the project_root path used to locate the tianluo/calls/ output directory. <!--#fc13bde9d61f7a1d-->
  - `HumanCallWriter.write_call` (method) — Builds and atomically writes the full merge-conflict call file, pairing each conflicted file's three-way content with the LLM's proposed resolution, rejecting and reporting orphan resolution paths as `rejected_orphans`, and tolerating a missing resolution under the strict strategy. <!--#f46c87170d7e12eb-->
  - `HumanCallWriter.write_degraded_call` (method) — Writes a minimal fallback call file carrying the branch, pre-merge SHA and failure message when conflict context could not be built, so the strict strategy's every-conflict-reaches-a-human contract still holds. <!--#67f0b749fc8ce1a4-->
  - `HumanCallWriter.print_instructions` (method) — Prints localised, response-file guidance for a call file, re-reading it to branch between conflict and already-settled (degraded) wording so the operator is never told to run merge commands on a tree with no merge in progress. <!--#8c7a0231c4c0e5a8-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/merge/issue_renumber.py` (python) — Shared collection of pure primitives used by both `luo merge` issue channels to renumber colliding issue IDs while preserving cross-references — rewriting standalone `#<old>`→`#<new>` reference tokens (individually, in order-independent bulk, or only on merge-added lines), scanning/allocating/advancing the fcntl-locked `.next_id` counter to keep IDs collision-free, and recording durable renumber-trace and ambiguous-reference audit notes that dedup logic can later parse, strip, or mask. <!--#9d44e172fdd509fb|4b27dd25df9bc4bb-->
- `_norm_id` (function) — Helper that coerces an issue ID given as a zero-padded string or int into its plain integer value. <!--#c0fe01f0b823bc4e-->
- `_issue_files` (function) — Generator yielding every `*.yaml` file under `tianluo/issues/{open,closed}/` in sorted order for deterministic, stable-order rewrites. <!--#cf6b91512a25d8da-->
- `rewrite_issue_references` (function) — Repoints standalone `#<old_id>` cross-reference tokens to a zero-padded `#<new_id>` across scoped issue files (matching by integer value), requiring caller-supplied scope_files to disambiguate which side of a collision to move. <!--#100c2b8f41889dba-->
- `rewrite_issue_references_bulk` (function) — Applies a whole batch of `#<old>`→`#<new>` rewrites in one simultaneous pass resolved against the original text, so chained-ID mappings stay order-independent (required for multi-issue runtime-sync adoption). <!--#ca479e371794ac3c-->
- `_string_lines` (function) — Recursively yields every logical line of every string value nested inside a dict/list/str YAML node. <!--#f6fc170e8f103cba-->
- `count_reference_tokens` (function) — Counts standalone `#<digits>` tokens in a text string whose integer value equals a target ID, using the same boundary/zero-padding rules as the rewriters. <!--#686c93555aee3b3d-->
- `live_reference_count` (function) — Counts *live* `#<target_id>` references in an issue file, first stripping renumber-trace/ambiguity audit lines from the parsed YAML string values so historical records aren't miscounted. <!--#1f4efb96691e716c-->
- `rewrite_references_in_added_lines` (function) — Rewrites `#<old_id>`→`#<new_id>` only in lines a file gained relative to a pre-merge baseline (using logical YAML string lines with per-occurrence budgeting, falling back to physical lines when unparseable), with a dry_run mode to detect ambiguous targets. <!--#a2e5508c3a227c93-->
- `scan_max_issue_id` (function) — Returns the highest numeric issue ID present in the store, considering both each file's `NNN_` filename prefix and its parsed YAML `id` field. <!--#ada6637710240d46-->
- `resolve_issue_numeric_id` (function) — Resolves a single issue file's numeric identity, preferring the parsed YAML `id` field and falling back to the filename prefix, returning None if neither is present. <!--#9e9970c053f9c781-->
- `find_issue_id_owner` (function) — Returns the issue file (excluding given paths) whose resolved numeric identity — parsed `id` then filename prefix — equals target_id, so a renumber's reference rewrite can be scoped away from a kept-side owner. <!--#dd753b9e3babd3fb-->
- `reserve_next_id` (function) — The single ID-allocation primitive that, under an fcntl `.next_id` lock, reserves `max(counter, on-disk max + 1)` and advances the counter in the same locked section so concurrent allocators never collide. <!--#7ccbcc1064e61874-->
- `advance_next_id_to_max` (function) — Monotonically pushes the `.next_id` counter up to at least `max(existing ID) + 1` under an fcntl lock (scanning both filename prefixes and parsed `id` fields, never lowering an ahead counter), preventing re-minting of a renumbered file's number. <!--#4a2bc921dd2afe11-->
- `format_renumber_trace` (function) — Renders the Chinese `旧号 #014 → 新号 #240 (luo merge)` audit line appended to the tail of a renumbered issue's description. <!--#ec41384490561f40-->
- `format_ambiguous_reference_note` (function) — Renders the durable `歧义引用 #005 → 候选 #011 / #012 (luo merge)` note recording a `#<old>` reference that has no single provable renumber target. <!--#e132532e9cca2f4c-->
- `append_description_note` (function) — Appends a note as a trailing line of an issue file's YAML `description` (leaving non-mapping files untouched) so it never shifts the title-deriving first line. <!--#72e70d953cfb5b7f-->
- `strip_renumber_traces` (function) — Removes every merge-machinery audit line (renumber traces and ambiguity notes) from a description so content-signature dedup stays match-stable across re-runs. <!--#e2b980dcd6ca5727-->
- `parse_renumber_traces` (function) — Extracts the recorded `(old, new)` renumber pairs from a description's trace lines so dedup can confirm that a digit change was an actual recorded renumber. <!--#9060d9f01f82ccb2-->
- `mask_issue_references` (function) — Replaces every standalone `#<digits>` token with a fixed `#REF` placeholder to give a rewrite-invariant (but coarse) signature key for shortlisting dedup candidates. <!--#eeacb0031c213645-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/merge/orchestrator.py` (python) — MergeOrchestrator library module that sequentially merges branches into the current branch, coordinating pre-flight handling of SE3 self-managed dirty paths (tianluo/issues/, tianluo/code-index.md), deterministic and LLM-backed conflict resolution, runtime/issue-id sync, version aggregation, and post-condition checks, and returning an aggregated MergeReport (aliased MergeResult) to the caller. <!--#4a91299e71d32ede|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/merge/reconcile.py` (python) — The merge-side version-reconciliation core: its unconditional, idempotent `reconcile()` collects outstanding `VersionIntent`s from merged-in worktree sessions and derives the final version once against master's current version — via a deterministic `max_bump` channel or, when `tianluo/version-rules.md` exists, an LLM channel — enforcing no-regression/no-collision guards and optionally creating an annotated SemVer tag, so concurrent sessions can no longer share or drop a version bump. <!--#312652fbb8724da2|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/merge/runtime_sync.py` (python) — Synchronizes git-ignored tier-A runtime content (including issue files, with renumber-aware issue merging) from a source branch's worktree `tianluo/` directory into the current branch after a `luo merge`, using hardened symlink-safe, bounded, atomic file copying (renameat2/RENAME_NOREPLACE with os.rename fallback) plus collision detection, sidecar writes for bypassed collisions, and a SyncReport summary. <!--#d33f41f865f9bc6b|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/merge/strategy.py` (python) — Defines the StrategyDecider and its DecisionAction/StrategyDecision types, encoding the safe/strict/fast decision matrix that translates an LLM conflict resolution's confidence and spec-guardrail signals into an accept, reject, or escalate-to-human outcome across both the legacy single-resolution and newer batch resolve-and-decide paths. <!--#12c358f3d1939594|fd94ea476199f009-->
- `DecisionAction` (class) — String enum of the three terminal decisions a strategy can reach: ACCEPT, HUMAN_CALL, or REJECT. <!--#bc263ff5be2b5d9d-->
- `StrategyDecision` (class) — Dataclass bundling a strategy's chosen action, a human-readable reason, and optional batch outcome / unresolved-file details for downstream orchestration. <!--#5a5765bc74c70683-->
- `StrategyDecider` (class) — Decision engine that maps an LLM conflict resolution (or a live resolver run) onto an ACCEPT / REJECT / HUMAN_CALL action according to the selected `MergeStrategy` (safe, strict, fast), in both the legacy single-resolution form and the newer batch form. <!--#4455c535e2b06070-->
  - `StrategyDecider.decide` (method) — Public entry point that dispatches an `LLMResolution` to the safe, strict, or fast decision helper, warning and falling back to safe for an unknown strategy. <!--#8448aa0815c066ba-->
  - `StrategyDecider._decide_safe` (method) — Safe-strategy gate that accepts unless a global or per-file `requires_human_review` flag is set (confidence ratings are informational only), in which case it escalates to HUMAN_CALL. <!--#2cf0504c61c3f537-->
  - `StrategyDecider._decide_strict` (method) — Strict-strategy fallback (normally short-circuited by the orchestrator) that demands HIGH confidence on every hunk, file, and the resolution overall plus no human-review flags, otherwise returning HUMAN_CALL. <!--#0fa312d67a7f3edb-->
  - `StrategyDecider._decide_fast` (method) — Fast-strategy gate that never escalates to a human — it REJECTs only on a global `requires_human_review` flag and otherwise ACCEPTs, logging per-file flags it deliberately ignores. <!--#7043ddeca558c5be-->
  - `StrategyDecider.resolve_and_decide` (method) — Newer batch entry point that runs the resolver and dispatches to the per-strategy *_batch deciders, translating the outcome into a StrategyDecision. <!--#ea291ee351b07a3d-->
  - `StrategyDecider._run_resolver` (method) — Helper that builds a `ConflictContext` from a `BatchContext`, invokes `ConflictResolver.resolve` (tolerating legacy two-positional-argument mocks), and returns the attached or re-derived `BatchResolveOutcome` with the resolution stashed on it. <!--#28d63149044da2c0-->
  - `StrategyDecider._decide_fast_batch` (method) — Batch fast-strategy decision that runs the resolver and REJECTs when conflict markers remain after `max_iterations`, otherwise ACCEPTing subject to the flag-based `_decide_fast` gate. <!--#b214a964a07d7e55-->
  - `StrategyDecider._decide_safe_batch` (method) — Batch safe-strategy decision that runs the resolver and escalates unresolved files to HUMAN_CALL (marking `escalation_reason="safe_to_human"`), otherwise ACCEPTing subject to the flag-based `_decide_safe` gate. <!--#a83c03fd8f534287-->
  - `StrategyDecider._decide_strict_batch` (method) — Strict batch decider that short-circuits the resolver and routes every conflict file straight to a human MCP call without invoking the LLM. <!--#49e4c40caceb9a2d-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/merge/version_aggregator.py` (python) — Computes each merged branch's SemVer bump by comparing pyproject.toml versions at merge-base versus branch tip, takes the maximum bump, and atomically rewrites the version while amending the last merge commit—with section/triple-quote-aware TOML parsing and fail-loud rollback handling for no-op, corrupt, and write/git-failure paths. <!--#274ec5f46f2134d2|d5342d20e0b318f0-->
- `VersionNotAdvanced` (class) — Documentation-only RuntimeError describing the fail-loud 'on-disk version already at or above target' condition that callers may raise instead of accepting a false success. <!--#147a2fa2febe45c7-->
  - `VersionNotAdvanced.__init__` (method) — Stores the pre-merge, current, and target version strings and builds the explanatory 'no bump applied' message. <!--#b12259069490d4d2-->
- `_slice_to_next_section` (function) — Returns TOML content from a section start up to the next line-anchored section header, skipping over triple-quoted strings. <!--#199ed868d02d591f-->
- `_strip_triple_quoted_strings` (function) — Returns the content with all triple-quoted string blocks removed so embedded version-like literals aren't matched. <!--#f9d97057fabebb37-->
- `_find_triple_quoted_regions` (function) — Returns half-open (start, end) offset ranges of every triple-quoted block in the content. <!--#c934417522f7a342-->
- `_find_version_match_in_section` (function) — Returns the first `version = "..."` regex match that lies outside any triple-quoted region, or None. <!--#bfaf31411e2b9cdc-->
- `_parse_pyproject_version` (function) — Extracts the version string from pyproject.toml content, preferring [project] over [tool.poetry] with section and triple-quote awareness. <!--#a1708031992d7430-->
- `read_version_at_ref` (function) — Reads and parses pyproject.toml's version as it existed at a given git ref, returning None when absent or unparseable. <!--#dfc1c3ff78c29e16-->
- `_diff_bump` (function) — Returns the BumpType (MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH) going from a base Version to a branch Version, treating prerelease→release as PATCH and None when not advanced. <!--#0a2cdd1198ba4f38-->
- `InferResult` (class) — Dataclass pairing an inferred bump type (or None) with a human-readable reason string. <!--#4a852784336bceba-->
- `infer_branch_bump` (function) — Infers a branch's SemVer bump by comparing pyproject versions at the merge-base and branch tip, returning None (with a reason) on missing/unreadable/non-advancing versions. <!--#607a0a1cb38faaad-->
- `max_bump` (function) — Returns the highest-priority bump from a list, defaulting to PATCH for an empty list. <!--#ae0a425b7d47d771-->
- `AggregateResult` (class) — Dataclass capturing the outcome of aggregate_and_apply, including success, before/after versions, bump type, error, and the already-at/higher-than-target anomaly flags. <!--#5a2fc7e603d44e55-->
- `_atomic_write_text` (function) — Writes text to a path atomically via temp-file + fsync + os.replace, preserving mode, guarding against destination symlinks, and flushing the parent directory. <!--#a93e22e5d1af0a4a-->
- `_safe_write_version` (function) — Locates the version field's byte offset and rewrites pyproject.toml's version atomically, optionally reusing a caller-supplied content snapshot to avoid cross-read drift. <!--#fad8303d4e307893-->
- `_reset_staged_pyproject` (function) — Runs `git reset HEAD pyproject.toml`, logging and returning an error string on timeout/OSError/non-zero exit so a failed amend leaves no stale staged change. <!--#49cd07058d20978d-->
- `aggregate_and_apply` (function) — Computes the maximum bump across all merged branches, applies it to the pre-merge version, atomically rewrites `pyproject.toml`, and amends (or creates) the last commit — returning an `AggregateResult` that fails loud on unparseable/already-advanced versions rather than silently no-opping. <!--#e741590f3cb74b1a-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/merge/worktree_gc.py` (python) — Standalone garbage collector for leaked isolation-worktree (`luo run --worktree`) runs that escape the normal finalize/merge cleanup — it enumerates terminal, over-age worktree runs and, per run, archives (a hard gate), promotes engine state, removes the directory, and deletes only provably-merged branches while always retaining and surfacing unmerged ones, returning a WorktreeGCReport and reusing the hardened cleanup primitives shared by the CLI and daemon triggers. <!--#63665f2a14392e35|7d405a8ae20dbbb6-->
- `WorktreeGCReport` (class) — A dataclass capturing the outcome of one `gc_worktree_runs` sweep, tracking `archived`, `retained_unmerged` branches, `reclaimed_bytes`, `skipped`, and `errors`. <!--#669e82dc8b97f8ab-->
- `_dir_size` (function) — Best-effort helper that totals the byte size of a directory tree (0 if missing), stat-ing symlinks without following them and skipping per-entry errors, for the reclaimed-space report. <!--#a78bc9d7c8d25026-->
- `_branch_is_merged` (function) — Fail-closed safety check that returns whether a branch is provably merged into its recorded original base, retaining the branch on any ambiguity and never falling back to HEAD. <!--#5ccdca4db8de2ca4-->
- `_load_worktree_header` (function) — Safely reads a worktree engine.json header dict, returning None (never raising) for corrupt/unreadable/non-object files so one bad state file can't abort the sweep. <!--#d353e352eaa27e5f-->
- `find_stale_worktree_runs` (function) — Enumerates terminal, over-age isolation-worktree runs eligible for GC by globbing `tianluo/worktrees/*/tianluo/state/engine.json` and filtering on worktree mode, terminal status, and mtime age. <!--#d2b0391c862612ec-->
- `gc_worktree_runs` (function) — Reclaims leaked terminal worktree runs by archiving each (a hard gate), promoting its engine.json, removing the working directory, and deleting the branch only when provably merged, returning a `WorktreeGCReport`. <!--#c3b602a17055a1a7-->

## `src/tianluo/engine/steps/` — The flow engine's step-handler package: one module per StepType (discovery → analyze → investigate/plan → implement → test/e2e → self_check/invariant_check/adjudicate → confirm → commit/version/merge/summarize), each translating its inputs into step.outputs and a StepStatus, plus shared helpers (_project_root, _fix_context) and colocated tests. <!--#827835495b35a36b|311d7c695047e410-->
