### `src/tianluo/engine/steps/__init__.py` (python) — The step-handlers package init that imports every flow-engine step handler, assembles the STEP_HANDLERS registry mapping each StepType to its handler, and defines backward-compatibility stubs that forward deprecated PROPOSE/DESIGN/PROJECT_SUMMARY step types to their unified replacements so old persisted flows can still resume. <!--#7e6bf118e4282fda|4b179c6ca8599baf-->
- `propose_stub_handler` (function) — Backward-compatibility stub for the deprecated PROPOSE step type that logs a warning and forwards to plan_handler so old persisted flows can resume. <!--#6fb89b174cba579c-->
- `design_stub_handler` (function) — Backward-compatibility stub for the deprecated DESIGN step type that logs a warning and forwards to plan_handler so old persisted flows can resume. <!--#ab925d0e54c6959b-->
- `project_summary_stub_handler` (function) — Backward-compatibility stub for the deprecated PROJECT_SUMMARY step type (now merged into ANALYZE) that logs a warning and forwards to project_summary_handler so old persisted flows can resume. <!--#0ddfcccc8427c3ad-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/steps/_fix_context.py` (python) — Shared helper module that renders the fix-loop context block for step LLM prompts, providing schema-tolerant extraction of issue display fields (severity/description/location), compact iteration-count formatting, and the multi-line fix-context prompt builder that deliberately omits fix_history to avoid biasing reviewers. <!--#879eff276f120e3b|e1e167a8536068b1-->
- `format_fix_iteration_display` (function) — Formats a fix iteration and cap as a compact `<n>/<cap>` (or `<n>/unlimited`) string for log lines. <!--#20f94d99307f7201-->
- `extract_issue_display_fields` (function) — Schema-tolerant reader that pulls (severity, description, location) out of an issue dict whether it uses the new self_check schema or the legacy verify_spec one, defaulting missing fields to empty strings. <!--#7c6be96c5a8cbcf4-->
- `render_fix_context` (function) — Builds the multi-line fix-context prompt block for a step (initial-pass message, iteration count, final-attempt warning, and previously-reported issues), deliberately omitting fix_history to avoid biasing reviewers. <!--#8395e1ce73d6743f-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/steps/_project_root.py` (python) — A shared helper module exposing resolve_flow_project_root, which resolves a flow's authoritative project root by preferring flow.state.context['project_root'] and falling back to flow.change_path.parent then Path.cwd(), so every step handler converges on a single history home per flow (critically the worktree root for worktree-mode flows). <!--#e9ba8d3dbf7b199a|fcba78a8bc08bfd0-->
- `resolve_flow_project_root` (function) — Resolves a flow's authoritative project root by preferring flow.state.context['project_root'] and falling back to flow.change_path.parent then Path.cwd(), so every step handler converges on one history home per flow. <!--#3165b0a9de91a4ef-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/steps/adjudicate.py` (python) — Implements the ADJUDICATE step handler, which mines the cross-round ledger for oscillating or 打脸 (fixed-then-reopened) positions, builds and retries an LLM ruling prompt until the verdict is actionable, then stages the ruling's description/plan overrides, superseded fix_instructions and dead-clause abolitions into step outputs for the state machine to apply to the persisted ledger once the ruling lands. <!--#e0d667287f9eae1e|280692b25f72438f-->
- `_ledger` (function) — Returns the read-only cross-round ledger sub-tree from the flow's context, tolerating an absent/malformed ledger by yielding an empty dict. <!--#a23000ada9ea4ced-->
- `_active_nonrejected_observations` (function) — Filters the ledger's observations down to those still counting toward triggers — neither abolished nor at a position the adjudicator already ruled benign. <!--#6bd8662db445556a-->
- `_candidate_positions` (function) — Builds the prompt's candidate-contradiction list from quote-anchored positions showing ≥2 materially different expected behaviors (oscillation) unioned with explicit trigger positions, each carrying its per-round expected-behavior timeline. <!--#df54c70c6026d38e-->
- `_fixed_then_reopened` (function) — Collects positions the ledger declared 'fixed' yet flagged again (打脸), surfaced in the prompt as extra evidence of a real contradiction. <!--#e65ca03f02fe1187-->
- `_position_fingerprints` (function) — Returns all still-active fingerprints at the given positions so a ruling can abolish every ledger entry grounded on a clause it removed. <!--#204675b35520fea5-->
- `_latest_adjudicated_output` (function) — Walks a flow's step_history in reverse to return the most recent completed/partial ADJUDICATE step's non-empty outputs[key], optionally skipping one step to fetch the pre-ruling baseline value in effect before a given ruling. <!--#93446a9bdc495a63-->
- `_latest_adjudicated` (function) — Thin no-exclusion wrapper over _latest_adjudicated_output that returns the latest completed ADJUDICATE step's value for a given output key. <!--#a25efebee83b3080-->
- `_effective_task_description` (function) — Resolves the currently-effective pre-interjection base task_description (injected base, else the flow's recomputed effective base) so the LLM's corrected description installs cleanly at the base layer without duplicating interjections. <!--#b126a5ee450237a1-->
- `_effective_task_groups` (function) — Resolves the currently-effective plan task_groups for the ruling prompt, preferring injected inputs then prior adjudicated plan then the latest completed PLAN step's output. <!--#2fc438efc803e1be-->
- `_format_task_groups` (function) — Pretty-prints the plan task_groups as indented JSON (or a placeholder when empty) for inclusion in the prompt. <!--#230849a8084b858a-->
- `_format_candidates` (function) — Renders the candidate-contradiction list into human-readable prompt sections showing each candidate's file, quoted clause, and per-round expected-behavior timeline. <!--#57c3fe9b552bef33-->
- `_format_fixed_reopened` (function) — Renders the fixed-then-reopened rows into prompt bullets showing each location's quote and the behavior it was previously fixed as. <!--#9eba39a5beb13b74-->
- `_build_prompt` (function) — Formats the ADJUDICATE_PROMPT from the trigger reasons, effective task description, candidate contradictions and 打脸 (fixed-then-reopened) rows, then best-effort appends the project charter so spec-vs-hard-constraint conflicts are visible to the LLM. <!--#b792e2815ecb604d-->
- `_normalized_covered_surfaces` (function) — Sanitizes an LLM ruling's optional `covered_surfaces` field into a stripped list plus a validity flag, treating absent/empty as valid but rejecting any malformed entry that lacks a non-blank `surface` or `justification`. <!--#ae4211ea6a12b908-->
- `_ruling_rejection_reason` (function) — Single source of truth for whether an LLM ruling may land, returning a human-readable reason string (missing `adjudication_rationale`, no covering `adjudicated_description`, malformed `covered_surfaces`) or None when actionable — reused verbatim in the retry re-prompt and the FAILED error message. <!--#1b350fa7d756bf06-->
- `_normalized_overrides` (function) — Coerces and type-validates the ruling's two override fields into (description, plan), accepting only a non-empty string and a non-empty list respectively, else None. <!--#c4ed0a1f83c7869f-->
- `_ruling_is_actionable` (function) — Thin boolean view over `_ruling_rejection_reason`, documenting why every ruling needs a rationale and why any non-`review_divergence` verdict needs a covering description override. <!--#36d278f53ac9f512-->
- `_effective_source_pool` (function) — Returns the text surfaces (effective task description plus project-constraint texts) that a finding may still quote after a ruling lands, mirroring `self_check._build_source_pool` so dead-clause detection uses the same acceptance surface. <!--#0a043849e561b637-->
- `_constraint_source_texts` (function) — Harvests the project-constraint texts (charter, WHY:/INVARIANT: comments) reachable from every IMPLEMENT step's `files_changed` plus each candidate's file, returning None when the constraint channel is unreadable so the caller abolishes nothing. <!--#c1ed9a2ec522b658-->
- `_positions_with_dead_clause` (function) — Narrows candidate positions to those whose quoted clause (matched via self_check's relaxed quote variants) no longer appears in any post-ruling source-pool entry, so a clause the ruling preserved keeps counting toward the oscillation triggers. <!--#6d7cd3492f8404b9-->
- `adjudicate_handler` (function) — The ADJUDICATE step entry point: assembles the ledger-based ruling prompt (plus any reviewer revision feedback), calls the LLM with a bounded semantic-retry loop until the ruling is actionable, fails the step if it never is, and otherwise delegates to `_apply_ruling`. <!--#ddc833aa1dba0da4-->
- `_coerce_override` (function) — Normalizes a nullable override field, treating empty or literal 'null'/'none' strings as absent so the effective-text layer falls through to the prior generation. <!--#3c6b688bb8a3aa34-->
- `_apply_ruling` (function) — Writes the ruling into `step.outputs` on one of two gated paths — a transparent no-op for `review_divergence` (audit-only verdict, all candidates closed out as rejected, patch keys popped) or the patch path for a real contradiction (description override, covered_surfaces, superseded fix_instructions, staged abolitions) — leaving the persisted ledger untouched until the ruling lands. <!--#3152e3e555c90e8a-->
- `apply_landed_ledger_effects` (function) — Idempotently applies a ruling's staged abolish/reject ledger effects to the persisted ledger, called by the state machine only once the ruling has landed (confirmed or免确认). <!--#5c06f6163813815e-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/steps/analyze.py` (python) — The analyze step module: classifies a task via a single LLM call (type, scope, complexity, root-cause clarity) using collected project context, sanitizes and persists the resolved task types, and rebuilds the flow's step sequence — including the conditional INVESTIGATE insert before PLAN, optional steps, worktree merge steps, and confirmation gates. <!--#2703c917098a6c77|e44ce3a991ed7bc3-->
- `analyze_handler` (function) — The "super-analyze" step handler that programmatically assembles project context and charter/code-index/runtime injections, makes a single LLM call to classify the task (type, scope, complexity, root_cause_clear), then reconciles the result with any explicit --type override, records `analyzed_type` in flow context, and decides whether a bugfix needs an extra INVESTIGATE round before planning. <!--#bc72187c570d6905-->
- `_extract_task_type` (function) — Validates and normalizes the LLM-returned task_type, preserving 'discovery' only when the --discover flag was explicitly set and falling back to 'feature' for anything invalid. <!--#dda0f377b990136b-->
- `_sanitize_analyzed_type` (function) — Returns the LLM's genuine task type for persistence as analyzed_type, degrading run modes like 'discovery' and any invalid value to 'feature' so downstream commit/version consumers get a clean type. <!--#58efeb45e96d8228-->
- `_extract_root_cause_clear` (function) — Parses the LLM's root_cause_clear judgement (accepting boolean or unambiguous string spellings) and defaults to False when missing or malformed, so uncertainty errs toward running an investigation round. <!--#8d7f144b224aefe8-->
- `_handle_type_conflict` (function) — Returns the explicit --type flag value when set, overriding the task type the LLM analysis resolved. <!--#581b4b10d216bb7d-->
- `_collect_project_summary` (function) — Helper that runs `ProjectContextCollector` and flattens the raw git status, active flows, and backlog data into a short plain-text summary block for the analyze prompt, replacing the former LLM-based PROJECT_SUMMARY step. <!--#1a9099178f654dec-->
- `_update_flow_steps` (function) — Rebuilds `flow.state.selected_steps` from the task type's default sequence, re-applying in fixed order the optional INVESTIGATE insertion, tianluo.yaml step config, opt-in E2E step, worktree merge steps, and confirmation gates so none are lost by the analyze-time re-derivation. <!--#1bd13ab2a5fff6fa-->
- `_insert_investigate_before_plan` (function) — Idempotently inserts an INVESTIGATE step immediately before the first PLAN in a step sequence, returning sequences without a PLAN unchanged. <!--#d78df24ef6136db3-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/steps/charter_freshness.py` (python) — A never-blocking flow-end step handler that detects whether a diff touched the charter's three content classes and, only after a COMPLETED invariant_check, runs a self-contained propose→gate→apply closed loop (mechanical anchored-patch validation plus an admission size/altitude LLM gate) to auto-write tianluo/charter.md via an atomic temp-file rename, degrading fail-safe to advisory-only (charter untouched) on any failure while also firing the human-amendment monitoring trigger. <!--#b9c66c9803ae3c84|dd74b1d1d7f2a98f-->
- `_changed_files` (function) — Helper that extracts a flat list of changed file paths from the `changes_made` payload, tolerating both string and dict `files_changed` entry shapes. <!--#8b6c4d2c442424e0-->
- `_format_changes` (function) — Helper that renders the diff's changed-files list (with actions and explanations) into a human-readable string for the freshness prompt. <!--#63fed8bbe4faa206-->
- `_resolve_edits` (function) — Resolves a validated anchored-patch op list into concrete (start, end, replacement) spans against the text, mapping insert_after to a zero-width span after the anchor and replace to the span covering the quoted old text. <!--#ebae0c706a3c4db2-->
- `_validate_anchored_patch` (function) — Mechanically validates an anchored patch against the on-disk charter text — enforcing op/char bounds, verbatim-unique anchors and quoted deletions, and non-overlapping edits — returning (ok, human-feedable reason). <!--#e3a2b68097fb95e3-->
- `_apply_patch` (function) — Applies an already-validated anchored patch to the text in a single order-independent left-to-right pass, returning the candidate charter (unchanged for an empty patch). <!--#b78987f3e6bef80c-->
- `_atomic_write_charter` (function) — Helper that writes new charter text to tianluo/charter.md atomically via a temp file in the same directory plus os.replace, so a crash leaves either the old or complete new charter but never a partial write. <!--#e1101852e3e5c51d-->
- `_unified_charter_diff` (function) — Helper that returns a unified diff (old -> new) of the charter text for inclusion in the step's outputs. <!--#d5509396f6005c17-->
- `_invariant_check_completed` (function) — Returns True iff the flow contains a COMPLETED invariant_check step, the precondition certifying the code change already passed review before an auto-update. <!--#d6aa1d92f36f9e30-->
- `_run_admission_trigger` (function) — Human-amendment path that, when the diff itself edited tianluo/charter.md, runs the non-blocking admission check and annotates step.outputs with any charter-size monitoring-light warning. <!--#964f8c0a53ee0903-->
- `_run_gate` (function) — Runs the two-part auto-update gate over the in-memory candidate — mechanical anchored-patch check, gating admission size red light, then the admission LLM gate for altitude/content-class and removal-weakening — returning (ok, candidate, verdicts, reason). <!--#153b3d3fa0568d07-->
- `_record_advisory` (function) — Records the advisory freshness output fields (charter_update_needed, touched_classes, reason, suggested_update) on the step from the propose response, defaulting them when no proposal exists. <!--#bee2ecd9ee971400-->
- `charter_freshness_handler` (function) — Main charter_freshness step handler that always returns COMPLETED (non-blocking): it fires the admission trigger, cheap-passes on an empty diff, and otherwise runs the propose -> gate -> apply closed loop to possibly auto-update the charter, degrading safely to advisory-only on any failure. <!--#37b04f0b878bec01-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/steps/commit.py` (python) — Implements the flow engine's commit step: it stages and commits the flow's changes with a generated message, strips se3 runtime-leak paths, and for release-point flows writes the authoritative version, README badge and VERSIONS.md entry under a race guard that detects concurrent version drift and its own replays, plus fallback summary generation. <!--#a1220422ac256879|f4ec726d2e8c6583-->
- `_detect_runtime_leaks` (function) — A pure path predicate that flags staged repo-relative paths carrying a tianluo/se3 runtime signature that leak outside the ignored top-level runtime root, returning the offending subset in input order. <!--#e58c7369db39d96d-->
- `_strip_runtime_leaks` (function) — A fault-tolerant regression backstop that, between `git add -A` and commit, unstages any runtime-leak paths (via `_detect_runtime_leaks`) with a warning and reports whether any leak was found, never failing the commit. <!--#14b980a1bc733ef1-->
- `_index_has_staged_changes` (function) — Checks whether anything remains staged after leak-stripping, returning True (assume committable) on any git error so it never short-circuits a legitimate commit. <!--#4ef01544d2b8b91f-->
- `_root_deny_excludes` (function) — A fault-tolerant helper that uses `git check-ignore -v` to determine whether a path is ignored specifically by the root `/*` default-deny whitelist rule (as opposed to any ordinary ignore rule). <!--#e3684880b347e214-->
- `_detect_root_whitelist_exclusions` (function) — Diagnostic-only backstop run between `git add -A` and commit that enumerates top-level untracked paths swept up by the root `/*` whitelist rule and logs a single WARNING listing them, without modifying .gitignore, staging, or commit control flow. <!--#905992454b796cf0-->
- `commit_handler` (function) — The main commit step handler that git-commits changes, applying authoritative version bumping, VERSIONS.md/`Version:` stamping and race-guard reconciliation only for synchronous (non-worktree) release-point runs while deferring versioning for worktree flows to merge time. <!--#ab99bf7c5d8b6d50-->
- `_load_version_config` (function) — Thin wrapper that lazily imports and loads the project's VersionConfig to avoid circular imports. <!--#4c9c3fe4b832d2e3-->
- `_resolve_target_version` (function) — Resolves the authoritative target version from the version_analyze step's `suggested_version` (inputs then step outputs), raising `RuntimeError` if that step failed or produced none so the commit halts rather than inventing a version. <!--#7b976dfdce6d2199-->
- `_normalize_version` (function) — Helper that canonicalizes a version string for equality checks by trimming whitespace and a leading v/V prefix, collapsing non-strings to an empty string that never matches a real version. <!--#b4d44c3588ab5143-->
- `_resolve_analyze_baseline` (function) — Resolves the disk-version reference the race guard compares against — version_analyze's observed current_version (which already includes this flow's own commits), falling back to the pre-session baseline and ignoring 'unknown' sentinels. <!--#072849081914d207-->
- `_version_at_commit` (function) — Reads and parses the version recorded in a version file at a given git commit (via git show of the blob through the same handler), returning None on any fault so callers never treat failure as a match. <!--#02c99b05464bcd10-->
- `_record_flow_committed_version` (function) — Best-effort persistence of the version this flow just committed onto durable flow state, so a re-entered commit step can later recognise its own already-landed bump even in script mode or when the Version: message trailer is absent. <!--#8a25545f1c7b008a-->
- `_flow_wrote_version` (function) — Determines whether this flow's own earlier commit already stamped a given version by matching commits carrying its Flow: trailer against the version-file blob (with a Version:-line grep fallback), distinguishing a legitimate replay/resume from concurrent drift. <!--#2a02d51857b6cb2a-->
- `_version_commit_already_landed` (function) — Decides, before this call commits anything, whether an earlier invocation of the same flow already committed the target version (via the durable flow marker or a git-durable Flow: trailer plus version-file blob probe), so the tag block knows if it is re-entering. <!--#8c921cf520cba0ae-->
- `_guard_version_race` (function) — A helper that, while holding the merge lock, compares the in-lock disk version against the baseline version_analyze observed and returns either the resolved target verbatim (no drift, or the drift is this flow's own already-committed or crash-resumed write) or a freshly recomputed version when a concurrent flow bumped the file first. <!--#621239349074b3c9-->
- `_reanalyze_version_with_baseline` (function) — Re-runs the version_analyze handler against a drifted on-disk baseline after a concurrent bump, returning the freshly derived version and forwarding refreshed artifacts (bump_type, commit_message, is_tag, etc.) onto the commit step to avoid a colliding version. <!--#c1e86aa9deda7c6f-->
- `_stage_file` (function) — Stages a single file via `git add`, resolving it relative to the project root and raising RuntimeError on failure. <!--#23f43a7c6b6b7a0b-->
- `_update_docs` (function) — Best-effort mechanical update of the README.md badge and VERSIONS.md changelog via DocumentationUpdater, staging both, swallowing any failure so docs never abort the commit. <!--#56d644ab0a00578e-->
- `_rollback_version` (function) — Restores the version file to its original value via VersionBumper.rollback, re-raising if the rollback itself fails. <!--#25140dabaebd94dc-->
- `_has_changes` (function) — Determines whether there is anything to commit, diffing a baseline commit against HEAD when available and falling back to `git status --porcelain`. <!--#c3879be18295377b-->
- `_generate_commit_message` (function) — Builds the git commit message for a flow's commit step, choosing the subject line via a priority chain (version_analyze `commit_message` → `implement_summary` → task-description fallback) prefixed by the effective task type, then appending optional bump-type decoration, changed-file list, incomplete-task notes for partial completions, the new version, and the flow reference. <!--#785cd60eb07b266d-->
- `_read_head_commit` (function) — Reads HEAD's commit hash via git rev-parse, returning (hash, "") on success or (None, stderr) when unreadable so the caller decides whether that is benign or fatal. <!--#3a3c602382b7b733-->
- `_describe_head_location` (function) — Best-effort human-readable locator for HEAD (its branch name, or an honest "could not be determined") used in messages when HEAD's hash cannot be read. <!--#8e5ea0e472345a00-->
- `_generate_template_summary` (function) — Builds and writes an LLM-free, template-based work-summary Markdown document (task, type, commit, version, changed files, test results) to tianluo/state when no summarize step is present in the flow. <!--#681ee7949fe61726-->
- `_collect_changes_from_flow` (function) — Gathers the list of changed file paths from all implement-step outputs in the flow history. <!--#9eb8c57d96e672be-->
- `_collect_test_results_from_flow` (function) — Returns the most recent test step's test_results dict from the flow history, or an empty dict if none exists. <!--#dc428ebd61d1ef28-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/steps/confirm.py` (python) — CONFIRM step handler that gates a prior step's output through either a synchronous LLM review (with iteration-cap auto-approval) or an asynchronous human review flow via call/response sidecar files, returning COMPLETED, REVISION_NEEDED, or PAUSED. <!--#01494d1713e56ade|ebc50be1da48293f-->
- `TimeoutError` (class) — Custom exception raised when polling for a human review response exceeds the allotted time. <!--#a6c6b7f03a421c70-->
- `_check_existing_response` (function) — Reads a `.response` sidecar file (if present) for a given call file and returns the parsed approval/feedback dict, used to detect human responses on resume. <!--#9723ee1681b75054-->
- `_wait_for_human_response` (function) — Blocks by polling for a human response file at a fixed interval, returning the response or raising TimeoutError when a timeout elapses. <!--#2d3854fcd84f716d-->
- `_create_call_file` (function) — Helper that writes a timestamped JSON call file under runtime_dir/calls for a human-review CONFIRM step, embedding flow/step/review metadata, a CALL_KIND_CONFIRM discriminant, a built prompt, and (for adjudicate reviews) the before/after ruling context so the daemon/web console can render an Approve/Reject UI. <!--#50897a2672199460-->
- `_llm_review` (function) — Runs the LLM-based review of a reviewed step's output — enforcing the persisted cross-revision iteration cap (auto-approving once max_iterations is hit), building either the plan-specific confirm prompt (under the flow's recorded decomposition/granularity doctrine) or the generic review prompt, then calling the LLM and parsing its approved/feedback verdict into a (StepStatus, review_result) pair. <!--#7e1d8fa702b5c4ac-->
- `confirm_handler` (function) — Main CONFIRM step handler that routes non-human reviewers through synchronous LLM review and human reviewers through call-file interaction — creating a call file and returning PAUSED on first run, or reading an existing response on resume to return COMPLETED (approved) or REVISION_NEEDED (changes requested). <!--#d2ee86c7084b0183-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/steps/conftest.py` (python) — A pytest conftest that sets collect_ignore to exclude the step-handler implementation modules test.py and test_with_fail_loop.py, preventing pytest from mistaking their test-prefixed names for actual test modules/functions. <!--#93a55fa5e88f5424|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/steps/discovery.py` (python) — Implements the SE3 discovery step: a multi-turn, PAUSED-driven requirement-clarification conversation with the LLM that gathers project/recency context, asks clarifying questions, executes proposed issue operations, renders each round to the console, and ends at a programmatic confirmation gate (response "1") on the refined task description before the flow advances to analyze. <!--#e7af0f7cfdf22788|796978823c2265e8-->
- `discovery_confirm_hint` (function) — Returns the i18n-rendered textual fallback hint ("type 1 to confirm") that accompanies the GUI confirm button at the discovery confirmation gate. <!--#ac0801c43937e9ce-->
- `discovery_confirm_metadata` (function) — Builds the (prompt, options) display metadata — a Markdown prompt carrying the proposed refined description plus a single one-click confirm option whose value is the normative "1" — for pausing a non-interactive discovery step at the programmatic confirmation gate. <!--#6cf5f054c946c924-->
- `_gather_project_context` (function) — Detects and formats basic project context (project type/name, test framework, git remote and branch) from files in the project root for inclusion in the discovery prompt. <!--#2efc5e2fb07052a6-->
- `_summary_recency_key` (function) — Computes a comparable epoch-float sort key for a `summary-*.md` file, parsing the filename's `YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS` timestamp as local time when present and otherwise falling back to file mtime so recency comparisons stay on a single numeric scale. <!--#cf902648d5769663-->
- `_collect_session_summaries` (function) — Reads the most recent `tianluo/state/summary-*.md` files (ordered by filename timestamp, then mtime), extracting a capped excerpt of the `**Task:**` line plus first body paragraph from each, to feed discovery's round-0 recency context best-effort. <!--#322525bf70056188-->
- `_collect_recent_commits` (function) — Returns subject lines of the most recent non-merge git commits via `git log`, best-effort and read-only with a timeout, yielding an empty list on any failure. <!--#89f42ded4fd71f5c-->
- `_gather_recency_context` (function) — Combines recent session summaries and recent commits into a single titled Markdown "Recent Activity Context" block for round-0 discovery, returning "" when both sources are empty. <!--#63d5bacc3853f06b-->
- `discovery_handler` (function) — The discovery step handler that drives a multi-turn, PAUSED-gated LLM conversation to clarify requirements — running discovery rounds, tracking conversation state and user-directed issue operations across resumes, and returning COMPLETED once a refined description is programmatically confirmed. <!--#f2ffdde4e4b0363c-->
- `_run_discovery_round` (function) — Builds and sends one discovery-round prompt to the LLM (assembling history, round-0 recency, charter/code-index/language/runtime injections), then parses, validates against emptiness, and returns the structured result plus raw response text. <!--#4656dcdec2db4e27-->
- `_format_conversation_history` (function) — Formats the accumulated conversation history list into a plain ROLE: content text block for prompt inclusion. <!--#ce6ad351fc217e64-->
- `_format_issue_op_engine_note` (function) — Builds an engine note summarizing this round's executed issue operations and the current set of in-scope tracked issue IDs, to append to the conversation history for the LLM. <!--#15b7d36de96e91b3-->
- `_generate_summary` (function) — Produces a short summary string counting assistant rounds and user inputs from the discovery conversation history. <!--#3e9395a1b38195a0-->
- `_extract_narrative_from_raw` (function) — Strips fenced and bare JSON blocks out of the raw LLM result text to recover any surrounding narrative prose for display. <!--#951c0061d894ad35-->
- `_proposed_description_block` (function) — Builds a nested cyan luo reverse-color Rich block (title, Markdown-rendered refined description, footer) that visually delimits the LLM's proposed task description for the user. <!--#b7d82a186184c193-->
- `_display_discovery_message` (function) — Renders a discovery turn to the console, assembling Rich renderables for narrative, content, proposed description, questions, per-round issue-operation results, and token-usage footer according to whether it is a confirmation, synthesis-with-questions, question, or general message. <!--#5b36de40ae1dac00-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/steps/e2e.py` (python) — Implements the engine's `e2e` step handler, which loads the E2E configuration, bootstraps or incrementally evolves the flow-owned `tianluo/e2e/` content (guarded to one evolution pass per flow, aimed by implement-step change hints), executes the scenarios via `run_e2e` into a per-flow artefacts directory, and translates the verdict into COMPLETED, REVISION_NEEDED with described fix-context issues for the fix loop, or a FAILED environment/config outcome that deliberately skips the fix loop. <!--#a557bcf1f971db8f|6b5e2c80e6acdaaf-->
- `e2e_handler` (function) — The e2e step's entry point: loads E2EConfig, maintains/evolves the flow-owned e2e content, runs the scenarios via run_e2e, and maps the verdict onto COMPLETED, REVISION_NEEDED (with fix instructions/context for the fix loop), or FAILED (environment/config problems). <!--#81af59a6d2d1e22d-->
- `_describe_issues` (function) — Adds a human-readable `description` (and `location`) to each e2e fix-context issue so the engine's generic issue renderer can display it in later fix iterations' implement prompts. <!--#fc7bb170cfed0b51-->
- `_fail_environment` (function) — Records a host-side e2e failure on the step as FAILED with message plus remediation, deliberately leaving `fix_needed` unset so it never enters the fix loop. <!--#f00ed1bffc754769-->
- `_fail_config` (function) — Records a malformed e2e configuration on the step as FAILED with the locating message, likewise bypassing the fix loop. <!--#1bacfa43a4a50c24-->
- `_maintain_content` (function) — Keeps `tianluo/e2e/` in step with the flow's code changes by bootstrapping the content directory on first use or otherwise delegating to a single per-flow evolution pass, returning a short summary note. <!--#b1b8585c1a3703b8-->
- `_evolve_content` (function) — Performs this flow's one guarded incremental-evolution pass over existing e2e content, aimed by change hints and degrading to a warning when the proposal is unusable. <!--#7d70297f5d8e37ec-->
- `_already_evolved` (function) — Checks the flow state context for the guard flag marking that this flow has already had its evolution attempt. <!--#5acf551328a0914c-->
- `_mark_evolved` (function) — Sets the guard flag in the flow state context so at most one evolution pass runs per flow. <!--#10a61dcf55e572cd-->
- `_evolution_hints` (function) — Builds the list of change hints for the evolution prompt from the flow's task description and the implement step's `changes_made`/`implement_summary` inputs rather than from a git diff. <!--#66a4433c64275878-->
- `_changed_paths` (function) — Normalizes `changes_made.files_changed` into a deduplicated list of path strings, accepting both the plain-string and `{"path": ...}` mapping shapes. <!--#7af4f41198560cf0-->
- `_group_labels` (function) — Normalizes `changes_made.implemented_groups` into deduplicated, capped labels, accepting both bare group ids and `{"name", "description"}` mappings. <!--#cb3999fe5af89361-->
- `_artifacts_dir` (function) — Returns the per-flow artefacts directory for screenshots and captures, placed under the runtime log directory so per-run output never lands beside committed baselines. <!--#ded955b4c0785852-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/steps/implement.py` (python) — The implement step handler: builds the implement/fix/holistic/capability-group LLM prompt templates (with version-file, why-comment, and test-scope/headless guardrails) and drives code-writing execution — single-call, holistic, or DAG-scheduled parallel groups in git worktrees with leaf-branch merging, conflict resolution and salvage, plus fix-iteration rounds for the test-verify-fix loop. <!--#56e2f7dce1d15aef|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/steps/invariant_check.py` (python) — Implements the anchored INVARIANT_CHECK step handler, which audits a flow's diff against an explicitly-recorded, flow-start-frozen anchor set (task text, charter, and the touched code's why-comments), cheap-passing when there is no diff or no anchors, raising REVISION_NEEDED for surviving verbatim-grounded violations plus hard-guarded deletions/rewrites of MARKED (WHY:/INVARIANT:) comments, and advisorily LLM-triaging unmarked comment losses into step outputs without spinning the fix loop. <!--#aac81bfed28f5125|2295e0f6fd3f3363-->
- `_is_marked_why_comment` (function) — Predicate that returns true when a marker-stripped comment body carries an explicit WHY:/INVARIANT: tag (case-insensitive, colon required), marking it as machine-protected. <!--#3f87b85f4e531865-->
- `_extract_comments` (function) — Best-effort textual harvest returning the bodies of single-line `#`/`//` comments from a block of text. <!--#90739f6db8d26015-->
- `_read_baseline_file` (function) — Reads a file's original pre-implementation content at the flow's frozen baseline commit via `git show`, returning None when there is no baseline or the file is unavailable. <!--#2e17a8cbfdf0c653-->
- `_harvest_why_comments` (function) — Collects colocated why-comments from each touched file, merging baseline and working-tree content so original invariant-documenting comments survive even if the diff deleted or rewrote them. <!--#d9851e8426c286b3-->
- `_deleted_comments_by_file` (function) — Best-effort per-file multiset diff of colocated comments between the frozen baseline commit and the working tree, returning comments present at baseline but now deleted or rewritten. <!--#faba99f56dee4fa3-->
- `_marked_comments_with_pos` (function) — Extracts each MARKED (WHY:/INVARIANT:) comment from text as (line_index, body) tuples, without inspecting surrounding code, for use in positional pairing. <!--#685db2c13a1cd060-->
- `_rewritten_marked_exemptions` (function) — Computes per-file counts of deleted marked comments that are exempt from the hard guard because they pair one-to-one (by text similarity then proximity) with a newly added/rewritten marked comment in the SAME file. <!--#a892ed9438e81979-->
- `_build_why_comment_guard_issues` (function) — Turns each lost WHY:/INVARIANT:-tagged comment into a high-severity anchored issue (quoting the comment body so it passes verbatim-quote validation), while consuming one same-file exemption per comment that the diff re-declared so only net losses reach the fix loop. <!--#f49543643bdd1c39-->
- `_build_anchor_inputs` (function) — Assembles the synthetic step_inputs (task description, charter text, harvested why-comments, changed files) that let invariant_check reuse self_check's issue-validation helpers, reading frozen step inputs first and falling back to on-disk/baseline harvesting. <!--#f63e1bc6b970538e-->
- `_anchor_pool_is_empty` (function) — Returns True when the frozen anchor set normalizes to no usable text, signaling the anchor-less case where the check must be refused. <!--#1bdb8c1632821713-->
- `_format_deleted_comments_block` (function) — Renders unmarked deleted comments grouped by file into a markdown block for the advisory LLM re-judge prompt. <!--#7fdccd42842a50bc-->
- `_rejudge_why_losses` (function) — Advisory-only, never-raising LLM triage that filters unmarked comment deletions down to meaningful why/intent losses destined for step.outputs only (never the fix loop). <!--#a58118bb188c7f23-->
- `_has_changed_files` (function) — Returns True iff the `changes_made` payload reports at least one changed file/path. <!--#cbe8e49e3e236b70-->
- `_format_changes` (function) — Renders the diff's changed-file list into prompt text mirroring self_check's view. <!--#68b655da37aa3b06-->
- `invariant_check_handler` (function) — Step handler that audits the diff against recorded invariants (charter, why-comments, task description) via an LLM call plus anchor validation, cheap-passing when there is no diff or no anchors, additionally guarding deleted/rewritten why-comments, and returning COMPLETED or REVISION_NEEDED for the state machine's fix loop. <!--#a9d80dd55ec893a7-->
- `_build_fix_outputs` (function) — Populates the step's fix-loop outputs (issues, fix instructions, iteration counts) from validated invariant violations and returns REVISION_NEEDED, mirroring self_check's fix output shape. <!--#259888a25e114e3e-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/steps/investigate.py` (python) — Implements the `investigate` step handler that runs one bounded round of LLM-driven root-cause investigation — feeding prior rounds' reports into the prompt, coercing the LLM's JSON into a canonical root-cause report in `step.outputs`, and enforcing a net-zero-diff contract against a persisted pre-step workspace baseline (with one best-effort revert round-trip before failing), while leaving loop/termination control to the state machine. <!--#df27a84b9f5ff9c5|de97d1271b937840-->
- `_format_previous_reports` (function) — Renders earlier investigation rounds' reports into a prompt section (hypothesis / evidence / confidence per round, plus a "don't repeat these experiments" instruction), returning an empty string on the first round. <!--#b2122f011e500314-->
- `_coerce_str_list` (function) — Normalizes a JSON field that should be a list of strings, wrapping a bare string and degrading anything else to an empty list instead of raising. <!--#99f22a570be81377-->
- `_coerce_conclusive` (function) — Interprets the LLM's `conclusive` verdict as a bool, defaulting to False so an unparsable or missing verdict schedules another bounded round rather than promoting a half-formed hypothesis. <!--#c358a54dc936eb8b-->
- `_build_report` (function) — Projects the parsed LLM JSON into the canonical root-cause report shape (root_cause, evidence, files_involved, suggested_fix_direction, confidence, conclusive) with per-field coercion. <!--#a1c955eb3d4d37bc-->
- `ensure_workspace_baseline` (function) — Idempotently captures the pre-step workspace snapshot into `step.inputs[BASELINE_INPUT_KEY]` (persisted before the step is marked RUNNING) so every re-entry or resume still compares against the tree as it was before the investigation started. <!--#cb32dc0b2aaa3ca7-->
- `_resolve_baseline` (function) — Thin wrapper that returns the attempt's workspace baseline via `ensure_workspace_baseline`, logging when an existing baseline is being reused on a re-entry. <!--#0ce53dc3e10f3fcf-->
- `investigate_handler` (function) — Runs one round of root-cause investigation — builds the prompt with prior reports and context injections, calls the LLM for a JSON report, then enforces the net-zero-diff contract (one revert round-trip before FAILED) and writes the report into `step.outputs`, leaving loop control to the state machine. <!--#e5ef1434a6904786-->
- `_request_revert` (function) — Best-effort LLM call asking it to undo its experimental workspace changes, swallowing errors because the caller's re-snapshot — not this call — decides the step status. <!--#ba4eff1012341dc1-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/steps/merge_integrate.py` (python) — Step handler that performs the integration half of a worktree flow — resolving the main checkout (fail-loud if the isolation worktree would be used by mistake), delegating the actual branch-into-master merge to tianluo.engine.merge.integrate under the already-held lock with deletion deferred, and mapping success to COMPLETED and failure/human-escalation to FAILED so version_reconcile never runs for work that didn't land. <!--#b5ab6ad7741c369f|b156ff6df3aed18c-->
- `_resolve_merge_root` (function) — Resolves the main-checkout root a merge step operates on, preferring the step's `cwd` override and otherwise strictly probing the main repo, failing loud with `MergeCheckoutResolutionError` rather than silently degrading to the isolation worktree. <!--#21523518f4d5d095-->
- `merge_integrate_handler` (function) — Step handler that merges the flow's isolation branch (from `flow.worktree_branch`) back into master by delegating to `tianluo.engine.merge.integrate` (with `acquire_lock=False` since the state machine already holds the merge lock and `delete_merged=False`), records the `MergeResult` on `step.outputs`, and returns COMPLETED on clean success or FAILED on failure/pending-human so `version_reconcile` never runs for work that didn't land. <!--#084438a4c85db26d-->
- `_summarize_result` (function) — Helper that extracts a JSON-safe dict summary of a `MergeResult`'s key fields (coercing enums/paths to strings) for storage on step outputs and history. <!--#b71352e034b521c0-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/steps/plan.py` (python) — Implements the unified PLAN step handler, which resolves the flow's planning doctrine (capability groups vs. granular tasks) and granularity, builds the LLM prompt with charter/code-index/root-cause context, validates and normalizes the returned `task_groups` enumeration (ids, ordering, acyclic `depends_on`), stores it as the flow's scheduling data, and renders it to the console. <!--#2cf2bfc1863a71c4|d230cf31e8750e67-->
- `_is_capability` (function) — Predicate returning True when a decomposition value (enum or its raw string) selects the capability planning doctrine. <!--#91ba4bc69c1d80d9-->
- `render_root_cause_section` (function) — Formats an INVESTIGATE step's `root_cause_report` dict into an optional prompt section (with an exhausted-budget warning when applicable), returning `""` for missing or empty reports so non-investigated flows keep byte-identical prompts. <!--#f7dfe7b5420c43a9-->
- `_resolve_plan_mode` (function) — Reads back the flow's committed plan decomposition/granularity via the shared `effective_mode` projection so PLAN, CONFIRM, and IMPLEMENT all act under the same doctrine. <!--#98e173a6636dda7d-->
- `_granularity_directive` (function) — Maps a granularity value (falling back to `PlanGranularity.AUTO` on anything unrecognized) to the single directive line injected into the capability prompt. <!--#91c95d49d542320c-->
- `_capability_cycle` (function) — Depth-first walk over a `depends_on` adjacency map that returns one cycle as an id path, or an empty list when the graph is acyclic. <!--#aa14671eecd83c64-->
- `_capability_groups_error` (function) — Validates an LLM-emitted capability `task_groups` enumeration against every shape scheduling depends on (list container, per-entry mapping, unique non-empty `group_id`, `description`, numeric `group_order`, acyclic non-dangling `depends_on`), returning a retryable error message or "" while normalizing ids and edges in place. <!--#488eaeed10c087d9-->
- `_build_prompt` (function) — Assembles the PLAN step's LLM prompt by concatenating a header, optional root-cause section, guardrails, and either the capability-group or granular task schema depending on the flow's decomposition doctrine and granularity. <!--#95faec1b6b444b1f-->
- `plan_handler` (function) — Step handler for the unified PLAN step: builds the prompt with charter/code-index/language/runtime injections, calls the LLM in two-phase JSON mode, validates the returned `task_groups` enumeration shape, and stores it as the flow's task-group scheduling data. <!--#d442d59b3d22f315-->
- `_display_plan` (function) — Renders the produced task groups to the console as a Rich tree plus summary panel via `TaskFormatter`. <!--#c24261b522bf26a7-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/steps/plan_tasks.py` (python) — Flow-step module that breaks an implementation into logical, verifiable task groups: its handler assembles a design/proposal/spec prompt (augmented with charter, code-index, discovery, and revision injections), calls the LLM, and stores the parsed task groups and complexity estimates, with helpers that render the design doc and proposal into prompt text. <!--#0dc32fef6abe5c95|082d773d725c8833-->
- `plan_tasks_handler` (function) — Handler for the `plan_tasks` step that turns the design doc (or a synthesized minimal one when DESIGN was skipped for bugfix/small tasks) plus proposal, spec content, revision feedback, and charter/code-index/runtime-environment injections into an LLM prompt, then parses the response into `task_groups` and complexity/effort outputs on the step. <!--#4040968f2c5931c2-->
- `_format_design_doc` (function) — Helper that renders a design-document dict into a readable prompt string covering overview, key decisions, components, and implementation plan. <!--#408d2cc21b753960-->
- `_format_proposal` (function) — Helper that renders a proposal dict into a prompt string summarizing the proposal and the files to modify and create. <!--#8f0ab84037ee5337-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/steps/project_summary.py` (python) — Defines the PROJECT_SUMMARY flow step, which collects raw project context (git status, flow engine state, backlog, specs) via ProjectContextCollector and calls the LLM to produce a concise natural-language project summary that downstream steps and the `se3 summary` CLI command reuse. <!--#6d0a7c0ae008f8fb|90d3d47590cc5270-->
- `generate_project_summary` (function) — Collects project context (git state, flow engine stats, backlog) via ProjectContextCollector, renders it into PROJECT_SUMMARY_PROMPT with any issue-discovery injection appended, and returns the LLM's natural-language project summary — shared by both the PROJECT_SUMMARY step and the `luo summary` CLI command. <!--#0367909e8a02ac72-->
- `project_summary_handler` (function) — Handler for the `project_summary` step that resolves the flow's project root, calls `generate_project_summary` via the LLM, stores the result in `step.outputs["project_summary"]` for downstream steps, and returns `StepStatus.COMPLETED` or `StepStatus.FAILED` on error. <!--#ab4cce3f65bcf7e2-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/steps/self_check.py` (python) — Handler for the Self Check step, which runs an LLM code review of the completed task after tests pass and validates each reported issue against strict evidence-grounding rules (verbatim expectation quotes, evidence_lines within the changed-file review scope, drop tallies in validation_stats) so that only substantiated findings drive REVISION_NEEDED into the fix loop. <!--#81f43d299746e5e5|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/steps/summarize.py` (python) — The summarize step module: builds an LLM prompt from the flow's changes, test/verification verdicts, completion status, investigation report and knowledge-guard outputs, then persists the resulting work summary to step outputs and tianluo/state/summary-{flow_id}.md, always falling back to a deterministic Markdown summary when the LLM produces nothing. <!--#ac5c3a17e8a9305c|7e25f0197d136dbc-->
- `_build_investigation_section` (function) — Renders the INVESTIGATE step's root-cause report plus a summarize-specific instruction into a prompt section, returning an empty string when no investigation ran so non-investigating flows keep byte-identical prompts. <!--#236d6e3aa6a850ef-->
- `summarize_handler` (function) — The summarize step handler: gathers changes, test results, verification verdict, completion status, investigation report and knowledge-guard results into an LLM prompt, saves the generated summary to the step outputs and a file, and always completes by falling back to a deterministic summary on empty or failed LLM responses. <!--#1758c6434dfa65ff-->
- `_format_changes` (function) — Renders the changes_made dict into a Markdown bullet list of modified files, tolerating both plain-string paths and structured change dicts. <!--#e9f2222313255a7b-->
- `_gated_tests_passed` (function) — Returns the gated test pass/fail verdict, preferring critical-acceptance-gated `overall_passed` over the legacy raw `passed` key so skipped critical tests aren't reported green. <!--#b3909e825e66b5f8-->
- `_format_test_results` (function) — Formats test results into a one-line 'Tests passed: <bool>' string using the gated verdict. <!--#fc3da81113dda393-->
- `_format_verification` (function) — Formats the verification_result dict into prompt text covering the verified flag, summary, and issue/error counts. <!--#d8353e5d6198d067-->
- `_collect_knowledge_guard_outputs` (function) — Scans the flow's completed steps to pull charter_freshness outputs and invariant_check why-comment losses (last-occurrence wins), returning them as a tuple so summarize can report knowledge-artifact guard results self-contained. <!--#6ef47fbaa7333440-->
- `_format_why_loss` (function) — Renders a single removed/rewritten why-comment advisory entry (file, comment, why-it-matters) as one markdown line. <!--#68efd30d25c0c676-->
- `_format_knowledge_guards` (function) — Builds the flow-level "Knowledge Guards" markdown section from collected charter/why-comment outputs, covering charter auto-update (with capped diff excerpt), charter update advisories, and removed why-comment losses, returning "" when nothing happened. <!--#7d84415b24d7b685-->
- `_resolve_verified` (function) — Extracts the authoritative boolean `verified` verdict from verification_result, returning None when no verify_spec step ran. <!--#f1b90fb72a3da192-->
- `_verification_gate_lines` (function) — Returns prompt instruction lines forbidding 'complete/all-green' claims, but only when verification explicitly failed (verified is False). <!--#77b6a8199fa1459e-->
- `_build_completion_section` (function) — Assembles the optional completion-status prompt section (incomplete tasks, restricted edits, and the verification gate), returning empty for the clean complete-and-verified case. <!--#7577870ce91e6575-->
- `_format_root_cause_report` (function) — Formats an investigation report dict (root cause, evidence, files involved, suggested fix direction, confidence) as Markdown lines for the fallback summary, returning an empty list when no usable report exists. <!--#95fa3c2e18b487af-->
- `_create_basic_summary_text` (function) — Builds the deterministic Markdown fallback summary — status label, verification-failure warning, investigation report, changed files, incomplete tasks, testing status, handoff context and knowledge guards — used whenever LLM summary generation yields nothing or raises. <!--#fde10ecf98a8f249-->
- `_save_summary` (function) — Persists the generated work summary as a Markdown file at tianluo/state/summary-{flow_id}.md with flow metadata (id, task, timestamp), logging on success and warning on failure. <!--#386085568023cfb2-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/steps/test.py` (python) — Implements the engine's `test` step: it runs the configured test command(s) with dynamic timeouts, parallel/xdist handling and timeout retry, parses per-test results across pytest/jest/go formats, gates on critical acceptance tests (skipped or silently un-collected), separates inherited baseline failures from newly introduced regressions, and returns a shared `TestVerdict` (also consumed by SPEC_GATE) that drives COMPLETED / REVISION_NEEDED / FAILED plus fix instructions, slimmed archive output, and discovery-issue filing for pre-existing failures. <!--#60b30dce93bfc586|6ad91143d473914a-->
- `TestVerdict` (class) — Dataclass capturing the classified result of one test-suite run (results dict, pass flag, fix trigger, fix guidance/context, inherited failures), shared so the test step and SPEC_GATE consume one identical verdict. <!--#2fe28d757ce5a9dd-->
- `_extract_failures_section` (function) — Extracts the pytest FAILURES/ERRORS diagnostic section from stdout, per-block-truncating it to fit a character budget while preserving assertions and traceback tails. <!--#48ac6719f45bd66e-->
- `_parse_test_summary_counts` (function) — Best-effort fallback parser that sums aggregate `passed`/`failed` counts from runner summary lines (pytest, cargo, jest), returning `(passed, failed)` or `None` when no recognizable counts exist. <!--#fe55181a996f6bca-->
- `_summarize_passed_phase_output` (function) — Builds a compact archive summary (count line plus output tail) for a PASSED phase's otherwise-noisy verbose stdout/stderr, using a three-tier count fallback. <!--#1659723ff3b743eb-->
- `_slim_passed_phase_archive` (function) — Mutates a test_results dict in place to replace each passed phase's (and the top-level) stored stdout/stderr with the slimmed summary, leaving failed phases intact. <!--#c54a963da6a47643-->
- `_render_estimate` (function) — Formats an estimated_test_duration value for display, rendering whole floats as ints and None as 'not set'. <!--#ab9da39a8180758d-->
- `test_handler` (function) — The test step entry point — a thin shell that loads `TestConfig`, delegates to `run_and_classify_tests`, then writes step outputs, records history, files inherited-failure issues once per flow, and maps the verdict to COMPLETED / REVISION_NEEDED / FAILED. <!--#cbaf2b56e65cc500-->
- `_fail_test_environment` (function) — Turns an `XdistUnavailableError` into a FAILED step carrying the error message and remediation, deliberately omitting `fix_needed` so a broken test environment reaches the human instead of the fix loop. <!--#8706b0410b650371-->
- `_e2e_enable_suggestion` (function) — Returns an optional, failure-tolerant hint text (via the lazily imported `suggest_enable`) advising the user to turn on `e2e.enabled`, raised from the test step because the `E2E` step only exists once that switch is already on. <!--#07e2f406a5fc497f-->
- `run_and_classify_tests` (function) — The shared, Step-decoupled core that computes the dynamic timeout, runs the primary command plus phases (with timeout retry and parallel/xdist handling), applies the critical-acceptance gate, splits inherited vs introduced failures, and returns a `TestVerdict` with fix instructions/context. <!--#4703e6c7a053fc49-->
- `_build_baseline_fix_section` (function) — Builds the prompt text prepended to the fix loop that lists the inherited baseline test failures and states the narrowly-scoped rules for repairing them (equal priority, relaxed user-prompt scope only for those ids, charter/invariants still binding, code-first over test-placating). <!--#380f0198103e8444-->
- `_extract_failure_reason` (function) — Extracts a brief failure reason string for a given test id from pytest's short summary output, falling back to a generic message. <!--#8b7946881d8e5999-->
- `_report_pre_existing_issues` (function) — Files inherited (pre-implement baseline) test failures as a single medium-priority A-class discovery issue, relying on the caller for the once-per-flow guard. <!--#11f4592b36f9fb6f-->
- `_is_timeout_result` (function) — Classifies a command result as a timeout-class failure via the structured flag, stderr marker, or -1 returncode sentinel, short-circuiting to False for any passing run. <!--#5cf69f14034df1cf-->
- `_run_command_with_timeout_retry` (function) — Runs a command and, on a timeout-class failure only, retries it once in place (without incrementing the fix iteration), returning the result and whether a retry occurred. <!--#118ae307f8169959-->
- `_run_command` (function) — Runs a single test command via subprocess.Popen with a live dot progress indicator and enforced timeout, guards against recursive invocation via the SE3_TEST_RUNNING env sentinel, and returns a result dict using distinct returncodes for timeouts (-1) versus spawn failures (-2). <!--#6cdfdd9d2d838026-->
- `_classify_results` (function) — Splits parsed test ids into new_tests vs regression buckets (passed/failed) based on whether each id matches the implement step's added test files. <!--#1198d5758658cb17-->
- `_iter_pytest_per_test_results` (function) — Extracts ordered, pair-deduplicated `(test_id, status)` tuples from both serial and pytest-xdist verbose per-test lines, so classification and the critical-test gate work identically under parallel runs. <!--#2202b18cd63eb850-->
- `_parse_test_ids` (function) — Parses per-test `(test_id, passed)` results from runner output, trying pytest (serial and xdist) first, then jest, then go test formats. <!--#9619a4c5d4c03adb-->
- `_parse_skipped_test_ids` (function) — Returns the deduplicated, in-order list of SKIPPED test IDs from pytest verbose output (serial or xdist per-test lines only, not the `-rs` short summary). <!--#86d4d925ab8874eb-->
- `_critical_pattern_matches` (function) — Returns whether a critical-test pattern matches a test id by substring (covering exact and prefix forms). <!--#ec1772ef7be60c0f-->
- `_detect_critical_failures` (function) — Detects critical acceptance tests that were skipped or silently un-collected/missing (which would otherwise exit 0 falsely green), returning the skipped and missing lists. <!--#37c95ee988a1a3c4-->
- `_is_pytest_command` (function) — Heuristic check for whether a command invokes pytest (bare, path-suffixed, or via python -m pytest). <!--#daec89699f707a0a-->
- `_ensure_verbose_pytest` (function) — Appends -v to a pytest command when critical tests are configured but no verbose flag is present, so per-test SKIPPED lines become parseable (warning if the command isn't pytest). <!--#a56631f4701dbfd3-->
- `_has_numprocesses_flag` (function) — Predicate detecting whether a command already pins an xdist worker count in any accepted spelling (`-n 4`, `-n4`, `-nauto`, `--numprocesses[=]N`). <!--#0d1a0d00b333271c-->
- `_has_dist_flag` (function) — Predicate detecting whether a command already pins an xdist `--dist` distribution mode. <!--#a8a7280006b17bc9-->
- `_render_parallel_workers` (function) — Renders a validated `test.parallel` config value as the string passed to xdist's `-n` argument (`auto` for strings, the number otherwise). <!--#a720e5330e9f17a4-->
- `_apply_parallel` (function) — Appends `-n <workers>` and `--dist loadgroup` to the primary pytest command when `test.parallel` is set, leaving non-pytest commands, user-pinned flags, and configured phases untouched. <!--#7db00031805b1e56-->
- `XdistUnavailableError` (class) — Exception signalling that pytest-xdist is missing from the environment that runs the tests, carrying a message plus an install `remediation` line so the failure reaches the human rather than the fix loop. <!--#191e239348fb333c-->
  - `XdistUnavailableError.__init__` (method) — Stores the error `message` and optional `remediation` install line on the exception. <!--#5dda7167c08a236e-->
  - `XdistUnavailableError.__str__` (method) — Renders the exception as the message followed by the remediation line when one is present. <!--#a83f335597cc443a-->
- `_pytest_module_launcher` (function) — Returns the launcher prefix of a `<launcher> -m pytest ...` command (the only shape that names the interpreter actually running the tests), or `None` for other command shapes. <!--#4deefe1442b4c6a7-->
- `_preflight_xdist` (function) — Probes `<launcher> -c "import xdist"` in `project_root` before any test runs and raises `XdistUnavailableError` on a genuine import failure, treating unrunnable or unrelated probe failures as inconclusive. <!--#763e84d38176357d-->
- `_is_missing_xdist_result` (function) — Post-hoc detector deciding whether a failed run is really "pytest doesn't know about -n", requiring the unrecognized-argument message plus no parsed results and pytest's usage-error exit code to avoid swallowing real regressions. <!--#2a58e46d4697f7bd-->
- `_xdist_unavailable_error` (function) — Builds the single localized `XdistUnavailableError` shared by the pre-flight and post-hoc paths, with a pasteable `pip install pytest-xdist` command derived from the user's own launcher prefix when known. <!--#246e10afb5a4b4c9-->
- `_resolve_cwd` (function) — Resolves a phase's optional cwd to an absolute path relative to the project root. <!--#df0454357359e938-->
- `_detect_test_command` (function) — Auto-detects the test command from project marker files (pyproject/pytest.ini → pytest, package.json → npm, Cargo.toml → cargo, go.mod → go), defaulting to pytest. <!--#2ffafee5e990e5d8-->
- `_record_test_history` (function) — Records synthetic prompt/response entries for a test run (commands, per-phase pass/fail, and truncated stdout/stderr tails for failures) into the chat-history system so test results persist in tianluo/history/ across worktree isolation and fix-loop iterations. <!--#802b99aa63b3d27b-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/steps/test_discovery_recency.py` (python) — Colocated unit-test module for the discovery round-0 recency helpers, verifying that `_collect_session_summaries`, `_collect_recent_commits`, and `_gather_recency_context` correctly extract/rank/format recent work-summary excerpts and git commit subjects, and that this recency block is injected into the discovery prompt only on round zero. <!--#e0421bf510cedd21|d0914f7f569a3147-->
- `_write_summary` (function) — Test helper that writes a well-formed `summary-{flow_id}.md` work-summary file (with header, flow ID, task, and body) into the `tianluo/state` directory under a project root. <!--#b3c9cf5a035b2891-->
- `_git` (function) — Test helper that runs a git subcommand in the given directory, capturing output and raising on non-zero exit. <!--#b62f856133927749-->
- `_init_repo` (function) — Test helper that initializes a git repo and sets a test user name/email in the given directory. <!--#26d1dd0001999960-->
- `test_collect_summaries_extracts_task_and_first_paragraph` (function) — Asserts `_collect_session_summaries` extracts the task line and only the first paragraph after the `---` divider, excluding later body text. <!--#609b7a3475972c81-->
- `test_collect_summaries_truncates_long_task_line` (function) — Asserts an overly long task line is truncated to `_RECENCY_TASK_MAX_CHARS` with an ellipsis in the collected excerpt. <!--#f877933c066213a7-->
- `test_collect_summaries_hard_caps_each_excerpt` (function) — Asserts a huge first paragraph cannot push an excerpt past the `_RECENCY_SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS` per-entry cap. <!--#f6b8f08d4753098a-->
- `test_collect_summaries_returns_most_recent_three` (function) — Asserts the collector returns the three most-recent summaries ordered by filename timestamp descending. <!--#790a3c98564d4f08-->
- `test_collect_summaries_timestamped_outranks_nonconforming_name` (function) — Regression test asserting that `_collect_session_summaries` ranks a genuinely recent timestamped summary above an older, oddly-named non-conforming file that would otherwise win a naive reverse-filename sort. <!--#3244f17f7c2050a1-->
- `test_collect_summaries_recent_nonconforming_outranks_old_timestamped` (function) — Regression test verifying that a freshly-written non-conforming summary (newest mtime) ranks ahead of older timestamped summaries, confirming filename timestamps and mtime fallbacks share the same epoch scale. <!--#3c4b910a99c13490-->
- `test_collect_summaries_fewer_than_three` (function) — Asserts the collector returns a single excerpt when fewer than three summaries exist. <!--#96af4e40c7117f37-->
- `test_collect_summaries_ignores_json_siblings` (function) — Test confirming `_collect_session_summaries` ignores non-`.md` sibling files such as `summary-*.json` and returns an empty list. <!--#8c463bd6cad91a09-->
- `test_collect_summaries_no_files_returns_empty` (function) — Test ensuring `_collect_session_summaries` returns an empty list without raising when the `tianluo/state` directory does not exist. <!--#b8d50f4cabe00a86-->
- `test_collect_commits_filters_merges_and_returns_subjects_only` (function) — Asserts `_collect_recent_commits` returns commit subjects only, excluding merge commits and body lines. <!--#f18dded05cbfd397-->
- `test_collect_commits_respects_limit` (function) — Asserts the commit collector honors its `limit` argument, returning at most that many commits. <!--#e7a766133bb608f1-->
- `test_collect_commits_no_commits_returns_empty` (function) — Asserts the commit collector returns an empty list for an initialized repo with no commits. <!--#0bcd885269b4088f-->
- `test_collect_commits_non_git_returns_empty` (function) — Asserts the commit collector returns an empty list (no raise) when the directory is not a git repo. <!--#0605d0ac18369d86-->
- `test_gather_recency_both_sections` (function) — Asserts `_gather_recency_context` emits both the session-summaries and commits subsections when both data sources exist. <!--#bdebed087d49f331-->
- `test_gather_recency_only_summaries` (function) — Asserts the recency block includes only the summaries subsection when there are summaries but no commits. <!--#b1e17cc937383435-->
- `test_gather_recency_only_commits` (function) — Asserts the recency block includes only the commits subsection when there are commits but no summaries. <!--#6ac98e676da175f9-->
- `test_gather_recency_empty_returns_empty_string` (function) — Asserts `_gather_recency_context` returns an empty string when neither summaries nor a git repo are present. <!--#0cc410273b439aa6-->
- `_FakeCaller` (class) — Test double for `LLMCaller` that records each prompt it receives and returns a minimal valid discovery JSON instead of making a real LLM call. <!--#ec2efd6a2ed3f642-->
  - `_FakeCaller.__init__` (method) — Initializes the fake caller, accepting any args and setting an empty `last_raw_result`. <!--#12a36b3cf5d5c3b0-->
  - `_FakeCaller.call` (method) — Records the prompt on the class-level list and returns a canned question-mode discovery JSON response. <!--#70c9b0f319aff832-->
- `_make_flow_and_step` (function) — Test helper that builds lightweight `SimpleNamespace` stand-ins for a flow and a discovery-type step used to drive discovery-round tests. <!--#db4e8cdbf98ce5b7-->
- `_run_round` (function) — Test helper that drives `discovery._run_discovery_round` with the recency-context gatherer stubbed to a sentinel and `LLMCaller` mocked, returning the prompt captured by the fake caller. <!--#cb8fd36e32151159-->
- `test_recency_injected_on_round_zero` (function) — Asserts the recency context block is injected into the discovery prompt on round zero alongside the per-round project context. <!--#0f3d3d682f26fcfe-->
- `test_recency_not_injected_after_round_zero` (function) — Asserts the recency block is omitted on rounds after zero while per-round project context still appears. <!--#675a59625c307eca-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/steps/test_project_root_resolution.py` (python) — Colocated engine test module covering the shared resolve_flow_project_root three-level priority resolver (context['project_root'] → change_path.parent → Path.cwd(), plus the bare-flow None-state fallback) and a regression for the WebUI "first message/reply invisible" bug, verifying that worktree-mode discovery round-1 writes its chat history under the worktree root from context rather than the process cwd (falling back to cwd when no context is set). <!--#9310db46cd23beb7|6bec68c73d5fea0d-->
- `test_context_project_root_wins_over_cwd_and_change_path` (function) — Unit test asserting that a set context['project_root'] takes priority over both the process cwd and a present change_path in resolve_flow_project_root. <!--#ed547e11267218e8-->
- `test_change_path_used_when_context_missing` (function) — Unit test asserting that resolve_flow_project_root falls back to change_path.parent when context['project_root'] is absent. <!--#172a0029e9117f90-->
- `test_cwd_used_when_context_and_change_path_missing` (function) — Unit test asserting that resolve_flow_project_root falls back to Path.cwd() when neither context value nor change_path is present. <!--#27ad066cdd6d7a67-->
- `test_bare_flow_with_no_state_falls_back_to_cwd` (function) — Unit test asserting that a bare flow with flow.state set to None does not raise and resolves to the process cwd. <!--#6f84496a9553c44c-->
- `test_empty_context_value_falls_through` (function) — Unit test asserting that an empty-string context['project_root'] is treated as absent and resolution falls through to change_path.parent. <!--#3fa4d11697eabdb3-->
- `_FakeLLMCaller` (class) — A test double replacing LLMCaller that records prompt and response to chat_history under its constructed project_root (like the real caller) then returns a canned discovery question-mode JSON response, avoiding any real subprocess or LLM. <!--#6d038a81d9c0d4a3-->
  - `_FakeLLMCaller.__init__` (method) — Constructor capturing the project_root, flow_id, step_id, and step_type on the fake caller and initializing last_raw_result. <!--#081585caec273000-->
  - `_FakeLLMCaller.call` (method) — Mirrors the real caller's write side by recording the prompt and an empty response into chat_history under self.project_root, then returns a fixed question-mode discovery JSON string and stores it in last_raw_result. <!--#29d384facbba97d6-->
- `_make_discovery_flow` (function) — Helper that builds a discovery-step FlowInstance with an optional context['project_root'], a None change_path, and seeded discovery inputs to reproduce the bug-triggering flow shape. <!--#c1089f024d7f7aa0-->
- `test_discovery_round1_history_lands_in_worktree_not_cwd` (function) — Regression test asserting that a worktree-mode discovery round-1 writes its chat history under the worktree root (not the process cwd pinned to the main checkout), and pauses in question mode. <!--#dfb5c47ee692e47b-->
- `test_discovery_round1_falls_back_to_cwd_without_context` (function) — Compatibility test verifying that with no context['project_root'] and no change_path, discovery round-1 history falls back to being written under the process cwd. <!--#9999f99c8fea14f8-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/steps/test_version_reconcile.py` (python) — Pytest suite for the merge-side version reconcile() core, exercising the deterministic SemVer bump channel (including max-bump, no-substance no-op, and changelog-forces-patch cases), the stubbed custom-rules LLM channel, annotated-tag creation and failure handling, every branch of no-regression validation, changelog merging, operator-edit replay, git-timeout-to-ReconcileError mapping, and idempotent/no-op re-entry. <!--#48e8927bbb7624c0|2962dfe2b4afed55-->
- `_git` (function) — Test helper that runs a git subcommand against a given repo root and returns the completed process. <!--#9f1bc200ef078687-->
- `_make_project` (function) — Fixture helper that builds a git-initialized project with committed pyproject.toml and VERSIONS.md at a given version. <!--#3a3b7320976c668e-->
- `_put_intent` (function) — Helper that writes a VersionIntent for a flow id into the project's version-intent store. <!--#ec8080377cc6ca71-->
- `_tag_body` (function) — Test helper that reads an annotated git tag object with `git cat-file -p` and returns just its message body. <!--#0f27da8c876e0e44-->
- `test_deterministic_max_bump_applied` (function) — Asserts the deterministic channel applies the maximum bump across pending intents (patch+minor → minor), writes the new version, and creates an annotated tag on the reconcile commit with the expected message. <!--#016435fea812dff2-->
- `test_deterministic_no_bump_no_substance_leaves_version_unchanged` (function) — Verifies an intent with no bump and no changelog substance leaves the version unchanged yet still consumes the intent and creates a reconcile commit. <!--#0f950607343703d2-->
- `test_deterministic_changelog_substance_without_bump_hint_forces_patch` (function) — Regression guard that an intent carrying a changelog note but no bump_type still forces a patch bump so the note is filed rather than silently dropped. <!--#2c7df6a37a279ccd-->
- `test_compute_deterministic_pure` (function) — Unit-tests the pure compute_deterministic function for a major-bump computation. <!--#702fddb15b4c3b30-->
- `test_deterministic_major_creates_tag` (function) — Asserts a major bump produces the next major version and an annotated tag pointing at the reconcile commit. <!--#25a1d95045d02543-->
- `test_deterministic_patch_does_not_create_tag` (function) — Asserts a patch bump raises the version but creates no tag. <!--#ded5f524bbb893af-->
- `test_changelog_entries_merged_under_final` (function) — Asserts changelog bullets from multiple intents are merged under the single final version in VERSIONS.md. <!--#f237e4a16bf56a7c-->
- `test_operator_edit_survives_residue_reset_timeout` (function) — Regression test asserting that a git stall during the crash-residue reset window still reaches the operator-edit reattach, so an uncommitted README edit is replayed rather than silently lost. <!--#76354bb9eebdcd22-->
- `test_reattach_git_timeout_surfaces_as_reconcile_error` (function) — Test that a git stall inside the finally-block reattach's 3-way `git merge-file` surfaces as a typed ReconcileError instead of a raw TimeoutExpired escaping reconcile(). <!--#a55913777b05b9b8-->
- `test_prepass_git_timeout_surfaces_as_reconcile_error` (function) — Test that a git stall in the read-only replayability pre-pass (before the try/finally) is also mapped to a typed ReconcileError rather than escaping untyped. <!--#175b2535d7a7c23d-->
- `test_empty_changelog_still_recorded_in_versions_md` (function) — Asserts a reconcile with no changelog bullets still records the released version header so the anti-collision historical set includes it. <!--#ca096198545d3075-->
- `test_custom_rules_channel_uses_llm_output` (function) — Test that a project with tianluo/version-rules.md routes reconcile through the custom-rules LLM channel, honoring the LLM's date-style version, tag decision, and change-anchored prompt. <!--#d1f3e199bb35d35f-->
- `test_custom_rules_is_tag_false_does_not_create_tag` (function) — Test that when the custom-rules LLM returns is_tag=false, reconcile records the version but creates no tag. <!--#70cf2fa8e56110c3-->
- `test_tag_failure_raises_reconcile_error` (function) — Test that a VersionTagError from create_annotated_version_tag is wrapped into a ReconcileError naming the failed tag. <!--#1a6c863f90107c97-->
- `test_noop_after_tag_failure_does_not_create_missing_tag` (function) — Test that after a tag failure (recoverable only manually), a later re-run with no outstanding intents completes as a no-op and refuses to self-heal by creating the missing tag. <!--#f30ef2c121f64275-->
- `test_tag_failure_error_names_tag_and_reconcile_commit` (function) — Test that a tag-creation failure's ReconcileError message includes the tag name, reconcile commit hash, and exit code so an operator can hand-create the tag. <!--#265954546cf43b35-->
- `test_reconcile_commit_hash_read_failure_raises` (function) — Test that a tag-owing bump whose post-commit reconcile-commit hash cannot be read fails loud (ReconcileError) rather than silently skipping the tag. <!--#c4daed200813f549-->
- `test_no_tag_bump_survives_unreadable_reconcile_hash` (function) — Test that a non-tagging patch bump tolerates an unreadable reconcile-commit hash and still completes, since the sha's only consumer is the (absent) tag block. <!--#0f5d57d701f34e11-->
- `test_unscoped_noop_does_not_resurrect_deleted_historical_tag` (function) — Asserts a no-op reconcile leaves an older tag the operator deliberately deleted deleted, rather than re-creating it from history. <!--#10f16a8af073ff7b-->
- `test_unscoped_noop_survives_historical_tag_collision` (function) — Asserts the no-op path still succeeds when an older version tag has been rewritten to point at an unrelated commit. <!--#cf260249a599443e-->
- `test_custom_rules_empty_response_raises` (function) — Test that an empty LLM response in the custom-rules channel raises ReconcileError. <!--#609941d102942c39-->
- `test_validate_rejects_numeric_regression` (function) — Asserts validate_no_regression rejects a final version numerically below the current version. <!--#7297728cb46bf5c5-->
- `test_validate_rejects_no_advance` (function) — Asserts validate_no_regression rejects a final version equal to the current when a bump was declared. <!--#1e3d5ea47ec31515-->
- `test_validate_rejects_historical_collision` (function) — Asserts validate_no_regression rejects a final version that collides with a previously released historical version. <!--#d62357b889bb3793-->
- `test_validate_rejects_nonsemver_under_default_channel` (function) — Asserts validate_no_regression raises ReconcileError for a non-SemVer string under the default channel. <!--#af54bcb90265a2f6-->
- `test_validate_accepts_forward_bump` (function) — Asserts validate_no_regression accepts a legitimate forward version advance. <!--#63cb7fcc6d1723dc-->
- `test_validate_custom_rules_rejects_unchanged` (function) — Asserts validate_no_regression rejects an unchanged version even under the custom-rules channel. <!--#80a989d1bc501ca4-->
- `test_validate_custom_rules_accepts_build_metadata_only_advance` (function) — Asserts the custom-rules channel accepts a build-metadata-only advance that SemVer would treat as equal. <!--#24c9cdaa2e30c76b-->
- `test_validate_default_channel_still_rejects_build_metadata_only` (function) — Asserts the default SemVer channel still rejects a build-metadata-only change as a non-advance. <!--#6e3a78128a851894-->
- `test_reconcile_rejects_llm_regression` (function) — Test that an LLM-proposed version lower than the base version raises VersionRegressionError. <!--#3e4f009f246c9555-->
- `test_reconcile_idempotent_reentry` (function) — Verifies a second reconcile run is a no-op that does not double-bump the version. <!--#782278da6085761f-->
- `test_reconcile_commit_carries_trailer` (function) — Asserts the reconcile commit message carries the Version-Reconcile-Session trailer with consumed flow ids. <!--#8f8f16da9b046912-->
- `test_reconcile_noop_when_no_intents` (function) — Asserts reconcile with no pending intents reports the no-op channel, leaves the current version untouched, and creates no tag. <!--#152e3c6c9da8d713-->
- `test_version_reconcile_handler_outputs_tag_fields` (function) — Test that version_reconcile_handler surfaces a ReconcileResult's tag fields (is_tag/tag_name/tag_created) into the step's flat outputs and nested reconcile_result. <!--#2d4ec51c9addccda-->
