- `test_reconcile_runs_on_already_ancestor_shape` (function) — Verifies reconcile still computes and writes a version when an intent file is present but the git merge produced no merge commit. <!--#1548ef8ec800d8e8-->
- `test_historical_versions_parsed` (function) — Asserts historical_versions parses the committed version out of VERSIONS.md. <!--#97cee8c2fe925242-->
- `_make_script_project` (function) — Helper fixture building a git project whose version lives in pyproject.toml and is bumped via tianluo/scripts/version.py, auto-activating script mode. <!--#6b4a995cc989fa4e-->
- `test_script_project_fixture_activates_script_mode` (function) — Anchor test verifying the script-project fixture truly trips script mode (detect_version_file returns the script) and that the script's get/set round-trips pyproject.toml, guarding the script-mode regression suite from passing for the wrong reason. <!--#d63e66d3e00cfd30-->
- `test_script_mode_bump_lands_in_reconcile_commit` (function) — Verifies that in script mode the version bump is recorded inside the reconcile commit itself and leaves no uncommitted working-tree dirt on pyproject.toml. <!--#18bee70a8ade7f9c-->
- `test_script_mode_operator_dirt_on_version_file_preserved` (function) — Checks that an operator's unrelated uncommitted edit on the version file is neutralized before the bump (so the bump lands clean in the commit) and replayed afterward (so the operator's edit survives in the working tree). <!--#c1ea432393a620f4-->
- `test_fail_loud_when_version_file_missed_by_commit` (function) — Test the git-layer check: when the script-written version file is dropped from the commit pathspec, reconcile raises a ReconcileError naming the stray file with a recovery hint. <!--#35b9423d0e41b821-->
- `test_fail_loud_when_committed_version_value_wrong` (function) — Test the semantic-layer check: when the committed version file's readback value differs from final_version, reconcile raises a mismatch ReconcileError. <!--#053c0f4b63b12c15-->
- `test_fail_loud_checks_skipped_on_noop` (function) — Confirms the no-bump no-op path (docs-only intent, no versionable change) settles final == current version without firing the fail-loud checks, leaving the version file untouched and the tree clean. <!--#0dc015c5e382dfda-->
- `test_fail_loud_when_written_set_measures_empty` (function) — Test that an empty measured written_set (which would skip the git clean-check and let the semantic readback vacuously pass) is treated as unverifiable and raises ReconcileError. <!--#8b66a7c8f17a9bdc-->
- `test_written_set_diff_measurement_fault_raises` (function) — Test that a git fault while measuring the before/after diff bracket in _write_final_version raises rather than degrading to a silently-wrong empty set. <!--#31207a348534e9a6-->
- `_make_unicode_script_project` (function) — Helper fixture building a script-mode project whose version lives in a non-ASCII-named file (tianluo/版本.txt) to reproduce the quotePath octal-escape encoding path. <!--#89ba5ad48e5a85ba-->
- `test_script_mode_bump_lands_when_version_file_is_non_ascii` (function) — Test that a script-mode bump to a non-ASCII-named version file lands in the reconcile commit with a clean working tree, proving the `-z` diff measurement closes the core.quotePath vacuous-pass hole. <!--#515eba315fc1b729-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/steps/test_with_fail_loop.py` (python) — A test-only step handler module that deliberately injects a bug into a target project's calculator on the first test run (tracked via a persisted run-count file) so tests fail, then runs pytest normally on later runs to exercise and verify the engine's fix-loop mechanism. <!--#f3f9f64eb83d8a46|8fff20a98050d566-->
- `test_handler_with_fail_loop` (function) — A test step handler that deliberately injects a temporary bug on its first run (tracked via a run-count file) so that pytest fails and the fix loop is exercised, then runs tests normally on subsequent runs, recording pass/fail results into the step's outputs. <!--#c3240eb4fe972be8-->
- `_get_run_count` (function) — Reads the persisted run count from the tracker JSON file, returning 0 if missing or unreadable. <!--#7a98a6120b25eac3-->
- `_increment_run_count` (function) — Increments the run count and writes it back to the tracker file, returning the new count. <!--#bc0552dcc5f0422e-->
- `_introduce_temporary_bug` (function) — Edits the target project's calculator.py to replace addition with subtraction, deliberately breaking tests on the first run. <!--#46937d61991f40e5-->
- `_run_pytest` (function) — Runs `pytest -v` in the project root via subprocess and returns the completed process result. <!--#675f6b2ee4815506-->
- `reset_test_tracker` (function) — Deletes the run-count tracker file to reset state before starting a new test. <!--#da1a842a593e2517-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/steps/version_analyze.py` (python) — Step module that drives LLM-based next-version analysis — formatting session changes, commits, and verification results into a prompt (optionally overridden by a project's tianluo/version-rules.md), validating the parsed result into a normalized suggested_version/bump_type/is_tag decision, and either returning it authoritatively for synchronous flows or writing a provisional VersionIntent onto the flow branch for worktree flows. <!--#585c00a8ef17952c|96362c629651a784-->
- `version_analyze_handler` (function) — Step handler that asks the LLM to decide the project's next version from the session's changes, verification results, and optional project-specific version rules, emitting an authoritative `suggested_version` for synchronous flows or a branch-committed VersionIntent for worktree flows. <!--#dd144ed611ff1456-->
- `_emit_version_intent` (function) — Builds a VersionIntent from the analysis result and writes it to `tianluo/version-intents/` on the flow branch (exposing only a `provisional_suggested_version`, never the authoritative one), letting write failures propagate so the merge-side `version_reconcile` never silently loses the bump. <!--#9e8a0f40a04a8f03-->
- `_build_change_summary` (function) — Composes the intent's free-form change digest by reusing the already-formatted Changes/Verification prompt sections, skipping empty ones. <!--#eb1c1848d33036e1-->
- `_read_version_rules_file` (function) — Reads the optional project-specific tianluo/version-rules.md Markdown file (truncating past VERSION_RULES_MAX_BYTES and swallowing all read errors as None) so it can be injected verbatim into the version_analyze prompt to override the default SemVer rules. <!--#868857a3c7e663b7-->
- `_version_bumping_enabled` (function) — Returns whether the project has version bumping enabled by mirroring the commit step's version_config.enabled gate, defaulting to enabled on any config-load fault. <!--#c2b12563eb3d7b45-->
- `_get_current_version` (function) — Helper that reads the project's current version string via `VersionBumper` (respecting disabled config and missing version files), returning an `"unknown"`-style fallback on any failure. <!--#f949f142a357e75e-->
- `_format_changes` (function) — Renders the implement step's changed-files and implementation-group data into a markdown block for the prompt's "Changes Made" section. <!--#6c7938dd04d95393-->
- `_format_session_commits` (function) — Renders implement-stage commits already landed on the main branch as a capped, file-folded markdown list so the prompt can treat them as the baseline-excluded session changes. <!--#916117384c2b9364-->
- `_format_verification` (function) — Renders the verification step's pass/summary/issue results into a markdown block for the prompt's "Verification Results" section. <!--#2ae548847100d2c2-->
- `_parse_response` (function) — Extracts the JSON object from the raw LLM response, requiring a `suggested_version` key, and hands it to `_validate_result`. <!--#402c4b4db481597b-->
- `_validate_result` (function) — Validates and normalizes the parsed LLM result, requiring a non-empty suggested_version, defaulting/sanitizing auxiliary fields (bump_type, confidence, versions_changes), and computing is_tag either from the LLM under custom rules or from a SemVer version-advance policy by default. <!--#c9b7b96ac55efa82-->
- `_fallback_commit_message` (function) — Builds a fallback commit-subject line from the task type and description (first sentence, 72-char capped) when the LLM omits or fails to produce one. <!--#8502a2c669ba9cb5-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/steps/version_reconcile.py` (python) — The second merge-side step handler of a worktree flow: a thin adapter over the reconcile() library that re-derives and applies the flow's final project version at merge time against master's current version, resolving the main-checkout root strictly, handling the by-design no-intent, human-review revision-undo, missing-intent, and version-disabled cases while recording ReconcileResult on step.outputs and mapping faults to a resumable FAILED. <!--#b2111c9b216367cf|91f78548c8bea3cb-->
- `_resolve_merge_root` (function) — Resolves the main-checkout root that reconcile writes to, returning step.cwd if set and otherwise strictly probing the main repo from the flow's project_root, raising MergeCheckoutResolutionError rather than silently degrading to the isolation worktree. <!--#4442023c0c711f99-->
- `version_reconcile_handler` (function) — Derives and applies the final version at merge time by calling reconcile() scoped to this flow's own intent, short-circuiting flows without a VERSION_ANALYZE step, undoing a rejected prior reconcile commit on the human-review revision path, guarding against silently dropped intents, and mapping the ReconcileResult onto step.outputs as COMPLETED or FAILED. <!--#5dbc4fc029ea16ff-->

## `src/tianluo/engine/utils/` — The engine's utils subpackage, currently housing a robust JSON parser (`json_parser.py`) that extracts and repairs JSON payloads from messy LLM responses (stream-json/NDJSON, markdown-fenced, or embedded) via a lenient repair chain and key validation. <!--#cf8b92c9acea31cb|2c490044f02a9400-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/utils/__init__.py` (python) — Empty package initializer marking `src/tianluo/engine/utils/` as the utils subpackage of the engine. <!--#e3b0c44298fc1c14|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/engine/utils/json_parser.py` (python) — A robust JSON parser for LLM responses that handles stream-json/NDJSON, markdown-fenced, and embedded JSON, extracting the payload and running it through a repair chain (trailing commas, unescaped quotes, single quotes, truncation-closing) before validating required keys, and exposes lenient looks_like_json predicates. <!--#41772d21d16224bb|d655d5bc22787606-->
- `parse_json_response` (function) — Public entry point that parses JSON from an LLM response, collecting text from stream-json assistant messages when multi-line, otherwise parsing the response directly. <!--#bfc1ed6667139fbc-->
- `_extract_and_parse_json` (function) — Helper that extracts a JSON string from text, parses it through the repair chain, and validates that required keys are present. <!--#70254293e3b33aea-->
- `_extract_json_string` (function) — Locates the JSON payload within text by stripping tool-preview lines, unwrapping markdown code blocks, and falling back to first-brace-to-last-brace or trailing-object extraction. <!--#20dcab890ff12010-->
- `_extract_trailing_json_string` (function) — Walks backwards from the last '}' to find its matching '{' (respecting strings and escaped quotes) to extract the rightmost complete JSON object. <!--#ad42bc21e87f46a3-->
- `_count_unescaped_quotes` (function) — Utility that counts unescaped double quotes in a string, skipping backslash-escaped characters. <!--#8be78ab15a58c787-->
- `_repair_unescaped_quotes` (function) — Iteratively escapes unescaped interior double quotes in JSON string values using json.loads error positions to fix LLM quoting mistakes. <!--#c7f178fd4cf6cc12-->
- `_repair_json` (function) — Repairs common LLM JSON errors by removing trailing commas, converting single quotes to double quotes, and closing truncated structures. <!--#fedcf1c86d1564bc-->
- `_close_truncated_json` (function) — Attempts to make length-truncated JSON parseable by closing open strings and balancing unclosed objects and arrays. <!--#cfd0092566cd7de7-->
- `_validate_keys` (function) — Checks that the parsed data is a dict containing all required keys (trivially true when no keys are required). <!--#a69714e9aba6d385-->
- `_try_parse_with_repairs` (function) — Shared parsing core that tries strict json.loads then escalates through the structural and quote repair chain, returning the parsed object or None. <!--#2529ab7af10ffe44-->
- `looks_like_json_object` (function) — Lenient predicate returning whether text parses as a JSON dict after the full repair chain, mirroring parse_json_response's dict-only semantics. <!--#5fa87d39d7511b7c-->
- `looks_like_json` (function) — Lenient predicate returning whether text parses as any valid JSON value via the repair chain, with a strict fallback to distinguish literal `null` from failure. <!--#9155397a29d59ee8-->

## `src/tianluo/i18n/` — The CLI's internationalization package: it holds per-locale JSON catalogs under `locales/`, a `loader.py` that discovers/caches those flat `key -> str` catalogs and normalizes locale codes to a supported code (base `en-US`), and an `__init__.py` that lazily resolves the active UI language via the SE3_LANG → project/global config → system-locale → en-US precedence chain and exposes the never-raising `t`/`t_status` translation helpers. <!--#614bf7579dab306f|60f139f2f1f13952-->

### `src/tianluo/i18n/__init__.py` (python) — Public i18n entry point that resolves the active UI language through the SE3_LANG → config → system-locale → en-US precedence chain (with set/get/bind/reset seams) and exposes the `t` translation helper plus status-token key normalization and translation. <!--#27ed4a366bcc9a4a|d32ddf1b66a7afbb-->
- `_decide_explicit` (function) — Resolves an explicit language request (from env var or config value), returning None for unset/empty values so resolution falls through, but mapping any set-but-unsupported value (including non-string YAML types) to BASE_LANGUAGE so a lower-priority tier can't silently override the user's explicit choice. <!--#0065f3e2ba662a28-->
- `_safe_cwd` (function) — Returns the process working directory, or None if it cannot be read (e.g. deleted worktree), so language resolution never raises. <!--#cae38b9c8441a6ba-->
- `resolve_language` (function) — Resolves the effective UI language by walking the precedence chain — SE3_LANG env override, merged project/user config, then system locale — falling back to BASE_LANGUAGE, with explicit tiers authoritative when set and only unset tiers falling through. <!--#3db5cde2e7930d2b-->
- `set_language` (function) — Explicitly sets the active UI language (unknown/None falls back to en-US) and returns the effective code. <!--#d718115194fcaba5-->
- `get_language` (function) — Returns the active UI language, lazily resolving it on first access. <!--#384ce0f141f206ed-->
- `bind_project_root` (function) — Re-runs language resolution against a command's actual project root, correcting the language cached at import time from the cwd. <!--#44a90f6ef691f7ef-->
- `reset_language` (function) — Test seam that clears the cached _current_language selection so the next resolution runs the full chain from a clean state. <!--#be3cf30aabb38ff4-->
- `t` (function) — Translates a catalog key into the active language with kwargs formatting, falling back through en-US to the raw key and never raising. <!--#c4a5b1943393acaa-->
- `status_key` (function) — Normalizes a status token or Enum into a canonical `status.<snake_case>` catalog key shared by issue, flow and step vocabularies. <!--#23076fd178cdec6f-->
- `t_status` (function) — Translates a status token for display, falling back to the raw token (not the key) when no catalog entry exists. <!--#74736fec0b8d97f9-->

### `src/tianluo/i18n/loader.py` (python) — Backing store for the i18n layer: discovers `<code>.json` locale catalogs in the sibling `locales/` directory via `importlib.resources` (with a filesystem fallback), loads/caches them fail-safe as flat `key -> str` maps, normalizes arbitrary config or system locale codes (`zh_CN.UTF-8`, bare `zh`, non-string YAML scalars) to a supported code, and defines `en-US` as the base fallback language — so adding a language is a pure data drop-in. <!--#7dc478f7375125f8|f2a438a9e2fc75d6-->
- `_iter_locale_resources` (function) — Discovers available translation catalogs by yielding `(language_code, traversable)` pairs for each `<code>.json` under the `locales/` package, preferring `importlib.resources.files` and degrading to a filesystem glob next to this module so lookup works from both wheels and source trees without ever raising on the console-output path. <!--#a859a7539f2c1440-->
- `supported_languages` (function) — Returns the sorted, deliberately uncached list of locale codes found in `locales/`, so dropping in a new language file takes effect without a restart. <!--#5e90534f30a2aa79-->
- `load_catalog` (function) — Loads and caches the flat `key -> str` translation catalog for a locale code, returning `{}` (never raising) when the file is missing, unreadable, or not a JSON object. <!--#de53c8f88213788d-->
- `normalize_language` (function) — Normalizes an arbitrary config or system locale value (e.g. `zh_CN.UTF-8`, `ZH-cn`, bare `zh`, or a non-string YAML scalar) to a supported locale code, or `None` if unsupported. <!--#b36db2217038eae3-->
- `clear_caches` (function) — Test seam that clears the cached catalogs so locale-file mutations are picked up. <!--#7b1436e83f936825-->

## `src/tianluo/i18n/locales/` — The CLI's locale-catalog package, holding an `__init__.py` package marker (needed so `importlib.resources.files` can load the bundles under Python 3.9) alongside per-locale JSON translation catalogs (en-US.json, zh-CN.json) that map dotted i18n keys to user-facing CLI strings with interpolation placeholders. <!--#885108dc39ca5d20|c243487c79b130a8-->

### `src/tianluo/i18n/locales/__init__.py` (python) — Marker module that makes the `locales` directory a regular (non-namespace) package so `importlib.resources.files("tianluo.i18n.locales")` can load the `<code>.json` locale catalogs under Python 3.9, where `files()` rejects namespace packages. <!--#537835b508968030|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/i18n/locales/en-US.json` (json) — The English (en-US) translation catalogue for tianluo: a flat map of ~1,167 dotted message keys to user-facing strings — CLI banners, menus, help text, prompts and errors (`cli.*`), plus engine, history, e2e, end_session, merge, migrate, issue, worktree, status and code_index namespaces — many with `{placeholder}` interpolation slots, mirrored key-for-key by `zh-CN.json`. <!--#68748a8720221ecb|feb3005853066e72-->
- `cli.common.done` (json-key) — Generic English label for a completed operation ("Done"). <!--#91828f63e876c4f2-->
- `cli.common.cancelled` (json-key) — Generic English label shown when an operation is cancelled. <!--#a2947f257eb321ea-->
- `cli.common.error` (json-key) — Generic English "Error" label used across CLI output. <!--#97c63b98f6b3757f-->
- `cli.common.warning` (json-key) — Generic English "Warning" label used across CLI output. <!--#5de54721632ce1a2-->
- `cli.common.yes` (json-key) — Affirmative answer word used in prompts and boolean rendering. <!--#1009a718d1d45cd5-->
- `cli.common.no` (json-key) — Negative answer word used in prompts and boolean rendering. <!--#23c8f99a0e4f6343-->
- `cli.run.starting` (json-key) — Banner shown when a run begins, interpolating the task description. <!--#df0ee805b0631d11-->
- `cli.run.resume_hint` (json-key) — Hint string telling the user how to resume a saved flow with `luo run --resume`. <!--#aea421991ee72117-->
- `cli.run.completed` (json-key) — Message reporting that a run finished, with its elapsed seconds. <!--#7296b17c3fccf3c0-->
- `cli.error.not_a_project` (json-key) — Error shown when the current path has no `tianluo.yaml` and is therefore not a luo project. <!--#3e0e466b10802cb3-->
- `cli.greeting` (json-key) — Sample/demo greeting string used to exercise the i18n interpolation machinery. <!--#c74ca3164cfcacac-->
- `cli.run.choice.select` (json-key) — Prompt asking the user to type a number to select a menu option. <!--#8c043234fdc180ae-->
- `cli.run.choice.enter_between` (json-key) — Validation message telling the user their selection must fall within the offered range. <!--#3a2156944335d9c4-->
- `cli.run.choice.enter_valid` (json-key) — Validation message shown when the selection input is not a number. <!--#63417d735b681f0f-->
- `cli.run.choice.non_interactive` (json-key) — Notice that, with no TTY, a menu option was auto-selected on the user's behalf. <!--#fef1b3890a3fd448-->
- `cli.run.what_to_do` (json-key) — Heading for the top-level run menu asking the user what action to take. <!--#b6c4b1e1c6753ccb-->
- `cli.run.start_new_flow` (json-key) — Menu option label for starting a brand-new flow. <!--#949d8602da8c6ee5-->
- `cli.run.confirm.review_prompt` (json-key) — Prompt asking the user to review a step's output before deciding. <!--#e54461f07c88fe39-->
- `cli.run.confirm.opt_approve` (json-key) — Confirmation-gate option label for approving the step and continuing. <!--#f4be7be64fddf41c-->
- `cli.run.confirm.opt_request_changes` (json-key) — Confirmation-gate option label for requesting changes to the step output. <!--#051456bdd5dbe208-->
- `cli.run.confirm.opt_exit` (json-key) — Confirmation-gate option label for exiting and pausing the flow. <!--#8b94b8a207574364-->
- `cli.run.confirm.feedback_title` (json-key) — Panel title for the free-text feedback input at a confirmation gate. <!--#09017126d3527eb4-->
- `cli.run.confirm.feedback_message` (json-key) — Instructions for entering multi-line change-request feedback, including the finish/cancel keys. <!--#6d010a96c285510e-->
- `cli.run.confirm.approved` (json-key) — Result text shown when the user approves a confirmation gate. <!--#881215dfb3a790be-->

- `end_session.detail.ownership_claim_lost` (json-key) — Detail explaining that a `run.pid` marker reappeared after the liveness check, so archive/cleanup was skipped. <!--#78adaabe059eea6b-->

### `src/tianluo/i18n/locales/zh-CN.json` (json) — Simplified-Chinese (zh-CN) locale bundle for the tianluo CLI, providing translated message strings keyed under namespaces such as cli.common, cli.run (choice prompts, confirmation gates, adjudicate surface listings, interjections), cli.run.resume/marker (flow resume, cross-machine and local state-directory lock errors), and cli.error, many with interpolation placeholders and Rich markup. <!--#39b5fb23279e6e78|cf599377e445cc66-->
- `cli.common.done` (json-key) — Shared CLI label for the word "done" (完成). <!--#493dc211a2941efa-->
- `cli.common.cancelled` (json-key) — Shared CLI label for a cancelled action (已取消). <!--#9199f6d2dd14865b-->
- `cli.common.error` (json-key) — Shared CLI label for the word "error" (错误). <!--#fdd635d7c5cbb2fb-->
- `cli.common.warning` (json-key) — Shared CLI label for the word "warning" (警告). <!--#0759a42085198ea4-->
- `cli.common.yes` (json-key) — Shared CLI label for an affirmative answer (是). <!--#54735afd6c0386ef-->
- `cli.common.no` (json-key) — Shared CLI label for a negative answer (否). <!--#3e844d96300ac538-->
- `cli.run.starting` (json-key) — Message announcing the start of a run, interpolating the task description. <!--#48afa1831398d3e0-->
- `cli.run.completed` (json-key) — Message announcing a completed run with its elapsed seconds. <!--#6f7fe5a9cb666c9b-->
- `cli.error.not_a_project` (json-key) — Simplified-Chinese error message shown when the current directory is not a luo project because no tianluo.yaml was found at the given path. <!--#965edba6ac98ddc9-->
- `cli.greeting` (json-key) — Simple greeting string interpolating a name (demo/sample message key). <!--#f5d9d877e884fcf1-->
- `cli.run.choice.select` (json-key) — Prompt asking the user to pick a numbered choice. <!--#93da4979ed4e3c96-->

- `cli.run.choice.enter_valid` (json-key) — Validation message telling the user to enter a valid number. <!--#0475dd67d92847f1-->

## `src/tianluo/server/` — The optional `tianluo[server]` extra's WebUI Control Plane backend: a FastAPI application that aggregates live state from many dialed-in daemons over the `/ws` WebSocket link (handshake, heartbeats, downlink spawn/respond routing) and exposes it through REST endpoints and a bundled vanilla-JS static frontend, backed by an in-memory owner-scoped aggregated-state layer with lazy history-detail shaping, a thread-safe SQLite `Store` for owners/identities/daemon keys/message history, credential cryptography, and a pluggable fail-closed authentication layer with a break-glass bootstrap-token CLI. <!--#7449efb0d4669552|bc6bd10ac349e119-->

### `src/tianluo/server/__init__.py` (python) — Package init and console-script entry module for the optional `tianluo-server` control-plane backend, exposing `main` (which handles `--version`, the FastAPI-free `bootstrap-token` subcommand, and the `server`-extra check before delegating to `tianluo.server.app.main`) and the deprecated `legacy_main` `se3-server` migration shim removed in 13.0.0. <!--#164e341f85ba1263|9fc4412830bb18e7-->
- `legacy_main` (function) — Deprecated `se3-server` console-script shim that prints a stderr migration notice pointing to `tianluo-server`, then delegates to `main`; removed in 13.0.0. <!--#c4176cc35f5aca2f-->
- `main` (function) — The `tianluo-server` console-script entry point that handles `--version` and the FastAPI-free `bootstrap-token` subcommand early, verifies the optional `server` extra (FastAPI/uvicorn) is importable with an install hint on failure, then delegates to `tianluo.server.app.main`. <!--#6f6367cd5ecde593-->

### `src/tianluo/server/app.py` (python) — Assembles the SE3 central-server FastAPI application — the `/ws` daemon endpoint plus the REST API for machines, flows, projects, uploads, and lazily-fetched history/detail records — and mounts the bundled static frontend with its i18n locale discovery, isolated behind the `tianluo[server]` extra so the core CLI never imports FastAPI. <!--#32efdd05c6365d7f|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/server/bootstrap.py` (python) — A deliberately dependency-light module providing the `tianluo-server bootstrap-token` CLI subcommand that mints the one-time break-glass admin escape-hatch token, persisting only its SHA-256 hash while revealing the plaintext to the console exactly once. <!--#b476dd54ceddbb7e|aa87810d05a4dd59-->
- `issue_breakglass_token` (function) — Mints a break-glass token against a given store, persisting only its hash and returning the (plaintext, token_id) pair with an optional TTL. <!--#43a92d1a8aa0f88a-->
- `print_breakglass_token` (function) — Opens the sqlite store at a path, mints a token, prints it once to a stream (the design-mandated single console reveal), and returns the plaintext. <!--#4e816632366833c2-->
- `_print_banner` (function) — Helper that writes a boxed, one-time console banner displaying a freshly minted break-glass admin token (plaintext, id, optional TTL) plus instructions for redeeming it at the break-glass auth endpoint. <!--#eb3bcc6b464048eb-->
- `main` (function) — Entry point for the dependency-light `tianluo-server bootstrap-token` subcommand that parses --db-path and --ttl args and mints a one-time break-glass admin token without importing FastAPI/uvicorn. <!--#5984d604c8491c75-->

### `src/tianluo/server/crypto.py` (python) — Credential cryptography module for the se3 multi-tenant server, providing slow salted password hashing (argon2id preferred, bcrypt fallback with deferred backend imports), high-entropy token generation with SHA-256 hashed storage, and constant-time comparison plus safe redaction/fingerprint helpers for logging. <!--#94b51872592a5e14|7f035102747c14d4-->
- `PasswordBackendUnavailable` (class) — A RuntimeError subclass raised on the server auth path when neither argon2-cffi nor bcrypt is importable, signalling the tianluo[server] extra is not installed. <!--#4600a69273f14c89-->
- `_argon2_hasher` (function) — Lazily import argon2 and return a PasswordHasher instance, or None if the backend is unavailable. <!--#fc52a7d3aa6dc5df-->
- `_bcrypt_module` (function) — Lazily import and return the bcrypt module, or None if it is unavailable. <!--#307a490487c8b7a8-->
- `_bcrypt_prep` (function) — Normalize a password into a fixed-length, NUL-free bytes value (SHA-256 + base64) to work around bcrypt's 72-byte and NUL-byte limitations. <!--#bb06af56be76fe88-->
- `hash_password` (function) — Hashes a password string with a slow salted algorithm, preferring argon2id and falling back to bcrypt, returning a self-describing PHC/bcrypt-format string and raising PasswordBackendUnavailable when no backend is available. <!--#b108f2d4373b75a7-->
- `verify_password` (function) — Verify a password against a stored hash by dispatching on its algorithm prefix, returning False rather than raising on any mismatch or malformed input. <!--#647d73f726c8eeb8-->
- `token_hash` (function) — Return the hex SHA-256 of a token plaintext for fast, deterministic hashed storage and lookup. <!--#439625ff8bcb39f8-->
- `generate_token` (function) — Generate a high-entropy random token (optionally prefixed) and return its one-time plaintext alongside its storage hash. <!--#4604b91686f646f1-->
- `verify_token_hash` (function) — Constant-time check that a token plaintext hashes to a given stored hash. <!--#1e8b2fd48a378aaa-->
- `const_eq` (function) — Constant-time equality wrapper over hmac.compare_digest that accepts str or bytes and returns False on unsupported types. <!--#0378385214c29b7c-->
- `token_fingerprint` (function) — Return a short, non-reversible SHA-256-derived fingerprint of a secret for safe identification in logs/UI. <!--#07765d495538db1c-->
- `redact` (function) — Return a fixed placeholder for a credential that reveals neither its value nor its length. <!--#593a6a3cb211b8ef-->

### `src/tianluo/server/history_summary.py` (python) — Server-side shaping pass for WebUI history payloads: it walks each addressable record's heavy bodies (`stream_progress` `tool_detail`, `raw_json` tool_use/tool_result blocks, step-event `inputs`), replaces them with header-preserving elision stubs plus `detail_flow`/`detail_version` markers only when the wire saving genuinely exceeds the marker cost, and exposes the helpers the detail endpoint uses to serve the held-back bodies back on demand. <!--#ef9273d415dddbc3|ed55e75e09f40efe-->
- `elide_string` (function) — Builds the standard elision stub for one oversize string, keeping a short head plus its line and character counts so a collapsed header still renders. <!--#10a39820c492e156-->
- `_rough_wire_len` (function) — Approximates a value's JSON wire size (optionally under the spaced encoder via `pad`), bailing out once a cap is exceeded, so shaping decisions never cost a second full serialization. <!--#6bb1bba9b1d1cec2-->
- `_wire_saving` (function) — Reports how many wire bytes are gained by shipping a replacement stub instead of the original, pricing the stub wide and the original narrow so the verdict holds on both the REST and WebSocket legs. <!--#dfa9512fa56891f6-->
- `_lazy_id_cost` (function) — Prices what naming one `tool_use_id` in `lazy_tool_use_ids` (plus its mask character) costs, so a body's saving is charged for its own lazy marker. <!--#e823cc8d4da1345f-->
- `_tail_stub` (function) — Returns the stub marker that stands in for a dropped list tail, shaped like every other elision stub plus an `items` count of what was held back. <!--#f1be898f3ba1bee2-->
- `_tail_wire_len` (function) — Approximates the JSON size of a list's tail without slicing it, stopping once the cap is passed, to decide whether dropping the tail is worth it. <!--#53f2b2f24ceadaea-->
- `_elide_list` (function) — Elides inside a list and, when truncation is enabled, keeps only a JSON-prefix head plus a tail stub — but only when dropping the tail actually pays for the stub. <!--#5adeb6cdda5babb6-->
- `_elide_value` (function) — Recursively replaces oversize bodies in any value with stubs, copying containers only when something below changed and gating every leaf on whether the stub is genuinely smaller. <!--#1a59391ddb6ddda1-->
- `_extract_result_text` (function) — Python mirror of the frontend's `_toolExtractText` walk over a `tool_result` content, so a stub built from it renders the same collapsed header as the original. <!--#4468dc5072aff0ce-->
- `_collapse_result_content` (function) — Replaces an entire `tool_result` content with a single header stub, since the header only ever reads it through `_extract_result_text`. <!--#68c1cf75b9bd537f-->
- `_blocks_of_line` (function) — Unwraps one raw_json line into its message dict and content block list, tolerating both enveloped and bare shapes. <!--#a41ef4282c00897b-->
- `_block_kind` (function) — Returns a block's lowercased `type` string, or empty for anything that is not a dict. <!--#e43b7bc621b98fef-->
- `_result_id` (function) — Reads a tool_result block's tool-use id, accepting either the `tool_use_id` or `toolUseId` spelling. <!--#86a9f9cd4b6b56f5-->
- `_is_error_block` (function) — Tells whether a block reports an error, accepting either the `is_error` or `isError` spelling. <!--#a9c1fe2a4625b2cf-->
- `iter_tool_blocks` (function) — Yields every `tool_use` / `tool_result` in a raw_json list as `(kind, block)` pairs in stream order, matching how the frontend walks it. <!--#cc4367aaef7bdfc6-->
- `_failed_tool_use_ids` (function) — Collects the tool-use ids whose result reported an error, which are exempted from elision because their chips auto-expand. <!--#6ea47a387ed0460c-->
- `_elide_raw_json` (function) — Elides the heavy tool_use inputs and tool_result contents in one record's raw_json, returning the reshaped lines plus the lazy ids, per-id body mask, and net wire saving, while leaving fold-visible and unaddressable bodies inline. <!--#308b1454ea1e4878-->
- `_feed_digest` (function) — Streams a value's content into a hasher incrementally instead of serializing it, since only cross-delivery stability matters, not JSON fidelity. <!--#91c099750cd11b7a-->
- `_detail_version` (function) — Computes a short blake2b digest over the ORIGINAL held-back bodies (step inputs, progress detail, and the lazy tool_use/tool_result blocks) so the browser's address-keyed detail cache is invalidated when a retry rewrites a record in place under the same address. <!--#a74ed06964de8506-->
- `_holder_of` (function) — Returns the container that holds a record's fields (`record["message"]` when an envelope is present, else the record) plus whether an envelope existed, mirroring `normalizeRecord`. <!--#d68b47bb7f171059-->
- `_owner_of` (function) — Resolves which container actually holds a given key under the message-first / envelope-fallback rule, the single lookup both shaping and extraction must use to stay consistent. <!--#919ed44a25746b4c-->
- `_pick` (function) — Reads a record field through the message-first, envelope-fallback lookup. <!--#eb755cb710b2de78-->
- `_record_ordinal` (function) — Returns the record's 0-based physical line number, envelope-first with a `message.ordinal` fallback, or `None` when absent or not an int. <!--#1ac243091f9dc3d4-->
- `record_address` (function) — Returns the record's stable `(step_id, ordinal)` identity used by the detail endpoint, or `None` for a record that cannot be addressed and therefore must keep its bodies inline. <!--#0d219cac88da8ce2-->
- `_step_inputs_target` (function) — For a step event record, locates its effective `inputs` dict using the same resolution order as the frontend's `normalizeRecord` (data.step → message.step → data → record) and returns it together with a `rebuild` closure describing the single container edit that would replace it. <!--#cde1ace988514ae0-->
- `_stub_step_inputs` (function) — Reduces a step snapshot's `inputs` to just the allowlisted `STEP_INPUT_INLINE_KEYS` the card actually renders, keeping the inline remainder after the bulk is held back for lazy fetch. <!--#b6d190ae4ed21410-->
- `_progress_detail_saving` (function) — Computes the wire bytes gained by dropping a `stream_progress` record's `tool_detail`, net of the `tool_detail_lazy` marker that replaces it. <!--#f6c596bdc4ca1968-->
- `_record_marker_cost` (function) — Prices the two per-record markers (`detail_flow` at the flow id's real length and `detail_version`) that any lazified record must carry. <!--#50b14f9a13eff02a-->
- `_summarize_record` (function) — The core shaping pass: for one addressable history record it evaluates the three lazification candidates (stream_progress `tool_detail`, `raw_json` tool bodies, step-event `inputs`), picks whichever combination nets a real wire saving after marker cost, and rewrites the record with stubs plus the `detail_flow`/version markers the browser needs to fetch the bodies back. <!--#6e8924aecb9d34e7-->
- `summarize_history_records` (function) — Entry point that shapes a whole bundle slice uniformly — headers inline, bodies on demand — returning the same list object when nothing needed shaping. <!--#eb1b178e16739343-->
- `_raw_pair_detail` (function) — Rebuilds one chip's detail payload from the unchanged raw `tool_use` / `tool_result` pair, letting the browser's existing formatters render the expanded panel. <!--#2b9faa982ef8a3e6-->
- `_step_event_detail` (function) — Builds the on-demand detail payload for a lazified step event, returning the daemon-delivered message holder plus its original `inputs` so the browser can restore a byte-identical raw view without a second server-side renderer. <!--#220ff2d99f24aec5-->
- `_detail_of_record` (function) — Extracts one record's detail payload for a given `tool_use_id` in strictly the requested source (step / raw pair / progress), deliberately refusing cross-source fallback so the panel shown always matches what the chip promised. <!--#31e4f933ae1c3635-->
- `locate_record_detail` (function) — Scans a cached record bundle for the message addressed by (step_id, ordinal) and returns its detail along with `record_found` and `passed` flags that tell the detail route whether the answer is authoritative, permanently unavailable, or merely late and worth waiting for. <!--#cf2c4851b27aa073-->

### `src/tianluo/server/identity.py` (python) — The multi-tenant server's provider-independent identity/authorization layer over the persistence Store, resolving owners from hashed daemon keys and external (provider, external_id) identities, gating sensitive cross-provider identity linking behind an admin/verified-claim trust gate, and maintaining a live in-memory machine→owner binding index. <!--#e9e642f0e3d84228|3948191864038871-->
- `UntrustedIdentityLink` (class) — Exception raised when an external identity is linked to an existing owner without passing the trust gate, guarding against account-takeover via blind auto-merge. <!--#f5020a578fd0f10a-->
- `IdentityService` (class) — Service that resolves owners from daemon keys and external identities, gates cross-provider identity linking, and maintains the live in-memory machine→owner binding index. <!--#e688faa5f37e4f48-->
  - `IdentityService.__init__` (method) — Initializes the service with a backing Store, an empty machine→owner dict, and a lock guarding that live index. <!--#949331c4e76504ed-->
  - `IdentityService.resolve_owner_for_key` (method) — Hashes a daemon key plaintext and delegates to the Store to resolve its owner_id, returning None for missing or non-matching keys. <!--#19b0bdb7d1db42ab-->
  - `IdentityService.resolve_owner_by_identity` (method) — Resolves a (provider, external_id) auth identity to its owner_id via the Store. <!--#874d22333f39d734-->
  - `IdentityService.link_identity_to_owner` (method) — Links an external identity to an existing owner only through the trust gate (admin override or both-sides-verified claim), staying idempotent for the same owner and rejecting conflicts. <!--#40178afed914ab1d-->
  - `IdentityService.bind_machine` (method) — Records under lock that a machine_id is currently owned by a given owner_id in the live index. <!--#bbba8ed39a3d379a-->
  - `IdentityService.owner_of_machine` (method) — Returns the owner bound to a machine_id, or None if unbound. <!--#80b6670164d240c6-->
  - `IdentityService.unbind_machine` (method) — Drops a machine's owner binding, e.g. on daemon disconnect. <!--#92a047a6ee556f74-->
  - `IdentityService.machines_for_owner` (method) — Returns the list of machine ids currently bound to a given owner_id. <!--#8c16d5f8ea6b335b-->
  - `IdentityService.snapshot_bindings` (method) — Returns a copy of all current (machine_id, owner_id) bindings under lock. <!--#aa1ad1922a731355-->

### `src/tianluo/server/persistence.py` (python) — SQLite-backed persistence layer for the server, defining the `Owner`/`DaemonKey`/`MessageHistoryEntry`/`MessageHistoryAppend` records, the `IdentityAlreadyBound` error, and the `Store` repository that owns the database file (WAL pragmas, thread-local connections, read-safe locking, a versioned append-only migration ladder) and exposes the CRUD for owners and admin flags (with atomic last-real-admin guards), external identity bindings, hashed local passwords, hashed daemon keys, break-glass tokens, and per-(owner, channel) message history. <!--#f540109f1cd92f9e|d7e2e31950bc85f0-->
- `Owner` (class) — Dataclass record for a persisted owner (stable owner_id, optional display name, admin flag, creation time) returned by the repository instead of a raw Row. <!--#bfe14bf8541354b0-->
- `DaemonKey` (class) — Dataclass record for a persisted daemon-key hash bound to an owner, with metadata and a revoked-at timestamp. <!--#b89b153a17848a21-->
  - `DaemonKey.revoked` (method) — Convenience property reporting whether the daemon key has been revoked (revoked_at is set). <!--#fb4bc884e0c8e4a4-->
- `MessageHistoryEntry` (class) — Dataclass for one stored message-history row (entry_id, text, created_at), whose server-assigned entry_id is the identity the browser merges its local sends on. <!--#f38ef76b602f5d72-->
- `MessageHistoryAppend` (class) — Dataclass reporting the result of one history append — whether a new row was created and which entry_id the append became (None only for blank, non-message text). <!--#eb094668772b03f6-->
- `Store` (class) — SQLite-backed repository holding the server's persisted facts (owners, identity bindings, local credentials, daemon keys, message history), wrapping one database file or `:memory:` with thread-safe connection management, WAL/pragma setup, and a versioned migration ladder. <!--#32f71745ccdd0a79-->
  - `Store.__init__` (method) — Initializes the store for a file or in-memory DB, setting up locking/thread-local connection state, ensuring the parent dir exists, and running schema init. <!--#1d462c82a964e6e5-->
  - `Store._new_connection` (method) — Creates a new sqlite3 connection configured with Row factory, WAL journaling (file DBs), busy timeout, and per-connection foreign-key enforcement. <!--#1f7d9b1eb489947a-->
  - `Store._conn` (method) — Returns the appropriate connection for the caller — the shared one for in-memory DBs, otherwise a lazily-created thread-local connection. <!--#7be1eb71508e7627-->
  - `Store._reading` (method) — Context manager yielding a connection safe for reads, taking `_lock` only in the shared `:memory:` case so file-backed deployments keep fully parallel reads. <!--#aeaab7ad5fe09f63-->
  - `Store._read_one` (method) — Helper running a single read query and returning at most one row via a read-safe connection. <!--#b5cba450a7442963-->
  - `Store._read_all` (method) — Helper running a single read query and returning all rows via a read-safe connection. <!--#3a3114928651c024-->
  - `Store.close` (method) — Closes the shared and current-thread connections, clearing their stored references. <!--#9378a1bb19b255bb-->
  - `Store._init_schema` (method) — Reads the DB's user_version under lock and applies migrations if it is behind the current SCHEMA_VERSION. <!--#c387f248c591076c-->
  - `Store._apply_migrations` (method) — Applies the ordered (target_version, sql) migration steps from the database's current user_version up to SCHEMA_VERSION, with the invariant that published steps are appended to, never edited. <!--#a89d88467ad6bc8c-->
  - `Store._now` (method) — Static helper returning the current wall-clock time for created/updated timestamps. <!--#194cd7b5e7248d18-->
  - `Store._new_id` (method) — Static helper generating a fresh opaque hex UUID for primary-key identifiers. <!--#205e13ff4affe569-->
  - `Store.create_owner` (method) — Inserts a new owner row and returns its stable internal owner_id. <!--#cfda8cc79821f6eb-->
  - `Store.get_owner` (method) — Looks up one owner by `owner_id` and returns it as an `Owner`, or `None` when absent. <!--#e7f49ede5fdab333-->
  - `Store.list_owners` (method) — Returns all owners as `Owner` records ordered oldest-first by creation time. <!--#774cde469fb38f8d-->
  - `Store.delete_owner` (method) — Deletes an owner (cascading to its bindings/credentials/keys) and reports whether a row was removed. <!--#711d2b75fecce53e-->
  - `Store.set_admin` (method) — Updates an owner's is_admin flag, returning whether the owner existed; backs the admin toggle-admin endpoint. <!--#e69d5b897d58e73f-->
  - `Store._count_real_admins` (method) — Lock-held helper counting admin owners excluding the break-glass subject, used to enforce the last-real-admin invariant in the same critical section as a write. <!--#1f3d3d282a0a0e14-->
  - `Store.delete_owner_guarded` (method) — Deletes an owner but atomically refuses if it is the last real admin, returning a 'not_found'/'last_admin'/'deleted' status. <!--#dc19e70db5cc369c-->
  - `Store.set_admin_guarded` (method) — Sets an owner's admin flag but atomically refuses a last-real-admin demotion, returning a 'not_found'/'last_admin'/'updated' status. <!--#7dfd730f059f977d-->
  - `Store.create_local_user` (method) — Atomically creates an owner, its `(provider, external_id)` identity binding, and a local password-hash credential in one transaction, raising `IdentityAlreadyBound` (and rolling back) on a duplicate identity. <!--#15e5664d82286e80-->
  - `Store.link_identity` (method) — Attaches a (provider, external_id) binding to an owner (idempotent for the same owner), raising IdentityAlreadyBound if it maps to a different owner. <!--#fff8ca88f8ed33c9-->
  - `Store.resolve_owner_by_identity` (method) — Maps an external `(provider, external_id)` identity binding to its owner id, or `None` if unbound. <!--#6621c315ba1275c2-->
  - `Store.list_identities` (method) — Returns the `(provider, external_id)` identity bindings attached to one owner, oldest-first. <!--#f4927b8e55fa2081-->
  - `Store.set_password` (method) — Upserts the already-hashed local password for an `owner_id` into `local_credentials`, never handling plaintext. <!--#98ae15b50cdbccec-->
  - `Store.get_password_hash` (method) — Returns the stored local-credential password hash for an owner, or `None` when none is set. <!--#905bf2b4005dca85-->
  - `Store.issue_daemon_key` (method) — Persists a hashed daemon key bound to an `owner_id` (with optional label) and returns the generated `key_id`, storing only the hash of the one-time plaintext key. <!--#19ed849ce4257db4-->
  - `Store.resolve_owner_by_daemon_key` (method) — Maps a daemon key hash to its owner id, ignoring revoked keys. <!--#a2d892f0b124e538-->
  - `Store.revoke_daemon_key` (method) — Marks a daemon key revoked by key_id (idempotent), returning False only if the key_id genuinely does not exist. <!--#910630e46c88ad28-->
  - `Store.list_daemon_keys` (method) — Returns an owner's `DaemonKey` records oldest-first, optionally filtering out revoked ones. <!--#58451b2443c6d11b-->
  - `Store.append_message_history` (method) — Appends a sent prompt to one (owner_id, channel) history under one write lock — dropping blank text, folding an adjacent duplicate onto the existing row, trimming to the newest max_entries — and returns which row the append became. <!--#b57a089168223870-->
  - `Store.list_message_history` (method) — Returns the newest `limit` message-history entries for one `(owner_id, channel)`, re-ordered oldest-first for the arrow-key navigator. <!--#7edc83d0414c5164-->
  - `Store.count_message_history` (method) — Returns the message-history row count for one `(owner_id, channel)`, used as the truncation probe. <!--#cb5bfb4d1c607a27-->
  - `Store.put_breakglass` (method) — Persists a break-glass admin token hash (with optional expiry) and returns its token_id. <!--#d0cf28881699ea5b-->
  - `Store.consume_breakglass` (method) — Atomically consumes a break-glass token by hash, returning True exactly once for a valid/unexpired/unconsumed token and marking it consumed. <!--#42e03299c1a89b1d-->
  - `Store.purge_breakglass` (method) — Deletes all break-glass tokens (e.g. before re-issuing) and returns the number removed. <!--#e0a39cb75dfc461e-->
- `IdentityAlreadyBound` (class) — Exception raised when linking an external identity that is already bound to another owner. <!--#e57ce650eec6fb27-->

### `src/tianluo/server/state.py` (python) — Defines `ServerState`, the central server's non-persisted, `asyncio.Lock`-guarded in-memory store of every dialed-in daemon machine (`MachineRecord`/`FlowSnapshot`), plus the history-bundle cache with its byte-estimation helpers (`_estimate_json_bytes`, `records_reach_bytes`), generation/cursor and replay-delivery bookkeeping, step-window slicing, usage aggregation, and hot/cold budget eviction that back the WebUI's history and status APIs. <!--#f5fbf9017168fcbd|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/server/ws.py` (python) — The central server's daemon-facing WebSocket layer: it defines the `ConnectionManager` pool that maps `machine_id` to sockets and routes downlink instructions (`SPAWN_FLOW` / `RESPOND_CALL`) from the REST API, plus `handle_daemon_connection`, which validates the opening `HELLO`, replies `WELCOME`, and runs the receive and `PING`/`PONG` heartbeat loops — ingesting history reports (with chunked, event-loop-yielding JSON rendering and oversized-frame tripwires) and publishing `/ws/ui` events such as `interjection_event` and `spawn_failed`. <!--#5c4e15655d677770|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

## `src/tianluo/server/auth/` — The pluggable authentication layer (A-layer) for the multi-tenant server, providing the unified fail-closed "resolve the current owner" seam — an AuthProvider/OwnerIdentity/ProviderChain vocabulary, a hashed-token session store with secure cookies, the default built-in LocalAuthProvider (username/password) with brute-force rate limiting, disabled-by-default OIDC and reverse-proxy-header provider seams, and a config-driven registry that assembles the provider chain and exposes the FastAPI require_owner dependency (with all web deps kept behind deferred imports). <!--#6a5b911a509a252d|c5ccecef9ff03f88-->

### `src/tianluo/server/auth/__init__.py` (python) — Package init for the pluggable authentication layer (A-layer) that resolves the current request owner for the multi-tenant server; it re-exports the public API — AuthProvider/OwnerIdentity/ProviderChain, session and cookie primitives, LocalAuthProvider, rate-limit types, and the registry's chain-builder and require_owner dependency — while keeping FastAPI web deps behind deferred imports so the package loads without the server extra. <!--#42f390e1cb67fbd5|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/server/auth/base.py` (python) — Defines the server auth A-layer vocabulary — the transport-independent OwnerIdentity result, the abstract AuthProvider 'resolve the current owner' interface, and a fail-closed ProviderChain that tries enabled providers in order and returns the first non-None owner resolution. <!--#a4313bcbfa5cbac9|cd9faafc057e0b60-->
- `OwnerIdentity` (class) — A dataclass-style value object representing the authenticated owner of a request, carrying the stable internal `owner_id` used for authorization plus UI-only `display_name`, diagnostic `provider`, and an `is_admin` flag. <!--#b4b306c9da00b7e6-->
- `AuthProvider` (class) — Abstract base class for the unified 'resolve the current owner' interface, carrying a name discriminator and an enabled flag for registry/chain participation. <!--#32eaf7eb12361308-->
  - `AuthProvider.resolve_owner` (method) — Abstract method that resolves a request-like object to an OwnerIdentity or returns None (could-not-authenticate, never authorize-anonymous). <!--#519521172c8b189d-->
- `ProviderChain` (class) — Ordered composition of AuthProviders that drops disabled ones, returns the first non-None resolution, and is falsy when empty to enforce fail-closed. <!--#8c9764f1b32445c0-->
  - `ProviderChain.__init__` (method) — Builds the chain by filtering the given providers down to those whose enabled flag is truthy. <!--#111e6b192e809c5b-->
  - `ProviderChain.providers` (method) — Property returning a copy of the chain's enabled providers list. <!--#9fed3349e6dcd43c-->
  - `ProviderChain.resolve_owner` (method) — Iterates the enabled providers in order and returns the first non-None OwnerIdentity, else None. <!--#f6ba975245faf121-->
  - `ProviderChain.__bool__` (method) — Truthiness reflecting whether the chain has any enabled providers (used to enforce fail-closed serving). <!--#fc551b5bfab86264-->
  - `ProviderChain.__len__` (method) — Returns the number of enabled providers in the chain. <!--#a0fd978e084ff45a-->

### `src/tianluo/server/auth/local.py` (python) — Defines LocalAuthProvider, the default built-in username/password/session authenticator over the local store, whose login ceremony rate-limits, resolves the owner, verifies the password hash (with a dummy verify to equalize timing against unknown users), and mints a session on success while never logging secrets. <!--#b2bee9c99004142b|039a69b633851c14-->
- `LocalAuthProvider` (class) — A `SessionAuthProvider` implementation that authenticates username/password credentials against the local store, applying `LoginRateLimiter` gating and timing-equalization (dummy hash verify) before minting a session and returning an `OwnerIdentity`. <!--#5e1820afb64c215b-->
  - `LocalAuthProvider.__init__` (method) — Constructs the provider with a store, session store, and an optional (else default) login rate limiter, deferring the dummy timing hash. <!--#10228702a0a41f9c-->
  - `LocalAuthProvider.rate_limiter` (method) — Property exposing the provider's login rate limiter. <!--#97b7c30b9d9fae0f-->
  - `LocalAuthProvider._dummy_verify` (method) — Best-effort dummy password verification that equalizes login timing on the unknown-user path to mitigate user enumeration. <!--#516f8841211cbaef-->
  - `LocalAuthProvider.login` (method) — Authenticates a username/password pair by rate-limit gating, resolving the owner, verifying the stored hash (with timing-equalized dummy verify on unknown users), and returning `(session_id, OwnerIdentity)` on success, `None` on bad credentials, or raising `LoginRateLimited` when locked out. <!--#5b753d0634bcfb86-->

### `src/tianluo/server/auth/oidc.py` (python) — A disabled-by-default OIDC authentication seam that keeps the auth layer's schema and call path open for future social login by defining the stable `issuer|sub` external-identity key and a fail-closed `OidcProvider`, while leaving the actual login/callback ceremony unimplemented (NotImplementedError) in v1. <!--#ed99ce6366d1dc58|6ed5aab56df6cf65-->
- `oidc_external_id` (function) — Composes the globally stable OIDC external identity as `"{issuer}|{sub}"`, the key used to bind an OIDC subject to an owner_id. <!--#4ce6c3586d1745a6-->
- `OidcProvider` (class) — A disabled-by-default OIDC auth provider that enables only when explicitly opted in and fully configured, otherwise failing closed and leaving the login ceremony unimplemented. <!--#32c9223628687a08-->
  - `OidcProvider.__init__` (method) — Validates the required OIDC config keys and sets `enabled` only when the operator opts in and all keys are present, logging a fail-closed warning on incomplete config. <!--#9f166fbf12760eee-->
  - `OidcProvider.resolve_owner` (method) — Returns None when disabled (never inspecting the request) and otherwise delegates to the standard session-cookie owner resolution. <!--#0b7f86218d50c7cd-->
  - `OidcProvider.begin_login` (method) — Seam for building the authorization-endpoint redirect URL with state/nonce; raises NotImplementedError in v1. <!--#d9ab4af1dc1c8197-->
  - `OidcProvider.complete_login` (method) — Seam for handling the OIDC callback (validate state/nonce, exchange code, link owner, mint session); raises NotImplementedError in v1. <!--#fa4c032f2483c13e-->

### `src/tianluo/server/auth/proxy_header.py` (python) — A fail-closed AuthProvider seam that resolves an owner identity from a reverse-proxy-injected header, staying disabled by default and refusing to trust the header unless the operator both enables it and affirms the proxy-trust precondition. <!--#5c4747182c6d7b05|c97844013e24d778-->
- `_read_header` (function) — Helper that safely extracts a named header value from a request's headers mapping, returning None when absent or on any access error. <!--#5f41b5f49adf1583-->
- `ProxyHeaderProvider` (class) — AuthProvider implementation that resolves an owner from a proxy-injected identity header, enabling only when the operator opts in and affirms trust. <!--#fbcc83a32474b846-->
  - `ProxyHeaderProvider.__init__` (method) — Reads config to set the header name and computes the fail-closed enabled flag, warning and staying disabled if enabled without an affirmed trust precondition. <!--#40b36c30c2f1b731-->
  - `ProxyHeaderProvider.header` (method) — Property exposing the configured (lowercased) identity header name. <!--#83cc214723e36afc-->
  - `ProxyHeaderProvider.resolve_owner` (method) — Resolves the request's header value to an OwnerIdentity via the store, returning None when disabled, header missing, or no owner is bound (no auto-creation). <!--#99444a685b125cf3-->

### `src/tianluo/server/auth/ratelimit.py` (python) — An in-memory, thread-safe login rate limiter that tracks per-key failed attempts in a sliding window and locks a key out for a configured duration once failures exceed a threshold, clearing the counter on success and raising LoginRateLimited (with a Retry-After delay) while locked. <!--#73e31186e06a45dc|f04b6c8845ceaf3e-->
- `RateLimitConfig` (class) — Dataclass holding the tunable thresholds — max failures, lockout duration, and sliding window — for the rate limiter. <!--#a6a5eb383f7136a0-->
- `_Entry` (class) — Private per-key state record holding the list of recent failure timestamps and the time until which the key is locked. <!--#10591451905b3f36-->
- `LoginRateLimited` (class) — Exception raised when a login key is currently locked out, carrying a retry_after delay suitable for an HTTP 429 Retry-After header. <!--#1dd2b3f40fd525d2-->
  - `LoginRateLimited.__init__` (method) — Constructs the exception with a human-readable message and stores the retry_after seconds. <!--#ba5a287e1e640a20-->
- `LoginRateLimiter` (class) — Thread-safe per-key failure counter that records attempts, trips a lockout once over threshold, and clears on success. <!--#dc80045151f25360-->
  - `LoginRateLimiter.__init__` (method) — Initializes the limiter with a config, an injectable clock, an empty entry map, and a lock for thread safety. <!--#61fee3463d2384b5-->
  - `LoginRateLimiter._prune` (method) — Drops failure timestamps older than the sliding window from an entry. <!--#cb829de6f8f922c0-->
  - `LoginRateLimiter.is_locked` (method) — Returns whether the given key is currently within its lockout period. <!--#1a4772931c2f9874-->
  - `LoginRateLimiter.retry_after` (method) — Returns the seconds remaining on a key's lockout, or 0 if not locked. <!--#b9a0362606992fb2-->
  - `LoginRateLimiter.check` (method) — Raises LoginRateLimited if the key is currently locked, otherwise returns silently. <!--#3c7783c70f3655b5-->
  - `LoginRateLimiter.record_failure` (method) — Registers a failed attempt and trips the lockout once the failure count reaches the configured threshold. <!--#b1e2b4c4f685ed5f-->
  - `LoginRateLimiter.record_success` (method) — Clears a key's entire failure history on a successful login. <!--#e931a75cb8fbf1f7-->
  - `LoginRateLimiter.reset` (method) — Drops all tracked keys, as a test helper or administrative clear. <!--#af382ab8e4ab2f2c-->

### `src/tianluo/server/auth/registry.py` (python) — Assembles the configuration-driven, fail-closed authentication provider chain (raising AuthNotConfigured when no usable provider remains) and builds the FastAPI `require_owner` dependency that resolves the current OwnerIdentity or rejects anonymous requests with HTTP 401. <!--#7b974058ccca3293|462425ce67bb7394-->
- `AuthNotConfigured` (class) — Exception raised when configuration yields no usable auth provider, signaling the server to refuse serving rather than fall back to an identity-unaware open control plane. <!--#18ef78762ac12051-->
- `_normalize_entry` (function) — Helper that normalizes a providers-list entry (bare type string or mapping with `type` plus options) into a `(type, options)` tuple. <!--#4006889c26eb61dc-->
- `build_provider_chain` (function) — Constructs the ordered `ProviderChain` from `server.auth` config, keeping only enabled providers and raising `AuthNotConfigured` (fail-closed) if the chain ends up empty. <!--#86279238c9bb36f0-->
- `_construct_provider` (function) — Factory that instantiates the appropriate provider (local, OIDC, or proxy-header) for a given type discriminator, returning None for unknown types. <!--#40a7f3b75d64da4f-->
- `make_require_owner` (function) — Builds the FastAPI `require_owner` dependency that resolves the current `OwnerIdentity` via the chain and raises HTTP 401 when none resolves, wiring up annotations so FastAPI injects the request. <!--#6b40cb227e95e093-->

### `src/tianluo/server/auth/session.py` (python) — Implements the UI session-auth layer: a thread-safe in-memory `SessionStore` of hashed, expiring session tokens (with secure `CookieConfig` cookie attributes and create/resolve/destroy/sweep operations) plus a `SessionAuthProvider` base class that reads the session cookie and resolves it to the current owner identity. <!--#d35eea174ab621aa|cf36262b4e3d8f0f-->
- `CookieConfig` (class) — Dataclass holding the secure-cookie attributes (name, HttpOnly, SameSite, Secure, Path, Max-Age) for the UI session cookie. <!--#c7b2a206e0272a4d-->
- `Session` (class) — Dataclass representing one live server-side session, storing the session id's hash, owner, and creation/expiry timestamps. <!--#88ed149b1e808cda-->
  - `Session.is_expired` (method) — Returns whether the session's absolute expiry time has been reached at the given clock value. <!--#3e82312554a4481a-->
- `read_cookie` (function) — Best-effort, fail-closed helper that reads a named cookie from a request-like object, returning None on missing/malformed input. <!--#61826ca40012c71a-->
- `SessionStore` (class) — Thread-safe, in-memory table of hashed, expiring sessions keyed by session-id hash, providing create/resolve/destroy/sweep operations. <!--#cb3f9ac1c88e95b1-->
  - `SessionStore.__init__` (method) — Initializes the store with a TTL, cookie config, injectable clock, empty session dict, and a lock. <!--#0b8b8aab7201d1e2-->
  - `SessionStore.cookie_config` (method) — Property exposing the store's CookieConfig. <!--#7a7d3c67f0add4a8-->
  - `SessionStore.create` (method) — Mints a new session for an owner, returning the plaintext session id (cookie value) plus the stored hash-only Session. <!--#1d7f5f94d8a13d82-->
  - `SessionStore.resolve` (method) — Resolves a presented session-id plaintext to a live Session via hash lookup, constant-time compare, and expiry check, evicting expired ones. <!--#569b377aa1f11fde-->
  - `SessionStore.destroy` (method) — Idempotently invalidates a single session by its plaintext id (logout). <!--#d991cc867c95d63f-->
  - `SessionStore.destroy_owner` (method) — Invalidates all sessions belonging to an owner (e.g. on account disable) and returns the count removed. <!--#1ca7efc34f2a4fdc-->
  - `SessionStore.sweep_expired` (method) — Prunes all expired sessions from the table and returns how many were removed. <!--#59bf4dc9b4eb8817-->
  - `SessionStore.__len__` (method) — Returns the current number of stored sessions under the lock. <!--#0852865572e6c842-->
- `SessionAuthProvider` (class) — The base AuthProvider that resolves the current OwnerIdentity from the session cookie by looking up the SessionStore and store.get_owner (failing closed and destroying the session if the owner was deleted), and handles logout by destroying the cookie's session; subclasses like LocalAuthProvider only add their own login ceremony atop this uniform resolution path. <!--#d02e067613547ded-->
  - `SessionAuthProvider.__init__` (method) — Initializes the provider with the owner store and the SessionStore. <!--#3b6497b6377e6176-->
  - `SessionAuthProvider.sessions` (method) — Property exposing the provider's SessionStore. <!--#4282f203f8e12aba-->
  - `SessionAuthProvider.store` (method) — Property exposing the provider's owner store. <!--#2a6b2d7f5dc053b4-->
  - `SessionAuthProvider.resolve_owner` (method) — Reads the session cookie, resolves it to a session and owner, and returns an OwnerIdentity (failing closed and dropping the session if the owner is gone). <!--#a647ecb75f2dd934-->
  - `SessionAuthProvider.logout` (method) — Idempotently destroys the session referenced by the request's cookie. <!--#41bf329b337e43e8-->

## `src/tianluo/server/static/` — The WebUI Control Plane's static asset bundle served to browsers — the index.html shell and its style.css dark-theme stylesheet, the vanilla-JS app.js single-page frontend that opens the authenticated WebSocket and renders the machine/flow/issue/running-flow views, the per-locale i18n/ JSON translation bundles, and the favicon.ico. <!--#0ef4a752ffe1d25b|18016ea36f80a696-->

### `src/tianluo/server/static/app.js` (text) — The tianluo web console's single-file browser client, holding the global `state` object and diff-aware render signatures alongside the auth/user-permission helpers, registered-project dialog logic, the DOM-free upload layer (validation, placeholder tokens, attachment strips, drag/paste/picker wiring), the `I18N` translation subsystem, flow-status predicates, the localStorage `DRAFTS` store, owner-scoped ↑/↓ message-history recall, and the connection-status and fetch-deadline plumbing that drive the running-flow and history views. <!--#21329b4f7a2385f2|5f63ed9328c14109-->
- `chunk:1` (chunk) [degraded:chunk] — Module header and the start of the global `state` object for the tianluo web console, documenting auth/identity fields, upload-attachment bookkeeping, machine/flow selection, and the running-flow conversation's progress token, signature, epoch and in-flight-pull guards. <!--#c25620ce3e2c5227-->
- `chunk:2` (chunk) [degraded:chunk] — Continues the global `state` object declaration, documenting the running-flow/history view bookkeeping fields — periodic snapshot flag, intervention entries, history session index and records, progress/signature tokens, the cursor self-check budgets (`backfillInFlight`/`backfillAttempts`/`backfillUnfillable`), interrupted-delivery recovery timers, and the step-block window state. <!--#ed4f8d46a852a3c2-->

### `src/tianluo/server/static/index.html` (text) — The single-page HTML shell for the tianluo Control Plane WebUI, declaring the localized top bar (version badge, live connection status, language selector, hamburger overflow menu with history/issues/keys/users/new-task/logout controls gated by auth-only and admin-only classes), the login gate with password and break-glass admin token forms, and the main layout panes (machines list, etc.) that app.js populates and translates via data-i18n attributes. <!--#44205e50e565d2ab|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

## `src/tianluo/server/static/i18n/` — Directory holding the WebUI's client-side localization bundles — one JSON file per locale (en-US and zh-CN) that map dotted UI keys (lang/topbar/nav/login/machines/flows/common/history/issues/issueModal/issueAction/endSession/issueLaunch/flow) to the display strings for navigation, panels, dialogs, form fields, placeholders, and empty/loading states. <!--#fdfb3e6c2a387829|a8bd86082629b0ad-->

### `src/tianluo/server/static/i18n/en-US.json` (json) — The English (en-US) translation catalogue for the tianluo WebUI, mapping dotted i18n keys to the user-facing strings for the language switcher, top bar and navigation, login (including break-glass), machine/flow lists, history and issue views, the issue-creation and issue-action dialogs, the end-session dialog, and shared common labels such as size formats, stale-connection banners, and worktree options. <!--#10376a7bc49bb79f|159f7e6e50db639b-->

### `src/tianluo/server/static/i18n/zh-CN.json` (json) — Simplified-Chinese (zh-CN) locale bundle for the WebUI, providing flat dot-namespaced translation keys covering the language switcher, top bar and navigation, login (including break-glass admin entry), machines and flows lists, shared common labels and size/stale-banner formats, and the history, issues, issue-creation/action modal, and end-session dialog views. <!--#eb110100b15729e4|159f7e6e50db639b-->

## `src/tianluo/templates/` — Package of project-scaffolding and pipeline assets rendered by `luo init`/`luo migrate` and used across runs — Markdown/Jinja templates for a project's charter, base spec, README, VERSIONS.md changelog, and a standalone semver version-management CLI stub, plus a prompts/ subdirectory of LLM-run step templates (e.g. doc-sync.md), with __init__.py exposing the canonical `CHARTER_TEMPLATE` filename constant. <!--#ef91f0a34ae0c4b9|96827374fe959a3e-->

### `src/tianluo/templates/__init__.py` (python) — Package init for tianluo's project-initialization templates (charter.md, legacy base_spec.md, readme_md.md, versions_md.md, version_script.py.tmpl rendered by `luo init`/`luo migrate`), exposing the canonical `CHARTER_TEMPLATE` filename constant. <!--#35faa28a3271b289|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `src/tianluo/templates/base_spec.md` (markdown) — The `luo init`-generated base specification template that, with placeholders for project identity/structure/conventions/constraints, establishes a project's baseline spec auto-loaded into every run, and codifies a SemVer 2.0.0 version-management policy driven by `version_analyze`'s authoritative suggested version with no silent patch-bump fallback. <!--#7ca93ec3c5e43541|a3af382958bb3a94-->
- `{project_name} — Base Specification` (heading) — Top-level document title parameterized by the project name. <!--#d111501fa2c349b2-->
  - `Purpose` (heading) — Explains that this base spec captures the project's foundational conventions, is generated by `luo init`, and is auto-loaded into every `luo run` flow. <!--#eb2a31227f570415-->
  - `Requirements` (heading) — Container heading grouping all the requirement subsections of the spec. <!--#d8416f1863ce5290-->
    - `Requirement: Project Identity` (heading) — Records the project's name, description, and primary languages/frameworks via placeholders. <!--#8f8680697bd5dba4-->
    - `Requirement: Directory Structure` (heading) — Placeholder requirement describing the project's directory layout. <!--#fda3fd8b0889a9d0-->
    - `Requirement: Coding Conventions` (heading) — Placeholder requirement capturing the project's coding style conventions. <!--#c4a2c6cbe902bea6-->
    - `Requirement: Key Constraints` (heading) — Placeholder requirement listing the project's key constraints. <!--#224404c163fbb0c3-->
    - `Requirement: Workflow Conventions` (heading) — Placeholder requirement describing the project's workflow conventions. <!--#ccc10176db969929-->
    - `Requirement: Version Management` (heading) — Mandates Semantic Versioning 2.0.0, naming the single source-of-truth version file per language, and defining a version-decision model where `version_analyze`'s `suggested_version` is authoritative (optionally guided by `tianluo/version-rules.md`) and `commit` writes it with no silent patch-bump fallback. <!--#b5b7f0354e141620-->

  - `Requirements` (heading) — Container heading grouping the charter's requirement subsections. <!--#d8416f1863ce5290-->
    - `Requirement: Project Identity` (heading) — Records the project's name, description, and primary languages/frameworks via placeholders. <!--#8f8680697bd5dba4-->
    - `Requirement: Top-Level Architecture` (heading) — Requirement section holding the `{top_level_architecture}` global picture of major subsystems and their boundaries, restricted to judgment-based architectural decisions and explicitly excluding mechanical location info that `luo code-index` maintains. <!--#fd3d0b65d374697f-->
    - `Requirement: Coding Conventions` (heading) — Holds project-wide, cross-cutting coding conventions every step should follow. <!--#9d68141915bc34f0-->
    - `Requirement: Key Constraints` (heading) — Lists hard project-level constraints whose violation is treated as an error. <!--#d6e0ccfe4259b72e-->
    - `Requirement: Workflow Conventions` (heading) — Placeholder section for project workflow conventions. <!--#ccc10176db969929-->
