### `tests/test_daemon_status_gating.py` (python) — A test module locking the daemon's G6 traffic-reduction contract: it uses an in-memory fake WebSocket and a hand-configured DaemonClient to verify that unchanged ticks collapse to keepalives (only for rev-3 lean peers, never legacy), changed or force-pushed ticks send full STATUS_UPDATEs, per-message-type byte metrics accumulate, and aggregated snapshots are thinned by clipping issue descriptions and pending-call prompts to the shared `_DESC_CLIP` (200) standard. <!--#c132866a486d4b59|224f12d8f1a116e8-->
- `_FakeWS` (class) — A minimal in-memory WebSocket stand-in that decodes and records every frame the daemon client sends, letting tests inspect the message stream. <!--#c3ad43269d7be7e8-->
  - `_FakeWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the fake WebSocket with an empty `sent` list to accumulate captured frames. <!--#b8b92aad379d234c-->
  - `_FakeWS.send` (method) — Async send override that decodes the outgoing frame via `protocol.decode` and appends it to the captured `sent` list. <!--#7d44362527b3e749-->
- `_client` (function) — Test helper that builds a `DaemonClient` around a snapshot provider and directly sets its learned peer protocol version to model a rev-3 (lean) or legacy peer without a full handshake. <!--#f804c2648e99bfd6-->
- `_types` (function) — Helper returning the list of message types from a fake WebSocket's captured frames for concise assertions. <!--#1847dfb55e9608b9-->
- `test_unchanged_tick_collapses_to_keepalive` (function) — Asserts that two identical snapshots (differing only in the excluded `generated_at` stamp) produce one full STATUS_UPDATE then a KEEPALIVE carrying the same content signature the gate matched on. <!--#c898c1355579076c-->
- `test_changed_tick_sends_full_status_update` (function) — Asserts that a substantive content change (adding an issue) between ticks yields a fresh full STATUS_UPDATE rather than gating to a keepalive. <!--#64560a4ecf7d3d22-->
- `test_legacy_peer_never_gets_a_keepalive` (function) — Asserts that a pre-rev-3 peer always receives full STATUS_UPDATEs even on unchanged ticks, since it would reject the revision-3 keepalive frame. <!--#4fe5f05411039296-->
- `test_force_bypasses_the_gate` (function) — Asserts that an event-driven `force=True` push sends a full STATUS_UPDATE even when the content is unchanged and would otherwise gate to a keepalive. <!--#bbd9767523dca862-->
- `test_metrics_accumulate_per_message_type` (function) — Asserts that each sent frame is metered per message type in `client.metrics`, that a keepalive costs fewer bytes than a full update, and that the synthetic `__total__` roll-up sums both frames. <!--#f5cd4f5c5863b2f9-->
- `test_desc_clip_standard_is_200` (function) — Pins that the snapshot's description clip standard `_DESC_CLIP` equals the shared history value of 200. <!--#da6c8b9cc69871e8-->
- `test_collected_issue_description_is_clipped` (function) — Verifies DaemonAggregator._collect_issues truncates each issue's description to _DESC_CLIP (200) chars plus a "..." ellipsis, so the STATUS_UPDATE snapshot carries only a preview rather than the full body. <!--#71e8ba2a873794cb-->
- `test_issue_snapshot_to_dict_is_a_summary` (function) — Asserts that `IssueSnapshot.to_dict` emits exactly the webui summary field set and nothing more. <!--#52a079e5c5ff833a-->
- `test_machine_wide_pending_call_prompt_is_clipped` (function) — Verifies PendingCall.to_dict() emits the verbatim prompt by default but clips it to _DESC_CLIP chars plus "..." when clip_prompt=True, the flag both STATUS_UPDATE pending_calls surfaces pass to avoid inlining full prompts. <!--#ebf5a95d7226321e-->

### `tests/test_daemon_traffic_reduction.py` (python) — Test suite locking the G2 daemon traffic-reduction contract: aggregator clipping of issue descriptions and machine-wide call prompts, signature-gated keepalive-vs-full STATUS_UPDATE pushing (including legacy-peer and force cases), on-demand DETAIL_REQUEST fetch of untruncated text with graceful error replies, and per-frame wire-byte metering, using in-memory WebSocket and client fakes. <!--#5a1deda4ecc405db|7381946786761b5d-->
- `_FakeWS` (class) — A minimal in-memory WebSocket stand-in that decodes and records every frame the client sends so tests can assert on the wire output. <!--#e6c82bc92db5d9fa-->
  - `_FakeWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the fake WebSocket with an empty `sent` list to accumulate captured frames. <!--#ce393d52044e73f0-->
  - `_FakeWS.send` (method) — Async send stub that decodes the outgoing payload via `protocol.decode` and appends it to the `sent` list. <!--#154edf553e8ef4d4-->
- `_make_client` (function) — Test factory that builds a `DaemonClient` with canned identity/version fields and a default snapshot provider, allowing per-test overrides. <!--#f3137c441b7b6c4e-->
- `_write_issue` (function) — Test helper that writes a minimal open-issue YAML file under `tianluo/issues/open` using the `NNN_slug` filename convention so IssueManager/aggregator can locate and read it. <!--#f9faaa28fd26095d-->
- `test_issue_snapshot_description_clipped` (function) — Verifies that DaemonAggregator._collect_issues clips an overlong issue description to at most _DESC_CLIP characters plus a trailing "..." ellipsis, and that to_dict() carries the same clipped preview. <!--#adb50fa45d337e67-->
- `test_short_issue_description_untouched` (function) — Verifies that a short issue description passes through DaemonAggregator._collect_issues unchanged (no clipping applied). <!--#8d1e503b47caba1c-->
- `test_status_update_pending_call_prompts_clipped_on_both_surfaces` (function) — Asserts that a long PendingCall prompt is clipped to `_DESC_CLIP` (with trailing `...`) on both the machine-wide `MachineStatus` and the per-flow `FlowSnapshot` wire serializations, while the raw `PendingCall.to_dict()` still returns the verbatim body. <!--#08d3f0f880144a49-->
- `test_status_signature_ignores_generated_at` (function) — Confirms `_status_signature` ignores the `generated_at` timestamp but changes when the flow content changes. <!--#9b2855228c77e7c1-->
- `test_unchanged_snapshot_sends_keepalive_when_peer_supports` (function) — Verifies that an unchanged snapshot sends a full baseline first then a lean keepalive (carrying the matched signature) when the peer speaks revision 3. <!--#7007c7e2aba72a13-->
- `test_changed_snapshot_sends_full_update` (function) — Verifies that a changing snapshot yields two full STATUS_UPDATE frames rather than a keepalive. <!--#a31730ecd4bae1ec-->
- `test_legacy_peer_never_gets_keepalive` (function) — Verifies a legacy (revision-2) peer always receives full STATUS_UPDATE frames and never lean keepalives. <!--#5aee5d5470255ca2-->
- `test_force_bypasses_keepalive_gate` (function) — Verifies that `force=True` on `_push_status` sends a full update even when the snapshot is unchanged. <!--#d57744a4fb5847b0-->
- `test_detail_request_returns_full_issue` (function) — Verifies a DETAIL_REQUEST for an issue returns a successful DETAIL_DATA reply with the untruncated description and echoed request id. <!--#8f5c19136426c050-->
- `test_detail_request_returns_full_call_prompt` (function) — Verifies that a DETAIL_REQUEST for a call dispatched through `DaemonClient._dispatch` replies `ok=true` with the untruncated `prompt` and correct `call_id` read from the on-disk call JSON. <!--#a5d11176c8f012c8-->
- `test_detail_request_normalizes_legacy_call_fields` (function) — Verifies that a DETAIL_REQUEST normalizes legacy call bodies storing their text under `message` or `question`, surfacing the full text under the canonical `prompt` key in the reply. <!--#e55568cabe78f6fe-->
- `test_detail_request_missing_target_replies_error` (function) — Verifies a DETAIL_REQUEST for a nonexistent target returns an `ok=false` DETAIL_DATA error reply with no `detail` body rather than dropping. <!--#91d967fe656dcd93-->
- `test_detail_request_resolves_via_known_roots` (function) — Verifies a DETAIL_REQUEST lacking a `project_root` falls back to the client's last-known roots to locate and return the full issue. <!--#c7124c3794952c94-->
- `test_send_accrues_wire_metrics` (function) — Verifies every `_send` accrues per-type and total frame counts and byte totals into the client's `metrics`. <!--#f4451eb935e75f4b-->
- `test_session_dials_with_permessage_deflate` (function) — Verifies `_session` pins `compression="deflate"` and `max_size=MAX_WS_MESSAGE_BYTES` on the websockets connect call, using a stub that aborts at `__aenter__`. <!--#467fcf58aa2d63d2-->

### `tests/test_daemon_worktree_discovery_multiround.py` (python) — Test module exercising DaemonHistoryReader's multi-round worktree discovery-file handling — verifying that incremental appends, from-scratch full reads, late worktree-copy appearance, cross-root merge selection, and post-merge primary/sidecar streams all yield stable, globally unique (step_id, ordinal) keys so frontend reconciliation never drops or duplicates records. <!--#d60482cafd136cef|a60dd48ce2db6247-->
- `_write_jsonl` (function) — Helper that creates parent directories and writes a list of dicts to a file as JSONL lines. <!--#f321072562a278a4-->
- `_append_jsonl` (function) — Helper that appends dicts as JSON lines to an existing JSONL file. <!--#826510bf1d7d8393-->
- `_msg` (function) — Helper that builds a minimal chat-message dict with a role and content. <!--#67f68ff7e3aa1c72-->
- `_make_reader` (function) — Helper that constructs a DaemonHistoryReader whose project-roots provider yields the given root paths. <!--#f5fb70620f9f4765-->
- `_flow_dir` (function) — Test helper that creates and returns the `tianluo/history/<flow_id>` directory under a given root. <!--#d29934aed956126e-->
- `_make_worktree` (function) — Test helper that creates and returns a `tianluo/worktrees/<name>` worktree directory under a given main root. <!--#a95c859ac4949026-->
- `_keys` (function) — Helper that extracts the (step_id, ordinal) identity pairs the frontend reconciles records by. <!--#4b068bb00274497d-->
- `test_live_worktree_discovery_all_rounds_unique_and_stable` (function) — Verifies that a growing worktree discovery file read via one full snapshot plus incremental appends delivers every round exactly once with globally unique, stable (step_id, ordinal) keys. <!--#1f23f622991a4500-->
- `test_full_read_reproduces_append_ordinals` (function) — Verifies that a fresh from-scratch full read assigns each line the same (step_id, ordinal) identity that the earlier incremental append path produced. <!--#6baa8acb3b823db7-->
- `test_late_worktree_copy_switch_reemits_all_rounds` (function) — Verifies that when the worktree copy of a discovery file appears after the main-repo copy was already read, the reader re-reads it from line 0 so later rounds arrive and re-emitted early lines keep their original keys for idempotent reconciliation. <!--#70821b78bb531d22-->
- `test_merge_selection_sticks_to_worktree_copy` (function) — Verifies that cross-root merge selection consistently picks the worktree copy over the same-named main copy regardless of which file is transiently larger. <!--#d947a699af2bc7f8-->
- `test_live_worktree_reads_stay_incremental_no_reemit` (function) — Verifies that with a stable worktree selection, successive reads of a growing live flow stay in append mode and never re-emit round 1, despite a stale same-named main copy existing throughout. <!--#544a85d8cbebb3a4-->
- `test_post_merge_primary_and_sidecar_distinct_streams` (function) — Verifies that after merge-back both the primary discovery file and its from-worktree sidecar are read as distinct streams with different display step_ids so their per-file ordinals never collide. <!--#989fb7460917c1d1-->
- `test_pre_fix_collision_would_lose_sidecar_records` (function) — Documents the fixed bug by simulating the frontend's key-based reconcile and asserting the sidecar's ordinal-0 record no longer shares a key with (and thus is not dropped by) the primary's. <!--#7d0a99c6358707f4-->

### `tests/test_daemon_worktree_gc.py` (python) — Unit tests for the Daemon's periodic worktree-GC tick, verifying that _maybe_run_gc fires _gc_once at most once per (positive) gc_interval, that _gc_once sweeps every tracked project root via a mocked gc_worktree_runs while forwarding max-age and tolerating per-root failures, and that retained completed-but-unmerged branches are surfaced as WARNING log records. <!--#5dd6607e66bb9979|2c8d7251ba59e07f-->
- `_make_daemon` (function) — Test helper that constructs a `Daemon` with an isolated `pid_dir` (avoiding `~/.se3` side effects) and an optional project root, returning the daemon and its root path. <!--#b0da6faab1d2e21d-->
- `_run` (function) — Tiny helper that runs a coroutine to completion via asyncio.run for the synchronous test bodies. <!--#48a8d32a4a8529d2-->
- `test_gc_config_defaults` (function) — Asserts DaemonConfig defaults the GC interval to 3600s and max age to 86400s. <!--#89d0629c99c8ff0a-->
- `test_maybe_run_gc_fires_on_first_poll` (function) — Verifies _maybe_run_gc invokes _gc_once once and records _last_gc_at on the very first poll. <!--#a228b3bbf5eb1bb4-->
- `test_maybe_run_gc_skips_within_interval` (function) — Verifies a second immediate _maybe_run_gc call is skipped because it falls inside the GC interval. <!--#c13fd965a64257ba-->
- `test_maybe_run_gc_reruns_after_interval` (function) — Verifies _maybe_run_gc runs _gc_once again once the simulated last-sweep time is more than one interval in the past. <!--#8ad9f44160f9ec67-->
- `test_maybe_run_gc_disabled_when_interval_nonpositive` (function) — Verifies a non-positive gc_interval fully disables the GC tick, leaving _gc_once uncalled and _last_gc_at unset. <!--#e0fb8cfc1ce0cf57-->
- `test_gc_once_sweeps_each_root_with_max_age` (function) — Verifies _gc_once calls gc_worktree_runs once per tracked (realpath'd) project root, forwarding gc_max_age_seconds and dry_run=False. <!--#a15cda739b55045a-->
- `test_gc_once_survives_one_root_failure` (function) — Verifies _gc_once swallows (rather than propagates) an exception raised while sweeping a single root. <!--#4f8f0cf140e08ccd-->
- `test_retained_unmerged_branch_warns` (function) — Test asserting that `Daemon._gc_once` emits a WARNING mentioning "未 merge" and the branch name when the mocked `gc_worktree_runs` returns a `WorktreeGCReport` with a retained unmerged worktree. <!--#38bdbf7e82a3ab6d-->
- `test_clean_report_emits_no_warning` (function) — Test verifying that `Daemon._gc_once` logs no WARNING records when the mocked `gc_worktree_runs` returns an empty (clean) `WorktreeGCReport`. <!--#dbd6e89c5b7ae47d-->

### `tests/test_dag_dangling_dependency.py` (python) — Test suite for DAG crash-recovery dangling-dependency handling, verifying that `_prune_recovered_dependencies` drops completed groups and prunes inbound edges without mutating input, and that `DAGScheduler._build_dag` defends against any leftover dangling edges by skipping-and-warning while still enforcing cycle, duplicate-id, and missing-id validation. <!--#159da49e66ebc721|e233edc8c907dda0-->

  - `TestPruneRecoveredDependencies.test_empty_completed_set_is_identity_copy` (method) — Asserts an empty completed set returns an equivalent but distinct (copied) list of all groups. <!--#e312703b23ec214d-->
- `TestRecoveryBuildsValidScheduler` (class) — Test class checking that pruned recovery groups build a valid DAGScheduler and that the scheduler's defense handles unpruned dangling edges. <!--#3f59eb16db89f3b4-->
  - `TestRecoveryBuildsValidScheduler.test_pruned_groups_build_without_raising` (method) — Asserts pruned groups build a scheduler and topologically order without raising on the removed group. <!--#036cc74a7dfaaec4-->
  - `TestRecoveryBuildsValidScheduler.test_unpruned_dangling_edge_would_have_dangled` (method) — Asserts the scheduler tolerates an unpruned dangling edge by skipping it rather than failing. <!--#509e674976efdc0d-->
- `TestBuildDagDanglingDefense` (class) — Test class verifying DAGScheduler._build_dag skips/warns on dangling edges while still enforcing cycle, duplicate-id, and missing-id validation. <!--#6e809daf05c428a2-->
  - `TestBuildDagDanglingDefense.test_dangling_edge_skipped_and_warned` (method) — Asserts a dangling edge is skipped (no in-degree, not in reverse deps) with a warning logged, while legal edges remain intact. <!--#d07ca7239b562c5c-->
  - `TestBuildDagDanglingDefense.test_defense_does_not_swallow_cycle_detection` (method) — Asserts cycle detection still raises ValueError despite the dangling-edge defense. <!--#40acd9c1ad8f7d13-->
  - `TestBuildDagDanglingDefense.test_defense_does_not_swallow_duplicate_id` (method) — Asserts duplicate group ids still raise ValueError. <!--#7cf066c0683d0631-->
  - `TestBuildDagDanglingDefense.test_defense_does_not_swallow_missing_id` (method) — Asserts a group missing its group_id still raises ValueError. <!--#e62e812d8f27faac-->
- `_deps` (function) — Test helper that looks up a group's depends_on list by group_id (or name), raising KeyError if not found. <!--#623e456484868e94-->

### `tests/test_dag_scheduler_status.py` (python) — Unit tests for the DAGScheduler's optional `on_group_status` lifecycle callback, verifying the correct ordered emission of per-group statuses (queued → running → completed/failed/skipped) for success, failure, and downstream-skip cases, and that the scheduler tolerates an absent or exception-raising callback. <!--#64a18dd1e8331b54|880dc3b1d2bca17d-->
- `_completed` (function) — Helper that builds a GroupResult with status 'completed' for a given group id. <!--#41873e858830f33d-->
- `_Collector` (class) — Thread-safe callable test double that records (group_id, status) emissions in order for later assertions. <!--#ae385767a50dab48-->
  - `_Collector.__init__` (method) — Initializes the collector's lock and empty events list. <!--#4bebd83e05c532d5-->
  - `_Collector.__call__` (method) — Records a (group_id, status) emission under the lock when invoked as the status callback. <!--#3a497bd42468aa2c-->
  - `_Collector.statuses_for` (method) — Returns the ordered list of statuses recorded for a specific group id. <!--#5bacaefcb0c1be69-->
- `TestStatusEmission` (class) — Test group asserting the correct sequence and uniqueness of emitted status transitions for success, failure, and downstream-skip cases. <!--#1b5132450013bd4b-->
  - `TestStatusEmission.test_success_chain_queued_running_completed` (method) — Asserts a successful group emits queued → running → completed in order. <!--#c35caa842780c760-->
  - `TestStatusEmission.test_terminal_status_emitted_once_per_group` (method) — Asserts each lifecycle status is emitted exactly once per group. <!--#8d45c7a3fd6f25c2-->
  - `TestStatusEmission.test_failure_emits_failed_and_downstream_skipped` (method) — Asserts an upstream exception emits 'failed' and transitively skips downstream groups (queued → skipped). <!--#9f978d13064c1998-->
  - `TestStatusEmission.test_returned_failed_status_emits_failed` (method) — Asserts a returned GroupResult.failed() (no exception raised) still emits 'failed' and skips downstream. <!--#bd21e69b4115b468-->
- `TestCallbackRobustness` (class) — Test group verifying the scheduler tolerates an absent or exception-raising status callback. <!--#71a5196b52f6ee45-->
  - `TestCallbackRobustness.test_no_callback_is_default` (method) — Asserts omitting on_group_status preserves normal scheduling and results. <!--#3429da429c108f87-->
  - `TestCallbackRobustness.test_callback_exception_does_not_break_run` (method) — Asserts a callback that raises never disrupts scheduling or the returned results. <!--#c78c11e50cb830a5-->

### `tests/test_dag_topology_display.py` (python) — Unit and integration tests for TaskFormatter's DAG topology display, covering topological wave computation (_compute_topo_waves), rendered topology diagrams with edge/merge symbols and LLM call numbering (_build_dag_topology), and when format_implement_plan includes or gracefully omits the Execution Topology section. <!--#0bf3b4a35c49198d|c4753f5a31d144ca-->

  - `TestBuildDagTopology.test_llm_call_numbering` (method) — Asserts LLM call numbers are assigned sequentially across topological waves. <!--#371b57c6523204a5-->

  - `TestFormatImplementPlanTopology.console` (method) — Pytest fixture providing a fixed-width forced-terminal Rich Console for deterministic rendering. <!--#d25ce632aaa5c1be-->

### `tests/test_discovery_analyze_ws_delivery.py` (python) — End-to-end boundary regression suite for issue #260 that drives the real DaemonHistoryReader over a scripted on-disk engine.json/jsonl evolution mimicking the discovery→analyze transition — replaying the daemon's signature-gated push loop through the real server cache and /ws/ui fanout — to prove every disk append streams incrementally with no loss, duplication, or freeze, and to lock the fix where a same-(mtime,size) middle rewrite of a large active engine.json must yield a fresh parse and shift the active-flow signature. <!--#21cd3526e56a97f9|d770d978f3bf56f5-->
- `_UiWS` (class) — A minimal UI-WebSocket stand-in that records every decoded frame sent to it and can filter captured `history_data` frames by flow id. <!--#7ad41ce10c30c033-->
  - `_UiWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the stub's `sent` list that accumulates received frames. <!--#d14bbb740fc91394-->
  - `_UiWS.send_text` (method) — Async send hook that JSON-decodes each outgoing text frame and appends it to the capture list. <!--#015e8192c9e42ee8-->
  - `_UiWS.history_frames` (method) — Returns the captured `history_data` frames, optionally narrowed to a single flow id. <!--#bf1df282dc320385-->
- `_write_engine` (function) — Test helper that writes a realistic `engine.json` (flow_id, status, `state.steps` table, current_step_index) under `tianluo/state/` to simulate the discovery→analyze boundary where the full steps table first appears and status flips PAUSED→RUNNING. <!--#7c5cf4b2eac3b176-->
- `_hist` (function) — Tiny test helper returning the per-flow history directory path `root/tianluo/history/<flow_id>`. <!--#601cb88cd9e45820-->
- `_write_jsonl` (function) — Writes a list of records as a fresh JSONL file, creating parent directories. <!--#4f3e9d9b8f5030ea-->
- `_append_jsonl` (function) — Appends a list of records as JSONL lines to an existing file. <!--#50fd55bc5ca4ef54-->
- `_chat` (function) — Builds a chat-message record dict with role, content, and timestamp. <!--#653f232ec7903ab1-->
- `_started` (function) — Builds a `step_started` record dict for the given step id and type. <!--#ebbba86f08b85fb3-->
- `_completed` (function) — Builds a `step_completed` record dict wrapping the finished step's data. <!--#7aa09ab2396593b4-->
- `_boundary_mutations` (function) — Returns an ordered list of mutation callables that replay the discovery→analyze boundary (empty-steps discovery, pause/resume, first steps-table write with PAUSED→RUNNING flip, new analyze jsonl, and mid-step appends), each returning the labels it wrote. <!--#eccdc279506015fb-->
- `_normal_step_mutations` (function) — Returns a control sequence of mutation callables for an ordinary analyze→plan boundary (steps table already present, index simply increments) to guard against regression. <!--#2315f8ce06d69b90-->
- `_GatedBoundaryDriver` (class) — A test driver that reproduces `DaemonClient`'s per-tick push loop — computing the active-flow signature debounce gate and reading+broadcasting deltas through the real reader, server cache, and `/ws/ui` fanout. <!--#cc8f703904eac054-->
  - `_GatedBoundaryDriver.__init__` (method) — Wires up the driver's real reader, server state, UI hub, stub WebSocket, request registry, and per-tick signature/cursor tracking maps. <!--#21228bf34e67c0de-->
  - `_GatedBoundaryDriver.setup` (method) — Registers the test machine with the server state and subscribes the stub UI WebSocket to the hub under the owner id. <!--#23c02f78d7a08db2-->
  - `_GatedBoundaryDriver.tick` (method) — Runs one push-loop tick: debounces when the active-flow signature is unchanged, else reads active-flow deltas, rebuilds cursors (retaining live terminal flows), and broadcasts each increment via the real message handler. <!--#c6ccf804ffd74a5f-->
  - `_GatedBoundaryDriver.ui_bodies` (method) — Returns, in order, every conversation content body that actually reached the live UI for a given flow. <!--#28ea0806d4a04a3f-->
- `_run_gated_scenario` (function) — Applies each mutation, ticks the gated driver (asserting steady-state debounce on a second tick), and records the labels expected versus the bodies delivered after each step. <!--#d8967d26695f7a0e-->
- `test_boundary_each_disk_append_delivered_via_gated_push` (function) — Core #260 test asserting every disk append across the discovery→analyze boundary is delivered incrementally over the live `/ws/ui` stream with no mid-stream full reload. <!--#cf448f6af31fc189-->
- `test_boundary_streamed_records_equal_full_snapshot_no_loss_no_dup` (function) — Asserts that concatenating all broadcast frames exactly equals the authoritative full snapshot across the boundary — nothing lost and nothing duplicated. <!--#49681e4f97b44c27-->
- `test_normal_step_boundary_not_regressed` (function) — Control test locking that an ordinary analyze→plan boundary still streams every append through the same gated harness. <!--#d167405e6fe0004b-->
- `_build_large_engine` (function) — Constructs a >128 KiB `engine.json` whose only varying bytes are a marker buried in the true middle of the steps table, outside the head+tail verify windows. <!--#6d883d0aa6eb1d04-->
- `test_active_engine_json_middle_rewrite_returns_fresh_parse` (function) — Locks the #260 primary fix: a same-(mtime,size) rewrite differing only in the file's middle must return the fresh parse rather than the stale cached one. <!--#51dc102375135d56-->
- `test_active_flow_signature_moves_on_engine_middle_rewrite` (function) — Regression test (G5) asserting that `DaemonHistoryReader.active_flow_signature` shifts when a large `engine.json` is rewritten in the middle with the same `(mtime, size)`, because the folded whole-content digest changes — so an engine-only PAUSE→resume tick is no longer debounced and the push loop reads the delta immediately. <!--#4bfbf71da421f5cf-->
- `_build_large_worktree_engine` (function) — Like `_build_large_engine` but produces a `--worktree`-mode `engine.json` with worktree tail keys trailing the giant steps table. <!--#f6625d89c059e4bd-->
- `test_worktree_engine_middle_rewrite_fresh_and_tail_keys_preserved` (function) — Worktree non-regression test verifying the whole-content freshness hash catches a middle rewrite while still surfacing the worktree tail keys on the live read. <!--#9573777a0b903b45-->

### `tests/test_discovery_error_i18n.py` (python) — Pytest module verifying that the discovery step's LLMCallError console panel (title and body, both rendered and persisted to step.error_message) is resolved through i18n and differs correctly between en-US and zh-CN. <!--#63ac682325f3d8f1|ef52fa3a6091903c-->

- `test_json_extraction_failure_panel_is_translated` (function) — Parametrized over en-US/zh-CN, asserts a JSON-extraction LLMCallError makes discovery fail and render/persist the translated `error_json_extraction` body and `error_title` rather than raw i18n keys. <!--#8fd43acf1f29ac9e-->

### `tests/test_discovery_interactive_pause.py` (python) — Test module exercising the interactive discovery-pause dual-path wait in tianluo.commands.run, verifying that terminal question/confirm pauses mirror themselves to tianluo/calls/ call files answerable from the web console, that whichever of the terminal or web response answers first drives the same live process forward while keeping the flow RUNNING (or persists PAUSED on cancel) with correct file cleanup, and that the DaemonAggregator deduplicates multiple call files per (flow, step). <!--#d0875dd58dc363c3|fd2424055c942019-->

### `tests/test_disk_json_cache.py` (python) — Unit tests for the unified daemon disk-JSON parse cache (#243/#260/#209), asserting via json.loads-seam counting that unchanged files parse at most once across many ticks, real changes (including same-(mtime,size) mid-file rewrites and size/mtime-preserving flow swaps) trigger exactly one re-parse, active engine.json is content-hashed but never re-parsed while unchanged, and oversized files are never full-parsed but have their header keys recovered by a bounded degraded head+tail read with warn-once on failure and no cache pollution. <!--#07ae4f065058c1fa|61a0cdd424f5e251-->
- `_clean_cache` (function) — Autouse pytest fixture that clears the module-level parse cache and warn-once set before and after each test. <!--#f901622b842eabe8-->
- `_count_parses` (function) — Test helper that monkeypatches `_parse_json` to count full-file JSON parses and returns the counter dict. <!--#1aa04823ea8aa141-->
- `_engine_json` (function) — Test helper building an indent=2 engine.json string with the real head/state/tail key ordering emitted by FlowInstance.to_dict, to exercise the degraded head+tail scan. <!--#f5d9ce7bafcb4cb8-->
- `test_unchanged_file_parsed_once_across_many_calls` (function) — Asserts an unchanged file is parsed exactly once despite 21 cached reads returning identical results. <!--#9c8b30dc3d49a80e-->
- `test_reparsed_after_content_change` (function) — Asserts a genuine rewrite (new mtime/size) triggers exactly one re-parse and no further parses while unchanged. <!--#0baac5a282dd8071-->
- `_count_file_parses` (function) — Test helper that monkeypatches `_parse_json_file` to count whole-file read+parse calls, which the active path must not repeat for an unchanged file. <!--#09e6098abfd6d331-->
- `test_active_unchanged_not_reparsed` (function) — Asserts that an unchanged active engine.json (verify_content=True) is re-read and re-hashed each poll but never re-parsed via json.loads, keeping the #260 fix off the #209 parse sink. <!--#e1d556ae4aa00395-->
- `test_active_large_underguard_parsed_once_but_middle_rewrite_caught` (function) — Verifies the #260 core trade on a ~1 MiB under-guard file: unchanged polls parse zero times, yet a same-(mtime,size) rewrite buried in the middle state block is still detected (exactly one re-parse) because the hash covers the whole file rather than the old head+tail window. <!--#b7728239acf811ba-->
- `test_active_same_size_same_mtime_swap_detected` (function) — Confirms a completed→new-flow swap that preserves both size and mtime is still caught by the whole-content hash, so the daemon never reports the stale superseded flow. <!--#a400ea85df1facb5-->
- `test_active_underguard_midfile_change_is_reparsed` (function) — Checks that an under-guard file changed only in its middle state block is reparsed via the advanced (mtime,size) stat key (mtime forced forward here), complementing the same-(mtime,size) middle case locked by the large-underguard test. <!--#e144a28927c00842-->
- `test_active_reparses_after_real_change` (function) — Asserts a genuine rewrite (new mtime/size) is re-parsed in active verify_content mode. <!--#fa9c3d5f5408bbd3-->
- `test_parse_failure_returns_none_and_is_not_reparsed` (function) — Asserts invalid JSON returns None once and a corrupt-but-unchanged file is not re-parsed on every tick. <!--#132f471a7699d925-->
- `test_missing_file_returns_none` (function) — Asserts both read_json_cached and read_engine_header return None for a nonexistent file. <!--#8e3d262c0603c9f1-->
- `test_small_engine_header_uses_full_cached_parse` (function) — Asserts an under-threshold engine.json header is served via a single cached full parse routed through `_parse_json`. <!--#73ffc9bb08f0a1eb-->
- `_write_oversized` (function) — Test helper writing a well-formed engine.json larger than SIZE_GUARD_BYTES with a padding blob in `state` so the degraded head+tail read must straddle it. <!--#d32b4ea46b5a0049-->
- `test_oversized_file_never_full_parsed_but_header_extracted` (function) — Asserts an oversized file is never full-parsed yet its head- and tail-cluster header keys (including is_worktree_mode) are extracted, with no cache pollution. <!--#179d3f23062ee673-->
- `test_oversized_extraction_failure_warns_once` (function) — A pytest test verifying that when read_engine_header encounters an oversized engine.json file with no recoverable top-level flow_id, it returns None, logs the WARNING only once across repeated calls, never triggers a full parse, and leaves the cache empty. <!--#a16d8fb5f8b405c3-->

### `tests/test_docs_updater.py` (python) — Boundary/unit test suite for DocumentationUpdater covering VERSIONS.md entry insertion and same-version merging (empty file, no title, duplicate/prefix-collision, custom and file-fallback templates), README badge placement around front-matter, independent update_both error handling, and Template placeholder rendering. <!--#c755cff6c87e570d|ab3d6cccb6811daa-->
- `TestEmptyVersionsFile` (class) — Tests that an empty VERSIONS.md file correctly receives a freshly inserted version entry. <!--#8d74e2522a708f58-->
  - `TestEmptyVersionsFile.test_empty_file_gets_entry` (method) — Asserts that updating an empty VERSIONS.md (with the default entry template forced) inserts the version heading and change bullet. <!--#5020936fc130a710-->
- `TestVersionsWithoutTitle` (class) — Tests insertion behavior when VERSIONS.md lacks a `# Version History` title. <!--#65faa944a931adf3-->
  - `TestVersionsWithoutTitle.test_no_title_inserts_before_first_content` (method) — Asserts that with no markdown heading present, the new entry is inserted before the existing prose while preserving it. <!--#f048e0b95692a667-->
- `TestDuplicateVersionMerge` (class) — Test class verifying DocumentationUpdater.update_versions_md merges new changelog entries into an already-present version block instead of duplicating headers, across suffixed, suffixless, custom-template, and prefix-collision cases. <!--#fd63daa3003f5243-->
  - `TestDuplicateVersionMerge.test_existing_version_header_not_duplicated` (method) — Asserts a distinct entry for an already-present version is merged into the single existing header rather than swallowed or duplicated. <!--#f42302829edd3cc2-->
  - `TestDuplicateVersionMerge.test_verbatim_rewrite_is_noop` (method) — Asserts re-writing an identical bullet for an existing version is idempotent and adds no duplicate line. <!--#f2b84cd194c77196-->
  - `TestDuplicateVersionMerge.test_suffixless_custom_template_header_is_merged` (method) — Asserts a second update merges into a suffixless `## {{version}}` custom-template header instead of inserting a duplicate. <!--#ae1c1e6692b55fab-->
  - `TestDuplicateVersionMerge.test_suffixless_header_merged_under_default_template` (method) — Asserts a bare `## 1.2.3` header (no date tail) is recognised and merged into even when the effective template is the default suffixed one. <!--#fa0d7dcbaecf332c-->
  - `TestDuplicateVersionMerge.test_prefix_version_not_matched_as_duplicate` (method) — Anti-prefix guard asserting version `11.13` creates a new header rather than being mis-merged into an existing `## 11.13.1` block. <!--#2725e50e69f420d1-->
- `TestReadmeFrontMatter` (class) — Tests README badge placement across leading YAML front-matter, HTML-comment headers, and heading-less files. <!--#e6d2aabc8dfe9f3c-->
  - `TestReadmeFrontMatter.test_badge_inserted_after_heading_not_breaking_front_matter` (method) — Asserts the version badge is placed after the heading and after intact YAML front-matter, before body content. <!--#b70585e97cb48ccb-->
  - `TestReadmeFrontMatter.test_html_comment_header_is_skipped` (method) — Asserts a leading HTML comment is preserved and the badge is inserted after the heading that follows it. <!--#f4b31a0ea0bef416-->
  - `TestReadmeFrontMatter.test_no_heading_prepends_badge` (method) — Asserts the badge is prepended to the file when README.md has no heading at all. <!--#f04486d700104338-->
- `TestConfigCustomEntryTemplate` (class) — Test class verifying DocumentationUpdater honors a configured `versions_entry_template`, rendering with it and still detecting/merging same-version entries for non-heading templates. <!--#4967db2072cf4c36-->
  - `TestConfigCustomEntryTemplate.test_custom_entry_template_used` (method) — Asserts the custom entry template is stored and renders the version and changes into VERSIONS.md as configured. <!--#2a384d33f0504f57-->
  - `TestConfigCustomEntryTemplate.test_non_heading_template_merges_same_version` (method) — Asserts a non-heading custom entry template still merges repeated same-version updates, stays idempotent on identical rewrites, and keeps different versions as distinct entries. <!--#4a82cb66ebc5caf8-->
- `TestVersionsTemplateFileFallback` (class) — Tests fallback selection of the versions_entry template from the packaged versions_md.md file versus config and the built-in default. <!--#4098f347e903b010-->
  - `TestVersionsTemplateFileFallback.test_fallback_reads_first_section_block` (method) — Asserts a placeholder-bearing first `##` block in versions_md.md is adopted as the entry template and substitutes real version/changes. <!--#446edf1e64c44ef4-->
  - `TestVersionsTemplateFileFallback.test_concrete_first_block_rejected_falls_back_to_default` (method) — Asserts a concrete (non-placeholder) first block is rejected, falling back to the DEFAULT template so the real version/changes are written. <!--#d8000cb90e87b9d2-->
  - `TestVersionsTemplateFileFallback.test_fallback_to_default_when_file_absent` (method) — Asserts that a missing versions_md.md yields None from the file helper and the updater uses the built-in DEFAULT entry template. <!--#e8346f1eeda91920-->
  - `TestVersionsTemplateFileFallback.test_config_template_wins_over_file` (method) — Asserts a config-supplied entry template takes precedence over the versions_md.md file template. <!--#872e4fe24c10ef6b-->
- `TestUpdateBothIndependentErrors` (class) — Tests that update_both handles README and VERSIONS failures independently. <!--#226389aca3d08c7a-->
  - `TestUpdateBothIndependentErrors.test_missing_readme_does_not_block_versions` (method) — Asserts a missing README yields readme=False while VERSIONS still updates successfully (versions=True). <!--#72eb81eb9e3325fe-->
  - `TestUpdateBothIndependentErrors.test_both_sides_succeed` (method) — Asserts update_both returns True for both when valid README.md and VERSIONS.md exist. <!--#8ca38bff64dd47d8-->
- `TestTemplateRendering` (class) — Unit tests for the Template placeholder-substitution rendering behavior. <!--#30867f09179f990a-->
  - `TestTemplateRendering.test_context_overrides_defaults` (method) — Asserts render-time context values override the Template's default placeholders. <!--#fece7685e8e02d23-->
  - `TestTemplateRendering.test_unknown_placeholder_preserved` (method) — Asserts placeholders absent from the context are left literally unsubstituted in the output. <!--#90bfed3767d74037-->

### `tests/test_end_session_cmd.py` (python) — End-to-end test suite for the `end-session` command, covering worktree and main-branch session archival (including history collision sidecars, flow_id resolution, and stale/unregistered worktree removal), live-process discovery and SIGTERM/SIGKILL process-tree termination, and safety guards that skip destructive cleanup when a process survives, an archive step fails, or the target flow cannot be confirmed. <!--#c4a1050823230675|59bb456ffbaf3832-->
- `_init_repo` (function) — Helper that initializes a git repo at the given path with a configured user and an initial committed README. <!--#1635ad85954c81ae-->
- `_branch_exists` (function) — Helper that returns whether a given git branch exists in the repo via `git rev-parse --verify`. <!--#fe856a428f75db97-->
- `_write_fake_se3` (function) — Test helper that writes an executable `tianluo`/`se3` shebang script running a given body, so a spawned process presents psutil the real console-script cmdline shape that `_cmdline_is_se3_run` matches. <!--#4f6f1af05478003d-->
- `_make_worktree_session` (function) — Test helper that creates a real git worktree session with engine.json, a resumable snapshot, and a history jsonl file inside the worktree, returning its path. <!--#a1c50ee74b71543b-->
- `_make_main_session` (function) — Test helper that creates a main-branch (non-worktree) session by writing engine.json and a resumable snapshot under main/tianluo/state. <!--#3a29739b15ac76eb-->
- `test_worktree_session_is_archived` (function) — Verifies end_session archives a PAUSED worktree session (worktree archived under .archive, engine state promoted with project_root restamped, history synced) and cleans up the branch and worktree directory. <!--#a3a4a3eca2510b73-->
- `test_worktree_session_history_collision_uses_sidecar` (function) — Verifies that when a worktree history file name collides with an existing main-project file, the original is preserved and the worktree copy lands as a `.from-<branch>` sidecar. <!--#58003515edd3abe5-->
- `test_main_branch_session_is_archived` (function) — Verifies end_session on a main-branch session moves engine.json into archive/ and clears the resumable snapshot. <!--#8ee987a513aa099b-->
- `test_flow_id_resolved_from_main_engine` (function) — Verifies that when flow_id is omitted, end_session reads it from the main engine.json and still archives that session. <!--#965cf94487ad8d89-->
- `test_terminate_by_pid_sigterm` (function) — Verifies that end-session with `--pid` terminates a live long-running child process via SIGTERM. <!--#03b178844d9667b7-->
- `test_terminate_sigkill_escalation` (function) — Verifies that a process ignoring SIGTERM is escalated to SIGKILL after the grace period. <!--#7b9aee7aa64c72ad-->
- `test_terminate_kills_child_subprocess` (function) — Verifies that ending a session kills the whole process tree, not just the parent, so agent/test child subprocesses are not orphaned. <!--#08581e7e7cf1d8e7-->
- `test_worktree_without_branch_is_still_cleaned_up` (function) — Verifies a worktree session whose engine.json lacks worktree_branch is still cleaned up by inferring the branch from git's worktree metadata. <!--#ae5410a4b80513ec-->
- `test_stale_unregistered_worktree_dir_is_removed` (function) — Verifies a stale worktree dir with no git registration and no branch is archived and then fully removed from disk rather than reported cleaned while surviving. <!--#897e271d5c46804e-->
- `test_discovers_live_worktree_parent_by_descendant_cwd` (function) — Verifies that a live `luo run --worktree` parent (which keeps cwd at main_root) is discovered for its flow via a descendant agent subprocess whose cwd is inside the worktree path. <!--#602105da0154f4de-->
- `test_discovers_live_worktree_parent_via_pidfile` (function) — Verifies `_discover_pids_for_flow` locates a live `se3 run --worktree` parent via the worktree's run.pid marker when cwd/descendant heuristics cannot find it. <!--#3b26aad111ab357a-->
- `test_stale_pidfile_is_ignored` (function) — Verifies a run.pid pointing at a dead pid is not reported as a live process by `_discover_pids_for_flow`. <!--#1807213945028af0-->
- `test_no_live_process_still_archives` (function) — Verifies a PAUSED worktree with no live process is still archived cleanly and its branch cleaned up. <!--#47c09b6cc0163bb0-->
- `test_unkillable_process_skips_destructive_archive` (function) — Verifies that when a `--pid` target survives SIGKILL, destructive archival is skipped, the worktree/branch are preserved, and the command exits non-zero. <!--#53445b7e8ff0d055-->
- `test_missing_worktree_degrades_to_main_archive` (function) — Verifies that with no worktree found, end-session falls back to the main-branch archival path without error. <!--#04b51133a080e5f7-->
- `test_mismatched_main_flow_is_not_archived` (function) — Verifies ending flow A (worktree gone) does not archive an unrelated active flow B whose engine.json owns the main state. <!--#264002757fec8665-->
- `test_unreadable_main_flow_is_not_archived` (function) — Verifies that when the main engine.json carries no readable flow_id, the destructive clear is skipped rather than archiving the wrong session. <!--#36955028d44ceb60-->
- `test_archive_failure_preserves_worktree_and_branch` (function) — Verifies that a failed worktree archive (patched to raise) skips destructive cleanup so the branch and worktree survive and the command exits non-zero. <!--#5a5c3af40567f379-->
- `test_step_failure_does_not_abort_and_exit_nonzero` (function) — Verifies a raising sub-step (patched promote) is recorded and yields a non-zero exit without aborting, while later steps still run and clean up the branch. <!--#b1b1f38ff6b6d2e2-->
- `test_unresolvable_root_returns_one` (function) — Verifies that an unresolvable project root causes end_session to return exit code 1. <!--#a6b850b8cf6bf46e-->
- `_FakePsutil` (class) — A minimal stand-in for the `psutil` module whose `Process` objects always raise a configurable exception from `cmdline()`, while reusing the real exception classes and `STATUS_ZOMBIE` so production `except` clauses still match. <!--#1f2a38f4d95380d7-->
  - `_FakePsutil.__init__` (method) — Stores the caller-supplied exception factory that the fake process will raise when its cmdline is inspected. <!--#aa0d3bf5bb4401a8-->
  - `_FakePsutil.Process` (method) — Returns a throwaway process object mirroring the `psutil.Process` API whose `cmdline()` raises the configured exception. <!--#fddbbe561f76bd78-->
- `test_unreadable_cmdline_keeps_live_verdict` (function) — Regression guard asserting `_pid_is_live_se3_run` still reports True when a confirmed-alive pid's cmdline is unreadable, so end-session cleanup cannot run under a still-executing flow. <!--#95aad214c0ba63d4-->
- `test_vanished_pid_is_not_live` (function) — Asserts `_pid_is_live_se3_run` returns False when the process disappears mid-inspection (`NoSuchProcess`), i.e. a genuinely stale pid. <!--#fe16939db6a30c61-->
- `test_unreadable_cmdline_marker_is_not_cleared` (function) — End-to-end check that `_clear_stale_local_run_pidfile` refuses to reclaim and leaves the `tianluo/state/run.pid` marker on disk when the recorded pid is live but its cmdline is inaccessible. <!--#fe99c34cdedbfcbc-->

### `tests/test_end_session_frontend.py` (python) — A frontend guard suite that verifies the end-session feature's static wiring across app.js, index.html, and style.css and runs the standalone Node isFlowEndable/endFlow assertion suite covering all decision-matrix branches and HTTP receipt handling. <!--#a7b2982fe7c21231|40f07371958d3d17-->

- `test_app_js_has_end_session_helpers` (function) — Statically guards that app.js defines all expected end-session helper functions and the endSessionRequests debounce set. <!--#b45cbc44e1a63edf-->
- `test_app_js_exports_end_session_pure_helpers` (function) — Checks that app.js's module.exports block exposes the pure helpers (isFlowEndable, isEndInProgress, makeEndButton) for the Node tests. <!--#b9ae20aab1676420-->
- `test_app_js_end_button_injected_into_card_and_sidebar` (function) — Asserts makeEndButton(flow) is invoked at least twice so the End button appears on both the flow card and the detail sidebar. <!--#40bdd5688d39974a-->
- `test_app_js_end_flow_handles_all_receipts` (function) — Verifies the endFlow function POSTs to /end, branches on 404/409/503 responses, and debounces via endSessionRequests. <!--#5a6dca2a7fb3ab57-->
- `test_index_html_has_end_session_modal` (function) — Confirms index.html contains the end-session confirmation modal's elements and that the modal defaults to hidden. <!--#c1821487f8bd258d-->
- `test_style_css_has_btn_end` (function) — Checks style.css defines the .btn-end rule using the danger (--red) accent plus a disabled-state rule. <!--#63f89e1c4a9e12d0-->

### `tests/test_end_session_protocol_daemon.py` (python) — Unit tests for the END_SESSION control-plane path (feature group G2), covering the daemon protocol's MSG_END_SESSION registration/make_end_session round-trip, the spawner's end-session argv assembly, the daemon's request_end_session flow lookup with worktree-to-main folding and error cases, and the DaemonClient's END_SESSION dispatch/routing including empty-flow ignore, project_root reverse-resolution, and handler-exception containment. <!--#aa6dd838a93fbc86|0f7ee9ebf8749172-->
- `test_msg_end_session_is_server_to_daemon` (function) — Asserts MSG_END_SESSION has the right name and is registered as a server→daemon message in the correct protocol sets. <!--#576fc568a0cafaa3-->
- `test_protocol_version_current` (function) — Pins the daemon wire `protocol.PROTOCOL_VERSION` to the current revision "9", documenting in its docstring the successive feature additions (END_SESSION, traffic reduction, presence, upload/fetch, spawn strategy, plan mode, history step-window) that drove each bump. <!--#5e101ee9c6759cfe-->
- `test_make_end_session_roundtrip` (function) — Checks a fully-populated make_end_session message survives a JSON encode/decode round-trip with all fields intact. <!--#d371965e5bb78e55-->
- `test_make_end_session_omits_empty_optionals` (function) — Verifies empty optional fields (project_root, reason) are dropped from the wire payload while a defaulted reason is kept. <!--#a68acc0ddbb54efa-->
- `_capturing_spawner` (function) — Test helper that builds a DaemonSpawner whose _launch is patched to capture argv/cwd/label instead of spawning a subprocess. <!--#ea42f4def5dd3040-->
- `test_end_session_builds_argv` (function) — Asserts spawner.end_session assembles the expected `luo end-session <flow_id> -p ... --pid ...` argv and task label. <!--#be8e5197fb7efd8d-->
- `test_end_session_omits_pid_when_none` (function) — Verifies the --pid flag is omitted from the argv when no pid is supplied. <!--#305ab835fde3e1b6-->
- `test_end_session_uses_resolved_se3_command` (function) — Confirms the argv prefix comes from _resolve_se3_command() rather than a hardcoded 'se3' literal. <!--#6daf8a8de0efb5a5-->
- `_StubSpawner` (class) — Test double standing in for the spawner that records end_session calls without launching a real subprocess. <!--#60e232d13b47e345-->
  - `_StubSpawner.__init__` (method) — Initializes the stub spawner's empty calls-recording list. <!--#052d7032db4d16d0-->
  - `_StubSpawner.end_session` (method) — Records each (flow_id, project_root, pid) invocation and returns a placeholder object. <!--#c4b856cbe3382914-->
- `test_request_end_session_locates_flow_and_spawns` (function) — Verifies request_end_session looks up a supervised flow and dispatches end_session with its resolved root and pid. <!--#ae5e672bfab5d383-->
- `test_request_end_session_prefers_supplied_root` (function) — Asserts a server-supplied project_root overrides the supervisor's registered root. <!--#a1a318767822f163-->
- `test_request_end_session_folds_worktree_root_to_main` (function) — Test verifying that Daemon.request_end_session normalizes a worktree project_root (<main>/tianluo/worktrees/<name>) back to its <main> repo path (with pid=None) before spawning the end-session run, so the worktree can be located and archived. <!--#2ad78bc118761b32-->
- `test_request_end_session_unknown_flow_raises` (function) — Asserts request_end_session raises ValueError and never spawns when the flow is unknown and no root is given. <!--#5aab9260ef552cbe-->
- `test_request_end_session_unsupervised_flow_with_root_dispatches` (function) — Verifies a dangling (non-live) flow still dispatches end_session—with no pid hint—when the server supplies a root. <!--#d45b06b0ec1eea3e-->
- `test_request_end_session_empty_flow_raises` (function) — Asserts request_end_session raises ValueError on an empty flow_id. <!--#ddca5db47319cda1-->
- `_make_client` (function) — Test helper that constructs a DaemonClient with default identity/snapshot args and overridable handlers. <!--#2166366244481ca6-->
- `test_dispatch_end_session_routes_to_handler` (function) — Verifies the client's async _dispatch routes a decoded END_SESSION message to the configured handler with flow/root/reason. <!--#497088df98906f11-->
- `test_handle_end_session_ignores_empty_flow_id` (function) — Verifies DaemonClient._handle_end_session drops payloads with an empty flow_id, never invoking the end-session handler. <!--#db11deaf155b9740-->
- `test_handle_end_session_resolves_root_from_index` (function) — Verifies that when project_root is missing, _handle_end_session reverse-resolves it from the history provider's index and forwards it (with the default reason) to the handler. <!--#522ca82a96c92415-->
- `test_handle_end_session_without_handler_is_noop` (function) — Verifies _handle_end_session is a safe no-op that raises nothing when no end_session_handler is configured on the client. <!--#e293a7271a63eea8-->
- `test_handle_end_session_swallows_handler_exception` (function) — Verifies _handle_end_session catches and logs a handler exception so the daemon connection survives rather than propagating the error. <!--#0e4f5e8e51f73015-->

### `tests/test_end_session_server.py` (python) — Test suite for the POST /api/flows/{id}/end REST endpoint, verifying its honest-receipt branches — 404 (unknown/cross-owner), 409 (already completed), 503 (daemon disconnected), and 202 (dispatched) — and that the 202 path dispatches MSG_END_SESSION carrying the flow's project_root and reason, including default-reason and dangling-worktree cases. <!--#2ef3b27a81649bb4|a9e6f953651aedd3-->
- `client_and_app` (function) — Pytest fixture yielding an authenticated admin-owner TestClient paired with its app. <!--#7d83389c850ee0e5-->
- `_snapshot` (function) — Helper that builds a daemon STATUS_UPDATE snapshot dict for a machine with the given flows. <!--#bb6cf1d39dab98d7-->
- `_report_flow` (function) — Test helper that opens a daemon WebSocket, sends an authenticated HELLO plus a STATUS_UPDATE reporting one flow with the given id/status/project_root, and polls the REST API until that flow becomes visible (or fails after 100 tries). <!--#b24883fe39952fed-->
- `test_end_flow_unknown_returns_404` (function) — Asserts ending an unknown flow_id returns 404 and leaks nothing. <!--#75e7bb681254ccf1-->
- `test_end_flow_cross_owner_returns_404` (function) — A server test verifying that a flow owned by another owner reads as absent (404, never 409/503) when a different owner attempts to end it, while the true owner's daemon-connected end request returns 202. <!--#5583276ec36d6b66-->
- `test_end_flow_completed_returns_409` (function) — Asserts a COMPLETED flow returns 409 (exists but already done) with no misleading end_dispatched status. <!--#b14568a5e2b2d798-->
- `test_end_flow_completed_worktree_dispatches` (function) — A server test verifying that a COMPLETED session under a `<main>/tianluo/worktrees/<name>` root stays endable (202, END_SESSION dispatched with the worktree project_root forwarded) so a dangling orphan worktree can be archived, unlike an ordinary completed flow. <!--#49b9014305a7e23f-->
- `test_end_flow_daemon_disconnected_returns_503` (function) — Asserts a still-visible flow whose owning daemon has disconnected returns 503. <!--#b4b7567524e79b33-->
- `test_end_flow_dispatches_end_session` (function) — Asserts that ending a non-completed flow on a connected daemon returns 202 and dispatches MSG_END_SESSION carrying the flow's flow_id, machine_id, project_root, and the request's reason. <!--#53ab46a2e3c5f23f-->
- `test_end_flow_default_reason_when_body_omitted` (function) — Asserts that POSTing to the end endpoint with no request body still returns 202 and dispatches MSG_END_SESSION with the default reason "user terminated". <!--#e8dc816c74703d9d-->

### `tests/test_engine_hot_cold_split.py` (python) — Write-path test suite for the engine.json hot/cold split (issue #244/G5), verifying that the persisted header stays KB-scale and hotcold-formatted, that each save rewrites only the cold files whose step or context content actually changed, that resumable snapshots share the cold partition without bloating with payload size, and that content-hash keying plus save/load round-trips preserve payloads correctly. <!--#164a6313309b8803|ec32135b80eb06ea-->
- `pm` (function) — Pytest fixture returning a PersistenceManager rooted at a temporary directory. <!--#2f092c27109e7260-->
- `_big_step` (function) — Helper that builds a single completed Step whose inputs and outputs each carry a ~payload_kb KiB blob. <!--#4af4ea8b472836c5-->
- `_flow_with_steps` (function) — Helper that constructs a RUNNING FlowInstance with n_steps heavy steps and a large shared context for exercising the hot/cold split. <!--#d3a569982b3199c1-->
- `_WriteSpy` (class) — Test double that monkeypatches PersistenceManager._atomic_write_json to record the basenames of every file a persist touched, enabling write-amplification assertions. <!--#f12c27015d2c69dc-->
  - `_WriteSpy.__init__` (method) — Installs the monkeypatch that wraps _atomic_write_json to log each written path's name while delegating to the original. <!--#72eb0ef7a5b20b5f-->
  - `_WriteSpy.reset` (method) — Clears the recorded list of written filenames between assertions. <!--#5c2e6bd0ec5341f4-->
  - `_WriteSpy.written` (method) — Property exposing the recorded write names as a set for membership assertions. <!--#1883677d8dbeefab-->
- `test_header_is_hotcold_format` (function) — Asserts a saved flow's header uses the hotcold/1 format with per-step cold_ref entries and an externalized context_ref rather than inlined payloads. <!--#1dfd5f0522557b4b-->
- `test_header_under_100kb_with_large_payloads` (function) — Verifies the header stays under 100 KB even when steps and context hold >800 KiB of cold data actually written to the cold directory. <!--#ee30f497d507ad7d-->
- `test_header_size_independent_of_step_count` (function) — Confirms header size scales only with the small per-step status table, staying under budget regardless of step count or payload size. <!--#d790e4f3e1a53fb6-->
- `test_first_save_writes_all_cold_files` (function) — Checks that the initial save writes the engine.json header plus every step's cold file and the context cold file. <!--#f54b660fd5bc9e0a-->
- `test_single_step_change_touches_only_that_cold_file` (function) — Verifies that changing one step re-writes only that step's cold file (plus the two headers), leaving other steps' and the context's cold files untouched. <!--#ce372093e6d5db2a-->
- `test_no_change_rewrites_only_headers` (function) — Ensures an unchanged re-save rewrites only the headers, touching no step or context cold files. <!--#b10809e1c3103bbe-->
- `test_context_change_touches_only_context_cold_file` (function) — Verifies mutating the shared context re-writes only the context cold file and no step cold files. <!--#3d69805973857fff-->
- `test_resumable_snapshot_is_split_and_small` (function) — Asserts the resumable snapshot is itself a hotcold-format header under 100 KB rather than a copy of the megabytes of payload. <!--#5b25a304d7378db1-->
- `test_resumable_snapshot_shares_cold_partition` (function) — Confirms the snapshot reuses the single steps/<flow_id>/ cold partition, writing each cold file exactly once instead of duplicating it. <!--#d59f239fa81cd8d3-->
- `test_resumable_snapshot_does_not_grow_with_payload` (function) — Verifies the in-flight snapshot header size tracks the header, not the payload, staying nearly constant across a 200×-larger payload. <!--#a1cbf853ae1278ef-->
- `test_roundtrip_preserves_payloads_and_context` (function) — Round-trips a flow through save/load and asserts status, context, per-step inputs/outputs, and artifacts are preserved. <!--#6b102bce68cb965b-->
- `test_content_hash_is_key_order_independent` (function) — Asserts _canonical_json and _content_hash ignore dict key ordering so unchanged steps are not spuriously re-flagged dirty. <!--#d0769590066c4dd9-->
- `test_content_hash_is_stable_across_repeated_serialization` (function) — Verifies hashing the same payload twice yields an identical digest, proving no hidden serialization state. <!--#b69b5a15a4fb7df2-->
- `test_content_hash_coerces_non_json_native_like_the_writer` (function) — Confirms _content_hash uses default=str like the writer so Path values hash the same as their string forms. <!--#cec5c5b85b0be74d-->
- `test_deleted_cold_file_is_rewritten_on_next_save` (function) — Verifies that a hash-matching step whose cold file was deleted is regenerated on the next save via an on-disk existence check and reloads correctly. <!--#bf3cc10cad8be7d1-->
- `test_resumable_roundtrip` (function) — Round-trips a flow through the resumable snapshot and asserts per-step outputs are restored. <!--#a9eac16ef5dd41d5-->

### `tests/test_event_stream.py` (python) — Unit tests for the unified event stream subsystem, covering the EventType/Event model (serialization, round-trips, new_event kwarg routing) and the pluggable Sink implementations — EventEmitter subscription/isolation/scoping, JsonSink NDJSON output, CliSink rendering rules, and HistorySink jsonl persistence — including how CliSink and HistorySink diverge on interactive terminal events. <!--#3ba21a529be06fd3|a45302fb58a4f64d-->
- `test_event_type_covers_full_lifecycle` (function) — Asserts the EventType enum contains exactly the expected full set of flow/step lifecycle event names. <!--#506825669025cff5-->

- `test_event_round_trips_through_dict` (function) — Checks an Event survives a to_dict/from_dict round-trip with type, flow_id, and data preserved. <!--#75a54afd115e14fc-->
- `test_new_event_collects_kwargs_into_data` (function) — Confirms new_event() routes known fields to attributes, collects extra kwargs into data, and stamps a timestamp. <!--#482564ed8c171e52-->

  - `_RecordingSink.__init__` (method) — Initializes the recording sink with an empty events list. <!--#89af3002cb8ba46e-->
  - `_RecordingSink.consume` (method) — Appends each received event to the sink's events list. <!--#cff777c6609049e9-->
- `test_emit_notifies_all_subscribed_sinks` (function) — Verifies EventEmitter.emit() delivers an event to every subscribed sink. <!--#18b757cd7c21814c-->
- `test_subscribe_is_idempotent` (function) — Asserts subscribing the same sink twice results in only one delivery per emit. <!--#f28940217687e086-->
- `test_unsubscribe_stops_delivery` (function) — Confirms an unsubscribed sink no longer receives emitted events. <!--#a611bae4e3b59e75-->
- `test_unsubscribe_unknown_sink_is_noop` (function) — Checks unsubscribing a never-subscribed sink does not raise. <!--#6b0706ff279fd733-->
- `test_emit_isolates_failing_sink` (function) — Verifies a sink that raises during consume does not prevent delivery to other sinks. <!--#f2148ffd30d84912-->
- `test_scope_restores_subscriber_list` (function) — Confirms EventEmitter.scope() yields the emitter and drops sinks added within the scope on exit. <!--#5108fc0d9cf75432-->
- `test_event_stream_alias_is_event_emitter` (function) — Asserts EventStream is an alias for EventEmitter. <!--#9ff8c1c11f292689-->
- `test_json_sink_emits_ndjson` (function) — Verifies JsonSink writes one NDJSON line per event with the expected serialized field set. <!--#bb723b39d09bb07d-->

### `tests/test_extract_failures.py` (python) — Unit tests for `_extract_failures_section` (from tianluo.engine.steps.test), verifying it extracts pytest FAILURES/ERRORS sections, falls back to the trailing max_chars of output when no such section exists, respects the max_chars cap via per-block truncation, stops before the short-test-summary separator, and handles empty/whitespace-only inputs. <!--#87e244931b83400a|a35fea15630566a0-->
- `TestExtractFailuresSection` (class) — Test class grouping all cases for `_extract_failures_section`, covering section extraction, fallback-to-tail behavior, max_chars limits, and edge cases. <!--#560d68a3f0666517-->
  - `TestExtractFailuresSection.test_empty_string` (method) — Asserts an empty input string yields an empty result. <!--#ce61b9c61384f763-->
  - `TestExtractFailuresSection.test_standard_failures_section` (method) — Checks that a standard pytest FAILURES section is extracted with its header, failing test names, and assertion errors. <!--#29d95865dd8b7ce4-->
  - `TestExtractFailuresSection.test_errors_section` (method) — Verifies an ERRORS section (e.g. collection ModuleNotFoundError) is extracted as well as the FAILURES section. <!--#241a822e3ae3606b-->
  - `TestExtractFailuresSection.test_no_failures_section_falls_back_to_tail` (method) — Confirms that output with no FAILURES section falls back to returning the last max_chars of text. <!--#f9ce86c388a73fa2-->
  - `TestExtractFailuresSection.test_respects_max_chars_on_fallback` (method) — Ensures the tail-fallback path honors the max_chars cap and returns exactly the last max_chars characters. <!--#6dd922b04a291b63-->
  - `TestExtractFailuresSection.test_full_section_within_limit` (method) — Checks that a FAILURES section shorter than max_chars is returned in full. <!--#d56dcd5101368819-->
  - `TestExtractFailuresSection.test_truncation_of_long_section` (method) — Verifies a FAILURES section exceeding max_chars is truncated (per-block) while staying within the limit and keeping the header. <!--#2173d0410519f676-->
  - `TestExtractFailuresSection.test_section_extraction_stops_at_next_separator` (method) — Asserts extraction stops before the 'short test summary info' separator so the summary is excluded. <!--#ca7987be3eddc1a5-->
  - `TestExtractFailuresSection.test_none_like_empty` (method) — Edge case confirming whitespace-only input yields effectively empty (tail) output. <!--#4b8bc0513513719e-->

### `tests/test_fix_history_and_normalize.py` (python) — Unit tests for two issue-handling helpers — state_machine's `_normalize_issue_fields` (cross-filling severity/priority) and implement's `_format_fix_history` (rendering fix-attempt history across legacy and new self_check schema variants). <!--#ee43df86a95fd58b|421d88be79e11a76-->

  - `TestNormalizeIssueFields.test_adds_severity_from_priority` (method) — Asserts a missing `severity` is derived from an existing `priority`. <!--#147266bc0bde178e-->
  - `TestNormalizeIssueFields.test_adds_priority_from_severity` (method) — Asserts a missing `priority` is derived from an existing `severity`. <!--#8e020cad731a1370-->

  - `TestNormalizeIssueFields.test_neither_present_unchanged` (method) — Asserts neither field is added when both are absent. <!--#79414babab171618-->
  - `TestNormalizeIssueFields.test_non_dict_items_skipped` (method) — Asserts non-dict list entries pass through unchanged while dict entries are still normalized. <!--#2c69e3fccfa23180-->
  - `TestNormalizeIssueFields.test_empty_list` (method) — Asserts an empty input list yields an empty list. <!--#900a6350b37607f9-->
  - `TestNormalizeIssueFields.test_mutates_in_place` (method) — Asserts the function mutates and returns the same list object rather than a copy. <!--#e26d44ba86f412b4-->
- `TestFormatFixHistory` (class) — Tests that `_format_fix_history` renders fix-attempt history into a readable summary across schema variants and edge cases. <!--#993849ee208b42b0-->
  - `TestFormatFixHistory.test_empty_returns_no_attempts` (method) — Asserts an empty history renders the 'No previous fix attempts.' sentinel. <!--#890a24edba8eaf87-->
  - `TestFormatFixHistory.test_none_returns_no_attempts` (method) — Asserts a None history renders the 'No previous fix attempts.' sentinel. <!--#59491e1bba0a091a-->

  - `TestFormatFixHistory.test_issues_capped_at_five` (method) — Asserts only the first five issues render with a '+N more issue(s)' overflow note. <!--#8cf48e40ceb7eab7-->
  - `TestFormatFixHistory.test_backward_compat_fix_instructions_summary` (method) — Asserts legacy `fix_instructions_summary` entries render under a 'Summary:' line. <!--#eb2671d554b06fe8-->
  - `TestFormatFixHistory.test_issues_preferred_over_summary` (method) — Asserts structured `issues` take precedence over `fix_instructions_summary` when both exist. <!--#967997bd8f283c64-->

  - `TestFormatFixHistory.test_missing_fields_use_defaults` (method) — Asserts an empty iteration dict renders placeholder defaults ('Iteration ?', 'unknown'). <!--#77486491f09a6f06-->
  - `TestFormatFixHistory.test_no_location_omits_at_suffix` (method) — Asserts the '@ location' suffix is omitted when an issue has no location. <!--#770b5a0ac83e526e-->
  - `TestFormatFixHistory.test_multiple_iterations` (method) — Asserts multiple iterations each render their number and issue descriptions. <!--#d404d04045647cf8-->
  - `TestFormatFixHistory.test_renders_new_schema_self_check_issues` (method) — Regression test asserting new self_check schema fields (actual_behavior/divergence/evidence_lines) are extracted into the rendered output. <!--#13e5424c19213fea-->

### `tests/test_fix_loop_logic.py` (python) — Unit tests for the TEST-step fix-loop logic, covering failure-reason extraction, IssueDiscovery's creation of pre-existing/inherited-failure issues, and baseline-driven classification that triggers the fix loop only for newly introduced or new-test failures while inherited failures complete the step and are reported (but not persisted) once per flow. <!--#7e54e0f838640a4a|3d621d0d5515674c-->
- `project_root` (function) — Pytest fixture that builds a minimal tianluo project skeleton (state/ and issues/{open,closed}/ dirs) under tmp_path and returns its root. <!--#14f9718217d6acf5-->
- `basic_flow` (function) — Pytest fixture returning a basic RUNNING FlowInstance for an authentication-bug task. <!--#56592a53b96e086c-->
- `issue_manager` (function) — Pytest fixture constructing an IssueManager rooted at the temp project. <!--#0454d9e7853ad51b-->
- `discovery` (function) — Pytest fixture constructing an IssueDiscovery bound to the issue_manager and a test flow id. <!--#4b9b4b2c4d42a493-->
- `TestExtractFailureReason` (class) — Test class verifying the _extract_failure_reason helper parses, falls back, handles empty inputs, and truncates. <!--#02a8519cb5a08bea-->
  - `TestExtractFailureReason.test_extracts_from_short_summary` (method) — Asserts the failure reason is pulled from a pytest short-summary FAILED line. <!--#fc0d38e873d85a3e-->
  - `TestExtractFailureReason.test_returns_generic_when_not_found` (method) — Asserts a generic 'test failed' reason is returned when the test id is absent from output. <!--#52571feaf5997412-->
  - `TestExtractFailureReason.test_empty_inputs` (method) — Asserts empty stdout or test id yields the 'unknown failure' reason. <!--#73845b1420413e5a-->
  - `TestExtractFailureReason.test_truncates_long_reason` (method) — Asserts an overly long failure reason is truncated to at most 200 characters. <!--#925b66a6e45b97d0-->
- `TestCreateFromPreExistingFailures` (class) — Test class covering IssueDiscovery.create_from_pre_existing_failures behavior for inherited failures. <!--#c3751829cd2ed279-->
  - `TestCreateFromPreExistingFailures.test_creates_medium_priority_issue` (method) — Asserts a created pre-existing-failure issue has medium priority. <!--#dae731d1c8d5105c-->
  - `TestCreateFromPreExistingFailures.test_correct_tags` (method) — Asserts the issue carries the auto-discovered and source:test-pre-existing tags. <!--#3cc70bb2e68df250-->
  - `TestCreateFromPreExistingFailures.test_includes_all_test_names` (method) — Asserts every failing test name and its reason appear in the issue description. <!--#d23e40cd79cfd936-->
  - `TestCreateFromPreExistingFailures.test_title_contains_count` (method) — Asserts the issue title reports the plural count of failing tests. <!--#a4f52d05049f3b71-->
  - `TestCreateFromPreExistingFailures.test_singular_count_in_title` (method) — Asserts the issue title uses singular phrasing for a single failure. <!--#6888aadf64a62367-->
  - `TestCreateFromPreExistingFailures.test_empty_failures_returns_none` (method) — Asserts no issue is created when the failures list is empty. <!--#167da47104d56978-->
  - `TestCreateFromPreExistingFailures.test_deduplicates` (method) — Asserts a repeated identical failure set does not create a duplicate issue. <!--#48d6097f68890fc5-->
  - `TestCreateFromPreExistingFailures.test_description_mentions_task` (method) — Asserts the issue description references the originating flow's task description. <!--#778207738ddb74d1-->
- `TestFixLoopLogic` (class) — Test class verifying the test_handler fix-loop trigger logic: inherited/baseline failures don't loop while new tests or introduced regressions return REVISION_NEEDED with fix_needed set. <!--#1fb3826dce248e59-->
  - `TestFixLoopLogic._make_step_and_flow` (method) — Helper that constructs a PENDING TEST Step (with tests_added/is_fix_iteration/baseline_failures inputs) and a RUNNING FlowInstance pointing at project_root/tianluo.yaml. <!--#31b18720955c7c64-->
  - `TestFixLoopLogic._mock_run_command` (method) — Helper producing a mocked _run_command result dict for a pass/fail outcome. <!--#f251a53fc840dad0-->
  - `TestFixLoopLogic.test_inherited_failure_no_fix_loop` (method) — Asserts a baseline-inherited failure completes the step without triggering the fix loop. <!--#d9333c31651e5107-->
  - `TestFixLoopLogic.test_new_test_failure_triggers_fix_loop` (method) — Asserts a newly added test's failure triggers the fix loop (REVISION_NEEDED). <!--#5863ed84d6b08356-->
  - `TestFixLoopLogic.test_introduced_regression_triggers_fix_loop` (method) — Asserts a regression absent from an empty baseline triggers the fix loop. <!--#725ab6d821e065eb-->
  - `TestFixLoopLogic.test_mixed_inherited_and_new_triggers_fix_loop` (method) — Asserts a mix of inherited and new failures still triggers the fix loop. <!--#7889d8fd507444c7-->
  - `TestFixLoopLogic.test_all_pass_returns_completed` (method) — Asserts all-passing tests return COMPLETED with overall_passed true. <!--#a24fd0257e42f2ed-->
  - `TestFixLoopLogic.test_overall_passed_reflects_actual_exit_status` (method) — Asserts overall_passed mirrors the pytest exit code even when the fix loop is not triggered. <!--#b1bfa8a0af3370bb-->

  - `TestInheritedFailuresOutput._make_step_and_flow` (method) — Helper building a PENDING TEST Step and RUNNING FlowInstance (flow_id test-flow-pre) for the inherited-failures output tests. <!--#7ae52aa372b58993-->

  - `TestInheritedFailuresOutput.test_inherited_in_outputs` (method) — Asserts inherited failures populate both legacy pre_existing_failures and new inherited_failures output keys. <!--#761159aa72d3991b-->
  - `TestInheritedFailuresOutput.test_introduced_regression_not_persisted` (method) — Asserts an introduced regression is classified as introduced (not inherited) and never written to known_test_failures.json. <!--#11faaff78096db8a-->
  - `TestInheritedFailuresOutput.test_no_inherited_when_all_pass` (method) — Asserts inherited/pre-existing failure output lists are empty when all tests pass. <!--#eb7ca20311aebee6-->
  - `TestInheritedFailuresOutput.test_report_called_for_inherited` (method) — Asserts _report_pre_existing_issues is called once with the inherited failures present. <!--#aa36837fa0f6040b-->
  - `TestInheritedFailuresOutput.test_report_not_called_when_no_inherited` (method) — Asserts _report_pre_existing_issues is not called when there are no inherited failures. <!--#237a63ab130aeda7-->
  - `TestInheritedFailuresOutput.test_inherited_issue_filed_once_across_iterations` (method) — Runs the test step three times over one flow and asserts the inherited-failure issue is reported only once, guarded by the flow's inherited_failures_filed context flag. <!--#9e3dd6526f67f501-->
- `step_handler_call` (function) — Helper that invokes test_handler with TestConfig/WorkflowConfig mocked (baseline_fix_max_attempts=0) to disable mechanism-B looping and exercise the surface-not-loop path. <!--#9793654582060275-->

### `tests/test_frontend_discovery_analyze_scroll.py` (python) — Pytest bridge for the issue #260 discovery→analyze silent-rebuild scroll fix that asserts the DOM-stub scroll test module exists and is registered in the Node harness, runs that Node suite to confirm both the bottom-follower-sticks and scrolled-up-reader-anchors boundary checks pass, and statically guards that app.js wires the persistent flowConversationFollowingBottom intent (ORed with the frozen isNearBottom measurement and maintained by the scroll / scroll-to-bottom paths) into the silent stick decision. <!--#673ff056ef3b2cb9|c82c42c276629491-->

- `test_following_bottom_intent_wired_into_silent_stick` (function) — Static-source guardrail asserting app.js carries the persistent flowConversationFollowingBottom intent and ORs it with the frozen isNearBottom measurement in the silent-rebuild stick decision, maintained by the conversation scroll and scroll-to-bottom paths. <!--#cb8dbd3669f114d1-->

### `tests/test_frontend_file_upload.py` (python) — Python-side guard suite for the WebUI file-upload feature: it statically asserts that app.js/index.html/style.css still carry the upload constants, element ids, wiring calls and CSS rules, that every referenced `upload.*` / `common.size.*` i18n key exists (with interpolation slots intact) in both language packs, and that the Node harness modules `file_upload.test.mjs` and `inline_upload_images.test.mjs` are registered and pass when executed as a subprocess. <!--#4833b5089cb2596a|31240a54c87476b9-->

- `test_reset_reply_box_clears_the_docked_strip` (function) — Statically inspects `resetReplyBox()` in app.js to confirm it calls `clearAttachments("flow-attachments")`, so switching flows retires the stale attachment strip and its preview object URLs. <!--#25fca5f4671fe91b-->
- `test_new_task_target_selects_recheck_the_attachments` (function) — Statically inspects `init()` to confirm both the `nt-machine` and `nt-project` change handlers call `syncNewTaskUploadTarget()`, so re-targeting a New Task re-checks whether its pasted paths still resolve. <!--#ecdae66c1b59b0fd-->
- `test_style_css_styles_the_strip_and_the_drop_target` (function) — Asserts that style.css still contains every CSS rule the upload UI depends on — the attachment strip, thumbnails, icons, remove button, drop-active state, stored-name reveal, scroll, and the inline conversation image rules. <!--#230a9e1e957bc92e-->
