### `tests/test_frontend_mobile.py` (python) — Static-analysis test suite that guards the WebUI's phone-portrait mobile experience by parsing style.css @media (max-width: 600px) blocks (via _media_ranges/_inside_media/_block_text helpers) to assert overflow guards, touch targets, panel switches, off-canvas drawer, full-screen modals, topbar overflow menu, chat/tool-marker/step-report wrapping and indent-ladder rules while proving the desktop cascade stays untouched, and cross-checks app.js/index.html for the matching auto-grow textarea, panel-switch functions, and mobile control ids plus the companion Node mjs assertion suite. <!--#e59aeb1b0a57dbdc|44d343a1219829af-->
- `_media_ranges` (function) — Helper that returns the brace-matched character ranges of every @media block in a CSS string. <!--#93483a1d9ccf02d4-->
- `_inside_media` (function) — Helper that reports whether a character index falls inside any of the given @media ranges. <!--#873cdc8e2a7b1b20-->
- `_block_text` (function) — Helper that extracts the brace-balanced body text of the CSS block introduced by a given header. <!--#3632f3819be42ab7-->
- `test_mobile_responsive_module_present_and_registered` (function) — Asserts the G7 mjs module exists and is registered in the Node test harness. <!--#4b8b62a7231135ba-->
- `test_frontend_mobile_node_suite_passes` (function) — Runs the Node assertion suite and confirms the named G7 mobile checks actually executed and passed. <!--#71e4a845985eaa94-->
- `test_style_has_phone_portrait_breakpoint` (function) — Asserts style.css contains the @media (max-width: 600px) phone-portrait breakpoint. <!--#a74dd20f0cc6b132-->
- `test_mobile_block_has_horizontal_scroll_guard` (function) — Asserts the phone breakpoint clamps the document against sideways scrolling via overflow-x hidden and a width clamp. <!--#a768b9eb33d20299-->
- `test_mobile_block_has_touch_targets_and_safe_form_fonts` (function) — Asserts the mobile block gives controls a ~40px touch-target floor and pins form fields to 16px to suppress iOS zoom. <!--#79d9bcccbe27ac83-->
- `test_mobile_block_has_panel_switches` (function) — Asserts the mobile block contains the main-list and History single-view panel-switch rules. <!--#1201301e3d294387-->
- `test_mobile_block_has_flow_view_off_canvas_drawer` (function) — Asserts the mobile block turns the flow-view sidebar into a transform-based off-canvas drawer with slide-in and backdrop rules. <!--#84b85cb17813ff2b-->
- `test_mobile_block_has_near_full_screen_modals` (function) — Asserts the mobile block makes modal cards near full-screen using full viewport width and 100dvh height. <!--#de24612fea66769b-->
- `test_mobile_block_has_topbar_overflow_menu` (function) — Asserts the mobile block collapses the topbar controls behind a hamburger toggle and open-dropdown nav menu. <!--#59f77de953af83aa-->
- `test_mobile_block_reclaims_chat_horizontal_whitespace` (function) — Asserts the mobile flow-chat drops the record's left bar/padding and widens bubbles toward full width. <!--#56d3014f995bfa02-->
- `test_mobile_block_compresses_tool_marker_to_one_line` (function) — Asserts the mobile tool-call chip detail truncates to a single line via nowrap/ellipsis and flex-basis 0. <!--#8759735636ab65ad-->
- `test_mobile_block_tool_marker_toggle_strips_native_appearance` (function) — Asserts the mobile tool-marker toggle strips native control appearance and the chip re-centers its head so the folded card collapses to text height. <!--#c9406bd41aa517cc-->
- `test_desktop_tool_marker_toggle_rule_unchanged` (function) — Asserts the desktop (non-media) .tool-marker-toggle rule stays byte-for-byte unchanged with no appearance declaration leaked from the mobile fix. <!--#a764d07b8175dd3e-->
- `test_mobile_block_shares_call_chip_with_reply_head_row` (function) — Asserts the mobile docked reply flips to a wrapping row so a single call chip shares the reply-head row and the input row spans full width. <!--#85bd04663e823df3-->
- `test_mobile_block_tiles_reply_meta_horizontally` (function) — Asserts the mobile docked reply head and prompt toggle tile horizontally on one row. <!--#2875352970c16c97-->
- `test_mobile_block_hardens_history_overflow` (function) — Asserts the mobile History panes clip overflow (min-width 0 / overflow-x hidden) and wrap long content rather than introducing horizontal scrollbars. <!--#8cdf9de7d80dc01f-->
- `test_mobile_block_hardens_flow_conversation_overflow` (function) — Asserts the mobile breakpoint in style.css pins `.flow-conversation` to `overflow-x: hidden`, adds inherited `overflow-wrap: anywhere` / `word-break: break-word` wrapping shared by the Flow and History views, gives every `.step-report__*` construct `min-width: 0` / `max-width: 100%`, relaxes the kv key column's min-width, and never introduces a horizontal-scroll escape hatch. <!--#f6ed2bca95b8f2dd-->
- `test_mobile_block_bounds_the_nested_kv_indent_ladder` (function) — Asserts the mobile breakpoint narrows one `.step-report__kv-nested` indent level and caps the ladder via a self-descendant selector chain (shared with History) so deep generic-outputs nesting stays bounded, while the desktop 16px/8px base rule outside all media queries is untouched. <!--#851cebd78374a522-->
- `test_mobile_step_report_constructs_are_covered_by_inherited_wrapping` (function) — Guards the inheritance assumption behind the CSS fix by asserting app.js's `renderStepEventRecord` still builds the report card inside a `.conv-record` row and that every class in `STEP_REPORT_CONSTRUCTS` is still emitted. <!--#63930ba530238a2a-->
- `test_mobile_block_releases_the_constructs_that_opt_out_of_wrapping` (function) — Asserts the mobile block explicitly releases the three constructs that override the inherited wrapping — `.agent-badge` (`white-space: normal`) and the `flex-shrink: 0` chip items `.tool-marker-name` / `.tool-marker-input-key` / glyph / toggle — across both views, while confirming `.tool-marker-detail` deliberately keeps its one-line ellipsis. <!--#d898d4d66d29809d-->

- `test_step_report_rules_stay_out_of_the_desktop_cascade` (function) — Asserts every new report-card hardening selector appears only inside media queries so wide viewports never match it, and that the desktop `.step-report__kv-k` `min-width: 100px` alignment floor survives untouched. <!--#395599f8ee9a3503-->
- `test_mobile_block_textarea_is_auto_grow_not_fixed` (function) — Asserts the mobile reply textarea is a WeChat-style auto-grow box capped at 35vh with no manual resize and the old fixed 104px min removed. <!--#074c4b135b434c0d-->
- `test_app_js_has_auto_grow_textarea_logic` (function) — Asserts app.js carries the pure clamp, matchMedia-gated grower, input listener, and the height-reset-to-0 fix that drives auto-grow. <!--#8e2f568ccf9db45c-->

- `test_index_html_has_mobile_controls` (function) — Asserts index.html includes the mobile toggle/back control element ids. <!--#fcb92fb448b6e045-->
- `test_app_js_has_switch_functions` (function) — Asserts app.js defines the mobile nav-menu, flow-sidebar, and panel-switch functions. <!--#e560a6800187a4f6-->

- `test_mobile_visual_rules_are_inside_media_queries` (function) — Regression guard asserting every mobile-only selector/token appears only inside @media blocks so the desktop layout stays unchanged. <!--#cb4569426cd1c7e4-->

### `tests/test_frontend_mobile_overflow.py` (python) — Playwright-driven regression suite that renders the production WebUI conversation (flow and history views) at mobile widths of 390px and 320px to prove no construct — report cards, markdown, chips, `.agent-badge`, `.tool-marker-name`, analyze scope stats, or the nested-kv indent ladder — overflows or horizontally scrolls the column, while guarding that intentional internal scroll/truncation designs, the desktop 1280px layout, and the fixture's renderer coverage remain untouched. <!--#3cc9926e0f5f99e2|ad5c1a1d5c34b98b-->
- `_browser_page` (function) — Helper that launches headless Chromium via Playwright at a given viewport width, loads the production `static/index.html` over `file://`, waits for `renderConversation` to be defined, and returns the (context, browser, page, page-error list) tuple — skipping the test when Playwright or the browser libraries are unavailable. <!--#32b1335de86e9b32-->
- `_sweep` (function) — Helper that renders the fixture step outputs into the flow or history view at a given width (optionally stress-planting the long unbreakable token into every text node) and returns the geometry measurement of the conversation column plus the set of rendered CSS classes. <!--#34aebca4cdba8381-->
- `_fmt` (function) — Small formatter that renders a list of overflow hits as an indented, human-readable `+Npx kind what` failure message. <!--#07bd9214b202ab96-->
- `test_flow_console_has_no_horizontal_scroll_on_mobile` (function) — Asserts the reported defect is fixed: at 390px and 320px the `#flow-conversation` column has `scrollWidth == clientWidth`, cannot be swiped sideways, and the document itself still does not scroll horizontally. <!--#3e295428ac3286dc-->
- `test_no_conversation_construct_overflows_the_column` (function) — Comprehensive stressed sweep at 390px over both the flow and history views asserting that no rendered construct — report card, markdown node, chip or anonymous inline box — paints past the conversation column edge. <!--#9651a9f0db0bdced-->
- `test_analyze_scope_row_wraps_inside_the_column` (function) — Asserts the user-visible symptom is fixed on real (non-stressed) analyze output: the ANALYZE card's scope stat inherits `overflow-wrap: anywhere`, fits inside the column and status bar, and wraps onto several lines rather than being clipped. <!--#3d73de89de487d22-->
- `test_agent_badge_and_tool_name_wrap_instead_of_being_clipped` (function) — Asserts that the constructs which override the inherited wrapping — `.agent-badge`, `.tool-marker-name` and `.tool-marker-input-key` — fit inside the flow/history column at 390px and 320px and actually wrap onto multiple lines instead of being truncated or merely hidden. <!--#8d8ed0a0fc49c691-->
- `_nested_outputs` (function) — Helper that builds a generic step-output payload nested to an arbitrary depth, with the long unbreakable token at the leaf, to drive the nested-kv indent ladder. <!--#78757c85e27db642-->
- `test_deeply_nested_generic_outputs_stay_inside_the_column` (function) — Asserts the `.step-report__kv-nested` indent ladder saturates rather than accruing per level: at 14 and 30 levels on a 320px screen total indentation stays bounded, the innermost row keeps a usable width, and nothing overflows or scrolls sideways. <!--#efd3213dd9453aa5-->
- `test_internal_scroll_and_truncation_designs_are_preserved` (function) — Regression guard that the mobile hardening does not flatten intentional designs — `.step-report__diff` keeps its captive 320px-tall `overflow: auto` viewport, `.tool-marker-detail` keeps its single-line ellipsis truncation, and the conversation keeps `overflow-x: hidden`. <!--#cec1d03be0f0af47-->
- `test_desktop_conversation_is_untouched_by_the_mobile_overlay` (function) — Hard-constraint guard that the fix is breakpoint-local: at 1280px the conversation keeps `overflow-x: auto`, stats keep `overflow-wrap: normal`, the kv key column keeps its 100px floor, and the badge/tool-name columns keep their nowrap/non-shrinking desktop behaviour. <!--#1d13d8a3df605fa3-->
- `test_step_outputs_fixture_reaches_the_report_renderers` (function) — Guards-the-guard test asserting the fixture still renders every report construct the sweeps rely on (`step-report*`, `msg-chip`, `history-step-title`, …) so a renderer rename or fixture drift cannot make the overflow sweeps pass vacuously. <!--#952ff03a2f611887-->

### `tests/test_history_head_truncation_interlock.py` (python) — Regression test module that reproduces the confirmed #287 head-truncation chain end-to-end over the real `DaemonHistoryReader` plus `ServerState` (empty `full` frame, a lost frame whose cursor was wrongly committed, then a late `append`), with jsonl-flush/state helpers, asserting the empty bundle is never installed, the truncating append is refused, and the recovery pull restores the complete history. <!--#ca7bf76ebad874d5|cab2113bc492e430-->
- `_flush` (function) — Test helper that appends `count` synthetic discovery-step jsonl records (with sequential `ordinal`s) to a flow's history step file under `tianluo/history/<FLOW>/<STEP_FILE>`, simulating rounds of history landing on disk. <!--#b5530dfbedbdc74e-->
- `_mark_active_worktree_flow` (function) — Test helper that registers the flow with `ServerState` as a running flow rooted at the given worktree path, so the server treats it as an active worktree flow (the condition that scopes the empty-full guard). <!--#bdcb4644b1910410-->
- `_apply` (function) — Test helper that feeds a `DaemonHistoryReader` read result into `ServerState.apply_history_frame` as if it had arrived over the wire from the daemon. <!--#1a31ee67fae1a1fb-->
- `_ordinals` (function) — Test helper that extracts the list of record ordinals currently held in `ServerState`'s cached history bundle for the flow, returning `[]` when no bundle exists. <!--#5270d67182955825-->
- `test_lost_frame_then_empty_full_still_yields_complete_history` (function) — Regression test (driving its own asyncio loop) that reproduces the live head-truncation interlock — an empty full frame plus a lost-then-cursor-advanced frame on an active worktree flow — and asserts the daemon refuses the head-truncated bundle, arms a recovery pull, and re-reads from line 0 so the browser still sees the complete history. <!--#cac5005cee48b44a-->

### `tests/test_history_sink_step_started.py` (python) — Unit/integration test suite for the step_started/step_status event-chain that persists lightweight running/paused anchor lines into per-step history jsonl, verifying record_step_started/record_step_status writers, has_step_started/status_event detection, get_step_history's skipping of these non-chat anchors, and HistorySink plus full run_flow behavior around idempotent, re-armed-after-pause, terminal-suppressed, and deduped lifecycle anchors for non-LLM steps. <!--#2f9e793338bcad8a|b17f0c81b9dfe564-->
- `_step_path` (function) — Test helper that builds the `tianluo/history/<flow_id>/<step_id>.jsonl` path where a step's lifecycle/chat records live under a project root. <!--#5e55ef6a26e6bd7f-->
- `_read_lines` (function) — Helper that reads a jsonl file and returns its non-blank lines parsed as a list of dicts (empty list if absent). <!--#3a7c0ef3252423a1-->
- `test_record_step_started_writes_running_record` (function) — Verifies `record_step_started` appends a single non-chat `step_started`/`running` record carrying the step id, type, and an ISO-string timestamp derived from an epoch float. <!--#6ab8b2f366d545c5-->
- `test_record_step_started_default_timestamp_is_iso_string` (function) — Checks that `record_step_started` with no explicit timestamp still writes a non-empty ISO-string timestamp. <!--#c93990071028462b-->
- `test_has_step_started_event_detection` (function) — Confirms `has_step_started_event` returns False for an absent file, True after a started record is written, and stays step-scoped (a different step id is unaffected). <!--#60eb6eacc6ebf7a2-->
- `test_get_step_history_skips_step_started` (function) — Asserts `get_step_history` ignores `step_started` lines — a started-only file yields a None session, and a started line interleaved with a real prompt surfaces only the chat message. <!--#b2d1262b9f6abb8e-->
- `_make_event` (function) — Test helper that constructs an engine event via `new_event` with fixed flow/step ids and optional `step` payload for feeding into `HistorySink`. <!--#4b72abed3fed161a-->
- `test_history_sink_persists_step_started` (function) — Verifies that consuming a `STEP_STARTED` event through `HistorySink` persists exactly one `step_started`/`running` record to the step's jsonl. <!--#e165e419ac9f4f42-->
- `test_history_sink_step_started_is_idempotent_while_running` (function) — Ensures re-emitting `STEP_STARTED` while the step is already running does not stack duplicate started records (only one persists). <!--#0889d8496458bf44-->
- `test_history_sink_step_started_rearms_after_pause` (function) — Verifies that after a step pauses, a re-emitted `STEP_STARTED` re-arms a fresh `running` anchor (two started records, latest status running), while further starts while running don't stack. <!--#b4802407b49a8414-->
- `test_history_sink_step_started_skipped_after_terminal` (function) — Confirms a late `STEP_STARTED` arriving after a terminal `STEP_COMPLETED` is a no-op, so a finished step never gains a spurious running anchor. <!--#9c3b6140f99be0d6-->
- `test_history_sink_terminal_events_unchanged` (function) — Regression guard that terminal events (e.g. `STEP_COMPLETED`) still persist the full step record with its outputs unchanged. <!--#e78c773c56fb5e61-->
- `_build_flow` (function) — Helper that constructs a single-step RUNNING FlowInstance of a given step type for run_flow integration tests. <!--#21d5b5b1ef5abf2a-->
- `_run_single_step` (function) — Test helper that drives `run_flow` for one step with `PersistenceManager`, `StateMachine`, `STEP_HANDLERS` and `render_full` patched out, wiring the mock `run_step` to invoke the `on_running` callback so the orchestrator's STEP_STARTED persistence path is exercised and returning the given `run_result`. <!--#b90df299c91351c4-->
- `test_run_flow_emits_step_started_for_non_llm_step` (function) — Asserts a non-LLM TEST step gets one running step_started anchor at entry alongside its terminal step_completed through the full run_flow chain. <!--#eea698beb03f259d-->
- `test_run_flow_resume_after_pause_rearms_running_then_completes` (function) — Asserts running a step PAUSED then COMPLETED re-arms a second running anchor after the paused row and still lands its completion. <!--#e53666bca47fbd82-->
- `test_record_step_status_writes_status_record` (function) — Verifies `record_step_status` writes a non-chat `step_status` record carrying the given status (e.g. `paused`), step type, and ISO-string timestamp. <!--#4a68892b06c91ada-->
- `test_has_step_status_event_is_status_specific` (function) — Confirms `has_step_status_event` matches a specific status token case-insensitively and does not match a different status. <!--#a5152676793843cc-->
- `test_get_step_history_skips_step_status` (function) — Asserts `get_step_history` skips `step_status` lines — a status-only file yields no session, and interleaving with a real prompt surfaces only the chat message. <!--#4b0d67f5dd65d745-->
- `_run_discovery_pause` (function) — Sibling test helper that drives `run_flow` for a DISCOVERY step returning `StepStatus.PAUSED`, additionally stubbing `_handle_discovery_pause` to simulate the user exiting so the loop returns cleanly right after the step_status is persisted. <!--#82bd87f16fd41fcf-->
- `test_run_flow_persists_step_status_on_pause` (function) — Asserts a DISCOVERY step returning PAUSED persists a single paused step_status anchor alongside its running step_started anchor. <!--#78f13b15452f47e8-->
- `test_run_flow_step_status_records_paused_after_running_rearm` (function) — Verifies a multi-round running→paused→running→paused step records the second `paused` after the intervening `running` re-arm, so the latest persisted lifecycle status is `paused` rather than a stale `running`. <!--#6e42df3e798f8606-->
- `test_run_flow_step_status_dedups_back_to_back_paused` (function) — Verifies that without an intervening `running` anchor a re-recorded `paused` is suppressed, so back-to-back identical statuses don't stack (only one row). <!--#6b1954c2a2bca516-->

### `tests/test_history_summary_extraction.py` (python) — Unit test suite verifying that history-title extraction stays aligned across the marker-level parser (extract_user_content), the CLI extractor (100-char clip), and the daemon extractor (untruncated), asserting they share the same three-tier priority (USER_CONTENT markers → Task-description regex → raw-content fallback) and identical extraction source while each keeps its own truncation contract. <!--#bedbde8a375ab68b|1735fdca01ccda6f-->
- `_three_segment` (function) — Helper that builds a canonical three-segment prompt body with template-prefix-end and USER_CONTENT begin/end markers around the user input. <!--#ce1c7fb9f0f87739-->
- `_two_segment` (function) — Helper that builds a legacy two-segment prompt body with a USER_CONTENT_BEGIN marker but no closing END. <!--#c1c6b9991dee12f5-->
- `test_extract_user_content_three_segment_hit` (function) — Asserts extract_user_content returns the user text from a well-formed three-segment marker body. <!--#1e13bd23125d3bd7-->
- `test_extract_user_content_strips_edge_newlines` (function) — Asserts extract_user_content strips surrounding newlines but preserves interior spaces of the extracted user content. <!--#29b38f382a95ab60-->
- `test_extract_user_content_missing_markers` (function) — Asserts extract_user_content returns None when the body contains no markers. <!--#811f5b297c2d7bd1-->
- `test_extract_user_content_two_segment_returns_none` (function) — Asserts a two-segment body (BEGIN without END) yields None since the tail is framework-injected rather than user input. <!--#db80ad8d2acad804-->
- `test_extract_user_content_empty_middle_returns_none` (function) — Asserts extract_user_content returns None when the marker-enclosed middle is effectively empty. <!--#6138357c44aa1564-->
- `test_extract_user_content_non_string` (function) — Asserts extract_user_content returns None for non-string and empty-string inputs. <!--#83f91e1b426e7884-->
- `test_extract_user_content_begin_before_template_end_is_none` (function) — Asserts extract_user_content returns None when markers appear out of canonical order (BEGIN before the template prefix end). <!--#161d4db56fc6847c-->
- `_write_first_line` (function) — Fixture helper that creates a flow directory and writes a single first-line JSONL user record to drive the extractor tests. <!--#b5d6bdb1154e1e3e-->
- `_build_cases` (function) — Helper returning a labeled matrix of prompt-body inputs paired with their expected untruncated extraction source across all three priority tiers. <!--#ab79ca9dc7ef17ff-->
- `test_cli_and_daemon_share_extraction_source` (function) — Parametrized test asserting the daemon returns the untruncated extraction source while the CLI applies the 100-char clip, both from the same source. <!--#7085829d7ab011de-->
- `test_three_segment_marker_takes_priority_over_regex` (function) — Asserts that when a body contains both USER_CONTENT markers and a Task description block, the marker-level content wins for both extractors. <!--#693c52b84afdda38-->
- `test_content_as_text_block_list` (function) — Asserts both extractors handle a JSONL record whose content is a list of text blocks rather than a plain string. <!--#d03e01122f11ca9c-->
- `test_no_jsonl_returns_no_history_data` (function) — Asserts both extractors return the '(no history data)' sentinel when the flow directory contains no JSONL file. <!--#689d081a8f1bfdc6-->
- `test_corrupt_json_returns_no_state_data` (function) — Asserts both extractors return the '(no state data)' sentinel when the first JSONL line is malformed JSON. <!--#cc7236afd112c939-->
- `test_plain_text_fallback_matches_pre_change_behavior` (function) — Regression test ensuring a marker-less plain-text first line yields the raw content (clipped to 100 chars for the CLI, untruncated for the daemon). <!--#2b24e6f312e28f5e-->

### `tests/test_history_summary_scan.py` (python) — Regression tests asserting both the daemon and CLI history-only title extractors do a bounded forward scan past no-content `step_started` event records to recover the real user prompt, exercising the tiered marker/task-block/raw-content extraction, empty/unparseable-record skipping, CLI 100-char clipping, and the no-user-record and no-jsonl fallback sentinels. <!--#9223607b4bcd16f3|44c16148d74ddf9b-->
- `_wrap` (function) — Test helper that builds a step-prompt body wrapping the given user text in the three USER_CONTENT marker segments. <!--#193cad533a86b4a5-->

- `_user_record` (function) — Test helper returning a JSON-encoded `role=user` record wrapping the given content. <!--#e5a52f4b7db7d81c-->

- `test_first_line_step_started_recovers_user_prompt` (function) — Asserts a `step_started`-first flow recovers the real user prompt from the following user record. <!--#fd8cd17ca6b03618-->
- `test_first_line_is_user_prompt_unchanged` (function) — Asserts an already-first-line user prompt is extracted unchanged (preserving prior behaviour). <!--#a090e2a09c2e7422-->
- `test_task_description_block_tier` (function) — Asserts second-tier extraction pulls the title from a `Task description:` block when USER_CONTENT markers are absent. <!--#d296229e6bd8fea4-->
- `test_raw_content_fallback_tier` (function) — Asserts third-tier fallback returns the raw user content when neither markers nor a task block exist. <!--#59fabdfa8bf8273d-->
- `test_list_content_first_text_block` (function) — Asserts block-array user content reduces to its first text block before extraction. <!--#8f173886b49b1d5f-->
- `test_no_user_record_returns_fallback` (function) — Asserts a flow with no user-content record returns the `(no state data)` fallback rather than an empty title. <!--#5d039f785c5a26a1-->
- `test_empty_user_record_skipped` (function) — Asserts an empty `role=user` record is skipped so the next non-empty one supplies the title. <!--#29a06e94901431c4-->
- `test_cli_clips_to_100_chars` (function) — Asserts the CLI clips long titles to 100 chars plus ellipsis while the daemon returns them untruncated. <!--#a7716b105be70a69-->
- `test_bounded_scan_does_not_read_whole_file` (function) — Asserts a user record beyond `SUMMARY_MAX_SCAN_LINES` is not found, confirming the scan is bounded. <!--#3bd5adc57afde5d6-->
- `test_unparseable_lines_skipped` (function) — Asserts malformed jsonl lines are skipped without raising so a later valid record is still recovered. <!--#d3fd2b32779449ca-->
- `test_no_jsonl_files_returns_no_history` (function) — Asserts a flow directory with no jsonl files returns the `(no history data)` sentinel. <!--#6002ba79984c42d8-->

### `tests/test_human_call.py` (python) — Unit tests for the merge human-call writer, covering call-filename generation (required segments, `/`→`__` branch encoding, uniqueness under rapid-fire and threaded races, monotonic sequence numbers), atomic JSON writes with temp-file cleanup, uniform rejection of orphan resolution files into `rejected_orphans` with evidence, and the `write_degraded_call` `merge_context_unavailable` payload shape. <!--#bf564528b0b08738|176f7a41bcc30a87-->
- `_make_context` (function) — Test helper that constructs a `ConflictContext` with sensible defaults and overridable branch/files/SHA fields. <!--#017f65d43b5fbf52-->
- `_make_resolution` (function) — Test helper that wraps the given file resolutions into a high-confidence `LLMResolution`. <!--#2ec70d58e10752a9-->
- `_make_file_resolution` (function) — Test helper that builds a `FileResolution` for a given path and resolved content, pre-populated with a single HIGH-confidence hunk covering lines 1-5. <!--#69b8b1fd3f8a0357-->
- `TestGenerateCallFilename` (class) — Test class covering F1/F5 filename generation: required segments, slash-to-`__` replacement, uniqueness, and monotonic sequence numbers. <!--#611849acc56ebe80-->
  - `TestGenerateCallFilename.test_format_contains_required_segments` (method) — Asserts generated filenames contain the expected timestamp, PID, sequence, sha8, and branch segments. <!--#94697c5aaab48f1b-->
  - `TestGenerateCallFilename.test_branch_slash_replaced_with_double_underscore` (method) — Asserts `/` in branch names is replaced with `__` (not `-`) in the filename. <!--#76879ea67b2f1a17-->
  - `TestGenerateCallFilename.test_unique_under_rapid_fire` (method) — Asserts 100 sequential same-branch filename generations are all unique. <!--#4b15e9017796d6d2-->
  - `TestGenerateCallFilename.test_unique_under_threaded_race` (method) — Asserts filenames remain unique under concurrent generation across multiple threads. <!--#45310000b173bbcc-->
  - `TestGenerateCallFilename.test_monotonic_seq` (method) — Asserts embedded sequence numbers increase monotonically and are distinct. <!--#e68632a24d1cab4d-->
- `TestWriteCallFilename` (class) — Test class verifying `write_call` emits new-format (T-separated timestamp) filenames. <!--#b6a0b072b0c43bc5-->
  - `TestWriteCallFilename.test_call_file_uses_new_format` (method) — Asserts the written call file uses the new T-separated timestamp format and not the old pattern. <!--#7794641b07bb2651-->
- `TestAtomicWriteJson` (class) — Test class covering F2 atomic JSON writes: validity, atomic replacement, and temp-file cleanup on success and error. <!--#ef3a66d690622378-->
  - `TestAtomicWriteJson.test_produces_valid_json` (method) — Asserts `_atomic_write_json` writes parseable JSON matching the input data. <!--#2f58172e639e18f9-->
  - `TestAtomicWriteJson.test_atomic_replacement` (method) — Asserts an existing file is atomically overwritten with the new content. <!--#dbb3c639c119ac5f-->
  - `TestAtomicWriteJson.test_no_tmp_file_left_behind` (method) — Asserts no `.tmp_*` temp files remain after a successful write. <!--#c5116662ddef58c1-->
  - `TestAtomicWriteJson.test_tmp_file_cleaned_on_error` (method) — Asserts the temp file is cleaned up when the write fails on a read-only directory. <!--#14fe3d06521acc68-->
- `TestOrphanFileHandling` (class) — Test class asserting that `HumanCallWriter.write_call` uniformly rejects resolution files whose paths are absent from the conflict context, recording them under `rejected_orphans` with evidence (content preview/size, conflict markers) instead of emitting them in `files`. <!--#9d63ff8313832fd5-->
  - `TestOrphanFileHandling.test_orphan_file_rejected_and_recorded` (method) — Asserts a mixed resolution keeps only the context-matching file in `files` while the orphan lands in `rejected_orphans` with its reason and content-preview/size evidence. <!--#070f6c8c047901c7-->
  - `TestOrphanFileHandling.test_no_orphan_when_all_match` (method) — Asserts that when every resolution file matches a context file, the call JSON carries no `is_orphan` flag and no `rejected_orphans` key at all. <!--#0997469e4216802d-->
  - `TestOrphanFileHandling.test_every_orphan_rejected_regardless_of_path_shape` (method) — Regression test that spec-shaped, nested and top-level orphan paths are all rejected with the same reason and none of the retired spec-specific evidence keys, proving no path shape is privileged. <!--#9fc9f8143991c197-->
  - `TestOrphanFileHandling.test_orphan_evidence_flags_conflict_markers` (method) — Asserts that orphan content still containing conflict markers is rejected with `evidence.has_conflict_markers` set to true. <!--#585a4c4f21a23e31-->
- `TestWriteDegradedCall` (class) — Test class covering `HumanCallWriter.write_degraded_call`, verifying the `merge_context_unavailable` payload shape, the empty-SHA default and non-colliding filenames for repeat calls on one branch. <!--#dcdca7a19bd00e81-->
  - `TestWriteDegradedCall.test_writes_degraded_call_file` (method) — Asserts a degraded call file is written under `tianluo/calls` with type `merge_context_unavailable`, branch, pre-merge SHA, message, accept/abort/manual options, response-file instructions and no `files` key. <!--#803e2cff4a6f7164-->
  - `TestWriteDegradedCall.test_degraded_call_defaults_pre_merge_sha_to_empty` (method) — Asserts `pre_merge_sha` defaults to an empty string when the caller omits it. <!--#d99ce9267360b1e3-->
  - `TestWriteDegradedCall.test_degraded_calls_do_not_collide` (method) — Asserts two degraded calls for the same branch produce distinct files that each retain their own message. <!--#35a738e4be03b5e2-->
- `TestNamingConvention` (class) — Test class pinning the call-filename branch encoding — `/` becomes `__` for both degraded and merge calls, and plain branch names gain no extra separator. <!--#19e2f5a4a47a5b5b-->
  - `TestNamingConvention.test_branch_slash_becomes_double_underscore_in_degraded_call` (method) — Asserts a degraded call for `feature/foo/bar` yields a filename containing `feature__foo__bar` with no slashes or hyphen-separated form. <!--#91575bde5e812764-->
  - `TestNamingConvention.test_branch_slash_becomes_double_underscore_in_merge_call` (method) — Asserts merge call filenames use `__` (not `-`) for slashes in branch names. <!--#fe132b4814bf6b33-->
  - `TestNamingConvention.test_plain_branch_no_separator` (method) — Asserts a slash-free branch name appears verbatim with no `__` or `-` separator. <!--#93df7821c5def745-->

### `tests/test_i18n.py` (python) — Unit test suite for the tianluo.i18n layer, covering locale-catalog discovery and auto-registration, t()'s fault-tolerant lookup with per-key en-US fallback and placeholder degradation, language-code normalization, the five-tier resolution precedence chain (SE3_LANG env → project tianluo.yaml → global ~/.se3 config → system locale → en-US base), and the lazy language singleton's reset seam — all with the process-wide i18n state and the developer's real home config/locale env isolated per test. <!--#83d855a488a5d455|27944e28cf16e5d5-->
- `_reset_i18n` (function) — An autouse fixture that resets the process-wide i18n language singleton and catalog cache, repoints Path.home to an empty dir, and clears SE3_LANG/locale env vars so each test starts from an isolated, deterministic language state. <!--#d264f39e1bcd3938-->
- `TestCatalogLoading` (class) — Tests that locale JSON catalogs are discovered and loaded, including auto-registration of newly dropped language files and empty results for unknown codes. <!--#525e4a7939764da5-->
  - `TestCatalogLoading.test_shipped_languages_discovered` (method) — Asserts the shipped en-US and zh-CN catalogs appear in supported_languages(). <!--#eb12714b8ccaa3e8-->
  - `TestCatalogLoading.test_en_us_holds_seed_keys` (method) — Asserts the en-US catalog contains the expected baseline CLI keys and values. <!--#1cf71404ee048ee5-->
  - `TestCatalogLoading.test_unknown_code_loads_empty_catalog` (method) — Asserts loading an unknown language code yields an empty catalog rather than raising. <!--#cbee43f1f6a193f5-->
  - `TestCatalogLoading.test_new_language_file_autoregistered` (method) — Asserts a new <code>.json dropped into locales/ becomes a supported language with no code change, by faking the locale resource iterator. <!--#49ae41a7a3ca5b02-->
- `TestTranslate` (class) — Tests the t() translation function: returns the selected language's string, falls back to en-US then to the raw key on missing entries, renders placeholders, and never raises on missing/extra kwargs or malformed templates. <!--#7f9dcbdc4e55052c-->
  - `TestTranslate.test_returns_selected_language_string` (method) — Asserts t() returns the active language's translation for a known key. <!--#802fc32bae8c0454-->
  - `TestTranslate.test_missing_key_falls_back_to_en_us` (method) — Asserts a key absent from the active catalog falls back to the en-US string. <!--#e7f5ca940302590d-->
  - `TestTranslate.test_missing_everywhere_returns_key` (method) — Asserts a key missing from every catalog renders as the key itself. <!--#73fac6a19e12c755-->
  - `TestTranslate.test_unknown_language_uses_en_us` (method) — Asserts selecting an unsupported language code falls back to the base en-US language. <!--#d20f13e0ebb45236-->
  - `TestTranslate.test_placeholder_rendered` (method) — Asserts t() formats template placeholders from keyword arguments. <!--#1d6785964878ca5e-->
  - `TestTranslate.test_missing_placeholder_returns_unformatted_template` (method) — Asserts a missing format kwarg degrades to the raw template instead of raising KeyError. <!--#fbcfd8447ed9676c-->
  - `TestTranslate.test_extra_placeholder_kwargs_ignored` (method) — Asserts unused keyword arguments passed to t() are harmlessly ignored. <!--#49dd6bf4b1dd7f2a-->
  - `TestTranslate.test_never_raises_on_any_input` (method) — Smoke-asserts t() never raises across empty, known, unknown, and placeholder-bearing keys. <!--#16fb9a7168a18901-->
  - `TestTranslate.test_bad_field_access_in_template_returns_template` (method) — Asserts that a translator-authored template using attribute/subscript field access (which makes str.format raise AttributeError/TypeError) causes t() to degrade to the raw template rather than crash. <!--#27bcb519fda4c478-->
- `TestNormalization` (class) — Tests normalize_language()'s mapping of raw locale strings to supported codes and its safe None result for unknown or non-string inputs. <!--#3c390ca3d31bffc9-->
  - `TestNormalization.test_normalizes_to_supported` (method) — Parametrized check that locale variants (case, underscores, encodings, bare language tags) normalize to the canonical supported codes. <!--#55f2ee9540f7d90d-->
  - `TestNormalization.test_unknown_returns_none` (method) — Asserts empty, blank, None, and unsupported locale strings normalize to None. <!--#e66739b8f0749d98-->

  - `TestNormalization.test_set_language_with_non_string_selects_base` (method) — Asserts set_language() with a non-string argument selects the base en-US language. <!--#ddf90e4133e939ad-->
- `TestResolveLanguageChain` (class) — Tests resolve_language()'s precedence chain (SE3_LANG env > project tianluo.yaml > global config.yaml > system locale > en-US base), including that explicit-but-unsupported config values fall back to base rather than leaking to a lower tier. <!--#b43c983425527c18-->
  - `TestResolveLanguageChain._write_project` (method) — Helper that writes a project-level tianluo.yaml with the given language (or null) under a test root directory. <!--#016965590abd266b-->

### `tests/test_implement.py` (python) — Unit tests for the implement step handler that use a helper-built IMPLEMENT `Step`/`FlowInstance` pair to verify the repo-commit gate: with no commits it falls back to the sequential per-group path (one LLMCaller call per group) instead of `_run_dag_parallel`, and with commits present it delegates once to the parallel DAG path, both returning StepStatus.COMPLETED. <!--#4803ac0535e00507|9b16392928adc66a-->
- `_make_step_and_flow` (function) — Test helper that builds a paired IMPLEMENT-type `Step` (carrying task_description, task_type, task_groups and an empty design_doc as inputs) and a `FlowInstance` rooted at a tmp_path change_path, for exercising the implement step handler. <!--#834bfc69b49d3e18-->
- `TestImplementHandlerEmptyRepoFallback` (class) — Test class verifying implement_handler falls back to the sequential path when the repo has no commits and uses the parallel DAG path when commits exist. <!--#a368cda0a183b683-->
  - `TestImplementHandlerEmptyRepoFallback.test_skips_dag_when_no_commits` (method) — Asserts that with has_commits()=False, _run_dag_parallel is never called and the sequential path invokes LLMCaller once per group (FORK_GROUPS → 3), completing with StepStatus.COMPLETED. <!--#df0d147f37c39797-->
  - `TestImplementHandlerEmptyRepoFallback.test_uses_dag_when_commits_exist` (method) — Asserts that with has_commits()=True, implement_handler calls _run_dag_parallel exactly once and returns StepStatus.COMPLETED. <!--#478d4c5fcf1ef2b2-->

### `tests/test_implement_dag_relay.py` (python) — Test module for the implement step's DAG relay execution, covering LOC computation and threshold routing, leaf-branch merging with LLM/take-theirs conflict resolution, context-rich conflict resolution in worktree.py, and _run_dag_parallel's transitive-reduction/relay-plan/leaf-only-merge integration. <!--#85b4331f47e5b34b|a2bdd1fd1c07b12d-->
- `TestComputeTotalLoc` (class) — Test class verifying `_compute_total_loc` sums task LOC across groups, defaulting missing/legacy estimates and ignoring non-dict tasks. <!--#dd65d08bb8a6314c-->
  - `TestComputeTotalLoc.test_empty_groups` (method) — Asserts an empty group list yields a total LOC of 0. <!--#ac55c55acc7d5501-->
  - `TestComputeTotalLoc.test_groups_without_estimated_loc` (method) — Asserts tasks lacking `estimated_loc` each default to 50 LOC. <!--#6a96849897e72c96-->

  - `TestComputeTotalLoc.test_mixed_tasks_some_without_loc` (method) — Asserts groups mixing explicit and missing LOC sum the explicit values plus 50 for each missing one. <!--#184ee81c28dbe6ac-->
  - `TestComputeTotalLoc.test_string_tasks_ignored` (method) — Asserts legacy plain-string tasks contribute 0 to the LOC total. <!--#5a3e2f6ed644043f-->
  - `TestComputeTotalLoc.test_no_tasks_key` (method) — Asserts a group with no `tasks` key contributes 0 LOC. <!--#6d6a3ec85dcd9171-->
  - `TestComputeTotalLoc.test_single_group_single_task` (method) — Asserts a single group/task returns that task's explicit LOC. <!--#e468b008ce7e6a15-->
- `TestLocThresholdRouting` (class) — Test class verifying that `implement_handler` routes IMPLEMENT steps by total estimated LOC — small multi-group tasks go to `_run_single_llm_call` while larger forked DAGs go to `_run_dag_parallel`. <!--#77169d825b9d10f5-->
  - `TestLocThresholdRouting.test_below_threshold_single_call` (method) — Asserts that two granular groups totalling 100 estimated LOC route to `_run_single_llm_call` and never invoke `_run_dag_parallel`. <!--#4ea40934886b9f35-->
  - `TestLocThresholdRouting.test_above_threshold_uses_dag` (method) — Asserts that a forked group graph exceeding the LOC threshold routes to _run_dag_parallel rather than a single call. <!--#e37f6670184907ff-->
  - `TestLocThresholdRouting.test_no_estimated_loc_defaults_to_50` (method) — Asserts that tasks lacking `estimated_loc` fall back to 50 LOC each, keeping the total under the threshold so the step routes to the single LLM call. <!--#285c15ee2739f62d-->
- `TestMergeLeafBranch` (class) — Unit tests for `_merge_leaf_branch`, covering clean merges, LLM conflict resolution, the take-theirs fallback path with audit recording, commit-failure aborts, non-conflict failures, and checkout back to the original branch. <!--#2ee43111d045aad8-->
  - `TestMergeLeafBranch.test_clean_merge` (method) — Asserts a conflict-free merge returns True without ever invoking the LLM conflict resolver. <!--#6286e671d6b5decb-->

  - `TestMergeLeafBranch.test_llm_exhausted_falls_back_to_take_theirs` (method) — Asserts that when the LLM resolver gives up, the merge is completed via `checkout --theirs` + add + commit and an audit event is recorded. <!--#340b8ded01beea90-->
  - `TestMergeLeafBranch.test_take_theirs_commit_failure_aborts` (method) — Asserts that a failing take-theirs commit aborts the merge, returns False, and records no audit event. <!--#be0e3f9873d66059-->
  - `TestMergeLeafBranch.test_non_conflict_failure` (method) — Asserts a merge failure unrelated to conflicts aborts and returns False without querying conflicting files. <!--#3cb2de02fbb21cba-->
  - `TestMergeLeafBranch.test_checkout_to_original_branch` (method) — Asserts that when HEAD is not on `original_branch`, the first git call is a checkout to it before stashing and merging. <!--#c1a16b2f00527b9e-->
- `TestResolveLeafMergeConflicts` (class) — Unit tests for `resolve_merge_conflicts_with_context` in worktree.py, covering successful resolution, retry on leftover markers or LLM exceptions, exhaustion returning False, missing/already-clean files, and rich task context in the prompt. <!--#f2a4120711cc0472-->
  - `TestResolveLeafMergeConflicts.test_successful_resolution` (method) — Asserts a first-attempt LLM resolution returns True and writes the resolved content back to the conflicted file. <!--#bc96d79dc4b632b6-->
  - `TestResolveLeafMergeConflicts.test_markers_in_output_triggers_retry` (method) — Asserts LLM output still containing conflict markers triggers a second attempt that succeeds. <!--#059fd043c57bdfc2-->
  - `TestResolveLeafMergeConflicts.test_all_retries_fail_returns_false` (method) — Asserts that exhausting `max_retries` with marker-laden output returns False with no `--theirs` fallback inside the resolver. <!--#49d35d615ea92397-->
  - `TestResolveLeafMergeConflicts.test_llm_exception_triggers_retry` (method) — Asserts an exception raised by the LLM caller is retried rather than fatal, succeeding on the next attempt. <!--#d246034adbe1be14-->
  - `TestResolveLeafMergeConflicts.test_missing_file_returns_false` (method) — Asserts a conflict path that does not exist on disk causes the resolver to return False. <!--#b8af385fa467d68e-->
  - `TestResolveLeafMergeConflicts.test_already_resolved_file_skipped` (method) — Asserts files lacking conflict markers are treated as resolved and never sent to the LLM. <!--#8e614160314f53a5-->
  - `TestResolveLeafMergeConflicts.test_rich_context_in_prompt` (method) — Asserts the resolver's LLM prompt carries the task description (and group summaries) as context. <!--#8d34e3e4b030ca61-->
- `TestDagParallelRelayIntegration` (class) — Integration tests that `_run_dag_parallel` wires transitive reduction and the relay plan into `DAGScheduler`, merges only leaf (or fallback-leaf) branches, and deduplicates shared-worktree cleanup. <!--#5d355376ee43c2bf-->

- `test_fix_round_key_excludes_restricted_edits_carried_from_earlier_rounds` (function) — Asserts the round key lists only the newly applied restricted-edit file while `restricted_edits_applied` stays cumulative across rounds. <!--#20cd70b7808fa008-->
- `test_unparseable_fix_round_clears_the_previous_rounds_value` (function) — Asserts a fix round with an unparseable LLM response resets `fix_round_files_changed` to empty instead of leaving the prior round's value. <!--#06004ee1282fd023-->
- `test_existing_outputs_are_untouched_for_a_non_fix_round` (function) — Regression test that a plain non-fix round still populates all the usual outputs (`files_changed`, `tests_added`, `test_mapping`, `summary`, `completion_status`, `estimated_test_duration`, `group_summaries`). <!--#51b58fe745a7515b-->
- `test_fix_round_with_empty_summary_still_keeps_the_previous_one` (function) — Asserts the pre-existing rule that an empty round summary preserves the earlier `summary` while the round key still records this round's files. <!--#34a96afea44c8b75-->
- `test_resolve_files_changed_still_overwrites_only_the_cumulative_key` (function) — Asserts `_resolve_files_changed` overwrites `files_changed` from the git diff without disturbing `fix_round_files_changed`. <!--#b9bc60908aa78c32-->

### `tests/test_implement_group_status.py` (python) — Integration tests for the DAG implement step's per-group status wiring, using fake schedulers, LLM callers, and agent runners to verify that _run_dag_parallel persists running/completed group_status records (enriched with step_type, live agent, and parsed model) to the main repo's step jsonl and that history salvage never re-touches that file. <!--#42a4b209648ca87e|ffa37fff6b2d5525-->
- `_read_step_records` (function) — Test helper that reads and JSON-parses the per-step jsonl history file at tianluo/history/<flow_id>/<step_id>.jsonl, returning its records as a list of dicts (empty if absent). <!--#2daf1c34bf4f737f-->
- `_FakeScheduler` (class) — Stand-in DAGScheduler that drives the captured on_group_status callback through running→completed for each group without worktrees, threads, or git. <!--#dd96eb6c92490dea-->
  - `_FakeScheduler.__init__` (method) — Captures the groups and on_group_status callback, mirroring the real DAGScheduler constructor signature so it can be patched in. <!--#f4c2c6e6f6b1848a-->
  - `_FakeScheduler.run` (method) — Emits running then completed status callbacks per group and returns completed GroupResults without exercising merge/cleanup paths. <!--#ffe0fbec7bc40574-->
  - `_FakeScheduler.get_fallback_leaves` (method) — Returns an empty list, stubbing the scheduler's fallback-leaves query. <!--#2ff7e2bce848f327-->
- `TestDagGroupStatusWiring` (class) — Test class asserting that DAG-parallel implement execution writes group_status records into the main step jsonl. <!--#c5aa55b4c242f8a6-->
  - `TestDagGroupStatusWiring.test_running_and_completed_records_written` (method) — Runs _run_dag_parallel over two dependent groups with a fake scheduler and checks the main step jsonl gains 'running' and 'completed' group_status records for G1/G2, each tagged step_type 'implement'. <!--#9843035c19dc0e4a-->
- `_FakeResult` (class) — Minimal fake agent-run result object exposing success, output, returncode, and related fields consumed by the LLMCaller. <!--#caa03cd2aea62b03-->
  - `_FakeResult.__init__` (method) — Initializes the fake result's success/output/returncode plus fixed interrupted, cmd_used, and stderr_tail fields. <!--#e4e0fd1f80948ec5-->
- `_AgentStreamRunner` (class) — Fake AgentRunner test double that streams an init line carrying a model name plus one tool_use event before returning a pre-programmed success/failure result, so agent/model tracking and on_agent_change callbacks can be exercised. <!--#587adf04842b0b37-->
  - `_AgentStreamRunner.__init__` (method) — Stores the desired success outcome and the model string to be revealed in the streamed init line. <!--#82c09b3957a7bc3a-->
  - `_AgentStreamRunner.build_call_args` (method) — Stub that returns a minimal ['-p', prompt] argument list instead of building real CLI arguments. <!--#7f6ced27ed062dca-->
  - `_AgentStreamRunner.detect_infra_error` (method) — Stub method on the fake runner that always reports InfraErrorType.NONE (no infrastructure error detected). <!--#ef6e030cdd122d10-->
  - `_AgentStreamRunner.run_with_monitor` (method) — Feeds the on_output callback an init line and a tool_use assistant message, then returns a _FakeResult reflecting the configured success/failure. <!--#e42150cf573af5fe-->
- `TestLLMCallerOnAgentChange` (class) — Test class verifying LLMCaller's on_agent_change fires (agent, None) at selection then (agent, model) after parsing, with each rotated attempt reporting its own agent. <!--#09350c43c75853ec-->
  - `TestLLMCallerOnAgentChange.test_fires_agent_then_model` (method) — Asserts the first on_agent_change event is the agent-only notification and that the agent·model event follows once the model init line is parsed. <!--#d47477de3781f881-->
  - `TestLLMCallerOnAgentChange.test_rotation_reports_each_attempts_agent` (method) — Asserts that after a failed first attempt the agent rotates and each attempt announces its own agent (agentA then agentB), never carrying a stale one over. <!--#1a55f92eff1564b5-->
- `_ExecutingScheduler` (class) — Scheduler stand-in that actually invokes execute_fn (with worktree/git/LLM deps mocked) to exercise the on_agent_change relay and the status sink's agent/model enrichment. <!--#7ccc498ac6ff14f6-->
  - `_ExecutingScheduler.__init__` (method) — Captures the groups and on_group_status callback, mirroring the real DAGScheduler constructor. <!--#f4c2c6e6f6b1848a-->
  - `_ExecutingScheduler.run` (method) — Emits running, calls execute_fn per group, then emits completed, collecting each group's result. <!--#1ab3ce790e148d28-->
  - `_ExecutingScheduler.get_fallback_leaves` (method) — Returns an empty list, stubbing the fallback-leaves query. <!--#2ff7e2bce848f327-->
- `_RelayCaller` (class) — Fake LLMCaller whose call() fires the on_agent_change relay (agent-only then agent·model) like the real in-worktree caller. <!--#85ae00d7c4e6685d-->
  - `_RelayCaller.__init__` (method) — Captures the on_agent_change callback while ignoring other constructor arguments. <!--#0ffe4acf00f5785a-->
  - `_RelayCaller.call` (method) — Fires the agent-only then agent·model relay callbacks and returns an empty JSON object. <!--#4ed094f3c1d2c3d8-->
- `_GitStub` (class) — Minimal stub of a git subprocess result with empty stdout/stderr and a zero returncode. <!--#d4148739844e286d-->
  - `_GitStub.__init__` (method) — Initializes the git stub's empty stdout/stderr and zero returncode. <!--#1fd9c4b25336d79c-->
- `TestDagAgentModelRelay` (class) — Test class verifying that agent and model names are relayed into group_status records during DAG execution, and that history salvage never re-appends to the main step file. <!--#12bd08aa29ffd7f2-->
  - `TestDagAgentModelRelay.test_running_and_completed_records_carry_agent_and_model` (method) — Drives _run_dag_parallel with a streaming fake runner and asserts running records pick up agent_name 'dclaude' then model_name 'claude-opus-4-8', and that the final completed record is enriched with the same agent/model. <!--#48a9dcf28952ff56-->
  - `TestDagAgentModelRelay.test_salvage_does_not_append_to_main_step_file` (method) — Test that _salvage_results_history copies a worktree's _G1 conversation history into the main repo while leaving the main step file's group_status records unchanged (no duplication). <!--#036b17ca9cc9294c-->

### `tests/test_import_isolation.py` (python) — Import-isolation test module that spawns fresh Python subprocesses to verify a core-only install (without the `tianluo[server]` extra) keeps the CLI functional and never leaks the heavy `fastapi`/`uvicorn` web dependencies into core imports. <!--#e6ff138b16d16846|efa015293387c7f4-->
- `_subprocess_env` (function) — Test helper that returns a copy of the process environment with the project's src directory prepended to PYTHONPATH so subprocesses import the in-tree package. <!--#239b143ce4a730af-->
- `_run_python` (function) — Test helper that runs a dedented code snippet in a fresh Python interpreter subprocess (with the src PYTHONPATH) and returns the CompletedProcess for assertions. <!--#9ef4fa206e0ca541-->
- `test_core_modules_import_without_server_modules_leaking` (function) — Asserts that importing every core module in a clean interpreter never pulls fastapi or uvicorn into sys.modules. <!--#94bea6d904dd0fd9-->
- `test_importing_se3_does_not_import_server_package` (function) — Test asserting that importing tianluo and tianluo.cli in a clean interpreter does not pull in the optional tianluo.server package. <!--#a425f3ce5f3cd7f7-->
- `test_core_command_help_has_no_import_error` (function) — Parametrized test asserting that `se3 <command> --help` (via python -m tianluo.cli) succeeds without triggering any ImportError/ModuleNotFoundError from the missing server extra. <!--#257a92d4fdb4cdbc-->
- `test_se3_server_reports_clear_hint_when_extra_missing` (function) — Test that simulates a core-only install (fastapi/uvicorn unimportable) and verifies se3-server exits 1 with a friendly `pip install tianluo[server]` hint on stderr instead of a raw traceback. <!--#a3394f4669c1b57d-->

### `tests/test_init_cmd.py` (python) — Unit tests for the `init` command, covering `run_init`'s scaffolding of `tianluo/charter.md`, `tianluo.yaml`, the `tianluo/` runtime dir and `VERSIONS.md` (placeholder substitution, no-overwrite vs `--force`, idempotent reruns), the generated `.gitignore` (root default-deny with whitelists, uploads ignoring, append/negation handling verified via `git check-ignore`), the `tianluo.local.yaml` shadowing signal, and the git helpers `is_git_repository`, `init_repository` and `create_gitignore`. <!--#af156288482a4c64|3aadc739c6f1ff64-->
- `TestRunInit` (class) — Tests for `run_init`, covering scaffolding of `tianluo/charter.md` and `tianluo.yaml` (with project-name placeholder substitution and no retired `specs/base/spec.md`), non-overwrite/idempotent reruns, git repo initialization or detection, and `.gitignore` creation/appending. <!--#b17cf0d163beafcc-->
  - `TestRunInit.test_creates_charter` (method) — Asserts run_init generates tianluo/charter.md from template with the project name and records it in result['created'], while the retired base spec corpus is not scaffolded. <!--#4b4545ae9731309b-->
  - `TestRunInit.test_creates_se3_yaml` (method) — Asserts run_init creates tianluo.yaml carrying the project name and lists it under result['created'] when it doesn't already exist. <!--#e477c90b07ae7114-->
  - `TestRunInit.test_creates_se3_directory` (method) — Asserts run_init creates the tianluo/ runtime directory without scaffolding the retired specs/ subdirectory. <!--#9df82a80a703a65b-->
  - `TestRunInit.test_no_overwrite_existing_charter` (method) — Asserts run_init leaves a pre-existing charter's content intact and reports it as skipped/'already exists'. <!--#8545746004fbcd8f-->
  - `TestRunInit.test_no_overwrite_existing_se3_yaml` (method) — Asserts run_init preserves an existing tianluo.yaml and reports it as skipped/'already exists'. <!--#1f822b8edd0e7574-->
  - `TestRunInit.test_default_project_name_placeholder` (method) — Asserts template {project_name} placeholders in the generated charter are replaced with the supplied project name. <!--#ddd32016c05a50e9-->
  - `TestRunInit.test_idempotent_full_run` (method) — Asserts a second run_init produces no new created files, skips the two config products, and flags the .gitignore as already existing. <!--#4307251a963bdbf4-->
  - `TestRunInit.test_init_creates_git_repo` (method) — Asserts init initializes a git repository in a non-git directory. <!--#f7bc3756f1e22b20-->
  - `TestRunInit.test_init_respects_existing_git` (method) — Asserts init does not reinitialize git when already inside a repo. <!--#92081a3b5b7ebb5e-->
  - `TestRunInit.test_init_creates_gitignore` (method) — Asserts a fresh `run_init` writes a `.gitignore` whose content carries the runtime-dir default-deny `/tianluo/*` plus whitelists for `code-index.md`, `charter.md` and `issues/`, and an ignore line for `/tianluo/uploads/`. <!--#76f5ad9abdf6a11c-->
  - `TestRunInit.test_gitignore_ignores_uploads_dir` (method) — End-to-end check that after `run_init` git's own `git check-ignore` actually ignores an uploaded attachment under `tianluo/uploads/`, rather than relying on string matching. <!--#7d97e628256c76db-->
  - `TestRunInit.test_gitignore_has_root_default_deny` (method) — Asserts the generated .gitignore contains a standalone `/*` line establishing root default-deny so stray junk isn't staged by `git add -A`. <!--#42f9aebb58e59593-->
  - `TestRunInit.test_gitignore_whitelists_all_tracked_top_level_entries` (method) — Asserts every top-level product run_init lands, plus standard project files, has a matching `!/<name>` un-ignore line under the root default-deny .gitignore. <!--#77a65c4aafc634f2-->
  - `TestRunInit.test_gitignore_does_not_block_init_products` (method) — End-to-end check via `git check-ignore` that none of the top-level paths run_init lands are actually ignored by the generated .gitignore. <!--#cf1abc55440b9034-->
  - `TestRunInit.test_init_force_overwrites_gitignore` (method) — Asserts run_init(force=True) overwrites an existing .gitignore with the standard template, discarding the prior custom content. <!--#3f5075a0789de068-->
  - `TestRunInit.test_init_appends_local_pattern_to_existing_gitignore` (method) — Verifies that with a pre-existing `.gitignore`, `run_init` reports `gitignore_appended` and adds the `tianluo.local.yaml` and `tianluo/uploads/` patterns while preserving original content. <!--#76fc9c9c67aa0cd7-->
  - `TestRunInit.test_init_local_overrides_yaml_signal` (method) — Asserts run_init surfaces the local_overrides_yaml flag when a tianluo.local.yaml already exists, warning the operator that the committed tianluo.yaml is shadowed at load time. <!--#e4085ac548f49a37-->
  - `TestRunInit.test_init_local_overrides_yaml_false_when_no_local` (method) — Asserts `local_overrides_yaml` is False when no tianluo.local.yaml exists. <!--#b199f486a953e8f2-->
  - `TestRunInit.test_init_surfaces_gitignore_negated_for_explicit_negation` (method) — End-to-end assertion that an explicit `!tianluo.local.yaml` negation in .gitignore sets gitignore_negated (not appended/created) and leaves the file unmutated. <!--#5c5d481907b8c01f-->
  - `TestRunInit.test_init_force_with_existing_local_still_surfaces_signal` (method) — Asserts run_init(force=True) regenerates tianluo.yaml yet still sets local_overrides_yaml when a tianluo.local.yaml shadows it, without touching the local file. <!--#6b95f9193af89546-->
  - `TestRunInit.test_creates_versions_md` (method) — Asserts init creates VERSIONS.md from template with the canonical title, initial 0.1.0 entry, and substituted placeholders. <!--#99d83ba5a0a540da-->
  - `TestRunInit.test_no_overwrite_existing_versions_md` (method) — Asserts init leaves an existing VERSIONS.md untouched and flags it as already-existing. <!--#1f35ad73f1552f55-->
  - `TestRunInit.test_versions_md_force_overwrites` (method) — Asserts `--force` regenerates VERSIONS.md from the template. <!--#9a9006639f012817-->
  - `TestRunInit.test_charter_mentions_version_rules` (method) — Asserts the generated charter documents the tianluo/version-rules.md mechanism rather than locking in static version-bump rules. <!--#2c83530023b96bec-->
- `TestGitHelpers` (class) — Tests for the git helper functions `is_git_repository`, `init_repository` and `create_gitignore`, focusing on repo detection (including parent lookup) and the created/appended/unchanged/negated semantics of ensuring ignore rules. <!--#bf08358c70b8d7a6-->
  - `TestGitHelpers.test_is_git_repository_returns_true_in_git_repo` (method) — Asserts `is_git_repository` returns True inside a git repo. <!--#d293edd16d38f6b5-->
  - `TestGitHelpers.test_is_git_repository_returns_false_outside_git_repo` (method) — Asserts `is_git_repository` returns False outside a git repo. <!--#23cf0d74e41826c5-->
  - `TestGitHelpers.test_is_git_repository_finds_parent_git_repo` (method) — Asserts `is_git_repository` detects a .git directory in a parent path. <!--#fbcd2c3d9e5059f9-->
  - `TestGitHelpers.test_init_repository_creates_git_repo` (method) — Asserts `init_repository` creates a git repo and returns a success message. <!--#ab31da07d3a43f5a-->
  - `TestGitHelpers.test_create_gitignore_creates_file` (method) — Asserts `create_gitignore` on a clean directory returns status `created` and writes exactly `DEFAULT_GITIGNORE_TEMPLATE`. <!--#1ea10f0ec8de7012-->
  - `TestGitHelpers.test_create_gitignore_appends_local_pattern_to_existing` (method) — Asserts `create_gitignore` returns `appended` and adds `tianluo.local.yaml` to an existing `.gitignore` without discarding its content. <!--#77c53242598afa04-->
  - `TestGitHelpers.test_create_gitignore_idempotent_when_pattern_present` (method) — Asserts `create_gitignore` is a byte-for-byte no-op returning `unchanged` when every ensured rule is already present. <!--#422db7c2f27d0c61-->
  - `TestGitHelpers.test_create_gitignore_idempotent_with_trailing_slash_pattern` (method) — Asserts a directory-only `tianluo.local.yaml/` line counts as existing ignore intent so no duplicate plain rule is appended. <!--#d4051255def25170-->
  - `TestGitHelpers.test_create_gitignore_detects_negation_and_refuses_to_append` (method) — Asserts an explicit `!tianluo.local.yaml` un-ignore makes `create_gitignore` return `negated` with a warning message and leave the file untouched instead of creating a last-line-wins conflict. <!--#ee8735a626b66db3-->
  - `TestGitHelpers.test_create_gitignore_broad_negation_does_not_trigger_negated` (method) — Asserts broad un-ignores like `!*.yaml`, `!se3.*` or `!*` still yield `appended` rather than a misleading `negated` status. <!--#fc9db8ded6615faf-->
  - `TestGitHelpers.test_create_gitignore_recursive_glob_prefix_is_recognised` (method) — Asserts a `**/tianluo.local.yaml` rule is recognised as already ignoring the file (the `**` prefix is stripped before matching) so nothing redundant is appended. <!--#fa03e3379066fa3d-->
  - `TestGitHelpers.test_create_gitignore_appends_uploads_pattern` (method) — Asserts a legacy `.gitignore` predating the upload channel gains the `tianluo/uploads/` rule, returned in both the file and the reported patterns list. <!--#b8b0c01bfe94b0ac-->
  - `TestGitHelpers.test_create_gitignore_appends_only_the_missing_pattern` (method) — Asserts only the absent rule is appended — the already-present `tianluo.local.yaml` line is not duplicated. <!--#105e57f74fcf8c14-->
  - `TestGitHelpers.test_create_gitignore_uploads_idempotent_under_runtime_deny` (method) — Asserts an existing `/tianluo/*` default-deny already covers the uploads dir, so `create_gitignore` returns `unchanged` instead of adding a redundant rule. <!--#1d6705f94250504f-->
  - `TestGitHelpers.test_create_gitignore_uploads_idempotent_with_bare_pattern` (method) — Asserts a slash-free `uploads/` rule is recognised via component-wise matching (git ignores it at any depth) so no redundant rule is appended. <!--#4d6306383f1516c3-->
  - `TestGitHelpers.test_create_gitignore_uploads_uses_legacy_runtime_dir_name` (method) — Asserts that on a project still using the legacy `se3/` runtime layout the appended rule names `se3/uploads/` rather than `tianluo/uploads/`. <!--#f278432ca5028300-->
  - `TestGitHelpers.test_create_gitignore_negation_of_uploads_is_refused` (method) — Asserts an explicit `!tianluo/uploads/` negation yields status `negated` with that pattern reported and the file left unmodified. <!--#e14f4fedb656ae11-->
  - `TestGitHelpers.test_create_gitignore_runtime_dir_whitelist_is_not_a_negation` (method) — Asserts the template's `!/tianluo/` descend-into-directory line is not misread as un-ignoring `tianluo/uploads`, so `create_gitignore` still appends both ensured rules. <!--#0c6f78cb652ecf2b-->
  - `TestGitHelpers.test_uploads_dir_name_matches_daemon` (method) — Pins `init_cmd`'s locally re-declared `UPLOADS_DIR_NAME` to the daemon's `tianluo.daemon.uploads.UPLOADS_DIR_NAME`, since the CLI deliberately avoids importing the daemon package. <!--#5ccccb1b13672259-->
  - `TestGitHelpers.test_create_gitignore_overwrites_with_force` (method) — Asserts `create_gitignore(..., force=True)` replaces an existing `.gitignore` wholesale with `DEFAULT_GITIGNORE_TEMPLATE` and reports status `created`. <!--#9e3d23d71a5df205-->
- `TestSpecLoadingSurfaceRemoved` (class) — Regression test class asserting that the retired `tianluo/specs/` scaffolding is fully gone — `luo init` no longer creates specs and the spec-reading `ContextBuilder` surface was deleted rather than left as an empty stub. <!--#d34a5ed480fadc2a-->
  - `TestSpecLoadingSurfaceRemoved.test_context_builder_removed` (method) — Asserts that the `tianluo.engine.context_builder` module no longer exposes a `ContextBuilder` attribute. <!--#fefd371a96dad396-->

### `tests/test_integration_g8.py` (python) — Group G8 cross-layer integration regression tests verifying end-to-end contracts across CLI, daemon, server, and frontend—covering legacy issue YAML loading without migration, source-field semantics ('human' vs 'system'), archived/active flow resume acceptance and argv routing, cross-owner rejection, and IssueManager→DaemonAggregator→ServerState→REST round-trips. <!--#4d6957c6dd79de66|413ed4cbb1bdec62-->
- `_NullWS` (class) — Async WebSocket stand-in whose send() just records frames, used to drive the async _handle_spawn coroutine in success-path unit tests. <!--#173e38f814eeb3ba-->
  - `_NullWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the stub's empty list for capturing sent frames. <!--#b8b92aad379d234c-->
  - `_NullWS.send` (method) — Awaitable no-op that appends the outgoing data to the captured-frames list. <!--#5d99d04813c9aa58-->
- `_run_handle_spawn` (function) — Test helper that runs the async DaemonClient._handle_spawn coroutine to completion against a _NullWS socket. <!--#0d4509317bb2c4c5-->
- `_write_legacy_yaml` (function) — Test helper that writes a minimal legacy issue YAML (missing `source` and other modern fields) into `tianluo/issues/open/` and returns its path. <!--#587e760ebdbaf1b1-->
- `_write_modern_yaml` (function) — Test helper that writes a fully-specified modern issue YAML (with `source`, `title`, `priority`, `type`, timestamps, etc.) into `tianluo/issues/open/` and returns its path. <!--#648ccaec743a6ae2-->
- `_make_identity_with_key` (function) — Test helper that builds an in-memory IdentityService with one owner and an issued daemon key, returning (identity, owner_id, key_plaintext). <!--#e5a51c28c81aaacd-->
- `TestLegacyYamlCompatibility` (class) — Test class asserting legacy issue YAML (missing newer fields) loads correctly with sensible defaults and no migration step. <!--#630b9e6958c91fc2-->
  - `TestLegacyYamlCompatibility.test_missing_source_defaults_to_system` (method) — Asserts a YAML without a source field loads with source defaulting to 'system'. <!--#ef47fed5ac09dd5d-->
  - `TestLegacyYamlCompatibility.test_missing_title_loads_as_none` (method) — Asserts a YAML without a title field loads with Issue.title as None. <!--#0ebebd2f75768e48-->
  - `TestLegacyYamlCompatibility.test_missing_priority_loads_as_none` (method) — Asserts a YAML without a priority field loads with Issue.priority as None. <!--#707c6a3d02874a76-->
  - `TestLegacyYamlCompatibility.test_missing_type_loads_as_none` (method) — Asserts a YAML without a type field loads with Issue.type as None. <!--#72d816c999919d46-->
  - `TestLegacyYamlCompatibility.test_display_title_derives_from_description` (method) — Asserts display_title falls back to the description's first line when title is None. <!--#7b8090d75b865388-->
  - `TestLegacyYamlCompatibility.test_legacy_yaml_roundtrip_preserves_data` (method) — Asserts loading then re-saving a legacy issue (via status update) preserves source, description, and the new status. <!--#529fcb9d1dbaa5d5-->
  - `TestLegacyYamlCompatibility.test_legacy_yaml_list_issues_includes_it` (method) — Asserts legacy issues appear in list_issues output with their defaulted source. <!--#95ffa4b91886155b-->
  - `TestLegacyYamlCompatibility.test_legacy_yaml_with_missing_source_in_from_dict` (method) — Asserts Issue.from_dict defaults source to 'system' when the key is absent. <!--#c1f45223ff4c6f92-->
  - `TestLegacyYamlCompatibility.test_from_dict_with_explicit_source_preserved` (method) — Asserts Issue.from_dict preserves an explicitly provided source value. <!--#8ada6f04cfb95c03-->
- `TestSourceFieldSemantics` (class) — Test class verifying the issue source field ('human' vs 'system') is assigned correctly per creation path and survives YAML roundtrips and filtering. <!--#3dc6d66052b58be1-->
  - `TestSourceFieldSemantics.test_issue_manager_create_default_source_is_system` (method) — Asserts IssueManager.create() defaults source to 'system'. <!--#0f2cbb46e99d098e-->
  - `TestSourceFieldSemantics.test_issue_manager_create_explicit_human` (method) — Asserts IssueManager.create(source='human') writes 'human'. <!--#ef35fc67cd067151-->

### `tests/test_interaction_calls.py` (python) — Test suite for the unified interaction-call channel, exercising the three layers that turn every human-in-the-loop flow interaction into a JSON call file under tianluo/calls/: the daemon protocol (MSG_INTERJECT_FLOW, CALL_KIND constants, decode backward-compat), the DaemonAggregator parsing of every call kind including legacy files, and the interaction_calls engine module for writing calls, reading response siblings, draining queued interjections, and handling retry-decision and CLI-confirm flows. <!--#2da2ceae877a4260|02aebbef3381c520-->
- `test_make_interject_flow_payload_and_direction` (function) — Asserts make_interject_flow builds the correct payload and that MSG_INTERJECT_FLOW is registered as a server→daemon (not daemon→server) message type. <!--#ce856c65ac66617e-->
- `test_interject_flow_round_trips_through_decode` (function) — Verifies an interject-flow message survives JSON encode/decode with its text preserved and project_root defaulting to empty string. <!--#ac2793896657f29a-->
- `test_call_kind_constants_are_complete_and_distinct` (function) — Asserts that the protocol's CALL_KINDS set contains exactly the six expected CALL_KIND_* constants (call, interjection, retry-decision, cli-confirm, discovery-confirm, confirm) and that all six are distinct string literals. <!--#2a6d703f03d1a0b1-->
- `test_decode_still_rejects_unknown_types` (function) — Ensures decode raises ProtocolError on a genuinely unknown message type despite newly added known types. <!--#398349aec6b9786b-->
- `test_decode_tolerates_interject_without_optional_fields` (function) — Confirms a minimal interject frame carrying only the required type decodes successfully with an empty payload. <!--#2ebdd7b6b0959937-->
- `_write` (function) — Test helper that JSON-serializes a payload to a file, creating parent directories as needed. <!--#65d03e595cacafc0-->
- `test_aggregator_parses_every_call_kind` (function) — Verifies that DaemonAggregator._enumerate_calls parses every call kind (call, interjection, retry_decision, cli_confirm) from the tianluo/calls dir, preserving enriched fields (prompt, options, context) through to_dict() serialization. <!--#dddba82215ed0d22-->
- `test_aggregator_legacy_call_file_without_kind` (function) — Asserts that a pre-feature legacy call file lacking a `kind` key is reported as a plain `call` (with empty prompt/context/options) rather than dropped by the aggregator. <!--#ae74e36b38839000-->
- `test_aggregator_unknown_kind_falls_back_to_call` (function) — Checks that both an unrecognised `kind` value and a non-object JSON body degrade gracefully to the `call` kind during aggregation. <!--#bcd92ed3b8b432be-->
- `test_write_and_read_call_round_trip` (function) — Round-trips interaction_calls.write_call / read_call for a cli_confirm call, confirming the file name and that kind/prompt/context/options persist. <!--#4b695bd849c66726-->
- `test_write_call_rejects_unknown_kind` (function) — Asserts interaction_calls.write_call raises ValueError when given an unknown call kind. <!--#ff4d72cdcefcf4f5-->
- `test_read_call_legacy_file_defaults_kind` (function) — Verifies that reading a legacy call file with no `kind` key defaults to `call` via both read_call and classify_kind. <!--#f1538c4fc77fce59-->
- `test_read_call_handles_missing_and_malformed` (function) — Asserts read_call returns None for a missing file and for malformed JSON. <!--#687b30bb968163c8-->
- `test_classify_kind_defensive` (function) — Checks classify_kind defensively returns 'call' for None/empty/unknown inputs and the correct kind for valid ones. <!--#092af2612a47bc38-->
- `test_write_response_round_trip` (function) — Round-trips interaction_calls.write_response / read_response, confirming read_response returns None before a response exists and the written body afterward. <!--#2246c3bab3521b0e-->
- `test_read_response_accepts_daemon_response_json` (function) — Confirms read_response also recognises the daemon client's `<stem>.response.json` sibling file format, not just the primary response file. <!--#f1bf98edc02cf309-->
- `test_drain_interjection_requests_consumes_and_is_idempotent` (function) — Verifies drain_interjection_requests returns queued interjection texts/call_ids in order and that a second drain returns nothing since each request is marked consumed. <!--#e33280d794125a65-->
- `test_drain_ignores_non_interjection_kinds` (function) — Asserts drain_interjection_requests drains only `interjection` kind calls, ignoring `call` and `retry_decision` files. <!--#a2e43bbfaa28cb01-->
- `test_drain_skips_empty_text_requests` (function) — Checks that a whitespace-only interjection is skipped from the drain results yet still marked consumed so it is not re-examined. <!--#cfa477ce069cbca3-->
- `test_drain_missing_calls_dir_returns_empty` (function) — Confirms draining when the calls directory does not exist returns an empty list. <!--#cb65df987afe9643-->
- `test_drain_unlinks_call_file_and_writes_served_sibling` (function) — Verifies drain seals each consumed call via write-response-then-delete: the .json file is unlinked while a sibling .response marker (consumed=true, served_by=run_loop, served_at) remains. <!--#c2dd0ab84cf2501f-->
- `test_drain_returns_step_id_and_step_type_when_present` (function) — Confirms drained interjection entries surface step_id/step_type/created_at fields pulled from the call's context. <!--#c0ded16e4178daa8-->
- `test_drain_legacy_call_without_context_step_fields_empty` (function) — Asserts legacy interjection calls lacking context.step_id still drain cleanly with empty step_id/step_type strings. <!--#412ffdc9be40b16a-->
- `test_drain_second_pass_is_idempotent_after_unlink` (function) — Verifies a second drain pass finds nothing because the first pass's unlink prevents re-processing. <!--#bbb5fbbed21f1274-->
- `test_write_retry_decision_call_shape` (function) — Checks write_retry_decision_call derives a step-based filename and writes the retry kind, retry/skip/abort options, and context/prompt fields. <!--#8cc0d13c846f142c-->
- `test_cli_confirm_handler_returns_answer_when_response_arrives` (function) — Tests that make_cli_confirm_handler polls and returns the answer once a response is written while the child subprocess reports alive. <!--#bf6e5551d4c146dc-->
- `test_cli_confirm_handler_marks_orphan_consumed_when_child_exits` (function) — Verifies the cli_confirm handler returns None and marks the orphaned call file consumed (skipped=subprocess_exited) when the child exits before answering. <!--#b5715d9fdb72bc6d-->
