### `tests/test_interjection_fast_push.py` (python) — Test suite for the interjection fast-push pipeline, covering pending-calls signature computation and change detection in DaemonClient, fast-push event wiring on interject dispatch, the per-machine interjection chip tracker's pending/consumed event lifecycle, UI broadcast of interjection events, and ServerState history-append/full-pull-throttle behavior. <!--#be32fe2887f5d455|31c5176c323bc688-->
- `_write` (function) — Helper that JSON-serializes a payload to a file, creating parent directories first. <!--#65d03e595cacafc0-->
- `_FakeWS` (class) — Fake WebSocket test double that records decoded frames passed to its send method. <!--#9ebf99b26f1ca2c6-->
  - `_FakeWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the fake WebSocket's empty list of sent frames. <!--#b8b92aad379d234c-->
  - `_FakeWS.send` (method) — Decodes and appends an outgoing frame to the recorded sent list. <!--#7d44362527b3e749-->
- `_make_client` (function) — Factory building a DaemonClient with default test arguments and overridable keyword options. <!--#6a90ceaf2230f869-->
- `test_pending_calls_signature_empty_when_no_calls_dir` (function) — Asserts the calls signature is empty when a tracked root has no tianluo/calls directory. <!--#8abf6c1278b51914-->
- `test_pending_calls_signature_lists_each_file_with_stat` (function) — Asserts DaemonAggregator.pending_calls_signature returns, per project root, a sorted list of (name, mtime, size) entries covering every tianluo/calls file with populated stat values. <!--#e5ed6474a38cf41c-->
- `test_pending_calls_signature_changes_when_file_added` (function) — Verifies the pending-calls signature changes after a new call file is written into the calls directory. <!--#a8bf5f6d7a17fe9d-->
- `test_pending_calls_signature_changes_when_file_removed` (function) — Verifies the pending-calls signature changes after an existing call file is removed from the calls directory. <!--#bfcd0e78c6b8aefd-->
- `test_pending_calls_signature_skips_hidden_files` (function) — Confirms the pending-calls signature ignores dot-prefixed/hidden files and lists only real call JSON files. <!--#1e3a8c3717461ead-->
- `_FakeSignatureProvider` (class) — Mutable callable test double standing in for the aggregator's pending_calls_signature provider. <!--#611bef6672883121-->
  - `_FakeSignatureProvider.__init__` (method) — Initializes the fake provider's mutable signature dict to empty. <!--#18a8e68f80a604da-->
  - `_FakeSignatureProvider.__call__` (method) — Returns a copy of the provider's current signature when invoked. <!--#b26d94ff89630a64-->
- `test_calls_changed_detects_signature_delta` (function) — Verifies _calls_changed reports changes on signature deltas and debounces after observation. <!--#30addebcac22bbd9-->
- `test_calls_changed_without_provider_is_false` (function) — Asserts _calls_changed returns False when no signature provider is configured. <!--#11e465f9818d0de7-->
- `test_calls_changed_provider_failure_forces_push` (function) — Verifies a provider exception conservatively reports a change so a push still fires. <!--#0c1f599c7dd33483-->
- `test_handle_interject_sets_fast_push_event` (function) — Checks that dispatching an interject-flow message writes the interjection_*.json file and flips the client's _fast_push_event so the push loop wakes immediately. <!--#1ec402d7e24d9af5-->
- `test_handle_interject_no_event_when_text_empty` (function) — Verifies empty interjection text writes no file and never wakes the push loop. <!--#76a7afc61b5fe732-->
- `test_handle_interject_no_event_when_handler_raises` (function) — Verifies a failing interject handler does not flip the fast-push event. <!--#effc51a45ec3d976-->
- `_snapshot_with_interjections` (function) — Helper building a machine snapshot whose flow contains interjection-kind pending calls for the given call ids. <!--#45b0762c4fc787ca-->
- `test_tracker_emits_pending_on_first_appearance` (function) — Asserts the tracker emits a fully-populated pending interjection_event when a chip first appears. <!--#1c053a85ee4796eb-->
- `test_tracker_emits_consumed_when_call_disappears` (function) — Verifies the tracker emits a consumed event when a previously-seen interjection chip disappears. <!--#3c8fcb655f702d66-->
- `test_tracker_does_not_double_emit_same_phase` (function) — Confirms a still-present chip produces no duplicate pending event on the next diff. <!--#c072ecf3e8a2a0eb-->
- `test_tracker_ignores_non_interjection_kinds` (function) — Verifies only interjection-kind chips, not retry/call kinds, drive the event lifecycle. <!--#931c9dd65ef9d55b-->
- `test_tracker_emits_consumed_when_flow_vanishes` (function) — Checks that a flow dropping out of the snapshot emits consumed events for its chips. <!--#76bc00172c4b9ded-->
- `test_tracker_reset_machine_replays_pending_after_reconnect` (function) — Verifies reset_machine causes still-pending chips to replay as pending after a reconnect. <!--#639c8e5c9d518b1b-->
- `test_tracker_per_machine_state_is_isolated` (function) — Confirms each machine's diff state is independent so chips don't bleed across machines. <!--#b8b114d3a2ee6315-->
- `test_status_update_broadcasts_interjection_event_to_ui_clients` (function) — End-to-end test asserting that a daemon STATUS_UPDATE introducing an interjection-kind pending_call causes the server to broadcast an interjection_event frame (with matching machine_id, flow_id, call_id, pending phase, and prompt text) to connected /ws/ui clients. <!--#11cbe3b9e0d0ce21-->
- `test_tracker_handles_malformed_snapshots_gracefully` (function) — Verifies the tracker returns no events and never raises on missing-key or malformed snapshot inputs. <!--#847b4a02b5780a69-->
- `test_pending_calls_signature_includes_worktree_run_calls` (function) — Ensures a --worktree isolation run's <worktree>/tianluo/calls directory is included in the fast call signature so worktree discovery clarifications surface promptly. <!--#3b645e359a12ff3b-->
- `test_history_relay_preserves_step_id_and_ordinal_identity` (function) — Asserts the ServerState history relay preserves each record's step_id and ordinal verbatim, keeping two same-ordinal but distinct-step_id sidecar rounds uncollapsed. <!--#42523637b033202f-->
- `test_history_append_does_not_dedupe_same_ordinal_records` (function) — Verifies append_history extends the bundle without deduping a later round that reuses an existing ordinal under a distinct step_id. <!--#f9fa1bb6d6a923b9-->
- `test_reconcile_full_pull_respects_existing_throttle` (function) — Checks that after mark_full_pull a flow reads as full_pull_throttled, so the self-heal reconcile shares the same throttle and cannot fan out one daemon pull per idle tick. <!--#4341f5b4591a1772-->

### `tests/test_invariant_check.py` (python) — Test suite for the INVARIANT_CHECK step, covering cheap no-diff/no-anchor short-circuits, two-sided grounding rules (verbatim_quote must exist in the charter/task/why-comment anchor pool and evidence must point at a changed file), why-comment harvesting including recovery of comments deleted by the diff via the flow-start git baseline, FAILED handling of unparsable LLM responses, and the 2026-07-28 regression that out_of_scope findings now route to the fix loop and the prompt no longer offers that field. <!--#0f37391c89695308|93c77889c1c90d8b-->
- `_make_flow` (function) — Helper that builds a feature FlowInstance with a given task description and a change_path under the test's project root. <!--#ffc7ea4176dbfbe2-->
- `_make_step` (function) — Helper that constructs an INVARIANT_CHECK Step from a given inputs dict. <!--#3e4d116d5efe7203-->
- `_install_fake_caller` (function) — Helper that monkeypatches the step's LLMCaller with a scripted fake recording prompts/call counts and returning queued responses. <!--#48f66cdee783b441-->
- `_grounded_issue` (function) — Test helper that builds a well-formed high-severity issue dict whose `verbatim_quote` and evidence line are supplied by the caller, so the issue is grounded in the anchor/source pool. <!--#8aa8d07694875bde-->
- `test_no_diff_passes_cheap_without_llm` (function) — Asserts that an invariant_check with no changed files passes as COMPLETED with skipped_reason 'no_diff' and makes no LLM call. <!--#5cc2d026d2acee1f-->
- `test_no_anchors_refuses_anchorless_check` (function) — Asserts that a diff with zero recorded anchors yields a cheap COMPLETED pass (skipped_reason 'no_anchors') rather than inventing an invariant. <!--#27e66bb91cab2036-->
- `test_ungrounded_nit_is_filtered` (function) — Asserts that an issue whose `verbatim_quote` appears nowhere in the charter/task/why-comment source pool is dropped, leaving the step COMPLETED with empty issues and `quote_not_in_source_count` incremented. <!--#4ac2c75a60fdbe1f-->
- `test_grounded_violation_routes_to_fix` (function) — Asserts that a violation quoting the charter verbatim with evidence in a changed file survives to REVISION_NEEDED with fix outputs populated. <!--#49d21b341c9eecf2-->
- `test_evidence_must_point_at_changed_file` (function) — Asserts the two-sided anchoring: a valid charter quote whose evidence path is not among the changed files is dropped and counted in bad_evidence_count. <!--#b76a319f2c06bd08-->
- `test_why_comment_anchor_is_harvested_from_changed_file` (function) — Asserts that a why-comment present in a changed file enters the anchor pool, so a violation quoting it survives to REVISION_NEEDED. <!--#1eecbca80eae666d-->
- `_git` (function) — Helper that runs a git subcommand in a given working directory, raising on failure. <!--#eae0deaeea597400-->
- `test_deleted_why_comment_invariant_recovered_from_baseline` (function) — Regression test verifying that a why-comment documenting a binding invariant stays anchorable even when the violating diff deletes it, by confirming the harvest recovers the original comment from the flow-start baseline (via git show) and still yields exactly one hard, anchored violation while treating the unmarked deletion as advisory-only. <!--#c458c7c31dc01e07-->
- `test_unparsable_llm_response_fails` (function) — Asserts that a non-JSON LLM response makes the step return FAILED with an error message set. <!--#c00d17d5f8570232-->
- `test_all_findings_out_of_scope_still_route_to_fix` (function) — Regression test (2026-07-28) that a grounded finding self-marked `out_of_scope` is no longer discarded but routed to the fix loop, yielding REVISION_NEEDED with one actionable issue and no `out_of_scope_count` stat. <!--#3088a4dedb3c2905-->
- `test_prompt_no_longer_offers_out_of_scope` (function) — Asserts the LLM prompt no longer advertises the `out_of_scope` field, keeping the prompt contract consistent with the handler's behaviour. <!--#edeb8d84537ffe24-->

### `tests/test_issue209_live_append_regression.py` (python) — Regression lock for issue #209 that replays the real captured frame sequence (on-disk jsonl fixtures + recorded daemon_frames.json) through DaemonHistoryReader to prove the discovery→analyze transition and step-error retry surface as no-loss/no-dup/no-truncation append deltas, and that the ~1 MB active engine.json is parsed at most once per actual change (verifying the daemon push-loop starvation fix). <!--#fcdf855881c6cdc5|aa69f71a45017b3d-->
- `_load_fixture_lines` (function) — Helper that reads each real fixture jsonl file and returns its raw newline-kept lines keyed by file name. <!--#211d170bf7b36abd-->
- `_load_captured_frames` (function) — Helper that loads the recorded daemon frame sequence (the expected per-tick read output) from daemon_frames.json. <!--#1438223a67f62bae-->
- `_ondisk_messages` (function) — Helper that returns every on-disk fixture record in file-then-line order as the no-loss ground-truth message sequence. <!--#d97b6673519977bb-->
- `_write_active_engine` (function) — Test helper that writes a RUNNING active `engine.json` under `<root>/tianluo/state/`, with `blob_steps` inflating it toward the ~1 MB size of a real long-running flow so the per-tick parse-count guard measures the operation the #209 fix collapses. <!--#687dd0c68490b778-->
- `_replay_real_frames` (function) — Helper that drives the reader through the captured tick sequence, growing the on-disk jsonl files to each frame's cursor and returning the per-tick FlowRead lists produced. <!--#9f360f95e17b879c-->
- `test_real_frame_sequence_matches_captured_daemon_frames` (function) — Test that replaying the real on-disk records of the #209 flow through `DaemonHistoryReader` reproduces the captured `daemon_frames.json` sequence tick-for-tick (mode, record count, cursor) across both trigger boundaries — the discovery→analyze transition and the `03_plan` step error — with analyze/plan records surfacing only as the final append delta. <!--#fcd3963cc5bfd26d-->
- `test_real_frame_replay_no_loss_no_dup_no_truncation` (function) — Strongest no-loss/no-duplication/no-truncation/correct-order test: gathers every record delivered across all replay ticks and asserts it equals, item-for-item and in order, the concatenated on-disk fixture lines (discovery 8 + analyze 6 + plan 6 = 20). <!--#8e0b787072bf0e16-->
- `test_retry_after_error_same_jsonl_append_surfaces` (function) — Test of #209's second trigger — after `03_plan` ends in `step_failed`, an operator retry appends more records under the SAME step_id to the SAME jsonl — asserting those retry records stream as a fresh `HISTORY_MODE_APPEND` delta with the parse cache on, re-delivering none of the prior failure records and advancing the cursor to the new tail. <!--#4362be3145cbc7da-->
- `_count_engine_parses` (function) — Test helper that clears the disk-JSON cache and monkeypatches `disk_json_cache._parse_json` to count full parses of the active engine.json, isolating the exact GIL-bound seam the #209 fix collapses so tests can assert per-tick re-parses are eliminated. <!--#f650ce0ea068dc3e-->
- `test_real_frame_replay_parses_active_engine_json_once_per_change` (function) — The bite test: replays the real frames against a ~1 MB active `engine.json` while every per-tick reader (`active_flow_signature`, `build_index`, `read_active_flows`, `live_flow_ids`) touches the unchanged file, asserting `_parse_engine_json` runs at most once — locking in the memoization fix against the per-tick re-parse starvation that froze the WebUI. <!--#52ee0e8588ce065c-->
- `test_active_engine_json_reparsed_on_transition_and_retry` (function) — Test asserting the content-keyed parse cache serves repeats without re-parsing but re-parses when a genuine engine.json rewrite (transition/retry) changes the content, avoiding stale state. <!--#70d262a1d58807db-->

### `tests/test_issue243_disk_json_cache.py` (python) — Regression test suite for issue #243's disk-JSON read-path cache, verifying that unchanged engine.json files are fully parsed only once (keyed by path/mtime/size), reparse on change, and that over-guard oversized files are never fully parsed nor cached while head+tail scanning still yields hot keys, plus daemon aggregator scans of giant/new-format engine.json files avoid full parses. <!--#86d48f0b8f3e10ef|1eecf4bb0b8af53b-->
- `_clear_cache` (function) — Autouse pytest fixture that clears the disk-JSON cache before and after each test to isolate cache state. <!--#06929c6a0cd57978-->
- `_count_full_parses` (function) — Helper that monkeypatches the single `_parse_json_file` seam to count full-file JSON parses, returning a mutable counter dict. <!--#6459d0ca4d566bad-->
- `_write_engine` (function) — Helper that writes an `indent=2` engine.json with head hot keys (flow_id/status), an inflatable middle `state` blob, and tail keys (is_worktree_mode/worktree_branch), mimicking persistence's on-disk layout. <!--#55e2fe7c5eae3bd1-->
- `test_unchanged_file_parsed_once` (function) — Asserts an unchanged engine.json is fully parsed only once across ten reads, cached by (path, mtime, size). <!--#6cfe3caedc4ee5a2-->
- `test_reparse_on_change` (function) — Asserts rewriting the engine.json with different content/size invalidates the cache key and triggers exactly one reparse. <!--#c52e3e418f2c91e7-->
- `test_oversized_file_never_fully_parsed` (function) — Asserts an over-guard (>MAX_PARSE_BYTES) engine.json is never fully parsed yet still yields head and tail hot keys via head+tail scanning. <!--#44f70d26f2b54037-->
- `test_oversized_file_not_cached` (function) — Asserts `read_json_cached` refuses to store or return over-guard files, returning None as a memory guard. <!--#ad8d45935e5bdbfc-->
- `test_degraded_extraction_failure_warns_once` (function) — Asserts an over-guard file with no recognizable top-level flow_id degrades to None and logs a warning only once, not per read. <!--#a0b12a5ddab98a7d-->
- `_make_worktree_run` (function) — Test helper that builds a worktree-style run directory containing a tianluo engine.json (optionally padded to ~20MB via a giant size_key) for the given flow_id, returning the worktree path. <!--#fa49e3358f748656-->
- `test_worktree_scan_no_full_parse_on_giant_files` (function) — Asserts the daemon aggregator's active-worktree scan performs zero full parses on two giant legacy engine.json files while both runs remain observable. <!--#0f4d0fd56041d78e-->
- `test_snapshot_for_root_reads_new_format_header_only` (function) — Test verifying that DaemonAggregator._snapshot_for_root can derive flow_id, status, and total_steps from a new-format engine.json header alone, without reading the large cold step payloads. <!--#dc7d2bfa60cce0b2-->

### `tests/test_issue244_split_format.py` (python) — Regression test suite for issue #244's engine.json hot/cold split (Part B / G7 B4/B5), verifying that saving/loading round-trips equal with per-step inputs/outputs and shared context externalized to bounded cold files, that legacy inline formats still load, that persistence and lazy hydration touch only changed/requested cold files, that missing/corrupt/truncated cold data degrades gracefully, and that clear_state archives header plus cold partition together while handling archive-name collisions and preserving surviving resumable snapshots. <!--#ba5bb23558b349cf|dafbdf1fa62ecb3f-->
- `_make_flow` (function) — Test helper that builds a FlowInstance whose steps, context, and fix-iteration carry large blob payloads, simulating a realistic heavyweight flow for the split-format persistence tests. <!--#8e2204fdf4d67620-->
- `test_new_format_save_load_roundtrip_equal` (function) — Asserts save_flow writes the hot/cold engine.json header (per-step inputs/outputs and context externalized to cold_ref/context_ref) and that load_flow reconstructs an object equal to the original. <!--#4bf3e6af9ac21a8a-->
- `test_resumable_snapshot_roundtrip_equal` (function) — Checks that saving a non-completed (paused) flow also writes a resumable snapshot that round-trips equal via both load_resumable_snapshot and load_flow_by_id. <!--#54eaed83e44148fe-->
- `test_legacy_inline_engine_json_loads` (function) — Verifies a legacy fully-inline engine.json (no engine_format marker, no cold files) still loads verbatim into an equal FlowInstance. <!--#abfad20c2aa1240e-->
- `test_legacy_inline_resumable_snapshot_loads` (function) — Verifies load_resumable_snapshot correctly reads a legacy inline resumable/<flow_id>.json snapshot back to an equal flow. <!--#37f59899d5749f23-->
- `test_header_bounded_under_100kb` (function) — Confirms the engine.json header stays under 100KB even for a large 31-step × 700KB flow, proving payloads are externalized rather than inlined. <!--#0ac5906f0a040411-->
- `test_per_step_persistence_touches_only_changed_cold_file` (function) — Verifies that mutating one step's outputs and re-saving rewrites only that step's cold file, with the other steps' cold files and _context.json skipped by the sha1 change guard. <!--#0037fde7592aace1-->
- `test_missing_cold_step_file_degrades_gracefully` (function) — Checks that a deleted or corrupted cold step file degrades that step's inputs/outputs to empty dicts while surviving steps load intact, without crashing. <!--#3ccda229c6759390-->
- `test_missing_cold_context_degrades_gracefully` (function) — Checks that a missing cold _context.json degrades the shared context to an empty dict instead of raising. <!--#4203446aca6ab88c-->
- `test_resume_partial_flow_reloads_full_fidelity` (function) — Verifies a mid-flow PAUSED flow reloads via a fresh manager with current-step position and full fidelity, and that re-saving keeps the hot/cold format (never re-inlines). <!--#b08296edeff0dc55-->
- `test_load_flow_by_id_defers_step_cold_files` (function) — Tests the B4 lazy-load: load_flow_by_id reads only the shared context cold file up front and faults in each step's cold body exactly once, on demand, when fetched by id. <!--#43b510e60ec9a4c0-->
- `test_hydrate_step_loads_only_requested_cold_file` (function) — Verifies hydrate_step lazily materializes only the requested step's cold file from a header-only flow (from_header_dict) while leaving others empty, and is an idempotent no-op that never clobbers already-loaded data. <!--#2fdbc584586981d8-->
- `test_clear_state_archives_header_and_cold_files` (function) — Asserts clear_state moves the header and its cold step/context files into a single timestamped archive entry preserving format and identity, leaving no live cold dir behind. <!--#0e20aa9270dbe5c4-->
- `test_clear_state_same_second_archives_do_not_collide` (function) — Uses a frozen second-granular timestamp to verify two flows archived within the same second get uniquely-named headers and cold partitions, so both remain listed and recoverable. <!--#8381e99510137090-->
- `test_load_resumable_snapshot_defers_step_cold_files` (function) — Tests that load_resumable_snapshot lazily reads only the shared context up front and faults in each paused-flow step's cold body exactly once on first fetch. <!--#3d40a32e5a26d89e-->
- `test_list_resumable_snapshots_defers_step_cold_files` (function) — Verifies enumerating multiple paused/failed resumable snapshots consults only header (and possibly context) data, never reading any per-step cold body up front. <!--#db6fb9a9e57990f2-->
- `test_clear_state_archive_collision_stays_reference_consistent` (function) — Verifies that when archive/steps/<flow_id> already exists, this flow's cold files move to a suffixed partition recorded in the header so full-fidelity reload reads the correct payloads and the sibling archive is untouched. <!--#4edcc4fc75684e5b-->
- `test_clear_state_archive_double_collision_does_not_abort` (function) — Verifies clear_state probes past both an occupied primary and first timestamp-suffixed partition to a numeric-suffixed name rather than copytree-ing onto them and aborting, keeping both pre-existing archives intact and the reload reference-consistent. <!--#912f1b91ff23c6ea-->
- `test_list_all_flows_mixed_formats` (function) — Confirms list_all_flows enumerates both a new hot/cold archived flow and a legacy inline archive snapshot dropped alongside it. <!--#4c283f3dd0c951a1-->
- `test_export_context_and_progress_on_new_format` (function) — Checks that export_context_from_flow and export_progress_markdown work on a loaded new-format flow, producing non-empty structured context and a progress markdown containing the flow id and steps section. <!--#287d4abc59e3159f-->
- `test_export_context_hydrates_lazy_loaded_flow` (function) — Regression test (fix iteration 6) ensuring export_context_from_flow first hydrates cold bodies of a lazily-loaded flow so real step inputs/outputs reach the exported context instead of empty payloads from un-hydrated _LazyStepDict iteration. <!--#db66aa2f9c8d7274-->
- `test_clear_state_preserves_surviving_resumable_snapshot_fidelity` (function) — Verifies clear_state on a non-completed flow copies (not moves) the cold partition into the archive, so the still-advertised resumable snapshot resumes at full fidelity while the archive holds a complete copy. <!--#6c4d6fdf8b166be0-->
- `test_load_flow_tolerant_recovers_truncated_hotcold_header` (function) — Verifies load_flow_tolerant salvages a crash-truncated hot/cold header (leading engine_format marker survives) by repairing the JSON and resolving intact cold step/context files instead of degrading to empty payloads or returning None. <!--#0e370ccc04faf351-->

### `tests/test_issue_209_push_starvation.py` (python) — Regression-lock test module for issue #209 (daemon push-loop starvation): it proves DaemonHistoryReader parses the large active engine.json at most once per actual change via a stat-keyed cache, while verifying discovery→analyze and retry live-append deltas still stream incrementally. <!--#4f9954f5a5bdc84f|b7392309b695ff4e-->
- `_write_engine` (function) — Test helper that writes a synthetic tianluo/state/engine.json for a flow with a given status, optionally padding it with many RUNNING step blobs to mimic the ~1 MB active engine.json whose repeated parse #209 traced as the per-tick CPU sink. <!--#ae12a1f5de663c17-->
- `_write_jsonl` (function) — Test helper that writes a per-step history jsonl file containing n simple assistant-message records. <!--#bb20aacf8e3df4bc-->
- `_count_engine_parses` (function) — Test helper that monkeypatches `disk_json_cache._parse_json` to count full engine.json parses (the GIL-bound `json.loads` seam the #209 fix collapses), returning a mutable counter after clearing the module cache so the test can assert parses happen once per actual change rather than once per reader-call per push tick. <!--#bcc5c8ff141c8d88-->
- `test_active_engine_json_parsed_once_per_change_across_readers` (function) — Drives every per-tick reader (active_flow_signature, build_index, read_active_flows/_is_still_active, live_flow_ids) over 10 unchanged ticks and asserts the large active engine.json is parsed at most once, locking in the stat-keyed cache that collapses the pre-fix per-reader-per-tick re-parse starvation. <!--#0206df1a0f8172cd-->
- `test_active_engine_json_reparsed_after_change` (function) — Verifies the stat-keyed engine.json parse cache is not stale-serving: an unchanged read reuses the cached parse while a genuine rewrite (step transition / retry, changing content and size) triggers exactly one fresh parse. <!--#e081717947f6693c-->
- `test_discovery_to_analyze_transition_surfaces_via_read_active_flows` (function) — Correctness guard proving that with the engine.json parse cache enabled the discovery→analyze append still streams incrementally, delivering the 4 new analyze records as an HISTORY_MODE_APPEND delta rather than being suppressed. <!--#ead222560773f80a-->
- `test_retry_after_error_append_surfaces_via_read_active_flows` (function) — Correctness guard for #209's retry trigger, asserting that appended retry records under the same step_id and same jsonl still surface incrementally via read_active_flows with the engine.json parse cache on. <!--#37201ae3f5b8e9b4-->

### `tests/test_issue_cmd.py` (python) — Unit/CLI tests for the `issue` command, covering issue creation across all input modes (positional, piped stdin, interactive TTY, and `--editor` YAML), the `edit` command, and the supporting helpers for description resolution, editor invocation, and YAML template parsing/validation. <!--#6ff636294d206cee|844c2d6e33ba7b65-->
- `project_dir` (function) — Fixture yielding a temp directory marked with a `.git` folder to act as a project root. <!--#de7aeab2179db4d4-->

- `_run_cmd` (function) — Test helper that invokes the CLI app with the given args while patching issue_cmd.get_project_root to a test project directory. <!--#3190f0f7b4aadb14-->

### `tests/test_issue_manager.py` (python) — Unit tests for SE3's YAML-based IssueManager and its Issue dataclass, covering serialization round-trips, legacy/retired-field handling, display-title derivation, slug generation, and create/load behavior (ID assignment, directory creation, open/closed lookup). <!--#77913ff24e33e32c|4c2c2200a7cf8d3a-->

  - `TestIssueModel.test_from_dict_missing_description_degrades` (method) — Confirms YAML lacking a description loads with description="" and derives display_title from the title. <!--#901c5337ac8b6338-->

### `tests/test_issue_renumber_helper.py` (python) — Unit tests for the shared issue_renumber merge primitives — token-precise `#NNN` reference rewriting (single/bulk/added-lines/masking), `.next_id` counter advancement to max ID, issue-ID ownership resolution, and renumber-trace/ambiguity-note formatting — that both luo merge channels reuse to renumber colliding issues. <!--#9cfcf6921122ad56|3242e8a90e5b9bf2-->
- `_write_issue` (function) — Test helper that writes a minimal issue YAML with an explicit ID into the manager's open/ or closed/ directory and returns its path. <!--#bb5e01423c8462ed-->
- `_read_next_id` (function) — Test helper that reads and parses the integer value from an issue project's tianluo/issues/.next_id counter file. <!--#e270e4ee988ed9d7-->
- `test_rewrite_leaves_non_reference_hashnumbers_untouched` (function) — Asserts reference rewriting is token-precise, changing a standalone `#123` while leaving superstrings like `#1234` and leading-alnum tokens like `abc#123` untouched. <!--#1528cb022d95d2e7-->
- `test_rewrite_leaves_trailing_alnum_tokens_untouched` (function) — Asserts rewrite_issue_references treats `#123abc` as prose and rewrites only the standalone `#123` token. <!--#797fb7c055b94094-->
- `test_rewrite_treats_zero_padding_as_equivalent` (function) — Asserts zero-padding variants (`#14`, `#014`, `#0014`) all denote the same issue and are all rewritten to the new ID. <!--#4d8e4147365745d6-->
- `test_rewrite_counts_across_open_and_closed` (function) — Asserts a rewrite spans both open/ and closed/ issues and returns the total number of references replaced. <!--#d1e051cc68657f99-->
- `test_rewrite_confined_to_issues_dir` (function) — Verifies rewrite_issue_references only touches files under tianluo/issues/ and leaves stray #-references elsewhere (e.g. tianluo/logs) untouched. <!--#ba530f8fa16b70a1-->
- `test_rewrite_new_id_is_zero_padded` (function) — Asserts the replacement reference token is zero-padded to at least three digits (e.g. `#7` becomes `#007`). <!--#14a16b30094067df-->
- `test_bulk_rewrite_does_not_chain_through_overlapping_pairs` (function) — Verifies rewrite_issue_references_bulk resolves each token against the original text so overlapping pairs (005→010, 010→011) don't chain. <!--#43839b01665610c9-->
- `test_bulk_rewrite_ignores_identity_pairs_and_scopes` (function) — Checks bulk rewrite skips identity pairs (007→007) and only touches files within the given scope_files. <!--#a5fd4b46f90e44e2-->
- `test_mask_replaces_only_standalone_reference_tokens` (function) — Confirms mask_issue_references replaces standalone `#NNN` tokens with `#REF` while leaving leading-alnum forms like `abc#123` intact. <!--#44cbb9ef8c5d416c-->
- `test_mask_makes_rewritten_reference_sign_equal` (function) — Asserts masking renders two bodies differing only in reference numbers identically, so pre/post-renumber texts compare equal. <!--#da743f71ba56ffb6-->
- `test_advance_from_missing_counter` (function) — Verifies advance_next_id_to_max creates a missing .next_id file set to the highest existing issue ID plus one. <!--#b68982019c0c3c48-->
- `test_advance_from_lagging_counter` (function) — Verifies advance_next_id_to_max pushes a stale counter that lags behind the true max issue ID forward to max+1. <!--#ae7abf7697f8ae03-->
- `test_advance_from_garbage_counter` (function) — Verifies advance_next_id_to_max discards a non-numeric/corrupt counter value and recomputes it from the on-disk issue files. <!--#b66b3b5bc02c703c-->
- `test_advance_with_no_issues` (function) — Asserts that with an empty issue store the counter initializes to 1 (max of 0, plus 1). <!--#e44420b4a93c07a4-->
- `test_advance_counts_parsed_id_not_just_filename` (function) — Verifies advance_next_id_to_max counts a parsed `id` field that exceeds its filename prefix, advancing the counter past it. <!--#cca9dde48b61c8ec-->
- `test_find_issue_id_owner_prefers_parsed_id_over_filename` (function) — Checks find_issue_id_owner / resolve_issue_numeric_id resolve ownership by the parsed `id`, not the filename prefix. <!--#dbc76a8b55615a5c-->
- `test_find_issue_id_owner_excludes_given_files` (function) — Verifies find_issue_id_owner honors exclude_files and falls back to filename prefix when a body lacks a parseable id. <!--#75eb80c27a28b379-->
- `test_advance_never_lowers_ahead_counter` (function) — Verifies advance_next_id_to_max is monotonic and leaves a counter that is ahead of the scanned max untouched (it may be a peer allocator's live reservation). <!--#2a7e8770a92cf2ad-->
- `test_added_lines_rewrite_only_touches_new_lines` (function) — Confirms rewrite_references_in_added_lines renumbers references only on merge-added lines, leaving baseline references intact. <!--#28bbb2b52bc959be-->
- `test_added_lines_rewrite_is_token_precise` (function) — Checks added-line rewriting respects `#NNN` token boundaries, ignoring `#1234` and `abc#123` while rewriting standalone `#123`. <!--#d925aa5155377a58-->
- `test_added_lines_rewrite_no_hits_leaves_file_untouched` (function) — Verifies a file whose added lines carry no matching reference returns zero hits and is left byte-identical. <!--#b6afcbb9910e8355-->
- `test_added_lines_rewrite_survives_yaml_quote_style_shift` (function) — Ensures added-line detection compares parsed YAML logical lines, so appending a description line doesn't misclassify a shifted quote-boundary line as added. <!--#38be5c4783cd8b0a-->
- `test_added_duplicate_of_existing_line_still_follows_renumber` (function) — Verifies baseline membership is counted per occurrence so an appended duplicate of an existing YAML line still follows the renumber. <!--#1f862887578f73b3-->
- `test_added_duplicate_line_raw_fallback_still_follows_renumber` (function) — Checks the non-YAML physical-line fallback path also counts baseline lines per occurrence for duplicate added lines. <!--#198110940a910233-->
- `test_trace_contains_old_and_new_ids` (function) — Asserts the formatted renumber trace string contains both the old and new issue IDs. <!--#9fac3d3751279c32-->
- `test_trace_normalizes_and_zero_pads` (function) — Verifies format_renumber_trace zero-pads both old and new IDs to three digits regardless of input padding or type. <!--#9d46ec4b43692612-->
- `test_trace_appended_preserves_display_title` (function) — Asserts appending the renumber trace at the tail of a description leaves the issue's display_title (first non-empty line) derivation intact. <!--#29877799ca9b6224-->
- `test_ambiguous_note_lists_all_candidates_zero_padded` (function) — Verifies format_ambiguous_reference_note zero-pads the ambiguous reference and all candidate IDs when listing merge-conflict candidates. <!--#7a99eaed5a2b3c58-->
- `test_strip_removes_traces_and_ambiguity_notes` (function) — Verifies strip_renumber_traces removes both renumber-trace and ambiguity audit lines while preserving live text verbatim. <!--#ab86f083289582bf-->
- `test_count_reference_tokens_is_token_precise` (function) — Checks count_reference_tokens counts standalone tokens precisely, absorbing zero-padding and ignoring superstring/leading-alnum prose forms. <!--#ecf1d3e8dc466a2e-->
- `test_live_reference_count_ignores_audit_lines` (function) — Verifies live_reference_count counts genuine references but ignores historical `#NNN` mentions inside audit/trace lines. <!--#ed5c53030ea2a3ed-->
- `test_append_description_note_preserves_title_and_parses` (function) — Confirms append_description_note appends a note while preserving the issue title and keeping the YAML parseable. <!--#28a0f5c90681ff12-->
- `test_added_lines_dry_run_counts_without_writing` (function) — Asserts rewrite_references_in_added_lines dry_run reports would-be hits while leaving the file byte-identical. <!--#b7cc4c41c1f1ddbd-->

### `tests/test_json_parser.py` (python) — Unit and integration tests for tianluo.engine.utils.json_parser, exercising unescaped-quote repair, JSON extraction/parsing, the shared repair chain, and the dict-only/lenient JSON detectors for consistency with parse_json_response. <!--#1fbbf16f94b018c5|392b6f8fa4fd9043-->
- `TestRepairUnescapedQuotes` (class) — Test class for _repair_unescaped_quotes, verifying it fixes unescaped interior double quotes in JSON string values while leaving valid/escaped input untouched. <!--#d40a15a363dcf61b-->

  - `TestRepairUnescapedQuotes.test_bug_report_json` (method) — Asserts repair handles the exact multi-field JSON pattern from the originating bug report. <!--#c911b6885cdc2b7d-->

  - `TestExtractAndParseJsonWithQuoteRepair.test_markdown_block_with_unescaped_quotes` (method) — Asserts JSON inside a markdown ```json fence with unescaped quotes is extracted and parsed. <!--#7d0232530e1b7d92-->
  - `TestExtractAndParseJsonWithQuoteRepair.test_raw_json_with_unescaped_quotes` (method) — Asserts raw (unfenced) JSON with unescaped interior quotes is extracted and parsed. <!--#c1589a339f0bc5b1-->
  - `TestExtractAndParseJsonWithQuoteRepair.test_valid_json_passes_through` (method) — Asserts already-valid JSON is extracted and parsed to the exact expected dict. <!--#1da98f7c8853d69e-->
  - `TestExtractAndParseJsonWithQuoteRepair.test_bug_report_full_json` (method) — Asserts a large, realistic bug-report JSON with mixed escapes and Chinese text is parsed correctly. <!--#a5f45c48b73ab352-->
  - `TestExtractAndParseJsonWithQuoteRepair.test_trailing_json_with_escaped_quotes` (method) — Asserts the backward boundary walker selects the trailing JSON object even when it contains escaped quotes. <!--#db097c853bade56f-->

### `tests/test_language_config.py` (python) — Test suite for SE3's language configuration layer, covering LanguageConfig.load()'s parsing of the tianluo.yaml language section (present, missing, null, malformed) and its per-field project-over-global merge with ~/.se3/config.yaml, plus get_language_instruction()/get_step_language_instruction() behavior determining which pipeline steps receive general-language, spec-language, or no language injection. <!--#76b655a3925ab95d|f6e54c093c882331-->

### `tests/test_llm_caller.py` (python) — Unit tests for `LLMCaller`, covering the two-phase JSON call path (`required_keys` fast-path vs. Phase 2 fallback and per-phase usage records), `_create_runner` forwarding `project_root` so `claude_subprocess.setting_sources` from `tianluo.yaml` takes effect, invocation-intent handling on legacy runners, and — via an args-capturing fake runner — the `--disallowedTools` write-tool lock applied to read-only step types (`code_index`, `migrate`, `analyze`) but not writable ones. <!--#ad68f9c936406cc3|9ad1cfb7c5846aa9-->
- `_make_caller` (function) — Test helper that builds an LLMCaller pre-populated with sensible default kwargs (overridable) for use across the test cases. <!--#53c2c9b618dac53f-->
- `TestCallTwoPhaseRequiredKeys` (class) — Test class covering `LLMCaller._call_two_phase`'s `required_keys` gate — verifying that Phase 1 JSON containing (or, with `required_keys=None`, simply being valid) the required keys short-circuits Phase 2, that missing keys trigger a second extraction sequence on the same caller rather than a fresh `JSONExtractor` caller, and that each phase is billed as its own usage record. <!--#65f57e9ee3b36836-->
  - `TestCallTwoPhaseRequiredKeys.test_fast_path_with_matching_required_keys` (method) — Asserts that when Phase 1 JSON already contains the required keys, Phase 2 is skipped (only one _call_with_retry). <!--#f0e671f6aedbb0c0-->
  - `TestCallTwoPhaseRequiredKeys.test_fast_path_missing_required_keys_falls_back_to_phase2` (method) — Asserts that valid-but-incomplete Phase 1 JSON triggers a second extraction pass on the same caller's _call_with_retry (two calls), not a separate JSONExtractor LLMCaller. <!--#1d189b9b064ab2f9-->
  - `TestCallTwoPhaseRequiredKeys.test_fast_path_with_none_required_keys` (method) — Asserts backward-compatible behavior: with required_keys=None any valid JSON satisfies the fast path and Phase 2 is skipped. <!--#f13d8be437160bd6-->
  - `TestCallTwoPhaseRequiredKeys.test_phase1_and_json_phase2_are_distinct_usage_calls` (method) — Drives a fake two-phase runner end-to-end through `caller.call(json_mode="two_phase")` and asserts the generation and JSON-extraction phases produce two separate usage records with distinct `usage_event_ids` and correctly summed input/output tokens. <!--#ec4ee2c373965707-->
- `TestCallPassesRequiredKeys` (class) — Test class verifying call() forwards required_keys into _call_two_phase. <!--#821b322efa876976-->
  - `TestCallPassesRequiredKeys.test_call_passes_required_keys_to_two_phase` (method) — Asserts call() with json_mode='two_phase' passes the required_keys argument through to _call_two_phase. <!--#f891263d91df07f0-->
- `TestCreateRunnerForwardsProjectRoot` (class) — Regression test class verifying that LLMCaller._create_runner forwards project_root to ClaudeCodeRunner so that claude_subprocess.setting_sources from the project's tianluo.yaml actually reaches the subprocess instead of silently falling back to the default ['user']. <!--#b6ff2bd0adc12b70-->
  - `TestCreateRunnerForwardsProjectRoot.test_project_root_forwarded_so_yaml_setting_sources_takes_effect` (method) — Asserts that when tianluo.yaml declares setting_sources: [user, project], the current runner's setting_sources reflects that configured value. <!--#e26a8892780da968-->
  - `TestCreateRunnerForwardsProjectRoot.test_default_setting_sources_when_no_yaml` (method) — Asserts that with no project tianluo.yaml present, the current runner's setting_sources falls back to the built-in default ['user']. <!--#9445d96b586331ad-->
- `_FakeResult` (class) — Minimal fake runner-result object (success/output/interrupted) stand-in used by _call_with_retry in tests. <!--#e5bad293c6e3a5e1-->
  - `_FakeResult.__init__` (method) — Initializes the fake result with success=True, given output, and interrupted=False. <!--#58240185257cf568-->
- `_ArgsCapturingRunner` (class) — Test double runner that mirrors `ClaudeCodeRunner`'s CLI-arg construction and records the args handed to `run_with_monitor`, so tests can assert on the flags `LLMCaller` ultimately produces. <!--#414d79c8169e4bb2-->
  - `_ArgsCapturingRunner.__init__` (method) — Initializes the capturing runner with captured_args set to None. <!--#dda13561f9da658c-->
  - `_ArgsCapturingRunner.build_call_args` (method) — Replicates the real runner's arg building — stream-json output flags, the prompt, a single `--disallowedTools` list (write tools only when `read_only`, always `ReportFindings`), and `--file` entries for existing context files. <!--#36bc45f60524c94b-->
  - `_ArgsCapturingRunner.run_with_monitor` (method) — Records the passed args and returns an empty _FakeResult. <!--#03ab16e216fcd671-->
- `test_direct_intent_keeps_legacy_runner_on_plain_autonomous_prompt` (function) — Asserts that a runner predating the invocation-intent protocol still receives the raw prompt unprefixed by `/goal` when called with `AgentInvocationIntent.DIRECT_IMPLEMENTATION`. <!--#09ff207e625f0f05-->
- `_disallowed_values` (function) — Helper that asserts exactly one `--disallowedTools` flag is present and extracts the tool names it carries, stopping at the next `--`-prefixed flag. <!--#8153ec62287afd7e-->
- `TestReadOnlyToolDisallowList` (class) — Tests that read-only step types (`code_index`, `migrate`, `analyze`) get write tools added to `--disallowedTools` while writable steps (`implement`, `update_spec`, unregistered types) carry only the unconditional `ReportFindings` denial. <!--#3b77bbf07507e5c2-->
  - `TestReadOnlyToolDisallowList._run_and_capture_args` (method) — Helper that runs call() for a given step_type through a capturing runner and returns the recorded CLI args. <!--#219cd50f7078a1e8-->
  - `TestReadOnlyToolDisallowList.test_code_index_args_contain_disallowed_write_tools` (method) — Asserts the code_index step's args include --disallowedTools with all four write tools, since it is a pure-data sub-agent. <!--#b99feb5aeb687284-->
  - `TestReadOnlyToolDisallowList.test_migrate_args_contain_disallowed_write_tools` (method) — Asserts the migrate step is treated as read-only and its args disallow Write and Edit. <!--#a54152a15bde806b-->
  - `TestReadOnlyToolDisallowList.test_read_tools_not_disallowed` (method) — Asserts that read tools (`Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `Bash`) stay available even on a read-only step. <!--#0b3f72ce5b2dc360-->
  - `TestReadOnlyToolDisallowList._assert_writable` (method) — Shared assertion that a writable step's args contain exactly one `--disallowedTools` flag listing only `ReportFindings` and none of the write tools. <!--#751d71fa32693de0-->
  - `TestReadOnlyToolDisallowList.test_unknown_step_args_have_no_write_tool_lock` (method) — Verifies an unregistered step type is treated as writable and receives no write-tool lock. <!--#9b9530855a2b4700-->
  - `TestReadOnlyToolDisallowList.test_implement_args_have_no_write_tool_lock` (method) — Verifies the `implement` step keeps its write tools available. <!--#984193841c3bc6a6-->
  - `TestReadOnlyToolDisallowList.test_update_spec_args_have_no_write_tool_lock` (method) — Verifies the `update_spec` step keeps its write tools available. <!--#0fd5128bb019d737-->
  - `TestReadOnlyToolDisallowList.test_analyze_read_only_step_has_disallowed_tools` (method) — Asserts STEP_POOL read-only steps like analyze also receive --disallowedTools enforcement. <!--#5472ec36bba480a2-->
- `TestForceReadOnlyOverride` (class) — Tests the call-level `force_read_only=True` override, checking both enforcement points (runner `--disallowedTools` lock and the prompt's READ-ONLY STEP CONSTRAINT block) fire on the otherwise-writable `charter_freshness` step without changing `is_step_read_only`. <!--#38943c26bfed5257-->
  - `TestForceReadOnlyOverride._run_and_capture_args` (method) — Helper that runs a caller for a given step/force flag through an args-capturing stub runner and returns the runner CLI args, with prompt/response recording patched out. <!--#400dfaa211a39bc5-->
  - `TestForceReadOnlyOverride.test_baseline_charter_freshness_is_writable` (method) — Baseline check that `charter_freshness` is registry-writable and, without the override, gets no write-tool lock. <!--#dd0f18b0078b38ed-->
  - `TestForceReadOnlyOverride.test_force_read_only_adds_runner_disallowed_tools` (method) — Asserts enforcement point 1: force_read_only=True passes read_only through to the runner so Write/Edit/NotebookEdit appear under `--disallowedTools` despite the step being writable. <!--#11837a3b905b2a43-->
  - `TestForceReadOnlyOverride.test_force_read_only_injects_prompt_constraint` (method) — Asserts enforcement point 2: force_read_only=True injects the READ-ONLY STEP CONSTRAINT block into the retry-call prompt. <!--#1e6bc6910662567a-->
  - `TestForceReadOnlyOverride.test_default_no_force_no_prompt_constraint` (method) — Asserts the default force_read_only=False leaves a writable step's prompt free of the READ-ONLY STEP CONSTRAINT block, matching pre-override behavior. <!--#ba119edf9d115fb9-->
- `_streaming_side_effect` (function) — Test helper that builds a `run_with_monitor` side-effect function which records the argv of each call and replays a queue of canned NDJSON outputs line-by-line through the `on_output` callback, returning a successful result namespace. <!--#8892a16bbd9b777b-->
- `TestDirectIntentPlainExecution` (class) — Test class asserting that `AgentInvocationIntent.DIRECT_IMPLEMENTATION` now issues a single plain print-mode call with the same argv as `DEFAULT`, with the retired `/goal` prefix absent. <!--#fc1c889a7261a4fc-->
  - `TestDirectIntentPlainExecution.test_direct_intent_runs_single_plain_call` (method) — Verifies that a `DIRECT_IMPLEMENTATION` call through `LLMCaller.call` triggers exactly one subprocess whose `-p` prompt starts with the raw instruction and carries no `/goal` prefix. <!--#c8afce15f57bab70-->
- `TestDirectCallerRotation` (class) — Test class covering agent rotation under the DIRECT_IMPLEMENTATION intent — the successor inherits the failed caller's partial workspace plus retry context, and failed attempts and rotations share one authoritative token-usage ledger. <!--#ad4503f95dacdc78-->
  - `TestDirectCallerRotation.test_successor_continues_partial_workspace_with_retry_context` (method) — Drives a failing first runner and a succeeding second runner to verify rotation preserves the partial workspace, forwards retry context and the DIRECT_IMPLEMENTATION intent, and injects no /goal command into either prompt. <!--#bb04afcf634d145d-->
  - `TestDirectCallerRotation.test_failed_attempt_and_rotation_share_authoritative_usage_ledger` (method) — Parametrized test asserting that both the usage-limit failure and the successful rotation emit distinct usage records with correct `usage_status`, agent/provider/model resolution and source, and that `_record_response` is called once per attempt with matching `call_id`s. <!--#7db84e65c20c9c8f-->
  - `TestDirectCallerRotation.test_runner_exception_still_records_unavailable_attempt` (method) — Verifies that a runner raising mid-spawn surfaces as `LLMCallError` while still emitting one `UNAVAILABLE` usage record whose provider/model come from `get_startup_metadata` (`resolved_model_source == "runner_startup"`). <!--#f784ce800494b945-->

### `tests/test_llm_caller_stream_progress_chip.py` (python) — Pytest module verifying StreamJSONTracker's single-chip stream_progress protocol, asserting each tool call emits an in-flight and a terminal chip with correct structured tool_detail payloads (read_text, edit_diff with hunk lines, bash_output, is_error flags), preserves emoji-prefixed CLI stdout, keeps narrative-text jsonl records byte-identical to the legacy schema, and round-trips the new chip fields (tool_use_id, is_error, tool_detail) into the jsonl record. <!--#300097aa115739c0|221fa544b849b6f5-->
- `_make_tracker` (function) — Test helper that monkeypatches chat_history.record_stream_progress to capture every call and returns a fresh StreamJSONTracker alongside the captured-records list. <!--#ecadaf395ed240c7-->
- `_tool_records` (function) — Test helper that filters captured records down to only those carrying a tool_use_id, dropping narrative text progress entries. <!--#858f4e18f023e307-->
- `test_read_success_emits_in_flight_and_terminal` (function) — Verifies that a successful `Read` tool call produces exactly two progress-chip records — an in-flight one (`is_error` None, `tool_detail.kind == "tool_input"`, plain `[Read` header) followed by a terminal success one (`[Read ✓` header, `read_text` detail with `file_path`, `start_line` computed as offset+1, and the file text). <!--#21de05ec4c19b19c-->
- `test_edit_success_terminal_has_edit_diff_detail_with_hunk_start` (function) — Verifies that a successful `Edit` tool call emits an in-flight `[Edit` chip with a `tool_input` detail and then a terminal `[Edit ✓` chip whose `edit_diff` detail carries the `file_path`, a diff containing an `@@` hunk header, and `old_start_line`/`new_start_line` parsed from it. <!--#0872a62d7bc75b2f-->
- `test_bash_failure_emits_terminal_with_is_error_true` (function) — Verifies that a failing `Bash` tool call still emits the in-flight `[Bash` chip and then a terminal chip marked `is_error` True with a `[Bash ✗` header and a `bash_output` detail echoing the executed `command`. <!--#84c212899594a314-->
- `test_cli_stdout_emoji_lines_preserved` (function) — Test verifying the tracker prints emoji-prefixed CLI stdout lines ('🔧 Read:' on start and '✅ Read' on completion) to stdout. <!--#128ea4fd4ce8fdba-->
- `test_narrative_text_progress_jsonl_byte_identical_to_legacy` (function) — Verifies that a narrative-text progress write (no chip fields) via chat_history.record_stream_progress produces a jsonl record whose key set exactly matches the pre-extension schema, ensuring no extra keys leak. <!--#7af6d41dc761ea7a-->
- `test_record_stream_progress_writes_new_chip_fields_when_provided` (function) — Verifies that when the new chip fields (tool_use_id, is_error, tool_detail) are passed to record_stream_progress they round-trip intact into the jsonl record for the daemon reader to forward to the frontend. <!--#19a058a8b3905972-->

### `tests/test_llm_reviewer.py` (python) — Unit tests for the confirmation step's LLM-based reviewer, covering the approve (COMPLETED), revise (REVISION_NEEDED), and max-iterations/error-handling auto-approve paths, the review_result/revision_feedback outputs, config propagation of reviewer/agents/max_iterations into the confirm step, and the build_llm_review_prompt assembly. <!--#8b755033f15aa829|6816bb96b2e89115-->
- `TestLLMReviewApproval` (class) — Test class verifying that when the mocked LLMCaller approves a step, confirm_handler returns COMPLETED and populates review_result/revision_feedback outputs correctly. <!--#65b55a853e09838d-->

  - `TestLLMReviewApproval.test_approval_sets_revision_feedback` (method) — Asserts the revision_feedback output is set to the LLM's feedback text even when the step is approved. <!--#5f4971552358f441-->
- `TestLLMReviewRevision` (class) — Test class verifying that when the mocked LLM does not approve, confirm_handler returns REVISION_NEEDED and stores the rejection feedback. <!--#6cc909e386b2abb5-->
  - `TestLLMReviewRevision.setup_method` (method) — Builds a temp project, FlowInstance, a completed implement/design step, and a pending llm-reviewer confirm step for the revision tests. <!--#4fb194ce826b464d-->
  - `TestLLMReviewRevision.teardown_method` (method) — Removes the temporary project directory after each revision test. <!--#c34398a3746e8dbf-->
  - `TestLLMReviewRevision.test_revision_returns_revision_needed` (method) — Asserts confirm_handler returns StepStatus.REVISION_NEEDED when the mocked LLM response signals approved=False. <!--#63073e212a47f39a-->
  - `TestLLMReviewRevision.test_revision_stores_feedback` (method) — Asserts rejection feedback is stored in both review_result and revision_feedback outputs when the LLM declines approval. <!--#01f0a6df7a5566ed-->
- `TestLLMReviewMaxIterations` (class) — Test class verifying the max_iterations safeguard that auto-approves without calling the LLM once the persisted per-step review counter reaches the cap. <!--#5abb49ae705c8034-->
  - `TestLLMReviewMaxIterations.setup_method` (method) — Builds a temp project, FlowInstance, and a completed plan step for the max-iterations tests. <!--#91c057b3c1618872-->
  - `TestLLMReviewMaxIterations.teardown_method` (method) — Removes the temporary project directory after each max-iterations test. <!--#c34398a3746e8dbf-->
  - `TestLLMReviewMaxIterations.test_auto_approve_when_max_iterations_exceeded` (method) — Asserts that when flow.state.review_iterations meets max_iterations, confirm_handler auto-approves (COMPLETED) without invoking the LLM and notes the cap in feedback. <!--#d59a57e3d789b7c6-->
  - `TestLLMReviewMaxIterations.test_auto_approve_at_exact_limit` (method) — Edge-case test asserting auto-approval triggers when the persisted iteration count exactly equals max_iterations. <!--#85167488690508a8-->
- `TestLLMReviewErrorHandling` (class) — Test class covering confirm_handler's resilience to LLM failures and malformed responses (exceptions auto-approve; unparseable/missing-field JSON yields REVISION_NEEDED; fenced or text-wrapped JSON is extracted). <!--#7fb68d4afd25581d-->

  - `TestLLMReviewErrorHandling.test_llm_call_failure_auto_approves` (method) — Asserts that an LLMCaller exception causes confirm_handler to auto-approve (COMPLETED) with a 'LLM call failure' note to avoid blocking. <!--#c8ac2de1a029378c-->
  - `TestLLMReviewErrorHandling.test_malformed_json_response` (method) — Asserts a non-JSON LLM response is treated as not approved, returning REVISION_NEEDED. <!--#01ba340b3a6769b7-->

- `TestLLMReviewerConfigPropagation` (class) — Test class verifying that confirmation config (reviewer agent, agents list, max_iterations) propagates from tianluo.yaml into the CONFIRM step's inputs via StateMachine.transition_to_next. <!--#78bab7a36ba2b8d7-->
  - `TestLLMReviewerConfigPropagation.setup_method` (method) — Creates a temporary project root for the config-propagation tests. <!--#881089b2ffaae546-->

  - `TestLLMReviewerConfigPropagation.test_config_default_max_iterations` (method) — Asserts that with an empty step config, reviewer is None, max_iterations defaults to 3, and agents fall back to load_agents() defaults. <!--#e240f6f033807dfe-->
- `TestLLMReviewPrompt` (class) — Test class verifying build_llm_review_prompt embeds the step type/output, task description, revision feedback (only when present), JSON schema keys, and evaluation criteria. <!--#c12f382962e5d5ad-->

### `tests/test_llm_trace_fsync_batching.py` (python) — Unit tests covering two merge-subsystem concerns: that the LLMTrace writer batches/throttles fsync (firing on count/time thresholds, stop/exit, and rotation rather than per-record) while keeping the jsonl stream complete and readable, and that the leaf-merge guard rejects a missing target branch ref diagnosably before ever invoking git merge. <!--#915b4eb4757ee0ab|7e2a479aae727a88-->
- `fsync_counter` (function) — Pytest fixture that monkeypatches os.fsync in the llm_trace module with a no-op recorder so tests can count when fsync is invoked. <!--#2f60a6b8c6fdac6f-->
- `TestFsyncThrottling` (class) — Test class asserting LLMTrace fsyncs on count/interval thresholds, on stop/rotation, and per-record when disabled, rather than on every write. <!--#9297bb467922118d-->
  - `TestFsyncThrottling.test_no_fsync_under_thresholds` (method) — Asserts no fsync fires while records are written when both the count and time thresholds remain unmet. <!--#8b61fdce063fcfe3-->
  - `TestFsyncThrottling.test_fsync_fires_every_n_records` (method) — Asserts fsync fires exactly once per N records, with the batch counter resetting after each flush. <!--#d3743d17c52837f8-->
  - `TestFsyncThrottling.test_per_record_fsync_when_every_n_nonpositive` (method) — Asserts a non-positive fsync_every_n restores per-record fsync semantics. <!--#1caa0572e1f01e50-->
  - `TestFsyncThrottling.test_stop_forces_tail_fsync` (method) — Asserts stop/__exit__ fsyncs the tail even when the batch threshold was never reached, ensuring trailing records are durable. <!--#a7cdebb1b46dea89-->
  - `TestFsyncThrottling.test_rotation_forces_fsync` (method) — Asserts a file rotation fsyncs and completes the rotated-out file before opening the next one. <!--#bf371111c88e3a1d-->
- `TestRecordsRemainComplete` (class) — Test class verifying every record stays flushed, ordered, and readable even when fsync is throttled away until close. <!--#7d1bf62947363aa6-->
  - `TestRecordsRemainComplete.test_no_tail_loss_with_batched_fsync` (method) — Asserts all 50 records are written in sequence with the tail intact despite fsync being throttled to never fire mid-run. <!--#ee1914f3fb80b1cb-->
  - `TestRecordsRemainComplete.test_records_readable_mid_run_before_fsync` (method) — Asserts a record is readable from the file before any fsync occurs because each line is flushed to the OS page cache. <!--#bb6828f14f0646b6-->
- `_git` (function) — Helper that runs a git subcommand inside a given repo path and returns the completed process. <!--#9bef257c44286ed8-->
- `repo` (function) — Pytest fixture that initializes a fresh git repo with an initial commit on the main branch. <!--#d27143b094612b5a-->
- `TestLeafMergeRefValidation` (class) — Test class covering the ref-existence guard in `_attempt_merge_with_resolution` (tianluo.engine.steps.implement), asserting a missing leaf branch fails fast and diagnosably while an existing one merges cleanly. <!--#1ca6279ba0b60814-->
  - `TestLeafMergeRefValidation.test_missing_ref_fails_safely` (method) — Asserts that merging a non-existent leaf branch returns False before any merge starts, leaves no `.git/MERGE_HEAD` state, and logs a 'does not resolve to a commit' error instead of git's opaque message. <!--#b57278ddd40f7428-->
  - `TestLeafMergeRefValidation.test_existing_ref_proceeds_to_merge` (method) — Asserts that a real leaf branch adding a new file passes the ref guard, merges successfully (returns True), and lands its file on the target branch. <!--#291fcd6b8ab20583-->

### `tests/test_load_docs_config.py` (python) — Unit test module for tianluo.config's DocsConfig and load_docs_config, verifying from_dict parsing of the documentation: section (defaults, non-mapping/non-string rejection, non-None-only to_updater_config), worktree-aware tianluo.yaml loading with tianluo.local.yaml shadowing, and that loaded keys actually drive DocumentationUpdater output end-to-end. <!--#4a3899221bc26111|24af88009620a145-->
- `_write_yaml` (function) — Test helper that serializes a dict to YAML and writes it to the given path. <!--#9513281fbf5817c0-->

  - `TestDocsConfigFromDict.test_empty_dict_is_empty_config` (method) — Asserts an empty dict yields a config whose to_updater_config is empty. <!--#4c9585f1d9bdaddd-->
  - `TestDocsConfigFromDict.test_missing_documentation_section_is_empty` (method) — Asserts a dict lacking a documentation: section produces an empty updater config. <!--#d23af381ea5b2664-->
  - `TestDocsConfigFromDict.test_non_mapping_documentation_section_is_empty` (method) — Asserts a non-mapping documentation: value is ignored and yields an empty config. <!--#d90c59d3d404b3e9-->
  - `TestDocsConfigFromDict.test_keys_parsed` (method) — Asserts the three template keys are parsed onto the corresponding DocsConfig fields. <!--#8f342b8592ce2e1a-->
  - `TestDocsConfigFromDict.test_non_string_values_ignored` (method) — Asserts non-string template values (int, None, list) are ignored, leaving the config empty. <!--#da742ed6fe43619e-->
  - `TestDocsConfigFromDict.test_to_updater_config_only_non_none` (method) — Asserts to_updater_config emits only keys whose values are set (non-None). <!--#025195eb620cf9a8-->
- `TestLoadDocsConfig` (class) — Test class verifying load_docs_config's project-root resolution: a missing tianluo.yaml or one without a documentation: section yields an empty updater config, a documentation: section is loaded into DocsConfig, and tianluo.local.yaml shadows tianluo.yaml via the worktree-aware lookup. <!--#46309d22e3012b4d-->
  - `TestLoadDocsConfig.test_missing_yaml_returns_empty` (method) — Asserts a project root with no tianluo.yaml yields an empty config. <!--#a2b8b0bef14251f4-->
  - `TestLoadDocsConfig.test_yaml_without_documentation_section` (method) — Asserts that a tianluo.yaml lacking a documentation: section produces a DocsConfig whose to_updater_config() is empty. <!--#e71910a9a26dc81b-->
  - `TestLoadDocsConfig.test_yaml_with_documentation_section` (method) — Asserts that a documentation: section's readme_badge_template and versions_entry_template are loaded and surfaced by to_updater_config(). <!--#906cc2a50c51c47e-->
  - `TestLoadDocsConfig.test_local_yaml_shadows_yaml` (method) — Asserts that tianluo.local.yaml overrides tianluo.yaml, so the loaded readme_badge_template comes from the local file. <!--#43fce2b586f2d163-->
- `TestConfigForwardsToUpdater` (class) — Test class confirming that documentation: keys loaded by load_docs_config are forwarded through to_updater_config() into a live DocumentationUpdater. <!--#e9e591d2978361b5-->
  - `TestConfigForwardsToUpdater.test_documentation_keys_take_effect_in_updater` (method) — Asserts that a custom versions_entry_template from the documentation: section actually shapes the VERSIONS.md content written by DocumentationUpdater.update_versions_md. <!--#cebbfa5af1433ae8-->

  - `TestCleanupManagerDeleteMergedBranches.test_skips_dirty_worktree` (method) — Asserts a branch with a dirty worktree is skipped (skipped_dirty) and both branch and worktree survive. <!--#aac18d8ddc07acc5-->
