### `tests/test_merge_committed_issue_collision.py` (python) — Test suite for the git three-way-merge channel of `luo merge` issue-ID reconciliation, driving `MergeOrchestrator._reconcile_committed_issue_ids` after real merges to verify that when two branches commit different issue files parsing to the same numeric ID, the merge-introduced side is renumbered via the shared G1 primitives (rename, trace, reference rewrite, `.next_id` advance) and landed as a fix-up commit — while covering keeper selection among pre-fork/branch survivors, parsed-id-vs-filename detection, ambiguous multi-candidate references left annotated rather than guessed, byte-identical no-op merges, the LLM-conflict resolution path, non-mapping bodies, and surgical rollback that preserves unrelated drafts and never rewinds the monotonic counter. <!--#c6991d21abc9abfd|ca17b0a5d3e88e38-->
- `_git` (function) — Thin helper that runs a git subcommand inside a given repo path and returns the completed process, asserting success. <!--#cf40306ebf6a3046-->
- `_init_repo` (function) — Test helper that initializes a git repo tracking the tianluo/issues (and specs) store while gitignoring the rest of the tianluo/ runtime, then makes an initial commit. <!--#a8e012fc16e3b2ca-->
- `_head` (function) — Returns the current HEAD commit SHA of the given repo. <!--#3fcb38d33f4242ff-->
- `_parent` (function) — Returns the SHA of the first parent of the given ref. <!--#522753588e085378-->
- `_commits_since` (function) — Counts how many commits are reachable from HEAD but not from the given base ref. <!--#a9bc96d07fa3961e-->
- `_working_tree_clean` (function) — Reports whether the repo's tracked files have no uncommitted changes (ignoring untracked files). <!--#921f3d316e7e9a28-->
- `_write_issue_file` (function) — Test helper that writes a minimal valid issue YAML (id, description, status, timestamps) to tianluo/issues/<status>/<id>_<slug>.yaml and returns its path. <!--#89f14c10bd63778f-->
- `_set_next_id` (function) — Test helper that writes a value into the tianluo/issues/.next_id counter file. <!--#ff7196e7dec64963-->
- `_read_next_id` (function) — Test helper that reads and returns the integer value of the tianluo/issues/.next_id counter. <!--#e60bd036e8e78b0a-->
- `_open_issue_ids` (function) — Test helper that returns the sorted list of numeric IDs parsed from the filename prefixes of all open issue YAMLs. <!--#878539050feb42ff-->
- `_find_issue_by_slug` (function) — Test helper that locates and returns the first issue YAML file matching a given status directory and slug, or None. <!--#ec12f490d96cb03f-->
- `test_committed_id_collision_is_renumbered_and_committed` (function) — Test asserting that when two branches commit different issue #005 files, the merge keeps main's copy, renumbers the incoming one to global max+1 with an old→new trace and repointed self-reference, advances .next_id, and lands one fix-up commit recorded in the report. <!--#d8b5c35fb6d93222-->
- `test_references_added_to_preexisting_files_follow_the_renumber` (function) — Test asserting that a #old reference a branch adds to an already-existing issue file follows the renumber while the file's pre-existing #old stays, and that the new number is allocated via the shared .next_id primitive (honoring a counter running ahead of the on-disk max). <!--#3031e5452b6a09a4-->
- `_write_issue_file_with_id` (function) — Test helper that writes an issue YAML whose filename prefix and stored id field deliberately differ, returning its path. <!--#2765a38c206f89d4-->
- `test_collision_detected_by_parsed_id_not_filename_prefix` (function) — Test asserting that collisions are detected by the parsed id field rather than the filename prefix, so two files with differing prefixes but the same stored id are reconciled and one is renumbered. <!--#88861c3a1bbeba64-->
- `test_multiple_incoming_files_sharing_old_id_keep_ambiguous_references` (function) — Test asserting that when a merge brings in two different files both carrying #005, each is renumbered but its #005 tokens keep their digits as ambiguous, with a durable ambiguity note in each holder and entries in the merge report. <!--#f630a753ddd95bad-->
- `test_incoming_keeper_keeps_group_ambiguous` (function) — Test asserting that when the branch supplies two #005 files and main had none, the lexicographically-first branch file becomes the fallback keeper (retaining 005) while its peer is renumbered, and both #005 references stay ambiguous with the kept number on the candidate list. <!--#355d1cd2e4bc3651-->
- `test_preexisting_keeper_on_branch_keeps_references_ambiguous` (function) — Test asserting that when a keeper #005 predates the fork (so the branch inherits it) and the branch adds a second #005 plus a dependent reference, the single renumbered loser next to the pre-existing keeper keeps #005 references ambiguous rather than repointing them. <!--#f6a2487b0cd83c9b-->
- `test_ambiguous_incoming_reference_is_recorded_not_guessed` (function) — Test asserting that a merge-added #005 reference to a shared old ID with two colliding candidates keeps its digits and is annotated (note plus report entry) rather than guessed/repointed at either candidate. <!--#9a17bcb228a96faa-->
- `test_identical_issue_same_path_is_not_renumbered` (function) — Test asserting that when both branches commit a byte-identical issue #005 at the same path, git folds them into one file so reconciliation performs no renumber, no extra commit, and leaves the counter untouched. <!--#7d65de7f432159fa-->
- `test_llm_resolved_conflict_merge_still_reconciles_issue_ids` (function) — Test asserting that the LLM-resolved conflict commit path (_apply_resolution) runs the same committed-issue reconciliation as the clean-merge path, renumbering a duplicate ID even when the merge conflicted on an unrelated file. <!--#c6e14448ba983fb2-->
- `test_non_mapping_colliding_file_is_still_renumbered` (function) — Test asserting that a colliding file whose body is not a YAML mapping is still renamed to max+1 (body left byte-identical) to restore uniqueness, with the skipped in-file rewrite surfaced as a WARNING and a normal report record. <!--#32537cd5f870e2a8-->
- `test_keeper_chosen_among_preexisting_survivors` (function) — Test asserting that when multiple pre-merge survivors share an ID, the keeper is chosen among the current branch's copies rather than the incoming file, even when the incoming file's path sorts lexicographically first. <!--#1a7efbc8815478e9-->
- `test_reconcile_rollback_preserves_unrelated_uncommitted_issues` (function) — Test asserting that when the renumber fix-up commit fails, the rollback is surgical — undoing only this run's changes while preserving unrelated pre-existing untracked draft issues rather than blanket-cleaning the issue store. <!--#149633712bcf2992-->
- `test_reconcile_rollback_never_pulls_next_id_backwards` (function) — Test asserting that a failed fix-up commit rolls back the reconcile's file changes but never lowers the strictly-monotonic .next_id below a live concurrent reservation. <!--#59c33c7b18e4b382-->
- `test_untracked_draft_reference_to_keeper_is_not_corrupted` (function) — Test asserting that a main-side untracked draft referencing the keeper's #old is left untouched and not swept into the fix-up commit, because authorship is read from git trees rather than the dirty working directory. <!--#0fc5005b99eadcbd-->
- `test_untracked_draft_sharing_id_is_not_a_collision_loser` (function) — Test asserting that an untracked draft sharing a number with a merged committed issue is not treated as a collision loser, since detection is restricted to files tracked at the merge commit. <!--#6a808db874ba7c54-->
- `test_dirty_tracked_id_edit_does_not_fabricate_a_collision` (function) — Test asserting that an uncommitted working-tree edit to a tracked issue's id does not fabricate a collision, because detection reads ids from the committed merge tree rather than the dirty working copy. <!--#acf78f8d98aafda0-->
- `_default_branch` (function) — Returns the name of the currently checked-out branch of the given repo. <!--#32a8fa10d61d713c-->

### `tests/test_merge_conflict_resolver.py` (python) — Test suite for the LLM merge-conflict resolution pipeline, covering `StrategyDecider` gating under the SAFE/STRICT/FAST `MergeStrategy` variants (confidence ratings vs. `requires_human_review` flags), `HumanCallWriter`'s `merge_`-prefixed call-file schema and localized `print_instructions` output for normal/degraded/unreadable cases, plus end-to-end integration against a real git repo with a seeded conflict. <!--#b30d2cd6efa36f5f|256d3648ae27b667-->
- `_git` (function) — Helper that runs a git subcommand inside a given repo path and returns the completed process. <!--#8dcfd7712386df15-->
- `_init_repo` (function) — Helper that initializes a fresh git repo at a path with test user identity configured. <!--#63bfb3f5ba420316-->
- `_commit` (function) — Helper that stages all changes and creates a commit with the given message in a repo. <!--#af29a90485ca5f27-->
- `_current_branch` (function) — Helper returning the current branch name of a repo via git rev-parse. <!--#95be0c69f317516b-->
- `_setup_conflict` (function) — Helper that builds a two-branch repo with a deliberate single-file merge conflict and returns the ours/theirs branch names. <!--#287f770ecdb793e4-->
- `_make_resolution` (function) — Test helper that builds a mock `LLMResolution` with a single `FileResolution`/`HunkResolution`, parameterised by path, content, confidence levels, and the `requires_human_review` flag. <!--#ac849bfd7fa0f95f-->
- `TestStrategyDeciderDefault` (class) — Tests that under `MergeStrategy.SAFE` the `StrategyDecider` treats confidence as informational (accepting even LOW ratings) and only routes to `HUMAN_CALL` on an explicit global or per-file `requires_human_review` flag. <!--#e383465b28b32eb4-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderDefault.test_default_high_confidence_no_flags_accept` (method) — Asserts a HIGH-confidence, unflagged resolution is ACCEPTed under the SAFE strategy. <!--#3d49f8d3ffdebe6e-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderDefault.test_default_low_overall_confidence_accepted_without_flags` (method) — Asserts LOW global confidence without flags is still ACCEPTed under SAFE, since the on-disk marker scan — not the rating — is the success signal. <!--#92452d305794e9df-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderDefault.test_default_requires_human_review_flag_human_call` (method) — Asserts a global `requires_human_review` flag under SAFE yields `HUMAN_CALL` with the flag named in the decision reason. <!--#063b0ef5d4525fbd-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderDefault.test_default_per_file_flag_human_call` (method) — Asserts a per-file `requires_human_review` flag alone is enough to trigger `HUMAN_CALL` under SAFE. <!--#e2c3e1a865b1c4f5-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderDefault.test_default_medium_hunk_high_overall_accept` (method) — Asserts MEDIUM hunk confidence with HIGH file and global confidence is ACCEPTed under SAFE. <!--#fa2be6e8d0a86b62-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderDefault.test_default_low_file_overall_accepted_without_flags` (method) — Asserts SAFE ignores a LOW file-level confidence rating when no `requires_human_review` flag is present. <!--#4f4fc461a50c4f96-->
- `TestStrategyDeciderStrict` (class) — Tests that `MergeStrategy.STRICT` requires HIGH confidence at hunk, file, and global levels, sending anything less to `HUMAN_CALL`. <!--#db3b8b43a07aa444-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderStrict.test_strict_all_high_accept` (method) — Asserts uniformly HIGH confidence is ACCEPTed under STRICT. <!--#0332f14bb768b7bb-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderStrict.test_strict_low_hunk_human_call` (method) — Asserts a LOW hunk confidence triggers `HUMAN_CALL` under STRICT with a hunk/confidence-related reason. <!--#3c9b4d9fda0fb1a8-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderStrict.test_strict_low_file_overall_human_call` (method) — Asserts a merely MEDIUM file-level confidence triggers `HUMAN_CALL` under STRICT. <!--#4f63927744c16427-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderStrict.test_strict_low_global_overall_human_call` (method) — Asserts a MEDIUM global confidence triggers `HUMAN_CALL` under STRICT. <!--#315cbbe560025039-->
- `TestStrategyDeciderFast` (class) — Tests that `MergeStrategy.FAST` never parks on a human — accepting any confidence level and downgrading per-file `requires_human_review` to a warning — while a global flag yields `REJECT` (abort). <!--#b84d0254cff53541-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderFast.test_fast_regular_low_confidence_accept` (method) — Asserts FAST accepts a resolution with LOW confidence at every level. <!--#b43d92e5ec5f8a27-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderFast.test_fast_low_file_confidence_accept` (method) — Asserts FAST has no per-file confidence gate, accepting with the plain reason `"Fast strategy: accepted"`. <!--#c406f28ec77a1c51-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderFast.test_fast_per_file_human_review_flag_accepts_with_warning` (method) — Asserts a per-file `requires_human_review` flag under FAST still ACCEPTs but surfaces a WARNING naming the affected file in the decision reason. <!--#47e9781b1c288e27-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderFast.test_fast_global_requires_human_review_reject` (method) — Asserts a global `requires_human_review` flag under FAST yields `REJECT` (abort without a human call). <!--#c53f558128792811-->
  - `TestStrategyDeciderFast.test_fast_mixed_confidence_files_accept` (method) — Asserts FAST accepts a multi-file resolution mixing LOW- and HIGH-confidence files. <!--#61fc71253cf66f2d-->
- `TestHumanCallWriter` (class) — Tests `HumanCallWriter`'s call-file output (schema, `merge_` prefix distinct from loop-mode `merge_conflict_*`) and its `print_instructions` rendering for the conflict, degraded, localized, and unreadable-file variants. <!--#fcaf3ab71bc2dbcd-->
  - `TestHumanCallWriter.test_call_file_created` (method) — Asserts `write_call` produces a `merge_`-prefixed JSON file containing the conflict type, branch, decision reason, accept/abort/manual options, and per-file entries. <!--#f883833fe0770c0c-->
  - `TestHumanCallWriter.test_call_file_prefix_distinguishes_from_merge_conflict` (method) — Asserts call files use a 'merge_' prefix distinct from legacy 'merge_conflict_' loop-mode files. <!--#e77dfac4746f413d-->
  - `TestHumanCallWriter.test_print_instructions_renders_merge_conflict_guidance` (method) — Asserts `print_instructions` for a normal conflict call prints the review header, the `.response` path, the choice-JSON template, and the `git merge --abort` hint. <!--#b811c0d2f5c28a25-->
  - `TestHumanCallWriter.test_print_instructions_degraded_call_omits_conflict_commands` (method) — Asserts a degraded call's instructions report the already-rolled-back state and omit conflict-editing and `git merge --abort` guidance that would fail. <!--#1685a493a3674aed-->
  - `TestHumanCallWriter.test_print_instructions_is_localized` (method) — Asserts the degraded-call guidance is fully catalog-driven by rendering under `zh-CN` and checking no English literals survive. <!--#8bd3be0d0d0ea6c5-->
  - `TestHumanCallWriter.test_print_instructions_unreadable_call_file_degrades` (method) — Asserts a missing or corrupt call file still prints usable conflict guidance and the `.response` path. <!--#008f4be520317569-->
- `TestResolverStrategyIntegration` (class) — Integration tests that build a real conflicted repo and `ConflictContext`, then check that a mocked resolution flows through `StrategyDecider` to ACCEPT or `HUMAN_CALL` as the flags dictate. <!--#5a2560e334b0a5a0-->
  - `TestResolverStrategyIntegration.test_end_to_end_mock_llm_high_confidence_accept` (method) — Asserts a HIGH-confidence mock resolution over a real conflict context is ACCEPTed under SAFE. <!--#01a3b423601a9add-->
  - `TestResolverStrategyIntegration.test_end_to_end_mock_llm_review_flag_human_call` (method) — Asserts a review-flagged mock resolution routes to `HUMAN_CALL` under SAFE regardless of its LOW confidence. <!--#4d3ed84645dcb9b9-->

### `tests/test_merge_context.py` (python) — Test suite for the merge conflict context builder, combining unit tests of pure helpers (`_looks_binary`, `_parse_hunks`) with git-fixture integration tests that assert `build()` returns a `ConflictContext` carrying three-way file contents, hunk line ranges, merge metadata, and per-branch oneline logs across single-file, nested-path, binary, and multi-file/multi-hunk conflict scenarios. <!--#b3101fdc2ff88f8f|940727d09fc376a7-->
- `_git` (function) — Helper that runs a git subcommand inside a given repo path and returns the completed process. <!--#8dcfd7712386df15-->

- `TestPureHelpers` (class) — Unit tests for the module's pure helpers, covering `_looks_binary` null-byte detection and `_parse_hunks` line-range extraction for single, multiple, diff3-style, and marker-free conflict text. <!--#cc7ecec7242bd219-->
  - `TestPureHelpers.test_looks_binary_detects_null_bytes` (method) — Asserts _looks_binary flags content with null bytes as binary and treats text/empty content as non-binary. <!--#b7e2376753e448e0-->
  - `TestPureHelpers.test_parse_hunks_single_hunk` (method) — Asserts _parse_hunks finds one conflict hunk and records its correct start/end line numbers. <!--#eb0d38928f821a93-->
  - `TestPureHelpers.test_parse_hunks_multiple_hunks` (method) — Asserts _parse_hunks identifies two separate conflict hunks and their respective line ranges. <!--#054688e471a73d3b-->
  - `TestPureHelpers.test_parse_hunks_diff3_marker_inside` (method) — Asserts _parse_hunks treats a diff3-style conflict (with base marker) as a single hunk spanning all markers. <!--#00704608e20b65c6-->
  - `TestPureHelpers.test_parse_hunks_no_markers` (method) — Asserts _parse_hunks returns an empty list when text contains no conflict markers. <!--#ac1d9924663757cf-->
- `TestBuildSingleFileSingleHunk` (class) — Tests that `build()` on a basic one-file conflict returns a `ConflictContext` with all three sides of content, correct hunk line numbers, populated merge metadata (branches, SHAs, messages), and oneline logs for both sides. <!--#46f300dd074cdc7e-->
  - `TestBuildSingleFileSingleHunk.test_three_way_contents_non_empty` (method) — Asserts `build()` yields one `ConflictFile` for `shared.txt` with non-empty base/ours/theirs content, conflict-marked working content, and `is_binary` False. <!--#cb596d88b7f11a3a-->
  - `TestBuildSingleFileSingleHunk.test_hunk_line_numbers_recorded` (method) — Verifies build() records hunk line numbers that map to the actual conflict marker lines in the working content. <!--#28eb90cf322331f3-->
  - `TestBuildSingleFileSingleHunk.test_merge_metadata_populated` (method) — Verifies build() populates merge metadata such as branch names, merge base, head SHAs, and commit messages. <!--#7e2a48339f44dd0a-->
  - `TestBuildSingleFileSingleHunk.test_oneline_logs_collected` (method) — Verifies build() collects per-branch oneline commit logs containing the expected commit messages. <!--#11ef98ddc0cfc024-->
- `TestBuildNestedPath` (class) — Tests that a conflict in a deeply nested directory is reported with its repo-relative path verbatim and full three-way content. <!--#8c3348ccbeec05fe-->
  - `TestBuildNestedPath.test_deeply_nested_path_reported_verbatim` (method) — Creates a conflict at `docs/design/example/notes.md` and asserts `build()` preserves the nested path and collects base/ours/theirs content plus one hunk. <!--#6af66e6fd8a84747-->
- `TestBuildBinaryFile` (class) — Integration test class verifying build() correctly handles binary file conflicts. <!--#f155e81294578ae3-->

  - `TestBuildMultipleFilesMultipleHunks.test_two_files_three_hunks_total` (method) — Verifies build() detects two conflicting files with the correct per-file hunk counts (two and one) and valid hunk line mappings. <!--#b81381669d0d2c68-->

### `tests/test_merge_delete_merged_default_flip.py` (python) — Regression test module verifying the merge command's default 'delete-merged' behavior — that `run_merge` deletes the merged branch and archives its bound worktree by default, preserves both when `delete_merged=False`, and that the `--no-delete-merged` CLI flag correctly overrides the on-by-default setting. <!--#8b35b911e67f60b2|ece2c21f90e069ab-->

- `test_run_merge_no_delete_merged_preserves_branch_and_skips_archive` (function) — Asserts that calling `run_merge` with `delete_merged=False` preserves both the merged branch and its bound worktree and creates no archive directory. <!--#6ca8380c663e794a-->
- `test_cli_no_delete_merged_flag_overrides_default` (function) — Verifies via `CliRunner` that the `--no-delete-merged` CLI flag causes the `merge` command to invoke `run_merge` with `delete_merged=False`. <!--#10cfd26cbbe102d4-->
- `test_cli_default_delete_merged_is_on` (function) — Verifies via `CliRunner` that without `--no-delete-merged` the `merge` command invokes `run_merge` with `delete_merged=True` (the `MergeConfig` default). <!--#eda9bdc3b841c040-->

  - `TestMergeFlowHasNoGuardrailsPhase.test_spec_weakening_merge_is_not_blocked` (method) — End-to-end check that merging a branch which rewrites SHALL→SHOULD and deletes a Requirement succeeds with no human call, no rollback, and the weakened spec on disk. <!--#bdb78e8825e4b568-->
- `TestGuardrailsCommandRemoved` (class) — Test class asserting the `guardrails` CLI surface is gone: absent from `--help`, failing when invoked, undefined in the cli module, and with no guardrail keys left in the en-US/zh-CN locale files. <!--#a303580ac3c30e21-->
  - `TestGuardrailsCommandRemoved.test_not_listed_in_help` (method) — Asserts "guardrails" does not appear in the CLI `--help` output. <!--#e6f6263deda418db-->
  - `TestGuardrailsCommandRemoved.test_invoking_it_fails` (method) — Asserts invoking `guardrails --sizes` exits non-zero. <!--#d2cdaa41db75060b-->
  - `TestGuardrailsCommandRemoved.test_cli_module_defines_no_guardrails_command` (method) — Asserts `tianluo.cli` defines neither `guardrails_cmd` nor `_run_spec_size_guardrails`. <!--#3fd550d0d76d705e-->
  - `TestGuardrailsCommandRemoved.test_locale_has_no_guardrail_keys` (method) — Parametrised check that the `en-US` and `zh-CN` locale JSON files contain no key mentioning "guardrail". <!--#7b4137f25d1566be-->
- `TestLegacyArtefactTolerance` (class) — Test class ensuring leftover guardrail artefacts stay harmless — legacy call files abort or accept cleanly and archived guardrail failure reasons still render. <!--#58616dfd624b894d-->

  - `TestLegacyArtefactTolerance.test_legacy_orphan_violation_field_is_ignored_on_accept` (method) — Asserts a legacy `orphan_guardrails_violations` field no longer blocks an `accept` response, and the recorded resolution is written to the conflicted file. <!--#d2541f14f9ad9ec5-->

### `tests/test_merge_issue_renumber.py` (python) — Pytest suite exercising cross-worktree issue merging and ID renumbering (IssueManager.adopt_issue and merge_worktree_issues), covering collision-free renumbering, content dedup/idempotency, monotonic .next_id allocation, reference rewriting, retired-number and ambiguous-shared-ID handling, and trace-based recognition on re-run. <!--#3734088b860dc1b3|129784483d5dc394-->
- `_read_next_id` (function) — Test helper that reads and returns the integer value of a project's tianluo/issues/.next_id counter file. <!--#b2d2fa2bca9543a5-->
- `_ids_on_disk` (function) — Helper returning the set of all issue IDs (open and closed) an IssueManager sees on disk. <!--#e586fc58b9e4bbaf-->
- `test_overlapping_ids_renumbered_without_conflict` (function) — Verifies that a worktree issue whose ID collides with an existing main issue is folded in under a fresh non-colliding ID, leaving main's original untouched and advancing .next_id. <!--#93c4f5fc37ea07bf-->
- `test_duplicate_content_not_merged_again` (function) — Asserts worktree issues whose content already exists in main (including whitespace/case variants) are not re-added and the counter stays put. <!--#5bdcb8dec6ca8551-->
- `test_idempotent_rerun_does_not_duplicate` (function) — Asserts that re-running the merge folds in nothing the second time since the new content now exists in main, leaving IDs and counter unchanged. <!--#ed47d16df2054af6-->
- `test_next_id_monotonic_with_multiple_new_issues` (function) — Asserts `.next_id` advances by exactly the number of merged issues, allocating contiguous non-colliding IDs. <!--#9bd32e7ba30e6da5-->
- `test_closed_worktree_issue_renumbered_into_closed_dir` (function) — Verifies that a new closed worktree issue is adopted into the main project's closed/ directory with its CLOSED status and content preserved. <!--#e8c3e30f51659782-->
- `test_missing_worktree_issues_dir_is_noop` (function) — Verifies that merging when the worktree has no tianluo/issues/ directory returns an empty result and errors nothing, leaving main untouched. <!--#d3675a29bb85f997-->
- `test_adopt_issue_preserves_fields_and_allocates_new_id` (function) — Checks IssueManager.adopt_issue reassigns a fresh non-colliding ID while preserving all issue fields (title, priority, tags, type, source) and appending a renumber trace. <!--#da78575f76ce4495-->
- `test_adopt_retired_number_rewrites_store_wide_references` (function) — Verifies that adopting an incoming issue whose old ID is owned by no kept main issue retires that number and repoints existing store-wide `#<old>` references to the new ID. <!--#4aabc45d3057f186-->
- `test_adopt_scopes_rewrite_when_kept_owner_has_mismatched_filename` (function) — Verifies that ownership of an ID is decided by a kept issue's parsed YAML id (not filename prefix), so a reference to that number is not incorrectly rewritten to follow an adopted issue's renumber. <!--#513b4ee5e155d332-->
- `test_adopt_issue_rejects_empty_description` (function) — Verifies that IssueManager.adopt_issue raises ValueError when given an issue with a blank description. <!--#00de1477f006fb46-->
- `test_renumber_rewrites_self_reference_and_records_trace` (function) — Verifies that renumbering a worktree issue rewrites its own #old cross-references to #new, appends a traceable old→new line, preserves both sides, and lands .next_id at max(ID)+1. <!--#152ad14bd00e0244-->
- `test_batch_retired_number_rewrites_preexisting_store_reference` (function) — Verifies that when an incoming issue's old number is owned by no kept main issue, that number is retired and a pre-existing dependent reference is repointed store-wide rather than left dangling. <!--#db3a90d43906d486-->
- `test_batch_collision_leaves_kept_owner_reference_scoped` (function) — Verifies that when the incoming number is still owned by a kept main issue, the batch rewrite stays scoped to the adopted file and the dependent `#<old>` keeps pointing at the kept owner. <!--#45f35c15c07ac3af-->
- `test_colliding_old_ids_in_source_leave_own_references_ambiguous` (function) — Verifies that two source issues sharing one old ID are adopted under distinct new IDs while their ambiguous #005 references keep their digits and each records a durable ambiguity note. <!--#9b7f34c9b8ba71f6-->
- `test_ambiguous_shared_old_id_reference_left_and_recorded` (function) — Verifies that a third issue referencing a shared/ambiguous old ID keeps its original digits with a durable ambiguity note recorded, and that the batch merge stays idempotent on re-run. <!--#a468442ba41b30a0-->
- `test_runtime_sync_ambiguity_surfaced_via_out_param` (function) — Verifies that the runtime-sync merge channel reports each ambiguous #old reference via a caller-supplied out list carrying {file, old_id, candidates} entries mirroring the committed-issue channel. <!--#f480aa005594faee-->
- `test_shared_old_id_with_identity_keeper_stays_ambiguous` (function) — Verifies that a collision where one copy keeps its old number and a peer is renumbered stays ambiguous — tokens keep their digits and both live candidates (including the kept number) are recorded. <!--#0c2e53bc46e942ae-->
- `test_renumber_then_idempotent_rerun` (function) — Confirms a second merge is idempotent: the already-adopted issue is recognised via its trace-stripped content signature and not re-folded, leaving the counter unchanged. <!--#8055bd340fc9a4ca-->
- `test_cross_references_between_merged_worktree_issues_rewritten` (function) — Verifies a worktree issue referencing a renumbered sibling is repointed to the sibling's new ID while main's own issues remain untouched. <!--#924da3c41344842c-->
- `test_batch_renumber_does_not_chain_overlapping_ids` (function) — Verifies that when one member's new ID equals another member's old ID, references land on the correct target and do not chain onward through the second rename. <!--#bf3e69d45c145131-->
- `test_rerun_idempotent_after_reference_rewrite` (function) — Verifies a renumber that rewrote references stays idempotent on re-run because the recorded renumber trace vouches for the digit difference so nothing is re-adopted. <!--#47662ff88cc5e5ff-->
- `test_issue_differing_only_by_reference_is_not_lost` (function) — Verifies dedup does not collapse two issues that differ only by their referenced number, adopting the genuinely-different worktree issue under a fresh ID. <!--#b10fb269ddbe9583-->
- `test_unrelated_trace_pair_does_not_absorb_different_issue` (function) — Verifies a renumber trace recorded on one adopted issue cannot vouch for a different candidate elsewhere in the store, so a genuinely-different worktree issue is still adopted. <!--#ed8c8037512073c3-->
- `test_same_numbered_unrelated_issue_cannot_borrow_foreign_trace` (function) — Verifies that sharing a numeric ID with a traced adopted copy does not license borrowing that stranger's renumber trace, so an unrelated worktree issue is adopted rather than absorbed. <!--#76c32d82c5747489-->
- `test_adopted_copy_keeping_its_number_still_dedups_on_rerun` (function) — Verifies that a same-numbered adopted copy whose batch-mate reference was rewritten is still recognized on re-run (via the worktree-vouched renumber pair) so nothing is re-adopted. <!--#71f3a266404a97ea-->
- `test_next_id_matches_max_after_renumber` (function) — Verifies that after adoption .next_id self-heals to on-disk max ID + 1 even from a garbage counter, and that a forced-collision self-reference is repointed to the new ID. <!--#de6deedd7422fd27-->
- `test_stale_lagging_counter_cannot_mint_duplicate_id` (function) — Regression test verifying that a .next_id lagging behind the store is reconciled against on-disk IDs before allocating, so adoption never writes two files sharing one ID. <!--#63fa83cadb8545d3-->

### `tests/test_merge_llm_editor_resolver.py` (python) — Regression test suite for the merge package's LLM-as-editor batch conflict resolver, using scripted stub editors (via monkeypatch, no real Claude subprocess) to verify fast-mode single- and multi-file convergence, iteration-exhaustion failure without human escalation, and the excision of the legacy take-theirs fallback path. <!--#43202cb920b641ac|9b176f805e0d442b-->
- `_git` (function) — Helper that runs a `git -C <path>` subprocess and returns the completed process with captured output. <!--#8dcfd7712386df15-->
- `_init_repo` (function) — Helper that initializes a git repository at a path and configures a test user identity. <!--#63bfb3f5ba420316-->
- `_commit` (function) — Helper that stages all changes and creates a git commit with the given message. <!--#af29a90485ca5f27-->
- `_current_branch` (function) — Helper that returns the current branch name of a git repo. <!--#95be0c69f317516b-->
- `_setup_conflict_file` (function) — Helper that builds a two-branch repo with divergent edits to a file, returning the ours/theirs branch names for conflict scenarios. <!--#77c02ef3cde68ba9-->
- `_write_with_markers` (function) — Helper that writes a file containing standard git conflict markers around the given ours/theirs content. <!--#88009d004cc3a65e-->
- `_make_conflict_file` (function) — Test helper that builds a minimal `ConflictFile` (empty base/ours/theirs, given path and conflict-marked working content) for feeding into `resolve_batch`. <!--#232d810887936b13-->
- `_make_batch_context` (function) — Test helper that constructs a `BatchContext` with fixed dummy branch names, SHAs, commit messages and logs plus the given `MergeStrategy`, rooted at `tmp_path`. <!--#5f5554ff47ba7f60-->
- `_ScriptedEditor` (class) — Callable stub that simulates an LLM editor by invoking a scripted action per iteration and asserting against unexpected extra calls. <!--#f7e20ef0e5e12cf4-->
  - `_ScriptedEditor.__init__` (method) — Initializes the scripted editor with its list of per-iteration actions and a zeroed call counter. <!--#fb8f854f28f3882f-->
  - `_ScriptedEditor.__call__` (method) — Dispatches the next scripted action for the current call, raising AssertionError if the script is exhausted. <!--#df6e41f3fd51446b-->
- `_install_stub` (function) — Helper that monkeypatches ConflictResolver._call_llm to delegate to a scripted editor stub. <!--#5a3a855c5f9a5553-->
- `test_fast_single_file_one_iteration_success` (function) — Test that fast mode resolves a single conflict file in one LLM iteration, clearing all markers and reporting success. <!--#93505f52a772ff06-->
- `test_fast_strategy_decider_accepts_single_file` (function) — Test that the StrategyDecider returns ACCEPT after the resolver clears a single-file conflict in fast mode. <!--#aa3ebb3ddddb4b7f-->
- `test_fast_multi_file_multi_round_convergence` (function) — Test that fast mode batched over multiple conflicting files converges across successive rounds, recording markers_remaining history for incomplete rounds. <!--#f70fe2a772b9535e-->
- `test_fast_exhausts_iterations_fails_without_human_call` (function) — Test that fast mode failing to converge within max iterations yields a REJECT with reason 'fast_failed' and no human-call escalation. <!--#79fd646b8faadcf4-->
- `test_no_take_theirs_helper_remains_in_merge_package` (function) — Regression guard that iterates over every module in the tianluo.engine.merge package and asserts none still exposes the removed _robust_take_theirs_commit or _record_take_theirs_event helpers, preventing reintroduction of the take-theirs fallback excised in G4. <!--#5d02aff40b47e8e4-->
- `test_replay_resolves_via_llm_without_take_theirs` (function) — Test that a previously take-theirs-prone scenario now resolves cleanly via the LLM editor loop on a second round with no take-theirs side effect. <!--#b57f8d064aee8085-->
- `test_synthesis_osfailure_does_not_synthesise_deletion` (function) — Regression test that a resolved conflict whose post-resolution read-back raises OSError is flagged for human review with non-empty resolved_content (rather than degrading to an empty content that _apply_resolution would treat as a file deletion), verifying ConflictResolver._synthesize_resolution_from_outcome sets requires_human_review and LOW confidence at both file and overall level. <!--#621c8de52141894d-->

### `tests/test_merge_orchestrator.py` (python) — Pytest suite for `MergeOrchestrator`'s sequential branch-merge logic, using git helper functions to build throwaway repos, branches, and worktrees and asserting on `MergeReport` outcomes plus behaviours like version-intent probing that gates legacy per-branch version aggregation. <!--#d76a40d27260a27d|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/test_merge_respond.py` (python) — Pytest suite for `process_merge_response`, driving real git repos through a mid-merge conflict to verify call/response file validation, the strict-mode sentinel safety refusal, and the accept/abort/manual choice paths (including non-`merge_conflict` and legacy `guardrail_*` call types, main-worktree merge-lock root resolution, and missing `llm_resolution` edge cases). <!--#4cf07098569b7cef|f25b8223765bfce8-->
- `_init_repo` (function) — Test helper that initializes a git repo with configured user identity and an initial commit on branch 'main'. <!--#aa9497932bc71f23-->
- `_start_merge_conflict` (function) — Test helper that sets up diverging 'feature' and 'main' branches and starts a git merge to leave the repo in a mid-merge conflicted state. <!--#0af2eba6d64d606b-->
- `_create_merge_call_file` (function) — Test helper that writes a merge_call.json file with the given files list and call type. <!--#a686a06c1780ca59-->
- `_create_response_file` (function) — Test helper that writes the sibling .response file containing the user's choice and optional feedback. <!--#6a344efb139b38c6-->
- `TestCallFileNotFound` (class) — Test class verifying a missing call file is handled as an error. <!--#ec494d7efe3ba7c0-->
  - `TestCallFileNotFound.test_returns_error` (method) — Asserts process_merge_response returns exit code 1 when the call file does not exist. <!--#1f11ddae3e9d5d91-->
- `TestResponseFileNotFound` (class) — Test class verifying a missing response file is handled as an error. <!--#4d70373e22d5cef0-->
  - `TestResponseFileNotFound.test_returns_error` (method) — Asserts process_merge_response returns exit code 1 when the .response file is absent. <!--#88015a670c912317-->
- `TestInvalidJson` (class) — Test class verifying malformed JSON in either the call or response file is rejected. <!--#9cc25ffd615df8c8-->
  - `TestInvalidJson.test_invalid_call_file` (method) — Asserts exit code 1 when the call file contains invalid JSON. <!--#d513b9c4a71e4ce3-->
  - `TestInvalidJson.test_invalid_response_file` (method) — Asserts exit code 1 when the response file contains invalid JSON. <!--#657f74e084669a94-->
- `TestInvalidChoice` (class) — Test class verifying an unrecognized choice value is rejected. <!--#3c065107a158b4ef-->
  - `TestInvalidChoice.test_unknown_choice` (method) — Asserts exit code 1 when the response specifies an unknown choice. <!--#bdcefaa24d328302-->
- `TestStrictSentinelDetection` (class) — Test class for the critical safety rule that strict-mode placeholder content must never be written to disk. <!--#a9765cb23d7c8c76-->
  - `TestStrictSentinelDetection.test_refuses_strict_placeholder` (method) — Asserts an accept is refused when resolved content contains the strict-mode sentinel. <!--#44fcf6ce19964a53-->
  - `TestStrictSentinelDetection.test_refuses_mixed_files_with_sentinel` (method) — Asserts the entire accept is refused if any one file among several carries the strict sentinel. <!--#fe731df406438616-->
  - `TestStrictSentinelDetection.test_allows_accept_without_sentinel` (method) — Asserts a normal sentinel-free accept succeeds and writes the resolved content back. <!--#835d0d748eb0bf2b-->
- `TestAcceptChoice` (class) — Tests that the "accept" response writes each file's `llm_resolution.resolved_content` back to the working tree and commits the merge, skips files with empty resolved content, and — for non-`merge_conflict` call types (including `DEGRADED_CALL_TYPE`, retired `guardrail_*` spellings, and unknown types) — treats acceptance as a manual-fix acknowledgement that writes nothing. <!--#9730aadfca245fcc-->
  - `TestAcceptChoice.test_writes_files_and_stages` (method) — Asserts accept writes resolved file content (including nested paths) and commits the merge, clearing MERGE_HEAD. <!--#79e9b5d0038cfe28-->
  - `TestAcceptChoice.test_skips_empty_resolved_content` (method) — Asserts files with empty resolved_content are skipped during write-back. <!--#b9c1e0e028eb633f-->
  - `TestAcceptChoice.test_commits_merge` (method) — Asserts accept produces a merge commit so the log no longer shows the initial commit. <!--#93ab57d1bf08c397-->
  - `TestAcceptChoice.test_non_merge_conflict_type_accepts_as_manual_fix` (method) — Parametrized test asserting that accepting a non-`merge_conflict` call type exits 0, leaves the working tree untouched, and reports "no per-file resolution to write back" along with the operator's note. <!--#c595f30f59bd4f55-->
  - `TestAcceptChoice.test_legacy_guardrail_call_file_fields_tolerated` (method) — Asserts that an old call file with `type: "guardrail_violation"` and retired `violations` / `orphan_guardrails_violations` payload keys is still answered cleanly by `process_merge_response` instead of raising. <!--#f54c2f307a969e8a-->
- `TestAbortChoice` (class) — Tests that the "abort" response runs `git merge --abort` for a real in-progress merge (including unknown call types), but skips it for settled call types such as `DEGRADED_CALL_TYPE` and legacy `guardrail_*` types, reporting rollback as already complete. <!--#70b85a57c48b43c8-->
  - `TestAbortChoice.test_aborts_merge` (method) — Asserts abort runs git merge --abort and leaves no MERGE_HEAD. <!--#2cfba9d4ac64958a-->
  - `TestAbortChoice.test_no_active_merge_type_abort_skips_git_merge_abort` (method) — Parametrized test asserting that aborting a settled call type with no merge in progress exits 0 and prints "rollback to pre-merge state is already complete" plus the operator's note. <!--#a95c23f832fa94c0-->
  - `TestAbortChoice.test_abort_unknown_type_still_runs_git_merge_abort` (method) — Asserts that a call type outside the no-active-merge list still performs a real `git merge --abort`, leaving no `MERGE_HEAD` behind. <!--#9cdf02a41373fdd5-->
- `TestManualChoice` (class) — Tests that the "manual" response returns success with manual-resolve instructions and the operator's note, while leaving the conflict markers, the in-progress merge, and the call-file directory untouched (no retired `.pending_guardrails` sidecar). <!--#3805e056dc1b33be-->
  - `TestManualChoice.test_returns_success` (method) — Asserts that the manual choice exits 0 and prints "resolve the conflicts manually" together with the operator's note. <!--#d9b6bd67cbe8c021-->
  - `TestManualChoice.test_manual_parks_nothing_on_disk` (method) — Asserts that manual resolution writes no sidecar beyond `<call>.response`, leaves conflict markers in the working tree, and keeps `MERGE_HEAD` in place for the human to finish. <!--#68a5aec46d2cfcf4-->
- `TestMainWorktreeLockRoot` (class) — Test class verifying that process_merge_response acquires the main-worktree merge mutex on the resolved main-repo root (via _resolve_main_lock_root) rather than the bare project_root, so worktree-launched merges contend on the single project-wide lock. <!--#2a5e186bdd4e5a06-->
  - `TestMainWorktreeLockRoot.test_lock_targets_resolved_main_repo_root` (method) — Asserts process_merge_response calls _resolve_main_lock_root(project_root) and constructs MergeLock with the resolved sentinel root in blocking mode. <!--#0085a60042218694-->
- `TestEdgeCases` (class) — Test class covering graceful handling of missing or null llm_resolution data. <!--#95954be7992659ea-->
  - `TestEdgeCases.test_missing_llm_resolution_key` (method) — Asserts files lacking an llm_resolution key are skipped while others resolve, succeeding overall. <!--#a4adda37cbb7df53-->
  - `TestEdgeCases.test_none_llm_resolution` (method) — Asserts files with a null llm_resolution value are handled gracefully. <!--#86d8b3a275735afd-->
- `TestGitAddReturncode` (class) — Test class (G8 task 43) ensuring git add failures during merge-respond are surfaced as errors rather than silently swallowed. <!--#c2443e0131274bd5-->
  - `TestGitAddReturncode.test_git_add_failure_returns_error` (method) — Monkeypatches subprocess.run so 'git add' returns 128 and asserts process_merge_response returns exit code 1. <!--#b078dbd76e651f05-->
- `TestFirstParentSha` (class) — Test class (G8 task 42) for the _first_parent_sha helper that walks the octopus-safe first parent of HEAD. <!--#0593d8ba757f28ca-->
  - `TestFirstParentSha.test_two_parent_merge_first_parent` (method) — Creates a --no-ff merge and asserts _first_parent_sha returns the mainline (first-parent) commit that HEAD was on before the merge. <!--#ba32062324bae16b-->
  - `TestFirstParentSha.test_root_commit_raises_runtime_error` (method) — Asserts _first_parent_sha raises RuntimeError('no parents') when HEAD is a parentless root commit. <!--#c688a6e7cd674760-->
- `TestVersionBumpAfterAccept` (class) — Test class verifying the accept path enforces that the version advanced when a version file was part of the resolution. <!--#94b1ee72161884d2-->
  - `TestVersionBumpAfterAccept._setup_repo_with_pyproject_and_conflict` (method) — Test helper setting up a repo with pyproject.toml and a README.md merge conflict, returning the pre-merge SHA and feature branch name. <!--#7654419b305311ad-->
  - `TestVersionBumpAfterAccept.test_accepts_when_version_advanced` (method) — Asserts accept succeeds when the resolved pyproject.toml version changed from pre-merge. <!--#170b4f314d0102f4-->
  - `TestVersionBumpAfterAccept.test_rejects_when_version_unchanged` (method) — Asserts accept fails (exit 1) when the resolved pyproject.toml version did not change. <!--#528dd8fb6b4ffe0e-->
  - `TestVersionBumpAfterAccept.test_no_version_file_skips_check` (method) — Asserts the version-advance check is skipped when no version file is part of the resolution. <!--#17a7aa848500fbd8-->

### `tests/test_merge_robust_cleanup.py` (python) — Test module verifying the merge cleanup's archive-before-delete behavior, covering the low-level `_archive_worktree` helper (tracked/untracked capture, .git exclusion, collision suffixing) and the full `CleanupManager.delete_merged_branches` integration where archiving precedes worktree/branch destruction, failures preserve the branch, and the CleanupReport exposes archive-tracking fields. <!--#4d36bbd89806d73f|9fd431f10c54660a-->
- `_init_repo_with_worktree_branch` (function) — Test helper that initializes a git repo with a feature branch merged into the base branch and a bound worktree on disk, optionally leaving an untracked file, returning the branch name, worktree path, and base branch. <!--#4d7d12a8ee53b3d3-->
- `TestArchiveWorktreeHelper` (class) — Unit tests for the low-level `_archive_worktree` helper, verifying it archives tracked+untracked worktree files (excluding `.git`) with metadata into `tianluo/worktrees/.archive/` and appends a sequence suffix on timestamp collisions. <!--#035184b5302003e8-->

  - `TestArchiveWorktreeHelper.test_archive_collision_appends_seq_suffix` (method) — Asserts that when a same-timestamp archive slot already exists (via a patched `time.time`), `_archive_worktree` avoids clobbering by appending a `-1`/`-2` sequence suffix to the new archive directory name. <!--#ba39250fcc624ab6-->
- `TestCleanupArchiveIntegration` (class) — Integration tests for `CleanupManager.delete_merged_branches`, verifying it archives each worktree before destroying it, preserves worktree+branch when archiving fails, and cleanly skips archiving for branches with no bound worktree. <!--#6a955047c5230587-->
  - `TestCleanupArchiveIntegration.test_delete_merged_archives_before_destroying` (method) — Asserts `delete_merged_branches` archives a clean worktree into `tianluo/worktrees/.archive` (reported in `report.archived` with tracked content) before removing the worktree and deleting the git branch. <!--#3192d7a7fd22207a-->
  - `TestCleanupArchiveIntegration.test_archive_failure_preserves_worktree_and_branch` (method) — Asserts that when `shutil.copytree` fails during archiving, `delete_merged_branches` deletes nothing, records the branch under `report.skipped_archive_failed` with the error reason, and leaves the worktree and branch intact for recovery. <!--#6f71e605f98dc3a6-->
  - `TestCleanupArchiveIntegration.test_delete_without_worktree_skips_archive_cleanly` (method) — Confirms a merged branch with no bound worktree is deleted cleanly with no archive entry and no archive-failure entry. <!--#4e90fd5e0250b85b-->
- `TestCleanupReportFields` (class) — Test class checking that the CleanupReport dataclass exposes the new archive-tracking fields. <!--#2e304771abce3c6f-->
  - `TestCleanupReportFields.test_cleanup_report_has_archive_fields` (method) — Asserts a freshly constructed CleanupReport defaults its `archived` and `skipped_archive_failed` fields to empty lists. <!--#01c17c6a9f3120fc-->

### `tests/test_merge_runtime_sync.py` (python) — Pytest module for tianluo.engine.merge.runtime_sync, exercising the tier A/B/C branch-runtime sync logic (file copying, mtime/permission preservation, symlink-escape safety, and collision handling) using filesystem fixtures with a mocked worktree lookup instead of real git. <!--#b0cbd52052344241|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/test_merge_stash_concurrent_repro.py` (python) — End-to-end and unit regression suite proving that both merge call sites (the `luo merge` fast path and the DAG implement leaf-back merge) route through the shared archive-first stash-pop recovery so concurrent untracked files colliding on stash-pop are preserved in `tianluo/worktrees/.archive` with an audit issue pointing at them, and that an incomplete/unresolved recovery is surfaced as a merge failure. <!--#9f7aafb900bd8939|a0d88f20dbe88a0c-->
- `_git` (function) — Thin helper that runs a git subcommand inside a given repo directory and returns the completed process with captured output. <!--#9bef257c44286ed8-->
- `_init_repo` (function) — Test helper that inits a fresh git repo, sets a test identity, gitignores only the tianluo/worktrees/ archive sink (leaving tianluo/issues artefacts untracked), makes an initial commit, and returns the default branch name. <!--#1e2ff271c86752be-->
- `_archived_files` (function) — Walks the archive directory and returns a mapping of each archived file's run-relative path to its recovered content across all archive runs. <!--#afa7fb9228491f88-->
- `_open_issue_texts` (function) — Test helper that reads and returns the text of every open audit-issue YAML file under tianluo/issues/open, or an empty list if none exist. <!--#7c957ef16d7de2a4-->
- `test_fast_merge_path_archives_concurrent_untracked` (function) — End-to-end test that the `se3 merge` fast path recovers concurrent untracked main-repo files (a colliding one plus a 229-style issue file) from the archive on stash-pop collision and files an audit issue pointing at the archive path and blob sha. <!--#488c6e028fcefeba-->
- `test_fast_stash_pop_unit_archives_and_audits` (function) — Unit test that drives `_fast_stash_pop` directly, forcing a same-path stash-pop collision, and asserts the merged-tree version is untouched while stashed content is archived and a recovery message is recorded in the audit log. <!--#46ae6be9996723ce-->
- `test_leaf_merge_path_archives_concurrent_untracked` (function) — Verifies that the implement leaf-back merge path preserves the leaf version of a colliding file while archiving concurrent uncommitted main-repo files (both the colliding one and an unrelated new issue file) under ARCHIVE_DIR, and records an audit issue containing the archive path and blob sha — i.e. the same invariant, archive sink, and audit contract as the fast path. <!--#d71c3252f276f0e5-->
- `_incomplete_outcome` (function) — Test fixture building a `StashPopOutcome` representing a case-a recovery that archived both sides but left the index unmerged (archive_failed with unresolved files). <!--#504f64f90546a256-->
- `_stash_with_collision` (function) — Helper that stashes an untracked file then repopulates its path so a subsequent pop is non-clean, returning the stash label to drive recovery over. <!--#dba309ca457bfd4f-->
- `test_fast_stash_pop_signals_incomplete_when_unresolved` (function) — Unit test patching `resolve_stashpop_safely` to leave unmerged paths, asserting `_fast_stash_pop` returns True (recovery not finalized) and the audit issue still carries INCOMPLETE archive manifest pointers. <!--#82d8b7d3e940d711-->
- `test_run_merge_fast_reports_failure_on_incomplete_stashpop` (function) — Test that when post-merge stash-pop recovery does not finalize, `run_merge`'s fast path returns a non-zero exit even though the branch merge itself landed, so it never reports success over an unreconciled tree. <!--#27cde9df5c22c358-->
- `test_leaf_merge_reports_failure_on_incomplete_stashpop` (function) — Verifies that when post-merge stash-pop recovery does not finalize (patched `_resolve_stashpop_safely` returns an incomplete outcome), `_merge_leaf_branch` returns False so the DAG step reflects the unreconciled main repo, while the leaf commit still lands on the default branch and an INCOMPLETE audit issue carries the archive manifest pointers. <!--#b73258b9807bc54e-->

### `tests/test_merge_strategy_alignment.py` (python) — Unit tests verifying that the merge conflict resolver's decision logic aligns with each `MergeStrategy` — FAST only ever ACCEPTs or REJECTs (never HUMAN_CALL), STRICT's fallback escalates to HUMAN_CALL (with the orchestrator short-circuiting it), and SAFE gates purely on the explicit `requires_human_review` flag rather than confidence ratings — using a shared `_make_resolution` helper to build mock `LLMResolution` inputs. <!--#a63f86ed9be1a8f8|550eeb2ffc51959b-->
- `_make_resolution` (function) — Test helper that builds a mock `LLMResolution` with one `FileResolution`/`HunkResolution`, parameterised by path, content, overall/hunk confidence, and the `requires_human_review` flag. <!--#ac849bfd7fa0f95f-->
- `TestFastStrategyAcceptOrRejectOnly` (class) — Tests asserting `MergeStrategy.FAST` only ever yields ACCEPT or REJECT — never HUMAN_CALL — with the global `requires_human_review` flag as the sole reject gate and a per-file flag merely appended as a warning. <!--#3d54cf9f471ccfce-->
  - `TestFastStrategyAcceptOrRejectOnly.test_fast_never_returns_human_call_across_various_inputs` (method) — Property-style sweep over confidence combinations and both flag scopes, asserting fast mode never returns HUMAN_CALL and maps only the global flag to REJECT. <!--#eb7e89426c2c7f37-->
  - `TestFastStrategyAcceptOrRejectOnly.test_fast_low_confidence_accept` (method) — Asserts LOW confidence under fast strategy still yields ACCEPT with reason "Fast strategy: accepted". <!--#6c55c5911841dab6-->
  - `TestFastStrategyAcceptOrRejectOnly.test_fast_medium_confidence_accept` (method) — Asserts MEDIUM confidence under fast strategy yields ACCEPT with reason "Fast strategy: accepted". <!--#b97ae7ae883ceb34-->
  - `TestFastStrategyAcceptOrRejectOnly.test_fast_per_file_requires_human_review_accepted_with_warning` (method) — Asserts a per-file `requires_human_review` flag in fast mode is accepted but surfaced as a WARNING suffix in the decision reason rather than rejecting. <!--#eff2f7733320a681-->
  - `TestFastStrategyAcceptOrRejectOnly.test_fast_global_requires_human_review_reject` (method) — Asserts a global `requires_human_review` flag in fast mode aborts with REJECT and a reason stating no human call is made. <!--#ded32bf0262c11aa-->
  - `TestFastStrategyAcceptOrRejectOnly.test_fast_mixed_confidence_files_accept` (method) — Asserts a multi-file resolution with mixed per-file confidence and no flags is accepted under fast strategy. <!--#8bc2899bf90baf85-->
- `TestStrictStrategyPlaceholder` (class) — Tests for the strict strategy's fallback path — documenting that the orchestrator short-circuits it — covering ACCEPT on all-high confidence and HUMAN_CALL on low hunk confidence or either flag scope. <!--#584145db41865b86-->
  - `TestStrictStrategyPlaceholder.test_strict_docstring_mentions_orchestrator_short_circuit` (method) — Asserts the _decide_strict docstring documents that the orchestrator short-circuits/placeholders strict handling. <!--#dc43bd68fc8717e5-->
  - `TestStrictStrategyPlaceholder.test_strict_fallback_all_high_accept` (method) — Asserts the strict fallback accepts an all-HIGH-confidence, flag-free resolution with the strict-strategy reason string. <!--#87bd6e0e53ce329a-->
  - `TestStrictStrategyPlaceholder.test_strict_fallback_low_hunk_human_call` (method) — Asserts a LOW-confidence hunk under strict escalates to HUMAN_CALL rather than REJECT. <!--#e4e7c2544585f6e6-->
  - `TestStrictStrategyPlaceholder.test_strict_fallback_global_requires_human_review_human_call` (method) — Asserts a global `requires_human_review` flag under strict yields HUMAN_CALL with the strict-strategy reason string. <!--#34aa4f5f7ba0e051-->
  - `TestStrictStrategyPlaceholder.test_strict_fallback_per_file_requires_human_review_human_call` (method) — Asserts a per-file `requires_human_review` flag alone under strict yields HUMAN_CALL naming the offending file. <!--#2ef9c15b78e4bf7d-->
- `TestSafeStrategy` (class) — Tests that `MergeStrategy.SAFE` gates solely on the explicit `requires_human_review` flag (global or per-file), treating confidence ratings as informational. <!--#b18b3132fd7b35f5-->
  - `TestSafeStrategy.test_safe_high_confidence_accept` (method) — Asserts a HIGH-confidence, flag-free resolution is accepted under safe strategy with the "No human-review flags set" reason. <!--#5316bb91df52d021-->
  - `TestSafeStrategy.test_safe_low_overall_accepted_without_flags` (method) — Asserts LOW overall confidence without flags is still accepted under safe strategy, since confidence is informational under the LLM-as-editor model. <!--#b96e570f6e72580b-->
  - `TestSafeStrategy.test_safe_global_requires_human_review_human_call` (method) — Asserts a global `requires_human_review` flag under safe strategy yields HUMAN_CALL with the safe-strategy reason string. <!--#9a25a2707cfca195-->
  - `TestSafeStrategy.test_safe_per_file_requires_human_review_human_call` (method) — Asserts a per-file `requires_human_review` flag alone escalates to HUMAN_CALL under safe strategy, naming the file in the reason. <!--#71cae7085adcbb9b-->

### `tests/test_merge_strategy_consolidation.py` (python) — Regression test suite for the merge-strategy consolidation (G7): it uses git/repo and ConflictFile/BatchContext helpers to verify safe mode escalates to a human MCP call after exhausting resolve iterations, strict mode routes conflicts straight to a human without invoking the LLM, the CLI and run_merge default to the 'fast' strategy, and the legacy 'robust'/'default' strategy names are rejected fail-fast both at MergeStrategy.from_str and the CLI. <!--#e882c152c3add2ac|dc1e0c223b3b838a-->
- `_git` (function) — Helper that runs a `git -C <path>` subprocess and returns the completed process with captured text output. <!--#8dcfd7712386df15-->
- `_init_repo` (function) — Helper that initializes a git repo at a path and sets a test user name/email. <!--#63bfb3f5ba420316-->
- `_write_with_markers` (function) — Helper that writes a file containing standard git conflict markers around the given ours/theirs content. <!--#689f68a75494ff1a-->
- `_make_conflict_file` (function) — Test helper that builds a minimal text `ConflictFile` for a given path and working-tree content, stubbing base/ours/theirs contents as empty while marking all three sides as existing. <!--#ddc22a9c552068db-->
- `_make_batch_context` (function) — Test helper that constructs a `BatchContext` with fixed placeholder branch names, SHAs and commit messages under `tmp_path`, parameterised only by the `MergeStrategy` under test. <!--#2079c8167f184408-->
- `test_safe_exhausts_iterations_escalates_to_human` (function) — Verifies that safe mode, when the LLM never clears markers, escalates to a human call after exhausting iterations while preserving conflict markers on disk. <!--#1d6e43bbb56f484b-->
- `test_strict_skips_llm_and_routes_to_human` (function) — Verifies that strict mode routes conflicts directly to a human call without ever invoking the LLM (zero iterations). <!--#19198f079fd16273-->
- `test_run_merge_default_strategy_is_fast` (function) — Asserts via inspect.signature that run_merge's strategy parameter defaults to 'fast'. <!--#505a108ea49d8e8f-->
- `test_cli_merge_defaults_to_fast` (function) — Runs `se3 merge feature` through the Typer CliRunner with run_merge stubbed, verifying the omitted --strategy resolves to strategy='fast'. <!--#bbcb767b55001918-->
- `test_legacy_robust_strategy_name_rejected` (function) — Asserts MergeStrategy.from_str('robust') raises ValueError whose message references both 'robust' and the replacement 'fast'. <!--#3ce35c9e3a8819e9-->
- `test_legacy_default_strategy_name_rejected` (function) — Asserts MergeStrategy.from_str('default') raises ValueError whose message references both 'default' and the replacement 'safe'. <!--#43db7f5baff01443-->
- `test_cli_rejects_robust_strategy` (function) — Verifies `se3 merge feature --strategy robust` exits non-zero without ever invoking run_merge (guarded by an asserting stub). <!--#f72b0068f84c1866-->
- `test_cli_rejects_default_strategy` (function) — Verifies `se3 merge feature --strategy default` exits non-zero without ever invoking run_merge (guarded by an asserting stub). <!--#e4621ca16e0b48c0-->

### `tests/test_merge_unlock.py` (python) — Test suite for merge-lock release: covers `inspect_lock` holder/staleness classification (missing, alive, dead PID, empty, corrupt, read-only), `break_lock_file` removal, `release_merge_lock` outcomes (`no_lock`, `released_stale`, `refused_alive`, `released_force`, `failed_remove`), and the `merge-unlock` CLI's `--force`/`-f` behaviour, foreign-machine holder reporting, and `_lock_busy_message` wording. <!--#42257013f9f84267|d2bf6a044e27907a-->
- `_lock_path` (function) — Helper returning the absolute merge-lock file path (`tianluo/state/merge.lock`) under a given project root. <!--#db4c4674fe3e9a27-->
- `_write_lock` (function) — Helper that creates the lock file with the given body content and returns its path. <!--#4a20343d55e0ce24-->
- `_dead_pid` (function) — Helper that scans downward from a large number to find a PID confirmed non-existent via `os.kill(pid, 0)` raising ESRCH. <!--#fde38f4d452aeeab-->
- `test_inspect_lock_missing_file` (function) — Asserts `inspect_lock` reports a missing lock as non-existent, holderless, and reclaimable (stale). <!--#8a000da44494f371-->
- `test_inspect_lock_alive_holder` (function) — Asserts `inspect_lock` recognizes a lock held by the live current process as alive and not stale. <!--#06604a0f76c53a6c-->
- `test_inspect_lock_dead_holder` (function) — Asserts `inspect_lock` treats a lock owned by a dead PID as not-alive and stale. <!--#3ea9cee0acd1c667-->
- `test_inspect_lock_empty_file_is_stale` (function) — Asserts an empty lock file is reported as existing but holderless and stale. <!--#9ceaee7d60ac0c2e-->
- `test_inspect_lock_corrupt_record` (function) — Asserts a non-numeric lock body is reported as corrupt, holderless, and stale. <!--#145a85cf4fabd8fd-->
- `test_inspect_lock_does_not_write` (function) — Asserts `inspect_lock` is read-only by verifying the lock file bytes are unchanged after inspection. <!--#f6c84c8238682557-->
- `test_break_lock_file_removes_existing` (function) — Asserts `break_lock_file` deletes an existing lock and returns True. <!--#774a993f5bfb8c9c-->
- `test_break_lock_file_noop_when_absent` (function) — Asserts `break_lock_file` returns False and is a no-op when no lock exists. <!--#0fffa971484c7f9c-->
- `test_release_no_lock` (function) — Asserts `release_merge_lock` returns the `no_lock` outcome with exit code 0 when no lock is present. <!--#da7f3c75b57e39e8-->
- `test_release_stale_dead_pid` (function) — Asserts a stale lock held by a dead PID is released (`released_stale`) without requiring `--force`. <!--#b7dc02044944394d-->
- `test_release_stale_no_pid` (function) — Asserts an empty (holderless) lock is released as stale without force. <!--#b6ad97ef2781937f-->
- `test_release_stale_corrupt` (function) — Asserts a corrupt lock record is released as stale, with the outcome flagging corruption. <!--#795092016b95b8d9-->
- `test_release_refused_when_alive_without_force` (function) — Asserts release is refused (`refused_alive`, nonzero exit, lock preserved) when a live process holds the lock and `--force` is absent. <!--#ecaf17f195d49934-->
- `test_release_force_removes_live_lock` (function) — Asserts `--force` releases a lock held by a live process, yielding `released_force` and removing the file. <!--#219aa438c6f6b448-->
- `_make_unremovable` (function) — Helper that strips write permission from the lock's parent directory so unlinking the file raises PermissionError. <!--#ff724d541bbdd637-->
- `_restore` (function) — Helper that restores normal (0o700) permissions on the lock's parent directory after an unremovable-file test. <!--#b369467d8e93b67e-->
- `test_release_stale_failed_remove_when_unlink_denied` (function) — Asserts a stale lock that cannot be unlinked yields `failed_remove`, nonzero exit, and the file remaining on disk. <!--#0d36005306b6a72c-->
- `test_release_force_failed_remove_when_unlink_denied` (function) — Asserts a forced release whose unlink is denied yields `failed_remove`, nonzero exit, and the file remaining. <!--#5840a05f6d4c480b-->
- `cli_project` (function) — A pytest fixture that monkeypatches tianluo.commands.run.get_project_root to return tmp_path, redirecting the CLI's project root at the test's temporary directory. <!--#ad7199c2a9839834-->
- `_run` (function) — A helper that invokes the tianluo CLI app with the given args via Click's CliRunner and returns the result. <!--#e45a6c74a63499fd-->
- `_flat` (function) — Helper that collapses rich-rendered newlines and spaces so output can be substring-matched. <!--#3f2ff121b29cf474-->
- `test_cli_no_lock_reports_and_exits_zero` (function) — Asserts the CLI reports no lock to release and exits 0 when none exists. <!--#4ba317c686c41159-->
- `test_cli_refuses_live_holder` (function) — Asserts the CLI refuses (nonzero exit) a live-held lock, printing the holder PID and a `--force` hint while preserving the file. <!--#f007af9f69db8fe7-->
- `test_cli_force_flag_releases_live_holder` (function) — Asserts `merge-unlock --force` releases a live-held lock, prints a WARNING, and removes the file. <!--#8dd64165bd391644-->
- `test_cli_short_force_flag` (function) — Asserts the short `-f` flag behaves like `--force` in releasing a live-held lock. <!--#b8716ef7108d0ab2-->
- `test_cli_stale_cleanup_without_force` (function) — Asserts the CLI cleans up a stale (dead-PID) lock without force, reporting "Released stale" and exiting 0. <!--#3a6792b68e9bccc2-->
- `test_cli_failed_remove_reports_error_and_nonzero` (function) — Asserts that when a stale lock cannot be unlinked, the CLI reports an ERROR, exits nonzero, and does not falsely claim the lock was released. <!--#f576f5430fb87325-->
- `_write_foreign_lock` (function) — Test helper that writes a merge.lock file under a project root holding a dead PID plus the FOREIGN_MACHINE id, via merge_lock._encode_holder_record, and returns its path. <!--#b1d2c734edf89381-->
- `test_cli_foreign_holder_names_the_machine_and_refuses` (function) — Asserts that `merge-unlock` on a lock held by another machine exits non-zero, names that machine in the output instead of the generic "holder alive" text, and leaves the lock file in place. <!--#a5a92d2f5a3beaea-->
- `test_cli_force_still_releases_a_foreign_holder` (function) — Asserts that `merge-unlock --force` remains the explicit escape hatch, removing a foreign-machine lock and exiting zero. <!--#de716705e8fc2de9-->
- `test_lock_busy_message_names_foreign_machine` (function) — Asserts that merge_cmd._lock_busy_message includes both the holding machine id and the holder PID when a MergeLockBusy carries a foreign holder_machine. <!--#50d7f7c632fded80-->
- `test_lock_busy_message_local_holder_uses_generic_text` (function) — Asserts that _lock_busy_message falls back to the plain `cli.merge.lock_busy` i18n string when holder_machine is None or equals the local stable_machine_id(). <!--#7d1fb4bf3c924ed0-->

### `tests/test_merge_version_aggregator.py` (python) — Unit tests for the merge orchestrator's SemVer version aggregator, covering max_bump selection, per-diff bump classification (including prerelease/build-metadata precedence rules), end-to-end branch bump inference from pyproject version diffs, and aggregate_and_apply's writing/committing/amending of the new version with rollback on failure, plus git-repo test helpers. <!--#1db7b1c4dfb2884d|9025a32a8658039c-->

- `_last_commit_files` (function) — Helper returning the list of files modified in the HEAD commit. <!--#8813dffb71f598b7-->
- `TestMaxBump` (class) — Test class verifying max_bump selects the highest bump level (defaulting to PATCH on empty input). <!--#bbde82e5b6be0dd9-->
  - `TestMaxBump.test_empty_list_returns_patch` (method) — Asserts max_bump of an empty list returns PATCH. <!--#2c6dd3fd43dc1606-->
  - `TestMaxBump.test_single_patch` (method) — Asserts max_bump of a single PATCH returns PATCH. <!--#fe4d3cd4ebfb5e31-->
  - `TestMaxBump.test_patch_plus_patch_plus_minor_returns_minor` (method) — Asserts max_bump of patch+patch+minor returns MINOR. <!--#631d31612562453e-->
  - `TestMaxBump.test_minor_plus_major_returns_major` (method) — Asserts max_bump of minor+major returns MAJOR. <!--#3ff3f9590e1de749-->
  - `TestMaxBump.test_any_with_major_returns_major` (method) — Asserts any bump set containing MAJOR returns MAJOR. <!--#26e49ed0ef7bd477-->
  - `TestMaxBump.test_only_minor` (method) — Asserts max_bump of only MINOR values returns MINOR. <!--#2802fe8d734cbcd8-->
- `TestDiffBump` (class) — Unit-test class exercising the `_diff_bump` helper across major/minor/patch/no-change/backward cases plus SemVer prerelease and build-metadata precedence edge cases. <!--#94d97059eaeb91e1-->
  - `TestDiffBump.test_major` (method) — Asserts `_diff_bump` returns `BumpType.MAJOR` when the branch version jumps from 1.2.3 to 2.0.0. <!--#ad51e8e53c522c09-->
  - `TestDiffBump.test_minor` (method) — Asserts `_diff_bump` returns `BumpType.MINOR` for a 1.2.3 → 1.3.0 change. <!--#29ba19d3dc2cb912-->
  - `TestDiffBump.test_patch` (method) — Asserts `_diff_bump` returns `BumpType.PATCH` for a 1.2.3 → 1.2.4 change. <!--#cc6fbf09c8132781-->
  - `TestDiffBump.test_no_change_returns_none` (method) — Asserts `_diff_bump` returns `None` when base and branch versions are identical. <!--#c86e408af1b3e85b-->
  - `TestDiffBump.test_backward_returns_none` (method) — Asserts `_diff_bump` returns `None` when the branch version is lower than the base. <!--#386ae07246cd0c44-->
  - `TestDiffBump.test_prerelease_to_release_returns_patch` (method) — Asserts a prerelease-to-release transition (4.5.0-alpha → 4.5.0) is treated as a PATCH per SemVer §11. <!--#f844f50930583dc4-->
  - `TestDiffBump.test_release_to_prerelease_returns_none` (method) — Asserts a release-to-prerelease step (4.5.0 → 4.5.0-alpha) counts as backward and returns `None`. <!--#98f28c6836dff513-->
  - `TestDiffBump.test_build_metadata_only_returns_none` (method) — Asserts build metadata (4.5.0 → 4.5.0+build.42) is ignored in precedence and returns `None`. <!--#9a39022fce4f7f00-->
  - `TestDiffBump.test_prerelease_bump_with_numeric_change` (method) — Asserts a numeric minor change dominates a prerelease difference (4.5.0-alpha → 4.6.0 = MINOR). <!--#4dfa5526dd61073e-->
- `TestInferResult` (class) — Test class verifying the InferResult dataclass holds a bump (possibly None) and a reason string. <!--#689b8efc432a3531-->

- `TestInferBranchBump` (class) — Test class for infer_branch_bump, deriving a branch's bump from the end-to-end pyproject version diff against a base ref across many scenarios. <!--#40030e1b34866b0f-->
