  - `TestInferBranchBump.test_minor_bump` (method) — Asserts a branch raising the version 4.4.0→4.5.0 infers MINOR. <!--#8a0b4318baf14b53-->
  - `TestInferBranchBump.test_major_bump` (method) — Asserts a branch raising the version 4.4.0→5.0.0 infers MAJOR. <!--#e238dd897fb34d56-->
  - `TestInferBranchBump.test_no_version_change_returns_none` (method) — Asserts a branch that doesn't advance the version infers None ('did not advance'). <!--#0681bce2837ccbc2-->
  - `TestInferBranchBump.test_no_pyproject_returns_none` (method) — Asserts a repo with no readable version infers None ('no readable version'). <!--#19831748b57c0ee8-->
  - `TestInferBranchBump.test_branch_lower_version_returns_none` (method) — Asserts a branch that lowers the version contributes no bump. <!--#3f09f829b94b303c-->
  - `TestInferBranchBump.test_end_to_end_diff_ignores_intermediate_bumps` (method) — Asserts only the merge-base-to-tip diff matters, ignoring intermediate in-branch bumps. <!--#106be7e155ca162d-->
  - `TestInferBranchBump.test_spec_example_branch_bumps` (method) — Asserts the spec example where branch B infers PATCH and branch C infers MINOR from their end-to-end diffs. <!--#c05e20444440e5b7-->
  - `TestInferBranchBump.test_prerelease_to_release_infers_patch` (method) — Asserts finalizing a prerelease on a branch infers PATCH. <!--#80a9a47ff0abcb30-->
  - `TestInferBranchBump.test_release_to_prerelease_no_bump` (method) — Asserts adding a prerelease suffix on a branch infers no bump. <!--#228bd9164d0bcfb0-->
  - `TestInferBranchBump.test_build_metadata_only_no_bump` (method) — Asserts a build-metadata-only change on a branch infers no bump. <!--#e2b027a6a8337d48-->
- `TestAggregateAndApply` (class) — Test class for `aggregate_and_apply`, covering bump aggregation, pyproject.toml amendment into the merge commit, and error/rollback paths for git add/amend failures and timeouts. <!--#ea1987761cae62e6-->
  - `TestAggregateAndApply._setup_repo_with_merge_commit` (method) — Helper creating a repo with a versioned pyproject and a merge-like commit available to amend. <!--#80ee109aef93f6fd-->
  - `TestAggregateAndApply.test_patch_patch_minor_bumps_to_4_5_0` (method) — Asserts aggregating patch+patch+minor on 4.4.0 produces and writes 4.5.0. <!--#cb2c1b0d88b26939-->
  - `TestAggregateAndApply.test_minor_major_bumps_to_2_0_0` (method) — Asserts aggregating minor+major on 1.2.3 produces and writes 2.0.0. <!--#8af6b1ce670db730-->
  - `TestAggregateAndApply.test_amend_includes_pyproject_in_last_commit` (method) — Asserts the amended HEAD commit includes pyproject.toml and changes the commit SHA. <!--#2712ce49d0c5da64-->
  - `TestAggregateAndApply.test_only_patch_bumps_patch` (method) — Asserts a sole PATCH bump on 4.4.0 yields 4.4.1. <!--#d80c7d6411e21151-->
  - `TestAggregateAndApply.test_empty_bumps_fails` (method) — Asserts an empty bump list fails with a 'no bumps' error. <!--#ba62232c2693a294-->
  - `TestAggregateAndApply.test_invalid_pre_merge_version_fails` (method) — Asserts an unparseable pre-merge version fails with an error. <!--#98dbe9df3f859adf-->
  - `TestAggregateAndApply.test_missing_pyproject_fails_gracefully` (method) — Asserts a missing pyproject.toml fails gracefully with an explanatory error. <!--#7f2e743b62874c92-->
  - `TestAggregateAndApply.test_amend_failure_rollback` (method) — Verifies that when `git commit --amend` fails, pyproject.toml is rolled back to its original version and the error surfaces the amend failure. <!--#9fe48b4daf3ef806-->
  - `TestAggregateAndApply.test_amend_failure_and_reset_also_fails` (method) — Verifies the combined error message reports both the amend failure and the subsequent `git reset HEAD` rollback failure. <!--#a3a8a2ffc3e500c3-->
  - `TestAggregateAndApply.test_git_add_failure_rollback` (method) — Verifies that a non-zero `git add pyproject.toml` triggers restoration of pyproject.toml and a failed result carrying the git error. <!--#d87c0e171c837a14-->
  - `TestAggregateAndApply.test_git_add_timeout_rollback` (method) — Verifies that a `TimeoutExpired` during `git add` rolls back pyproject.toml and reports a timeout failure. <!--#d0b0e82539279f6a-->
  - `TestAggregateAndApply.test_git_amend_timeout_rollback` (method) — Verifies that a `TimeoutExpired` during `git commit --amend` restores/unstages pyproject.toml and reports a timeout failure. <!--#47eb029a4ccd0927-->
  - `TestAggregateAndApply.test_spec_example_aggregate_to_4_7_0` (method) — Asserts the spec example max(PATCH,MINOR) applied to 4.6.0 yields 4.7.0. <!--#6c434dd46b0f53da-->
- `TestParsePyprojectVersion` (class) — Test class for _parse_pyproject_version, covering project/poetry precedence and TOML edge cases like multiline strings and inline arrays. <!--#5519dbd5c30df19e-->
  - `TestParsePyprojectVersion.test_simple_project_version` (method) — Asserts a simple [project] version is parsed correctly. <!--#bc271fb12539822d-->
  - `TestParsePyprojectVersion.test_poetry_version` (method) — Asserts a [tool.poetry] version is parsed when no [project] version exists. <!--#02525dcd6ad4e58d-->
  - `TestParsePyprojectVersion.test_project_takes_precedence_over_poetry` (method) — Asserts [project] version takes precedence over [tool.poetry]. <!--#64a4232df0aa02a5-->
  - `TestParsePyprojectVersion.test_multiline_string_with_bracket_not_section_boundary` (method) — Asserts a triple-quoted value containing `[` isn't mistaken for a section boundary. <!--#93a600019d39f0f2-->
  - `TestParsePyprojectVersion.test_single_quote_multiline_string_with_bracket` (method) — Asserts a single-quoted triple-string value with `[` is likewise handled correctly. <!--#d9d1f0a456adb7ca-->
  - `TestParsePyprojectVersion.test_no_version_returns_none` (method) — Asserts a section without a version field returns None. <!--#fa6c680b890c5cc0-->
  - `TestParsePyprojectVersion.test_inline_array_not_misread` (method) — Asserts an inline array value (e.g. keywords) doesn't prematurely terminate the section. <!--#6a55577431ca53c3-->
- `TestSliceToNextSection` (class) — Test class for _slice_to_next_section, which extracts a TOML section's body up to the next real section header. <!--#49cc12f4c4d2577a-->
  - `TestSliceToNextSection.test_finds_next_section` (method) — Asserts the slice stops at the next section header. <!--#937e0f815ec718b4-->
  - `TestSliceToNextSection.test_no_next_section_returns_rest` (method) — Asserts the slice returns the rest of the content when no further section exists. <!--#d76dcfd83a43b466-->
  - `TestSliceToNextSection.test_skips_bracket_inside_triple_quoted_string` (method) — Asserts brackets inside a triple-quoted string aren't treated as section boundaries. <!--#079a25348f1c6a4f-->
- `TestReadVersionAtRef` (class) — Test class for read_version_at_ref, which reads the pyproject version from a git ref's tree. <!--#4d294a036486ed0d-->
  - `TestReadVersionAtRef.test_reads_version_at_head` (method) — Asserts the version is read from pyproject.toml at the HEAD ref. <!--#ee254925fffbfa49-->
  - `TestReadVersionAtRef.test_returns_none_when_no_pyproject` (method) — Asserts None is returned when the ref has no pyproject.toml. <!--#7cfde47283d4fb9e-->
  - `TestReadVersionAtRef.test_returns_none_when_no_version_field` (method) — Asserts None is returned when pyproject.toml lacks a version field. <!--#cb58e18943420793-->
  - `TestReadVersionAtRef.test_reads_poetry_version` (method) — Asserts a poetry-style version is read at the ref. <!--#6dda63e605811c13-->
- `TestOrchestratorVersionAggregation` (class) — Integration tests that drive `MergeOrchestrator.execute` over throwaway git repos to verify cross-branch version aggregation — that the max bump across merged branches (patch/minor/major) is applied to `pyproject.toml`, that aggregation is skipped when no branch changed the version or when a merge ends in HUMAN_CALL, and that the spec's 4.4.0/4.4.1/4.6.0 → 4.7.0 scenario holds end to end. <!--#f84ea54463e771e7-->
  - `TestOrchestratorVersionAggregation.test_three_branches_bump_to_4_5_0` (method) — Asserts merging two patch-fallback branches plus a minor branch bumps 4.4.0 to 4.5.0. <!--#39896a4183f603b1-->
  - `TestOrchestratorVersionAggregation.test_no_version_change_skips_aggregation` (method) — Asserts aggregation is skipped (final_version None) when no branch changed the version, while the merge still commits. <!--#3c3d712444da384c-->
  - `TestOrchestratorVersionAggregation.test_minor_plus_major_bumps_to_2_0_0` (method) — Asserts a patch-fallback plus a major branch bumps 1.2.3 to 2.0.0. <!--#9e6acf47286aca61-->
  - `TestOrchestratorVersionAggregation.test_human_call_skips_aggregation` (method) — Asserts that when a conflicting branch merge yields LOW confidence (mocked `ConflictResolver.resolve`) and the run goes pending-human, the orchestrator reports `version_aggregation_skipped` with no `final_version` and leaves `pyproject.toml` at its original version. <!--#1b68e51530d27b47-->
  - `TestOrchestratorVersionAggregation.test_conflict_reject_skips_aggregation` (method) — Verifies that under the `safe` strategy a failed LLM conflict resolution escalates to pending-human and skips aggregation with the version preserved. <!--#db9a7018110e993f-->
  - `TestOrchestratorVersionAggregation.test_no_pyproject_skips_aggregation` (method) — Asserts a repo without pyproject.toml still merges while silently skipping aggregation. <!--#b8daba6bdf561de1-->
  - `TestOrchestratorVersionAggregation.test_partial_failure_preserves_version` (method) — Verifies that when a later branch merge fails, the version is not further bumped and aggregation is reported as skipped. <!--#95ea7c2ba13f6198-->
  - `TestOrchestratorVersionAggregation.test_aggregate_result_dataclass` (method) — Asserts the AggregateResult dataclass default field values. <!--#12816f035f01c2d4-->
  - `TestOrchestratorVersionAggregation.test_orchestrator_passes_merge_base_to_infer_branch_bump` (method) — Verifies the orchestrator computes the correct merge-base SHA and passes it as `base_ref` into `infer_branch_bump`. <!--#49a472859216342b-->
  - `TestOrchestratorVersionAggregation.test_merge_base_failure_skips_bump_inference` (method) — Verifies that a failing `git merge-base` skips bump inference/aggregation while the merge itself still succeeds. <!--#6d246e4c311126f2-->
  - `TestOrchestratorVersionAggregation.test_end_to_end_spec_example_4_7_0` (method) — End-to-end check of the spec example where the base branch has advanced to 4.6.0 after a PATCH branch (4.4.1) and a MINOR branch (4.6.0 via noisy intermediate bumps) were cut, asserting that merging both — with the conflict resolver mocked to keep "ours" — produces a `minor` bump to 4.7.0 on disk and in the report. <!--#8df8b91a41ed20ff-->
- `TestAmendFalseOrchestratorPath` (class) — Integration-test class for the `amend=False` code path used when HEAD is published, verifying the version bump lands as a new fixup commit on top of a preserved merge commit and passes the post-aggregation topology check. <!--#097fe32db5079d98-->
  - `TestAmendFalseOrchestratorPath.test_aggregate_and_apply_amend_false_succeeds` (method) — Directly verifies `aggregate_and_apply(..., amend=False)` creates a new commit while preserving the original merge commit as HEAD^1. <!--#92dcac23b4c8ffd7-->
  - `TestAmendFalseOrchestratorPath.test_orchestrator_amend_false_preserves_merge_commit` (method) — Verifies that with `_is_head_published` mocked True the orchestrator's amend=False path leaves a single-parent bump commit as HEAD atop the multi-parent merge commit at HEAD^1. <!--#97b107f39ddb9dbc-->
  - `TestAmendFalseOrchestratorPath.test_orchestrator_amend_false_post_topology_check_passes` (method) — Regression guard confirming the post-aggregation `assert_head_is_merge_commit(allow_fixup_parent=True)` accepts the amend=False fixup layout without failing execution. <!--#c4623caf54b18f5e-->

### `tests/test_migrate.py` (python) — Test suite for the `luo migrate` command and its first spec-to-new-system migrator, covering the migrator registry (register/list/get with duplicate rejection), CLI wiring, and the fault-tolerant migration pipeline that writes the charter exactly once, injects colocated why-comments, builds the authoritative code-index, deletes salvaged specs only after success, and idempotently rewrites .gitignore with default-deny whitelists for tracked top-level paths. <!--#c9ebcea2cff7e4d8|4ef8b1d225aebcd4-->
- `_git` (function) — Helper that runs a git subcommand in the given project root, raising on failure. <!--#881bf8d1b379498d-->
- `_init_git_project` (function) — Helper that initializes a git repo with a test user identity in the given root. <!--#6aabffa4b0cbf3dc-->
- `FakeSummarizer` (class) — Deterministic stand-in code-index summarizer that maps each target to a fixed `S:<name>` string instead of calling the LLM. <!--#35adba97abbabfe3-->
  - `FakeSummarizer.__call__` (method) — Returns a dict mapping each target's id to a deterministic `S:<name>` summary. <!--#1d61334eb28ddb92-->
- `_make_salvager` (function) — Factory returning a fake salvager callable that ignores its input and yields a fixed `SalvageResult` (charter body + colocations). <!--#59b18ab05a11927b-->
- `project` (function) — A pytest fixture that builds a committed git project containing a base spec, two non-base specs (one `_changelog` to be skipped), a source file, and a default-deny `.gitignore`, returning its root path. <!--#cb8e085c826880a5-->
- `test_registry_has_first_migrator` (function) — Asserts the `spec-to-new-system` migrator is registered and bound to `run_spec_to_new_system`. <!--#cd2233b643f97a14-->
- `test_registry_register_and_duplicate_rejection` (function) — Verifies migrators can be registered and that re-registering a duplicate id raises `ValueError`. <!--#c9c23b945b202a87-->
- `test_list_migrators_sorted` (function) — Asserts `list_migrators` returns migrators ordered by id. <!--#a17aab8ec2db6e4a-->
- `test_cli_registers_migrate` (function) — Asserts that the `migrate` command group is registered on `cli.app` via Typer's `add_typer`. <!--#2e158c3f05498f8e-->
- `test_migrate_list_command_runs` (function) — Checks that `migrate list` exits 0 and lists the `spec-to-new-system` migrator. <!--#f940357e936fa538-->
- `test_migrate_run_unknown_id_errors` (function) — Verifies `migrate run` with an unknown migrator id exits with code 1. <!--#74122669765932a3-->
- `test_full_migration_happy_path` (function) — End-to-end test that a successful spec-to-new-system migration writes the charter, colocates why-comments into source (still parseable), builds `code-index.md` without a JSON sidecar, deletes `specs`, and rewrites `.gitignore`. <!--#8512be0bb6c1a739-->
- `test_charter_written_exactly_once` (function) — Monkeypatches `Path.write_text` to assert the charter is assembled in memory and written exactly once (no overwrite window). <!--#c635b97250aa4ac2-->
- `test_specs_kept_when_charter_fails` (function) — Verifies that when the salvager raises, the charter step is FAIL, spec deletion is SKIP, specs survive, and the report is not-ok. <!--#8759dfd93a5159ff-->
- `test_no_delete_specs_flag_keeps_specs` (function) — Confirms that passing `delete_specs=False` keeps the specs directory and marks the delete step SKIP while the report stays ok. <!--#52e38196a1e14732-->
- `test_missing_colocation_target_is_skipped` (function) — Verifies that when one colocation target is missing, the real one applies, the ghost is noted as skipped, and the incomplete salvage keeps the specs corpus. <!--#af8ed012eab6b023-->
- `test_all_colocations_skipped_keeps_specs` (function) — Confirms that if every colocation target is unresolvable, the spec corpus is kept and the delete step is SKIP since no code-bound intent was salvaged. <!--#d5def2c4ed77e240-->
- `test_gitignore_rewrite_idempotent` (function) — Checks that `_rewrite_gitignore` adds the new whitelist and removes `!/tianluo/specs/` on first run and is a no-op on the second. <!--#8fe94998d67850b1-->
- `test_gitignore_whitelists_after_se3_anchor` (function) — Verifies the rewritten `.gitignore` places the tianluo whitelists immediately after the `/tianluo/*` anchor and drops `!/tianluo/specs/`. <!--#5cba8ef7fe91e8ff-->
- `_check_ignored` (function) — Test helper that runs `git check-ignore` in a repo and returns whether a given relative path is ignored by the current .gitignore. <!--#dde6b71d331773dd-->
- `legacy_project` (function) — A pytest fixture building a committed legacy git project with tracked top-level files/dirs and a flat (non-default-deny) `.gitignore`, representing the shape the migration must protect. <!--#5f522bf60f51b0c0-->
- `test_root_deny_protects_tracked_toplevel` (function) — Verifies that introducing a `/*` default-deny whitelists every tracked top-level path (files as `!/name`, dirs as `!/name/`) so none are silently dropped, while a new stray root file is still ignored. <!--#9aa3c31e48c4a518-->
- `test_root_deny_idempotent` (function) — Verifies that running `_rewrite_gitignore` a second time reports no changes and leaves the .gitignore content byte-identical. <!--#d77ea16c2aa27d1b-->
- `test_root_deny_skipped_when_ls_files_unavailable` (function) — Confirms that when `git ls-files` fails (non-git dir), `_tracked_toplevel_whitelists` returns None and no `/*` deny is added, degrading safely without raising. <!--#c59d5114b27f7549-->
- `test_root_deny_skipped_when_ls_files_raises` (function) — Verifies that an unexpected subprocess failure during whitelist discovery is swallowed so `/*` is not added and non-git edits still run without raising. <!--#7383a97ffdfd29c4-->
- `test_load_spec_corpus_splits_and_skips` (function) — Checks that `_load_spec_corpus` returns the base spec text and only the non-base spec ids, skipping the `_changelog` directory. <!--#cf9b5886173f5051-->
- `test_colocation_preserves_shebang` (function) — Asserts inserting a why-comment keeps a script's shebang on the first line while still adding the why marker. <!--#8ed6c42f2d73dcf6-->

### `tests/test_migrate_rename.py` (python) — Pytest suite for the 'rename-to-tianluo' migrator (issue #270), exercising the one-shot se3/ -> tianluo/ layout and config-file rename via a legacy-project fixture — covering migrator registration, the end-to-end happy-path rename with history-preserving commit and .gitignore rewrite, idempotence, and preflight/dirty-index/existing-dir guard skips. <!--#66d24cc788405016|dd92862613ab57c6-->
- `_git` (function) — Test helper that runs a git subcommand against a given repo root via subprocess and returns the captured, check=True CompletedProcess. <!--#a76d8e522388f107-->
- `legacy_project` (function) — Pytest fixture that builds and commits a legacy-layout project (se3/ runtime dir, se3.yaml/se3.local.yaml, matching .gitignore) plus untracked runtime state, returning its root path. <!--#2eb482356dcaf505-->
- `test_registered` (function) — Asserts the 'rename-to-tianluo' migrator is registered and its run attribute is the run_rename_to_tianluo function. <!--#dd6596fc1b4e6453-->
- `test_full_rename_happy_path` (function) — End-to-end test that run_rename_to_tianluo moves the se3/ layout and yaml files to tianluo names, carries untracked state along, rewrites .gitignore, and produces a single history-preserving rename commit with a clean working tree. <!--#0a553ffaf243b0fb-->
- `test_idempotent_second_run` (function) — Verifies a second run_rename_to_tianluo invocation succeeds but SKIPs the dir/yaml renames and commit, leaving still just the one migration commit. <!--#a1b1a22773fb02c9-->
- `test_dirty_index_renames_but_skips_commit` (function) — Verifies that with unrelated staged changes present the rename still runs (OK) but the commit step is SKIPped with a 'staged changes' note and nothing is committed. <!--#48141fd9af42b707-->
- `test_non_git_directory_fails_preflight` (function) — Verifies that running the migrator on a non-git directory fails at the preflight step (report not ok, first result preflight/FAIL). <!--#30eb80cd5fbf0d6a-->
- `test_existing_tianluo_dir_skips_dir_rename` (function) — Verifies that when a tianluo/ directory already exists the rename-dir step is SKIPped. <!--#1603980b544f2e4b-->

### `tests/test_preset_loader.py` (python) — Pytest suite for the preset loader, covering built-in preset registration and runtime resolution from package data (including the assertion that no packaged prompt still references the retired spec-corpus mirrors), project-level overrides via tianluo/prompts plus tianluo.yaml type metadata, error paths for unknown presets and missing prompt files, and list_presets enumeration across both layers. <!--#bf9f92567f5427cd|7383ebc8d3b4c19e-->
- `project_root` (function) — Pytest fixture returning a fresh tmp_path to stand in as an isolated project root directory. <!--#8cf80cae6e4c6d2a-->
- `_write_project_preset` (function) — Test helper that writes a project-level preset by creating tianluo/prompts/<name>.md and (optionally) a tianluo.yaml entry declaring its feature type and prompt_file path. <!--#04a0f3e7a3981650-->
- `TestBuiltinLayer` (class) — Test class asserting the built-in preset layer works: `doc-sync` is registered as a `feature` at `LAYER_BUILTIN`, its body is resolved at runtime from package data without copying anything into the project tree, and no built-in prompt still references the retired spec-corpus directories. <!--#aeb8275d83c77d63-->
  - `TestBuiltinLayer.test_builtin_doc_sync_present` (method) — Asserts the built-in 'doc-sync' preset appears in the loaded registry with the builtin layer and 'feature' type. <!--#dc0db7a70c2ac98b-->
  - `TestBuiltinLayer.test_builtin_read_at_runtime_from_package` (method) — Asserts resolve('doc-sync') returns the built-in-layer feature prompt from package data (non-empty, mentions README) without ever creating tianluo/prompts in the project. <!--#0e440b8add873a60-->
  - `TestBuiltinLayer.test_builtin_prompts_carry_no_spec_corpus_references` (method) — Resolves every preset in `preset_loader._BUILTIN_PRESET_METADATA` and asserts none of the packaged prompt bodies mention the retired `tianluo/specs` or `se3/specs` mirrors. <!--#c6714228405c3cb0-->
- `TestProjectOverride` (class) — Test class covering project-level preset resolution: overriding a same-named built-in, registering a bare .md without YAML using the default type, and applying an explicit type from tianluo.yaml. <!--#4d3072401d54e44b-->
  - `TestProjectOverride.test_project_overrides_builtin_same_name` (method) — Asserts a project-level 'doc-sync' file shadows the built-in, resolving to the project layer and its content. <!--#21633430081225e2-->
  - `TestProjectOverride.test_project_preset_without_yaml_uses_default_type` (method) — Asserts a project prompt file with no tianluo.yaml metadata still resolves at LAYER_PROJECT using preset_loader.DEFAULT_PRESET_TYPE. <!--#6ed395eb07891a8a-->
  - `TestProjectOverride.test_yaml_type_override` (method) — Asserts a tianluo.yaml preset entry declaring type: bugfix causes resolve to return that type at LAYER_PROJECT. <!--#1d8cf975aff835a8-->
- `TestErrors` (class) — Test class covering error paths: an unknown preset raises PresetNotFoundError listing available presets, and a YAML-declared preset with a missing prompt file raises PresetError. <!--#9d664f966616fa48-->
  - `TestErrors.test_unknown_preset_lists_available` (method) — Asserts resolving an unknown preset raises PresetNotFoundError whose message lists available presets including 'doc-sync'. <!--#851b090d61dd5b59-->
  - `TestErrors.test_missing_prompt_file_raises` (method) — Asserts resolving a preset declared in tianluo.yaml whose prompt_file does not exist raises PresetError mentioning the preset name and 'missing'. <!--#31302b92d980bb1d-->
- `TestListPresets` (class) — Test class verifying list_presets enumerates both built-in and project layers in sorted order. <!--#0e86d9b438d77794-->
  - `TestListPresets.test_list_includes_both_layers` (method) — Asserts list_presets returns both the built-in 'doc-sync' and a project-only preset, name-sorted with correct layer tags. <!--#3719eb084e0f2581-->

### `tests/test_pricing.py` (python) — Unit tests for the token-pricing subsystem, covering the built-in `PricingCatalog`'s completeness and provenance (Anthropic cache rates as input multipliers, unknown OpenAI cache-creation rates, no entry for subscription-billed `codex`), `canonicalize_pricing_model` alias and dated-snapshot normalization, `estimate_cost` arithmetic with its unknown-rather-than-zero discipline, and `with_overrides` merge/validation/round-trip behavior. <!--#a2550c981a9bd816|9705381287935318-->
- `TestBuiltinCatalog` (class) — Tests that the built-in `PricingCatalog` is complete and honest — Anthropic rows price all six `TokenCategory` values with cache rates as fixed input multipliers, OpenAI rows leave cache-creation unknown, every entry carries version/source/effective date, and subscription-billed `codex` has no entry at all. <!--#d2f972ec2116bbde-->
  - `TestBuiltinCatalog.test_anthropic_entries_price_all_six_categories` (method) — Asserts each built-in Claude model entry exists and returns a non-None `price_for()` value for every `TokenCategory`. <!--#8a90cfad99eeb5ca-->
  - `TestBuiltinCatalog.test_anthropic_cache_prices_are_input_multipliers` (method) — Checks the `claude-opus-5` cache prices are the published multiples of `uncached_input` (0.10x read, 1.25x creation/5m, 2.0x 1h). <!--#fe4028aaaaa1e602-->
  - `TestBuiltinCatalog.test_openai_entries_leave_cache_creation_unknown` (method) — Verifies the `gpt-5` entry prices input and cache reads but leaves all cache-creation fields None, since OpenAI publishes no such rates. <!--#f4385327c7468134-->
  - `TestBuiltinCatalog.test_every_entry_records_version_source_and_date` (method) — Asserts every built-in catalog entry carries `catalog_version` equal to `PRICING_CATALOG_VERSION` plus a non-empty `source` and `effective_date`. <!--#724f49e1dc1ae957-->
  - `TestBuiltinCatalog.test_codex_has_no_per_token_price` (method) — Asserts `codex` has no catalog entry, so its cost resolves as unknown rather than zero. <!--#aaebb7b35eed1030-->
- `TestModelAliases` (class) — Tests `canonicalize_pricing_model` name normalization — case/whitespace-insensitive aliases, unmappable inputs (empty, None, env-var placeholders, bare date suffix) yielding None, and dated snapshot ids collapsing to their base model row for pricing. <!--#05124abeb05e8750-->
  - `TestModelAliases.test_alias_normalizes_to_canonical` (method) — Parametrized check that aliases differing by case, spacing, or short form normalize to the canonical model name. <!--#4b1e89f017d2ad34-->
  - `TestModelAliases.test_unmappable_names_stay_unknown` (method) — Parametrized check that empty, None, and unexpanded env-var model names normalize to None instead of a bogus key. <!--#3ec0a17058dd95fa-->
  - `TestModelAliases.test_unknown_model_has_no_builtin_entry` (method) — Confirms a well-formed but uncatalogued name normalizes to itself (usable as an override key) yet resolves to no built-in price. <!--#a5e46ecb4b393ad4-->
  - `TestModelAliases.test_dated_snapshot_id_normalizes_to_base_model` (method) — Parametrized check that dated snapshot ids reported by runner stream events strip their date and map to the base model that owns the price row. <!--#f73816bca49226e5-->
  - `TestModelAliases.test_dated_snapshot_id_resolves_to_catalog_price` (method) — Verifies the dated ids emitted by the usage fixtures resolve to real catalog entries with the expected base model and rates, so they don't count as unknown models. <!--#4f00e1ebfe0f479b-->
  - `TestModelAliases.test_dated_unknown_base_stays_unknown` (method) — Confirms a dated id with an uncatalogued base normalizes to that base name but still resolves to no price. <!--#fec1ddbbfc4e0894-->
  - `TestModelAliases.test_pure_date_suffix_is_unmappable` (method) — Asserts a name consisting only of a date suffix normalizes to None. <!--#750959c0434996dd-->
- `TestEstimateCost` (class) — Tests `estimate_cost` arithmetic and its unknown-vs-zero discipline — per-million unit pricing, separate cached/uncached input rates, and None results (with reasons or `unknown_categories`) for empty usage, unknown models, missing cache-TTL prices, and the logical-input aggregate. <!--#83a0502ed435e6c8-->
  - `TestEstimateCost.test_one_million_tokens_costs_the_unit_price` (method) — Asserts one million input plus one million output tokens costs exactly the per-million unit prices and is flagged `is_estimated`. <!--#6aade9e11fc7fb71-->
  - `TestEstimateCost.test_cached_and_uncached_input_are_priced_separately` (method) — Asserts uncached input, cache reads, and 5-minute cache creation each price at their own rate rather than a blended input rate. <!--#0a864fdf74c12232-->
  - `TestEstimateCost.test_no_tokens_is_not_a_zero_cost` (method) — Asserts empty token usage yields a None cost with reason `"no token usage"` instead of 0.0. <!--#2bfb4a6ea7728645-->
  - `TestEstimateCost.test_unknown_model_is_unknown_not_zero` (method) — Asserts a None price entry yields a None cost with reason `"unknown model"`. <!--#89c32af91501f735-->
  - `TestEstimateCost.test_missing_cache_ttl_price_is_unknown_not_partial` (method) — Asserts nonzero tokens in an unpriced category make the whole estimate None and record that category in `unknown_categories`, rather than returning a partial sum. <!--#b20b61dbf4918b3f-->
  - `TestEstimateCost.test_zero_token_unknown_category_does_not_block` (method) — Asserts a zero-token unpriced category is ignored so the remaining priced tokens still produce a cost. <!--#f89c33655dacda13-->
  - `TestEstimateCost.test_estimate_never_prices_logical_input` (method) — Asserts the aggregate `logical_input` key carries no price, so asking for it returns None instead of a guessed cost. <!--#70fb79e1e158703b-->
- `TestOverrides` (class) — Tests `PricingCatalog.with_overrides` — merging by canonical name while preserving untouched categories, friendly category aliases, `PricingOverrideError` on negative/non-numeric/non-mapping values, warn-and-skip for unknown category keys, new price rows from unknown model keys, and `to_dict`/`from_dict` round-tripping. <!--#ddbe3a378127cfbc-->
  - `TestOverrides.test_override_merges_by_canonical_model` (method) — Asserts an alias-keyed override applies to the canonical entry, leaves untouched categories at built-in values, tags the source as an override, and emits no warnings. <!--#7f0b6235c3c6e692-->
  - `TestOverrides.test_override_accepts_friendly_category_keys` (method) — Asserts user-facing keys `input` and `cache_write` map onto the `uncached_input` and `cache_creation` fields. <!--#fa1c4aa50648df9c-->
  - `TestOverrides.test_non_negative_validation_rejects_bad_values` (method) — Parametrized check that negative, boolean, and string price values raise `PricingOverrideError`. <!--#2b3a9b8350af15d8-->
  - `TestOverrides.test_non_mapping_model_entry_raises` (method) — Asserts a scalar in place of a per-model category mapping raises `PricingOverrideError`. <!--#a785eac330e63612-->
  - `TestOverrides.test_unknown_model_key_defines_a_new_entry` (method) — Asserts an override key unknown to the built-in table creates a new price row silently rather than being dropped or warned about. <!--#9a4d03d1dc309363-->
  - `TestOverrides.test_unknown_category_key_warns_and_is_skipped` (method) — Asserts an unrecognized category key is skipped with a warning naming that key. <!--#19cc2a7c5e250b89-->
  - `TestOverrides.test_new_model_entry_created_from_override` (method) — Asserts an override-created entry holds exactly the supplied prices and leaves untouched categories None rather than guessed. <!--#00e5ddaf191f7762-->
  - `TestOverrides.test_catalog_dict_round_trip` (method) — Asserts `PricingCatalog.from_dict(catalog.to_dict())` preserves version, entry set, and individual entry equality. <!--#129fe3b4b6f3769b-->
- `TestPricingConfig` (class) — Tests `load_pricing_catalog` / `PricingConfig` reading the `pricing:` section of a project `tianluo.yaml` — falling back to the built-in catalog when absent, applying valid overrides, logging and dropping only the invalid entries, and warning on a non-mapping section. <!--#2371b64efa6e860c-->
  - `TestPricingConfig._write_yaml` (method) — Helper that writes the given YAML text to `tianluo.yaml` under `tmp_path` and returns that directory. <!--#90c7db8b0f12a910-->
  - `TestPricingConfig.test_load_without_pricing_section_returns_builtin` (method) — Asserts a config with no `pricing:` section loads the unmodified built-in catalog. <!--#1fa79a2ba4e26a23-->
  - `TestPricingConfig.test_load_project_override` (method) — Asserts `pricing.models` entries in the project YAML override the corresponding built-in prices. <!--#3132c485415669a4-->
  - `TestPricingConfig.test_invalid_override_drops_only_that_entry` (method) — Asserts an invalid model override is logged and discarded (reverting to the built-in price) while a valid sibling override still applies. <!--#8423bf60d9cdd0dc-->
  - `TestPricingConfig.test_non_mapping_section_warns_and_returns_builtin` (method) — Asserts a `pricing:` section that is a list logs a warning and leaves the built-in catalog intact. <!--#0fa3294ec5332382-->
  - `TestPricingConfig.test_pricing_config_dataclass_empty_default` (method) — Asserts a default-constructed `PricingConfig` has no overrides and builds a catalog at `PRICING_CATALOG_VERSION`. <!--#533f83ae7b8edc81-->

### `tests/test_prompt_accuracy_discipline.py` (python) — Regression tests that lock down prompt wording discipline: the ACCURACY DISCIPLINE section must exist, be byte-identical, state all four rules, and sit right after the HARD INVARIANT block in both INITIAL_DISCOVERY_PROMPT and CONTINUE_DISCOVERY_PROMPT, and the parallel-safety test convention (DEFAULT_PARALLEL_SAFE_TESTS_CONVENTION) must cover its required points and be carried by both the `luo init` charter template and the degraded `luo migrate` fallback charter. <!--#8783fcc7f1f9cbe6|15144d4ad8281ac3-->
- `_extract_section` (function) — Test helper that slices the single ACCURACY DISCIPLINE section (heading through the next blank line) out of a discovery prompt, asserting the heading occurs exactly once. <!--#02b2794286009d97-->
- `test_both_discovery_prompts_carry_the_accuracy_section` (function) — Asserts both the initial and continue discovery prompts still contain an ACCURACY DISCIPLINE section. <!--#4adfb4ec74f79949-->
- `test_accuracy_section_is_identical_in_both_prompts` (function) — Guards against one-sided edits by asserting the extracted ACCURACY DISCIPLINE section is byte-identical between INITIAL_DISCOVERY_PROMPT and CONTINUE_DISCOVERY_PROMPT. <!--#d737448eaeb0b2fb-->
- `test_accuracy_section_states_all_four_rules` (function) — Semantic spot-check that the section still expresses all four accuracy rules, asserting on the load-bearing tokens of each rather than whole sentences. <!--#225a03f0f7ed6d69-->
- `test_accuracy_section_sits_next_to_the_hard_invariant` (function) — Asserts the ACCURACY DISCIPLINE section stays immediately after the HARD INVARIANT block in both prompts, with no other section slipping in between. <!--#516e6bc98d83c136-->
- `test_parallel_safety_convention_covers_the_three_required_points` (function) — Checks DEFAULT_PARALLEL_SAFE_TESTS_CONVENTION mentions its required points (并行安全, 执行顺序, 全局状态, 唯一路径). <!--#6ddcd0abc95b48d0-->
- `test_init_scaffolded_charter_carries_the_convention` (function) — Verifies the charter template rendered by `luo init` embeds the parallel-safety test convention. <!--#79b58c2acb17bfcd-->
- `test_migrate_fallback_charter_carries_the_convention` (function) — Verifies the degraded `luo migrate` fallback charter (used when the LLM call fails) still carries the parallel-safety test convention. <!--#c72808e4f3db6673-->

### `tests/test_prompt_history.py` (python) — Unit tests for tianluo.engine.prompt_history covering get_prompt_history's creation of the tianluo/history/ directory and a persistent, idempotent FileHistory, plus _truncate_history's trimming to the most recent MAX_ENTRIES while handling multiline entries and missing/empty files. <!--#80db3393aed5685b|458619e1b9722c9e-->
- `test_get_prompt_history_creates_directory_and_returns_file_history` (function) — Test verifying that get_prompt_history creates the tianluo/history/ directory, returns a prompt_toolkit FileHistory, and that storing an entry writes the HISTORY_FILENAME file. <!--#52bc0184cb6b2d33-->
- `test_get_prompt_history_idempotent` (function) — Verifies get_prompt_history can be called repeatedly without error, each returning a FileHistory. <!--#1f6fcdc3a3b6a98d-->
- `test_get_prompt_history_preserves_existing_entries` (function) — Test verifying that get_prompt_history loads pre-existing entries from an on-disk history file, so entries persist across separate FileHistory instances. <!--#5221868818ec1a69-->
- `test_truncate_history_no_op_when_under_limit` (function) — Confirms _truncate_history leaves all entries intact when the count is at or below max_entries. <!--#571ec19d683f5b5c-->
- `test_truncate_history_keeps_last_n_entries` (function) — Confirms _truncate_history retains only the most recent max_entries entries and drops older ones. <!--#ef83236fa7ff4bb3-->
- `test_truncate_history_preserves_multiline_entries` (function) — Verifies _truncate_history treats multiline entries as single units when trimming to max_entries. <!--#7fbbe7dee9feb5d1-->
- `test_truncate_history_no_op_on_missing_file` (function) — Ensures _truncate_history does not raise when the target history file does not exist. <!--#e16ec4109387cbaf-->
- `test_truncate_history_no_op_on_empty_file` (function) — Ensures _truncate_history leaves an empty history file unchanged. <!--#d05aedd8d87ed270-->

### `tests/test_protocol_history.py` (python) — Unit tests for the daemon/server wire protocol module, pinning PROTOCOL_VERSION at "7", asserting each message type is registered in the correct direction table, and round-tripping the history index/request/data, spawn-flow (discover, resume_flow_id, implementation_strategy), and issue-command builders through encode/decode — including additive-field omission and ProtocolError handling for unknown types and invalid history modes. <!--#73d69a587f1b11a4|0ffc376a8b05e567-->
- `test_protocol_version_current` (function) — Pins the daemon protocol handshake revision at `"9"`, with a comment log of what each revision added (keepalive/index-delta/detail, presence, upload, fetch, spawn strategy fields, and the history step-window channel) so version bumps are deliberate. <!--#41316e5f940ca414-->
- `test_history_message_types_registered` (function) — Verifies the history index/data/request message types are registered in the correct daemon/server direction tables and the all-types set. <!--#98449cc460ce40f9-->
- `test_history_index_request_type_registered` (function) — Checks the history-index-request type is server-to-daemon only and never sent back to the server. <!--#fe65f847ae6110c0-->
- `test_make_history_index_request_round_trip` (function) — Confirms make_history_index_request produces an empty-payload re-push trigger that survives encode/decode. <!--#ef2bd936d51d230e-->
- `test_make_history_index_round_trip` (function) — Confirms make_history_index serializes a session list and round-trips it through encode/decode unchanged. <!--#64643c014944da17-->
- `test_make_history_request_full_snapshot` (function) — Verifies make_history_request without a cursor yields a full-snapshot request carrying flow_id, project_root, and an empty cursor. <!--#2b4eec0f25eb436d-->
- `test_make_history_request_with_cursor` (function) — Verifies make_history_request preserves a per-stage byte-offset cursor through the round-trip. <!--#f67024e99736f136-->
- `test_make_history_data_full_round_trip` (function) — Confirms make_history_data in FULL mode round-trips flow_id, mode, records, and an empty cursor. <!--#20941efe2e81108b-->
- `test_make_history_data_append_with_cursor` (function) — Confirms make_history_data in APPEND mode round-trips records, the advancing cursor, and the seq number. <!--#f5bca4b43def2be4-->
- `test_make_history_data_rejects_bad_mode` (function) — Asserts make_history_data raises ProtocolError when given an invalid history mode. <!--#eb6b0938307aedd1-->
- `test_decode_unknown_type_raises_protocol_error` (function) — Asserts decode rejects an unrecognized message type with ProtocolError rather than crashing. <!--#6460f879cf60220a-->
- `test_decode_unknown_type_is_catchable` (function) — Shows known frames decode while unknown ones raise a catchable ProtocolError, enabling forward/backward peer tolerance. <!--#4c2d88e7a8fada6b-->
- `test_make_spawn_flow_discover_defaults_false` (function) — Verifies make_spawn_flow sets the discover field to False by default and round-trips it. <!--#4b85f3c1b0ebd829-->
- `test_make_spawn_flow_discover_true` (function) — Verifies make_spawn_flow with discover=True round-trips the discover flag and the task description. <!--#71786b5aac22427d-->
- `test_issue_command_type_registered` (function) — Test verifying that the MSG_ISSUE_COMMAND message type is registered in protocol.SERVER_TO_DAEMON and ALL_MESSAGE_TYPES but absent from DAEMON_TO_SERVER. <!--#30afdbe9a17d53b3-->
- `test_make_issue_command_create_round_trip` (function) — Test that protocol.make_issue_command builds a 'create' issue-command message whose payload survives a JSON encode/decode round trip with all fields (operation, project_root, description, title, priority, type, tags) intact. <!--#d0c98fa50f42ce6f-->
- `test_make_issue_command_edit_round_trip` (function) — Confirms make_issue_command for an edit operation round-trips issue_id and description while omitting empty fields. <!--#020423f3b51e05dd-->
- `test_make_issue_command_close_with_reason` (function) — Confirms make_issue_command for a close operation round-trips the issue_id and close reason. <!--#b25a1f484512a702-->
- `test_make_issue_command_reopen` (function) — Confirms make_issue_command for a reopen operation round-trips the operation and issue_id. <!--#5642607b20c47373-->
- `test_make_issue_command_omits_empty_optional_fields` (function) — Asserts make_issue_command omits all empty optional fields from the wire payload. <!--#f002bfa0e93eb26f-->
- `test_make_spawn_flow_resume_flow_id_omitted_by_default` (function) — Verifies a normal spawn payload does not include a resume_flow_id field. <!--#086170fe904f1bb5-->
- `test_make_spawn_flow_resume_flow_id_round_trip` (function) — Verifies a resume spawn payload carries resume_flow_id and preserves project_root and the empty task description. <!--#8bdb6a41fde9c660-->
- `test_make_spawn_flow_resume_flow_id_falsey_values_not_included` (function) — Asserts an empty-string resume_flow_id is not added to the spawn payload. <!--#858864b3819d51e6-->
- `test_make_history_data_usage_round_trip` (function) — Asserts that a `usage` payload passed to `make_history_data` survives JSON encode/decode intact on a `HISTORY_MODE_FULL` frame. <!--#e1aafe6c6231072b-->
- `test_make_history_data_omits_usage_by_default` (function) — Verifies `make_history_data` omits the `usage` key entirely when no usage is supplied, keeping frames compatible with pre-revision-7 peers. <!--#ab6baf4d29a4da84-->
- `test_make_history_data_usage_catalog_round_trip` (function) — Checks the `usage_catalog` pricing table round-trips through both `HISTORY_MODE_APPEND` and `HISTORY_MODE_FULL` frames so server and daemon aggregate with the same table. <!--#3f34df965964c222-->
- `test_make_history_data_omits_usage_catalog_by_default` (function) — Verifies the `usage_catalog` key is additive and absent from frames built without one, preserving byte compatibility. <!--#d8d68259b02dd9f7-->
- `test_make_spawn_flow_strategy_round_trip` (function) — Checks `make_spawn_flow` round-trips the revision-7 `implementation_strategy` field and omits it when unset so plain spawn payloads stay unchanged. <!--#bd2e046fcee922b8-->

### `tests/test_protocol_traffic_reduction.py` (python) — Unit tests for the protocol revision 3 traffic-reduction messages, verifying the four new constructors (keepalive, history-index-delta, detail-request, detail-data) build, round-trip through JSON, register in the correct daemon↔server direction sets, honor the supports_traffic_reduction version gate, and still reject unknown or invalid types. <!--#7e19a8ddc90b8031|2efe83e084c37d6d-->
- `test_new_types_registered_in_correct_directions` (function) — Asserts the new traffic-reduction message types (keepalive, history-index-delta, detail-data, detail-request) are registered in ALL_MESSAGE_TYPES and confined to their correct daemon↔server direction sets. <!--#d1ce35f7d39d6012-->
- `test_supports_traffic_reduction_gate` (function) — Verifies the version-gate helper enables traffic reduction for protocol versions 3/4 while degrading legacy, empty, None, or garbage versions to full frames. <!--#ecb8f29048afc25d-->
- `test_make_keepalive_round_trip` (function) — Checks that a constructed keepalive message carries the given signature and seq and survives a JSON encode/decode round trip. <!--#68af9b7cfd93e60f-->
- `test_make_keepalive_defaults_empty_signature` (function) — Checks that make_keepalive with no arguments defaults to an empty signature that persists through decoding. <!--#9e998c96d4405986-->
- `test_make_history_index_delta_round_trip` (function) — Verifies a history-index-delta message preserves its upserts, removed list, and seq across JSON serialization. <!--#2f6915be6e2774a6-->
- `test_make_history_index_delta_defaults_empty` (function) — Checks that make_history_index_delta with no arguments produces empty upserts/removed lists that round-trip intact. <!--#c089cc989421e140-->
- `test_make_detail_request_issue_round_trip` (function) — Verifies a detail-request for an issue carries kind, target_id, project_root, and request_id through a JSON round trip. <!--#42c559e5daf6818e-->
- `test_make_detail_request_omits_empty_optionals` (function) — Checks that make_detail_request omits project_root and request_id from the payload when they are not provided. <!--#539ca66fade21d6e-->
- `test_make_detail_request_rejects_bad_kind` (function) — Asserts make_detail_request raises ProtocolError when given an invalid detail kind. <!--#a9ddc426d1b93dc7-->
- `test_make_detail_data_success_round_trip` (function) — Verifies a successful detail-data message carries request_id, kind, ok=True, and the full detail payload (with no error field) across a round trip. <!--#f8efc32ffb04af0a-->
- `test_make_detail_data_failure_omits_detail` (function) — Checks that a failure detail-data message sets ok=False with an error string and omits the detail field. <!--#18b008ba91e4d035-->
- `test_make_detail_data_rejects_bad_kind` (function) — Asserts make_detail_data raises ProtocolError when given an invalid detail kind. <!--#e87f8f0381cc4af0-->
- `test_unknown_type_still_rejected` (function) — Confirms decoding a message with an unregistered type still raises ProtocolError. <!--#6f54599d477b48d9-->

### `tests/test_read_only_injection.py` (python) — Test module covering the read-only step mechanism end to end: that every STEP_POOL entry carries a valid `read_only` flag, that `is_step_read_only`/`get_read_only_injection` classify pool-flagged steps and internal pure-data sub-agents (`code_index`, `migrate`) as read-only while writable, unknown, and retired `sync_*` pseudo-steps are not, and that `LLMCaller.call()` injects the READ-ONLY STEP CONSTRAINT into prompts across all json_mode dispatch paths and after any user extra_prompt. <!--#7be87bb2baa6b87f|e88b3bc1e0e9d372-->
- `TestStepPoolReadOnly` (class) — Test class verifying every STEP_POOL entry carries a correct read_only boolean attribute. <!--#b3d94c8da62bce0a-->
  - `TestStepPoolReadOnly.test_all_steps_have_read_only_key` (method) — Asserts every STEP_POOL entry contains a 'read_only' key whose value is a bool. <!--#229d9b47828d2fc0-->
  - `TestStepPoolReadOnly.test_read_only_steps` (method) — Checks that discovery/analyze/plan and other analysis steps are marked read_only=True. <!--#e1b6359ad322dcb5-->
  - `TestStepPoolReadOnly.test_non_read_only_steps` (method) — Checks that propose/implement/commit and other mutating steps are marked read_only=False. <!--#0290108d94f1f62e-->
  - `TestStepPoolReadOnly.test_discovery_is_read_only` (method) — Asserts the DISCOVERY step is specifically marked read_only=True. <!--#1bcf20cf73f33882-->
- `TestGetReadOnlyInjection` (class) — Test class verifying get_read_only_injection() returns the right constraint text or empty string per step. <!--#a4f4cc539f606988-->
  - `TestGetReadOnlyInjection.test_read_only_steps_return_constraint` (method) — Parametrized test that read-only steps yield a non-empty constraint mentioning 'READ-ONLY' and 'MUST NOT modify'. <!--#e2b1fb44ced455b9-->
  - `TestGetReadOnlyInjection.test_non_read_only_steps_return_empty` (method) — Parametrized test that writable steps yield an empty injection string. <!--#9468c073be0ea5a5-->
  - `TestGetReadOnlyInjection.test_unknown_step_returns_empty` (method) — Asserts unknown or empty step names safely return an empty string. <!--#02f3b1452617bf55-->
  - `TestGetReadOnlyInjection.test_constraint_forbids_write_edit` (method) — Asserts the constraint text explicitly forbids the Write and Edit tools. <!--#7e75f30aa23d3311-->
  - `TestGetReadOnlyInjection.test_constraint_allows_read_grep_glob` (method) — Asserts the constraint text explicitly permits the Read, Grep, and Glob tools. <!--#0ec87c801b130f69-->
- `TestStepReadOnlyClassification` (class) — Test class asserting that `is_step_read_only`/`get_read_only_injection` derive read-only status from exactly two sources — the STEP_POOL `read_only` attribute and the internal pure-data sub-agent set (`code_index`, `migrate`) — while writable, unknown, and retired `sync_*` pseudo-steps classify as not read-only. <!--#b3bd2f62043c81c0-->
  - `TestStepReadOnlyClassification.test_is_step_read_only_retired_sync_steps_false` (method) — Asserts the retired `sync_scan`/`sync_analyze`/`sync_resolve`/`sync_respond` pseudo-steps are no longer a third read-only source and now classify as `False`. <!--#abc5e456741c10d5-->

  - `TestStepReadOnlyClassification.test_injection_for_internal_pure_data_steps_non_empty` (method) — Asserts `get_read_only_injection` returns a non-empty prompt block containing "READ-ONLY" for the `code_index` and `migrate` steps. <!--#c645e019c73d3fb2-->
  - `TestStepReadOnlyClassification.test_injection_for_retired_sync_steps_empty` (method) — Asserts `get_read_only_injection` returns an empty string for the retired `sync_scan`/`sync_resolve` pseudo-steps. <!--#18bf08d2080bb638-->
- `TestLLMCallerReadOnlyIntegration` (class) — Integration tests verifying that `LLMCaller.call()` injects the READ-ONLY STEP CONSTRAINT into the prompt for read-only steps across all json_mode dispatch paths (off/strict/two_phase) and after extra_prompt, while omitting it for writable steps. <!--#dcef479bb07eb419-->

### `tests/test_readme_badge_idempotent.py` (python) — Regression tests guarding the README version badge: they assert that `DocumentationUpdater.update_readme` is a byte-for-byte no-op on the committed `README.md`, and that both the English and Chinese READMEs still carry the exact placeholder-free `readme_badge_template` literal configured in `tianluo.yaml`'s `documentation:` block. <!--#4eebc46790475597|7fd556141c9ab2b2-->
- `_load_documentation_config` (function) — Test helper that loads the committed `tianluo.yaml` and returns its `documentation:` block, asserting (rather than skipping) when the file or block is absent since that absence is itself the regression under test. <!--#886a32f564c63a60-->
- `test_readme_badge_update_is_a_no_op` (function) — Verifies that running the real `DocumentationUpdater.update_readme` over a copy of the repository's `README.md` leaves it byte-identical, with exactly one `![Version](` badge and no injected version leaking in. <!--#6b704a45c27451d2-->
- `test_readme_carries_the_configured_dynamic_badge` (function) — Parametrized check that each README file contains the exact `readme_badge_template` literal from `tianluo.yaml` — placeholder-free and appearing exactly once — so the English and Chinese READMEs cannot drift apart. <!--#5cf594f109f5b9ed-->

### `tests/test_relay_plan_linearity_integration.py` (python) — Integration tests feeding realistic DAGs through the full transitive_reduce → classify_chains → _relay_plan_is_linear pipeline that implement_handler uses, verifying that redundant-edge chains stay linear while genuine forks are not flattened, across a range of topology shapes and pipeline invariants. <!--#a64351511a8828b0|1e27f06711d57ac8-->
- `_is_linear` (function) — Test helper that runs the complete TR → classify → linearity-check pipeline on a list of group dicts and returns the boolean verdict. <!--#812062e40d5b42d1-->
- `_g` (function) — Compact factory helper that builds a group dict with the given id, order, and dependency list. <!--#0383f1b0979aaf98-->
- `TestRedundantEdgesStillLinear` (class) — Test class asserting that chains carrying redundant transitive edges remain detected as linear while genuine forks are not flattened. <!--#370646d1081282fe-->
  - `TestRedundantEdgesStillLinear.test_redundant_edge_stays_linear` (method) — Verifies the A→B,A→C,B→C redundancy is treated as a convergence rather than a fork, staying linear before and after transitive reduction. <!--#ed6ce66a9c71b33f-->
  - `TestRedundantEdgesStillLinear.test_cascading_redundant_edges_stay_linear` (method) — Verifies a fully transitively-closed chain (A→B→C→D plus all redundant edges) is still recognized as linear. <!--#60d238f7ddcb1553-->
  - `TestRedundantEdgesStillLinear.test_genuine_fork_stays_fork_after_reduction` (method) — Verifies a true fork (A→B, A→C with no B↔C edge) is non-linear and unchanged by transitive reduction. <!--#859340a1a548c020-->
  - `TestRedundantEdgesStillLinear.test_diamond_with_redundant_root_edge` (method) — Verifies a diamond with a redundant root edge stays non-linear because the B/C fork from A is real. <!--#fa26c99d98969f10-->
- `TestExtendedTopologies` (class) — Test class covering topology shapes beyond the unit tests: long chains, wide forks, disconnected components, out-of-order declarations, and trailing/converging forks. <!--#14c0544fd7b8b986-->
  - `TestExtendedTopologies.test_long_linear_chain` (method) — Verifies a 10-node linear chain is detected as linear. <!--#ab7d88be999d89a4-->
  - `TestExtendedTopologies.test_wide_fork_from_single_root` (method) — Verifies a single root with four independent dependents is non-linear. <!--#6d0e6fead8834c19-->
  - `TestExtendedTopologies.test_two_disconnected_linear_chains` (method) — Verifies two independent chains (two roots) are reported as non-linear. <!--#ef94561a36e81d7f-->
  - `TestExtendedTopologies.test_chain_with_out_of_order_declaration` (method) — Verifies that declaring chain nodes in reverse order doesn't affect linearity detection. <!--#d6d702d2db271fda-->
  - `TestExtendedTopologies.test_trailing_fork_off_linear_prefix` (method) — Verifies a fork branching off the tail of an otherwise linear prefix breaks linearity. <!--#0625b96838d54087-->
  - `TestExtendedTopologies.test_converging_two_chains_at_tail` (method) — Verifies two independent chains converging at one tail are non-linear due to having multiple roots. <!--#a195c25304e6123b-->
- `TestPipelineInvariants` (class) — Test class checking structural invariants of the pipeline: return type, input immutability, and single/empty-node edge cases. <!--#3bf88fa7116e5ac6-->
  - `TestPipelineInvariants.test_pipeline_returns_relayplan_instance` (method) — Verifies classify_chains returns a RelayPlan instance even after transitive reduction. <!--#7ac9d81d62dc3d7c-->
  - `TestPipelineInvariants.test_pipeline_does_not_mutate_input` (method) — Verifies transitive_reduce deep-copies so the caller's original group dicts are left unmutated. <!--#b5bf3eafe801dd0c-->
  - `TestPipelineInvariants.test_single_node_pipeline_is_linear` (method) — Verifies a single-node plan passes the pipeline and is reported linear. <!--#621ffc568d8b0171-->
  - `TestPipelineInvariants.test_empty_pipeline_is_not_linear` (method) — Verifies an empty group list yields an empty RelayPlan that is reported non-linear (zero roots). <!--#c0e9a7e90c37ae82-->

### `tests/test_repo_parallel_landing.py` (python) — Repo-level guard tests for parallel test execution: they assert the `tests/test_worktree*.py` family is uniformly pinned to one serial `xdist_group`, that the `xdist_group` marker is declared in `pyproject.toml`, that the committed `tianluo.yaml` keeps `test.parallel: auto`, that a real `pytest -n 4 --dist loadgroup` subprocess lands the whole serial group on a single worker, and that module-level rich `Console` width follows the live `COLUMNS` env var rather than xdist's injected default. <!--#eddcfaf41dcf4cce|4cb25e4b6e19db36-->

- `test_worktree_modules_are_all_in_the_serial_group` (function) — Asserts the worktree module family is non-trivially sized and that every one of its modules is pinned to the shared serial `xdist_group`. <!--#5b3bc04947e3fcd1-->
- `test_xdist_group_marker_is_registered_in_pyproject` (function) — Asserts `pyproject.toml`'s pytest ini options declare a `markers` entry covering `xdist_group`, so xdist-less environments don't warn. <!--#37c4f2fa6164b110-->
- `test_committed_config_enables_parallel_tests` (function) — Reads the committed `tianluo.yaml` directly (bypassing local-override config loading) to assert `test.parallel` is `auto`. <!--#0b03281c60c57241-->
- `test_serial_group_lands_on_a_single_worker_under_loadgroup` (function) — End-to-end check running two marked worktree modules through a real `pytest -n 4 --dist loadgroup` subprocess and asserting all their tests land on one `gwN` worker. <!--#0e5fd03e6c86b7cb-->
- `test_module_level_console_width_follows_the_environment` (function) — Pins that module-level rich `Console` width tracks the live `COLUMNS` env var, proving `tests/conftest.py` drops the xdist-injected `COLUMNS=80` before tianluo imports. <!--#56ed5edd3b47779b-->

- `test_drain_does_not_buffer_for_running_step` (function) — Verifies that draining an interjection for a non-PAUSED (PENDING) step returns the text but leaves the `_pending_paused_interjections` prefix buffer empty. <!--#2290a396931f00f8-->
- `test_drain_does_not_buffer_for_confirm_paused_step` (function) — Verifies that a CONFIRM-paused step drains the interjection into `user_interjections` but does NOT populate the prefix buffer (which is reserved for discovery reply paths), preventing stale-interjection leakage. <!--#aaf08bb125880aa6-->
- `test_drain_writes_history_jsonl` (function) — Confirms that each drained interjection is appended to the per-step history jsonl as a `kind=interjection`, `role=user` line with the interjection text as content. <!--#a4084d25adea5adb-->
- `test_drain_invalidates_incremental_self_check_round` (function) — Test asserting that draining a pending interjection request mid-flow invalidates any active incremental self-check round, dropping `active_round`, marking `last_round` as `"invalidated"`, and setting `force_full_reason` to `"effective_requirements_changed"`. <!--#42fc8f1906af456e-->
- `test_drain_with_no_calls_is_noop` (function) — Asserts draining with no pending call files returns an empty list and produces no side effects. <!--#17c0192566f16991-->
- `test_consume_prefix_joins_and_clears_buffer` (function) — Asserts the consumer joins buffered entries into a bracketed prefix string and clears the buffer. <!--#85fc8a465c47ab54-->
- `test_consume_prefix_empty_returns_empty` (function) — Asserts consuming an empty buffer returns an empty string. <!--#bccfa591d558a503-->
- `test_consume_prefix_tolerates_missing_state` (function) — Asserts the consumer returns an empty string instead of crashing when the flow lacks a .state attribute. <!--#e85f35c4189071a9-->
- `test_consume_prefix_skips_whitespace_entries` (function) — Asserts the consumer skips whitespace-only buffered entries when building the prefix. <!--#766aa5282e3e5aa9-->

### `tests/test_run_failure_dual_channel.py` (python) — Test suite for `luo run`'s dual-channel failure-decision flow, verifying that a step failure unconditionally writes a `retry_decision` call file and emits FLOW_PAUSED, that the CLI-prompt vs. webui-poller whoever-first-wins race (`_await_terminal_or_web_choice`) resolves and cleans up correctly across web/CLI/interactive/Ctrl+C paths, and that non-interactive pauses and max-retries auto-fail behave as expected — driven via mocked StateMachine/PersistenceManager, NDJSON event assertions, and prompt_toolkit fakes. <!--#7ed020ba9e18eded|93e4910636d17036-->
- `_build_failed_flow` (function) — Test helper that constructs a RUNNING FlowInstance with a single PENDING IMPLEMENT step pre-loaded with an error_message and configurable retry_count, so the orchestrator's failure handler sees a step primed to fail. <!--#276b0c02610861c9-->
- `_run_failed_flow` (function) — Test helper that invokes `run_flow` in JSON output mode against a flow whose `StateMachine`/`PersistenceManager` are mocked to fail (with non-interactive stdin), capturing stdout and returning the exit code alongside the list of emitted NDJSON event types. <!--#803b1a84d2b16682-->
- `_calls_dir` (function) — Tiny helper returning the interaction-calls directory for a project root. <!--#8aa336cdb0d2829b-->
- `test_failure_writes_retry_decision_call_and_emits_flow_paused` (function) — Asserts a failed step with retries remaining unconditionally writes a retry_decision call file and emits both step_failed and flow_paused events. <!--#8bf5e5d1aa49aef0-->
- `test_webui_answer_skip_completes_and_transitions` (function) — Asserts a pre-seeded webui 'skip' answer force-completes the step, advances the flow, and cleans up the call/response artifacts. <!--#d24b55a34319790b-->
- `test_webui_answer_abort_fails_flow` (function) — Asserts a pre-seeded webui 'abort' answer fails the flow with exit code 1 and removes the call artifact. <!--#9800d18049c80d04-->
- `test_webui_answer_retry_resets_step_and_increments_counter` (function) — Asserts a pre-seeded webui 'retry' answer resets the step to PENDING, bumps retry_count, re-runs (succeeding), and cleans up the consumed answer. <!--#d0076d7da124d786-->
- `test_max_retries_autofails_without_call_or_pause` (function) — Asserts retry_count >= 3 auto-fails the flow with no retry_decision call, no FLOW_PAUSED, and no race. <!--#dd56b69739569949-->
- `_seed_call` (function) — Helper that writes a retry_decision call file for the race-helper tests and returns its path. <!--#c808609b7846e988-->
- `test_race_web_answer_already_on_disk_wins_and_is_cleaned` (function) — Asserts a web response already on disk wins the choice race outright, is consumed, and leaves no residual artifacts. <!--#0e63407ed7698f29-->
- `test_race_cli_first_wins_tears_down_webui_artifacts` (function) — Asserts that when the CLI answers first (non-TTY plain branch), the poller is torn down and the concurrent webui chip is cleaned. <!--#288ff3b01cb8cd4a-->
- `test_race_web_answer_landing_during_cli_read_wins` (function) — Asserts a web answer landing while the CLI prompt blocks still wins, since the result is re-checked after the read. <!--#c2e6270fe26ae2a4-->
- `test_race_no_call_file_degrades_to_plain_cli_choice` (function) — Asserts that with no call file the helper degrades to a plain prompt_user_choice (pre-dual-channel behavior). <!--#790a549431c4da18-->
- `test_failure_decision_to_choice_normalizes_unknown_to_abort` (function) — Asserts `_failure_decision_to_choice` maps retry/skip/abort to 0/1/2 and any unknown value or None to abort (2). <!--#a78f8c0dfaf50e44-->
- `_FakePromptApp` (class) — Test double for `PromptSession.app` supporting the cross-thread cancel handshake via an `exit()` that resolves a stored future. <!--#65eac4b0a4df197f-->
  - `_FakePromptApp.__init__` (method) — Initializes the fake app's running flag and the slot for the in-flight prompt future. <!--#f0063f168287a254-->
  - `_FakePromptApp.exit` (method) — Resolves the blocking prompt future (if pending) and clears the running flag, simulating the poller cancelling the live prompt. <!--#7e12137b8b71feed-->
- `_FakePromptSession` (class) — Fake PromptSession whose `prompt_async` behavior (return value, raise KeyboardInterrupt, or block until cancelled) is driven by a configured mode. <!--#b18ecc889f00e782-->
  - `_FakePromptSession.__init__` (method) — Constructs the fake session with a _FakePromptApp and stores the chosen mode and return value. <!--#30b87f717c7b1a81-->
  - `_FakePromptSession.prompt_async` (method) — Async prompt stub that returns immediately, raises KeyboardInterrupt, or blocks on a future per mode to exercise the cancellation path. <!--#3e851c3bfa559dd7-->
- `_patch_prompt_session` (function) — Monkeypatch helper that swaps in the fake PromptSession and a no-op patch_stdout so the interactive path touches no real terminal. <!--#3132208505b1c295-->
- `test_interactive_race_web_first_cancels_prompt_and_cleans` (function) — Asserts that a web answer found by the poller while the live prompt blocks wins, cancels the prompt via app.exit, and leaves no residual artifacts. <!--#6afa472a72a0b697-->
- `test_interactive_race_terminal_first_tears_down_poller_and_cleans` (function) — Asserts that when the operator types a choice first, the interactive helper returns it, tears down the poller, and cleans the webui chip. <!--#663d24111c58328a-->
- `test_interactive_race_ctrl_c_aborts_and_cleans_webui_artifact` (function) — Asserts Ctrl+C/EOF at the failure prompt returns CANCEL and dismantles the deterministic retry_decision call file so the chip stops surfacing. <!--#57b5d5e31a0945e0-->

### `tests/test_run_lock_lifecycle.py` (python) — Unit tests for the deferred main-worktree lock lifecycle in `luo run` (via `_ensure_main_lock_for_step`), verifying discovery steps never lock, free/stale locks acquire without a wait state, contended locks persist and stream `waiting_for_lock=True` then clear it on acquire, `--worktree` bodies are no-ops, the flag round-trips through engine.json, and a Ctrl+C while waiting clears the flag before persist and exits 130. <!--#3ec5813407ae62a3|f6ba42b86a2f993f-->
- `project` (function) — A pytest fixture that creates the `tianluo/state` directory under a temp path and returns that path as a fake project root. <!--#462027d6885bf5f6-->
- `_make_flow` (function) — Helper that builds a RUNNING FlowInstance containing a single RUNNING step of the given StepType. <!--#7e690c403fae6b4f-->
- `_read_engine` (function) — Test helper that reads and JSON-parses the project's `tianluo/state/engine.json` file into a dict. <!--#ba6defc747c346a9-->
- `_jsonl_path` (function) — Test helper that computes the path to a step's streaming JSONL history file under `tianluo/history/<flow_id>/<step_id>.jsonl`. <!--#e0be861d9ba0ca0e-->
- `test_waiting_for_lock_roundtrips_true` (function) — Asserts a True `waiting_for_lock` flag serializes and round-trips through FlowInstance dict conversion. <!--#9aa058df1ebf86a0-->
- `test_waiting_for_lock_false_omitted_and_reads_false` (function) — Asserts a default-False `waiting_for_lock` is omitted from serialization and legacy files lacking the key read back as False. <!--#f7596474f23d651f-->
- `test_discovery_step_does_not_acquire_lock` (function) — Verifies a discovery step never acquires the main-worktree lock (1a), leaving it genuinely free for another acquirer. <!--#1917614de3187410-->
- `test_free_lock_acquired_without_waiting_state` (function) — Verifies a free lock is acquired immediately with no `waiting_for_lock` flag set and no streaming event written. <!--#c13a70cfc785211d-->
- `test_already_held_lock_is_noop` (function) — Verifies that calling the helper when the lock is already held is a no-op with no waiting state. <!--#fb10b44cff47523b-->
- `test_worktree_body_none_lock_is_noop` (function) — Verifies that a `--worktree` flow body (main_lock is None) is a pure no-op leaving `waiting_for_lock` False. <!--#7e09f0d84a0e9043-->
- `test_busy_lock_surfaces_waiting_state_then_acquires` (function) — Concurrency test asserting that when a `MergeLock` is already held by another holder, a run persists `waiting_for_lock` to `engine.json` and streams a `waiting_for_lock` jsonl event before blocking, then acquires the lock and clears the flag once the holder releases. <!--#63b73f53780227ff-->
- `test_stale_lock_reclaimed_without_waiting` (function) — Verifies that a lock file recording a dead PID is silently reclaimed by `_ensure_main_lock_for_step` without surfacing any waiting state or writing a JSONL history file. <!--#280ec6bd65f1126f-->
- `test_interrupt_while_waiting_clears_flag_before_persist` (function) — Regression test asserting that a Ctrl+C while `run_flow` is blocked acquiring the main lock exits 130 and clears `waiting_for_lock` before the final persist, so a dead process is never left recorded as waiting. <!--#c0ec3ba4bf500bc2-->

### `tests/test_run_waiting_for_lock_clear.py` (python) — Pytest suite verifying that acquiring a *contended* main-worktree merge lock emits a clearing 'step_status' running anchor (idempotent, skipped from CLI/retry history) to unfreeze the web transcript's '等待锁' row while free/stale acquires write nothing, and refuting the theory that a step error during retry releases the merge lock — showing it stays held until run_flow's finally on flow exit. <!--#bc6c44132392b8b5|b83eeb87c86ba534-->
- `project` (function) — pytest fixture that builds an empty project tree with a `tianluo/state` directory under `tmp_path` and returns its root. <!--#462027d6885bf5f6-->
- `_make_flow` (function) — Helper that builds a running FlowInstance with a single running step of the given type, set as the current step. <!--#7e690c403fae6b4f-->
- `_jsonl_path` (function) — Helper computing the per-step raw-history jsonl path (`tianluo/history/<flow_id>/<step_id>.jsonl`) for a given flow and step. <!--#e0be861d9ba0ca0e-->
- `_read_records` (function) — Helper that reads and JSON-parses each line of a step's jsonl history file, returning an empty list if absent. <!--#0955a7f0ee5ced3d-->
- `_read_engine` (function) — Helper that loads and returns the parsed `tianluo/state/engine.json` state as a dict. <!--#ba6defc747c346a9-->
- `test_contended_acquire_emits_lock_acquired_clear_event` (function) — Verifies that when `_ensure_main_lock_for_step` blocks on a contended merge lock it writes a `waiting_for_lock` anchor and, upon acquiring, appends exactly one `step_status`/`running` clear anchor after it while clearing `waiting_for_lock` in the flow and engine.json. <!--#a95456b2af33edc5-->
- `test_free_acquire_writes_no_clear_event` (function) — Asserts that acquiring an uncontended main lock writes no jsonl anchors at all (neither waiting nor clear) and leaves `waiting_for_lock` false. <!--#9d29a2287bd06b2a-->
- `test_stale_reclaim_writes_no_clear_event` (function) — Asserts that silently reclaiming a stale merge lock (dead PID) surfaces no wait and writes no jsonl clear/waiting anchors. <!--#0d555ebf696d533d-->
- `test_record_lock_acquired_is_idempotent` (function) — Checks that calling `record_lock_acquired` twice for the same step appends only a single `step_status`/`running` anchor rather than a duplicate. <!--#a7c568cd9f969b50-->
- `test_record_lock_acquired_skipped_by_get_step_history` (function) — Confirms the lock-acquired clear anchor is excluded from `get_step_history` so it never pollutes CLI history or retry context with chat messages. <!--#4b095c49ee199d33-->
- `test_merge_lock_held_through_retry_not_released_until_flow_exit` (function) — Refutes the 'error releases the merge lock → freeze' theory by proving (via a monkeypatched `_run_flow_impl`) the lock stays held and uncontendable across simulated retries and is released only in `run_flow`'s finally on flow exit. <!--#f58610be1d7ec317-->
