- `TestSeedUploads` (class) — Test class covering `seed_uploads`/`create_worktree` attachment seeding into a forked worktree — path fidelity (including the legacy `se3/uploads` layout), hard-link sharing with copy fallback, non-clobbering of existing sandbox files, flat-directory-only scope, and never failing the fork on write errors. <!--#c2584cd362c1aebf-->
  - `TestSeedUploads._seed_attachment` (method) — Helper that writes an attachment file under `<root>/tianluo/uploads/` (creating parents) and returns its path. <!--#3ab2cb44fb28f5ed-->
  - `TestSeedUploads.test_worktree_carries_pre_fork_attachments` (method) — Asserts an attachment written before the fork lands in the new worktree with identical bytes. <!--#e2381715afa0136a-->
  - `TestSeedUploads.test_seeded_path_matches_the_prompt_relative_path` (method) — Asserts the seeded file is reachable at the exact project-relative path embedded in the prompt (`tianluo/uploads/...`). <!--#476cc3966341d974-->
  - `TestSeedUploads.test_uploads_directory_is_a_real_directory` (method) — Asserts the seeded uploads location is a real directory rather than a symlink, so the trailing-slash gitignore rule still covers it. <!--#bb87a07f415f6312-->
  - `TestSeedUploads.test_no_uploads_directory_is_not_an_error` (method) — Asserts worktree creation succeeds and creates no uploads directory when the source project has none. <!--#0710acdc870dec50-->
  - `TestSeedUploads.test_seeds_share_storage_with_the_source` (method) — Asserts the seeded file shares an inode with the source, confirming hard-linking keeps forks cheap. <!--#446cf07a8d529cb8-->
  - `TestSeedUploads.test_falls_back_to_copying_when_linking_is_refused` (method) — Patches `os.link` to raise `OSError` and asserts `seed_uploads` falls back to copying, still seeding the file's contents. <!--#033b0cc67217d849-->
  - `TestSeedUploads.test_legacy_layout_seeds_the_legacy_path` (method) — Asserts a 12.x project using `se3/uploads/` is seeded at that same legacy path and not re-spelled as `tianluo/`. <!--#2787a3aa8d891cdf-->
  - `TestSeedUploads.test_existing_sandbox_attachment_is_left_alone` (method) — Asserts a same-named file already present in the sandbox keeps its own contents and is not overwritten by the source copy. <!--#f50774cec8b09a2a-->
  - `TestSeedUploads.test_write_failure_never_breaks_the_fork` (method) — Patches both `os.link` and `shutil.copy2` to fail and asserts `seed_uploads` returns 0 instead of raising, so the fork survives. <!--#128c078541e1a5ff-->

- `TestDeleteBranchWorktreeVerification` (class) — Test class covering delete_branch's worktree handling: delete directly when none exists, force-cleanup then delete when one does, and still attempt branch deletion when cleanup fails. <!--#5866e60893d4b951-->

- `_make_modify_delete_unmerged` (function) — Test helper that constructs a modify/delete unmerged index state with MERGE_HEAD removed, simulating a crashed merge's stale leftover. <!--#ad0d687b6a5573bd-->
- `TestDetectUnmergedPaths` (class) — Tests detect_unmerged_paths returning empty on a clean repo and a deduped path on unmerged state. <!--#f6f816e5d75aa6f7-->

### `tests/test_worktree_history_sidecar.py` (python) — Tests that DaemonHistoryReader correctly handles worktree sidecar history files (`.from-<branch>` jsonl variants) — folding primary and sidecar files into logical steps for id parsing, enumeration, and counting, while merging their records on read with distinct display step ids, per-physical-file incremental cursors, and safe handling of half-written tails. <!--#e06b66717ef9328c|54bda54716beaf34-->
- `_write_jsonl` (function) — Test helper that writes a list of dicts as newline-delimited JSON to a file, creating parent directories as needed. <!--#18930ad89d1ea5fb-->
- `_append_jsonl` (function) — Test helper that appends a list of dicts as JSON lines to an existing jsonl file. <!--#b174bd6540498b15-->
- `_msg` (function) — Tiny factory building a `{role, content}` message dict for test records. <!--#67f68ff7e3aa1c72-->
- `_make_reader` (function) — Test helper constructing a `DaemonHistoryReader` whose project-roots provider returns the given roots. <!--#808724bfc5456a05-->
- `_flow_dir` (function) — Test helper that creates and returns the `tianluo/history/<flow_id>` directory under the given root, used to set up per-flow history fixtures for the worktree sidecar merging tests. <!--#d29934aed956126e-->
- `test_logical_step_id_strips_sidecar_suffix` (function) — Verifies `_logical_step_id` reduces primary and sidecar file names to the bare logical step id and leaves non-jsonl names unchanged. <!--#ca19f99c1adbf894-->
- `test_display_step_id_keeps_sidecar_marker` (function) — Verifies that _display_step_id strips the .jsonl suffix but preserves the .from-<branch> sidecar marker (including hash-disambiguated ones), so a step's primary file and each sidecar map to distinct frontend-facing step ids. <!--#2b880caf012d6101-->
- `test_parse_step_type_strips_sidecar_suffix` (function) — Verifies `parse_step_type_from_step_id` extracts the step type from logical ids as well as raw primary/sidecar file names. <!--#c8102b38ca7efffe-->
- `test_iter_history_jsonl_includes_sidecars_sorted` (function) — Asserts `_iter_history_jsonl` enumerates both primary files and their sidecars in sorted order. <!--#ea418105857d9ccf-->
- `test_count_jsonl_counts_logical_steps` (function) — Asserts `_count_jsonl` collapses multiple physical files (primary + sidecars) into a count of distinct logical steps. <!--#c43040e8aed2e32d-->
- `test_read_flow_merges_primary_and_sidecar` (function) — Asserts that read_flow returns all records from a step's primary file and its sidecar in order without loss or duplication, with distinct display step ids preventing (step_id, ordinal) collisions and a cursor keyed per physical file. <!--#d49ebe2dd91f7024-->
- `test_read_flow_sidecar_only_step` (function) — Checks that a step whose records exist only in a sidecar file is still fully read, keeping the branch marker in its step id while parsing the folded logical step type. <!--#a0acb25b514509b6-->
- `test_read_flow_incremental_cursor_advances_over_sidecar` (function) — Verifies incremental reads: after appending to a sidecar, a cursor-based re-read returns only the new records in append mode, advances the sidecar's cursor, and a further read with no new writes yields nothing. <!--#a383adfe68c77820-->
- `test_read_flow_multiple_sidecars_for_one_step` (function) — Confirms that a step with multiple hash-disambiguated sidecars reads all files in order, with each physical file emitting a distinct step id, unique (step_id, ordinal) keys, and independent cursor entries. <!--#c0194fab2108cbe7-->
- `test_read_flow_first_record_nonempty_with_midwrite_sidecar_tail` (function) — Verifies a half-written (truncated) sidecar line is held back rather than consumed mid-stream, then read in full once completed, with the cursor never advancing past it prematurely. <!--#b00e44a639a043f4-->

### `tests/test_worktree_paused_history_reconcile.py` (python) — Regression lock for issue #287 (worktree discovery chat going blank): builds a paused `--worktree` flow's real two-root on-disk history, pins `DaemonHistoryReader.read_flow` to distinguish an unresolvable root from a genuinely empty flow, and drives a self-heal reconcile through the real `/api/history/{flow_id}` endpoint with a fake daemon socket to assert that a `full` reconcile frame may only ever add records — never roll the cached bundle back to zero — while still applying frames that bring more. <!--#1afaa1614db26121|c813e924ad2de13e-->
- `_line` (function) — Tiny helper that builds a `{role, content}` chat-line dict used as the message payload of a history record. <!--#2b2d6e3857a596de-->
- `_wire` (function) — Wraps a chat line into a wire-shaped discovery history record (`step_id`/`step_type`/`ordinal`/`message`) for ordinal `n`. <!--#e465cae66c0b24f1-->
- `_write_jsonl` (function) — Writes a list of records as a JSONL file at `path`, creating parent directories as needed. <!--#4b264541129f2baf-->
- `_write_engine_json` (function) — Test helper that writes a live `tianluo/state/engine.json` for `FLOW_ID` under a given root with the supplied status, making the reader treat the flow as `source="active"` and thus a candidate for `read_active_flows`. <!--#57a0ff8508ca302b-->
- `_build_two_root_history` (function) — Test helper that lays out the on-disk shape of a paused `--worktree` discovery, writing the pre-fork round-1 copy in the main repo and the live round-1+round-2 file in the worktree, and returns `(main_root, worktree_root)`. <!--#99459ceda0afc07b-->
- `test_read_flow_merges_both_roots_for_a_worktree_flow` (function) — Happy path: a cursorless `read_flow` against the authoritative worktree root returns a `full` frame merging both roots (all of round 2). <!--#f5f0b068a4f02dc6-->
- `test_read_flow_unresolvable_root_falls_back_to_the_registry_walk` (function) — Test asserting that when `_resolve_flow_dirs` cannot find the history dir under the handed-in (ghost) root, `read_flow` falls back to the registry walk and re-expands the full main+worktree merge (round 2 included) with a diagnostic warning, instead of returning a pseudo-empty full frame — issue #287 hop 1. <!--#6cac6135e95d3b67-->
- `test_read_flow_truly_unknown_flow_returns_empty_with_a_warning` (function) — Test asserting the opposite case — a genuinely unknown flow that resolves nowhere returns an empty full frame but must still emit a "no history directory resolved" warning so callers can distinguish unresolvable from truly-empty. <!--#ddfdad64478a26ce-->
- `test_read_active_flows_keeps_streaming_a_paused_worktree_flow` (function) — Test locking `_is_active_status` so a PAUSED worktree flow stays in the active set and keeps producing append deltas (round 2 while still paused), since only COMPLETED/FAILED are terminal. <!--#5d20bd6a28b1df70-->
- `_FakeDaemon` (class) — Test double for a connected daemon over the real `/ws` socket, serving `HISTORY_REQUEST` replies from a mutable record list on a background thread so a blocking `TestClient.get` can trigger a reconcile. <!--#4e48bad91e46cec7-->
  - `_FakeDaemon.__init__` (method) — Opens the websocket, completes the authenticated HELLO/WELCOME handshake, seeds the reply payload with round 1, and starts the receive-loop thread. <!--#b59289f0fa9a6438-->
  - `_FakeDaemon._serve` (method) — Background receive loop that counts incoming `HISTORY_REQUEST` messages and answers each with a `full` HISTORY_DATA frame built from the current `reply_records`. <!--#f24e6fc5a1143dc5-->
  - `_FakeDaemon.push_full` (method) — Unprompted push of a `full` HISTORY_DATA frame for `FLOW_ID`, simulating the daemon's live history broadcast. <!--#5fdbcf94bf3d80f0-->
  - `_FakeDaemon.report_paused_worktree_flow` (method) — Sends a STATUS_UPDATE putting `FLOW_ID` in the state #287 requires — `paused` under a worktree project root — which is what opens the server's self-heal reconcile window. <!--#2bff15735e3afd91-->
  - `_FakeDaemon.close` (method) — Stops the receive thread and tears down the websocket context. <!--#8425f1499b69c7eb-->
- `client_and_app` (function) — Pytest fixture yielding an authenticated `TestClient` plus its FastAPI app, already logged in, for the endpoint-level reconcile tests. <!--#c78c8fc0ec5446bd-->
- `test_paused_worktree_reconcile_must_not_empty_the_cached_bundle` (function) — End-to-end test through the real `/api/history` endpoint asserting the reconcile-only-adds invariant: an empty cursorless reconcile frame from an unresolvable worktree root must not roll the cached round-1 bundle back to zero records nor bump the generation — issue #287. <!--#4ddd2196641c472a-->
- `test_reconcile_that_brings_more_records_still_replaces` (function) — The other half of the invariant: a reconcile that brings *more* records (round 2) must still apply and grow the cached bundle, so any #287 fix cannot simply stop honouring reconcile frames. <!--#4071cb8950b17821-->

- `test_worktree_root_excluded_from_project_roots` (function) — Asserts the snapshot's dropdown-facing project_roots includes the main root but never the worktree copy root. <!--#f4f42d86bf2fa4dc-->

### `tests/test_worktree_registry_seam.py` (python) — Unit tests verifying that the shared project-root aggregator seam normalizes worktree isolation paths back to their main root across all registration entry points (add/append/sanitize), persists the folded root to the on-disk registry, sanitizes pre-existing worktree pollution on daemon startup (tolerating missing/corrupt/clean files), and keeps worktrees observable via run-roots yet absent from the displayed project-root set. <!--#08a76da0d3ce0691|1ab79b2838871912-->
- `_make_project` (function) — Test helper that creates a minimal tianluo project root (with a `tianluo/state` directory) under the given path and returns it. <!--#bc20270756a8497c-->

- `test_all_entry_points_normalize_through_seam` (function) — Asserts that driving a worktree path through the shared aggregator seam normalizes both the in-memory set and the on-disk registry, covering all five registration entry points. <!--#c277da825f3abaa1-->
- `test_append_project_root_normalizes_worktree` (function) — Asserts the disk write point _append_project_root folds a worktree path back to its main root before persisting. <!--#b7aead7edb298071-->
- `test_sanitize_removes_worktree_entry` (function) — Verifies that `_sanitize_project_roots` cleans a registry pre-polluted with a worktree-copy entry, dropping the worktree path while keeping the main root. <!--#cea9d44f1cb3484d-->
- `test_sanitize_no_change_leaves_file_untouched` (function) — Asserts _sanitize_project_roots leaves an already-clean registry file unwritten (mtime unchanged). <!--#db62dc439fced750-->
- `test_sanitize_missing_file_is_noop` (function) — Asserts _sanitize_project_roots is a fault-tolerant no-op when the registry file does not exist. <!--#7ff3f36d1a7bfdcb-->

- `test_worktree_observable_but_not_registered` (function) — Checks that a worktree remains visible through `DaemonAggregator.all_observable_roots()` but is normalized out of the displayed `all_project_roots()` set. <!--#ddd409e502ca5b7d-->

### `tests/test_worktree_seam_regression.py` (python) — Regression suite locking the worktree-mode observability seam: it proves an eagerly saved INIT engine.json makes a worktree observable and its discovery replies readable live while never entering the active set, registry, or New Task dropdown, and — via a `_FrontendConsole` mirror of `app.js` reconcile logic — drives real reader → server relay → frontend chains so every round of multi-round and split-root (`.from-<branch>` sidecar) discoveries renders without drops or duplicates. <!--#f4f15fb75af87e4a|9c669479a3a9e69d-->
- `_eager_save_worktree_flow` (function) — Test helper that mimics the run command's eager save by creating a pending worktree-mode flow and immediately persisting its engine.json at status INIT. <!--#1c56a9651dab0d1a-->
- `test_eager_save_persists_is_worktree_mode_at_init` (function) — Verifies the eager save writes an INIT-status engine.json carrying is_worktree_mode=True, worktree_path, and a flow_id before any discovery LLM call. <!--#00955ed29b664300-->
- `test_worktree_observable_at_discovery_startup_window` (function) — Asserts DaemonAggregator admits a worktree into the observable set from its first INIT engine.json (not only at RUNNING) while keeping it out of the New Task dropdown's project-roots view. <!--#ede48ea893d2613f-->
- `test_discovery_first_reply_read_live_at_init` (function) — Checks that a discovery first reply flushed complete-but-unterminated is indexed active and read in full via build_index/read_active_flows, then keeps appending incrementally with no loss, dup, or truncation. <!--#69a2236fc57dbee4-->
- `test_dag_isolation_worktree_stays_excluded` (function) — Ensures a DAG implement-isolation worktree lacking an is_worktree_mode flow record stays excluded from the observable set despite sharing the tianluo/worktrees/ parent. <!--#1a86d3950a9d3d0a-->
- `test_seam_observable_and_readable_yet_never_registered` (function) — The G3 bidirectional lock asserting both seam invariants in one test — the worktree is observable and its first reply reads live (Bug1) yet never enters the active set, registry, or dropdown project list even when its path is mistakenly registered (Bug2). <!--#b458c0c64265e443-->
- `_disc_msg` (function) — Builds a minimal discovery chat message dict with the given role and content. <!--#0921d926f4665974-->
- `_FrontendConsole` (class) — A faithful Python mirror of the WebUI's `app.js` history reconcile logic, consuming the daemon's `(mode, records)` push frames so tests can assert what the chat would actually render. <!--#18426c328ec9a1a1-->
  - `_FrontendConsole.__init__` (method) — Initializes the console with an empty list of held (rendered) records. <!--#8eef94d1ac7269b2-->
  - `_FrontendConsole._ordinal` (method) — Extracts a record's integer ordinal from the record itself or its nested message, returning None if absent. <!--#4b1a3ef8f604450d-->
  - `_FrontendConsole._legacy_key` (method) — Computes the content-based fallback identity key (step_id, role, content length, content prefix) mirroring app.js legacyKeyFromNorm. <!--#b3be1a71cd61e99d-->
  - `_FrontendConsole._record_key` (method) — Returns a record's stable identity as stepId#ordinal when both are present, else falls back to the legacy content key. <!--#652e8aa2170aa046-->
  - `_FrontendConsole._dedupe_snapshot_clones` (method) — Mirrors the JS `dedupeSnapshotClones`, dropping byte-identical duplicates of any step from a `full` snapshot while keeping same-key records whose content differs. <!--#071ba1d6ed758f6e-->
  - `_FrontendConsole._reconcile_append` (method) — Idempotently merges an append batch into held records, converging same-key records to newest content in place and never creating duplicate bubbles. <!--#9608bc6c8742b98f-->
  - `_FrontendConsole.apply` (method) — Applies a single daemon push frame like the WebUI would — a `full` frame replaces the held records after clone de-dup, anything else merges idempotently as an append. <!--#41264c22fba0c0d2-->
  - `_FrontendConsole.contents` (method) — Returns the message content strings of all held records, i.e. what the chat would show. <!--#b6fe36bc7af50d3b-->
  - `_FrontendConsole.keys` (method) — Returns the stable record key for each held record, used to assert identity uniqueness. <!--#48ae915d408f5a64-->
- `_make_reader` (function) — Constructs a DaemonHistoryReader whose project-roots provider yields the given root paths. <!--#a53d3c7a25b35ec7-->
- `_wt_flow_dir` (function) — Test helper that creates and returns a worktree's tianluo/history/<flow_id> directory. <!--#94cf6049e1cea523-->
- `_make_worktree` (function) — Test helper that creates and returns a tianluo/worktrees/<name> worktree directory under a main root. <!--#a95c859ac4949026-->
- `_write_jsonl` (function) — Writes the given records as a fresh JSONL file, creating parent directories as needed. <!--#f321072562a278a4-->
- `_append_jsonl` (function) — Appends the given records as JSONL lines to an existing file. <!--#826510bf1d7d8393-->
- `test_e2e_worktree_multiround_discovery_all_rounds_reach_frontend` (function) — #278 end-to-end regression test chaining real reader → real server relay → frontend reconcile to assert every round of a live multi-round worktree discovery (including the final verdict) reaches the frontend chat without drops or duplicates and matches the server's authoritative bundle. <!--#8611047cfa66114d-->
- `test_e2e_worktree_discovery_cross_source_rounds_all_render` (function) — #278 end-to-end test for the split-root topology where a primary discovery file and a .from-<branch> sidecar each start at ordinal 0, asserting distinct step_ids keep their keys from colliding so both sources render fully instead of the sidecar being dropped as a duplicate. <!--#7e522cae26a74618-->

### `tests/test_ws_rejected_full_not_broadcast.py` (python) — Regression tests for #287 pinning that a `full` history frame rejected by `ServerState.apply_history_frame` (a shrinking same-machine snapshot for an active worktree flow) is flagged via `rejected_full` and suppressed by the `/ws/ui` handler, while legitimate growing frames and non-worktree flows still broadcast to the UI as before. <!--#4a6bece0bc92f910|abc9e638c0397610-->
- `RecordingHub` (class) — A minimal stand-in for the WebSocket `UiHub` that records every `broadcast_owned`/`broadcast_scoped` call so tests can assert exactly what (if anything) was fanned out to browser consoles. <!--#303a661440235cd9-->
  - `RecordingHub.__init__` (method) — Initialises the fake hub with a fixed client count and empty `owned`/`scoped` recording lists. <!--#037e799bfb43ad93-->
  - `RecordingHub.client_count` (method) — Reports the configured number of connected UI clients so the fan-out code believes someone is listening. <!--#854f4922a8380908-->
  - `RecordingHub.distinct_owners` (method) — Returns the single anonymous owner set `{None}` matching the ownerless flows these tests register. <!--#b1dfd7732fb9e9b5-->
  - `RecordingHub.broadcast_scoped` (method) — Records a per-owner broadcast payload instead of sending it over any socket. <!--#24ae51509d068209-->
  - `RecordingHub.broadcast_owned` (method) — Records an owner-targeted broadcast payload instead of sending it over any socket. <!--#e03c98c48ffe7f09-->
- `_history_pushes` (function) — Helper that filters a `RecordingHub`'s recorded owned broadcasts down to the `history_data` payloads. <!--#b25cfe61843d556e-->
- `_register_flow` (function) — Async helper that registers machine `m1` and reports one flow with the given status and `project_root`, since those fields decide whether a shrinking full frame is rejected. <!--#038fac2f523d12c4-->
- `_paused_worktree_flow` (function) — Test helper coroutine that registers a flow with the given state as a paused, worktree-based flow (project_root under tianluo/worktrees) for use in WebSocket broadcast-rejection tests. <!--#55f74610c976a3ac-->
- `test_apply_history_frame_flags_a_rejected_shrinking_full` (function) — Asserts `ServerState.apply_history_frame` sets `rejected_full` for shrinking and empty full frames (but not identical ones) while still resolving the pull waiter and leaving the cached bundle intact. <!--#c1f98eecd6056767-->
- `test_rejected_shrinking_full_is_not_broadcast_to_ui` (function) — Regression test for #287: a truncated full frame for a worktree flow is applied-but-rejected and must reach no UI client, with the cache keeping both rounds. <!--#f8ccb3897df5b4d7-->
- `test_shrinking_full_for_a_non_worktree_flow_is_still_broadcast` (function) — Guards the fix's scope: an ordinary (non-worktree) flow's legitimately shrinking full frame is still applied and relayed to the UI as before. <!--#bb649d969e0702f0-->
- `test_growing_full_still_broadcasts_to_ui` (function) — Confirms the suppression doesn't break the worktree self-heal path — a full frame that adds records is accepted and broadcast to the UI. <!--#58b7512d986b9cf0-->

### `tests/test_xdist_output_parsing.py` (python) — Test suite verifying that the test-step output parser handles pytest-xdist (`-n`) worker-prefixed output correctly — parsing per-test pass/fail/skip ids and summary counts across tricky line shapes, and proving that new-test/regression classification and the critical-test gate yield identical results for xdist and serial recordings while Jest, Go, and Cargo parsing stay unchanged. <!--#528604874c06000b|1bebbbd4b6da1bf5-->
- `_fixture` (function) — Helper that reads a recorded test-runner output fixture file from FIXTURE_DIR as text. <!--#9c584e9ac40c5b79-->
- `xdist_output` (function) — Fixture supplying the recorded `pytest -n` (xdist) verbose output used across the parsing tests. <!--#567de7ddbc1ed45d-->
- `serial_output` (function) — Fixture supplying the recorded serial pytest verbose output used as the equivalence baseline. <!--#b74ddbceb2673423-->
- `TestParseTestIdsXdist` (class) — Test class verifying that `_parse_test_ids`/`_parse_skipped_test_ids`/`_parse_test_summary_counts` correctly harvest per-test results from real xdist output without duplication or miscounting. <!--#33de4e59ff85f622-->
  - `TestParseTestIdsXdist.test_parses_every_per_test_line` (method) — Asserts every passed and failed test id in the xdist recording is parsed with the right verdict. <!--#6903fcae776c270c-->
  - `TestParseTestIdsXdist.test_no_duplicates_and_stable_order` (method) — Asserts parsed ids are unique and preserve the interleaved worker ordering of the result lines. <!--#2e36985d711fc9ca-->
  - `TestParseTestIdsXdist.test_skipped_tests_are_not_reported_as_passed` (method) — Asserts skipped tests never appear among the parsed pass/fail results. <!--#429a55588089d539-->
  - `TestParseTestIdsXdist.test_dispatch_lines_without_status_are_ignored` (method) — Asserts xdist's bare `file::test` dispatch lines are not counted, so tests are not double-counted. <!--#f01912309935a079-->
  - `TestParseTestIdsXdist.test_parses_skipped_ids` (method) — Asserts `_parse_skipped_test_ids` extracts exactly the expected skipped ids from xdist output. <!--#3c78e9ea4a7d8927-->
  - `TestParseTestIdsXdist.test_summary_counts_not_double_counted` (method) — Asserts `_parse_test_summary_counts` returns the true (5, 2) pass/fail totals rather than inflated counts. <!--#6be954ace4ffd593-->
  - `TestParseTestIdsXdist.test_passed_phase_summary_uses_per_test_counts` (method) — Asserts the slimmed passed-phase summary reports the per-test-derived "5 passed, 2 failed" figures. <!--#54cedfdbac0cc2e8-->
- `TestParseTestIdsXdistLineShapes` (class) — Test class covering edge-case line shapes the xdist parser must accept or reject (optional percent field, multi-digit workers, xfail/xpass, traceback headers, `-rA` summary lines, mixed formats, reruns). <!--#5e9ab6f4a64b892b-->
  - `TestParseTestIdsXdistLineShapes.test_percent_field_is_optional` (method) — Asserts a worker-prefixed result line without the progress-percent field still parses. <!--#762b48e211d65c3a-->
  - `TestParseTestIdsXdistLineShapes.test_two_digit_worker_ids` (method) — Asserts worker ids with two or more digits (e.g. `[gw11]`) are recognised. <!--#f13683b6620083dd-->
  - `TestParseTestIdsXdistLineShapes.test_xpass_xfail_not_treated_as_pass_or_fail` (method) — Asserts XFAIL/XPASS lines are ignored rather than classified as passes or failures. <!--#6e4107ab99dd96c2-->
  - `TestParseTestIdsXdistLineShapes.test_worker_prefixed_traceback_header_is_not_a_result` (method) — Asserts the worker-prefixed platform line inside a FAILURES traceback block is not mistaken for a test result. <!--#b527420a8f388c03-->
  - `TestParseTestIdsXdistLineShapes.test_short_summary_lines_are_not_per_test_results` (method) — Asserts `-rA` short-summary lines are not harvested, since they would duplicate the real per-test lines. <!--#3a0da6527327f6f0-->
  - `TestParseTestIdsXdistLineShapes.test_mixed_serial_and_xdist_output_is_deduplicated` (method) — Asserts a test reported in both serial and xdist line shapes yields a single entry. <!--#50f8403b0c8cec87-->
  - `TestParseTestIdsXdistLineShapes.test_same_id_with_conflicting_status_keeps_both` (method) — Asserts a rerun test id reported with conflicting verdicts keeps both entries so the failure is not hidden. <!--#963a9b24f395d316-->
- `_normalized_classification` (function) — Helper that runs `_classify_results` against TESTS_ADDED and sorts the passed/failed lists so two runs can be compared deterministically. <!--#4fe0d25376629c1a-->
- `TestClassificationEquivalence` (class) — Test class asserting new-test vs regression classification is identical and correct for xdist and serial recordings. <!--#5d6e43aaf52ca693-->
  - `TestClassificationEquivalence.test_xdist_matches_serial` (method) — Asserts classification of the xdist recording equals that of the serial recording. <!--#aba21cee41438c2b-->
  - `TestClassificationEquivalence.test_xdist_classification_is_correct` (method) — Asserts the exact new-test and regression pass/fail sets and counts derived from xdist output. <!--#dfc12c79907409f3-->
  - `TestClassificationEquivalence.test_serial_recording_still_classifies_identically` (method) — Zero-regression anchor asserting the serial format keeps its original classification counts. <!--#8fbdc78e8c52da3d-->
- `TestCriticalGateEquivalence` (class) — Test class asserting the critical-test gate (`_detect_critical_failures`) behaves identically and stays effective when fed xdist output. <!--#f323543062b781f8-->
  - `TestCriticalGateEquivalence._detect` (method) — Helper that parses ran and skipped ids from output and runs `_detect_critical_failures` against CRITICAL_PATTERNS. <!--#d23527e0b85bd9b6-->
  - `TestCriticalGateEquivalence.test_xdist_matches_serial` (method) — Asserts the critical-gate verdict is the same for xdist and serial recordings. <!--#25c1bce2f28099c9-->
  - `TestCriticalGateEquivalence.test_gate_stays_live_under_xdist` (method) — Asserts the gate still flags skipped critical tests and never-collected critical patterns while leaving tests that actually ran alone. <!--#4702e2446f49c7a9-->
  - `TestCriticalGateEquivalence.test_missing_detection_is_not_silently_disabled` (method) — Asserts xdist output yields parseable ran and skipped ids, so the missing-critical-test detection is not silently short-circuited. <!--#0dca6771eb888089-->
- `TestOtherFormatsUnchanged` (class) — Test class guarding that serial pytest, Jest, Go test, and Cargo output parsing are unaffected by the xdist support. <!--#b17967ffcf4369fb-->
  - `TestOtherFormatsUnchanged.test_serial_pytest` (method) — Asserts serial pytest output still yields the expected passed, failed, skipped ids and summary counts. <!--#0378985f1f64675d-->
  - `TestOtherFormatsUnchanged.test_jest` (method) — Asserts Jest ✓/✕ output still parses into pass/fail test names. <!--#16a248e6386f4971-->
  - `TestOtherFormatsUnchanged.test_go_test` (method) — Asserts `--- PASS/FAIL` Go test output still parses into pass/fail test names. <!--#4e670a5537af0b6e-->
  - `TestOtherFormatsUnchanged.test_cargo_summary_counts` (method) — Asserts Cargo's `test result:` line still yields the correct summary pass/fail counts. <!--#89fe3f92674a80b1-->

## `tests/commands/` — Pytest package for the CLI command layer, bundling the `merge` subsystem suite plus tests for `run` (resume/interrupt, retry-decision arbitration, plan-mode and preset/type flags, worktree mode), session/run-marker ownership in `end_session`, `--from-issue` finalization and merge-time issue backfill, `review-scope diff` baseline and `--path` filtering, `code-index search`, and CLI i18n key/rendering guarantees. <!--#8b8dfdc402206fe2|f571990478477555-->

### `tests/commands/__init__.py` (python) — Package init marker for the se3 command tests directory, containing only a header comment and no functional code. <!--#2e351cd9cd7e4289|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/commands/test_cli_i18n.py` (python) — Test suite guarding the CLI i18n migration: it AST-scans migrated modules to verify every literal `t()` key exists in the en-US catalog, checks zh-CN adds no orphan keys and falls back per key, and drives CLI commands (issue/history/merge/plan-mode/scope/usage) under SE3_LANG=en-US vs zh-CN to assert status tokens, prose labels, and prompt chrome are genuinely localized at call time. <!--#69c316a84c31d344|5ee17cc8b2fe96b2-->
- `_t_literal_keys` (function) — Test helper that AST-parses a source file and returns the set of string-literal first arguments passed to `t(...)`, i.e. the translation keys that must resolve against the catalog. <!--#124ba74559d1d53a-->
- `test_every_used_key_present_in_en_us` (function) — Parametrized test asserting that every literal `t()` key used by a migrated module exists in the en-US catalog. <!--#cdc6c0782d82c9d5-->
- `test_all_modules_actually_migrated` (function) — Sanity test asserting each module listed in MIGRATED_MODULES actually contains at least one `t()` call site. <!--#d66f3785d1de66ca-->
- `test_zh_keys_are_subset_of_en_base` (function) — Asserts zh-CN introduces no orphan keys, i.e. its key set is a subset of the en-US base catalog. <!--#4f9598f4007c3a89-->
- `test_missing_zh_key_falls_back_to_en_per_key` (function) — Verifies per-key fallback: a key present only in en-US renders the en-US string even when the language is zh-CN. <!--#503206e35e411056-->
- `test_command_output_switches_language` (function) — Parametrized end-to-end test that invokes CLI commands under SE3_LANG=en-US vs zh-CN and asserts the output contains the expected localized substrings and genuinely differs. <!--#be8d6573c1c80fff-->
- `test_se3_lang_env_drives_cli_output` (function) — Asserts the SE3_LANG environment variable (top of the precedence chain) selects the CLI output language, using the `merge` command's error message. <!--#c035ffeb3e10862b-->
- `test_multiline_prompt_chrome_is_resolved_at_call_time` (function) — Verifies that cli._read_multiline_input resolves its prompt title/message translations at call time (defaults None, resolved in body) rather than at import time, so the task-input prompt follows the project language. <!--#108a34766bb022a7-->
- `_cell_texts` (function) — Test helper that renders a Rich console callable into plain recorded text so table contents can be asserted on. <!--#ca75136990bf0ee5-->
- `test_issue_list_and_show_localize_status_values` (function) — Asserts that issue_cmd's list and show commands localize the status token (e.g. open -> 待处理) under zh-CN instead of emitting the raw enum value. <!--#78a481c5a5683dac-->
- `test_history_tables_localize_status_values` (function) — Asserts that history_cmd's flow-list table renders engine status tokens as translated text (e.g. completed -> 已完成) under zh-CN rather than the raw enum value. <!--#043f85c3fd625134-->
- `test_history_show_scope_round_localized` (function) — Verifies that `history show`'s SELF_CHECK scope-audit row renders through a localized i18n template — producing the translated Chinese text (including a localized `scope_mode` value) under `SE3_LANG=zh-CN` while preserving the historical English `incremental diff #2 (fix 1)` format under `en-US`. <!--#c7effb75677616c1-->
- `test_history_show_plan_mode_value_and_legacy_reason_localized` (function) — CLI test asserting that under SE3_LANG=zh-CN the `history show` output translates plan-mode enum values and the projection-authored LEGACY_INFER_REASON sentence, while an engine-persisted reason string is printed verbatim as flow data. <!--#5ef2e6e7765d4b4b-->
- `test_g10_cli_keys_exist_in_both_catalogs` (function) — Catalog-completeness test verifying every G10 plan-mode/scope/usage CLI key in G10_CLI_KEYS is present in both the en-US and zh-CN catalogs loaded via load_catalog. <!--#550e46fc9c93bdb6-->
- `test_g10_cli_prose_keys_are_translated` (function) — Test asserting the prose G10 CLI labels (plan_mode, scope, usage header, actual/estimated cost) are genuinely translated in zh-CN rather than raw dotted keys or copies of the en-US strings. <!--#0440988582ebc735-->

### `tests/commands/test_code_index_search.py` (python) — Pytest suite driving the `luo code-index search` CLI (grep-style search over code-index item lines) against a hand-authored `code-index.md`, verifying regex-vs-`-F` literal matching, case sensitivity/`-i`, `-m` max-count and exit codes, symbol path rendering, fingerprint-comment stripping, `-n` no-op acceptance, and rebuild hints for invalid/unbuilt states. <!--#6674d5cef7a156b0|f75e7bb6223de2e3-->
- `built_project` (function) — A pytest fixture that scaffolds a temporary project whose tianluo/code-index.md holds the hand-authored `_MD` map and monkeypatches `code_index_cmd.get_project_root` to resolve there, so `code-index search` CLI tests run against deterministic fixed content. <!--#6af1ff9712d318b6-->
- `_match_lines` (function) — Test helper that extracts only the emitted item-bullet match lines (those starting with '- `') from command output, dropping diagnostics. <!--#056ae148d158e41a-->
- `test_regex_match_hits_and_exit_zero` (function) — Asserts patterns are treated as regex by default, so `Greet.r` matches the `Greeter` lines and exits 0. <!--#333e9cc6a95a364e-->
- `test_fixed_strings_literal_not_regex` (function) — Verifies the `-F` flag treats the pattern as a literal string, matching only the line containing `a.*b` verbatim rather than as a regex. <!--#5dfd3f6ae508ccaf-->
- `test_case_sensitive_by_default_and_ignore_case` (function) — Checks searches are case-sensitive by default (lowercase `greeter` misses) and that `-i` enables case-insensitive matching. <!--#dc1c4359c11a2045-->
- `test_symbol_match_carries_owning_file_path` (function) — Confirms a symbol hit is rendered with its full `relpath::local_id` path (e.g. `src/mod.py::Greeter.hello`) rather than a bare bullet. <!--#6dc17e774f91a844-->
- `test_output_has_no_fingerprint_comments` (function) — Ensures search output rebuilt from the structured index never leaks the md's embedded `<!--#...-->` fingerprint comments. <!--#2708961ec2df9843-->
- `test_max_count_truncates` (function) — Verifies `-m 2` caps the number of emitted matches at two even when more lines would match. <!--#5316c1705585f9e8-->
- `test_max_count_zero_prints_nothing_exits_one` (function) — Verifies `-m 0` prints no lines and exits 1, matching grep's exit-status behavior. <!--#c1a5c2be6fe0714b-->
- `test_no_match_exits_one_with_message` (function) — Asserts an unmatched pattern exits 1 and prints the 'No code-index item matched' message with no match lines. <!--#820feaceaafb191e-->
- `test_invalid_regex_exits_two` (function) — Asserts a malformed regex (unbalanced `[`) yields grep-style exit 2 and an 'Invalid regular expression' message. <!--#90ae44b0f8839252-->
- `test_line_number_flag_accepted_exit_zero` (function) — Asserts the grep-muscle-memory `-n` flag is accepted (no longer a 'No such option' error) and that a matching code-index search still exits 0 with match lines. <!--#e7aea693883a5e41-->
- `test_line_number_output_identical_to_without` (function) — Verifies `-n` is a true byte-for-byte no-op by asserting a search with `-n` produces identical exit code and output to the same search without it. <!--#230e8880e4f468c5-->
- `test_line_number_combines_with_other_flags` (function) — Confirms `-n` composes cleanly with `-i`, `-F`, and `-m`, leaving each flag's semantics, exit code, and line-for-line output unchanged versus the same call without `-n`. <!--#a339dc6a5cb38654-->
- `test_unbuilt_map_hints_rebuild` (function) — Asserts that with no code-index.md on disk the search exits 1 and hints to run `code-index rebuild`, like the other subcommands. <!--#1b4d50face2f5cec-->

### `tests/commands/test_end_session_run_marker.py` (python) — Test suite for `end-session`'s `run.pid` ownership marker handling, covering machine-scoped marker discovery (foreign markers ignored, local and legacy single-line markers still found), recovery of markers abandoned by killed runs, refusal to terminate or archive when the marker is foreign or unreadable (even with an operator `--pid` hint), and the claim/hold/release of ownership across the destructive cleanup window. <!--#7a80ca411565b4a7|67d7ce00504c2e4a-->
- `_state_dir` (function) — Test helper returning the `tianluo/state` directory under a given project root. <!--#9f86e3797e795c3d-->
- `_live_local_pid` (function) — Test helper returning a pid that is alive on this machine but distinct from the test process (the parent pid), standing in for a real concurrent `luo run` as seen from the far side. <!--#b7930121f874fa9d-->
- `_write_marker` (function) — Test helper that creates the state directory and writes the given text into its `run.pid` marker file, returning the marker path. <!--#decfa930d92de4f7-->
- `TestForeignMarkerIsIgnoredLocally` (class) — Tests that a `run.pid` recorded on another machine is neither read nor probed locally, while local and legacy single-line markers are still discovered. <!--#2b5352cca10c91ab-->
  - `TestForeignMarkerIsIgnoredLocally.test_read_run_pidfile_returns_none_for_foreign_record` (method) — Asserts `_read_run_pidfile` returns `None` when the marker names a foreign machine. <!--#43666a902b637805-->
  - `TestForeignMarkerIsIgnoredLocally.test_foreign_pid_never_reaches_the_liveness_probe` (method) — Asserts `_discover_pids_for_flow` skips a foreign marker entirely, so its PID is never handed to the liveness probe (which would otherwise match an unrelated local process). <!--#33d5273bf7fe397f-->
  - `TestForeignMarkerIsIgnoredLocally.test_local_marker_is_still_discovered` (method) — Asserts a marker recorded with this host's `stable_machine_id()` is still discovered by `_discover_pids_for_flow`. <!--#77de6cbcd180c203-->
  - `TestForeignMarkerIsIgnoredLocally.test_legacy_single_line_marker_is_still_discovered` (method) — Asserts a legacy PID-only `run.pid` (no machine line) remains discoverable for backward compatibility. <!--#bc23ba81d3edc8b1-->
- `TestAbandonedMarkerRecovery` (class) — Tests `_clear_stale_local_run_pidfile` and `end_session` reclaiming a marker abandoned by a killed run — clearing dead local/legacy markers, keeping live ones, and never touching foreign ones. <!--#5d7d77f651007f08-->
  - `TestAbandonedMarkerRecovery.test_dead_local_marker_is_cleared` (method) — Asserts a local marker whose PID is dead is removed and the call reports `True`. <!--#6cfc57670bf3e1e8-->
  - `TestAbandonedMarkerRecovery.test_dead_legacy_marker_is_cleared` (method) — Asserts a legacy single-line marker with a dead PID is also cleared. <!--#fa21fc4a0ba0197e-->
  - `TestAbandonedMarkerRecovery.test_live_local_marker_is_kept` (method) — Asserts a local marker whose PID is still alive is preserved and the call reports `False`. <!--#c9f1fa8fdb2d6568-->
  - `TestAbandonedMarkerRecovery.test_foreign_marker_is_never_cleared_from_here` (method) — Asserts a foreign-machine marker is left intact even when the local liveness probe would call it dead, since only the owning host may judge its own PID. <!--#c088fb7578c0bbe5-->
  - `TestAbandonedMarkerRecovery.test_end_session_clears_marker_and_unblocks_resume` (method) — End-to-end check that running `end_session` on the owning machine deletes the abandoned marker so `foreign_run_holder` no longer reports a holder and other machines can resume. <!--#be231f12475f5204-->
- `test_own_pid_marker_is_treated_as_stale` (function) — Asserts a marker naming the current (non-`luo run`) process is treated as a recycled PID and cleared. <!--#194cc93fdfc1c736-->
- `TestForeignMarkerBlocksCleanup` (class) — Asserts that a `run.pid` marker owned by another machine makes `_terminate_session_process` report inconclusive — even against an operator `--pid` hint or an unstamped flow id — while a different flow's or a local marker still terminates, and that `end_session` then preserves the remote flow's review baselines. <!--#f1b8b59c2d44888b-->
  - `TestForeignMarkerBlocksCleanup.test_terminate_is_inconclusive_on_foreign_marker` (method) — A marker naming a foreign machine makes termination return `ok is False` with the machine id surfaced in the detail string. <!--#16a3eefcc821dde0-->
  - `TestForeignMarkerBlocksCleanup.test_operator_supplied_pid_does_not_override_a_foreign_marker` (method) — An explicit `--pid` must not unblock the destructive path over a foreign marker nor signal that unrelated local pid. <!--#1ea279e09078b38d-->
  - `TestForeignMarkerBlocksCleanup.test_unstamped_foreign_marker_also_blocks` (method) — A foreign marker with no flow id stamped yet cannot be proved to be a different flow, so termination refuses. <!--#630c1df9340753c4-->
  - `TestForeignMarkerBlocksCleanup.test_foreign_marker_of_a_different_flow_does_not_block` (method) — A foreign marker explicitly stamped with another flow id is not this flow's owner, so termination proceeds normally. <!--#29c8f2422b72ea73-->
  - `TestForeignMarkerBlocksCleanup.test_local_marker_still_terminates_normally` (method) — A marker from this machine whose recorded pid is not a live run does not block termination. <!--#b5ec6c0c4ab6aff3-->
  - `TestForeignMarkerBlocksCleanup.test_end_session_keeps_review_scopes_of_a_remotely_running_flow` (method) — End-to-end: `end_session` against a remotely-held marker exits 1, skips archiving, and leaves the review-scope baselines intact. <!--#4ed5e2bad4b53ce1-->
- `TestUnreadableMarkerBlocksCleanup` (class) — Asserts that a malformed or unreadable `run.pid` blocks cleanup exactly like a foreign one (never collapsing into "no marker"), while a genuinely absent marker still allows termination. <!--#c879c5a2c72e147a-->
  - `TestUnreadableMarkerBlocksCleanup.test_malformed_marker_makes_termination_inconclusive` (method) — Parametrised over empty/garbage/invalid-pid marker bodies, termination reports failure and names the marker path in its detail. <!--#88abcb8368ea4c45-->
  - `TestUnreadableMarkerBlocksCleanup.test_unreadable_marker_makes_termination_inconclusive` (method) — A marker whose read raises (simulated by making `run.pid` a directory) makes termination inconclusive rather than assumed-free. <!--#a406b02e8f2767d2-->
  - `TestUnreadableMarkerBlocksCleanup.test_operator_supplied_pid_does_not_override_an_unreadable_marker` (method) — An operator `--pid` must not force termination past an undecodable marker, and no signal is sent. <!--#916651b9105400e7-->
  - `TestUnreadableMarkerBlocksCleanup.test_absent_marker_still_terminates_normally` (method) — With no `run.pid` present at all, termination succeeds — confirming the guard keys on marker existence, not on decode failure. <!--#ba38d20b2ab97def-->
  - `TestUnreadableMarkerBlocksCleanup.test_end_session_keeps_review_scopes_on_an_unreadable_marker` (method) — End-to-end: a torn marker makes `end_session` exit 1 without archiving or deleting review baselines. <!--#44f1e698c5ce4bd8-->
- `TestOwnershipClaim` (class) — Test class asserting that `end-session` takes, holds, and releases the `run.pid` ownership marker across its destructive termination/cleanup window, so a concurrent resume on another machine is excluded and the flow is left resumable afterwards. <!--#a825016974e71b14-->
  - `TestOwnershipClaim.test_claim_creates_a_marker_naming_this_process` (method) — `_claim_run_marker` writes a marker recording this pid, this machine id, and the target flow id. <!--#b41b0a2ab479a755-->
  - `TestOwnershipClaim.test_claim_fails_when_a_marker_already_exists` (method) — Claiming returns None when a marker is already present and leaves the existing holder record untouched. <!--#a4c932bbefbd059a-->
  - `TestOwnershipClaim.test_operator_supplied_relative_root_is_absolutized` (method) — Asserts `_resolve_main_root` turns operator-supplied relative roots (`.`, `..`) into absolute paths, since `acquire_run_marker` rejects a cwd-relative state dir. <!--#75c174a7e48c8762-->
  - `TestOwnershipClaim.test_relative_root_claims_and_completes_the_destructive_window` (method) — Asserts `end_session(project_root=Path("."))` still claims the marker in the real state dir, holds it across archiving, and releases it — so a relative root cannot abort after the run process was already killed. <!--#5e4240e25d847767-->
  - `TestOwnershipClaim.test_release_only_unlinks_our_own_claim` (method) — `_release_run_marker` deletes the marker only when it still names this process, leaving a marker that was overwritten by another owner in place. <!--#f18badb898e035fb-->
  - `TestOwnershipClaim.test_cleanup_runs_under_the_claim_and_releases_it` (method) — The claim is observably held for the whole archive step and removed afterwards, so the flow becomes resumable again. <!--#5f3024e6803f7a1c-->
  - `TestOwnershipClaim.test_marker_appearing_after_the_liveness_check_blocks_cleanup` (method) — The reported race: a remote resume publishing a marker just after the liveness check makes `end_session` exit 1, skip archiving, and leave both the baselines and the resumer's marker untouched. <!--#c8d35158b2d689b0-->
  - `TestOwnershipClaim.test_worktree_archive_never_carries_the_claim` (method) — The worktree archive excludes `tianluo/state/run.pid`, so the snapshot records the terminated flow rather than end-session's own claim. <!--#c94d870c39d03543-->
- `TestClaimExcludesStartAndResume` (class) — Checks the other direction of the protocol: `luo run` refuses to publish over a held or foreign `run.pid`, a live local run marker blocks end-session's claim, a dead marker does not wedge a new run, and a live end-session claim is never judged stale. <!--#dd14b562ab86b79e-->
  - `TestClaimExcludesStartAndResume._persistence` (method) — Helper building a `PersistenceManager` rooted at the given temp path for the run-side acquisition calls. <!--#9f54133c21a8ef1f-->
  - `TestClaimExcludesStartAndResume.test_a_run_cannot_publish_over_a_held_claim` (method) — `run._acquire_run_pidfile` reports blocked and leaves an existing live local claim intact. <!--#11959efdea93cb74-->
  - `TestClaimExcludesStartAndResume.test_a_foreign_run_marker_cannot_be_published_over` (method) — A marker from another machine likewise blocks acquisition and is preserved byte-for-byte. <!--#15b9ec5dec614e60-->
  - `TestClaimExcludesStartAndResume.test_run_flow_refuses_while_the_claim_is_held` (method) — `run_flow` exits 1 against a held claim without clearing the owner's marker on its way out. <!--#4dc35a8a4faf8073-->
  - `TestClaimExcludesStartAndResume.test_a_live_local_run_marker_blocks_the_claim` (method) — End-session may not claim while a live local run owns the state dir; `_claim_run_marker` returns None. <!--#c02de4910f516804-->
  - `TestClaimExcludesStartAndResume.test_a_dead_local_marker_does_not_wedge_a_new_run` (method) — A local marker whose pid is dead is treated as stale, so a fresh run still acquires the pidfile. <!--#5674a7ffbddf303e-->
  - `TestClaimExcludesStartAndResume.test_a_live_end_session_claim_is_never_judged_stale_by_a_run` (method) — `_run_marker_is_stale` returns False for a live end-session claim, so staleness heuristics cannot steal it and reopen the race window. <!--#fa3352137d87cd34-->
- `TestClaimIsRevalidatedThroughoutTheWindow` (class) — Asserts ownership is re-read immediately before every irreversible step — main/worktree archive, state clear, resumable clear, branch and worktree deletion — so a pre-upgrade run that overwrites the claim mid-window aborts the rest with FAIL rows and preserves snapshots and baselines. <!--#c81e23db894cb6e5-->
  - `TestClaimIsRevalidatedThroughoutTheWindow.test_main_archive_aborts_when_the_claim_was_taken_over` (method) — A takeover before `_archive_main_session` yields a FAIL row and leaves `engine.json` and the review baselines in place. <!--#04bb53f49d93360b-->
  - `TestClaimIsRevalidatedThroughoutTheWindow.test_worktree_archive_aborts_when_the_claim_was_taken_over` (method) — A takeover before `_archive_worktree_session` yields a FAIL row and leaves the worktree and its baselines intact. <!--#c1c9dcb828397ff8-->
  - `TestClaimIsRevalidatedThroughoutTheWindow.test_worktree_deletion_is_skipped_when_ownership_changes_mid_run` (method) — A takeover landing during the history sync — after the archive copy, before the delete — stops both branch and worktree deletion and records a cleanup_branch FAIL. <!--#641e66f89bb0ab54-->
  - `TestClaimIsRevalidatedThroughoutTheWindow.test_resumable_and_baselines_survive_a_takeover_mid_worktree_cleanup` (method) — A mid-window takeover in the worktree path retires the resumable snapshot and the review baselines on the same ownership re-read, so both survive and a clear_resumable FAIL is recorded. <!--#a1e5e2fb8723fcf0-->
  - `TestClaimIsRevalidatedThroughoutTheWindow.test_main_baselines_survive_a_takeover_after_the_state_archive` (method) — A takeover landing inside `clear_state` leaves the main flow's resumable snapshot and baselines intact with a clear_resumable FAIL. <!--#1065fef00ca62552-->
  - `TestClaimIsRevalidatedThroughoutTheWindow.test_branch_inference_window_is_revalidated_before_deletion` (method) — Because `_infer_worktree_branch` shells out to git for an unbounded time, ownership is re-read after it — a takeover inside the inference stops every deletion path. <!--#31a236cfd7d41e17-->
  - `TestClaimIsRevalidatedThroughoutTheWindow.test_main_state_archive_is_revalidated_before_clear_state` (method) — A takeover during the `engine.json` read prevents `clear_state` from running at all, preserving state file, snapshot, and baselines with an archive_session FAIL. <!--#87f3c3f4603863dd-->
- `TestTerminalDispositionGatesTheBaselineReclaim` (class) — Asserts review baselines are only reclaimed on a landed terminal disposition — when the state or worktree archive fails (ENOSPC/EACCES) the flow stays resumable, so its baselines survive even though the recoverable resumable snapshot is still cleared. <!--#bc4f16f87d377b15-->
  - `TestTerminalDispositionGatesTheBaselineReclaim.test_main_baselines_survive_a_failed_state_archive` (method) — When `clear_state` raises, `engine.json` and the baselines are kept (the flow is still offered by the resume picker) while the rebuildable snapshot is still cleared OK. <!--#0301fbeefd9fc4a4-->
  - `TestTerminalDispositionGatesTheBaselineReclaim.test_worktree_baselines_survive_a_failed_archive` (method) — When the worktree archive raises, the worktree and its baselines are preserved as the only copy of the unfinished work, with cleanup_branch SKIP and clear_resumable OK. <!--#16000d6a83f49ea6-->

### `tests/commands/test_from_issue_finalize.py` (python) — Test module covering synchronous and worktree `--from-issue` finalization: proving the source-issue lifecycle is closed out from run_flow's persisted terminal status (not the process exit code), that the cli wrapper only self-reverts genuine pre-flow dispatch failures, and that fresh-process resumes and in-flow merges resolve/reopen the issue idempotently end-to-end. <!--#65816e97e43b2241|967f18f32ab04605-->
- `_make_in_progress_issue` (function) — Test helper that creates an issue on disk and advances it to IN_PROGRESS, mirroring what a from-issue run does before dispatch, and returns the issue id. <!--#f6abe7c9c6b25e3d-->
- `_flow_with_source_issue` (function) — Test helper that builds a FlowInstance carrying source_issue_id and round-trips it through to_dict/from_dict to prove the id survives persistence for process-decoupled finalization. <!--#85f1a810d0a4356b-->
- `TestFinalizeSyncSourceIssue` (class) — Unit test class exercising run._finalize_sync_source_issue directly across completed/failed/worktree/no-issue/non-in-progress/error/missing cases. <!--#f4b8de6a321c3b00-->
  - `TestFinalizeSyncSourceIssue.test_completed_sync_resolves_issue` (method) — Asserts a COMPLETED non-worktree flow's source issue is transitioned to RESOLVED. <!--#3bcbd01a60d218c3-->
  - `TestFinalizeSyncSourceIssue.test_failed_sync_reopens_issue` (method) — Asserts a FAILED non-worktree flow reopens its source issue back to OPEN. <!--#11f7c2bb1d89ccf9-->
  - `TestFinalizeSyncSourceIssue.test_worktree_flow_is_skipped` (method) — Asserts a COMPLETED worktree flow does not resolve here (deferred to the trailing merge), leaving the issue IN_PROGRESS. <!--#e465ddc0f0622c7b-->
  - `TestFinalizeSyncSourceIssue.test_no_source_issue_is_noop` (method) — Asserts finalize is a safe no-op when the flow has no source_issue_id. <!--#d091839be2f1fdef-->
  - `TestFinalizeSyncSourceIssue.test_non_in_progress_issue_is_not_touched` (method) — Asserts an issue not held IN_PROGRESS (already RESOLVED) is left untouched by finalize. <!--#0a7a64915aae6a34-->
  - `TestFinalizeSyncSourceIssue.test_best_effort_swallows_update_errors` (method) — Asserts a raising IssueManager.update_status never propagates out of finalization, leaving the issue unchanged. <!--#05a637430da833bc-->
  - `TestFinalizeSyncSourceIssue.test_missing_issue_is_noop` (method) — Asserts finalize is a no-op when source_issue_id points at a non-existent issue. <!--#7c29df7e95951fac-->
- `TestFromIssueWrapperNoExitCodeFinalize` (class) — Test class asserting the `--from-issue` run wrapper never resolves or reopens an issue based on run_flow's exit code alone, leaving finalization to run_flow's own terminal branches. <!--#7666d88ccb796f72-->
  - `TestFromIssueWrapperNoExitCodeFinalize._invoke` (method) — Helper that invokes `run --from-issue 1` via CliRunner with get_project_root and run_flow patched to a fixed return code, returning the result and the run_flow mock. <!--#b0d7fc6d4c9756a5-->
  - `TestFromIssueWrapperNoExitCodeFinalize.test_pause_exit_zero_does_not_resolve` (method) — Asserts a run_flow return of 0 (pause/completion) leaves the issue IN_PROGRESS and confirms source_issue_id is threaded through to run_flow. <!--#caa9669649596745-->
  - `TestFromIssueWrapperNoExitCodeFinalize.test_nonzero_exit_with_persisted_flow_does_not_reopen_via_wrapper` (method) — Verifies that a non-zero run_flow exit which persisted an engine.json carrying source_issue_id suppresses the wrapper's self-recovery, leaving the issue exactly as run_flow left it (IN_PROGRESS). <!--#3488d8597e6bce62-->
- `TestFromIssueEarlyDispatchFailureReverts` (class) — Test class covering the wrapper's self-recovery that reverts the OPEN→IN_PROGRESS transition when a dispatch fails before any flow state carries the issue, while leaving persisted-flow failures alone. <!--#fc7e623a7ae06d46-->
  - `TestFromIssueEarlyDispatchFailureReverts.test_sync_pre_flow_failure_reverts_issue_to_open` (method) — Verifies a non-zero sync run_flow that persisted no engine.json reverts the issue back to OPEN so re-running `--from-issue` isn't blocked by the in-progress gate. <!--#a5fd8b7ce882ff6e-->
  - `TestFromIssueEarlyDispatchFailureReverts.test_sync_pre_flow_failure_reverts_despite_stale_prior_engine_json` (method) — Regression test that a pre-flow failure still reverts the issue to OPEN even when a stale prior-run engine.json carries the same source_issue_id, so the stale slot isn't mistaken for this dispatch's own flow. <!--#408d1e074cc815e5-->
  - `TestFromIssueEarlyDispatchFailureReverts.test_worktree_fork_failure_reverts_issue_to_open` (method) — Verifies a worktree dispatch failing before any worktree/engine.json exists reverts the issue to OPEN since no persisted flow carries it. <!--#089ba69cd96f8b1f-->
  - `TestFromIssueEarlyDispatchFailureReverts.test_worktree_completed_merge_failure_is_not_reverted` (method) — Verifies a COMPLETED worktree flow whose trailing merge failed (and whose engine.json carries source_issue_id) is left IN_PROGRESS, not reverted, so the retry-merge path can own the resolve. <!--#0966e6ac6bfb5ae7-->
- `_init_git_repo` (function) — Test helper that initializes a git repo with one commit so the real run_merge can inspect HEAD/branch and take the merge lock. <!--#2597e1701494528c-->
- `_create_ancestor_branch` (function) — Test helper that creates a branch at HEAD so it is an ancestor of the default branch, modeling the post-in-flow-merge landed state that finalize verifies before resolving the source issue. <!--#10e724931d88b980-->
- `_write_wt_engine` (function) — Test helper that writes a worktree engine.json under a given path carrying source_issue_id and worktree metadata, mirroring how a real `--worktree` from-issue flow persists state. <!--#45f263b8f730a9a7-->
- `_patch_real_merge` (function) — Test helper that lets the real run_merge execute while stubbing only its git orchestrator and branch-existence probe and capturing render_text output. <!--#86d3d910aac912e2-->
- `_success_report` (function) — Test helper returning a successful MergeReport for the given branch. <!--#d3bd772e64e45df8-->
- `_failure_report` (function) — Test helper returning a failed MergeReport for the given branch. <!--#401d2d05ed3f25c4-->
- `TestWorktreeFromIssuePauseResumeMergeResolvedE2E` (class) — End-to-end test class for the worktree pause → fresh-process resume → COMPLETED chain, exercising the real finalize/backfill path (only run_flow stubbed) across resolve, cleanup-skip, not-landed, and failed cases. <!--#f88a63fb6c5b2ef6-->
  - `TestWorktreeFromIssuePauseResumeMergeResolvedE2E.test_pause_then_fresh_resume_completed_resolves_issue` (method) — Verifies a paused worktree run resumed by a fresh process to COMPLETED (branch landed as a master ancestor) has its source issue resolved by the wrapper's real post-merge cleanup backfill. <!--#7a8ad12f4c6f25be-->
  - `TestWorktreeFromIssuePauseResumeMergeResolvedE2E.test_resume_completed_resolves_even_when_branch_cleanup_skips` (method) — Verifies that when CleanupManager fails to delete the landed branch, the independent source-issue resolve still fires and the resume still returns success. <!--#07721452cc2adf81-->
  - `TestWorktreeFromIssuePauseResumeMergeResolvedE2E.test_resume_completed_but_branch_not_landed_does_not_resolve` (method) — Regression test that a COMPLETED resume whose branch never merged (not an ancestor of master) neither resolves the issue nor reports a merge and signals failure, leaving the issue IN_PROGRESS. <!--#6dd2a56f4885f6a8-->
  - `TestWorktreeFromIssuePauseResumeMergeResolvedE2E.test_resume_to_failed_reopens_issue` (method) — Verifies a resumed worktree flow ending FAILED returns the source issue to OPEN and never invokes run_merge. <!--#b9560ec7f7be3cf6-->
- `TestSyncFromIssueResumeFinalizeE2E` (class) — End-to-end tests asserting that a synchronous (non-worktree) `--from-issue` flow resumed by a fresh process still finalizes its source issue purely from the persisted `source_issue_id`, covering the completed, max-retries, and abort exit paths. <!--#6f91b6feb2b67497-->
  - `TestSyncFromIssueResumeFinalizeE2E._persisted_running_flow` (method) — Helper building a resumable synchronous RUNNING flow with a running IMPLEMENT step, round-tripped through serialization to recover source_issue_id. <!--#a6962e9c1285e0d4-->
  - `TestSyncFromIssueResumeFinalizeE2E._persisted_exhausted_flow` (method) — Helper building a resumable synchronous flow whose PENDING step has already hit max retries so the next failure drives run_flow's mid-loop auto-fail branch. <!--#9a42df025303c08c-->
  - `TestSyncFromIssueResumeFinalizeE2E.test_resume_completed_resolves_source_issue` (method) — Asserts that resuming a persisted synchronous flow to COMPLETED via `run.resume_run` returns 0 and marks the source issue RESOLVED, without the `--from-issue` wrapper ever running. <!--#a4205caaa20811d6-->
  - `TestSyncFromIssueResumeFinalizeE2E.test_resume_mid_loop_max_retries_reopens_issue` (method) — Asserts that a resumed step failing with its retry budget already exhausted takes run_flow's mid-loop auto-fail early return (rc 1) and still reopens the source issue to OPEN. <!--#361a560a51d95bf2-->
  - `TestSyncFromIssueResumeFinalizeE2E.test_resume_mid_loop_abort_reopens_issue` (method) — Asserts that the other mid-loop early exit — a step failure routed through the failure-decision resolver to 'abort' — also returns 1 and reopens the source issue to OPEN. <!--#314473ba42b09c31-->

### `tests/commands/test_merge_backfill_issue.py` (python) — Test suite for `luo merge`'s source-issue backfill, verifying that branch→source-issue resolution (via live or archived worktree engine.json), the pre-delete branch→issue mapping, and the idempotent IN_PROGRESS→RESOLVED backfill together resolve a merged branch's source issue end-to-end while correctly skipping paused, failed, open, unmerged, and missing cases. <!--#0ddbd7aee9655e3e|6440c61811235cd3-->

- `_write_worktree_engine_json` (function) — Test helper that writes a worktree engine.json (live or under .archive/) with configurable name, branch, source_issue_id, status, worktree-mode and archived flags, returning its path. <!--#7809ec5a019eb129-->
- `_make_in_progress_issue` (function) — Test helper that creates an issue and transitions it OPEN → IN_PROGRESS, returning its id. <!--#3d30b404ee84fafb-->

- `_patch_merge` (function) — Test helper that monkeypatches render_text, MergeOrchestrator, _branch_exists, and the intent-scope scan so run_merge exercises the backfill path against a canned MergeReport. <!--#16416c4581e6aa94-->
- `TestFindWorktreeSourceIssueByBranch` (class) — Test class verifying find_worktree_source_issue_by_branch maps a merged branch back to its source issue only for completed worktree flows, handling live/archived state, paused/failed/non-worktree exclusions, missing data, and corrupt JSON. <!--#8de9d1cc375d951b-->
  - `TestFindWorktreeSourceIssueByBranch.test_live_worktree_match` (method) — Asserts a live worktree's branch resolves to its recorded source issue id. <!--#328038d4974c6154-->
  - `TestFindWorktreeSourceIssueByBranch.test_archived_worktree_match` (method) — Asserts a GC'd/archived worktree's engine.json under .archive/ still resolves its branch to the source issue. <!--#d5e8dcafe5979c06-->
  - `TestFindWorktreeSourceIssueByBranch.test_completed_flow_not_excluded` (method) — Asserts a COMPLETED flow is excluded from resumable runs but is still mapped by the branch→issue scanner. <!--#27bddd0d6759341e-->
  - `TestFindWorktreeSourceIssueByBranch.test_paused_flow_not_mapped` (method) — Asserts a PAUSED flow's branch is NOT mapped, so hand-merging partial work never resolves its still-in-progress issue. <!--#2d71825b83a87d99-->
  - `TestFindWorktreeSourceIssueByBranch.test_failed_flow_not_mapped` (method) — Asserts a FAILED flow's branch is NOT mapped back to its source issue. <!--#690ceacffe00e276-->
  - `TestFindWorktreeSourceIssueByBranch.test_no_match_returns_none` (method) — Asserts an unknown branch with no matching worktree returns None. <!--#8e8be71e70469ecc-->
  - `TestFindWorktreeSourceIssueByBranch.test_no_source_issue_returns_none` (method) — Asserts a worktree whose engine.json has a null source_issue_id returns None. <!--#26bc4176bec390df-->
  - `TestFindWorktreeSourceIssueByBranch.test_non_worktree_flow_ignored` (method) — Asserts a non-worktree-mode flow's branch is ignored and returns None. <!--#b9b4896765f16db1-->
  - `TestFindWorktreeSourceIssueByBranch.test_corrupt_engine_json_skipped` (method) — Test asserting a corrupt engine.json is skipped without raising while a valid sibling still resolves the branch's source issue. <!--#c7943dd8e244d9a9-->
  - `TestFindWorktreeSourceIssueByBranch.test_no_worktrees_dir_returns_none` (method) — Asserts a missing tianluo/worktrees directory returns None rather than erroring. <!--#53be37be7fac69de-->
  - `TestFindWorktreeSourceIssueByBranch.test_empty_branch_returns_none` (method) — Asserts an empty branch name returns None. <!--#bf91a2d8cedeac40-->
- `TestMapBranchesToSourceIssues` (class) — Test class verifying _map_branches_to_source_issues yields only branches with a source issue and that a pre-captured map still drives backfill after the worktree state is deleted. <!--#c5772b8d7e7c606b-->
  - `TestMapBranchesToSourceIssues.test_maps_only_branches_with_source_issue` (method) — Asserts the map includes only branches that have a source issue, excluding source-less and unknown branches. <!--#8133f47c61d124c8-->
  - `TestMapBranchesToSourceIssues.test_captures_before_worktree_deleted` (method) — Test simulating --delete-merged: the branch→issue map captured before worktree removal still resolves the source issue to RESOLVED even after the worktree state is gone. <!--#a6aca517b20a2757-->
- `TestBackfillResolvedSourceIssues` (class) — Test class verifying _backfill_resolved_source_issues resolves IN_PROGRESS source issues for merged branches while being idempotent and skipping open, unmerged, empty-map, and missing-issue cases. <!--#5a06fb98d29b4207-->
