- `TestRunMergeBackfill` (class) — Test class exercising run_merge's end-to-end source-issue backfill across success, paused-branch non-resolution, leftover/archived retry, and stash-pop-incomplete cases. <!--#e3d4ed8b91fa49ae-->
  - `TestRunMergeBackfill.test_success_resolves_source_issue` (method) — Asserts a successful merge of a completed worktree branch resolves its source issue and renders a 'Resolved source issue' line. <!--#6fd09edec4efff6d-->
  - `TestRunMergeBackfill.test_merge_of_paused_branch_does_not_resolve` (method) — Asserts hand-merging a PAUSED flow's branch succeeds but leaves the issue IN_PROGRESS with no resolve line. <!--#112eddad5cd5a28d-->
  - `TestRunMergeBackfill.test_retry_merge_of_leftover_branch_resolves` (method) — Asserts re-merging a leftover branch whose worktree was archived still catches up and resolves the source issue. <!--#64da2698ad245b3b-->
  - `TestRunMergeBackfill.test_stash_pop_incomplete_still_backfills` (method) — Test asserting that when the merge lands but stash-pop recovery fails (exit code 1), the source issue is still backfilled to RESOLVED and reported in the recovery panel. <!--#fa15fa74f74428d6-->
  - `TestRunMergeBackfill.test_success_without_source_issue_no_backfill_line` (method) — Asserts a successful merge with no worktree mapping emits no 'Resolved source issue' line. <!--#57bf3c529b5c8723-->
  - `TestRunMergeBackfill.test_retry_already_ancestor_branch_resolves` (method) — Asserts retrying a branch that now classifies as already-ancestor still resolves its still-IN_PROGRESS source issue via the guaranteed retry path. <!--#7cb2aaa41b293b98-->

### `tests/commands/test_review_scope_cmd.py` (python) — CLI tests for the `review-scope diff` command, covering baseline selection (implementation vs fix, plus active-flow defaults), the `--stat` summary view, and extensive `--path` filter semantics — directories, equivalent/re-rooting spellings, blank and whitespace-exact names, C-quoted tokens, and submodule inner paths — asserting diff and `--stat` views agree and out-of-scope filters exit 6. <!--#22859e5e7210a57f|bdcc88d9b7c271ae-->
- `_git` (function) — Helper that runs a git subcommand in a given repo root with output captured and returns its stdout. <!--#86876f4a28e71bc5-->
- `_repo` (function) — Helper that builds a throwaway git repo with `alpha.py`/`beta.py` committed and `/tianluo/` gitignored, returning its root. <!--#bfac269aef3b58ae-->
- `_persist` (function) — Helper that saves a `FlowInstance` carrying the given `review_scope` context so the CLI can look it up by flow id. <!--#c0e91e97abf88d02-->
- `_invoke` (function) — Helper that runs `review-scope diff` through the Typer `CliRunner` with `get_project_root` patched to the test repo. <!--#cc0992df85dc324f-->
- `_tree_fingerprint` (function) — Helper that returns a sorted list of relative paths plus SHA-256 content digests for every entry under a directory, used to assert nothing was written. <!--#d602128d1246415c-->
- `flow_with_baselines` (function) — Fixture producing a repo and flow holding both an implementation baseline (before the `alpha.py` edit) and a fix baseline (before the `beta.py` edit). <!--#fbb8437c971b6b3d-->
- `flow_with_a_changed_directory` (function) — Fixture producing a flow whose changes span a `pkg/` subdirectory plus one file outside it, for exercising `--path <directory>` filters. <!--#4f4c2caa7a6f84fb-->
- `TestReconstruction` (class) — Tests that baseline selection works: implementation spans the whole task, fix spans only the fix delta, implementation and the active flow are the defaults, and an empty scope reports no changes. <!--#0ccaaf5fb723ea26-->
  - `TestReconstruction.test_implementation_baseline_spans_the_whole_task` (method) — Asserts `--baseline implementation` shows both the implementation-era and the fix-era additions. <!--#6b7601f8c2ef0954-->
  - `TestReconstruction.test_fix_baseline_spans_only_the_fix_delta` (method) — Asserts `--baseline fix` shows the fix addition and excludes the earlier implementation change. <!--#6539469f6a6ad3af-->
  - `TestReconstruction.test_default_baseline_is_implementation` (method) — Asserts omitting `--baseline` reconstructs against the implementation baseline. <!--#129c03d647e37dd6-->
  - `TestReconstruction.test_active_flow_is_the_default_target` (method) — Asserts omitting `--flow` targets the active flow and still renders its diff. <!--#2d898985ea092a46-->
  - `TestReconstruction.test_empty_scope_reports_no_changes` (method) — Asserts a baseline captured with no subsequent edits exits 0 and prints "No changes". <!--#167cfcf1b5881938-->
- `TestStatView` (class) — Tests that `--stat` prints per-file insertion/deletion counts and a totals summary without the diff body, and that it honours `--path`. <!--#a09318238a13668e-->
  - `TestStatView.test_stat_lists_per_file_counts_and_a_summary` (method) — Asserts `--stat` emits one `| +N -M` row per changed file plus a totals line, and never leaks diff content. <!--#cdab7c529ecaf691-->
  - `TestStatView.test_stat_honours_the_path_filter` (method) — Asserts `--stat --path beta.py` counts only the selected file. <!--#0f9313cbc99ab754-->
- `TestPathFilter` (class) — Tests `--path` filter semantics — single/repeated files, directory containment, equivalent and re-rooting spellings, blank values, exact whitespace, and C-quoted tokens — requiring diff and `--stat` views to agree and out-of-scope filters to exit 6. <!--#4d9aef903344a64f-->
  - `TestPathFilter.test_single_file_view` (method) — Asserts `--path alpha.py` shows only that file's diff. <!--#b23f71620b9427a1-->
  - `TestPathFilter.test_repeated_paths_select_several_files` (method) — Asserts repeating `--path` unions the selected files into one view. <!--#f824b4782d7ec49c-->
  - `TestPathFilter.test_path_outside_the_scope_is_an_error` (method) — Asserts a path not in the scope exits 6 with an error that names both the bad path and what is in scope. <!--#b13853be67a7c215-->
  - `TestPathFilter.test_path_below_a_changed_file_is_an_error` (method) — Asserts a filter beneath a regular changed file (`alpha.py/not-real`) is refused with exit 6 rather than resolved to that file. <!--#e0ad1ea95d1132c8-->
  - `TestPathFilter.test_path_below_a_changed_file_is_refused_by_the_stat_view_too` (method) — Asserts the `--stat` view refuses the same below-a-file filter with exit 6. <!--#74bb99560e0bfbed-->
  - `TestPathFilter.test_directory_filter_selects_the_files_under_it` (method) — Asserts `--path pkg` shows the changed files under that directory and nothing outside it, never reporting "No changes". <!--#ea8b5092e841ed95-->
  - `TestPathFilter.test_directory_filter_agrees_between_the_diff_and_stat_views` (method) — Asserts a directory filter selects exactly the same file set in the diff headers and the `--stat` rows. <!--#c744013171d40a1a-->
  - `TestPathFilter.test_equivalent_directory_spellings_select_the_same_files` (method) — Asserts `pkg/`, `./pkg`, and `pkg//` normalize to the same selection in both views. <!--#5316aab0cc306538-->
  - `TestPathFilter.test_normalization_admits_no_filter_that_names_nothing` (method) — Asserts normalization never re-roots a non-relative or below-a-file spelling into scope — `/pkg`, `../pkg`, and `pkg/mod_a.py/not-real/` all exit 6. <!--#61daba287d6dea1d-->
  - `TestPathFilter.test_blank_path_is_refused_rather_than_silently_dropped` (method) — Asserts an empty or whitespace-only `--path` exits 6 instead of being dropped and widening the view to the whole diff. <!--#41e0282a440d8394-->
  - `TestPathFilter.test_a_blank_path_alongside_a_real_one_still_fails` (method) — Asserts a blank `--path` combined with a valid one still fails with exit 6 and prints no diff. <!--#c26c89e5ab235472-->
  - `TestPathFilter.test_directory_outside_the_scope_is_still_an_error` (method) — Asserts a directory filter naming nothing in scope exits 6 and is echoed in the error. <!--#d58b9818a0d63dc1-->
  - `TestPathFilter.test_surrounding_whitespace_is_part_of_the_name` (method) — Asserts filters are not trimmed: for a file under `" pkg"`, `--path pkg` exits 6 while the exact `--path " pkg"` selects it. <!--#c922e02408fe16a7-->
  - `TestPathFilter.test_quoted_token_is_a_usable_filter_in_both_views` (method) — Asserts the C-quoted token a file is displayed as is accepted back as a `--path` filter in both views, while a malformed token exits 6 with the well-formed spelling in the hint. <!--#6d4a322e151b7e01-->
  - `TestPathFilter.test_a_copied_token_selects_the_file_it_was_shown_for` (method) — Asserts a copied quoted token resolves to the file it was displayed for, not to a literal namesake whose own escaped token remains separately reachable. <!--#2ab3a939b557c740-->
- `TestSubmoduleInnerPathFilter` (class) — Tests that a submodule's inner file can be filtered on its own without dragging in sibling entries, and that filtering the submodule itself still selects everything under it, with diff and `--stat` agreeing. <!--#15ec1a32b0086298-->
  - `TestSubmoduleInnerPathFilter.flow_with_submodule` (method) — Fixture building a repo with a `vendor` submodule whose `inner.py` is edited after the implementation baseline is captured. <!--#56b36acd38e7b773-->
  - `TestSubmoduleInnerPathFilter.test_inner_path_view_agrees_with_the_stat_view` (method) — Asserts `--path vendor/inner.py` selects exactly that one file in both the diff and `--stat` views. <!--#801423118344e99f-->
  - `TestSubmoduleInnerPathFilter.test_the_submodule_filter_still_selects_everything_under_it` (method) — Asserts `--path vendor` selects the gitlink entry and its inner file identically in both views. <!--#fbc7d40e25e48870-->
- `TestErrorPaths` (class) — Tests the command's distinct exit codes for unknown/absent flows (3), missing or unusable baselines (4), reclaimed snapshots (5), undecidable comparisons (1), and a bad `--baseline` value (2). <!--#84763a22aa1df880-->
  - `TestErrorPaths.test_unknown_flow_exits_flow_not_found` (method) — Asserts an unknown `--flow` exits 3 and names the missing flow. <!--#5e38fdf5c7d28f1e-->
  - `TestErrorPaths.test_no_active_flow_exits_flow_not_found` (method) — Asserts running with no active flow exits 3 and points at `--flow`. <!--#3836bca3352397b2-->
  - `TestErrorPaths.test_uncaptured_fix_baseline_exits_baseline_missing` (method) — Asserts requesting `--baseline fix` before any fix iteration exits 4 with an explanatory message. <!--#ed1a333bd7b87fe0-->
  - `TestErrorPaths.test_uncaptured_implementation_baseline_exits_baseline_missing` (method) — Asserts a flow that never reached IMPLEMENT exits 4 with that reason. <!--#b8da8d0dd2da15e7-->
  - `TestErrorPaths.test_unusable_baseline_reports_its_diagnostic` (method) — Asserts a baseline recorded as unavailable exits 4 and surfaces its stored diagnostic text. <!--#d1e64c2a61e5dea6-->
  - `TestErrorPaths.test_reclaimed_snapshots_exit_cleaned` (method) — Asserts deleting the flow's snapshot directory makes the command exit 5 and report the scope as reclaimed. <!--#bdede0955b284978-->
  - `TestErrorPaths.test_undecidable_comparison_exits_one` (method) — Asserts a baseline pointing at a commit the repo never held exits 1 rather than rendering an empty diff. <!--#28a9852544cc0954-->
  - `TestErrorPaths.test_unknown_baseline_value_is_a_usage_error` (method) — Asserts an unrecognised `--baseline` value is a usage error (exit 2) echoing the bad value. <!--#60cc58a36f6bd051-->
- `TestReadOnly` (class) — Tests the invariant that the command is a pure display surface, mutating neither the runtime state tree nor the git worktree. <!--#3837a47bd187429a-->
  - `TestReadOnly.test_the_command_writes_nothing` (method) — Asserts diff, `--stat`, and fix-baseline invocations leave the runtime-state fingerprint and `git status` output unchanged. <!--#3dc476da2bbf0707-->
- `flow_with_a_gitignored_change` (function) — Fixture producing a flow whose only change is a gitignored `generated/out.js` recorded solely in `review_scope.declared_changed_paths`. <!--#04de882958efeaa8-->
- `TestDeclaredIgnoredPaths` (class) — Tests that a gitignored declared path — which no snapshot comparison can attribute to a baseline — appears in neither view nor as an admissible `--path` filter. <!--#578ad7dff5cf945e-->
  - `TestDeclaredIgnoredPaths.test_gitignored_declared_path_is_not_claimed_by_a_baseline_view` (method) — Asserts the diff view exits 0 without listing the gitignored declared path. <!--#b0e03899ac615854-->
  - `TestDeclaredIgnoredPaths.test_gitignored_declared_path_is_not_admitted_as_a_filter` (method) — Asserts filtering on the gitignored declared path exits 6. <!--#bc6197277b1efd9e-->
  - `TestDeclaredIgnoredPaths.test_the_stat_view_does_not_count_it_either` (method) — Asserts `--stat` likewise omits the gitignored declared path. <!--#8ffc8cd91cfb98e8-->
  - `TestDeclaredIgnoredPaths.test_undeclared_ignored_file_stays_out_of_scope` (method) — Asserts an ignored file that was never declared is equally out of scope as a filter (exit 6). <!--#143781fbe09dad00-->
- `TestLocalization` (class) — Tests that the review-scope message catalog is complete in zh-CN and that reloading the command module under zh-CN renders genuinely Chinese help rather than an en-US fallback. <!--#f34aee4cbceb40f2-->
  - `TestLocalization.test_every_key_is_present_in_both_catalogs` (method) — Asserts every `review_scope.*` and `cli.help.review_scope*` key in en-US also exists in zh-CN. <!--#1fb44a2d2f2172ff-->
  - `TestLocalization.test_help_renders_in_chinese` (method) — Asserts reloading `review_scope_cmd` under zh-CN (then restoring en-US) yields help containing zh-only tokens and no English fallback text. <!--#509bc85130c300f2-->
- `flow_with_declared_paths` (function) — Fixture producing a flow with implementation and fix baselines plus a flat, flow-wide union of two ignored declared paths reported at different stages. <!--#f0375d6e057b5d99-->
- `TestDeclaredPaths` (class) — Tests that neither baseline view inherits the flow-wide union of declared paths, since no persisted comparison can attribute such a path to one domain. <!--#807f20a59812e04a-->
  - `TestDeclaredPaths.test_implementation_view_shows_only_what_its_baseline_compares` (method) — Asserts the implementation view shows its tracked change but neither declared ignored path. <!--#a3b5b2db8ed81c39-->
  - `TestDeclaredPaths.test_fix_view_does_not_inherit_the_earlier_stage_report` (method) — Asserts the fix view shows its own tracked change but no declared ignored path from either stage. <!--#195e55b63f618048-->
  - `TestDeclaredPaths.test_declared_path_is_not_a_usable_filter_in_either_view` (method) — Asserts filtering on a declared ignored path exits 6 under both the implementation and fix baselines. <!--#d0e07d2debe3ecfc-->
- `TestAmbiguousHeaderPaths` (class) — Tests that a filename containing the header's own `" b/"` separator still parses into the right section so the diff and `--stat` views select the same file. <!--#b56766afe893c1cb-->
  - `TestAmbiguousHeaderPaths._flow` (method) — Helper building a flow whose changed file is `pkg b/generated.py`, a name that makes the `diff --git` header ambiguous. <!--#becde9a15277e1fc-->
  - `TestAmbiguousHeaderPaths.test_header_paths_survive_the_split` (method) — Asserts `split_diff_sections` recovers the full old and new paths from a header whose filename embeds `" b/"`. <!--#584a6ba4a4160a0f-->
  - `TestAmbiguousHeaderPaths.test_rename_paths_come_from_the_rename_lines` (method) — Asserts rename sections take their old/new paths from the `rename from`/`rename to` lines rather than the ambiguous header. <!--#906834f2ff5e1e0c-->
  - `TestAmbiguousHeaderPaths.test_diff_and_stat_views_select_the_same_file` (method) — Asserts filtering on the ambiguous pathname yields the file in `--stat` and its real diff body, never "No changes". <!--#73b12c146f52c18c-->
- `TestLineBreakInAPathname` (class) — Tests that a tracked filename containing a newline still keeps a single intact `diff --git` header so the filter resolves identically in the diff and `--stat` views. <!--#35729d3762053814-->
  - `TestLineBreakInAPathname._flow` (method) — Helper building a flow whose only changed file is named `line\nbreak.py`. <!--#ff6e9c9d485dddaf-->
  - `TestLineBreakInAPathname.test_the_header_stays_one_line` (method) — Asserts reconstructing the scope and splitting it yields one section whose old and new paths are the line-break filename. <!--#700e1cae2490b219-->
  - `TestLineBreakInAPathname.test_diff_and_stat_views_select_the_same_file` (method) — Asserts filtering on the line-break filename counts `+1 -1` in `--stat` and shows the real diff body, never "No changes". <!--#6c769b406aa061a1-->
- `TestExactRenameFilter` (class) — Tests that an exact rename stays one indivisible section reachable by either side, with the diff and `--stat` views agreeing on both paths while the filter remains a restriction. <!--#e6489f3b9ef148f7-->
  - `TestExactRenameFilter._flow` (method) — Helper building a flow whose only change is renaming `alpha.py` to `gamma.py` after the implementation baseline. <!--#25aa45060146e5fd-->
  - `TestExactRenameFilter._stat_rows` (method) — Helper extracting the set of file names from `--stat` output rows. <!--#65c03918d32b5ce9-->
  - `TestExactRenameFilter._diff_paths` (method) — Helper collecting both rename sides from a diff's `rename from`/`rename to` lines. <!--#7286220a24d6204a-->
  - `TestExactRenameFilter.test_the_rename_renders_as_one_section` (method) — Asserts the unfiltered view renders the rename as a single section naming both sides. <!--#d0c4530de0cdb436-->
  - `TestExactRenameFilter.test_either_side_selects_the_same_files_in_both_views` (method) — Asserts filtering by either rename side yields both paths in both views and counts two changed files. <!--#7c4fb8ac08d2cb49-->
  - `TestExactRenameFilter.test_the_filter_is_still_a_restriction` (method) — Asserts an unrelated changed file does not ride along with a rename-side filter in either view. <!--#62c859b7aff99cb5-->
  - `TestExactRenameFilter.test_a_path_below_a_rename_side_is_still_refused` (method) — Asserts a path beneath either rename side is refused with exit 6. <!--#da7e82740e177c9e-->

### `tests/commands/test_run.py` (python) — Unit tests for the `run` command's flow-resume behaviour — resuming interrupted RUNNING steps (status reset to PENDING, `resumed` flag, output preservation, logging), retrying FAILED flows/steps (retry_count reset and input retry increment), refusing to resume COMPLETED flows from engine.json or stale snapshots, the interactive resume menu's inclusion/exclusion rules, and `_handle_step_interrupt` persisting Ctrl-C user interjections into flow context and the step's task_description. <!--#3d553bed03739d37|1768c83a0f5105ce-->
- `_stub_state_dir` (function) — Test helper that assigns a real absolute `tianluo/state` path to a mocked `PersistenceManager`'s `state_dir`, so `acquire_run_marker` doesn't mkdir a bogus `MagicMock/...` path or trip its absolute-path guard. <!--#d2c7a510ef5c5f25-->
- `TestResumeDetection` (class) — Test class covering `run_flow` resume semantics for a RUNNING (interrupted) step — transition to PENDING, `resumed` flag injection, output preservation, log output — plus rejection of resuming COMPLETED flows from either engine.json or a stale snapshot. <!--#71059c94cd4db241-->
  - `TestResumeDetection.setup_method` (method) — Fixture that builds a temp project with a RUNNING FlowInstance (completed ANALYZE/PLAN plus an interrupted RUNNING IMPLEMENT step) and persists it via PersistenceManager for the resume tests. <!--#f3bb10eb99c01bb3-->
  - `TestResumeDetection.teardown_method` (method) — Removes the temporary project directory after each test. <!--#f17fb20a9042d3fa-->
  - `TestResumeDetection.test_resume_detects_running_step_and_transitions_to_pending` (method) — Asserts that resuming a flow whose current step is RUNNING flips that step's status to PENDING so it can be re-executed. <!--#e6e5b5185b69e5d5-->
  - `TestResumeDetection.test_resume_rejects_completed_active_flow` (method) — Asserts that resuming a COMPLETED flow loaded from engine.json returns exit code 1 and never dispatches a step to the state machine. <!--#d44b9f49020d5434-->
  - `TestResumeDetection.test_resume_rejects_completed_snapshot_flow` (method) — Asserts that a stale COMPLETED per-flow snapshot under `tianluo/state/resumable/` is refused — exit code 1, no `save_flow`, no step dispatch. <!--#f7f1eab1509ed2e7-->
  - `TestResumeDetection.test_resume_injects_resumed_flag_into_step_inputs` (method) — Asserts that resuming an interrupted step sets `inputs["resumed"] = True` so the handler knows it is a continuation. <!--#3dd3a431a765cab4-->
  - `TestResumeDetection.test_normal_run_does_not_trigger_resume_logic` (method) — Asserts a fresh run (no flow_id, task_description given) calls create_flow to make a new flow rather than taking the resume path. <!--#a89401697ec5f8db-->
  - `TestResumeDetection.test_resume_preserves_existing_step_outputs` (method) — Asserts that partial outputs recorded before the interruption survive resume, and the `resumed` flag lands in `inputs` rather than `outputs`. <!--#63756b7eb3ab8071-->
  - `TestResumeDetection.test_resume_with_non_running_step_does_not_modify_status` (method) — Asserts that resuming a flow whose current step is already PENDING leaves the status untouched and injects no `resumed` flag. <!--#1c9e027713d780d4-->
  - `TestResumeDetection.test_resume_logs_interrupted_step_info` (method) — Asserts that resume emits an INFO log naming the interrupted step ("Resuming interrupted step" plus the step id). <!--#257dee275bf3591f-->
- `TestResumeFailedFlow` (class) — Test class covering `run_flow` resume of a FAILED flow/step — reset to PENDING, flow status back to RUNNING, `retry_count` reset on the model while the input retry counter increments, and retry logging. <!--#f8bb12b735c65787-->
  - `TestResumeFailedFlow.setup_method` (method) — Fixture that builds a temp project with a FAILED FlowInstance whose IMPLEMENT step is FAILED with exhausted retries, persisted via PersistenceManager for the failed-resume tests. <!--#b5b8cce540c4971a-->
  - `TestResumeFailedFlow.teardown_method` (method) — Removes the temporary project directory after each test. <!--#f17fb20a9042d3fa-->
  - `TestResumeFailedFlow.test_resume_failed_step_transitions_to_pending` (method) — Asserts that resuming a FAILED step flips its status to PENDING for re-execution. <!--#5ba226809e047dc7-->
  - `TestResumeFailedFlow.test_resume_failed_resets_flow_status_to_running` (method) — Asserts that resuming a FAILED flow persists it with a non-FAILED (RUNNING/COMPLETED) status via `save_flow`. <!--#10a674e7e1210fdd-->
  - `TestResumeFailedFlow.test_resume_failed_resets_retry_count` (method) — Asserts that the step model's exhausted `retry_count` is reset to 0 on resume. <!--#4bedbf95ee4eeef3-->
  - `TestResumeFailedFlow.test_resume_failed_increments_input_retry_count` (method) — Asserts that the `retry_count` carried in step inputs (used for conversation history) is incremented and the `resumed` flag set. <!--#69de12d0d589ec69-->
  - `TestResumeFailedFlow.test_resume_failed_logs_retry_info` (method) — Asserts that resuming a FAILED step logs "Retrying failed step from breakpoint" together with the step id. <!--#dea6e5d280ddd540-->
- `TestHandleResumeInteractiveFailedFlows` (class) — Test class verifying handle_resume_interactive lists FAILED flows (returning the chosen id with a 'failed'/retry label) while excluding COMPLETED flows from the menu. <!--#bdc29c164ca6374e-->
  - `TestHandleResumeInteractiveFailedFlows.test_failed_flow_appears_in_resume_menu` (method) — Asserts a FAILED flow appears in the resume menu and its id is returned when selected. <!--#4217027da5d41d60-->
  - `TestHandleResumeInteractiveFailedFlows.test_completed_flow_excluded_from_resume_menu` (method) — Asserts a COMPLETED flow is excluded from the resume menu (handle_resume_interactive returns None). <!--#c8071aeba6e59e51-->
  - `TestHandleResumeInteractiveFailedFlows.test_failed_flow_shows_retry_label` (method) — Asserts the resume menu renders a FAILED flow with a 'failed'/retry action label. <!--#9a98ca4549f26712-->
- `TestHandleStepInterrupt` (class) — Test class for _handle_step_interrupt: persisting Ctrl-C user interjections into flow.state.context['user_interjections'] and appending them (without doubling the '## Additional Instructions' section) into the step's inputs['task_description'], while handling empty and cancelled input. <!--#0a4c78f973748366-->
  - `TestHandleStepInterrupt._make_flow_and_step` (method) — Helper that builds a RUNNING flow and IMPLEMENT step seeded with a base task_description for interrupt tests. <!--#eb7933be8912fd4a-->
  - `TestHandleStepInterrupt.test_user_input_persists_to_context_and_step_inputs` (method) — Asserts a non-empty interjection is saved to flow context (with step_id/type/timestamp), appended once under '## Additional Instructions' in the step's task_description, the step reset to PENDING, and the flow persisted. <!--#487bffbd326aa9ea-->
  - `TestHandleStepInterrupt.test_repeated_interjections_compose_against_original_base` (method) — Asserts two successive interjections compose against the original base task, yielding exactly one section header with both bullets in order (no nesting). <!--#e3b11f4ca17debd3-->
  - `TestHandleStepInterrupt.test_empty_input_does_not_persist_or_modify` (method) — Asserts empty user input retries the step as-is: no interjection persisted, task_description unchanged, but status still reset to PENDING. <!--#3d22ebb9c05ab772-->
  - `TestHandleStepInterrupt.test_interrupt_on_later_step_does_not_double_section` (method) — Regression test that a second interrupt on a step whose task_description already carries a pre-composed interjection section does not double the '## Additional Instructions' section. <!--#17d79fe3b36f8212-->
  - `TestHandleStepInterrupt.test_cancelled_input_returns_none` (method) — Asserts cancelling the input prompt (Ctrl-C, returns None) saves the flow and returns None to exit, leaving step status RUNNING and no interjection persisted. <!--#683b5ebb6c69cc29-->
- `TestOutputFormatEventStream` (class) — Test class verifying the `--output-format` wiring: JSON mode emits the full NDJSON lifecycle (flow_started/step_started/step_completed/flow_completed) without touching the Rich renderer, while CLI mode still routes step output through `step_renderers.render_step_output`. <!--#9dad63d34b8ab759-->
  - `TestOutputFormatEventStream.setup_method` (method) — Fixture that builds and persists a temp RUNNING single-IMPLEMENT-step flow for the output-format event-stream tests. <!--#f28b251fa4b93ff7-->
  - `TestOutputFormatEventStream.teardown_method` (method) — Removes the temporary project directory after each test. <!--#c34398a3746e8dbf-->
  - `TestOutputFormatEventStream._run` (method) — Shared harness that mocks `PersistenceManager` and `StateMachine` (with a `run_step` side effect that fires the `on_running` callback like the real one) and invokes `run_flow` with the given `output_format`. <!--#eb6ff72108df8329-->
  - `TestOutputFormatEventStream.test_json_mode_emits_valid_ndjson` (method) — Asserts JSON mode writes the full flow lifecycle (flow_started/step_started/step_completed/flow_completed) as parseable NDJSON. <!--#0d712aaf27148a5a-->
  - `TestOutputFormatEventStream.test_cli_mode_routes_step_output_through_renderer` (method) — Asserts CLI (default) mode renders step output via step_renderers.render_step_output exactly once and returns exit code 0. <!--#c45e88d7a134ce2f-->

### `tests/commands/test_run_failure_action.py` (python) — Unit tests verifying the retry_decision mutual-exclusion between the CLI TTY prompt and the webui, covering how `_resolve_step_failure_action` adopts an existing webui response or falls back to race/pause/prompt across interactive and non-interactive paths, and how the `_cleanup_retry_decision_artifacts` helper idempotently removes only the deterministic call file and its sibling response variants. <!--#a5efa0cb57468a6e|da5a765665f0b15b-->

- `test_interactive_without_response_returns_race_and_writes_call` (function) — Asserts that interactive mode with no webui answer returns action "race" while still writing a retry_decision call file (the web-console chip) and no sibling response. <!--#2ddad507a85acd5a-->

- `test_interactive_unrecognized_decision_defaults_to_abort` (function) — Asserts that a garbled/unrecognized webui decision payload is treated as "abort" but still consumed (call file removed) in interactive mode. <!--#6704bb3a4a203401-->
- `test_cleanup_helper_removes_all_three_artifacts` (function) — Asserts run._cleanup_retry_decision_artifacts deletes the call file plus both the .response and .response.json sibling responses. <!--#809ae373b83e57ce-->

- `test_run_module_no_longer_speaks_the_retired_vocabulary` (function) — Source-level guard asserting the `run` module text no longer contains the retired `implementation_strategy` identifier. <!--#94ba1c744b8c7946-->
- `test_legacy_strategy_maps_onto_plan_mode` (function) — Parametrised test that each legacy `--implementation-strategy` value is translated into the expected `plan_decomposition`/`plan_granularity` pair passed to `run_flow`. <!--#2765e9593ce40142-->
- `test_legacy_strategy_prints_deprecation_notice` (function) — Verifies using the legacy `--implementation-strategy` flag still succeeds but prints a deprecation notice pointing at `--plan-decomposition`. <!--#66b5f71ec6123d12-->

### `tests/commands/test_run_worktree_mode.py` (python) — Unit tests for the worktree-mode run orchestration in `tianluo.commands.run` — covering branch-name slug helpers, `run_flow`'s main-repo `MergeLock` acquire/release contract, `run_worktree_mode` forking and merge/cleanup behavior (including `run.pid` marker ownership and PAUSED/failure skip cases), `find_resumable_worktree_runs` discovery, and `resume_run` routing between main-repo and worktree resumes. <!--#611eba7a66825cd7|70fc1043e7d71c61-->
- `TestBranchNameHelpers` (class) — Tests the slugify and worktree-branch-name generation helpers used to derive a branch from a task description. <!--#c5f0bce3c9d56342-->
  - `TestBranchNameHelpers.test_slugify_basic` (method) — Asserts _slugify_for_branch lowercases, drops punctuation, and hyphenates a normal task string. <!--#ba6a8a5ce922ae7d-->
  - `TestBranchNameHelpers.test_slugify_collapses_and_trims` (method) — Asserts _slugify_for_branch collapses runs of separators and trims leading/trailing junk. <!--#b080cead3111a330-->
  - `TestBranchNameHelpers.test_slugify_empty_falls_back_to_task` (method) — Asserts _slugify_for_branch returns the literal 'task' when the input slugifies to empty. <!--#694270524ccee34a-->
  - `TestBranchNameHelpers.test_slugify_truncates_to_30` (method) — Asserts _slugify_for_branch caps the slug length at 30 characters. <!--#af4f4f428d296548-->
  - `TestBranchNameHelpers.test_generate_worktree_branch_name_shape` (method) — Asserts _generate_worktree_branch_name produces a 'worktree/<slug>-<suffix>' name with exactly one slash. <!--#bd626727aa7fbf02-->
- `TestRunFlowMainLock` (class) — Test class verifying `run.run_flow`'s main-repo lock lifecycle across worktree and non-worktree modes, using mocked `MergeLock`, `PersistenceManager`, `StateMachine`, and `_run_flow_impl`. <!--#0023f6d46610f1bf-->
  - `TestRunFlowMainLock.test_sync_run_defers_acquire_and_releases_lock` (method) — Asserts that with `acquire_main_lock=True` the lock is built for the resolved main repo root and passed to `_run_flow_impl` as `main_lock` without being acquired up front, yet is still released on exit. <!--#c41e2c109b26cdd0-->
  - `TestRunFlowMainLock.test_worktree_body_takes_no_lock` (method) — Asserts that a worktree-mode run (`acquire_main_lock=False`) never constructs a `MergeLock` at all. <!--#d26050c8b82437b7-->
  - `TestRunFlowMainLock.test_lock_released_even_when_impl_raises` (method) — Asserts the main lock is still released exactly once when `_run_flow_impl` raises an exception. <!--#2831e59ddf3713e7-->
- `TestRunWorktreeMode` (class) — Test class covering `run.run_worktree_mode` orchestration — forking a worktree off the current branch, delegating to `run_flow` in worktree mode, skipping merge on failure or PAUSED status, handling fork errors, and keeping the `run.pid` marker alive across the whole flow-plus-cleanup lifecycle. <!--#c3a641f4e8fed3bf-->
  - `TestRunWorktreeMode.own_run_marker` (method) — Fixture that patches `run._acquire_run_pidfile` to return an already-held `MarkerClaim`, so the orchestration tests can use a fictitious worktree path without the real marker acquisition failing. <!--#0e5a8f66b63c362c-->
  - `TestRunWorktreeMode.test_success_merges_back` (method) — Asserts that a successful run forks a `worktree/`-prefixed branch off `main`, invokes `run_flow` inside the worktree with the lock-free worktree-mode kwargs, and finishes via `_finalize_worktree_cleanup` instead of a trailing `run_merge`. <!--#5a0150e2ba115409-->
  - `TestRunWorktreeMode.test_failure_preserves_and_skips_merge` (method) — Asserts that a non-zero `run_flow` return propagates as the exit code and no merge is attempted, preserving the worktree. <!--#dba6f632760fda7c-->
  - `TestRunWorktreeMode.test_paused_json_flow_skips_merge` (method) — Regression test that a run returning 0 but whose on-disk status is PAUSED skips the merge, so the paused flow's branch and worktree state are not deleted or archived. <!--#2632203e9350dd7f-->
  - `TestRunWorktreeMode.test_worktree_creation_failure_returns_error` (method) — Verifies a fork_worktree failure causes run_worktree_mode to return error code 1. <!--#d75b887f4222f144-->
  - `TestRunWorktreeMode.test_run_pidfile_survives_into_trailing_merge` (method) — Regression test asserting the wrapper (not `run_flow`, which is passed `manage_pidfile=False`) owns the worktree's `run.pid` marker — readable as (pid, `stable_machine_id()`) during both the flow body and the post-merge cleanup, and only cleared after `run_worktree_mode` fully returns — so `end-session` can't archive the worktree mid-merge. <!--#bbdc8b65c73fce28-->
- `_write_worktree_engine_json` (function) — Test helper that writes a worktree-mode engine.json under a synthetic worktree-x-1 state dir with configurable flow_id/status/branch fields, returning the data dict. <!--#6f95e8e2a0a24984-->
- `TestWorktreeRunDiscovery` (class) — Tests find_resumable_worktree_runs scanning for incomplete, worktree-mode engine.json files. <!--#7858c6cdcb782020-->
  - `TestWorktreeRunDiscovery.test_find_resumable_worktree_runs` (method) — Verifies a failed worktree run is discovered with its id, worktree flag, and branch metadata. <!--#7445ae57d587bf18-->
  - `TestWorktreeRunDiscovery.test_completed_worktree_run_excluded` (method) — Verifies a completed worktree run is excluded from resumable discovery. <!--#3bb8e480f4104f57-->
  - `TestWorktreeRunDiscovery.test_non_worktree_engine_json_ignored` (method) — Verifies engine.json files without is_worktree_mode set are ignored by discovery. <!--#66b41ccaa5400aef-->
  - `TestWorktreeRunDiscovery.test_no_worktrees_dir` (method) — Verifies discovery returns empty when no worktrees directory exists. <!--#28851cbefcab1f9d-->
- `TestResumeRun` (class) — Test class for resume_run routing: plain main-repo resumes acquire the lock by default, discoverable worktree runs re-dispatch lock-free in the worktree and trigger _finalize_worktree_cleanup only on success (skipping on failure or re-PAUSE), resumes where project_root IS the worktree drive cleanup from the resolved main repo, and COMPLETED worktree engine.json at project_root is not self-resumed. <!--#4430102d8e56f3fb-->
  - `TestResumeRun.test_resume_main_repo_flow` (method) — Verifies resuming with no worktree runs dispatches a plain main-repo resume that keeps the default (locked) behavior. <!--#e67c8165548d1775-->
  - `TestResumeRun.test_resume_worktree_run_then_merge` (method) — Asserts resuming a failed worktree run re-dispatches run_flow lock-free in the worktree and, on success, calls _finalize_worktree_cleanup once with the main root, branch, original branch, and worktree path. <!--#91fe4564019e60b6-->
  - `TestResumeRun.test_resume_worktree_run_failure_skips_merge` (method) — Verifies a failed worktree resume propagates the return code and skips the trailing merge. <!--#40c2b6e88d145d29-->
  - `TestResumeRun.test_resume_worktree_run_paused_again_skips_merge` (method) — Verifies a worktree resume that pauses again (status stays PAUSED) returns 0 but performs no merge. <!--#59e34856d21bbfd5-->
  - `TestResumeRun.test_resume_when_project_root_is_the_worktree_itself` (method) — Asserts a daemon resume whose project_root is the worktree itself still runs the flow body lock-free in that worktree but drives cleanup from the resolved MAIN repo, threading the worktree path through. <!--#a1bf3f70820d533b-->
  - `TestResumeRun.test_self_worktree_run_ignores_completed` (method) — Asserts a COMPLETED worktree engine.json at project_root is not self-resumed but falls through to a plain main-repo resume with the lock acquired by default. <!--#02e67279a637df1a-->
- `_make_in_progress_issue` (function) — Test helper that creates a bug issue in the given main repo and moves it to IN_PROGRESS, mimicking the state a from-issue worktree run holds. <!--#ee8a120730cfdb85-->
- `_write_wt_engine_with_source_issue` (function) — Test helper that writes a worktree engine.json carrying a persisted source_issue_id (plus status/branch/original) for source-issue finalize tests. <!--#b284294f2ed78dba-->
- `TestFinalizeWorktreeSourceIssue` (class) — Unit-test class asserting _finalize_worktree_source_issue reopens the source issue only on FAILED and is a no-op for every other terminal/paused status (resolution being run_merge's job). <!--#67e15fd3da50394e-->
  - `TestFinalizeWorktreeSourceIssue.test_failed_moves_issue_to_open` (method) — Asserts a FAILED worktree status moves the in-progress source issue back to OPEN. <!--#d94f49ee394b58a5-->
  - `TestFinalizeWorktreeSourceIssue.test_completed_merge_failed_keeps_in_progress` (method) — Asserts a COMPLETED status with a failed merge (merge_rc=1) leaves the issue IN_PROGRESS for a later retry-merge. <!--#ddf9d4fa1f059005-->
  - `TestFinalizeWorktreeSourceIssue.test_completed_merge_success_leaves_resolve_to_run_merge` (method) — Asserts a COMPLETED status even with a successful merge (merge_rc=0) does not resolve the issue, deferring resolution to run_merge. <!--#d5c8eb86b5618efa-->
  - `TestFinalizeWorktreeSourceIssue.test_paused_status_is_noop` (method) — Asserts a PAUSED (non-terminal) status never moves the source issue. <!--#5d004b9546c2f62b-->
  - `TestFinalizeWorktreeSourceIssue.test_no_source_issue_is_noop` (method) — Asserts that with no persisted source_issue_id the finalize does nothing and does not crash. <!--#48d217f027066e30-->
  - `TestFinalizeWorktreeSourceIssue.test_non_in_progress_issue_not_clobbered` (method) — Asserts an issue that is not IN_PROGRESS (e.g. still OPEN) is never touched, guarding against a second terminal pass clobbering it. <!--#52697ed5ad655965-->
- `TestRunWorktreeModeSourceIssue` (class) — Integration test class asserting run_worktree_mode wires source-issue finalize into its terminal branches: a COMPLETED (in-flow-merged) flow hands off to cleanup which owns the resolve, a FAILED flow reopens the issue and skips cleanup, and a json-mode PAUSED flow touches neither. <!--#f601c2852fcadc1d-->
  - `TestRunWorktreeModeSourceIssue._run` (method) — Test helper that runs run_worktree_mode with a fake run_flow persisting a source-issue-carrying worktree engine.json at the given exit code and on-disk status, returning the return code and the (possibly mock) cleanup callable. <!--#ab9fcd20ee20ae3b-->
  - `TestRunWorktreeModeSourceIssue.test_completed_flow_runs_cleanup_which_owns_resolve` (method) — Asserts a COMPLETED worktree flow (already merged in-flow) triggers `_finalize_worktree_cleanup`, which owns resolving the source issue. <!--#022629a1a855de9a-->
  - `TestRunWorktreeModeSourceIssue.test_failed_flow_reopens_issue_and_skips_cleanup` (method) — Asserts a FAILED worktree flow skips cleanup, returns the failure code, and reopens the source issue to OPEN. <!--#83f148b4189fbc7f-->
  - `TestRunWorktreeModeSourceIssue.test_paused_flow_does_not_touch_issue_or_cleanup` (method) — Asserts a json-mode PAUSED flow (exit 0 but on-disk paused) neither resolves/reopens the issue nor runs cleanup, leaving the issue IN_PROGRESS. <!--#a88d1bb1fc570a63-->
- `TestFinalizeWorktreeCleanup` (class) — Unit test class for _finalize_worktree_cleanup verifying that after an in-flow merge it deletes the merged worktree branch and resolves the (now-merged) source issue, with CleanupManager, MergeLock, and the branch-landed ancestry guard stubbed. <!--#f4b6ae3ecbef5fef-->
  - `TestFinalizeWorktreeCleanup.test_resolves_source_issue_after_inflight_merge` (method) — Asserts _finalize_worktree_cleanup calls delete_merged_branches once for the worktree branch and marks the source issue RESOLVED, with git/lock touchpoints and the branch-landed guard stubbed. <!--#1f7595649d6b54d0-->
- `TestResumeWorktreeSourceIssue` (class) — Integration test class asserting a fresh --resume process finalizes the source issue off the persisted status (decoupled from the original wrapper): COMPLETED runs cleanup, FAILED reopens the issue, and re-PAUSED touches neither issue nor cleanup. <!--#724ffbedf13432ac-->
  - `TestResumeWorktreeSourceIssue._resume` (method) — Test helper that seeds a discoverable non-terminal worktree engine.json then drives resume_run with a fake run_flow re-persisting the engine.json at the given exit code and status, returning the return code and the (possibly mock) cleanup callable. <!--#1db0ffe01933670e-->
  - `TestResumeWorktreeSourceIssue.test_resume_completed_runs_cleanup` (method) — Asserts a resumed worktree flow that completes hands off to `_finalize_worktree_cleanup` (which owns the resolve). <!--#0ac946ef8d6aaffa-->
  - `TestResumeWorktreeSourceIssue.test_resume_failed_reopens_issue` (method) — Asserts a resumed worktree flow that fails skips cleanup, returns the failure code, and reopens the source issue to OPEN. <!--#048959cd9cb6ff08-->
  - `TestResumeWorktreeSourceIssue.test_resume_paused_again_does_not_touch_issue` (method) — Asserts a resumed worktree flow that pauses again leaves the source issue IN_PROGRESS with no cleanup fired. <!--#cf33fed4bc8b6d24-->

### `tests/commands/test_worktree_cmd.py` (python) — CLI tests for the `luo worktree gc` command that patch the engine GC core (gc_worktree_runs) with crafted WorktreeGCReport objects to assert on flag plumbing (dry-run, --max-age-hours→seconds), the three-section report rendering (archived/reclaimed, unmerged-retention warning, skipped/errors), and non-zero exit-code mapping on errors. <!--#83a55bc24be9e903|fcb22b782aaf2c09-->
- `project_root` (function) — A pytest fixture returning a bare tmp_path directory to stand in for the project root (since get_project_root is patched to return it). <!--#f14a7a57a646fa9e-->
- `_invoke` (function) — Test helper that invokes the `worktree gc` CLI command while patching the project root, mocking `gc_worktree_runs` to return a supplied *report*, and swapping in a wide Rich console so table output doesn't wrap; returns the invocation result and the mock. <!--#b2ff1e0510f664f8-->
- `test_help_lists_gc` (function) — Asserts that `worktree gc --help` renders successfully and lists the --max-age-hours and --dry-run options. <!--#f727eeb9a19f8b71-->
- `test_dry_run_passes_flag_and_default_age` (function) — Verifies that --dry-run threads dry_run=True and the default 24h max-age to the core and that the rendered output shows the DRY RUN notice and reclaimed space. <!--#9655d15ade502f5d-->
- `test_max_age_hours_converted_to_seconds` (function) — Verifies that --max-age-hours N is converted to N*3600 seconds passed to the core with dry_run defaulting to False. <!--#2cc5e33f3180fd1f-->
- `test_report_three_sections_and_unmerged_warning` (function) — Asserts the rendered `worktree gc` report renders all three sections — archived (with reclaimed space), retained-unmerged (with a loud WARNING), and skipped — and exits 0. <!--#6355a02896ad2daa-->
- `test_errors_map_to_nonzero_exit` (function) — Asserts that a report containing any errored run makes the `worktree gc` command exit non-zero (1) and surface the error in output. <!--#1ded74e631e532b8-->
- `test_empty_report_reports_nothing_and_exits_zero` (function) — Confirms that an empty sweep exits 0 and prints a 'No worktree runs matched' message. <!--#23c854416e79b4bf-->

## `tests/commands/merge/` — Pytest package covering the `merge` command subsystem end-to-end: CLI input validation and integrate→reconcile version/changelog/tag behavior, dirty-working-tree pre-flight sweeping, the fcntl MergeLock (including cross-machine holder records and stale-break races), guardrail-repair amend/reset regressions, post-condition ancestry/version assertions, and the supporting modules ConflictResolver, FailureReason, LLMTrace, result models, runtime_sync, secret_redact, and version_aggregator. <!--#08578b43801bf30b|b9d9d38868672cb8-->

### `tests/commands/merge/__init__.py` (python) — Empty package-initializer marking tests/commands/merge as a Python package so its merge-command test modules can be discovered and imported. <!--#e3b0c44298fc1c14|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/commands/merge/test_amend_reset_regression.py` (python) — Regression test module for `MergeOrchestrator` that pins its merge post-condition checks to fail closed — stray non-merge commits on HEAD must report `silent_merge_loss`, a check timeout must report `postcond_check_timeout`, an unreadable/empty `post_merge_sha` must never be mistaken for a no-op success (while a genuine merge commit still passes), and `_verify_post_merge_conditions` must expose no fix-up-parent escape hatch — plus end-to-end `execute` runs on a real git repo asserting merged-branch ancestry and populated typed `MergeOutcome` entries on both success and failure paths. <!--#945c84d703ec7502|eddf8d39d8e08317-->
- `_init_repo` (function) — Test helper that initializes a git repo with an initial commit and returns its SHA. <!--#391e1f1299f3c599-->
- `_git` (function) — Test helper that runs a `git -C <path>` subprocess with `check=True` and returns its stripped stdout. <!--#412bef18ebc42d48-->
- `_add_feature_branch` (function) — Test helper that creates the named branch off current HEAD, commits one file on it, and checks the default branch back out. <!--#07b4178b8739275e-->
- `_mask_post_merge_rev_parse` (function) — Test helper that monkeypatches `orchestrator._run_git` so the first `rev-parse HEAD` after a `git merge` returns a failure, forcing `post_merge_sha` to be empty, and returns a state dict so callers can assert the mask actually fired. <!--#889d493de71244db-->
- `TestStrayCommitTripsSilentMergeLoss` (class) — Test class asserting that a stray non-merge commit stacked on HEAD makes the per-branch post-condition fail with `silent_merge_loss`, and that `_verify_post_merge_conditions` exposes no fix-up-parent tolerance knob. <!--#bf618a9e64e10825-->
  - `TestStrayCommitTripsSilentMergeLoss.test_stray_commit_trips_silent_merge_loss` (method) — Injects a stray single-parent commit just before `_verify_post_merge_conditions` runs and asserts the merge report fails with `silent_merge_loss` on the `feature` branch. <!--#4fe20ba74e0c9e0f-->
  - `TestStrayCommitTripsSilentMergeLoss.test_verify_post_merge_conditions_has_no_fixup_tolerance` (method) — Uses `inspect.signature` to pin `_verify_post_merge_conditions` to exactly `self`/`branch`/`already_ancestor`/`report`, guarding against re-introducing an `allow_fixup_parent` escape hatch. <!--#a4deb94943f4bc0c-->
- `TestTimeoutFailClosed` (class) — Test class asserting that a timeout during the merge post-condition check fails closed rather than being downgraded to a warning. <!--#f457844927c79215-->
  - `TestTimeoutFailClosed.test_postcond_check_timeout_returns_failure` (method) — Patches the orchestrator's bound `assert_branch_merged` to raise `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` and asserts the report fails with `postcond_check_timeout` on the `feature` branch. <!--#d68b0e53fd95da05-->
- `TestEmptyPostShaFallback` (class) — Test class covering the unreadable post-merge SHA path: an empty `post_merge_sha` must never be read as a no-op success, yet must still allow a genuine merge commit to pass. <!--#b0eeee4e4cbb7a2a-->
  - `TestEmptyPostShaFallback.test_empty_post_sha_with_lost_merge_refuses_success` (method) — With the branch already fast-forwarded in (HEAD is a plain commit) and the post-merge SHA read masked, asserts the merge is reported as `silent_merge_loss` and HEAD is left untouched. <!--#24977aec7e06fb61-->
  - `TestEmptyPostShaFallback.test_empty_post_sha_with_real_merge_succeeds` (method) — Counterpoint case: with a diverged default branch producing a real merge commit and the post-merge SHA read masked, asserts the merge still succeeds and HEAD has two parents. <!--#4cecf9444da6bccf-->
- `TestEndToEndMergeInvariants` (class) — Test class exercising `MergeOrchestrator.execute` end-to-end on a real repo, checking the merged branch stays an ancestor of HEAD and that typed `MergeOutcome` entries are populated on both success and failure paths. <!--#420f3b9d1606c5f1-->
  - `TestEndToEndMergeInvariants.test_full_merge_keeps_branch_merged` (method) — Runs a real `execute` and then calls `assert_branch_merged` directly to prove every step preserved the merge commit. <!--#777f6d8f9e45013e-->
  - `TestEndToEndMergeInvariants.test_outcomes_populated_for_successful_merge` (method) — Asserts a successful merge yields exactly one `MergeOutcome` with the branch name, `success=True`, no failure reason, and a captured merge commit SHA. <!--#9a3a3e4c401a021b-->
  - `TestEndToEndMergeInvariants.test_outcomes_populated_for_failed_merge` (method) — Stubs `_merge_single_branch` to return `merge_conflict` and asserts the failure path still records one `MergeOutcome` carrying the typed `FailureReason.MERGE_CONFLICT`. <!--#bad8e6b86c651e87-->

### `tests/commands/merge/test_cli.py` (python) — Pytest suite hardening the merge CLI's input layer, covering branch-name validation against flags/metachars/git-ref rules, fail-closed _branch_exists behavior when git is unavailable, run_merge and end-to-end Typer CliRunner rejection of bad input, and correct partitioning/rendering of newly-merged vs already-ancestor branch buckets (defects I1–I4). <!--#ceaa6f67f20e01c3|91f8e1a0a955fe99-->
- `_init_repo` (function) — Test helper that initializes a git repo at a given path with user config and an initial committed README. <!--#ae786cd150546416-->

  - `TestValidateBranchNames.test_empty_list_raises` (method) — Asserts an empty branch list raises ValueError demanding at least one branch. <!--#15b508df42863c6a-->

  - `TestValidateBranchNames.test_leading_dash_rejected` (method) — Asserts a leading-dash name like '-rf' is rejected as a potential flag. <!--#20c6678eede3c537-->
  - `TestValidateBranchNames.test_double_dash_rejected` (method) — Asserts a double-dash name like '--force' is rejected as a flag. <!--#f7624ce99e185a97-->

  - `TestValidateBranchNames.test_git_ref_format_rules_rejected` (method) — Parametrized test asserting names violating git ref-format rules (e.g. '..', leading/trailing slash, '.lock', reflog syntax) are rejected. <!--#d610c956f05d4cb9-->
  - `TestValidateBranchNames.test_HEAD_rejected` (method) — Asserts the pseudo-ref 'HEAD' is rejected. <!--#c6ae23a881e92df9-->
  - `TestValidateBranchNames.test_at_sign_rejected` (method) — Asserts the pseudo-ref '@' is rejected. <!--#e4943f2bc0bf3387-->
  - `TestValidateBranchNames.test_valid_names_accepted` (method) — Asserts a set of legitimate branch names passes validation without raising. <!--#add788c436a91775-->
  - `TestValidateBranchNames.test_multi_invalid_names_listed` (method) — Asserts all invalid names in a mixed list appear in the error message so the operator can fix them at once. <!--#4aaff2d0797585f5-->
- `TestBranchExistsHardening` (class) — Test class asserting that `_branch_exists` (defect I4) inspects git's returncode and fails closed—returning False—when a ref is absent, the git binary is missing, or the subprocess times out. <!--#64fc21241a08d1a4-->
  - `TestBranchExistsHardening.test_existing_branch_returns_true` (method) — Asserts _branch_exists returns True for an existing branch. <!--#94be4fb26f4e9029-->
  - `TestBranchExistsHardening.test_missing_branch_returns_false` (method) — Asserts _branch_exists returns False for a non-existent branch by inspecting the show-ref returncode. <!--#9dbf2a3f21bf29f9-->
  - `TestBranchExistsHardening.test_missing_git_treated_as_missing_branch` (method) — Verifies `_branch_exists` returns False when `_run_git` raises FileNotFoundError (git not on PATH), so the caller refuses to merge an indeterminate ref. <!--#90d40fdda9f7a02a-->
  - `TestBranchExistsHardening.test_timeout_treated_as_missing_branch` (method) — Verifies `_branch_exists` catches a `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` from `_run_git` and returns False rather than letting the exception propagate. <!--#44b0571788533759-->
- `TestRunMergeRejectsBadInput` (class) — Test suite verifying programmatic run_merge validates input and returns exit code 1 on empty, flag-like, or metachar branch names. <!--#8539ec026e989c2f-->
  - `TestRunMergeRejectsBadInput.test_run_merge_rejects_empty_list` (method) — Asserts run_merge with an empty branch list returns exit code 1. <!--#d1c0242bdaf9049d-->
  - `TestRunMergeRejectsBadInput.test_run_merge_rejects_leading_dash` (method) — Asserts run_merge with a leading-dash branch name returns exit code 1. <!--#d9d4fb0700585113-->
  - `TestRunMergeRejectsBadInput.test_run_merge_rejects_metachar` (method) — Asserts run_merge with a metacharacter-containing branch name returns exit code 1. <!--#f283e4329b420d92-->
- `TestCliMergeBadInput` (class) — End-to-end Typer CliRunner tests asserting `se3 merge` exits non-zero on bad input (defects I1/I2): empty branch list, leading-dash branch names, and shell metacharacters are all rejected before any merge runs. <!--#d2a0a7ae8c54c418-->
  - `TestCliMergeBadInput._invoke` (method) — Helper that inits a repo, chdirs into `tmp_path`, and invokes the `merge` subcommand through Typer's CliRunner, returning the result. <!--#095c92eb470d4eee-->

  - `TestCliMergeBadInput.test_leading_dash_branch_rejected` (method) — Asserts 'luo merge -- -rf' exits non-zero and never reports the dash arg as a successfully merged branch. <!--#7950325b4baccede-->

- `TestSplitMergedBuckets` (class) — Test class for `_split_merged_buckets` (defect I3), covering typed newly/already-ancestor buckets, the legacy-aggregate fallback, the empty case, and the project_root-driven git-ancestry fallback. <!--#ce40f71528ca1c2f-->
  - `TestSplitMergedBuckets.test_split_with_typed_buckets` (method) — Asserts `_split_merged_buckets` returns the report's `newly_merged_branches` and `already_ancestor_branches` verbatim when both typed buckets are populated. <!--#52e159c925722e69-->
  - `TestSplitMergedBuckets.test_split_falls_back_to_legacy_aggregate` (method) — Asserts that when the typed buckets are empty but the legacy `merged_branches` is populated, all branches are treated as newly merged. <!--#43d43d07849a6860-->
  - `TestSplitMergedBuckets.test_split_empty_when_nothing_merged` (method) — Asserts `_split_merged_buckets` returns two empty lists when nothing was merged. <!--#922c9d62fe2f6860-->
  - `TestSplitMergedBuckets.test_fallback_uses_git_ancestry_when_project_root_provided` (method) — Builds a real repo with one ancestor and one non-ancestor branch and asserts the legacy fallback, given a `project_root`, uses git ancestry to sort the branch into the `already` vs `newly` bucket. <!--#6846bcb8b22ee0b5-->
- `TestCliRendersBucketSplit` (class) — Test class exercising `run_merge`'s rendered output (defect I3) with a mocked orchestrator, asserting the newly-merged and already-ancestor sections render separately and only when non-empty. <!--#71897f1911cd3f77-->
  - `TestCliRendersBucketSplit.test_success_renders_only_newly_merged_section` (method) — Asserts that when all branches produced new merge commits, only the 'Newly merged' section renders and the already-ancestor section is absent. <!--#f42d91c74016e4b2-->

  - `TestCliRendersBucketSplit.test_success_renders_both_sections_disjoint` (method) — Reproduces the user's confusing `se3 merge scn discoverbug` scenario and asserts the output renders both sections in order with each branch listed under only its correct bucket. <!--#a1ddc984987af28d-->
- `TestCliMergeBadInput` (class) — End-to-end Typer CliRunner tests asserting `se3 merge` exits non-zero on bad input (defects I1/I2): empty branch list, leading-dash branch names, and shell metacharacters are all rejected before any merge runs. <!--#d2a0a7ae8c54c418-->
  - `TestCliMergeBadInput._invoke` (method) — Helper that inits a repo, chdirs into `tmp_path`, and invokes the `merge` subcommand through Typer's CliRunner, returning the result. <!--#095c92eb470d4eee-->

  - `TestCliMergeBadInput.test_leading_dash_branch_rejected` (method) — Asserts 'luo merge -- -rf' exits non-zero and never reports the dash arg as a successfully merged branch. <!--#7950325b4baccede-->
  - `TestCliMergeBadInput.test_metachar_branch_rejected` (method) — Asserts 'luo merge feat;ls' with a shell metachar exits non-zero. <!--#d505be1b357e8950-->
- `TestRunMergeEndToEndAcceptance` (class) — Real-repo acceptance test class guarding against silent merge loss: a successful `run_merge` must yield a true merge commit (parent_count >= 2), reachable feature branch, and an advanced version file. <!--#393df83ca8fb28d6-->
  - `TestRunMergeEndToEndAcceptance._init_versioned_repo` (method) — Helper that scaffolds a git repo with `.gitignore`, a versioned `pyproject.toml` (1.0.0), and README, then returns the default branch name. <!--#d38b1a50758fa643-->

### `tests/commands/merge/test_cli_reconcile.py` (python) — Pytest suite for the `se3/tianluo merge` CLI thin-adapter (`run_merge`), verifying the back-to-back integrate→reconcile contract: it lands a deterministic max-bump SemVer version with merged changelog bullets and one annotated tag, treats intent-free merges as no-op successes, stays idempotent on rerun, surfaces reconcile faults as non-zero exit codes, and scopes reconciliation to only the merged branches' own version-intents (excluding concurrent or inherited-from-master intents). <!--#680d503cfce82050|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/commands/merge/test_conflict_resolver.py` (python) — Unit-test suite for the merge ConflictResolver's defensive edges, covering HunkResolution line-number validation, the resolved-content byte cap, indentation-tolerant conflict-marker detection, _resolve_sha error paths against a real temp git repo, binary/gitattributes/BOM/UTF-16/lossy-UTF-8 file classification and decoding, and the shared LLM caller. <!--#0a3f0ed9f2490726|2d28c6d1f6801c7b-->
- `TestHunkResolutionValidation` (class) — D1 test class verifying HunkResolution rejects malformed start/end line numbers (negative, zero, huge, non-int, float, bool, None, end-before-start) while accepting valid and digit-string inputs. <!--#d42ae0584b6b38ef-->
  - `TestHunkResolutionValidation.test_basic_valid_hunk` (method) — Asserts a HunkResolution with valid start/end lines stores them unchanged. <!--#1192ba2e85f35d10-->

### `tests/commands/merge/test_dirty_preflight.py` (python) — Test module for the merge command's dirty-working-tree pre-flight, verifying via temp git repos that dirty self-managed issue-state files (tianluo/issues, .next_id, code-index.md) are auto-swept into a 'chore: sync issue state' commit with deterministic NextIdResolver conflict handling, while any dirty path outside the self-managed whitelist (including renames leaving it, exact-path sibling mismatches, and pre-existing merge conflicts) fails loudly as dirty_working_tree with the real git diagnostic preserved, plus edge cases like untracked-only, gitignored whitelist entries, nothing-to-commit syncs, and -z porcelain rename parsing. <!--#9c7427e21c556c8b|f2a4db0c28c98d1e-->
- `_git` (function) — Helper that runs a git command in the given repo path with output captured and non-zero exit raising. <!--#cf40306ebf6a3046-->
- `_init_repo` (function) — Test helper that bootstraps a git repo in the given path with a test identity, an initial README commit, and a .gitignore mirroring the real init/migrate template (ignore /tianluo/* but whitelist the committed data dirs). <!--#964a9798a9a9e52d-->
- `_default_branch` (function) — Helper returning the repo's current (default) branch name via rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD. <!--#876df53e47218b67-->
- `_log_subjects` (function) — Helper returning all commit subject lines of the repo's log for assertion on which commits exist. <!--#6e86814f6cdb6277-->
- `_write_next_id` (function) — Test helper that writes the given value into tianluo/issues/.next_id (creating parent dirs) and returns its Path. <!--#7db7b4d8b49efa21-->
- `test_dirty_issue_state_auto_committed_and_nextid_resolver_takes_over` (function) — Verifies the pre-flight auto-commits dirty tracked plus untracked issue state (staging the new yaml into the git index) and that NextIdResolver deterministically settles the .next_id conflict to max(285,290)=290 with no LLM call, using a _boom tripwire on resolve_and_decide. <!--#d675ae66a0accbb0-->
- `test_dirty_file_outside_self_managed_fails_loud` (function) — Verifies a dirty tracked file outside tianluo/issues/ (src/foo.py) blocks the merge with failure_reason 'dirty_working_tree', names the file, leaves the branch unattempted, and makes no sync commit. <!--#6d9c1fb769488b10-->
- `test_mixed_dirty_lists_both_and_fails` (function) — Verifies that when both a self-managed file (.next_id) and an outside file (src/foo.py) are dirty, the merge fails with 'dirty_working_tree', lists both paths, and attempts no auto-commit. <!--#0c8f2456f7b2ed9b-->
- `test_preexisting_conflict_blocks_merge_not_masked_as_clean` (function) — Regression test ensuring a pre-existing unresolved merge conflict (UU entry with MERGE_HEAD) is seen by the pre-flight and blocks the new merge as dirty_working_tree instead of being skipped as clean, leaving the in-flight merge untouched. <!--#a80fa33478cee25b-->
- `test_clean_working_tree_unchanged_behaviour` (function) — Verifies the baseline behaviour that a clean working tree merges successfully without producing any sync commit. <!--#f018934b10da4c91-->
- `test_untracked_only_does_not_commit` (function) — Verifies an untracked-only issue file provokes no sync commit (only dirty TRACKED files trigger git's overwrite refusal), the merge succeeds, and the untracked file is left in place. <!--#0209164ee754bc8f-->
- `test_rename_within_self_managed_with_space_is_committed` (function) — Verifies robust -z porcelain parsing by auto-committing a staged rename of a space-containing path wholly inside tianluo/issues/ (both ends whitelisted), calling _preflight_dirty_tracked_files directly. <!--#c498ed93204de792-->
- `test_rename_out_of_self_managed_fails` (function) — Verifies a staged rename whose destination leaves tianluo/issues/ (into src/) has one end outside the whitelist and fails with 'dirty_working_tree' listing the offending path rather than being auto-committed. <!--#6fd8720c45b54198-->
- `test_dirty_code_index_is_self_managed_and_auto_committed` (function) — Verifies the whitelisted, routinely-dirty tianluo/code-index.md is treated as self-managed and swept into the sync commit rather than blocking the merge, leaving no dirty tracked files afterward. <!--#30c4c5f48d0562c6-->
- `test_self_managed_nothing_to_commit_proceeds` (function) — Verifies that a self-managed file reported dirty but whose staged content equals HEAD (edited then restored) yields 'nothing to commit', so the merge proceeds with no spurious sync commit instead of being rejected. <!--#11b0ef7d51736cc3-->
- `test_premerge_failure_not_masked_as_merge_abort_failed` (function) — Regression test ensuring that when git refuses to start a merge (untracked file would be overwritten, no MERGE_HEAD), the harmless 'no merge to abort' outcome does not overwrite the real failure with merge_abort_failed, preserving the genuine git diagnostic in both the compound reason and failure_detail. <!--#bff30de60422de3f-->
- `test_code_index_sibling_is_not_self_managed` (function) — Verifies a FILE whitelist entry matches only its exact path, so a dirty sibling like tianluo/code-index.md.bak is not prefix-matched as self-managed and is reported loudly as 'dirty_working_tree' rather than silently left unstaged. <!--#6805fdcab3b004b0-->
- `test_gitignored_code_index_does_not_abort_issue_sync` (function) — Verifies that when code-index.md exists on disk but is gitignored+untracked, the auto-commit derives its add pathspec only from the dirty tracked path (tianluo/issues) and never hands git the ignored path, so the sync commit and merge succeed. <!--#50f7ee0d2d95c3bb-->

### `tests/commands/merge/test_failure_reason.py` (python) — Unit tests pinning the FailureReason enum contract for merge failures — the exact numeric code of each member (including DIRTY_WORKING_TREE's place in the 93x repo-state fail-fast group), legacy-string conversion in both directions (legacy_string, to_legacy_string, from_legacy_string with None/empty/unknown/compound 'reason: detail' inputs, retired values degrading to UNEXPECTED), full round-trip and _LEGACY_STRING_MAP completeness guards, and IntEnum ordering/equality behaviour. <!--#96fdb9ee5fda89b3|9752d3606fe172cb-->
- `TestFailureReasonValues` (class) — Asserts the numeric values of each FailureReason enum member and that DIRTY_WORKING_TREE sits inside the 93x repo-state fail-fast group, pinning the code ranges that group failure kinds. <!--#a18375db8aa389b8-->
  - `TestFailureReasonValues.test_none` (method) — Asserts FailureReason.NONE equals 0. <!--#cedff100d4558f9f-->
  - `TestFailureReasonValues.test_pending_human` (method) — Asserts FailureReason.PENDING_HUMAN equals 100. <!--#a7e648f8b3b7eccf-->
  - `TestFailureReasonValues.test_merge_conflict` (method) — Asserts FailureReason.MERGE_CONFLICT equals 200. <!--#a4a0da736a8c9f58-->
  - `TestFailureReasonValues.test_fast_abort` (method) — Asserts FailureReason.FAST_ABORT equals 400. <!--#cd779e45086dd10c-->
  - `TestFailureReasonValues.test_rollback_failed` (method) — Asserts FailureReason.ROLLBACK_FAILED equals 600. <!--#2e64a6ecb3ab9bbb-->
  - `TestFailureReasonValues.test_runtime_sync_collision` (method) — Asserts FailureReason.RUNTIME_SYNC_COLLISION equals 800. <!--#67d983fc5d4558c3-->
  - `TestFailureReasonValues.test_postcond_branch_not_merged` (method) — Asserts FailureReason.POSTCOND_BRANCH_NOT_MERGED equals 900. <!--#bb001a9ef953df0a-->
  - `TestFailureReasonValues.test_dirty_working_tree` (method) — Asserts FailureReason.DIRTY_WORKING_TREE has the numeric value 934. <!--#9e04058c8cc1438f-->
  - `TestFailureReasonValues.test_dirty_working_tree_in_repo_state_group` (method) — Asserts DIRTY_WORKING_TREE is ordered within the 93x repo-state fail-fast group, between REPO_UNSUPPORTED_STATE and NO_BRANCHES. <!--#2e25d5aad10fa15a-->
  - `TestFailureReasonValues.test_lock_busy` (method) — Asserts FailureReason.LOCK_BUSY equals 990. <!--#af6ba7d75f035207-->
  - `TestFailureReasonValues.test_unexpected` (method) — Asserts the catch-all FailureReason.UNEXPECTED equals 9999. <!--#4e8f278db179fabd-->
- `TestLegacyString` (class) — Covers conversion between FailureReason members and their legacy string forms — the legacy_string property, to_legacy_string, from_legacy_string (None/empty/unknown/compound "reason: detail" inputs), full round-trip of every member, and a guard that each member has a matching _LEGACY_STRING_MAP entry. <!--#06b34573166a8c48-->
  - `TestLegacyString.test_legacy_string_property` (method) — Checks that the legacy_string property renders MERGE_CONFLICT and FAST_ABORT as their snake_case legacy names. <!--#39f9709641725592-->
  - `TestLegacyString.test_from_legacy_string_exact_match` (method) — Verifies an exact legacy string parses to its member with no detail. <!--#90543e85c97a12db-->
  - `TestLegacyString.test_dirty_working_tree_legacy_string_property` (method) — Asserts DIRTY_WORKING_TREE's legacy_string property is "dirty_working_tree". <!--#3589d29d8238ac99-->
  - `TestLegacyString.test_from_legacy_string_dirty_working_tree` (method) — Asserts from_legacy_string("dirty_working_tree") resolves to FailureReason.DIRTY_WORKING_TREE with no detail. <!--#fd7be7355a1a4f11-->
  - `TestLegacyString.test_dirty_working_tree_round_trips` (method) — Asserts DIRTY_WORKING_TREE round-trips exactly through to_legacy_string and back via from_legacy_string. <!--#1239a5dab1b61bbc-->
  - `TestLegacyString.test_from_legacy_string_none` (method) — Verifies a None input parses to (None, None). <!--#5db88e68f8f3e2b2-->
  - `TestLegacyString.test_from_legacy_string_empty` (method) — Verifies an empty string parses to FailureReason.NONE with no detail. <!--#c2e19c31d805f517-->
  - `TestLegacyString.test_from_legacy_string_whitespace` (method) — Verifies a whitespace-only string parses to FailureReason.NONE with no detail. <!--#01c1a35a1a3fbe4a-->
  - `TestLegacyString.test_from_legacy_string_unknown` (method) — Verifies an unrecognized string parses to UNEXPECTED, preserving the original text as detail. <!--#d3484a7856f703fb-->
  - `TestLegacyString.test_from_legacy_string_retired_guardrail_violation` (method) — Verifies that the retired "guardrail_violation" string found in archived merge reports degrades to FailureReason.UNEXPECTED with the original text preserved as the detail rather than raising. <!--#16a6fc028364be78-->
  - `TestLegacyString.test_from_legacy_string_compound_fast_abort` (method) — Verifies a 'fast_abort: ...' compound string splits into the FAST_ABORT member and a detail string. <!--#7f34ad80814834d5-->
  - `TestLegacyString.test_from_legacy_string_compound_fast_failure` (method) — Verifies a 'fast_failure: ...' compound string splits into the FAST_FAILURE member and a detail string. <!--#6fb0c72aabb5129c-->
  - `TestLegacyString.test_from_legacy_string_compound_merge_failed` (method) — Verifies a 'merge_failed: ...' compound string splits into the MERGE_FAILED member and a detail string. <!--#8ec329e4fedc00e5-->
  - `TestLegacyString.test_from_legacy_string_bare_prefix_no_separator` (method) — Verifies a prefix without a ': ' separator (e.g. 'fast_abort_extra') does NOT match and falls through to UNEXPECTED. <!--#5c5c8e65ede4f5de-->
  - `TestLegacyString.test_to_legacy_string_none` (method) — Verifies to_legacy_string(None) returns None. <!--#57b88ab720633b2b-->
  - `TestLegacyString.test_to_legacy_string_none_reason` (method) — Verifies to_legacy_string(FailureReason.NONE) returns the empty string. <!--#fddc2e9b7623d9ef-->
  - `TestLegacyString.test_to_legacy_string_normal` (method) — Verifies to_legacy_string returns the expected legacy string for a normal member. <!--#b8154ca2a8d3c540-->
  - `TestLegacyString.test_round_trip_all_members` (method) — Verifies every member except UNEXPECTED round-trips exactly through to_legacy_string and from_legacy_string. <!--#7c57328c3f49b608-->
  - `TestLegacyString.test_every_member_has_legacy_map_entry` (method) — Test asserting every FailureReason member's legacy_string is a key in _LEGACY_STRING_MAP resolving back to that same member (with special handling for NONE and UNEXPECTED), guarding against typos in future enum additions that would silently route to UNEXPECTED. <!--#180258d15e5fa34d-->
- `TestFailureReasonComparison` (class) — Test class confirming FailureReason behaves as an IntEnum supporting numeric ordering and equality. <!--#86adcf32a89de1c3-->
  - `TestFailureReasonComparison.test_lt` (method) — Asserts NONE is less than MERGE_CONFLICT via numeric comparison. <!--#b973668ab5a03086-->
  - `TestFailureReasonComparison.test_gt` (method) — Asserts UNEXPECTED is greater than LOCK_BUSY via numeric comparison. <!--#fd389677a0569d5c-->

### `tests/commands/merge/test_llm_trace.py` (python) — Unit-test suite for the merge module's LLMTrace per-call JSONL logger and its LLMCallRecord dataclass, covering start/stop lifecycle and context-manager use, record writing (sequence numbering, field serialization, preview truncation, empty fields, auto-start), size-based file rotation with unique filenames, and dataclass-to-dict serialization. <!--#f3207a1f0134af9c|f80a066a266f67fb-->
- `tmp_project` (function) — Pytest fixture returning a temporary directory path used as the project root for each LLMTrace test. <!--#148d54b377839e21-->
- `TestLLMTraceLifecycle` (class) — Test class verifying LLMTrace start/stop behavior and its context-manager protocol. <!--#7ee74ab2c11bcd3b-->
  - `TestLLMTraceLifecycle.test_start_creates_file` (method) — Asserts that calling start() creates the current trace file on disk. <!--#ade501c12d1ce6d3-->
  - `TestLLMTraceLifecycle.test_context_manager` (method) — Asserts that using LLMTrace as a context manager sets started/file on entry and clears started on exit. <!--#a8ecafb1955bdac6-->
  - `TestLLMTraceLifecycle.test_stop_closes_file` (method) — Asserts that stop() closes and clears the underlying file handle. <!--#ccae2c1c2811ba8a-->
  - `TestLLMTraceLifecycle.test_idempotent_start` (method) — Asserts that a second start() call is a no-op leaving the current path unchanged. <!--#f0af30f54d12f869-->
- `TestLLMTraceRecord` (class) — Test class verifying record() writes correct JSONL output, sequence numbering, previews, and auto-start. <!--#fabad25326ed3477-->
  - `TestLLMTraceRecord.test_seq_monotonic` (method) — Asserts that successive record() calls return monotonically increasing sequence numbers starting at 1. <!--#c59b5bb482d7718a-->
  - `TestLLMTraceRecord.test_record_content` (method) — Asserts a recorded entry serializes all fields (agent, previews, duration, outcome, meta, seq, timestamp) correctly to JSONL. <!--#b115470033f7a923-->
  - `TestLLMTraceRecord.test_preview_truncation` (method) — Asserts that a long prompt is truncated to the configured preview_chars length in the written record. <!--#e0c58e4528b58d34-->
  - `TestLLMTraceRecord.test_empty_prompt_and_response` (method) — Asserts that omitting prompt/response yields empty-string preview fields. <!--#004463f8fcbee644-->
  - `TestLLMTraceRecord.test_auto_start_on_record` (method) — Asserts that calling record() without an explicit start() auto-starts the trace. <!--#2fc8e3ca505c85b1-->
- `TestLLMTraceRotation` (class) — Test class verifying LLMTrace's file rotation behavior when a trace file exceeds its size limit, covering both basic rotation (first file is closed and retains its record) and unique filename generation across rapid successive rotations. <!--#8071508b2081507c-->
