  - `TestLLMTraceRotation.test_rotation_filenames_unique_in_same_microsecond` (method) — Regression test that freezes datetime.now to a fixed instant and forces three rotations, asserting rotated trace filenames stay unique even when the timestamp collides (guarding against the old bug that reused the record-counter as the filename suffix). <!--#3a61a585c7a89144-->
- `TestLLMCallRecord` (class) — Test class verifying LLMCallRecord dataclass serialization. <!--#4dfb415b3d1003d8-->
  - `TestLLMCallRecord.test_to_dict` (method) — Asserts that LLMCallRecord.to_dict() emits the expected key/value fields. <!--#78d9689cb6100eea-->

### `tests/commands/merge/test_merge_lock.py` (python) — Pytest suite for the fcntl-based MergeLock exclusive merge lock, covering acquire/release lifecycle, contention/busy errors, stale dead-PID detection and breaking, blocking (queued) acquisition, and cross-process exclusivity via subprocesses. <!--#e5c7051006a241bb|723715331b9dbd01-->
- `tmp_project` (function) — Pytest fixture returning a temporary project root with the tianluo/state/ directory pre-created for holding the merge.lock file. <!--#a21c68798068f059-->
- `TestMergeLockAcquireRelease` (class) — Tests the basic `MergeLock` lifecycle — that `acquire()` creates the lock file and an fd, `release()` clears it, the context-manager form works, the PID is recorded, and a repeated `acquire()` is a no-op. <!--#7a32b84e88cae5f5-->
  - `TestMergeLockAcquireRelease.test_acquire_creates_lock_file` (method) — Asserts that acquiring the lock creates the resolved lock file on disk. <!--#6ca01a9ff773d7cc-->
  - `TestMergeLockAcquireRelease.test_release_removes_fd` (method) — Asserts that releasing the lock clears the held file descriptor back to None. <!--#71a776b3137df160-->
  - `TestMergeLockAcquireRelease.test_context_manager` (method) — Verifies the lock works as a context manager, holding the fd inside the `with` block and releasing on exit. <!--#695257470f18115f-->
  - `TestMergeLockAcquireRelease.test_lock_file_contains_pid` (method) — Asserts the held lock file's first line is the current process's PID, tolerating the newer multi-line holder record (PID + machine-id + padding). <!--#8f16c579075a8872-->
  - `TestMergeLockAcquireRelease.test_idempotent_start` (method) — Verifies a second acquire on an already-held lock is a no-op rather than an error. <!--#b5bdde0487673e57-->
- `TestMergeLockContention` (class) — Test class covering two lock instances competing for the same lock and the busy-error behavior. <!--#51fb302227f092c8-->
  - `TestMergeLockContention.test_second_acquire_raises_busy` (method) — Asserts a second acquire while one is held raises MergeLockBusy. <!--#be8f6f881202ac48-->
  - `TestMergeLockContention.test_second_acquire_sees_holder_pid` (method) — Asserts the MergeLockBusy exception exposes the current holder's PID. <!--#c2464523a2846cda-->
  - `TestMergeLockContention.test_factory_function` (method) — Verifies the `acquire_merge_lock` factory returns an already-acquired lock. <!--#60272630d1b5c0e4-->
- `TestMergeLockStale` (class) — Tests stale-lock handling — a dead-PID lock file raises `MergeLockStale` with the holder PID, `acquire(break_stale=True)` removes and re-acquires it, and an unparseable record held by another process reports `holder_pid=None`. <!--#dcae93dd3fe57ab2-->
  - `TestMergeLockStale.test_stale_lock_raises_stale` (method) — Verifies acquire() raises MergeLockStale with holder_pid set to the dead PID when the lock file names a nonexistent process. <!--#4092843c1d262419-->
  - `TestMergeLockStale.test_break_stale_removes_and_reacquires` (method) — Verifies `acquire(break_stale=True)` over a dead-PID lock file succeeds and rewrites the holder record with the current PID. <!--#d1e68fb0b1390e67-->
  - `TestMergeLockStale.test_unparseable_pid_raises_stale_with_none` (method) — Spawns a subprocess that holds the flock with a non-numeric holder record and asserts `MergeLockStale` carries `holder_pid=None` and an "unparseable" message rather than the ambiguous sentinel 0. <!--#981963d59fd478a5-->
- `TestMergeLockBlocking` (class) — Tests queueing acquisition semantics — `acquire(blocking=True)` waits for the holder instead of raising `MergeLockBusy`, the `blocking=True` constructor/factory flags propagate, an unheld stale file doesn't wedge the wait, and blocking serializes across processes. <!--#b4d5b80f39ff18c8-->
  - `TestMergeLockBlocking.test_blocking_acquire_waits_for_release` (method) — Holds the lock in one `MergeLock` released by a background thread after a delay, then asserts a second blocking `acquire()` waits out that delay and records its own PID. <!--#891779fa4fb4e709-->
  - `TestMergeLockBlocking.test_blocking_context_manager_default` (method) — Verifies constructing `MergeLock(root, blocking=True)` seeds blocking mode for context-manager acquire. <!--#156e03b82948bd73-->
  - `TestMergeLockBlocking.test_blocking_acquire_over_unheld_stale_file` (method) — Asserts a blocking acquire over a leftover dead-PID lock file that nobody holds is granted immediately and overwrites the stale record with the current PID. <!--#ce879a0230185b47-->
  - `TestMergeLockBlocking.test_factory_passes_blocking` (method) — Verifies the `acquire_merge_lock` factory forwards the `blocking` flag. <!--#8d86aff6f7facd79-->
  - `TestMergeLockBlocking.test_blocking_serializes_across_processes` (method) — Verifies a blocking acquire queues behind a real holder in another process and only returns after that subprocess releases the lock. <!--#f8f34dd5fe0e93d5-->
- `TestMergeLockSubprocess` (class) — Test class confirming the lock is genuinely exclusive across OS processes via a spawned subprocess. <!--#470861086e85299e-->
  - `TestMergeLockSubprocess.test_subprocess_cannot_acquire_while_parent_holds` (method) — Verifies that while the parent holds the lock, a subprocess attempting acquire() reports BUSY (raises MergeLockBusy). <!--#cd6c57d8105a82fd-->

### `tests/commands/merge/test_merge_lock_cross_machine.py` (python) — Test suite for the cross-machine merge-lock guard, covering the fixed-width holder-record codec (encode/decode, truncation, legacy PID-only records, corruption, capped reads) and the acquire/inspect_lock semantics that keep foreign-machine holders always busy and never stale-broken, abort the stale-break retry loop once the unlink-race winner is foreign/blank/live-local, and preserve existing same-machine and legacy behaviour where local dead PIDs remain stale and reclaimable. <!--#4fd681e3c6e2fc30|33691e10ec467f2d-->
- `tmp_project` (function) — Pytest fixture creating a throwaway project root with a `tianluo/state/` directory for merge-lock tests. <!--#761f6b86db530ad0-->
- `_lock_path` (function) — Helper returning the `tianluo/state/merge.lock` path under a given project root. <!--#2f45683241098675-->
- `TestHolderRecordCodec` (class) — Tests the fixed-width holder-record encode/decode helpers, covering round-trips, truncation, legacy PID-only records, corruption detection, and capped reads. <!--#83440742f94470f9-->
  - `TestHolderRecordCodec.test_new_record_round_trips_pid_and_machine` (method) — Asserts a newly encoded record has the expected length and decodes back to its PID, machine id, and a not-corrupt flag. <!--#64d110c46864fc2f-->
  - `TestHolderRecordCodec.test_record_is_fixed_width_regardless_of_machine_len` (method) — Asserts encoded records are always `_HOLDER_RECORD_LEN` bytes regardless of machine-id length. <!--#4df5dac908071e27-->
  - `TestHolderRecordCodec.test_overlong_machine_id_is_truncated_not_corrupting` (method) — Asserts an absurdly long machine id is truncated to fixed width while the PID stays parseable and the record is not flagged corrupt. <!--#a22a19cc680aa4bc-->
  - `TestHolderRecordCodec.test_legacy_pure_pid_record_decodes_machine_none` (method) — Asserts a pre-upgrade 17-byte PID-only record still decodes, yielding the PID with `machine_id=None`. <!--#4852f0ab06217f25-->
  - `TestHolderRecordCodec.test_non_numeric_first_line_is_corrupt` (method) — Asserts a record whose first line is not a number decodes to `pid=None` with the corrupt flag set. <!--#6ad7a670a595e5bc-->
  - `TestHolderRecordCodec.test_reader_caps_read_at_record_len` (method) — Asserts `_read_holder_pid` stops at `_HOLDER_RECORD_LEN` so trailing garbage in the lock file cannot poison the parsed PID or machine id. <!--#da637dacff50174e-->
- `TestForeignHolderNeverStale` (class) — Tests that a lock held by another machine is always reported busy — never stale, never force-broken — across acquire with and without `break_stale` and via `inspect_lock`. <!--#5849ba49aae04310-->
  - `TestForeignHolderNeverStale._spawn_foreign_holder` (method) — Helper spawning a subprocess that flocks the lock file and writes a forged foreign-machine record carrying a locally-dead PID. <!--#448fa51982ad5427-->
  - `TestForeignHolderNeverStale.test_foreign_holder_raises_busy_not_stale_and_not_broken` (method) — Asserts `acquire(break_stale=True)` against a foreign holder raises `MergeLockBusy`, never enters the stale-break path, and leaves the lock file byte-identical. <!--#b6556825cfa73f1b-->
  - `TestForeignHolderNeverStale.test_foreign_holder_raises_busy_even_without_break_stale` (method) — Asserts `acquire(break_stale=False)` against a foreign holder also raises `MergeLockBusy` (not `MergeLockStale`) so callers queue instead of breaking. <!--#70c7164240785675-->
  - `TestForeignHolderNeverStale.test_inspect_lock_reports_foreign_holder_alive_not_stale` (method) — Asserts `inspect_lock` reports a foreign-machine record as alive and not stale so auto-clean leaves it intact. <!--#b2cd380eac5853dd-->
- `TestBreakStaleRetryAbortsOnForeignWinner` (class) — Tests that the stale-break retry loop stops unlinking as soon as the lock file's holder is no longer a confirmed local dead PID, preventing eviction of a live remote or local race winner. <!--#e150a2e6825c2ed0-->
  - `TestBreakStaleRetryAbortsOnForeignWinner.test_retry_stops_unlinking_once_holder_is_foreign` (method) — Simulates a foreign process winning the unlink race and asserts exactly one unlink occurs, `MergeLockBusy` is raised, and the foreign record survives. <!--#c46f981963e799a2-->
  - `TestBreakStaleRetryAbortsOnForeignWinner.test_retry_stops_when_race_winner_has_not_written_its_record_yet` (method) — Asserts a blank (not-yet-written) record after an `EAGAIN` stops the break loop rather than being treated as a legacy local holder and unlinked again. <!--#9c4e853139954589-->
  - `TestBreakStaleRetryAbortsOnForeignWinner.test_retry_stops_when_race_winner_is_a_live_local_pid` (method) — Asserts a live local PID winning the unlink race yields `MergeLockBusy` after a single unlink, with its record left intact. <!--#ea8350fb646fdea1-->
  - `TestBreakStaleRetryAbortsOnForeignWinner.test_retry_continues_while_holder_stays_local` (method) — Asserts the bounded retry loop still runs its full `_MAX_BREAK_STALE_ATTEMPTS` unlinks while the holder remains a local dead PID. <!--#43962e81e1c44570-->
- `TestLegacyRecordIsLocal` (class) — Tests that pre-upgrade PID-only lock records are treated as local, so a dead legacy PID is still reported and reclaimable as stale. <!--#d8743d72ca7dab94-->
  - `TestLegacyRecordIsLocal.test_legacy_dead_pid_still_raises_stale` (method) — Asserts `acquire()` on a legacy dead-PID record raises `MergeLockStale` with `holder_machine is None`. <!--#1c5eb0d7ad29e750-->
  - `TestLegacyRecordIsLocal.test_legacy_dead_pid_reclaimed_with_break_stale` (method) — Asserts `acquire(break_stale=True)` reclaims a legacy dead-PID lock and rewrites it as a machine-aware record for this process. <!--#4233fbc65a5e833e-->
  - `TestLegacyRecordIsLocal.test_inspect_lock_legacy_dead_pid_is_stale` (method) — Asserts `inspect_lock` reports a legacy dead-PID record as not alive and stale. <!--#0df5ba668f3e11cc-->
- `TestSameMachineStaleRecovery` (class) — Tests that the machine guard preserves existing same-machine behaviour: local dead PIDs are stale and reclaimable, while a live local holder is busy. <!--#d2b7b33ce50d7f43-->
  - `TestSameMachineStaleRecovery.test_local_dead_pid_record_raises_stale` (method) — Asserts `acquire()` on a machine-aware local record with a dead PID raises `MergeLockStale`. <!--#4a7facaa12e6a132-->
  - `TestSameMachineStaleRecovery.test_local_dead_pid_reclaimed_with_break_stale` (method) — Asserts `acquire(break_stale=True)` reclaims a local dead-PID lock and records the current process's PID. <!--#c0e723290a8fecd3-->
  - `TestSameMachineStaleRecovery.test_local_live_holder_across_processes_is_busy` (method) — Spawns a real subprocess holding the lock and asserts a second `acquire(break_stale=True)` raises `MergeLockBusy` with the local machine id. <!--#34f92eff57766702-->

- `TestAssertHeadIsMergeCommit` (class) — Test class covering the `assert_head_is_merge_commit` post-condition against real temporary git repos, exercising genuine merge commits, non-merge/empty-repo failures with `FailureReason.POSTCOND_HEAD_NOT_MERGE_COMMIT`, octopus merges via `min_parents`, and the `allow_fixup_parent`/`max_fixup_depth` tolerance for commits stacked on top of the merge. <!--#901f0eb16bf538e2-->

### `tests/commands/merge/test_result_model.py` (python) — Unit tests for the typed merge result models, verifying MergeOutcome's per-branch field defaults/state combinations, MergeReport's add_outcome routing into semantic branch buckets, and backward-compatible legacy-dict serialization including committed-issue renumber records. <!--#75b91bf198aac959|594445a3ee3eb007-->
- `TestMergeOutcome` (class) — Test class covering the per-branch MergeOutcome record's fields and state combinations. <!--#97a2a89429609cf9-->
  - `TestMergeOutcome.test_defaults` (method) — Asserts a MergeOutcome built with only a branch name has the expected default field values. <!--#19e186860f40eddc-->
  - `TestMergeOutcome.test_success_no_warnings` (method) — Checks a successful outcome carries its success flag and merge commit SHA without warnings. <!--#a395f1475dd0fa90-->
  - `TestMergeOutcome.test_success_with_warnings` (method) — Checks a successful outcome correctly records the warnings_repaired flag. <!--#689d8b2fceaa71b3-->
  - `TestMergeOutcome.test_already_ancestor` (method) — Verifies an already-ancestor outcome sets that flag while remaining a non-success. <!--#868950226b7d9ea0-->
  - `TestMergeOutcome.test_failure_with_reason` (method) — Verifies a failed outcome stores its FailureReason and failure detail message. <!--#c36cb12bb98b1509-->
  - `TestMergeOutcome.test_pending_human` (method) — Verifies an outcome can carry the PENDING_HUMAN failure reason. <!--#6d478d9b404209d7-->
- `TestMergeReportDefaults` (class) — Test class covering default construction of MergeReport and its call-file string handling. <!--#216c6c814064566f-->
  - `TestMergeReportDefaults.test_empty_report` (method) — Asserts a freshly constructed MergeReport has all empty/false default fields. <!--#9100e10f3eb133ba-->
  - `TestMergeReportDefaults.test_none_call_file_str` (method) — Checks that with no human call file set, both the path and its string form are None. <!--#7080c4c4ed1cd419-->
  - `TestMergeReportDefaults.test_call_file_str_present` (method) — Checks call_file_str returns the string path when a human_call_file Path is set. <!--#869162aed5b14d4a-->
- `TestMergeReportAddOutcome` (class) — Test class verifying add_outcome routes outcomes into the correct semantic branch buckets. <!--#f06e1eb5a160b915-->
  - `TestMergeReportAddOutcome.test_add_newly_merged` (method) — Verifies a successful outcome lands in newly_merged_branches and the newly_merged alias. <!--#cf8231b162a53971-->
  - `TestMergeReportAddOutcome.test_add_already_ancestor` (method) — Verifies an already-ancestor outcome lands in already_ancestor_branches and the already_merged alias. <!--#bd821ce9669214aa-->
  - `TestMergeReportAddOutcome.test_add_merged_with_warnings` (method) — Verifies a warnings-repaired success lands in the merged_with_warnings bucket. <!--#70576f59421708f6-->
  - `TestMergeReportAddOutcome.test_add_failure_sets_failed_branch` (method) — Verifies a conflict outcome sets failed_branch and is excluded from all merged buckets. <!--#474949852ac20c86-->
  - `TestMergeReportAddOutcome.test_add_failure_not_in_any_bucket` (method) — Confirms a failed outcome appears in none of the merged-branch buckets. <!--#284db8d71417eea7-->
  - `TestMergeReportAddOutcome.test_add_pending_human_not_in_any_bucket` (method) — Confirms a pending-human outcome stays out of all buckets and does not set failed_branch. <!--#7c9188b14ca54d9f-->
  - `TestMergeReportAddOutcome.test_multiple_outcomes` (method) — Verifies a mix of outcomes is distributed correctly across all semantic buckets and failed_branch. <!--#1ed8548224bf56d4-->
- `TestMergeReportLegacyCompatibility` (class) — Test class verifying that MergeReport serializes to a backward-compatible legacy dict — covering its overall shape, failure fields, per-branch outcomes, committed-issue renumber records, and the merged_branches alias buckets. <!--#c80b7697c4dc47bf-->
  - `TestMergeReportLegacyCompatibility.test_to_legacy_dict_shape` (method) — Checks to_legacy_dict produces the expected legacy keys, combined merged_branches, and empty-string failure reason. <!--#2ba3396c7f1c33bd-->
  - `TestMergeReportLegacyCompatibility.test_to_legacy_dict_with_failure` (method) — Checks to_legacy_dict serializes failure reason, detail, and failed branch for a failed report. <!--#487c02b6c221ef24-->
  - `TestMergeReportLegacyCompatibility.test_to_legacy_dict_outcomes` (method) — Checks to_legacy_dict includes serialized per-branch outcome entries. <!--#7ff1d72939cf65cd-->
  - `TestMergeReportLegacyCompatibility.test_to_legacy_dict_committed_issue_renumbers` (method) — Asserts that IssueMergeRecord entries in a MergeReport's committed_issue_renumbers are serialized by to_legacy_dict() into plain old_id/new_id/status_dir dicts. <!--#69a6ab5e11255446-->
  - `TestMergeReportLegacyCompatibility.test_merged_branches_alias` (method) — Verifies all_merged_branches falls back to semantic buckets while the legacy merged_branches field stays empty. <!--#6b6f5e646202d88b-->

### `tests/commands/merge/test_runtime_sync.py` (python) — Regression test suite for the runtime_sync merge-hardening fixes (G6/Tasks 30-33), covering symlink-destination rejection in atomic writes, lenient-vs-strict rollback on unexpected failures, sidecar self-collision filtering for idempotent repeated syncs, and bounded chunked read/write I/O with iteration/byte/duration caps. <!--#61351ebcaa3205ae|04b4047a774a4cd0-->
- `_make_sync_call` (function) — Test helper that returns a callable invoking sync_branch_runtime with the per-branch worktree lookup stubbed to a fixed source directory. <!--#e2f317124895190d-->
- `TestSymlinkDestinationRejected` (class) — Test class asserting that `_atomic_write_bytes` refuses symlink destinations (ELOOP) to prevent TOCTOU redirect attacks, including a post-write recheck, while regular writes and overwrites still work. <!--#b7dde1f59491b745-->
  - `TestSymlinkDestinationRejected.test_planted_symlink_to_external_file_is_rejected` (method) — Verifies a symlink planted at the destination pointing to an external file causes `_atomic_write_bytes` to raise OSError(ELOOP) and leaves the external file and symlink untouched. <!--#88939b0cbee651bf-->
  - `TestSymlinkDestinationRejected.test_planted_symlink_to_inside_target_tree_is_rejected` (method) — Verifies even an in-tree symlink destination is uniformly rejected with ELOOP, leaving the real target file untouched. <!--#a05ffa046a801fcd-->
  - `TestSymlinkDestinationRejected.test_normal_write_still_works` (method) — Regression check that `_atomic_write_bytes` writes a regular file normally without the symlink guard interfering. <!--#c49d45043e257ccf-->
  - `TestSymlinkDestinationRejected.test_write_overwrite_regular_file_still_works` (method) — Regression check that `_atomic_write_bytes` correctly overwrites an existing regular file despite the symlink guard. <!--#fd71fe067eaf823b-->
  - `TestSymlinkDestinationRejected.test_toctou_post_write_recheck_catches_late_symlink_swap` (method) — Simulates a symlink planted mid-write via a hooked `_bounded_write_all` and confirms the post-write recheck still rejects it with ELOOP and preserves the external file. <!--#a68717366b63dc4d-->
- `TestLenientModePreservesSuccess` (class) — Test class verifying the outer exception net in `sync_branch_runtime` is mode-aware: lenient mode preserves already-succeeded files/sidecars on unexpected failure while strict mode still rolls everything back. <!--#1045f23e184ef4ef-->
  - `TestLenientModePreservesSuccess.test_already_copied_files_preserved_on_unexpected_failure` (method) — Monkeypatches `_atomic_write_bytes` to succeed then raise RuntimeSyncCollision, asserting lenient mode preserves the first copied file and the `tianluo/` root. <!--#4c480358b4a958f5-->
  - `TestLenientModePreservesSuccess.test_strict_mode_still_rolls_back` (method) — Same failure injection under strict mode, asserting the first copied file and the created `tianluo/` root are fully rolled back. <!--#d01ee66be67a81f3-->
  - `TestLenientModePreservesSuccess.test_lenient_mode_preserves_already_written_sidecars` (method) — Monkeypatches `_write_sidecar` to raise an uncaught RuntimeError after one success, asserting lenient mode leaves at least one already-written sidecar on disk. <!--#f141224b6d486706-->
- `TestSidecarSelfCollisionFiltered` (class) — Test class asserting sidecar-named source files are filtered out at collection time so repeated syncs stay idempotent and never build `.from-A.from-B` chains. <!--#dbe0a879652a305d-->
  - `TestSidecarSelfCollisionFiltered.test_is_sidecar_filename_pattern` (method) — Unit-tests the _is_sidecar_filename regex against positive sidecar shapes (plain, hash-disambiguated, safe-label) and negative non-sidecar names. <!--#1174d91c8a23f631-->
  - `TestSidecarSelfCollisionFiltered.test_source_sidecar_files_are_filtered` (method) — Confirms leftover sidecar files in the source (plain and hash-disambiguated shapes) are neither copied nor recorded as skipped. <!--#47485f810ec12670-->
  - `TestSidecarSelfCollisionFiltered.test_repeated_sync_is_idempotent_no_chain_accumulation` (method) — Runs sync three times against a colliding target and asserts the result is exactly `x.log` plus one sidecar with no nested `.from-feature.from-` chains. <!--#c7c24ab42c7238d1-->
  - `TestSidecarSelfCollisionFiltered.test_sidecar_glob_pattern_files_skipped` (method) — Confirms sidecar leftovers under glob-pattern paths (e.g. `state/summary-*`) are also filtered from copy and skip records. <!--#8687dc48870f9af2-->
- `TestBoundedReadAndWrite` (class) — Test class verifying all chunked-I/O loops enforce byte, iteration, and duration caps (raising EFBIG/ETIMEDOUT/EIO) so a runaway read or write cannot hang `se3 merge`. <!--#98cdb132eed58ec3-->
  - `TestBoundedReadAndWrite.test_bounded_read_byte_cap` (method) — Asserts _bounded_read_chunks raises OSError(EFBIG) once the total-byte cap is exceeded. <!--#6a7baa01c6db66ab-->
  - `TestBoundedReadAndWrite.test_bounded_read_iteration_cap` (method) — Asserts the read iteration cap raises EFBIG independently of total bytes read. <!--#ee5b76d24688595d-->
  - `TestBoundedReadAndWrite.test_bounded_read_duration_cap` (method) — Asserts an exceeded read duration deadline raises OSError(ETIMEDOUT). <!--#04a3cc10e9ea7124-->
  - `TestBoundedReadAndWrite.test_bounded_read_returns_full_content_within_caps` (method) — Regression check that bounded reads return the full file content when within all caps. <!--#610f47729155ee41-->
  - `TestBoundedReadAndWrite.test_bounded_write_zero_progress_raises` (method) — Patches `os.write` to always return 0 and asserts `_bounded_write_all` raises OSError(EIO) after a single attempt instead of spinning forever. <!--#a33be4d61f591683-->
  - `TestBoundedReadAndWrite.test_bounded_write_duration_cap` (method) — Asserts _bounded_write_all honors the time deadline by raising ETIMEDOUT. <!--#cdb80a3f318f9b88-->
  - `TestBoundedReadAndWrite.test_bounded_write_empty_content_no_op` (method) — Asserts writing empty content is a no-op that returns immediately without touching the fd. <!--#6d59a9ff7ffba05f-->
  - `TestBoundedReadAndWrite.test_symlink_loop_bounded_via_read_caps` (method) — End-to-end check that an oversized source file trips the lowered read byte cap and is skipped in lenient mode, letting the merge complete without hanging. <!--#47c313e24490c50a-->
- `TestIdempotentEndToEnd` (class) — Test class sanity-checking that the four hardening fixes compose so repeated clean and colliding syncs are idempotent no-ops after the first run. <!--#1c207fa8b7724e2b-->
  - `TestIdempotentEndToEnd.test_repeated_clean_sync_is_no_op` (method) — Verifies a second sync of identical content is a no-op with no copy, collision, or skip recorded. <!--#762e11e886cd5df2-->
  - `TestIdempotentEndToEnd.test_repeated_collision_sync_idempotent` (method) — Verifies a conflicting sync creates one sidecar the first run, then reports idempotent bypasses on subsequent runs, ending with exactly `x.log` plus one sidecar. <!--#67973d05f10b9443-->

### `tests/commands/merge/test_secret_redact.py` (python) — Unit tests for the merge command's secret_redact module, exercising redact_text/redact_diff convenience functions and the SecretRedactor/RedactConfig classes to verify common secret formats are masked, diff structure is preserved, and allowlist/extra-pattern/default-config behaviors work. <!--#ac32f538cd8e8fa7|1ec9c20ee7d3b81e-->
- `TestRedactText` (class) — Test class verifying redact_text masks common secret formats (API keys, tokens, passwords) while leaving non-secret text unchanged. <!--#d9f45396cfcdcc7d-->
  - `TestRedactText.test_openai_api_key` (method) — Asserts an OpenAI-style sk- API key is replaced with the sk-*** mask. <!--#0898c8cdb24ad4cd-->
  - `TestRedactText.test_github_token` (method) — Asserts a GitHub ghp_ token is redacted to gh*** with the original prefix gone. <!--#e0405895ec55c7d1-->
  - `TestRedactText.test_bearer_token` (method) — Asserts an HTTP Bearer token is replaced with 'Bearer ***'. <!--#d19917f3220c15b0-->
  - `TestRedactText.test_toml_password` (method) — Asserts a TOML-style quoted password assignment is masked to password = "***". <!--#2055916663112f87-->
  - `TestRedactText.test_json_password` (method) — Asserts a JSON password field value is masked to "password": "***". <!--#7a0019a4a3124b2b-->
  - `TestRedactText.test_generic_token_param` (method) — Asserts a generic token= URL query parameter value is redacted to token=***. <!--#4778353d38987e8f-->
  - `TestRedactText.test_no_false_positive_short_token` (method) — Asserts short token values (under the 8-char minimum) are left untouched to avoid false positives. <!--#a230cf925eb83973-->
  - `TestRedactText.test_no_secret_no_change` (method) — Asserts ordinary text containing no secrets passes through unchanged. <!--#0f887002ab527ea7-->
  - `TestRedactText.test_empty_string` (method) — Asserts redacting an empty string returns an empty string. <!--#a781ce47f712166c-->
  - `TestRedactText.test_multiple_secrets` (method) — Asserts multiple distinct secrets in one text block are all redacted in a single pass. <!--#ed69f09a77b61a6a-->
- `TestRedactDiff` (class) — Test class verifying redact_diff masks secrets while preserving git diff line-prefix structure. <!--#5267b9ed033cdfe8-->
  - `TestRedactDiff.test_diff_line_prefixes_preserved` (method) — Asserts diff headers and +/- line prefixes survive redaction while the embedded secret is masked. <!--#a940063c7a30962f-->
  - `TestRedactDiff.test_diff_empty` (method) — Asserts redacting an empty diff returns an empty string. <!--#e5a3275de7d5b496-->
- `TestSecretRedactorAllowlist` (class) — Test class verifying RedactConfig.allowlist restores known-fake values after redaction. <!--#86af9e48f73e63de-->
  - `TestSecretRedactorAllowlist.test_allowlist_restores_fake_secret` (method) — Asserts an allowlisted fake key is restored to its original value rather than left masked. <!--#906ac70de7c9ab79-->
  - `TestSecretRedactorAllowlist.test_allowlist_no_effect_on_real_secrets` (method) — Asserts the allowlist does not exempt non-matching real secrets from redaction. <!--#d5ae50330e8e138d-->
- `TestSecretRedactorExtraPatterns` (class) — Test class verifying user-supplied extra_patterns in RedactConfig are applied during redaction. <!--#c1516396b1a41743-->
  - `TestSecretRedactorExtraPatterns.test_extra_pattern` (method) — Asserts a custom regex pattern passed via RedactConfig redacts its matching token. <!--#c097aca953f4af1b-->
- `TestRedactConfig` (class) — Test class verifying the RedactConfig dataclass default field values. <!--#ae428e07fc949da8-->
  - `TestRedactConfig.test_defaults` (method) — Asserts RedactConfig defaults to an empty allowlist, empty extra_patterns, and preview_length of 80. <!--#cf703857683bf605-->

### `tests/commands/merge/test_version_aggregator.py` (python) — G4 regression test suite for the merge `version_aggregator` module, hardening version bumping across seven concerns (C1–C7): fail-loud when the on-disk version isn't advanced beyond the target, whitespace/quote-tolerant and comment-ignoring pyproject version regex parsing, fail-loud on unparseable versions, atomic temp+rename writes that never leave a partial file, and git-add-failure cleanup that restores the file and clears staged residue. <!--#427cb91905d4d67b|12231888d6259859-->
- `_init_repo` (function) — Test helper that initializes a git repo with user config and an initial committed README. <!--#17fee5b8bfcab244-->
- `_write_pyproject` (function) — Test helper that writes a minimal pyproject.toml with the given version string. <!--#941f0476c7694b5a-->
- `_commit` (function) — Test helper that stages all changes and creates a git commit with the given message. <!--#c07027700d648223-->
- `_setup_with_pyproject` (function) — Test helper that builds a repo with a committed pyproject and a stand-in merge commit so HEAD is amendable. <!--#95447e1974fb440a-->
- `_read_disk_version` (function) — Test helper that reads pyproject.toml from disk and returns its parsed version string. <!--#d6c8bfdd5b26fc91-->
- `TestC1VersionNotAdvanced` (class) — Test class verifying C1 fail-loud behavior when the on-disk version is already at or above the computed target. <!--#e778010a0dfa8471-->
  - `TestC1VersionNotAdvanced.test_current_equal_to_target_returns_failure` (method) — Asserts that current == new_version returns success=False with version_already_at_target set and the on-disk version reported. <!--#c03b2a9790d959ad-->
  - `TestC1VersionNotAdvanced.test_current_higher_than_target_returns_failure` (method) — Asserts that current > new_version fails loud and additionally sets version_higher_than_target with a 'higher' error. <!--#9faadac173b64bb7-->
  - `TestC1VersionNotAdvanced.test_4_7_0_to_4_7_0_fails_loud` (method) — Spec-acceptance test that a 4.7.0→4.7.0 non-advance fails loud rather than silently succeeding. <!--#4ec5c45b59f5506c-->
  - `TestC1VersionNotAdvanced.test_misreport_4_6_1_to_4_7_0_no_longer_happens` (method) — Asserts the old 4.6.1→4.7.0 misreport is gone: no pyproject modification and no extra commit occur. <!--#e7b44a14acaf4938-->
  - `TestC1VersionNotAdvanced.test_normal_bump_still_succeeds` (method) — Regression guard that the C1 fix preserves the normal happy-path bump (4.4.0→4.4.1). <!--#dff64cee49e16734-->
  - `TestC1VersionNotAdvanced.test_version_not_advanced_class_constructor` (method) — Asserts the VersionNotAdvanced exception carries pre/current/target fields and renders them in its message. <!--#3e94b6f53192f0bd-->
- `TestC2RegexTolerance` (class) — Test class verifying the pyproject version regex tolerates varied whitespace/quoting and ignores commented or triple-quoted matches. <!--#e638ff02bf8a1781-->
  - `TestC2RegexTolerance.test_no_space_double_quote` (method) — Asserts version parsing works with no whitespace and double quotes. <!--#28d25c0fa1178b06-->
  - `TestC2RegexTolerance.test_no_space_single_quote` (method) — Asserts version parsing works with no whitespace and single quotes. <!--#b680f0764501a8bf-->
  - `TestC2RegexTolerance.test_one_space_each_side` (method) — Asserts version parsing works with one space on each side of the equals sign. <!--#583b925aeaa80207-->
  - `TestC2RegexTolerance.test_many_spaces_each_side` (method) — Asserts version parsing tolerates many spaces around the equals sign. <!--#1f000ce16545d75b-->
  - `TestC2RegexTolerance.test_tab_around_equals` (method) — Asserts version parsing tolerates tabs around the equals sign. <!--#c33e733da9b0ca7e-->
  - `TestC2RegexTolerance.test_mixed_spaces_and_tabs` (method) — Asserts version parsing tolerates mixed spaces and tabs around the equals sign. <!--#4382e19d6cf3dea9-->
  - `TestC2RegexTolerance.test_indented_version_still_parses` (method) — Asserts an indented version line still parses correctly. <!--#c745fd1e047a07f1-->
  - `TestC2RegexTolerance.test_version_inside_triple_quoted_string_ignored` (method) — Asserts a version-like string inside a triple-double-quoted literal is not matched. <!--#3e539133e17c8e37-->
  - `TestC2RegexTolerance.test_single_triple_quote_variant_ignored` (method) — Asserts a version-like string inside a triple-single-quoted literal is ignored. <!--#7976a05cc19836cf-->
  - `TestC2RegexTolerance.test_commented_section_header_ignored` (method) — Asserts a commented-out [project] header and its version are not treated as the real section. <!--#64deb87bb3f49efa-->
  - `TestC2RegexTolerance.test_commented_tool_poetry_ignored` (method) — Asserts a commented-out [tool.poetry] header and version are skipped in favor of the real one. <!--#0eec83cbfa776cc4-->
  - `TestC2RegexTolerance.test_commented_project_prefers_real` (method) — Asserts that when [project] is commented out, parsing falls back to the real [tool.poetry] version. <!--#360449abd9b50a29-->
- `TestC3VersionParseFailLoud` (class) — Test class verifying that unparseable current or pre-merge versions fail loud without overwriting the file. <!--#def83e72f84cce5d-->
  - `TestC3VersionParseFailLoud.test_unparseable_current_version_returns_failure` (method) — Asserts an unparseable on-disk version causes refusal to write and an 'unparseable' error, leaving the file untouched. <!--#0f110b31fafd2577-->
  - `TestC3VersionParseFailLoud.test_unparseable_pre_merge_version_returns_failure` (method) — Asserts an unparseable pre_merge_version argument fails loud and leaves the disk version unchanged. <!--#f3b87ce0d78abf3d-->
- `TestC4AtomicWrite` (class) — Test class verifying atomic version writes via temp+rename never leave pyproject.toml partial or unparseable. <!--#6b1de168f77fc766-->
  - `TestC4AtomicWrite.test_atomic_write_replaces_file` (method) — Asserts _atomic_write_text replaces a file's contents with the new text. <!--#d19fe53787d49ca5-->
  - `TestC4AtomicWrite.test_atomic_write_no_temp_files_remain` (method) — Asserts no leftover .tmp files remain after a successful atomic write. <!--#3d60862708dc3cf7-->
  - `TestC4AtomicWrite.test_safe_write_version_uses_atomic_write` (method) — Asserts _safe_write_version routes its write through _atomic_write_text with the expected path and content. <!--#5bda5f002328345d-->
  - `TestC4AtomicWrite.test_safe_write_version_handles_no_space_format` (method) — Asserts _safe_write_version updates the version in a no-space pyproject format (C2+C4 combo). <!--#6383e3552cbca5cb-->
  - `TestC4AtomicWrite.test_safe_write_version_preserves_inline_array` (method) — Asserts _safe_write_version preserves an inline array (keywords) while updating the version. <!--#ca8277968fd98587-->
  - `TestC4AtomicWrite.test_safe_write_version_raises_on_missing_field` (method) — Asserts _safe_write_version raises ValueError when no version field is present. <!--#321263d9bdd15611-->
  - `TestC4AtomicWrite.test_disk_still_parseable_after_write_failure` (method) — C4 acceptance test that a simulated write failure leaves pyproject.toml parseable and at the original version. <!--#eb6cdde4974b1a98-->
- `TestC5GitAddFailureCleanup` (class) — Test class verifying a git-add failure restores pyproject.toml and clears any partially-staged change. <!--#b5405f1e44798123-->
  - `TestC5GitAddFailureCleanup.test_no_staged_residue_after_add_failure` (method) — Asserts a non-zero git-add return code restores the file and leaves no staged pyproject.toml residue. <!--#3ebec15c7c9b2b16-->
  - `TestC5GitAddFailureCleanup.test_git_add_oserror_resets_staged` (method) — Asserts a git-add OSError restores the file, resets the index, and reports the error. <!--#c28514b410d3b643-->
- `TestC6NoBareExcept` (class) — Test class verifying the version_aggregator module contains no bare `except Exception:` handlers. <!--#253076974a30e578-->
  - `TestC6NoBareExcept.test_no_bare_except_in_module` (method) — Greps the module source via regex to assert zero bare `except Exception:` occurrences remain. <!--#5d470c5c56caefab-->
- `TestC7AmendExceptionRestore` (class) — Test class verifying that amend or write-version exceptions restore pyproject.toml and unstage changes. <!--#d07437f88c52e892-->
  - `TestC7AmendExceptionRestore.test_amend_oserror_restores_and_resets` (method) — Asserts a `git commit --amend` OSError restores the disk version and unstages pyproject.toml. <!--#36a2e15ba05999a6-->
  - `TestC7AmendExceptionRestore.test_write_version_exception_restores` (method) — Asserts that when _safe_write_version raises mid-write, the original pyproject.toml content is fully restored. <!--#a5cc59c836997fc7-->
- `TestAggregateResultDefaults` (class) — Test class asserting AggregateResult's default field values, including the new version_already_at_target/higher flags. <!--#822d3eb94e916497-->
  - `TestAggregateResultDefaults.test_default_values_include_version_already_at_target` (method) — Asserts a default-constructed AggregateResult has success=False, None fields, and both version-flag defaults False. <!--#d5e00341ea39c4f2-->
- `TestAmendFalsePath` (class) — Test class covering aggregate_and_apply(amend=False), which adds a new single-parent commit atop the merge instead of rewriting history. <!--#0b9ac64ac1152342-->
  - `TestAmendFalsePath.test_amend_false_creates_new_commit_on_top` (method) — Asserts amend=False creates a new single-parent commit whose parent is the original merge commit. <!--#ab4efca0d69db324-->
  - `TestAmendFalsePath.test_amend_false_commit_message_includes_version` (method) — Asserts the amend=False new commit's subject references the bumped version. <!--#8c3c9676b026d96a-->
  - `TestAmendFalsePath.test_amend_false_failure_restores_disk` (method) — Asserts a failed amend=False commit restores the disk version and unstages pyproject.toml. <!--#451fb8a48c37747c-->
  - `TestAmendFalsePath.test_amend_false_skipped_when_already_at_target` (method) — Asserts C1 fail-loud still applies on the amend=False branch when already at target. <!--#4d0bd727f23ea565-->
  - `TestAmendFalsePath.test_amend_false_preserves_merge_commit_below_head` (method) — Asserts the original merge commit remains intact as HEAD^1 after an amend=False bump. <!--#464a11b6df7c484a-->

### `tests/commands/merge/test_version_collision_regression.py` (python) — End-to-end regression suite freezing the G9 version-collision accident (two concurrent worktree sessions off one baseline both baking 11.12.0, one changelog entry lost), asserting through the real luo merge adapter and reconcile()/commit-guard libraries that concurrent sessions now land distinct monotonic versions, no-op/ancestor merges still reconcile, resume is idempotent, and the non-worktree drift guard recomputes to prevent collisions. <!--#3fca3bb12d79a9ed|b000938cd303a03d-->
- `_git` (function) — Test helper that runs a git subcommand in a given repo root with output captured and check=True. <!--#9f1bc200ef078687-->

- `TestConcurrentWorktreeCollision` (class) — Regression test class (Task 1) proving two concurrent worktree sessions diverging from one baseline receive distinct, monotonically-advancing versions with both changelog entries preserved, reproducing and validating the fix for the 11.12.0 collision accident. <!--#9966e2b9ff3919f2-->
  - `TestConcurrentWorktreeCollision.test_two_concurrent_minor_sessions_do_not_share_a_version` (method) — Test that two sequentially-merged concurrent minor sessions off 11.11.2 land 11.12.0 then 11.13.0 (reconcile re-basing on master's current version), with both changelog entries surviving under distinct headers and both intents consumed once. <!--#0f9227fa83611d75-->
  - `TestConcurrentWorktreeCollision.test_changelog_entries_are_filed_under_distinct_versions` (method) — Asserts each session's changelog bullet lands under a different `## <version>` block, proving neither collapsed via version-number dedup. <!--#20f5fbdd8ea49268-->

- `TestNoOpMergeReconcile` (class) — Suite proving reconcile runs unconditionally and bumps from outstanding intents even for already-ancestor/no-merge-commit shapes. <!--#6f2903f2f80ef521-->
  - `TestNoOpMergeReconcile.test_already_ancestor_merge_still_advances_version` (method) — Fast-forwards an unconsumed intent onto master (no merge commit) and asserts luo merge's reconcile still advances the version to 11.12.0. <!--#6fbdae9be52d9ba0-->
  - `TestNoOpMergeReconcile.test_intent_on_master_with_no_branch_still_reconciles` (method) — Asserts reconcile() derives and applies a version deterministically from an intent already committed on master with no branch to merge. <!--#002f4bd64f6ab859-->
- `TestReconcileResumeIdempotent` (class) — Suite proving a re-entered reconcile never double-bumps, backed by both the consumed flag and a git-durable reconcile-commit trailer. <!--#cae1fb119221b327-->
  - `TestReconcileResumeIdempotent.test_reconcile_twice_does_not_double_bump` (method) — Asserts a second reconcile after a successful one is a clean already-reconciled noop with no further version advance. <!--#4d31ff7d9de3330f-->
  - `TestReconcileResumeIdempotent.test_reconcile_idempotent_even_if_consumed_flag_lost` (method) — Asserts the git-durable reconcile-commit trailer alone short-circuits a re-bump when the on-disk consumed flag is cleared (crash-window simulation). <!--#77e1fb23cd1f91dd-->
- `TestReconcileCommitFailureRecovery` (class) — Test class (Task 2b') verifying reconcile stays recoverable when its git commit fails or crashes mid-write — rolling back half-applied version/changelog/consumed writes and correctly re-landing the version on resume rather than trusting an uncommitted consumed flag. <!--#f19b453b77a2f700-->
  - `TestReconcileCommitFailureRecovery.test_failed_commit_rolls_back_and_resume_lands_version` (method) — Test that a reconcile whose _commit_reconcile raises rolls back to a clean tree with the intent un-consumed, and a resumed reconcile then recomputes and commits the version. <!--#09a0822c823fc3de-->
  - `TestReconcileCommitFailureRecovery.test_resume_recovers_consumed_but_uncommitted_intent` (method) — Test that a hard-crash residue of on-disk version/changelog/consumed writes without a reconcile commit is recovered on resume (not treated as already-done), restoring to HEAD and re-committing the version. <!--#6f07754833bc3880-->
  - `TestReconcileCommitFailureRecovery.test_resume_recovers_dirty_version_file_without_consumed_flag` (method) — Test the narrowest crash window — a dirty version file with no changelog and no consumed flag — where resume must read its base from committed 11.11.2 and reconcile back to 11.12.0 rather than double-bumping to 11.13.0. <!--#af0c5a3dcb3ad6b6-->
- `TestNonWorktreeDriftGuard` (class) — Test class (Task 2c) exercising the direct-run commit drift guard _guard_version_race in isolation, covering recompute-on-drift, pass-through when no drift, and hard-halt when re-analysis still returns the colliding disk version. <!--#5e7429a5e5eed03f-->

  - `TestNonWorktreeDriftGuard.test_no_drift_passes_target_through_unchanged` (method) — Asserts the guard is a pure pass-through (no re-analysis) when disk equals the recorded baseline. <!--#5d423d2f5b484891-->
  - `TestNonWorktreeDriftGuard.test_drift_reanalysis_returning_disk_version_halts` (method) — Asserts the guard raises rather than returns when re-analysis against the drifted baseline still yields the colliding disk version. <!--#d325bf87d31faaa1-->
- `TestFlowWroteVersionBlobDetection` (class) — Test class (Issue 4) verifying _flow_wrote_version detects a flow's own version write from its Flow: trailer commit and the version-file blob, independent of the optional Version: commit-message line. <!--#543b31bce4bfc27e-->

- `TestNonWorktreeCommitHandlerDriftGuard` (class) — Test class exercising Change D end-to-end through the real commit_handler wiring against a live git repo, confirming the in-lock disk re-read feeds the drift guard and that the guard's baseline is version_analyze's observed current_version, not the audit-only pre_session_version. <!--#3eb9363032208e63-->
  - `TestNonWorktreeCommitHandlerDriftGuard._make_direct_flow` (method) — Test helper that builds a non-worktree FlowInstance with a completed VERSION_ANALYZE step and a pending COMMIT step wired with the given observed and suggested versions. <!--#c17dd034f4c48737-->
  - `TestNonWorktreeCommitHandlerDriftGuard.test_commit_handler_recomputes_on_concurrent_disk_drift` (method) — Asserts commit_handler re-reads a concurrently-published 10.7.1, recomputes past it via version_analyze, and lands 10.7.2 on disk. <!--#3470d98a0bd981c7-->
  - `TestNonWorktreeCommitHandlerDriftGuard.test_commit_handler_no_drift_writes_resolved_target` (method) — Asserts commit_handler writes the resolved 10.7.1 without re-analysis when disk still matches version_analyze's observed current_version. <!--#b9f9a12608fc7b4b-->
  - `TestNonWorktreeCommitHandlerDriftGuard.test_commit_handler_own_session_advance_is_not_drift` (method) — Asserts the guard compares disk against version_analyze's observed current_version (not pre_session_version), so own-session advances are not treated as drift and 10.8.0 lands verbatim. <!--#51d7272560078532-->
  - `TestNonWorktreeCommitHandlerDriftGuard.test_commit_handler_halts_when_reanalysis_still_collides` (method) — Asserts commit_handler fails and writes nothing when the in-lock recompute still returns the concurrent flow's released version, leaving the file and HEAD unchanged. <!--#f9b9334944b043cb-->

## `tests/core/` — Unit test package for `tianluo`'s core utility modules, covering `machine_id` host-identity generation and local/remote detection, `run.pid` marker encoding/parsing and cross-machine holder attribution, and the `truncate_preview` string helper. <!--#176291c336c50d1c|3bf70a80cbcf4c1b-->

### `tests/core/__init__.py` (python) — Package init marker for the core-utilities test suite, declaring the tests/core directory as a Python package. <!--#ac166613d2af2787|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/core/test_machine_id.py` (python) — Unit tests for the core `machine_id` helpers, covering the legacy `<hostname>-<getnode hex>` id format, per-process caching, the `is_local_machine()` local/remote truth table under patched host identities, and the backward-compatible `tianluo.daemon.aggregator._stable_machine_id` re-export. <!--#f07570f07bbc93e0|dc7e4ded37c838ba-->
- `_clear_machine_id_cache` (function) — Autouse fixture that resets `machine_id._cached_machine_id` to None before and after each test so monkeypatched host identities never leak across tests. <!--#0056fb82704d0973-->
- `test_stable_machine_id_format_matches_legacy_aggregator` (function) — Asserts `stable_machine_id()` still produces the legacy aggregator format `<hostname>-<uuid.getnode() hex>`. <!--#0698c2905297435e-->
- `test_stable_machine_id_is_stable_within_process` (function) — Verifies repeated `stable_machine_id()` calls return the same cached value within one process. <!--#d5b844750d06e5d7-->
- `test_is_local_machine_truth_table` (function) — Checks the `is_local_machine()` truth table: None/empty legacy records and the current machine id are local, any other id is remote. <!--#1901318bc2698cca-->
- `test_is_local_machine_respects_patched_identity` (function) — Monkeypatches `socket.gethostname`/`uuid.getnode` to confirm the derived id and the local/remote verdict follow the patched machine identity. <!--#474f1baec3450dcc-->
- `test_aggregator_alias_matches_core` (function) — Guards the backward-compatible re-export by asserting `tianluo.daemon.aggregator._stable_machine_id()` matches the core `stable_machine_id()`. <!--#14f464515ef3c513-->

### `tests/core/test_run_pidfile.py` (python) — Unit tests for the `run.pid` marker layer in `tianluo.core.run_pidfile`, covering record encode/decode round-trips (including legacy truncated formats), `owns_flow` attribution, `foreign_run_holder` cross-machine detection, `probe_run_marker`'s absent-vs-undecidable distinction, and `acquire_run_marker`'s exclusive-ownership semantics — first-writer-wins, idempotent self-reclaim, stale-only reclamation, an absolute-`state_dir` guard, and fail-closed blocking on foreign, corrupt, or IO-failed markers. <!--#bb2f3076a3a4c915|7a31fa3672033dfc-->
- `_write` (function) — Test helper that creates the state dir and writes the given raw text into its `run.pid` marker, returning the marker path. <!--#4a5b2d61c643f660-->
- `TestCodecRoundTrip` (class) — Tests that `encode_run_pidfile` / `read_run_holder` / `read_run_pidfile` round-trip full records, tolerate omitted flow ids and truncated legacy formats, and reject unusable ones. <!--#893a47b4c7c869ee-->
  - `TestCodecRoundTrip.test_full_record_round_trips` (method) — Asserts a fully populated pid/machine/flow record encodes and decodes back to the identical `RunHolder`. <!--#797073f479a8b35b-->
  - `TestCodecRoundTrip.test_flow_id_omitted_when_not_yet_minted` (method) — Asserts a marker stamped before the engine mints a flow id decodes with `flow_id` of `None`. <!--#d540c161a02c3abf-->
  - `TestCodecRoundTrip.test_legacy_records_decode_by_truncation` (method) — Asserts older pid-only and pid+machine marker formats still decode, with the missing trailing fields left as `None`. <!--#ec8e6e8c402cac10-->
  - `TestCodecRoundTrip.test_narrow_view_still_returns_pid_and_machine` (method) — Asserts the legacy `read_run_pidfile` accessor keeps returning just the `(pid, machine)` pair from a full record. <!--#f898888b3045e82e-->
  - `TestCodecRoundTrip.test_unusable_records_yield_nothing` (method) — Asserts `read_run_holder` returns `None` for absent, empty, non-numeric, and zero-pid markers. <!--#60cb8e346f160bd6-->
- `TestOwnsFlow` (class) — Tests `RunHolder.owns_flow` attribution rules for stamped versus unstamped records, including the `flow_scoped` directory case. <!--#6f22f544c7d7e6ab-->
  - `TestOwnsFlow.test_recorded_flow_id_decides` (method) — Asserts a stamped flow id is authoritative — it matches only its own flow, even inside a flow-scoped worktree. <!--#6dec6261071b41c3-->
  - `TestOwnsFlow.test_unstamped_record_is_claimed_only_in_a_flow_scoped_dir` (method) — Asserts a record with no flow id is claimed by a flow only in that flow's own isolation worktree, never in the shared project root. <!--#8594e68ee94854f6-->
- `TestForeignHolder` (class) — Tests that `foreign_run_holder` surfaces whole records from other machines while treating local and legacy markers as not foreign. <!--#6f1248a648815204-->
  - `TestForeignHolder.test_foreign_record_is_returned_whole` (method) — Asserts a marker from another machine is returned as a complete `RunHolder`, flow id included. <!--#9d761386d528e864-->
  - `TestForeignHolder.test_local_and_legacy_records_are_not_foreign` (method) — Asserts records stamped with `stable_machine_id()` and machine-less legacy records both yield `None` from `foreign_run_holder`. <!--#65793b3878bb685a-->
- `TestMarkerProbe` (class) — Tests that `probe_run_marker` keeps "marker absent" distinguishable from "marker present but unreadable/malformed", so a caller cannot mistake a failed read for proof that no run owns the state dir. <!--#be69d14b595c143b-->
  - `TestMarkerProbe.test_absent_marker_is_not_present` (method) — Asserts that probing a state dir with no `run.pid` reports not present, no holder, and not undecidable. <!--#099985196fee3831-->
  - `TestMarkerProbe.test_decodable_marker_is_present_with_a_holder` (method) — Asserts that a well-formed marker probes as present and decodes into the expected `RunHolder` (pid, machine id, flow id). <!--#3d302f9faee95429-->
  - `TestMarkerProbe.test_malformed_marker_is_present_but_undecidable` (method) — Asserts that empty, blank, non-numeric, and zero-pid marker bodies all probe as present yet undecidable. <!--#aee6a5897f8e5219-->
  - `TestMarkerProbe.test_unreadable_marker_is_present_but_undecidable` (method) — Uses a directory named `run.pid` to stand in for a permission/IO read failure and asserts the probe reports present-but-undecidable rather than absent. <!--#2dba7f63e7df1c66-->
- `TestExclusivePublication` (class) — Tests `acquire_run_marker` as an exclusive ownership token — first writer wins, own-marker re-claims are idempotent, only stale local markers are reclaimable, and every ambiguous case (foreign, undecodable, IO failure, failed write) fails closed as blocked. <!--#a2c73c21bd89f98d-->
  - `TestExclusivePublication.test_first_writer_wins_and_the_second_is_blocked` (method) — Asserts a second acquisition against another owner's record is blocked, names that holder, and leaves the existing record untouched. <!--#8e1c6be2dd7d5eeb-->
  - `TestExclusivePublication.test_reclaiming_our_own_marker_is_idempotent` (method) — Asserts a run can re-acquire its own marker to fill in the flow id the engine mints later. <!--#29cc35a301583c23-->
  - `TestExclusivePublication.test_a_dead_local_marker_is_reclaimable_when_allowed` (method) — Asserts a local marker holds by default but is reclaimed when an `is_stale` predicate is supplied, so a crashed run cannot wedge the project forever. <!--#521dd96f787888ec-->
  - `TestExclusivePublication.test_a_foreign_marker_is_never_reclaimed_as_stale` (method) — Asserts a record from another machine blocks acquisition without the staleness predicate ever being consulted, since foreign pid liveness is undecidable. <!--#13a5e6411b999176-->
  - `TestExclusivePublication.test_an_undecodable_marker_blocks` (method) — Asserts a corrupted marker body blocks acquisition with no holder reported. <!--#af8fab3265f85dc9-->
  - `TestExclusivePublication.test_an_io_failure_blocks_instead_of_starting_unowned` (method) — Monkeypatches `os.open` to raise EIO and asserts acquisition fails closed as blocked rather than letting the caller proceed owning no token. <!--#6a7f490e7c62654c-->
  - `TestExclusivePublication.test_an_io_failure_still_names_the_owner_it_can_read` (method) — Asserts that when the open fails with EACCES but the existing record still decodes, the blocked claim reports the owning `RunHolder` for a more actionable refusal. <!--#5b0adc80f251e350-->
  - `TestExclusivePublication.test_a_failed_record_write_blocks_and_leaves_no_marker` (method) — Monkeypatches `os.fdopen` to raise ENOSPC and asserts the half-created marker is removed and the claim still reads as blocked, since ownership was never established. <!--#ee38629e5b7f644f-->
- `TestAbsoluteStateDirGuard` (class) — Test class asserting that `acquire_run_marker` rejects any non-absolute `state_dir` (including the relative path an unconfigured `MagicMock` produces) by raising `ValueError` without creating directories, while still folding genuine runtime failures into a fail-closed blocked `MarkerClaim`. <!--#96bf0247352bfd17-->
  - `TestAbsoluteStateDirGuard.test_a_bare_magicmock_state_dir_raises_and_writes_nothing` (method) — Verifies that passing a bare `MagicMock` attribute as `state_dir` raises `ValueError` and leaves the current working directory untouched, preventing the silent `MagicMock/...` directory leak. <!--#73f92571f3b9597d-->
  - `TestAbsoluteStateDirGuard.test_a_relative_state_dir_raises_and_writes_nothing` (method) — Verifies that a plain relative `Path` as `state_dir` raises `ValueError` and creates nothing under the current working directory. <!--#1b3678f4628a717f-->
  - `TestAbsoluteStateDirGuard.test_the_guard_precedes_the_never_raises_contract` (method) — Verifies the argument guard is the only raising path — with `Path.mkdir` patched to fail with `EACCES`, `acquire_run_marker` still returns a non-acquired, blocked `MarkerClaim` rather than propagating the error. <!--#f50be3c2e602f67d-->
- `TestReleaseRules` (class) — Tests that release and ownership checks respect the token's owner — `release_run_marker` drops only the current process's record (with `drop_undecodable` as the exiting owner's escape hatch) and `holds_run_marker` reflects actual ownership. <!--#dac235dc10b00710-->
  - `TestReleaseRules.test_release_only_drops_our_own_record` (method) — Asserts release refuses and preserves a foreign record but removes the marker when it belongs to this pid and machine. <!--#e4a36a7c9b82b434-->
  - `TestReleaseRules.test_undecodable_record_is_dropped_only_for_the_owning_run` (method) — Asserts a corrupted record survives an ordinary release but is removed under `drop_undecodable=True`, so it cannot read as held forever. <!--#58e688ec97318dd1-->
  - `TestReleaseRules.test_holds_run_marker_tracks_ownership` (method) — Asserts `holds_run_marker` is false with no marker, true after this process acquires it, and false again once a foreign record replaces it. <!--#108ce98e9331764c-->

### `tests/core/test_utils.py` (python) — Unit tests for the core `truncate_preview` utility, covering empty/short/exact-length passthrough, ellipsis truncation, unicode handling, custom max_length and ellipsis parameters, and edge cases like ellipsis longer than max_length. <!--#1c4ced0849fa1814|ac06f7bbf86b6eb6-->

## `tests/daemon/` — Test package for the tianluo daemon side, covering the daemon↔server protocol and client keepalive, project registry/resume/uploads/usage backends, and — most heavily — the DaemonHistoryReader's history delivery pipeline (incremental cursor reads, prefix-hash verification, windowed/chunked byte-budgeted delivery, record compaction budgets, push/drain cursor races, and the caching and dirty-sentinel optimizations that keep idle polling cheap). <!--#bbc07cacd1d695c9|0e46f4b54e9c6291-->

### `tests/daemon/__init__.py` (python) — Empty package marker that makes tests/daemon a Python package for the daemon-related test modules. <!--#e3b0c44298fc1c14|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/daemon/test_chunked_delivery_livelock.py` (python) — Regression test module for the daemon→server history-delivery livelock (Defect A), driving the real DaemonHistoryReader over a multi-MB jsonl backlog through byte-budgeted websocket stubs to assert byte-bounded chunked reads that cursor-resume without loss, strictly positive monotonic per-window progress and full catch-up under short-lived connections, fast-push re-arming on truncated rounds, and correct websocket close-reason formatting/logging plus cursor preservation across reconnect. <!--#c45df6d426f333d4|8d9e48d47cea0fdc-->
- `_write_backlog` (function) — Test helper that writes `count` multi-megabyte JSONL records (each far larger than one MAX_BYTES_PER_REPORT chunk, with its index embedded) into one history step file and returns their content bodies for order verification. <!--#500ecd726f05f107-->
- `_keys` (function) — Test helper returning the `(step_id, ordinal)` identity tuples the frontend reconciles history records by. <!--#62a330d402d6f088-->
- `_bodies` (function) — Test helper extracting each record's `message.content` body into a list. <!--#7f2face56564f9c2-->
- `_Provider` (class) — A minimal `HistoryProvider` stub scoped to fixed flow ids that delegates the three `_push_history` methods to a real `DaemonHistoryReader` so byte-bounded chunking and cursor-resume behaviour are genuine. <!--#ba0072fb833f1d3e-->
  - `_Provider.__init__` (method) — Stores the real reader, project root, and the fixed list of flow ids the provider is scoped to. <!--#7ee4b07333ef65a1-->
  - `_Provider.build_index` (method) — Returns an empty index list (the test provider builds no index). <!--#17a111c8d858317e-->
  - `_Provider.read_active_flows` (method) — Reads each scoped flow through the real reader using the supplied per-flow cursors, returning the list of flow reads. <!--#0390b9bb231c7169-->
  - `_Provider.read_flow` (method) — Delegates an on-demand single-flow read straight to the real reader so HISTORY_REQUEST-path chunking stays genuine. <!--#a88091d7867fc344-->
  - `_Provider.live_flow_ids` (method) — Returns the scoped flow ids as a set of live flows. <!--#1ae3dea316cf1bf6-->
- `_ShortLivedWS` (class) — A websocket stub that counts sent frame bytes and, once a bounded per-window budget would be exceeded, marks itself dead and raises (dropping that frame unrecorded), modelling the partial-transfer loss of a connection recycled mid-flight. <!--#6b0d9d251a91fc9f-->
  - `_ShortLivedWS.__init__` (method) — Initialises the byte budget, spent counter, dead flag, and captured-frames list. <!--#d1b3861cf0101a01-->
  - `_ShortLivedWS.send` (method) — Accepts a frame if it fits the remaining byte budget (recording it), otherwise marks the socket dead and raises `ConnectionError` without counting or recording it. <!--#dce27f87d4f7e14f-->
  - `_ShortLivedWS.history_frames` (method) — Returns the payloads of all recorded `MSG_HISTORY_DATA` frames, optionally filtered to one flow id. <!--#057dede3883a820a-->
- `_client` (function) — Test factory building a `DaemonClient` wired to a given `_Provider` and pre-binding a `_fast_push_event` so the truncated-round fast-push re-arm is observable. <!--#5b92653d70675186-->
- `_cursor_line` (function) — Test helper returning the committed delivery water-mark line for a flow's step (0 if none). <!--#827edb0b562410f6-->
- `test_read_flow_is_byte_bounded_and_resumes_without_loss` (function) — Asserts a single `read_flow` returns at most the byte cap (plus the one crossing record) and that successive cursor-resumed reads cover the whole multi-MB backlog exactly once in ordinal order. <!--#a9973ffd4fd8d6b3-->
- `test_short_lived_windows_make_monotonic_progress_and_catch_up` (function) — Regression test asserting that when each connection window fits only one byte-bounded chunk, every window makes strictly positive cursor progress and the server assembles the whole backlog in order exactly once (no zero-progress livelock). <!--#3eb8089eba8edf54-->
- `test_truncated_round_rearms_fast_push` (function) — Asserts each truncated (backlog-remaining) `_push_history` round re-arms the fast-push event while the final draining round does not, letting one long-lived window drain the whole backlog without waiting out an idle tick. <!--#e32e07da507fda21-->
- `_ClosingWS` (class) — A websocket stub that optionally yields preframes then ends its receive loop via `StopAsyncIteration` or a supplied exception, with `close_code`/`close_reason` populated as a transport would leave them for close-reason formatting tests. <!--#d5737da97e46412d-->
  - `_ClosingWS.__init__` (method) — Initialises the close code/reason, optional raised exception, queued preframes, and sent-frame list. <!--#a2164bfc2020816e-->
  - `_ClosingWS.__aiter__` (method) — Returns self as the async iterator for the receive loop. <!--#bebf40482a72eae1-->
  - `_ClosingWS.__anext__` (method) — Yields queued preframes first, then raises the supplied exception or `StopAsyncIteration` to end the receive loop. <!--#a1a94bc450017d32-->
  - `_ClosingWS.send` (method) — Records each sent frame into the `sent` list. <!--#5bd706f54c804ef9-->
- `_FakeConnect` (class) — The async context manager that `websockets.connect(...)` returns, yielding the wrapped `_ClosingWS` on enter. <!--#c5da591f6b76e6b1-->
  - `_FakeConnect.__init__` (method) — Stores the `_ClosingWS` to hand out on context entry. <!--#4bb2c8a66be2fc22-->
  - `_FakeConnect.__aenter__` (method) — Returns the wrapped `_ClosingWS` on async context entry. <!--#fe3a93d51eafca4e-->
  - `_FakeConnect.__aexit__` (method) — Returns False on exit so exceptions propagate normally. <!--#cd12f1ac9bb0c283-->
- `_FakeWebsockets` (class) — A stand-in for the `websockets` module passed into `_session`, whose `connect` yields a `_FakeConnect` over a fixed `_ClosingWS`. <!--#540d4531303e09ec-->
  - `_FakeWebsockets.__init__` (method) — Stores the `_ClosingWS` its `connect` will serve. <!--#4bb2c8a66be2fc22-->
  - `_FakeWebsockets.connect` (method) — Returns a `_FakeConnect` wrapping the fixed `_ClosingWS`, ignoring all connect arguments. <!--#9e3cc46fdd6447ba-->
- `_session_client` (function) — Test factory building a provider-less `DaemonClient` with fast cadences so `_session` runs HELLO plus primer and then races quickly to teardown. <!--#b5813b1bccdd3feb-->
- `_run_session` (function) — Drives one full `_session` against a `_ClosingWS` (via `_FakeWebsockets`) to its non-shutdown unwind under a 5s timeout. <!--#37310bd1907ac928-->
- `test_format_close_reason_variants` (function) — Asserts `_format_close_reason` renders each close class (server close, abnormal 1006 drop, no-frame-with-exception, no-frame-no-exception) into a non-empty, readable reason. <!--#a4e8a61eaa2c4404-->
- `test_session_logs_server_initiated_close` (function) — Test verifying that a server-initiated WebSocket close (code + reason) is logged as a warning and recorded in `client.last_error` rather than silently swallowed. <!--#e8130803cf73855a-->
- `test_session_logs_transport_drop_with_distinguishable_reason` (function) — Test verifying that an abnormal transport drop with no close frame logs a distinguishable network-class reason (1006/ABNORMAL_CLOSURE) without leaking the daemon key. <!--#29d3bc079c8262bd-->
- `test_auth_rejected_session_does_not_log_a_disconnect` (function) — Test confirming that an auth-rejected WELCOME(accepted=false) unwinds the session without emitting a spurious disconnect warning while preserving the rejection reason. <!--#08e302bdadb56eda-->
- `test_session_preserves_delivery_cursor_across_reconnect` (function) — Asserts a fresh `_session` does not wipe the inherited `_history_cursors` delivery water-mark, so the next window resumes from the last confirmed chunk rather than re-reading from line 0. <!--#36306b6dc0c5d482-->
- `test_reconnect_resumes_drain_instead_of_restarting_from_zero` (function) — Test that across simulated real reconnects (per-session state reset but cursor preserved) the backlog catches up and the server assembles every record exactly once, without re-delivering the leading chunk each window. <!--#1bdaaea4950108b1-->
- `test_push_loop_fast_push_wake_drains_static_backlog` (function) — With all other push drivers neutralised, asserts the `_push_loop` drains a terminal (no-disk-change) backlog purely on fast-push wakes converted into history pushes, rather than consuming them as bare status updates and leaving the cursor pinned. <!--#dd4d65ef19b9c131-->
- `test_history_request_delivers_full_backlog_despite_byte_cap` (function) — Test that an on-demand HISTORY_REQUEST for a large inactive flow drains the entire backlog across multiple chunk frames (one FULL baseline plus contiguous APPENDs) so the byte cap never silently truncates the delivered history. <!--#10f2b886ba4ca665-->

### `tests/daemon/test_client_keepalive.py` (python) — A unit test module that pins DaemonClient's WebSocket keepalive tuning by driving `_session` with a fake `websockets` module and asserting `connect` is called with the relaxed `ping_interval=20`/`ping_timeout=60` params (so lossy links don't drop the connection and truncate history reloads). <!--#043754e4c29494d9|a8852af020c612d7-->
- `_AbortSession` (class) — A sentinel exception raised from the fake connect context manager to short-circuit `DaemonClient._session` before its body runs. <!--#0a8556eca9ab6faf-->
- `_FakeConnectCM` (class) — A fake async context manager standing in for a websockets connection that records connect kwargs and aborts on entry by raising `_AbortSession`. <!--#0a2bdb63fc568d3a-->
  - `_FakeConnectCM.__init__` (method) — Stores the connect kwargs passed to the fake connection context manager. <!--#55e4ee1be60191f6-->
  - `_FakeConnectCM.__aenter__` (method) — Raises `_AbortSession` on entry to skip all HELLO/receive-loop session machinery. <!--#44e218c5c08ce94a-->
  - `_FakeConnectCM.__aexit__` (method) — No-op async exit that suppresses nothing, returning False. <!--#d4b4e991ba16221e-->
- `_FakeWebsockets` (class) — A fake `websockets` module whose `connect` captures the connection kwargs and returns the aborting fake context manager. <!--#0974a17078141e60-->
  - `_FakeWebsockets.__init__` (method) — Initializes the captured `connect_kwargs` dict to empty. <!--#d47da5788c461596-->
  - `_FakeWebsockets.connect` (method) — Records the keyword arguments of a connect call and returns a `_FakeConnectCM` for them. <!--#4f3bb42b8b83bfd9-->
- `_client` (function) — Factory building a `DaemonClient` configured with test machine/host/version values and a stub snapshot provider. <!--#2b8b9cf3d53fe04a-->
- `test_connect_uses_relaxed_ping_params` (function) — Asserts that `DaemonClient._session` calls websockets connect with the relaxed keepalive params `ping_interval=20` and `ping_timeout=60`. <!--#07e977f816e72556-->

### `tests/daemon/test_dirty_sentinel.py` (python) — Test suite for the G6 dirty-sentinel optimization, verifying both the engine side (every `PersistenceManager` persist/clear path atomically bumps `tianluo/state/.dirty`'s seq while a sentinel write/read failure never breaks persistence) and the daemon side (`DaemonHistoryReader` gates idle terminal roots to one sentinel stat and zero deep scans per tick, un-gates on a seq bump, fails open when the sentinel is missing or deleted, never gates active-flow roots, and bounds out-of-band writes via the status-tick `clear_sentinel_gate` backstop), including async push-loop cases driven through `asyncio.run` with fake history providers and WebSockets. <!--#4952a3da5597cd05|0d26d3ac1bd9ae05-->
- `_fresh_disk_cache` (function) — Autouse-style fixture that clears the module-level disk JSON cache before and after each test to isolate cache state. <!--#86d041daa61d28a0-->
- `_make_flow` (function) — Helper that builds a minimal but realistic FlowInstance with one RUNNING DISCOVERY step for the given flow_id and status. <!--#bbeff7e2055f4fcb-->
- `_sentinel_path` (function) — Test helper returning the path to a root's dirty-sentinel file at tianluo/state/.dirty. <!--#fd2dfb884845b126-->
- `_read_seq` (function) — Helper that reads the sentinel JSON and returns its integer seq value. <!--#1381e87a0a923c85-->
- `_write_engine_raw` (function) — Test helper that writes engine.json directly to disk (bypassing PersistenceManager) so no dirty sentinel is bumped. <!--#adec0afc69734211-->
- `_bump_sentinel_raw` (function) — Helper that advances the sentinel seq via atomic temp-file rename, mimicking PersistenceManager's bump. <!--#97e0366a9d08acbe-->
- `_make_reader` (function) — Helper that constructs a DaemonHistoryReader scoped to a single project root. <!--#b42b7537c80ac81f-->
- `deep_scans` (function) — Fixture that monkeypatches DaemonHistoryReader._scan_root_signature to record every per-root deep scan. <!--#52be8ff641463b47-->
- `sentinel_stats` (function) — Fixture that monkeypatches history_module._sentinel_stat to record every sentinel stat call in the signature pass. <!--#674ed6ad5512a34e-->
- `test_save_flow_bumps_seq_strictly` (function) — Asserts each save_flow persist strictly advances the sentinel seq. <!--#661380095d1f2bde-->
- `test_save_resumable_snapshot_standalone_bumps_seq` (function) — Asserts a standalone save_resumable_snapshot bumps the sentinel seq. <!--#e69bc0f7d031c59a-->
- `test_clear_resumable_snapshot_bumps_seq` (function) — Asserts clearing a resumable snapshot removes its file and bumps the sentinel seq. <!--#2311dbda5987c70c-->
- `test_clear_state_archive_bumps_seq` (function) — Asserts clear_state archives/removes the state file and bumps the sentinel seq. <!--#c6b4a4cbb48bc04a-->
- `test_clear_state_without_state_file_is_a_noop` (function) — Asserts clear_state with nothing on disk writes no sentinel (a no-op). <!--#589416b7f394df8b-->
- `test_corrupt_sentinel_restarts_from_scratch` (function) — Asserts a corrupt (non-JSON) sentinel is discarded and the seq restarts near zero rather than poisoning persistence. <!--#cc7a63dc45e97b34-->
- `test_sentinel_write_failure_never_breaks_persistence` (function) — Asserts an injected OSError on the sentinel write leaves save_flow/clear paths intact (sentinel is optional). <!--#af5cb6f6dde5cb0d-->
- `test_sentinel_read_failure_still_bumps` (function) — Asserts an unreadable existing sentinel degrades to a fresh seq instead of crashing. <!--#8fffec0abdaf29ee-->
- `test_idle_root_gated_to_one_sentinel_stat_per_tick` (function) — Asserts an idle terminal root with an unmoved sentinel does zero deep scans and exactly one sentinel stat per tick after the gate arms. <!--#9fcdf35cb7403c90-->
- `test_sentinel_bump_restores_deep_scan_and_surfaces_the_change` (function) — Asserts a seq bump un-gates the root so the next tick rescans and surfaces the new flow's signature token. <!--#b2e67e7c13ea29fe-->
- `test_missing_sentinel_fails_open_to_per_tick_deep_scan` (function) — Asserts a sentinel-less root deep-scans every tick (pre-G6 behavior) and picks up changes immediately. <!--#90633455be149288-->
- `test_active_flow_root_is_never_gated` (function) — Verifies a live root with an active flow always deep-scans on each fast tick — a bare jsonl append surfaces immediately despite an unchanged sentinel, since HistorySink streaming bypasses the sentinel. <!--#e6c63146fc4547dc-->
- `test_flow_going_terminal_arms_the_gate_only_after_a_scan` (function) — Asserts a live→terminal transition (which moves the sentinel) is rescanned once and then settles into the gated, scan-free state. <!--#a4cee7a0c2014122-->
- `test_out_of_band_write_is_bounded_by_clear_sentinel_gate` (function) — Asserts a sentinel-bypassing write stays hidden while gated and surfaces only on the status-tick backstop via clear_sentinel_gate. <!--#cf56f28efd32dbae-->
- `test_sentinel_deletion_fails_open` (function) — Asserts deleting a gated root's sentinel un-gates it so deep scanning resumes. <!--#ca5263a795234ea2-->
- `test_persistence_and_gate_mesh_end_to_end` (function) — End-to-end assertion that engine-side sentinel bumps alone break the daemon-side gate and surface a new flow. <!--#c8e1b4b44fb3e1d3-->
- `_GateAwareHistory` (class) — Minimal fake history provider that records counts of signature scans and gate-clears for the async push-loop tests. <!--#889b3531424b1401-->

  - `_MinimalHistory.active_flow_signature` (method) — Stub returning an empty signature. <!--#9bea134021468dd8-->
  - `_MinimalHistory.invalidate_index_cache` (method) — No-op stub for the index-cache invalidation hook. <!--#b6f55685eeed3252-->
  - `_MinimalHistory.live_flow_ids` (method) — Stub returning an empty set of live flow ids. <!--#ede7672505587e63-->
- `_FakeWS` (class) — Minimal fake WebSocket capturing sent payloads for the push-loop tests. <!--#ece999e56c9ab42d-->
  - `_FakeWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the fake WebSocket's sent-payload list. <!--#eb11ca3925a0aa08-->
  - `_FakeWS.send` (method) — Async send stub that appends the payload to the sent list. <!--#5bd706f54c804ef9-->
- `_client` (function) — Helper constructing a DaemonClient wired to a given history provider with configurable fast/status intervals. <!--#09cec5710a08635c-->
- `_run_push_loop` (function) — Helper that drives the client's async _push_loop for a fixed duration via asyncio.run and then stops it cleanly. <!--#1491eb4692d5e150-->
- `test_status_tick_clears_gate_fast_ticks_do_not` (function) — Asserts status ticks clear the sentinel gate while the more frequent fast ticks scan without clearing, preserving the gate's savings between heartbeats. <!--#5b5155dea7ca9201-->
- `test_provider_without_gate_hook_is_tolerated` (function) — Asserts the push loop's status tick tolerates a legacy provider lacking clear_sentinel_gate without crashing. <!--#8594051ce8bba152-->
- `_build_idle_estate` (function) — Test helper that builds a two-root on-disk estate (a settled terminal root with an issue farm and oversized archive, plus a history-only root) with sentinels planted for the idle-profile gating tests. <!--#54d8a36a62b73b65-->
- `io_counters` (function) — Fixture monkeypatching the expensive-IO seams (full read, json parse, degraded header, YAML load, index rebuild) to count each and assert the idle profile keeps them at zero. <!--#8fcc8623edce7fd9-->
- `test_idle_fast_ticks_cost_one_sentinel_stat_per_root` (function) — Asserts gated idle fast ticks over the two-root estate incur zero reads/parses/deep scans and exactly one sentinel stat per root per tick. <!--#b9157358067ed4d3-->
- `test_idle_status_ticks_reuse_every_cache` (function) — Asserts ungated idle status ticks reuse every cache — no YAML parses, cold rebuilds, big-file scans, or extra parses — while snapshot/index correctness stays intact. <!--#1cfd56542c09632a-->
