- `test_calls_signature_skips_gated_idle_root` (function) — Verifies a gated root's calls dir is not re-enumerated and its fingerprint is reused verbatim, while un-gating re-scans it and surfaces newly-added call files. <!--#7107ef8b05fe7aee-->
- `test_calls_signature_gate_source_failure_scans_all` (function) — Verifies a raising calls-gate source fails open to a full scan, treating gating as an optimization rather than a correctness dependency. <!--#e88989311dcb5bfb-->
- `test_gated_roots_reports_idle_roots_from_reader` (function) — Asserts the reader's gated_roots reflects the last signature pass — a settled terminal root is reported, an active root is not. <!--#34c6c3f6f43dacf3-->

### `tests/daemon/test_disk_json_cache.py` (python) — Unit tests for tianluo.daemon.disk_json_cache's degraded-header result cache (idle-CPU fix, group G2), locking in that oversized (> MAX_PARSE_BYTES) engine.json snapshots are head+tail-scanned exactly once per unchanged file, keyed by (path, st_mtime_ns, st_size), then served from cache with zero disk opens — while covering stat-change rescans, cached None extraction failures with warn-once, force_fresh bypass, deleted-file eviction, LRU bounding, clear_cache flushing, and non-pollution of the main full-parse cache. <!--#64070b225dce06b6|a0e173cc5aeced66-->
- `_clean_cache` (function) — Autouse fixture that clears the disk_json_cache parse/degraded caches and warn-once set before and after each test for isolation. <!--#5fc9bcc041f437bf-->
- `_count_degraded_scans` (function) — Test helper that monkeypatches djc._degraded_header to count how many head+tail disk scans occur, returning a mutable counter dict. <!--#44a555e11a7138bb-->
- `_write_oversized` (function) — Test helper that writes a well-formed indent=2 engine.json above the parse-size guard, with head/tail flow metadata around a fat state blob. <!--#d0f5ccfcba04527f-->
- `test_second_read_zero_disk_scans` (function) — Asserts an unchanged oversized engine.json is head+tail-scanned exactly once and later reads are served from cache with zero rescans. <!--#77d54500602ee36e-->
- `test_stat_change_rescans_and_updates_cache` (function) — Verifies the degraded cache re-scans and refreshes only when the file's stat key (size or mtime) changes, staying cached otherwise. <!--#3e40810e2ccca994-->
- `test_extraction_failure_cached_and_warns_once` (function) — A pytest test verifying that read_engine_header on a broken oversized JSON file (no flow_id) is scanned and logs a WARNING only once, then caches the None failure so repeated reads don't re-scan or re-warn per tick. <!--#557e1171db32cad8-->
- `test_clear_cache_drops_degraded_store` (function) — Confirms clear_cache also flushes the degraded header store, forcing a fresh scan on the next read. <!--#e29787f9707313c3-->
- `test_full_parse_cache_never_polluted_by_oversized` (function) — Ensures oversized files only populate the degraded store's tiny header while the main full-parse cache stays empty and read_json_cached still refuses them. <!--#ed6d578bd1e02d9e-->
- `test_deleted_oversized_file_drops_degraded_entry` (function) — Verifies that reading a since-deleted oversized path returns None and evicts its degraded cache entry rather than pinning it forever. <!--#be39a593e9f82b48-->
- `test_force_fresh_bypasses_degraded_cache` (function) — Asserts force_fresh=True reaches disk even on a colliding stat-key hit, surfacing an in-place same-size/mtime rewrite and refreshing the cache. <!--#49f531d9fea32755-->
- `test_degraded_lru_bounded` (function) — Checks the degraded store honours the shared _MAX_CACHE_ENTRIES LRU cap, keeping recent entries and evicting the oldest. <!--#095dc581c7d0653a-->

### `tests/daemon/test_history_drain_push_race.py` (python) — Regression test module reproducing the daemon history full-pull drain ↔ push-loop cursor race by driving a real DaemonHistoryReader over a multi-frame backlog, injecting a concurrent `_push_history` mid-drain via websocket/frame stubs, and replaying frames into a real ServerState to assert the per-flow `draining` marker and drain-end cursor sync prevent server cursor-gap discards and the resulting full-pull re-request loop. <!--#6fcfcd9eb8e4192b|aa01291181d4f353-->
- `_step_path` (function) — Test helper that builds the on-disk path to a flow's step jsonl file under `<root>/tianluo/history/<flow_id>/<step>`. <!--#6be767235643edac-->
- `_append_backlog` (function) — Helper that appends `count` fat, index-embedded records to a step file (append mode, modelling a live flow growing on disk) and returns their body strings. <!--#a2e1b8add468a6c1-->
- `_keys` (function) — Helper that extracts each record's `(step_id, ordinal)` identity tuple — the key the frontend reconciles by. <!--#62a330d402d6f088-->
- `_bodies` (function) — Helper that extracts the `message.content` body string from each record. <!--#7f2face56564f9c2-->
- `_Provider` (class) — A minimal HistoryProvider stub scoped to fixed flow ids, delegating to a real DaemonHistoryReader so chunked delivery and cursor-resume behaviour are genuine. <!--#e07a5b240a9273b3-->
  - `_Provider.__init__` (method) — Stores the real reader, the project root, and the fixed list of flow ids the provider serves. <!--#7ee4b07333ef65a1-->
  - `_Provider.build_index` (method) — Returns an empty index (indexing is out of scope for these push/drain race tests). <!--#17a111c8d858317e-->
  - `_Provider.read_active_flows` (method) — Reads each configured flow through the real reader, passing per-flow resume cursors, and returns the flow snapshots. <!--#0390b9bb231c7169-->
  - `_Provider.read_flow` (method) — Delegates a single-flow read to the real DaemonHistoryReader, defaulting the project root when none is passed. <!--#602bc75d15dd54e4-->
  - `_Provider.live_flow_ids` (method) — Returns the fixed set of flow ids as the currently-live flows. <!--#1ae3dea316cf1bf6-->
- `_RecordingWS` (class) — A websocket stub that records every sent frame and optionally awaits an `on_frame` hook per frame, letting tests deterministically inject a concurrent push mid-drain. <!--#d9f1d924ecd01566-->
  - `_RecordingWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the recorded-frames list and the optional per-frame hook. <!--#93c92472f9b66409-->
  - `_RecordingWS.send` (method) — Parses and records each sent JSON frame, then awaits the `on_frame` hook if one is set. <!--#748527ce131b3b1d-->
  - `_RecordingWS.history_frames` (method) — Returns the payloads of recorded HISTORY_DATA frames, optionally filtered to a given flow id. <!--#057dede3883a820a-->
- `_client` (function) — Factory that constructs a DaemonClient wired to the given provider and pre-binds `_fast_push_event` so re-arm-on-truncation is a no-op in these tests. <!--#b2b5531be59f9516-->
- `_apply` (function) — Async helper that replays one HISTORY_DATA payload into a ServerState via `apply_history_frame`, passing `cursor_base` so the server's cursor-gap guard sees the real coverage window. <!--#2498903a732fefe9-->
- `test_push_during_drain_is_skipped_and_server_never_gaps` (function) — Regression test asserting that a `_push_history` append fired mid-drain emits NO frame for the draining flow, so replaying the drain and push frames into a real `ServerState` never triggers a cursor-gap self-heal and the backlog assembles once, in order, to the file's end. <!--#27b09cbb9d29d7d8-->
- `test_drain_syncs_push_cursor_so_next_append_is_accepted` (function) — Regression test asserting the drain resets `_history_cursors` to the drain-end water mark, so a subsequent `_push_history` append declares a `cursor_base` matching the server's mark and is accepted (extended) rather than discarded as a gap. <!--#007a5f02046866de-->
- `test_drain_synced_cursor_survives_concurrent_push_rebind` (function) — Test that a push tick's wholesale cursor rebind preserves a flow whose drain finished (and synced its cursor) mid-tick, rather than reverting it to the stale pre-drain snapshot. <!--#e3c071377b49f720-->
- `test_drain_starting_mid_send_loop_skips_that_flows_append` (function) — Test that a drain starting for a later pending flow while the send loop awaits an earlier send causes the per-flow pre-send drain re-check to skip that flow's already-computed append. <!--#f9ba8326ab24ce4d-->
- `test_drain_send_failure_does_not_write_a_dirty_cursor` (function) — Test that when a drain frame fails to leave the socket, the drain marker is released and the push cursor is left untouched — avoiding a partially-drained water mark that would manufacture a gap. <!--#663be2bf55afd5a2-->

### `tests/daemon/test_history_index_cache.py` (python) — Test module locking the build_index cache-invalidation contract fixed for the idle-CPU issue (G2): freshness is driven by change signals — the push loop invalidates when `active_flow_signature` moves, per-root source stat tokens surface new/archived flows, and state-changing commands (END_SESSION, ISSUE_COMMAND, HISTORY_INDEX_REQUEST) invalidate on arrival — while the 60s `BUILD_INDEX_TTL` is only a backstop, so consecutive no-change status ticks cost zero cold rebuilds; it uses fake WebSocket/client/history-provider stubs and helpers that count fresh rebuilds and drive the push loop deterministically. <!--#0dafe63089453d2e|03743e5b967614d2-->

- `_FakeWS` (class) — Minimal async WebSocket stand-in that decodes and records every frame the client sends for assertion. <!--#e6c82bc92db5d9fa-->
  - `_FakeWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the fake WebSocket's `sent` list that captures outgoing frames. <!--#ce393d52044e73f0-->
  - `_FakeWS.send` (method) — Async send that decodes the payload via `protocol.decode` and appends it to the captured `sent` list. <!--#154edf553e8ef4d4-->
- `_make_client` (function) — Test factory building a `DaemonClient` with default machine/host/version/snapshot fields, overridable by keyword args. <!--#f3137c441b7b6c4e-->
- `_write_active_flow` (function) — Test helper that materializes a running flow on disk under a root — writing a RUNNING `tianluo/state/engine.json` plus a `tianluo/history/<flow_id>/01_discovery_ab12.jsonl` record — to set up `build_index` cache-invalidation scenarios. <!--#f5a2f80eb7ad47e4-->
- `_count_fresh_builds` (function) — Helper that monkeypatches `reader._build_index_fresh` to count how many actual cold rebuilds occur. <!--#d0f84beb3cf827cf-->
- `test_ttl_is_a_60s_backstop` (function) — Asserts `BUILD_INDEX_TTL` equals 60.0 so the cache backstop far exceeds the 5s status heartbeat. <!--#314625207405a5ba-->
- `test_consecutive_status_ticks_no_change_zero_cold_rebuilds` (function) — Verifies ten 5s-spaced no-change status ticks yield exactly one fresh build (served from cache thereafter). <!--#9a5f4a444aa315c3-->
- `test_ttl_backstop_still_rebuilds` (function) — Verifies that aging the cache past the 60s TTL forces a second fresh rebuild (direct-disk-edit safety). <!--#b22342f8527a4293-->
- `test_invalidate_forces_immediate_rebuild` (function) — Verifies `invalidate_index_cache` forces the next `build_index` to rebuild fresh instead of reusing the cache. <!--#0288e63fbb600f79-->
- `test_new_history_only_flow_rebuilds_without_explicit_invalidate` (function) — Asserts that adding a new history-only flow dir (no engine.json, no signal) shifts the per-root source stat token so `DaemonHistoryReader.build_index` rebuilds and surfaces the flow without an explicit `invalidate_index_cache` call, rather than waiting out the 60 s TTL. <!--#e10a5b9b5fde7b7e-->
- `test_archived_engine_json_rebuilds_via_source_token` (function) — Verifies that an end-session-style archival (moving `engine.json` into `state/archive/`) shifts the source token so `build_index` rebuilds and reclassifies the flow's source from `"active"` to `"archived"`. <!--#82ada6c1e82d2405-->
- `_run_push_ticks` (function) — Helper that deterministically drives `DaemonClient._push_loop` for N forced status ticks then stops it. <!--#f735031f675c848b-->
- `test_push_loop_idle_status_ticks_do_not_cold_rebuild` (function) — Verifies five idle push-loop status ticks with no disk change reuse the cached index (one build only). <!--#d41f4530201cc80c-->
- `test_push_loop_disk_change_rebuilds_next_tick` (function) — Checks that a jsonl append which moves `active_flow_signature` causes the daemon client's push loop to invalidate and rebuild the index on the next tick rather than serving the still-within-TTL cache. <!--#68711e5c862d4046-->
- `_StubProvider` (class) — History-provider stub recording invalidation and build counts with no-op index/active-flow reads. <!--#5715c1ff9b46797b-->
  - `_StubProvider.__init__` (method) — Initializes the stub's `invalidations` and `builds` counters to zero. <!--#3ee5052457123d86-->

### `tests/daemon/test_history_linear_read.py` (python) — Pytest module verifying `DaemonHistoryReader.read_flow`'s incremental cursor-based reading of `tianluo/history` `.jsonl` flow files — that per-round and full-drain read volume stays linear/bounded (via an `open`-monkeypatching byte-counting fixture), that multi-round drains reproduce the exact full-read record sequence, and that edge cases (partial tails, blank/unparseable lines, unterminated final records, worktree copy switches, out-of-range cursors, invalid UTF-8) are handled without data loss or errors. <!--#429f3ecd6fce055f|859809a606633a92-->
- `_make_reader` (function) — Test helper that builds a `DaemonHistoryReader` whose project-roots provider returns the given temporary roots as strings. <!--#f5fb70620f9f4765-->
- `_flow_dir` (function) — Test helper that creates and returns the `tianluo/history/<flow_id>` directory under a given root. <!--#d29934aed956126e-->
- `_msg` (function) — Test helper producing a minimal history message dict (role, content, empty `raw_json`, `step_type` "implement"). <!--#952ac7140b802b74-->
- `_write_lines` (function) — Test helper writing raw text fragments verbatim to a file so tests control exact byte layout (partial tails, blank lines, missing trailing newline). <!--#589dae48034c0301-->
- `_keys` (function) — Test helper reducing records to their `(step_id, ordinal)` identity pairs for sequence comparison. <!--#1b1254c91ba6472e-->
- `_CountingHandle` (class) — Delegating file-object wrapper that tallies every byte the reader pulls through `read`/`readline`/iteration into a shared state dict. <!--#317be33f6b2b2f00-->
  - `_CountingHandle.__init__` (method) — Stores the wrapped file handle and the shared byte-counting state dict. <!--#59acd1950bf2cc61-->
  - `_CountingHandle.read` (method) — Delegates `read` and bills the returned byte/char count to the shared counter. <!--#73c6e31ae21f42f0-->
  - `_CountingHandle.readline` (method) — Delegates `readline` and bills the returned line's length to the shared counter. <!--#2ded7f251d9031e1-->
  - `_CountingHandle.__iter__` (method) — Returns self so the wrapper can be iterated in place of the underlying handle. <!--#ad419825cfa617c2-->
  - `_CountingHandle.__next__` (method) — Delegates iteration to the wrapped handle and bills each yielded line to the shared counter. <!--#ef22e8504edfe4b9-->
  - `_CountingHandle.__enter__` (method) — Returns the wrapper itself so `with open(...)` still yields the counting handle. <!--#e11a445075fd069e-->
  - `_CountingHandle.__exit__` (method) — Forwards context-manager exit to the wrapped file handle. <!--#3876fe6eb707563e-->
  - `_CountingHandle.__getattr__` (method) — Forwards any other attribute access to the wrapped file handle. <!--#9a68fe95d76619ff-->
- `read_bytes` (function) — Pytest fixture that monkeypatches `open` (and mutes `history._hash_span` reads) to measure how many `.jsonl` bytes `read_flow`'s record path consumes, exposing a `take()` reset-and-report helper. <!--#414edae6de64c61b-->
- `_big_flow` (function) — Test helper writing a multi-MB single-step flow file of many large records, used as the fixture for read-volume assertions. <!--#110da22c50223165-->
- `_drain` (function) — Test helper that repeatedly calls `read_flow` with the returned cursor until untruncated, returning every round and the concatenated records. <!--#3c8e9d2dc2cc6536-->
- `test_incremental_round_reads_at_most_one_budget` (function) — Asserts each cursor-driven incremental round reads no more than one byte budget plus one record plus fixed fingerprint overhead, never the tail it won't ship. <!--#7b6ac322d5f3fbab-->
- `test_full_drain_read_volume_stays_linear` (function) — Asserts a full multi-round drain of a multi-MB backlog reads O(file) total bytes (under a 4x ceiling) rather than re-reading the tail quadratically. <!--#380a67cfa41af7cc-->
- `test_drain_reproduces_the_full_read_record_sequence` (function) — Asserts a capped multi-round drain yields exactly the same `(step_id, ordinal, message)` sequence as a from-scratch full read. <!--#64e8785a74510819-->
- `test_partial_tail_is_not_consumed_until_it_is_terminated` (function) — Asserts a half-flushed final line is left unconsumed (offset/cursor not advanced) and is later delivered at its original ordinal once the writer terminates it. <!--#7445b2a359ecc559-->
- `test_blank_lines_occupy_physical_line_numbers` (function) — Asserts blank and unparseable lines still consume physical line numbers so `ordinal` remains a stable line index across full and incremental reads. <!--#8d744b5ebeacc707-->
- `test_unterminated_final_record_is_consumed_when_parseable` (function) — Asserts a newline-less but parseable final record is consumed to EOF, while a parseable non-dict tail is not treated as a record. <!--#481acbb59b505fca-->
- `test_copy_switch_rereads_the_new_copy_from_line_zero` (function) — Asserts that when a bare cursor filename resolves to a different file (worktree copy), the read restarts at line 0 instead of skipping the new copy's leading lines. <!--#13a887e5e239a98f-->
- `test_cursor_past_end_of_file_resets_to_the_head` (function) — Asserts a cursor beyond the file's physical line count is discarded and re-read from the head, while a cursor exactly at the line count is honoured. <!--#285f1a376b7cdb55-->
- `test_invalid_utf8_line_is_skipped_not_fatal` (function) — Asserts a corrupt UTF-8 line is skipped like any other unparseable line instead of raising out of `read_flow` and losing the whole flow. <!--#6caccc7fcf901644-->

### `tests/daemon/test_history_prefix_hash_cache.py` (python) — Tests for the daemon history reader's cached prefix-hash verification, covering both the I/O-cost properties (linear-not-quadratic verification bytes across long drains, idle files not re-hashed, geometrically doubling full re-verifications, bounded per-round head/boundary windows) and the correctness properties it must preserve (from-scratch, equal-size in-place, and mid-prefix rewrites still detected and re-delivered from ordinal 0, worktree-copy switches discarding stale verifier state), plus unit-level `_PrefixVerifier` cases for cold hashing, inode changes, truncation, and unreadable or mismatched prefixes. <!--#dec3aea899e3f817|084423179e9c9b5e-->
- `_make_reader` (function) — Test helper that builds a `DaemonHistoryReader` whose project-roots provider returns the given root paths as strings. <!--#f5fb70620f9f4765-->
- `_flow_dir` (function) — Test helper that creates and returns the `tianluo/history/<flow_id>` directory under a given root. <!--#d29934aed956126e-->
- `_line` (function) — Test helper that renders one jsonl history record as bytes with a caller-controlled tag and padding so its byte length is predictable. <!--#9eae9872588f1afd-->
- `_keys` (function) — Test helper that reduces delivered records to their `(step_id, ordinal)` identity pairs for order/position assertions. <!--#1b1254c91ba6472e-->
- `hash_io` (function) — Pytest fixture that monkeypatches `_hash_span` and `_window_signatures` to record every prefix-verification disk read, exposing span bytes, window bytes, totals, and from-byte-0 re-hash offsets per file. <!--#52722f2d0c64ae9a-->
- `_read_all` (function) — Test helper wrapping a single `reader.read_flow` call with optional cursor and project root. <!--#40a2b389ee7ba1ce-->
- `_write_step_file` (function) — Test helper that writes a step jsonl file of N padded records into a flow directory and returns its path. <!--#5c7f08208be63ee5-->
- `_drain` (function) — Test helper that calls `read_flow` repeatedly until the frame is no longer truncated, returning the round count and all accumulated records. <!--#58b46a828b70d329-->
- `test_long_drain_verification_io_stays_linear` (function) — Asserts a many-hundred-round two-file drain spends only ~3x the history size in verification I/O rather than the quadratic per-round whole-prefix re-hash of issue #287. <!--#6b32a7080431bd90-->
- `test_idle_file_is_not_rehashed_once_more_files_are_draining` (function) — Asserts a step file that finished draining costs zero re-hash bytes (only bounded per-round window checks) while another file keeps draining for hundreds of rounds. <!--#75300f012f90fe86-->
- `test_full_reverifications_follow_a_doubling_schedule` (function) — Asserts from-byte-0 re-verifications still happen per file but at geometrically doubling offsets, keeping them logarithmically few and their total cost bounded. <!--#944d4cb12f8bd5c2-->
- `_warm_cached_verifier` (function) — Test helper that reads a step file over several append rounds so the reader holds a warm `_PrefixVerifier` cache before a rewrite is staged. <!--#976f4d2a3adf03dc-->
- `test_from_scratch_rewrite_is_detected_with_a_warm_cache` (function) — Asserts a retry that rewrites and grows a step file from record 0 is detected against a warm cache, forcing a re-read from line 0 and dropping the stale verifier. <!--#74dfcaad29553a99-->
- `test_equal_size_inplace_rewrite_is_detected_with_a_warm_cache` (function) — Asserts the issue #209 shape — identical size and pinned mtime but different content — is still caught by content hashing and re-delivered from line 0. <!--#ce790c2ec40c9a00-->
- `test_middle_of_prefix_rewrite_in_the_fresh_span_is_detected_at_once` (function) — Asserts a same-size mutation inside the span the previous round consumed is detected immediately, since a cached round always re-reads that span. <!--#d10b4cf8f8d57c63-->
- `test_middle_of_prefix_rewrite_in_an_old_region_is_caught_by_the_doubling` (function) — Asserts a surgical mutation in an already-verified old region survives only a bounded number of rounds and is caught by the next doubling re-hash, which then re-delivers from ordinal 0. <!--#03c57d4296091293-->
- `test_idle_file_is_verified_by_bounded_windows` (function) — Asserts polling a settled file costs only two bounded head/boundary window reads per round yet still catches an equal-size in-place retry on the next poll. <!--#793e54d1d9c4c7dc-->
- `test_copy_switch_discards_the_verifier_for_the_new_key` (function) — Asserts switching between a main-root and worktree copy of the same flow discards any verifier state held for the file being switched to, so the copy is re-read from line 0. <!--#6c361c0d9e5c9c81-->
- `test_verifier_and_prefix_hasher_share_one_lifetime` (function) — Asserts the consumed-side prefix hasher and disk-side verifier stay mutually consistent across full reads, incremental reads, and detected rewrites. <!--#0da8f0f25c1739d9-->
- `_digest` (function) — Test helper computing the 16-byte blake2b digest the verifier compares against. <!--#1bb04f7bab58f9df-->
- `test_verifier_falls_back_to_a_full_hash_without_a_cache` (function) — Unit-tests that a cold `_PrefixVerifier` hashes the whole prefix once, after which an append is verified by re-reading only the appended span. <!--#917baef824b0b270-->
- `test_verifier_falls_back_when_the_file_identity_changes` (function) — Unit-tests that an atomic-replace inode change invalidates the path-keyed cache and forces a full re-hash even though the bytes are a superset. <!--#c8b9d98646c91242-->
- `test_verifier_rejects_a_file_shorter_than_the_offset` (function) — Unit-tests that a file truncated below the verified offset fails verification and drops the cached hasher. <!--#64448fac3871d276-->
- `test_verifier_rejects_changed_and_unreadable_prefixes` (function) — Unit-tests the verifier's rejection paths: mismatched digest, missing expected digest, nonexistent file, and an `OSError` on open. <!--#088e0246553a745d-->

- `test_every_tool_chip_survives_compaction_in_order` (function) — Asserts compaction preserves all 412 tool chips with identical identities and document order, since the WebUI reconciles chips by ordinal. <!--#63dfc8e271609641-->

### `tests/daemon/test_history_signature.py` (python) — A test module verifying the cheap terminal-flow fast path of DaemonHistoryReader's active_flow_signature, asserting that settled terminal engine.json flows are parsed/read at most once and thereafter poll via pure stat peeks with zero full reads, while live active flows keep full verify_content read-and-hash semantics each poll so same-(mtime, size) in-place rewrites and status flips still move the signature. <!--#57a7f7104460c2f4|29858a1076d16a34-->
- `_fresh_disk_cache` (function) — An autouse-style fixture that clears the module-level disk JSON cache before and after each test to isolate per-test cache state. <!--#86d041daa61d28a0-->
- `_make_reader` (function) — Helper that builds a DaemonHistoryReader whose project_roots_provider returns the single given root. <!--#b0b9102cbf5f3b87-->
- `_write_engine` (function) — Test helper that writes a JSON `engine.json` under `tianluo/state/` for the given root, optionally pinning its mtime so a same-size in-place rewrite keeps an identical (mtime, size) stat key. <!--#30a411190929fbe7-->
- `full_reads` (function) — Fixture that monkeypatches disk_cache._read_active_content to record every verify_content whole-file read, returning the call list for assertions. <!--#b651843e04d6180f-->
- `test_terminal_flow_repeat_polls_zero_full_reads` (function) — Asserts that repeated signature polls over a settled terminal flow pay one initial verify read and then zero further full reads (the per-tick hotspot fix). <!--#27fdd6e0c94c6470-->
- `test_terminal_flow_already_cached_pays_no_full_read` (function) — Asserts that when another reader has already stat-keyed the engine header, a terminal flow's signature pass never touches the verify_content path at all. <!--#ce9b5c3a56b3bb5e-->
- `test_terminal_flow_parsed_once_then_stat_only` (function) — Asserts that a terminal engine.json is JSON-parsed exactly once, after which every later poll is a pure stat hit with no re-parse. <!--#6e3020e0734e99ac-->
- `test_active_flow_still_verifies_content_each_poll` (function) — Asserts that a live RUNNING flow keeps re-reading and re-hashing its engine.json on every poll, preserving verify_content semantics. <!--#ff425778a6ddcc19-->
- `test_active_same_stat_inplace_rewrite_still_moves_signature` (function) — Asserts that a same-(mtime, size) in-place content rewrite of an active flow still changes the signature via the content digest, surviving the cheap stat path. <!--#05796e50dd9f44a1-->
- `test_active_same_stat_flip_to_terminal_drops_flow` (function) — Asserts that a same-stat in-place flip of an active flow to FAILED is caught by verify_content and drops the flow from the signature in the same poll. <!--#ce4d4077548931f9-->
- `test_signature_structure_unchanged_for_active_flow` (function) — Asserts that a RUNNING flow's `active_flow_signature()` token has the exact expected shape: an `__engine__` part carrying a folded content digest, a `__status__` part, and one (name, mtime, size) part per history jsonl. <!--#7dc8ad10dc835af0-->
- `test_terminal_then_new_flow_rewrite_detected` (function) — Asserts that replacing a COMPLETED engine.json with a new RUNNING flow is detected on the next poll because the full rewrite moves (mtime_ns, size) past the peek. <!--#904ea091b7dc6f0c-->
- `test_jsonl_append_still_moves_signature` (function) — Verifies that appending a line to a flow's history jsonl still changes its `active_flow_signature()`, confirming jsonl fingerprinting is unaffected by the cheap-path optimization. <!--#def6173d0535b381-->

### `tests/daemon/test_history_usage_catalog.py` (python) — Tests that DaemonHistoryReader.read_flow attaches a serialized pricing catalog to history frames — full snapshots carry both the usage payload and catalog priced from the project's tianluo.yaml overrides, append deltas carry the catalog without a payload (or omit it when there are no usage records), and an unknown project root degrades to the built-in price table so no frame ever reaches the server catalog-less. <!--#483ca6420a771faf|6a867f1e71c32b9b-->
- `_record` (function) — Test helper that builds a fully-populated AVAILABLE UsageRecord for a claude-code/anthropic call on claude-opus-5 with the given call_id and input-token count (100 output tokens, no cache, no actual cost). <!--#e147fd8baedfadd3-->
- `_usage_msg` (function) — Test helper that wraps a _record into an assistant chat-history message dict carrying it under the `usage_records` key. <!--#6ca83435a4109186-->
- `_write_jsonl` (function) — Test helper that creates parent directories and writes the given dicts as a fresh newline-delimited JSON file. <!--#f321072562a278a4-->
- `_append_jsonl` (function) — Test helper that appends the given dicts as additional JSONL lines to an existing history file, simulating incremental step output. <!--#826510bf1d7d8393-->
- `_hist` (function) — Test helper returning the `tianluo/history/<FLOW>` directory path under a given project root. <!--#9083f192757febee-->
- `test_full_read_carries_usage_priced_with_project_catalog` (function) — Asserts that a full-snapshot DaemonHistoryReader.read_flow returns both the usage payload and the serialized pricing catalog, with the estimated cost computed from the project's tianluo.yaml price overrides and no unknown-price entries. <!--#dd5cff095f1d6bfd-->
- `test_append_read_carries_catalog_but_no_payload` (function) — Asserts that an append-mode delta read ships the pricing catalog but omits the usage payload, since a delta would under-count and the server must re-aggregate itself. <!--#322d832c508950bd-->
- `test_append_without_usage_omits_catalog` (function) — Asserts that an append frame containing no usage records omits the catalog key entirely, leaving the server's stored payload untouched. <!--#df87290d0020dd28-->
- `test_unknown_root_degrades_catalog_to_builtin` (function) — Asserts that with no project tianluo.yaml the frame still carries a catalog — the built-in price table — so pricing falls back to built-in rates rather than the override and the server never receives a catalog-less frame. <!--#8ae96aa4d319e64a-->

### `tests/daemon/test_history_window_read.py` (python) — End-to-end unit tests for the backwards history-window feature, covering DaemonHistoryReader.read_flow_window semantics (tail default, `before_step` paging to block 00, explicit `steps` selection, empty/oversized/unresolvable edge cases, physical-line ordinals shared with the cursor read and non-interference with it), the protocol registration, capability gate and round-tripping of the window request/data messages, and the DaemonClient handler's chunked, correlated, error-reporting replies. <!--#3c9f8dd607c9c543|6bfe23412b5c178b-->
- `_reader` (function) — Test helper that builds a DaemonHistoryReader whose project-roots provider returns the given temporary roots. <!--#bfdf0807171dcf1b-->
- `_flow_dir` (function) — Test helper that creates and returns the `tianluo/history/<flow_id>` directory under a fake project root. <!--#d29934aed956126e-->
- `_write_step` (function) — Test helper that writes a list of records as a JSONL step-block file and returns its path. <!--#8d9a35cbc2c17363-->
- `_seed_flow` (function) — Test fixture helper that materialises a flow of N numbered step-block files, each holding a fixed number of assistant records, returning the root, flow id and block names. <!--#eef81f24760cf611-->
- `_keys` (function) — Test helper that reduces records to their `(step_id, ordinal)` identity pairs for comparison. <!--#1b1254c91ba6472e-->
- `test_the_default_window_is_the_flow_tail` (function) — Asserts a countable window read with no anchor returns the last N step blocks and their records, so a WebUI open lands on the end of the conversation. <!--#79e49ea0f02a5223-->
- `test_the_whole_block_index_rides_along` (function) — Asserts every window reply carries the full flow-ordered block index plus per-file line counts, so a client can page backwards and self-check without another round trip. <!--#ae705c4657b2d6c3-->
- `test_paging_back_walks_to_the_very_first_block` (function) — Drives repeated `before_step` page-ups and asserts each block is reached exactly once down to block 00, proving the flow is fully browsable backwards. <!--#052ac4ed4288de14-->
- `test_an_unknown_anchor_yields_an_empty_window_not_the_tail` (function) — Asserts an unrecognised `before_step` returns an empty window anchored at the flow's end (not a silent fallback to the tail), while still shipping the block index. <!--#0cd88eac4c1d87fd-->
- `test_explicit_step_selection_reads_exactly_those_blocks` (function) — Asserts an explicit `steps` selection reads exactly the named blocks in flow order and ignores unknown ids, as the detail lookup requires. <!--#15949e8c2d4f1109-->
- `test_a_selection_matching_no_block_is_empty_but_not_at_the_head` (function) — Asserts a `steps` selection matching nothing yields an empty window whose `first_index` sits at the flow end rather than at the head. <!--#080f1e3fa779daeb-->
- `test_a_window_larger_than_the_flow_is_the_whole_flow` (function) — Asserts an oversized `count` clamps to the entire flow starting at index 0 rather than erroring or truncating. <!--#a1bfa4911e1e0881-->
- `test_ordinals_are_physical_lines_shared_with_the_cursor_read` (function) — Asserts window and cursor reads agree on physical-line ordinals across blank, unparseable and newline-less trailing lines, so a record has one identity under both paths. <!--#bd9e60d53581cfcd-->
- `test_an_unresolvable_flow_is_an_empty_window_not_a_raise` (function) — Asserts a window read for a nonexistent flow degrades to a fully empty window instead of raising. <!--#a30eababce614760-->
- `test_the_window_read_does_not_disturb_the_cursor_read` (function) — Asserts backwards window reads share no offset state with the incremental cursor drain, so a subsequent `read_flow` stays caught up. <!--#3fcc25aae0f19138-->
- `test_window_messages_are_registered_in_the_right_directions` (function) — Asserts the history-window request/data message types are registered in the correct one-way protocol direction tables. <!--#d3d8bb41cdb84891-->
- `test_the_capability_gate_refuses_every_older_revision` (function) — Asserts `supports_history_window` accepts protocol version 9 and above (including whitespace-padded strings) and rejects older or malformed values, so requests are never sent to a daemon that would drop them. <!--#ae6bd6df04122ebe-->
- `test_window_request_round_trips` (function) — Asserts a history-window request message encodes and decodes back to the exact expected payload fields. <!--#a05c62524a516e95-->
- `test_window_request_rejects_a_request_that_names_nothing` (function) — Asserts constructing a window request without a flow id, correlation id, or with a non-positive count raises ProtocolError instead of producing a degenerate frame. <!--#1573b271a1296ba9-->
- `test_window_data_round_trips_with_its_description` (function) — Asserts a history-window data message round-trips its records, block index, window, counts and `final` flag intact. <!--#604f82194ac0d0e9-->
- `_Provider` (class) — Minimal fake history provider that records `read_flow_window` calls and returns a canned window or raises, standing in for DaemonHistoryReader. <!--#2cea1cf6d0d2d5de-->
  - `_Provider.__init__` (method) — Stores the canned window and failure flag and initialises the call-recording list. <!--#a9588f98f06d27c3-->
  - `_Provider.read_flow_window` (method) — Records the call arguments and then either raises the simulated read failure or returns the canned window. <!--#e678537cfb281dda-->
- `_Sock` (class) — Fake WebSocket that decodes and collects every frame the handler sends, for assertion in tests. <!--#3e3ad8929cd77e9d-->
  - `_Sock.__init__` (method) — Initialises the list of decoded sent messages. <!--#b8b92aad379d234c-->
  - `_Sock.send_text` (method) — Decodes the outgoing raw frame and appends the resulting message to the sent list. <!--#a9f8fbbda8d4a77a-->
- `_client` (function) — Test helper that constructs a bare DaemonClient without its normal init, wiring only the history provider, sequence counter and send hook needed to exercise the window handler. <!--#422233db5eb663be-->
- `_run` (function) — Tiny helper that runs a coroutine to completion via `asyncio.run`. <!--#48a8d32a4a8529d2-->
- `test_the_handler_answers_with_the_window_and_its_description` (function) — Asserts the daemon-side window handler replies with a single successful final frame carrying the tail window, the full block index and all its records. <!--#445b2abf34ca29ea-->
- `test_a_window_over_one_frame_is_chunked_and_only_the_last_is_final` (function) — Asserts an oversized window is split across multiple frames where each record travels exactly once, the block index rides every frame, and only the last frame is marked final. <!--#69071c491d30e8f6-->
- `test_a_read_failure_is_reported_not_dropped` (function) — Asserts a provider exception produces an explicit `ok: false` error reply rather than silence, so the server can degrade to a full pull immediately. <!--#44ae759698a64900-->
- `test_a_request_without_a_correlation_id_is_ignored` (function) — Asserts a window request lacking a `request_id` is dropped without any reply, since no response could be routed. <!--#b3506783e90a7471-->
- `test_the_explicit_step_selection_reaches_the_provider` (function) — Asserts the handler forwards an explicit `steps` selection through to the history provider unchanged. <!--#b842b5d596c7945c-->
- `test_a_window_read_mints_a_signature` (function) — Asserts every window read hands back a non-empty signature probe with `not_modified` false, ready for the next conditional read. <!--#3323bb67bde66529-->
- `test_echoing_the_signature_of_an_unchanged_flow_reads_nothing` (function) — Asserts re-presenting a signature for an unchanged flow returns `not_modified` with the same signature and no records, window or counts populated. <!--#0acc0a1ced748e0b-->
- `test_the_conditional_read_never_opens_a_block` (function) — Spies on `_consumable_lines` to pin that a signature-matched conditional read opens no step-block file at all. <!--#438785c243786c58-->
- `test_a_grown_block_invalidates_the_signature` (function) — Asserts appending a record to an existing block invalidates the signature and yields a fresh signature plus the grown record set. <!--#e69a981814114f24-->
- `test_a_new_block_invalidates_the_signature` (function) — Asserts adding a new step block invalidates the signature so the reader is not frozen on the stale tail window. <!--#ac675ab362e9d5a5-->
- `test_a_signature_is_bound_to_the_request_shape` (function) — Asserts signatures differ between a tail read and a page-up read, and that presenting one against the other is not honoured as unchanged. <!--#5bbc10d637fc6f12-->
- `test_the_handler_relays_the_probe_and_answers_not_modified` (function) — Asserts the handler surfaces the signature in its reply and, when the client echoes it back for an unchanged flow, answers a single final `not_modified` frame carrying no payload. <!--#b4425b17c204fd37-->
- `test_a_stale_probe_still_gets_the_whole_window` (function) — Asserts an unrecognised `if_signature` produces a normal full window reply with no `not_modified` field. <!--#045909c65a9deaf0-->
- `test_the_probe_is_optional_on_the_wire` (function) — Asserts the signature fields are omitted entirely from request and reply payloads when unused, preserving compatibility with peers that never learned them. <!--#a39fe01179b63f6c-->

### `tests/daemon/test_issue_snapshot_cache.py` (python) — Test suite for DaemonAggregator._collect_issues's stat-signature cache, verifying that an unchanged issue tree re-parses zero YAML files while any mtime/size/content change, add/remove, or open→closed move invalidates the cache and is reflected in the next snapshot, while also covering CSafeLoader/SafeLoader selection, malformed-file tolerance, per-root isolation, and worktree/missing-dir edge cases. <!--#8c45c02bd7fe040d|79a3615bb8713f7d-->
- `_write_issue` (function) — Test helper that writes a minimal valid issue YAML file (id/title/description/status/source) under a root's tianluo/issues/<subdir>/ directory and returns its path. <!--#724991ace4b57e9d-->
- `parse_calls` (function) — Pytest fixture that monkeypatches yaml.load to record every call and the Loader passed, returning the list of recorded Loaders for parse-count assertions. <!--#49b90c5a5278803f-->
- `test_unchanged_tree_second_call_zero_parses` (function) — Verifies a second _collect_issues call over an untouched issue tree hits the cache and performs zero additional YAML parses while returning identical snapshots. <!--#0064e33f60ef3d2f-->
- `test_mtime_only_change_invalidates_cache` (function) — Asserts that bumping only a file's mtime (content and size unchanged) shifts the cache signature and forces exactly one re-parse. <!--#be1332f7d0f113e1-->
- `test_size_only_change_invalidates_cache` (function) — Asserts that a byte-size change with mtime pinned back still moves the signature so the rewritten title is re-parsed and reflected. <!--#1c1a37f096a82211-->
- `test_rewrite_reflected_in_snapshot` (function) — Confirms rewriting an issue's content busts the cache so the updated title appears in the next collected snapshot. <!--#8f6e6768ff940f46-->
- `test_added_and_deleted_files_reflected` (function) — Checks that adding and removing issue files change the signature and are reflected in the resulting snapshot set. <!--#3d60bdf1a5eb0220-->
- `test_open_to_closed_move_reflected` (function) — Verifies moving an issue from open/ to closed/ shifts the signature and updates the snapshot's reported status. <!--#6fd143b7bb279f51-->
- `test_worktree_copy_root_empty_and_uncached` (function) — Asserts that DaemonAggregator._collect_issues treats a worktree copy root as yielding no issues and never inserts it into _issue_cache, while the main root still returns its one issue. <!--#8c0dd12e66edcd21-->
- `test_missing_issues_dir_returns_empty_and_drops_cache` (function) — Verifies that after an initial cached collection, removing the entire tianluo/issues tree makes _collect_issues return empty and evicts the root from _issue_cache. <!--#e272c6be3a741b1f-->
- `test_csafeloader_used_when_available` (function) — Asserts the C-accelerated CSafeLoader (when libyaml is present) is the loader used for parsing. <!--#9c2cf1174570a55d-->
- `test_safeloader_fallback_behaves_identically` (function) — Confirms that without the C extension the pure-Python SafeLoader is used and produces data identical to the C loader. <!--#1d66f64382af4eaf-->
- `test_malformed_file_tolerated_and_cached` (function) — Checks that a corrupt YAML file is skipped (only the valid issue is returned) yet still participates in the stat signature, so a subsequent unchanged collection triggers zero re-parses. <!--#155942b68d3341c1-->
- `test_caches_are_per_root` (function) — Ensures two distinct roots maintain independent cache entries that update and invalidate separately. <!--#0b8296f4278fb12f-->

### `tests/daemon/test_presence_gearing.py` (python) — Test suite locking the daemon-side presence-gearing contract (revision-4 viewers signalling): using fake WebSocket, history, and calls providers, it verifies DaemonClient folds MSG_VIEWERS edges and PING-borne viewers levels into one viewer_count belief, that a 0→non-zero edge forces a full STATUS_UPDATE plus re-baselined HISTORY_INDEX while viewers==0 on a v4+ peer downshifts push and poll cadence to the idle gear, and that legacy peers, unknown/malformed inputs, server-command fast pushes, and the stop event all keep or interrupt gearing fail-open. <!--#8b466e4b1c75169e|ee7e7fad9b7fb4a6-->
- `_FakeWS` (class) — A minimal async WebSocket stand-in that decodes and records every protocol frame the client sends to it. <!--#5f9bcc99d752df8b-->
  - `_FakeWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the fake WebSocket with an empty list of captured/decoded sent messages. <!--#1fa42a3bd57f7e13-->
  - `_FakeWS.send` (method) — Decodes an outbound frame and appends it to the captured-message list. <!--#8b40f828f4fde955-->
- `_FakeHistory` (class) — A minimal history-provider fake exposing the push loop's surface while counting index invalidations and signature scans. <!--#03ee0707858b85c6-->
  - `_FakeHistory.__init__` (method) — Initializes the fake history's invalidation and signature-call counters to zero. <!--#e0e53f8753010480-->
  - `_FakeHistory.build_index` (method) — Returns an empty history index. <!--#4e594b1e12294f63-->
  - `_FakeHistory.read_active_flows` (method) — Returns no active flows regardless of the provided cursors. <!--#7511d19f655313cd-->
  - `_FakeHistory.active_flow_signature` (method) — Increments the signature-call counter and returns an empty signature dict. <!--#c17361405a55de98-->
  - `_FakeHistory.invalidate_index_cache` (method) — Increments the invalidation counter to record that the index cache was forcibly refreshed. <!--#ee893e296d381333-->
  - `_FakeHistory.live_flow_ids` (method) — Returns an empty set of live flow ids. <!--#ede7672505587e63-->
- `_CountingCalls` (class) — A calls-signature provider callable that counts how many times the fast tick scans for pending calls. <!--#cd5fcf85b7f3ba04-->
  - `_CountingCalls.__init__` (method) — Initializes the scan-call counter to zero. <!--#b0d35264a46fe6a9-->
  - `_CountingCalls.__call__` (method) — Increments the scan counter and returns an empty calls-signature dict. <!--#79f05fd3025734a5-->
- `_client` (function) — Factory building a DaemonClient wired with fake providers and a directly-set peer protocol version for presence-gearing tests. <!--#6bd1ca1af57b5213-->
- `_viewers` (function) — Builds a MSG_VIEWERS protocol message carrying the given viewer count. <!--#9fa21ed899b9eb5b-->
- `_types` (function) — Returns the list of message types captured by a _FakeWS in send order. <!--#aae81d3d242b54d0-->
- `_run_push_loop_for` (function) — Async helper that runs the client's push loop concurrently around a test body, then signals stop and awaits the task. <!--#ee2477bf75543b40-->
- `_wait_until` (function) — Async helper that polls a predicate until it holds or the timeout elapses, returning its final truth value. <!--#9bd113832ae3e68d-->
- `test_viewers_edge_updates_count_and_wakes_push` (function) — Asserts a MSG_VIEWERS 0→1 edge updates the viewer count and arms the forced full-refresh wake, while emitting no outbound frames. <!--#e71e50fedf8d059a-->
- `test_first_nonzero_report_of_a_session_also_wakes` (function) — Asserts a None→non-zero first report arms the wake (0→1 race fix) while later 1↔2 changes do not. <!--#7516e2ffe445edf6-->
- `test_ping_viewers_level_updates_count_and_pong_is_unchanged` (function) — Asserts a PING-borne viewers level heals the client's belief and arms a wake while the PONG replies remain unaffected. <!--#bab04c39b3101a83-->
- `test_v3_server_never_reports_an_effective_zero` (function) — Asserts that against a pre-v4 peer no viewers input downshifts the client, keeping the count unknown and cadence full-speed. <!--#f2542fba45a89e83-->
- `test_missing_or_malformed_viewers_keeps_current_gear` (function) — Asserts level-less or garbage viewers inputs leave the count and wake state unchanged. <!--#8afed093ed65c1eb-->
- `test_unknown_message_type_is_silently_ignored` (function) — Asserts an unrecognized inbound frame is dropped without error or reply. <!--#231e9cb6c3943794-->
- `test_effective_intervals_switch_with_viewer_count` (function) — Asserts _effective_intervals selects idle constants only at viewers==0 and full-speed config otherwise (unknown or >0). <!--#b502d61c519b3089-->
- `test_idle_gear_slows_the_scan_cadence` (function) — Asserts that with zero viewers the fast tick's disk scans effectively stop while active viewers drive many scans. <!--#c82abd3ad433fefd-->
- `test_presence_wake_forces_full_status_and_full_index` (function) — Asserts a mid-idle 0→1 edge forces a full STATUS_UPDATE plus re-baselined HISTORY_INDEX (with cache invalidation), not a keepalive, within a tick. <!--#63204d7d72fe7ef8-->
- `test_trigger_fast_push_stays_instant_in_idle_gear` (function) — Asserts a server-command _trigger_fast_push bypasses the idle cadence and immediately emits a STATUS_UPDATE. <!--#d8bcbe170df80d75-->
- `_daemon` (function) — Factory constructing a Daemon with GC disabled and a fast poll interval for cadence-timing tests. <!--#bbf8c09bbb7d639d-->
- `_count_polls` (function) — Helper that stubs _poll_once with a counter and runs the daemon's poll loop for a duration, returning the poll count. <!--#09913c74fa0f3139-->
- `test_poll_loop_downshifts_when_no_viewers` (function) — Asserts a connected client with viewers==0 stretches the poll wait to the idle gear while viewers>0 keeps polling. <!--#180d22b2e57f0c76-->
- `test_poll_loop_without_client_keeps_full_speed` (function) — Asserts a local-only daemon with no server client never downshifts its poll cadence. <!--#988fe315127c9d56-->
- `test_degraded_client_shapes_count_as_watched` (function) — Asserts disconnected, attribute-less, or malformed client shapes all resolve to "watched" (unknown count, not idle), while only a live zero is idle. <!--#4732f0cd8e25fa13-->
- `test_stop_event_interrupts_an_idle_gear_wait` (function) — Asserts that setting the stop event interrupts a deep idle-gear poll wait instead of blocking until the interval elapses. <!--#a7456ae2bd0d925c-->
- `test_status_file_reports_the_poll_gear` (function) — Asserts daemon_status.json records viewer_count and a poll_gear of "idle" or "full" for operators. <!--#93e1a58a023b1da3-->
- `test_v4_daemon_on_v3_server_stays_full_speed_revision3` (function) — Asserts a v4 daemon pinned to a v3 peer by WELCOME never downshifts, keeps configured cadence, and emits only v3-understood daemon→server frames. <!--#2095ce7dbe163735-->
- `test_unknown_frame_mid_stream_does_not_kill_the_receive_loop` (function) — Asserts the receive loop drops an unknown-typed frame and still answers a following PING, proving a v4 MSG_VIEWERS broadcast is safe for v3 daemons. <!--#6b80efa785549bbd-->

### `tests/daemon/test_project_registry.py` (python) — Pytest suite covering the daemon's project-root registry — the low-level `project_roots.json` read/modify/write helpers (matching, worktree fold-back, alias spellings, vanished/corrupt entries, `_REGISTRY_LOCK` serialization) and the `Daemon.request_add_project`/`request_remove_project` commands with their validation, `ProjectCommandError` codes, live-flow protection, and the `registered_projects()` snapshot surface. <!--#1c1123983609ebcb|97f098f53c98f3d1-->
- `_write_registry` (function) — Test helper that writes a `project_roots.json` registry file containing the given list of roots, creating parent directories as needed. <!--#2f968d66c0af4401-->
- `_make_project` (function) — Test helper that creates a fake project directory under `base` with a `tianluo/state` subtree and returns its path. <!--#bab9aa39960d4682-->
- `_make_worktree_dir` (function) — Test helper that creates a worktree directory under a main root's `tianluo/worktrees/<wt_name>` with its own `tianluo/state` subtree and returns its path. <!--#b4cd0c60aef6fdb7-->
- `test_remove_project_root_deletes_matching_entry` (function) — Asserts `_remove_project_root` returns True and drops only the matching root, leaving other registered entries intact. <!--#ecc2f65d994cca30-->
- `test_remove_project_root_miss_never_writes` (function) — Asserts a non-matching removal returns False and leaves the registry file byte- and mtime-identical (no needless rewrite). <!--#aecb5e980cc95e62-->
- `test_remove_project_root_folds_worktree_back_to_main` (function) — Asserts removing a worktree path folds back to its main root so the main entry is the one deleted. <!--#7b0c772a637c7c22-->
- `test_remove_project_root_matches_alias_spelling` (function) — Asserts removal matches the registered root when the caller passes a symlinked or `..`-containing alias spelling of the same directory. <!--#a8bdd00de93449bc-->
- `test_remove_project_root_matches_alias_entry_in_file` (function) — Asserts removal also matches when the *stored* registry entry is an alias (e.g. symlink path written by an older daemon) of the requested root. <!--#4a4a47051819f78b-->
- `test_remove_project_root_removes_vanished_entry` (function) — Asserts a stale registry entry whose directory no longer exists is still removable. <!--#9d9bb6ba446e0cdc-->
- `test_remove_project_root_tolerates_missing_and_corrupt_file` (function) — Asserts removal against a missing or malformed-JSON registry returns False without creating or rewriting the file. <!--#00cbfa44352d2e84-->
- `test_registry_writers_hold_the_lock_across_read_modify_write` (function) — Parametrized test spying on `_read_project_roots_raw` to assert every registry read-modify-write path performs its read while `_REGISTRY_LOCK` is held. <!--#0a43b8452d1c8ee7-->
- `test_concurrent_add_and_remove_do_not_lose_writes` (function) — Races a remove against an append with an artificially slowed atomic write to assert the lock serializes them so neither write is clobbered. <!--#295d3ef4b938aa82-->
- `_daemon` (function) — Test helper constructing a `Daemon` with a `DaemonConfig` rooted at a tmp_path runtime directory. <!--#7f607fbff67cb095-->
- `test_request_add_project_registers_and_persists` (function) — Asserts `request_add_project` returns the resolved path and records it in both the aggregator's in-memory roots and the on-disk registry. <!--#be4a0c8ad0fd5f52-->
- `test_request_add_project_normalizes_worktree_path` (function) — Asserts adding an isolation-worktree path registers the main project root instead. <!--#fb7518ef1f3e2b25-->
- `test_request_add_project_rejects_relative_path` (function) — Asserts a relative path raises `ProjectCommandError` with code `invalid_path`. <!--#b7e47b536a5fcf63-->
- `test_request_add_project_rejects_empty_path` (function) — Asserts a blank/whitespace path raises `ProjectCommandError` with code `invalid_path`. <!--#851253a2a5571441-->

- `test_request_add_project_rejects_missing_path` (function) — Asserts a nonexistent directory raises `ProjectCommandError` with code `not_found`. <!--#8a59d0cbaf52c3bd-->

- `test_request_remove_project_deregisters` (function) — Asserts `request_remove_project` returns the resolved path and clears the root from the registry file, the active roots, and `all_project_roots()`. <!--#1aaa9490dd36bacb-->
- `test_request_remove_project_leaves_project_data_untouched` (function) — Test asserting that `Daemon.request_remove_project` is registry-only—deregistering a project leaves its on-disk data (e.g. `engine.json`) and directory fully intact. <!--#76dc9468717a2815-->
