### `tests/daemon/test_protocol.py` (python) — Unit tests for the daemon/server wire protocol module, pinning PROTOCOL_VERSION at 9 and its capability gates (presence, uploads, spawn plan mode, history window) as monotonically additive, verifying message-type constants are registered in the correct SERVER_TO_DAEMON/DAEMON_TO_SERVER directions, and round-tripping the make_* frame builders (viewers, ping, project_command/result, upload_command/result) through JSON encode/decode while checking field coercion, omission of unset optional fields, size limits, and ProtocolError on invalid values. <!--#073987927fc41897|22bedd9495ff05ac-->
- `test_protocol_version_bumped_to_9` (function) — Pins `protocol.PROTOCOL_VERSION` at "9", documenting that the history step-window channel is the capability the latest bump advertises so peers can degrade immediately instead of timing out. <!--#63d757564ea4b4c5-->
- `test_revision_9_does_not_regress_earlier_gates` (function) — Asserts that a revision-9 peer still passes every earlier capability gate (traffic reduction, presence, uploads, fetch, spawn strategy, spawn plan mode, history window), enforcing that bumps only add capabilities. <!--#dc2eb0ba4faae4bd-->
- `test_supports_spawn_plan_mode_gate` (function) — Checks `supports_spawn_plan_mode` accepts versions ≥ 8 in string/int/whitespace forms and rejects lower, empty, `None`, non-numeric or non-scalar values, with `MIN_SPAWN_PLAN_MODE_PROTOCOL_VERSION == 8`. <!--#25c52fb5b374a2ac-->
- `test_spawn_plan_mode_field_validation` (function) — Verifies `protocol.make_spawn_flow` carries valid `plan_decomposition`/`plan_granularity` values in the payload, omits them entirely when unset for backward compatibility, and raises `ProtocolError` naming the legal set for invalid values. <!--#be0dc01976bdec37-->
- `test_supports_presence_gate` (function) — Checks that supports_presence returns True for version 4 and above (across str/int/whitespace forms) and False for older, empty, non-numeric, or None inputs. <!--#acc3b6cd26f9f09e-->
- `test_viewers_registered_as_server_to_daemon` (function) — Confirms the MSG_VIEWERS message type equals "viewers" and is registered in SERVER_TO_DAEMON and ALL_MESSAGE_TYPES but not DAEMON_TO_SERVER. <!--#587e1482916aacc7-->
- `test_make_viewers_round_trip` (function) — Verifies make_viewers builds a viewers message with the given count and seq that survives a decode/encode JSON round-trip intact. <!--#bfb705eaa4569a6c-->
- `test_make_viewers_zero_count_is_carried` (function) — Ensures a viewers count of 0 (the "last browser closed" edge) is carried on the wire and never dropped as falsy. <!--#1736e2f51730f5bd-->
- `test_make_viewers_coerces_count_to_int` (function) — Checks that make_viewers coerces bool/float count arguments into integers in the payload. <!--#c326d29d53e6e3cd-->
- `test_make_ping_without_viewers_matches_revision_3_payload` (function) — Verifies make_ping with no viewers omits the field entirely, producing a payload byte-identical to the revision-3 PING for backward compatibility. <!--#9f16ee78bd87ca32-->
- `test_make_ping_with_viewers_round_trip` (function) — Verifies make_ping with a viewers argument embeds {"viewers": n} and survives a decode round-trip with type, payload, and seq intact. <!--#c5654c70bae4e976-->
- `test_make_ping_viewers_zero_is_carried` (function) — Ensures a ping viewers level of 0 ("nobody watching", the self-heal path for a lost 1→0 edge) is preserved on the wire. <!--#25fe7e8ad52692b3-->
- `test_make_ping_coerces_viewers_to_int` (function) — Checks that make_ping coerces a float viewers argument into an integer in the payload. <!--#dec60827cfec566e-->
- `test_project_messages_registered_in_correct_directions` (function) — Asserts the project_command/project_result message-type constants have the expected string values and are registered in the right direction tables (SERVER_TO_DAEMON, DAEMON_TO_SERVER, ALL_MESSAGE_TYPES). <!--#4ed59c2a90bbd356-->
- `test_project_management_did_not_bump_protocol_version` (function) — Records that the project-management frame types were purely additive and rode on an existing revision, pinning only the current version and `supports_presence` rather than a version of their own. <!--#05f3eb9bfb5931e1-->
- `test_project_operations_set` (function) — Checks the PROJECT_OP_ADD/PROJECT_OP_REMOVE constants and that PROJECT_OPERATIONS is exactly the frozenset of "add" and "remove". <!--#7c3e1b233bfed35f-->
- `test_make_project_command_round_trip` (function) — Parametrized round-trip test that make_project_command produces a project_command frame whose payload survives JSON encode/decode with operation, project_root and request_id intact. <!--#557a46c8e5e2ef93-->
- `test_make_project_command_omits_empty_request_id` (function) — Verifies make_project_command leaves request_id out of the payload entirely when none is supplied, rather than emitting an empty value. <!--#e3a72a2306a88fc3-->
- `test_make_project_command_rejects_unknown_operation` (function) — Parametrized test that make_project_command raises ProtocolError for operations outside the allowed add/remove set. <!--#6d6b97c0dcaeb827-->
- `test_make_project_result_success_round_trip` (function) — Round-trip test that a successful make_project_result yields a project_result frame carrying request_id, ok=True and project_root through encode/decode. <!--#c5084bfef9be1a41-->
- `test_make_project_result_omits_empty_optional_fields` (function) — Asserts make_project_result omits the error, error_code and project_root keys when unset, so the server can distinguish "absent" from "empty string" by key presence. <!--#be60eee62e21ae34-->
- `test_make_project_result_failure_carries_code_round_trip` (function) — Round-trip test that a failure make_project_result preserves ok=False along with the human-readable error and machine-readable error_code. <!--#78683cb5910aad8f-->
- `test_supports_uploads_gate` (function) — Exercises supports_uploads across string/int/whitespace forms of ">= 5" and confirms it fails closed for older, empty, non-numeric, or non-scalar versions. <!--#f4773ef545dc5f28-->
- `test_upload_messages_registered_in_correct_directions` (function) — Verifies MSG_UPLOAD_COMMAND is server-to-daemon only and MSG_UPLOAD_RESULT daemon-to-server only, and that both surface in the derived ALL_MESSAGE_TYPES union. <!--#c1d4dddb4aefff56-->
- `test_max_upload_bytes_is_20mb_and_fits_a_ws_frame` (function) — Asserts MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES is 20 MiB and that its base64-inflated size still fits under MAX_WS_MESSAGE_BYTES. <!--#6b8053a831e8074c-->
- `test_upload_error_codes_set` (function) — Pins the exact frozenset of declared UPLOAD_ERROR_CODES. <!--#895a612e9e23396a-->
- `test_make_upload_command_round_trip` (function) — Builds an upload command and decodes its JSON to confirm the type and full payload (project_root, filename, content_b64, size, request_id) survive the round trip. <!--#c7b3ecfae4a73308-->
- `test_make_upload_command_omits_empty_request_id` (function) — Confirms an absent request_id is dropped from the upload-command payload rather than sent empty. <!--#3d3ae9c455eec00d-->
- `test_make_upload_command_accepts_empty_file` (function) — Confirms a 0-byte attachment is a legal upload command, since only oversized payloads are rejected. <!--#0fd14ebc5daa46f5-->
- `test_make_upload_command_accepts_exactly_the_limit` (function) — Confirms a declared size of exactly MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES is accepted, fixing the boundary as inclusive. <!--#24d3838e0f6ba0be-->
- `test_make_upload_command_rejects_empty_filename` (function) — Parametrised check that blank or missing filenames raise ProtocolError when building an upload command. <!--#dab4c1d20852e8f0-->
- `test_make_upload_command_rejects_non_absolute_project_root` (function) — Parametrised check that a non-absolute project_root raises ProtocolError when building an upload command. <!--#7f91c2f2774ac446-->
- `test_make_upload_command_rejects_oversized_declared_size` (function) — Confirms a declared size one byte over MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES raises ProtocolError. <!--#143a615ad4306316-->
- `test_make_upload_result_success_round_trip` (function) — Builds a successful upload result and decodes it to confirm request_id, ok, path, size, and deduplicated all survive the JSON round trip. <!--#773b588423d1db21-->
- `test_make_upload_result_success_carries_zero_defaults` (function) — Confirms falsy-but-real values (size 0, deduplicated False) are emitted on the wire rather than dropped, so the server can tell them from "not reported". <!--#9acc13dd5cdd1131-->
- `test_make_upload_result_failure_carries_code_round_trip` (function) — Confirms a failed upload result round-trips exactly request_id, ok=False, error, and error_code. <!--#6cf42b338b1281be-->
- `test_make_upload_result_failure_omits_success_fields` (function) — Confirms a failure result omits path, size, and deduplicated so it cannot be misread as a 0-byte success. <!--#cdc7c019dfa67a2f-->
- `test_make_upload_result_rejects_unknown_error_code` (function) — Parametrised check that an error_code outside UPLOAD_ERROR_CODES raises ProtocolError. <!--#95025f5647f9ce92-->
- `test_make_upload_result_accepts_every_declared_error_code` (function) — Parametrised check that each code in UPLOAD_ERROR_CODES is accepted and preserved in the result payload. <!--#8fbe07f302eac070-->
- `test_supports_fetch_gate` (function) — Exercises `supports_fetch` across int/string/whitespace forms, confirming it accepts >= 6 and fails closed on "5", older values, empty, None, and non-numeric input. <!--#cf076082af29bbc9-->
- `test_supports_fetch_is_bound_to_min_fetch_protocol_version` (function) — Ties `supports_fetch`'s boundary exactly to `protocol.MIN_FETCH_PROTOCOL_VERSION` (6) and checks the current revision satisfies its own floor. <!--#77069a8d382a3395-->
- `test_fetch_messages_registered_in_correct_directions` (function) — Verifies `MSG_FETCH_COMMAND` is server→daemon only, `MSG_FETCH_RESULT` is daemon→server only, and both surface in the derived `ALL_MESSAGE_TYPES` union. <!--#57853c27b3b036c9-->
- `test_fetch_error_codes_set` (function) — Pins `protocol.FETCH_ERROR_CODES` to the exact frozenset of six read-failure codes. <!--#3cfb156fdab27f6f-->
- `test_fetch_error_codes_are_distinct_from_upload_codes` (function) — Checks the fetch and upload error-code sets stay disjoint where they should be, using `not_found` and `invalid_filename` as sentinels. <!--#b68cc28d7a106642-->
- `test_make_fetch_command_round_trip` (function) — Round-trips `make_fetch_command` through `protocol.decode`, asserting the payload carries exactly `project_root`, `path`, and `request_id`. <!--#6c2d714bd5e553cf-->
- `test_make_fetch_command_omits_empty_request_id` (function) — Confirms `make_fetch_command` leaves `request_id` out of the payload when none is supplied. <!--#ad5bfd5fb8623bb4-->
- `test_make_fetch_command_accepts_legacy_se3_layout_path` (function) — Confirms a pre-rename `se3/uploads/...` path passes through unchanged, so the protocol hard-codes neither the se3 nor tianluo layout. <!--#5a322b03a7c96d28-->
- `test_make_fetch_command_rejects_non_absolute_project_root` (function) — Parametrized check that `make_fetch_command` raises `ProtocolError` for non-absolute `project_root` values. <!--#3417a56c01f8dbf2-->
- `test_make_fetch_command_rejects_empty_path` (function) — Parametrized check that `make_fetch_command` raises `ProtocolError` for empty or blank paths. <!--#e52df8c064ac6939-->
- `test_make_fetch_command_rejects_absolute_path` (function) — Parametrized check that absolute paths are rejected, preventing filesystem-layout leaks and arbitrary reads. <!--#5bf5db1391ff3556-->
- `test_make_fetch_command_rejects_traversal_path` (function) — Parametrized check that paths containing `..` segments raise `ProtocolError`. <!--#52fb30d0cacc59bd-->
- `test_make_fetch_command_allows_dotdot_inside_a_filename` (function) — Confirms traversal detection is segment-based, so a filename merely containing `..` (e.g. `ab_v..1.png`) is still accepted. <!--#866494f1ea8864d6-->
- `test_make_fetch_result_success_round_trip` (function) — Round-trips a successful `make_fetch_result`, asserting the decoded payload carries `request_id`, `ok`, `content_b64`, `size`, and `name`. <!--#26b949ad4425ba92-->
- `test_make_fetch_result_success_carries_zero_size` (function) — Confirms a 0-byte result keeps `size: 0` and an empty `content_b64` rather than dropping them as falsy. <!--#f18121d8b2d234f8-->
- `test_make_fetch_result_accepts_exactly_the_limit` (function) — Confirms a declared size of exactly `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` is accepted (inclusive boundary). <!--#c38d40f3d5d3487e-->
- `test_make_fetch_result_rejects_oversized_declared_size` (function) — Confirms a size one byte over `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` raises `ProtocolError`, so fetch shares the upload frame ceiling. <!--#8ef09b7b89e204fe-->
- `test_make_fetch_result_rejects_negative_size` (function) — Confirms a negative declared size raises `ProtocolError`. <!--#2c40f6e45443b60b-->
- `test_make_fetch_result_failure_carries_code_round_trip` (function) — Round-trips a failed `make_fetch_result`, asserting the payload carries `request_id`, `ok: False`, `error`, and `error_code`. <!--#68b63cb8591486d7-->
- `test_make_fetch_result_failure_omits_success_fields` (function) — Confirms a failure payload omits `content_b64`, `size`, and `name` so it cannot be mistaken for a 0-byte success. <!--#57acc0ff41486e49-->
- `test_make_fetch_result_rejects_unknown_error_code` (function) — Parametrized check that `make_fetch_result` raises `ProtocolError` for error codes outside `FETCH_ERROR_CODES`. <!--#6111fa26430b4bd8-->
- `test_make_fetch_result_accepts_every_declared_error_code` (function) — Parametrized check that every code in `FETCH_ERROR_CODES` is accepted and echoed back in the payload. <!--#f65d2418f92d4141-->

### `tests/daemon/test_push_delivery_terminator.py` (python) — Regression tests for daemon history push delivery termination, using a stubbed HistoryProvider/websocket and a shrunken `MAX_RECORDS_PER_REPORT` to verify that reads ending exactly on the chunk bound — including flows that go terminal there — still emit exactly one `final: true` terminator frame so `ServerState` settles the delivery, while under-bound reads settle immediately without extra frames. <!--#2a0b8a1393795456|662f0bb4fbb9d89b-->
- `_append_records` (function) — Test helper that appends JSONL message records to a flow's step file under `<root>/tianluo/history/<flow_id>/<step>`, creating parent directories as needed. <!--#e7f9318b07f7614d-->
- `_msg` (function) — Tiny factory building a minimal history record dict from a role and content string. <!--#bfbb3b9d14c45ada-->
- `_Provider` (class) — Test double implementing the daemon's HistoryProvider interface over a real `DaemonHistoryReader`, with a mutable `live` set so a test can drive a flow terminal and observe final-flush behaviour. <!--#adb59dc65db3186e-->
  - `_Provider.__init__` (method) — Stores the reader, project root, and flow ids, and seeds `live` with all flows as initially ACTIVE. <!--#9abd0aed10b28983-->
  - `_Provider.build_index` (method) — Stub returning an empty index, since these tests exercise history push rather than indexing. <!--#17a111c8d858317e-->
  - `_Provider.read_active_flows` (method) — Reads each flow through the real reader at the given cursor and returns only flows that are still live or still have records, mimicking how terminal flows drop out of the read set. <!--#964852f8b659d1b3-->
  - `_Provider.live_flow_ids` (method) — Returns a copy of the currently live (non-terminal) flow id set. <!--#18598568cd04f790-->
- `_StubWS` (class) — Fake websocket that captures every sent frame as parsed JSON and can filter them down to history-data payloads for one flow. <!--#c1890089e8b17196-->
  - `_StubWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the empty list of captured frames. <!--#a7398c2f87176427-->
  - `_StubWS.send` (method) — Parses the outgoing JSON frame and records it instead of transmitting it. <!--#16c00f1eb4b61e0e-->
  - `_StubWS.history_frames` (method) — Returns the payloads of all captured `MSG_HISTORY_DATA` frames belonging to the given flow id. <!--#7b34268436476d42-->
- `_client` (function) — Builds a `DaemonClient` wired to a stub snapshot provider and the supplied test history provider, pointed at a non-routable URL. <!--#c8485900f2ca9e02-->
- `_apply` (function) — Feeds one wire history frame into `ServerState` exactly as `ws.py` does, applying the frame and then recording the replay verdict with the same `applied` pairing. <!--#7a754969560d4fda-->
- `capped_reads` (function) — Fixture that monkeypatches `MAX_RECORDS_PER_REPORT` down to 2 so a two-record flow ends its read exactly on the chunk bound. <!--#fff9f6ce86ebf17f-->
- `flow_env` (function) — Fixture assembling a temp project root, flow id, step filename, and a `_Provider` over a real `DaemonHistoryReader` for that root. <!--#fe5108936a93155c-->
- `test_eof_on_the_bound_still_declares_the_delivery_finished` (function) — Asserts that for a still-active flow whose chunk landed exactly on the bound, the next empty EOF-confirming read ships a `final: true` terminator frame that settles the server-side delivery exactly once. <!--#6ba42b4c76a9e2e2-->
- `test_a_flow_that_went_terminal_on_the_bound_is_still_closed` (function) — Reproduces the live defect shape: a flow that goes terminal after a bound-aligned chunk gets a synthesized terminator frame so the daemon closes the delivery it opened, and does not repeat it. <!--#95423f1cecca0bac-->
- `test_an_unbounded_read_still_settles_without_a_terminator` (function) — Guards the common path — a read under the bound marks itself `final` and settles immediately, with idle ticks shipping no extra terminator frames. <!--#94f2bdbf15a4910f-->

### `tests/daemon/test_push_history_cursor_commit.py` (python) — Daemon test module covering `_push_history` cursor-commit semantics: using a real `DaemonHistoryReader`-backed provider stub and a websocket stub that can fail HISTORY_DATA sends, it asserts cursors only advance on successful delivery, dropped batches are re-read and re-sent as exact deltas next round, empty deltas still commit, one flow's failure does not roll back another's cursor, and the resulting `ServerState` bundle stays complete and duplicate-free. <!--#71c7baf3c95a208e|f374423835590228-->
- `_append_records` (function) — Test helper that appends the given messages as JSONL lines to the `<root>/tianluo/history/<flow>/<step>` file, creating parent directories as needed. <!--#cb5f1a9791ca9253-->
- `_msg` (function) — Test helper building a minimal `{role, content}` message dict. <!--#bfbb3b9d14c45ada-->
- `_keys` (function) — Test helper extracting the `(step_id, ordinal)` identity tuples the frontend reconciles records by, used to assert no duplicates. <!--#62a330d402d6f088-->
- `_bodies` (function) — Test helper extracting each record's `message.content` string so assertions can compare frames by their message bodies. <!--#7f2face56564f9c2-->
- `_Provider` (class) — A minimal HistoryProvider stub wrapping a real `DaemonHistoryReader` over a fixed flow-id list, implementing only the three methods `_push_history` calls so tests exercise the active-flow read/send path with genuine cursor-based re-reads. <!--#7ae1a71893c7117b-->
  - `_Provider.__init__` (method) — Stores the real reader, the project root, and the fixed set of flow ids the provider serves. <!--#7ee4b07333ef65a1-->
  - `_Provider.build_index` (method) — Returns an empty index so tests exercise the active-flow path alone. <!--#17a111c8d858317e-->
  - `_Provider.read_active_flows` (method) — Reads each configured flow through the real `read_flow`, passing the per-flow cursor so retained water marks actually drive what is re-read. <!--#0390b9bb231c7169-->
  - `_Provider.live_flow_ids` (method) — Reports the fixed flow ids as the currently live flows. <!--#1ae3dea316cf1bf6-->
- `_StubWS` (class) — A websocket stub that records every sent frame and raises `ConnectionError` on `MSG_HISTORY_DATA` frames for flows listed in `fail_flows`, simulating a socket that dies mid-push. <!--#5e95dee39e9dbe6a-->
  - `_StubWS.__init__` (method) — Initialises the empty `fail_flows` set and the recorded-frames list. <!--#e8ef1ceeb2f5e2f5-->
  - `_StubWS.send` (method) — Parses the outgoing frame, raises `ConnectionError` if it is a HISTORY_DATA frame for a failing flow, and otherwise records it as delivered. <!--#537996454563aa28-->
  - `_StubWS.history_frames` (method) — Returns the payloads of all recorded HISTORY_DATA frames, optionally filtered to one flow id. <!--#057dede3883a820a-->
- `_client` (function) — Test helper constructing a `DaemonClient` wired to the given history provider and a trivial snapshot provider. <!--#3d5c1809b21d73a1-->
- `flow_env` (function) — Pytest fixture yielding a temporary project root plus flow id, step filename, and a `_Provider` over a real reader for a single discovery flow. <!--#215fb61724315b5b-->
- `test_failed_send_does_not_advance_cursor` (function) — Asserts that when the HISTORY_DATA send raises, no frame is delivered and the flow's cursor is not recorded, so the batch is not silently lost. <!--#6b5999180db386dd-->
- `test_failed_batch_is_re_read_and_re_sent_next_round` (function) — Asserts that after a failed send the same records are re-read from the retained water mark and shipped on the next round as the flow's first full frame. <!--#642028348dae1254-->
- `test_mid_flow_send_failure_re_sends_only_the_dropped_delta` (function) — Asserts that a send failure on a later append re-ships exactly that append delta on the next round rather than the whole flow. <!--#c90cac8e8aae5829-->
- `test_empty_delta_commits_and_send_is_skipped` (function) — Asserts that a flow with no new records sends no frame yet still keeps (commits) its cursor, since there is no delivery that could fail. <!--#52c065985165b9d6-->
- `test_successful_flow_cursor_survives_another_flows_failure` (function) — Asserts that a flow already shipped in the same round keeps its cursor when a later flow's send fails, avoiding needless duplicate traffic. <!--#d0a08c4b4344226c-->
- `test_server_bundle_is_complete_and_duplicate_free_after_a_drop` (function) — Test asserting that after a mid-flight socket send failure, `_push_history`'s retained water mark re-sends dropped records so the replayed `ServerState` bundle contains every record exactly once, in order, with the correct final cursor. <!--#c72ad3b48e8dcd03-->

### `tests/daemon/test_record_budget.py` (python) — Unit tests for the standalone `record_budget` module, building a synthetic replica of the pathological 23.6 MB history record and asserting that its byte thresholds, telemetry folding, watermark solving, per-event shrinking, and full-record compaction stay within budget while preserving tool chips, tail events, usage fields, and import-free standalone-ness. <!--#c2056c4567fb55ff|22bb240ab13fbf7b-->
- `_thinking_event` (function) — Test helper building a synthetic `system`/`thinking_tokens` telemetry event with the given index baked into its token counts and uuid. <!--#2aed34af7312a00b-->
- `_tool_use_event` (function) — Test helper building an assistant event carrying a `thinking` block plus a `tool_use` block with a deterministic `toolu_%04d` id. <!--#456d6211c0bf43ef-->
- `_tool_result_event` (function) — Test helper building a user event carrying a single `tool_result` block matching the `toolu_%04d` id of the same index. <!--#e3457a54a0b4ed22-->
- `_result_event` (function) — Test helper returning a terminal `result` event with realistic cost and usage token fields. <!--#c6dfcc841661ad3e-->
- `_build_record` (function) — Test fixture builder that assembles a history record shaped like the pathological 23.6 MB discovery record — interleaved telemetry, tool chips, one oversized body, and terminal events at the tail. <!--#776e08bf8f322844-->
- `_chips` (function) — Test helper extracting the ordered `(kind, id)` list of every `tool_use`/`tool_result` block in a record, used to assert chip preservation. <!--#8704546549ebfbeb-->
- `test_thresholds_match_the_measured_distribution` (function) — Asserts the module's fast-path, per-event, and per-record byte constants hold their measured values. <!--#824e9fdcec61e5d0-->
- `test_needs_compaction_boundary` (function) — Parametrised check that `needs_compaction` flips exactly at the record-size boundary. <!--#c8373ffbc030d7d0-->
- `test_module_has_no_daemon_internal_imports` (function) — Guards the module's standalone-ness by asserting its source contains no relative or `tianluo` imports, so offline scripts can import it without the daemon. <!--#a94a573cc99499fc-->
- `_ExplodingList` (class) — A `list` subclass used as a `raw_json` stand-in that raises on any access, proving the fast path never traverses events. <!--#118c2f251e36a34e-->
  - `_ExplodingList.__iter__` (method) — Raises `AssertionError` if the fast path iterates `raw_json`. <!--#b58d8f926d4d03e2-->
  - `_ExplodingList.__len__` (method) — Raises `AssertionError` if the fast path measures `raw_json`. <!--#4a90c803d8ee3b35-->
  - `_ExplodingList.__getitem__` (method) — Raises `AssertionError` if the fast path indexes into `raw_json`. <!--#261bc63bc80f8c4a-->
- `test_fast_path_returns_the_same_object_without_traversing_raw_json` (function) — Verifies a sub-threshold record is returned identically, uncompacted, and without touching its events. <!--#1134b91525109a13-->
- `test_fold_collapses_measured_thinking_token_volume_to_thousands` (function) — Checks `fold_telemetry_events` collapses ~46k thinking events into fewer than 2000 entries with one marker per run and exact counts preserved. <!--#0edca1d34d0535a9-->
- `test_fold_leaves_assistant_user_and_result_events_untouched` (function) — Asserts folding replaces only telemetry runs, leaving assistant/user/result events as the very same objects in order. <!--#9191aec6432bd673-->
- `test_fold_never_touches_types_outside_the_whitelist` (function) — Asserts non-whitelisted event kinds (init, rate limit, task, stream) pass through folding identity-unchanged. <!--#4b46735fee87f131-->
- `test_fold_of_a_pure_telemetry_record_keeps_one_marker` (function) — Checks an all-telemetry event list folds down to a single marker carrying the full count. <!--#402737135972c7f1-->
- `_bare_thinking_event` (function) — Test helper producing a minimal telemetry event deliberately smaller than the fold marker that would replace it. <!--#0d21f6a18f741ee4-->
- `test_fold_leaves_a_run_alone_when_the_marker_would_be_bigger` (function) — Verifies a one-event telemetry run is left alone when folding it would grow the record. <!--#ab12b4d858036a68-->
- `test_fold_is_never_a_net_size_loss_when_telemetry_is_interleaved` (function) — Asserts folding interleaved single-event telemetry never increases total size or event count. <!--#7c50aa268b3772df-->
- `test_solve_watermark_returns_cap_when_everything_fits` (function) — Checks `solve_watermark` returns the per-event cap when the budget is not binding. <!--#f00357206775033e-->
- `test_solve_watermark_is_the_largest_feasible_level` (function) — Verifies the returned watermark is maximal — feasible at the level, infeasible one byte higher. <!--#cf300b99d3899f69-->
- `test_solve_watermark_never_exceeds_the_per_event_cap` (function) — Asserts the solved level is clamped to `MAX_EVENT_BYTES` even with an enormous budget. <!--#0f823bc3c3bb6bbc-->
- `test_solve_watermark_degenerate_inputs` (function) — Covers empty, zero, negative, and below-structural-floor budgets, where the level collapses to the cap or to 0 and overflow reporting is the caller's job. <!--#9f247293802ece11-->
- `test_shrink_event_returns_the_same_object_when_under_limit` (function) — Checks `shrink_event` is a no-op returning the identical object for events already within the limit. <!--#5e8bcae64b895be5-->
- `test_shrink_event_brings_an_oversized_event_within_the_cap` (function) — Verifies an oversized `tool_result` is trimmed under the cap, its structural fields and id survive, the truncation flag is set, and the input is not mutated. <!--#4f7b4f0b0b2e0e8f-->
- `test_truncation_marker_is_machine_recognisable` (function) — Asserts the injected truncation marker matches `TRUNCATION_MARKER_PATTERN` with a positive byte count while the body prefix is retained. <!--#d4d0f772b3a4c592-->
- `test_shrink_event_does_not_nest_markers_across_passes` (function) — Checks re-shrinking an already-truncated event yields exactly one truncation marker and still meets the tighter limit. <!--#e15d63c05cee797c-->
- `test_shrink_event_reports_nothing_when_only_structural_noise_remains` (function) — Verifies an event with no trimmable payload is returned unchanged with zero dropped bytes rather than being mangled. <!--#d2b6de1f6fe20a61-->
- `test_compact_record_preserves_every_tool_chip_count_and_order` (function) — Asserts compaction of the pathological record keeps every `tool_use`/`tool_result` chip in the same order. <!--#f256ed46dfc3404b-->
- `test_compact_record_never_drops_tail_events` (function) — Verifies the terminal `result` event and the final `tool_result` — the first casualties of naive truncation — survive compaction. <!--#c8ed6a1c0ae117c7-->
- `test_compact_record_meets_the_raw_json_budget` (function) — Checks the compacted `raw_json` actually serialises under `MAX_RECORD_RAW_JSON_BYTES` with no overflow and a real size reduction. <!--#df396aaf9c42f8d2-->
- `test_compact_record_caps_every_event_at_the_per_event_ceiling` (function) — Asserts every non-immune event in the compacted record is at or under the per-event byte ceiling. <!--#48d777c8701d3c76-->
- `test_compact_record_leaves_usage_fields_byte_identical` (function) — Verifies compaction passes through `usage_records`, `token_usage`, content, step type, and timestamp untouched. <!--#6970856e556db3cd-->
- `test_compact_record_leaves_the_result_event_untouched` (function) — Asserts the trailing `result` event is the same object after compaction with its usage numbers intact. <!--#629211949a689157-->
- `test_compact_record_does_not_mutate_the_input_record` (function) — Checks compaction leaves the caller's original record and its event list unmodified. <!--#d4f3bdfa43cd2b1d-->
- `test_sub_budget_record_is_not_folded_but_oversized_event_is_capped` (function) — Covers the 64 KB–1 MB band where only the per-event cap applies and telemetry events are left unfolded. <!--#a57f6465972ccf79-->
- `test_compact_record_returns_input_when_nothing_needs_shrinking` (function) — Verifies a record above the fast path but needing no trimming is returned as-is with `compacted` false. <!--#cafa1c9fe1f4d18d-->
- `test_compact_record_reports_overflow_instead_of_dropping_events` (function) — Asserts that when the structural floor exceeds the budget, every event is kept and `overflow` is flagged rather than events being dropped. <!--#e998801cc5fc313e-->
- `test_compact_record_never_ships_a_bigger_record_than_it_was_given` (function) — Guards against growth: interleaved one-event telemetry yields the original record back, uncompacted but still honestly reported as over budget. <!--#34e6501dd84c947e-->
- `test_compact_record_discards_a_pass_that_did_not_shrink_anything` (function) — Backstop test monkeypatching `shrink_event` to inflate events, asserting the resulting pass is discarded and the original record returned. <!--#dd6d99cdd1755d60-->
- `test_compact_record_handles_records_without_raw_json` (function) — Checks records lacking `raw_json` are returned unchanged instead of erroring. <!--#1a1b2f4d70789fbd-->
- `test_compacted_record_round_trips_through_json` (function) — Verifies a compacted record survives a JSON dump/load round trip with its tool chips identical. <!--#d5302c08309ba66c-->

### `tests/daemon/test_resume_cross_machine.py` (python) — Test suite for the cross-machine resume guard, covering how `run.pid` markers (foreign / local / legacy / unstamped, in both the main root and worktree state dirs) block or permit resumes across the daemon's `request_resume`, the CLI's `resume_run` / `_cross_machine_resume_block` preflight, and the server's `POST /api/flows/{id}/resume` 409 response, including the attribution wording that distinguishes a co-tenant flow from the flow's own marker. <!--#b2d917e263c3d4f9|06f7070e5f2b2851-->
- `_state_dir` (function) — Helper returning the `tianluo/state` directory under a given project root. <!--#9f86e3797e795c3d-->
- `_write_engine` (function) — Helper writing a minimal `engine.json` (flow id, status, mid-flow step state, plus arbitrary extra keys) into a root's state dir. <!--#6fa97fb8d07d845b-->
- `_make_worktree_flow` (function) — Helper creating a `--worktree` flow whose `engine.json` lives only in `<main>/tianluo/worktrees/wt-1`, mirroring what `run_worktree_mode` leaves on disk. <!--#4adf51fd0098cc5b-->
- `_write_run_pid` (function) — Helper writing a `run.pid` marker in either the machine-id-stamped format (optionally with a flow id) or the legacy bare-pid single line. <!--#560fb16f26f327a3-->
- `fake_se3` (function) — Fixture that patches `_resolve_se3_command` to a throwaway script emitting a single `flow_completed` NDJSON event, so spawned resumes finish instantly. <!--#55a95da3ecafad8e-->
- `test_request_resume_rejects_foreign_active_holder` (function) — Asserts `daemon.request_resume` raises naming the foreign machine and spawns nothing when a non-COMPLETED flow's `run.pid` is held by another host. <!--#e211dca1b452743a-->
- `test_request_resume_foreign_holder_paused_flow_rejected` (function) — Asserts an otherwise-resumable PAUSED flow is still refused while a foreign machine holds its marker. <!--#6485602b1f18c960-->
- `test_request_resume_legacy_marker_resumes_via_local_path` (function) — Asserts a legacy single-line `run.pid` without a machine id is treated as local and the normal `--resume` spawn proceeds. <!--#0e0b2dd7821ebde3-->
- `test_request_resume_local_machine_marker_resumes` (function) — Asserts a marker stamped with this host's `stable_machine_id()` is local, leaving the existing resume path intact. <!--#8227fee44d1c437d-->
- `test_request_resume_no_marker_resumes` (function) — Asserts a flow with no `run.pid` at all resumes normally, since there is no foreign holder to block it. <!--#501c138dccf22756-->
- `test_cli_resume_run_refuses_foreign_holder` (function) — Asserts the CLI `resume_run` returns exit code 1 instead of calling into `run_flow` when the marker is foreign. <!--#29295b313764e6de-->
- `test_cli_cross_machine_block_truth_table` (function) — Exercises `_cross_machine_resume_block` across foreign / legacy / local markers and a COMPLETED flow, asserting only the foreign non-COMPLETED case blocks. <!--#5bd6f915340a83dd-->
- `test_cross_machine_block_reads_worktree_marker` (function) — Asserts the CLI guard looks inside the worktree state dir, so a foreign worktree marker blocks a resume requested from the main root. <!--#c6e2c21bcee75ecf-->
- `test_cli_resume_run_refuses_foreign_worktree_holder` (function) — Asserts `resume_run` never enters `_resume_worktree_run` for a foreign worktree holder and leaves the remote machine's marker byte-identical. <!--#46fd37ec82b674c5-->
- `test_worktree_local_and_legacy_markers_do_not_block` (function) — Asserts local and legacy worktree markers keep the existing same-machine resume path unblocked. <!--#dfbeb9493c161f6d-->
- `test_completed_worktree_flow_skips_the_guard` (function) — Asserts a COMPLETED worktree flow's leftover foreign marker does not wedge resume. <!--#7e190a75cddaf263-->
- `test_foreign_main_root_marker_does_not_block_worktree_flow` (function) — Parametrized over the worktree marker's flavour, asserts a foreign main-root marker for an unrelated flow never blocks a worktree flow. <!--#58e7b326de401db0-->
- `test_foreign_main_root_marker_still_blocks_a_main_root_flow` (function) — Asserts the main root's foreign marker still blocks a genuine main-root flow even when unrelated worktrees exist. <!--#17a1c4b1a7c8d0da-->
- `test_daemon_foreign_main_root_marker_does_not_block_worktree_flow` (function) — Asserts `request_resume` judges a worktree flow by its own worktree marker, resuming despite a foreign main-root marker for another flow. <!--#d40d2c1e6e8eab1e-->
- `test_daemon_request_resume_reads_worktree_marker` (function) — Asserts the daemon guard consults the worktree `run.pid` and refuses when it is foreign, even though the flow was located via the main root's `engine.json`. <!--#1207bb852efd8a57-->
- `test_daemon_request_resume_worktree_root_still_resumes_locally` (function) — Asserts a locally-stamped worktree marker leaves the daemon's normal resume spawn untouched. <!--#6c5109e8fd7797a6-->
- `test_daemon_refusal_names_the_co_tenant_flow_not_the_requested_one` (function) — Asserts the refusal message names the co-tenant flow actually running remotely and omits `end-session`, rather than blaming the requested flow. <!--#dcfa89eea94f91fc-->
- `test_daemon_refusal_blames_the_flow_when_the_marker_is_its_own` (function) — Asserts a marker stamped with the requested flow yields the flow-specific wording plus the `end-session` recovery hint. <!--#f6799743c4dde287-->
- `test_daemon_unstamped_root_marker_is_not_attributed_to_the_flow` (function) — Asserts a foreign main-root marker carrying no flow id refuses without attributing the run to the requested flow or suggesting `end-session`. <!--#8804631965ce33f5-->
- `test_daemon_unstamped_worktree_marker_still_belongs_to_the_flow` (function) — Asserts an unstamped foreign worktree marker is attributed to the requested flow, since a worktree state dir is resolved by flow id. <!--#2c5e0998ea3994e7-->
- `test_cli_block_message_for_a_co_tenant_marker` (function) — Asserts the CLI preflight message mirrors the daemon's attribution rules for co-tenant vs own-flow markers, locale-independently via the `end-session` token. <!--#68f97b4bac811f55-->
- `test_cli_worktree_unstamped_marker_is_the_flows_own` (function) — Asserts the CLI guard treats an unstamped foreign worktree marker as the flow's own and includes the `end-session` hint. <!--#55eb646a280c172e-->
- `_server_flow_payload` (function) — Helper returning a status-update payload for a RUNNING, non-resumable flow held live by the reporting node. <!--#c55ab4d24ebd0f3f-->
- `test_server_resume_409_names_holding_machine` (function) — Drives a daemon WebSocket session against the FastAPI app and asserts `POST /api/flows/{id}/resume` returns 409 with the holder in both `detail` and the machine-readable `holder_machine` field. <!--#f4a539fcd0c3c2de-->
- `test_server_resume_409_names_no_machine_when_several_report_the_flow` (function) — Asserts that when two daemons on a shared filesystem report the same flow the 409 stays machine-agnostic — no `holder_machine`, no hostname in `detail`, only `reason: still_running`. <!--#db42b8f12cd9949d-->

### `tests/daemon/test_uploads.py` (python) — Unit tests for the daemon upload subsystem, covering `uploads_dir` resolution across canonical `tianluo` and legacy `se3` layouts, `store_upload` semantics (relative POSIX paths, hash-prefixed names, content dedup, size limits, empty files, lazy directory creation, atomic/unique temp writes), `sanitize_upload_filename` hardening (path stripping, control-character scrubbing, byte-accurate truncation within `NAME_MAX`, fallback names, traversal containment), plus end-to-end `UPLOAD_COMMAND` dispatch through a fake WebSocket asserting `MSG_UPLOAD_RESULT` acks. <!--#cd4aaa64635a2ee7|e6273cd22d42c622-->
- `_project` (function) — Test helper that creates a temporary project root containing a runtime directory (default `tianluo`, or `se3` for legacy-layout cases). <!--#780f804acd33c873-->
- `_stored_files` (function) — Test helper returning the sorted names of files currently present in a project's `<runtime>/uploads` directory, or an empty list if it does not exist. <!--#e9d18e57d13d9a28-->
- `test_uploads_dir_uses_canonical_runtime_dir` (function) — Asserts `uploads.uploads_dir` resolves to `<root>/tianluo/uploads` for a canonical-runtime project. <!--#938ecf13b42bc21a-->
- `test_uploads_dir_follows_legacy_se3_layout` (function) — Asserts `uploads.uploads_dir` resolves under the legacy `se3` runtime directory when that is the project's layout. <!--#f94d5a7ce859078c-->
- `test_store_upload_lands_under_legacy_se3_layout` (function) — Checks that `store_upload` writes into `se3/uploads/` and returns a matching relative path for legacy-layout projects. <!--#b100991d9364f526-->
- `test_store_upload_returns_relative_posix_path_and_writes_content` (function) — Verifies a successful `store_upload` returns a POSIX-style relative path plus size/dedup metadata and writes the exact bytes to disk. <!--#b9aed3b619aca765-->
- `test_store_upload_name_is_hash_prefix_plus_original_name` (function) — Checks the stored filename format is a hex hash prefix of `HASH_PREFIX_LEN` followed by `_` and the original name. <!--#397b56dc7e969635-->
- `test_store_upload_same_content_twice_is_deduplicated` (function) — Verifies re-uploading identical content reuses the same path, flags `deduplicated`, and leaves only one file on disk. <!--#8216f1fbbf999062-->
- `test_store_upload_same_name_different_content_keeps_both` (function) — Verifies two uploads sharing a filename but differing in content are stored side by side under distinct paths. <!--#3b57107fdc810e11-->
- `test_store_upload_rejects_oversized_content_without_writing` (function) — Checks that content above `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` raises `UPLOAD_ERR_TOO_LARGE` before the uploads directory is even created. <!--#61ef2c5039c85f52-->
- `test_store_upload_accepts_content_exactly_at_the_limit` (function) — Boundary test confirming content of exactly `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` is accepted and stored. <!--#bdb7aa402d48b73a-->
- `test_store_upload_handles_empty_file` (function) — Checks a zero-byte upload is stored successfully with size 0. <!--#b869d2635e334863-->
- `test_store_upload_creates_uploads_dir_when_missing` (function) — Verifies the first upload lazily creates the `<runtime>/uploads` directory. <!--#080c3f1cdf42da7b-->
- `test_store_upload_leaves_no_partial_temp_file_behind` (function) — Asserts the atomic write leaves only the final file, with no `.part` or dot-prefixed temp remnants. <!--#08ed08fbeee3ccfb-->
- `test_store_upload_temp_path_is_unique_per_call` (function) — Spies on `os.replace` to prove two writes of the same name/content use distinct temp paths, so concurrent writers cannot clobber each other. <!--#f3fe4d32765a8fb2-->
- `test_store_upload_accepts_a_max_length_multibyte_name` (function) — Checks a multibyte name that exactly fills `MAX_NAME_BYTES` is stored verbatim, meaning the temp component also fits the byte budget. <!--#04893c5a83d0bc16-->
- `test_store_upload_stores_a_long_cjk_name` (function) — Regression test that a long CJK filename is byte-truncated within `NAME_MAX`, keeps its extension, and stores without an ENAMETOOLONG failure. <!--#583dceefc6748dc3-->
- `test_sanitize_strips_every_directory_component` (function) — Parametrized test that `sanitize_upload_filename` removes all path separators and never yields `.` or `..`. <!--#ea2646ea4bcb4846-->
- `test_sanitize_replaces_nul_and_control_characters` (function) — Checks NUL and other control characters are scrubbed from filenames while the extension survives. <!--#075b9514deab93af-->
- `test_sanitize_replaces_whitespace` (function) — Checks spaces are replaced in sanitized filenames. <!--#c19f2981c431d1aa-->
- `test_sanitize_drops_leading_dots_and_dashes` (function) — Checks sanitization strips leading dots and dashes so names cannot become hidden files or look like CLI flags. <!--#8be5bb2c1166bd63-->
- `test_sanitize_falls_back_for_names_that_vanish` (function) — Parametrized test that names sanitizing down to nothing yield `uploads.FALLBACK_NAME`. <!--#f6bdc35b745b3673-->
- `test_sanitize_truncates_long_names_keeping_the_extension` (function) — Checks an over-long ASCII name is truncated within `MAX_NAME_BYTES` while retaining its extension. <!--#0c80701db5088fc5-->
- `test_sanitize_truncates_extensionless_names` (function) — Checks an extensionless over-long name is truncated to exactly `MAX_NAME_BYTES`. <!--#33daac7a5ca9f46c-->
- `test_sanitize_caps_on_encoded_bytes_not_characters` (function) — Parametrized test that the name cap is measured in UTF-8 bytes and never cuts through a multibyte sequence. <!--#c7251ca1dedec487-->
- `test_sanitize_keeps_the_whole_target_component_within_name_max` (function) — Checks the sanitized name leaves room for the `<12 hex>_` prefix so the full on-disk component stays within 255 bytes. <!--#946df0c423513df0-->
- `test_sanitize_preserves_unicode_names` (function) — Checks ordinary Unicode filenames pass through sanitization unchanged. <!--#18682e5f59bdcb11-->
- `test_store_upload_traversal_attempts_stay_inside_uploads_dir` (function) — Parametrized test that path-traversal filenames still land inside the uploads directory and yield a contained relative path. <!--#98c1438841771dcc-->
- `test_store_upload_refuses_a_name_escaping_containment` (function) — Monkeypatches sanitization to return an escaping name and asserts the independent containment check raises `UPLOAD_ERR_INVALID_FILENAME` with nothing written. <!--#ec305f076c628a1f-->
- `_FakeWS` (class) — Minimal WebSocket stand-in that decodes and records every message the daemon client sends. <!--#4bcd88a41b8c0413-->
  - `_FakeWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the fake WebSocket's list of captured messages. <!--#b8b92aad379d234c-->
  - `_FakeWS.send` (method) — Async `send` that decodes the outgoing payload via `protocol.decode` and appends it to the captured list. <!--#7d44362527b3e749-->
- `_make_client` (function) — Test helper constructing a `DaemonClient` with stub identity fields and a snapshot provider reporting the given project root. <!--#94d7117bfeb07f69-->
- `_run_upload` (function) — Test helper that dispatches one `UPLOAD_COMMAND` through the client's real `_dispatch` path inside `asyncio.run`. <!--#dbcdd17a502a51af-->
- `_acks` (function) — Test helper filtering a fake WebSocket's captured messages down to `MSG_UPLOAD_RESULT` acks. <!--#c597942df8fd67a1-->
- `_upload_kwargs` (function) — Test helper building the base64-encoded payload kwargs for `make_upload_command`. <!--#476f57d0ecc05f5c-->
- `test_upload_command_stores_file_and_acks_with_path` (function) — End-to-end dispatch test that an upload command stores the bytes and acks with request id, path, size, and dedup flag. <!--#cc9f723b88252a44-->
- `test_upload_command_reports_deduplication_on_the_second_attempt` (function) — Checks two identical upload commands ack with `deduplicated` false then true, sharing one path. <!--#ce474548e04d8f03-->
- `test_upload_command_rejects_undecodable_base64` (function) — Checks a malformed `content_b64` is rejected with `UPLOAD_ERR_INVALID_PAYLOAD` without invoking the upload handler. <!--#163c7d1614173b22-->
- `test_upload_command_rejects_oversized_decoded_content` (function) — Checks the size limit is enforced on decoded length rather than the declared `size`, rejecting an under-declared oversized payload. <!--#9132976f8ca19e90-->
- `test_upload_command_rejects_relative_project_root` (function) — Checks a non-absolute `project_root` is rejected with `UPLOAD_ERR_INVALID_PATH`. <!--#3bb4f5363402feb3-->
- `test_upload_command_rejects_unregistered_project_root` (function) — Security test that an upload targeting a root outside the registered set is refused with `UPLOAD_ERR_NOT_REGISTERED` and writes nothing. <!--#0d03528689dc1889-->
- `test_upload_command_accepts_a_worktree_root_of_a_registered_project` (function) — Checks a worktree sandbox of a registered project is accepted, with bytes landing in the worktree rather than the main root. <!--#28456f9f202d94a1-->
- `test_upload_command_rejects_a_worktree_of_an_unregistered_project` (function) — Checks the worktree allowance does not extend to worktrees of unregistered projects, which are still refused as not registered. <!--#0911b91ccb85f960-->
- `test_upload_command_without_handler_replies_unsupported` (function) — Checks a client with no wired upload handler fails fast with `UPLOAD_ERR_UNSUPPORTED` instead of leaving the caller hanging. <!--#02e9bc43ff02c3ac-->
- `test_upload_command_rejects_empty_filename` (function) — Checks a whitespace-only filename is rejected with `UPLOAD_ERR_INVALID_FILENAME` before reaching the handler. <!--#9c7cb4bfeee64f60-->
- `test_upload_command_relays_upload_error_code` (function) — Checks an `UploadError` raised by the handler is relayed to the ack with its original error code and message. <!--#f770e4d846e6f714-->
- `test_upload_command_maps_unknown_failure_to_write_failed` (function) — Checks an unexpected handler exception is mapped to `UPLOAD_ERR_WRITE_FAILED` rather than an invalid code. <!--#cc13e2be9fcb33da-->
- `test_upload_command_without_request_id_sends_nothing` (function) — Checks a missing `request_id` suppresses the ack while the file is still stored. <!--#9c1db3b155772376-->
- `test_upload_command_does_not_trigger_fast_push` (function) — Checks handling an upload does not trigger a fast status push, since no snapshot state changes. <!--#9eb830e624afa31d-->
- `test_upload_command_runs_the_handler_off_the_event_loop` (function) — Records the handler's thread name to prove blocking disk I/O runs off the asyncio event loop thread. <!--#de85a089bdf83d65-->
- `test_daemon_wires_an_upload_handler_into_its_client` (function) — Integration test that a real `Daemon` actually wires a working `_upload_handler` into its client. <!--#7812abf9893deba4-->
- `test_upload_command_uses_cached_roots_without_resnapshotting` (function) — Checks the upload hot path reads cached project roots, invoking the snapshot provider only once across two uploads. <!--#ade66cd71059fe86-->
- `test_read_upload_returns_the_stored_bytes` (function) — Asserts `read_upload` round-trips a file written by `store_upload`, returning its exact bytes, size, and hash-prefixed file name. <!--#f75354b21784a6ca-->
- `test_read_upload_accepts_a_str_project_root` (function) — Checks `read_upload` accepts a plain string project root, not just a `Path`. <!--#29e3f479b5f04fbc-->
- `test_read_upload_handles_an_empty_file` (function) — Asserts a zero-byte upload reads back as empty data with size 0 rather than being treated as missing. <!--#74dcf6282b76f0bd-->
- `test_read_upload_follows_the_legacy_se3_layout` (function) — Verifies uploads stored under the legacy `se3/uploads/` runtime directory are still written there and read back correctly. <!--#70a9e39bc75c21f4-->
- `test_read_upload_rejects_an_empty_path` (function) — Parametrized test that blank or whitespace-only relative paths raise `UploadError` with `FETCH_ERR_INVALID_PATH`. <!--#0852a31f30944cf3-->
- `test_read_upload_refuses_paths_outside_the_uploads_dir` (function) — Parametrized containment test that paths escaping the uploads directory (traversal or sibling runtime dirs) are rejected as invalid. <!--#5876327f7e56e8bb-->
- `test_read_upload_refuses_an_absolute_path` (function) — Parametrized test that absolute paths are rejected with `FETCH_ERR_INVALID_PATH`. <!--#3792a88170d48c5c-->
- `test_read_upload_refuses_a_symlink_escaping_the_uploads_dir` (function) — Asserts a symlink planted inside uploads pointing outside is refused as invalid, and the link is left in place rather than deleted. <!--#5e7d83102d07683c-->
- `test_read_upload_reports_a_missing_file_as_not_found` (function) — Asserts a nonexistent file inside uploads yields `FETCH_ERR_NOT_FOUND`. <!--#fb84a136551e59c8-->
- `test_read_upload_reports_a_directory_as_not_found` (function) — Asserts pointing at a directory inside uploads yields `FETCH_ERR_NOT_FOUND` rather than a read error. <!--#cc86ba2a8b87664e-->
- `test_read_upload_refuses_an_oversized_file_before_reading_it` (function) — Uses a sparse file and a monkeypatched `Path.read_bytes` to prove the `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` limit is decided from `stat` with no bytes ever read. <!--#9db230d339824e82-->
- `test_read_upload_accepts_a_file_exactly_at_the_limit` (function) — Boundary test that a file of exactly `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` is accepted rather than rejected. <!--#ed20c017f531fdba-->
- `test_read_upload_reports_an_unreadable_file_as_read_failed` (function) — Chmods an upload to 0o000 (skipping when running as root) and asserts the failure surfaces as `FETCH_ERR_READ_FAILED`. <!--#a12a0411a8ad6a35-->
- `test_read_upload_error_codes_are_all_protocol_members` (function) — Guards the wire contract by asserting every error code `read_upload` can raise belongs to `protocol.FETCH_ERROR_CODES`. <!--#33713f1dcc78f2d4-->
- `_run_fetch` (function) — Test helper that dispatches one `FETCH_COMMAND` through the client's real `_dispatch` path under `asyncio.run`. <!--#272b99a5f1888149-->
- `_fetch_acks` (function) — Test helper that filters a fake websocket's sent messages down to `MSG_FETCH_RESULT` frames. <!--#1732a400868c9b7d-->
- `test_fetch_command_returns_the_stored_bytes` (function) — End-to-end dispatch test that a valid fetch command replies with one ack carrying the correlated request id, base64 content, size, and name. <!--#bc627fc211deea16-->
- `test_fetch_command_rejects_a_traversal_path` (function) — Asserts `make_fetch_command` itself raises `ProtocolError` on an obvious traversal path before anything reaches the wire. <!--#461c7882a2e4fd33-->
- `test_fetch_command_rejects_a_traversal_surviving_the_frame_validator` (function) — Hand-builds a hostile message bypassing the constructor and asserts the client still answers `FETCH_ERR_INVALID_PATH`. <!--#587a9da422c13129-->
- `test_fetch_command_rejects_an_empty_path` (function) — Asserts a whitespace-only path is rejected as invalid without ever invoking the fetch handler. <!--#ae297b6a98d3416e-->
- `test_fetch_command_rejects_relative_project_root` (function) — Asserts a non-absolute `project_root` is rejected as invalid without invoking the fetch handler. <!--#b9207a6beece45ef-->
- `test_fetch_command_rejects_unregistered_project_root` (function) — Security gate test that a fetch for an unregistered project root returns `FETCH_ERR_NOT_REGISTERED` and no content field. <!--#5d35876f63eefbb3-->
- `test_fetch_command_accepts_a_worktree_root_of_a_registered_project` (function) — Asserts attachments stored under a registered project's worktree root are readable through the fetch command. <!--#a5b60607a64ea2ce-->
- `test_fetch_command_rejects_a_worktree_of_an_unregistered_project` (function) — Asserts the worktree allowance does not leak: a worktree under an unregistered project is still `FETCH_ERR_NOT_REGISTERED`. <!--#df0ab822facbddbd-->
- `test_fetch_command_without_handler_replies_unsupported` (function) — Asserts a client with no fetch handler answers immediately with `FETCH_ERR_UNSUPPORTED` instead of leaving the server to time out. <!--#aade111e039d45cf-->
- `test_fetch_command_relays_a_missing_file_as_not_found` (function) — Asserts the handler's not-found error is relayed to the ack as `FETCH_ERR_NOT_FOUND`. <!--#5ca9c156b3269278-->
- `test_fetch_command_maps_unknown_failure_to_read_failed` (function) — Asserts an unexpected handler exception is normalized to `FETCH_ERR_READ_FAILED` so the ack stays protocol-valid. <!--#52690e153712ba2d-->
- `test_fetch_command_without_request_id_sends_nothing` (function) — Asserts a fetch command lacking a `request_id` produces no reply, since there is nothing to correlate it to. <!--#2013b30a886c2837-->
- `test_fetch_command_does_not_trigger_fast_push` (function) — Asserts serving a fetch leaves snapshot state alone and never calls `_trigger_fast_push`. <!--#fa192d418166258b-->
- `test_fetch_command_runs_the_handler_off_the_event_loop` (function) — Records the handler's thread name to prove blocking disk I/O runs off the event loop thread serving status pushes. <!--#c23174f8c8750f5a-->
- `test_daemon_wires_a_fetch_handler_into_its_client` (function) — Integration test that `Daemon._start_server_client` actually attaches a working `_fetch_handler` to the client it creates. <!--#26d49ed5bad070ad-->

### `tests/daemon/test_usage_backend.py` (python) — Unit tests for the daemon's `flow_usage_summary` usage-resolution backend, asserting its source precedence (session `session_usage_records` ledger → inline step `usage_records` → `cold_ref` cold-storage files, including archived ones under `state/archive/steps/` → legacy `session_token_usage` tally) plus edge cases like retained UNAVAILABLE records and empty-vs-round-tripped ledgers, so daemon totals match the CLI. <!--#403c54cce5cd8bbb|430b65095db3f643-->
- `_record` (function) — Test helper that builds a fully-populated AVAILABLE `UsageRecord` (claude/anthropic/claude-opus-5) for a given `call_id` and token count and returns it as a dict. <!--#4fdd7ff03959be6e-->
- `test_session_ledger_wins` (function) — Asserts `flow_usage_summary` prefers the top-level `session_usage_records` ledger as its usage source when one is present. <!--#91815bf32ec6040f-->
- `test_inline_step_outputs_recover_when_ledger_empty` (function) — Checks that with no session ledger, usage is recovered from `usage_records` embedded inline in a step's `outputs`. <!--#d17d773896356500-->
- `test_cold_ref_step_outputs_recover_when_ledger_empty` (function) — Checks that usage is recovered by resolving a step's `cold_ref` to its cold-storage JSON file under `tianluo/state/steps/<flow_id>/`. <!--#5041c5e9bb17c97d-->
- `test_legacy_tally_is_last_resort` (function) — Verifies the legacy `session_token_usage` five-field tally is used only as the final fallback and is adapted with its input split out as uncached, matching the CLI. <!--#e86efcb884529b04-->
- `test_unavailable_records_kept_in_daemon_and_counted` (function) — Verifies UNAVAILABLE usage records are retained rather than dropped, surfacing as `unknown_call_count` and a `partial` completeness verdict. <!--#10eabb7a09d9fca5-->
- `test_modern_empty_ledger_reports_no_usage` (function) — Guards that a present-but-empty ledger alongside an all-zero legacy tally means "zero calls" and yields `None` instead of a fabricated legacy record. <!--#fdd322ad721bccbc-->
- `test_round_tripped_legacy_tally_still_adapts` (function) — Guards the complementary case: an empty ledger beside a non-zero legacy tally is re-saved pre-ledger data, so its totals and `actual_cost_usd` must still be adapted. <!--#5b3e64955f24bcf6-->
- `test_step_records_still_win_over_round_tripped_legacy_tally` (function) — Asserts recoverable per-call step records take precedence over the round-tripped legacy tally projection. <!--#a99397675a6ffe92-->
- `test_archived_cold_step_outputs_recover_when_ledger_empty` (function) — Asserts the daemon is archive-aware, resolving cold step files moved to `state/archive/steps/` by `clear_state` so it agrees with the CLI history path. <!--#a6639d1710fa5573-->

## `tests/e2e/` — Runtime-free test suite for the tianluo e2e subsystem, using shared FakeRunner/FakeBackend/FakeClock stubs to cover the isolation-backend contract, ContainerBackend argv assembly, runtime probing, content bootstrap, config loading and schema validation, readiness probes, executor actions and assertion tiers, session orchestration, the `luo e2e` CLI, Dockerfile templates, error routing, and core import isolation from the optional e2e extra — all without touching a real container runtime, Pillow, or an LLM. <!--#41a7739db89106fa|a60c7ff75cc83426-->

### `tests/e2e/__init__.py` (python) — Package marker for the `tianluo.e2e` test suite, documenting that these tests never touch a real container runtime because every shell-invoking module accepts an injectable `runner`. <!--#fd38f30133411d97|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/e2e/_stubs.py` (python) — Shared test-double toolkit for the e2e test suite, providing a recording FakeRunner for container-CLI invocations, an in-memory FakeBackend isolation backend, a deterministic FakeClock, and factory helpers that build specs, scenarios, content, and tiny PNG fixtures without touching YAML, Pillow, or a real runtime. <!--#685d492edd5f321c|3189b0f432b65c8b-->
- `Call` (class) — Value object recording one runtime CLI invocation's argv and kwargs, with convenience accessors for the binary, verb, and remaining args. <!--#7b12e796909a650d-->
  - `Call.__init__` (method) — Stores defensive copies of the recorded argv sequence and kwargs mapping. <!--#7c13ef26049f7ec2-->
  - `Call.binary` (method) — Returns the invoked binary, i.e. the first argv element. <!--#064b878f96849a79-->
  - `Call.verb` (method) — Returns the subcommand verb (second argv element), or an empty string when the call had none. <!--#1ea0bffb1e47653d-->
  - `Call.args` (method) — Returns everything after the binary as the argument list. <!--#529e1f2dc6b0af92-->
  - `Call.__repr__` (method) — Debug-friendly representation showing the recorded argv. <!--#bde8fff0770fbbed-->
- `FakeRunner` (class) — Callable stand-in for the container-runtime CLI runner that records every invocation and answers it from an ordered list of predicate/result rules, defaulting to empty success. <!--#7c731b2eea4db8d2-->
  - `FakeRunner.__init__` (method) — Initialises the empty call log and the optional list of scripted response rules. <!--#5c96149746f55b9e-->
  - `FakeRunner.respond` (method) — Appends a predicate/result rule and returns self so rules can be chained. <!--#860f2d4c4bf02d9e-->
  - `FakeRunner.__call__` (method) — Records the invocation, then returns the first matching rule's CompletedProcess — raising exceptions or calling callables as the rule dictates — or a success with empty output. <!--#3e2642dacfd5faef-->
  - `FakeRunner.argv_for` (method) — Returns every recorded argv whose verb matches the given one. <!--#b9910776a5565e67-->
  - `FakeRunner.first` (method) — Returns the first recorded argv for a verb, or None if it was never invoked. <!--#bcc15ff1d8c515ae-->
  - `FakeRunner.verbs` (method) — Returns the verbs of all recorded calls in invocation order. <!--#5065c638995900da-->
- `probe` (function) — Builds a successful RuntimeProbeResult for a named runtime, optionally marked rootless. <!--#aa12303ea4c1bbe6-->
- `sample_spec` (function) — Builds a representative EnvironmentSpec with a default two-service (app + db) layout covering mounts, env, ports, and build steps. <!--#f5b7adcf74965edc-->
- `FakeBackend` (class) — In-memory IsolationBackend used by every test layered above the container implementation, scripting exec/snapshot results and lifecycle failures while recording create/start/exec/snapshot/destroy activity. <!--#6f6e45fd51d362c3-->
  - `FakeBackend.__init__` (method) — Stores the scripted exec/snapshot behaviour and lifecycle errors and initialises the recording state. <!--#55c341b41aa10adc-->
  - `FakeBackend.create` (method) — Builds an EnvironmentHandle with fake container names and publishes it before honouring any scripted create failure, mirroring the real backend's partial-creation leak. <!--#2d7c6c75473d5e97-->
  - `FakeBackend.start` (method) — Raises the scripted start error if set, otherwise records the handle and marks it started. <!--#5e85454e759d5cf4-->
  - `FakeBackend.exec` (method) — Records the exec call, then answers it via the scripted error, handler, queued results, or a default success. <!--#63ccf90729c67839-->
  - `FakeBackend.snapshot` (method) — Records the snapshot request and returns a Snapshot, writing screenshot bytes to a given destination, returning no path for destination-less logs, and otherwise pointing at a scratch path. <!--#518fd974275f0d9c-->
  - `FakeBackend._scratch` (method) — Lazily creates and returns a throwaway temp directory for artifacts the caller gave no destination for. <!--#619d041f6cd73b53-->
  - `FakeBackend.destroy` (method) — Counts teardown calls so tests can assert the environment was destroyed. <!--#924e6225b4096c83-->
  - `FakeBackend.argv_containing` (method) — Returns every recorded exec argv that contains the given part. <!--#ab6933964493285e-->
- `marked` (function) — Formats a payload as the marker-prefixed JSON stdout an in-container helper program emits, surrounded by noise. <!--#33e19ccf631af7cd-->
- `assertion` (function) — Builds an AssertionDecl from a kind and params, splitting the tier-declaration boolean flags out of the params. <!--#d0675a7b7acb619a-->
- `action` (function) — Builds an ActionDecl from a kind and params. <!--#d36d8fa672784b17-->
- `scenario` (function) — Builds a ScenarioDecl directly with sensible defaults, bypassing the YAML layer. <!--#acdcd97e726263b6-->
- `service_decl` (function) — Builds a ServiceDecl with a default base image. <!--#92599d36ed85406a-->
- `content` (function) — Builds an E2EContent object with derived root/baseline paths and default services, bypassing YAML parsing. <!--#3601a011c8694653-->
- `_png_chunk` (function) — Encodes one PNG chunk with its length prefix, tag, data, and CRC32 trailer. <!--#331bda0a07267326-->
- `write_png` (function) — Writes a tiny hand-encoded 8-bit RGB PNG fixture to disk, avoiding a Pillow import so core-only installs can still collect these tests. <!--#9f7f6db413bab4d2-->
- `png_bytes` (function) — Returns the same tiny PNG as raw bytes for callers that need the encoded image rather than a file on disk. <!--#4d667d91435e6498-->
- `pillow_installed` (function) — Reports whether the optional tianluo[e2e] Pillow dependency is importable, used to skip the real pixel-comparison tests. <!--#2063327d9b36882f-->
- `FakeClock` (class) — Deterministic monotonic clock that advances only when the code under test sleeps, recording each sleep duration. <!--#ed1c01df40e5058e-->
  - `FakeClock.__init__` (method) — Sets the starting time and initialises the recorded sleep list. <!--#27f05f601f16b645-->
  - `FakeClock.__call__` (method) — Returns the current fake time, standing in for a monotonic clock function. <!--#193d95a53f785f0b-->
  - `FakeClock.sleep` (method) — Records the requested sleep and advances the fake clock by at least a minimal tick. <!--#d0114bb3157e8767-->

### `tests/e2e/test_assertions.py` (python) — Unit-test suite for the e2e assertions engine, exercising every assertion kind against a FakeBackend — tier-1 exit_code/stdout/stderr, http_status/http_body (host-side and in-container fetch), file existence/content, DOM queries and the browser-bridge program, tier-2 screenshot baseline diffing with Pillow isolation, tier-3 LLM semantic_visual verdicts — plus declared timeout coercion, tier gating/dispatch, and config-error paths. <!--#8a8630e7240269da|36f2bc69b05b214b-->
- `make_ctx` (function) — Test helper that builds an AssertionContext wired to a FakeBackend, a fake EnvironmentHandle, and tmp_path-based project/baselines/artifacts directories, with keyword overrides. <!--#d21ef830ad6300e1-->
- `TestExitCodeAndStreams` (class) — Test class covering tier-1 exit_code/stdout/stderr assertions: default and explicit expectations, timed-out commands never passing, internal helper execs being excluded from the `last_exec` slot, missing commands, and config errors for bad expectations or regexes. <!--#6c30d065894ad391-->
  - `TestExitCodeAndStreams.test_exit_code_matches_default_zero` (method) — Asserts a bare `exit_code` assertion defaults to expecting 0, passes on a successful command, and reports tier 1. <!--#f2b3eec718e7fcd9-->
  - `TestExitCodeAndStreams.test_exit_code_failure_reports_both_sides` (method) — Asserts a failing exit_code check reports expected, actual, and the offending command in details. <!--#08cd71a8a5ac1b0b-->
  - `TestExitCodeAndStreams.test_exit_code_non_zero_expectation` (method) — Asserts an explicit non-zero expectation (`equals=1`) passes when the command exits 1. <!--#66562b9c7c30c4ca-->
  - `TestExitCodeAndStreams.test_timed_out_command_never_passes` (method) — Asserts a timed-out command fails the exit_code check even when its recorded exit code matches, with 'timed out' in the actual. <!--#7f766c311547ed17-->
  - `TestExitCodeAndStreams.test_timed_out_command_never_passes_a_stream_match` (method) — Asserts partial stdout from a killed command cannot satisfy a stream assertion, and the timeout is surfaced in details. <!--#91d4b3f4fd0dcce9-->
  - `TestExitCodeAndStreams.test_internal_helper_is_not_the_exec_under_assertion` (method) — Asserts execs marked `internal=True` (tianluo's own helper commands) do not displace the user command as the assertion target. <!--#254add145a779bce-->
  - `TestExitCodeAndStreams.test_without_any_command_the_assertion_fails_loudly` (method) — Asserts an exit_code assertion with no recorded command fails with a 'no command' message rather than passing vacuously. <!--#eb36c885e671813a-->
  - `TestExitCodeAndStreams.test_bad_expectation_is_a_config_error` (method) — Asserts a non-numeric `equals` value for exit_code raises E2EConfigError. <!--#c13de6fd41af11e1-->
  - `TestExitCodeAndStreams.test_stdout_matchers` (method) — Parametrized check that the stdout `contains`/`equals`/`matches` matchers pass or fail exactly as expected. <!--#7a0fabd36e1b5dba-->
  - `TestExitCodeAndStreams.test_stderr_reads_the_other_stream` (method) — Asserts a `stderr` assertion inspects stderr and does not leak into or from stdout. <!--#59d5486ae1ea8a4c-->
  - `TestExitCodeAndStreams.test_invalid_regex_is_a_config_error` (method) — Asserts an unparseable `matches` regex raises E2EConfigError rather than a re.error. <!--#7deb2136aa071cc3-->
- `_Response` (class) — Minimal stub of an HTTP response object supporting read/getcode and the context-manager protocol, used to fake urlopen results. <!--#0cca8915b890210b-->
  - `_Response.__init__` (method) — Stores the canned status code and body bytes. <!--#8ea82575298fb212-->
  - `_Response.read` (method) — Returns the canned body bytes. <!--#d55a2768e9fcd59d-->
  - `_Response.getcode` (method) — Returns the canned status code. <!--#7ce8773b5c06cfea-->
  - `_Response.__enter__` (method) — Returns self so the stub can be used in a `with` block. <!--#e11a445075fd069e-->
  - `_Response.__exit__` (method) — No-op exit that never suppresses exceptions. <!--#775f3bde6e4b1937-->
- `stub_urlopen` (function) — Test helper that monkeypatches `urllib.request.urlopen` to return a canned response, raise a given error, and optionally record (url, timeout) calls. <!--#37c02df3fbfa368b-->
- `TestHttpAssertions` (class) — Test class covering http_status/http_body assertions: host-side fetches, status and body/json_path matching, HTTPError and URLError handling, in-container fetch via `python3 -c` in a named service, and the stdlib-only constraint on the HTTP path. <!--#31f287f50d7cc67f-->
  - `TestHttpAssertions.test_status_from_the_host` (method) — Asserts a host-side http_status fetch hits the given URL and reports the observed status in details. <!--#8fb7a9bd6b61c838-->
  - `TestHttpAssertions.test_status_mismatch_reports_both_sides` (method) — Asserts a status mismatch fails with both the expected and the observed status in the message fields. <!--#7498842a39765591-->
  - `TestHttpAssertions.test_http_error_status_is_an_observation_not_a_crash` (method) — Asserts an HTTPError (e.g. 404) is treated as an observed status, so `equals=404` passes. <!--#a183d67948e25501-->
  - `TestHttpAssertions.test_unreachable_url_fails_with_guidance` (method) — Asserts a connection URLError fails the assertion with the underlying reason and a 'from:' hint in the message. <!--#1dfb6d44f534ba66-->
  - `TestHttpAssertions.test_body_matcher` (method) — Asserts an http_body assertion with `contains` matches text in the fetched response body. <!--#e61af583a8dc1610-->
  - `TestHttpAssertions.test_json_path_reads_a_field` (method) — Asserts `json_path` navigates nested objects and list indices in a JSON body and compares the extracted value. <!--#5322799ed8c413b0-->
  - `TestHttpAssertions.test_missing_json_path_fails_with_the_body` (method) — Asserts an unresolvable json_path fails with the path echoed in the message rather than raising. <!--#9970f57c531c0063-->
  - `TestHttpAssertions.test_from_service_routes_through_the_container` (method) — Asserts `from: <service>` routes the fetch through a `python3 -c` exec in that container and parses the marked payload. <!--#cab5b31c5b286393-->
  - `TestHttpAssertions.test_in_container_fetch_without_payload_is_reported` (method) — Asserts an in-container fetch whose exec produces no payload returns a record carrying the stderr as its error. <!--#fda5ef19bcf801df-->
  - `TestHttpAssertions.test_in_container_fetch_snippet_is_valid_python` (method) — Compiles the `_IN_CONTAINER_FETCH` snippet to catch syntax slips that would otherwise only surface inside a container, and checks it uses only urllib.request. <!--#369d537cfab6a500-->
  - `TestHttpAssertions.test_host_fetch_uses_stdlib_only` (method) — Guards the assertions module source against any `requests`/`httpx` dependency creeping into the e2e HTTP path. <!--#8951e74ce79139c2-->
- `TestDeclaredTimeBudgets` (class) — Test class asserting per-assertion `timeout` values are coerced and validated, so quoted numbers work and non-numeric or non-positive values raise a scenario-located E2EConfigError. <!--#b8eed1b4a01461fe-->
  - `TestDeclaredTimeBudgets.test_a_quoted_number_is_accepted` (method) — Asserts a string `timeout: "5"` is coerced to 5.0 and passed through to the fetch call. <!--#cff8740c14f65c7c-->
  - `TestDeclaredTimeBudgets.test_a_non_numeric_timeout_is_a_located_config_error` (method) — Parametrized check that non-numeric, zero, negative, boolean, or list timeouts raise E2EConfigError naming the scenario. <!--#0b3e7d8788e01a47-->

- `TestFileAssertions` (class) — Test class covering file_exists/file_content assertions: the `test -e` and `cat` probes, absence expectations, probes that could not run, unreadable files, and per-assertion service overrides. <!--#9a6408730ec0d442-->

  - `TestFileAssertions.test_unreadable_file_fails_with_the_error` (method) — Asserts a failed `cat` fails the assertion with the container's stderr in the actual. <!--#b0ab4e843a033f76-->

- `TestDomAssertions` (class) — Test class covering dom assertions against executor-supplied observations — text/equals/count/attribute/absent expectations, browser-side errors, lazy single-query execution through BrowserBridge, and the config error when no browser driver is configured. <!--#4ee9228fe413c276-->
  - `TestDomAssertions.test_observation_supplied_by_the_executor` (method) — Asserts a dom assertion evaluates an observation passed in by the executor and echoes the element count in details. <!--#adc178982184f517-->

  - `TestDomAssertions.test_absent_element_fails_a_presence_check` (method) — Asserts a zero-count observation fails a plain presence check with 'no element' in the actual. <!--#15e063269c48a277-->
  - `TestDomAssertions.test_absent_expectation` (method) — Asserts `absent: true` passes when the selector matched no elements. <!--#a3792f8909e75cde-->

  - `TestDomAssertions.test_browser_side_error_fails_the_assertion` (method) — Asserts an error reported by the browser (e.g. a Playwright timeout) fails the assertion and surfaces in the actual. <!--#70fca5ed347aa563-->
  - `TestDomAssertions.test_lazy_single_query_run_without_browser_actions` (method) — Asserts a dom assertion with no prior browser actions lazily runs a one-query Playwright program via `node -e` in the driver service. <!--#51d4b2a8ed478da3-->
  - `TestDomAssertions.test_dom_without_a_browser_driver_is_a_config_error` (method) — Asserts a dom assertion with no browser bridge raises E2EConfigError mentioning playwright. <!--#bc6be3a90aa2c4e0-->
- `TestBrowserBridge` (class) — Test class covering BrowserBridge program building and execution: op/query ordering in the rendered JS, one idempotent exec per scenario, failed-op reporting, node --check validation of the generated program, and turning unusable output into an error instead of a crash. <!--#9f91a6ba08260768-->
  - `TestBrowserBridge.test_program_carries_ops_and_queries_in_order` (method) — Asserts the rendered program preserves the order in which ops and queries were added and includes the result marker. <!--#c4715aa61293d993-->
  - `TestBrowserBridge.test_one_program_per_scenario` (method) — Asserts the whole browser flow runs in a single exec and that a second `run()` is idempotent, with observations and failed_ops read back from the one result. <!--#cb6f27f783e3bc44-->
  - `TestBrowserBridge.test_failed_op_is_reported` (method) — Asserts a browser op reported as not-ok surfaces through `failed_ops()` with its error message. <!--#5b9b8c431d345532-->
  - `TestBrowserBridge.test_rendered_program_is_valid_javascript` (method) — Writes the rendered program to disk and validates it with `node --check` (skipped when node is absent) to catch template typos and quoting bugs. <!--#cd6189d1b3578a43-->
  - `TestBrowserBridge.test_unparseable_output_becomes_an_error_not_a_crash` (method) — Asserts a failed browser exec sets `bridge.error` and leaves observations as None instead of raising. <!--#15feecca68e5f2c4-->
- `TestScreenshotDiff` (class) — Test class covering tier-2 screenshot_diff assertions: the `visual_regression` opt-in gate, baseline path containment, pixel-ratio and geometry comparisons, thresholds, missing-baseline guidance and `--write-baselines` capture, and reuse of already-captured or container-side screenshots. <!--#ae2a9ed6d13c0c58-->
  - `TestScreenshotDiff._ctx` (method) — Helper building a FakeBackend preloaded with screenshot bytes plus its AssertionContext. <!--#1e1c59836d71dd3d-->
