### `tests/engine/test_knowledge_asset_language.py` (python) — Tests that `spec_language` alone (never the human `language` setting) governs language injection into knowledge-asset LLM prompts, verifying that both the charter-freshness propose prompt and the code-index summary prompt gain the respond-in-language directive, preserve-symbols clause, and knowledge-asset framing when it is set, carry zero injection when it is not, and that summaries still honour the single-line contract. <!--#aafa49a08afd41cc|502f095fedb976bf-->
- `_isolated_global_home` (function) — An autouse-style pytest fixture that redirects `tianluo.config.Path.home` to a fresh empty temp dir so a developer's real `~/.se3/config.yaml` `language:` block can't leak in and break the tests' zero-injection assertions. <!--#bfed5560726a81d1-->
- `_write_project_language` (function) — Test helper that writes a `tianluo.yaml` file under a given project root containing a `language:` section with the specified `language` and `spec_language` values (defaulting to null). <!--#f16b720b29ac4a78-->
- `_install_fake_caller` (function) — Helper that monkeypatches `charter_freshness.LLMCaller` with a stub returning a canned response and records every prompt it is called with. <!--#c2f81c724a0eb789-->
- `_make_flow` (function) — Helper that builds a minimal `FlowInstance` whose `change_path` points inside the temp project root, so the handler loads config from that root. <!--#397f11c215a7ea6a-->
- `_make_step` (function) — Helper that builds a CHARTER_FRESHNESS `Step` with a non-empty changed-files diff, which is what forces the propose LLM call instead of the cheap no-LLM path. <!--#2f1e3acf2ce07a17-->
- `_charter_prompt` (function) — Helper that runs the charter-freshness handler against a temp project with the given language settings and returns the captured propose prompt. <!--#4b70dcd4ec92b7e9-->
- `test_charter_prompt_injects_spec_language_when_set` (function) — Asserts that with `spec_language` set the charter prompt gains the respond-in-language directive, the preserve-symbols clause, and knowledge-asset framing, while spec-file/SHALL-MUST wording stays out. <!--#e9c40cc9c2f0afad-->
- `test_charter_prompt_zero_injection_when_spec_language_unset` (function) — Asserts that with no `spec_language` the charter prompt carries no language directive or preserve-symbols clause at all. <!--#6943c3bd342fe065-->
- `test_charter_prompt_ignores_human_language_when_spec_language_unset` (function) — Asserts that the unified human `language` setting alone never drives the charter prompt — only `spec_language` governs a knowledge asset. <!--#5a722ba161fbf5e3-->
- `_install_fake_summary_caller` (function) — Test helper that monkeypatches `tianluo.engine.llm_caller.LLMCaller` with a stub whose `call` records every summary prompt and returns a canned JSON response, so tests can inspect the prompts sent by `_summarize_group`. <!--#e69f5de6b3e6c4db-->
- `_make_summary_target` (function) — Helper that builds a single symbol-level `SummaryTarget` for a trivial `foo.py::foo` function. <!--#9e712a6aa4ecc5c1-->
- `_code_index_prompt` (function) — Helper that runs the code-index LLM summarizer against a temp project with the given language settings and returns the captured summary prompt. <!--#522b5d5043e8f163-->
- `test_code_index_prompt_injects_spec_language_when_set` (function) — Asserts that with `spec_language` set the code-index summary prompt gains the respond-in-language directive, preserve-symbols clause, and knowledge-asset framing, without spec-file/SHALL-MUST wording. <!--#472112c46c772389-->
- `test_code_index_prompt_zero_injection_when_spec_language_unset` (function) — Asserts that with no `spec_language` the code-index summary prompt contains no language injection. <!--#dbd165258578ceaf-->
- `test_code_index_prompt_ignores_human_language_when_spec_language_unset` (function) — Asserts that the human `language` setting alone never injects into the code-index summary prompt. <!--#4e3348ae559e2dad-->
- `test_code_index_summary_stays_single_line_with_injection` (function) — Asserts that language injection touches only the prompt, so returned summaries are still surfaced verbatim as single lines and the `_flatten_summary` markdown contract holds. <!--#d8476928571fb9e7-->

### `tests/engine/test_llm_caller.py` (python) — Pytest suite for `tianluo.engine.llm_caller`, covering the tool preview/formatting helpers (`truncate_preview`, `format_tool_use_preview`, `format_tool_result_preview`) plus `StreamJSONTracker` and `LLMCaller`, asserting truncation rules, per-tool vs. generic parameter formatting, and result preview rendering. <!--#3b0805dec63fc9a4|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/engine/test_llm_caller_agents.py` (python) — Unit tests for LLMCaller's multi-agent management, covering agent-list initialization, runner factory/caching, per-attempt rotation on infra and generic errors, exhaustion, single-agent backward-compat, agent-name attribution in chat history, per-sequence rotation reset, tail-on-last, and two-phase JSON reset semantics. <!--#c0cbb0d5f70fae38|8aa4c6408c74ee89-->
- `_make_success_result` (function) — Test helper building a mock MonitoredResult representing a successful agent run with the given output. <!--#255ed86d161fbea7-->
- `_make_fail_result` (function) — Test helper building a mock MonitoredResult representing a failed agent run with a given return code, output, and command. <!--#5af90c7b47c1402e-->
- `_setup_per_agent_runners` (function) — Test helper that pre-populates the caller's runner cache with one scripted MagicMock runner per agent and returns a shared call log recording which agent ran each attempt. <!--#949a6f291319a13d-->
- `_json_ok` (function) — Test helper producing a success result whose output is a valid JSON document. <!--#faa748979be7476b-->
- `TestAgentInitialization` (class) — Tests that LLMCaller initializes its agent list either from an explicit `agents` parameter or, by default, by loading from config (defaulting the first agent to type `claude-code`). <!--#cefbb8b7590f40e0-->
  - `TestAgentInitialization.test_explicit_agents_parameter` (method) — Asserts an explicitly passed agents list is used directly with the index starting at zero. <!--#a31ea64677d27078-->
  - `TestAgentInitialization.test_default_loads_from_config` (method) — Verifies that without an explicit `agents` param, LLMCaller loads at least one agent from config with the first agent's type being `claude-code`. <!--#13079d9ae5cfe3aa-->
- `TestCreateRunner` (class) — Tests the runner factory: `_create_runner` builds a `ClaudeCodeRunner` for `claude-code` agents, an unknown agent type raises `ValueError`, and repeated `_get_current_runner` calls return the same cached runner. <!--#eef1ec2d0dda1b62-->
  - `TestCreateRunner.test_creates_claude_code_runner` (method) — Verifies `_create_runner` produces a `ClaudeCodeRunner` instance carrying the agent's configured command. <!--#3a4fc61a21105df4-->
  - `TestCreateRunner.test_unknown_type_raises` (method) — Asserts constructing an LLMCaller with an unknown agent type raises ValueError. <!--#c98c9fb3ec933d3c-->
  - `TestCreateRunner.test_runner_caching` (method) — Asserts repeated _get_current_runner calls return the same cached runner instance. <!--#67d1a7c9189aad31-->
- `TestRotateAgent` (class) — Test class covering the _rotate_agent index-advancing logic. <!--#67c9e57bdf1b7f9a-->
  - `TestRotateAgent.test_rotate_increments_index` (method) — Asserts rotation advances the current agent index and returns True. <!--#88d936fb86e4a085-->
  - `TestRotateAgent.test_rotate_exhausted_returns_false` (method) — Asserts rotation returns False and leaves the index unchanged when already at the last agent. <!--#b6ba2876a6c99b1a-->
  - `TestRotateAgent.test_single_agent_cannot_rotate` (method) — Asserts rotation returns False when only one agent is configured. <!--#0e954f725787b273-->
- `TestInfraErrorRotation` (class) — Tests that infrastructure errors (usage limit, timeout) detected via `detect_infra_error` cause LLMCaller to rotate from the failing agent to the next one and retry successfully. <!--#c8d99398a6f5cf98-->
  - `TestInfraErrorRotation.test_usage_limit_triggers_rotation` (method) — Asserts a usage-limit infra error rotates to the next agent, which then succeeds. <!--#bcbba194c8955dfc-->
  - `TestInfraErrorRotation.test_timeout_triggers_rotation` (method) — Asserts a timeout infra error rotates to the next agent, which then succeeds. <!--#3424ab3e064dff94-->
- `TestOtherErrorRotation` (class) — Tests that unclassified/OTHER failures (including a cert-verification error classified as `InfraErrorType.NONE`) also trigger rotation to the next agent. <!--#284b3dd29c95ea45-->
  - `TestOtherErrorRotation.test_other_error_rotates_to_next_agent` (method) — Asserts a generic failure classified as NONE still rotates to the next agent. <!--#4f0d52a4ca561cd4-->
  - `TestOtherErrorRotation.test_unknown_certificate_error_triggers_rotation` (method) — Asserts an UNKNOWN_CERTIFICATE_VERIFICATION_ERROR (classified NONE) triggers rotation to the next agent. <!--#82411f85bbca8815-->
- `TestAllAgentsExhausted` (class) — Tests that when every agent fails with infra errors, LLMCaller raises `LLMCallError` once all agents are exhausted. <!--#e93c4a97a16bb9c9-->
  - `TestAllAgentsExhausted.test_raises_after_exhaustion` (method) — Verifies that with both agents returning usage-limit failures, `caller.call` raises `LLMCallError` after exhausting rotations. <!--#e35c4de1f0bfee01-->
- `TestSingleAgentScenario` (class) — Tests single-agent (backward-compat) behavior: a lone agent succeeds normally, and infra/OTHER errors cannot rotate so they fall through to same-agent retries with the agent index staying at 0. <!--#4a27c4aa234b956e-->
  - `TestSingleAgentScenario.test_single_agent_success` (method) — Asserts a single agent returning success yields the expected output. <!--#8d052fb7fd35a93b-->
  - `TestSingleAgentScenario.test_single_agent_infra_error_no_rotation` (method) — Asserts a single agent's infra error cannot rotate and falls through to a same-agent retry that succeeds. <!--#32bb1a8428ff9b15-->
  - `TestSingleAgentScenario.test_single_agent_other_error_falls_through` (method) — Asserts a single agent's unclassified error falls through to a same-agent retry that succeeds. <!--#53279fe800e716c8-->
- `TestAgentAttributionInHistory` (class) — Tests that LLMCaller records the current attempt's agent name into chat history via `_record_prompt`/`_record_response`, that rotation attributes distinct agent names to successive attempts, and that recording failures don't block the call. <!--#c218b8bda794e6f7-->
  - `TestAgentAttributionInHistory.test_record_prompt_gets_agent_name` (method) — Verifies `_record_prompt` stores the given agent name on the recorded prompt message in the step history. <!--#9b525745dd23efbe-->
  - `TestAgentAttributionInHistory.test_record_response_gets_agent_name` (method) — Verifies `_record_response` stores the given agent name on the recorded assistant message in the step history. <!--#85e3d1659f5fc4d0-->
  - `TestAgentAttributionInHistory.test_rotation_records_different_agent_names` (method) — Verifies that after `_rotate_agent`, subsequent recorded messages carry the new agent's name while earlier messages retain the original agent's name. <!--#bea15a99b7f9b74e-->
  - `TestAgentAttributionInHistory.test_record_failure_does_not_block_call` (method) — Asserts that a failure while recording history does not raise and the call proceeds. <!--#0b6dca932af2399b-->
  - `TestAgentAttributionInHistory.test_call_with_retry_passes_agent_name` (method) — Verifies that a full `call` snapshots the current agent name and attributes both the user prompt and assistant response in history to the first agent (`agent-a`). <!--#0eca5d60c7b253a7-->
- `TestPerSequenceAgentReset` (class) — Regression test class ensuring each new internal retry sequence restarts rotation from the preferred agent rather than staying pinned to the last one. <!--#92a26445d95f193b-->
  - `TestPerSequenceAgentReset.test_index_starts_at_zero_each_call_when_reused` (method) — Asserts a reused caller resets to the preferred agent on a second call after the first rotated to the last agent. <!--#bf666587a79268a9-->
  - `TestPerSequenceAgentReset.test_reset_refreshes_legacy_runner` (method) — Asserts the entry reset also refreshes the legacy self._runner back to the preferred agent's runner. <!--#5487502383c4654e-->
- `TestTailOnLastWithinSequence` (class) — Tests that when `max_retries` exceeds the agent count, rotation advances through agents to the last one and then keeps retrying (tails) on that last agent without wrapping, eventually raising via the retry cap. <!--#8c533dc468e86949-->
  - `TestTailOnLastWithinSequence.test_tail_on_last_then_raises` (method) — Verifies a 3-agent, 5-retry sequence calls a→b→c then tails twice more on c (no wrap) and raises `LLMCallError` reporting "after 5 attempts" with the agent index at the last agent. <!--#dc47ca2d19320d26-->
- `TestTwoPhasePerPhaseReset` (class) — Test class verifying that in two_phase JSON mode each Phase-1 sequence resets rotation independently and Phase 2 runs verbatim. <!--#0cea97fa439ec081-->
  - `TestTwoPhasePerPhaseReset.test_phase1_resets_each_call` (method) — Asserts each separate two_phase call's Phase 1 starts rotation over from the preferred agent. <!--#29cc1a0e805d6fd0-->
  - `TestTwoPhasePerPhaseReset.test_phase2_starts_from_first_agent` (method) — Asserts that when Phase 1's non-JSON output forces production Phase 2, the extraction sequence resets back to the preferred agent. <!--#130c1bb74a65aade-->
  - `TestTwoPhasePerPhaseReset.test_phase2_runs_extraction_prompt_verbatim_on_step_retry` (method) — Regression test asserting Phase 2's extraction prompt runs verbatim (no continue-mode retry-context injection) even when the step is retried at the state-machine level. <!--#33b6fb31320094d6-->
- `TestJsonContinuationNoReset` (class) — Test class verifying the JSON-continuation recursion stays on the current agent rather than resetting to the preferred one. <!--#e64bef40f9c74fcc-->
  - `TestJsonContinuationNoReset.test_json_retry_keeps_current_agent` (method) — Asserts a non-JSON response triggers a continuation that remains on the same rotated-to agent until it returns valid JSON. <!--#6259ff49e2bd6612-->

### `tests/engine/test_llm_caller_rotation_error.py` (python) — Pytest module that drives LLMCaller with stub always-failing agent runners to verify the LLMCallError raised after retry exhaustion names every attempted agent with its exit code, command, and infra-error label — including rotating attempts, so the message never degrades to a bare 'failed after N attempts'. <!--#1885ff1d5ff15912|b6f4e5c1265b9bd6-->
- `_FailingRunner` (class) — Stub AgentRunner used by these tests that always returns a failing result with a fixed exit code and command name, and never reports an infra error. <!--#030161f6b5049c48-->
  - `_FailingRunner.__init__` (method) — Stores the fixed exit code and command string the stub runner will always report. <!--#abba69c15a5887a3-->
  - `_FailingRunner.build_call_args` (method) — Returns a trivial argument list containing just the stub's command name. <!--#bbb319965eb0c43c-->
  - `_FailingRunner.run_with_monitor` (method) — Returns a canned failing _Result carrying the stub's exit code and command. <!--#c77b82924603bf0a-->
  - `_FailingRunner.detect_infra_error` (method) — Always classifies the failure as InfraErrorType.NONE so rotation, not infra handling, drives the test. <!--#ce73a329c5bde7f2-->
- `_Result` (class) — Minimal stand-in for an agent run result, fixed to the failure shape (success False, empty output) with the given exit code and command. <!--#2a5474d4c2e20b6b-->
  - `_Result.__init__` (method) — Initialises the stub result fields to a non-interrupted failure with the supplied returncode and cmd_used. <!--#39159297a3b0fcaf-->
- `make_caller` (function) — Pytest fixture that clears SE3_TEST_RUNNING, patches LLMCaller to hand out the stub runners per agent, and returns a factory building an LLMCaller with a chosen max_retries. <!--#6c92ef0245b1e405-->
- `test_error_names_every_agent_and_exit_code` (function) — Asserts that after exhausting three attempts the raised LLMCallError message names every agent along with its exit code and command, including the rotating attempts that used to be dropped. <!--#a721dae72cc2872d-->
- `test_all_attempts_rotating_still_yields_a_reason` (function) — Asserts that when every attempt ends in a rotation the error message still carries a non-empty reason listing the two agents actually tried, rather than a bare 'failed after N attempts:'. <!--#91dcb0cb175f2331-->
- `test_infra_error_label_is_reported` (function) — Asserts the raised LLMCallError message includes the infra_error label for the failure. <!--#659fbf9e0e7a31e7-->

### `tests/engine/test_llm_caller_step_override.py` (python) — Unit tests for LLMCaller's per-step agent override wiring, verifying that a declared `llm_caller.steps.<step>` override is used verbatim (no default fallback appended), that unoverridden steps fall back to the default agent chain, that exhausting an override chain raises LLMCallError instead of rotating into the default, and that an explicit `agents=` argument takes precedence over both. <!--#747a72dff5e62443|101a184685881979-->
- `_make_fail_result` (function) — Helper building a MagicMock LLM result representing a failed (unsuccessful) agent call, e.g. a usage-limit infra error. <!--#443242c628427894-->
- `_make_success_result` (function) — Helper building a MagicMock LLM result representing a successful agent call. <!--#7cc32192812158d1-->
- `_write_override` (function) — Test helper that writes a tianluo.yaml into tmp_path with an agents registry plus a per-step llm_caller override, defaulting to a registry of override-a/override-b/solo-override agents when none is given. <!--#931f5a90c9dc3d0a-->
- `TestStepOverrideChain` (class) — Test class verifying that a declared per-step override replaces the agent chain (no default fallback tail) while steps without an override still get the built-in default chain. <!--#c27236e8f7a925e5-->
  - `TestStepOverrideChain.test_override_used_when_declared` (method) — Asserts that when a step declares override agents, LLMCaller._agents is exactly those overrides with the default claude NOT appended as a fallback. <!--#d82ddc3d2ec8618e-->
  - `TestStepOverrideChain.test_other_step_falls_back_to_default_chain` (method) — Asserts that a step lacking an override (with which() pinned to claude only) falls back to the single-agent built-in default claude chain. <!--#2c217654b965e350-->
- `TestExhaustionDoesNotFallBack` (class) — Test class guarding that exhausting all override agents on infra errors raises LLMCallError rather than rotating into the default chain. <!--#f08173845d8b53c9-->
  - `TestExhaustionDoesNotFallBack.test_override_exhaustion_raises_without_falling_back` (method) — Mocks a single-agent override whose runner always hits a USAGE_LIMIT infra error and asserts caller.call raises LLMCallError while the agent index stays within the override list rather than falling through to default claude. <!--#91643d99406f9e4f-->
- `TestExplicitAgentsArgHighestPriority` (class) — Test class asserting that an explicit agents= argument to LLMCaller takes highest priority, bypassing both per-step overrides and the default chain. <!--#5385cedd4e370ef8-->
  - `TestExplicitAgentsArgHighestPriority.test_explicit_agents_bypasses_override_and_default` (method) — Asserts that passing an explicit agents list makes caller._agents that exact list (by identity), overriding the declared per-step override and the default chain. <!--#7411b06bfb990032-->

### `tests/engine/test_merge_deterministic_resolvers.py` (python) — Unit tests for the deterministic merge resolvers, covering code-index markdown parse/render round-tripping, per-entry conflict picking against worktree fingerprints, `CodeIndexResolver` and `NextIdResolver` behaviour, and the `resolve_deterministic` staging/degrade-to-LLM path. <!--#80058dc08f76a2cd|116abcc31d9c15aa-->
- `_fp_comment` (function) — Test helper that formats the `<!--#content_fp|list_fp-->` fingerprint comment appended to code-index headings. <!--#7ee31e36e855dc69-->
- `_md` (function) — Test helper that assembles a minimal but format-faithful code-index markdown document from a list of pre-rendered entries. <!--#beaf0dbadf66834b-->
- `_entry` (function) — Test helper that renders a single `### relpath (python) — summary <!--#fp-->` code-index file entry plus its symbol bullets. <!--#0d20e841771ca74f-->
- `_block` (function) — Test helper that builds a `FileBlock` for `x.py` with the given fingerprints, summary, and bullets, for driving `_pick` directly. <!--#1f76830d200c5ff3-->
- `test_parse_extracts_fingerprints_and_bullets` (function) — Asserts `_parse_md_blocks` recovers dir headings, content/list fingerprints, summary, and bullet lines from code-index markdown. <!--#771d9e501025dacf-->
- `test_render_is_deterministic_and_marker_free` (function) — Asserts `_render` is idempotent, emits no conflict markers, and orders entries by sorted relpath regardless of input order. <!--#bc30a09839dfaf40-->
- `test_roundtrip_on_repository_index_is_byte_identical` (function) — Verifies that parsing and re-rendering the real tianluo/code-index.md is byte-for-byte identical (skipped if the index has not been built). <!--#fc785ae98d6a0071-->
- `test_pick_keeps_the_only_side_that_has_the_entry` (function) — Asserts `_pick` returns the single present side with reason `only-ours`/`only-theirs` when the other side lacks the entry. <!--#0725c1321695d669-->
- `test_pick_takes_theirs_when_both_sides_are_identical` (function) — Asserts `_pick` reports `identical` and returns theirs when both sides' blocks agree entirely. <!--#8037077e91607b1e-->
- `test_pick_takes_the_side_whose_fingerprint_matches_the_worktree` (function) — Asserts `_pick` resolves a fingerprint disagreement in favour of whichever side matches the post-merge working-tree file. <!--#c7686f3f3bf0cb1d-->
- `test_pick_falls_back_to_theirs_when_neither_side_matches_the_worktree` (function) — Asserts `_pick` deterministically falls back to theirs (reason `neither-matches-worktree`) when the worktree fingerprint matches neither side or is unknown. <!--#dc2f8fbb28e63c24-->
- `test_pick_keeps_theirs_symbols_whole_when_neither_side_matches_the_worktree` (function) — Asserts that when both sides are stale, theirs' bullet list is taken whole rather than merged with ours, keeping the result a pure function of its inputs. <!--#718d18ced6e3e996-->
- `test_pick_takes_the_matching_sides_symbols_whole` (function) — Asserts the worktree-matching side's bullet list is used verbatim, so stale symbols from the losing side are never grafted in. <!--#b900370483417f33-->
- `test_pick_takes_theirs_when_fingerprints_agree_but_summaries_differ` (function) — Asserts a pure wording disagreement over identical content is settled on theirs with reason `same-fp-different-summary`. <!--#2a878a2748bec267-->
- `_stage_stub` (function) — Test helper returning a fake `_git_show_stage` that serves canned ours/theirs blob text per merge stage. <!--#63090386bd661070-->
- `test_resolve_unions_entries_and_drops_those_whose_file_vanished` (function) — Asserts `CodeIndexResolver.resolve` unions both sides' entries, drops entries whose working-tree file is gone, settles disagreements by worktree fingerprint, and emits no conflict markers. <!--#4d754309ce0627ef-->
- `test_resolve_is_deterministic` (function) — Asserts repeated `CodeIndexResolver.resolve` calls on the same inputs produce identical output, falling back to theirs when neither side matches. <!--#a569c4db4e130ee5-->
- `test_resolve_survives_a_missing_side` (function) — Asserts `CodeIndexResolver.resolve` still produces an index when one merge stage has no blob (add/delete-shaped conflict). <!--#0fdb71af0837b465-->
- `test_resolve_raises_when_both_sides_are_missing` (function) — Asserts `CodeIndexResolver.resolve` raises `ValueError` rather than inventing content when neither stage supplies an index. <!--#8ef657d729123add-->
- `test_code_index_resolver_matches_only_its_own_path` (function) — Asserts CodeIndexResolver.matches() accepts exactly tianluo/code-index.md and rejects lookalike paths (.bak suffix, other directories). <!--#ee45b662740ca25e-->
- `test_next_id_resolver_takes_the_maximum` (function) — Parameterised test that `NextIdResolver` resolves the issue-counter conflict to the larger of the two sides' values. <!--#03713a5a30abbc3d-->
- `test_next_id_resolver_raises_when_no_side_is_usable` (function) — Parameterised test that `NextIdResolver` raises rather than staging a counter value that came from neither side, which would reissue allocated IDs. <!--#d3743988b8b96b6c-->
- `test_next_id_resolver_propagates_git_failure` (function) — Asserts a `git show` failure propagates out of `NextIdResolver` instead of masquerading as an absent side and silently dropping the larger counter. <!--#434b6a353fd8763c-->
- `test_resolve_deterministic_falls_back_when_git_show_fails` (function) — Asserts `resolve_deterministic` records the git error as a failure and leaves the path in `remaining` for the LLM. <!--#f48802ddbc8f1551-->
- `test_registry_holds_two_resolvers_with_disjoint_matches` (function) — Asserts the resolver `REGISTRY` has exactly two entries and that each deterministic path is claimed by exactly one of them. <!--#92ae1adffb669111-->
- `_StubResolver` (class) — Minimal fake resolver that matches one relpath and either returns canned text or raises, used to drive `resolve_deterministic` in isolation. <!--#dcc73293dbc03077-->
  - `_StubResolver.__init__` (method) — Stores the relpath this stub claims and the text (or exception) its `resolve` will produce. <!--#f0ca9a1d39c0d394-->
  - `_StubResolver.matches` (method) — Returns True only for the exact relpath the stub was constructed with. <!--#e1066e19fa5c3c3b-->
  - `_StubResolver.resolve` (method) — Returns the canned output, or raises it if the stub was configured with an exception. <!--#a19580e98867f3d9-->
- `git_calls` (function) — Pytest fixture that patches `_git_add`/`_git_rm` to record staging calls instead of touching git. <!--#ddd9ea21e1443ccb-->
- `test_unmatched_paths_are_left_for_the_llm` (function) — Asserts paths no resolver claims pass through untouched into `remaining` with no git staging. <!--#557a3506f953909d-->
- `test_resolved_path_is_written_and_staged` (function) — Asserts a resolved path has its resolver output written to the working tree and `git add`-ed, while unclaimed paths remain. <!--#ec1d989cd827714e-->
- `test_empty_output_deletes_the_path` (function) — Asserts an empty resolver result means "deleted by the merge" and triggers `git rm` for the path. <!--#00b2bf204b5e06a9-->
- `test_a_raising_resolver_degrades_to_the_llm_without_staging` (function) — Asserts a resolver exception is captured in `failures`, the path degrades to `remaining`, and the conflicted file is left untouched and unstaged. <!--#2460bfb8ea750a52-->
- `test_output_with_conflict_markers_is_never_staged` (function) — Asserts resolver output still containing conflict markers is rejected, recorded as a failure, and never written or staged. <!--#ee868e6f11a0aafa-->
- `test_a_failed_stage_restores_the_conflicted_working_tree` (function) — Asserts a `git add` failure rolls the working-tree file back to its original conflicted content so the LLM inherits the real conflict. <!--#1b6b4972be671175-->
- `test_a_failed_stage_removes_the_file_the_conflict_never_had` (function) — Asserts that when a staging failure follows a conflict with no working-tree copy, the written file is removed rather than left looking already-resolved. <!--#4cbaed83acb42603-->
- `test_resolved_and_remaining_partition_the_input_in_order` (function) — Asserts `resolve_deterministic`'s `resolved` and `remaining` lists exactly partition the input paths while preserving input order. <!--#25d11e1c0a884b25-->
- `_git` (function) — Test helper that runs a `git -C repo …` command and returns its stdout, raising on failure. <!--#4bcee364727a85d9-->
- `_real_fp` (function) — Helper returning the content fingerprint that code_index would record for a given text, via the real _fp/_sha256_prefix functions. <!--#1dbc34bfafc991a9-->
- `_index_md` (function) — Test helper that renders a full code-index markdown document from `(relpath, summary, content_fp)` triples for the integration fixture. <!--#ec7c9663b6a998b4-->
- `_write` (function) — Test helper that writes text to a repo-relative path, creating parent directories as needed. <!--#f70dcb0dc6f581d0-->
- `conflicted_repo` (function) — Fixture building a real mid-merge git repo where both deterministic files (code-index.md and issues/.next_id) are genuinely conflicted, mirroring the real index-regeneration failure the resolver targets. <!--#7e12063e63284bcf-->
- `no_llm` (function) — Fixture that monkeypatches LLMCaller.call to fail, guaranteeing deterministic conflicts are resolved without any LLM invocation. <!--#8ef7e18ea4c3083e-->
- `test_real_merge_conflict_is_resolved_without_the_llm` (function) — Checks resolve_deterministic() clears both conflicting paths from git's index (no unmerged entries) without calling the LLM. <!--#c93ccb45d45f3545-->
- `test_resolved_index_unions_entries_and_drops_the_deleted_file` (function) — Verifies the merged code-index unions both sides' entries, drops the deleted file's entry, and resolves per-entry disagreements by fingerprint match to the working tree (ours) or regenerated wording (theirs). <!--#6acc7315ed0830db-->
- `test_staged_index_matches_the_working_tree` (function) — Asserts the git-staged code-index.md content exactly matches the resolved working-tree file. <!--#fbd7204c4c8b5d6a-->
- `test_next_id_takes_the_larger_counter` (function) — Verifies the NextIdResolver merge picks the larger of the two conflicting .next_id counter values (12). <!--#f0152c26b62f902a-->
- `test_the_merge_commits_cleanly_after_deterministic_resolution` (function) — Confirms that after deterministic resolution the merge commits as a real two-parent merge with both sides' file changes present in the tree. <!--#03499673b3fa221c-->
- `orchestrator_repo` (function) — Pytest fixture that yields the `conflicted_repo` with the merge orchestrator's `build_conflict_context` monkeypatched to raise, asserting that deterministic resolvers short-circuit before any LLM/context work happens. <!--#1f64bf5d1cd38c89-->
- `_handle_conflict` (function) — Helper that constructs a MergeOrchestrator for a given strategy and invokes its _handle_conflict against branch 'feature', returning the result and report. <!--#0f138bc46b01c5fb-->
- `test_a_fully_deterministic_conflict_merges_without_the_llm` (function) — Parametrised over strategy, asserts a fully deterministic conflict merges cleanly (result 'merged', no human call, two-parent commit, counters/index resolved) without the LLM. <!--#4b3c82da8aaebb85-->
- `test_a_leftover_conflict_still_reaches_the_context_builder` (function) — Verifies that one non-deterministic remaining conflict keeps the LLM path alive, reaching build_conflict_context with only the unresolved file in conflict_files. <!--#5a847b77fa72e466-->
- `test_a_broken_deterministic_pass_degrades_to_the_pre_change_behaviour` (function) — Parametrised over which internal call crashes, asserts a failure in the deterministic pass degrades gracefully to the LLM path, handing build_conflict_context conflict_files=None rather than a half-filled outcome or error. <!--#e0879bf5a24852e1-->

### `tests/engine/test_plan_decomposition.py` (python) — End-to-end regression suite for the plan-decomposition/granularity axes that replaced the retired implementation-strategy concept, covering `PlanModeResolver` request/config/default precedence and error contracts, write-once context persistence and legacy-strategy projection, the invariant that a flow's step sequence depends only on task type (PLAN always survives), persistence/resume round trips, progress and context projections, `holistic_execution_mode` shape resolution for new and legacy flows, and the ANALYZE step no longer emitting any routing question or strategy output. <!--#e4ae0a1195b900a6|af2501ba8f991b9c-->
- `test_module_exposes_no_step_sequence_transform` (function) — Asserts by source inspection that the plan-mode module never imports step-sequence vocabulary and that `PlanModeResolver` has no sequence-rewriting or legacy-inference methods, so it is structurally unable to trim a flow's steps. <!--#4208ce04069d0b92-->
- `test_retired_module_is_gone` (function) — Asserts that importing the retired `tianluo.engine.implementation_strategy` module raises `ImportError`. <!--#20b3f8607b7b3a1d-->
- `test_engine_package_exports_only_the_new_symbols` (function) — Checks that `tianluo.engine` re-exports `PlanModeResolver` and that all five retired implementation-strategy names are absent from both the module and its `__all__`. <!--#725949c4fb6c0764-->
- `test_defaults_are_capability_auto` (function) — Asserts that `resolve_requested()` with no arguments defaults to `(CAPABILITY, AUTO)`. <!--#b5e978faad1817b9-->
- `test_explicit_request_wins_over_configuration` (function) — Verifies an explicit decomposition/granularity request overrides explicitly configured `WorkflowConfig` values. <!--#26633c67c47a26e8-->
- `test_configuration_wins_over_default` (function) — Verifies explicitly configured `WorkflowConfig` values are used when no explicit request is passed. <!--#a88a7cce92170dbf-->
- `test_axes_resolve_independently` (function) — Verifies the decomposition and granularity axes resolve separately, so an explicit granularity does not pull the decomposition off its configured value. <!--#80644b28c43690ed-->
- `test_mapping_shaped_configuration_is_accepted` (function) — Verifies `resolve_requested` accepts a plain mapping as the configuration source, not just a `WorkflowConfig` object. <!--#518e5b409d67a7c9-->
- `test_invalid_values_raise_plan_mode_error_listing_the_legal_set` (function) — Parametrized check that invalid explicit decomposition/granularity values raise `PlanModeError` whose message enumerates the legal values for the offending axis. <!--#8da7eca29a857d74-->
- `test_invalid_configured_value_names_the_config_path` (function) — Asserts an invalid configured granularity raises `PlanModeError` naming the `workflow.plan_granularity` config path. <!--#4c908d203a3b277f-->
- `test_initialize_context_persists_all_three_keys` (function) — Verifies `initialize_context` writes the decomposition, granularity and reason keys into the flow context and returns a matching view. <!--#0c1b8ed0dbb4c0df-->
- `test_initialize_context_is_write_once` (function) — Verifies `initialize_context` leaves an already-populated context untouched and reports the previously recorded values. <!--#a563af03497d29c2-->
- `test_reason_records_which_source_won` (function) — Checks the persisted reason string names its winning source — explicit request, project configuration, or default. <!--#3745b23af7448b49-->
- `test_non_explicit_configuration_reads_as_default` (function) — Asserts a `WorkflowConfig` left at its defaults resolves to the defaults without the reason claiming project configuration made the choice. <!--#d65386710328ace5-->
- `test_view_returns_persisted_values` (function) — Verifies `PlanModeResolver.view` reads back persisted context keys with `legacy_strategy` None and `inferred` False. <!--#00b229ff8da3ab20-->
- `test_view_projects_legacy_flows_without_writing_back` (function) — Parametrized check that `view` projects a legacy effective-strategy marker onto the new axes, flags it as inferred, and does not mutate the context. <!--#25c163f93cad70fd-->
- `test_view_of_an_empty_context_reports_defaults_as_inferred` (function) — Asserts `view({})` returns the default plan mode marked `inferred` with no legacy strategy. <!--#2dc7731477b9e401-->
- `test_projection_carries_the_legacy_annotation` (function) — Verifies `to_projection` adds the `legacy_strategy` annotation while `to_dict`'s write payload stays exactly the three context keys. <!--#8f6e93979071e577-->
- `test_plan_survives_every_plan_mode` (function) — Parametrized end-to-end check that flows created under any task type and plan mode keep PLAN and IMPLEMENT and never leave an orphaned CONFIRM gate. <!--#44820343f95586a3-->
- `test_sequence_is_a_function_of_task_type_alone` (function) — Verifies a forced single-group plan mode produces the same step sequence as the baseline flow for the same task type. <!--#e7a791706cfd6015-->
- `test_planless_sequences_are_untouched` (function) — Verifies a created flow's `selected_steps` equals `get_default_step_sequence(task_type)` regardless of plan mode. <!--#80cd36602ed7d41a-->
- `test_fallback_sequence_types_also_keep_plan` (function) — Verifies an unmapped task type such as `refactor`, which falls back to the feature sequence, still includes PLAN. <!--#abcacf00dab9a31a-->
- `test_new_flow_persists_the_plan_mode_into_context` (function) — Verifies `create_flow` persists the requested decomposition, granularity and reason into the flow context. <!--#3540a754748a6596-->
- `test_invalid_explicit_request_uses_the_config_error_contract` (function) — Verifies an invalid `plan_decomposition` passed to `create_flow` surfaces as a `ConfigError` listing the legal values. <!--#c00016ae7bf052f8-->
- `test_plan_mode_round_trips_through_hot_cold_persistence` (function) — Verifies the persisted plan mode survives a save/load round trip through the hot-cold persistence layer. <!--#93f43e866cd2b3ec-->
- `test_resume_keeps_the_persisted_plan_mode_after_a_config_change` (function) — Verifies a resumed flow retains its originally persisted plan mode even after the project config changed underneath it. <!--#b290988a81f28fd7-->
- `test_legacy_direct_flow_resume_does_not_rewrite_its_sequence` (function) — Verifies resuming a legacy `direct` flow preserves its PLAN-less recorded sequence and legacy marker without injecting new plan-mode keys. <!--#c81285802759c141-->
- `test_progress_projection_exposes_the_persisted_plan_mode` (function) — Verifies `StateMachine.get_progress` surfaces the persisted decomposition, granularity and a null `legacy_strategy`. <!--#6908de97b8b947c3-->
- `test_context_projection_reads_group_count_off_the_plan_output` (function) — Verifies `build_context_from_flow` exposes the plan mode plus a `plan_group_count` derived from PLAN's `task_groups` output, with no retired strategy keys. <!--#ee48476de690c860-->
- `test_context_projection_of_a_legacy_flow_is_read_only` (function) — Verifies projecting a legacy flow dict reports the legacy strategy and its inferred axes without mutating the input dict. <!--#309a78810bc2499c-->
- `test_context_projection_of_a_planless_new_flow_has_no_group_count` (function) — Verifies a flow with no PLAN step projects `plan_group_count` as None. <!--#38961d9e65e6214c-->
- `_shape` (function) — Test helper that calls `holistic_execution_mode` with keyword inputs split into task type, step inputs and context. <!--#d9e518d2c8606db0-->
- `test_single_group_is_the_whole_task_shape` (function) — Verifies a capability plan yielding one group classifies as the single-group holistic mode. <!--#dc939e2f922dec88-->
- `test_auto_granularity_lets_the_group_count_decide` (function) — Verifies `auto` granularity with multiple capability groups yields no holistic mode, i.e. grouped execution. <!--#641475b2acf88e72-->
- `test_forced_single_pins_one_call_whatever_plan_emitted` (function) — Parametrized check that `single` granularity forces the single-group mode even when PLAN emitted several groups, preserving the retired `direct` strategy's one-call guarantee. <!--#cdb6b176f684de7c-->
- `test_forced_single_is_honoured_from_persisted_context_alone` (function) — Verifies forced-single is honoured when the granularity lives only in the flow context rather than the step inputs. <!--#29caec9bb2f12c35-->
- `test_forced_single_does_not_apply_to_the_granular_doctrine` (function) — Verifies `single` granularity does not collapse a `granular` decomposition into one call. <!--#0c4a5653d5ad02c2-->
- `test_a_flow_with_no_doctrine_key_falls_back_the_way_plan_does` (function) — Verifies a flow missing the decomposition key falls back to the capability default downstream, matching PLAN's own fallback, while a legacy `planned` marker still forces grouped execution. <!--#9e9fd8bb45537c59-->
- `test_legacy_direct_flow_keeps_the_whole_task_shape_on_resume` (function) — Verifies a legacy `direct` flow with no plan or groups classifies as the legacy-direct holistic mode rather than grouped execution. <!--#83c995dacc8bb858-->
- `test_legacy_direct_is_recognised_from_step_inputs_too` (function) — Verifies the legacy `direct` marker is recognised case-insensitively from step inputs, not just flow context. <!--#4b8bf550600b7999-->
- `test_legacy_direct_flow_that_did_run_plan_reads_its_shape_off_the_plan` (function) — Parametrized check that a legacy `direct` flow which has since acquired task groups switches to the single-group mode instead of the legacy-direct branch. <!--#66e3f801b762ab52-->
- `test_legacy_direct_projects_onto_capability_and_forced_single` (function) — Verifies a legacy `direct` flow reads as both capability decomposition and forced-single group via the predicate helpers. <!--#59dd02f82d8c8876-->
- `test_legacy_planned_flow_stays_grouped` (function) — Verifies a legacy `planned` flow yields no holistic mode and stays grouped. <!--#4ab526acd0552dd5-->
- `test_persisted_doctrine_wins_over_a_stale_legacy_strategy_key` (function) — Verifies an explicit persisted plan mode makes a leftover legacy `direct` marker inert. <!--#af4f0a552ba14afa-->
- `test_small_type_outranks_a_legacy_direct_marker` (function) — Verifies task type `small` classifies as the small holistic mode in preference to the legacy-direct branch. <!--#d5c495b5a3b0f5d5-->
- `test_is_legacy_direct_flow_predicate` (function) — Exercises `is_legacy_direct_flow` across markers, a new-model decomposition key, and empty vs populated `task_groups`. <!--#2b370371cadf0c44-->
- `test_is_forced_single_group_reads_inputs_then_context` (function) — Verifies `is_forced_single_group` reads the granularity from step inputs then context and is false for `auto`, `conservative`, or absence. <!--#f052f3a982f97dd5-->
- `_run_analyze` (function) — Test helper that creates a flow and runs `analyze_handler` with the project summary, `LLMCaller` and all context-builder injections patched, returning the flow, step, status and captured LLM call kwargs. <!--#ca2f020c9986b334-->
- `test_analyze_prompt_carries_no_routing_question` (function) — Verifies the ANALYZE prompt and JSON schema hint no longer ask the LLM to choose an implementation strategy. <!--#5bb16c739948049f-->
- `test_analyze_writes_no_strategy_outputs_or_context` (function) — Verifies ANALYZE ignores stray strategy fields in the LLM response, writing no strategy keys to step outputs or context while keeping PLAN in the sequence. <!--#2a73515fff357433-->
- `test_reclassified_flow_gets_a_planned_sequence` (function) — Verifies ANALYZE reclassifying a `small` task as `feature` rebuilds the sequence to include PLAN and IMPLEMENT. <!--#38c14e82015b5461-->
- `test_worktree_flow_keeps_its_merge_tail_after_the_rebuild` (function) — Verifies a worktree-mode flow's ANALYZE-driven sequence rebuild keeps PLAN and preserves VERSION_RECONCILE immediately after MERGE_INTEGRATE. <!--#bf72fed1e7c5963c-->
- `test_bugfix_with_unclear_root_cause_still_gets_investigate` (function) — Verifies a bugfix with an unclear root cause gets INVESTIGATE inserted ahead of PLAN. <!--#aac7fc9eddf51f4a-->
- `test_implement_inputs_carry_the_plan_mode_not_a_strategy` (function) — Verifies `_build_step_inputs` for IMPLEMENT carries the plan-mode keys and no retired strategy or `strategy_reason` fields, including inside `analysis_context`. <!--#f8912fc0b4d4a860-->

### `tests/engine/test_plan_proposal_design_retired.py` (python) — Regression suite verifying that the PLAN step's retired proposal/design/depth-tiering machinery is gone end to end — prompts and STEP_POOL declarations solicit only the scheduling fields, the handler and IMPLEMENT prompts drop any `plan` wrapper or `design_doc` channel, while the display and history render paths still handle archived legacy-shaped flows. <!--#c43741d03982de26|4173642607cb3f06-->
- `_plan_prompt` (function) — Test helper that renders the PLAN step prompt via `_build_prompt` with fixed task fields and a caller-supplied decomposition doctrine and task type. <!--#629b9d01b4dc4187-->
- `test_plan_prompt_never_asks_for_a_proposal_or_design` (function) — Parametrized test asserting the PLAN prompt mentions neither "proposal" nor "design" for any doctrine/task-type combination. <!--#3668a266c6e61e13-->
- `test_plan_prompt_solicits_only_the_scheduling_fields` (function) — Asserts the PLAN prompt requests only `task_groups`, `total_complexity`, and `estimated_effort`, with no `plan` wrapper key. <!--#2c5362e3014fc342-->
- `test_plan_module_drops_the_retired_sections_and_depth_tiering` (function) — Asserts the retired prompt sections, per-depth JSON schemas, and `_get_prompt_depth` no longer exist as attributes of the plan step module. <!--#7a12bbda1a9c4813-->
- `test_plan_prompt_builder_takes_no_depth_argument` (function) — Asserts `_build_prompt`'s signature no longer accepts a `depth` parameter. <!--#126fb110463d2b45-->
- `test_display_plan_takes_no_depth_argument` (function) — Asserts `_display_plan`'s signature no longer accepts `depth` or `plan` parameters. <!--#f40161f52cd0bc12-->
- `test_step_pool_plan_outputs_carry_no_plan_wrapper` (function) — Asserts the STEP_POOL declaration for PLAN lists `task_groups` as an output but not `plan`. <!--#45c1db74f4fb8297-->
- `test_step_pool_downstream_inputs_drop_the_retired_channels` (function) — Asserts IMPLEMENT no longer declares a `design_doc` input and COMMIT no longer declares a `proposal` input. <!--#63b4395f55c6ad24-->
- `_flow_and_step` (function) — Test helper building a running FlowInstance (with a chosen `plan_decomposition`) plus a matching PLAN Step with standard inputs. <!--#ef670806a1a2ea85-->
- `_run_plan` (function) — Test helper that invokes `plan_handler` with LLMCaller and all context-builder injections patched out, returning the resulting status and the mock caller. <!--#4a5b3ad276e2b2f8-->
- `test_plan_handler_writes_no_proposal_or_design` (function) — Asserts a successful PLAN run persists only the scheduling outputs and no `plan`/`proposal`/`design` keys. <!--#47cf78f074ceb939-->
- `test_plan_handler_drops_a_model_supplied_plan_wrapper` (function) — Asserts PLAN discards a `plan` wrapper even when the model volunteers one in its JSON response. <!--#ddd1b0bd6e54b41f-->
- `_implement_templates` (function) — Test helper returning each IMPLEMENT prompt template (single-call, holistic, grouped, capability-group, fix) paired with dummy format fields. <!--#67786a3eb6aca783-->
- `test_implement_prompt_paths_have_no_design_document` (function) — Parametrized test asserting no IMPLEMENT prompt template carries a `{design_section}` placeholder or renders a "## Design Document" heading. <!--#2f655b8b65eca15f-->
- `test_implement_handler_ignores_a_legacy_design_doc_input` (function) — Asserts a resumed flow whose IMPLEMENT step still carries a legacy `design_doc` input injects nothing into the built prompt. <!--#2b44ece5b620b94e-->
- `test_plan_confirm_prompt_reviews_scheduling_data_only` (function) — Asserts `build_plan_confirm_prompt` presents the task_groups output for review and no longer directs the reviewer to the proposal and design. <!--#0190a7f427f77e2a-->
- `test_legacy_plan_step_still_renders_its_proposal_and_design` (function) — Asserts `_render_plan` still renders proposal, design, and task groups for archived flows holding the legacy output shape. <!--#17b6e13f6301539b-->
- `test_new_plan_step_renders_without_a_plan_wrapper` (function) — Asserts `_render_plan` renders the new wrapper-free output shape via `render_full` alone, without proposal/design rendering. <!--#96080a3278ba29eb-->
- `test_display_helpers_survive_for_the_legacy_render_path` (function) — Asserts `render_proposal` and `render_design` remain callable in the display module because the legacy render path still calls them. <!--#a5886694a33fdbbe-->
- `test_history_show_renders_a_legacy_plan_flow` (function) — End-to-end check that `history_cmd._show_plan_artifacts` prints non-empty output for a legacy-shaped PLAN step detail dict. <!--#5e10d7bdc0bee59f-->

### `tests/engine/test_prompt_dedup.py` (python) — Unit test suite for tianluo.engine.prompt_dedup.deduplicate_prompt_lines(), exhaustively verifying that repeated multi-line blocks in a prompt are collapsed to their first occurrence plus a content-hash marker across edge cases (empty/short input, custom min_block_lines, triple/adjacent/overlapping repeats, pre-existing markers, blank-line handling, and large-prompt performance). <!--#249f8dc68c973914|a7c86424c88e4fd0-->
- `_expected_marker` (function) — Test helper that computes the expected '[DUPLICATED CONTENT: ...]' marker string (with sha256 hash and truncated first/last lines) for a given block of lines. <!--#0d52f5093d78b812-->
- `TestDeduplicatePromptLines` (class) — Test class grouping all unit tests for the deduplicate_prompt_lines() function. <!--#0eb57bae48ebc839-->
  - `TestDeduplicatePromptLines.test_no_duplicates_returns_unchanged` (method) — Asserts a prompt with no repeated blocks is returned unchanged. <!--#9bcc6aa552c5ab0b-->
  - `TestDeduplicatePromptLines.test_empty_input` (method) — Asserts an empty string is returned as-is. <!--#a6b2ffed1ff9fd56-->
  - `TestDeduplicatePromptLines.test_single_line` (method) — Asserts a single-line prompt is returned unchanged. <!--#031fb7b819b20e5f-->
  - `TestDeduplicatePromptLines.test_two_lines` (method) — Asserts a two-line prompt (below the default min_block_lines) is returned unchanged. <!--#b400c52d14ffcc3e-->
  - `TestDeduplicatePromptLines.test_single_duplicate_block` (method) — Asserts a single repeated 3-line block keeps its first occurrence and replaces the second with a content-based marker while preserving surrounding text. <!--#44a862b1160a4686-->
  - `TestDeduplicatePromptLines.test_multiple_duplicate_blocks` (method) — Asserts multiple distinct repeated blocks are each deduplicated independently with separators preserved. <!--#d71c411d543a0310-->
  - `TestDeduplicatePromptLines.test_short_repeat_not_deduplicated` (method) — Asserts blocks shorter than the default min_block_lines (3) are left untouched. <!--#6d49f8ee57305ea5-->
  - `TestDeduplicatePromptLines.test_custom_min_block_lines` (method) — Asserts passing min_block_lines=2 deduplicates two-line repeated blocks. <!--#80306b0a30cb5d0f-->
  - `TestDeduplicatePromptLines.test_custom_min_block_lines_larger` (method) — Asserts a 3-line repeat is not deduplicated when min_block_lines=5. <!--#fdd778e913bfefb9-->
  - `TestDeduplicatePromptLines.test_triple_repeat` (method) — Asserts a thrice-repeated block keeps the first occurrence and replaces the other two with markers. <!--#77081aad94684931-->
  - `TestDeduplicatePromptLines.test_content_based_marker_correct` (method) — Asserts the generated marker references the correct first/last lines of the duplicated block. <!--#5c070ffd9ac5b08b-->
  - `TestDeduplicatePromptLines.test_adjacent_duplicate_blocks` (method) — Asserts duplicate blocks placed back-to-back with no separator are still deduplicated. <!--#80a89180fc40865c-->
  - `TestDeduplicatePromptLines.test_preserves_blank_lines` (method) — Asserts blank lines within non-duplicate content are preserved. <!--#0fbb125af53c6b91-->
  - `TestDeduplicatePromptLines.test_first_call_noop` (method) — Asserts a typical first-call prompt with no internal repetition is returned unchanged. <!--#c66d964c6b6337af-->
  - `TestDeduplicatePromptLines.test_realistic_retry_prompt` (method) — Asserts repeated spec content in a simulated retry prompt collapses to one full occurrence plus a marker. <!--#0e179612a9647ebe-->
  - `TestDeduplicatePromptLines.test_min_block_lines_one` (method) — Asserts min_block_lines=1 deduplicates single repeated lines. <!--#f0b2ce7ababbc158-->
  - `TestDeduplicatePromptLines.test_large_prompt_performance` (method) — Asserts dedup of a 5000-line prompt completes under 5 seconds and replaces the four redundant spec blocks. <!--#a8fe4eeaa11c250e-->
  - `TestDeduplicatePromptLines.test_dedup_with_retry_context_structure` (method) — End-to-end test that dedup works correctly on a prompt combining retry context with the original prompt (simulating _call_with_retry). <!--#94eb37f8784dc787-->
  - `TestDeduplicatePromptLines.test_existing_marker_not_deduplicated` (method) — Asserts pre-existing dedup markers are preserved and excluded from participating in a new dedup pass. <!--#477dc2918e55aa8f-->
  - `TestDeduplicatePromptLines.test_blank_line_blocks_not_deduplicated` (method) — Asserts blocks made entirely of blank lines are not deduplicated and all blanks are preserved. <!--#742a542d46a4acb0-->
  - `TestDeduplicatePromptLines.test_min_block_lines_zero_returns_unchanged` (method) — Asserts min_block_lines=0 returns the prompt unchanged (guarding against IndexError). <!--#d385c5a8ee30bafc-->
  - `TestDeduplicatePromptLines.test_min_block_lines_negative_returns_unchanged` (method) — Asserts a negative min_block_lines returns the prompt unchanged. <!--#760026df4029bb2a-->
  - `TestDeduplicatePromptLines.test_long_line_truncated_in_marker` (method) — Asserts first/last lines over 80 chars are truncated in the marker and full-length lines never appear. <!--#c5a6170c575b6cd5-->
  - `TestDeduplicatePromptLines.test_multi_retry_cross_pass_with_existing_markers` (method) — Asserts a multi-retry scenario where a later dedup pass correctly handles both prior markers and fresh duplicate content. <!--#53ac44829642075c-->
  - `TestDeduplicatePromptLines.test_min_block_lines_exceeds_total_lines` (method) — Asserts a min_block_lines larger than the total line count returns the prompt unchanged. <!--#20cc97ad8f10adf5-->
  - `TestDeduplicatePromptLines.test_source_replaced_lines_not_extended` (method) — Asserts matching does not extend through already-replaced source lines so repeated occurrences all reference the same source block. <!--#986ded3560b94989-->
  - `TestDeduplicatePromptLines.test_partial_overlap_blocks_produce_distinct_markers` (method) — Asserts two blocks sharing first/last lines but differing in the middle produce distinct markers disambiguated by content hash. <!--#1648d88b79197766-->

### `tests/engine/test_prompt_markers.py` (python) — Unit tests for the engine's prompt_markers helpers (wrap_user_content, wrap_user_section, inject_boundary, _marker_pair_present), verifying correct marker insertion/ordering, empty-input passthrough, idempotency against pre-existing markers, and that every engine step prompt carries exactly one properly-positioned template-end/user-content boundary separating the system role opener from the user/task content. <!--#f30442499e333064|20c4806bb0f244db-->
- `test_wrap_user_content_injects_marker_pair` (function) — Asserts wrap_user_content inserts both the template-end and user-content-begin markers in the right order while preserving the original header and task text. <!--#6aa7c18d1165d4e3-->
- `test_wrap_user_content_empty_user_passthrough` (function) — Verifies wrap_user_content returns the system text unchanged when the user content is empty. <!--#15c4e8d227ddfdd6-->
- `test_wrap_user_content_empty_prefix_passthrough` (function) — Verifies wrap_user_content returns the user text unchanged when the prefix is empty. <!--#a0fe7cc86c36cb74-->
- `test_wrap_user_content_idempotent_on_marker_in_prefix` (function) — Checks that re-wrapping already-marked text just appends the new content rather than injecting a second marker pair. <!--#2238ab85bb237da6-->
- `test_wrap_user_section_three_segment_order` (function) — Asserts wrap_user_section emits all three markers exactly once in the strict prefix→template-end→user-begin→user→user-end→suffix order. <!--#4484359185b10ae8-->
- `test_wrap_user_section_idempotent_on_already_wrapped` (function) — Confirms passing an already-wrapped string as the prefix concatenates inputs without injecting a second marker triple. <!--#72de1c722781e98d-->
- `test_wrap_user_section_idempotent_when_markers_in_user_content` (function) — Confirms wrap_user_section does not double-wrap when its user-content argument already contains a marker triple. <!--#84afc7317029f109-->
- `test_wrap_user_section_empty_prefix_and_suffix` (function) — Verifies wrap_user_section still emits the full three-marker record (no stray prefix/suffix) when prefix and suffix are empty. <!--#a929043e404bd6fb-->
- `test_wrap_user_section_empty_user_content_still_wraps` (function) — Verifies an empty middle segment is still wrapped with begin/end markers so the frontend distinguishes an empty bubble from no marker at all. <!--#1b950b27367105f3-->
- `test_marker_pair_present_helper` (function) — Tests _marker_pair_present returns true only for full three-segment text, rejecting empty, marker-less, and legacy two-segment strings. <!--#8d7d5c37165f0a92-->
- `test_wrap_user_section_does_not_affect_legacy_helpers` (function) — Ensures the legacy two-segment helpers (wrap_user_content, inject_boundary) still emit their two markers and never emit USER_CONTENT_END. <!--#9dc17855618a704b-->
- `test_inject_boundary_inserts_before_anchor` (function) — Asserts inject_boundary places the boundary markers immediately before the named anchor heading in the template. <!--#c42f29851b33a6a1-->
- `test_inject_boundary_missing_anchor_is_noop` (function) — Verifies inject_boundary leaves the template unchanged when the anchor text is absent. <!--#96e759f52dfef0e1-->
- `test_inject_boundary_idempotent` (function) — Checks that applying inject_boundary twice with the same anchor yields the same result as applying it once. <!--#38ea4851c588b911-->
- `test_all_step_prompts_have_exactly_one_marker_pair` (function) — Asserts every engine step prompt contains exactly one template-end and one user-content-begin marker in the correct order. <!--#84960131bcc258df-->
- `test_role_opener_is_in_prefix_segment` (function) — Asserts each step prompt's boilerplate role opener ("You are…") sits before the template-end marker so it collapses into the system-prompt chip. <!--#a3aa5e9e5c071832-->
- `test_user_content_anchor_is_in_suffix_segment` (function) — Asserts each step prompt's user/task-content anchor sits after the user-content-begin marker so it renders as an expanded user bubble. <!--#6eac6fa1141dcd64-->

### `tests/engine/test_retry_context_injection.py` (python) — Test module covering retry-context injection paths: that implement (and other) step handlers forward retry_count as external_attempt to LLMCaller, that _get_retry_context logs at WARNING on failure, that format_history_for_retry and extract_conversation_from_ndjson degrade gracefully on malformed NDJSON, that history is filtered by fix_iteration (with 0 as wildcard), and that the record APIs and ChatMessage persist/default the fix_iteration field for backward compatibility. <!--#8c341deb8fd5ccc2|ee7bd1f525282080-->
- `TestImplementPassesRetryCount` (class) — Test class verifying the implement_handler reads retry_count from step inputs and forwards it to LLMCaller as external_attempt (defaulting to 0 when absent). <!--#8048d112024f20a1-->
  - `TestImplementPassesRetryCount.test_implement_passes_retry_count` (method) — Asserts that on a RETRYING step with retry_count=2, implement_handler constructs LLMCaller with external_attempt=2. <!--#64c343a78061f0a7-->
  - `TestImplementPassesRetryCount.test_implement_defaults_retry_count_to_zero` (method) — Asserts that when inputs omit retry_count, implement_handler constructs LLMCaller with external_attempt=0. <!--#afd46b715da34fb9-->
- `TestGetRetryContextWarning` (class) — Test class verifying LLMCaller._get_retry_context returns None and logs at WARNING level (not debug) when format_history_for_retry raises. <!--#d86f13637d4353ff-->
  - `TestGetRetryContextWarning.test_logs_warning_on_exception` (method) — Patches format_history_for_retry to raise ValueError and asserts _get_retry_context returns None while emitting a WARNING-level 'Failed to get retry context' log record. <!--#b37aa704b0b0f7a8-->
- `_make_session` (function) — Test helper building a ChatSession with fixed flow/step/type ids around the given messages. <!--#c890988af505c899-->
- `TestFormatHistoryMalformedNDJSON` (class) — Test class verifying format_history_for_retry degrades gracefully — falling back to simplified content or partial context — when raw_json entries are malformed or unparseable rather than crashing. <!--#85fdc99b33657f17-->
  - `TestFormatHistoryMalformedNDJSON.test_malformed_raw_json_falls_back_to_content` (method) — Asserts that fully malformed raw_json falls back to the message's plain content without crashing. <!--#cd0acaf94c82409f-->
  - `TestFormatHistoryMalformedNDJSON.test_partial_valid_ndjson_returns_partial_context` (method) — Asserts that a mix of valid and malformed raw_json entries still yields the valid entries' text. <!--#5ac6398f2bf6c01c-->
  - `TestFormatHistoryMalformedNDJSON.test_completely_broken_raw_json_falls_back` (method) — Asserts that broken raw_json structure causes a graceful fallback to message content rather than an exception. <!--#124a6e28fffab860-->
- `TestExtractConversationFromNDJSONResilience` (class) — Test class verifying extract_conversation_from_ndjson skips malformed list items and string lines instead of failing. <!--#78a0a559d5c0499a-->
  - `TestExtractConversationFromNDJSONResilience.test_handles_non_dict_items_in_list` (method) — Asserts non-dict list items (strings, ints, None) are skipped while valid entries are parsed. <!--#12b0484c92a4374e-->
  - `TestExtractConversationFromNDJSONResilience.test_handles_empty_list` (method) — Asserts an empty list input returns an empty message list. <!--#d648c31f481a0b15-->
  - `TestExtractConversationFromNDJSONResilience.test_handles_items_missing_type` (method) — Asserts dict items lacking a 'type' key are skipped while typed entries are parsed. <!--#33a6fac6748671b8-->
  - `TestExtractConversationFromNDJSONResilience.test_handles_malformed_string_lines` (method) — Asserts malformed/incomplete JSON lines in string input are skipped, keeping valid parsed messages. <!--#64d022247508743d-->
- `TestFormatHistoryFixIterationBoundary` (class) — Test class verifying format_history_for_retry filters messages by current_fix_iteration, treating fix_iteration=0 as a wildcard and returning None when the filter drops every message. <!--#781d5538e79c189d-->
  - `TestFormatHistoryFixIterationBoundary._msg` (method) — Test helper constructing a ChatMessage with configurable content, role, attempt, fix_iteration, and timestamp. <!--#aa813529c0886178-->
  - `TestFormatHistoryFixIterationBoundary.test_filters_to_current_iteration_when_set` (method) — Asserts that with a non-zero current_fix_iteration, only matching-iteration messages are included. <!--#8010ccbb5616db35-->
  - `TestFormatHistoryFixIterationBoundary.test_zero_fix_iteration_messages_act_as_wildcard` (method) — Asserts legacy fix_iteration=0 messages are always included regardless of the current iteration. <!--#aef43291461e84c1-->
  - `TestFormatHistoryFixIterationBoundary.test_current_zero_means_no_filtering` (method) — Asserts that current_fix_iteration=0 disables iteration filtering so all messages are included. <!--#b21f40e63690c672-->
  - `TestFormatHistoryFixIterationBoundary.test_returns_none_when_filter_drops_everything` (method) — Asserts the function returns None when the iteration filter excludes every message. <!--#9d6661f405ffc450-->
  - `TestFormatHistoryFixIterationBoundary.test_default_argument_preserves_pre_upgrade_behavior` (method) — Asserts that omitting current_fix_iteration defaults to wildcard behavior, including all messages. <!--#9b8191699f1a637c-->
- `TestRecordAPIAcceptsFixIteration` (class) — Test class verifying record_prompt/record_response accept and persist a fix_iteration field on ChatMessages, defaulting to 0 for legacy callers. <!--#76014c42c7f56dc4-->
