  - `TestRecordAPIAcceptsFixIteration.test_record_response_persists_fix_iteration` (method) — Asserts record_response stores fix_iteration=4 on the recorded response message retrievable via get_step_history. <!--#8fd13f779b902c8a-->
  - `TestRecordAPIAcceptsFixIteration.test_record_prompt_default_fix_iteration_zero` (method) — Asserts record_prompt called without fix_iteration defaults the persisted message's fix_iteration to 0. <!--#ea5f1a8ba50f1a1b-->
- `TestChatMessageBackwardCompat` (class) — Test class verifying legacy ChatMessage records without a fix_iteration field deserialize with a default of 0. <!--#39ee94911957bfd0-->
  - `TestChatMessageBackwardCompat.test_from_dict_missing_fix_iteration_defaults_to_zero` (method) — Asserts ChatMessage.from_dict defaults fix_iteration to 0 for dicts lacking that key. <!--#930c9d0ad43821e7-->

### `tests/engine/test_retry_context_safety_cap.py` (python) — Regression test suite for the retry-context safety cap, verifying that spec-text dedup runs before any hard truncation, that the post-dedup `_post_dedup_safety_cap` fallback truncates history-head while preserving the new-prompt tail (including line-boundary, missing-marker/separator, over-limit tail, and retry-of-retry anchoring edge cases), that `_call_with_retry` wires the cap in only on retry paths, and that literal `\n` preprocessing lets dedup collapse JSON-embedded multi-line content. <!--#1790332ec1568fc4|3334ef73f5ac708b-->
- `_make_session` (function) — Test helper that wraps a list of ChatMessages in a ChatSession with fixed flow/step/type identifiers. <!--#c890988af505c899-->
- `_big_spec_block` (function) — Test helper that builds a deterministic ~130K-char multi-line spec text block to exercise dedup and the safety cap. <!--#db69d4f20851724e-->
- `TestRepeatedSpecNoTruncation` (class) — Test class asserting that format_history_for_retry() no longer applies a per-user-prompt hard truncation and that dedup collapses spec text repeated across attempts to below the post-dedup safety limit without warnings. <!--#ef7ccf957ca08eec-->
  - `TestRepeatedSpecNoTruncation.test_repeated_spec_not_truncated_by_format_history` (method) — Verifies that a >130K-char spec inside an old user prompt survives format_history_for_retry() intact with no 'hit safety limit' truncation warning. <!--#18f7b089758e973b-->
  - `TestRepeatedSpecNoTruncation.test_dedup_eliminates_repetition_below_safety_limit` (method) — Asserts that dedup substantially shrinks a doubly-repeated spec prompt below the safety limit, leaving the cap a no-op and the new-prompt tail intact. <!--#23a6af1e5ac7a8b0-->
- `TestPostDedupSafetyCap` (class) — Test class exercising _post_dedup_safety_cap() edge cases: no-op under limit or without the retry marker, head-truncation preserving the tail, oversized-tail preservation with a distinguishing warning, separator-missing warning, and line-boundary alignment of the kept body. <!--#cb08f8579056c2c1-->
  - `TestPostDedupSafetyCap.test_cap_noop_when_under_limit` (method) — Asserts the cap leaves a small marker/separator prompt unchanged when under the limit. <!--#e6ec454720c716fa-->
  - `TestPostDedupSafetyCap.test_cap_noop_when_no_history_marker` (method) — Asserts the cap refuses to truncate an oversized prompt that lacks the retry-history marker. <!--#4a70f2ed500af6db-->
  - `TestPostDedupSafetyCap.test_cap_truncates_history_head_preserves_tail` (method) — Feeds unique non-dedup-able history exceeding the limit and asserts the cap truncates the history head, strictly bounds length, preserves the new-prompt tail plus separator, and logs a 'Post-dedup safety cap triggered' warning. <!--#e28c56ac2f31af04-->
  - `TestPostDedupSafetyCap.test_cap_preserves_tail_even_when_tail_exceeds_limit` (method) — Asserts that when the tail alone exceeds the limit the cap keeps the tail intact (accepting over-limit size) and emits a distinguishing 'could not bound size / tail exceeds limit' warning instead of the generic triggered one. <!--#2b5374d19da21fc8-->
  - `TestPostDedupSafetyCap.test_cap_warns_when_separator_missing` (method) — Asserts that an oversized prompt with the marker but no separator is returned unchanged (cap cannot locate the tail) while logging an observable 'marker found but separator missing' warning. <!--#0fd2dc6b88544e44-->
  - `TestPostDedupSafetyCap.test_cap_kept_body_starts_at_line_boundary` (method) — Asserts the cap rounds its kept-body slice forward to a newline boundary so truncation never starts mid-line. <!--#9c9141937a8699b8-->
- `TestRetryOfRetryAnchoring` (class) — Regression test class guarding that on a retry-of-retry (prompt containing nested marker+separator pairs) the safety cap anchors on the OUTER separator via rfind, so the new-prompt tail survives. <!--#8ae7308c69b8784b-->
  - `TestRetryOfRetryAnchoring.test_cap_anchors_outer_separator_on_retry_of_retry` (method) — Builds a replayed attempt-0 effective_prompt with inner and outer separators, runs dedup + cap, and asserts the cap anchors on the outer separator, preserves the new-prompt tail, keeps the marker/separator invariant, and bounds length. <!--#9f44adcd3fcc8407-->
- `TestCallWithRetryInvokesSafetyCap` (class) — End-to-end test class pinning llm_caller wiring: _post_dedup_safety_cap is invoked after deduplicate_prompt_lines on the retry path (with a marker+separator-bearing prompt) but not on a first call. <!--#8014c71be777772b-->
  - `TestCallWithRetryInvokesSafetyCap.test_safety_cap_called_on_retry_path` (method) — Drives LLMCaller._call_with_retry with external_attempt=1 and a realistic retry context, spying to assert _post_dedup_safety_cap is called once with a prompt carrying both the marker and separator. <!--#8f9ab523ca927106-->
  - `TestCallWithRetryInvokesSafetyCap.test_safety_cap_not_called_on_first_call` (method) — Drives LLMCaller._call_with_retry on a first (non-retry) call and asserts _post_dedup_safety_cap is never invoked since dedup is also skipped. <!--#adeba7d83ea0e80d-->
- `TestDedupLiteralNewlinePreprocessing` (class) — Test class covering the backslash-n preprocessing that splits JSON-embedded literal '\n' content into real lines so dedup can collapse it. <!--#0bed9eec699b8c5e-->
  - `TestDedupLiteralNewlinePreprocessing.test_replace_lets_dedup_collapse_embedded_blocks` (method) — Asserts dedup misses repeated embedded multi-line tool_result content without the '\n' replace but hits it afterward. <!--#864099dc5971dea6-->
  - `TestDedupLiteralNewlinePreprocessing.test_replace_does_not_touch_real_newlines` (method) — Asserts the '\n' replace is idempotent on strings that already contain only real newlines. <!--#93cfc0631f8f5793-->
  - `TestDedupLiteralNewlinePreprocessing.test_replace_does_not_touch_other_escapes` (method) — Asserts the replace converts only literal '\n' and leaves other escapes like '\t', '\\', and '\"' intact. <!--#f6a6373e104c2e75-->

### `tests/engine/test_retry_continuation.py` (python) — Integration tests verifying step retry continuation: the state machine injects is_retry/retry_count metadata, LLMCaller's retry_mode ('continue' vs 'retry') shapes the effective prompt, and load_or_create_flow/init_flow handle FAILED, PAUSED, and COMPLETED flows idempotently. <!--#9a4fb4e872a17ea0|36f3a19a525e3552-->
- `TestLLMCallerRetryMode` (class) — Unit-test class covering `LLMCaller`'s `retry_mode` parameter — its default (`continue`), attribute storage, and how the effective `-p` prompt differs between `continue`, `retry`, and first-attempt runs. <!--#3d9bda1d61cbe383-->
  - `TestLLMCallerRetryMode.test_default_retry_mode_is_continue` (method) — Asserts LLMCaller defaults retry_mode to 'continue'. <!--#067bf61792d4d812-->
  - `TestLLMCallerRetryMode.test_retry_mode_stored` (method) — Asserts an explicit retry_mode argument is stored as an instance attribute. <!--#bd978db1dae1e8eb-->
  - `TestLLMCallerRetryMode.test_continue_mode_uses_continuation_prompt` (method) — Asserts that on a retry with `retry_mode="continue"`, the prompt sent to the runner combines the prior-conversation context with a "continue from where you left off / do not repeat work" instruction instead of re-sending the original prompt. <!--#4d4e208d58a12127-->
  - `TestLLMCallerRetryMode.test_retry_mode_uses_original_prompt` (method) — Asserts that on a retry with `retry_mode="retry"`, the prompt sent to the runner prepends the prior-conversation context and re-appends the original task prompt. <!--#0d4fd14e89ea1410-->
  - `TestLLMCallerRetryMode.test_first_attempt_unchanged` (method) — Asserts that on the first attempt (`external_attempt=0`) the original prompt is passed through verbatim and `_get_retry_context` is never called, regardless of `retry_mode`. <!--#43d0322c3a3a453a-->
  - `TestLLMCallerRetryMode.test_get_retry_context_passes_mode` (method) — Verifies _get_retry_context forwards self.retry_mode (and current_fix_iteration) to chat_history.format_history_for_retry with the expected positional and keyword arguments. <!--#cf8b23369f25273c-->
- `TestStateMachineRetryMetadata` (class) — Test class checking that retrying a step injects is_retry and retry_count into step.inputs while a first execution leaves that retry metadata absent. <!--#24e7d17c60bea8c3-->
  - `TestStateMachineRetryMetadata.test_retry_injects_metadata` (method) — Simulates the orchestration retry branch and asserts is_retry is True and retry_count is incremented to 1 in the step's inputs. <!--#395fd3da9b880b8f-->
  - `TestStateMachineRetryMetadata.test_first_execution_no_retry_metadata` (method) — Asserts a freshly created PENDING step has neither is_retry nor retry_count in its inputs before any retry. <!--#b5820ee42937640b-->
- `TestStateMachineLoadOrCreateFailedFlow` (class) — Test class confirming StateMachine.load_or_create_flow treats a FAILED flow as resumable (returns is_resumed=True) but creates a fresh flow for a COMPLETED one. <!--#2c7eedec8891082e-->
  - `TestStateMachineLoadOrCreateFailedFlow.test_load_or_create_returns_resumed_for_failed_flow` (method) — Verifies load_or_create_flow returns the existing FAILED flow with is_resumed=True. <!--#d1e69a33d3e120cc-->
  - `TestStateMachineLoadOrCreateFailedFlow.test_load_or_create_creates_new_for_completed_flow` (method) — Verifies load_or_create_flow ignores a COMPLETED flow and returns a newly created flow with is_resumed=False. <!--#e349352957d244f1-->
- `TestInitFlowIdempotency` (class) — Test class asserting StateMachine.init_flow is safe (idempotent) to call on FAILED, PAUSED, and COMPLETED flows, invoking _write_flow_meta and _record_baseline_commit each once. <!--#10ed9a79e04a3e98-->
  - `TestInitFlowIdempotency.test_init_flow_safe_for_failed_flow` (method) — Verifies init_flow on a FAILED flow calls _write_flow_meta and _record_baseline_commit exactly once each. <!--#328b8230301ffd8d-->
  - `TestInitFlowIdempotency.test_init_flow_safe_for_paused_flow` (method) — Verifies init_flow on a PAUSED flow calls _write_flow_meta and _record_baseline_commit exactly once each. <!--#d5d723c3f1adfcc3-->
  - `TestInitFlowIdempotency.test_init_flow_safe_for_completed_flow` (method) — Verifies init_flow on a COMPLETED flow calls _write_flow_meta and _record_baseline_commit exactly once each. <!--#901016ddd5a94054-->

### `tests/engine/test_retry_count_reset.py` (python) — Test module pinning the reset of the stale `retry_count` input at each new-LLM-call transition site — the `_reset_retry_counter_for_new_call` helper itself, plus the fix-loop, revision, and discovery-user-response paths — so a fresh prompt isn't discarded in favor of a retry-context wrapper. <!--#775b16fc72f3809c|ebae87be20cb5cb3-->
- `TestResetHelper` (class) — Tests for the `_reset_retry_counter_for_new_call` helper in isolation, covering both the present and absent cases. <!--#bcbf858bc82be8d0-->
  - `TestResetHelper.test_pops_retry_count_when_present` (method) — Asserts the helper removes `retry_count` from a step's inputs while leaving other input keys untouched. <!--#1bcf7e8fdf830fc1-->
  - `TestResetHelper.test_noop_when_absent` (method) — Asserts the helper is a safe no-op (no error, other keys kept) when `retry_count` is not present. <!--#d2eaa0f6ce2a10fb-->
- `_build_flow_with_implement_fix` (function) — Test fixture builder that constructs a flow with a completed IMPLEMENT step and a VERIFY_SPEC step in REVISION_NEEDED, seeding a given `retry_count`, to exercise the fix-loop transition. <!--#c2ce0596a5525e9f-->
- `TestFixLoopResetsRetryCount` (class) — Tests that `StateMachine._transition_to_fix` clears `retry_count` on the target step while preserving the fix-iteration inputs. <!--#59befedc430db817-->
  - `TestFixLoopResetsRetryCount.test_stale_retry_count_cleared_on_fix_iteration` (method) — Verifies a stale `retry_count` is removed and the fix-iteration flags (`is_fix_iteration`, `fix_instructions`) are still set after a fix transition. <!--#34c14025a92a2460-->
  - `TestFixLoopResetsRetryCount.test_no_retry_count_stays_absent_after_fix_iteration` (method) — Baseline check that a fix transition does not inject `retry_count` when none was present beforehand. <!--#c4b60ec891d14713-->
- `_build_flow_with_plan_revision` (function) — Test fixture builder that constructs a flow with a completed PLAN step and a CONFIRM step in REVISION_NEEDED, seeding a given `retry_count`, to exercise the revision transition. <!--#8be01dda26b7554b-->
- `TestRevisionResetsRetryCount` (class) — Tests that `StateMachine._transition_to_revision` clears `retry_count` on the revised step while preserving the revision inputs. <!--#0f399443c76f62e2-->
  - `TestRevisionResetsRetryCount.test_stale_retry_count_cleared_on_revision` (method) — Verifies a stale `retry_count` is removed and the revision flags (`is_revision`, `revision_feedback`) remain set after a revision transition. <!--#da275b0df18fbd65-->
- `TestDiscoveryUserResponseResetsRetryCount` (class) — Test class asserting that advancing a discovery round after a user reply clears the stale retry_count so the next CONTINUE_DISCOVERY_PROMPT (carrying user_response) is not discarded by LLMCaller's retry-context wrapping, checking both behavior and run.py source. <!--#b14fd3bbfd235586-->
  - `TestDiscoveryUserResponseResetsRetryCount.test_user_response_path_clears_stale_retry_count` (method) — Behavioral test that reproduces the run.py DISCOVERY+PAUSED user-response branch on a Step and asserts it sets user_response/resumed, pops retry_count, and transitions status to PENDING. <!--#a41613a6523dba64-->
  - `TestDiscoveryUserResponseResetsRetryCount.test_run_py_branch_source_does_the_reset` (method) — Source-level pin that inspects run.py's discovery user-response branch and asserts it still contains the inputs.pop("retry_count") call, guarding against a regression that silently removes the reset. <!--#371a3e876b4ce5ae-->

### `tests/engine/test_review_scope.py` (python) — End-to-end test suite for review-scope baseline capture and reconstruction, driving real temporary git repos (including submodules) to assert that a flow's own changes — dirty, deleted, renamed, binary, symlink, untracked, gitignored, typechanged and odd-spelling paths — are diffed with correct causal/deletion anchors, that pre-existing dirt stays out of scope, and that ambiguous cases (rewritten HEAD, corrupt blobs or descriptors, changed repo identity) degrade to a safe undecidable fallback rather than a silently empty diff. <!--#19b53a7b99247286|0dea8bafb001483e-->
- `_git` (function) — Test helper that runs a git subcommand in a given repo root with check=True and returns its stdout as text. <!--#86876f4a28e71bc5-->
- `_repo` (function) — Test fixture helper that builds a committed temporary git repo seeded with clean, dirty, deleted, renamable, binary, symlink and .gitignore fixtures covering the file kinds review scoping must handle. <!--#5c27173fdc05956b-->
- `test_baseline_descriptor_round_trip_and_runtime_blob` (function) — Asserts baseline capture classifies tracked/untracked files as git- or blob-stored, survives JSON round-trip via ReviewBaseline.from_dict, stores exact blob bytes, and leaves the user's git status untouched. <!--#1cb422e1111bb4f3-->
- `test_full_diff_excludes_preexisting_dirty` (function) — Verifies a full-scope reconstruction reports only the flow's own edits — pre-existing dirty, untracked and deleted files stay out of changed_paths and the unified diff — and writes the diff to the artifact path with causal anchors. <!--#9c194aa3760cc6fc-->
- `test_head_advanced_by_flow_commits_still_reconstructs` (function) — Asserts that flow commits advancing HEAD past the baseline (as the IMPLEMENT merge path does) still reconstruct exactly, covering both committed and later uncommitted changes. <!--#16f6236908d1258d-->
- `test_head_rewritten_off_the_baseline_is_undecidable` (function) — Asserts that rewritten history no longer descending from the baseline commit (amend/rebase/reset) degrades to the safe undecidable fallback with an empty diff rather than diffing blindly. <!--#6b6a6242826eb7f9-->
- `test_unrelated_head_relation_failure_degrades_to_undecidable` (function) — Asserts that an inconclusive ancestry probe (_is_ancestor returning None) also degrades to undecidable with a 'could not relate' diagnostic. <!--#4880c2ed669acd97-->
- `test_dirty_deleted_renamed_symlink_binary_and_untracked_restore_on_resume` (function) — Asserts baseline capture records the right storage kind for dirty, deleted, renamed, binary, symlink and untracked entries, and that a fresh manager resuming from the serialized descriptor reconstructs an empty change set. <!--#5f6bb281661aeef0-->
- `test_diff_covers_rename_symlink_binary_and_untracked` (function) — Asserts the reconstructed diff renders renames, binary-file markers, symlink retargets and new untracked files, all appearing in changed_paths. <!--#82fcd5c602cf717b-->
- `test_corrupt_blob_and_repository_identity_are_undecidable` (function) — Asserts a tampered baseline blob (integrity failure) and a changed repository identity each force the undecidable fallback with a matching diagnostic. <!--#71cd2d3bedbd188f-->
- `test_incremental_undecidable_falls_back_to_reconstructable_full` (function) — Asserts resolve() falls back from an undecidable incremental baseline to the still-reconstructable full implementation baseline, flagging fallback_from_incremental while keeping a real diff. <!--#59582c800b694d5b-->
- `test_missing_or_corrupt_descriptor_never_becomes_empty_diff` (function) — Asserts a corrupted descriptor.json yields an undecidable scope with a 'descriptor' diagnostic instead of a silently empty diff. <!--#7d06c9649e8cb633-->
- `test_deleted_code_line_goes_to_deletion_anchor_space` (function) — Asserts deletion-only changes populate deletion_anchors and leave causal_anchors empty, so old-side line numbers can never validate a current-file `path:N` citation. <!--#773663cf6c54d56a-->
- `test_deleted_and_added_lines_stay_in_separate_anchor_spaces` (function) — Asserts a replace hunk records new-side ranges in causal_anchors and old-side ranges in deletion_anchors as independent line-number spaces. <!--#21139d5866503143-->
- `_repo_with_submodule` (function) — Test helper that builds a repo containing a committed file-protocol git submodule at `vendor` for the submodule scoping tests. <!--#707019e59043e6ca-->
- `test_submodule_commit_without_staging_gitlink_is_in_scope` (function) — Asserts a commit made inside a submodule without staging the superproject gitlink still enters scope, with anchors keyed by the inner path rather than the bare submodule path. <!--#5eed30b4100cd689-->
- `test_submodule_worktree_edit_without_commit_is_in_scope` (function) — Asserts an uncommitted worktree edit inside a submodule enters scope under the same inner-path anchor contract as the commit case. <!--#6ff92aded645f26c-->
- `test_preexisting_dirty_submodule_excluded_and_flow_edit_isolated` (function) — Asserts pre-existing dirty submodule content is excluded from the baseline diff while the flow's later delta on the same and other inner files is reported under both the gitlink and inner paths. <!--#a202b223ef753252-->
- `test_submodule_inner_deletion_is_a_citable_changed_path` (function) — Asserts a deleted inner submodule file is listed in changed_paths (so path-level grounding works) even though it carries no current-side causal anchor. <!--#069f6e9a5923cf1b-->
- `test_submodule_unstaged_typechange_renders_an_inner_hunk` (function) — Asserts an unstaged symlink-to-file typechange inside a submodule — invisible in the index sha and mode — is still detected, rendered as an inner hunk, and anchored. <!--#7868026035f9ed28-->
- `test_gitignored_declared_path_stays_in_scope` (function) — Asserts a git-ignored file the flow wrote is invisible to plain reconstruction but becomes a citable changed path when passed via declared_paths, without fabricating line anchors. <!--#bd7f05fdd52c154b-->
- `test_declared_path_does_not_re_add_an_unchanged_tracked_file` (function) — Asserts declared_paths cannot widen the scope with files the baseline proves unchanged or that do not exist. <!--#5d4d8090c1dd647a-->
- `test_declared_spelling_that_resolves_stops_the_trimmed_fallback` (function) — Asserts that a declared path whose exact spelling (including a trailing space) resolves to a real file is used as-is, with the whitespace-trimmed fallback only applying when the reported spelling resolves to nothing. <!--#264ece0efc3c034d-->
- `test_declared_backslash_spelling_resolves_before_separator_fallback` (function) — Asserts that a declared path containing a literal POSIX backslash is resolved verbatim first, with the Windows-style separator rewrite used only as a fallback when the literal spelling names nothing. <!--#288f0ca1ed89cc72-->
- `test_git_visible_literal_backslash_path_is_captured_and_diffed` (function) — Verifies a root-level file literally named `tianluo\state\note.py` is captured and diffed as an ordinary file rather than misread as excluded runtime state, while real `tianluo/state/` paths stay excluded. <!--#99ad2a5af98a99a9-->
- `test_causal_ranges_classify_by_marker_not_content_prefix` (function) — Unit-tests _causal_ranges on a hand-written diff to prove hunk lines are classified by their leading marker, so content starting with `--`/`++` does not skew old- or new-side line numbering. <!--#5b2cc2e97d663b5b-->
- `test_complete_clean_honors_persisted_pending_closure_marker` (function) — Asserts SelfCheckRoundController honors a persisted next_scope_mode marker with no active round, demanding a full closure round and clearing the marker only when that round starts. <!--#c3c9ea6e9be2d097-->
- `test_mid_round_full_fallback_does_not_credit_a_clean_full_round` (function) — Asserts a round that degraded to full mid-way is not credited as the mandatory clean full round, leaving the closure round still owed. <!--#5cb961a90572a231-->
- `test_pass_one_full_fallback_is_credited_as_a_full_round` (function) — Asserts a round that degraded to full before any pass ran genuinely reviewed the full diff and is counted toward completed_full_rounds. <!--#9e37648917909757-->
- `test_legacy_round_without_accounting_mode_uses_executing_mode` (function) — Asserts rounds persisted before round_scope_mode existed fall back to their recorded executing mode so a resume does not rewrite the path underway. <!--#041b17d07c85e7f3-->
- `test_complete_clean_without_active_round_or_marker_advances` (function) — Asserts complete_clean() returns False (advance onward) when there is neither an active round nor a pending closure marker. <!--#74313923cb70f426-->
- `test_constructing_a_controller_does_not_materialize_round_state` (function) — Asserts constructing and read-probing a SelfCheckRoundController leaves the self_check_review key absent — so resumed multi-pass chains keep their pass index — until the first real mutation publishes state. <!--#7f572bb4ccaa3c16-->
- `test_force_full_publishes_state_on_a_fresh_context` (function) — Asserts force_full() publishes self_check_review with the given force_full_reason even on an empty context. <!--#4b289fee61b83897-->
- `test_plain_diff_terminates_missing_newline_lines_and_keeps_anchors` (function) — Unit-tests _render_plain_file_diff to ensure a baseline last line lacking a trailing newline is still terminated in the rendered diff and does not corrupt the causal/deletion anchor line numbers. <!--#f3aae8779eb9a898-->
- `test_incremental_scope_carries_whole_task_anchors` (function) — Checks that an incremental round keeps its own attention on the fix delta while additionally exposing the whole-task domain (task baseline id, changed paths, anchors, artifact) as a separate, unmerged evidence set. <!--#a2763ae0f56ea08a-->
- `test_incremental_scope_names_delta_paths_that_carry_earlier_work` (function) — Verifies `prior_work_paths` uses the two baseline snapshots — not line anchors — to flag anchor-less binary paths that earlier implement/fix work already touched. <!--#5a7685db4939f8cf-->
- `test_path_the_fix_alone_produced_carries_no_earlier_work` (function) — Confirms a path created only by the fix appears in the delta but is absent from `prior_work_paths`, since neither baseline snapshot holds it. <!--#5729df15e9a3eb6b-->
- `test_full_round_names_delta_paths_present_at_the_last_full_round` (function) — Checks that on a full round with a pinned fix-delta baseline, `prior_work_paths` names only the delta paths that already differed at that fix baseline. <!--#f1485f33c09d3a0f-->
- `test_full_scope_carries_no_separate_whole_task_domain` (function) — Asserts a full round, which already diffs from the implementation baseline, exposes no redundant second whole-task domain (`task_scope_available` is False and task fields are empty). <!--#27498fe26da31cc7-->
- `test_incremental_scope_on_the_implementation_baseline_adds_no_second_domain` (function) — Asserts an incremental round whose own baseline is the implementation baseline stays decidable but carries no duplicate whole-task domain. <!--#218ce390641a9e06-->
- `test_undecidable_fallback_still_carries_no_whole_task_domain` (function) — Verifies that when a corrupt fix-baseline blob forces the incremental→full fallback, the round stays decidable and attaches no separate whole-task domain since its own diff already is one. <!--#b7f440db3144b7e4-->
- `test_unrebuildable_whole_task_domain_falls_back_to_full` (function) — Verifies that losing the whole-task domain (broken or absent implementation baseline) routes through the same full-scope fallback and degrades to `undecidable`, with a diagnostic naming the whole-task evidence domain. <!--#bc24df3359dfdfa2-->
- `test_whole_task_fallback_stays_decidable_when_the_implementation_rebuilds` (function) — Confirms the ordinary fallback — broken fix baseline but intact implementation baseline — yields a decidable full scope covering the whole task with no relaxation. <!--#4ec3ccd7aa7d6597-->
- `test_fallback_diagnostic_names_the_domain_that_actually_failed` (function) — Asserts `fallback_cause` and the diagnostic distinguish a broken fix baseline (`fix_baseline`) from a broken or missing whole-task baseline (`task_baseline`) instead of blaming a healthy snapshot. <!--#2834dfa800009405-->
- `test_no_fallback_leaves_the_cause_empty` (function) — Checks that a healthy incremental round reports `fallback_from_incremental` False and an empty `fallback_cause`. <!--#bad134c3f2071112-->
- `test_whole_task_domain_keeps_deletion_anchors_in_their_own_space` (function) — Verifies whole-task deletion anchors are exposed via `task_deletion_anchors` and kept out of `task_causal_anchors`. <!--#09c5169f0e1b5357-->
- `test_full_scope_carries_the_fix_delta_since_the_last_full_round` (function) — Checks that a full round attaches a purely descriptive fix-delta annotation (baseline id, changed paths, anchors) isolating hunks added since the last full round, without narrowing the round or writing extra on-disk diffs. <!--#629f531ad329cdc8-->
- `test_unrebuildable_fix_delta_never_degrades_a_full_round` (function) — Asserts an unrebuildable fix-delta baseline leaves the full round decidable and intact, merely marking the annotation unavailable with a diagnostic. <!--#ef305d25a1956ebd-->
- `test_fix_baseline_after_full_round_follows_the_persisted_marker` (function) — Verifies `earliest_fix_baseline_after_full_round` picks the first fix baseline captured after the persisted `full_round_fix_head` marker, and returns None once the marker reaches the newest entry. <!--#e70e2358b4e38f67-->
- `test_fix_baseline_after_full_round_omits_a_missing_earliest_baseline` (function) — Asserts a later fix baseline never substitutes for an unloadable earlier one — the annotation is dropped rather than making a false "already present" claim. <!--#60b7f6e6dc53d8f6-->
- `test_diff_path_quoting_round_trips_every_unrenderable_name` (function) — Checks `quote_diff_path`/`unquote_diff_path` round-trip exactly for names containing any line-ending-like character, quotes, or backslashes while keeping diff headers on one line and leaving ordinary paths untouched. <!--#4d3522f31abfe345-->
- `test_degraded_inner_note_is_split_out_under_its_own_path` (function) — Verifies a gitlink diff gives every inner submodule label its own `diff --git` header so a degraded "baseline content unavailable" note is split under its own path rather than riding inside the parent or a sibling section. <!--#a6f11e6f64a72fb4-->
- `test_line_range_algebra_merges_adjacent_and_drops_unusable_pairs` (function) — Exercises `normalize_line_ranges`, `union_line_ranges`, and `subtract_line_ranges` for merging adjacent ranges, dropping malformed pairs, and handling a missing subtrahend. <!--#603134ef2a9b5b49-->
- `test_intersect_line_ranges_clips_to_the_overlap` (function) — Exercises `intersect_line_ranges`, confirming it clips to the overlap, merges adjacent survivors, and yields nothing when either side is missing so an annotation can never widen its domain. <!--#006e3e5fd60580c0-->
- `test_submodule_inner_binary_touched_before_the_fix_is_earlier_work` (function) — Verifies prior-work detection looks through the parent gitlink manifest so a submodule-inner binary rewritten by both IMPLEMENT and the fix is credited as earlier work, unlike one the fix alone added. <!--#3a749abef5c96b15-->
- `test_submodule_inner_path_the_fix_alone_touched_carries_no_earlier_work` (function) — Confirms a submodule-inner path first touched by the fix appears as changed but contributes no `prior_work_paths` entry. <!--#cb91a508cc420bf9-->
- `test_edge_whitespace_path_is_quoted_so_a_stripped_citation_recovers_it` (function) — Asserts paths with leading/trailing whitespace are rendered as quoted tokens that survive a citation's `str.strip()`, while interior-space paths stay verbatim. <!--#4e5ce5e872c4a8e9-->
- `test_malformed_quoted_token_is_rejected_not_repaired` (function) — Verifies `decode_quoted_diff_path` rejects malformed tokens (returning None, with the lenient reader keeping them verbatim) while still decoding well-formed ones, including octal escapes for non-UTF-8 bytes. <!--#f9c090113f35c5eb-->
- `test_declared_literal_backslash_is_not_read_as_runtime_state` (function) — function test_declared_literal_backslash_is_not_read_as_runtime_state <!--#de4eb6464fb72cb6-->
- `test_non_utf8_path_byte_reconstructs_instead_of_going_undecidable` (function) — Verifies a Git-visible non-UTF-8 path byte survives capture, descriptor reload, diff rendering (as an ASCII C-quoted token), and section splitting instead of collapsing into an undecidable empty scope. <!--#a88401b235408fe8-->
- `test_non_utf8_path_byte_survives_every_channel_up_to_self_check` (function) — Extends the non-UTF-8 path guarantee end-to-end through the flow context, `PersistenceManager` save/load round trip, scope reconstruction, and the SELF_CHECK scope history record. <!--#62dfb64b8b71c628-->

### `tests/engine/test_review_scope_cleanup.py` (python) — Test suite covering the full lifecycle of review-scope snapshot reclaim — that the engine deletes a flow's baselines only on its terminal COMPLETED transition (never mid-flow, on FAILED, or across flows), that state is persisted before reclaim so a failed save leaves a resumable flow with its snapshots, that unsafe flow ids are refused by `discard_snapshots` while `discard_flow_snapshots` stays non-raising and idempotent, and that the non-engine disposition channels (`salvage`, `end-session` resumable clear, worktree archiving) exclude, spare, or reclaim the store correctly under takeover and failure conditions. <!--#bfd296f8ced2029e|d101410e08471f82-->
- `_flow_id` (function) — Test helper that mints a unique synthetic flow id string of the form `flow-<12 hex chars>`. <!--#8c9debd58072ef99-->
- `_seed_snapshots` (function) — Test helper that materializes a realistic review-scope snapshot store (an `implementation-*` descriptor plus a content blob) under a flow's `ReviewScopeManager.root` and returns that path. <!--#6fdeb21fdc4c8a53-->
- `_run_flow` (function) — Test helper that drives a `StateMachine` flow to a terminal state by repeatedly running the current step and transitioning, bounded by `max_steps`. <!--#7a988dbbcce6223c-->
- `_register_passing_handlers` (function) — Test helper that registers a handler returning `StepStatus.COMPLETED` for every `StepType`, so a flow runs end-to-end without real step work. <!--#a70d659dd5e5a1ed-->
- `TestEngineTerminalReclaim` (class) — Tests that the engine reclaims a flow's review-scope snapshots exactly on its terminal COMPLETED transition — not mid-flow, not on FAILED (still retryable), never another flow's store, and never failing the flow if the reclaim raises. <!--#24aaa6ed7c785a3a-->
  - `TestEngineTerminalReclaim.test_completed_flow_reclaims_its_snapshots` (method) — Asserts a flow that runs to COMPLETED has its seeded snapshot store deleted. <!--#06e71678052f9995-->
  - `TestEngineTerminalReclaim.test_failed_flow_keeps_its_snapshots` (method) — Asserts a flow driven to FAILED by an exhausted fix loop keeps its baselines, because a FAILED flow can still be resumed as a retry. <!--#c30743f9e7120f8f-->
  - `TestEngineTerminalReclaim.test_mid_flow_transitions_keep_the_snapshots` (method) — Asserts a single non-terminal step transition leaves the flow RUNNING and its snapshot store intact. <!--#45fc3d242151d675-->
  - `TestEngineTerminalReclaim.test_reclaim_touches_only_the_terminating_flow` (method) — Asserts the terminal reclaim deletes only the completing flow's store while a second flow's snapshots and descriptor survive untouched. <!--#43b128c2fa243398-->
  - `TestEngineTerminalReclaim.test_reclaim_failure_does_not_fail_the_flow` (method) — Asserts a `discard_snapshots` OSError is swallowed so the flow still lands COMPLETED. <!--#08a0d5a60a7cc15d-->
- `TestReclaimOrdering` (class) — Tests that the terminal flow state is persisted to disk *before* baselines are reclaimed, so a failed save leaves a resumable flow with its snapshots intact (leaking disk beats irrecoverable loss). <!--#9f26f1217d415e63-->
  - `TestReclaimOrdering.test_a_failing_terminal_save_leaves_the_snapshots_intact` (method) — Asserts that when only the COMPLETED `save_flow` raises OSError, the propagated error leaves the still-resumable flow's snapshot store on disk. <!--#a554c0dbc9173b5f-->
  - `TestReclaimOrdering.test_run_loop_fallback_saves_before_reclaiming` (method) — Asserts `run._complete_flow_via_fallback` only flips status (destroying nothing) and that the run loop's save-then-`_reclaim_review_snapshots` order is what removes the store. <!--#704271e25d108812-->
  - `TestReclaimOrdering.test_surviving_resumable_snapshot_keeps_the_baselines` (method) — Asserts that when a swallowed `unlink` failure leaves the resumable snapshot on disk, `_reclaim_review_snapshots` spares the baselines the flow could still resume into. <!--#8225f6f3238c3577-->
- `TestReclaimSafety` (class) — Tests the path-safety contract of snapshot reclaim: unsafe flow ids raise `ValueError` and cannot escape to sibling directories, while the module helper `discard_flow_snapshots` never raises and reports idempotently whether anything was removed. <!--#deec48ffcfd9e9cd-->
  - `TestReclaimSafety.test_unsafe_flow_ids_are_refused` (method) — Parametrized assertion that `discard_snapshots` raises `ValueError` for traversal, nested, empty, hidden, and whitespace-bearing flow ids. <!--#29719603b36c599d-->
  - `TestReclaimSafety.test_unsafe_flow_id_cannot_reach_a_sibling_directory` (method) — Asserts a `../review-scopes` flow id raises rather than deleting the shared parent holding another flow's store. <!--#1ed62b8dad4c8544-->
  - `TestReclaimSafety.test_module_helper_never_raises` (method) — Asserts `discard_flow_snapshots` converts an unsafe flow id into a `False` return instead of an exception. <!--#1c992a0a41539e14-->
  - `TestReclaimSafety.test_module_helper_reports_whether_anything_was_removed` (method) — Asserts `discard_flow_snapshots` returns `True` when it deletes a store and `False` on a repeat call, making the reclaim idempotent. <!--#94187526c3dd6e65-->
- `TestDispositionChannels` (class) — Tests the non-engine channels that retire a flow for good — `salvage`, `end-session` resumable clear, and worktree archiving — covering snapshot exclusion from the permanent archive, the ownership re-read that spares baselines on takeover, and the FAIL row it surfaces. <!--#bbe23e68f09377ad-->
  - `TestDispositionChannels.test_salvage_reclaims_the_salvaged_flow` (method) — Asserts `salvage_cmd._archive_session` reclaims the salvaged flow's snapshot store. <!--#bcf406d8275d830a-->
  - `TestDispositionChannels.test_end_session_worktree_clear_reclaims` (method) — Asserts `end_session_cmd._clear_resumable` deletes the named flow's snapshot store. <!--#99fdd024854d2421-->
  - `TestDispositionChannels.test_worktree_archive_never_carries_the_snapshots_into_the_copy` (method) — Asserts worktree archiving passes the snapshot store via `exclude_relpaths` (with the live store still present at copy time) so the permanent archive never receives it, while the reclaim still lands afterwards. <!--#e511c0d7f558b183-->
  - `TestDispositionChannels.test_worktree_archive_excludes_snapshots_when_the_reclaim_fails` (method) — Asserts that with the reclaim stubbed to fail, the archive still excludes only this flow's store — sparing the live copy, a second flow's baselines, ordinary WIP files, and a same-named decoy directory nested elsewhere. <!--#11a4b31073f0d731-->
  - `TestDispositionChannels.test_end_session_without_a_flow_id_reclaims_nothing` (method) — Asserts `_clear_resumable(root, None)` leaves existing snapshot stores untouched. <!--#b79df8435b716a1d-->
  - `TestDispositionChannels.test_takeover_during_the_snapshot_clear_spares_the_baselines` (method) — Asserts that when another host steals the session claim mid-clear, `_clear_resumable` re-reads ownership, returns `False`, and leaves the re-owned flow's baselines intact. <!--#599b1f4c3e7edd08-->
  - `TestDispositionChannels.test_a_held_claim_still_reclaims_the_baselines` (method) — Asserts that with the session claim still held, `_clear_resumable` returns `True` and removes the snapshot store. <!--#011a9059f3bbec57-->
  - `TestDispositionChannels.test_main_session_cleanup_reports_the_spared_baselines` (method) — Asserts `_archive_main_session` records a FAIL result row (not a silent OK) when a mid-step takeover forces it to spare the baselines. <!--#53676fc8ef62b384-->
- `_git` (function) — Test helper that runs a `git` subcommand in a given directory with output captured and non-zero exit raised. <!--#4bdbf4ef339f050b-->
- `TestCommandContractAfterReclaim` (class) — Tests that `luo review-scope diff` distinguishes a reclaimed-baseline flow (exit 5 with a "reclaimed" message, including history-only flows) from a genuinely unknown flow (exit 3). <!--#a51326de96809303-->
  - `TestCommandContractAfterReclaim.test_reclaimed_flow_reports_cleaned_with_exit_five` (method) — Asserts that in a real git repo the diff command succeeds before `discard_snapshots` and afterwards exits 5 reporting "reclaimed". <!--#0a4c84c3c95528b8-->
  - `TestCommandContractAfterReclaim.test_history_only_flow_reports_cleaned_not_flow_not_found` (method) — Asserts a flow surviving only as a `history/` record — evicted from the single active engine.json slot — still reports the actionable reclaimed error (exit 5) rather than not-found. <!--#5e6fd3bbe287ecd7-->
  - `TestCommandContractAfterReclaim.test_genuinely_unknown_flow_still_reports_not_found` (method) — Asserts a flow id with no trace anywhere still exits 3 (flow not found). <!--#994959ce4a79ef1e-->
- `TestSnapshotRetirementGatesTheReclaim` (class) — Tests that baselines are dropped only once the resumable snapshot is confirmed retired — across the engine COMPLETED landing, `end-session`, and `salvage` — since a surviving snapshot keeps the flow resumable into a SELF_CHECK round that needs them. <!--#178bb81101c35e79-->
  - `TestSnapshotRetirementGatesTheReclaim.test_engine_completion_keeps_baselines_when_the_snapshot_survives` (method) — Asserts that when the resumable snapshot's `unlink` fails on the COMPLETED save, the flow still completes but keeps both the snapshot and its baselines. <!--#4d88b7d9543b4785-->
  - `TestSnapshotRetirementGatesTheReclaim.test_end_session_keeps_baselines_when_the_snapshot_survives` (method) — Asserts `_clear_resumable` returns `False` and spares the store when `clear_resumable_snapshot` reports the snapshot survived. <!--#a9afd0f3d4486bc3-->
  - `TestSnapshotRetirementGatesTheReclaim.test_salvage_keeps_baselines_when_the_snapshot_survives` (method) — Asserts `salvage_cmd._archive_session` still succeeds but leaves the baselines when the resumable snapshot could not be retired. <!--#787a3b5cd8a6bdc5-->
  - `TestSnapshotRetirementGatesTheReclaim.test_salvage_reclaims_when_the_snapshot_is_retired` (method) — Asserts salvage does remove the snapshot store in the normal case where the resumable snapshot is retired successfully. <!--#8076bf7786732170-->

### `tests/engine/test_review_scope_lookup.py` (python) — Unit tests for `ReviewScopeManager` baseline lookup — role resolution (implementation vs fix, active round, history fallback), every reportable baseline status (ok, not-captured, unavailable, corrupt, missing, cleaned), store-scan recovery when flow context is lost, read-only `reconstruct(write_artifact=False)`, and the diff-view helpers for section splitting, path-filter normalization, and `--stat` output. <!--#d38c0b1737763497|70078a2e61ccb210-->
- `_git` (function) — Test helper that runs a git subcommand in the given repository root with output captured and returns its stdout. <!--#86876f4a28e71bc5-->
- `_repo` (function) — Test helper that creates a throwaway git repository under tmp_path with a .gitignore and two committed Python files, returning its root path. <!--#473669652568910b-->
- `_scope_context` (function) — Test helper that wraps keyword arguments into a flow-context dict under the `review_scope` key. <!--#8c6e904da07b5953-->
- `TestBaselineLookup` (class) — Test class covering `ReviewScopeManager.lookup_baseline` role resolution (implementation vs fix, active round, history fallback) and every baseline status it can report — ok, not-captured, unavailable, corrupt/misfiled descriptors, and reclaimed store — plus store-scan fallback and `list_baselines` ordering. <!--#419a47eae04c7cd1-->
  - `TestBaselineLookup.test_implementation_role_resolves_declared_baseline` (method) — Asserts the implementation role resolves the baseline declared in flow context with status ok. <!--#5778e5ed7e3838a6-->
  - `TestBaselineLookup.test_fix_role_takes_the_active_round_baseline` (method) — Asserts an active self-check round's own baseline wins for the fix role, rather than falling through to the uncovered-fix search. <!--#149ceb1a73da8076-->
  - `TestBaselineLookup.test_fix_role_falls_back_to_earliest_unreviewed` (method) — Asserts that with no active round the fix role resolves to the earliest unreviewed fix baseline in history. <!--#d66354a339f425be-->
  - `TestBaselineLookup.test_full_round_does_not_hijack_the_fix_role` (method) — Asserts a full-scope round anchored on the implementation baseline does not override the fix role's own latest fix baseline. <!--#2fcd4923e55d1d3e-->
  - `TestBaselineLookup.test_missing_fix_baseline_is_not_captured` (method) — Asserts a fix lookup with no fix baseline recorded reports status not-captured and ok=False. <!--#f3ea7d3ea71aafd8-->
  - `TestBaselineLookup.test_unavailable_capture_is_reported_with_its_diagnostic` (method) — Asserts an explicitly unavailable baseline resolves to status unavailable carrying its capture diagnostic. <!--#a2f6b8a6271d1dd0-->
  - `TestBaselineLookup.test_failed_capture_without_a_descriptor_is_not_read_as_reclaimed` (method) — Asserts a state-machine-synthesized `available=False` record with no on-disk descriptor reports unavailable with its diagnostic instead of being mistaken for cleanup. <!--#e7d22220ee7e4d59-->
  - `TestBaselineLookup.test_failed_fix_capture_is_reported_from_the_history_record` (method) — Asserts a failed fix capture surfaces the diagnostic stored in its `fix_baseline_history` entry rather than the empty latest record. <!--#5c845c56d40ec66a-->
  - `TestBaselineLookup.test_reclaimed_store_is_distinguishable_from_never_captured` (method) — Asserts that removing the whole scope store yields status cleaned (not not-captured) while still naming the baseline id. <!--#556222ef45793526-->
  - `TestBaselineLookup.test_corrupt_descriptor_in_a_live_store_is_not_reported_as_reclaimed` (method) — Asserts a truncated descriptor in a surviving store reports unavailable/corrupt rather than cleaned. <!--#c0d68501afde8225-->
  - `TestBaselineLookup.test_descriptor_of_another_flow_is_corrupt_not_usable` (method) — Asserts a descriptor owned by a different flow is rejected as corrupt by lookup, load, store scan, and reconstruction rather than rendered as this flow's scope. <!--#75e20a3ea9eb4717-->
  - `TestBaselineLookup.test_descriptor_under_a_foreign_id_is_corrupt_not_usable` (method) — Asserts a descriptor whose recorded id disagrees with its directory is treated as corrupt while intact sibling baselines still load. <!--#ffa28de086012a4b-->
  - `TestBaselineLookup.test_removed_descriptor_in_a_live_store_is_not_reported_as_reclaimed` (method) — Asserts deleting one baseline directory reports that baseline as unavailable/missing while its siblings still resolve ok. <!--#6c4f13f40f8d9c6b-->
  - `TestBaselineLookup.test_lost_flow_record_resolves_from_the_store` (method) — Asserts that with no flow context at all, both roles resolve by scanning the self-describing descriptors on disk. <!--#e337551b6b8e31c3-->
  - `TestBaselineLookup.test_lost_flow_record_and_lost_store_reads_as_cleaned` (method) — Asserts that losing both the flow context and the store yields status cleaned. <!--#ef26b802f78076db-->
  - `TestBaselineLookup.test_list_baselines_is_ordered_and_empty_without_a_store` (method) — Asserts `list_baselines` returns an empty list before any capture and afterwards lists baselines in capture order. <!--#49ceccefdcc94548-->
- `TestReadOnlyReconstruct` (class) — Test class verifying that `reconstruct(write_artifact=False)` produces the diff without touching the store, while the default call still writes the artifact file. <!--#3d63b5ad2c2e5137-->
  - `TestReadOnlyReconstruct.test_write_artifact_false_leaves_no_trace` (method) — Asserts a read-only reconstruct returns the diff with an empty artifact path and leaves the store tree byte-for-byte unchanged. <!--#8af13d2cc38368b2-->
  - `TestReadOnlyReconstruct.test_default_reconstruct_still_materializes_the_artifact` (method) — Asserts the default reconstruct writes an artifact file whose contents equal the returned unified diff. <!--#1734687e15060bd0-->
- `TestDiffViewHelpers` (class) — Test class for the diff presentation helpers — section splitting, path containment/normalization rules for `--path` filters, rename handling, filtered section/stat view agreement, and `--stat` line counting. <!--#1b6d5ecc6025d68a-->
  - `TestDiffViewHelpers.test_sections_split_verbatim` (method) — Asserts `split_diff_sections` yields one section per changed file and reassembles into the original diff verbatim. <!--#4dddcda37a3160eb-->
  - `TestDiffViewHelpers.test_a_parent_section_is_not_selected_by_an_inner_path_filter` (method) — Asserts a section is selected only by filters naming it or its ancestors, so a parent section is not pulled in by a filter naming a path inside it. <!--#41b67e4f1e44c12d-->
  - `TestDiffViewHelpers.test_section_covers_a_directory_filter` (method) — Asserts a directory filter selects the sections for files beneath it while rejecting partial-segment and unrelated prefixes. <!--#ee2b263cca58cc80-->
  - `TestDiffViewHelpers.test_paths_related_contains_one_way_only` (method) — Asserts `paths_related` answers containment in one direction only (changed path at or under the filter) and rejects blank paths. <!--#8e61f6ecad550138-->
  - `TestDiffViewHelpers.test_equivalent_directory_spellings_are_normalized` (method) — Asserts trailing/duplicate slashes and `./` prefixes all name the same directory across `paths_related`, `section_covers_path`, and `select_filtered_view`. <!--#953e36cbc915221d-->
  - `TestDiffViewHelpers.test_normalization_widens_nothing` (method) — Asserts normalization never admits filters that name nothing — absolute paths, `..` segments, `.`, `/`, and non-existent subpaths all stay unmatched. <!--#cd49705b33509c44-->
  - `TestDiffViewHelpers.test_normalization_keeps_whitespace_significant` (method) — Asserts leading/trailing spaces in path segments are preserved as significant filename characters while separator and dot collapsing still apply. <!--#700154db394b42af-->
  - `TestDiffViewHelpers.test_rename_section_keeps_both_sides` (method) — Asserts a rename produces one section recording both old and new paths, selectable by either side. <!--#cfacfae6b130330f-->
  - `TestDiffViewHelpers.test_filtered_views_agree_on_a_rename` (method) — Asserts a filter naming either side of a rename yields the same section and the same two-row stat table in both views. <!--#4ef6280effa7b75e-->
  - `TestDiffViewHelpers.test_a_selected_section_widens_no_further_than_itself` (method) — Asserts stat widening adds only the other side of an already-selected section, never unrelated sibling files. <!--#11a0425c1884bac0-->
  - `TestDiffViewHelpers.test_a_section_never_invents_a_stat_row` (method) — Asserts the filtered stat table never adds a path the reconstruction did not record. <!--#8725dbcf49a4c967-->
  - `TestDiffViewHelpers.test_stat_counts_come_from_the_anchors` (method) — Asserts `diff_stat` derives per-file added/removed line counts from the reconstruction's anchors. <!--#006389889994eaef-->
  - `TestDiffViewHelpers.test_stat_keeps_anchorless_changed_paths` (method) — Asserts a binary change with no line anchors still appears in the stat table with zero counts. <!--#37b236175da4c801-->
  - `TestDiffViewHelpers.test_count_anchor_lines_tolerates_junk` (method) — Asserts `count_anchor_lines` handles None, inverted ranges, and malformed entries without failing. <!--#afcb9c87bd8f6a23-->

### `tests/engine/test_runtime_environment_injection.py` (python) — Test suite for context_builder.get_runtime_environment_injection, verifying the default per-step command whitelist/blacklist injection content, FORBIDDEN-step precedence, yaml override narrowing/widening/malformed handling, graceful fallback with single-warning caching on missing markdown, and end-to-end delivery of the runtime-environment block into the final LLM prompt. <!--#d5f0b9c327aaefc5|e00e6a1ae17c693b-->
- `_reset_cache` (function) — Autouse fixture that resets the runtime-environment markdown cache before and after each test so file-removal and load-count assertions are isolated. <!--#2491e76944ff0f32-->
- `test_default_whitelist_returns_full_content` (function) — Asserts that a whitelisted step ("plan") yields a non-empty injection beginning with the HEADING and containing every whitelist command, blacklist command, path reference, workflow hint, and the verbatim blacklist preamble strings. <!--#18987d626d307077-->
- `test_forbidden_steps_always_return_empty_even_with_yaml` (function) — Verifies that FORBIDDEN steps (commit, version_analyze) always return "" even when explicitly listed in tianluo.yaml, while a co-listed non-forbidden step (plan) still receives the injection. <!--#52c47357b3628638-->
- `test_yaml_override_narrows_and_widens_whitelist` (function) — Checks that the yaml `runtime_environment_injection.steps` list fully replaces the default whitelist (narrowing and widening), and that FORBIDDEN steps still return "" regardless of override. <!--#02162207c4937542-->
- `test_missing_markdown_returns_empty_and_warns_once` (function) — Monkeypatches the markdown loader to a non-existent path to confirm the function returns "" instead of raising and logs only a single warning across multiple calls. <!--#fccf88e772888729-->
- `test_null_yaml_falls_back_to_defaults` (function) — Ensures an explicit `runtime_environment_injection: null` in tianluo.yaml does not crash and falls back to the default whitelist. <!--#0d19a5c2ad568fd4-->
- `test_non_list_yaml_override_ignored` (function) — Confirms that a bare-string `steps: plan` override (instead of a list) is ignored so defaults apply and no substring-matching whitelist semantics leak. <!--#981e9cf5b02a53d9-->
- `test_defaults_cover_expected_steps` (function) — Asserts that every LLM-decision step (analyze, plan, plan_tasks, implement, investigate, verify_spec, update_spec, self_check, discovery, summarize) is in RUNTIME_ENV_INJECTION_DEFAULT_STEPS while mechanical steps like commit and version_analyze are forbidden and excluded from the defaults. <!--#8c32d23d08a08bb3-->
- `test_markdown_is_cached_across_calls` (function) — Counts Path.read_text calls to verify the runtime-environment markdown is read from disk only once across multiple injection calls. <!--#38bb79dda4eabcbd-->
- `test_runtime_env_appears_in_prompt_end_to_end` (function) — End-to-end test that patches LLMCaller in implement_handler and asserts the captured prompt sent to the LLM contains the HEADING plus representative whitelist and blacklist commands. <!--#629408f1815bc353-->

### `tests/engine/test_schema_step_type_mirror.py` (python) — Regression test module asserting that the `StepType` enum in the engine models and the `StepTypeValue` enum in the persistence schema stay in exact bidirectional sync (including the newly added `investigate` value), so persisted flow steps can never be rejected by schema validation. <!--#3a9d13aaa416428a|9af15e16d00e347f-->
- `test_schema_mirrors_every_serializable_step_type` (function) — Asserts that the `StepType` enum in models and the `StepTypeValue` enum in the persistence schema contain exactly the same set of values in both directions, so no persisted flow step can be rejected by schema validation. <!--#a7e48c8c3c308b47-->
- `test_investigate_is_present_in_both` (function) — Pins the newly added `investigate` step type to the literal value "investigate" in both `StepType` and `StepTypeValue`. <!--#244993b267b3b668-->

### `tests/engine/test_self_check_adjudication.py` (python) — Pytest suite (with helpers for building validated issues, a RUNNING flow, a SELF_CHECK step, and a mocked LLMCaller) covering the self_check step's adjudication integration: recording rounds and observations into the ledger with idempotent step_id replay, safely pairing previous-issue resolutions to prior issue fingerprints under cardinality/reordering guards, and ensuring repeated or oscillating findings still trigger the fix loop rather than being suppressed by the convergence guard. <!--#0063edded451702a|7e78047a6b5e022d-->
- `_issue` (function) — Test helper that builds a well-formed self_check issue dict (with severity, expected/actual behavior, expectation source quote, and evidence lines) crafted to survive `_validate_and_filter_issues`. <!--#19e5df050b5324eb-->
- `_make_flow` (function) — Test helper that constructs a minimal RUNNING FlowInstance for adjudication self-check tests. <!--#7aed81d2ed1a7bfe-->
- `_make_step` (function) — Test helper that assembles a SELF_CHECK Step with configurable pass/convergence/fix-iteration inputs and optional step_id/prev_issues. <!--#eae8ad2b398a764e-->
- `_run` (function) — Test helper that invokes the self_check_handler for a given step/flow while patching tianluo.engine.steps.self_check.LLMCaller with a mock whose call returns a JSON payload built from the supplied issues (and optional previous_issue_resolutions). <!--#a341da6a37e95c57-->
- `TestRoundRecording` (class) — Test class verifying self-check rounds (including clean rounds) are recorded into the adjudication ledger and that same-step-id replays stay idempotent. <!--#e8d6b2d9cfde43ae-->
  - `TestRoundRecording.test_issues_recorded_into_ledger` (method) — Asserts a validated issue is recorded as a ledger observation with the correct fingerprint and increments round_count. <!--#f41702fcaf902e86-->
  - `TestRoundRecording.test_clean_round_still_records_and_advances` (method) — Asserts an issue-free round still completes and advances round_count while recording no observations. <!--#507210c49ccc81b4-->
  - `TestRoundRecording.test_replay_same_step_id_is_idempotent` (method) — Asserts re-running a step carrying the same step_id (resume replay) does not double-count rounds or observations. <!--#bf31c22bfbd58542-->
- `TestResolutionRecording` (class) — Test class verifying how previous-issue resolutions are paired to prior issues (by position, guarded against cardinality mismatch and reordering) and recorded with fingerprints. <!--#d425d626dec72ce8-->
  - `TestResolutionRecording.test_pair_resolutions_by_position` (method) — Asserts equal-count resolutions pair positionally to their corresponding prev issues. <!--#7a2a65b182f279f3-->
  - `TestResolutionRecording.test_pair_cardinality_mismatch_skips_positional_pairing` (method) — Asserts a resolution count differing from prev issue count leaves all resolutions unpaired rather than misaligned. <!--#9818db800ad740ae-->
  - `TestResolutionRecording.test_pair_omitted_first_entry_does_not_mislabel` (method) — Asserts the cardinality guard refuses positional pairing when an entry is omitted, avoiding a wrong-fingerprint 'fixed' verdict. <!--#fdcf0d16fbe1da41-->
  - `TestResolutionRecording.test_pair_preserves_already_identified_issue_on_mismatch` (method) — Asserts a resolution carrying its own machine-identified issue keeps it even when counts mismatch suppresses positional inference. <!--#c286408baca796d0-->
  - `TestResolutionRecording.test_pair_reordered_entries_refuses_wrong_fingerprint` (method) — Asserts the content-match reorder guard leaves reversed-order (but equal-count) resolutions unpaired to avoid stamping verdicts onto the wrong issue. <!--#b28dc8a30b45f6dc-->
  - `TestResolutionRecording.test_pair_in_order_signal_pairs_correctly` (method) — Asserts equal-count, in-order, content-discriminating resolutions pair correctly by position. <!--#eb1f3a9f4be1a75a-->
  - `TestResolutionRecording.test_fixed_resolution_recorded_with_fingerprint` (method) — Asserts a fix round's 'fixed' verdict lands on the ledger paired to the prev issue's fingerprint so trigger (b) can match it. <!--#401dbc8559230c48-->
- `TestRepeatedFindingAdjudication` (class) — Test class asserting that repeated self-check findings — whether oscillating between contradictory expectations or simply repeating — still enter the fix loop rather than being suppressed by the convergence/oscillation guard. <!--#7748a93615d00809-->
  - `TestRepeatedFindingAdjudication._seed_prior_round` (method) — Helper that records a prior self-check round (round_id="prior") flagging the shared position with a given `expected` value, via `adjudication.record_self_check_round`. <!--#ae316339a892f041-->
  - `TestRepeatedFindingAdjudication.test_oscillation_enters_fix_and_remains_available_to_adjudication` (method) — Verifies that a finding demanding the opposite expectation at the same position as a prior round still returns REVISION_NEEDED with `fix_needed` set and is not marked converged. <!--#36f0df33a43b113b-->
  - `TestRepeatedFindingAdjudication.test_non_oscillation_repetition_still_enters_fix` (method) — Verifies that a validated finding repeating the same expectation as the prior round also yields REVISION_NEEDED with `fix_needed` and no convergence. <!--#a75a10c78f043e2d-->
  - `TestRepeatedFindingAdjudication.test_convergence_disabled_no_suppression_effect` (method) — Verifies that with `convergence_enabled=False` (the default) the oscillation guard is inert and any issue-bearing pass still returns REVISION_NEEDED. <!--#8a2e6e1f5128cc44-->

### `tests/engine/test_self_check_defer_fix.py` (python) — Test suite for the self_check deferred-fix feature, covering `WorkflowConfig` parsing/validation of the `self_check_defer_fix_threshold` option, signature-based dedup in `_merge_dedup_issues` (including transfer of carried fold blocks and severity onto surviving issues), and position-keyed lossless folding of still-present previous findings by `_fold_still_present_into_current` with its identity/dedup-key stability guarantees, built on local helpers that fabricate issues, flows, SELF_CHECK steps, and a patched-LLMCaller handler run. <!--#2a02ee96c834fb23|f7e165d1c9c66c84-->
- `_valid_issue` (function) — Helper that builds a self_check issue dict shaped to survive _validate_and_filter_issues, with configurable severity, path, and source quote. <!--#edd9f2bd98d54935-->
- `_make_flow` (function) — Helper that constructs a minimal RUNNING feature FlowInstance for the tests. <!--#39911d8baec83067-->
- `_make_step` (function) — Helper that builds a SELF_CHECK Step with inputs parameterized by pass index, passes-required, defer threshold, and deferred stash. <!--#c56ce8ea0dcdfb81-->
- `_run_handler` (function) — Test helper that invokes self_check_handler with the LLMCaller patched to return a fixed JSON payload of the given issues and a stub summary. <!--#e8ddbe9bac5374f5-->
- `TestDeferThresholdConfig` (class) — Test class covering `WorkflowConfig.from_dict` parsing of the `self_check_defer_fix_threshold` option — default/zero/null disable it, explicit ints are kept, bool and float values warn and fall back to 0, and negatives raise `ConfigError`. <!--#3eebd884a539db37-->
  - `TestDeferThresholdConfig.test_default_is_zero` (method) — Asserts an empty `workflow` config yields `self_check_defer_fix_threshold == 0`, matching `DEFAULT_SELF_CHECK_DEFER_FIX_THRESHOLD`. <!--#397def9d319ba7d6-->
  - `TestDeferThresholdConfig.test_explicit_value` (method) — Asserts an explicit threshold value is preserved from config. <!--#d66fbab3fd7131d2-->
  - `TestDeferThresholdConfig.test_zero_disables` (method) — Asserts a threshold of 0 disables deferral. <!--#1be4c65bb90f7b8d-->
  - `TestDeferThresholdConfig.test_null_disables` (method) — Asserts a null threshold is normalized to 0 (deferral disabled). <!--#7f31634d67751d3a-->
  - `TestDeferThresholdConfig.test_bool_warns_and_falls_back` (method) — Asserts a boolean `self_check_defer_fix_threshold` logs a WARNING naming the key and falls back to 0 instead of being treated as an int. <!--#42da83bfdec0f84d-->
  - `TestDeferThresholdConfig.test_float_warns_and_falls_back` (method) — Asserts a float `self_check_defer_fix_threshold` logs a WARNING naming the key and falls back to 0 rather than being coerced. <!--#77744f13ee9fbbeb-->
  - `TestDeferThresholdConfig.test_negative_fails_fast` (method) — Asserts a negative threshold raises ConfigError. <!--#5eee044670d60ef6-->
- `TestMergeDedup` (class) — Unit tests for `_merge_dedup_issues`, covering signature-based deduplication of self-check findings, retention of unsignable issues, and the baseline drop of a plain duplicate. <!--#0b606197d3f02f33-->
  - `TestMergeDedup.test_dedup_drops_matching_signature` (method) — Asserts merging drops a duplicate issue sharing the same signature while keeping distinct ones. <!--#88c272c1966f24e5-->
  - `TestMergeDedup.test_unsignable_issue_kept` (method) — Asserts issues that produce no signature are not deduplicated (all kept). <!--#dde7aa76f97edb26-->
  - `TestMergeDedup.test_duplicate_carrying_nothing_is_dropped_exactly_as_before` (method) — Asserts the pre-existing dedup behaviour is unchanged: a duplicate carrying no folded content is discarded and the existing issue survives untouched. <!--#88ce1d2ed4075c18-->
- `TestDedupCarryBlockTransfer` (class) — Tests that when dedup drops a duplicate that carries a folded previous finding, the carried statement and its raised severity transfer onto the surviving issue without changing the dedup verdict or the survivor's identity. <!--#2fee3a1271d3510e-->
  - `TestDedupCarryBlockTransfer._carrying` (method) — Static helper that builds a current issue which has folded a previous finding into it via `_fold_still_present_into_current`, returning the carrying issue and the folded-in previous issue. <!--#176afd2ee8be5bcd-->
  - `TestDedupCarryBlockTransfer.test_carried_statement_moves_onto_the_survivor` (method) — Verifies the survivor of a dedup keeps its own wording while the dropped duplicate's carried statement, quote and evidence line remain readable in the survivor's `divergence`. <!--#7b9877d8a9d93c80-->
  - `TestDedupCarryBlockTransfer.test_transfer_does_not_shift_the_survivor_identity` (method) — Checks that transferring a carry block leaves both the dedup signature and `_issue_identity_tokens` of the survivor identical to the original stashed issue. <!--#03c46ca5dba71166-->
  - `TestDedupCarryBlockTransfer.test_transfer_raises_the_survivor_severity` (method) — Confirms a transferred carry block lifts the survivor's severity to the carried one (flipping `_has_critical_or_high`) while leaving the original stashed audit dict unmutated. <!--#56c15cab242d1ee2-->
  - `TestDedupCarryBlockTransfer.test_transfer_never_lowers_the_survivor_severity` (method) — Asserts a carry transfer from a lower-severity duplicate never downgrades the survivor's existing severity. <!--#a01d70d364815077-->
  - `TestDedupCarryBlockTransfer.test_transfer_stacks_behind_what_the_survivor_already_carries` (method) — Verifies that when both survivor and duplicate carry folded statements, the transferred block appends rather than replaces, leaving two fold markers and both statements readable. <!--#64d234266eebe73e-->
- `TestFoldStillPresentIntoCurrent` (class) — The main test suite for `_fold_still_present_into_current`, covering position-keyed folding of `still_present` previous findings, losslessness, severity raising, identity/dedup-key stability, non-folding cases, and downstream rendering into the fix loop. <!--#726eb8563ef9d5d9-->
  - `TestFoldStillPresentIntoCurrent._assert_carries` (method) — Static helper asserting that every descriptive field, evidence line and expectation-source quote of the given statements appears in a rendered string. <!--#7fa67a851eea1536-->
  - `TestFoldStillPresentIntoCurrent.test_same_position_folds_without_mutating_the_original` (method) — Checks that a previous finding at the same position folds losslessly into the current one, with this round's wording leading and both input dicts left verbatim as audit records. <!--#a4ada22b8f9ecfd3-->
  - `TestFoldStillPresentIntoCurrent.test_folded_statement_keeps_unknown_schema_fields` (method) — Ensures the fold rendering is schema-agnostic by preserving an unknown extra field of the folded previous issue. <!--#3625d5ead890963e-->
  - `TestFoldStillPresentIntoCurrent.test_fold_does_not_shift_the_signature_dedup_key` (method) — Asserts that writing the carry block into `divergence` leaves `_issue_signature` equal to the unfolded issue's, so equality-based dedup still matches. <!--#0b95bceb0fcd2818-->
  - `TestFoldStillPresentIntoCurrent.test_fold_leaves_the_pairing_identity_unchanged` (method) — Verifies carried text is readable but contributes no `_issue_identity_tokens`, so resolution summaries cannot be mispaired onto a folded finding. <!--#a3439ce6de0690ce-->
  - `TestFoldStillPresentIntoCurrent.test_fold_scaffolding_never_becomes_identity` (method) — Confirms the fold's own markers, labels and `severity_raised` note appear in the text but never enter the finding's identity tokens. <!--#2a70d5f63d671e94-->
  - `TestFoldStillPresentIntoCurrent.test_two_previous_findings_at_one_position_both_fold` (method) — Checks that two previous findings sharing a position both fold into the single current issue, yielding two fold markers and both statements preserved. <!--#9a675edbdd0a5777-->
  - `TestFoldStillPresentIntoCurrent.test_different_position_is_left_to_the_readmission_path` (method) — Asserts previous findings at a different line or file do not fold and are returned as unfolded for the separate re-admission path. <!--#cb5d1ac75e6bf6c5-->
  - `TestFoldStillPresentIntoCurrent.test_case_differing_paths_are_distinct_positions` (method) — Verifies path matching is case-sensitive, so findings in `Foo.py` and `foo.py` are treated as distinct positions and never folded. <!--#44ba8059b20704d5-->
  - `TestFoldStillPresentIntoCurrent.test_identical_case_sensitive_position_still_folds` (method) — Confirms case sensitivity does not break the normal case: an exactly matching mixed-case path still folds. <!--#d7aef347d496872f-->
  - `TestFoldStillPresentIntoCurrent.test_positionless_previous_issue_is_not_folded` (method) — Checks that previous entries with no position — or that are not dicts at all — are passed through unfolded instead of raising. <!--#89557357d11b0a2a-->
  - `TestFoldStillPresentIntoCurrent.test_fail_closed_sweep_entry_is_never_folded` (method) — Asserts findings re-admitted by the fail-closed sweep (not individually identified) are never folded and keep the existing re-admission path. <!--#4e1cbff3005238c1-->
  - `TestFoldStillPresentIntoCurrent.test_only_the_identified_entries_fold` (method) — Verifies that with a mix of identified and swept entries at one position, only the verdict-named one folds and the swept one stays out of the carry block. <!--#77e0c98089157b05-->
  - `TestFoldStillPresentIntoCurrent.test_classify_marks_sweep_entries_unidentified` (method) — Checks that `_classify_still_present_prev_issues` re-admits all previous findings but marks none as individually identified when a `still_present` verdict is unpairable. <!--#15e865969483eb47-->
  - `TestFoldStillPresentIntoCurrent.test_classify_marks_paired_verdicts_identified` (method) — Checks that a summary-paired `still_present` verdict yields exactly that previous finding, flagged as individually identified. <!--#73c8145d0ccc9130-->
  - `TestFoldStillPresentIntoCurrent.test_same_missing_in_without_evidence_lines_does_not_fold` (method) — Asserts a shared `missing_in` target with no evidence lines is not a position match, so two distinct omissions stay separate findings. <!--#e2cd236eadc48913-->
  - `TestFoldStillPresentIntoCurrent.test_legacy_location_alone_does_not_fold` (method) — Verifies the legacy `location` field alone does not constitute a foldable position match. <!--#3eb404ec85bee1ee-->
  - `TestFoldStillPresentIntoCurrent.test_fold_raises_top_level_severity_to_the_higher_one` (method) — Checks that folding a still-present high finding into a medium re-report raises the top-level severity (so it cannot be deferred) while recording the round's own severity in the text. <!--#e4fbe861295841c5-->
  - `TestFoldStillPresentIntoCurrent.test_fold_never_lowers_the_current_severity` (method) — Asserts folding a lower-severity previous finding leaves the current severity untouched and emits no `severity_raised` note. <!--#f6b66a47e6d7f3c1-->
  - `TestFoldStillPresentIntoCurrent.test_describe_issue_carries_every_folded_statement` (method) — Verifies `_describe_issue` renders every field, quote and evidence citation of both the current and the folded previous statement. <!--#10f22be34fbc089c-->
  - `TestFoldStillPresentIntoCurrent.test_describe_issue_unchanged_without_folding` (method) — Pins the exact `_describe_issue` output format for an unfolded issue, guarding against rendering drift. <!--#c6a1414e3d3960cc-->
  - `TestFoldStillPresentIntoCurrent.test_deferred_stash_rescue_prompt_carries_folded_statements` (method) — Checks that `StateMachine._route_deferred_into_fix_loop`, a route into IMPLEMENT bypassing `_build_fix_outputs`, still surfaces all folded content as a single fix-instruction bullet. <!--#3e6c0f39dec1779c-->
  - `TestFoldStillPresentIntoCurrent.test_implement_fix_context_carries_folded_statements` (method) — Checks that `_format_fix_context_structured` in the implement step renders both the current and folded statements as one bullet with nothing lost. <!--#12d7bd26e7e2ee47-->
  - `TestFoldStillPresentIntoCurrent.test_implement_fix_context_unchanged_without_folding` (method) — Pins the exact line-by-line fix-context output for an unfolded issue as a regression baseline. <!--#e0309d129c31d351-->
- `TestFoldedFindingMeetsTheDeferredStash` (class) — End-to-end test class for the fold's interaction with the deferred-stash merge, running `self_check_handler` against a mocked LLM response. <!--#8e0ff90d3ad0f938-->
  - `TestFoldedFindingMeetsTheDeferredStash._run` (method) — Static helper that patches `LLMCaller` to return a canned JSON payload and invokes `self_check_handler`. <!--#82fd11682871ea1a-->
  - `TestFoldedFindingMeetsTheDeferredStash.test_stash_duplicate_keeps_the_folded_statement` (method) — Verifies that when a folded current finding duplicates a stashed one, the stash entry still wins the dedup but the folded previous statement and its quote still reach the fix instructions. <!--#517a53e81a94b199-->
- `TestFoldedSeverityReachesFixImmediately` (class) — End-to-end test class asserting a still-present high finding folded into a medium re-report keeps high severity and so is fixed now rather than deferred. <!--#8628a8663ae80438-->
  - `TestFoldedSeverityReachesFixImmediately._run` (method) — Static helper that patches `LLMCaller` to return a canned JSON payload and invokes `self_check_handler`. <!--#82fd11682871ea1a-->
  - `TestFoldedSeverityReachesFixImmediately.test_high_prev_folded_into_medium_report_fixes_now` (method) — Runs the full self-check handler to confirm the folded issue is emitted at high severity, skips the deferral path, and puts both rounds' wordings into the fix instructions. <!--#e5587cdb291531b4-->
