  - `TestFixLoopInheritedOnly.test_inherited_issue_filed_at_most_once_per_flow` (method) — Asserts that across three test-step invocations on the same flow the inherited-failure issue is filed at most once. <!--#5b3899a7a1d3ba08-->
- `TestFixLoopNewTestFail` (class) — Test class verifying that failures in newly-added tests trigger the fix loop. <!--#63224ac8166e3ea1-->
  - `TestFixLoopNewTestFail.test_returns_revision_needed` (method) — Asserts a new-test failure returns StepStatus.REVISION_NEEDED with fix_needed set and fix_instructions present in outputs. <!--#39f83814e36bda09-->
- `TestFixLoopIntroducedRegression` (class) — Test class verifying that regression failures absent from an empty baseline are classified as introduced and trigger the fix loop. <!--#31107afc69c7746a-->
  - `TestFixLoopIntroducedRegression.test_returns_revision_needed` (method) — Asserts an introduced regression (empty baseline) returns REVISION_NEEDED with the failure in introduced_failures and tests_blocking true. <!--#56024373a895a9bd-->
- `TestFixLoopMixedScenario` (class) — Test class verifying that a mix of inherited and new failures still triggers the fix loop while surfacing and filing the inherited failure. <!--#21b4aa8127652a4e-->
  - `TestFixLoopMixedScenario.test_triggers_fix_and_reports_inherited` (method) — Asserts a mixed inherited+new failure returns REVISION_NEEDED, records the new failure as introduced, and surfaces/files the inherited one once. <!--#ee62ba54bd8b56d9-->
- `TestFixLoopAllPass` (class) — Test class verifying that when all tests pass no fix loop runs and no issue is reported. <!--#07a88b88d661ec0c-->
  - `TestFixLoopAllPass.test_returns_completed` (method) — Asserts an all-pass run returns COMPLETED with tests_passed true, empty failure lists, and no report call. <!--#5d13b4f3e82caf1c-->
- `TestNoAutoPopulate` (class) — Test class asserting known_test_failures.json is neither created nor modified, removing the failure-laundering vector so the baseline is the sole exemption source. <!--#4514cd61033c3dd9-->
  - `TestNoAutoPopulate.test_regression_failure_does_not_create_known_file` (method) — Asserts a regression failure does not auto-create known_test_failures.json. <!--#ae3bc73d0cb0398c-->
  - `TestNoAutoPopulate.test_existing_known_file_left_untouched` (method) — Asserts a pre-existing known_test_failures.json is left byte-for-byte unchanged during a regression failure. <!--#e5b943b90ded08a4-->
- `_timeout_result` (function) — Helper that builds a _run_command-style result dict representing a command timeout. <!--#9bc4e35b9d78d630-->
- `TestDynamicTimeout` (class) — Test class covering dynamic timeout computation from estimated_test_duration, fallback timeouts, phase timeouts, and timeout-related fix_context fields. <!--#33a60822ea296b87-->
  - `TestDynamicTimeout.test_uses_dynamic_timeout_when_estimated_duration_provided` (method) — Asserts the primary run uses estimated_test_duration × timeout_multiplier (100 × 2.5 = 250s) as its timeout. <!--#8ec3bc9dc7946772-->
  - `TestDynamicTimeout.test_uses_fallback_timeout_when_no_estimated_duration` (method) — Asserts the primary run falls back to config.timeout when no estimated_test_duration is provided. <!--#2fcfffa2c9a1c19f-->
  - `TestDynamicTimeout.test_timeout_in_fix_context_when_test_times_out` (method) — Asserts a primary timeout returns REVISION_NEEDED and populates fix_context with timeout_reason, previous_timeout, previous_estimated_test_duration, and timeout_multiplier. <!--#3372822b18361e11-->
  - `TestDynamicTimeout.test_phases_use_fixed_timeout_not_dynamic` (method) — Asserts the primary command uses the dynamic timeout while a configured phase uses its own explicit fixed timeout. <!--#e4dafd6063ad3ce3-->
  - `TestDynamicTimeout.test_no_timeout_context_when_not_timeout` (method) — Asserts an ordinary (non-timeout) failure omits timeout_reason and previous_timeout from fix_context. <!--#0c237aadc8913fce-->
  - `TestDynamicTimeout.test_timeout_at_cap_flagged_in_fix_context` (method) — Asserts that when the computed timeout is clamped by max_dynamic_timeout, fix_context sets timeout_at_cap true and mentions the cap in timeout_reason. <!--#36d35cf86aefde23-->
  - `TestDynamicTimeout.test_timeout_at_cap_false_when_below_cap` (method) — Asserts fix_context.timeout_at_cap is False when the computed timeout stays below the cap. <!--#e7cd50e3e2796677-->
  - `TestDynamicTimeout.test_timeout_fix_context_flows_to_rendered_prompt` (method) — End-to-end test that the fix_context produced on timeout renders through _format_fix_context_structured with all four timeout fields (and whole floats rendered without trailing '.0'). <!--#f2633c926a3948d4-->
  - `TestDynamicTimeout.test_phase_timeout_hint_in_fix_instructions` (method) — Asserts that when a required phase (and its one-shot retry) times out, a phase-timeout hint mentioning the phase name is added to fix_instructions. <!--#4c5c1bc3e1b65591-->

### `tests/engine/test_test_step_timeout_retry.py` (python) — Unit tests for the test step's two behaviors — the one-shot in-place retry on a timed-out command (when it fires vs. not, its timeout-vs-assertion fix labeling, and that it doesn't bump fix_iteration) and the passed-phase history archive slimming (replacing a passing phase's stored stdout with an accurate count+tail summary while failed phases keep full output), built around helpers that fabricate flows, TEST steps, configs, and normal/timeout command-result dicts. <!--#1b323c721c4fa0bd|48b480f848d8ac62-->
- `_make_flow` (function) — Test helper that builds a minimal FlowInstance whose change_path points at a tianluo.yaml under the given tmp_path. <!--#a5f440a661ff22f2-->
- `_make_step` (function) — Helper that constructs a TEST Step with configurable inputs (tests_added, fix flags, fix_iteration, estimated duration). <!--#685a5ca095f49984-->
- `_config` (function) — Helper that returns a MagicMock TestConfig with default command/timeout settings, overridable via keyword args. <!--#dfe3092505c4b5e0-->
- `_primary_result` (function) — Helper that builds a normal (non-timeout) command-result dict for a pass or fail outcome. <!--#d8d70383efcd5adc-->
- `_timeout_result` (function) — Helper that builds a timeout-shaped command-result dict (returncode -1, timed_out flag, timeout marker). <!--#4cc873d2b0739a73-->
- `TestTimeoutRetry` (class) — Test class verifying the test_handler's one-shot in-place retry logic for timed-out test runs — distinguishing timeouts (retried once) from real assertion/spawn failures (not retried) and labeling persistent timeouts in fix_context. <!--#c0b7215b31f608a1-->
  - `TestTimeoutRetry.test_retry_success_continues_normally` (method) — Asserts that a first-run timeout followed by a passing in-place retry yields COMPLETED with exactly two run calls and no fix context. <!--#a4703121e09332bf-->
  - `TestTimeoutRetry.test_retry_still_timeout_enters_fix_with_timeout_label` (method) — Asserts that when both the primary run and its retry time out, the handler enters the fix loop (REVISION_NEEDED) with timeout-not-assertion metadata and a canonical human-readable reason. <!--#075c3cc43d9f2613-->
  - `TestTimeoutRetry.test_retry_does_not_increment_fix_iteration` (method) — Asserts the in-place retry does not bump the fix-iteration counter, so fix_context['iteration'] is just input fix_iteration + 1 with only one retry. <!--#da846765426f20e0-->
  - `TestTimeoutRetry.test_non_timeout_failure_does_not_retry` (method) — Asserts an ordinary assertion failure runs the primary only (no retry) and carries no timeout metadata in fix_context. <!--#5fc6c3e7b647e8a7-->
  - `TestTimeoutRetry.test_marker_only_timeout_is_retried` (method) — Asserts a timeout-shaped result recognized only by its 'Timeout after' stderr marker and returncode -1 (no timed_out flag) still triggers one in-place retry. <!--#f67a22bd6d824e06-->
  - `TestTimeoutRetry.test_required_phase_timeout_is_retried_once` (method) — Asserts a required configured phase that times out gets the same one-shot in-place retry, and a passing phase-retry avoids the fix loop (3 total run calls). <!--#e5bc7901f1fa9ed6-->
  - `TestTimeoutRetry.test_persistent_required_phase_timeout_labels_fix_context` (method) — Asserts a required phase that times out twice enters the fix loop with timeout-not-assertion metadata naming the phase, rather than a generic test_failure. <!--#28096faa9920161c-->
  - `TestTimeoutRetry.test_returncode_minus_one_without_marker_is_retried` (method) — Asserts a bare returncode -1 result with no timed_out flag and no stderr marker is still recognized as a timeout via the -1 sentinel and retried once. <!--#27ab097b71e09148-->
  - `TestTimeoutRetry.test_passing_result_with_timeout_stderr_is_not_retried` (method) — Asserts a PASSING run whose stderr happens to contain 'Timeout after' is kept as-is (authoritative passed verdict short-circuits the heuristic) with no retry. <!--#254ffd3b24e67f89-->
  - `TestTimeoutRetry.test_retry_passes_with_timeout_stderr_not_recorded_as_timeout` (method) — Asserts that when the in-place retry passes but its stderr carries a timeout marker, it is not classified as a persistent timeout and no timeout metadata is set. <!--#ead99c3ad8e7557e-->
  - `TestTimeoutRetry.test_exception_fallback_returncode_minus_two_not_retried` (method) — Asserts the generic subprocess-spawn exception fallback (returncode -2) is not misclassified as a timeout — no retry and no timeout metadata. <!--#e18db9dcf87a9386-->
- `_big_passing_stdout` (function) — Helper that generates verbose multi-line passing pytest stdout with a head sentinel and a summary tail for archive-slimming tests. <!--#2c41eafa07a270d5-->
- `TestPassedPhaseArchiveSlimming` (class) — Test class verifying that passing phases have their stored stdout slimmed to a compact archived summary with accurate parsed pass/fail counts, while failed phases keep full stdout verbatim. <!--#c15444f0411cd693-->
  - `TestPassedPhaseArchiveSlimming.test_passed_phase_stdout_is_slimmed` (method) — Asserts a large passing stdout is replaced by a bounded '[archived summary — passed phase:' summary keeping the tail/final line and dropping the head sentinel, applied to both top-level and default-phase entries. <!--#fa835fc4d8b6b720-->
  - `TestPassedPhaseArchiveSlimming.test_failed_phase_stdout_preserved` (method) — Asserts a FAILED phase keeps its full stdout verbatim (with head sentinel) and is not replaced by an archived summary. <!--#a9a29f1949e013ed-->
  - `TestPassedPhaseArchiveSlimming.test_quiet_runner_summary_counts_are_accurate` (method) — Asserts a passing phase with no per-test lines (e.g. cargo) archives accurate counts parsed from the aggregate 'test result:' summary line, not a false 0 passed/0 failed. <!--#17bde321f42dc1a1-->
  - `TestPassedPhaseArchiveSlimming.test_cargo_workspace_multi_summary_counts_are_totalled` (method) — Asserts a cargo workspace's multiple 'test result:' lines are totalled across all binaries (7+5+3=15 passed) rather than reporting only the first binary's counts. <!--#49f82d1f324dfc4c-->
  - `TestPassedPhaseArchiveSlimming.test_cargo_workspace_identical_summary_lines_are_totalled` (method) — Asserts two binaries reporting identical counts (5 passed each) are totalled to 10 passed and not de-duplicated into a single 5. <!--#a73e0d7b9f797d9b-->
  - `TestPassedPhaseArchiveSlimming.test_unparseable_passed_output_uses_truthful_fallback` (method) — Asserts a passing phase with no per-test lines or count summary archives a truthful 'passed (per-test counts unavailable)' fallback rather than a fabricated 0 passed, 0 failed. <!--#84712cf5e2eccd73-->
  - `TestPassedPhaseArchiveSlimming.test_mixed_phases_slims_only_passed` (method) — Asserts that with a passing primary plus a failing required phase, only the passing phase's stdout is slimmed to an archived summary while the failing phase keeps its full stdout. <!--#64008b430392e6a2-->

### `tests/engine/test_tool_formatters.py` (python) — Unit-test suite for tianluo.engine.tool_formatters, covering truncate_preview's length/ellipsis/newline/coercion rules, truncate_path's project-root-relative conversion and 160-char filename-preserving middle truncation (plus the set_project_root/get_project_root helpers), and the generic fallback format_tool_use_preview/format_tool_result_preview renderers used for unregistered tools. <!--#32c8236b3f5fdd50|73c4747735dbe758-->
- `TestTruncatePreview` (class) — Test class exercising truncate_preview's length capping, ellipsis handling, newline replacement, and type coercion. <!--#d72f8fc1a144ba89-->
  - `TestTruncatePreview.test_empty_string` (method) — Asserts an empty input string yields an empty result. <!--#329321bda3b6d25e-->
  - `TestTruncatePreview.test_none_returns_empty` (method) — Asserts None input is treated as empty string. <!--#015cf5ddc46c07af-->
  - `TestTruncatePreview.test_short_text_unchanged` (method) — Asserts text under max_length passes through unchanged. <!--#27716f841cc2a3c2-->
  - `TestTruncatePreview.test_exact_max_length_unchanged` (method) — Asserts text exactly at max_length is left untruncated. <!--#da35d5a7d46f1e54-->
  - `TestTruncatePreview.test_over_max_length_truncated` (method) — Asserts over-length text is truncated to max_length with a trailing ellipsis. <!--#77baf880de593713-->
  - `TestTruncatePreview.test_newlines_replaced_with_spaces` (method) — Asserts embedded newlines are replaced with spaces in the preview. <!--#6a2feea46dbb1600-->
  - `TestTruncatePreview.test_custom_ellipsis` (method) — Asserts a custom ellipsis string is used and length is respected. <!--#8e51466d644d9b3b-->
  - `TestTruncatePreview.test_very_short_max_length_uses_ellipsis_prefix` (method) — Asserts that when max_length is at/below ellipsis length, the result is just the ellipsis. <!--#3af1d34021ef37ae-->
  - `TestTruncatePreview.test_default_max_length_is_60` (method) — Asserts the default max_length is 60 characters. <!--#a61c16516db184b4-->
  - `TestTruncatePreview.test_non_string_input_converted` (method) — Asserts non-string input is coerced to its string form. <!--#cb936a812e1235c2-->
  - `TestTruncatePreview.test_max_length_1_with_single_char_ellipsis` (method) — Asserts a max_length of 1 with a one-char ellipsis yields just that character. <!--#7679ad7f0ebe37b2-->
- `TestTruncatePath` (class) — Unit-test suite for tianluo.engine.tool_formatters.truncate_path (and the set_project_root/get_project_root helpers), covering relative pass-through, absolute-to-relative conversion via explicit or module-level project root, 160-char middle truncation that preserves the filename, paths outside the root, and the module-level project-root getter/setter API. <!--#9d7d2e52fb2cd45c-->
  - `TestTruncatePath.test_empty_string` (method) — Asserts an empty path returns empty. <!--#bd883ed0795ba02e-->
  - `TestTruncatePath.test_short_relative_path_unchanged` (method) — Asserts a short relative path is returned unchanged. <!--#11fe79c68479bd0c-->
  - `TestTruncatePath.test_absolute_to_relative_with_project_root` (method) — Asserts an absolute path is made relative when an explicit project_root is passed. <!--#6db0bd51edc54689-->
  - `TestTruncatePath.test_absolute_to_relative_with_module_level_root` (method) — Verifies truncate_path converts an absolute path to a project-relative one using the module-level root set via set_project_root, restoring the prior root afterward. <!--#390468cae2636cfb-->
  - `TestTruncatePath.test_explicit_project_root_overrides_module_level` (method) — Asserts that an explicit project_root argument to truncate_path takes precedence over the module-level root when the two differ. <!--#c1455830f96db24e-->
  - `TestTruncatePath.test_long_path_middle_truncation` (method) — Asserts a >160-char path is middle-truncated while preserving the leading segment and filename. <!--#fe403cdfe519eb62-->
  - `TestTruncatePath.test_filename_never_truncated` (method) — Asserts a single very long filename segment is returned untruncated. <!--#13852d026cb6b47b-->
  - `TestTruncatePath.test_filename_preserved_in_deep_path` (method) — Asserts the filename is preserved when truncating a deeply nested path. <!--#e7dcf16235c62780-->
  - `TestTruncatePath.test_no_project_root_still_works` (method) — Confirms truncate_path returns a relative path unchanged when no module-level project root is set (_project_root is None). <!--#50cc0551a8361cb6-->
  - `TestTruncatePath.test_path_outside_project_root_not_converted` (method) — Asserts paths outside the project root are not converted to relative form. <!--#c17a423bcc5007c2-->
  - `TestTruncatePath.test_default_max_length_is_160` (method) — Asserts a path of exactly 160 chars (the default max) is not truncated. <!--#7e29ca3fa7da7355-->
  - `TestTruncatePath.test_path_161_chars_is_truncated` (method) — Asserts a 161-char path crosses the threshold and is truncated while keeping its filename. <!--#8e3f8b1d086ea80c-->
  - `TestTruncatePath.test_set_get_project_root` (method) — Checks the round-trip contract that get_project_root returns the Path previously stored via set_project_root. <!--#9e90aa49e497373c-->
  - `TestTruncatePath.test_initial_project_root_is_none` (method) — Asserts get_project_root returns None or a Path, tolerating cross-test state. <!--#8993216bf882c97b-->

  - `TestGlobFormatter.test_result_no_files` (method) — Asserts an empty Glob result is labeled 'no files'. <!--#8823830ec4c4fd83-->
- `TestExtractText` (class) — Test class for the _extract_text helper that normalizes strings, content dicts, block lists, and scalars into plain text. <!--#d3674656f6ad5ba5-->
  - `TestExtractText.test_none` (method) — Asserts None extracts to an empty string. <!--#7755a5cc724cd2e0-->
  - `TestExtractText.test_plain_string` (method) — Asserts a plain string extracts to itself. <!--#7215bbe8130c13c4-->
  - `TestExtractText.test_dict_with_content_string` (method) — Asserts a dict with a string content field extracts that string. <!--#78bb1e116b9284d9-->
  - `TestExtractText.test_dict_with_content_blocks` (method) — Asserts a dict with text content blocks extracts them joined by newlines. <!--#5cf6b6e1b562610e-->
  - `TestExtractText.test_dict_error_flag` (method) — Asserts an error-flagged dict still extracts its content text. <!--#94986ced9f8d50a3-->
  - `TestExtractText.test_list_of_text_blocks` (method) — Asserts a list of text blocks extracts them joined by newlines. <!--#68e8a023ed27cb4d-->
  - `TestExtractText.test_list_of_strings` (method) — Asserts a list of strings extracts them joined by newlines. <!--#b182c1feea04133d-->
  - `TestExtractText.test_numeric_input` (method) — Asserts a numeric input extracts to its string form. <!--#e8d05839dddda45e-->
  - `TestExtractText.test_dict_no_content_returns_empty` (method) — Asserts a dict lacking a content field extracts to empty. <!--#5b3da50b10ed0207-->
- `TestRegistry` (class) — Test class verifying the TOOL_FORMATTERS registry contains the expected tools, each with callable use/result entries. <!--#0bcc88b2a9280740-->
  - `TestRegistry.test_all_expected_tools_registered` (method) — Asserts the registry keys are exactly Edit, Write, Read, Bash, Grep, and Glob. <!--#bffb930f9099ea9e-->
  - `TestRegistry.test_each_entry_has_use_and_result` (method) — Asserts every registry entry has callable 'use' and 'result' formatters. <!--#dda7bb864f858c95-->
- `TestRouting` (class) — Test class verifying format_tool_use/result_preview route registered tools to specific formatters and unregistered tools to the generic fallback. <!--#2e8f633be8c385fc-->
  - `TestRouting.test_registered_tool_uses_specific_use_formatter` (method) — Asserts a registered tool (Edit) uses its specific use formatter, not the generic one. <!--#bcf53bed2abd9493-->
  - `TestRouting.test_unregistered_tool_uses_generic_use_formatter` (method) — Asserts an unregistered tool (Agent) falls back to the generic use formatter. <!--#0ab77d6e127ac456-->
  - `TestRouting.test_registered_tool_uses_specific_result_formatter` (method) — Asserts a registered tool (Bash) uses its specific result formatter. <!--#14fa7f61bad5b313-->
  - `TestRouting.test_unregistered_tool_uses_generic_result_formatter` (method) — Asserts an unregistered tool falls back to the generic result formatter. <!--#a8199e936034884d-->
  - `TestRouting.test_result_formatter_accepts_tool_name_first_arg` (method) — Asserts the result formatter takes the tool name as its first argument. <!--#1e56544c64a999f1-->
  - `TestRouting.test_formatter_exception_falls_back_to_generic` (method) — Asserts a per-tool formatter given None input degrades gracefully (falling back to generic). <!--#5e5223fdb238e4d1-->
  - `TestRouting.test_all_registered_tools_produce_tool_name_prefix` (method) — Asserts every registered tool's use preview starts with its own tool-name prefix. <!--#8a371b94b2fdcc76-->
- `TestChipGrammarLeadsWithToolName` (class) — Test class asserting that in-flight and terminal tool chip headers both lead with the tool's own name (not a generic `Tool:` prefix) for unregistered/MCP/Agent calls, while registered tools and the CLI preview helper keep their existing framing. <!--#f2a981281d0248f3-->
  - `TestChipGrammarLeadsWithToolName.test_unregistered_in_flight_leads_with_tool_name` (method) — Checks that the in-flight header for an unregistered tool starts with `<tool_name>: ` and no longer carries the generic `| Input:` framing. <!--#5bc59bac03b7cc8c-->
  - `TestChipGrammarLeadsWithToolName.test_unregistered_terminal_leads_with_same_tool_name` (method) — Checks that the terminal (completed) chip header for an unregistered tool starts with the same `<tool_name> ✓` token as the in-flight one. <!--#b9c39e89242615e8-->
  - `TestChipGrammarLeadsWithToolName.test_agent_in_flight_body_is_key_value_summary` (method) — Asserts an `Agent` call's in-flight header renders its arguments as a `key=value, ...` body after the tool name. <!--#9a33ade72d759744-->
  - `TestChipGrammarLeadsWithToolName.test_mcp_name_kept_whole` (method) — Asserts a fully-qualified `mcp__server__tool` name is kept intact in the in-flight header rather than being split or shortened. <!--#9cb4239a71287720-->
  - `TestChipGrammarLeadsWithToolName.test_empty_input_renders_none_body` (method) — Asserts an empty or missing tool input renders as `<tool_name>: (none)`. <!--#a3c100cfde23b411-->
  - `TestChipGrammarLeadsWithToolName.test_registered_tools_unchanged` (method) — Parametrized regression check that registered tools (Read/Bash/Edit/Write/Grep/Glob) still produce their exact pre-existing in-flight header strings. <!--#2547f828cd42c219-->
  - `TestChipGrammarLeadsWithToolName.test_preview_helpers_keep_their_cli_framing` (method) — Asserts `format_tool_use_preview` deliberately retains the `Tool: <name> | Input: ...` shape used by the CLI stdout line and chat_history transcript. <!--#73a984bd3c5c74b2-->
- `TestInFlightDetailPayload` (class) — Test class covering `build_tool_in_flight_detail_payload`, the running chip's detail panel — verifying its shape/discriminator, that full arguments survive unsummarized, JSON-safety of odd keys and values, and the truncation flag around `TOOL_DETAIL_PAYLOAD_MAX_CHARS`. <!--#d0e9ce03ae36fea2-->
  - `TestInFlightDetailPayload.test_shape_and_discriminator` (method) — Asserts the in-flight payload's exact shape: `kind="tool_input"`, `tool_name`, verbatim `input`, and `truncated=False`. <!--#b376f810a030cd69-->
  - `TestInFlightDetailPayload.test_bash_command_is_carried_whole` (method) — Asserts a long Bash `command` is carried in full (untruncated) in the in-flight payload. <!--#69e879c3cda8ed05-->
  - `TestInFlightDetailPayload.test_agent_prompt_is_carried_whole` (method) — Asserts a multi-line, multi-thousand-character Agent `prompt` and its `description` survive intact in the in-flight payload. <!--#13e756ae930b03d7-->
  - `TestInFlightDetailPayload.test_every_generic_key_survives` (method) — Asserts the payload keeps every input key and value type (list, bool, None) rather than dropping keys like the 3-key chip header summary does. <!--#4d91a3870bf55a0f-->
  - `TestInFlightDetailPayload.test_oversize_string_is_tail_truncated_and_flagged` (method) — Asserts a value exceeding `TOOL_DETAIL_PAYLOAD_MAX_CHARS` is cut to the cap from the head and the payload is flagged `truncated`. <!--#939fa4bac60e36b6-->
  - `TestInFlightDetailPayload.test_exactly_at_the_cap_is_not_flagged` (method) — Boundary check that a value exactly at `TOOL_DETAIL_PAYLOAD_MAX_CHARS` is kept whole and not flagged as truncated. <!--#c1b821c2bfab597f-->
  - `TestInFlightDetailPayload.test_one_long_value_flags_the_whole_payload` (method) — Asserts a single oversize value sets `truncated` for the entire payload while short sibling values pass through untouched. <!--#3812b1115e646f23-->
  - `TestInFlightDetailPayload.test_empty_and_missing_input` (method) — Asserts both `{}` and `None` inputs yield an empty `input` dict with `truncated=False` and the `tool_input` discriminator. <!--#b4021f31d211e10c-->
  - `TestInFlightDetailPayload.test_unserializable_value_becomes_str` (method) — Asserts a non-JSON-serializable value is coerced via `str()` so the payload still serializes. <!--#a713e64cba95bf06-->
  - `TestInFlightDetailPayload.test_payload_is_json_safe` (method) — Round-trip check that a payload mixing nested structures and an unserializable object survives `json.dumps`/`json.loads` unchanged. <!--#a46bf7ddf20bbf69-->
  - `TestInFlightDetailPayload.test_non_string_key_is_stringified` (method) — Asserts non-string input keys are stringified so the payload remains valid JSON. <!--#086f713d337f020c-->
- `TestGenericTerminalDetailCarriesInput` (class) — Test class asserting that settled (terminal) unregistered tool calls carry their `input` in the generic text detail payload — matching the in-flight panel's richness — while registered tools keep their own payload shapes. <!--#2f817b6f121ebb39-->
  - `TestGenericTerminalDetailCarriesInput.test_generic_text_detail_has_input` (method) — Asserts `_build_generic_text_detail` returns a `text` payload carrying both the result text and the call's `input`, unflagged when small. <!--#f2e7d87344c4aca5-->
  - `TestGenericTerminalDetailCarriesInput.test_routed_through_build_tool_detail_payload` (method) — Asserts an unregistered tool routed through the public `build_tool_detail_payload` also lands on the generic `text` payload with its `input` attached. <!--#eba0c1ffa3d97f50-->
  - `TestGenericTerminalDetailCarriesInput.test_input_truncation_flags_the_payload` (method) — Asserts an oversize `input` value is capped and flags `truncated` while the result text is left intact. <!--#77d2e2d4f6a6e6be-->
  - `TestGenericTerminalDetailCarriesInput.test_result_truncation_still_flags_the_payload` (method) — Asserts an oversize result text flags `truncated` while a short `input` passes through unchanged. <!--#ea425ce6e60ae4c7-->
  - `TestGenericTerminalDetailCarriesInput.test_empty_input_yields_empty_dict_not_missing_key` (method) — Asserts an empty input still produces an `input` key holding `{}` rather than omitting the key entirely. <!--#49ebd82a443989c6-->
  - `TestGenericTerminalDetailCarriesInput.test_registered_payload_structure_unchanged` (method) — Parametrized regression check that registered tools (Bash/Read/Grep/Glob) keep their specific payload `kind` and fields with no `input` key added. <!--#fcb505364b508967-->

### `tests/engine/test_verify_spec_renderer.py` (python) — Unit tests for the VERIFY_SPEC step renderer, verifying that summary and recommendations fall back to the nested verification_result dict (with top-level fields taking precedence) and that issue priorities produce well-formed Rich close tags. <!--#e4658029ecbe028e|17e1e29728c5483e-->
- `_make_step` (function) — Helper that builds a COMPLETED VERIFY_SPEC Step with the given outputs dict for use in renderer tests. <!--#8c5d91b6af6da929-->
- `TestSummaryFallback` (class) — Test class verifying that `_render_verify_spec` derives its summary text with top-level `summary` taking precedence over the nested `outputs['verification_result']['summary']`, gracefully handling missing or non-dict verification results. <!--#80ea2edf502e1422-->
  - `TestSummaryFallback.test_reads_from_nested_verification_result` (method) — Asserts the rendered content pulls the summary from the nested `verification_result` dict when no top-level summary is present. <!--#f78c37c1bf5012ab-->
  - `TestSummaryFallback.test_toplevel_takes_precedence` (method) — Asserts a top-level `summary` is used and the nested `verification_result` summary is excluded when both exist. <!--#fa15961b03c730a5-->
  - `TestSummaryFallback.test_no_summary_anywhere` (method) — Asserts rendering still succeeds and emits a PASSED marker when no summary field exists anywhere. <!--#9253608414ba93e0-->
  - `TestSummaryFallback.test_verification_result_not_dict` (method) — Asserts rendering does not crash and still emits PASSED when `verification_result` is a string rather than a dict. <!--#0677d0cc5285864c-->
- `TestRecommendationsFallback` (class) — Test class verifying that `_render_verify_spec` sources `recommendations` from the nested `verification_result` dict as a fallback, with a top-level `recommendations` list taking precedence. <!--#1e0f4bf57370eb3d-->
  - `TestRecommendationsFallback.test_reads_from_nested_verification_result` (method) — Asserts both nested recommendation items appear in the rendered content when only the nested `verification_result` supplies them. <!--#3be4a17aa2d7df8c-->
  - `TestRecommendationsFallback.test_toplevel_takes_precedence` (method) — Asserts top-level recommendations are rendered and nested ones excluded when both are provided. <!--#ec901385227e94ef-->
- `TestRichCloseTag` (class) — Test class verifying that issue-priority rendering emits well-formed Rich close tags (`[/red]`, `[/yellow]`, `[/dim]`) without a spurious extra `]` bracket across all priority levels. <!--#82e0b55430fe4fd3-->
  - `TestRichCloseTag.test_red_close_tag_for_high_priority` (method) — Asserts a high-priority issue produces a clean `[/red]` close tag and never the malformed `[/red]]`. <!--#bd0618e1496491be-->
  - `TestRichCloseTag.test_yellow_close_tag_for_medium_priority` (method) — Asserts a medium-priority issue produces a clean `[/yellow]` close tag and never the malformed `[/yellow]]`. <!--#55afee4a1bb6e4f3-->
  - `TestRichCloseTag.test_dim_close_tag_for_low_priority` (method) — Asserts a low-priority issue produces a clean `[/dim]` close tag and never the malformed `[/dim]]`. <!--#9da0e0179b83cb9c-->
  - `TestRichCloseTag.test_all_priorities_correct_tags` (method) — Asserts that a mix of critical/high/medium/low issues yields all correct close tags and none of the malformed double-bracket variants. <!--#68fcd33ebbc70864-->

### `tests/engine/test_workspace_snapshot.py` (python) — Unit test suite for `workspace_snapshot`, exercising `snapshot_workspace`/`compare_snapshots` over throwaway git repos to verify that tracked/untracked additions, modifications, removals and commits made during a window are detected and named, that pre-existing dirt, gitignored files and the engine's own `tianluo/`(or legacy `se3/`) runtime directory are excluded, that snapshots survive dict round-trips, and that non-repos or missing git degrade fail-open to an `undecidable` yet clean delta. <!--#6a174c67975b58a9|c1bbd00047438e81-->
- `_git` (function) — Test helper that runs a git subcommand inside a given repo directory with output suppressed and failures raised. <!--#836c49dd876919ac-->
- `repo` (function) — Pytest fixture creating a throwaway git repo in tmp_path with a single committed `tracked.py` file as the baseline for snapshot tests. <!--#f7231b09371de409-->
- `TestSnapshotAndCompare` (class) — Core test class for `snapshot_workspace`/`compare_snapshots`, covering clean/dirty detection, named tracked and untracked add/modify/remove paths, HEAD movement from commits, serialization round-trips, gitignore invisibility, and graceful degradation when git's path output can't be aligned. <!--#8ee007121f590a1e-->
  - `TestSnapshotAndCompare.test_no_change_is_clean` (method) — Asserts two back-to-back snapshots of an untouched repo compare as clean. <!--#782ea965e3053e0c-->
  - `TestSnapshotAndCompare.test_tracked_modification_is_reported` (method) — Asserts editing a tracked file yields a non-clean delta with `tracked_changed` set and a 'Tracked files' mention in `describe()`. <!--#956bf6bcb9ac2805-->
  - `TestSnapshotAndCompare.test_tracked_modification_names_the_file` (method) — Asserts a tracked edit is reported with the concrete path in `added_tracked`, `tracked_paths`, `changed_paths` and the description, so the revert instruction is actionable. <!--#bfd2a0b8a335a02c-->
  - `TestSnapshotAndCompare.test_probe_on_top_of_preexisting_work_is_named_as_modified` (method) — Asserts an edit layered onto an already-dirty file lands in `modified_tracked` and the description warns to undo only the agent's own edits. <!--#634e297116603fc7-->
  - `TestSnapshotAndCompare.test_wiped_preexisting_work_is_named_as_removed` (method) — Asserts reverting away pre-existing uncommitted work is itself reported, as a named path in `removed_tracked`. <!--#3b228cf36dc3fce2-->
  - `TestSnapshotAndCompare.test_only_the_touched_tracked_path_is_named` (method) — Asserts unrelated pre-existing dirty files are excluded from `tracked_paths` and the description, leaving only the path touched during the window. <!--#2ceb91f0e6092b26-->
  - `TestSnapshotAndCompare.test_unalignable_diff_degrades_to_a_file_less_report` (method) — Monkeypatches `_run_git` to return unexpected `--name-only` output and asserts the delta still flags a tracked change while marking paths unavailable and saying so in `describe()`. <!--#4c7b25237c1b4ee0-->
  - `TestSnapshotAndCompare.test_snapshot_survives_a_serialization_round_trip` (method) — Asserts a snapshot survives `to_dict`/`from_dict` unchanged and still produces correct deltas, as required for persisting the baseline across step attempts. <!--#671f9252ceb99558-->
  - `TestSnapshotAndCompare.test_from_dict_rejects_garbage` (method) — Asserts `WorkspaceSnapshot.from_dict` returns None for None, non-dict, and malformed-field payloads. <!--#30bc30960284e937-->
  - `TestSnapshotAndCompare.test_new_untracked_file_is_reported_as_added` (method) — Asserts a newly created untracked file makes the delta dirty and appears in `added_untracked` and the description. <!--#33f78edde86a0aaf-->
  - `TestSnapshotAndCompare.test_reverting_the_change_restores_cleanliness` (method) — Asserts that undoing a tracked edit and deleting a scratch file returns the delta to clean. <!--#066cd9cf76e38391-->
  - `TestSnapshotAndCompare.test_preexisting_dirty_tree_does_not_leak_into_the_delta` (method) — Asserts a tree already dirty at baseline contributes nothing to the delta, and that only changes layered on top register — the reason the check compares snapshots rather than demanding a clean tree. <!--#a0fa5907977326a4-->
  - `TestSnapshotAndCompare.test_untracked_content_change_is_reported_as_modified` (method) — Asserts a content edit to an existing untracked file is reported in `modified_untracked`. <!--#3d44a792af90657c-->
  - `TestSnapshotAndCompare.test_untracked_removal_is_reported` (method) — Asserts deleting an untracked file present at baseline is reported in `removed_untracked`. <!--#1317b7d1dbc09fac-->
  - `TestSnapshotAndCompare.test_commit_made_during_the_window_is_reported` (method) — Asserts a commit made during the window is caught via `head_changed`/'HEAD moved' even though the tracked diff hash is unchanged on both sides. <!--#f32b65bec9d155f5-->
  - `TestSnapshotAndCompare.test_commit_of_untracked_scratch_file_is_reported` (method) — Asserts committing a scratch file — which also empties it from the untracked set — is still caught through `head_changed`. <!--#fe6a09150f97dcf6-->
  - `TestSnapshotAndCompare.test_undoing_the_commit_restores_cleanliness` (method) — Asserts the documented restoration path (soft reset to the baseline HEAD plus a surgical file revert) brings the delta back to clean. <!--#a68d73ff6bd1d812-->
  - `TestSnapshotAndCompare.test_gitignored_files_are_invisible` (method) — Asserts files created under a gitignored directory never enter the snapshot and leave the delta clean. <!--#b20e4ef6326fcfba-->
- `TestRuntimeDirectoryIsExcluded` (class) — Test class asserting the engine's own runtime directory (`tianluo/`, legacy `se3/`, tracked artifacts included) is excluded from snapshots while lookalike top-level files and genuine leftovers are still detected. <!--#6a744498e3874daf-->
  - `TestRuntimeDirectoryIsExcluded.test_engine_writes_under_the_runtime_dir_do_not_dirty_the_delta` (method) — Asserts history JSONL appends and flow-state writes under `tianluo/` leave the delta clean with no changed paths. <!--#e528facd019db456-->
  - `TestRuntimeDirectoryIsExcluded.test_tracked_runtime_files_are_excluded_too` (method) — Asserts committed runtime artifacts such as `tianluo/code-index.md` are excluded even though they are tracked. <!--#edcc9265394f07b3-->
  - `TestRuntimeDirectoryIsExcluded.test_legacy_runtime_dir_is_excluded` (method) — Asserts a project still on the legacy `se3/` layout also has its runtime directory excluded. <!--#a1fce63703fe27ca-->
  - `TestRuntimeDirectoryIsExcluded.test_a_lookalike_top_level_file_is_still_watched` (method) — Asserts the exclusion is directory-scoped: a top-level `tianluo.example.yaml` is a project file and still reported as added. <!--#d8a3c69134e82651-->
  - `TestRuntimeDirectoryIsExcluded.test_real_leftovers_are_still_caught_alongside_engine_writes` (method) — Asserts real leftovers are still reported when engine runtime writes happen in the same window, with `changed_paths` listing only the non-runtime files. <!--#3e21413cd0da6634-->
- `TestDegradation` (class) — Test class covering fail-open behaviour: a non-repo, a missing git binary, or a one-sided unavailable snapshot yields an `undecidable` delta that still reads as clean. <!--#c954045b593680a3-->
  - `TestDegradation.test_non_repo_degrades_to_undecidable` (method) — Asserts snapshotting a non-git directory is unavailable and produces an undecidable-but-clean delta that says 'unavailable'. <!--#0d6a05a08dc09a4d-->
  - `TestDegradation.test_missing_git_binary_degrades` (method) — Monkeypatches `subprocess.run` to raise FileNotFoundError and asserts the snapshot degrades to unavailable rather than failing the step. <!--#1121349b34cf65a6-->
  - `TestDegradation.test_one_sided_unavailability_is_undecidable` (method) — Asserts a valid baseline compared against an unavailable second snapshot is undecidable and still clean. <!--#5cacab79e432ff5c-->
- `TestNoWriteOperations` (class) — Invariant-guard test class proving `workspace_snapshot` never mutates the workspace, both by scanning its executable source for destructive git subcommands and file writers and by checking a real tree is untouched after snapshotting. <!--#b227c0d8d8aca791-->
  - `TestNoWriteOperations.test_source_contains_no_destructive_git_or_file_writes` (method) — Strips comments and docstrings from the module source and asserts no quoted destructive git subcommand or filesystem-write call appears in executable lines. <!--#989e17a6180fdcd6-->
  - `TestNoWriteOperations.test_snapshotting_does_not_touch_the_working_tree` (method) — Asserts repeated `snapshot_workspace` calls leave dirty tracked and untracked file contents byte-identical. <!--#4b58257a435c541d-->

### `tests/engine/test_worktree_gc.py` (python) — Unit test suite for the worktree-GC engine module, exercising stale-run discovery (`find_stale_worktree_runs`), the `_dir_size` byte-summing helper, and the full GC sweep across merged, unmerged, unresolvable-base, dry-run, archive-failure, and multi-run-isolation scenarios using real git worktrees and engine.json run headers. <!--#532bed678f45d137|78aa405d786dea02-->
- `_git` (function) — Test helper that runs a `git -C <path>` subcommand with output captured, raising on non-zero exit. <!--#c3617b36133d72b8-->
- `_init_repo` (function) — Test helper that initializes a git repo with an identity and an initial README commit, returning the default branch name. <!--#3f2c447fc20652bb-->
- `_branch_exists` (function) — Test helper returning whether a given git ref/branch resolves in the repo. <!--#fe856a428f75db97-->
- `_make_worktree_run` (function) — Test helper that creates a real git worktree under `tianluo/worktrees/<name>` with a seeded `engine.json` run header, optionally merging the branch back into base and backdating the engine.json mtime to exercise the GC filters. <!--#86c8f916d7d8c542-->
- `TestFindStaleWorktreeRuns` (class) — Test class verifying that `find_stale_worktree_runs` returns only terminal (completed/failed), over-age, worktree-mode runs while excluding fresh, running, non-worktree, corrupt-JSON, archived, and missing-root cases. <!--#350c8a13db657705-->
  - `TestFindStaleWorktreeRuns.test_returns_only_terminal_over_age_worktree_runs` (method) — Asserts only the stale completed worktree run is returned (fresh, running, and non-worktree runs excluded) with its recorded fields intact. <!--#fec728ae6fb0c6dd-->
  - `TestFindStaleWorktreeRuns.test_failed_status_is_terminal` (method) — Asserts a `failed`-status over-age run counts as terminal and is reported stale. <!--#e5f4d4508e496fab-->
  - `TestFindStaleWorktreeRuns.test_corrupt_json_excluded` (method) — Asserts a run with unparseable engine.json is skipped rather than crashing the scan. <!--#f2601708bfefcb72-->
  - `TestFindStaleWorktreeRuns.test_archive_dir_not_scanned` (method) — Test asserting that `find_stale_worktree_runs` skips runs living under the `.archive` directory even when their engine.json is terminal and over-age. <!--#585f057802479f55-->
  - `TestFindStaleWorktreeRuns.test_missing_worktrees_root` (method) — Asserts an empty list is returned when the `tianluo/worktrees` root does not exist. <!--#22865e86df6dde0f-->
- `TestDirSize` (class) — Test suite for the `_dir_size` helper covering recursive byte summation and the missing-directory case. <!--#5cfbdc4540b3140f-->
  - `TestDirSize.test_sums_file_bytes` (method) — Asserts `_dir_size` recursively sums file byte counts across nested subdirectories. <!--#8719a6773515b7c5-->
  - `TestDirSize.test_missing_dir_is_zero` (method) — Asserts `_dir_size` returns 0 for a nonexistent directory. <!--#e131c67279883faf-->
- `TestGcMergedBranch` (class) — Test class verifying that `gc_worktree_runs` archives and deletes worktrees whose branch is provably merged into its recorded original branch, including the case where HEAD sits on an unrelated branch that does not contain it. <!--#2afec2dd0be6787d-->
  - `TestGcMergedBranch.test_archives_and_deletes_merged_branch` (method) — Test asserting the happy path where a merged, over-age worktree is archived under `.archive/worktree_<name>-<epoch>`, its branch and worktree are removed, and its terminal state is promoted into the main archive. <!--#559436d78c58d1ca-->
  - `TestGcMergedBranch.test_deletes_merged_branch_when_head_on_unrelated_branch` (method) — Regression test asserting GC still deletes a branch proven merged into its recorded base even though the current checkout is a divergent branch that would make `git branch -d` refuse. <!--#df351e1b0946b432-->
- `TestGcUnmergedBranch` (class) — Test suite verifying GC archives and removes an unmerged run's worktree but preserves its branch ref and reports it as retained_unmerged. <!--#4512cc62716a39a2-->
  - `TestGcUnmergedBranch.test_retains_unmerged_branch_ref` (method) — Asserts an unmerged run is archived with its worktree removed but its branch kept and recorded in retained_unmerged with branch/original metadata. <!--#4f02d9d61c87a810-->
- `TestGcUnresolvableBase` (class) — Test class asserting that GC retains a worktree's branch when merge cannot be proven against the recorded original branch (missing ref or none recorded), never falling back to a HEAD ancestor check. <!--#0e2acf42b89d00bc-->
  - `TestGcUnresolvableBase._rewrite_original_branch` (method) — Test helper that mutates a worktree's engine.json `worktree_original_branch` field (set or remove) and re-backdates its mtime past the age threshold. <!--#2bd5135a89142c34-->
  - `TestGcUnresolvableBase.test_retains_branch_when_original_branch_missing_ref` (method) — Asserts a branch is retained (with a 'no longer resolvable' reason) when its recorded original branch no longer resolves, despite being a HEAD ancestor. <!--#51bbb4cf3f1eb0e9-->
  - `TestGcUnresolvableBase.test_retains_branch_when_no_original_branch_recorded` (method) — Asserts a branch is retained (with a 'no recorded original branch' reason) when no original branch was recorded at all. <!--#e8be00d31c370061-->
- `TestGcDryRun` (class) — Test class verifying that `gc_worktree_runs` in dry-run mode populates the report accounting without touching the worktree, branch, or archive directory on disk. <!--#337532471eedcdba-->
  - `TestGcDryRun.test_dry_run_touches_nothing` (method) — Test asserting a dry-run GC reports the would-be archived run and reclaimed bytes while leaving the worktree and branch intact, writing no archive, and reporting a None archive path. <!--#ead7cbce1eafa336-->
- `TestGcArchiveFailure` (class) — Test suite verifying that when archiving or worktree removal fails, GC skips destructive steps, preserves the worktree/branch, and records the error instead of phantom reclamation. <!--#22620de52d631de4-->
  - `TestGcArchiveFailure.test_archive_failure_preserves_worktree_and_branch` (method) — Asserts an archive-step exception leaves the worktree and branch intact and records an 'archive' error with nothing reclaimed. <!--#1b3ff49f8e019176-->
  - `TestGcArchiveFailure.test_removal_failure_not_reported_as_reclaimed` (method) — Asserts that a silently-failing worktree removal is caught as a 'removal failed' error rather than reported as reclaimed, keeping the branch for a re-run. <!--#0d41e736760c2491-->
- `TestGcRunIsolation` (class) — Test suite verifying one run's failure during the GC sweep does not abort processing of subsequent runs. <!--#d60ff9e6c91820d9-->
  - `TestGcRunIsolation.test_one_failure_does_not_abort_sweep` (method) — Asserts that when the first (alphabetically) run's archive raises, the later good run is still archived and removed and only the failing run's error is recorded. <!--#134068b60a02ac64-->

## `tests/engine/formatters/` — Test package holding unit tests for SE3's engine formatters, currently covering TaskDataValidator's task-data validation/normalization rules and TaskFormatter's Rich rendering (tree/table/detail/summary/dependency views) plus the format_task_groups convenience function. <!--#0c872085036fe2d2|7daab9cb57e5825f-->

## `tests/engine/steps/` — Test package for the engine's flow-step handlers, dominated by the COMMIT step (version-read auto-repair, message generation and priority, baseline diffing, docs/README/VERSIONS updates, root-whitelist guard) and the IMPLEMENT step (resume idempotency, restricted edits and completion status, group summaries, estimated_test_duration, re-entry version/baseline preservation, and the DAG-parallel path with its worktree/branch topologies, merge-conflict robustness and cleanup safety net), plus coverage of the e2e step's switch, scenario-failure routing and environment-failure firewall. <!--#df7491d73dbf2917|f769d4c7c30b9050-->

### `tests/engine/steps/__init__.py` (python) — Package initializer marking the test directory for se3 engine step tests. <!--#429dc51c11cee801|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/engine/steps/test_commit.py` (python) — Unit tests for the COMMIT flow step, covering version-read auto-repair paths (RuntimeError/ValueError/KeyError in script vs. file mode, with and without an existing version file), template summary generation and its optional Version Analysis section, and the helpers that collect changed files and test results from the flow's prior steps. <!--#da084d33cebd711b|5574fe2342349e99-->
- `_make_flow` (function) — Test helper that builds a MagicMock(spec=FlowInstance) with sensible defaults (bugfix task, non-worktree mode) plus a mocked State carrying selected_steps/step_history, for the commit-step unit tests. <!--#e7b3b7588ad542b8-->

  - `TestRuntimeErrorScriptModeAutoRepair.test_runtime_error_script_mode_triggers_generate_version_script` (method) — Asserts that a first-call RuntimeError in script mode calls generate_version_script(project_root) and the successful second read_version yields StepStatus.COMPLETED. <!--#81eda9348479a18f-->

  - `TestRuntimeErrorFileModeAutoRepair.test_runtime_error_file_mode_triggers_initialize_version_system` (method) — Asserts a first-call RuntimeError in file mode calls initialize_version_system(project_root, initial_version='0.1.0') and the successful retry yields StepStatus.COMPLETED. <!--#8d7b7e53645ca243-->
  - `TestRuntimeErrorFileModeAutoRepair.test_runtime_error_file_mode_retry_fails_propagates` (method) — Asserts that when file-mode repair runs but read_version keeps raising, the step ends FAILED with the persistent error in step.error_message. <!--#21cfa33b6d9643a3-->
- `TestRuntimeErrorNoVersionFileAutoRepair` (class) — Test class covering the no-version-file path where initialize creates a file but read_version still raises RuntimeError, exercising script- and file-mode repair-then-retry success. <!--#53ba4ce190232802-->
  - `TestRuntimeErrorNoVersionFileAutoRepair.test_no_version_file_script_mode_runtime_error_triggers_repair` (method) — Asserts that with no initial version file in script mode, a read_version RuntimeError triggers generate_version_script() and the retry completes successfully. <!--#bb822f2f85ee4a9f-->
  - `TestRuntimeErrorNoVersionFileAutoRepair.test_no_version_file_file_mode_runtime_error_triggers_repair` (method) — Asserts that with no initial version file in file mode, initialize_version_system() is called twice (create then repair) and the retry completes successfully. <!--#177de76f44188d85-->
- `TestValueErrorKeyErrorRegression` (class) — Regression test class confirming the pre-existing ValueError/KeyError handling in read_version still triggers file-/script-mode auto-repair and propagates FAILED when the retry also fails. <!--#fcbbe512d86ebbb2-->
  - `TestValueErrorKeyErrorRegression.test_value_error_triggers_auto_repair_file_mode` (method) — Asserts a ValueError from read_version in file mode triggers initialize_version_system() repair and the step completes. <!--#3ff0b20c68827af2-->

- `TestCommitVersionTagIntegration` (class) — Integration test class running commit_handler against a real git repo to verify the direct-commit path's annotated version-tag behaviour (created on minor/major, skipped on patch/worktree, failure handling, re-entry). <!--#99035a91b1b2b447-->
  - `TestCommitVersionTagIntegration._run_version_commit` (method) — Helper that runs commit_handler with a version-bump step against a real repo, patching version config/_update_docs/code-index refresh, and returns the (StepStatus, Step) pair. <!--#fc735c2281c9d4e4-->
  - `TestCommitVersionTagIntegration.test_direct_minor_commit_creates_annotated_tag_on_version_commit` (method) — Asserts a minor-bump direct commit creates an annotated tag pointing at the version commit with the commit subject as its body. <!--#c8801dcdbc764b25-->
  - `TestCommitVersionTagIntegration.test_direct_patch_commit_does_not_create_tag` (method) — Asserts a patch bump commits and reports the version but creates no git tag. <!--#ade403b7655fdc34-->
  - `TestCommitVersionTagIntegration.test_worktree_commit_does_not_create_tag` (method) — Asserts that in worktree mode a minor bump completes without creating a version tag and never calls create_annotated_version_tag. <!--#6eb4d7faf0de59c3-->
  - `TestCommitVersionTagIntegration.test_tag_failure_fails_step_with_diagnostics` (method) — Asserts that a VersionTagError fails the step while still reporting the version commit as committed/durable and surfacing the tag name and stderr in the error message. <!--#2354e08372c153eb-->
  - `TestCommitVersionTagIntegration.test_tag_failure_error_names_tag_and_target_commit` (method) — Asserts that when tagging raises, the error message names both the tag (v2.0.0) and the target version commit hash so an operator can recover by hand. <!--#76426d2a7aae1ca5-->
  - `TestCommitVersionTagIntegration.test_unreadable_version_commit_hash_fails_without_fake_commit_ish` (method) — Asserts that an unreadable HEAD hash fails the step, skips tagging, and never fabricates an 'unknown' commit-ish, reporting the read failure and stderr instead. <!--#266e31da3eb230b3-->
  - `TestCommitVersionTagIntegration.test_reentry_after_tag_failure_commits_new_changes_and_never_backfills` (method) — Asserts that after a tag failure, a re-entry commits new working-tree changes as an ordinary commit, never backfilling the missing tag (tag_skipped_reentry=True). <!--#5c14c8dfbfe31075-->
  - `TestCommitVersionTagIntegration.test_reentry_after_successful_tagged_commit_completes` (method) — Asserts a fix-loop re-entry after a successfully tagged version commit completes without duplicating or moving the existing tag. <!--#93193a55e3998519-->
  - `TestCommitVersionTagIntegration.test_resume_after_lost_marker_skips_tag_via_git_durable_evidence` (method) — Asserts that after a crash loses the in-context re-entry marker, the step still recognises its own landed version commit via git-durable evidence and skips re-tagging. <!--#c88b940e64a18912-->
  - `TestCommitVersionTagIntegration.test_crash_before_commit_resume_still_tags_uncommitted_version_write` (method) — Asserts that an uncommitted version file already at the target is not treated as a re-entry, so the resuming commit still creates the tag. <!--#20b248508552c368-->
  - `TestCommitVersionTagIntegration.test_foreign_preexisting_tag_fails_loudly` (method) — Asserts a same-named tag not created by this flow is treated as a collision: the step fails with git's refusal and the foreign tag is left untouched. <!--#0886369fe1040e9a-->
- `TestDetectRuntimeLeaks` (class) — Parametrized pure-function test class for _detect_runtime_leaks, tabulating which paths count as leaking runtime artifacts (top-level .se3, nested runtime subtrees) versus legitimate tianluo/ and source files. <!--#8bcf67aee820ebe1-->
  - `TestDetectRuntimeLeaks.test_detect` (method) — Parametrized assertion that each path is correctly classified as a runtime leak or exempt. <!--#3058eb1dd82c66a1-->
  - `TestDetectRuntimeLeaks.test_mixed_batch_filters_only_leaks` (method) — Asserts _detect_runtime_leaks returns only the leaking paths (.se3/... and foo/tianluo/logs/...) from a mixed batch, preserving order. <!--#30efc718195cc0b1-->
  - `TestDetectRuntimeLeaks.test_empty_and_blank_inputs` (method) — Asserts empty and blank/whitespace path inputs yield no leaks. <!--#03983fab84123716-->
  - `TestDetectRuntimeLeaks.test_no_subprocess_or_io` (method) — Asserts _detect_runtime_leaks is a pure function that never invokes subprocess.run. <!--#ff7d710a8534bc8f-->
- `TestStripRuntimeLeaksFaultTolerance` (class) — Test class asserting _strip_runtime_leaks is a fault-tolerant backstop that never raises, even in a non-git directory or when the list/unstage subprocess calls throw. <!--#843299f95c127ba0-->
  - `TestStripRuntimeLeaksFaultTolerance.test_non_git_directory_does_not_raise` (method) — Asserts running the strip in a non-git directory only warns and does not raise. <!--#dc5dc0a16fc337f1-->
  - `TestStripRuntimeLeaksFaultTolerance.test_list_subprocess_exception_swallowed` (method) — Asserts _strip_runtime_leaks swallows an OSError from the initial 'git diff --cached' listing call without raising. <!--#3f9ca765110280df-->
  - `TestStripRuntimeLeaksFaultTolerance.test_unstage_subprocess_exception_swallowed` (method) — Asserts _strip_runtime_leaks swallows an OSError from the unstage/restore call (after a successful list) without raising. <!--#a54b66a1fbe43835-->
- `TestRuntimeLeakGuardIntegration` (class) — End-to-end test class for commit_handler's runtime-leak guard against a real repo: leaks are unstaged while normal artifacts commit, no-leak commits everything, guard git failures don't block, and a leak-only index is a clean no-op. <!--#d41500e5a58177de-->
  - `TestRuntimeLeakGuardIntegration._run_commit` (method) — Helper that runs commit_handler with version bumping disabled and a stubbed commit message against a real repo, returning the resulting StepStatus. <!--#7d4707891c7a0bd2-->
  - `TestRuntimeLeakGuardIntegration.test_leak_unstaged_normal_artifact_committed` (method) — Asserts a leaking .se3/ file is left untracked on disk (not committed) while normal source and whitelisted tianluo/ artifacts are committed. <!--#c0ccd76e75f5e55e-->
  - `TestRuntimeLeakGuardIntegration.test_no_leak_commits_everything` (method) — Asserts that with no leaks the guard commits everything, including top-level tianluo/state/engine.json which is exempt from stripping. <!--#1f1bd34f4b0c74a8-->
  - `TestRuntimeLeakGuardIntegration.test_guard_git_failure_does_not_block_commit` (method) — Asserts that when the guard's 'git restore --staged' errors on a bogus path, it only warns and the real commit still completes. <!--#1243bfd1a701dd97-->
  - `TestRuntimeLeakGuardIntegration.test_only_leak_empties_index_no_op_success` (method) — Regression asserting that when the sole change is a stripped runtime leak, the emptied index is treated as a clean no-op success (committed=False, commit_hash='no-changes', HEAD unchanged) rather than FAILED. <!--#05f05f87a301c653-->
- `TestIndexHasStagedChanges` (class) — Test class for _index_has_staged_changes, covering empty index (False), staged change (True), and fault-tolerant assumption of changes (True) on subprocess error. <!--#0721c8820dcbc9c8-->
  - `TestIndexHasStagedChanges.test_empty_index_returns_false` (method) — Asserts an empty index returns False. <!--#60139048b5536718-->
  - `TestIndexHasStagedChanges.test_staged_change_returns_true` (method) — Asserts a staged change returns True. <!--#6a1634457cbd0670-->
  - `TestIndexHasStagedChanges.test_subprocess_error_assumes_changes` (method) — Asserts _index_has_staged_changes returns True on an OSError so a git failure never short-circuits a real commit. <!--#e3ea5a56bb36e58f-->
- `TestCommitIdempotentVersionWrite` (class) — Regression test class asserting the commit step performs an authoritative overwrite, accepting a suggested_version equal to the on-disk version as a valid idempotent write rather than an error. <!--#40d65779139c679e-->
  - `TestCommitIdempotentVersionWrite.test_commit_idempotent_when_suggested_equals_disk` (method) — Asserts that with disk and suggested_version both 5.2.0, set_version is called exactly once, clear_backup runs (no rollback), and outputs report a successful bump/commit. <!--#217294b5f23c115c-->

### `tests/engine/steps/test_commit_baseline.py` (python) — Unit tests for the commit step's `_has_changes()` baseline-diff logic and `commit_handler`'s forwarding of the flow's baseline_commit, using mocked subprocess.run. <!--#0d75e8e17a3394e4|be474f048467ed02-->
- `_run_result` (function) — Helper that builds a MagicMock mimicking a subprocess.run result with given returncode/stdout/stderr. <!--#6df94754b52c262b-->
- `TestHasChangesBaseline` (class) — Unit tests for `_has_changes` verifying its behavior with and without a `baseline_commit`, covering `git status --porcelain` fallback, `git diff <baseline> HEAD --quiet` change detection, clean/dirty tree cases, and fallback to git status when git diff errors or raises. <!--#8b856a439676dfb3-->
  - `TestHasChangesBaseline.test_no_baseline_uses_git_status` (method) — Asserts that without a baseline, `_has_changes` uses `git status --porcelain` and reports True when output is non-empty. <!--#23ed2aff4d418b1f-->
  - `TestHasChangesBaseline.test_no_baseline_clean_working_tree` (method) — Asserts that without a baseline, an empty git status yields False (clean tree). <!--#e79d1781c26f41b8-->
  - `TestHasChangesBaseline.test_baseline_with_diff_detected` (method) — Asserts that with a baseline, a `git diff --quiet` exit code of 1 is treated as changes existing (True). <!--#2f8309c8d127ecbe-->
  - `TestHasChangesBaseline.test_baseline_no_diff_clean_tree` (method) — Asserts that no committed diff plus a clean working tree returns False via two git calls. <!--#90eaca72416547f0-->
  - `TestHasChangesBaseline.test_baseline_no_diff_but_dirty_tree` (method) — Asserts that no committed diff but a dirty working tree (git status output) returns True. <!--#d24d5b1f36bfdc9c-->
  - `TestHasChangesBaseline.test_baseline_git_diff_error_falls_back` (method) — Asserts that a git diff error (returncode > 1) makes `_has_changes` fall back to git status. <!--#d349c475c7a75ae8-->
  - `TestHasChangesBaseline.test_baseline_git_diff_exception_falls_back` (method) — Asserts that an exception raised by git diff makes `_has_changes` fall back to git status. <!--#e86b9e017cf1ef87-->
- `TestCommitHandlerPassesBaseline` (class) — Unit tests asserting that `commit_handler` forwards `flow.baseline_commit` (a value or `None`) into `_has_changes` when deciding whether to commit. <!--#75be5564861fc31c-->
  - `TestCommitHandlerPassesBaseline.test_baseline_commit_forwarded` (method) — Verifies `commit_handler` passes a non-null `flow.baseline_commit` ("deadbeef") to `_has_changes` and returns `StepStatus.COMPLETED` with `committed` set to False when no changes exist. <!--#8da6ff353487cb5c-->
  - `TestCommitHandlerPassesBaseline.test_no_baseline_commit_passes_none` (method) — Verifies `commit_handler` passes `baseline_commit=None` to `_has_changes` when the flow has no baseline commit. <!--#97f82b68efe9d54c-->

### `tests/engine/steps/test_commit_docs_update.py` (python) — Integration test suite for the DocumentationUpdater wiring in commit_handler, covering subtask 1.4 cases (a)-(f) — README badge update/insertion, VERSIONS.md creation/prepending, missing-README tolerance, docs-failure warnings, and skipping docs when no version bump occurs — using mocked VersionBumper/git but real deterministic file writes against a tmp_path project root. <!--#aefa9ca33297114d|c0fe7dbc7ce8257f-->
- `_make_flow` (function) — Test helper that builds a MagicMock(spec=FlowInstance) with docs-flow defaults (feature task, tmp_path as project root, is_worktree_mode=False) and an attached mock State whose selected_steps include COMMIT and SUMMARIZE. <!--#7e8e824fb6abcfa2-->

- `_docs_config` (function) — Test helper returning a DocsConfig-like MagicMock whose to_updater_config() yields a deterministic versions_entry_template, keeping the docs-wiring tests hermetic while still exercising the real load_docs_config().to_updater_config() forwarding path. <!--#5115456d05a618d5-->
- `TestReadmeAndVersionsUpdated` (class) — Test class asserting that the commit step bumps the README version badge and prepends a new dated entry (preserving prior history) to an existing VERSIONS.md. <!--#30c1d4ed7ca958fa-->
  - `TestReadmeAndVersionsUpdated.test_badge_and_versions_updated` (method) — Verifies commit_handler bumps 0.1.0→0.2.0, rewrites the README badge, and inserts the new VERSIONS.md entry (with change bullets) ahead of the preserved older entry. <!--#398349b7792a62aa-->
- `TestReadmeNoBadgeInsertsAfterHeading` (class) — Test class asserting that when the README has no existing version badge, one is inserted just after the title heading and both docs files are explicitly git-staged. <!--#3e05d5e1bb0cc6c4-->
  - `TestReadmeNoBadgeInsertsAfterHeading.test_badge_inserted_after_title` (method) — Verifies a badge-less README gets a 1.0.0 badge placed after '# My Project', and that `git add README.md` and `git add VERSIONS.md` were both invoked. <!--#440b45b4d058057f-->
- `TestVersionsCreatedWhenMissing` (class) — Test class asserting VERSIONS.md is created from scratch with a '# Version History' title and the new version entry when the file does not already exist. <!--#d601377094031a16-->
  - `TestVersionsCreatedWhenMissing.test_versions_md_created_with_title` (method) — Verifies commit_handler creates a missing VERSIONS.md that starts with '# Version History' and contains the 0.2.0 entry and its change bullet. <!--#3d5c40338fcd8af2-->
- `TestNoReadmeStillCommits` (class) — Test class asserting a missing README does not block the commit and is never fabricated, while VERSIONS.md is still created and written. <!--#38e7bfad436a24c5-->
  - `TestNoReadmeStillCommits.test_missing_readme_does_not_block_commit` (method) — Verifies commit_handler completes without a README (leaving it absent) yet still creates VERSIONS.md with the 0.2.0 entry. <!--#c796479bec611553-->
- `TestDocsUpdateFailureDoesNotBlockCommit` (class) — Test class asserting that a RuntimeError from the DocumentationUpdater is caught, logged as a warning, and does not fail the commit or leave partial file writes. <!--#0280d6ac15610d06-->
  - `TestDocsUpdateFailureDoesNotBlockCommit.test_runtime_error_logs_warning_and_completes` (method) — Verifies that when update_both() raises, commit_handler still returns COMPLETED, logs 'Documentation auto-update failed', and leaves the README untouched. <!--#a4e5db06198921f0-->
- `TestNoBumpSkipsDocs` (class) — Test class asserting that when version bumping is disabled, the docs updater is never instantiated (nor load_docs_config called) and docs files stay unchanged. <!--#1eee9a03473b04f3-->
  - `TestNoBumpSkipsDocs.test_docs_not_touched_when_no_bump` (method) — Asserts DocumentationUpdater and load_docs_config are never called, the README is unchanged, and version_bumped stays unset. <!--#c80cc0663efb0fcf-->

### `tests/engine/steps/test_commit_partial.py` (python) — Unit tests for the commit step's `_generate_commit_message`, covering subject-line source precedence (version_analyze `commit_message` > `implement_summary` > task description, with truncation and task_type prefix), partial-completion handling that appends an incomplete-tasks section, and the LLM-free template fallback that always appends a `Flow: <id>` trailer. <!--#b4febac9285eb3b8|de4d40abe889dbee-->
- `_make_flow` (function) — Test helper that builds a MagicMock spec'd as FlowInstance with default bugfix-flow attributes (overridable via kwargs) for use in commit-step message generation tests. <!--#e309bb69100e767f-->
- `_make_step` (function) — Test helper that builds a MagicMock Step with the given inputs dict and an empty outputs dict. <!--#c5e2b6b3737a76c0-->
- `TestCommitMessageFromVersionAnalyze` (class) — Tests that a `commit_message` supplied by the version_analyze step wins over `implement_summary`, gets the task_type prefix, is truncated to 72 chars, and falls through when empty or None. <!--#082aeb1ccb53d0d6-->
  - `TestCommitMessageFromVersionAnalyze.test_commit_message_from_version_analyze_is_used` (method) — Asserts the version_analyze `commit_message` appears in the subject line while `implement_summary` does not. <!--#75910d9e32ba344b-->
  - `TestCommitMessageFromVersionAnalyze.test_commit_message_from_version_analyze_truncated` (method) — Asserts a commit_message over 72 chars is truncated with an ellipsis in the subject line. <!--#94fb2d0a0f5b3990-->
  - `TestCommitMessageFromVersionAnalyze.test_commit_message_from_version_analyze_has_type_prefix` (method) — Asserts the subject line is prefixed with the flow's task_type (e.g. 'feature: '). <!--#2ac2298ac87bb725-->
  - `TestCommitMessageFromVersionAnalyze.test_empty_commit_message_falls_through` (method) — Asserts an empty `commit_message` falls back to `implement_summary` for the subject line. <!--#fc50105b7f1e308e-->
  - `TestCommitMessageFromVersionAnalyze.test_none_commit_message_falls_through` (method) — Asserts a None `commit_message` falls back to `implement_summary` for the subject line. <!--#6681ca57506b8635-->
- `TestCommitPartialCompletion` (class) — Tests how `_generate_commit_message` renders completion status — no incomplete section when complete or missing, an "Incomplete tasks (partial completion):" body for partial runs with string or dict tasks, and fallback to `implement_summary` (legacy `proposal` ignored). <!--#e281961981b7af0c-->
  - `TestCommitPartialCompletion.test_defaults_to_complete_when_missing` (method) — Asserts a missing `completion_status` is treated as complete, so no incomplete section is emitted. <!--#017795e6601b5c97-->
  - `TestCommitPartialCompletion.test_complete_status_no_incomplete_section` (method) — Asserts an explicit `completion_status` of "complete" produces no incomplete section. <!--#0c69753ac243df8e-->
  - `TestCommitPartialCompletion.test_partial_status_includes_incomplete_tasks_strings` (method) — Asserts partial completion lists plain-string `incomplete_tasks` under the incomplete-tasks heading. <!--#9385565c93ec5ce6-->
  - `TestCommitPartialCompletion.test_partial_status_includes_incomplete_tasks_dicts` (method) — Asserts dict-form `incomplete_tasks` render both their `description` and `reason` in the message body. <!--#533e05fc8d1150a2-->
  - `TestCommitPartialCompletion.test_partial_with_empty_incomplete_tasks_no_section` (method) — Asserts partial status with an empty `incomplete_tasks` list adds no incomplete section. <!--#9e031d5508d78e2a-->
  - `TestCommitPartialCompletion.test_subject_line_reflects_completed_work` (method) — Asserts the subject line reports the work actually done (`implement_summary`) even when the run is partial. <!--#50f3774b457ffa64-->
  - `TestCommitPartialCompletion.test_implement_summary_used_as_fallback` (method) — Asserts `implement_summary` becomes the subject line when no version_analyze `commit_message` is present. <!--#91942048f7bfbb6c-->
  - `TestCommitPartialCompletion.test_legacy_proposal_input_is_ignored` (method) — Asserts a legacy `proposal` carried by a resumed flow is skipped, so the subject falls back to the task description. <!--#78593f84c87cf5e9-->
- `TestCommitMessageTemplateFallback` (class) — Tests the last-resort commit message path — task description used directly and truncated to 60 chars, no LLM involvement, and the `Flow: <id>` trailer always appended. <!--#5f52c316f19fd6eb-->
  - `TestCommitMessageTemplateFallback.test_task_description_used_as_fallback` (method) — Asserts the task description becomes the subject line when no summary is available. <!--#97f1071b55abe0d5-->
  - `TestCommitMessageTemplateFallback.test_task_description_truncated_at_60_chars` (method) — Asserts a long task description is truncated to exactly 60 chars in the fallback subject line. <!--#0df42c5e05d99628-->
  - `TestCommitMessageTemplateFallback.test_no_llm_call_in_fallback_path` (method) — Asserts commit message generation produces a non-empty message purely template-side, with no LLM infrastructure required. <!--#b9cd62f7ec8f22ad-->
  - `TestCommitMessageTemplateFallback.test_flow_id_always_appended` (method) — Asserts the message always includes a 'Flow: <flow_id>' trailer. <!--#a9f65a0ad997c2d1-->

### `tests/engine/steps/test_commit_root_whitelist_guard.py` (python) — Unit and integration tests for the commit step's soft root-whitelist guard, verifying that _detect_root_whitelist_exclusions/_root_deny_excludes only warn (never stage or block) about new top-level paths silently denied by a `/*` default-deny .gitignore, degrade gracefully on subprocess failures, and that commit_handler forwards flow/step context to the code-index refresh without letting the detector affect control flow. <!--#52232d186b5c6479|a02f38b648dd0098-->

- `_head_tree_files` (function) — Test helper returning the list of file names touched by the repo's HEAD commit. <!--#1e10830178fec72a-->
- `_make_step` (function) — Test helper building a mock Step with patch/version inputs and empty outputs. <!--#84270e396e0d8d8e-->
- `_make_flow` (function) — Test helper that builds a MagicMock FlowInstance (with change_path, task metadata, and a mock State selecting COMMIT/SUMMARIZE steps) rooted at the given repo, for driving the commit handler. <!--#3b7452f498cee885-->
- `_disabled_version_config` (function) — Test helper returning a mock VersionConfig with versioning disabled and excluded from commit messages. <!--#13a381a4b0132634-->
- `TestDetectRootWhitelistExclusions` (class) — Test class verifying _detect_root_whitelist_exclusions correctly reports top-level files/dirs denied by the root `/*` deny rule while ignoring whitelisted, nested, and non-root-rule paths, and warns via logging. <!--#9725299d0fb08eba-->
  - `TestDetectRootWhitelistExclusions.test_top_level_file_excluded_by_root_deny_is_reported` (method) — Asserts a stray top-level file denied by `/*` is returned and logged with a root-whitelist guard warning. <!--#73beae18829836d1-->
  - `TestDetectRootWhitelistExclusions.test_top_level_dir_excluded_by_root_deny_is_reported` (method) — Asserts an ignored top-level directory is collapsed to a single reported entry. <!--#d443dcd2ac44a700-->
  - `TestDetectRootWhitelistExclusions.test_whitelisted_top_level_path_not_reported` (method) — Asserts an explicitly whitelisted top-level path is not reported. <!--#7d4d8d068c87c0d7-->
  - `TestDetectRootWhitelistExclusions.test_no_new_top_level_paths_returns_empty_silently` (method) — Asserts an empty result and no warning when there are no new top-level paths. <!--#48f64a06ee0ffba0-->
  - `TestDetectRootWhitelistExclusions.test_path_ignored_by_non_root_rule_is_not_reported` (method) — Asserts a path whose winning ignore rule is non-root (e.g. `*.log`) is excluded while a true root-deny stray is still reported. <!--#f714560aa6893a70-->
  - `TestDetectRootWhitelistExclusions.test_nested_path_under_whitelisted_dir_not_reported` (method) — Asserts that files inside a re-admitted (`!/tianluo/`) whitelisted top-level directory are not surfaced as root-whitelist exclusions. <!--#fe721c3823f7e54c-->
- `TestRootDenyExcludes` (class) — Test class checking _root_deny_excludes returns True only when a path's winning ignore rule is the root `/*` deny (False for other-rule matches, non-ignored paths, and swallowed subprocess errors). <!--#225bf1826fcfbc14-->
  - `TestRootDenyExcludes.test_true_for_root_deny_match` (method) — Asserts True for a stray top-level path matched by the root-deny rule. <!--#47a62a04bae2eb82-->
  - `TestRootDenyExcludes.test_false_for_other_rule_match` (method) — Asserts False for a path ignored by a non-root rule like `*.log`. <!--#ad389ab1d26ce5e2-->
  - `TestRootDenyExcludes.test_false_for_non_ignored_path` (method) — Asserts False for a whitelisted, non-ignored path. <!--#de684632222f10ff-->
  - `TestRootDenyExcludes.test_subprocess_raise_is_swallowed` (method) — Asserts _root_deny_excludes returns False (rather than raising) when the underlying git check-ignore subprocess.run throws OSError. <!--#ee2e663bde95b876-->
- `TestGuardFaultTolerance` (class) — Test class ensuring _detect_root_whitelist_exclusions degrades gracefully to an empty result (with warning logs) when git ls-files exits non-zero, raises, or when per-path check-ignore confirmations fail. <!--#20238ab6536b14a5-->
  - `TestGuardFaultTolerance.test_ls_files_nonzero_returns_empty` (method) — Asserts the detector returns [] and logs 'could not list ignored paths' when the git ls-files subprocess exits with a non-zero return code. <!--#51ea48a9c7fd7f89-->
  - `TestGuardFaultTolerance.test_ls_files_raise_returns_empty` (method) — Asserts the detector returns [] and logs 'listing ignored paths raised' when the git ls-files subprocess.run raises OSError. <!--#513f10c929bcf68c-->
  - `TestGuardFaultTolerance.test_check_ignore_failure_does_not_break_detection` (method) — Asserts the detector returns [] without raising when ls-files enumeration succeeds but every per-path check-ignore confirmation throws. <!--#269e0eb31130bf06-->
- `TestCommitHandlerIntegration` (class) — Integration test class driving the full commit_handler to verify the root-whitelist guard warns (but never stages) stray root-denied paths, stays silent otherwise, warns even when a denied file is the only change, forwards flow/step context to ensure_code_index_fresh, and never lets the detector's return value alter control flow. <!--#79411994e27ee9b7-->
