  - `TestCommitHandlerIntegration.test_warns_on_root_exclusion_and_commit_completes` (method) — Asserts a whitelisted change commits while a stray root-denied path is warned about but left unstaged on disk. <!--#4b8257ad28e2ce27-->
  - `TestCommitHandlerIntegration.test_no_root_exclusion_commits_silently` (method) — Asserts a clean whitelisted change commits with no root-whitelist guard warning. <!--#7e1c2261f39def8a-->
  - `TestCommitHandlerIntegration.test_warns_when_root_exclusion_is_the_only_work` (method) — Regression test asserting the guard still warns when a root-denied file is the only (otherwise invisible) change, committing nothing and leaving the file on disk. <!--#97b90ff2f385aab3-->
  - `TestCommitHandlerIntegration.test_no_changes_and_no_exclusion_is_silent` (method) — Asserts no warning is emitted when there are neither changes nor root exclusions. <!--#cc5870cc4e922105-->
  - `TestCommitHandlerIntegration.test_forwards_flow_and_step_context_to_code_index_refresh` (method) — Pins the commit→code-index seam, asserting ensure_code_index_fresh is called once with project_root positional and flow_id/step_id/step_type kwargs so per-node progress streams to the web console. <!--#acf59d73a4a0f95b-->
  - `TestCommitHandlerIntegration.test_detector_return_value_does_not_feed_control_flow` (method) — Asserts that even when _detect_root_whitelist_exclusions is stubbed to return a non-empty hit list, the detector is called exactly once and the commit still proceeds to COMPLETED, committing src.py. <!--#84fd9842daed77a9-->

### `tests/engine/steps/test_e2e_step.py` (python) — Tests for the engine's e2e step handler covering the disabled-switch path, per-flow-scoped passing runs, scenario-failure routing to REVISION_NEEDED with named failures, the environment-failure firewall that never sets fix_needed, and the optional content-maintenance hook that evolves scenarios before running them, with helpers for stubbing configs, flows, verdicts, and the bootstrap module. <!--#fbfd9e2eb6c675b8|5dc4488de73cd21d-->
- `no_content_generation` (function) — Autouse-style fixture that stubs out ``ensure_content``/``evolve_content`` so routing tests never reach a real agent, leaving content-generation coverage to ``tests/e2e/test_bootstrap.py``. <!--#3521fe1fa569413d-->
- `_write_config` (function) — Helper that writes a minimal ``tianluo.yaml`` with ``e2e.enabled`` set true or false into a project root. <!--#aa527c3235713fde-->
- `_flow` (function) — Helper that builds a RUNNING ``FlowInstance`` with ``project_root`` in its state context. <!--#0e78fb85ea49a532-->
- `_step` (function) — Helper that builds a RUNNING ``Step`` of type ``StepType.E2E``. <!--#296de222250564f3-->
- `_passing_verdict` (function) — Helper constructing a passing ``E2EVerdict`` with one successful 'login' scenario and a docker-runtime summary. <!--#c8ef206d446d5c84-->
- `_failing_verdict` (function) — Helper constructing a failing ``E2EVerdict`` whose 'login' scenario failed a tier-1 DOM assertion, with fix instructions/context attached. <!--#219981824f2bd827-->
- `TestDisabledSwitch` (class) — Tests that with e2e disabled (or no config file at all) the handler completes without ever calling the e2e subsystem and marks the outputs as skipped. <!--#a4fe7d558d00ba17-->
  - `TestDisabledSwitch.test_disabled_completes_without_running` (method) — Verifies disabled config yields COMPLETED, ``run_e2e`` is never called, and outputs record the skip without ``fix_needed``. <!--#70326d0a1348dd66-->
  - `TestDisabledSwitch.test_missing_config_file_is_disabled` (method) — Verifies a missing ``tianluo.yaml`` defaults to e2e off, so the handler completes without running anything. <!--#ae9e431e1a193960-->
- `TestScenariosPassed` (class) — Tests the happy path: all scenarios passing completes the step, the run is scoped per-flow (network suffix and artifacts dir), and an empty scenario selection is reported as a pass. <!--#62786eff4a88355d-->
  - `TestScenariosPassed.test_all_passed_completes` (method) — Verifies a passing verdict yields COMPLETED with pass/fail scenario lists and runtime recorded in outputs and no ``fix_needed``. <!--#b9e13e166239b215-->
  - `TestScenariosPassed.test_run_is_scoped_to_the_flow` (method) — Verifies ``run_e2e`` receives a per-flow ``network_suffix`` and per-flow ``artifacts_dir`` so concurrent worktree flows cannot share networks or overwrite artifacts. <!--#f9d397bf4c74e3de-->
  - `TestScenariosPassed.test_empty_selection_reported_as_completed` (method) — Verifies a verdict that selected zero scenarios still completes and reports ``total == 0`` in the summary. <!--#f4feab6e1dd015cf-->
- `TestScenarioFailure` (class) — Tests scenario-failure routing: failed scenarios yield REVISION_NEEDED with fix context, the error message names the failing and critical-unverified scenarios, and per-scenario assertion detail survives into outputs. <!--#2a0af3b47ca19187-->
  - `TestScenarioFailure.test_failure_requests_revision` (method) — Verifies a failing verdict yields REVISION_NEEDED with ``fix_needed``, fix context reason ``e2e_failure``, and no ``environment_error`` output. <!--#c7a8b48f2243f3e0-->
  - `TestScenarioFailure.test_an_unverified_critical_scenario_says_so` (method) — Verifies a critical scenario that never ran produces an error message naming it rather than the self-contradictory '0 e2e scenario(s) failed'. <!--#313390806f4860b7-->
  - `TestScenarioFailure.test_both_causes_are_named_when_both_hold` (method) — Verifies the error message names both the failed scenario and the critical-unverified scenario when both conditions hold. <!--#50576991d67c3dd1-->
  - `TestScenarioFailure.test_failed_scenario_detail_survives_into_outputs` (method) — Verifies per-assertion expected/actual detail from a failed scenario is preserved in ``e2e_results`` outputs. <!--#61dac816f635f7e9-->
- `TestEnvironmentFailure` (class) — Tests the fix-loop firewall: host problems (verdict-level or raised environment errors, missing extras, config errors) fail the step without ever setting ``fix_needed``. <!--#3d3cd328b622a73d-->
  - `TestEnvironmentFailure.test_verdict_environment_error_fails_without_fix` (method) — Verifies a verdict carrying ``environment_error`` yields FAILED with remediation surfaced in outputs and error message, and no fix request. <!--#e0ba4b324e3769cb-->
  - `TestEnvironmentFailure.test_raised_environment_error_fails_without_fix` (method) — Verifies a raised ``E2EEnvironmentError`` also yields FAILED with its remediation in the error message and no fix request. <!--#84d480ac211285e1-->
  - `TestEnvironmentFailure.test_missing_extra_is_an_environment_failure` (method) — Verifies ``E2EDependencyMissingError`` is treated as a host problem whose error message points at the ``tianluo[e2e]`` extra. <!--#d1461c0452a8277f-->
  - `TestEnvironmentFailure.test_config_error_fails_without_fix` (method) — Verifies ``E2EConfigError`` yields FAILED naming the offending scenario file and recording ``config_error`` in outputs, without a fix request. <!--#8d949320fc691844-->
- `_install_bootstrap` (function) — Helper that swaps a synthetic ``tianluo.e2e.bootstrap`` module into ``sys.modules`` and the package namespace with the given stand-in members. <!--#18b65b82e3d2f8ba-->
- `_EvolveResult` (class) — Stand-in for the bootstrap ``BootstrapResult`` returned by a successful evolution, exposing changed/note/errors/written/created attributes. <!--#2fb8fe2b3fb8a8a7-->
  - `_EvolveResult.__init__` (method) — Initialises the stand-in evolution result with configurable changed flag, note, errors, and derived ``written``/``created`` fields. <!--#6863cf089326f339-->
- `TestContentMaintenance` (class) — Tests the handler's content-maintenance hook: bootstrap is optional, existing content is evolved once per flow before scenarios run, fresh generation skips evolution, and rejected or partial evolution degrades gracefully. <!--#4769f45c3d625dca-->
  - `TestContentMaintenance.test_absent_bootstrap_module_does_not_block` (method) — Verifies a genuinely unimportable bootstrap module does not stop the run when content is already in place. <!--#0a7de192c094716d-->
  - `TestContentMaintenance.test_bootstrap_is_invoked_when_available` (method) — Verifies ``ensure_content`` is called with the project root when the bootstrap module is available, and the result is noted in outputs. <!--#ea4c41ed4414155c-->
  - `TestContentMaintenance.test_existing_content_is_evolved_not_left_alone` (method) — Regression test verifying pre-existing content is evolved with hints drawn from the task description and changed files, so new behavior gets scenarios instead of a stale green suite. <!--#e0ef71fd185210c1-->
  - `TestContentMaintenance.test_evolution_runs_before_the_scenarios` (method) — Verifies evolution happens before ``run_e2e`` so scenarios added this flow are exercised by this flow. <!--#fc9634e6c9fe69d4-->
  - `TestContentMaintenance.test_evolution_happens_once_per_flow` (method) — Verifies fix-loop re-entries do not re-evolve content, preventing the model from weakening the suite to make it pass. <!--#f20a2cd8637597db-->
  - `TestContentMaintenance.test_first_generation_skips_evolution` (method) — Verifies freshly generated content skips evolution and still sets the ``e2e_content_evolved`` guard for later iterations. <!--#bad86747aa123d96-->
  - `TestContentMaintenance.test_rejected_evolution_does_not_break_the_run` (method) — Verifies a rejected evolution proposal leaves the valid on-disk suite runnable and records the rejection note in outputs. <!--#aea9370b962165a3-->
  - `TestContentMaintenance.test_bootstrap_without_evolve_content_still_runs` (method) — Verifies a bootstrap module lacking ``evolve_content`` does not stop a runnable suite. <!--#f8e4aea2622d2c2f-->
  - `TestContentMaintenance.test_hints_cover_every_live_input_shape` (method) — Verifies evolution hints are extracted from every real input shape (string or mapping ``files_changed``/``implemented_groups`` plus the sibling ``implement_summary``). <!--#11f3c8cc11786a2c-->
  - `TestContentMaintenance.test_no_hints_means_no_evolution` (method) — Verifies evolution is skipped when no hints exist, avoiding unaimed churn against a working suite. <!--#62cf8440ff07181d-->
- `TestNoTopLevelSubsystemImport` (class) — Mechanical guard that the e2e step module keeps the engine core dependency-isolated by deferring every e2e-subsystem import out of module level. <!--#9346acbfde287b09-->
  - `TestNoTopLevelSubsystemImport.test_module_source_defers_every_e2e_import` (method) — Scans the step module's source asserting no top-level import line references the e2e subsystem or ``runtime_paths``. <!--#5d0309794330d081-->
- `test_handler_returns_a_step_status` (function) — Sanity test (parametrized) that the handler's contract is returning a ``StepStatus`` member, never a bool or None. <!--#c276bde0d278362a-->
- `test_fix_context_issues_carry_a_description` (function) — Verifies each fix-context issue is given a ``description`` and ``location`` so the engine's shared issue extractor can re-render it non-empty in later fix iterations. <!--#39ae7441906639a7-->

### `tests/engine/steps/test_implement.py` (python) — Unit test suite for the IMPLEMENT flow step, covering resume idempotency (skipping already-implemented groups and restoring accumulated state), partial-progress persistence into `step.outputs`, the `_should_use_dag()` predicate and its ordering against the fix-iteration/single-group/`has_commits` gates in `implement_handler`, empty-repo fallback from `_run_dag_parallel` to sequential execution, and stale-branch/worktree hygiene around group branch creation and post-merge deletion. <!--#93f338cb6f36c459|e72b04dc4704b3f7-->
- `TestImplementResumeIdempotency` (class) — Test class verifying that on resume the implement handler skips already-completed groups and restores accumulated state. <!--#b169530fe51d7c58-->

  - `TestImplementResumeIdempotency.test_fresh_start_processes_all_groups` (method) — Asserts a fresh (non-resumed) run processes all five groups in order. <!--#d93a12044e81c9ba-->
  - `TestImplementResumeIdempotency.test_resume_skips_already_completed_groups` (method) — Asserts resume filters out groups already listed in implemented_groups, leaving only the remainder. <!--#5e8e8b6a32a7c0a5-->
  - `TestImplementResumeIdempotency.test_resume_restores_accumulated_state` (method) — Asserts resume reconstructs all_results and total_files_changed from saved step.outputs. <!--#5503926e736af9c7-->
  - `TestImplementResumeIdempotency.test_resume_processes_remaining_groups` (method) — Asserts only the not-yet-completed groups (G3–G5) are processed after resume. <!--#a0eacad0b4cac0a1-->
  - `TestImplementResumeIdempotency.test_resume_updates_outputs_after_each_group` (method) — Asserts implemented_groups and total_files_changed are updated incrementally as each group completes. <!--#d77c9564ab05ee27-->
  - `TestImplementResumeIdempotency.test_no_resume_flag_processes_all_groups` (method) — Asserts that without the resumed flag all groups are queued for processing. <!--#6fcd5c0dc57ad99f-->
  - `TestImplementResumeIdempotency.test_resume_with_empty_implemented_groups_processes_all` (method) — Asserts resume with an empty implemented_groups list still processes all groups. <!--#a5be75176a587a88-->
  - `TestImplementResumeIdempotency.test_resume_with_all_groups_completed` (method) — Asserts resume with every group already completed leaves nothing to process. <!--#0093c2281feab014-->
  - `TestImplementResumeIdempotency.test_resume_preserves_other_step_outputs` (method) — Asserts resume processing preserves unrelated step.outputs keys while updating progress. <!--#0bdf73c16c5d150e-->
- `TestImplementStatePersistence` (class) — Test class verifying partial progress is persisted to step.outputs in a resume-ready structure. <!--#73144ef73f21612d-->
  - `TestImplementStatePersistence.setup_method` (method) — Per-test fixture building a temp dir, a feature FlowInstance, and two sample task groups. <!--#520d368bea267a3f-->
  - `TestImplementStatePersistence.teardown_method` (method) — Per-test cleanup that removes the temporary directory. <!--#ad184d68556ca43f-->
  - `TestImplementStatePersistence.test_partial_progress_saved_to_outputs` (method) — Asserts partial progress (implemented_groups, total_files_changed) is written to step.outputs. <!--#627a7783f754eaa4-->
  - `TestImplementStatePersistence.test_outputs_structure_for_resume` (method) — Asserts the saved outputs have the correct types (list of str, int) needed for resume. <!--#55c71be56b6d31f7-->
- `TestShouldUseDag` (class) — Test class verifying the `_should_use_dag()` predicate and its placement in `implement_handler`'s control flow — single/empty groups skip DAG while multiple groups (with or without dependencies) enable it, and fix-iteration/single-group/no-commits checks all short-circuit before the DAG decision. <!--#95655c08c53393e1-->
  - `TestShouldUseDag.test_single_group_returns_false` (method) — Asserts `_should_use_dag()` returns False for a single group. <!--#b8ebdb3f0a821e91-->
  - `TestShouldUseDag.test_single_group_with_depends_on_returns_false` (method) — Asserts a single group returns False even when it declares a `depends_on` (len <= 1 wins). <!--#d39de2c43de59897-->
  - `TestShouldUseDag.test_empty_groups_returns_false` (method) — Asserts `_should_use_dag([])` returns False for an empty group list. <!--#9fbdecedc2e9c55f-->
  - `TestShouldUseDag.test_multiple_groups_no_depends_on_returns_true` (method) — Asserts multiple independent groups (no `depends_on`) return True to enable parallel DAG execution. <!--#ce3ba597971ed6ee-->
  - `TestShouldUseDag.test_multiple_groups_empty_depends_on_returns_true` (method) — Asserts multiple groups with empty `depends_on` lists still return True for parallel execution. <!--#effa66cfb8cd988d-->
  - `TestShouldUseDag.test_multiple_groups_with_depends_on_returns_true` (method) — Asserts multiple groups with at least one non-empty `depends_on` return True. <!--#16b11b9fe1dfdd04-->

  - `TestShouldUseDag.test_fix_iteration_bypasses_dag` (method) — Uses source inspection of `implement_handler` to assert the `is_fix_iteration` check precedes the `_should_use_dag` check. <!--#573abe5a6f2e1072-->
  - `TestShouldUseDag.test_single_group_path_bypasses_dag` (method) — Uses source inspection to assert the `len(groups) <= 1` early-return precedes the `_should_use_dag` check. <!--#9099aea792e992aa-->
  - `TestShouldUseDag.test_no_commits_falls_back_to_sequential` (method) — Uses source inspection to assert the `has_commits(project_root)` gate sits inside the DAG block so `_run_dag_parallel` only runs when the repo has commits. <!--#947cee14ec56f5ca-->
- `TestDagEmptyRepoFallback` (class) — Test class verifying that `implement_handler` routes to sequential execution in an empty repo (no commits) but uses `_run_dag_parallel` once the repo has commits. <!--#3621711d4ed878be-->
  - `TestDagEmptyRepoFallback.setup_method` (method) — Per-test fixture building a fork-shaped DAG (G1→G2, G1→G3) so linear-chain short-circuits don't apply. <!--#8612f4ef684bdd26-->
  - `TestDagEmptyRepoFallback.teardown_method` (method) — Per-test cleanup that removes the temporary directory. <!--#c34398a3746e8dbf-->

- `TestStaleBranchHandling` (class) — Test class covering stale-branch/worktree hygiene in the IMPLEMENT step: `execute_fn` must defensively `branch -D` before recreating a group branch, and `_run_dag_parallel` must delete branches only post-merge (never in the `finally` block). <!--#2f99272a8f4e4aa2-->

  - `TestStaleBranchHandling.test_execute_fn_deletes_stale_branch_before_creation` (method) — Asserts that `_make_execute_fn`'s returned callable issues the `git branch -D impl/...` cleanup call before the `git branch <name> <base>` creation call. <!--#27ddf0fb48d9d697-->
  - `TestStaleBranchHandling.test_execute_fn_succeeds_when_no_stale_branch` (method) — Asserts the normal path still completes successfully (returning the group's `files_changed`) when the defensive `branch -D` fails because no stale branch exists. <!--#a68ef4bc1d98b1e2-->
  - `TestStaleBranchHandling.test_finally_cleans_up_branches_for_all_groups` (method) — Asserts that when the DAG scheduler raises, `_run_dag_parallel` propagates the error and does not call `delete_branch`, leaving branches for the next run's stale-branch cleanup. <!--#7a96403f0330f93b-->
  - `TestStaleBranchHandling.test_finally_cleans_up_branches_on_normal_completion` (method) — Asserts that on successful completion each group branch is deleted exactly once post-merge (with `_is_branch_reachable_from` mocked to model a successful merge). <!--#f1c0ae60aae2ac37-->
- `TestDagResumeFiltering` (class) — Test class verifying that `implement_handler` filters already-`implemented_groups` out of the DAG on resume and forwards `prior_outputs`, and that `_run_dag_parallel` merges those prior outputs into the step's aggregated results. <!--#ea26b93bf3e3d205-->

- `TestDagParallelResumeBehavior` (class) — Test class for end-to-end DAG resume semantics: completed groups are skipped, stale worktrees are force-cleaned before branch recreation, and accumulated prior state is restored and merged. <!--#a9782008a4144e01-->

- `TestImplementSubagentDecompositionHint` (class) — Test class asserting that both IMPLEMENT execution paths — the holistic prompt and the capability-group doctrine — explicitly instruct the runner that it may spawn its own subagents to decompose work in-call. <!--#7048fed8ba62c7a4-->

- `TestTestScopeAndHeadlessClause` (class) — Test class asserting that the shared TEST_SCOPE_AND_HEADLESS_CLAUSE is injected verbatim, in the right place, and with its key wording intact across every implement/fix prompt variant in `tianluo.engine.steps.implement`. <!--#c0212eba7293ab97-->

  - `TestTestScopeAndHeadlessClause.test_every_variant_states_the_three_key_points` (method) — Checks each variant still states the three substantive points: the flow's TEST step owns the full suite, this call tests only its own changes, and it runs headless with no background jobs left. <!--#94904200b99bc5b4-->
  - `TestTestScopeAndHeadlessClause.test_no_incomplete_task_for_an_unobserved_run` (method) — Asserts every variant keeps the instruction never to report an unobserved test run as an incomplete task. <!--#ea9f58a49951fbe8-->

  - `TestTestScopeAndHeadlessClause.test_fix_version_guardrail_clause_survives_the_injection` (method) — Asserts `FIX_VERSION_FILE_GUARDRAIL` is still present in FIX_PROMPT after the clause injection. <!--#2aba129dcd4bb4d3-->

### `tests/engine/steps/test_implement_dag.py` (python) — Test module for the IMPLEMENT step's DAG-parallel execution path, covering LOC-threshold routing between single-LLM-call and DAG modes, transitive reduction feeding classify_chains and DAGScheduler, relay/worktree topologies (linear, fork, diamond convergence), mid-chain failure fallback leaves, merge-conflict resolution and take-theirs fallback, per-group output aggregation across fresh/resumed/recovered runs, and unit coverage of classify_chains on assorted DAG shapes. <!--#6635d6c07220f0ba|50f09c242208033f-->

- `TestLocThresholdRouting` (class) — Test class asserting that the implement step's routing gate picks a single LLM call when total estimated_loc stays within the 300-line threshold and the DAG-parallel path when a forking group graph exceeds it. <!--#3168f505928bdf9a-->
  - `TestLocThresholdRouting.test_below_threshold_routes_to_single_call` (method) — Verifies that a granular two-group plan totalling 200 estimated_loc drives implement_handler into _run_single_llm_call and never into _run_dag_parallel. <!--#9b79d98443feb07b-->
  - `TestLocThresholdRouting.test_above_threshold_routes_to_dag` (method) — Asserts that a forked DAG totaling >300 LOC routes implement_handler to _run_dag_parallel. <!--#612a5458f93d0d69-->
- `TestTransitiveReductionIntegration` (class) — Test class asserting that `_run_dag_parallel` wires `transitive_reduce`'s output through `classify_chains` and into `DAGScheduler` rather than the raw group list. <!--#8fe085d16cf22ff2-->
  - `TestTransitiveReductionIntegration.test_reduced_dag_reaches_scheduler` (method) — Patches the reduction/classification/scheduler trio and asserts `transitive_reduce` gets the original groups while `classify_chains` and `DAGScheduler` receive the reduced DAG plus the resulting `RelayPlan`. <!--#c1ef88f7bcc3362c-->
- `TestLinearRelayChain` (class) — Test class covering a G1→G2→G3 linear relay chain, checking that all groups share one worktree/branch and produce a single merge. <!--#1dfcc48cbaf4386f-->
  - `TestLinearRelayChain.test_single_worktree_reuse_one_merge` (method) — Asserts a three-group linear chain on one shared branch returns COMPLETED with exactly one `_merge_leaf_branch` call and one deduplicated worktree cleanup. <!--#f18db6511ab8795e-->
  - `TestLinearRelayChain.test_relay_context_passes_worktree` (method) — Asserts `DAGScheduler.run` is invoked exactly once with a callable `execute_fn` as its first positional argument. <!--#8ca7c6bbf848f0ca-->
- `TestForkRelay` (class) — Test class covering a G1→{G2,G3} fork where G2 inherits G1's branch and G3 forks its own, yielding two leaf merges. <!--#e1d78008ff6b1a12-->
  - `TestForkRelay.test_fork_produces_two_leaf_merges` (method) — Asserts a forked DAG merges both distinct leaf branches and performs two worktree cleanups, one per unique branch. <!--#b4c78c051ec54ef4-->
  - `TestForkRelay.test_fork_from_in_relay_plan` (method) — Asserts the `relay_plan` handed to `DAGScheduler` carries the forked group in its `fork_from` mapping. <!--#50d7104114358d3e-->
- `TestDiamondConvergence` (class) — Test class covering a diamond DAG (G1→{G2,G3}→G4) where G4 is the convergence point and the sole branch merged back. <!--#f179b060989078a5-->
  - `TestDiamondConvergence.test_diamond_single_leaf_merge` (method) — Asserts the diamond topology returns COMPLETED with exactly one merge, of the relay-chain branch carrying leaf G4. <!--#4d4a40c9e8d6bbd7-->
  - `TestDiamondConvergence.test_convergence_info_in_relay_plan` (method) — Asserts the `relay_plan` passed to `DAGScheduler` records G4's `ConvergenceInfo` with the expected primary and secondary predecessors. <!--#f6c8c9c4d9046c96-->
- `TestMidChainFailure` (class) — Test class covering partial-failure behaviour when a mid-chain group fails — fallback-leaf merging, incomplete-task reporting, and total failure. <!--#eb0385b648fe4f46-->
  - `TestMidChainFailure.test_fallback_leaf_merged_on_midchain_failure` (method) — Asserts that when G2 fails after G1 completed, G1's branch is merged as a fallback leaf and the step returns PARTIAL with `completion_status == "partial"`. <!--#c392d518fad54bbd-->
  - `TestMidChainFailure.test_skipped_groups_recorded_in_incomplete_tasks` (method) — Asserts `step.outputs["incomplete_tasks"]` names both the failed group and the downstream group that was skipped. <!--#dd1b4378b912d19d-->
  - `TestMidChainFailure.test_all_groups_fail_returns_failed` (method) — Asserts that with every group failed and no fallback leaves the step returns FAILED, marks `completion_status == "failed"`, and performs no merge. <!--#2585d3fb626bde28-->

  - `TestConflictResolution.test_conflict_unresolved_falls_back_to_take_theirs` (method) — Asserts that when the LLM cannot resolve, the take-theirs fallback commits the leaf's version, leaving `merge_failures` empty while recording a single take-theirs audit event. <!--#88869f6be4b9aef7-->
  - `TestConflictResolution.test_take_theirs_fallback_helpers_present` (method) — Asserts _take_theirs_fallback and _take_ours_for_stashpop exist while the legacy _force_resolve_conflicts_theirs remains removed. <!--#bd7f3b8e8051d266-->

  - `TestOutputAggregation.test_resume_carries_pre_resume_group_summaries` (method) — Regression test asserting a resumed run keeps pre-interruption group summaries in both the structured `group_summaries` list and the joined `summary` string. <!--#cbb0c58fdc85bd01-->
  - `TestOutputAggregation.test_all_groups_recovered_keeps_prior_group_summaries` (method) — Asserts the all-groups-already-recovered early return republishes the prior `group_summaries` and their joined aggregate `summary`. <!--#6a62def3f2be17b4-->
  - `TestOutputAggregation.test_all_groups_recovered_without_summaries_uses_placeholder` (method) — Asserts a recovered run lacking persisted per-group summaries still emits a non-empty placeholder `summary` ("Recovered from previous run"). <!--#976db2e613cedd8b-->
- `TestClassifyChainsUnit` (class) — Unit-test class exercising classify_chains across linear, fork, diamond, independent, and empty DAG shapes. <!--#82809fb1a9547406-->

  - `TestClassifyChainsUnit.test_diamond` (method) — Checks that a diamond G1→{G2,G3}→G4 marks G4 as the sole leaf and a convergence point with G2 primary and G3 secondary predecessor. <!--#bc210a4f446099e5-->

### `tests/engine/steps/test_implement_dag_cleanup.py` (python) — Unit tests for the IMPLEMENT step's DAG cleanup safety net, verifying that `_is_branch_reachable_from` fails closed and that `_run_dag_parallel` deletes only successfully-merged/reachable leaf branches while preserving branches whose merges failed and propagating those merge_failures into an overall failed step status. <!--#6470d8d9726bf2f3|b6a3c3efc8f60703-->
- `_git` (function) — Helper that runs a git subcommand against a given repo directory and returns the completed process. <!--#9bef257c44286ed8-->
- `repo` (function) — Pytest fixture that creates an initialized git repo on branch 'main' with one empty commit for reachability tests. <!--#925870e77af94802-->
- `TestIsBranchReachable` (class) — Test class covering `_is_branch_reachable_from` for merged, unmerged, and missing branches. <!--#06cb8d3a117444cd-->
  - `TestIsBranchReachable.test_ancestor_returns_true` (method) — Asserts a branch fully merged into main is reported reachable (True). <!--#e9f471ffa409a590-->
  - `TestIsBranchReachable.test_unmerged_branch_returns_false` (method) — Asserts a branch with un-merged commits is not reachable (False) so cleanup won't delete it. <!--#3a6c400852ac6745-->
  - `TestIsBranchReachable.test_missing_branch_returns_false` (method) — Asserts a non-existent branch ref fails closed and returns False. <!--#d9d13515daf64cc1-->
- `_make_step` (function) — Helper that builds a minimal IMPLEMENT Step for driving `_run_dag_parallel`. <!--#e678abd775e27369-->
- `_make_flow` (function) — Helper that builds a MagicMock flow object with a fixed flow_id. <!--#9335b82b095c99d8-->
- `_make_groups` (function) — Helper that converts (gid, order, deps, loc) tuples into the group-dict shape the scheduler expects. <!--#01568bf988f20cd1-->
- `TestCleanupSafeDelete` (class) — Test class verifying that `_run_dag_parallel` only deletes leaf branches whose commits actually landed on the original branch, preserving branches whose merge failed and reporting them via `preserved_branches`. <!--#2c1339977f36cd85-->
  - `TestCleanupSafeDelete.test_failed_merge_branch_preserved` (method) — Asserts that when `_merge_leaf_branch` returns False, `delete_branch` is never called for that branch and the step reports it under `preserved_branches`/`merge_failures` with `completion_status='failed'`. <!--#de4afbd9d85e7f23-->
  - `TestCleanupSafeDelete.test_successful_merge_branch_deleted` (method) — Asserts the happy path where a successfully merged leaf branch is deleted, no `preserved_branches` output is emitted, and `merge_failures` stays empty. <!--#b1bd7aab64cf34f5-->
  - `TestCleanupSafeDelete.test_mixed_merge_outcomes` (method) — Asserts that with two independent leaves where one merge succeeds and the other fails, only the merged branch is deleted while the failed one is preserved. <!--#7fca27cb306d771a-->
- `TestOverallStatusReflectsMergeFailures` (class) — Test class verifying that the step's overall status is driven by merge outcomes — non-empty `merge_failures` forces a failed status even when every group completed. <!--#8b2cbd66d9c6a674-->
  - `TestOverallStatusReflectsMergeFailures.test_all_groups_complete_but_merge_failed_returns_failed` (method) — Asserts that a group with `completion_status='complete'` whose merge fails still yields `completion_status='failed'`, `merge_failures == ['G1']`, and a `StepStatus.FAILED` return. <!--#d3fb978184ba92cc-->
  - `TestOverallStatusReflectsMergeFailures.test_merge_success_status_complete` (method) — Asserts the happy path where all groups complete and the merge succeeds, yielding `completion_status='complete'`, empty `merge_failures`, and a `StepStatus.COMPLETED` return. <!--#2e4b4f83a9c351c9-->

  - `TestSequentialAggregation.test_each_group_gets_its_real_id_and_own_summary` (method) — Runs the handler over two groups with distinct parsed summaries and asserts each entry carries its real `group_id`, while the legacy joined `summary` and `implemented_groups` outputs are unaffected. <!--#4adc69e3e49495af-->
  - `TestSequentialAggregation.test_resume_keeps_the_list_aligned_with_implemented_groups` (method) — Resumes with `G1` already done and asserts its real pre-resume summary is preserved (not a placeholder) and the final list stays index-aligned with `implemented_groups`. <!--#3cfdeb8cf75cc5a4-->
  - `TestSequentialAggregation.test_resume_of_a_pre_field_flow_still_aligns` (method) — Resumes a flow that predates the `group_summaries` field and asserts the already-completed group gets an empty-summary placeholder slot so the list remains index-aligned. <!--#a2dbccf44f5c756b-->
- `TestSingleCallAggregation` (class) — Handler-level tests for the merged single-call implement path, asserting it emits exactly one `group_summaries` entry labelled with the real group id (or empty when there is no single group) and none at all for an empty summary. <!--#0daf4fc65545b9d2-->
  - `TestSingleCallAggregation.test_single_group_entry_carries_that_group_id` (method) — Asserts a single-group run labels its one entry with that group's actual id (`G4`) rather than a fabricated `G1`. <!--#0e9268b04209f481-->
  - `TestSingleCallAggregation.test_no_groups_yields_an_unlabelled_entry` (method) — Asserts a run with no task groups produces one entry with an empty `group_id` and the model's summary. <!--#92a8fb1f64ecbba6-->

  - `TestDagResumePayload.test_prior_outputs_carry_completed_group_summaries` (method) — Asserts the `prior_outputs` handed to `_run_dag_parallel` carries the completed group's summary and drops a stale entry for a group not in `implemented_groups`. <!--#275383aa065f7b9d-->
  - `TestDagResumePayload.test_all_completed_resume_also_carries_the_list` (method) — Asserts that when every group is already implemented, the resume still forwards the full `group_summaries` list in `prior_outputs`. <!--#e807cd47556e370d-->

### `tests/engine/steps/test_implement_merge_robustness.py` (python) — Integration and unit test suite exercising `_merge_leaf_branch`'s robustness against real temporary git repos, covering pre-merge stashing of dirty/untracked main-repo files, stash-pop and 3-way conflict recovery via take-ours/take-theirs fallbacks with best-effort YAML audit issue recording, clean abort on commit failure, and the `_parse_stashpop_already_exists` stderr parser. <!--#f1930b0094820b9c|19b76f4c41a945b9-->
- `_git` (function) — Test helper that runs a git subcommand inside a given repo path and returns the CompletedProcess. <!--#cc6b2a27c59d26c1-->
- `repo` (function) — A pytest fixture that builds a bare-bones git repo with an initial commit on `main` and a `.gitignore` excluding `tianluo/`, used as the sandbox for merge-robustness tests. <!--#f7274773d812a40f-->
- `_make_leaf_branch` (function) — Test helper that creates a named leaf branch off a base, populates it with given files, commits them, and returns to the base branch. <!--#1374a85c71c6a462-->
- `TestStashPrevention` (class) — Tests that untracked or modified files in the main repo no longer block a leaf-branch merge, covering both the colliding-path case (take-ours keeps the leaf version) and the unrelated-file case (the file survives the stash/pop round-trip), with no dangling stash left behind. <!--#037c813cf00e1e56-->
  - `TestStashPrevention.test_untracked_file_in_main_does_not_block_merge` (method) — Verifies that an untracked main-repo file colliding with a leaf file (the 20260507-200706 root cause) is stashed away so the merge succeeds, with the leaf content winning via take-ours and no stash remaining. <!--#20383e60c762dfb2-->
  - `TestStashPrevention.test_untracked_unrelated_file_preserved` (method) — Verifies that a non-colliding untracked file in the main repo is stashed and cleanly popped back, so both the merged leaf file and the user's file survive with no dangling stash. <!--#39a3914f9680fcaa-->
- `TestStashPopConflict` (class) — Tests that a conflicting post-merge stash pop resolves via take-ours while firing the audit event that records where the discarded content was archived. <!--#481c94c0e3072896-->
  - `TestStashPopConflict.test_stashpop_conflict_records_audit_issue` (method) — Asserts that a stash-pop conflict calls `_record_stashpop_takeours_event` exactly once with the branch name, an `ArchivedEntry` recovery manifest containing the affected path, and the flow id. <!--#4e789221b2e55b2d-->
- `TestTakeTheirsFallback` (class) — Tests that when LLM conflict resolution is exhausted, the take-theirs fallback preserves the leaf branch's content and completes the merge. <!--#6a4cc61add75089c-->
  - `TestTakeTheirsFallback.test_llm_exhausted_take_theirs_completes_merge` (method) — Builds a real 3-way conflict on `shared.py`, mocks `resolve_merge_conflicts_with_context` to fail, and asserts take-theirs keeps the leaf version, lands a merge commit, and records the take-theirs audit event. <!--#87e8b6ad043337ee-->
- `TestTakeTheirsCommitFailure` (class) — Tests that a failing take-theirs fallback aborts the merge cleanly, leaving no leftover merge state. <!--#75b6e77eab3bc955-->
  - `TestTakeTheirsCommitFailure.test_commit_failure_aborts` (method) — Stubs `_take_theirs_fallback` to return False on a real 3-way conflict and asserts `_merge_leaf_branch` returns False, `MERGE_HEAD` is gone, and main stays at its pre-merge commit. <!--#6dd43574b5c285b4-->
- `TestAuditIssueIntegration` (class) — Tests the audit path end-to-end: take-theirs/stash-pop events write real YAML issues under `tianluo/issues/open/`, and an IssueManager failure never blocks the merge. <!--#eec902d51538ab3b-->
  - `TestAuditIssueIntegration.test_take_theirs_writes_audit_issue_to_se3_issues` (method) — Runs a take-theirs merge with the real IssueManager and asserts a single YAML issue lands in `tianluo/issues/open/` containing the marker, branch, conflicted path, flow id, and `priority: medium`. <!--#250703c88b1973d0-->
  - `TestAuditIssueIntegration.test_audit_failure_does_not_block_merge` (method) — Makes `IssueManager.create` raise and asserts the merge still succeeds with the leaf content intact, proving audit recording is best-effort. <!--#053f6a985f91baa7-->
- `TestExceptionDuringMerge` (class) — Tests that an exception raised mid-merge still pops the pre-merge stash before propagating, so the user is never left with a hidden stash and an apparently empty working tree. <!--#c894b18e23309c01-->
  - `TestExceptionDuringMerge.test_raise_during_merge_still_pops_stash` (method) — Makes `_attempt_merge_with_resolution` raise a RuntimeError and asserts the error propagates while the stashed untracked file is restored and no stash entry remains. <!--#51e3e631de277501-->
- `TestParseStashpopAlreadyExists` (class) — Test class verifying `_parse_stashpop_already_exists` correctly extracts file paths from git's `<path> already exists, no checkout` stderr output. <!--#a90f3e2b3c2c5688-->
  - `TestParseStashpopAlreadyExists.test_single_file` (method) — Test that the parser extracts a single file path from one 'already exists, no checkout' stderr line. <!--#c56a5a764ab25993-->
  - `TestParseStashpopAlreadyExists.test_multiple_files` (method) — Test that the parser extracts multiple file paths from several 'already exists, no checkout' lines. <!--#c2697e4705b687f4-->
  - `TestParseStashpopAlreadyExists.test_mixed_with_unrelated_output` (method) — Test that the parser matches only lines containing 'no checkout' and ignores unrelated output like 'Already up to date'. <!--#04f1b026b3a0a3e9-->
  - `TestParseStashpopAlreadyExists.test_empty_output` (method) — Test that the parser returns an empty list when git produces no stderr output. <!--#39d26351f8d364ce-->
  - `TestParseStashpopAlreadyExists.test_path_with_subdirs` (method) — Test that the parser correctly extracts a nested subdirectory path from the stderr line. <!--#339cac2af25fe17e-->

### `tests/engine/steps/test_implement_reentry_preservation.py` (python) — Regression test module pinning the implement_handler re-entry fix from the double-bump bug, using a git-seeded temp repo and helpers to assert that on fix-iteration/DAG resume the handler preserves the originally-captured pre_session_version (stays at 5.1.0 despite a post-bump disk value) and recomputes session_commits against the flow-wide baseline commit so bump commits merged between entries remain visible to version_analyze. <!--#49c06398f82228c8|1b76afad1f3a1048-->

  - `TestReentryPreservesPreSessionVersion.test_fix_iteration_preserves_pre_session_version` (method) — Verifies that pre_session_version stays pinned to the original 5.1.0 across a re-entry after disk is bumped to 5.2.0, ensuring implement_handler captures it exactly once to avoid a double-bump. <!--#f51756f44ff8b60e-->
  - `TestReentryPreservesPreSessionVersion.test_session_commits_use_flow_baseline_not_per_entry_head` (method) — Verifies that a fix-iteration re-entry recomputes session_commits against flow.baseline_commit so a version-bump commit merged between entries still appears (attributed to pyproject.toml), rather than being missed by diffing the post-bump HEAD. <!--#a94ae9d7e57ce051-->

### `tests/engine/steps/test_investigate_step.py` (python) — Pytest suite for the INVESTIGATE step, covering its registration in STEP_HANDLERS/STEP_POOL, the behavioural contracts spelled out in INVESTIGATE_PROMPT and REVERT_PROMPT, parsing of conclusive/inconclusive/malformed LLM reports into step outputs, and net-zero-diff enforcement against a git workspace baseline (revert-then-fail on leftovers or commits, no destructive cleanup by the engine, baseline persistence across retries). <!--#0fef98861dc1af23|3d57841b02ba51b4-->
- `_git` (function) — Test helper that runs a git subcommand inside a given repo directory with output suppressed and errors raised. <!--#836c49dd876919ac-->

  - `TestRegistration.test_handler_is_registered` (method) — Asserts STEP_HANDLERS maps StepType.INVESTIGATE to investigate_handler. <!--#31021130ad1a0a7e-->
  - `TestRegistration.test_step_pool_entry_is_not_read_only` (method) — Asserts the STEP_POOL entry is named "investigate" and is not read-only, since writes are governed by snapshot comparison rather than the tool layer. <!--#877d041bdf4f93cf-->
- `TestPromptConstraints` (class) — Tests that INVESTIGATE_PROMPT and REVERT_PROMPT literally state their behavioural contracts (no commits, no fixing, net-zero diff, no report files, no destructive git). <!--#ce29441dbbc17c08-->
  - `TestPromptConstraints.test_prompt_forbids_git_commit` (method) — Asserts the investigation prompt explicitly bans committing. <!--#4fdf0f7b09e68a97-->
  - `TestPromptConstraints.test_prompt_routes_the_fix_to_plan_implement` (method) — Asserts the prompt tells the agent not to fix the problem and to defer it to PLAN -> IMPLEMENT. <!--#02d8417d3770b3a4-->

  - `TestPromptConstraints.test_prompt_forbids_report_files` (method) — Asserts the prompt forbids writing findings into project files. <!--#780a8e4bb2f4f3d6-->
  - `TestPromptConstraints.test_revert_prompt_forbids_destructive_git` (method) — Asserts the revert prompt names `git reset --hard`, `git stash`, and `git clean` as forbidden cleanup tools. <!--#2edc219c5d8e2b17-->
- `TestConclusiveParsing` (class) — Tests how investigate_handler parses the LLM's report into step outputs, including conclusive/inconclusive rounds, missing fields, unparsable text, and caller exceptions. <!--#0e9d539e99a9e5a1-->
  - `TestConclusiveParsing.test_conclusive_report_lands_in_outputs` (method) — Asserts a conclusive response completes the step and populates root cause, confidence, evidence, files, fix direction, iteration, and the full report in outputs. <!--#31739da516cdc86c-->
  - `TestConclusiveParsing.test_inconclusive_report_still_completes` (method) — Asserts an inconclusive round still returns COMPLETED with `conclusive=False`, leaving the looping decision to the state machine. <!--#14cd3965286c43b5-->
  - `TestConclusiveParsing.test_missing_conclusive_defaults_to_false` (method) — Asserts a report omitting the `conclusive` field defaults it to False rather than failing. <!--#e13ed2b40d9f13fd-->
  - `TestConclusiveParsing.test_unparsable_response_fails` (method) — Asserts free-text output with no parsable report fails the step with an error naming the missing `root_cause`. <!--#fd304400952680d4-->
  - `TestConclusiveParsing.test_llm_exception_fails_with_reason` (method) — Asserts an exception raised by the LLM caller fails the step and surfaces the underlying reason in error_message. <!--#72a657c04b9b11bd-->
- `TestNetZeroDiffEnforcement` (class) — Tests the net-zero-diff guard: leftover or committed changes trigger a single LLM revert instruction and then failure, the engine never cleans up destructively itself, baselines persist across retries, and pre-existing dirty trees or unavailable snapshots don't fail the step. <!--#46ede30779b058b2-->
  - `TestNetZeroDiffEnforcement.test_unrestored_changes_trigger_revert_then_fail` (method) — Asserts an unreverted probe file yields exactly one follow-up revert prompt naming the file, then FAILED with the delta in error_message and outputs. <!--#dad5eee94bc41add-->
  - `TestNetZeroDiffEnforcement.test_engine_never_reverts_the_workspace_itself` (method) — Asserts the failure path runs no destructive git commands and leaves the LLM's leftover edits untouched on disk. <!--#2c6eba264905a8a6-->
  - `TestNetZeroDiffEnforcement.test_revert_instruction_names_the_tracked_file` (method) — Asserts a modified tracked file is named in the revert prompt, the error message, and the workspace_delta output, so the stateless revert agent isn't left guessing. <!--#55cc928896ea0d4c-->
  - `TestNetZeroDiffEnforcement.test_retry_after_a_violation_keeps_the_original_baseline` (method) — Asserts a retry after a violation reuses the persisted baseline instead of re-baselining on the dirty tree, so the leftover probe still fails the second round. <!--#b9e41a5454012d01-->
  - `TestNetZeroDiffEnforcement.test_retry_passes_once_the_leftovers_are_restored_by_hand` (method) — Asserts a retry on a manually cleaned tree completes and clears both the stored baseline and the previous attempt's workspace_delta marker. <!--#a48779fdd7f9f2d2-->
  - `TestNetZeroDiffEnforcement.test_retry_clears_an_earlier_undecidable_marker` (method) — Asserts a stale "comparison unavailable" workspace_check note from a prior attempt is removed on a successful round. <!--#e8f0b3a40885ba73-->
  - `TestNetZeroDiffEnforcement.test_baseline_is_recorded_on_the_first_attempt` (method) — Asserts the first attempt stores a JSON-serializable workspace_baseline in step.inputs that predates the probe file. <!--#6f11a0a3b41e1359-->
  - `TestNetZeroDiffEnforcement.test_commit_made_during_the_step_fails_it` (method) — Asserts committing a probe patch during the step is caught by HEAD comparison, producing a "HEAD moved" revert prompt and delta despite a clean diff. <!--#ec89e40e2ca7fd1a-->
  - `TestNetZeroDiffEnforcement.test_restored_workspace_after_revert_instruction_passes` (method) — Asserts the step completes with no workspace_delta when the LLM cleans up its own experiment in response to the revert instruction. <!--#14d71a367fc057e1-->
  - `TestNetZeroDiffEnforcement.test_preexisting_dirty_tree_does_not_fail_the_step` (method) — Asserts uncommitted work carried in from earlier steps is baselined rather than blamed, leaving the step COMPLETED and the files intact. <!--#8ac098a9d3e2721d-->
  - `TestNetZeroDiffEnforcement.test_undecidable_snapshot_does_not_fail_the_step` (method) — Asserts an unavailable WorkspaceSnapshot degrades to a workspace_check note instead of failing the step. <!--#d8b7a27291680013-->
- `TestBaselineSurvivesAHardKill` (class) — Tests, through StateMachine.run_step, that the workspace baseline is persisted before the handler's LLM call so a mid-call SIGKILL and later --resume still catch leftovers, and that a failed capture degrades gracefully. <!--#9dda0f66dcb8e314-->
  - `TestBaselineSurvivesAHardKill._state_machine` (method) — Helper building a StateMachine with a mocked PersistenceManager and the investigate handler registered. <!--#ab3618756a6b74f3-->
  - `TestBaselineSurvivesAHardKill.test_baseline_is_persisted_before_the_handler_runs` (method) — Asserts the first save_flow call — the one preceding the LLM call — already carries workspace_baseline in step.inputs. <!--#d2d42807fe70dc18-->
  - `TestBaselineSurvivesAHardKill.test_resume_after_a_mid_call_kill_still_catches_the_leftover` (method) — Simulates a hard kill mid-call by rebuilding the step from only the pre-handler persisted inputs, and asserts the resumed run still fails on the leftover probe. <!--#43faa5bd3faef618-->
  - `TestBaselineSurvivesAHardKill.test_capture_failure_does_not_break_the_step` (method) — Asserts a snapshot_workspace error during baseline capture is swallowed, storing nothing so a later attempt can retry. <!--#e701494a9a968974-->
- `TestPromptAssembly` (class) — Tests how the investigation prompt is assembled: previous-round findings injection, round/max-iteration wording, runtime-environment block inclusion, and fast failure on a missing task description. <!--#b569096f25c655f7-->
  - `TestPromptAssembly.test_previous_reports_are_injected_on_a_repeat_round` (method) — Asserts a second round's prompt embeds the prior report's root cause and the "round 2 of at most 3" wording. <!--#9d570209100e2a82-->
  - `TestPromptAssembly.test_first_round_has_no_previous_findings_section` (method) — Asserts the first-round prompt omits the previous-rounds section entirely. <!--#a4f0a79b5c277337-->
  - `TestPromptAssembly.test_unlimited_max_iterations_renders_as_unlimited` (method) — Asserts a max-iterations value of 0 renders as "at most unlimited" in the prompt. <!--#b596e144e0ca40fe-->
  - `TestPromptAssembly.test_runtime_environment_block_is_injected_by_default` (method) — Regression test asserting investigate is in the runtime-env default whitelist, so the prompt carries the tianluo Runtime Environment block and `luo history list` hint. <!--#3f2db440125991ab-->
  - `TestPromptAssembly.test_missing_task_description_fails_fast` (method) — Asserts a step with no task description fails immediately with an explanatory error message. <!--#949296907595c2b4-->
- `TestPureHelpers` (class) — Unit tests for the module's pure helpers `_coerce_conclusive` and `_format_previous_reports`. <!--#1e612f6876ab70db-->
  - `TestPureHelpers.test_coerce_conclusive` (method) — Parametrized test that `_coerce_conclusive` maps booleans and truthy strings to True and everything else to False. <!--#dd546834671fe584-->
  - `TestPureHelpers.test_format_previous_reports_empty` (method) — Asserts `_format_previous_reports` returns an empty string for None or an empty list. <!--#7ff6194d5f286fd5-->
  - `TestPureHelpers.test_format_previous_reports_renders_rounds` (method) — Asserts `_format_previous_reports` numbers each round and joins evidence items with "; ". <!--#e601923f6a715e05-->
- `TestCliRendering` (class) — Tests the CLI rendering of the INVESTIGATE step: localized titles and panels in en-US and zh-CN, plus surfacing of the workspace delta on failure. <!--#ed9e396172ee635b-->
  - `TestCliRendering._isolate_console` (method) — Autouse fixture that saves and restores the module-global rich console so rendering tests don't leak state. <!--#9c273b3e8bce4c7f-->
  - `TestCliRendering._render` (method) — Helper that sets the language, renders a step into a StringIO-backed rich Console, and returns the captured text. <!--#898c1a7cfd864631-->
  - `TestCliRendering._completed_step` (method) — Helper building a COMPLETED INVESTIGATE Step with a full conclusive report in outputs for rendering assertions. <!--#9ee4314719f7571b-->
  - `TestCliRendering.test_renders_localized_panel_en_us` (method) — Asserts the en-US panel shows the localized title, CONCLUSIVE marker, section headings, and verbatim LLM content. <!--#020ae63eb7a1767e-->
  - `TestCliRendering.test_renders_localized_panel_zh_cn` (method) — Asserts the zh-CN panel uses Chinese headings and leaks no raw "investigate" step key. <!--#cb4dfe3041806bf1-->
  - `TestCliRendering.test_step_display_title_is_localized` (method) — Asserts `step_display_title` returns "Root-Cause Investigation" in en-US and 根因调查 in zh-CN. <!--#779f6735f022e159-->
  - `TestCliRendering.test_failed_step_surfaces_the_workspace_delta` (method) — Asserts a FAILED step's rendering shows both the leftover file from workspace_delta and the net-zero-diff error message. <!--#12eb29d81a7a3adf-->

### `tests/engine/steps/test_plan_capability_grouping.py` (python) — Prompt-text unit tests pinning the PLAN step's capability-grouping doctrine: that the capability prompt states a single splitting criterion with all four sizing rules and no proposal/design or per-task listings, that each PlanGranularity tier (auto/single/conservative, with fallback to AUTO and no effect under GRANULAR) contributes exactly one distinct directive, and that ARTIFACT_SPLIT_GUARDRAIL forbids test/docs/config and file/module/layer splits while keeping tests inside every group. <!--#866ee91bd2509873|9cac6a2f3e69a5d4-->
- `_capability_prompt` (function) — Test helper that renders the PLAN step prompt under `PlanDecomposition.CAPABILITY` at a given `PlanGranularity` (default `AUTO`), using the shared `_PROMPT_KWARGS` fixture data. <!--#0084eab685987107-->
- `_granular_prompt` (function) — Test helper that renders the PLAN step prompt under the legacy `PlanDecomposition.GRANULAR` doctrine, used as the frozen-baseline counterpart to `_capability_prompt`. <!--#4695adeb71ea38ed-->
- `TestCapabilityGroupingDoctrine` (class) — Asserts the capability prompt teaches the single splitting criterion ("can one autonomous implement call carry this?"), carries all four sizing criteria, groups by task rather than capability, drops proposal/design and per-task listings, and is identical across every task type. <!--#6ef71df7aefd1a63-->
  - `TestCapabilityGroupingDoctrine.test_prompt_states_the_single_splitting_criterion` (method) — Checks the prompt names one and only one splitting criterion — whether a single autonomous implement call can safely carry the work. <!--#e00a5f1df22ad7aa-->
  - `TestCapabilityGroupingDoctrine.test_prompt_carries_all_four_sizing_criteria` (method) — Asserts on the whitespace-flattened prompt that all four group-sizing rules are present: one task/one call → one group, over-large task → multiple groups, independent tasks → one group each, and default-to-aggregation with no pre-cutting along phases or artifact types. <!--#27724c045c451dd6-->
  - `TestCapabilityGroupingDoctrine.test_old_split_bias_wording_is_gone` (method) — Renders the prompt at every PlanGranularity tier and asserts none of the retired capability-unit / split-bias phrases survive in any tier directive. <!--#d197818b320172b0-->
  - `TestCapabilityGroupingDoctrine.test_thought_experiment_baseline_semantics` (method) — Pins the two sentences behind the "2 groups, not 4" baseline: a coherent task must not be pre-cut by PLAN, while mutually unrelated tasks each get a group for parallel worktree execution. <!--#a5b02065a19b4756-->
  - `TestCapabilityGroupingDoctrine.test_prompt_forbids_a_per_task_listing` (method) — Checks the capability prompt forbids enumerating individual tasks inside a group. <!--#95fa65f1cb5206b9-->
  - `TestCapabilityGroupingDoctrine.test_prompt_asks_for_no_proposal_or_design` (method) — Checks the capability prompt contains no "Proposal"/"Design" wording, since PLAN now emits scheduling data only. <!--#073cc4c08de1f456-->
  - `TestCapabilityGroupingDoctrine.test_prompt_labels_the_task_groups_section_once` (method) — Checks the task-groups section is titled `## Instructions: Task Groups (task units)` with no leftover "Part 1/2/3" numbering. <!--#b47cd9e118e20c64-->
  - `TestCapabilityGroupingDoctrine.test_every_task_type_gets_the_same_prompt` (method) — Parametrized check that all task types render a byte-identical capability prompt apart from the `## Task Type` line, proving depth tiering is gone. <!--#26a1d9bac366c0e2-->
  - `TestCapabilityGroupingDoctrine.test_capability_prompt_never_carries_the_granular_tasks_section` (method) — Checks the capability prompt never leaks the granular Task Structure section or estimated_loc. <!--#2180195e4a0c660e-->
- `TestGranularityTiers` (class) — Verifies the auto/single/conservative granularity directives are mutually exclusive, distinctly headed, carry their intended splitting bias, fall back to `AUTO` on an unknown value, and are ignored under the granular doctrine. <!--#b468ae605e2ad31f-->
  - `TestGranularityTiers.test_exactly_one_tier_appears_in_a_prompt` (method) — Checks a prompt embeds only the requested granularity tier's directive and none of the others. <!--#7ad552e8d4fc053e-->
  - `TestGranularityTiers.test_tier_headings_are_distinct` (method) — Checks the three granularity directives have three distinct heading lines. <!--#ed38463e9fb8daf2-->
  - `TestGranularityTiers.test_single_demands_exactly_one_group` (method) — Checks the single tier instructs the model to emit exactly one group and never split. <!--#79ccfb7cbc1a2827-->
  - `TestGranularityTiers.test_auto_sizes_by_independent_task_count` (method) — Checks the auto tier sizes group count by the number of mutually independent tasks, normally one group per task, splitting only at the capability edge. <!--#aa89b4f2ba651c3b-->
  - `TestGranularityTiers.test_conservative_is_more_split_prone_than_auto` (method) — Contrasts the conservative and auto tiers, asserting conservative lowers the splitting threshold toward one group per sub-task while auto keeps the aggregation default and never carries that lowering language. <!--#5047e78ca2ace3f3-->
  - `TestGranularityTiers.test_unknown_granularity_falls_back_to_auto` (method) — Checks a malformed persisted granularity value still renders `CAPABILITY_GRANULARITY_AUTO` instead of dropping the directive. <!--#cac1386a5466ea67-->
  - `TestGranularityTiers.test_granularity_is_ignored_under_granular` (method) — Checks every `PlanGranularity` value produces the same granular prompt, so the tier only affects the capability doctrine. <!--#f9db6667600611ae-->
- `TestArtifactSplitGuardrail` (class) — Verifies `ARTIFACT_SPLIT_GUARDRAIL` mirrors the form of `VERSION_FILE_GUARDRAIL`, forbids test/docs/config and file/module/layer splits, keeps tests inside each group, still permits a genuine test-system task, uses task-unit wording, and is attached only under the capability doctrine. <!--#2dece0ed8adc7a74-->
  - `TestArtifactSplitGuardrail.test_guardrail_has_the_same_form_as_the_version_guardrail` (method) — Checks both guardrails share the heading + prose + bullet-list + trailing-newline shape. <!--#b25111563df54b8f-->
  - `TestArtifactSplitGuardrail.test_guardrail_names_the_three_forbidden_group_shapes` (method) — Checks the guardrail explicitly forbids separate test, docs, and config groups. <!--#3ca23bb7f9f7b20f-->
  - `TestArtifactSplitGuardrail.test_guardrail_makes_tests_part_of_every_group` (method) — Checks the guardrail makes tests part of what each group itself delivers. <!--#764078ec062934c4-->
  - `TestArtifactSplitGuardrail.test_guardrail_forbids_file_module_and_layer_splits` (method) — Checks the guardrail rules out splitting along file sets, module boundaries, or code layers. <!--#36bd80c7e556ee93-->
  - `TestArtifactSplitGuardrail.test_guardrail_still_allows_a_test_system_task` (method) — Ensures the guardrail keeps its escape-hatch example so a task about the test system itself remains plannable. <!--#1f899bea01822139-->
  - `TestArtifactSplitGuardrail.test_guardrail_carries_the_task_grouping_unit` (method) — Asserts every unit-of-grouping statement in the guardrail names the task rather than the capability, since the guardrail sits right after the capability tasks section. <!--#8ee2c9e22ec6d871-->
  - `TestArtifactSplitGuardrail.test_guardrail_is_only_attached_under_capability` (method) — Checks the artifact-split guardrail appears in the capability prompt and is absent from the granular one. <!--#3fd9d24187a3fa9b-->
  - `TestArtifactSplitGuardrail.test_version_guardrail_survives_in_both_doctrines` (method) — Checks the version-file guardrail is still present under both capability and granular prompts. <!--#fc3a234739016389-->
- `TestCapabilitySchema` (class) — Asserts the capability JSON schema and its hint expose only the five scheduling fields, omit any `tasks` array, proposal/design or `plan` key, use task-not-capability example wording, document parallelism and acyclicity, and embed in the prompt as parseable JSON. <!--#da825eb4bee2eb3d-->
  - `TestCapabilitySchema.test_schema_declares_no_tasks_array` (method) — Checks the capability schema omits a tasks key and tells the model not to emit one. <!--#e5071af1d433ce14-->
  - `TestCapabilitySchema.test_schema_declares_the_five_scheduling_fields` (method) — Checks the capability schema declares group_id, name, description, group_order, and depends_on. <!--#d03aacd331f88bbe-->
  - `TestCapabilitySchema.test_schema_example_names_a_task_not_a_capability` (method) — Checks the schema's example group is labelled as the task it delivers, not the old capability wording. <!--#27888ef100054f42-->
  - `TestCapabilitySchema.test_schema_carries_no_proposal_or_design` (method) — Checks both the capability and granular JSON schemas mention no proposal, design, or `"plan"` key. <!--#f25fae95470809f7-->
  - `TestCapabilitySchema.test_schema_explains_that_independent_groups_run_in_parallel` (method) — Checks the schema tells the model that independent groups run in parallel. <!--#76ec4c7d937938c9-->
  - `TestCapabilitySchema.test_schema_requires_acyclic_dependencies` (method) — Checks the schema states dependencies must be acyclic, avoiding a costly re-plan on a cycle. <!--#a1c5a0714205fae5-->
  - `TestCapabilitySchema.test_schema_hint_carries_no_tasks_key` (method) — Checks the capability JSON schema hint has no tasks key while the granular hint still does. <!--#fa75512c53201af4-->
  - `TestCapabilitySchema.test_schema_hints_carry_no_proposal_or_design` (method) — Checks the capability and granular schema *hints* likewise carry no proposal, design, or `"plan"` key. <!--#0cf13cb87b009af3-->
  - `TestCapabilitySchema.test_schema_reaches_the_prompt_as_valid_json` (method) — Checks the schema block is appended verbatim (braces unescaped) and its JSON block parses. <!--#24da3be07de8640a-->
- `TestGranularDoctrineIsFrozen` (class) — Pins the legacy granular prompt as unchanged — its sections, `estimated_loc` wording, and section ordering are preserved, and none of the new capability-doctrine vocabulary leaks into it. <!--#0280ce7b0eb796fc-->
  - `TestGranularDoctrineIsFrozen.test_granular_sections_are_unchanged` (method) — Checks the granular prompt still contains `TASKS_SECTION`, the grouping principles, the cohesion bullet, and the `estimated_loc` instruction. <!--#d50f218ca757394b-->
  - `TestGranularDoctrineIsFrozen.test_granular_prompt_has_no_capability_doctrine_vocabulary` (method) — Checks no capability-doctrine wording leaks into the granular prompt. <!--#6f08fc2ccfcd277d-->
  - `TestGranularDoctrineIsFrozen.test_granular_prompt_matches_the_recorded_section_order` (method) — Checks the granular prompt keeps its frozen section order: task groups, then the version-file guardrail, then the JSON response block. <!--#66f84ba2477e8e6e-->
- `_flow_and_step` (function) — Test helper that builds a FlowInstance and a PLAN Step, optionally seeding the persisted decomposition and granularity into flow context. <!--#4f14d375f88be17c-->
- `_run_plan` (function) — Test helper that runs the PLAN handler with a mocked LLMCaller returning a canned JSON response and all context injections stubbed out, returning the status and the mock caller. <!--#63daa6039890ecac-->
- `TestPlanHandlerDispatch` (class) — End-to-end tests of the PLAN handler: it reads back the persisted doctrine to choose prompt/schema hint, records mode and group count, and under capability validates the emitted task_groups (identity, description, uniqueness, orderability, dependency edges) by failing the step instead of persisting a plan IMPLEMENT cannot schedule, while leaving granular behaviour untouched. <!--#cd60827e38923fd7-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_capability_parse_survives_groups_without_tasks` (method) — Checks a capability plan whose groups carry no tasks array parses and completes. <!--#a0b0f8a7db0ec626-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_outputs_record_the_mode_and_group_count` (method) — Checks the step outputs record plan_decomposition, plan_granularity, and plan_group_count. <!--#cd394b206671ea08-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_group_count_matches_a_single_group_plan` (method) — Checks plan_group_count is 1 for a single-group capability plan. <!--#2e4ca69ab74c1657-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_capability_prompt_is_sent_for_a_capability_flow` (method) — Checks a capability flow sends the guardrail, the single-granularity directive, and the capability schema hint to the LLM. <!--#0e6564dbf00f4753-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_granular_flow_gets_the_legacy_prompt_and_hint` (method) — Checks a granular flow sends the legacy prompt and hint and records the granular mode. <!--#385911104e33bc3f-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_flow_without_a_persisted_mode_plans_under_the_default` (method) — Checks a flow with no persisted decomposition defaults to capability. <!--#0e18908c46e4659c-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_legacy_planned_flow_keeps_the_granular_doctrine` (method) — Checks an old `planned`-strategy flow resumed into PLAN stays on the granular doctrine. <!--#0a684bccc9aec0e9-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_empty_capability_plan_fails_instead_of_completing` (method) — Checks a capability plan with zero groups fails the step rather than persisting an unreadable execution shape. <!--#f3f9955893fb2026-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_non_list_capability_groups_fail_instead_of_completing` (method) — Checks a task_groups value that is a dict or string fails the step and stores no groups or count. <!--#9f198ba44090d676-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_capability_groups_that_are_not_group_objects_fail` (method) — Checks list entries that are not well-formed group objects (bare strings, missing/blank/non-string group_id) fail the step. <!--#01fb1304a8f1167b-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_capability_group_named_but_without_group_id_fails` (method) — Checks a group carrying only `name` fails, since transitive_reduce indexes on group_id and would abort IMPLEMENT. <!--#c6d5187156c1a216-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_capability_group_without_a_description_fails` (method) — Checks a capability group missing its description fails, naming the offending group id, since the description is that group's whole work statement. <!--#c68b7827c508b2bf-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_capability_groups_with_a_repeated_group_id_fail` (method) — Checks a duplicate group_id is rejected at PLAN, where a retry can still produce a different plan. <!--#002f116a356a5952-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_capability_duplicate_survives_a_forked_dependency_shape` (method) — Checks the duplicate-id guard still fires on a forked DAG that would otherwise reach the scheduler. <!--#9f770583395353c7-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_capability_unorderable_group_order_fails` (method) — Checks a group_order the sort cannot compare (e.g. a quoted number) fails at PLAN instead of raising a TypeError in IMPLEMENT. <!--#16e0329f71e98b42-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_capability_quoted_group_order_would_abort_implement` (method) — Pins that `_extract_sorted_groups` really does raise TypeError on a quoted group_order, justifying the guard. <!--#24143e96951db0cd-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_capability_missing_group_order_is_accepted` (method) — Checks groups that omit group_order are accepted because they all take the same default. <!--#091d29e9487f3d8b-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_capability_distinct_group_ids_are_accepted` (method) — Checks the uniqueness guard does not fire on a well-formed multi-group plan. <!--#f69da8a5aef3573e-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_capability_dependency_cycle_fails` (method) — Checks a dependency cycle fails at PLAN rather than surfacing as a raw DAGScheduler ValueError. <!--#005dcb638a618cf3-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_capability_self_dependency_fails` (method) — Checks a group depending on itself is rejected as a one-node cycle. <!--#8cf014c50065c856-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_capability_cycle_behind_a_fork_fails` (method) — Checks a cycle among only some groups still fails the whole plan. <!--#16f62e2f8d110fb9-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_capability_non_list_depends_on_fails` (method) — Checks a depends_on that is not a list fails, since the scheduler iterates the edges directly. <!--#f7688010eb016d60-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_capability_non_id_depends_on_entry_fails` (method) — Checks a depends_on entry that is not an id string fails before scheduling can attempt membership tests. <!--#8b33562d9431e9d8-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_capability_acyclic_edges_are_accepted` (method) — Checks a well-formed chain, including a redundant edge, passes validation. <!--#c3c9d2a75aa7b954-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_capability_missing_depends_on_is_accepted` (method) — Checks an omitted or null depends_on is treated as 'no edges' rather than malformed. <!--#5390e62d96bd798f-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_capability_dangling_edge_fails` (method) — Checks an edge naming an undeclared group fails, instead of being silently dropped and running a group without its prerequisite's code. <!--#d2c9ae69783d6f06-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_capability_dangling_edge_alongside_a_valid_one_fails` (method) — Checks one resolvable edge does not excuse an unresolvable sibling edge. <!--#a4fb237f08843441-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_padded_ids_and_edges_are_persisted_stripped` (method) — Checks whitespace-padded ids and edges are persisted stripped so validation and DAGScheduler key on the same strings. <!--#7002b7c20e724731-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_a_rejected_plan_is_not_rewritten` (method) — Checks normalization is applied only after the whole enumeration passes, leaving a rejected plan's raw values intact. <!--#fa524e66ffc44eea-->
  - `TestPlanHandlerDispatch.test_a_padded_id_still_collides_with_its_unpadded_twin` (method) — Checks id stripping does not let a padded duplicate slip through the uniqueness guard. <!--#e238667e0fa10e5a-->

### `tests/engine/steps/test_self_check_correctness_regression.py` (python) — Regression test module for the self-check step, covering the SELF_CHECK_PROMPT text contract (six quality dimensions, effective-task authority over plan tasks, finding fields, format placeholders), requirement-source collection from charter and WHY:/INVARIANT: comments, and the `_validate_and_filter_issues` grounding rules for admissible expectation sources, causal/deletion anchors, prior still-open finding anchors, and undecidable-baseline scope relaxations. <!--#66a08a1a40c34ce6|6b53cf522974fc6f-->

- `TestEffectiveSourcePool` (class) — Test class covering requirement-source collection — that charter and WHY/INVARIANT comments are gathered, and that the source pool includes the effective base plus interjections and constraints while excluding plan/implement/original-task derivations. <!--#766924f9c3cfeeeb-->
  - `TestEffectiveSourcePool.test_constraint_collector_keeps_charter_and_marked_comments` (method) — Verifies get_self_check_constraint_sources reads charter.md and extracts only WHY:/INVARIANT:-marked comments from changed files, dropping ordinary comments. <!--#3f94926a96ab6a2f-->
  - `TestEffectiveSourcePool.test_effective_base_interjections_and_constraints_are_included` (method) — Verifies _build_source_pool admits the adjudicated task base, user interjections, and project constraints while excluding the superseded original task, plan task groups, and implement summary. <!--#eac21523eefe46cd-->
  - `TestEffectiveSourcePool.test_legacy_spec_carrier_is_not_requirement_authority` (method) — Verifies legacy spec_content contributes nothing to the source pool, which stays limited to the task description. <!--#857b07680c9271c2-->
- `TestValidation` (class) — Test class exercising _validate_and_filter_issues — which expectation-source types are admissible and how findings must ground their evidence against changed paths, causal/deletion anchors, prior still-open findings, and undecidable-baseline scopes. <!--#178db8bf7db433f8-->
  - `TestValidation._inputs` (method) — Helper returning a baseline self-check inputs dict with an effective task base, two changed files, and a charter constraint. <!--#2cc82b6bd763afe4-->
  - `TestValidation._issue` (method) — Helper building a well-formed self-check finding whose expectation source type and verbatim quote can be overridden per test. <!--#817b54072046446e-->
  - `TestValidation.test_task_and_constraint_grounded_findings_survive` (method) — Asserts findings grounded in the task description or the charter both pass validation and are counted as kept. <!--#d83d64cc87183f85-->
  - `TestValidation.test_plan_task_source_is_rejected` (method) — Asserts a finding whose expectation source is plan_task is filtered out and tallied as an unsupported source type. <!--#dca3613c8ea6b83d-->
  - `TestValidation.test_requirement_omission_can_use_missing_in` (method) — Asserts an omission finding with no evidence_lines still survives when it grounds on missing_in. <!--#dd98b46624cea7d1-->
  - `TestValidation.test_regression_requires_a_changed_causal_line` (method) — Asserts a regression finding survives only when it cites a changed-file line, and is rejected as bad evidence when it falls back to missing_in in the default scope. <!--#55c78bd9e08f2597-->
  - `TestValidation.test_deletion_only_regression_can_ground_on_missing_in` (method) — Asserts a regression on a deletion-only path can ground via missing_in, while a missing_in path outside the current scope is still rejected. <!--#233a39ef15302bc6-->
  - `TestValidation.test_still_open_finding_anchors_survive_a_narrow_incremental_scope` (method) — Asserts a still-open finding's own recorded anchors widen an incremental round's scope so its re-report survives, but the same citation is out of scope without the prior finding. <!--#b79c9b8ceaa2d41e-->
  - `TestValidation.test_prior_anchor_does_not_make_an_anchor_less_path_anchor_bearing` (method) — Asserts a prior finding's stale line number on a deleted (anchor-less) path does not make that path anchor-bearing, so bare-path re-reports — including regressions — still ground. <!--#2e659ce2727def22-->
  - `TestValidation.test_prior_anchor_does_not_extend_an_anchor_bearing_range_set` (method) — Asserts a prior finding's line never becomes a current-side causal anchor on an anchor-bearing path (new citations there are rejected), while on a deleted path the citation still grounds at path level. <!--#22df8f2adac0e291-->
  - `TestValidation.test_bare_path_prior_finding_widens_the_scope` (method) — Asserts a prior finding recorded as a bare path (or a missing_in entry with a line suffix) widens the changed-path set by path, so its re-report survives — and is out of scope once the prior finding is removed. <!--#db9afb90aecfab25-->
  - `TestValidation.test_prior_line_citation_does_not_widen_as_a_bare_path` (method) — Asserts scope widening strips line suffixes, so a prior line citation cannot ground at path level and bypass the causal-anchor check on an anchor-bearing path. <!--#2c563a0e20bfdaa8-->
  - `TestValidation.test_undecidable_scope_accepts_regression_missing_in` (method) — Asserts that under an undecidable baseline a regression grounds equally through missing_in or evidence_lines on a reported changed file. <!--#26309982b5e43723-->
  - `TestValidation.test_undecidable_scope_keeps_evidence_outside_the_summary_list` (method) — Asserts an undecidable baseline keeps a finding citing a file absent from the self-reported files_changed and tallies the relaxation, while a decidable scope still rejects it. <!--#4b9603bb81423d69-->
  - `TestValidation.test_undecidable_scope_unions_reconstructed_and_reported_paths` (method) — Asserts an undecidable baseline treats reconstructed diff paths and summary-reported paths as a union, so citations on either ground directly without counting as a relaxation. <!--#1474f2fad475cd64-->
  - `TestValidation.test_out_of_scope_flag_is_not_a_release_valve` (method) — Asserts an out_of_scope flag on a finding neither suppresses it nor produces a separate stats tally. <!--#9f53b8acb7ff97f1-->
- `test_handler_prompt_uses_effective_requirements_not_task_groups` (function) — End-to-end test that self_check_handler with a mocked LLMCaller builds a prompt carrying the effective task base and user interjections but not plan task-group text, and retaining the quality-dimension sections. <!--#3d79897d028cfdad-->
