  - `TestFormatSessionCommitsHelper.test_non_empty_renders_sha_and_subject` (method) — Asserts _format_session_commits renders each commit's shortened sha, subject, and file names for a non-empty commit list. <!--#66180b00c3a7cdcf-->
  - `TestFormatSessionCommitsHelper.test_renders_at_most_50_commits` (method) — Asserts the helper caps rendering at 50 commits and reports the remaining count as undisplayed. <!--#31863b1ebb0b85bd-->
  - `TestFormatSessionCommitsHelper.test_folds_long_file_lists` (method) — Asserts long per-commit file lists are truncated to 10 with a folded-remainder note. <!--#058b2f5fd1c1afdb-->
- `TestPromptIncludesSessionCommitsAndPreSession` (class) — Test suite verifying version_analyze_handler injects the Pre-Session Version and Session-Introduced Commits fields into the LLM prompt, including empty-list and disk-version fallback (with warning) cases. <!--#b79364ea59f2d80c-->
  - `TestPromptIncludesSessionCommitsAndPreSession.test_prompt_includes_pre_session_version_and_commit_list` (method) — Asserts the LLM prompt surfaces the pre_session_version baseline, the commit list (shas/subjects), the '视为未发生' instruction, and the disk version for cross-reference. <!--#50524b04324ef068-->
  - `TestPromptIncludesSessionCommitsAndPreSession.test_prompt_handles_empty_session_commits` (method) — Asserts an empty session_commits input still renders the explanatory line and pre-session version without crashing. <!--#673593d5de65b953-->
  - `TestPromptIncludesSessionCommitsAndPreSession.test_pre_session_version_fallback_to_current_version` (method) — Asserts that when pre_session_version is absent the handler falls back to the disk-read version and logs a warning. <!--#2a1c5bf3b717a0f2-->
- `TestWorktreeIntentPersistenceIsMandatory` (class) — Test suite asserting worktree-mode version intent persistence is mandatory: write_intent failure FAILs the step, success COMPLETEs with an on-disk intent, and version-bumping-disabled emits no intent at all. <!--#327c7d384b9b3c4a-->
  - `TestWorktreeIntentPersistenceIsMandatory.test_write_intent_oserror_fails_the_step` (method) — Asserts that an OSError from write_intent in worktree mode returns StepStatus.FAILED with a 'version-intents' error message and leaks no suggested_version into outputs. <!--#e8666453355e0723-->
  - `TestWorktreeIntentPersistenceIsMandatory.test_successful_persist_still_completes` (method) — Asserts a successful worktree run COMPLETEs and actually writes the intent JSON file under <project>/tianluo/version-intents/<flow_id>.json with the expected bump_type. <!--#3d0888646f63aec1-->
  - `TestWorktreeIntentPersistenceIsMandatory.test_version_disabled_worktree_emits_no_intent` (method) — Asserts that with version bumping disabled, a worktree flow COMPLETEs without emitting a version_intent/suggested_version and never calls write_intent or creates the intents directory. <!--#6da17740216b0887-->
- `TestEndToEndDoubleBumpReplay` (class) — End-to-end regression suite replaying the 20260512-225655 double-bump scenario through a real StateMachine/FlowInstance, mocking only the LLM and git/VersionBumper side-effects. <!--#7f2634bdf27478a2-->
  - `TestEndToEndDoubleBumpReplay._make_implement_step` (method) — Test fixture building a COMPLETED implement Step whose outputs carry pre_session_version=5.1.0 and a two-entry session_commits list (an inadvertent version bump plus a feature commit). <!--#28ccfb0b978eaea3-->
  - `TestEndToEndDoubleBumpReplay._make_flow_with_implement` (method) — Test fixture building a real FlowInstance with selected_steps [IMPLEMENT, VERSION_ANALYZE, COMMIT] and the pre-built implement step added to its state. <!--#8ac2b0e7580d2a88-->
  - `TestEndToEndDoubleBumpReplay.test_e2e_replay_writes_pre_session_baseline_not_disk_baseline` (method) — End-to-end test proving state_machine forwards pre_session_version/session_commits into version_analyze so the resolved and committed version is 5.2.0 (from the 5.1.0 baseline) rather than a double-bumped 5.2.1 off the disk value. <!--#7c7357615458e78f-->
- `TestGuardVersionRaceOwnReplay` (class) — Test suite for commit's _guard_version_race and _reanalyze_version_with_baseline, distinguishing the flow's own prior version write (keep target) from true concurrent drift (re-analyse), and verifying is_tag/halt behavior. <!--#3fceeae9311b3cf8-->
  - `TestGuardVersionRaceOwnReplay._guard_flow` (method) — Test helper producing a mock flow with a fresh State() and change_path under tmp_path for the race-guard tests. <!--#9ba12fb5518eeb59-->
  - `TestGuardVersionRaceOwnReplay.test_own_prior_write_is_not_treated_as_drift` (method) — Asserts that when _flow_wrote_version reports the disk version is the flow's own write, _guard_version_race keeps the resolved target and does not re-analyse. <!--#9b9e024f2cba03e3-->
  - `TestGuardVersionRaceOwnReplay.test_true_concurrent_drift_still_reanalyses` (method) — Asserts that when the disk version is another flow's write, _guard_version_race calls _reanalyze_version_with_baseline and returns the recomputed version. <!--#ee4dda9923c9b1e1-->
  - `TestGuardVersionRaceOwnReplay.test_reanalysis_forwards_refreshed_is_tag` (method) — Asserts _reanalyze_version_with_baseline forwards the recomputed is_tag (and bump_type) back into step.inputs so a minor→patch re-analysis stops tagging. <!--#42d13a8ab926dda0-->
  - `TestGuardVersionRaceOwnReplay.test_reanalysis_forwards_is_tag_true` (method) — Mirror-case assertion that a patch→minor re-analysis forwards is_tag=True so commit starts tagging the recomputed version. <!--#90a1c5271b6a7917-->
  - `TestGuardVersionRaceOwnReplay.test_reanalysis_returning_disk_version_halts` (method) — Asserts that if re-analysis still returns the drifted disk version (a colliding release), _guard_version_race raises RuntimeError rather than writing it. <!--#315f3932791b72d9-->

### `tests/engine/steps/test_version_rules_file.py` (python) — Pytest module verifying the `_read_version_rules_file` loader across all branches (missing file/se3 dir → None, normal read verbatim, oversize truncation with warning, unreadable-file degradation to None) and pinning the `VERSION_RULES_FILE_RELPATH` constant to `tianluo/version-rules.md`. <!--#bb91d627ee64cc0c|23bc3a2600fda277-->
- `TestVersionRulesFileLoader` (class) — Test class exercising every branch of `_read_version_rules_file`: missing file/dir returns None, normal file returned verbatim, oversized file truncated with a `Truncated by SE3` notice and warning, and OSError degrades to None plus a warning. <!--#7e9b609647a7f32a-->

  - `TestVersionRulesFileLoader.test_returns_none_when_se3_dir_missing` (method) — Asserts that a project root lacking a `tianluo/` directory entirely makes `_read_version_rules_file` return None. <!--#04892b9c6c1407bf-->
  - `TestVersionRulesFileLoader.test_returns_full_content_for_normal_file` (method) — Verifies a normal Markdown rules file is returned verbatim and untruncated (no `Truncated by SE3` notice). <!--#c90453fa5dc5c3a3-->
  - `TestVersionRulesFileLoader.test_truncates_oversized_file_and_warns` (method) — Verifies a file exceeding `VERSION_RULES_MAX_BYTES` is truncated to the cap with an appended `Truncated by SE3` notice and an `exceeds` warning logged. <!--#76461b5bebec3a57-->
  - `TestVersionRulesFileLoader.test_returns_none_when_file_unreadable` (method) — Patches `Path.read_bytes` to raise OSError for the rules file and asserts the loader degrades to None while logging a `Could not read` warning. <!--#bfa2282d77175a98-->
- `TestVersionRulesFileRelPath` (class) — Test class pinning the loader's location contract by asserting the `VERSION_RULES_FILE_SUBPATH` constant. <!--#cf1cc17cc486670c-->
  - `TestVersionRulesFileRelPath.test_relpath_is_the_documented_location` (method) — Asserts `VERSION_RULES_FILE_SUBPATH == "version-rules.md"`, pinning the documented rules-file location. <!--#10f69456f4705316-->

## `tests/fixtures/` — Static test-data directory holding non-code fixtures for parsing and replay tests — captured pytest console output (serial and `xdist` runs), JSONL provider usage transcripts (Claude CLI, claude-interactive, Codex exec, compat-proxy), and a sampled history-relay framing shape used by history backpressure tests. <!--#ab443823c68f647f|78d863e5170c375f-->

### `tests/fixtures/history_relay_shape_20260831.json` (json) — A test fixture capturing the structural shape (flow_id, 52 per-step record counts, and the uneven per-frame chunk boundaries) sampled from the real 4324-record flow tianluo/history/20260831-095750_23865927 via DaemonHistoryReader.read_flow, so history relay/backpressure tests can replay realistic framing with synthesized record bodies. <!--#6e60669e2aab50c7|5514535a53b5eaa5-->
- `_source` (json-key) — Provenance note recording that this fixture's shape was captured from the real flow tianluo/history/20260831-095750_23865927 (52 steps / 4324 records / ~49 MB) via DaemonHistoryReader.read_flow, and that only per-step and per-frame record counts are committed while record bodies are synthesized by the test. <!--#8d04af58a9752a2f-->
- `flow_id` (json-key) — The identifier of the source flow the shape was sampled from, "20260831-095750_23865927". <!--#ca2f37be687422b4-->
- `frames` (json-key) — Ordered list of per-frame record counts reproducing the daemon's real chunk-bounded read boundaries (highly uneven, including many 1-record and one trailing 0-record frame) so relay/backpressure tests replay realistic framing. <!--#e98de1f81ae0cced-->
- `steps` (json-key) — Ordered list of the flow's 52 steps, each with its step_id and record count, capturing the real distribution from tiny 4-record test steps up to a 2037-record implement step. <!--#f26fdc348a59c0f8-->

## `tests/fixtures/test_output/` — Test fixture directory holding captured pytest console output samples (serial verbose and `xdist` parallel verbose runs, each with mixed passed/failed/skipped results and tracebacks) used as static parsing input for test-result extraction tests. <!--#0e57ae92201d8131|a8ab33c5d821d54c-->

### `tests/fixtures/test_output/pytest_serial_verbose.txt` (text) — A captured pytest verbose (serial, non-xdist) console output fixture with 9 collected tests spanning passed/failed/skipped outcomes, failure tracebacks, and a short summary line, used as parsing input for test-result extraction tests. <!--#db8c3f6e90c7e698|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/fixtures/test_output/pytest_xdist_verbose.txt` (text) — A captured pytest sample-output fixture showing a verbose `-v` run under `xdist` with 2 workers and `LoadGroupScheduling`, containing per-worker `[gw0]`/`[gw1]` PASSED/SKIPPED/FAILED lines, two failure tracebacks, and the `2 failed, 5 passed, 2 skipped` summary — used to exercise parsing of parallel test output. <!--#c2a8a346fbf02501|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

## `tests/fixtures/usage/` — A directory of JSONL fixture transcripts capturing representative Claude CLI, claude-interactive, Codex exec, and compat-proxy provider sessions — including multi-turn dedup, subagent, goal-unavailable, and failure/missing-usage cases — used to exercise token-usage and cost parsing/aggregation. <!--#11a307df87ee50ac|ebca70d08a91d2bf-->

### `tests/fixtures/usage/claude_goal_direct.jsonl` (text) — A test fixture JSONL transcript of a minimal Claude CLI session (`system`/`init`, one `assistant` `Edit` tool_use, and a success `result` line) carrying `usage` token counts with `cache_creation` ephemeral 5m/1h breakdowns and `total_cost_usd`, used to exercise usage/cost parsing for a direct goal run. <!--#f5f1592247be72c3|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/fixtures/usage/claude_goal_unavailable.jsonl` (text) — A two-line JSONL test fixture capturing a Claude CLI session that initializes normally and then returns an `is_error` result of "Unknown slash command: /goal", used to exercise handling of the goal command being unavailable. <!--#c6fa4d10395c224d|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/fixtures/usage/claude_interactive.jsonl` (text) — Test fixture: a three-line Claude Code session transcript (JSONL) for the claude-interactive runner — an assistant tool_use message, its user tool_result reply, and a final end_turn assistant message — each carrying `usage` fields (input/output plus cache_creation_input_tokens and cache_read_input_tokens) so token-usage parsing can be exercised against a realistic provider session. <!--#a6ea5c7905102094|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/fixtures/usage/claude_multi_turn.jsonl` (text) — A JSONL test fixture simulating a multi-turn Claude CLI stream (one init event plus three result events sharing provider_session_id `claude-session-reused`, with `claude-turn-2` duplicated) used to verify token/cost usage aggregation, per-event deduplication by `usage_event_id`, and `event_delta` usage semantics. <!--#3561417356d351f2|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/fixtures/usage/claude_print.jsonl` (text) — Test fixture holding a three-line Claude CLI print-mode JSONL transcript (system init, one assistant message, and a success result), each carrying `usage` token counts and `total_cost_usd`, used to exercise token-usage/cost parsing of non-interactive claude runs. <!--#5da0cc9fc1336f8e|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/fixtures/usage/claude_subagent.jsonl` (text) — A two-line JSONL test fixture of a Claude CLI stream (init + success result) whose result event carries a `subagents` array with per-subagent `usage_event_id`, `provider_session_id`, and token usage, used to test subagent usage extraction/aggregation. <!--#07a87f30130fd158|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/fixtures/usage/codex_exec.jsonl` (text) — A JSONL test fixture simulating a Codex CLI exec-mode event stream (thread.started, turn.started, item.completed, turn.completed) whose final turn.completed event carries token usage and cost fields, used to test parsing of Codex usage output. <!--#562d53adfb674835|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/fixtures/usage/compat_proxy.jsonl` (text) — A three-line JSONL test fixture simulating a Codex-compatible proxy session (azure-openai provider, proxy-gpt-5-codex model) with thread.started, item.completed, and turn.completed events, the last carrying input/cached/output token usage for exercising usage-parsing logic. <!--#54a1b626faad34d5|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/fixtures/usage/failure_and_missing_usage.jsonl` (text) — A JSONL test fixture simulating a provider stream of error results — one failure carrying `usage`/`total_cost_usd`, one missing `usage` entirely, and one with explicit zero usage across two `provider_session_id` values — used to exercise token-usage accounting when calls fail. <!--#9ca6f719d07f28fe|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

## `tests/frontend/` — Node-based (DOM-stubbed) test suite for the WebUI console frontend, where `test_app_pure.mjs` acts as the shared harness registering dozens of `*.test.mjs` modules that exercise `src/tianluo/server/static/app.js` — history loading/lazy detail/step windows, live streaming append and scroll anchoring, step grouping and tool/confirm chips, i18n, uploads, flow resume/end-session and other console interactions — alongside browser/real-record render harnesses (`render_in_browser.mjs`, `render_real_records.mjs`), captured `fixtures/` frame replays, and a manual `SMOKE_CHECKLIST.md`. <!--#9e2ddfd0919b4b2e|0a0335a2103d697c-->

### `tests/frontend/SMOKE_CHECKLIST.md` (markdown) — Manual smoke-test checklist for the running-flow chat WebUI, walking through environment setup and then verifying layout, reply box, conversation rendering, three-tier progressive disclosure, intervention items, CLI↔Web parity standards, specific bugfix acceptance cases, mobile-portrait horizontal-overflow behavior, and a final pytest/JS regression gate, with the last recorded automated run's results appended. <!--#632e3572a1e1189f|83ddee565222a507-->
- `Running-Flow Chat View — Manual Smoke Checklist` (heading) — Top-level title and scope statement describing the full-screen chat view under test and which backend/static files trigger a re-run of this checklist. <!--#792347f5ecc19cd2-->
  - `Setup` (heading) — Step-by-step environment setup for the smoke pass: install server, start central server and daemon, launch a flow, and open the web console. <!--#54b20d62b22c8130-->
  - `Pure-function regression` (heading) — A single check that the pure-function interaction-view test suite reports zero failures before manual testing. <!--#27e8aaa7b1ed2f88-->
  - `Layout` (heading) — Checks that the running flow renders as a full-screen view with the conversation as the main scrollable column and no legacy drawer or context-free call modal. <!--#a7f59a53399f7006-->
  - `Reply input box` (heading) — Checks the always-present bottom reply box behavior: enabled textarea, Send as the gate, pending/no-pending placeholders, and the inline Interject (✎) button. <!--#43636e585cf618e6-->
  - `Conversation rendering` (heading) — Checks that assistant/intervention records render expanded while user/system template records collapse into one-line chips classified by structured role. <!--#5b9dc5aa14172c0b-->
  - `Three-tier progressive disclosure (message paradigm)` (heading) — Checks the B1 message paradigm's layered disclosure for user/assistant turns, paradigm-named step headers, and long-payload wrapping. <!--#658af6c353d97756-->
  - `Intervention items (one per kind, default-expanded & prominent)` (heading) — Checks that each intervention kind (call, interjection, retry_decision, cli_confirm) appears as a distinct, default-expanded, visually separate item. <!--#a11676c589c0c151-->
  - `Standards 1–5 CLI ↔ Web parity (G6 acceptance)` (heading) — Step-by-step parity checks pinning that the web flow view matches CLI Rich output across five standards, each backed by named automated tests. <!--#23530143e28feba2-->
  - `Bugfix smoke (actual-render acceptance)` (heading) — Actual-render acceptance checks for two bugfixes: shorter mobile folded tool-call cards and desktop replies showing exactly once without duplication. <!--#5b4ca3ce0e03018c-->
  - `Bugfix smoke (collectJsonRegions structural robustness)` (heading) — Checks that structured-step assistant turns with literal triple backticks inside JSON content still render as prose plus a structured card, not a raw json blob. <!--#fcec8c0ef74bcad3-->
  - `Mobile portrait — horizontal overflow (≤600px)` (heading) — A manual smoke-test checklist for phone-portrait viewports (390×844 and the 320px worst case) covering the visual judgements automated tests can't make — that the running console never scrolls sideways, that ANALYZE scope rows, step-result cards, long paths, agent/model badges and structured tool names wrap instead of overflowing, that deliberate truncation (chip summary ellipsis, charter-diff internal scroll) and the History detail view still behave, and that desktop layout above 600px is unchanged. <!--#5e6105b46e4c1130-->
  - `Regression` (heading) — Checks that the full pytest suite and both frontend JS test files pass before sign-off. <!--#cdfc2d0ee842253d-->
    - `Recorded automated results (2026-05-21)` (heading) — A recorded table of the last automated test run's pass/skip counts plus a note on pre-existing out-of-scope test_steps.py failures. <!--#6b3c940aa0ca3b76-->

### `tests/frontend/adjudicate_review.test.mjs` (text) — Dual-mode (harness-registrable via `registerAdjudicateReviewTests` and standalone `node`-runnable) frontend test suite verifying that `renderAdjudicateReview` surfaces an ADJUDICATE ruling's rationale panel, a baseline→adjudicated_description before/after diff, and covered-surfaces list during a CONFIRM gate — asserting it renders null for non-adjudicate targets and degrades gracefully when fields like `baseline` are missing. <!--#48c52f512d9d44d1|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/frontend/agent_badge_live.test.mjs` (text) — A Node-stub frontend test module (Group G3) exporting registerAgentBadgeLiveTests() that drives the parent harness's app module to verify live accumulating-bubble agent/model badge behavior: the first streaming fragment with an agent_name shows a badge, a later model_name upgrades the same badge in place to "agent · model", agent rotation clears the stale model, and fragments lacking agent metadata render no badge. <!--#1e4c2bd75fbb98dd|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/frontend/compacted_record_chips.test.mjs` (text) — Node-based frontend test module exporting `registerCompactedRecordChipTests({app, check, findOne, findAll})` (loaded by `tests/frontend/test_app_pure.mjs` after its DOM stub), which builds original vs. compacted history-record fixtures and asserts that the daemon's record-budget compaction preserves chip count/order and the trailing `result` event, that `tianluo_folded_telemetry` markers render no chips, and that truncated bodies still render with the visible truncation marker — with the marker literals re-read from `src/tianluo/daemon/record_budget.py` to pin the cross-language wire contract. <!--#3af7be4fdca0563f|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/frontend/confirm_chip.test.mjs` (text) — Dual-mode Node test suite (Group G3) that exercises the web console's `kind: 'confirm'` approval-gate chip — asserting it renders 批准/打回 buttons plus an optional note textarea, POSTs a structured `{response:{approved,feedback}}` decision, and maps free-text notes onto run.py's approval/rejection token sets with a second-guess confirm for unrecognized revision requests — exporting `registerConfirmChipTests(ctx)` for the shared test_app_pure.mjs harness while also installing its own DOM/fetch stubs when run standalone. <!--#0c4dcabed1342f2d|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/frontend/discovery_analyze_scroll_anchor.test.mjs` (text) — A node-stub frontend test suite (issue #260, group G5) that pins the discovery→analyze boundary scroll-anchor fix: after a silent progression rebuild, a bottom-follower (intent flag true) sticks to the new bottom despite a frozen-DOM isNearBottom misjudge, while a genuinely scrolled-up reader (flag false) keeps their anchored bubble's viewport offset when the analyze label appends below. <!--#a101f9422df42083|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/frontend/end_session.test.mjs` (text) — A DOM-free Node.js test module that exercises the pure End-session helper functions (isFlowEndable, isWorktreeSessionPath) exported from the WebUI's app.js, asserting which flow statuses, worktree paths, and source origins make a session endable. <!--#0bd1f45061c111b4|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/frontend/file_upload.test.mjs` (text) — A registerFileUploadTests suite loaded by tests/frontend/test_app_pure.mjs that exercises the file-attachment upload feature end to end against the shared DOM stub — pure helpers (size bound, formatters, caret insert, error-code→i18n map), resolveUploadTarget/uploadRequestUrl/performUpload/startUploads, the attachment strip renderer, and the remove/cancel/clear and paste/drop/picker handlers — with a fetch recorder and fake File objects, all centred on the invariant that the textarea text is the prompt. <!--#14e980fb05763b48|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/frontend/flow_detail_stall.test.mjs` (text) — Node-based frontend test module exporting `registerFlowDetailStallTests(ctx)` (loaded by `tests/frontend/test_app_pure.mjs` against its shared DOM stub) that installs a fake per-origin connection-pool `fetch` to pin the flow-view stall defect — covering cases S1–S8: the poll's in-flight guard against stacking hung `/api/history/` bundle pulls, the deferred self-heal catch-up, request deadlines/AbortController turning hangs into the localized "Retrying…" sidebar copy, and aborts on flow switch or view close without miscounting failures. <!--#954a4ede92fc7218|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/frontend/flow_resume.test.mjs` (text) — DOM-free Node.js assertion tests that require the WebUI's `app.js` directly and verify the Resume-flow pure helpers — `RESUMABLE_STATUSES`, and `isFlowResumable` across resumable/non-resumable statuses, case-insensitive matching, `archived`/`history` source exclusion, and the authoritative `resumable` flag's precedence over the legacy heuristic (with `completed` always winning). <!--#5a8f08a9aa57d908|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/frontend/group_status.test.mjs` (text) — Node-based frontend test module (registered by test_app_pure.mjs) that verifies the WebUI's per-group DAG status markers — that normalizeRecord parses `group_status` records, groupStatusLabel maps each status to its label with sensible fallbacks, and rendering produces a single in-place `.group-status-marker` card per (step, group) showing the latest state without disturbing interleaved chat bubbles. <!--#005fbbc00ad3153b|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/frontend/history_cursor_backfill.test.mjs` (text) — Node-based frontend test module (registered by tests/frontend/test_app_pure.mjs via `registerHistoryCursorBackfillTests`) that pins the WebUI conversation head-loss repair: it exercises `stepIdFromCursorKey` and `findMissingOrdinals` against the bundle `cursor` to detect missing/surplus/unkeyable ordinals, and drives stubbed `fetch` polls to assert the client requests numbered backfill (`?missing=step:0`) and renders the recovered bubbles in the DOM. <!--#fa94bfd753403c70|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/frontend/history_flow_id.test.mjs` (text) — A frontend test module exporting `registerHistoryFlowIdTests(ctx)` for the parent app-pure harness, verifying that the history list's meta rows render a `.history-item-flow-id` span (with full-value title), that `openHistorySession` shows the complete flow_id in the dedicated `#history-detail-flow-id` line independent of the task_description title, and that `closeHistory` clears that line and hides the usage badge. <!--#2dd585095b61ec8e|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

## `tests/server/` — Pytest package for the WebUI server layer, concentrating on the history delivery pipeline — frame folding and idempotence, cursor/water-mark gap detection and incremental self-heal backfill, token/signature REST protocol semantics (full/delta/not_modified/backfill/resync), cache memory budget and eviction, compacted and interrupted drains, event-loop offload of large payloads, and static analysis of the frontend rendering contract. <!--#6c7160b1239cdeb2|5d4c5df653118204-->

### `tests/server/test_event_loop_offload.py` (python) — Event-loop responsiveness test suite for the WebUI history path, asserting that large history responses gzip on worker threads and render JSON in bounded batches (byte-identical to the inline path, capped by `HISTORY_RENDER_CONCURRENCY` and shaped under the render gate) while small idle-poll payloads stay on the cheap one-pass inline path, plus companion checks on inbound daemon frame decoding/size tripwires, once-per-payload UI fan-out serialization with unchanged ordering and scoping, and memoized usage aggregation across repeated snapshot reads. <!--#5512db419ee468e9|cf734fc8fa851d1f-->
- `_record` (function) — Builds one synthetic history record dict (step_id/step_type/ordinal/message) of a given character size, optionally carrying a usage_records entry for usage-aggregation tests. <!--#f9cde61f20ea689d-->
- `_records` (function) — Returns a list of `count` synthetic history records for a step, starting at a given ordinal. <!--#8b5bf59b9634d92e-->
- `_big_payload` (function) — Builds a full-delivery history payload large enough to trip `HISTORY_RESPONSE_OFFLOAD_RECORDS`, i.e. to take the offloaded/batched render path. <!--#0f1d294cecdc55cc-->
- `_small_payload` (function) — Builds a tiny delta-delivery history payload representing the idle-poll steady state that must stay on the inline one-pass render path. <!--#3a5e7e7a836082cb-->
- `_Req` (class) — Minimal Request stand-in exposing only the `accept-encoding` header that `_history_response` actually reads. <!--#bee346dcee96c741-->
  - `_Req.__init__` (method) — Stores the given accept-encoding value as the stub request's headers mapping. <!--#52de56ac049dee07-->
- `_thread_spy` (function) — Monkeypatches a module attribute with a pass-through wrapper that records the thread id of each call, so tests can prove where work ran. <!--#1f17a4e5020f6d52-->
- `test_big_history_response_gzips_off_the_event_loop` (function) — Asserts that gzip compression of a big history response runs on a worker thread, never on the event loop thread. <!--#fd84939e65402493-->
- `test_big_history_response_renders_json_in_batches_on_the_loop` (function) — Asserts the big-payload JSON render stays on the loop but yields repeatedly, proving it is batched rather than one uninterrupted `json.dumps`. <!--#954d1903be5a09fa-->
- `test_small_history_response_renders_in_one_pass` (function) — Asserts a small payload never invokes the chunked renderer, so the steady-state poll pays no batching machinery. <!--#21f2970b02ffe9b6-->
- `test_small_history_response_renders_inline` (function) — Asserts a small payload goes through the plain one-pass `_render_history_body` on the event loop thread. <!--#7d087970144c1104-->
- `test_loop_keeps_running_while_a_big_response_gzips` (function) — Proves non-blocking gzip by parking the stubbed compression on an event that only a loop-scheduled coroutine can set — deadlock (turned into timeout failure) if it ran on the loop. <!--#0f4fd795c84398d9-->
- `test_batched_and_inline_renders_are_byte_identical` (function) — Asserts the batched/offloaded render produces exactly the same bytes and document as the inline render of the same payload, gzipped or not. <!--#06bb3bdc222ca857-->
- `test_big_render_declares_encoding_so_gzip_middleware_passes_through` (function) — Asserts the offloaded response sets `content-encoding: gzip` and `vary: Accept-Encoding` so Starlette's GZipMiddleware stands down instead of recompressing on the loop. <!--#6299c06d02d0eb63-->
- `test_big_bundle_shaping_runs_under_the_render_gate` (function) — Regression test asserting that `summarize_history_records` shaping for a big history bundle runs while the `_history_render_gate()` semaphore is held (and is skipped for small payloads), by monkeypatching `HISTORY_RENDER_CONCURRENCY` to 1 and spying on the shaping call to record the gate's locked state. <!--#1e3a263d42fc0b55-->
- `test_a_client_that_cannot_gzip_still_gets_plain_json` (function) — Asserts a client sending `accept-encoding: identity` receives uncompressed, valid JSON with no content-encoding header. <!--#867f83732cf443bb-->
- `test_concurrent_big_renders_are_capped` (function) — Asserts concurrent offloaded renders never exceed `HISTORY_RENDER_CONCURRENCY`, bounding the transient memory a burst of console reloads can hold. <!--#5c90d77370a7f2fa-->
- `test_daemon_frames_decode_inline` (function) — Asserts inbound daemon history frames are decoded on the event loop thread (a thread hop cannot free the GIL-bound parse). <!--#7ed7fa188152125a-->
- `test_the_inbound_parse_is_bounded_at_the_daemon_side` (function) — Asserts the `LARGE_FRAME_WARN_BYTES` tripwire sits above the daemon's own `MAX_BYTES_PER_REPORT` chunk cap so it only fires on real regressions. <!--#be872d740f9915ee-->
- `test_an_oversized_frame_is_still_applied_but_logged` (function) — Asserts an oversized frame is decoded and applied normally while emitting a warning, rather than being dropped into a history hole. <!--#42770b466947a3da-->
- `test_malformed_large_frame_still_raises_protocol_error` (function) — Asserts the frame-size tripwire does not swallow or reshape a `ProtocolError` from a malformed oversized frame. <!--#93dd596a2d924ba6-->
- `_UiWS` (class) — Minimal UI WebSocket stand-in that records the exact text sent to it and can decode those frames back to dicts. <!--#74aafc8367253dac-->
  - `_UiWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the stub socket's list of sent text frames. <!--#d14bbb740fc91394-->
  - `_UiWS.send_text` (method) — Records the sent text instead of writing to a real socket. <!--#8567c66129493684-->
  - `_UiWS.frames` (method) — Returns the recorded frames parsed from JSON. <!--#f882c0c6144b2ec7-->
- `test_fan_out_serializes_one_payload_once_for_every_client` (function) — Asserts `broadcast_owned` renders a payload exactly once and sends the identical bytes to every client of the owner, instead of re-dumping per client. <!--#8ae5331333b71af9-->
- `test_fan_out_renders_each_owners_payload_separately` (function) — Asserts render de-duplication keys on payload identity, so per-owner scoped broadcasts still render and deliver distinct frames. <!--#944e098090f3cdb9-->
- `test_big_history_frame_is_rendered_in_batches_for_the_ui` (function) — Asserts a large UI fan-out frame lets the loop turn during rendering while delivering bytes identical to the one-shot render. <!--#214367568d86f04c-->
- `test_small_ui_frames_are_rendered_inline` (function) — Asserts small UI broadcast frames are rendered inline on the event loop thread with no batching. <!--#c539c7e64ef536a8-->
- `test_fan_out_order_and_scoping_are_unchanged` (function) — Non-regression check that owner and admin clients still receive history_data frames in order with intact mode/cursor/signature/pending metadata, while other owners receive nothing. <!--#173a1f481c46f9d6-->
- `_full` (function) — Helper applying a FULL-mode history frame to a `ServerState`. <!--#f5bf7cff9f5abe75-->
- `_append` (function) — Helper applying an APPEND-mode history frame to a `ServerState`. <!--#6b7ef93a14132347-->
- `_count_usage_extractions` (function) — Monkeypatches `ServerState._usage_sources_from_records` with a counting wrapper so tests can see how often usage aggregation actually runs. <!--#f4ec0dbb8a52bce5-->
- `test_usage_rebuild_is_memoized_across_repeated_snapshot_reads` (function) — Asserts repeated snapshot reads aggregate usage only once and return the same payload, keeping the costliest under-lock work off every poll. <!--#2e1b0e3823e6b40a-->
- `test_usage_memo_also_covers_a_bundle_that_carries_no_usage` (function) — Asserts the memo also caches the negative result, so a usage-free bundle is walked once and then reports `None` for free. <!--#62242f05d6968ca9-->
- `test_usage_memo_tracks_appends` (function) — Asserts appending usage-bearing records invalidates the memo so the reported totals grow instead of under-reporting the flow's cost. <!--#0ef2acd503e04d21-->
- `test_a_late_pricing_catalog_invalidates_the_usage_memo` (function) — Asserts a later-arriving project pricing catalog clears the count-keyed usage memo so costs are re-priced instead of served from the fallback estimate. <!--#c39e6d9130dcfb3f-->
- `test_usage_memo_never_leaks_onto_the_wire` (function) — Asserts no history getter exposes the underscore-prefixed memo keys stored on the bundle dict to clients. <!--#b7e69d379ceaa010-->
- `_evictable` (function) — Collapses `ServerState._HISTORY_VIEW_HOT_WINDOW` to zero so a just-read bundle is immediately eligible for eviction instead of waiting out the real 30 s window. <!--#d5d29b1570f40888-->
- `test_a_snapshot_taken_before_an_eviction_still_renders_whole` (function) — Asserts a snapshot detached under the state lock still renders all its records even after its bundle is evicted from the cache. <!--#e402db0c678aa75c-->
- `test_eviction_running_during_an_offloaded_render_does_not_break_it` (function) — Asserts an eviction executed concurrently with an in-flight worker-thread gzip still yields a complete response and a consistent cache stat. <!--#34f1c826c2091010-->
- `test_evicted_flow_rebuilds_and_renders_through_the_offload_path` (function) — End-to-end check that eviction → cache miss → full re-source → offloaded gzipped render returns the whole bundle. <!--#a5c0d3f47f79d8e8-->
- `test_delivery_semantics_survive_the_offload` (function) — Integration test over a real app/WebSocket that full → not_modified → delta delivery semantics still hold for a bundle large enough to be offloaded, with and without gzip. <!--#f95c309a323b3407-->
- `_heavy_payload` (function) — Builds a realistic few-records-but-multi-MB bundle that sits well under every record-count gate, to exercise the byte-based gates. <!--#8942a4063bb77f72-->
- `test_few_but_huge_records_still_yield_to_the_loop` (function) — Asserts the byte-budgeted batching yields at least once per record for very large records while producing bytes identical to a plain `json.dumps`. <!--#dae58c8aaa2d931c-->
- `test_batches_do_not_degenerate_to_one_record_for_small_records` (function) — Asserts adaptive batch sizing does not collapse to one record per yield for many small records, keeping the yield count far below the record count. <!--#8e8ec12396641829-->
- `_batch_sizes` (function) — Shims `json` inside the `ws` namespace to capture the rendered byte size of every record batch `dump_json_chunked` cuts, while verifying the final body is unchanged. <!--#fb19275e3865f371-->
- `test_batch_bytes_stay_within_the_budget` (function) — Parametrized check that, for both light and heavy records, each batch stays within `JSON_RENDER_BATCH_BYTES` plus one record's own size. <!--#094e86826ddf6ad4-->
- `test_multi_mb_response_under_the_record_gate_takes_the_big_path` (function) — Asserts a 10-record multi-MB reply is classified by bytes, taking the chunked render plus off-loop gzip rather than the inline small-reply path. <!--#82aeffd8dc1c78e4-->
- `test_multi_mb_ui_frame_under_the_record_gate_is_batched` (function) — Asserts the same byte gate routes a multi-MB `/ws/ui` relay frame through chunked rendering while delivering byte-identical output. <!--#fda305e30573f16b-->
- `test_records_reach_bytes_stops_walking_at_the_threshold` (function) — Asserts `records_reach_bytes` short-circuits after a handful of records once the threshold is crossed, and handles under-threshold and non-list inputs. <!--#3696507c5111729e-->
- `_cjk_payload` (function) — Builds a full-delivery bundle whose records carry CJK text, to exercise the byte estimator on non-ASCII content. <!--#c59d545ff0aca747-->
- `test_the_estimate_bounds_the_wire_and_resident_cost_of_cjk_records` (function) — Asserts `_estimate_record_bytes` over-estimates both the UTF-8 wire size and the PEP 393 resident cost of CJK records. <!--#8b29f585d3b262ac-->
- `test_cjk_bundle_under_the_record_gate_takes_the_big_path` (function) — Asserts a multi-MB CJK reply under the record-count gate still takes the chunked render and off-loop gzip path. <!--#782ac4e1883c873f-->
- `test_cjk_ui_frame_under_the_record_gate_is_batched` (function) — Asserts the byte gate also routes a multi-MB CJK `/ws/ui` relay frame through chunked rendering with identical output bytes. <!--#88d10db2bc2a5584-->

### `tests/server/test_history_append_idempotence.py` (python) — Regression suite that replays production self-heal drain windows (rejected shrinking `full` HEAD followed by overlapping `append` tails re-read from line 0) against `ServerState` to prove history frames fold idempotently by (step_id, ordinal) — no duplication, in-place content updates, genuinely new tails still appended, unnumbered records appended verbatim, usage totals never double-counted, and internal `_key_index`/`_usage_sources` bookkeeping never leaking into payloads. <!--#6a545f6fa0f646d4|cf34cca08a8add07-->
- `_record` (function) — Builds a minimal history record dict with step_id, derived step_type, ordinal, and an assistant message whose content defaults to a per-ordinal marker. <!--#3a174010c32e2f19-->
- `_usage_record` (function) — Wraps `_record` to attach a modern per-call `usage_records` entry (call_id, token counts, model) for exercising usage accounting. <!--#94141381b2a10f22-->
- `_discovery` (function) — Returns `n` sequentially-numbered discovery-step records. <!--#4585d8f19313dfef-->
- `_plan` (function) — Returns `n` sequentially-numbered plan-step records. <!--#2d18e88062b5b1c7-->
- `_confirm` (function) — Returns `n` sequentially-numbered confirm-step records. <!--#dc2688079ed1c209-->
- `_full_bundle_records` (function) — Concatenates the full discovery + plan + confirm record set that stands in for the ~148-record production bundle. <!--#9e4a8f67ad26066a-->
- `_full_cursor` (function) — Returns the per-file line cursor matching the complete bundle (discovery/plan/confirm totals). <!--#b456a85697354f99-->
- `_active_worktree_flow` (function) — Pushes a machine status update so FLOW appears as a live `--worktree` flow of MACHINE with the given status. <!--#2ab7e1dda6529cb2-->
- `_full` (function) — Test helper that applies a `full`-mode history frame to `ServerState` for FLOW/MACHINE with the given records and cursor. <!--#9aa81a7e0a8c4b37-->
- `_append` (function) — Test helper that applies an `append`-mode history frame to `ServerState`, passing the declared cursor and optional cursor_base window. <!--#9d854da047cdf343-->
- `_seed` (function) — Sets up the standard fixture state: an active worktree flow plus a full history frame carrying the whole 148-record bundle. <!--#61e45ed15db0110c-->
- `_replay_rejected_drain` (function) — Replays one production self-heal window — a short `full` HEAD that the shrinking-full guard rejects, followed by overlapping `append` tails re-read from line 0. <!--#00e9d573ad5ae417-->
- `_keys` (function) — Projects records to their (step_id, ordinal) identity tuples for order/duplication assertions. <!--#98928812425201bc-->
- `test_repeated_selfheal_drain_leaves_the_bundle_unchanged` (function) — Asserts that five repeated self-heal drains leave the bundle at 148 records with identical order, generation, and signature, and that an already-synced client still gets `not_modified`. <!--#5b4fad4ca5c43502-->
- `test_a_genuinely_new_tail_still_appends_after_repeated_drains` (function) — Guards against over-correction: after repeated drains, a genuinely new confirm tail must still append and land at the end of the bundle. <!--#31002abeeaa45c23-->
- `test_changed_content_for_a_held_ordinal_updates_in_place` (function) — Verifies a rewritten line for an already-held ordinal replaces content in place — preserving length, order, generation, and signature — and that re-delivering it is a no-op. <!--#60d3f9c82ed7ca57-->
- `test_records_without_an_ordinal_are_appended_verbatim` (function) — Confirms records lacking an ordinal or step_id cannot be identity-folded and are appended verbatim, while numbered records alongside them still de-duplicate. <!--#852067457266d218-->
- `test_usage_summary_does_not_grow_with_repeated_usage_bearing_appends` (function) — Checks that re-delivering the same usage-bearing append tail does not double-count token totals, call entries, or per-step source record counts. <!--#56bdcacbf512129e-->
- `test_key_index_is_never_serialized_into_a_payload` (function) — Asserts the internal bookkeeping fields `_key_index`, `_key_index_len`, and `_usage_sources` never leak into history, bundle-meta, or snapshot payloads. <!--#9d24e0e0bbd7d740-->

### `tests/server/test_history_backfill.py` (python) — Server-side pytest suite for the WebUI history backfill path: it seeds history bundles over the daemon WebSocket and asserts that `/api/history` parses the `missing` query param safely, serves the named lost records as a `backfill` delivery (unioned with the token's tail, de-duplicated, generation-stamped), reports unlocatable ordinals as `unfillable` instead of rebuilding, falls back to a full bundle for legacy/unnumbered or stale-token cases, and leaves existing token/signature minting and not_modified/delta/full semantics unchanged. <!--#15cb9fbeeb3a432d|346be2ce768dc175-->
- `_rec` (function) — Test helper that builds one history record dict (step_id, step_type, ordinal, and a role/content message) for seeding bundles. <!--#bc4bc3d882169c52-->
- `client_and_app` (function) — Pytest fixture yielding a logged-in TestClient plus its authenticated FastAPI app for the history HTTP/WS endpoints. <!--#c78c8fc0ec5446bd-->
- `_seed_bundle` (function) — Test helper that connects a daemon WebSocket, pushes a full history bundle for a flow, and polls /api/history until the bundle is cache-visible, returning the daemon context, socket, and first response. <!--#086019b3c5461900-->
- `test_parse_missing_param_wire_forms` (function) — Asserts parse_missing_param decodes the `step:ordinals` wire syntax, including multi-step lists, duplicate/whitespace tolerance, and `.from-<branch>` sidecar step ids. <!--#a878016c6791f36a-->
- `test_parse_missing_param_degrades_to_none` (function) — Parametrised test asserting every malformed or over-long `missing` input degrades to None rather than raising. <!--#cf22ea9f11373383-->
- `test_malformed_missing_is_not_a_500` (function) — Asserts a garbage `missing` query param is ignored (HTTP 200, ordinary not_modified semantics) rather than erroring. <!--#fea2cff5c122b2be-->
- `test_live_shape_backfill_returns_exactly_the_head` (function) — Reproduces the live head-loss shape and asserts a `missing` request returns a `backfill` delivery carrying exactly the lost head record with the standard reply keys. <!--#f849788593e31fb2-->
- `test_backfill_unions_with_the_tail_in_bundle_order` (function) — Asserts a behind-the-count token plus a missing head yields the union of the named record and the token's tail, in bundle order, with no duplicates. <!--#83e2b74b183221a2-->
- `test_missing_number_naming_a_record_in_the_tail_travels_once` (function) — Asserts naming ordinals that also fall in the token's tail does not duplicate records in the backfill reply. <!--#ac55f62cd245b197-->
- `test_unlocatable_number_is_declared_unfillable_not_rebuilt` (function) — Asserts an ordinal the bundle holds no record for is returned in `unfillable` rather than escalating to a full rebuild, so the client can retire it. <!--#75de6298731bb253-->
- `test_partially_locatable_missing_serves_what_exists` (function) — Asserts a mixed `missing` list serves the ordinals that exist and reports the rest as `unfillable`. <!--#c2fbf6e881bfc7d8-->
- `test_legacy_records_without_ordinals_are_served_by_a_full_bundle` (function) — Asserts a bundle of pre-ordinal records answers a `missing` request with a full delivery (never `unfillable`), so un-numbered records still reach the client. <!--#ad0a4c4c80d793e2-->
- `test_mixed_bundle_serves_the_unnumbered_head_via_full` (function) — Asserts a partially numbered bundle (legacy head, numbered tail) answers an ambiguous `missing` lookup with the complete bundle rather than a numbered slice. <!--#e3eac1e15d3cec87-->
- `test_every_delivery_names_its_bundle_generation` (function) — Asserts not_modified, backfill, and full deliveries all carry the same bundle `generation`, giving the client a stable per-bundle identity to scope its repair state. <!--#92d8234fc185c18b-->
- `test_stale_token_ignores_missing_and_serves_full` (function) — Asserts a forged or absent progress token makes the server ignore `missing` and fall back to a full delivery. <!--#42819458d7dbe4c8-->
- `test_token_and_signature_minting_is_unchanged_by_missing` (function) — Asserts `missing` does not alter progress-token/signature minting nor the existing not_modified / delta / full state machine across an append. <!--#aea46800577e2b12-->

### `tests/server/test_history_cache_budget.py` (python) — Test suite for the WebUI server's history-cache memory budget: byte accounting across full/append frames, occupancy stats and diagnostic reports, the eviction sweep and its protections (watched, recently-viewed, active-worktree flows), and the post-eviction cold-suppression / self-heal re-pull behaviour. <!--#96b05040286b20c8|66784230cd808adc-->
- `_record` (function) — Builds one synthetic daemon history record with a large filler payload so that a handful of them exceed a small cache budget. <!--#715130f169f423ff-->
- `_records` (function) — Generates a contiguous run of `_record` entries for a flow starting at a given ordinal. <!--#fd3660e26eab0d9c-->
- `_step_file` (function) — Maps a flow id to the `<step>.jsonl` cursor key used in history frames. <!--#e50440cab5bdb2ba-->
- `_full` (function) — Test helper that applies a `HISTORY_MODE_FULL` frame to `ServerState` with a matching cursor. <!--#073bd2617945591c-->
- `_append` (function) — Test helper that applies a `HISTORY_MODE_APPEND` frame with explicit cursor and cursor_base water marks. <!--#9cea4a8058c40a74-->
- `_register_flows` (function) — Registers the given flow ids on `MACHINE` via `update_status` so eviction policy can see their project_root and status. <!--#4edcbaf30bb515bd-->
- `_age_view` (function) — White-box helper that backdates a flow's UI-read timestamp so it falls outside the hot window without sleeping. <!--#9bf13746360fe2e7-->
- `_cached` (function) — Reads a flow's cached bundle with `touch=False` so the read does not register as UI interest. <!--#e31b44eee340f601-->
- `test_bundle_bytes_are_accounted_and_track_appends` (function) — Asserts byte accounting grows incrementally with appends and does not double-charge a re-delivered frame. <!--#e5df45d34d3fde1e-->
- `test_stats_rank_flows_by_occupancy_for_attribution` (function) — Checks `history_cache_stats` ranks flows by occupancy with record counts, machine id, and used_percent for attribution. <!--#44af4fee8464d74e-->
- `test_least_recently_viewed_flow_is_evicted_first` (function) — Verifies the sweep evicts the least recently viewed flow only, stopping as soon as the budget is met. <!--#aa828352e152fbd0-->
- `test_exactly_at_budget_does_not_evict_and_one_byte_over_does` (function) — Pins the budget boundary: exactly at budget evicts nothing, one byte over is reclaimed by the next unprotected sweep. <!--#7ac4e3685b15f600-->
- `test_single_oversized_bundle_is_evicted_when_nobody_is_watching` (function) — Confirms a lone bundle far over budget is evicted and counted in `evictions`/`evicted_bytes` when unwatched. <!--#e1d0a893ad836c9f-->
- `test_zero_budget_keeps_only_what_a_ui_client_is_reading` (function) — Under a zero budget, only the flow a UI client is actively reading stays resident so the endpoint can still answer. <!--#fb6e418bee16c428-->
- `test_watched_flow_is_never_evicted_even_over_budget` (function) — A watched flow survives the sweep even far over budget while the unwatched sibling is dropped. <!--#40e785c5e0277a85-->
- `test_active_worktree_flow_is_evicted_last` (function) — When recency cannot separate two flows, the anti-shrink guard protects the active worktree flow over a plain one. <!--#1b66af96a1e2125f-->
- `test_evicted_flow_reads_as_a_cache_miss_and_rebuilds_from_a_full_frame` (function) — An evicted flow reads as a genuine miss, is re-admitted by that read, and rebuilds from the pull's full reply. <!--#fa3eed45e9055a82-->
- `test_rebuild_after_eviction_asks_for_a_full_not_a_daemon_side_increment` (function) — After eviction a daemon-side append is refused and `plan_recovery_pull` asks for a full rebuild rather than an increment. <!--#d1d2f8abcd91b066-->
- `test_evicted_flow_is_not_re_established_by_daemon_pushes` (function) — Repeated daemon pushes to an unwatched evicted flow never re-cache it or arm a pull, preventing the eviction⇄re-pull storm. <!--#5cb01ef47779df97-->
- `test_ui_read_re_admits_a_suppressed_flow` (function) — A suppressed (cold) flow becomes cacheable again as soon as a UI client reads it. <!--#dda3e9cb06347a2a-->
- `test_a_suppressed_frame_still_reports_its_cursor_for_the_console` (function) — A suppressed frame withholds records but still surfaces `cold_suppressed` and its cursor so a displaying console can notice it is short and re-pull. <!--#21a29b37c45fb07e-->
- `test_the_cold_advisory_is_debounced_per_flow` (function) — Only the first post-eviction frame raises the cold advisory; subsequent frames in the debounce window stay silent. <!--#845fdaa35ef9641c-->
- `test_a_re_eviction_re_arms_the_advisory_immediately` (function) — A fresh eviction re-arms the cold advisory immediately, ignoring the debounce from the previous one. <!--#37f62a478734f112-->
- `test_sweep_enforces_the_budget_without_logging_a_report` (function) — `sweep_history_cache` enforces the budget on its own, evicting without emitting the periodic diagnostic log line. <!--#67ffa19255377d4e-->
- `test_maintenance_task_runs_even_when_the_report_is_disabled` (function) — Drives the app lifespan to prove `report_interval_seconds: 0` silences only the log line, leaving the budget sweep task running. <!--#672d51399875c3ee-->
- `test_cursor_gap_detection_still_arms_the_self_heal_under_a_budget` (function) — A gapped append is refused and arms the recovery pull while the existing bundle stays intact, even with budgeting active. <!--#32d07e0ff97424a9-->
- `test_progress_token_and_generation_survive_appends_under_a_budget` (function) — Delta and `not_modified` snapshot delivery keep the same generation across appends under a budget. <!--#9a2f5f0fca313b52-->
- `test_pending_window_is_memoized_but_still_tracks_the_cursor` (function) — The pending-line window is memoized across reads yet invalidated by the next append that fills the gap. <!--#8cf54605b4e865f3-->
- `test_empty_full_rejection_for_an_active_worktree_flow_survives_eviction` (function) — An empty full reply for an active worktree flow is still rejected after eviction, keeping the self-heal armed instead of caching a blank chat. <!--#26bac9c28e9a53a8-->
- `test_shrinking_full_is_still_rejected_while_the_bundle_is_resident` (function) — A full frame that shrinks a resident worktree bundle is rejected and the longer record set is retained. <!--#46bfb08b1c30fa75-->
- `test_owner_takeover_clears_the_cold_marker_it_created` (function) — Re-registering a machine under a new owner clears the cold marker so the new owner can cache its own records. <!--#568a90fdb14166e2-->
- `test_accounting_and_pending_caches_never_leak_onto_the_wire` (function) — Ensures private bundle keys (`_bytes`, `_pending`, …) are stripped from every history payload returned to clients. <!--#d9bf9f5350001c15-->
- `test_cjk_bundles_are_not_under_counted_against_the_budget` (function) — CJK text is charged at its real 2 B/char cost so the budget does not under-count zh-CN history bundles. <!--#5de6ebcd9b4a8aa8-->
- `test_threshold_report_names_the_biggest_flows` (function) — Crossing the report threshold logs a `reason=threshold` history-cache report naming the largest flows. <!--#4644b17e4694817c-->
- `test_eviction_is_logged_with_the_flow_it_dropped` (function) — Each eviction emits an INFO log identifying the dropped flow. <!--#e7d01d345c60d63b-->
- `test_periodic_report_is_emitted_even_with_an_empty_cache` (function) — The periodic `reason=periodic` report is logged even when nothing is cached. <!--#89d5a41ae286d28b-->
- `test_server_config_history_cache_defaults_and_parsing` (function) — Covers `HistoryCacheConfig` defaults and parsing, including 0 as meaningful and negative/non-numeric values falling back to the default. <!--#9ec3241810803c04-->
- `test_yaml_budget_reaches_the_running_servers_state` (function) — End-to-end config wiring: a YAML `budget_mb` flows through `ServerConfig.load` and `create_app` into the live `ServerState`. <!--#dd88b4e4a85a2bb1-->
- `test_history_body_render_round_trips_and_gzips` (function) — `_render_history_body` round-trips payloads as JSON on both the plain and gzip paths. <!--#6aa8e7d04c3ac2cb-->
- `test_history_endpoint_serves_json_through_the_offloaded_renderer` (function) — End-to-end check that `/api/history/{flow}` returns valid JSON through the offloaded renderer for both render paths. <!--#647183bad2fd4bfd-->
- `_receive_until` (function) — Reads daemon websocket frames until the wanted message type, skipping expected background broadcasts. <!--#7b154efa085f0a6a-->
- `test_evicted_flow_is_re_sourced_through_the_real_cache_miss_pull` (function) — Full end-to-end contract: an evicted bundle's REST read triggers a cursorless full pull to the owning daemon that reinstates the whole conversation. <!--#75230c0a83af6be0-->

### `tests/server/test_history_compacted_delivery.py` (python) — End-to-end test module that drains a step JSONL containing one ~16 MB oversized assistant record through a real `DaemonHistoryReader` and replays the frames into a real `ServerState`, asserting compacted delivery stays gap-free, duplicate-free, monotonic, within `MAX_RECORD_RAW_JSON_BYTES` with all tool_use chips preserved, and byte-identical for small records. <!--#f0a60a2e9b772ae3|92a63a38eed98f45-->
- `_thinking_event` (function) — Test helper building a single `system`/`thinking_tokens` raw_json event whose token estimate and uuid are derived from the given index. <!--#c41a91898403980f-->
- `_chip_events` (function) — Test helper returning a matched assistant `tool_use` / user `tool_result` event pair (a "chip") with an index-derived `toolu_%04d` id and the supplied result body. <!--#51a838f0a10fac97-->
- `_oversized_record` (function) — Test helper assembling a ~16 MB assistant history record from hundreds of thinking events plus tool-use chips and a trailing `result` event, used to force record compaction. <!--#9d1aa352a50fdc13-->
- `_small_record` (function) — Test helper producing an ordinary multi-KB assistant history record that should pass through delivery untouched. <!--#aea869d4ff21ec10-->
- `drained_frames` (function) — Session fixture that writes a step JSONL file containing one oversized record among small ones, then drains it through a real `DaemonHistoryReader` and returns every emitted frame. <!--#ae86a7837b3646cf-->
- `_replay` (function) — Async helper that registers the flow on a real `ServerState` and feeds it the drained frames exactly as the daemon relay would, returning the state and per-frame outcomes. <!--#7875928831011c29-->
- `test_compacted_frames_assemble_without_gaps_or_duplicates` (function) — Asserts the replayed bundle contains every physical line exactly once with contiguous ordinals. <!--#63d82ba61671d729-->
- `test_every_frame_is_accepted_as_authoritative` (function) — Asserts every frame in the drain resolves its pull and none is rejected by the server's continuity guard. <!--#2859905a9e376c3c-->
- `test_head_loss_and_gap_selfheal_are_never_triggered` (function) — Negative test confirming no recovery pull is armed during the drain, since no bundle-level cap was introduced. <!--#a4c992b7c174ea99-->
- `test_cursor_advances_monotonically_across_the_drain` (function) — Asserts the per-file cursor never moves backwards, reaches the total line count, and matches the bundle's final cursor. <!--#5d8bff5be859a3d4-->
- `test_bundled_oversized_record_is_within_budget_with_all_chips` (function) — Asserts the compacted oversized record fits `MAX_RECORD_RAW_JSON_BYTES` while retaining all 206 tool_use chips in order and its trailing `result` event. <!--#f0925c36a81b4041-->
- `test_small_records_reach_the_bundle_unmodified` (function) — Asserts an under-budget record arrives in the server bundle byte-identical to what was written. <!--#c20e9157e19afd25-->

### `tests/server/test_history_cursor_base_coverage.py` (python) — Regression tests for the `ServerState` history cursor/`cursor_base` gap logic (issue #287), covering skipped blank lines, windows starting past the water mark, advanced files with no declared read window, overlapping re-sends, and an end-to-end run of the real `DaemonHistoryReader` feeding a real `ServerState`. <!--#03268e0768535715|50bbe1cbe0cc187b-->
- `_record` (function) — Test helper that builds a minimal discovery-step history record dict with the given ordinal and a matching assistant message. <!--#5d09d7ad027e7090-->
- `_running_flow` (function) — An async test helper that registers a single 'running' flow (FLOW on MACHINE) into a ServerState via update_status, seeding the state so subsequent history frames have a flow to attach to. <!--#41e613df51935595-->
- `_seed_bundle` (function) — Async test helper that seeds an authoritative history bundle via a `HISTORY_MODE_FULL` frame of *lines* records, establishing the step file's cursor water mark. <!--#5163c745e198ecb5-->
- `_append` (function) — Async test helper that applies a `HISTORY_MODE_APPEND` frame with explicit `cursor`/`cursor_base` and returns the resulting outcome. <!--#3cad69aa7d9b6928-->
- `test_append_that_skipped_a_line_is_contiguous_and_applies` (function) — Asserts an append whose declared window starts exactly at the water mark applies to the bundle even though its record count is short of the cursor advance (a skipped/blank line), and arms no recovery pull. <!--#14bf90375635296f-->
- `test_append_whose_window_starts_past_the_water_mark_is_still_a_gap` (function) — Asserts an append whose declared `cursor_base` starts past the water mark is rejected as a gap — neither records nor cursor are adopted — and arms a recovery pull. <!--#2debb764fbb24ec3-->
- `test_advanced_file_with_no_declared_window_is_a_gap` (function) — Asserts a frame that advances another step file's cursor without declaring a read window for it is judged a gap (the #287 root shape) rather than silently adopted. <!--#5768b386b9e2cf6b-->
- `test_overlapping_resend_window_still_applies` (function) — Asserts a window starting before the water mark is treated as a harmless re-send that still applies and arms no recovery pull. <!--#b723ac982be033ff-->
- `test_real_daemon_delta_over_a_blank_line_reaches_the_bundle` (function) — An end-to-end regression test driving the real DaemonHistoryReader over a step file that gains a blank line mid-stream and feeding its frames to a real ServerState, asserting that the delta (2 records but cursor advanced by 3) is anchored by cursor_base rather than record count so it lands in the history bundle without triggering a recovery pull. <!--#7350bbb196feba5e-->

### `tests/server/test_history_endpoint_signature.py` (python) — Endpoint-level test suite for the WebUI history REST API, exercising the token/signature delivery protocol (full / not_modified / delta, stale-token fallback), gzip thresholds, full-pull throttling, ADD-only self-heal reconcile for paused worktree flows (#287) plus its blast-radius guards, and usage-payload relay or reconstruction in the detail response. <!--#45ba04f8b0e3837e|966b1e8ff001fba5-->
- `client_and_app` (function) — Pytest fixture that builds an authenticated FastAPI app, logs in a TestClient, and yields the (client, app) pair for the endpoint tests. <!--#c78c8fc0ec5446bd-->
- `_seed_bundle` (function) — Test helper that connects a daemon over WebSocket, pushes a full history bundle for a flow, and polls the REST endpoint until that bundle is visible via the cache-hit path, returning the live daemon socket plus the first response. <!--#488fa951cec311a3-->
- `test_full_then_not_modified_then_delta` (function) — End-to-end test driving the history REST endpoint through its three delivery states — full (token+signature issued), not_modified (echoed token+sig), and delta (only the appended tail after the daemon adds a record). <!--#b1d101e5c8acc101-->
- `test_stale_token_falls_back_to_full` (function) — Test that a garbage/unvalidatable token+signature makes the endpoint fall back to a full rebuild carrying the complete bundle rather than a slice. <!--#24419869a9dd8a20-->
- `test_full_bundle_response_is_gzipped` (function) — Test that a full bundle exceeding the gzip size floor is served with Content-Encoding: gzip when the client accepts it. <!--#4708c6ab30265bd3-->
- `test_small_reply_is_not_gzipped` (function) — Test that a tiny not_modified reply stays below the gzip size floor and is left uncompressed. <!--#36d1b2a29ad69228-->
- `test_full_pull_throttle_rate_limits_repeated_misses` (function) — Async ServerState unit test verifying full_pull_throttled/mark_full_pull rate-limiting: a just-marked pull is throttled within the floor window, a zero window never throttles, and other flows are unaffected. <!--#af4149617b098746-->
- `_ReconcileDaemon` (class) — Test helper that impersonates a connected daemon over a real `/ws` WebSocket, serving `MSG_HISTORY_REQUEST` pulls from a background thread (so the server's self-heal reconcile can complete inside a blocking `TestClient.get`) while counting requests and letting tests dictate the reply payload. <!--#5ed72bd4e78a5707-->
  - `_ReconcileDaemon.__init__` (method) — Opens an authenticated daemon WebSocket, consumes the WELCOME frame, and starts the daemon-side serving thread with an empty canned reply set and a zeroed request counter. <!--#095295df4a2a356e-->
  - `_ReconcileDaemon._serve` (method) — Background loop that reads incoming frames and answers each `MSG_HISTORY_REQUEST` with a `HISTORY_MODE_FULL` data frame carrying the test-configured `reply_records`, bumping the request count. <!--#503798fbb3eec917-->
  - `_ReconcileDaemon.push_full` (method) — Unprompted daemon push of a `HISTORY_MODE_FULL` history-data frame for the flow, simulating the live history broadcast. <!--#146c60cf9dd13410-->
  - `_ReconcileDaemon.report_flow` (method) — Sends a status update registering the flow with a given status and project root, so the server sees it as worktree/non-worktree and running/paused. <!--#164efebd83cbec7f-->
  - `_ReconcileDaemon.seed` (method) — Pushes records and polls `/api/history/{flow_id}` until the server-side cache serves them, returning the cached bundle (or failing if it never appears). <!--#9e18e83eb903ecf6-->
  - `_ReconcileDaemon.close` (method) — Stops the serving thread and closes the daemon WebSocket context. <!--#8425f1499b69c7eb-->
- `test_paused_worktree_reconcile_record_count_never_decreases` (function) — Regression test for #287 asserting the paused-worktree self-heal reconcile is ADD-only at the endpoint boundary: empty or truncated daemon replies must never be served as a `full` rebuild that blanks or shrinks the cached bundle, while a longer reply is still applied. <!--#97e4486b0146a653-->
- `test_non_worktree_flow_is_served_from_cache_without_any_daemon_pull` (function) — Blast-radius guard that a running non-worktree flow never triggers a `MSG_HISTORY_REQUEST` pull and keeps its ordinary `not_modified`/`full` cache-served delivery behaviour. <!--#2cb44ab26b2ea0b7-->
- `test_paused_non_worktree_flow_never_reconciles` (function) — Blast-radius guard that `paused` status alone does not open the self-heal gate: a paused non-worktree flow is still served purely from cache with zero daemon pulls. <!--#b94dc12019c7133c-->
- `test_signature_moves_with_record_count` (function) — Unit test that bundle_signature acts as a content-version stamp — stable for identical state but changing when the record count or generation changes. <!--#957941fed00fb82c-->
- `test_not_modified_requires_a_signature` (function) — State-level test that not_modified is opt-in: an echoed token with a matching signature yields not_modified, while the same token without a signature degrades to a backward-compatible empty delta. <!--#79e7169a88e59d49-->
- `test_history_detail_carries_daemon_usage_payload` (function) — Verifies that when a daemon pushes a full HISTORY_DATA frame carrying an explicit `usage` payload over `/ws`, the `/api/history/{flow_id}` detail response relays that payload back verbatim once the bundle is cache-visible. <!--#d66497ba9918c661-->
- `test_history_detail_rebuilds_usage_from_cached_records` (function) — Verifies that when a full HISTORY_DATA frame arrives without a `usage` payload, the `/api/history/{flow_id}` detail reconstructs usage from the records' embedded `usage_records` via the shared backend, yielding `completeness == "complete"` with correct token totals and per-call entries. <!--#34d6d39576f32c5a-->

### `tests/server/test_history_expired_sig_recovery.py` (python) — Server-side regression tests (Defect-C) proving that WebUI history/flow polling with a stale, expired, or generation-rotated signed cursor recovers as a 200 `resync=True` full bundle rather than 401-ing, while genuinely unauthenticated requests still fail-closed with 401 and cross-owner reads still return 404 — using helpers that seed daemon-pushed FULL history bundles over `/ws` and poll the cache until visible. <!--#92568f75e9013ba2|b0b47fff3c968276-->

- `_seed_bundle` (function) — Helper that connects a daemon over `/ws`, pushes a FULL history bundle for a flow, and polls `/api/history/{flow_id}` until the bundle becomes cache-visible, returning the daemon context, socket, and first response body. <!--#35391c3310fa3263-->
- `_push_full` (function) — Helper that pushes a replacing FULL history frame over the daemon socket and polls until the flow's generation counter rotates, returning the new response body. <!--#a3370c67c92f8098-->

- `test_first_load_full_is_not_a_resync` (function) — Asserts that an initial `after`-less full history load reports `delivery=full` with `resync=False` while still carrying the authoritative resync inputs (progress, signature, positive generation). <!--#c5d5b8a97c34df4b-->
- `test_stale_signed_cursor_never_401_recovers_with_resync` (function) — Core Defect-C test asserting that a garbage/expired signed cursor with a valid owner cookie returns 200 (never 401) as a recoverable full flagged `resync=True` carrying the full records and fresh cursor. <!--#987070c8a4f07f00-->
- `test_rotated_generation_token_recovers_with_resync` (function) — Asserts that a once-valid token whose bundle generation has since rotated recovers as a 200 resync full (not 401) and re-adopting the fresh cursor settles back to the cheap `not_modified` path. <!--#cc7e2f08f611baeb-->
- `test_owner_polling_through_rotation_storm_never_401` (function) — Simulates a ~40s reconnect storm where the daemon repeatedly re-pushes fuller bundles, asserting the owner's polls with the pre-rotation cursor always return 200 resync fulls and self-heal to the fresh cursor each round. <!--#89b7da0f9fd11d06-->
- `test_flow_detail_owner_polling_never_401` (function) — Asserts `GET /api/flows/{id}` for a logged-in owner returns 404 for an unknown flow (never 401), proving auth isn't coupled to flow lookup. <!--#c354e48aa0a96372-->
- `test_unauthenticated_still_401` (function) — Asserts that genuinely unauthenticated requests still 401 (fail-closed) on both `/api/history` and `/api/flows` routes even when a would-be signed cursor is present. <!--#62543d1314547b3d-->
- `test_cross_owner_still_404` (function) — Asserts that a different owner (`bob`) reading another owner's flow reads as absent (404) — with or without a signed cursor — confirming owner scoping is not weakened by the resync path. <!--#8b05630cf1543575-->

### `tests/server/test_history_gap_recovery.py` (python) — Regression suite driving ServerState.apply_history_frame directly to lock the server's history bundle against head truncation: it asserts that an empty `full` frame on an active worktree flow with no cached bundle is rejected (arming exactly one self-heal recovery pull) while ordinary flows still accept genuinely empty fulls, that `append` frames whose per-step-file cursor does not continue the bundle's water mark are refused wholesale and healed by the following full, and that contiguous/overlapping appends still apply cleanly. <!--#29875bb416b6e690|8a22d8c656687575-->

- `_append` (function) — Async helper that pushes an `append` history frame with the given records and cursor into ServerState.apply_history_frame. <!--#0ba4df01a12c5a76-->
- `test_empty_full_on_empty_cache_is_rejected_and_keeps_selfheal_armed` (function) — Asserts an empty `full` on an active worktree flow with no cached bundle is rejected (no bundle, no pull resolution), leaves the recovery pull armed exactly once, and that the daemon's next resolved full heals the flow. <!--#bd5e2ff4a51c1aa5-->
- `test_empty_full_on_ordinary_flow_still_establishes_a_bundle` (function) — Asserts the empty-full guard is scoped to active worktree flows: an ordinary/terminal flow's genuinely empty full is still cached as an empty bundle and resolves the pull. <!--#0e71f18efee1742b-->
- `test_gapped_append_on_existing_bundle_is_refused_and_heals` (function) — Asserts an append whose cursor jumps past the bundle's water mark is discarded whole (records and cursor untouched), arms exactly one recovery pull across repeated gapped frames, and is healed by the following full. <!--#85a72815a9aaff30-->
- `test_nonzero_start_append_on_empty_bundle_is_refused` (function) — Asserts a first append starting at a nonzero line on a legitimately empty bundle is refused rather than extending onto nothing, arming the recovery pull whose full reply then rebuilds the history from line 0. <!--#fa5ef75ce32d60dc-->
- `test_gap_in_any_one_file_refuses_the_whole_frame` (function) — Asserts per-step-file water marks are checked independently, so a frame contiguous on one step file but gapped on another is refused in its entirety and arms the recovery pull. <!--#a52829f50f29bbd2-->
- `test_contiguous_and_overlapping_appends_apply` (function) — Parametrized happy path: appends that continue or overlap the bundle's water mark are applied, resolve the pull, produce the expected ordinals, and arm no recovery pull. <!--#eaaf70e425926000-->
- `test_timeline_empty_full_then_appends_still_serves_a_complete_history` (function) — End-to-end regression of the observed live failure: an unresolved empty full followed by later appends leaves no bundle, the self-heal fires once, and the resolved full then serves every client the complete history from line 0 with the live stream resuming. <!--#f6f001d230cb6baf-->

### `tests/server/test_history_incremental_backfill.py` (python) — Regression-lock test module that drives ServerState.plan_recovery_pull and the ws.py _handle_message seam to prove a reconnect-gap self-heal backfills history incrementally from the server's own water mark (monotonic, hole-free, convergent) rather than looping through cursorless full rebuilds, while still reserving a cursorless full for the no-bundle, machine-change, and active-worktree-flow cases. <!--#98a877368a0727ee|897cd1fbd5a63232-->

- `test_incremental_backfill_is_monotonic_non_decreasing` (function) — Test that across three successive reconnect-gap→plan→append cycles the bundle's record count is monotonic non-decreasing ([5, 8, 12, 15]). <!--#953665d5a6418460-->
- `test_truncated_backfill_leaves_no_hole_and_resumes_from_new_mark` (function) — Test that a backfill drain truncated by a disconnect leaves no hole or regression and the next self-heal resumes incrementally from the new water mark until it converges, never a cursorless full. <!--#96c69a51d626c101-->
- `test_racing_push_rearm_does_not_void_anchored_backfill` (function) — Test that a stale live push re-arming requires_full cannot discard a backfill anchored exactly at the server's water mark, which is still accepted and grows the bundle without a TTL stall. <!--#abaf1cebf9aea01f-->

- `test_plan_recovery_pull_full_for_active_worktree_flow` (function) — Test that an active worktree flow (history split across roots) always plans a cursorless full to reunite the discovery slice with later worktree steps. <!--#3c134d89705233ab-->
- `test_plan_recovery_pull_none_when_not_flagged_or_inflight` (function) — Test that a healthy flow plans nothing and that the in-flight marker—not the requires_full flag—is what dedups a rival recovery pull within the TTL. <!--#d4d610a5ace65406-->
