### `tests/server/test_history_interrupted_drain.py` (python) — Test suite covering interrupted history drains — using a 4324-record/147-frame sample flow, cuttable fake daemon legs, and a threaded `_InterruptibleDaemon` over a real `TestClient`, it asserts that a reply cut mid-delivery is reported `incomplete` by both WS bundle-meta and REST poll, arms exactly one add-only repair pull anchored at the server's water mark (including the stall-grace backstop and the old-daemon chunk-bound heuristic), and that races, rejected frames, later live appends, evictions, and `missing=`-directed backfills can neither falsely settle it nor spend its repair budget. <!--#1be3038012e08f39|90330eaffac3893f-->
- `_flat_records` (function) — Builds the sample flow's full record list (4324 records across the `_SHAPE` steps) in the order the daemon would read them. <!--#d22e3c995f67e4c7-->
- `_frames` (function) — Splits the sample records into the 147 wire frames of one pull reply, each carrying `cursor`/`cursor_base` and padded/`final=False` so the fixture exercises both the chunk-bound heuristic and the explicit `final` bit. <!--#710d57071d61b30c-->
- `_encode` (function) — Encodes one fixture frame as a `HISTORY_DATA` wire message, with `declare_final=False` modelling a pre-`final` daemon. <!--#64477430b4f7bbe6-->
- `scaled_chunk_bound` (function) — Fixture that monkeypatches `ws_module.MAX_BYTES_PER_REPORT` down to the fixture's chunk size so padded frames register as chunk-bounded. <!--#2127eb230e04980b-->
- `_CuttableLeg` (class) — A fake daemon websocket that replays a fixed list of frames and then raises on the next read, modelling a 1011 keepalive close mid-reply. <!--#1041194318b0c407-->
  - `_CuttableLeg.__init__` (method) — Stores the frame texts to replay and initialises the read index. <!--#5853108bd528e794-->
  - `_CuttableLeg.receive_text` (method) — Returns the next queued frame, or raises `RuntimeError` once exhausted to simulate the socket dying mid-reply. <!--#72f3248e3512b548-->
  - `_CuttableLeg.send_text` (method) — No-op sink for anything the server sends back to the fake daemon. <!--#12b0c285a50b35a1-->
  - `_CuttableLeg.close` (method) — No-op close so the leg satisfies the socket interface. <!--#49003e716cdb749e-->
- `_feed` (function) — Replays the given frame texts through the real daemon receive loop against a fresh manager/hub/registry and lets the connection die at the end. <!--#22b1579f1a7400cd-->
- `_state_with_pull` (function) — Builds a `ServerState` with the test machine registered and a history replay (pull) already armed for the sample flow. <!--#b2e854ca3ad69980-->
- `test_cut_drain_leaves_a_prefix_that_admits_it_is_one` (function) — Asserts a drain cut mid-reply leaves an internally self-consistent prefix (cursor matches, no pending, poll says not_modified) yet the bundle and its resync still report `incomplete=True`. <!--#1d4fe76b1b8006f8-->
- `test_a_completed_delivery_is_settled` (function) — Checks the `incomplete` flag is not vacuous — a reply run to its declared end clears it and yields all 4324 records, while a cut reply leaves it set. <!--#f6d39f685a28f96c-->
- `test_push_and_poll_agree_about_completeness` (function) — Verifies the WS bundle-meta advisory and the REST snapshot report the same `incomplete` bit and the same cursor. <!--#ff9cd65a7d7f35fb-->
- `test_old_daemon_without_the_bit_still_detects_a_cut_reply` (function) — Confirms the declared degradation path: with frames that never declare `final`, the chunk-bound heuristic alone still flags a cut reply and clears on a whole one. <!--#86e3e510e25b06f5-->
- `test_a_live_append_does_not_settle_a_drain_it_raced` (function) — Ensures a `final=True` live append that overtook a pull's dispatch cannot mark the pull reply it raced as complete. <!--#e4bfdab548230ee6-->
- `_apply_frame` (function) — Applies one frame through the exact `apply_history_frame` + `take_history_replay_verdict` pair that `ws.py` uses, returning both results. <!--#10d3313a32d03b06-->
- `test_frames_the_cache_refused_cannot_settle_the_delivery` (function) — Asserts gapped frames the cache rejects cannot clear the incomplete marker or the pending repair, no matter what completeness bits their sender declared. <!--#942b8394a4096b5f-->
- `test_a_later_live_append_cannot_settle_a_dead_delivery` (function) — Asserts an ordinary post-reconnect `final=True` append leaves the interrupted delivery still incomplete and its repair still due. <!--#8bef8c60c581645f-->
- `test_socket_death_arms_an_incremental_repair` (function) — Checks that the disconnect arms an add-only repair plan anchored at the server's own water mark, and that a second immediate poll does not stack another pull. <!--#d1978d6a8d754084-->
- `test_a_delivery_still_arriving_is_not_repaired` (function) — Verifies a drain that is unfinished but still alive is marked incomplete without becoming repair-due, so no rival pull is dispatched. <!--#d1872b214aa843a9-->
- `test_a_quiet_delivery_repairs_after_the_grace` (function) — Checks the time-based backstop: aging a live delivery's `last_frame_at` past the stall grace makes the repair due even with no disconnect. <!--#0498ad3ba7d46e74-->
- `test_asking_whether_to_repair_does_not_freeze_a_live_flow` (function) — Asserts `history_delivery_repair_due` is a pure query — merely asking must not latch `requires_full` and start discarding subsequent live appends. <!--#e4af09a0bb8e2ad1-->
- `test_an_evicted_flow_is_not_repaired` (function) — Confirms a bundle the cache budget just evicted is neither reported incomplete nor scheduled for repair, avoiding an eviction/re-pull storm. <!--#a63866c3659cff47-->
- `_InterruptibleDaemon` (class) — A threaded fake daemon over a real `TestClient` websocket that answers the first `HISTORY_REQUEST` with a prefix, drops the socket, reconnects, and serves the remainder from the server's water mark on the repair pull. <!--#4607e8af5d125d69-->
  - `_InterruptibleDaemon.__init__` (method) — Stores the client/app/frames and cut point, creates the cut/repaired/stop events, and opens the first connection. <!--#d63a1b506c415f4e-->
  - `_InterruptibleDaemon._connect` (method) — Opens a `/ws` session, completes the hello/WELCOME handshake, publishes a status update advertising the flow as `completed`, and starts the serve thread. <!--#87620d868d4979c1-->
  - `_InterruptibleDaemon._serve` (method) — Serve loop that records each pull's cursor, cuts the first reply after `cut_after` frames and reconnects, then asserts the repair pull is anchored at the water mark and sends the remaining frames. <!--#77b5c8c42a20fefd-->
  - `_InterruptibleDaemon._reconnect` (method) — Tears down the current websocket context and reopens a fresh connection unless the daemon is stopping. <!--#80e620e59ff6bec5-->
  - `_InterruptibleDaemon.close` (method) — Signals the serve thread to stop and closes the websocket context, ignoring teardown errors. <!--#b15474006baae592-->
- `test_completed_flow_repairs_its_cut_drain_through_the_poll` (function) — End-to-end acceptance over the HTTP API: a completed flow's cut drain is repaired through ordinary polling until all 4324 records land, having admitted `incomplete`, using exactly one repair pull, and then going quiet once settled. <!--#f06d72dc9612c11d-->
- `test_a_missing_backfill_never_spends_the_repair_budget` (function) — Asserts `missing=`-directed backfill reads are served from the cache without dispatching a pull or consuming the full-pull throttle the genuine repair depends on. <!--#15ba337a84b7602e-->

### `tests/server/test_history_lazy_detail.py` (python) — Test suite for the lazy tool-call detail path on the server→browser history leg — it covers `summarize_history_records`/`locate_record_detail` shaping (stripping `tool_detail` and eliding `raw_json` bodies while keeping collapsed-chip headers byte-identical, exempting failed and fold-visible calls), the `GET /api/history/{flow_id}/detail` endpoint (auth, 404/503, daemon re-pull, multi-frame recovery), WebSocket replay/live-append shaping, and the payload-size and detail-version invariants. <!--#4ed1598dde13e067|e3b0c44298fc1c14-->

### `tests/server/test_history_pending_vs_unfillable.py` (python) — A ServerState-level test module that pins the distinction between history-cursor gaps that are `pending` (declared-but-not-yet-streamed trailing ordinals the client keeps waiting on) versus `unfillable` (proven interior holes the daemon stepped over), verifying `_bundle_pending_positions` classification, that both keys ride every reply shape (not_modified/full/backfill) across poll, WS push, and REST, and that pending converges to empty as append frames arrive (the livelock cure). <!--#c59a9842c3d276d4|744560948e46a79e-->
- `_record` (function) — Test helper that builds a single daemon history record (an ``implement`` step message) tagged with the given physical line ``ordinal``. <!--#d8dd96aa78417600-->
- `_seed` (function) — Async helper that establishes an authoritative full-mode history bundle on a ServerState whose cursor may declare more lines than the frame actually delivered. <!--#6aea3c48b362f1c7-->
- `_token` (function) — Async helper that fetches the current bundle's in-sync progress token and signature via ``get_history_snapshot``. <!--#f3f0ea77c15e15e3-->
- `_snap` (function) — Async helper that requests a history snapshot ``after`` a token, optionally naming ``missing`` ordinals to backfill. <!--#48f323f89a789e1b-->
- `test_pending_is_the_trailing_declared_but_unsent_window` (function) — Asserts ``_bundle_pending_positions`` names the trailing ordinals a cursor declares but no record has yet delivered (3,4,5) as pending. <!--#5384436aff2e91fc-->
- `test_interior_blank_hole_is_not_pending` (function) — Verifies a gap below the highest delivered ordinal (a blank line stepped over) is treated as a proven hole, never pending. <!--#7477b51ebb2f8b7d-->
- `test_step_with_no_records_yet_is_wholly_pending` (function) — Verifies that when the cursor declares a file but no record has arrived, the entire declared range is reported pending. <!--#37d01032c074f1ba-->
- `test_full_bundle_without_a_cursor_names_nothing_pending` (function) — Verifies a full frame with no cursor yields empty pending, preserving pre-existing behaviour. <!--#e6659cf59900807e-->
- `test_unnumbered_step_is_skipped_not_claimed_pending` (function) — Verifies a step containing an un-numbered (legacy) record is skipped rather than claimed pending, since it isn't soundly ordinal-addressable. <!--#2a5fef1f815c43f8-->
- `test_pending_gap_returns_pending_and_empty_unfillable` (function) — End-to-end test that a backfill request for trailing undelivered ordinals returns them as pending with no records and no unfillable. <!--#e86e5d280c543f1a-->
- `test_interior_hole_is_unfillable_with_empty_pending` (function) — End-to-end test that a backfill request for a proven interior hole returns it as unfillable with empty pending. <!--#3ff601b156733c9c-->
- `test_backfill_and_pending_coexist_in_one_reply` (function) — End-to-end test that one request mixing a held ordinal, an interior blank, and a pending tail routes each to served/unfillable/pending respectively. <!--#e1719498bff52564-->
- `test_pending_converges_to_empty_as_records_arrive` (function) — End-to-end test (the livelock cure) that the pending set shrinks monotonically and empties as append frames deliver the trailing window. <!--#b3b47ab5ec0603e6-->
- `test_pending_is_present_on_every_delivery` (function) — Verifies the ``pending`` key (like ``unfillable``) rides every reply shape — not_modified, full, and backfill — so the client never branches on its presence. <!--#cf58b9b068f3966c-->
- `test_push_meta_reports_the_same_pending_as_the_poll` (function) — Verifies the WS push source (``get_history_bundle_meta``) and REST poll (``get_history_snapshot``) report identical pending sets from one bundle. <!--#7f7f215abc96d49a-->
- `test_rest_reply_carries_pending_key` (function) — Integration test via TestClient/WebSocket that the ``/api/history`` REST route spreads the snapshot so ``pending`` (and ``unfillable``) reach the JSON body. <!--#78f14cba00d0f6cb-->

### `tests/server/test_history_push_cursor.py` (python) — Server-side tests that drive fake UI/daemon WebSockets through `ServerState`/`UiHub` history pushes to verify that `history_data` frames carry the correct post-append cursor, signature and usage payload (relayed, rebuilt, or omitted), and that unanchored, gapped, suppressed or cache-evicted appends are never broadcast as records but instead trigger a daemon self-heal pull or an owner-scoped `history_cursor` advisory marked `incomplete`. <!--#d6d6b2b3ad383bc2|b441e2321960e5b5-->
- `_rec` (function) — Test helper that builds a single history record dict (step_id/step_type/ordinal plus a role/content message) for the fixture conversations. <!--#abc17151b02f7151-->
- `_UiWS` (class) — Fake UI WebSocket that records every frame the server sends it, decoded from JSON, with a helper to filter frames by type. <!--#f2d21712b7cecf70-->
  - `_UiWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the stand-in with an empty list of received frames. <!--#d14bbb740fc91394-->
  - `_UiWS.send_text` (method) — Captures an outbound frame by decoding its JSON and appending it to the recorded list. <!--#015e8192c9e42ee8-->
  - `_UiWS.frames` (method) — Returns the recorded frames whose `type` matches the given frame type. <!--#19c4724e0fc3abac-->
- `_DaemonWS` (class) — Fake daemon WebSocket that decodes what the server pushes and records the payloads of any `MSG_HISTORY_REQUEST` (self-heal pull) messages. <!--#a08a8f46de93b0ed-->
  - `_DaemonWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the daemon stand-in with an empty list of captured history requests. <!--#b21109e749814b4e-->
  - `_DaemonWS.send_text` (method) — Decodes an outbound protocol message and records its payload if it is a history request. <!--#cd0b216a9707ca53-->
- `_setup` (function) — Async fixture helper that builds a `ServerState` with one registered machine, a `UiHub` with a registered fake UI client, and a fresh `HistoryRequestRegistry`. <!--#1398b0b010ad0944-->
- `_msg` (function) — Test helper that builds a `history_data` protocol message for flow `f1` with the given mode, records, cursor/cursor_base and optional usage payload. <!--#ca4085ad5c468927-->
- `test_full_frame_carries_cursor_and_signature` (function) — Asserts a pushed full-history frame carries the same cursor and signature the REST snapshot would report at that instant. <!--#41e70af5457d72c1-->
- `test_append_frame_carries_cursor_after_the_append` (function) — Asserts an append frame relayed to the UI carries the post-append cursor and the snapshot's signature, not the pre-append state. <!--#45ae998cc565a5c2-->
- `test_full_frame_relays_the_backend_usage_payload` (function) — Asserts a full-mode history push forwards the daemon-supplied usage payload verbatim in the WS frame and that it matches the REST history snapshot. <!--#5b0500c7d3bb557a-->
- `test_frame_without_usage_omits_the_key` (function) — Asserts that when the incoming full frame carries no usage payload the pushed frame omits the `usage` key entirely rather than emitting null or a fabricated zero. <!--#29253863f80f301a-->
- `test_append_frame_relays_the_stored_usage_payload` (function) — Asserts a usage-free append frame relays the usage payload stored from the earlier full frame, avoiding a rebuild on the hot append path. <!--#17a3f57167bb957f-->
- `_usage_rec` (function) — Test helper producing an assistant history record carrying a schema-v2 `usage_records` entry (call `call-2`, 30 input / 3 output tokens). <!--#1abdbd22d6dde835-->
- `test_usage_bearing_append_refreshes_the_stored_summary` (function) — Asserts an append containing new usage records refreshes the stored summary from all cached records — the pushed frame and REST snapshot both include the new call and updated totals instead of the stale full-frame payload. <!--#2998c91cc588e167-->
- `test_full_frame_without_usage_rebuilds_from_records` (function) — Asserts that for a legacy daemon sending no usage payload, a full frame still rebuilds usage from the records themselves, matching the REST snapshot. <!--#fe1e7720e1d729ab-->
- `test_first_sighting_append_is_not_broadcast` (function) — Asserts an append arriving with no cached bundle behind it is rejected by the cache and relayed to no client, preventing the headless-conversation defect. <!--#b01d3d8e942d89b3-->
- `test_gapped_append_is_not_broadcast` (function) — Asserts an append whose cursor_base is past the cached water mark is discarded and never pushed, leaving the cached bundle unchanged. <!--#26294dc35b7b6881-->
- `test_suppressed_full_pull_reply_still_pushes_a_cursor_advisory` (function) — Asserts that when a full reply's records are suppressed for a parked REST pull, the server still broadcasts a record-free `history_cursor` advisory carrying the cursor and signature. <!--#16d3d721356ea844-->
- `test_head_loss_shape_end_to_end_the_head_is_announced` (function) — End-to-end regression test for the head-loss defect: an unanchored append is discarded and triggers exactly one daemon self-heal pull, and only the authoritative full bundle (head first, with its cursor) reaches the console. <!--#86710d11059441e7-->
- `test_evicted_flow_pushes_a_cursor_advisory_instead_of_records` (function) — Asserts that when a flow has been evicted from the history cache by the budget, a later daemon append frame relays no `history_data` records but instead a single `history_cursor` advisory carrying the flow's cursor, empty `pending`, no `signature`, and `incomplete: true`, so the WebUI can self-check and re-pull. <!--#102033c8e1272b7f-->
- `test_the_cold_advisory_keeps_an_armed_repair_armed` (function) — Regression test that the cold-flow `history_cursor` advisory always carries the `incomplete` key set to `True`, so an eviction cannot make a suppressed frame look like a settled delivery and retire the console's bounded recovery. <!--#230e7419c6570697-->
- `test_the_cold_advisory_is_scoped_to_the_owning_console` (function) — Asserts the cold-flow `history_cursor` advisory respects owner boundaries — delivered to the owning console and to the admin (owner-less) client, but never to a console belonging to a different owner. <!--#ab41a8069d6dd710-->

### `tests/server/test_history_recovery_inflight_dedup.py` (python) — Regression-lock test module driving ServerState directly to prove that a self-heal history recovery pull stays deduplicated to exactly one in-flight dispatch across a whole multi-frame drain (full HEAD + tail appends), preventing the cursor-gap DISCARD ⇄ HISTORY_REQUEST rival-pull livelock, while still re-arming a fresh pull once the recovery marker ages past _HISTORY_RECOVERY_TTL. <!--#6948f9a87fc479cb|cef57f2b7ab80e25-->
- `_record` (function) — Helper that builds a single history record dict (step_id, step_type, ordinal, and an assistant message) for a given ordinal. <!--#7db94bcbd2a6c468-->
- `_cursor` (function) — Helper that builds a cursor dict mapping the test's STEP_FILE to a given line count. <!--#0201f7aa1442d0ca-->
- `_flow` (function) — Async helper that registers a single flow on the ServerState via update_status with a given status (default 'running'). <!--#1ea13cb64bda6cd6-->
- `_full` (function) — Async helper that applies a HISTORY_MODE_FULL history frame to the ServerState for the test flow. <!--#67b4f78656d0b3ea-->
- `_append` (function) — Async helper that applies a HISTORY_MODE_APPEND history frame to the ServerState for the test flow. <!--#0ba4df01a12c5a76-->
- `test_recovery_marker_survives_drain_head_no_rival_pull` (function) — Test that the in-flight recovery marker survives the drain's full HEAD frame so a mid-drain cursor-gap discard does not dispatch a second, livelocking recovery pull. <!--#4c949b2f01b62a0f-->
- `test_rest_full_serve_mid_drain_keeps_recovery_marker` (function) — Test that a REST full-fallback snapshot poll during a recovery drain refreshes rather than pops the recovery marker, preventing a rival pull livelock. <!--#a7cd18e4517d36c8-->
- `test_recovery_marker_rearms_after_ttl` (function) — Test that a stalled recovery drain does not wedge a flow forever: once the marker ages past _HISTORY_RECOVERY_TTL, take_recovery_pull re-arms a fresh (still-deduped) pull. <!--#45300481fbf0e52f-->

### `tests/server/test_history_relay_backpressure.py` (python) — Backpressure and relay-correctness tests for the server's history pull path, using a 4324-record/147-frame sample flow plus fake slow consoles, scripted daemon legs, and a real TestClient end-to-end case to assert that a lagging `/ws/ui` console never stalls the daemon receive path, that its queue stays bounded without shedding history frames, and that REST-served replies are delivered exactly once while self-heal replays and live appends still stream through. <!--#e70a96886db77dd8|5fe0a1f326f97d68-->
- `_flat_records` (function) — Builds the full flat list of the sample flow's 4324 history records from `_SHAPE`, in daemon read order, each tagged with step_id/step_type/ordinal. <!--#d22e3c995f67e4c7-->
- `_frames` (function) — Packs those records into the 147 wire frames of one pull reply, padding all but the last frame to `_CHUNK_BYTES` (the "more to come" signal) and computing each frame's cursor and cursor_base. <!--#b17d7e107809abae-->
- `scaled_chunk_bound` (function) — Fixture that monkeypatches `ws_module.MAX_BYTES_PER_REPORT` down to `_CHUNK_BYTES` so the fixture's small record bodies still trigger the daemon's multi-frame reply behaviour. <!--#2127eb230e04980b-->
- `_SlowConsole` (class) — Fake `/ws/ui` client whose `send_text` sleeps a configurable delay per frame, used to model a browser that cannot keep up. <!--#0feee77c5d4b377a-->
  - `_SlowConsole.__init__` (method) — Records the per-frame delay and starts an empty received-frame list. <!--#be470da6d25872fe-->
  - `_SlowConsole.send_text` (method) — Sleeps the configured delay, then decodes and stores the frame — the simulated slow-consumer cost. <!--#51a8dcc842082f65-->
  - `_SlowConsole.typed` (method) — Returns the received frames whose `type` matches the given push type. <!--#b3017ac21cab3a1c-->
- `_DaemonLeg` (class) — Fake daemon socket that hands `_serve_loop` a scripted sequence of reply frames while timing the "park" — the gap before the loop asks for the next frame, i.e. the window in which inbound traffic goes undrained and the keepalive would fire. <!--#3506b74c9991c834-->
  - `_DaemonLeg.__init__` (method) — Stores the frame script and initialises the cursor, hand-off timestamp, and park measurements. <!--#6659161ad49fc543-->
  - `_DaemonLeg.receive_text` (method) — Records the park since the previous hand-off, then yields the next scripted frame, raising once the reply is exhausted to end the loop. <!--#ec08d905dfa86316-->
  - `_DaemonLeg.send_text` (method) — No-op outbound send; the test only cares about the receive path. <!--#12b0c285a50b35a1-->
  - `_DaemonLeg.close` (method) — No-op close so the loop can tear down cleanly. <!--#49003e716cdb749e-->
- `_drain` (function) — Encodes the given frames as HISTORY_DATA messages and replays them through the real `_serve_loop`, returning the measured parks. <!--#b7bf8eda773acb5d-->
- `_armed_state` (function) — Builds a `ServerState`/`UiHub`/`HistoryRequestRegistry` trio with one machine registered and one console attached, ready to receive daemon frames. <!--#33bfd0ba73132f53-->
- `test_slow_console_never_parks_the_daemon_receive_path` (function) — Asserts a 50 ms-per-frame console never charges its cost to the daemon receive path: parks stay small, wall time stays far below the console's own 7.35 s, the event loop keeps turning at least once per frame, and all 4324 records land. <!--#c4e99dae71ae213c-->
- `test_lagging_console_backlog_stays_bounded` (function) — Asserts a lagging console's queue stays within the hard frame/byte ceilings without ever shedding a history frame — the only permitted loss being disconnection, which the frontend can detect and repair. <!--#cf6b07d7f6ca8a11-->
- `test_healthy_console_still_has_its_frames_on_return` (function) — Asserts the queue is a backpressure valve rather than a deferral: for a consumer that keeps up, `broadcast_owned` returning means the frame was already delivered. <!--#87a7246c32757627-->
- `test_rest_served_pull_reply_is_not_also_pushed` (function) — Asserts a REST-served pull reply is delivered once — no `history_data` pushed to the console, at most one settled `history_cursor` advisory per reply, and the whole bundle held server-side. <!--#dd26c0edbca61b39-->
- `test_pull_reply_with_no_rest_caller_still_streams` (function) — Asserts push-suppression is scoped to the duplicate only: a replay with no REST caller (self-heal / reconnect backfill) is still relayed to the console in full. <!--#1a9f092bbed84e9f-->
- `test_live_appends_are_unaffected` (function) — Asserts an ordinary real-time append behind no pull marker still reaches the console intact. <!--#22d07a3de2aaa12e-->
- `_DrainDaemon` (class) — Test double for a connected daemon that authenticates, reports one completed flow, and answers a HISTORY_REQUEST from a background thread by streaming the whole frame sequence down its socket. <!--#e1c30984a5e8c39c-->
  - `_DrainDaemon.__init__` (method) — Opens the `/ws` socket, completes the hello/WELCOME handshake, publishes a status update advertising the flow, and starts the serving thread. <!--#e9a8134bdd6dda4e-->
  - `_DrainDaemon._serve` (method) — Background loop that reads inbound messages and, on each HISTORY_REQUEST, sends every frame as HISTORY_DATA and signals completion. <!--#df12f98f4cd3be11-->
  - `_DrainDaemon.close` (method) — Stops the serving thread and closes the websocket context, ignoring teardown errors. <!--#b15474006baae592-->
- `_Console` (class) — Test double for a browser `/ws/ui` subscriber that reads frames on its own thread, as a real console does. <!--#3e4f8e8160baa4dd-->
  - `_Console.__init__` (method) — Opens the `/ws/ui` socket and starts the background reader thread. <!--#6e446fc1c52f1ccc-->
  - `_Console._read` (method) — Reader loop that decodes each pushed frame into the collected list until stopped or the socket errors. <!--#d1d3910139ecc63b-->
  - `_Console.typed` (method) — Returns the collected frames whose `type` matches the given push type. <!--#b3017ac21cab3a1c-->
  - `_Console.close` (method) — Signals the reader thread to stop and closes the websocket context, ignoring teardown errors. <!--#b15474006baae592-->
- `test_open_of_a_big_completed_flow_reaches_the_tail` (function) — End-to-end acceptance over a real `TestClient`: a cache-miss open plus token-pinned polling converges on all 4324 records including the `52_summarize` tail, while none of those records are also pushed down `/ws/ui`. <!--#a7403a75ef1a9439-->

### `tests/server/test_history_step_payload_lazy.py` (python) — Test suite for lazy step-payload shaping in history: it verifies `summarize_history_records` holds back bulky step `inputs` behind lazy/detail_flow/detail_version markers while keeping the report-card fields (outputs, status, error_message, usage, and the `STEP_INPUT_INLINE_KEYS` scalars) inline, leaves small/unaddressable records untouched and the cache unmutated, and checks end-to-end that `/api/history/{flow}` ships the shaped bundle while `/api/history/{flow}/detail?source=step` serves the full original payload with proper 422/404 handling. <!--#6538eeae818de31d|f50b694387f4ef8b-->
- `_outputs` (function) — Test helper building a self_check step's `outputs` dict (issues, self_check_result, token_usage, usage_summary) — the part the report card must keep inline — with optional overrides. <!--#7b84ba0b923ba14a-->
- `_inputs` (function) — Test helper building a realistically large step `inputs` dict (scope_diff, test_results, fix_history, task descriptions) alongside the allowlisted inline scalars, with optional overrides. <!--#0127f341e422a6cb-->
- `_step_event` (function) — Test helper assembling one engine step event in the daemon's `{step_id, step_type, ordinal, message}` envelope, with tunable event type, status, step id, inputs and outputs. <!--#d0b7db5f15699fc7-->
- `_shaped_step` (function) — Test helper returning the `data.step` of a record after passing it through `summarize_history_records`, i.e. the copy the browser would receive. <!--#dfa03b6836ad2ce2-->
- `test_step_inputs_are_held_back_and_marked` (function) — Asserts that shaping strips the bulky `inputs` keys, sets the lazy/detail_flow/detail_version markers, and yields at least a tenfold size reduction. <!--#69a903e4c2ecc275-->
- `test_the_report_card_fields_still_ride_inline` (function) — Asserts the shaped step keeps `outputs`, `status`, `error_message` and both usage payloads byte-identical to the original so the default report card renders unchanged. <!--#c1b5bdc76a9b1cda-->
- `test_the_inputs_keys_the_card_reads_ride_inline` (function) — Asserts the surviving `inputs` keys are exactly `STEP_INPUT_INLINE_KEYS` with their original values, covering the scalars the fix-iteration and confirm-report renderers read. <!--#8c2982ba37209380-->
- `test_a_step_failed_record_is_shaped_the_same_way` (function) — Asserts a `step_failed` record is lazified identically while its `error_message` headline is never held back. <!--#ba1f89590b7dd733-->
- `test_a_step_output_record_keeps_its_usage_chip` (function) — Asserts a `step_output` record is lazified yet retains the token_usage and usage_summary values its usage-only chip renders. <!--#5fb7e784483a6e53-->
- `test_a_small_step_event_rides_inline` (function) — Asserts a step event whose inputs are smaller than the lazy markers is returned unchanged (identical object, no marker), since holding it back would be a net loss. <!--#1f8471ebd9712131-->
- `test_a_step_event_without_inputs_is_left_alone` (function) — Asserts a step event with empty `inputs` passes through shaping untouched. <!--#14306c07ff04cde6-->
- `test_an_unaddressable_step_event_is_never_lazified` (function) — Asserts a record missing its `ordinal` — hence unfetchable by the detail endpoint — is never lazified. <!--#e0ffc7c7734da2e8-->
- `test_shaping_does_not_mutate_the_cached_record` (function) — Asserts shaping is non-destructive: the cached source record keeps its full inputs and gains no markers, so it can still serve the detail request. <!--#a6315efc1133ddcc-->
- `test_the_detail_version_moves_when_the_held_back_inputs_change` (function) — Asserts the detail-version marker changes when held-back inputs are rewritten under the same address, so stale detail is not served from cache. <!--#1d622b8a630b921f-->
- `test_locate_returns_the_whole_original_record` (function) — Asserts `locate_record_detail` with the step source returns the full original inputs plus the untouched cached message for "View raw". <!--#ca54a0baa9ca84c3-->
- `test_locate_is_scoped_to_the_addressed_record` (function) — Asserts `locate_record_detail` resolves by `ordinal`, returning each record's own inputs when several share a step id. <!--#d885cf265035b3ae-->
- `test_a_non_step_record_has_no_step_detail` (function) — Asserts locating a step detail on a plain assistant-message record reports the record as found but yields `detail: None`. <!--#788a2a458aae757c-->
- `test_the_tool_sources_still_require_an_id` (function) — Asserts the progress and raw tool sources still refuse a lookup without a `tool_use_id`, unchanged by the new step source. <!--#d28157b77ff3284a-->
- `client_and_app` (function) — Pytest fixture yielding an authenticated `TestClient` and its app for the HTTP-level history tests. <!--#c78c8fc0ec5446bd-->
- `_seed` (function) — Test helper that opens a daemon WebSocket, handshakes, pushes a full history bundle for a flow, and polls `/api/history/{flow}` until the bundle is cache-visible. <!--#5084a1955f59a040-->
- `test_bundle_response_no_longer_inlines_the_step_payload` (function) — End-to-end assertion that the `/api/history/{flow}` bundle ships lazified step inputs with intact outputs and a tenfold-smaller payload. <!--#a88dde9f4b43ef9c-->
- `test_detail_endpoint_returns_the_full_step_payload` (function) — End-to-end assertion that `/api/history/{flow}/detail` with `source=step` returns the complete original inputs and an unmarked raw record. <!--#10b5b2e08248ef2b-->
- `test_detail_endpoint_still_rejects_a_tool_request_without_an_id` (function) — Asserts the detail endpoint returns 422 for tool sources lacking a `tool_use_id` and for a step request lacking its address. <!--#03b2bd4b2af465d0-->
- `test_detail_endpoint_404s_a_record_that_holds_no_step_payload` (function) — Asserts the detail endpoint returns 404 when the addressed record exists but carries no step payload. <!--#62278900be604f0d-->
- `test_the_cache_still_holds_the_full_step_payload` (function) — Asserts the server's in-memory history cache retains the full step inputs, confirming only the wire copy is shaped. <!--#54db5e2fa46068bf-->

### `tests/server/test_history_step_window.py` (python) — Tests the WebUI history step-window feature end to end — block-wise tail/page-up windowing over cached bundles and daemon-relayed reads, its interaction with progress tokens, eviction recency, pull pins and the cache budget, plus the `/api/history/<flow>` route's `window`/`before` parameters, size cap, usage reporting, and byte-for-byte backwards compatibility for unwindowed requests. <!--#1d163b7b9defe70d|07131c6e7b548446-->
- `_record` (function) — Test helper building a single history record dict for a given step id and ordinal with a padded assistant message payload. <!--#cd2af1a4fe74f6bf-->
- `_blocks` (function) — Test helper generating a flow-ordered list of records spanning `count` synthetic step blocks of `per_block` records each. <!--#f984a4d774abfd1a-->
- `_step_ids` (function) — Test helper returning the ordered synthetic step ids (`NN_implement_hNN`) matching those produced by `_blocks`. <!--#84a110c7990ebdd9-->
- `_cursor` (function) — Test helper building the per-step-file record-count cursor (`<step>.jsonl` → count) that accompanies a seeded bundle. <!--#d585b5d5d8ccf29e-->
- `_seed_state` (function) — Async test helper that loads records into a `ServerState` as a full history frame for a flow, with optional cursor. <!--#51f9991f39b62299-->
- `test_the_default_window_is_the_tail_of_the_flow` (function) — Asserts an unanchored window snapshot returns the last N step blocks in `tail` mode with correct `first_index`, `has_earlier`, and only those blocks' records. <!--#5c221914459d0379-->
- `test_the_block_index_travels_whole_so_the_client_can_page_itself` (function) — Asserts the window carries the full list of block ids (not just the loaded ones) so the browser can page and scope its own completeness check. <!--#38d5ed5558b4b309-->
- `test_paging_back_reaches_the_first_block_covering_every_record` (function) — Walks page-ups from the tail to the first block and asserts the concatenated pages reproduce the whole flow exactly, with no gaps or duplicates. <!--#a486ab6ac1fbe84c-->
- `test_a_window_wider_than_the_flow_is_the_whole_flow` (function) — Asserts a window larger than the flow yields `first_index` 0, `has_earlier` false, and every record. <!--#93c629da002c8195-->
- `test_an_unknown_anchor_yields_an_empty_window_not_the_tail` (function) — Asserts a page-up anchored on an unknown step returns an empty window that still reports `has_earlier` true rather than silently serving the tail or claiming the head is loaded. <!--#426bf4c6c2815e37-->
- `test_an_unresolvable_page_up_never_claims_the_head_is_loaded` (function) — Asserts that when a cached bundle holds only a prefix of the flow, an unresolvable page-up answers with an empty window past the end instead of `has_earlier` false at index 0. <!--#90958756a9ff5590-->
- `test_both_window_legs_answer_an_unresolvable_anchor_identically` (function) — Asserts the cached-state leg and the daemon-relay leg (`_window_payload_from_daemon`) produce identical window metadata for an unresolvable anchor. <!--#91e9735953d01623-->
- `test_the_progress_token_still_pins_the_WHOLE_bundle` (function) — Asserts a windowed read still mints its progress token at the full bundle count, so the follow-up delta poll returns `not_modified` instead of re-shipping the unloaded head. <!--#5ef986f1676eba51-->
- `test_a_window_read_is_a_ui_view_that_protects_the_bundle` (function) — Asserts a window read refreshes eviction recency like a whole-bundle read, so a paging reader's bundle is not swept out under a tiny cache budget. <!--#47b7981d78a447e6-->
- `test_a_bundle_from_another_machine_reads_as_a_miss` (function) — Asserts a window snapshot request with a mismatched `expected_machine_id` returns None (cache miss). <!--#81ebfae47ae26b68-->
- `test_a_flow_whose_pull_is_in_flight_is_never_evicted` (function) — Asserts `pin_history_pull`/`release_history_pull` protect a cold bundle from eviction only while its pull is in flight. <!--#833ea6cdeb3b3fe3-->
- `test_the_pull_pin_ages_out_so_a_lost_caller_cannot_wedge_the_budget` (function) — Asserts a pull pin older than `_HISTORY_PULL_PIN_TTL` stops protecting the flow, so a crashed caller cannot make it permanently unevictable. <!--#9aa66998a913210d-->
- `test_browsing_an_over_budget_flow_to_its_first_block_evicts_nothing` (function) — Acceptance test that paging a single flow larger than the entire cache budget back to its first block converges and triggers no eviction of that flow. <!--#2bfab096c4b1d6fa-->
- `test_the_over_budget_report_still_names_the_flow_holding_the_memory` (function) — Asserts `history_cache_stats` still reports over-budget bytes and attributes them to the offending flow after the no-evict windowing fix. <!--#ab7539e360f1f4c8-->
- `test_an_unwatched_flow_is_still_evicted` (function) — Asserts windowing does not disable the cache budget for flows nobody is reading — an unwatched bundle is still evicted. <!--#427db918d0225af1-->
- `client_and_app` (function) — Pytest fixture yielding a logged-in `TestClient` and the authenticated FastAPI app for the route-level window tests. <!--#c78c8fc0ec5446bd-->
- `_connect` (function) — Test helper opening an authenticated daemon WebSocket, completing the hello/WELCOME handshake, and announcing a history index entry for the test flow. <!--#6cc95d5ecf9b158d-->
- `_seed_bundle` (function) — Test helper that pushes a full HISTORY_DATA frame over the daemon socket and polls `/api/history/<flow>` until the bundle is cache-visible. <!--#844ee296754656a2-->
- `test_the_route_serves_a_tail_window_from_the_cache` (function) — Asserts `GET /api/history/<flow>?window=N` serves a cached tail window with the loaded block ids, its records, and the whole-flow cursor. <!--#07ef0c2ae591cd86-->
- `test_the_route_pages_backwards_by_block` (function) — Asserts the route's `before` parameter pages one window of blocks backwards in `before` mode with `has_earlier` still true. <!--#c7b6de20c7728d34-->
- `test_an_unwindowed_request_is_byte_for_byte_what_it_always_was` (function) — Asserts a request without `window` still returns the untouched `full` snapshot dialect with no `window` block, preserving older-client behaviour. <!--#91589c6fc98000bc-->
- `test_the_window_size_is_capped` (function) — Asserts an absurdly large `window` value is clamped to `HISTORY_WINDOW_MAX_BLOCKS` so the windowed route cannot degrade into a whole-flow read. <!--#14412c39b45e0704-->
- `test_a_cache_miss_is_served_by_a_daemon_window_read_without_caching` (function) — Asserts a cache-missed windowed request relays a HISTORY_WINDOW_REQUEST to the daemon and returns the reply straight through, with no bundle created, no token, and `incomplete` false. <!--#baec779c1f9e9991-->
- `test_a_relayed_window_still_carries_the_session_usage` (function) — Asserts a daemon-relayed window (which builds no bundle) reports usage from the daemon's pushed index summary rather than omitting it or aggregating only the window's records. <!--#2385136ba1dae59d-->
- `test_a_relayed_window_omits_usage_when_nothing_reports_any` (function) — Asserts a relayed window returns `usage: null` rather than a fabricated zero summary when no usage is reported anywhere. <!--#162a5d0bfe54abbf-->
- `test_a_daemon_window_read_is_chunked_and_settles_on_the_final_frame` (function) — Asserts multiple HISTORY_WINDOW_DATA chunks under one request id accumulate and only the `final` frame settles the response, delivering the whole window. <!--#f386317e946063b9-->
- `test_a_legacy_daemon_falls_back_to_the_full_pull_and_still_windows` (function) — Asserts a revision-8 daemon is never sent a window request and the route falls back to a full HISTORY_REQUEST pull, then slices the requested window out of the rebuilt bundle. <!--#7559e25746df385a-->
- `test_the_fallback_pull_pins_the_flow_against_eviction` (function) — Spies on `pin_history_pull` to assert the legacy fallback pull pins its flow during the drain and releases the pin once the pull settles. <!--#52ed1323638dee8a-->
- `test_a_windowed_request_for_an_unowned_flow_is_404` (function) — Asserts a windowed request for a flow the user does not own returns HTTP 404. <!--#64429f43fda48a79-->
- `test_the_windowed_records_are_summarized_like_every_other_delivery` (function) — Asserts windowed replies pass through the same summarization funnel as full snapshots, holding back large step inputs behind `STEP_INPUTS_LAZY_KEY`. <!--#f72e31c72d209e10-->
- `test_a_raw_chip_on_an_uncached_flow_reads_one_block_not_the_whole_flow` (function) — Asserts the `/detail` lookup on an uncached flow relays a single-step window request (never a whole-flow pull) and returns the held-back payload in full. <!--#5e4c5bad85c5b22b-->
- `test_the_window_registry_accumulates_until_the_final_frame` (function) — Unit-tests that `HistoryWindowRegistry` leaves its future pending across non-final chunks and resolves with the concatenated records on the final frame. <!--#43e1076efee6d71d-->
- `test_the_window_registry_reports_a_failed_read` (function) — Unit-tests that a registry frame with `ok: False` resolves the waiter carrying the failure and its error message. <!--#dabeb964ad279beb-->
- `test_a_frame_for_a_discarded_request_is_dropped` (function) — Unit-tests that a frame arriving after `discard` is dropped without re-creating accumulator state, preventing a slow leak keyed by abandoned request ids. <!--#a93f685939a2cb62-->
- `_relay_window` (function) — Test helper that issues a windowed GET on a worker thread, answers the relayed HISTORY_WINDOW_REQUEST via a caller-supplied reply builder, and returns the observed request and the response. <!--#a7dd8bea42dd402f-->
- `test_a_relayed_window_carries_the_probe_for_the_next_poll` (function) — Asserts a first relayed window sends no `if_signature` and returns the daemon's `signature` on the window block (with no bundle progress token) for the client's next poll. <!--#027a73f3c7c2f071-->
- `test_the_probe_is_relayed_and_an_unchanged_tail_ships_nothing` (function) — Asserts a `wsig` probe is relayed as `if_signature` and an unchanged tail answers `not_modified` with no records, no window/cursor block, `incomplete` false, and no bundle created. <!--#380ba0399180f04b-->
- `test_a_stale_probe_is_answered_with_the_window` (function) — Asserts a stale `wsig` probe is answered with the full window payload and the daemon's new signature. <!--#951a38ad432dae7c-->
- `test_a_daemon_that_ignores_the_probe_keeps_the_old_behaviour` (function) — Asserts a daemon reply omitting `signature` yields an empty window signature so the client simply polls unconditionally, degrading rather than wedging. <!--#298d2cb6557998b9-->
- `test_the_cached_leg_ignores_the_probe` (function) — Asserts the cached leg disregards the `wsig` probe (which describes daemon files) and answers from the bundle with a real progress token and signature. <!--#95ba8fe90366037c-->
- `test_the_window_registry_carries_the_probe_and_the_verdict` (function) — Unit-tests that `HistoryWindowRegistry` propagates the daemon's `signature` and `not_modified` verdict through to the waiter. <!--#7175076ddd1d11f4-->
- `test_the_registry_defaults_say_a_reply_is_a_real_window` (function) — Unit-tests that a reply lacking probe fields defaults to `not_modified: False` and an empty signature, so a pre-probe daemon's window is never read as unchanged. <!--#e2b7054534db0f74-->

### `tests/server/test_history_window_real_flow_acceptance.py` (python) — Acceptance tests that stand up a fake `_RealDaemon` serving history windows from an actual multi-hundred-megabyte on-disk jsonl flow, asserting the WebUI opens on a small tail window rather than pulling the whole flow, pages back to the first block, elides heavy step inputs behind lazy detail pointers that the raw-chip endpoint fetches back byte-identical, creates no cache bundle for over-budget flows, and answers matching-probe polls with a read-free not_modified while still delivering changed tails in full. <!--#096611ffdb128b3d|cf2b0cfd6d5861d4-->
- `_serve_window_request` (function) — Test-side stand-in for the daemon's HISTORY_WINDOW_REQUEST handler: reads the requested window off the real on-disk flow and sends it back as HISTORY_WINDOW_DATA frames chunked by wire bytes (or a single not_modified frame). <!--#617b863324e5d898-->
- `_RealDaemon` (class) — Test harness representing a connected daemon that answers the server's history window requests from the real jsonl flow, and fails loudly if the server ever falls back to a whole-flow pull. <!--#2acad32c002c1aac-->
  - `_RealDaemon.__init__` (method) — Opens the /ws connection, completes the authenticated HELLO/WELCOME handshake, announces the real flow in a HISTORY_INDEX, and wires up a DaemonHistoryReader plus a list recording every window served. <!--#efb5e36f836c51d7-->
  - `_RealDaemon.close` (method) — Tears down the websocket connection context. <!--#265e5a9fe9cb492b-->
  - `_RealDaemon.get` (method) — Issues a REST GET on a worker thread while pumping the daemon side of the socket — serving window requests and asserting no whole-flow HISTORY_REQUEST occurs — until the response arrives. <!--#05b301adc9667f31-->
- `daemon_and_client` (function) — Module-scoped fixture yielding one authenticated app, TestClient, and connected _RealDaemon, shared because every read walks hundreds of megabytes of real jsonl. <!--#1a9f3009d357f90e-->
- `tail_window` (function) — Fixture performing the default history open (last 10 step blocks) against the real flow and returning the parsed response body. <!--#5eb2ddf3bde890af-->
- `_wire_bytes` (function) — Helper measuring a response body's compact JSON serialization size in bytes. <!--#49b0713e294f1420-->
- `_event_type` (function) — Helper extracting the engine event type from a delivered record, looking inside the daemon's holder's message before falling back to the holder itself. <!--#f8bec444aa283044-->
- `test_the_real_flow_opens_on_its_tail_window` (function) — Asserts the default open delivers a daemon-sourced tail window of exactly 10 blocks ending on the summarize block's step_completed, an order of magnitude smaller on the wire than the old whole-flow delivery, and marked complete. <!--#fad7b6ccc483c03f-->
- `test_the_tail_window_creates_no_bundle_for_an_over_budget_flow` (function) — Asserts a flow far larger than the cache budget leaves no bundle in the server's _history_data after a tail open. <!--#3b52c367da37bcd0-->
- `test_the_real_flow_pages_back_to_its_very_first_block` (function) — Pages the real flow backwards window by window until it reaches the very first block, asserting full ordered coverage with no bundle created and no evictions. <!--#160942328052cdfb-->
- `_largest_step_event` (function) — Helper picking the biggest step_completed/step_failed/step_output record in a window by serialized size. <!--#c133704a991a10a6-->
- `_original_on_disk` (function) — Helper reading the record at a given ordinal directly from the block's jsonl file, as the engine originally wrote it. <!--#501898a9200ab116-->
- `test_real_step_events_ship_their_outputs_but_not_their_inputs` (function) — Asserts a real step event ships with its heavy inputs elided down to STEP_INPUT_INLINE_KEYS plus a lazy marker and detail pointers, while every other field stays byte-identical to the on-disk original. <!--#972cb4dded3990c4-->
- `test_the_raw_chip_fetches_a_real_step_payload_back_whole` (function) — Asserts the step detail endpoint returns the full original record — larger than the delivered one, free of the lazy wire marker, and equal to the on-disk line — even for an uncached over-budget flow. <!--#abbb1f3ca9e0fa1c-->
- `test_the_tail_window_hands_back_a_probe` (function) — Asserts the relayed tail window carries a signature so subsequent polls can be conditional. <!--#1ed3ce045232c8e5-->
- `test_watching_this_flow_costs_a_stat_per_block_not_a_re_read` (function) — Spies on _consumable_lines to assert a poll with a matching probe returns a tiny not_modified response that reads no lines off disk, ships no records or window block, and creates no bundle or evictions. <!--#f737dd78ac293361-->
- `test_a_changed_tail_is_still_delivered_in_full` (function) — Asserts a stale probe yields a full window delivery identical to the fresh tail, so the conditional poll can never freeze a live reader. <!--#618188b43c8a7c1f-->

### `tests/server/test_i18n_manifest.py` (python) — Pins the WebUI language registry contract: that GET /i18n/index.json is unauthenticated and derived from the static/i18n locale directory via _discover_ui_languages() (new locales discovered as a pure data change, malformed files skipped, missing endonyms falling back to the locale code), plus that all G10 strategy/scope/usage UI keys ship in both the en-US and zh-CN dictionaries. <!--#f57c68a3e570ed15|60b7814b3ff45051-->
- `client` (function) — Pytest fixture yielding a FastAPI TestClient over an authenticated app instance for exercising the server's i18n manifest endpoint. <!--#70dfbef10d3a1b20-->
- `test_manifest_lists_the_shipped_languages_unauthenticated` (function) — Asserts GET /i18n/index.json is reachable without login and lists the shipped locales (en-US, zh-CN) with their endonym labels drawn from each dictionary's own lang.<code> entry. <!--#5a4e889eb159af68-->
- `test_a_new_locale_file_is_discovered_without_a_code_change` (function) — Verifies _discover_ui_languages() picks up any locale JSON dropped into the locales directory (e.g. a new fr-FR) with no code change, returning code/label pairs in sorted order. <!--#e0154532f83fbeb6-->
- `test_a_malformed_locale_file_is_skipped_not_fatal` (function) — Verifies an unparseable locale JSON file is silently skipped rather than raising, so discovery still returns the valid locales. <!--#0bfed6196ed4a788-->
- `test_a_locale_without_its_own_endonym_labels_itself` (function) — Verifies a locale dictionary lacking its own lang.<code> endonym falls back to using the locale code itself as the display label. <!--#b33ded6decdd61a0-->
- `_locale_dict` (function) — Test helper that loads and parses a WebUI locale JSON file (e.g. en-US.json) from the server's static i18n directory. <!--#d2e9090500b20821-->
- `test_g10_ui_keys_ship_in_both_locales` (function) — Asserts that every G10 console UI label key (plan-mode/scope/usage) is present in both the en-US and zh-CN server locale dictionaries, indirectly pinning the directory-derived i18n manifest as complete. <!--#b412c6764ca79fe2-->

### `tests/server/test_message_history.py` (python) — Test suite covering the server's per-owner message-history feature end to end — store-level schema creation and v1→v2 in-place migration, append filtering (blank/adjacent-repeat folding), per-(owner, channel) cap and overflow eviction, owner deletion cascade and isolation — plus the `/api/message-history/{channel}` HTTP routes' fail-closed auth, GET/POST round trip, unknown-channel 404s, cross-owner isolation, and read cap. <!--#ea3a664142f59c49|51d5d89eb3b5eb92-->
- `_texts` (function) — Test helper that extracts just the `text` field from a list of history entries, for assertions concerned with ordering rather than ids. <!--#c3783e8d0894385e-->
- `_user_version` (function) — Test helper that opens a SQLite file directly and returns its `PRAGMA user_version` schema version number. <!--#ac562252bc769bea-->
- `test_message_history_channels_and_cap_match_the_cli` (function) — Asserts the server's message-history constants stay aligned with the CLI: channels are exactly `(REPLY, NEW_TASK)` and the cap equals `prompt_history.MAX_ENTRIES` (500). <!--#3b3040e57b2da5a1-->
- `test_fresh_database_is_created_at_v2_with_the_history_table` (function) — Verifies a newly created `Store` database lands at `SCHEMA_VERSION` 2 with a working message-history table that appends and reads back with a stable entry id. <!--#8b1e7fdca1923a1f-->
- `test_existing_v1_database_upgrades_in_place_and_keeps_its_data` (function) — Builds a legacy v1 database by hand and checks that opening it migrates to v2 without losing owners or identity bindings, exposes the new history table immediately, and is a no-op on reopen. <!--#273f204169b5b6e7-->
- `test_deleting_an_owner_takes_their_history_with_it` (function) — Confirms `delete_owner` cascades to message history so no entries outlive the owner they belong to. <!--#5a9e84b369bdd5fd-->
- `test_channels_are_separate_stacks` (function) — Confirms the REPLY and NEW_TASK channels of one owner hold independent entry lists. <!--#da2c827e0e71dd2c-->
- `test_blank_and_repeated_entries_never_enter_the_stack` (function) — Covers the store's append filtering: blanks are dropped with no entry id, an immediately repeated text folds onto the previous row's id, and a non-adjacent repeat is a genuine new entry with its own id. <!--#533a8b613786713e-->
- `test_overflow_drops_the_oldest_entries` (function) — Fills a channel past `MESSAGE_HISTORY_MAX_ENTRIES` and checks the oldest rows are evicted while ordering and entry ids stay stable, with the cap applied per (owner, channel). <!--#207347d4d927b566-->
- `test_store_level_owner_isolation` (function) — Checks at the store layer that owners' histories are disjoint and that one owner overflowing their channel evicts nothing from another's. <!--#bbe738345f676f50-->
- `client_and_app` (function) — Pytest fixture yielding a logged-in `TestClient` and its authenticated app backed by a temp-directory SQLite database. <!--#5dbcabb30b965c3e-->
- `test_history_routes_are_fail_closed` (function) — Asserts both GET and POST on `/api/message-history/{channel}` return 401 without a session. <!--#673c2a1769ad0a7a-->
- `test_get_and_post_round_trip` (function) — Exercises the HTTP round trip end to end: empty read, append, skipped repeat carrying the folded row's id, skipped blank with a null id, oldest-first listing with ids and count, and channel separation. <!--#0dc83639ee0127f4-->
- `test_a_non_adjacent_repeat_is_a_second_append_with_its_own_id` (function) — Over HTTP, distinguishes an adjacent fold (same id, `appended: false`) from an "A, B, A" sequence that yields two distinct entries with distinct ids. <!--#5a851c09aaa62c65-->
- `test_unknown_channel_is_a_404_on_both_verbs` (function) — Asserts an unrecognized or empty channel segment returns 404 on both GET and POST. <!--#bb29517967e69cc9-->
- `test_one_owner_never_reads_anothers_history` (function) — Logs in two owners (including an admin) against one app and confirms each reads only their own history, with no cross-owner access even for the operator role. <!--#63318d38533dfe88-->
- `test_api_read_is_capped_at_the_max` (function) — Seeds more than the cap through the store, then checks the GET route returns at most `MESSAGE_HISTORY_MAX_ENTRIES` newest entries, oldest first, with unique ascending ids. <!--#23a538fb7259a39b-->

### `tests/server/test_multi_machine_flow_resolution.py` (python) — Server test suite covering multi-machine flow→machine resolution: it seeds the same flow on several registered machines and asserts that every entry point (`get_flow`, `find_machine_for_flow`, resume/end gates, history-index aggregation and dedupe, RUNNING-flow routing, flow detail reads, and `find_call_owner` for pending human calls) prefers the actually-reachable daemon — via connectivity probe rather than the debounced `online` flag — while still respecting owner scoping, probe-failure fallback to the presence flag, and pre-fix insertion order when no machine is reachable or all are. <!--#ca464213e5765f5d|c50cb6d26fe82283-->
- `_flow_payload` (function) — Test helper building the canonical paused-but-resumable flow snapshot dict that a daemon would report for the shared flow. <!--#2b35207878e5a164-->
- `_session_meta` (function) — Test helper building one `MSG_HISTORY_INDEX` session-meta row for the shared flow on a given project root. <!--#fd3d5e9322761541-->
- `_running_flow` (function) — Test helper producing a RUNNING flow snapshot, with `resumable` cleared or kept to model a live `luo run` versus an interrupted-but-recoverable one. <!--#e6cfffa4c0c24ca3-->
- `_seed_machine` (function) — Async fixture helper that registers a machine on `ServerState` and has it report the shared flow, a history-index entry, and optionally go offline. <!--#2acaa640b44e0576-->
- `_resolve_all` (function) — Async helper invoking every flow→machine resolution entry point (`get_flow`, `find_machine_for_flow`, resumable/endable gates, history lookups) and collecting their answers. <!--#7a39b5a8e4f57c32-->
- `_machines` (function) — Tiny helper extracting the five machine-id answers from a `_resolve_all` result, dropping `project_root`. <!--#0a349c54409f042f-->
- `test_online_machine_wins_over_offline_reporter_of_same_flow` (function) — Asserts an online reporter of a shared flow beats an offline one registered earlier across all resolution entry points. <!--#708d9d57fc25bbc5-->
- `test_online_live_flow_beats_offline_history_index_and_cached_bundle` (function) — Asserts servability outranks evidence strength: a freshly connected machine wins even though the dead one holds the history index and cached bundle. <!--#3323a944c0447f4a-->
- `test_offline_index_still_wins_over_online_machine_without_the_flow` (function) — Asserts the online preference only ranks machines that actually report the flow, so an unrelated online machine never wins. <!--#23ec289548a01ac5-->
- `test_all_offline_falls_back_to_pre_fix_answer` (function) — Asserts that with no machine online, resolution degrades to the pre-fix first-insertion-order match. <!--#bf3ace8f009e0bfa-->
- `test_unknown_flow_still_resolves_to_nothing` (function) — Asserts the extra reachability pass never invents a machine or project root for a flow nobody reports. <!--#c3767e603a8d2d44-->
- `test_online_preference_never_crosses_owner_boundary` (function) — Asserts owner scoping still isolates identical flow ids, so each owner resolves only to machines in its own trust domain. <!--#7bcc2dcf638342f5-->
- `test_unscoped_admin_view_still_prefers_the_online_machine` (function) — Asserts `owner=None` keeps see-everything semantics while still preferring the online machine. <!--#f63709737fa2501c-->
- `_row` (function) — Test helper building a history-index row, with `flow_id=None` modelling a malformed daemon row. <!--#192cb46726244671-->
- `_by_flow` (function) — Tiny helper filtering history-index entries down to those matching a given flow id. <!--#42d61e2cd8dc7059-->
- `test_history_index_collapses_shared_flow_onto_the_online_machine` (function) — Asserts the aggregated history index emits one row per session, attributed to the online machine even when the offline one has the newer row. <!--#4d8b3c3a255caf0d-->
- `test_history_index_dedupe_falls_back_to_newest_updated_at` (function) — Asserts that when both reporters share the same online state, history-index dedupe keeps the row with the newest `updated_at`. <!--#54de4340c2acbe8b-->
- `test_history_index_keeps_rows_without_a_flow_id` (function) — Asserts rows lacking a usable `flow_id` are unaddressable and therefore passed through rather than collapsed together. <!--#2a1fb4cfaab95584-->
- `test_history_index_dedupe_preserves_ordering_and_other_flows` (function) — Asserts only same-id rows collapse while the list stays `updated_at`-descending and flows seen by only the offline machine remain listed. <!--#df5a35f71f8c6ee4-->
- `_probe` (function) — Test helper returning a connectivity-probe callable that reports exactly the named machines as connected. <!--#025d3bd8ff7c6dc2-->
- `test_dead_machine_inside_the_presence_grace_does_not_shadow_the_live_one` (function) — Asserts reachability, not the debounced `online` flag, decides routing so a dead machine inside its 60 s presence grace cannot shadow the live one. <!--#b51de1b804d54b2f-->
- `test_a_reconnected_machine_wins_before_its_record_is_flipped_back` (function) — Asserts the mirror case: a reconnected machine whose record still reads `online=False` is routable as soon as its socket is back. <!--#861470beff512d49-->
- `test_probe_failure_degrades_to_the_presence_flag` (function) — Asserts a raising connectivity probe degrades gracefully to the presence flag instead of declaring the whole fleet unreachable. <!--#2472b255b6859f2c-->
- `test_without_a_probe_the_presence_flag_still_decides` (function) — Asserts a bare `ServerState` with no probe installed keeps its previous presence-flag-based semantics. <!--#315935a6c8e4247e-->
- `test_running_flow_resolves_to_the_reachable_machine` (function) — Asserts a flow frozen as RUNNING on an unreachable node does not stay pinned there, so every entry point resolves to the reachable machine instead of answering 409. <!--#a8e21d0dd2db2e3b-->
- `test_flow_detail_read_shows_the_reachable_machines_view` (function) — Asserts `GET /api/flows/{id}` renders the reachable machine's snapshot (its `current_step` and `project_root`), never the unreachable node's stale frame. <!--#8640e40fb53c9e02-->
- `test_running_flow_verdicts_are_read_off_the_resolved_machine` (function) — Asserts the resume/end gates judge the snapshot of the machine the command will actually dispatch to, keeping resolution and gating in agreement. <!--#2335aa70af76a7e4-->
- `test_both_machines_reachable_keeps_insertion_order` (function) — Asserts the reachability preference only reorders across the reachable/unreachable boundary and leaves a fully-connected fleet in pre-fix insertion order. <!--#7d5693ef4247898e-->
- `test_interrupted_running_flow_still_switches_machines` (function) — Asserts the common hand-off shape — job died on one node, taken over by the next — resolves to the surviving machine. <!--#6cd906898daef81b-->
- `test_running_flow_resolution_never_crosses_owner_boundary` (function) — Asserts another owner's reachable machine stays invisible when resolving a RUNNING flow. <!--#d6a6c2675eb99501-->

- `test_pending_call_resolves_to_the_reachable_mirror` (function) — An async unit test asserting that when the same call is mirrored across an offline machine (node007) and a reachable one (node008), ServerState.find_call_owner and get_pending_call route to the reachable mirror (node008/ROOT_B) rather than the first-registered offline node, guarding against permanent 503s on GET /api/calls/{id}/detail. <!--#cc7b69f93132554f-->
- `test_pending_call_on_a_running_flow_resolves_to_the_reachable_node` (function) — Asserts a RUNNING flow blocked on a human call still resolves — flow and call owner alike — to the reachable node. <!--#d38b979fb84affe8-->
- `test_pending_call_falls_back_when_no_machine_is_reachable` (function) — Asserts call-owner resolution returns the pre-fix insertion-order answer when the whole fleet is unreachable. <!--#4a41ceb2b741fe28-->
- `test_pending_call_project_root_pin_survives_the_reachable_ordering` (function) — Asserts an explicit `project_root` pin is a correctness constraint that outranks reachability, since `call_id` is unique only within a project. <!--#a3cd291c1475ee57-->
- `test_pending_call_resolution_never_crosses_owner_boundary` (function) — Asserts another owner's reachable machine is never a candidate for pending-call resolution. <!--#faa8ea6f2d7d1b94-->
- `_issue` (function) — Test helper building an `IssueSnapshot` dict as a daemon mirrors it in STATUS_UPDATE. <!--#e63f4bdfededd5f8-->

- `test_issue_resolves_to_the_reachable_mirror` (function) — Asserts issue lookup and project→machine resolution pick the connected mirror, since issue writes dispatched at a dead node 404 permanently. <!--#604c5ded7376e6b3-->
- `test_issue_resolution_switches_inside_the_presence_grace` (function) — Asserts issue resolution and listing follow the connectivity probe rather than the 60 s-debounced `online` flag. <!--#ffbc975446f93058-->
- `test_issue_list_collapses_the_shared_issue_onto_one_row` (function) — Asserts the issue list emits one row per shared on-disk YAML, attributed to the reachable machine even when the dead node holds the newer mirror. <!--#68fedb80d57cce38-->
- `test_issue_list_dedupe_falls_back_to_newest_updated_at` (function) — Asserts that with both mirrors equally unreachable, issue dedupe keeps the fresher snapshot. <!--#bac6b9e9984d3862-->
- `test_issue_dedupe_is_scoped_to_the_project_root` (function) — Asserts issue dedupe keys on `(project_root, id)` so two projects reusing the same issue id both stay listed. <!--#da4124a38bec5643-->
- `test_issue_list_keeps_rows_without_an_id` (function) — Asserts a malformed id-less mirror row has no identity to collapse on and passes through behind the reachable machine's collapsed row. <!--#6b08051446c5ed13-->
- `test_issue_resolution_all_offline_falls_back_to_pre_fix_answer` (function) — Asserts issue lookup and project resolution return exactly the previous insertion-order answer when nothing is reachable. <!--#7d013243573a7c0d-->
- `test_issue_resolution_never_crosses_owner_boundary` (function) — Asserts a reachable machine belonging to another owner is not a candidate for issue lookup, project resolution, or listing. <!--#94fb9594137a0c20-->
- `test_issue_machine_pin_survives_the_reachable_ordering` (function) — Asserts an explicit `machine_id`/`project_root` still pins issue resolution, and a mismatched pin reads as not-found rather than being widened. <!--#6519c5d8c29d3a81-->
- `test_find_machine_for_project_prefers_a_reachable_registered_root` (function) — Asserts reachability outranks evidence source, so a machine that merely registered the root beats a dead one holding a full issue mirror. <!--#1f8aa5b6596cd3cc-->
- `test_issue_single_machine_deployment_is_untouched` (function) — Baseline asserting issue dedupe, ordering, and closed-filtering are unchanged for a single reporting machine. <!--#8ad3d25960bbe68e-->
- `test_history_index_single_machine_deployment_is_untouched` (function) — Baseline asserting history-index dedupe is a no-op and ordering stays `updated_at`-descending with one reporter. <!--#4817327103b3893d-->

- `test_active_worktree_predicate_follows_the_reachable_machine` (function) — Asserts `is_active_worktree_flow` judges off the reachable machine, so a resumed worktree run is not declared inactive by the node it moved away from. <!--#1b90cdcf4ff659aa-->
- `test_active_worktree_predicate_switches_inside_the_presence_grace` (function) — Asserts the active-worktree predicate follows the connectivity probe rather than the debounced `online` flag. <!--#5aa6f19b6504490c-->
- `test_active_worktree_predicate_all_offline_falls_back_to_pre_fix_answer` (function) — Asserts the active-worktree verdict falls back to the insertion-order snapshot when nothing is reachable. <!--#d442f2939662a03e-->
