### `tests/server/test_presence_debounce.py` (python) — Test suite verifying presence debounce so a daemon reconnecting within the grace window never flaps the WebUI online badge, covering PresenceDebouncer schedule/cancel/reschedule/shutdown semantics in isolation and handle_daemon_connection end-to-end (disconnect defers offline, reconnect cancels the pending task, the _go_offline backstop defuses stale grace tasks against a live reconnect, and legacy immediate-offline is preserved when no debouncer is passed). <!--#af07b3d24a6817b5|e6afed3266cdc3e2-->
- `test_schedule_offline_fires_after_delay` (function) — Asserts that PresenceDebouncer.schedule_offline runs the offline action exactly once after the grace delay elapses uninterrupted, and not while still inside the window. <!--#815d38b0fea788b7-->
- `test_cancel_prevents_offline` (function) — Asserts that calling cancel() within the grace window (simulating a reconnect) prevents the scheduled offline action from ever running. <!--#d3e8caca555f4294-->
- `test_reschedule_supersedes_without_leak` (function) — Asserts that re-arming schedule_offline for the same machine cancels the prior pending task, tracks only one task, and fires exactly once. <!--#fe2d204128e7ef3c-->
- `test_shutdown_cancels_pending` (function) — Asserts that PresenceDebouncer.shutdown() cancels every pending offline task, clears the pending table, and fires no actions. <!--#e2431581897940ff-->
- `_FakeWebSocket` (class) — A minimal daemon-side WebSocket stub for handle_daemon_connection that delivers one HELLO frame then raises to end the receive loop, collecting sent frames for inspection. <!--#166371d6d578dc1a-->
  - `_FakeWebSocket.__init__` (method) — Initializes the stub with a single queued HELLO frame for the given machine_id and an empty list of sent frames. <!--#bff5cc629d439ad3-->
  - `_FakeWebSocket.accept` (method) — No-op coroutine standing in for the WebSocket accept handshake. <!--#fae6e77d45b9fa2d-->
  - `_FakeWebSocket.receive_text` (method) — Pops and returns the next queued inbound frame, or raises RuntimeError to simulate a daemon disconnect once drained. <!--#f38646c008edbedd-->
  - `_FakeWebSocket.send_text` (method) — Records each outgoing frame into the sent list for later inspection. <!--#c3320b72a0b6059b-->
  - `_FakeWebSocket.close` (method) — No-op coroutine standing in for closing the WebSocket. <!--#9855161dd97b87cf-->
- `_run_connection` (function) — Helper that builds a _FakeWebSocket for a machine and drives it through handle_daemon_connection with the given state, manager, and presence debouncer. <!--#6c7914f212c54e9d-->
- `test_disconnect_defers_offline_still_online` (function) — Asserts that after a daemon disconnect the machine record stays online and a single grace task is armed during the debounce window. <!--#e847c7dba6168488-->
- `test_offline_after_grace_expires` (function) — Asserts that with no reconnect the armed grace task marks the machine offline exactly once and clears the pending table. <!--#71068e69913cc772-->
- `test_reconnect_within_grace_stays_online` (function) — Asserts that a quick reconnect within the grace window cancels the pending offline task so the machine remains online through the reconnect churn. <!--#a4f2c41a39935a1a-->
- `test_stale_grace_task_defused_by_live_reconnect` (function) — Asserts the _go_offline backstop defuses a stale grace task armed by an old handler after a newer live connection registered, keeping the reconnected machine online. <!--#fe0aadb30cc0cc26-->
- `test_no_debouncer_marks_offline_immediately` (function) — Asserts that when no debouncer is passed, handle_daemon_connection retains the legacy behavior of marking the machine offline immediately on disconnect. <!--#c439a4ef31e9d3a9-->

### `tests/server/test_project_registry_api.py` (python) — End-to-end and unit test suite for the WebUI project-registry surface, covering ProjectCommandRegistry future bookkeeping, PROJECT_RESULT handling, registered_projects sanitization/mirroring in MachineRecord and status updates, and the GET/POST/DELETE /api/machines/{id}/projects endpoints including auth, validation, daemon round trips, and error-code-to-HTTP-status mapping. <!--#1534e9106d57f62b|fe082e9f3e1a1f2c-->
- `client_and_app` (function) — Pytest fixture that spins up an authenticated FastAPI test app, logs a TestClient in, and yields the (client, app) pair for the project-registry API tests. <!--#c78c8fc0ec5446bd-->
- `_connect_daemon` (function) — Helper that opens an authenticated /ws daemon WebSocket, completes the HELLO/WELCOME handshake, and returns the context manager plus socket. <!--#417d1811e5597fc2-->
- `_push_registry` (function) — Helper that sends a STATUS_UPDATE carrying a registered_projects snapshot and polls /api/machines/{id}/projects until the server-side mirror reflects it. <!--#5b2e841e382ac176-->
- `_spy_on_downlink` (function) — Helper that monkeypatches the connection manager's send_to with a recording wrapper so tests can assert which frames (if any) were pushed to the daemon. <!--#d02371cd91bf85b8-->
- `_call_in_thread` (function) — Helper that runs a blocking REST call on a background thread, returning the thread and a result box so the test can service the daemon side meanwhile. <!--#f4ff6bc1f1f713d2-->
- `test_registry_resolves_registers_and_discards` (function) — Unit test that ProjectCommandRegistry resolves a parked future, forgets resolved ids so duplicate acks are no-ops, and that discard removes waiters without raising on unknown ids. <!--#6908a83010f78f6c-->
- `test_registry_wakes_every_waiter_on_one_id` (function) — Unit test that resolving a request id wakes all futures registered under it, not just the first. <!--#1366f3eab0b8bb6c-->
- `test_project_result_without_registry_is_ignored` (function) — Test that a PROJECT_RESULT arriving when no registry is wired into the handler is silently ignored rather than crashing the receive loop. <!--#0b44140df587f0a5-->
- `test_project_result_resolves_and_touches_machine` (function) — Test that handling a PROJECT_RESULT both resolves the waiting future with its payload and refreshes the machine's last_seen timestamp. <!--#b1891e59ac639133-->
- `test_project_result_without_request_id_is_ignored` (function) — Test that a PROJECT_RESULT with an empty request_id leaves parked futures unresolved. <!--#7a9b63911197b45c-->
- `test_sanitize_rejects_non_list_payloads` (function) — Parametrized test that _sanitize_registered_projects returns an empty list for any non-list input. <!--#be10cc360ce6dc81-->
- `test_sanitize_clips_entries_to_the_three_rendered_keys` (function) — Test that sanitization keeps only the path/exists/active keys, coerces flags to booleans, and drops non-dict or path-less entries. <!--#aede8540a407064c-->
- `test_machine_record_serializes_registered_projects` (function) — Test that MachineRecord.to_dict defaults registered_projects to an empty list and emits a defensive copy that callers cannot use to mutate the mirror. <!--#a90bfc3b6472bd64-->
- `test_status_update_replaces_then_clears_registered_projects` (function) — Test that a status update replaces the mirrored project list and that a snapshot omitting the field clears it instead of leaving stale rows. <!--#b35805be602569ca-->
- `test_get_projects_returns_mirror_with_exists_flags` (function) — End-to-end test that GET /api/machines/{id}/projects serves the mirrored list with exists/active flags and issues no daemon round trip. <!--#cca9fe7f9c01001b-->
- `test_get_projects_empty_for_daemon_without_the_field` (function) — Test that a snapshot from an older daemon lacking registered_projects degrades to an empty list with a 200, not a 500. <!--#c2bd4f7c07f52002-->
- `test_projects_endpoints_404_for_unknown_machine` (function) — Test that GET/POST/DELETE on the projects endpoints all return 404 for an unregistered machine id. <!--#458eea647ff70507-->
- `test_projects_endpoints_require_auth` (function) — Test that all three projects endpoints reject unauthenticated callers with 401. <!--#72478867a4e1b608-->
- `test_write_rejects_non_absolute_root_without_contacting_daemon` (function) — Parametrized test that POST/DELETE with a non-absolute project_root fail 422 at the server without dispatching any daemon frame. <!--#611eb5d1a6a73ba6-->
- `test_delete_without_project_root_param_is_422` (function) — Test that DELETE without the required project_root query parameter is rejected with 422. <!--#73752182bf5d22a8-->
- `test_write_is_503_when_machine_is_disconnected` (function) — Test that writes against a machine whose record survives disconnect pass the ownership gate but fail delivery with 503. <!--#c55c91ebd75ccee9-->
- `test_write_times_out_to_504_and_leaves_no_waiter` (function) — Test that an unanswered PROJECT_COMMAND times out to 504 and discards its parked future so retries cannot leak waiters. <!--#221be6c6ab2ea58f-->
- `_round_trip` (function) — Helper that issues a REST write on a thread, receives the resulting PROJECT_COMMAND frame, replies with a caller-supplied PROJECT_RESULT, and returns the frame plus HTTP response. <!--#5683de48590ac2b5-->
- `test_post_registers_project_and_returns_normalized_root` (function) — Test that POST strips whitespace, sends a PROJECT_OP_ADD command, and returns 201 with the daemon's normalized (worktree-folded) root. <!--#7cc3a14bfe8246dd-->
- `test_post_falls_back_to_requested_root_when_daemon_omits_it` (function) — Test that POST echoes the requested root in its 201 body when the daemon's result omits project_root. <!--#1a4ff34374259dfb-->
- `test_delete_deregisters_project` (function) — Test that DELETE sends a PROJECT_OP_REMOVE command and returns 200 with a removed-status body on daemon success. <!--#d8191c3c898c30dc-->
- `test_daemon_error_codes_map_to_http_status` (function) — Parametrized test that daemon error codes map to their HTTP statuses and that error_code is surfaced at the top level of the body for frontend i18n. <!--#f95ee2ae7ae36f21-->
- `test_delete_live_flow_refusal_is_409` (function) — Test that a daemon refusing removal because the project has a live flow yields 409 with error_code "live_flow". <!--#d27993a1d6d9f557-->
- `test_failure_body_falls_back_when_daemon_sends_no_prose` (function) — Test that a daemon failure without an error message still returns the mapped status plus a generic fallback detail string. <!--#ebd35eb77fd49724-->

### `tests/server/test_shared_fs_machine_switch.py` (python) — Server integration tests covering the shared-filesystem machine hand-off: when a flow's original reporting daemon (node007) dies and a second daemon (node008) on the same mount reports the same session, history detail/list, resume, end, respond, and interject must all route to the live machine with its own project_root — including inside the presence grace window and during a split brain where the dead node's last frame still reads RUNNING — while genuinely unreachable or unknown flows keep their distinguishable 404s. <!--#de8c5f59244fdf7a|e90e0fb446d66ddf-->
- `_server` (function) — A pytest fixture helper that builds an authenticated, logged-in TestClient against tianluo.server.app, shrinking history-refresh/pull timeouts and optionally overriding PresenceDebouncer's offline grace so tests can control when a dead machine flips offline. <!--#9785cd81ef314181-->
- `client_and_app` (function) — Fixture yielding a (client, app) pair from `_server` with a shortened offline grace, for tests that must observe a machine actually flipping offline. <!--#e0dcb8ed2185b895-->
- `_flow_payload` (function) — Builds the flow dict a daemon aggregator would report, defaulting to paused-and-resumable and parameterisable into the running/non-resumable live-process shape. <!--#6f1866de8f5027cf-->
- `_blocked_flow` (function) — Builds a RUNNING flow payload parked on a pending human call, with `live` controlling whether that node claims the local `luo run` process (and so is non-resumable). <!--#da943e73fc1252e6-->
- `_session_meta` (function) — Builds the matching `MSG_HISTORY_INDEX` row for the shared flow under a given project_root. <!--#016da269250b5fe1-->
- `_receive_until` (function) — Reads frames off a websocket until one of the requested message type arrives, skipping the index-request and presence broadcasts that precede it. <!--#8417d325d55556b2-->
- `_connect_daemon` (function) — Connects a stand-in daemon that handshakes and reports the shared flow (optionally a history bundle) plus its index row, returning the (ctx, sock) pair. <!--#39b8d855ceb0a8d2-->
- `_wait_for_index_row` (function) — Setup barrier that polls `GET /api/history` until the named machine's index row for the flow has landed, asserting nothing about de-duplication. <!--#43e857d6e6269620-->
- `_wait_offline` (function) — Polls `GET /api/machines` until the named machine's record has actually flipped to `online: false`. <!--#e37569dd93d0491b-->
- `_Fleet` (class) — Small handle over the post-switch fleet — offline-but-remembered node007 and live node008 — exposing the client, node008's socket, and a way to take it down. <!--#12dcaacdd85ee3f9-->
  - `_Fleet.__init__` (method) — Stores the test client plus node008's connection context and socket. <!--#ef10fa96c42e44ed-->
  - `_Fleet.disconnect_b` (method) — Closes the last live daemon's websocket and waits for node008's machine record to go offline. <!--#45f31b308efdbd11-->
- `fleet` (function) — Fixture replaying the job hand-off — node007 connects, seeds a cached bundle bound to itself, dies, then node008 reports the same session with no bundle — and yields the resulting `_Fleet`. <!--#613f87630773b73a-->
- `test_history_detail_repulls_from_the_live_machine` (function) — Asserts the stale node007-bound bundle reads as a cache miss and the detail request parks on a history pull dispatched to node008 carrying node008's own project_root. <!--#775f6fddcdd7822c-->
- `test_the_repull_happens_once_then_the_cache_serves` (function) — Asserts the re-pulled bundle re-binds to node008 so a second detail read is a plain cache hit rather than another daemon round-trip. <!--#00d78b4c1e81b66c-->
- `test_resume_dispatches_to_the_live_machine` (function) — Asserts `POST /api/flows/{id}/resume` returns 202 naming node008 and sends it a `MSG_SPAWN_FLOW` with node008's project_root. <!--#fb3dfcc88cd7d430-->
- `test_history_list_offers_the_session_once` (function) — Asserts the history list collapses both nodes' reports of the shared session into a single row attributed to the live node008. <!--#7d5bf7695ee71d22-->
- `test_resume_with_no_live_machine_is_the_old_404` (function) — Asserts that with every daemon disconnected, resume falls back to the pre-fix behaviour: 404 naming node007 as "is not connected". <!--#efcad3d5e772d7bb-->
- `test_unknown_flow_resume_404_is_distinguishable` (function) — Asserts resuming a never-reported flow yields a "not found" 404 whose detail is distinguishable from the machine-unreachable 404. <!--#a2b205ad5aab96f4-->
- `graced_fleet` (function) — Fixture staging the hand-off entirely inside the production 60 s presence grace, asserting node007 still reads `online: true` while node008 is the reachable node. <!--#14ff1dedf2fcb758-->
- `test_resume_inside_the_grace_window_reaches_the_live_machine` (function) — Asserts resume routes to node008 even while the dead node007 still displays as online, so the fix is not merely delayed by the presence grace. <!--#cbbb3968be1a609c-->
- `test_history_list_inside_the_grace_window_points_at_the_live_machine` (function) — Asserts the single history row inside the grace window names node008, matching where the detail fetch will route. <!--#f1ff38854c0b7428-->
- `_split_brain` (function) — Context manager staging the walltime-kill split brain: node007 goes unreachable with a frozen running/non-resumable frame while node008 reports the same session as recoverable. <!--#b6524b3ef76f58fb-->
- `split_brain_fleet` (function) — Fixture wrapper yielding the `_split_brain` fleet where the unreachable node's last frame still reads RUNNING. <!--#26a7df0284e1e5cd-->
- `test_resume_reaches_the_live_node_despite_the_dead_running_snapshot` (function) — Asserts the dead node's frozen running snapshot cannot wedge the flow: resume still dispatches to node008 rather than answering "still running". <!--#d3f6b0b3dfbdcad1-->
- `test_end_reaches_the_live_node_despite_the_dead_running_snapshot` (function) — Asserts `POST /api/flows/{id}/end` likewise routes to node008 during the split so the operator can close the session. <!--#cb80907273eaee53-->
- `test_reading_history_still_works_while_the_flow_runs_elsewhere` (function) — Asserts the history detail pull is still dispatched to the live node008 with its own project_root during the split brain. <!--#183f58399f1cd5af-->
- `test_flow_detail_reports_the_live_nodes_view_during_the_split` (function) — Asserts `GET /api/flows/{id}` renders node008's view rather than the unreachable node's frozen snapshot. <!--#04150ff120fd6df1-->
- `blocked_fleet` (function) — Fixture where node007 held a flow blocked on a pending human call before losing its link, leaving node008 on the same mount reporting the same blocked call. <!--#b2bf949227041a97-->
- `test_respond_reaches_the_live_machine` (function) — A test asserting that when a flow's first reporter is unreachable, an operator's /respond is routed to the still-live machine (MACHINE_B) with its own project_root, so the response file lands on shared disk where the flow can pick it up rather than 404-ing at the dead reporter. <!--#1c7bc3f220062d3d-->
- `test_respond_defaults_to_the_live_machines_pending_call` (function) — Asserts that with no explicit `call_id` the default pending call is read off the same machine the response is dispatched to. <!--#c5427216e28e2ea3-->
- `test_interject_reaches_the_live_machine` (function) — Asserts a mid-flow interjection is delivered to node008 with its own project_root. <!--#e173139677d040d7-->
- `test_resume_and_respond_agree_on_the_target_machine` (function) — Guards against the lookup re-splitting by asserting resume and respond both resolve to the same machine, node008. <!--#86446443283ac5c1-->
- `test_respond_with_no_live_machine_is_the_old_404` (function) — Asserts fallback parity: with the fleet dark, responding to the call is refused with the pre-fix 404 naming node007. <!--#f010efa75c72ef4d-->
- `test_call_detail_pulls_from_the_live_machine` (function) — Asserts `GET /api/calls/{id}/detail` parks on a detail pull routed at node008 rather than short-circuiting to the pre-fix 503 for the dead machine. <!--#71dda533e458f2f3-->
- `test_history_detail_with_no_live_machine_still_serves_the_cache` (function) — Asserts parity when nothing is online: resolution falls back to node007 and its still-matching cached bundle is served with no daemon involved. <!--#3fcd4be0ff484379-->
- `_issue_payload` (function) — Builds the shared issue dict as one node mirrors it, with the title naming which machine read it. <!--#f8aa6add982ada65-->
- `_connect_issue_daemon` (function) — Connects a stand-in daemon that handshakes and reports no flows but mirrors the shared issue and its project_root, returning (ctx, sock). <!--#096b3403bac2cb76-->
- `_wait_for_issue_mirror` (function) — Setup barrier polling `GET /api/issues` until the named machine's issue mirror has been applied, without asserting anything about collapsing. <!--#f73467e0ada9d050-->
- `issue_fleet` (function) — Fixture where node007 mirrored the shared issue and went offline, leaving node008 mirroring the identical YAML file. <!--#db8fbf868426ed0b-->
- `test_start_flow_from_issue_dispatches_to_the_live_machine` (function) — Asserts starting a flow from the shared issue dispatches a `MSG_SPAWN_FLOW` to node008 instead of the permanent pre-fix 404 at the dead mirror. <!--#933a97b3dc959dde-->
- `test_issue_list_offers_the_issue_once` (function) — Asserts the issue list collapses both nodes' mirrors of the same YAML file into one row carrying node008's view. <!--#3c7dc5db355b06a7-->
- `test_issue_detail_resolves_to_the_live_machine` (function) — Asserts `GET /api/issues/{id}` names node008, the machine a write would actually be routed to. <!--#581641b63c9567b7-->
- `test_issue_write_with_no_live_machine_is_the_old_error` (function) — Asserts fallback parity for issues with the fleet dark: flow-from-issue 404s and reopen 503s, both naming the unreachable node007. <!--#0484c9d9a7a5c25e-->

### `tests/server/test_ui_client_unsheddable_backlog.py` (python) — Server tests asserting the WebSocket hub never silently drops unsheddable UI frames — one-shot lifecycle events and history relay frames survive a blocked console's backlog, superseded whole-state frames are coalesced instead, oversized single frames still get delivered, and a backlog past the hard ceiling disconnects the client with code 1013 rather than delivering an incomplete stream. <!--#28cdeb88e0050fd7|1eda1cbac5f80fdc-->
- `_StuckConsole` (class) — A fake WebSocket console whose `send_text` blocks on a settable `gate` event, recording delivered frames and the close code so tests can build and then release an artificial backlog. <!--#b1752138950b3a45-->
  - `_StuckConsole.__init__` (method) — Initialises the stub with no gate, an empty frame log, and no recorded close code. <!--#392121bcc15dd4ba-->
  - `_StuckConsole.send_text` (method) — Awaits the gate (if set) before decoding the JSON payload and appending it to the frame log, simulating a socket that accepts nothing while blocked. <!--#e5e0483265ceecdb-->
  - `_StuckConsole.close` (method) — Records the close code the hub used to retire this client. <!--#82a15b25a4ae84b6-->
  - `_StuckConsole.typed` (method) — Returns the received frames whose `type` matches the given payload type. <!--#b3017ac21cab3a1c-->
- `_event` (function) — Builds a one-shot `spawn_failed` lifecycle payload — an event with no cursor or poll path, so it can never be re-derived after being dropped. <!--#d55053c346e7c9e4-->
- `_relay` (function) — Builds an append-mode `history_data` relay frame carrying a single record and cursor at the given index. <!--#9f01e61f6ecb8920-->
- `test_unsheddable_events_survive_a_backlog_the_trim_cannot_shrink` (function) — Asserts a blocked console queued with twice the soft frame bound of one-shot events drops nothing and, once released, receives every event in order. <!--#564f0f5c9542ae76-->
- `test_relay_frames_of_a_delivery_are_never_shed` (function) — Asserts a mixed backlog of relay and one-shot frames sheds none of them, so a delivery's completeness declaration can never arrive over a hole. <!--#0b9e60f0c5fab680-->
- `test_a_backlog_that_cannot_be_shed_disconnects_instead_of_deleting` (function) — Asserts that past the hard frame ceiling the hub retires the client and closes it with 1013 rather than silently deleting undeliverable events. <!--#5bdf609ca63220c0-->
- `test_a_delivery_backlog_disconnects_rather_than_declaring_it_complete` (function) — Asserts an over-ceiling history delivery closes the console with 1013 and never delivers the `final` terminator to a client that lost earlier frames. <!--#38e6dcf35b787f6c-->
- `test_superseded_whole_state_frames_are_coalesced_not_kept` (function) — Asserts superseded `status_update` whole-state frames are coalesced down to the newest one while an interleaved one-shot event survives as collateral-free. <!--#d245fd5187e1b1a9-->
- `test_a_single_oversized_relay_frame_is_still_delivered` (function) — Asserts the queue byte budget bounds the backlog rather than any individual frame, so a relay larger than `UI_CLIENT_QUEUE_MAX_BYTES` is still delivered. <!--#d102e51b1626589b-->

### `tests/server/test_upload_api.py` (python) — End-to-end and unit tests for the WebUI file-upload leg, covering UploadRequestRegistry waiter bookkeeping, UPLOAD_RESULT frame handling, and the /api/uploads REST endpoint's auth, ownership, target-resolution, path/size/filename validation, daemon capability gating, happy-path byte round-trip, and error/timeout-to-HTTP status mapping. <!--#38423fcefa5231db|9b9c2b5829565bb9-->
- `client_and_app` (function) — Pytest fixture yielding a logged-in TestClient plus the authed FastAPI app used by the upload endpoint tests. <!--#c78c8fc0ec5446bd-->
- `_connect_daemon` (function) — Helper that opens an authenticated daemon WebSocket, sends HELLO (optionally with a forced protocol_version to simulate a legacy daemon), and returns the context manager and socket. <!--#caf25a6530646505-->
- `_push_flow` (function) — Helper that sends a STATUS_UPDATE carrying flows and polls until the server's flow mirror exposes the flow. <!--#8e672975c1280c54-->
- `_push_empty` (function) — Helper that sends a flowless STATUS_UPDATE and waits until the machine appears in the server mirror. <!--#9c0abe76c1599b62-->
- `_spy_on_downlink` (function) — Helper that monkeypatches the connection manager's send_to to record every frame dispatched to daemons, so tests can assert nothing was sent. <!--#d02371cd91bf85b8-->
- `_call_in_thread` (function) — Helper that runs a blocking REST call on a background thread and returns the thread plus a box that will hold the response. <!--#f4ff6bc1f1f713d2-->
- `_upload` (function) — Helper that POSTs bytes to /api/uploads with a default filename and caller-supplied target params. <!--#d8076d65e199ca34-->
- `_round_trip` (function) — Helper that issues an upload off-thread, receives the resulting UPLOAD_COMMAND frame, answers it with a caller-built reply, and returns both frame and HTTP response. <!--#31c79bb2944af323-->
- `test_registry_resolves_registers_and_discards` (function) — Asserts UploadRequestRegistry resolves a registered waiter once, forgets resolved ids, and tolerates discarding unknown or already-discarded ids. <!--#c4e670f4cad9fffc-->
- `test_upload_and_project_registries_do_not_share_a_keyspace` (function) — Asserts the upload and project command registries are independent, so an identical request id acked on one leg never resolves the other's waiter. <!--#adf732349dbb2bc2-->
- `test_upload_result_resolves_and_touches_machine` (function) — Asserts an UPLOAD_RESULT frame resolves its waiter with the stored path and also refreshes the machine's last_seen timestamp. <!--#6213e2b93535e570-->
- `test_upload_result_without_registry_is_ignored` (function) — Asserts an UPLOAD_RESULT arriving with no upload registry wired is silently ignored rather than breaking the receive loop. <!--#98ffc8a3b4ac9985-->
- `test_upload_result_without_request_id_is_ignored` (function) — Asserts an UPLOAD_RESULT with an empty request_id leaves the empty-key waiter unresolved. <!--#9741dd3f5db162a9-->
- `test_upload_requires_auth` (function) — Asserts an unauthenticated POST to /api/uploads is rejected with 401. <!--#cc9a82545573aa5f-->
- `test_upload_404s_for_unknown_flow_and_machine` (function) — Asserts uploads targeting an unknown flow_id or machine_id return 404. <!--#af13913bae343c09-->
- `test_upload_404s_across_owners` (function) — Asserts a second owner's uploads to another owner's machine or flow are indistinguishable from unknown targets and return 404. <!--#b074ee206a1be1fd-->
- `test_upload_rejects_empty_filename` (function) — Parametrized test asserting blank or whitespace filenames yield 422 with no frame dispatched to the daemon. <!--#117c76fd853dd357-->
- `test_upload_without_a_resolvable_target_is_422` (function) — Parametrized test asserting requests lacking a resolvable target return 422 with error_code UPLOAD_ERR_NO_TARGET. <!--#e036b9a61151113a-->
- `test_upload_rejects_non_absolute_project_root` (function) — Parametrized test asserting a non-absolute project_root is rejected with 422 before any downlink frame is sent. <!--#1dd6de277c352707-->
- `test_upload_over_the_limit_is_413_without_a_downlink_frame` (function) — Asserts a body exceeding MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES is refused with 413/UPLOAD_ERR_TOO_LARGE on the declared length, never reaching the daemon. <!--#aca5254460fa77dd-->
- `test_upload_at_exactly_the_limit_is_dispatched` (function) — Asserts the size limit is inclusive by dispatching an exactly-MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES payload and returning 201. <!--#9792d889a231a3bb-->
- `test_upload_is_503_when_machine_is_disconnected` (function) — Asserts that after the daemon disconnects the mirrored machine still passes the ownership gate but the upload fails with 503/UPLOAD_ERR_NOT_CONNECTED. <!--#228935aeaf5befdc-->
- `test_upload_to_a_pre_revision_5_daemon_is_501` (function) — Asserts the capability gate returns 501/UPLOAD_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DAEMON for a daemon advertising protocol version 4 and sends it no frame. <!--#a9ca9426a8b198e2-->
- `test_upload_dispatches_recoverable_bytes_and_returns_201` (function) — End-to-end happy path asserting the dispatched frame carries a trimmed project_root, filename, size and byte-identical base64 content, and the 201 body echoes the stored path and metadata. <!--#18215e9a2e39aae1-->
- `test_upload_by_flow_id_resolves_machine_and_project_root` (function) — Asserts a flow_id-only upload has its machine and project_root resolved server-side and passes the daemon's deduplicated flag through to the 201 body. <!--#8d3c13196e525b2a-->
- `test_upload_by_flow_id_without_a_project_root_is_422` (function) — Asserts a flow lacking a project_root yields 422/UPLOAD_ERR_INVALID_PATH with no frame dispatched. <!--#2da8ee3fb095656d-->
- `test_empty_file_is_a_legal_upload` (function) — Asserts a zero-byte upload is dispatched with size 0 and stored successfully with a 201. <!--#e87c58b025ebebf2-->
- `test_mismatched_request_id_does_not_wake_the_waiter` (function) — Asserts an UPLOAD_RESULT bearing a different request_id leaves the pending upload waiting until it times out to 504. <!--#95846ce0a80c162b-->
- `test_upload_times_out_to_504_and_leaves_no_waiter` (function) — Asserts an unanswered UPLOAD_COMMAND returns 504/UPLOAD_ERR_TIMEOUT and discards its parked future so no waiter leaks. <!--#cd1379a608ffa688-->
- `test_daemon_error_codes_map_to_http_status` (function) — Parametrized test asserting each daemon-reported upload error_code maps to the expected HTTP status and is surfaced at the body's top level alongside the daemon's detail text. <!--#1d08d179a05d72c6-->
- `test_failure_body_falls_back_when_daemon_sends_no_prose` (function) — Asserts a failure ack carrying only an error_code still yields 500 with a default "upload failed on daemon" detail. <!--#60a75d3b7717153f-->

### `tests/server/test_upload_fetch_api.py` (python) — End-to-end and unit tests for the WebUI's `GET /api/uploads/file` fetch leg, covering auth and cross-owner 404 gating, target/path validation before the wire, the revision-6 daemon capability gate, FETCH_COMMAND/FETCH_RESULT round-trips with byte-exact base64 fidelity and cache/content-type headers, and failure paths (disconnect 503, timeout 504 with no waiter leak, daemon error-code mapping, undecodable payload 502). <!--#5514a6bd178721d9|4c53e9c73976c9ce-->
- `client_and_app` (function) — Pytest fixture yielding a logged-in `TestClient` plus its authenticated FastAPI app for the upload-fetch endpoint tests. <!--#c78c8fc0ec5446bd-->
- `_connect_daemon` (function) — Helper that opens an authenticated daemon WebSocket at `/ws`, sending a HELLO whose `protocol_version` can be overridden to exercise the revision-6 capability gate, and returns the context manager and socket. <!--#03739c12a8b9fc7c-->
- `_push_flow` (function) — Helper that sends a STATUS_UPDATE carrying one or more flows and polls `/api/flows/{FLOW}` until the server's flow mirror reflects it. <!--#8e672975c1280c54-->
- `_push_empty` (function) — Helper that sends a flowless STATUS_UPDATE and polls the machine-projects endpoint until the machine appears in the mirror. <!--#9c0abe76c1599b62-->
- `_spy_on_downlink` (function) — Helper that monkeypatches the connection manager's `send_to` to record every frame dispatched to daemons, so tests can assert nothing reached the wire. <!--#d02371cd91bf85b8-->
- `_call_in_thread` (function) — Helper that runs a blocking REST call on a background thread so the test loop can service the daemon socket, returning the thread and a result box. <!--#f4ff6bc1f1f713d2-->
- `_fetch` (function) — Helper that issues a `GET /api/uploads/file` request with a default `path` parameter and caller-supplied target parameters. <!--#afe3c238ffead274-->
- `_ok_reply` (function) — Helper that builds a successful FETCH_RESULT frame carrying base64-encoded content for a given request frame. <!--#bb898021637899e2-->
- `_round_trip` (function) — Helper that drives a full fetch exchange — call in a thread, assert the outgoing FETCH_COMMAND, answer it with the supplied reply — and returns the frame and HTTP response. <!--#aeb387393e7a1b6c-->
- `test_fetch_result_resolves_the_parked_waiter` (function) — Unit test asserting that handling a FETCH_RESULT resolves the future parked in the `UploadRequestRegistry` under its request id. <!--#0a624640b2aa13e4-->
- `test_fetch_and_upload_registries_do_not_share_a_keyspace` (function) — Test that upload and fetch registries are independent, so an identical request id in flight on both legs resolves only the matching waiter. <!--#05bea9746a5e3ade-->
- `test_fetch_result_without_registry_or_request_id_is_ignored` (function) — Test that a FETCH_RESULT with no registry attached, or with an empty request id, is a silent no-op. <!--#88b6361308fa857b-->
- `test_fetch_requires_auth` (function) — Test that an unauthenticated request to `/api/uploads/file` is rejected with 401. <!--#91d4c20f8fa9c22c-->
- `test_fetch_404s_for_unknown_flow_and_machine` (function) — Test that fetching against an unknown `flow_id` or unknown `machine_id` returns 404. <!--#c00ddf2e0a60e340-->
- `test_fetch_404s_across_owners` (function) — Test that another owner's flow and machine read as 404 and that the ownership gate refuses before any frame is dispatched to the daemon. <!--#2f0417f59eb34b16-->
- `test_fetch_without_a_resolvable_target_is_422` (function) — Parameterised test that requests lacking a resolvable target return 422 with `UPLOAD_ERR_NO_TARGET`. <!--#c9e352c972496b12-->
- `test_fetch_without_a_path_is_422` (function) — Parameterised test that a missing or empty `path` yields 422 with `FETCH_ERR_INVALID_PATH` and sends nothing to the daemon. <!--#48d0eda53455c6d8-->
- `test_fetch_rejects_malformed_paths_before_the_wire` (function) — Parameterised test that absolute or `..`-bearing paths are rejected early with 422 `FETCH_ERR_INVALID_PATH` so the frame never reaches the socket, while noting the real containment boundary lives in the daemon. <!--#00470abcda86fd10-->
- `test_fetch_rejects_non_absolute_project_root` (function) — Parameterised test that a non-absolute `project_root` is rejected with 422 before any daemon frame is sent. <!--#2e8eb36b23d48dcc-->
- `test_fetch_by_flow_id_without_a_project_root_is_422` (function) — Test that targeting a flow whose mirrored snapshot carries no `project_root` fails with 422 `UPLOAD_ERR_INVALID_PATH` and no downlink frame. <!--#f153c5350088fb8d-->
- `test_fetch_is_503_when_machine_is_disconnected` (function) — Test that a fetch for a mirrored-but-disconnected machine passes the ownership gate and fails at delivery with 503 `UPLOAD_ERR_NOT_CONNECTED`. <!--#e8ad6bee731ae5f2-->
- `test_fetch_from_a_pre_revision_6_daemon_is_501` (function) — Test that a daemon advertising protocol version 5 makes the fetch return 501 `UPLOAD_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DAEMON` without ever sending the unsupported frame. <!--#3afcabec86a36e9a-->
- `test_fetch_returns_the_exact_bytes_with_cache_and_type_headers` (function) — Happy-path test asserting byte-for-byte fidelity across the base64 hop, `project_root` trimming, and the response's content-type, `private`/`immutable` cache-control, `Vary: Cookie`, nosniff and inline-disposition headers. <!--#c6bc0f52bb4af09a-->
- `test_both_target_forms_reach_the_same_file` (function) — Test that targeting by `flow_id` and by `machine_id`+`project_root` produce identical FETCH_COMMAND payloads and identical bytes. <!--#410e66a386912a75-->
- `test_content_type_comes_from_the_extension_whitelist` (function) — Parameterised test that the response content-type is derived from the path's extension whitelist rather than sniffed, alongside the nosniff header. <!--#96c1007288c456a8-->
- `test_empty_file_is_a_legal_fetch` (function) — Test that a 0-byte file is served as a successful 200 with empty content rather than treated as missing. <!--#77618ebff82701fb-->
- `test_mismatched_request_id_does_not_wake_the_waiter` (function) — Test that a FETCH_RESULT bearing a different request id leaves the pending waiter parked, so the call times out to 504. <!--#59dc68fd4c5213c2-->
- `test_fetch_times_out_to_504_and_leaves_no_waiter` (function) — Test that an unanswered FETCH_COMMAND yields 504 `UPLOAD_ERR_TIMEOUT` and that the fetch registry's waiter map is left empty (no leak). <!--#844bd4b81c46fec0-->
- `test_daemon_error_codes_map_to_http_status` (function) — Parameterised test that daemon-reported error codes map to the right HTTP status, surface `error_code` and `detail` at the body's top level, and are never cached as immutable. <!--#ce657087c825b65a-->
- `test_failure_body_falls_back_when_daemon_sends_no_prose` (function) — Test that a daemon failure without an `error` message still returns the mapped status with a default `fetch failed on daemon` detail. <!--#e8dc02465a7e6868-->
- `test_undecodable_payload_from_daemon_is_502` (function) — Test that an `ok=true` reply whose `content_b64` is not valid base64 is reported as 502 `FETCH_ERR_READ_FAILED`. <!--#de4dbc6cf4606441-->

### `tests/server/test_viewers_presence.py` (python) — Unit tests for the server-side browser-presence publication (protocol revision 4), verifying the UiHub fires its on_presence_edge callback only on 0↔non-0 client-count transitions, ConnectionManager.broadcast_viewers fans MSG_VIEWERS frames to every connected daemon, and the heartbeat PING and v4 handshake carry the live viewers level — all exercised against lightweight fake WebSockets with no live network. <!--#0c8729133eb3de39|85de6f696367fad7-->
- `_Disconnect` (class) — A sentinel exception raised by fake sockets to signal that no more frames remain (a simulated client disconnect). <!--#0b594fd2b546acad-->
- `_FakeUiWS` (class) — A stand-in for a web-frontend UI WebSocket that records sent JSON payloads and can be marked broken to raise on send. <!--#5e6dfc7cfded4431-->
  - `_FakeUiWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the fake UI socket's captured-payload list and broken flag. <!--#a1bc4439ebd8a29d-->
  - `_FakeUiWS.send_text` (method) — Decodes and records the sent JSON payload, or raises RuntimeError when the socket is flagged broken. <!--#fcd543f5da0c83fa-->
- `_FakeDaemonWS` (class) — A stand-in for a server-side daemon WebSocket driven by a queued inbound frame list, recording decoded outbound frames and connection state. <!--#f922d160138b70c4-->
  - `_FakeDaemonWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the fake daemon socket's inbound queue, sent-frame list, accept/close flags, and broken flag. <!--#6d64fa8237ab8082-->
  - `_FakeDaemonWS.accept` (method) — Marks the fake daemon socket as accepted. <!--#5469a86e64b0aac3-->
  - `_FakeDaemonWS.receive_text` (method) — Pops and returns the next queued inbound frame, raising _Disconnect once the queue is empty. <!--#2531fa1e77e264fb-->
  - `_FakeDaemonWS.send_text` (method) — Decodes and records the sent protocol frame, or raises RuntimeError when the socket is flagged broken. <!--#95309e4b9e5cf8ad-->
  - `_FakeDaemonWS.close` (method) — Marks the fake daemon socket as closed. <!--#d37c335b4328d9f4-->
  - `_FakeDaemonWS.frames_of_type` (method) — Returns all recorded outbound frames matching a given message type. <!--#af090ea270f96f0b-->
- `_BlockingDaemonWS` (class) — A _FakeDaemonWS variant whose receive blocks forever and whose fail_next_send flag ends the heartbeat loop, used for heartbeat/PING tests. <!--#6fecf7eb379f0677-->
  - `_BlockingDaemonWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the blocking daemon socket and its fail_next_send flag. <!--#0899a49f202a2017-->
  - `_BlockingDaemonWS.receive_text` (method) — Blocks indefinitely on an unset asyncio.Event until cancelled at loop teardown. <!--#2d91ea2a71918451-->
  - `_BlockingDaemonWS.send_text` (method) — Records the sent frame, or raises RuntimeError when fail_next_send is set to terminate the heartbeat loop. <!--#1eefeb64ed2eb6c6-->
- `_EdgeRecorder` (class) — An async-callable that captures presence-edge callback invocations and can optionally raise to test failure isolation. <!--#1cd073c5a5889504-->
  - `_EdgeRecorder.__init__` (method) — Initializes the edge recorder's calls list and optional raise-on-call flag. <!--#c4fb28058dec2e98-->
  - `_EdgeRecorder.__call__` (method) — Records the presence count passed to the edge callback and optionally raises RuntimeError. <!--#b2493d70f2c85b80-->
- `test_first_connect_fires_edge_second_does_not` (function) — Asserts the UiHub fires the presence edge on the 0→1 client transition but stays silent on the 1→2 registration. <!--#2fa2f18bfa12f494-->
- `test_last_disconnect_fires_edge_penultimate_does_not` (function) — Asserts the UiHub fires the presence edge only on the final 1→0 disconnect, not on the intermediate 2→1 one. <!--#fc54274369c13dcd-->
- `test_unregister_unknown_socket_fires_no_edge` (function) — Asserts unregistering a never-registered socket triggers no presence edge and leaves the client count unchanged. <!--#ab1921e8a61beebf-->
- `test_edge_callback_exception_does_not_break_registration` (function) — Asserts a raising edge callback does not break register/unregister nor corrupt the client count. <!--#83ac323f2efe935f-->
- `test_no_callback_injected_behaves_as_before` (function) — Asserts a UiHub with no edge callback still tracks client_count and distinct_owners correctly. <!--#c9b13827e9ef9f33-->
- `test_fan_out_prune_of_last_client_fires_zero_edge` (function) — Asserts a broadcast that prunes the last dead client fires the non-0→0 edge at the prune and the late unregister does not re-fire it. <!--#e4bdfe9c369b4aaf-->
- `test_broadcast_viewers_sends_to_all_daemons_and_records_metrics` (function) — Asserts ConnectionManager.broadcast_viewers sends a MSG_VIEWERS count frame to every connected daemon and records wire metrics. <!--#b80e989a31dd73cc-->
- `test_broadcast_viewers_single_send_failure_does_not_block_others` (function) — Asserts a single broken daemon socket during broadcast_viewers does not prevent healthy daemons from receiving the frame. <!--#eca5237cfd3f48d4-->
- `test_broadcast_viewers_with_no_daemons_is_a_noop` (function) — Asserts broadcast_viewers is a safe no-op when no daemons are connected. <!--#50eab66fb56d48fb-->
- `test_app_assembly_wires_edge_to_daemon_broadcast` (function) — Asserts create_app wires the hub's presence edge to manager.broadcast_viewers so UI register/unregister emits MSG_VIEWERS to daemons. <!--#6e124396542b3e1f-->
- `_wait_for` (function) — An async polling helper that awaits until a predicate becomes true or raises AssertionError on timeout. <!--#255b5262c4557d36-->
- `test_heartbeat_ping_carries_live_viewers_count` (function) — Asserts the daemon heartbeat PING carries the current live viewer count, reflecting mid-connection changes on the next beat. <!--#c3d757424c9fb1b0-->
- `test_heartbeat_ping_without_hub_stays_revision3_compatible` (function) — Asserts that without a hub the heartbeat PING omits the viewers field, staying revision-3 compatible. <!--#53f7852ca45eec0c-->
- `test_handshake_sends_immediate_viewers_level` (function) — Asserts a v4 daemon handshake sends an immediate MSG_VIEWERS level after the WELCOME reflecting the current client count. <!--#3defedcb7b9fc406-->
- `test_handshake_skips_viewers_for_pre_v4_daemon` (function) — Asserts the handshake gates on advertised protocol_version and sends no MSG_VIEWERS to a revision-3 daemon. <!--#d59364e60d158b67-->
- `test_handshake_without_hub_sends_no_viewers` (function) — Asserts the daemon handshake sends no MSG_VIEWERS level when no hub is provided. <!--#21d8ccdb07e1dc6b-->
- `test_daemon_ping_with_viewers_still_replies_pong` (function) — Unit test asserting that DaemonClient._dispatch replies with a single MSG_PONG (matching seq) to a PING carrying an extra viewers field, confirming the level-piggyback field is safe to send to any daemon. <!--#d3ccc3f6271babd5-->
- `_ClientOutWS` (class) — The daemon client's outbound socket stand-in, capturing daemon→server frames and exposing their types. <!--#3dc7fd4960956972-->
  - `_ClientOutWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the client-out socket's sent-frame list. <!--#b8b92aad379d234c-->
  - `_ClientOutWS.send` (method) — Decodes and records an outbound daemon→server frame. <!--#7d44362527b3e749-->
  - `_ClientOutWS.types` (method) — Returns the message types of all recorded outbound frames. <!--#db4dd156b4e135b1-->
- `_PresenceBridgeWS` (class) — A server-side daemon socket that pipes downlink frames directly into a live DaemonClient's dispatcher, an in-memory stand-in for the WebSocket hop with a fail_next_send teardown hook. <!--#f15764803ce86cfb-->
  - `_PresenceBridgeWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the bridge with the target client, its outbound socket, and the fail_next_send flag. <!--#1ac920d8dc6a3b69-->
  - `_PresenceBridgeWS.accept` (method) — No-op accept for the presence-bridge socket. <!--#fae6e77d45b9fa2d-->
  - `_PresenceBridgeWS.receive_text` (method) — Blocks forever since the daemon uplink is captured elsewhere, cancelled at teardown. <!--#fd59e0157de181f6-->
  - `_PresenceBridgeWS.send_text` (method) — Decodes the server downlink frame and dispatches it directly into the live DaemonClient, or raises when fail_next_send is set. <!--#ef4afe94c738f3b1-->
  - `_PresenceBridgeWS.close` (method) — No-op close for the presence-bridge socket. <!--#4e88a37116abc426-->
- `_IndexedHistory` (class) — A minimal stub history provider returning empty index/flows so the DaemonClient's index-push behavior is observable. <!--#29dd89010522f16d-->
  - `_IndexedHistory.build_index` (method) — Returns an empty history index. <!--#c4f69f683d154763-->
  - `_IndexedHistory.read_active_flows` (method) — Returns an empty list of active flows for the given cursors. <!--#ed6782389aff458e-->
  - `_IndexedHistory.active_flow_signature` (method) — Returns an empty active-flow signature. <!--#d5e6eba440e59874-->
  - `_IndexedHistory.invalidate_index_cache` (method) — No-op index-cache invalidation. <!--#8488b095834d7518-->
  - `_IndexedHistory.live_flow_ids` (method) — Returns an empty set of live flow ids. <!--#e1b38827c0d4f406-->
- `_make_client` (function) — Factory building a DaemonClient wired with the stub history provider and configurable fast/status poll intervals for presence tests. <!--#db7bc209a8dc9ecd-->
- `test_presence_full_flow_open_upshift_close_downshift` (function) — End-to-end test that a UI connect fires the edge and upshifts the daemon to fast intervals with a forced full first screen, while UI disconnect downshifts it back into the idle gear. <!--#ccce1c23ad2929c1-->
- `test_ping_level_self_heals_lost_edges_in_both_directions` (function) — Asserts that with no edge callback wired, the heartbeat PING viewers level self-heals a lost presence edge within one interval in both the 0→1 and 1→0 directions. <!--#88df3e69f4b3f168-->
- `_SessionDaemonWS` (class) — A _FakeDaemonWS variant that stays connected after draining frames, exposing drained/release events so a test can act mid-session before the disconnect. <!--#105c92e122b7c7e5-->
  - `_SessionDaemonWS.__init__` (method) — Initializes the session daemon socket with drained and release asyncio events. <!--#0e74b9a35811f6df-->
  - `_SessionDaemonWS.receive_text` (method) — Returns queued frames, then signals drained and blocks on release before raising _Disconnect to end the session. <!--#e8c06901e11259ee-->
- `test_v3_daemon_session_survives_ui_churn_on_a_v4_server` (function) — Asserts a v3 daemon on a v4 server keeps a revision-3 handshake, shrugs off mid-session MSG_VIEWERS broadcasts from UI churn, and continues heartbeating through clean disconnect. <!--#2c01ebcab49aba3a-->

### `tests/server/test_ws_heartbeat_constants.py` (python) — Pytest module guarding the WebSocket keepalive configuration, asserting that `ws.PING_INTERVAL`/`ws.HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT` keep their relaxed values (20.0/90.0) and that `app_module.run` forwards them to uvicorn as `ws_ping_interval`/`ws_ping_timeout` so the transport keepalive never outpaces the application-level heartbeat. <!--#d71cc6d8ee6832a7|8e2caf5e8a99c5cb-->
- `test_heartbeat_constants_relaxed` (function) — Test asserting the WebSocket module's relaxed heartbeat constants, that ws.PING_INTERVAL equals 20.0 and ws.HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT equals 90.0. <!--#c75108242669d4b6-->
- `test_run_declares_the_transport_keepalive` (function) — Regression test asserting that `app_module.run` passes `ws_ping_interval`/`ws_ping_timeout` to uvicorn derived from the app's own `ws.PING_INTERVAL`/`ws.HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT`, so the transport keepalive never kills a connection the application-level heartbeat still considers alive (stubbing `uvicorn` via `monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules, ...)` to capture the kwargs). <!--#d2d1d1c7b4e6eb26-->
